commit.message:
Add initial workspace context to Copilot Agent Host chats (#337342)

* Add bounded initial workspace context for Copilot Agent Host

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Format workspace context regression tests

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Make workspace snapshot test headings platform independent

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Scope virtual timers to the workspace context timeout test

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Snapshot the worktree a Copilot turn actually runs in

The first-turn workspace snapshot read session state, which still names the
picked folder when a worktree session sends its first message: the worktree
is created in resolveWorkingDirectoryBeforeSend, but state only picks up its
path after the provider materializes. The snapshot therefore listed the
original checkout and showed its absolute path while the agent worked in the
worktree.

Pass the resolved working directories, the same ones handed to the agent's
sendMessage, to outgoing-turn contributions and build the snapshot from them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep the workspace snapshot to first turns and off the TTFT path

Only the first turn of a new conversation gets the snapshot: the default chat
or a user-created peer chat with no completed turns. Forks and side chats
already inherit the source chat's history, and tool-spawned chats receive a
focused task from the chat that delegated them.

Start enumerating when the first turn is accepted so the file list overlaps
working-directory, model and attachment resolution instead of adding to time
to first token. The warm-up is skipped while a worktree is pending, because
the worktree does not exist yet. The send now waits at most one second (was
two) and keeps the roots that are ready instead of dropping the whole
snapshot when one root is slow.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address workspace snapshot review findings

- Prepare the rendered snapshot for a worktree session as soon as the
  worktree exists (onDidChangeWorkingDirectoryPending) instead of when the
  outgoing-turn contribution runs, so creating it overlaps the checkpoint,
  model selection and attachment resolution.
- Isolate failures per root: a root that cannot be listed is logged and
  omitted, and the healthy roots are still sent.
- Tie preparation to the turn: it is stopped when the send stops waiting,
  the turn ends, or the preparation is replaced. The new uncached
  AgentHostWorkspaceFiles.enumerate stops its ripgrep process on
  cancellation and never starts a queued scan that was cancelled. The cached
  getFiles used by file completions is unchanged.
- Skip bare repositories and directories inside .git before scanning.
- Build the tree from path segments instead of URIs; at the 50,000-file cap
  this drops the synchronous build from about 360ms to about 37ms.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Never wait for the workspace snapshot on send, and release it with its chat

- The first send now includes only roots whose tree is already rendered for
  the directories the turn runs in, and omits roots still being listed,
  instead of waiting up to a second per root. Preparation still starts when
  the turn is accepted, or when a first-send worktree is created.
- If a session's worktree already exists when its first turn is accepted,
  the default chat prepares in the worktree, as the send path does.
- Stop preparation when a chat is removed (SessionChatRemoved) or its session
  is removed (onDidRemoveSession), not only on turn end.
- Recognize a linked worktree's admin directory (HEAD, gitdir, and a
  commondir naming a repository with objects/) even when its common
  directory is not named .git, and test it with a real linked worktree.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Build the workspace snapshot without blocking, for every waiting chat

- Build the tree in batches of 2,000 paths that yield to the event loop and
  stop once preparation is cancelled, so a large root cannot hold up the
  provider send. Sorted children are cached so rendering sorts each
  directory once.
- Track every first-turn chat waiting for a session's worktree instead of
  only the last one, and prepare or release each independently.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Make the initial workspace snapshot reliable, bounded, and observable

Evals showed the first model request leaves ~0.7s after the turn starts, and
13-14% of sessions dropped the snapshot because a full ripgrep enumeration
had not finished. Drops were logged only at trace, so misses could not be
diagnosed.

- Walk directories breadth first through IFileService, reading only the
  directories whose names fit the 2,000-character budget, instead of
  enumerating every file with ripgrep. A cold send-time walk takes 2-29ms on
  real repositories, including a 36k-file one that took ~0.8s to enumerate.
- Wait up to one second at send for roots still being prepared, and start
  preparation at send when the turn skipped ChatTurnStarted or its
  directories changed, instead of dropping the snapshot.
- Like the classic Copilot Chat workspace structure, skip hidden entries and
  a short list of dependency and build folders, and do not apply
  .gitignore, which emptied the tree for projects kept under ignored folders
  such as vendor/.
- Log every first send at info with the outcome of each root, and report
  agentHost.workspaceSnapshot telemetry with included, pending, empty, and
  unreadable root counts and the wait time.
- Revert the uncached enumerate added to AgentHostWorkspaceFiles, which is
  no longer used, so the expected ripgrep cancellation no longer logs a
  warning.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Do not add a second workspace snapshot to an unloaded restored chat

send_message can start a turn on a restored peer chat before its history is
loaded. Its merged session state then reports no turns, so the chat looked
new and could receive another snapshot on top of the one already in its
provider conversation. Treat a chat as new only when its chat state is
loaded and has no turns, matching classic Copilot Chat, where history is
always loaded before a request runs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Start the workspace snapshot for host-started first turns too

create_session, send_message, automations, and other
AgentHostTurnService.startTurnMessage paths dispatch ChatTurnStarted as a

  event. A tracked first turn that ends without it is remembered as
  undispatched, so it does not count as provider history.

  is still never treated as new.

Publish chat background work and show background shells above the chat input (#338723)

* Publish chat background work and show background shells

Publish Copilot's running and waiting shells and running background subagents as AHP chat background work, and project the shells onto the Agents window's Background Shells pill.

* Publish only background shells as background work

Follow the protocol change that starts background work with shells only. The provider still skips kinds it doesn't render, since newer hosts can send more.

* Stop publishing background shell status

Follow the protocol change that drops status from background work. Every listed shell is unfinished, and Copilot never reports a shell as idle. The pill now shows the attached or detached mode and elapsed time.

* Ignore background work in the read shell E2E snapshot

The async shell is now published as background work from a separate task-list read, so its timing against the tool calls isn't part of this scenario.

* Drop terminal from the background shell work protocol copy

Follow the protocol change that removes the unused terminal field. Nothing in VS Code set or read it.

* Show background shells in the editor window's chat

Move the Background Shells pill control and the background work projection into the workbench so the editor window's Agent Host chat input can show the same pill as the Agents window. Share the pill's accessibility help between both windows.

* Agent Host: reconcile background work after a Copilot client restart

Addresses review feedback on stale shells after a client restart or crash. A session that replaced another started with an empty baseline, so shells the new runtime no longer reported stayed listed. The host now passes the chat's current background work when a watch attaches, and the session removes entries missing from its first read.

* Agent Host: keep reading background work after an abort

Addresses review feedback on the abort race. Aborting a turn bumped the task status revision without queuing a read, so a read in flight was discarded and the detached shell poll could stop for good, since detached shells report no exit on their own. The session now reads again once the abort settles.

* Sync background work protocol with AHP

Match microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482: background shells can link their terminal, and background subagents are their own kind that points at the subagent's chat. The Background Shells pill still shows shells only.

* Publish background subagents as background work

Running background agents are published with their chat. Idle ones have already reported back, so they're left out. Shells don't set a terminal yet; that waits for output streaming.

* Key background shell rows by the protocol id

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338723#discussion_r4136322435.
Rows used Copilot's shell ID from _meta as their identity, which the protocol doesn't guarantee is unique. Key rows by the entry id instead, and show Copilot's shell ID separately, only when the agent reports one.

* Keep background work out of the retained subagent E2E snapshot

Running background subagents are now published as background work. Those actions come from a separate task-list read, so their timing against the subagent's tool calls isn't part of this scenario, and CI's snapshot comparison failed on every platform. Ignore them here, as the read-shell scenario already does.

* Remove a stray E2E snapshot artifact

A failing local run left this .actual file next to the retained background subagent snapshot, and it was committed by mistake. Hygiene rejects it, and the test runner logs when it deletes it, which fails the no-console-output check.

* Sync the background work docs with AHP

Match microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482 at d513c6fb, which says background work lists only active work.

* Show only Detached on background shells

Attached is the common case, so an unlabeled shell reads as attached and only detached shells carry a label, matching the GitHub app.

* Sync the AHP protocol with microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482

Take agent-host-protocol at c53aef24, the head of #482 after merging main, so this PR and #482 can merge back to back. That also brings in chat move and reorder from #484: reject moveChat with InvalidParams, since clients may only move chats that advertise movable: true and this host never does.

* Sync the shorter background work description from AHP

Take agent-host-protocol at ab694bfd, the head of microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482. The only change is the shortened backgroundWork doc text from its review.

* Read background shells from chat state instead of chat summaries

microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482 dropped ChatSummary.backgroundWork, so
session subscribers no longer receive every chat's background work. The
Agents window pill now reads ChatState.backgroundWork through the active
session's chat subscription, like the editor window already did, and the
state manager no longer mirrors the list into chat summaries.

Syncs the protocol to microsoft/agent-host-protocol@dc9ff6b0.

commit.message:
Mark virtual tool groups as used when they are activated (#338812)

Activating a virtual tool group never updated the group's own
lastUsedOnTurn, so a just-activated group ranked as least recently used.
When the activation pushed the tool count over HARD_TOOL_LIMIT, the trim
collapsed that same group before the request was sent, and the model
could never reach the tools it was told were activated.

commit.message:
chat: preserve reasoning across turns and custom providers (#338874)

* chat: preserve earlier-turn reasoning for opted-in models

Honor preserved-thinking capabilities in both Copilot and extension-contributed endpoints. Enable Kimi K3 by default and support per-model opt-in or opt-out while retaining same-model and Messages API safeguards.

Fixes #338820. Verified with red-green request serialization tests and 607 targeted tests.

* chat: carry reasoning protocol capabilities through model API

Declare the selected provider API and adaptive-thinking mode across language-model registration and selection. Unknown protocols no longer bypass the Messages safeguard, and extension-contributed endpoints honor family aliases when choosing the preserved-thinking default.

Address both CCR findings on #338874 with custom-provider red-green regressions and API transport coverage.

* chat: tolerate hosts without reasoning protocol API

Feature-detect the proposed model protocol enum during provider registration and endpoint construction. Published Insiders used by Copilot CI may predate the API; leave their protocol unknown to preserve replay safeguards.

* chat: preserve reasoning state through custom providers

Request opaque reasoning state from custom providers and retain it when a thinking completion marker arrives. Recognize the documented k3 and k3-256k aliases while preserving protocol-specific replay policy and explicit model overrides.

Add streaming regressions for stateless Responses and signed Messages, and cover both K3 aliases across the two history renderers. Refs #338820.

commit.message:
Don't cache prompt discovery results from a cancelled scan (#338893)

* Don't cache prompt discovery results from a cancelled scan

Follow-up to #338883. That fix made the filesystem branches of
computeListPromptFiles report cancellation as an error, but extension
prompt file providers bail out of their loop without throwing. When the
filesystem branches are policy-blocked or have already finished, the
combined Promise.all resolves and the partial list is cached permanently,
which is the same "no prompt files" state #338883 set out to fix.

Re-check the token after the combined computation so no branch that
swallows cancellation can have its result accepted and cached.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Addresses PR feedback: the coding guidelines limit comments inside method
bodies to a single line.

commit.message:
agentHost: recover SSH and WSL sessions after backend failure

Invalidate a shared SSH session when relay lease acquisition fails or times
out, closing all of its leases so the next attempt reconnects and rediscovers
the agent host endpoint. Skip the post-failure endpoint diagnostic after a
timeout and bound it otherwise so a half-open SSH client cannot hang reconnect.

Tear down a WSL session when its agent host exits after startup or when a
relay cannot be opened against it, so the next connect bootstraps fresh.

Guard the protocol client dispose callback so client cleanup always runs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: Reintroduce agent bakeoff (#337741)

* sessions: reintroduce agent bakeoff

Reapply the session comparison experience while preserving ordinary custom group status icons and actions. Exclude inline comparison stop controls and the session header close action.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 539210bd-556f-4d13-b55a-b9f0615b613d

* sessions: scope comparison header styling

Limit close-button reveal behavior to active comparison grids so ordinary Sessions headers retain their existing behavior.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: retire archived comparison groups

Remove the comparison-specific Done control, automatically delete a comparison-owned group once all participants are archived, and left-align its header text.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: restore comparison archive action

Show the archive checkmark only for completed comparison groups, ensure hidden controls cannot leak into active or ordinary groups, and archive all comparison participants when invoked.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: allow archiving active comparisons

Keep the comparison archive action available while participants are running. Session archival already cancels active chats before invoking the provider, so group archival remains safe and fails explicitly if cancellation fails.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: smooth comparison startup

Clear the comparison prompt as soon as submission begins, restore it if launch fails, and withhold a comparison-owned group until every attempt launch resolves so the list never flashes a partial group.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: gate comparison list on launch completion

Track the initial attempt launch explicitly so the Sessions list stays empty until every launch promise settles, even when all participant resources are assigned before the final session is published.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: show pending comparison startup

Render the comparison-owned group immediately with an explicit attempt-starting summary while withholding partial participant rows until launch completion.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: report comparison startup progress

Keep partial attempt rows hidden while reporting how many configured attempts are ready during comparison provisioning.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: advertise worktrees for all agent host agents

* sessions: address agent bakeoff review feedback

- Codex: derive whole-turn token totals from thread-cumulative usage instead of the last call
- Let the grid controller own side-pane hiding and skip it for opens that did not show the session
- Ignore archived comparisons for grid layout, Judge isolation, and inactive-pane notifications
- Strip remote connection details from comparison telemetry agent and model ids
- Drop a rolled-back Judge draft so Retry Judge is offered again
- Judge a completed attempt alongside failed ones instead of stalling
- Hold judging while an attempt is only missing from the catalog; confirmed deletion releases it
- Record attempts interrupted by a window reload as failed launches
- Hide Delete Group while a comparison is still launching
- Only retire a comparison from Archive once every participant is archived

* sessions: fix test and fixture stubs for agent bakeoff

- Restore the grid stub in the Mobile Sessions Part and Agents Part Card tests; `layoutSessionGrid` does not exist in this change
- Stub `setForceTabbedPicker` on the model picker widget in the action item test
- Stub the comparison lookups the Sessions list calls in its component fixtures

* sessions: keep ordinary group titles left-aligned

The stacked title and summary layout was applied to every session group, so the base section rule's
`align-items: center` centered ordinary group titles horizontally. Scope the column layout to
comparison groups so ordinary groups keep the section label layout.

* sessions: show comparison attempts while launching

Publish in-flight new sessions through the management catalog and track Agent Host pending skeletons per session so concurrent comparison attempts remain visible.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: use autopilot for allow all comparisons

commit.message:
sessions: Show per-chat modified times in sessions list (#338969)

* sessions: Show per-chat modified times in sessions list

Render the main and peer chats with their own modified times while keeping aggregate session recency for sorting. Resolve exact multi-chat timestamps lazily and preserve the single-chat subscription optimization.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Complete automation chat test fixtures

Add the main chat status and modified time consumed by session row rendering.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Address per-chat timestamp review feedback

Roll back incomplete restores, defer aggregate change stats until timestamps resolve, and keep offscreen chat rows from hydrating session details.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Stabilize peer chat detail rows

Reserve the non-compact details line without deferred height correction and accept the intentional session-list screenshot updates.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Persist peer chat modified times

Store exact peer chat recency in the central catalog and compatibility metadata so restart restoration does not require provider backing. Keep lifecycle updates synchronized through a chat contribution and align merged-base session list expectations.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Keep peer timestamps out of catalog

Persist each peer chat's modified time only in that chat's local metadata. Restore central and legacy peer catalogs to membership-only data while retaining restart-safe timestamp hydration.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Remove peer timestamp persistence

Revert the Agent Host persistence workaround and its associated tests. Keep peer modified times provider-owned rather than adding host-side production storage or lifecycle behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Keep peer restoration lazy

Do not require provider metadata while restoring peer catalog entries. Providers materialize peer backing and transcript on first access, so eager metadata requests can make otherwise valid sessions fail to reopen.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Complete main chat test fixtures

Populate main-chat status and modified-time observables in lightweight context-menu and automation fixtures so session rows can render per-chat timestamps.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Complete blocked session fixtures

Give blocked-session main-chat stubs the status and modified-time observables required by session row rendering.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: Defer client restarts until background subagents settle (#338962)

A background subagent can still be finishing after its root turn goes idle.
The deferred CopilotClient restart only waited for root turns, so a restart
requested in that window, for example when another window's sign-in changes
the credential mode, tore the session down under the subagent and left its
chat in progress.

Hold deferred restarts until each chat has no active turn or subagent, and
report idleness again when the last subagent settles after its root turn so
the parked restart still runs.

Refs #338600

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
github: introduce explicit authorization-scoped clients (#338864)

* github: introduce explicit authorization-scoped clients

Share admission and cooldown coordination across explicit clients while isolating credentials, caches and subscriptions by authorization context. Migrate workbench and Agent Host consumers without a compatibility singleton API.

Preserve selected-client caches, bound silent account selection, and make async lease adoption and credential-change handling safe.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: preserve cooldowns and clients across token renewal

Carry resolved-account core and secondary cooldowns into stable identity bootstrap coordination, recheck tokens after waits, and keep already-resolved peers eligible.

Distinguish workbench token renewal from account, scope, issuer, or session changes and ignore unchanged default-account metadata notifications. Restore CI formatting compliance and add targeted regressions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: preserve host account identity across token expiry

Forward optional account provenance through authentication metadata so known account switches do not inherit another account's bootstrap cooldown. Keep the legacy fallback, verify actual identity through GitHub, and preserve same-account renewal behavior.

Reconcile silent scoped-token selection changes during acquisition and lookup, retiring stale clients and notifying dependents after expiry or pruning. Cover forwarding, replay, cooldown isolation, expired renewal, and reentrant cancellation.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: retry session lookups invalidated by auth changes

Discard obsolete authentication snapshots when the provider changes during a silent session lookup. Keep retries within the existing cancellation/deadline scope and cover grant changes, removal, renewal and provider isolation.

Update the remote-host authentication assertion to include the account provenance now forwarded on the wire, fixing the shared browser/Electron CI failure.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
[4/4] authentication: enable multiple configured enterprise hosts (#338080)

* authentication: enable multiple configured enterprise hosts

Enable unordered enterprise host configuration, host-qualified account selection, and the extension-owned sign-in picker on top of the reviewed engine lifecycle and credential storage layers. Wire trust-aware enrollment and retain the complete eligible session list for platform account preferences.

Part of #277435.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: restore enterprise URL correction during setup

Validate configured instance URLs before starting authentication. Reuse enterprise input parsing across setup and onboarding, allow cloud and server URLs, and replace only the selected invalid entry while preserving current hosts. Cover cancellation, multiple corrections, keyboard focus, and changes made while the prompt is open.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: use the legacy enterprise setting in web builds

Default the enterprise enrollment setting to github-enterprise.uri when browser product metadata omits it. An empty key reads the whole configuration object and broke the legacy-only correction test in every browser CI job. Verified the failure before the fix and the affected suites in Chromium, WebKit and Electron afterward.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: preserve native enterprise session identities

Remove facade ID prefixes and session rewriting. Create account labels in the host engine, showing the instance only for multiple configured hosts and updating cached presentation without recreating engines or rewriting usernames in storage. Route native IDs using session provenance and cached ownership, preserve broker flows, and cover colliding account IDs through core RPC tests. Use async/await for configuration refresh error handling.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: keep Copilot enterprise enrollment on GHE.com

Restore GHE.com-only names and HTTPS URLs in Copilot setup and onboarding, including their examples and validation messages. Keep the generic enterprise authentication provider and configured-URI validation compatible with GHES, and preserve correction and cancellation behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: enroll a cloud instance when only GHES is configured

Require a GHE.com instance before proceeding with Copilot setup while leaving existing GHES authentication configuration intact. Cover both the quick-input and onboarding paths without choosing a default host.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: keep enterprise account labels stable

Always include the host in enterprise account labels under the fixed GitHub Enterprise provider label. Derive the label suffix once from the engine host and remove the suffix setter, cached relabeling and host-count flags. Preserve native IDs, stored usernames and public GitHub labels; verify menu labels across host additions and removals.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Fix HydraFusion in tabbed model picker to remove chevron and add link (#338913)

* Agent Host changes for lramos15/agents/fix-hydra-fusion-tabbed-picker

* Show HydraFusion's Learn more link in its picker description

Replace the HydraFusion flyout in the tabbed model picker with a description
under the entry, like the Auto tiers. Action list items gain a `detailLink`
that floats to the end of the last visible detail line, so a long (e.g.
translated) description is truncated instead of hiding the link. The link is
reached with Tab from the focused row and opens without selecting it.

* Keep HydraFusion's Learn more link at the line end in WebKit

WebKit lays out `-webkit-box` children as legacy flex items, so the floated
link became a full-width row there. Clamp a detail that has a link by height
instead, so the float works in every engine.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: carry the source turn's model configuration into side chats

The host-recorded fallback preserved the model id but not its config: the
first side-chat request read configuration from the session-level
`_runningModelConfigurations`, so the turn ran with global defaults instead
of the source turn's settings. Record the carried-over configuration per
chat (so it cannot affect the session's other chats), apply it to the side
chat's input model, and use it on the first committed request.

commit.message:
sessions: inherit the source chat's running model for side chats

`/btw` created and sent the side chat with no model when the Agents window
had not recorded one for the source chat (e.g. a resumed chat whose draft
has no model, where the picker is display-only). With signed-out BYOK
enabled, a request without a model is treated as requiring GitHub auth,
forcing the "Sign in to use GitHub Copilot" dialog.

Fall back to the model the host recorded the source chat running on (draft,
active turn, or last turn) when no selection is recorded.

Fixes #338867

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: harden late BYOK model registration

Review follow-ups to the fix for #337742:

- `syncByokModels` captures the session wrapper before resolving the
  current BYOK config and bails if a restart swapped it across the await,
  so a merge computed from the old wrapper's basis is never applied to a
  new one.
- Compare merged against registered config with `objects.equals` instead
  of `JSON.stringify`, removing a key-order dependency that would have
  silently produced a `provider.sync` per bridge event.
- Rename the free `resolveByokSessionConfig` to
  `synthesizeByokSessionConfig` so it no longer collides with the
  `ICopilotSessionLauncher` method of the same name, which had left the
  surrounding `{@link}` references pointing at themselves.
- Restore the loopback proxy URL in the `Wired N BYOK model(s)` log; it
  is what correlates a session with its proxy bind when reading logs.
- Cover the deliberate swallow in `setModel`, where a failed BYOK
  registration must not block the model change.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: register late BYOK models on live Copilot sessions

A chat restored during startup can resume its SDK session before the
renderer's first BYOK model snapshot reaches the agent host. The session
then launches with no BYOK providers, and every later switch to a BYOK
model fails with "Provider model '...' is not registered".

Track the BYOK providers and models each SDK session was launched with,
and register newly reported ones on live sessions through
session.rpc.provider.sync, both when the BYOK bridge changes and before
each model change. The sync only adds or updates entries: the runtime
deselects a model withdrawn from a live session, and the renderer can
transiently report an empty or partial set while a window reloads.

Fixes #337742

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
JSON - support ${workspaceFolder} in json.schemas fileMatch patterns (#326706)

* JSON - support ${workspaceFolder} in json.schemas fileMatch patterns

A fileMatch pattern has no way to target files in the workspace folder
root only: patterns are matched against the full document uri with an
implicit '**/' prefix, so `*.json` matches at every depth and a leading
`/` is redundant.

Expand a leading `${workspaceFolder}` (also after a `!` exclusion
prefix) to the workspace folder uri when collecting json.schemas
settings, in the two scopes with an unambiguous folder: workspace
folder settings in a multi-root workspace and workspace settings of a
single folder workspace. The expanded pattern is absolute, so the
implicit '**/' prefix no longer widens it and
`${workspaceFolder}/*.json` matches in the folder root only. The
server API stays unchanged.

Fixes #44135

* JSON - escape glob metacharacters when expanding ${workspaceFolder}

The service's glob has no escape syntax, so a folder name containing a
glob metacharacter altered the meaning of the expanded pattern: names
with brackets or braces made it match nothing and a '*' made it match
too much. Since the glob passes a backslash and alphanumerics through
to the resulting regular expression verbatim, encoding the folder
string's metacharacters as regex hex escapes makes them match
literally.

Also drop the query and fragment from the folder uri, mirroring what
the server does to document uris before matching.

* JSON - use startsWith to detect the ${workspaceFolder} prefix

* JSON - expand ${workspaceFolder} to the folder path

* JSON - move the glob escaping to a strings util

* JSON - percent-encode # and ? when expanding ${workspaceFolder}

commit.message:
github: harden request execution and add client attribution (#338831)

* github: bound request execution and add health telemetry

Add attributed admission limits, request deadlines, response bounds and shared cooldown handling to the existing GitHub engine. Preserve coalesced-read cancellation and mutation reconciliation, and record bounded privacy-safe health telemetry. Include architecture documentation and focused regression coverage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: honor retry hints during bootstrap and downloads

Preserve server-specified bootstrap cooldowns across identity attempts and enforce secondary limits and cooldown checks for authenticated downloads. Bound diagnostic body inspection without exposing private response contents, and cover cancellation and origin isolation with regression tests.

Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: identify requests with browser-safe metadata

Add trusted product and component attribution plus per-attempt retry markers. Restrict browser headers to the confirmed GitHub.com CORS allowlist and strip attribution from storage redirects without adding retry behavior. Keep the separately reviewed client inventory out of this change.

Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: fix request timeout safety and retained request state

Distinguish pre-dispatch timeouts from ambiguous writes, classify bounded HTTP error responses by status, and replace the backtracking GraphQL read classifier with a linear scan. Reclaim expired inactive-account quota state, detach cancelled shared readers, and avoid retaining one abort reaction per response chunk.

Address PR #338831 feedback and CodeQL with regression coverage. All 246 GitHub engine and binding tests pass; forced-GC probes confirm cancelled-reader and chunk-promise retention is removed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: preserve wake-ups across cooldown expiry

Use a consistent cooldown sample for dispatch selection and wake scheduling within each queue drain, so an expiry between the two scans cannot strand idle work until its deadline. Add a deterministic boundary regression and format the mutation timeout test flagged by CI hygiene.

Addresses the Opus review of PR #338831. All 247 affected engine/binding tests, client typecheck, PR-wide lint, and targeted hygiene pass.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: harden timer and admission bounds

Reuse bounded long-timeout scheduling for server cooldowns, reclaim expired active requests after wall-clock jumps without losing dispatch state, and admit unique reads before retaining coalescing entries or waiter timers.

Addresses three follow-up comments on PR #338831. Five regressions reproduced before the fixes; all 255 affected tests, client typecheck, targeted lint and hygiene pass.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: enforce deadlines at dispatch and result delivery

Recheck retained request deadlines before starting tasks, before every physical fetch attempt, and before successful settlement. Expired shared readers reject independently without cancelling live peers. Preserve prior dispatch state for mutation reconciliation and avoid counting blocked attempts in telemetry.

Addresses the two new deadline-boundary comments on PR #338831. Regression coverage includes delayed task start, payload serialization, retries, redirects and shared completion. All 149 targeted tests, client typecheck, lint, hygiene and real event-loop-stall probes pass.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: document runtime clients and migration boundaries

Add the runtime client inventory and link it from the engine README. Distinguish Agent Host consumers already using the engine from independent clients, and update the remaining-gap summary to reflect the implemented protections.

Part of PR #338831 and microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: bound credential waits and honor telemetry opt-out

Give each credential-resolution caller a five-minute budget without clearing shared server cooldowns or cancelling live peers. Recheck deadlines before settling failed queue work. Observe existing workbench and Agent Host telemetry configuration changes so opt-out immediately drops aggregates and invalidates completion handles, even during idle periods.

Addresses three additional comments on PR #338831. Six focused regressions reproduced before the fixes; all 276 engine/binding tests, client typecheck, targeted lint and hygiene pass.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: keep inactive cooldown cleanup after rejected reuse

A request rejected before admission must not cancel cleanup of an account that never became active again.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Preserve managed policy and Chat selection during refresh

Only affects configurations where `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` is effective and set to `true`. Addresses two related causes of Chat resetting from Agent to Ask:

1. **Background policy refresh:** After a successful fetch, keep the last accepted policy active while refreshing for the same account, authentication provider, and endpoint. In other words, don't temporarily drop the active policy while the refresh request is in flight. Failures and timeouts still fail closed until a retry succeeds.
2. **Startup and blocked/retry UI state:** Preserve the selected Chat mode while the freshness gate is pending or blocked, rather than persisting a temporary Ask/Edit fallback. Keep submission blocked, including after asynchronous saves and attachment preparation and before custom submit handlers. Revalidate when the gate resolves so an accepted policy that disables Agent still takes effect.

Startup and scope changes still require a successful fetch before AI use. Polling and cache expiry are unchanged. Unrelated model/custom-agent loading races are out of scope.

**Validation:** 187 targeted tests, client type check, and targeted ESLint pass. Covers initial fetch, forced/hourly background refresh, accepted Agent disablement, failure/retry, draft persistence, and submission races. Full-editor restart testing remains a manual follow-up.

Consolidates #338839. Includes the selection/submission guards adapted from #338826; no dependency on that PR merging.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

commit.message:
chat: offer Microsoft sign-in when an Entra account links to GitHub (#338823)

* chat: offer Microsoft sign-in when an Entra account links to GitHub

Sign-in surfaces can now offer "Continue with Microsoft" only to users who can
actually use it: those with a Microsoft work or school account that GitHub links
to a GitHub account (for example an Enterprise Managed User).

The workbench checks this silently in the background, through two session
options that only the workbench can set (extensions' getSession requests have
every `_workbench*` option stripped):
- microsoft-authentication returns silent tokens for the broker's work and
  school accounts, including ones not yet approved for VS Code, without
  approving, caching, persisting or announcing anything.
- github-authentication exchanges those tokens for a `read:user` token, reads
  the linked account, and revokes the token when the host and build allow it.

`chat.microsoftAuthentication.enabled` becomes `auto` / `always` / `never`,
defaulting to `never` and rolled out through experimentation (legacy `true` and
`false` keep their meaning). The chat setup dialog and the first-run onboarding
screen follow the result without ever waiting for it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: forget a found Microsoft link when accounts change

Adding or removing a Microsoft account now forgets a previously found link
and probes again, so signing out can no longer leave "Continue with
Microsoft" offered. A probe still running when the accounts change has its
answer discarded, since it answers for accounts that may be gone. Token
refreshes, which only report `changed`, are ignored so they do not mint
GitHub tokens.

Also stop promising unconditional revocation of the probe's GitHub token,
and describe the setting as covering sign-in surfaces, including the
welcome screen.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

particular the session-controls group kept its experimental styling after being
moved below the input. Gate those rules on the experimental class, and make the
disclosure chevron honor its [hidden] attribute (the base .monaco-text-button
display rule was overriding it, so the chevron showed when the feature was off).

Issue 2 - align the in-session chat input with the new composer: apply the
experimental-session-composer class to the in-session chat view when the setting
is enabled, activating the existing CSS that right-aligns the agent/model controls
and lifts the context-usage widget into the input's top-right corner. Also drive
the NewChatInSessionWidget (start-new-topic composer) off the same setting so its
controls match the new-session composer.

The collapse timer tracked focus with a boolean that desynced when focus moved
into a picker or a picker opened a dropdown overlay (whose in-row trigger stays
aria-expanded while the focused element is the overlay outside the row). The tray
could then collapse out from under the user mid-interaction.

Compute the interaction state live instead: stay open while the pointer is over
the row, the active element is within the row, or any picker opened from the row
is still expanded (excluding the disclosure toggle's own aria-expanded). Re-check
the same condition when the timer fires, so focus that lands in a picker after the
timer was scheduled still cancels the collapse.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Align the in-session chat input with the new-session composer

Add a renderSecondaryControlsInInput option to ChatInputPart (threaded through
ChatWidget view options) that lifts the secondary controls into the input to
match the Agents new-session composer: the mode/permissions pickers lead the
input toolbar row, and the context-usage widget becomes a direct child of the
input container so the existing experimental-session-composer CSS can position
it in the input's top-right corner. The sessions chat view enables it when the
experimental composer layout setting is on, and makes .chat-input-container the
positioning context for the usage widget.

Follow-up hardening for the in-session usage-widget placement. #337149 moved the
context-usage widget into the composer by reserving flow space, which expanded
the container past the editor cap and required the #337490 width fix. Avoid that
class of issue here:

- The widget is positioned absolutely, so it never reserves flow space or widens
  the input. The sessions chat also does not use the compact render style, so the
  toolbar width reservation that includes the usage widget never runs for it.
- Bind the absolute positioning to a .chat-secondary-controls-in-input marker
  class added by ChatInputPart at the moment it reparents the widget, instead of
  the reactive composer class. This makes the out-of-flow guarantee intrinsic to
  the reparent, so the widget can never briefly render in-flow and widen the input
  if the reactive class lags.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

  auto-collapse timer, restoring the toggle to a plain expand/collapse.

Reuse the context-usage placement mechanism from the earlier composer work
(microsoft/vscode#337149): placeContextUsageWidget() to reparent and
setInputEditorTrailingSpace() / inputEditorTrailingSpace to reserve room at the
editor's trailing edge, with a fixed CONTEXT_USAGE_WIDGET_TRAILING_SPACE (72)

editor width so the first line of text never slides under the widget.

microsoft/vscode#337490: the widget stays absolutely positioned and out of flow
(bound to the .chat-secondary-controls-in-input marker the reparent adds), so it

commit.message:
agentHost: Keep remote hosts alive while agents are running (#338392)

* agentHost: Keep remote hosts alive while agents are running

The --idle-timeout supervisor on remote agent hosts only counted connected clients, so it shut the agent host down 300s after the last client disconnected, even while a turn was still running. It now also counts the agent host server process as activity. The server already stays up while a turn is running and exits on its own once idle. Server exit is detected from the process itself rather than from its output pipes closing.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Avoid signaling a reused PID when killing the server

The task that owns the server process reaps it before the running-server state is cleared, so kill_running_server could run kill_tree on a PID the OS had already reassigned. Kill requests now go through that task, which either reaps a process that exited on its own or kills it before reaping.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Let run_server own the server process until it exits

start_server already spawns run_server and awaits only its readiness barrier, so run_server now waits for the process to exit or a kill request itself instead of handing the process to a second task. This leaves one owner for the process through startup, kill, and reap. The output reader stays a separate task because descendants can keep the pipes open after the server exits.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

agentHost: fix SSH and WSL relay reuse on reconnect

Keep protocol clients and their initialized transports together. Give each new protocol client a
fresh relay to prevent the "Method not found: initialize" error on repeated connections.

- Reuse connected SSH and WSL clients and join concurrent connection requests.
- Replace retained relays before a new protocol client starts its handshake.
- Keep the SSH session and selected endpoint when replacing its relay.
- Release old transport resources without closing the replacement connection.
- Add regression tests for repeated connects, retained relays, recovery, and resource cleanup.

commit.message:
[3/4] authentication: canonicalize enterprise credential storage (#338151)

* authentication: preserve enterprise credential namespaces

Use deterministic host and storage planning for the existing single enterprise URI. Retain original keychains and Microsoft account links across equivalent URI edits and restarts, reject storage collisions, and leave public GitHub usable when enterprise storage fails.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: derive enterprise storage keys instead of persisting them

Use a canonical URI-derived credential key and migrate the matching legacy tokens and Microsoft account links before starting the host engine. Keep legacy data until destination writes succeed, preserve canonical sign-out state, and retry incomplete migration without a registry or completion marker.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: preserve canonical logins during legacy migration

Read the canonical destination after inspecting legacy stores and recheck its token before copying. Cover concurrent canonical writes and assert exactly which credentials survive each failed migration write or cleanup.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: consolidate enterprise URI storage helpers

Rely on URI serialization for hostname casing, retain explicit scheme and trailing-slash normalization, and fold the single-host configuration helper into enterpriseStorage. Extend coverage for uppercase schemes, default ports, root paths, repeated slashes and escaped deployment paths.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: mark legacy storage migration for removal

Group temporary migration declarations and functions in a region scheduled for removal in 1.144, four releases after 1.140. Keep permanent URI and credential-key helpers outside the region.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: prefer canonical credentials over legacy aliases

Select legacy token and account-link sources only when their canonical component is absent. commit.message:
agentHost: settle in-flight turns when a remote connection is replaced (#338211)

* agentHost: settle in-flight turns when a remote connection is replaced

A remote Agent Host session could reopen showing a stale, in-progress conversation while the session list showed it idle (#336638). When a remote connection is replaced (host restart, or reconnect with a new clientId), the old AgentHostSessionHandler is disposed. A turn it was awaiting never settled, because its observer read the dead connection's state. The in-progress request kept the ChatModel alive, and loadRemoteSession reused that stale model instead of resolving the current state from the new connection.

- Track turns awaited by _invokeAgent/_handleTurn/_handleResumedTurn and settle them when the handler is disposed, without dispatching turnCancelled to the host.
- Complete an AgentHostChatSession's active turn when it is disposed, for restored and server-initiated streamed turns.
- Stop an invocation that is still preparing from creating a session, claiming an active client, or dispatching its turn on a handler that is being disposed.
- Keep treating a model's queue as server-managed after its session contribution is unregistered, so completing the stale turn does not send the host's queued messages from the client.

Fixes #336638

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: stop abandoned invocations at the remaining disposal windows

Address review feedback on #338211. An invocation on a handler disposed during these waits could still act on the replaced connection or hang:

- Check for abandonment after resolving trust folders, before a workspace-trust prompt.
- Check again after interactive authentication, before retrying createSession.
- Settle the wait for the new session's subscription to hydrate from the handler's lifetime. Disposing a subscription fires neither onDidChange nor onDidError, so the wait could hang and keep the stale model in progress.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
automations: fix timestamp placement in session history list (#338670)

automations: fix: prevent timestamp from being pushed to the end for failed items

The automation history list rendered failed items with the timestamp
pushed to the far right instead of appearing inline as
`<workspace> - Failed - <time ago>`.

`.session-description` shared a `flex: 1` rule with `.session-title`.
Whenever `getSessionStatusMessage()` returned a non-undefined message
(as it does for the Error/Failed status), the description element was
created and its `flex: 1` expanded to fill the remaining row space,
pushing `.session-time` to the end of the row. Completed items have no
description element (the function returns undefined), and
InProgress/NeedsInput items hide the whole details row, so Failed was
the only status exposing the bug.

Give `.session-description` its own rule without `flex: 1` so it sizes
to its content instead of expanding to push the timestamp away.

Fixes #337064

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
copilot: fix shell argument injection in generated commit messages (#337547)

* Fix shell argument injection in generated commit messages

The commit-message sanitizer escaped `"` before `\`, so the second replace
re-escaped the backslash the first one had just added and turned `"` into
`\\"`. Inside a double-quoted shell string that reads as an escaped backslash
followed by a closing quote, ending the `-m` argument early and leaving the
rest of the message to be parsed as separate shell tokens. Backticks were not
escaped at all, so a message containing `cmd` in backticks still triggered
command substitution.

Quote the message with single quotes instead, which suppress expansion and
substitution outright rather than depending on every metacharacter being
escaped individually. Quoting is shell-aware because `'` is not a quote
character in cmd.exe and PowerShell escapes an embedded `'` by doubling it
rather than with the POSIX `'\''` idiom. This also fixes the previous `\`
doubling silently corrupting backslashes under PowerShell.

The helper lives in its own module so it is covered by the fast unit suite
and can be reused by the other terminal sendText call sites.

Fixes #316995
Fixes #316996

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Harden commit-message quoting per shell, else use the commit box

The first fix still let a generated message break out of its quoted
argument in several shells. Because sendText turns every line break into an
Enter key press, a breakout in a multi-line message ran without the user
pressing Enter.

- PowerShell also ends a single-quoted string at the typographic single
  quotes U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B, which are common in generated
  text.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not escape an embedded double quote when it
  builds git's command line, so the quote split the argument. PowerShell 5.1
  and 7 both report the shell as pwsh, so a double quote is refused.
- fish treats \' and \\ as escapes inside single quotes, so a backslash
  defeated the POSIX '\'' idiom.
- nu has no escape for a single quote. cmd.exe expands %VAR% inside double
  quotes and runs each line as soon as it is entered. csh expands ! inside
  single quotes and cannot continue them onto a new line.

Typed control characters are also commands to the shell's line editor; for
example, a Backspace can erase the opening quote. A message containing one
is refused for every shell.

quoteShellArgument now uses an allowlist of shells whose quoting rules are
known, and returns undefined when a value cannot be quoted safely. The
command then puts the message in the Source Control commit box instead of
typing it into the terminal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Shorten comments in commit-message shell quoting

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Strip or replace unsafe characters instead of refusing them

Refusing a message sent it to the Source Control commit box. The Agents
window has no Source Control view, though, and Agent Host terminals never
report a shell type, so there every message was refused and then lost.

buildGitCommitCommand now always builds a command, except for agent CLIs:

- Control characters are stripped for every shell.
- PowerShell gets ' in place of ", and a space after a trailing \. Git's
  message cleanup removes that space again.
- cmd.exe and other or undetected shells get one -m per paragraph, reduced
  to characters that every shell treats literally inside double quotes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Show a fallback message when the web workbench fails to start (#338474)

* Show a fallback message when the web workbench fails to start

When the bootstrap scripts never run - for example because a reverse
proxy, browser extension or content filter blocks or rewrites them -
the web workbench renders nothing and the user is left with a blank
white page. The only hint is a `Cannot determine URI for module id!`
error in the console, which does not point at the actual cause.

Add static fallback content to the workbench templates that is
revealed by a delayed CSS animation and removed as soon as our own
script runs. Because it relies on neither script execution nor an
additional request, it also survives the case where every script on
the page is blocked, which is exactly when the blank page appears.

The styles are inlined and hardcoded rather than using theme tokens
since no theme or workbench CSS has loaded at that point, and the
message cannot be localized because NLS is not available either.

commit.message:
Engineering - decompose macOS build stage (#338655)

* Engineering - decompose macOS stage

Split the macOS product build into Compile, Test and Sign jobs so failed jobs can be retried without repeating successful work. Compile publishes the unpacked builds, Test applies the local entitlement signature and runs the tests with retry checkpoints, and Sign mixes in the CLI, packages, signs, notarizes and publishes the final artifacts. The arm64 test job gates publishing of the arm64 and universal artifacts.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - split macOS stage per architecture

Move the macOS x64, arm64 and universal product builds into dedicated macOSX64, macOSARM64 and macOSUniversal stages, following the Windows and Linux layout. The existing macOS stage continues to hold the CI test jobs. Rename the CLI job to macOS_<arch>_CLI / "macOS (ARCH) - CLI" to match the other platforms, and update publish.ts and the artifact sanity tests to the new stage names.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - publish unsigned macOS client from the Compile job

The macOS (UNIVERSAL) job only waits 60 minutes for the unsigned x64 and arm64 clients. Publishing them from the Sign job delayed them until the Compile and CLI jobs had completed and a new agent had set up and extracted the compilation artifact, so the universal job timed out. Mix in the CLI and publish the unsigned client from the Compile job again, at the same point as before the job split. The compilation artifact now contains the CLI, so the Test and Sign jobs only depend on the Compile job.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - fix Linux CLI producer name in package steps

The Linux CLI job was renamed to "Linux (ARCH) - CLI", so the CLI artifact wait no longer recognized its producer and could not short circuit when the CLI job failed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - align macOS UNIVERSAL stage display name

Use upper case for the architecture, matching the other product build stages.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - download remote Node.js in macOS test job

The remote integration tests run 'gulp node', which downloads the Node.js runtime from Azure Artifacts unless it is already cached. The macOS test job no longer builds the server, so the runtime is not cached and the download fails without authentication. Download it with Azure Artifacts authentication before running the tests, as the Linux test job does.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: stop injecting the artifact tools reminder (#338593)

ArtifactToolsContribution appended ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION to the first
user message of every chat whenever artifact tools were enabled, which is the
default outside Stable. Because it lives in the conversation, it was re-sent
with every model request for the rest of the session, and it prompted
add_artifact_or_reference calls even in headless sessions where nothing
surfaces artifacts.

The add_artifact_or_reference tool description already carries the same
guidance (optional registration, artifact vs. reference classification, what
not to record, batching), so remove the contribution and the instruction.
The skill's worked contribution example now uses
MarkdownPlanRichLinksContribution.

commit.message:
Retain full Codex shell output across chat reloads (#337390)

* Retain full Codex command output with its chat session

Store command output longer than 20,000 characters in the owning chat's
session database and publish a 2,000-character preview with a non-PTY
terminal resource, so "Open Full Output" works for Codex the same way it
does for Copilot. Restored chats get the same resource back when the
database has the output; other output keeps its restored text.

Use the Codex item id as the command's tool call id, live and on replay,
so the resource survives reloads. A sandbox pre-flight coalesced with its
re-run keeps the pre-flight's id on replay too, matching live.

The completion is still published synchronously and no terminal is kept
alive: subscribers get exited terminal state rebuilt from the database,
whose queued write is ordered ahead of later reads. Reverting or rolling
back turns removes the output retained for their commands.

* Keep Codex command output inline up to the shell output limit

Codex reports a command's complete output, so only retain output that is
longer than the SHELL_COMMAND_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES characters the agent host
already surfaces for shell output, instead of the workbench's model-facing
20,000-character limit. Output at or below that size renders exactly as it
did before.

When output is retained, keep its end inline as the preview rather than its
first 2,000 characters. The terminal card shows the end of the output, so the
card keeps showing what it showed before, and Open Full Output serves the rest.

* Unwrap PowerShell command executions in Codex chat

Treat PowerShell and pwsh -Command wrappers like the existing Bash and zsh
-c wrappers when rendering Codex command executions. Retained output remains
shell-neutral; this keeps Windows command rows and restored transcripts on the
same display path as POSIX shells.

* Show the beginning of retained Codex command output

Keep the first 80,000 characters as the inline preview when Codex output is
retained, matching Claude's first-chunk presentation. Below-limit output and
the complete stored terminal resource remain unchanged.

* Keep the beginning visible in retained Codex previews

Build a compact preview from the first three logical output lines and shorten
very long lines. This keeps the beginning visible in the terminal card's fixed
viewport while the complete output remains available through Open Full Output.

* Keep retained Codex previews as a raw prefix

Use the first 400 output characters exactly as emitted, without synthesizing
ellipsis markers or rewriting lines. The bounded prefix remains visible in the
terminal card while Open Full Output serves the complete stored result.

* Retain Codex output recovered at turn completion

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337390#discussion_r4092208196.
Queue retained-output storage before recovered command completions are mapped
from turn/completed, preserving the normal item/completed ordering.

* Restore retained Codex output during history refresh

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337390#discussion_r4092208234.
Enrich changed replayed turns from the session database before publishing
incremental history replacements, with a staleness guard after the async read.

* Keep recovered Codex subagent output inline

Preserve the PR's existing subagent exclusion while retaining parent command
output recovered from turn/completed. Share the recovery predicate with the
storage path and cover both parent and subagent outcomes.

* Fix Codex retained-output regression test types

Use the current generated protocol item shapes and narrow retained terminal
content before reading its resource. This keeps the Copilot review regressions
type-safe without changing production behavior.

* Codex: preserve full output when retention fails

Addresses review comment 4098872570. Wait for output storage before publishing completion, retain inline output on failure, and preserve per-chat progress order.

* Codex: skip encoding output above the retention limit

Addresses review comment 4098872582. Reject oversized strings before allocating a UTF-8 copy, and retain the exact byte check for multibyte output.

commit.message:
Suggest agent session storage cleanup when worktrees accumulate (#338502)

* Saving uncommitted changes before archiving session

* sessions: add agent session storage management

Detect accumulated session worktrees, surface cleanup guidance, and provide a storage manager with safe manual and automatic lifecycle cleanup.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add agent session storage cleanup suggestion and manager

Users who never enabled auto-archive accumulate session worktrees that
consume significant disk space. Surface a suggestion notice below the
Sessions list when cleanup is worthwhile, and add a Manage Agent Session
Storage editor to review and clean up eligible sessions.

- Show the notice when 20+ eligible worktrees exist or eligible inactive
  worktrees can reclaim 5 GiB or more. Only eligible candidates count
  toward the worktree threshold.
- Add the Manage Agent Session Storage editor with an inactivity-days
  filter, a worktree-only filter, and a suggestion toggle.
- Gate the notice behind chat.agentSessions.sessionStorageCleanupSuggestion.enabled
  and support per-window suppression.
- Add a Disable Session Storage Cleanup Suggestions command so screen
  reader users have a non-visual equivalent of Don't Show Again.
- Announce the notice to screen readers and document the flow in the
  Sessions accessibility help dialog.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Only show sessions with measurable worktrees in storage manager

Marking a session that has no worktree as done reclaims no disk space, so
it does not belong in a storage manager. Report only sessions with a
measured worktree and remove the "Sessions with worktrees only" filter,
the hasWorktree field, and the "No worktree" storage cell. The Sessions
list already owns decluttering sessions that hold no storage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Match storage cleanup notice dismiss button to standard close style

The dismiss (x) button used a monaco Button whose background and border
come from inline styles, so the intended borderless look could not be
applied from CSS and it rendered as a bordered box. Render it as a plain
borderless icon button matching the session input banner's close button,
with a hover background and focus-visible outline, and use IHoverService
for its tooltip.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address PR review feedback for session storage cleanup

- Identify the active session by sessionId instead of reference equality,
  since the active session is a VisibleSession wrapper while getSessions
  returns provider facades.
- Aggregate disk usage across every worktree an Agent Host session owns
  instead of only the first, and carry the worktree count through the
  cleanup model so the worktree threshold counts worktrees, not sessions.
- Only suppress the protocol NotFound error when measuring worktree disk
  usage; auth, permission, and transport failures now surface.
- Collapse the storage editor table to a stacked layout in narrow windows
  so Storage and Open Session are not clipped.
- Add an editor-scoped accessibility help provider, focus context key, and
  verbosity setting, and exclude the storage editor from the window-wide
  chat help.
- Report archiving rejections through the notification service instead of
  leaving an unhandled rejection.
- Remove a duplicate side-effect import of agentSessionsConfiguration.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Let ExP control the session storage cleanup suggestion default

The setting was tagged experimental but lacked the experiment metadata, so
ExP could not set its default through the config.<setting id> treatment.
Add experiment: { mode: 'auto' } to match the other experimental Agents
window settings.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Refine worktree cleanup UX from team feedback

- Focus the primary actions on the cleanup outcome: "Clean Up Agent
  Worktrees" for the command, editor, and Sessions-list notice, and
  "Clean Up {N} Worktrees" for the modal's primary button and confirmation.
- Open a session from its title link in the table and drop the separate
  Actions/Open Session column.
- Make the in-modal settings read clearly as settings: a "Cleanup Settings"
  heading with a gear icon and a note that the options change your settings.
- Update the accessibility help and tests to match the new terminology and
  the title-link interaction.

Keeps the settings inline in the modal and the entry point below the
Sessions list per the Agents window discussion.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Tighten worktree cleanup layout from UX feedback

- Drop the redundant "return here any time" paragraph from the editor.
- Move the primary cleanup button up beside the summary line, right
  aligned, instead of a full-width row below it.
- Remove the database icon from the Sessions-list notice to reclaim
  horizontal space and align the text and actions to the edge.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add per-setting "Configure in Settings" gear to cleanup editor

Each row in the Cleanup Settings section now has a gear button that opens
the Settings editor filtered to that setting, for users who prefer to
configure it there directly. The button names the setting for its hover
tooltip and its screen reader label.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
github-auth: Allow Entra exchange without a client secret (#338555)

* github-auth: allow Entra token exchange without a client secret

Some VS Code builds (e.g. OSS/dev builds) don't have a distro-configured
client secret for the Entra-to-GitHub token exchange. Previously this
threw and blocked sign-in entirely. Simplify resolveEndpoint() to return
a plain URL and stop requiring/sending client_secret in the exchange
request, so the exchange can proceed without one.

chat: make Draw use folded ribbon motion

Replace the legacy clip-path Draw variants with the approved parabolic folded-ribbon animation while keeping the existing colored, monochrome, and no-icon setting values. Remove the separate Ribbon option and make component fixtures drive and validate RAF motion through the shared animation control.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

chat: tune ribbon progress motion

Use mirrored cubic position curves for a stronger parabolic velocity profile while preserving zero-velocity rest points. Keep loops separate with a short clean pause and update coverage and user-facing descriptions to match.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

chat: add ribbon persistent progress animation

Add an experimental Ribbon progress style that animates the existing VS Code mark along arc-length geometry while preserving Draw's color and footprint. Honor reduced motion and live setting changes, and cover lifecycle, timing, geometry, and rendering behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

[2/4] authentication: separate enterprise provider lifecycles (#338150)

* authentication: separate enterprise provider and engine lifecycles

Keep the single configured enterprise instance and native account identities, while owning engine replacement, registration-safe session events and cleanup separately. Isolate OAuth callbacks by host and preserve the current Microsoft-brokered flows.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: discard superseded enterprise startup failures

Version enterprise configuration updates so a failed initial update cannot enqueue an error state after a newer configuration succeeds. Cover both A-to-B and A-to-B-to-A races through extension activation while preserving current-error fallback and later recovery.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: serialize enterprise failures and session publication

Remove activation generation bookkeeping by handling failure state inside each queued update. Reconcile preparation-time session removals, additions and changes before publishing a replacement, with regression coverage for consecutive initialization failures and pending-host events.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: own event buffering at the registration boundary

Buffer initial provider events in the extension host until its registration RPC completes. Remove the extension-side wrapper, microtask readiness inference and construction factory; directly construct a host-bound session engine with a side-effect-free cached session inventory. Preserve broker flows and exercise registration ordering through core RPC tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* authentication: clarify disposal and registration ownership

Keep the bundled README focused on user setup. Name disposal cancellation explicitly, verify cleanup while an engine is still being prepared, and clarify why core captures session events before awaiting registration.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:

fix(copilot): let extension host tests run on previous-minor insiders

The version bump on main raises engines.vscode before any Insiders build
of the new version exists, so the downloaded insiders-unreleased build is
rejected as incompatible and the suite runs without the extension loaded.

Relax the engine requirement by one minor for the test run when not
testing a local build (VSCODE_UNDER_TEST).
