commit.message:
chat: check nested subagent calls against the caller's allowlist (#337611)

* chat: check nested subagent calls against the caller's allowlist

RunSubagentTool resolved the current agent from the session's last
request, which is always the top-level agent because subagent requests
are not added to the chat model. A subagent's calls were therefore
checked against the top-level agent's `agents:` allowlist, so calls
two or more levels deep were rejected (regressed by #331442).

Tool invocation tokens now carry the id of the request they were issued
for. RunSubagentTool tracks running subagents by request id, and uses
the calling subagent's instructions and allowlist for nested calls. A
subagent that runs the tool without agentName now gets a copy of
itself, with its model, tools and hooks, instead of a copy of the
top-level agent.

Fixes #335257

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: model real tool enablement in the nested subagent copy test

The fake tools service only returned the tools an agent lists, while the
real service also returns every other known tool as disabled. Because
RunSubagentTool keeps an explicit `runSubagent: false`, the copy test
exercised a subagent calling runSubagent without having the tool, which
production does not allow. Mirror the real enablement map and list
runSubagent in the calling subagent's tools.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

checked against the top-level agent's `agents:` allowlist, so calls
two or more levels deep were rejected (regressed by #331442).

Tool invocation tokens now carry the id of the request they were issued
for. RunSubagentTool tracks running subagents by request id, and uses
the calling subagent's instructions and allowlist for nested calls. A
subagent that runs the tool without agentName now gets a copy of
itself, with its model, tools and hooks, instead of a copy of the
top-level agent.

Fixes #335257

The fake tools service only returned the tools an agent lists, while the
real service also returns every other known tool as disabled. Because
RunSubagentTool keeps an explicit `runSubagent: false`, the copy test
exercised a subagent calling runSubagent without having the tool, which
production does not allow. Mirror the real enablement map and list
runSubagent in the calling subagent's tools.

commit.message:
agentHost: surface staged Fusion client tools and give HydraFusion phases their own chats (#337621)

* agentHost: surface staged Fusion client tools and give HydraFusion phases their own chats

Client tools invoked during a provisional HydraFusion phase never ran: the SDK
handler waited on the client, the client waited for a tool start the runtime
was holding back until commit. Surface the start (or a synthesized one) when
the handler is invoked so skip-permission / auto-approved client tools and
tool search complete instead of hanging the response.

Also nest each phase's committed conversation (intermediate text, tool calls)
and review critiques under the phase tile as a child chat, both live and on
restore, and make the phase pill open that chat when one exists.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Guard Fusion phase chat closes against reopen during drain

A close that waits on file-edit completions cleared the open set immediately,
so a phase reopened on the error/resume path was closed by the stale callback.
Track the latest pending close per phase and only fire that one.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
managed settings: keep policy through transient refresh failures (#337583)

Copilot's OTel reload notification (reworked in #336701) exposed a managed-settings refresh regression from #330896. Enterprise users see "Copilot OTel endpoint will change to http://localhost:4318 after reload." every few hours, especially after idle, and reloading clears chat.

## Cause

Since #330896, a cached server-managed-settings response expires one hour after the last successful fetch. If a refresh fails after that (no response, 401/403, 429, 5xx, malformed), the policy is dropped rather than kept. A policy-backed OTel endpoint then reverts to its default and the notification appears. The next successful fetch restores the policy, so it keeps switching back and forth. Every other server-managed control switches back and forth in the same way, so for the length of the gap their restrictions are silently lifted.

## Change

Keep the policy unless the service answers affirmatively that it should change. A failed refresh without `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` now keeps the last successful response, however old, with its original timestamp. The failure therefore doesn't count as a refresh, and the next poll or focus retries. A 401/403 is treated as a failure because it can be temporary, for example while a token refreshes.

This keeps #330896's fix that a failure never renews the cache timestamp, and reverts only its dropping of stale policy. Before #330896, failures also kept the previous policy, but they renewed the timestamp.

These still behave as before:
- A 200 replaces the policy; a 404 or 466 clears it.
- Sign-out, or an account or scope change, clears or stops reusing the policy.
- `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` still fails closed.

## Follow-up

- A thrown session lookup error still makes `getDefaultAccountForAuthenticationProvider` return `null`, so `setDefaultAccount(null)` clears the policy without applying this retention. This path predates #330896 and changes account availability, so it needs a separate PR.
- `managedSettingsActive` (set when the server returns settings that no VS Code policy uses) is never cleared once set. This bug existed before this PR and will be fixed separately.

## Validation

- `defaultAccount.test.ts`: 49 passing. The updated test fails without this change.
- Account and policy suites: 250 passing.

commit.message:
sessions: run Agent Merge per chat folder and present multi-folder sessions (#337594)

* agentHost: run Agent Merge per folder

Each folder a chat works in can run its own Agent Merge. State moves to
per-folder session config (`agentMerge.folders`, host-owned
`agentMerge.controller.folders`), with the earlier session-level entries
read as the session folder's state and cleared on its first write. The
session-wide elevated configuration lives in
`agentMerge.injectedConfiguration`: applied while any folder runs and
restored when the last one stops.

The controller keeps one runtime per folder, bound to that folder's pull
request and checkout. Repair turns and notices go to the folder's owning
chat (the chat that turned Agent Merge on, else the first chat working in
that folder) and wait only for that chat to be idle; a turn ending in an
error also completes the repair. Tools, Create PR with Agent Merge, and
Mark Ready with Agent Merge resolve the invoking chat's or changeset's
folder.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: follow the active chat's folder for Agent Merge

Agent Merge actions, context keys and the chat input's pull request pill now read and write the Agent Merge settings of the folder the active chat works in. The provider writes a peer chat's folder into agentMerge.folders, recording the chat that turned it on, and keeps the legacy agentMerge key for the session folder until the host migrates it. Session-wide surfaces keep using the session folder.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: harden per-folder Agent Merge

Addresses review findings on the per-folder Agent Merge implementation:

- Lifecycle updates re-read the folder and write only host-owned state, so an
  evaluation never reverts settings the user changed meanwhile.
- Clients write only the folder they change, by working directory; the host
  merges it into the other folders and derives the key, so stale client maps
  cannot undo host changes and keys match across platforms.
- The owning chat must be a chat of the session; notices use it; a folder no
  chat works in waits instead of repairing from the session folder's checkout.
- Repair turns are tracked per chat: only that chat may use the repair's tool
  authorization, and removing it ends the turn.
- Turning a folder off clears its lifecycle state, and Create PR with Agent
  Merge binds afresh, so a new pull request is not judged by an old target.
- The elevated configuration of earlier versions carries over when migrating.
- Unrelated config changes no longer re-sync monitoring.
- A peer chat whose folders are still loading cannot change the session folder.
- Observable ref-counting and caches are per session.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: run Agent Merge tools for the invoking chat

Agent Merge tools passed the session URI, so a peer chat's repair turn could
not use its tools, a turn in another chat could use the default chat's repair
authorization, and the enable tool always changed the session folder. They now
pass the invoking chat.

A folder that no chat of the session works in any more now turns Agent Merge
off with a reason, instead of waiting and keeping the session resident, and the
host drops client entries for folders that are not the session's.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: keep other folders' Agent Merge settings during client writes

A client write of one folder is applied locally before the host merges it,
so until then the local config held only that folder: other folders looked
off, and a toggle there could turn them off. The provider now reads every
folder it has seen, as the host never removes a folder's settings.

Config replacement no longer sends the client's copy of the Agent Merge
settings, which could undo a host self-disable or a demoted merge choice; the
host carries them over when a replacement omits them. Notices waiting for a
chat that is removed are posted to the default chat.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: restore per-folder Git state and present multi-folder sessions

- The host persists the latest Git state of each chat's working-directory
  scope, so chats in other folders show their branch state right after a
  restore instead of the session folder's.
- Multi-folder sessions: the session hover summarizes every workspace, its
  changes and pull requests, and a chat's hover shows its own folder, branch
  changes and pull requests. The sessions list shows chat rows accordingly.
- The Changes view hides Session Changes in multi-folder sessions, and the
  input banners follow the active chat's folder and its Agent Merge settings.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: Keep search intent parameters literal in markdown table (#337561)

* chat: Keep search intent parameters literal in markdown table

The /search intent renders search parameters parsed from the model's own
response into a markdown table. Values were wrapped in single backticks with
only `|` escaped, so a backtick closed the code span early and the rest of
the value rendered as markdown (for example a live link), and a line break
ended the row and let the model inject table rows. Keys were not escaped.

Values now use a backtick fence longer than any run in the value, collapse
line breaks (including U+2028/U+2029), and pad only where CommonMark would
strip spaces. Pipes that follow an odd run of backslashes cannot be kept
inside a code span in marked, so the value is split around them and they are
emitted as `|`. Only the six known parameters, which the search
follow-up uses, are shown, so keys need no escaping.

Fixes #316997

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Handle backslash runs before pipes in search intent table

CodeQL flagged the `\|` replacement for escaping pipes without escaping
backslashes. Backslashes are literal inside a code span and must not be
escaped, so handle each backslash run together with the pipe after it in one
pass instead: an even run gets one extra backslash, and an odd run closes the
code span before the pipe, which is emitted as `|`.

Also reuse `appendEscapedMarkdownInlineCode` instead of a duplicate helper.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: harden SSH host key verification (#337516)

* Reject SSH host key algorithm downgrades

Treat a host known under another key algorithm as a mismatch when strict host key checking uses accept-new, and require an explicit prompt when certificate-authority entries cannot be validated. Add coverage across known_hosts matching, policy, shared-process evidence, and renderer handling. (Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Harden SSH host key identity resolution

Use HostKeyAlias consistently for verification, trust storage, and key rotation; migrate legacy resolved-host trust only after an exact match; reject unsupported dynamic trust and revocation sources; and hard-fail algorithm changes under every strict mode. (Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Preserve stored SSH host key authority

Only treat a different known_hosts algorithm as a mismatch when no exact key is already saved in the VS Code trust store. Add regression coverage for the precedence rule. (Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: tolerate delayed Windows process cleanup

Retry the post-taskkill identity check briefly so a stale Windows process-tree snapshot does not fail Agent Host E2E teardown after taskkill reports that the process is already gone. Preserve failure when the same process remains alive. (Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Preserve SSH key type compatibility

Prompt for hosts known only under another algorithm with the default policy, honor explicit host-checking opt-outs, and retain the hard failure for accept-new where silent persistence would bypass host identity verification. (Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Agents - Adopt ChangesetState.Recomputing in Agent Host (#337545)

* agentHost: adopt recomputing changeset status

Return cached file lists with Recomputing while refreshing and keep uncached changesets in Computing. Preserve successful empty results, refresh turn subscriptions without awaiting diffs, and align handshake snapshots with subscriber registration.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: adapt recomputing changesets to chat scopes

Preserve folder-owned Branch Changes and chat-owned Turn and Uncommitted Changes across cold subscription restore. Refresh cached states under their new owners, reattach file monitoring, and keep skipped uncommitted refreshes from leaving a transient status behind.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host changes for lszomoru/agents/adopting-changesetstate-recomputing

* agentHost: preserve pending-worktree changeset diffs

Keep the source-folder uncommitted diff available while a worktree is pending, and wait for asynchronous changeset initialization before asserting protocol action delivery and replay in tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: await recomputing changesets in conformance

A cached turn can return a Recomputing subscription snapshot while its new diff is still running. Wait for a completion action newer than that snapshot before asserting Ready, including when the cached result is empty.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: wait for the final changeset snapshot in conformance

A Git-state refresh can restart a cached turn recomputation after its first Ready action. Keep subscribing until the returned snapshot is terminal so the no-op turn assertion observes the final result.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: let chats work in their own folder, and show it (#337544)

* agentHost: let create_session start a chat in its own folder

`create_session` with the current-session relationship can now take a
`workspace` (and optional `worktree`): the host adds that folder to the
session, preparing a worktree when requested or inherited, and assigns
the resulting checkout only to the new chat. Without `workspace` the
chat keeps sharing the session workspace. `relationship` is optional and
defaults to a chat in the current session; agents set `independent` only
when the user asks for a separate session.

On the client, a folder that is a VS Code-created worktree reports its
repository as the folder's project, and the Changes view computes its
tree root and relative paths from the active chat's workspace.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: keep "new session" requests in the current session

Agents read "create it in a new session" as a request for an independent
session. Set `independent` only when the user explicitly asks for a
sibling or top-level session; requests for a "new session" or "new chat"
create a chat in the current session.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: choose the create_session relationship by relatedness

Let the agent decide the relationship from whether the work is related
to the current session, instead of listing user phrases. The argument
stays optional and defaults to a chat in the current session.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: reserve independent sessions for unrelated work

Describe `independent` as the exception, for work unrelated to the
current session's plan or deliverable, so a session without a plan yet
still defaults to a chat in the current session.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: note that current-session work can use another workspace

A different workspace alone is not a reason for an independent session:
a chat in the current session can work in its own folder.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: address review feedback on chats in their own folder

- Release a folder prepared for a chat that could not be created: remove
  the folder the preparation added, and delete a worktree it created,
  unless a chat uses it by then.
- Track the active chat and its folder in the Changes view's tree update,
  so switching between chats re-roots the tree and its relative paths.
- Document `worktree: false` and the defaults when it is omitted.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: keep chat folders when restoring a session

Providers only persist the folders a session started with, so a folder
added later for a peer chat was dropped from the restored session while
the chat kept it. Clients then built no workspace for that chat. Restore
now adds every chat's persisted folders to the session's working
directories.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: show a chat's folder in the list and command center

In the compact sessions list, a chat row shows the folder its chat works
in, on hover or focus, when the session spans more than one project and
the chat works in exactly one folder; screen readers hear it too. The
command center's project, icon, path, and branch now follow the active
chat's workspace instead of the session's.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: track and act on every folder's pull request

The pull request status service now watches the pull request of each
folder a chat works in, not only the session folder's, while a client
has the session open. Mark Ready, Merge, and auto-merge are offered on
every folder's Branch changes and act on that folder's pull request.
Agent Merge still follows the session folder's pull request.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: send chat turns from their own folder

Resolve the working directory from the addressed chat so peer chats do not fall back to the owning session's primary folder.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: Reject client dispatch of server-only actions (#337515)

* agentHost: Reject client dispatch of server-only actions

Validate incoming actions against the generated client-dispatchable allowlist and reject forged server-only actions before they reach synchronized state. Add coverage for a forged client tool request.\n\n(Written by Copilot)\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Cover server-only action rejection end to end

Exercise the full AHP server with distinct victim and attacker clients and verify that a forged server-only session action is rejected without mutating synchronized state. Refresh the checked-in E2E coverage reports.\n\n(Written by Copilot)\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Isolate rejected actions from host listeners

Return rejection envelopes to the protocol server for client reconciliation without publishing untrusted payloads through the state manager action event.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Broadcast service-level action rejections

Route all client rejection envelopes through a dedicated state manager event so the protocol server can reconcile clients without exposing rejected payloads to host action listeners.\n\n(Written by Copilot)\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Preserve service rejection notifications

Forward dedicated rejection envelopes through AgentService.onDidAction for client-facing reconciliation while keeping them isolated from internal state-manager action listeners.\n\n(Written by Copilot)\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: preserve sessions across window moves (#337232)

* chat: preserve sessions across window moves

Keep the chat model alive until its destination acquires ownership, preventing deletion of an autosaved empty session's initial log entry. Distinguish model disposal from history deletion so closed sessions remain discoverable and reopenable.

Fixes #336748

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: serialize local session refreshes

Adapt the refresh serialization and race coverage from #325536. Preserve immediate deletion by invalidating old snapshots and scoping delayed model updates to disposable listener lifetimes.

Refs #336748. Adapted from Lucas Taylor's work in #325536.

Co-authored-by: Lucas Taylor <lucastaylor000@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: honor move close results and session metadata updates

Publish metadata-only local session deltas. Scope close-confirmation suppression to the retained-model move and stop if closing the source editor fails or is vetoed. Add regression coverage for cancellation, errors, confirmation restoration, and working-directory changes.

Refs #336748. Addresses review feedback on #337232.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: preserve shared refresh requests and survey budgets

Keep coalesced session refreshes alive while any caller still needs them. Preserve per-session survey prompt limits on model unload while releasing response state that could block other chats.

Add cancellation and unload regression coverage for #336748.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: simplify local session refresh lifecycle

Make local session-list refreshes controller-owned so callers can stop waiting without cancelling shared work. Replace token pooling and version tracking with scoped cancellation for unload, deletion, and shutdown.

Update cancellation and lifecycle regression coverage for #336748.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* async: propagate queued Throttler rejections

Ensure all coalesced callers settle when queued work rejects, and verify that subsequent work still runs after successful or failed active work.

Refs #336748.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Lucas Taylor <lucastaylor000@gmail.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: scope pull requests to chat repositories (#337499)

* agentHost: scope pull requests to chat repositories

Each chat folder scope other than the main chat's keeps its own GitHub and pull request state. Chats in other folders can create pull requests against their own repository without affecting the session's pull request or Agent Merge, and a chat's pull request pill shows only pull requests from its repository.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: send chat-based Create PR to the active chat

The Create PR form's send-to-chat option always targeted the session's main chat, so a pull request for a chat working in another folder was requested from the chat in the main folder. Send it to the chat whose changes are shown instead.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: store pull requests per folder instead of per folder scope

A pull request belongs to a checkout and its branch, not to the combination of folders a chat has open. Key GitHub and pull request state by folder: the session's first folder keeps the session-level state and every other folder has its own. A chat's workspace reports each folder's state, so chats sharing a folder share its pull requests and a chat with several folders shows pull requests for all of them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: store every folder's pull requests in the folder map

Record the session folder's GitHub and pull request state in the same per-folder map as every other folder instead of special-casing it. The original single-folder entry is read as the session folder's state until the folder's own entry is written, and it keeps a copy of that state for readers of the original format and older clients.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: address review findings for per-folder pull requests

Consider every folder's pull requests when listing auto-archive candidates, and keep chat-based Create PR from another folder from changing the session's Agent Merge. migrated to the session folder on list, restore and reprojection.

commit.message:
Editor: Refine connected tabs UI (#337126)

* Editor: stabilize connected tabs across zoom levels

Let bottom-row connected tabs own the strip geometry directly instead of cancelling inherited pill gutters with negative offsets. This keeps their cap and document boundary aligned when Chromium rounds fractional zoom values while preserving upper-row pill spacing.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: update connected tab strip geometry

Update the editor-tab layout expectations for direct bottom-row geometry and the intentional one-stroke overlap with the document surface.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: align connected tab actions to the top edge

Top-align the non-wrapping connected strip and give editor actions the same full row height so their controls remain vertically centered with tab labels.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: update component screenshot baseline

Accept the Ubuntu CI hash for the dark responsive model resize fixture after verifying the delta is limited to corner antialiasing.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: share modern tab row geometry

Own the non-wrapping row-height formula in the shared Modern UI tab layout so connected editor actions cannot drift from tab density changes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: restore stable component screenshot baseline

Restore the original dark responsive model resize hash after CI oscillated back, confirming the alternate corner-antialias hash was nondeterministic.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: isolate connected tab colors and borders

Give connected document tabs their own strip color, restore shared 2026 tab colors for Classic and Agents surfaces, and use the existing strip separator color for connected cap and shoulder outlines.

Refs #336320

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: share connected tab left border

Overlap first and wrapped-row-start connected fills by one stroke so their left edge reuses the editor body border instead of drawing an adjacent double border.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: simplify connected tab color ownership

Use a single editorGroupHeader.connectedTabsBackground token and emit its derived styles only under the connected-tabs root marker.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: describe connected tab color as reusable

Document editorGroupHeader.connectedTabsBackground by visual role rather than feature enablement so it remains suitable for any connected tab treatment.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: centralize connected tab ownership

Share the connected-tab root marker across editor controls, contribution setup, and theming, and document the dedicated stylesheet scoping invariant.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs: define connected tab ownership

Document the reusable connected header color, border ownership, marker lifecycle, and separation between CSS geometry and editor control behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: derive connected action height from the row

Use flex stretch and the existing separator stroke so connected editor actions follow default and compact row heights without a special row-height variable.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: isolate all connected tab palettes

Move every strip background introduced by #335605 to editorGroupHeader.connectedTabsBackground while preserving the original shared tab backgrounds and independent foreground contrast fixes.

Refs #336320

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: balance connected tab close spacing

Reserve upper-row pill insets consistently in tab width and close-action positioning, with single, terminal, wrapped, and left-action regression coverage.

Consolidates #336791

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: complete connected tab spacing

Restore the terminal close-action shoulder reservation from the consolidated fix and remove the generic wrapped-row top inset so connected strips meet the header edge directly.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: balance terminal tab actions

Let the external shoulder reservation own terminal geometry so close actions keep the same visible inset as ordinary and wrapped tabs. Add a regression assertion for balanced label- and edge-side action spacing.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: share connected tab frame borders

Classify the outermost connected tab row explicitly so active tabs can reuse the editor frame's top stroke. First-position active tabs also reuse the left stroke, while inner wrapped rows retain pill gutters and balanced close actions.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: give frame sole border ownership

Avoid overlapping the connected tab and editor frame strokes. The outermost tab now starts at the frame's inner edge with transparent top and left borders, allowing the editor frame and its clipping radius to be the sole painter at every zoom level.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: center connected tab actions

Center the close glyph in its painted action surface and shift that surface outward by the same inset so label- and shoulder-side spacing remain balanced. Preserve sole editor-frame ownership of the outer border.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: repair connected tab outline regressions

Preserve high contrast outlines where the outer editor frame is transparent. Account for both cap radii when hiding clipped tab slivers, and update stale assertions for centered actions and editor-owned first-tab borders.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: derive close clearance from the tab surface

Share action clearance across row densities and label reservation, accounting for painted borders instead of shoulder width. Keep standard row starts on the editor frame and join top-row side strokes directly to its shared top edge.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: keep compact tab outlines visible under actions

Let the selected tab fill own its surface instead of painting a second opaque action-container background over the trailing cap stroke. Preserve the close target's own hover and keyboard focus treatment.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: keep wrapped tab reservation width invariant

Reserve the pill inset and active shoulder before classifying rows, and consume the inset in fill and action positioning rather than changing fit widths through row markers. Exercise wrapping boundary widths in both resize directions and with changing active tabs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: explicitly retain high contrast close indicators

Draw hover and focus outlines on the close action itself while keeping the surrounding action container transparent. Cover focused actions in both high contrast themes and both wrapped rows; account for Electron's hidden test window when checking CSS focus state.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: stabilize connected tab surfaces and close targets

Keep wrapped fills contiguous, round free corners, and reserve close-action stroke clearance independently of selection. Preserve high-contrast target indicators without a second action-container border. Add geometry and selection regressions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: respect disabled connected tab action hover state

Exclude disabled actions without raising hover specificity over keyboard focus. Cover the real Alt-to-Close-Others transition in both high-contrast themes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: consolidate connected tab high-contrast frames

Share the HC editor-group frame without changing close-target geometry, keep shared strip theming separate from the Modern UI editor palette, and update regression coverage and documentation.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Editor: ignore unrendered frame color in connected tab tests

All four browser and Electron CI failures asserted black for an absent frame whose unused border color inherits currentColor. Assert the color only for the rendered HC frame, retaining geometry and frame-presence coverage. Seed a non-black foreground so focused runs reproduce the full-suite inheritance.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agent-host: preserve identity and actor of admitted turns (#337364)

* agent-host: preserve identity and actor of admitted turns

Add turn and chat correlation to Microsoft send telemetry so accepted user turns can be deduplicated without relying on completions. Preserve actor classification for inline messages, modern subagent chats, and system-initiated workbench requests, including pending-message round trips.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agent-host: preserve provenance when resending remote pending messages

Carry the original actor, metadata, and system label through remote queue projection, reconciliation, persistence, and immediate resend. Keep generated turns from being counted as human input after client round trips or rejected-send recovery.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agent-host: retain participant routing for remote pending resends

Keep remote-only pending messages on their session participant when sent immediately instead of falling back to the global default chat agent. Preserve that routing if the resend is requeued, and test with distinct default and host participants.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

agentHost: prevent silent reconnects from hanging session requests (#336510)

agentHost: keep liveness checks active during reconnect

Start liveness checks once the replacement transport is established and let watchdog pings bypass the reconnect gate. A silent recovery RPC can then trigger another attempt instead of leaving session subscriptions waiting indefinitely.

Cover silent reconnect, initialize, and subscription restoration, plus slow transport establishment and responsive recovery.

commit.message:
Add governed OTel identity capture for Local agents (#336814)

Resolves #302930. Target: **1.140.0**. Builds on #336701.

## Summary

Adds opt-in, enterprise-governed identity capture to **Local Copilot Chat**:
- `user.name` on agent invocation spans, including subagents and inline agents.
- `process.user.name` and `host.name` on resources.

Identity is **off by default and independent of content capture**. Explicit managed policy wins over environment and personal preferences. Denial strips identity from subsequent exports, including queued data and SQLite, and stays latched until reload. Explicit resource attributes cannot bypass it.

Managed telemetry selects one whole block in priority order: native MDM > server > file. Omitted fields are not inherited from lower-priority sources. Resource batching is preserved; unavailable OS usernames do not stop telemetry.

**Scope:** Local only. Agent Host endpoint routing and native identity validation are tracked in #337413.

## Validation

- 314 focused tests, extension type-check, and targeted lint passed.
- Live Local checks passed: identity/content enabled, content disabled, and identity denied without reload. Re-enable/reload behavior has automated coverage, not live validation.
- Opus 5.5 re-review found no remaining issues; renewed signed approval is pushed.
- Latest CI status is tracked in the checks below.

chat: show MCP sign-in progress and preserve live server state (#337381)

* chat: show MCP sign-in progress and preserve live server state

- Show progress during MCP sign-in and prevent duplicate requests in lists and cards.
- Restore sign-in controls after completion, cancellation, or failure.
- Keep authentication challenges available and restart exhausted SDK auth attempts on retry.
- Apply authentication state transitions to each SDK update without a pending-transition flag.

- Prevent late inventory responses from replacing newer lifecycle or authentication state.

agentHost: apply pending configuration before MCP startup (#337370)

* agentHost: apply pending configuration before MCP startup

MCP Start can run before pending plugin configuration reaches the live SDK session. Apply that
configuration before Start and report failures instead of leaving the server in Starting.

- Share configuration refresh between Send and MCP Start, and preserve the SDK session ID.
- Wait for active turns before a Start-triggered refresh. Keep MCP RPCs outside the chat queue.
- Own Start cancellation in AgentSideEffects and pass the token through preparation and startup.
- Publish explicit Start errors without replacing newer requests or authoritative server states.
- Retry failed plugin sync without dropping healthy plugins or skipping identical inputs.
- Add tests for refresh, failure reporting, cancellation, idle waits, and queue independence.

commit.message:
minVersion UI: enterprised managed users not satisfying minVersion get explanatory overlay and banner

Fixes #337086

Enterprise Managed Settings `minVersion` lets administrators block AI features on outdated VS Code clients until users update—for example, to require newer sandboxing protections.

This PR explains that existing restriction without changing enforcement. Chat shows an update notice. **Agents shows one blocking overlay, without a redundant banner.** The editor retains a Workspace Trust-style banner even when Chat is closed, because other editing features remain available.

Native update actions are offered when available. If enterprise policy disables built-in updates, the notice directs users to their administrator for an approved update. Other unavailable-updater states do not imply administrator management, and **no generic fallback link is shown**. **Open Editor Window** opens a fresh editor window, preserving the existing recovery behavior.

## Screenshots

**Controlled simulations, real rendered UI.** Code - OSS Dev, isolated HTTP 466 requirement (installed 1.140.0; required 1.141.0), with the existing updater service temporarily set to `Idle` or `Disabled(Policy)` and then restored to `Disabled(NotBuilt)`. Agents captures were regenerated at the final review-fix head and matched the published PNGs byte-for-byte; unchanged Editor captures are retained. No DOM/text substitution, composites, shipping test switches, or actual update installation. Editor captures exclude the account area and show only a synthetic example file.

### Native updater available — simulated `Idle`

**Chat closed: the editor banner remains visible, with Check for Updates.**

![Editor with a synthetic text file and Chat closed, retaining the organizational update banner and Check for Updates action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc6d41c6-1f90-4f3c-ab21-35bedc4db4ce)

**Chat open: the same requirement and native update action appear beside the editor.**

![Editor showing the Chat update notice and persistent banner with Check for Updates](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9587a5b5-24f0-42f4-a7e2-c5860c573ea0)

**Agents: overlay only, with Check for Updates and Open Editor Window.**

![Agents update-required overlay with Check for Updates and Open Editor Window, without a window banner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eec22c2-4aa5-493a-bedb-67e0b45d280d)

### Enterprise-managed updates — simulated `Disabled(Policy)`

**Chat closed: the editor banner explains that an administrator manages the update path; no generic link.**

![Editor with Chat closed and a text-only banner explaining that built-in updates are disabled by the organization](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0999d027-f53c-4192-9337-4bda4355bf10)

**Chat open: administrator guidance, without a misleading fallback action.**

![Chat notice showing the required and installed versions and administrator guidance, with no update button or generic link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec6b9776-6351-429b-b107-bcb2cefbb414)

**Agents: administrator guidance and Open Editor Window; no redundant banner or generic link.**

![Agents overlay showing administrator-managed recovery guidance and only Open Editor Window as an action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/feb3a981-0d5d-45b3-8ca5-67cab57ad988)

<details>
<summary>Validation and remaining checks</summary>

- 158 focused tests passed in **each of Chromium and WebKit**, including focus ownership/restoration, startup fallback, long tokens and viewport resizing, available-action help, all disabled-updater reasons, and the unchanged fresh-editor-window action.
- Before the final push, all eight Compile & Hygiene scripts passed across documented runs: `core-ci`, `hygiene`, `eslint`, `valid-layers-check`, `define-class-fields-check`, `vscode-dts-compile-check`, `tsec-compile-check`, and `test-build-scripts`. The original aggregate hit environment blockers; it is not claimed as one successful unmodified run. The same `core-ci` command passed after GitHub's rate-limit reset. Build-script tests passed 462/462 with command-scoped empty Git configuration for synthetic fixture repos and canonical `/private/tmp`; the other checks used normal Git configuration. User signing settings were unchanged.
- Build-tool typecheck, Markdown manifest checks, conditional Codex protocol check (no changed inputs), and cyclic-dependency check (9,174 files) passed or correctly skipped before that push.
- Real Electron checks covered both updater states and editor-banner independence from Chat. A long version token at a 600×320 renderer viewport wrapped without horizontal overflow, and the focused recovery action remained visible after shrinking the viewport. Mock settings, updater state, and viewport were restored afterward.
- Earlier validation covered actual 320/480/900px Chat widths and HTTP 466 → `200 {}` → 466 recovery in both windows. All three Copilot review threads have concise inline replies and are resolved.
- Presentation consumes the existing compatibility signal; it does not invent extension/runtime-specific metadata. VoiceOver and full light/dark/high-contrast coverage remain pending.
- Draft review and a trusted signed approval checkpoint at the new head remain outstanding. No automatic merge.

</details>

* automations: test: register update-only dialog coverage

Move the nested regression to suite scope so filtered and normal runs both execute it.

* automations: fix: retain selected hosts when unavailable

Address UIUX-1: keep an Automation draft's selected host instead of silently falling back to another machine. Ordinary session pickers keep their existing defaults.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* automations: fix: cancel admitted runs before session creation

Address CORE-2: propagate caller cancellation through host admission and the session wait, forwarding it once and leaving lifecycle updates authoritative on the host.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* automations: fix: wait for provider authentication readiness

Address CORE-1: preserve due occurrences until provider-owned prerequisites are available and react to readiness changes without a renderer scheduler. Copilot gates missing/revoked credentials while allowing explicitly selected signed-out BYOK models.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* automations: fix: use update authority for tool target edits

Address ARCH-1/UIUX-2/CORE-3: allow same-host target edits without create capability, share cross-host validation, and report stale approvals before target eligibility failures.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* automations: fix: keep operation ordering stable after runs

Address PERF-1: restore Remove in canonical operation order so an unrelated configuration refresh does not rewrite history or republish an unchanged catalogue.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* automations: test: fix stale approval result assertion

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* automations: fix: keep observing admitted pending runs

Do not impose the browser mutation timeout on a host-admitted run waiting for a session. Preserve cancellation while the host waits for execution readiness.

commit.message:
agentHost: keep the default chat title in sync with a session rename (#337308)

* agentHost: keep the default chat title in sync with a session rename

Renaming a session from the sessions list left the session header showing
the old title, and committing that header handed the stale title back to
the session, silently overwriting the rename.

A session whose only chat is its default chat has no independently titled
chat - the header shows the session title - but the chat still owns
persisted title metadata written whenever something renamed it directly
(the rename tool, the chat header, an automatic title). A session-scoped
rename updated only the session, so that metadata went stale and restore
seeded it back as the chat's own title.

Mirror a session rename down onto the sole default chat in both live state
and persisted metadata. Handling this in onDidApplyClientAction covers
every session-channel rename rather than just the rename-tool path, and
repairs already-affected sessions the next time they are renamed. Sessions
that own peer chats are skipped: their default chat is independently
titled by design.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: isolate title stores in the rename test and fix replay contract

Two follow-ups to the sole-default-chat rename fix.

The new test passed one TestSessionDatabase to createSessionDataService,
which returns that same database for every channel. That aliased the
session and chat stores, so onHydrateChat could read the session's
customTitle and the test still passed with the chat-local writes removed.
Use createPerSessionDataService() and assert both databases, including the
companion source keys, so all four writes are independently covered.

Retitling the default chat also dispatches SessionChatUpdated on the
session channel - that is how a live header updates - so a session rename
now replays one more action than the protocol contract expected.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Dmitriy Vasyura <dmitriv@microsoft.com>

commit.message:
Show HydraFusion phases with compact progress pills (#337096)

* Show HydraFusion phases with compact progress pills

Render routing and phase progress, preserve workflow model identity, and handle replay and missing tool approvals.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix HydraFusion progress lifecycle and phase rendering

Preserve workflow ownership across cancellation and replay, persist interrupted phase timing, and separate phase presentation from tool execution accounting. Reconcile tool approvals, centralize activity publication, and cache phase model display while avoiding redundant rendering.

Addresses review feedback for #337096.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Consolidate Fusion tests and fix approval and replay edge cases

Move unique metadata and replay regressions into existing suites, retain focused timing and label checks, reject manual orphan approvals, and project ephemeral phase state without persisting transient updates.

Addresses review feedback for #337096.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address Fusion correlation, Stop timing, and import review feedback

Reject ambiguous SDK ownership, recover singly delivered workflow metadata after correlation, restore routing at trusted boundaries, and keep unowned failures out of durable replay. Finalize phase timing before host cancellation and preserve imported failure/cancellation outcomes.

Fixes review feedback on #337096; regression coverage remains in existing integrated suites.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Complete provisional Fusion tool calls surfaced for confirmation

Forward provisional Fusion tool lifecycle events on a dedicated wrapper
event and promote a held-back tool start when its permission request
must be shown, so the approved tool completes on its own lifecycle
instead of being cancelled at turn end. Remove a stale JSDoc left behind
by the isSyntheticUserMessage move.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: prevent duplicate Codex skills across sessions (#335475)

* agentHost: prevent duplicate Codex skills across sessions

Keep client-synced skills scoped to each thread's selectedCapabilityRoots instead of registering every live session's cache in the process-global skill catalogue.

Cover overlapping workspace bundles, retained revisions, and app-server reconnection with a regression test.

* agentHost: deliver Codex client skills on each turn

Advertise the current client skill catalogue through per-turn application context and grant read-only access through existing thread permission profiles. Reuse customization reconciliation for skill-directory and permission-profile changes instead of relying on selectedCapabilityRoots during resume.

Cover the original provider integration failure, add/remove after the first turn, native skill preservation, workspace isolation, and sandbox read-grant preservation and revocation with the pinned Codex SDK.

* agentHost: preserve Codex runtime access in skill sandboxes

Grant read access to the canonical Linux Codex executable through an inherited runtime profile. The sandbox helper re-executes that binary, and per-thread skill filesystem overrides must not erase this runtime grant. Do not expose the SDK directory or weaken sandbox restrictions.

Restore session-scoped skill regression coverage after main merges and verify native execution before checking permission denials, so a sandbox bootstrap failure cannot masquerade as successful access revocation.

* agentHost: isolate Windows native-skill integration fixtures

Codex resolves the Windows home through the OS profile API, not HOME or USERPROFILE overrides. Place the temporary native user skill under the explicitly configured CODEX_HOME on Windows; retain .agents coverage on POSIX and every native-skill preservation assertion on all platforms.

---------

Co-authored-by: copilot-swe-agent[bot] <198982749+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: retract stale sessions when a provider catalog becomes readable (#337214)

* agentHost: refresh stale zombie sessions when catalogs become readable

When a provider catalog transitions from unreadable to readable, refresh already-published provisional sessions so suppression reaches clients instead of only updating the next explicit list call.

The refresh is queued only on a genuine readability transition; already-readable imports keep their existing list-invalidation behavior without queueing the published-list refresh.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: do not lose the readable transition to a racing listing

The refresh decided whether to run by intersecting currently-published
sessions with the provisional markers, at the instant the provider became
readable. Both collections can be empty then: publication happens inside
`prepareSessionSummariesForListing`, so a fail-open listing that is still
computing has not published yet, and the marker mirror is an asynchronous
registry read. Either one empty dropped the refresh, and the transition is
one-shot -- the stale row was then published with nothing left to retract
it.

Decide inside the queued refresh instead, after awaiting the marker load,
and snapshot the published set only once the fresh listing has completed.
The no-op case is still cheap: a provider with no published provisional
session returns before invalidating anything.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: stabilize terminal sandbox smoke tests (#337223)

* chat: stabilize terminal sandbox smoke tests

Require terminal-tool availability in a fresh warm-up model request before
running sandbox probes, and use attempt-specific replies to avoid stale
response matches.

Carry forward #326150: restore the sandbox execution smoke test and accept
minified rewriter names while still requiring the sandbox-wrapping log.
Preserve the real TMPDIR write and zero-exit-code oracle.

Refs microsoft/vscode-engineering#3315

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: correlate sandbox warm-up requests with retry attempts

Give each sandbox warm-up retry a separate mock scenario and require the
captured request's latest user message to carry that attempt's tag.
This prevents a delayed request from receiving a newer reply or supplying
terminal-tool readiness for another attempt.

Share the existing latest-user tag matcher with the model-configuration
smoke suite, supporting both chat messages and Responses API input.

Addresses review feedback on #337223.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: Show catalog chats in the session list (#337162)

* sessions: Surface catalog chats without eager hydration

Carry lightweight ordered chat metadata through Agent Host session listings, seed stable peer-chat facades from it, and hydrate volatile details only when virtualized chat rows are rendered.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Start nested chats collapsed

Keep catalog-backed chat rows hidden until the user expands a session, while preserving expansion for an active child chat.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Preserve catalog chat interactivity

Carry hidden and read-only metadata through catalog persistence, AHP session listings, and stable chat facades so session-list presentation is correct before hydration.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Pin merged chat catalog protocol

Update the generated protocol revision to the canonical merge commit for agent-host-protocol#455.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Persist nested chat collapse state

Start multi-chat sessions expanded, then preserve each user's collapse choice across list and window recreation without treating temporary active-chat reveals as a preference change.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Keep catalog chats stable during hydration

Seed restored peer summaries before publishing live session state and preserve catalog-backed peers while capabilities hydrate, preventing nested chat rows from disappearing and returning.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Resolve peer chat details on observation

Load transient Agent Host peer-chat state when its observables gain consumers, and share the backing subscription through a reference collection. This keeps provider-specific hydration out of the shared Sessions contract.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Keep catalog chat hydration lazy

Avoid detail subscriptions from catalog-backed filtering and collapsed parent rendering, and recover active detail observers after subscription failures or reconnects. Reuse the shared catalog-origin parser and remove the test-only bind call.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: Prepare cloud sandbox repositories before session creation (#337173)

* sessions: Prepare cloud sandbox repositories before session creation

Resolve an advertised host checkout before creating a sandbox session and binding directory-scoped customizations. Preserve existing sessions and unsupported hosts, and stop creation on preparation failure or cancellation.

Keep this as temporary client compatibility until repository-backed creation is adopted.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Mark temporary cloning compatibility for removal

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Contain legacy sandbox preparation at session startup

Keep legacy repository preparation in the cloud connection customization instead of the platform service and transport factory. Remove the resolver class and scope metadata parsing to cloud sandboxes without adopting draft protocol fields.

Share concurrent preparations while keeping caller cancellation independent, release abandoned RPC tracking, and surface failed clone replies immediately.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: Keep cloning compatibility scoped to session preparation

Remove generic request-abandonment plumbing and its tests from this change. Preserve existing transport behavior while retaining independent cancellation, timeouts, and shared repository preparation waits.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
network: align URL trust and IDN domain policies (#336960)

* network: normalize Unicode wildcard domain patterns

Normalize wildcard suffixes with the URL-aware authority helper before validating the pattern. Add matching, policy, and fetch-tool regression coverage while preserving existing domain handling.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* network: normalize sandbox domains and IDN URL approvals

Canonicalize sandbox domain policies and preflight URL hosts, rejecting patterns that cannot be normalized. Match equivalent Unicode and Punycode literal host labels in URL trust and approval rules while preserving existing glob semantics.

Partial Unicode wildcard labels remain outside this change.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* url: align trust checks with effective HTTP destinations

Normalize authority separators and resolved paths consistently across trusted domains, URL approval rules, and web-page fetching. Preserve hostname case semantics, escaped path data, and actual request destinations, with regression coverage for approvals, exclusions, and declined tool calls.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sandbox: warn and deny network for invalid domain patterns

Keep shell-tool registration and offline sandboxed commands available when domain patterns cannot be normalized. Log a warning and use a deny-all policy instead of throwing, with regression coverage for both lists and recovery after settings are corrected.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* url: bound glob matching and preserve effective URL semantics

Replace the eager recursive matcher with iterative deduplicated states to avoid Unicode path allocation spikes and stack growth. Normalize configured patterns consistently, preserve effective authority and path semantics, and retain HTTP path case without changing non-HTTP drive normalization.

Add regression coverage for the PR feedback and verify real Code OSS trust, approval, fetch, and sandbox workflows.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: keep confirmations, reasoning, and progress consistent with persistent progress (#336961)

* chat: keep confirmations, reasoning, and progress consistent with persistent progress

Tool confirmations now render only in the carousel above the input,
regardless of the progress style. The transcript copy of a confirmation
decides its own visibility on every render, so re-rendering a pending tool
(a tool data change, or a row rebuilt while a request was being edited)
no longer shows a second inline copy next to the carousel.

Reasoning no longer fragments while background subagents run. Their child
tool calls stream into the parent response, which used to end the active
thinking part and start a new one for each following reasoning delta; the
model now merges deltas past nested subagent parts and the renderer groups
subagent tools before finalizing thinking.

The persistent footer describes what the response is waiting on: the
number of running subagents, or terminal output for a pending background
terminal read, instead of a generic working phrase. It also stops
reporting "Authentication required" for an MCP prompt that has no servers
left to authenticate; the prompt is published empty and drains as servers
authenticate, and only a mounted transcript row ever marked it used.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: address review of persistent progress consistency fixes

Recognize agent host MCP tool calls when deciding whether a confirmation
belongs in the carousel. Protocol tools all carry an internal source, and
Claude MCP calls are only identifiable by their `mcp__` tool id, so the
carousel predicate now shares `isMcpToolInvocation` with the pinning logic
instead of testing the source alone.

Keep the waiting label when subagents finish out of launch order: a trailing
launch counts as waiting whenever any agent is still active, since the count
already excludes the completed ones.

Exempt nested subagent progress from finalizing the reasoning timer, not
just from the merge target. A child tool used to stamp the duration and
clear the active reasoning, so the next delta re-armed it on an object that
was merged away and the header kept only the pre-tool duration.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

mcp: enforce URL policy after variable resolution (#336849)

* mcp: enforce URL policy after variable resolution

Distinguish preliminary definition checks from authoritative resolved launch checks. Validate the local resolved connection before starting its transport, and re-evaluate active connections whenever policy changes.

Add regression coverage for literal variable markers, resolved URL allow/deny rules, permitted unresolved definitions, and policy changes affecting running servers.

* mcp: preserve policy blocks and settle cancelled startup

Keep resolved policy blocks effective after disposing a connection, including suppression of cached tools and prompts. Settle startup waits on explicit stop or disposal so policy restoration permits a retry without regressing normal transport restarts.

Share configuration-variable parsing with preliminary MCP checks so literal incomplete markers do not defer allow/deny enforcement. Add regression coverage for retained blocks, definition changes, preliminary checks, and cancelled startup.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: invalidate retained policy identity on definition changes

Discard the retained resolved launch identity on the first non-equivalent definition change, including while a connection is live. Returning from definition B to A must not revive A's stale policy result or prevent its variables from being resolved again.

Reuse the existing policy-enforcement observer and preserve the equivalent-definition and resolved-launch checks. Add failing-first regressions for stopped and live connection histories.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: recover input retries and scan variables in linear time

Allow interactive retries to resolve current inputs after a retained policy denial without clearing the block that hides cached metadata. Quiet starts remain blocked, and cancellation or repeated denial keeps the cache hidden until a resolved destination is permitted.

Use one shared linear-time, constant-space balanced-variable detector for preliminary checks and workbench discovery instead of repeatedly parsing unmatched suffixes. Preserve the existing nested-variable syntax and avoid constructing resolver expressions just to detect variables.

Add failing-first edit/reset, cancellation, repeated-denial and 64 KiB discovery regressions, plus differential grammar coverage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Reject access and name restrictions before provider activation or variable resolution, including interactive retries that retain a previous URL denial.

Expose the shared preliminary identity check and apply it at rest and before allowing re-resolution. Defer only rules for unresolved URL/command fields; keep the resolved runtime check authoritative. Update test doubles for the internal service contract.

Add failing-first coverage for initial starts and retained-identity retries with input/command variables, plus command-policy deferral controls.

* mcp: enforce URL policy after variable resolution

Distinguish preliminary definition checks from authoritative resolved launch checks. Validate the local resolved connection before starting its transport, and re-evaluate active connections whenever policy changes.

Add regression coverage for literal variable markers, resolved URL allow/deny rules, permitted unresolved definitions, and policy changes affecting running servers.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: preserve policy blocks and settle cancelled startup

Keep resolved policy blocks effective after disposing a connection, including suppression of cached tools and prompts. Settle startup waits on explicit stop or disposal so policy restoration permits a retry without regressing normal transport restarts.

Share configuration-variable parsing with preliminary MCP checks so literal incomplete markers do not defer allow/deny enforcement. Add regression coverage for retained blocks, definition changes, preliminary checks, and cancelled startup.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: invalidate retained policy identity on definition changes

Discard the retained resolved launch identity on the first non-equivalent definition change, including while a connection is live. Returning from definition B to A must not revive A's stale policy result or prevent its variables from being resolved again.

Reuse the existing policy-enforcement observer and preserve the equivalent-definition and resolved-launch checks. Add failing-first regressions for stopped and live connection histories.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: recover input retries and scan variables in linear time

Allow interactive retries to resolve current inputs after a retained policy denial without clearing the block that hides cached metadata. Quiet starts remain blocked, and cancellation or repeated denial keeps the cache hidden until a resolved destination is permitted.

Use one shared linear-time, constant-space balanced-variable detector for preliminary checks and workbench discovery instead of repeatedly parsing unmatched suffixes. Preserve the existing nested-variable syntax and avoid constructing resolver expressions just to detect variables.

Add failing-first edit/reset, cancellation, repeated-denial and 64 KiB discovery regressions, plus differential grammar coverage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: enforce static policy before server resolution

Reject access and name restrictions before provider activation or variable resolution, including interactive retries that retain a previous URL denial.

Expose the shared preliminary identity check and apply it at rest and before allowing re-resolution. Defer only rules for unresolved URL/command fields; keep the resolved runtime check authoritative. Update test doubles for the internal service contract.

Add failing-first coverage for initial starts and retained-identity retries with input/command variables, plus command-policy deferral controls.

mcp: handle HTTP stream cancellation during disposal (#336921)

Disposing an MCP HTTP transport already aborts its fetch response. Cancelling the errored reader again creates a rejected promise that was previously discarded, surfacing an unhandled AbortError during normal stop/disposal.

Skip that redundant cancellation after disposal and await cancellation for active read failures. Add a failing-first disposal regression and a control that keeps genuine stream failures visible.

commit.message:
agentHost: retroactively recognise unmarked crash orphans (#336806)

* Hide empty orphaned agent sessions

During catalog reconciliation, retroactively marks provider-unresolvable sessions as provisional only when their local conversation storage is empty. Listing then reuses the existing provisional suppression path without per-listing storage opens.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 26730bc1-5d8d-48f1-a4c6-bde566082230

* agentHost: abandon a retroactive marker when the session changed

The retroactive provisional marker was written unconditionally after the
emptiness check. A mutation or a concurrent materialization landing during
source resolution could add turns or clear the marker, and the write would
then re-mark a session holding real work -- hiding it on the next listing.

Re-read the dirty marker and abandon the write when it has moved, matching
how `_park` already yields to the same race.

Also correct a test comment that described the opposite of its own
assertion: the listing stays fail-open until the marker read completes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
