commit.message:
agentHost: Separate substantive first progress from host bookkeeping (#336845)

* Attribute and reduce Agent Host turn pre-send latency

Agent Host turns report `timeToFirstProgress` as one opaque number, so the
host's own share of time-to-first-token cannot be attributed to any
particular piece of work. Add per-stage timings, then fix the two largest
contributors they expose.

Attribution: record the duration of each bounded pre-send stage
(workingDirectory, modelSelection, attachments, contributions, checkpoint)
plus `timeToProviderDispatch`, the total host cost before the provider is
called. This uses its own vocabulary rather than widening
`AgentHostTurnFailureStage`: "where did the turn break" and "where did the
turn spend its time" are different questions with different consumers. A
stage that ran instantly reports 0; one that never ran is absent.

Checkpoint overlap: the turn-start checkpoint ran a full git working-tree
snapshot (status --untracked-files=all, read-tree, write-tree) inline before
`sendMessage` — roughly 400ms-1s per turn on a large repository. Start it as
soon as the working directory is known so it overlaps the provider
round-trips, and keep awaiting it before the message is sent, so the snapshot
still reflects the tree the agent starts from. A turn already cancelled skips
the capture entirely, and because the cancel-time discard now runs before the
capture settles, the send path discards again afterwards.

Model validation: `_validateModelSelection` awaited an in-flight model-catalog
refresh on every turn. That await only guards against rejecting a model a
pending refresh is about to add, so skip it when the catalog already lists the
model — a refresh landing later cannot invalidate a selection that is valid
now.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address review feedback on pre-send latency changes

Four defects found in review, all real:

Catalog freshness: a scheduled model refresh is *invalidating* — it follows a
token rotation or client restart, and `_capiModels` is not cleared first, so the
published catalog still belongs to the previous credential. The fast path
therefore accepted a model the new credential may not have. Skip only an
ordinary in-flight refresh, which re-enumerates the same credential.

Failure cleanup: starting the checkpoint earlier meant a turn that failed during
model selection, attachment resolution, or contributions left a turn-start
checkpoint behind, which the non-resumable error path then paired with an end
checkpoint. Previously such a turn never captured at all. Discard the pending
capture unless `sendMessage` has begun.

Timing consistency: `turnCompleted` sampled `totalTime` before closing the open
stage, so a millisecond tick between the two samples could attribute stage time
past the reported turn duration. Close the stage first.

Checkpoint test fidelity: the fake let a discard complete while a capture was in
flight, which the production service's per-session sequencer forbids. The test
asserted an impossible interleaving, and the comment justifying the second
discard was wrong. Model the sequencer, assert the real guarantee, and document
the discard as idempotent cleanup that the failure path genuinely requires.

Both new behaviours are covered by tests confirmed to fail without their fix.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Track catalog invalidation across the in-flight refresh window

The previous guard checked `_scheduledModelRefresh`, but the scheduler clears
that field before it awaits the `models.list` request. The entire request
window therefore looked like an ordinary refresh, and a model from the
superseded catalog was accepted through the fast path — the exact case the
guard was added to prevent. The earlier regression test passed only because it
selected while the refresh was still scheduled, never after the request began.

Track `_invalidatingModelRefresh` instead, held from the credential or client
change that schedules the refresh until the replacement catalog is published,
which is strictly later than the scheduler clearing its own bookkeeping.

The new test waits for the credential-triggered request to start, keeps it
gated, and asserts the selection stays pending and then rejects. Confirmed to
fail against the scheduled-only guard (resolved while gated, setModel called).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Separate substantive first progress from host bookkeeping

`timeToFirstProgress` counts any visible output, including the `rename_chat`
call the host itself induces via the injected rename reminder. A turn whose
first visible act is naming the chat therefore looks fast while the user is
still waiting for real output — the same step-selection flaw that makes the
eval dashboard's Agent Host and Local numbers non-comparable.

Add `timeToFirstSubstantiveProgress`, which excludes the chat rename call.
Renaming is bookkeeping rather than work on the user's request, so it never
qualifies regardless of whether the host or the agent initiated it. Substantive
progress also marks plain progress, so the two keep the invariant that
`timeToFirstSubstantiveProgress >= timeToFirstProgress` whenever both are set.

Both are reported: comparing against another harness needs the substantive
value, comparing against "something appeared on screen" needs the plain one.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address review feedback on substantive first progress

Two defects found in review, both real:

Cross-provider metric: Claude surfaces host server tools through its MCP bridge
as `mcp__host__rename_chat`, so the bare-name comparison treated the injected
rename as substantive and defeated the metric for every Claude turn. Match
through a shared `isRenameChatTool` predicate that accepts both forms, following
the existing convention in `agentFeedbackAnnotations`.

Timing consistency: the turn stopwatch has millisecond resolution, and marking
plain then substantive progress read it twice. A millisecond boundary between
the reads implied a delay that never happened and could flake the equality
test. Stamp both metrics from a single reading.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Require real content for substantive first progress

The classifier excluded rename tool calls but counted every response part and
text/reasoning delta regardless of content. Providers open a part before
streaming into it — Claude emits empty `text`/`thinking` parts on
`content_block_start`, Codex an empty reasoning part — so the metric dated to
the moment the agent began thinking rather than the moment it produced
something, and a turn that ended without any content still reported a value
instead of none.

Classify content rather than shape: text and reasoning deltas must be
non-empty, markdown and reasoning parts must carry content, and host-authored
system notifications are structural. Tool calls other than the chat rename,
content references, and input requests remain substantive.

Legacy `timeToFirstProgress` is unchanged: everything rejected here still marks
plain progress, so only the new metric is affected.

Covers the mapper sequences directly — an empty opener followed by a delayed
delta, and empty openers with no content at all. Confirmed to fail against
content-blind classification (substantive populated at the empty opener).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: add per-item removal for recorded references and artifacts (#336688)

* sessions: add per-item removal for recorded references and artifacts (#336500)

Add a discoverable per-row remove action for individual recorded
session artifacts/references (files, resources, websites, commits,
GitHub issues and pull requests) in the Agents Window, invoking the
existing removeSessionArtifact operation by stable record ID.

Removability is gated purely on provenance: any persisted record with
a stable ID is removable when the owning provider advertises removal
support, regardless of its isArtifact flag or which pill/collection it
is rendered in. Durable artifacts are now equally removable (the
session record only; the underlying file/resource/PR/issue is never
mutated). Discovered-only GitHub associations that were never recorded
through add_artifact_or_reference remain non-removable, since they
have no recordedReferenceId to remove.

- sessionArtifacts.ts: presentation layer now offers a remove action
  for every SessionArtifactKind whenever the provider exposes a remove
  capability, independent of isArtifact.
- agentHostSessionArtifacts.ts / baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts:
  promoted GitHub issue/PR entries retain per-entry recordedReferenceId
  (no longer deduped by URL across recorded entries), so duplicate-
  looking resources remain independently removable by identity.
- protocolServerHandler.ts: local Agent Host transport now advertises
  vscode.removeSessionArtifact support so supportsRemoveArtifacts is
  populated correctly for the local provider.
- Preserves existing copy/open/hover/rich-preview behavior and the
  keyboard navigation added in #335583.

Docs (SESSIONS.md, AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md) updated to
describe isArtifact as presentation-only with respect to removability.

Tests added/updated across sessionArtifacts.test.ts (browser),
sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts, localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts,
sessionArtifactRemoval.test.ts, and protocolServerHandler.test.ts,
covering every artifact/reference kind, duplicate-ID removal,
idempotent removal of missing IDs, failure/retry, and preservation of
independently-discovered PR/issue associations after a recorded entry
is removed.

* sessions: harden per-item record removal

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: preserve GitHub reference provenance

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: cover focus restore and non-removable derived pills

Adds a regression test proving focus returns to a live pill after a context
menu action removes the pill it was opened from, and a negative test proving
file diff and browser pills never route through session record removal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: keep primary reference state consistent

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: stub context key service in removal accessibility test

The merged main adds a SessionsListPromoteNewChatActionContext read to
the Sessions chat accessibility help provider. The removal help test was
the only case still missing the shared stubContextKeyService setup, so it
threw on the undefined context key service in CI.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* sessions: keep the primary PR fallback icon when no ref matches

The primary pull request is now located by predicate rather than by
index, so a collection that does not contain the primary ref left every
entry without the fallback open icon and surfaced an icon-less pill.
Resolve the primary index once and reuse it for both the fallback icon
assignment and the primary lookup.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Fix built-in extensions manifest cache never being hit (#336383)

* extensions: fix built-in manifest cache never being hit

The manifest cache key includes the scan language, but the cache file name did
not. The window scans built-in extensions with a language while the shared
process scans without one, so both wrote the same file and the window missed
the cache on every startup, re-scanning every built-in extension on the
`code/willLoadExtensions` critical path.

Name the cache file after the scan language so the two callers stop clobbering
each other, and skip the throttled full re-scan that validated the built-in
cache on every hit: built-ins of an installed product cannot change behind our
back, and the product commit guarding them is already part of the cache key.
Invalidation now clears every per-language user cache file.

Measured on 1.139.0-insider (win32-x64, --disable-extensions, n=5 warm starts):
median built-in scan in the window 372ms -> 41ms, cache hits 0/5 -> 5/5.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: address review feedback on manifest cache fix

Inline the cache validation check at its only call site, tighten the user
cache file filter to require the .cache suffix, and document why install and
uninstall invalidation has to clear every per-language file.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: condense inline comments to single lines

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: make the cache file name identify the language exactly

The readable part of the name is lossy and file names are compared case
insensitively on some platforms, so languages differing only in case or in
separators mapped to one file while ExtensionScannerInput compared them
strictly - reintroducing the eviction loop this change fixes. Identify the
language by a hash of its exact value as well.

Also cover the skipped validation scan: a built-in cache hit must not scan
again, while a user cache hit still must.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: respect path casing when matching cache file names

Matching the file name with a plain string prefix ignored that file names are
compared case insensitively on some platforms. Move the predicate next to the
name generator so the two conventions cannot drift, and pass the extUri path
casing of the cache location so a differently cased name is recognized only
where it refers to the same file.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: identify the cache language with a digest, not a 32 bit hash

hash() is dense for short strings - 6016 of 9025 two character ASCII pairs
collide - so languages that also sanitize to the same readable part shared a
cache file and kept evicting each other. The unbounded readable part could
also push the name past the length a path component may have, which made the
cache write fail outright.

Use a truncated SHA1 of the exact language, which collides on none of those
pairs, and bound the readable part so the name stays short.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: drop the validation skip and validate every cached language

Skipping validation for built-in extensions was not worth its risk. It made an
incomplete scan - a built-in whose manifest failed to read is silently dropped -
stick permanently, since nothing else in the cache key changes when the read
recovers. It also removed the only in-session detection of built-ins changing
under a running window, which a product update does. None of the measured win
came from it: the gain is entirely from giving each language its own file.

Validation also kept a single mutable input, so with per-language files two
scans within the throttle window validated only the last language. Track a
pending input per cache file and validate each of them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Remove obsolete production build infrastructure (#336126)

* nls: precompute translation cache identity during packaging

Stamp the commit and NLS table fingerprint in product metadata and pass it through bootstrap. Reuse cached translations without reading or hashing default tables, while isolating different target tables and preserving legacy product compatibility.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* build: remove legacy compilation from standalone web packaging

Replace the redundant local compile/mangle prerequisite with explicit API proposal generation and build-date setup. Route both standalone web modes through the shared esbuild wrapper while preserving CI packaging and existing bundle flags.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* build: use esbuild for local server and server-web packaging

Route local server builds through the existing esbuild pipeline with explicit API, codicon, extension and date preparation. Avoid shipping a redundant server-web workbench bundle. Keep NLS cache protection in the independent #336109; the known same-commit localized local-target-switch limitation is accepted for this migration.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* build: remove obsolete production build infrastructure

Remove retired compile, mangle, bundle, and minify task chains and their exclusive helpers. Preserve current esbuild production transforms, Gulp orchestration, Monaco/development compilation, and translation routes. Share bootstrap entry definitions with packaging, drop unused mangling arguments, and prune exclusive dependencies and stale npm commands.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

chat: add opt-in persistent working progress (#336087)

* chat: add opt-in persistent working progress

Keep a stable progress indicator through thinking, tools and interactive prompts while preserving the collapsed-thinking exception and legacy behavior when disabled. Add configurable VS Code logo motion, regression coverage and live component fixtures. Preserve terminal and rich subagent activity animations, and undo the requested picker-label offsets.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: unify persistent progress and fix review regressions

Use one off-by-default animation enum for persistent progress. Keep approval status and footer ordering correct, preserve progressive reveal after interactions, track MCP authentication completion in the producer and response model, and restore verbose progress announcements.\n\nFix the reduced-motion terminal assertion and the nested MCP test, with configuration, lifecycle, and live-fixture regression coverage.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fold completed persistent responses and surface edit totals

Persistent progress now honors chat.agent.collapseCompletedResponses: completed
responses fold their expanded tool chains into "Completed N steps", counting
individual chain rows, and the summary gains a shared edit-stats button that
aggregates the response's file changes and opens the multi-diff editor. The
same button backs the thinking-header diff pill.

Also normalizes spacing for edit pills and markdown inside persistent tool
chains, adds a mock editing session so native markdown edit pills render in
tests and fixtures, and marks the setting as experiment-controlled
(default Off) with matching accessibility help and setting descriptions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 582f8a6c-b5dc-415f-a695-2ed8fdd8effd

* Stop persistent spacing and header height from depending on stylesheet order

The persistent spacing rules tied on specificity with main's
`.interactive-item-container .value > .chat-tool-invocation-part` margin,
so whichever stylesheet was imported first won; with every unit test file
loaded, the legacy 16px margin beat the shared gap token. Including the row
container class makes the persistent rules win outright.

Tool detail headers inherit a 1.5em line height computed at the response
font size while their label text is smaller, and Chromium builds disagree on
whether that block line height governs the label box (Playwright's Chromium
lays it out 1.5px short). Give the label text the header line height
directly so both engines agree.

Also allow one device pixel for the connector stroke checks at fractional
zoom, where Chromium snaps 1px strokes to whole device pixels.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 582f8a6c-b5dc-415f-a695-2ed8fdd8effd

* Address adversarial review of persistent progress

Footer state: tools waiting for MCP authentication and unused legacy
confirmation parts now surface as blocking states instead of a generic
working phrase, the per-tool watcher refreshes on those transitions, and
blocking labels are announced to screen readers once (rotating phrases stay
silent). Participant progress messages and unfinished tasks become the
footer text instead of being hidden behind it, and their rows fall back to
the check icon rather than a static spinner glyph.

Carousel: tool parts built for the input part's confirmation carousel use a
context without persistent presentation, and the gutter icon is scoped to
the response so it can no longer leak layout into another host.

Edit totals: content parts that render edits expose their current diff
(IChatContentPartDiffSource) so chains and subagents seed from values that
were emitted before they attached, for example restored sessions with cached
diffs. The completed-response aggregation collects each chain once (hooks
returned the same instance at several indices, doubling totals), and now
includes standalone edit markdown and subagent edits.

Also: the disclosure fast path recounts steps when chain rows are removed
after completion, a persistent reasoning preview defers its auto-collapse
until keyboard focus leaves it, and unknown animation values warn once.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 582f8a6c-b5dc-415f-a695-2ed8fdd8effd

commit.message:
Fix Copilot reasoning replay using API provenance instead of ID prefixes (#336626)

* Track reasoning provenance instead of inferring it from ids

Responses API reasoning was only round-tripped when its id began with `rs`.
That treated one provider's id convention as a protocol guarantee: CAPI's
production /responses endpoint issues reasoning ids that are long opaque blobs
with no `rs` prefix, so valid reasoning was silently dropped from the next
stateless tool continuation and the model re-derived work it had already done.

Record the producing API and model on the thinking envelope when a round is
created, and gate the round-trip on that origin. The envelope tag lives inside
the same opaque value as its payload so prompt pruning cannot separate them, and
it is carried across the vscode.lm boundary as part metadata since that API has
no envelope of its own. The model check also gives the vscode.lm path the gate
it never had.

History persisted before provenance tracking carries no origin and keeps the
previous `rs` prefix behavior.

Fix Copilot reasoning replay using API provenance instead of ID prefixes (#336626)

* Track reasoning provenance instead of inferring it from ids

Responses API reasoning was only round-tripped when its id began with `rs`.
That treated one provider's id convention as a protocol guarantee: CAPI's
production /responses endpoint issues reasoning ids that are long opaque blobs
with no `rs` prefix, so valid reasoning was silently dropped from the next
stateless tool continuation and the model re-derived work it had already done.

Record the producing API and model on the thinking envelope when a round is
created, and gate the round-trip on that origin. The envelope tag lives inside
the same opaque value as its payload so prompt pruning cannot separate them, and
it is carried across the vscode.lm boundary as part metadata since that API has
no envelope of its own. The model check also gives the vscode.lm path the gate
it never had.

History persisted before provenance tracking carries no origin and keeps the
previous `rs` prefix behavior.

commit.message:
copilot: fix slow content exclusion filtering of large search results (#336596)

* copilot: fix slow content exclusion filtering of large search results

filterIngoredResources queued every search result into a Limiter, whose
pending queue is drained with Array#shift. That is quadratic, and a
workspace-wide search over hundreds of thousands of files kept the shared
extension host busy for minutes. A fixed pool of workers now claims the
next index instead, so the work is linear again.

SearchServiceImpl.findFilesWithDefaultExcludes also filtered its results a
second time, even though the inherited implementation already routes
through the filtering findFiles override. The redundant override is removed.

Fixes #335194

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: bc4fa906-6b46-45f9-91fb-6a8b1f07b1a5

* copilot: stop remaining exclusion checks once one has failed

Promise.all rejects on the first failed check, but the other workers kept
claiming the rest of the batch. A shared flag set in finally now stops
them, matching what disposing the Limiter used to do.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

## Summary

Wait for `queryLocal()` before `workbench.extensions.installExtension` checks for an existing extension.

During startup, the synchronous installed-extension cache can still be empty. A command call with `{ enable: true }` can therefore treat an installed extension as missing and replace it with a Marketplace version. This affects the companion `/ContentMentor` route fix, which needs to preserve an installed pre-release even when the release is older.

pull_requests.title: chat: use SDK-owned customization installations
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Make the active customization harness's SDK/runtime inventory authoritative for marketplace installation state instead of persisting a second set of VS Code installation records.

- adds a harness installation-provider seam for provider-owned inventory, install, recovery, and uninstall operations
- routes Copilot SDK Skill and MCP operations through receipt-owned list/plan/confirm/apply/recover flows
- routes Copilot SDK plugin install/uninstall through the provider that owns `installedPlugins`
- validates the exact materialized policy session and the SDK confirmation review before approving a pending operation
- removes legacy `chat.customizations.marketplace.installationRecord.v1.*` profile records eagerly
- retains only bounded, in-memory associations for catalog presentation metadata such as icons
- derives fallback Local-harness plugin and MCP associations from their exact owning identities rather than persisted marketplace state

## Design

The provider inventory is the only source of installation truth. Discover joins that inventory to catalog resources by exact catalog identity first, then by compatible URL/source identities that reject conflicting versions or revisions.

Catalog metadata is deliberately non-authoritative. It can enrich an installed row with an icon or description after the matching catalog item is observed, but it cannot create an installed state.

Provider refreshes are bound to the exact harness/session and only the newest response may update the snapshot. SDK confirmation is likewise bound to the exact pending operation, policy session, expiry, and reviewed payload.

## Tradeoffs

- custom icons are best effort after restart; fallback type icons remain available until the catalog item is observed again
- SDK Skill and MCP inventory requires an exact materialized Copilot session because the SDK policy contract does not permit falling back to another live session
- fallback Local-harness Skill repair is window-local because VS Code no longer persists a parallel file manifest
- pinned direct catalog plugin installation is shown as unavailable for the Copilot SDK harness until the SDK exposes an exact pinned install contract; it does not silently fall back to VS Code-owned installation
- Connector lifecycle remains remotely authoritative and keeps its existing account-scoped in-memory association behavior

pull_requests.title: fix(extensions): re-run the restart-required query when the Show link is clicked again
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for using Markdown! -->

### Description

Fixes #321178

When extensions are updated in the background, the Extensions view shows a
banner like "2 extensions require a restart to take effect. **Show**". Clicking
**Show** filters the list with the `@restartrequired` query.

After **more** extensions are updated, the banner increments (e.g. to 4), but
the list still shows only the original 2. Clicking **Show** again does nothing,
and only clearing the filter and clicking **Show** once more reveals all 4
extensions (as reported in the issue, still reproducible on 1.136.1).

**Root cause** — `ExtensionsViewPaneContainer.search()` only sets the search
box value when it differs from the current one:

```ts
search(value: string): void {
    if (this.searchBox && this.searchBox.getValue() !== value) {
        this.searchBox.setValue(value);
    }
}
```

The first **Show** click puts `@restartrequired` into the search box, which
triggers the search. A second click requests the *same* value, so nothing is
set and no search is re-run — the list keeps the stale result.

### Fix

- `search()` accepts an optional `refresh` flag: when the search box already
  holds the requested value and `refresh` is set, the query is re-run
  (`doSearch(true)`) instead of being a no-op.
- The **Show** link (mouse click and Enter/Space key handling) passes
  `refresh: true`.
- The `refresh` flag is threaded through `doSearch()` →
  `showExtensionsViews()` → `ExtensionsListView.show(query, refresh)`, which
  discards the previous query result (including its change watcher) and
  re-queries. (Previously the flag was dropped, so the list view's existing
  refresh support was unreachable from the viewlet.)

### Testing

Added `extensionsRestartRequiredView.test.ts` which drives the real
`ExtensionsWorkbenchService` + `ExtensionsListView` and the
`ExtensionsViewPaneContainer.search()` entry point, simulating extension
updates that are installed while the previous version is still running (the
exact condition that puts extensions into the restart-required state):

- **`search() with refresh re-runs an already active query (#321178)`** — the
  regression test. Fails without the fix (the re-click never re-runs the
  search) and passes with it.
- `re-running the same query with refresh picks up newly
  restart-required extensions` — the list view re-query contract the fix
  relies on (1 extension → update → re-run with refresh → 2 extensions).
- `the @restartrequired list updates when more extensions require a restart`
  — the existing change-watcher live-update path still works.

- The full `extensionsViews.test.ts` (141 tests) and
  `extensionsWorkbenchService.test.ts` (214 tests) suites still pass.
- The touched files type-check cleanly under the repository's strict
  TypeScript settings.

pull_requests.title: copilot: dedup ADO auth-change events before rechecking repo status
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #320570

The ADO auth-change handler in `CodeSearchChunkSearch` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/node/codeSearch/codeSearchChunkSearch.ts`) re-fetched repo authorization status — an HTTP `semanticsearchstatus` request per tracked repo — on every `onDidAdoAuthenticationChange` event, including no-op silent token refreshes (e.g. triggered by window focus changes) that don't actually change the session identity. The existing GitHub auth handler already guards against this with a session-id + identity dedup; the ADO handler did not.

This splits the previously combined `Event.any(onDidAdoAuthenticationChange, onDidChangeIndexState)` listener into two independent listeners:
- The auth-change listener now dedups on session id + `authenticationSessionIdentityEquals` (mirroring the GitHub path), so no-op token refreshes no longer trigger a refetch.
- The index-state-change listener is left completely unguarded, so a real index-state notification can never be suppressed by the auth dedup.

Also promotes `anyAdoSession` from `BaseAuthenticationService` onto the `IAuthenticationService` interface (needed to read current session state from the dedup check), with two unrelated `IAuthenticationService` test mocks updated for interface compliance.

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] agentHost: forward tool-result images to BYOK models
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #339830 from `main`.

Fixes #339595
Fixes #339439

## Problem

In agent-host sessions, a BYOK (OpenAI-compatible) model never received images returned by tools such as `view`. It only received the text receipt `Viewed image file successfully.`

## Root cause

There were two problems:

1. **Vision capability never reached the runtime.** `synthesizeByokSessionConfig` registered BYOK models with token limits only. The renderer already reports `supportsVision`, but it wasn't passed on, so the Copilot runtime treated every BYOK model as text-only. It replaced tool-result images with the text receipt before the request reached the BYOK proxy. I confirmed this by running the SDK runtime against a stub `/responses` server. Without the capability, `function_call_output.output` is the plain string. With `capabilities.supports.vision: true`, it's an `[input_text, input_image]` array.
2. **The BYOK LM bridge had no image channel for tool outputs.** Once vision is declared, the array output was passed through untyped, and the renderer wrapped it in a text part.

## Changes

- `copilotSessionLauncher.ts`: forward `supportsVision` as `capabilities.supports.vision` on each BYOK `ProviderModelConfig`.
- `agentHostByokLm.ts`: add an optional `images` field to the two tool-output bridge items. `output` stays text, so a renderer that doesn't know the new field still gets today's text result.
- `byokResponsesTranslation.ts`: split array tool outputs into text plus images, reusing the existing data-URL and MIME validation from user messages.
- `agentHostByokLmHandler.ts`: forward the images as `data` parts inside the LM API `tool_result`, the same shape the in-extension path produces.

## How to test

1. Turn on `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`.
2. Add an OpenAI-compatible BYOK model that supports images (e.g. `gpt-4o`), with `"vision": true` and `"toolCalling": true`.
3. Put an image containing text the model can't guess (e.g. `ZEBRA-7341`) in the workspace.
4. In an agent-host session with that model, ask: *"Use the view tool to open probe.png and tell me exactly what text it contains. If you didn't receive image pixels, say so."*
   - Before this change: the model says it only got "Viewed image file successfully."
   - After this change: the model reads the text.
5. With `"vision": false`, the model should still get the text receipt and the turn should finish cleanly.

## Validation

pull_requests.title: Keep contributed tool sets whose members register late
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Related to #329320

## Problem

On VS Code Web, Agent mode never gives the model Copilot's `read_file` tool (`copilot_readFile`). The agent falls back to `cat` in the terminal and can't open tool output that was saved to a file (anything over about 8 KB). The same request works on VS Code Desktop.

In the attached debug logs, every Copilot tool in the `read`, `web`, `vscode` and `execute` sets is missing, and the `web` set doesn't appear in the tool picker. Copilot tools in `edit` and `search` reach the model.

## Cause

When core registers a contributed tool set, it looks up its member tools. If some were found, the set was created and later members were added as they registered. If none were found, the set was skipped and never recovered.

Tool lookup goes through `isPermitted`, which depends on `chat.agent.enabled`, so members can be unresolvable while the window starts up. `edit` and `search` each contain an always-permitted core tool (`rename`, `usages`), so they survived. The other sets had no such tool and were lost. I couldn't confirm why the timing is different on web; a late-arriving account policy or remote extension host are the likely candidates.

pull_requests.title: sessions: Open cloud sandbox sessions without waking the environment
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

Opening a cloud sandbox session in the Agents Window dialed the sandbox before anything rendered. A dormant environment sat behind a Mission Control compute resume on every click, and when the resume failed (deleted environment) the open rejected outright, so the persisted-history fallback from #329292 was unreachable.

The cause is #334863: it added an on-demand connect to the shared `RemoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.prepareSessionForOpen`, and `SessionsService` awaits that hook on open and runs it on restore. The sandbox provider inherited it, so every open became a wake.

A second gap sat behind that one. After the user presses **Connect** in the banner, the chat on screen stayed bound to the read-only history stand-in: the content provider was replaced under the same session type, but nothing reloaded the chat. The composer reappeared while the model's `isReadOnly` stayed `true`, so sends were silently rejected until the session was re-opened.

## Changes

- **`CloudSandboxSessionsProvider`** opts out of `prepareSessionForOpen`. Opening or restoring a sandbox session never dials it; `CloudSandboxSessionContribution` activation reads the environment's state and connects only to an online environment, otherwise serving Mission Control history read-only with the connection banner offering the connect action. Waking a dormant environment is always a user action (no auto-wake).
- **Agents Window `ChatView`** reloads a bound chat when its session type's content provider is unregistered and then registered again. It saves view state, releases the model, waits for the model store to actually dispose it (bounded by `REPLACED_PROVIDER_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS`), then runs the normal load. A newer load supersedes a pending reload; a provider that merely goes away leaves the transcript on screen. The same path recovers a remote host that reconnected with a new client id.
- Specs: one paragraph each in `REMOTE_AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md` (open never wakes) and `SESSIONS.md` (chat view ↔ provider replacement contract).
- **History replay (`taskEventReplay.ts`)** renders the right chat for a dormant single-chat session. A chat created together with its session is announced only in the subscribe snapshot, which Mission Control never mirrors; its later `session/chatUpdated` / `chatsReordered` frames do reach the mirror, but the reducer drops updates for a chat it never saw added, so replay counted them as an "explicitly emptied catalogue" (#339605's guard) and fell back to an empty legacy `<session>/chat` placeholder. The transcript came back with 0 items and the group view showed the centered "Environment Offline" state instead of the banner. Such a mention is now evidence the host has the chat. Peer chats — a tool-spawned subagent, a fork, or a side chat — *are* announced with `chatAdded` and carry an `origin.chat` naming the chat they came from, so they are set aside and the one remaining recorded chat is replayed; a removal, or a user chat advertised or named beside the candidate, still leaves the choice ambiguous. All of #339605/#339615's cases still hold.
- **`ChatView` reload arming** also covers a load still in flight: the banner is clickable while history loads, so the stand-in can be unregistered before the model is bound.
- **Protocol client watchdog during the initial handshake (`agentHostProtocolClient.ts`).** Observed live: a sandbox relay came up and acknowledged publishes while the host behind it never answered `initialize`; the client sat at "Connecting…" for minutes. The liveness watchdog was only armed *after* a successful handshake, and relay acks are deliberately not counted as host data, so nothing could time the handshake out until the 10-minute connection ceiling. The watchdog is now armed once the client transport is up (as `_attemptReconnect` already does), and its ping bypasses the pre-initialize outbox so it actually probes the wire. A silent handshake fails after the liveness window and takes the existing fresh-initialize retry path, bounded by the reconnect policy, so the banner comes back with **Retry** instead of spinning.

## How to test

1. Enable cloud sandboxes in the Agents Window and open a sandbox session whose environment is offline.
   - Expected: the transcript renders immediately from history, read-only, with the **"Environment offline." [Connect]** banner, and the log reads `[CloudSandboxReadOnly] Opened … with N history item(s)` for N > 0. No `/connect` request is issued (check the Agent Host / Cloud Sandbox log).
2. Press **Connect**.
   - Expected: "Connecting…" banner while the transcript stays visible; once the connection lands the chat reloads briefly at the same scroll position, the banner clears, and a message can be sent to the live sandbox.
3. If the connect fails, the read-only transcript stays and the banner offers **Retry**.
4. Reload the window with that session active: the environment is not woken on restore.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatGroupsView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts` — 744 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing
- New tests: `CloudSandboxSessionsProvider opening` (fails without the override: 2 dials; passes with it: 0) and three `ChatView` provider-replacement tests (reload after release without double-clear, newer load supersedes, timeout fallback)
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/taskEventReplay.test.ts` — 42 passing; the new snapshot-born-chat and peer-aside tests fail against the previous rules
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts` — 197 passing, including `watchdog fails a silent initial handshake instead of waiting on it indefinitely`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/remoteAgentHostService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.test.ts` — 167 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- `npx eslint` on the changed TypeScript files — clean
- Not run: manual end-to-end against a live sandbox.

## Notes for reviewers

- The post-Connect reload is one brief transcript re-render, coinciding with the banner clearing. Rebinding the same `ChatModel` to the new provided session would avoid it but means making `ChatServiceImpl.loadRemoteSession`'s wiring re-runnable for every contributed session type; deliberately out of scope here.
- The Editor window has the same stale-model gap after Connect; this PR only addresses the Agents Window flow.

pull_requests.title: Fix send button overflow in chat input toolbar for narrow widths
Fix UTF-8 encoding of MCP resource URI template values
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339843

Non-ASCII MCP resource-template values currently produce percent-encoded UTF-16 code units: `café` becomes `caf%E9`, and an emoji becomes two surrogate escapes. Encode valid Unicode strings as UTF-8 while retaining the existing ASCII punctuation escaping. Count prefix lengths by Unicode code point so a supplementary character remains intact. This follows [RFC 6570 §3.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6570.html#section-3.2.1).

The two added tests cover accented/CJK/supplementary characters, punctuation, and supplementary-character prefixes; all 26 existing tests, including control-character zero-padding, remain unchanged.

Validation:
- Actual-source targeted transpilation followed by `node test/unit/node/index.js --run src/vs/base/test/common/uriTemplate.test.ts`: 29 passing (28 URI-template tests plus the runner's error check); the two additions fail before the fix. Node 24.19.0 on Linux.
- Repository ESLint on both changed files and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Independent actual-source checks: 192 Unicode cases pass; 3,120 ASCII scalar and 32 string-composite controls remain unchanged.

No Electron/UI or live MCP-server test was run. Malformed lone-surrogate inputs now throw `URIError`, as reserved expansion already does; the encoder also string-coerces non-string array elements. Existing reserved-percent and composite-operator behavior is otherwise outside this fix.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and an independent review.

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #326538

## Problem

The Manage Models (Language Models) editor can show several groups that are all labelled **Copilot**. Copilot models come from:

- the regular Copilot provider (`copilot`)
- the Copilot CLI extension (`copilotcli`)
- each agent host harness. The Copilot CLI agent host groups its models under `copilotcli`; the Claude and Codex agent hosts group theirs under `copilot`, reaching them through the Copilot subscription (Claude via its `copilot` transport, Codex via `vscode-proxy`).

Each of these lists only works in its own harness, but they all appear together with the same label.

## Change

Manage Models now scopes the "Copilot" lists to the harness it was opened for:

- If the harness publishes its own Copilot models (models with `targetChatSessionType` equal to the harness), only that list is shown.
- Otherwise, only the regular Copilot models are shown.
- Models from other providers (BYOK, Ollama, OpenRouter, a harness's non-Copilot groups, …) are unaffected.

How the editor learns the harness:

- The model picker's **Manage Models...** action passes the harness it picks models for: `ChatInputPart.modelTargetSessionType` in the chat input, or the current model's target in the Agents window picker.
- Other entry points (Command Palette, account menu, notifications) fall back to the last focused chat's harness, then to the active customization harness.

Scope is limited to the Manage Models editor. The Chat Customizations editor's Models section and the model picker contents are unchanged.

## How to test

1. Make sure Copilot models from more than one harness are registered (e.g. local, Copilot CLI agent host, Claude/Codex agent hosts).
2. In a chat, select the **Local** harness, open the model picker and choose **Manage Models...**. Only the regular **Copilot** group is listed; other providers are unchanged.
3. Switch the chat to the **Copilot CLI** agent host harness and open **Manage Models...** again. Only the agent host's Copilot group is listed.
4. Repeat with the **Claude** and **Codex** agent host harnesses. Each shows only its own Copilot group.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "ChatModelsViewModel|ChatModelsWidget|modelPicker|ModelPicker|ChatInputPart"`: passed, 372 tests, including a new `ChatModelsViewModel` test covering all four Copilot sources plus a non-Copilot harness group.

pull_requests.title: nes: latch quota-triggered Copilot token refreshes
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #331579

Repeated NES quota errors can leave the legacy quota flags unchanged, causing the client to reset and mint a Copilot token on every failed request.

- Latch quota-triggered refreshes per account, endpoint, and model across completions and HTTP/WebSocket chat. Preserve known-exhausted guards and coalesce concurrent refreshes.
- Keep the latch across token rotations and elapsed time. A newer successful request rearms its scope; a five-minute backstop bounds failed refreshes and rapid recovery/failure cycles.
- Track request ordering so an older success cannot discard a newer quota failure or rearm its latch. Use GitHub account/issuer identity, snapshot static-session IDs separately.
- Stop successful requests from invalidating tokens based on unrelated legacy quota flags. Make the explicit `github.copilot.refreshToken` command force renewal so plan upgrades still refresh cached entitlement metadata.
- Add regression tests and forward the request context through the simulation fetcher.

The initial SDK compilation error is resolved without casts or narrowed production types.

No E2E assertions, gates, fixtures, prompt baselines, or AHP baselines were changed.

- `git diff --check` and commit hygiene — passed.

[GitHub Code OSS run 37341675492](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37341675492) passed on commit `d4bb3c96cbc`, including Windows/Linux/macOS Electron smoke and integration jobs.

pull_requests.title: Updated MCP
pull_requests.body:
## Description

Fixes an issue where MCP migration items in the **Agent Customizations → Migrations** dashboard could only be selected by clicking directly on the checkbox.

Previously, clicking elsewhere on a migration item row provided hover/focus feedback but did not select the item. The selection count remained at `0` and the **Migrate** button stayed disabled.

### Root Cause

The migration tree is configured with:

```ts
openOnSingleClick: true
```

As a result, every single click on a tree item triggered `onDidOpen`.

The `onDidOpen` handler unconditionally called `openMigrationItem()`, which opened the migration item's details instead of toggling its selection state.

The checkbox itself handled selection correctly because it stopped event propagation, which made selection work only when clicking directly on the checkbox.

### Fix

Updated the `tree.onDidOpen` handler in `customizationMigrationDashboard.ts` to distinguish between single-click selection and item activation.

For a normal single click:

- Toggle the migration item's selected state.
- Update the checkbox.
- Update the group selection count.
- Enable/disable the **Migrate** button accordingly.

For double-click, keyboard activation, or items requiring manual review:

- Preserve the existing behavior of opening the migration item details.

The distinction is made using `event.editorOptions` and `event.sideBySide`.

### Result

Migration items can now be selected by clicking anywhere on the row, making the selection behavior consistent with the expected tree interaction.

Double-clicking or using keyboard activation continues to open the item details, and items requiring manual review continue to open their details on single click.

## Testing

Tested the Agent Customizations → Migrations dashboard by:

1. Opening the migration dashboard with migration items available.
2. Clicking different areas of a migration item row.
3. Verifying that a single click toggles the checkbox.
4. Verifying that the selected item count updates correctly.
5. Verifying that the **Migrate** button reflects the selection state.
6. Verifying that clicking the checkbox directly still works.
7. Verifying that double-clicking opens the migration item details.
8. Verifying that keyboard activation continues to open the details.
9. Verifying that items with `manualReviewReason` continue to open their details as expected.

## Related Issue

Fixes  #339177

pull_requests.title: agentHost: forward tool-result images to BYOK models
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339595
Fixes #339439

## Problem

In agent-host sessions, a BYOK (OpenAI-compatible) model never received images returned by tools such as `view`. It only received the text receipt `Viewed image file successfully.`

## Root cause

There were two problems:

1. **Vision capability never reached the runtime.** `synthesizeByokSessionConfig` registered BYOK models with token limits only. The renderer already reports `supportsVision`, but it wasn't passed on, so the Copilot runtime treated every BYOK model as text-only. It replaced tool-result images with the text receipt before the request reached the BYOK proxy. I confirmed this by running the SDK runtime against a stub `/responses` server. Without the capability, `function_call_output.output` is the plain string. With `capabilities.supports.vision: true`, it's an `[input_text, input_image]` array.
2. **The BYOK LM bridge had no image channel for tool outputs.** Once vision is declared, the array output was passed through untyped, and the renderer wrapped it in a text part.

## Changes

- `copilotSessionLauncher.ts`: forward `supportsVision` as `capabilities.supports.vision` on each BYOK `ProviderModelConfig`.
- `agentHostByokLm.ts`: add an optional `images` field to the two tool-output bridge items. `output` stays text, so a renderer that doesn't know the new field still gets today's text result.
- `byokResponsesTranslation.ts`: split array tool outputs into text plus images, reusing the existing data-URL and MIME validation from user messages.
- `agentHostByokLmHandler.ts`: forward the images as `data` parts inside the LM API `tool_result`, the same shape the in-extension path produces.

## How to test

1. Turn on `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`.
2. Add an OpenAI-compatible BYOK model that supports images (e.g. `gpt-4o`), with `"vision": true` and `"toolCalling": true`.
3. Put an image containing text the model can't guess (e.g. `ZEBRA-7341`) in the workspace.
4. In an agent-host session with that model, ask: *"Use the view tool to open probe.png and tell me exactly what text it contains. If you didn't receive image pixels, say so."*
   - Before this change: the model says it only got "Viewed image file successfully."
   - After this change: the model reads the text.
5. With `"vision": false`, the model should still get the text receipt and the turn should finish cleanly.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokLmProxyService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostByokLmHandler.test.ts`: passed, 145 tests.
- New tests use the exact payload captured from the runtime, plus a renderer `tool_result` mapping test. The launcher snapshot test now covers `supportsVision`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: reports 20 errors, the same 20 as without this change. They come from the locally installed `@github/copilot-sdk` (1.0.16) being older than the version pinned in `package.json`. None are in files this PR touches.

pull_requests.title: fix: guard stale ghost text screen reader rendering (fixes #339819)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary While rendering ghost text (inline completions) for the screen reader, `GhostText.renderForScreenReader` builds a `TextEdit` whose replacement positions are taken from the cached ghost-text part columns. When the current editor line has become shorter than the cached ghost text expects (the document was edited during the deliberate `timeout(50)` + `waitForState` delay before the delayed screen-reader announcement), the line-capping step is a no-op and a replacement lands past the end of the capped text. `TextEdit.apply` then calls `rangeFromPositions(lastEditEnd, endPositionExclusive)` with `start > end`, which throws `BugIndicatingError: start must be before end`. Impact: an unhandled error is logged (921 users on stable 1.140.0) and the screen-reader announcement is lost; it does not crash the editor. Fixes microsoft/vscode#339819 Recommended reviewer: ``@hediet`` ### Culprit Commit Not identified — pre-existing. The `renderForScreenReader` capping logic (`cappedLineText = lineText.substr(0, lastPart.column - 1)`) dates back to the original ghost-text implementation (`7ec64f0dad5d`, 2021) and the `TextEdit`-based rendering (`a9cd99e83e03`, 2024); neither assumes `lineText` may be shorter than the cached part column. The issue itself records a prior occurrence (microsoft/vscode#287069) tracked since 1.97-era builds and anomaly hits in multiple releases, so this is a long-standing latent race re-bucketed for stable 1.140.0, not a new regression from a specific commit. | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — pre-existing | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | Capping logic never handled the case where the live line is shorter than the cached ghost-text columns; surfaced as a new stable bucket, not introduced by a recent change. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ctrl as inlineCompletionsController participant GT as GhostText.renderForScreenReader participant TE as TextEdit.apply participant RFP as rangeFromPositions Ctrl->>Ctrl: timeout(50) + waitForState (document may change) Note over Ctrl: Cached ghost text now stale
vs. current (shorter) line Ctrl->>GT: renderForScreenReader(lineText) Note over GT: ⚠️ Root cause:
substr cannot lengthen lineText;
lastPart.column-1 > lineText.length GT->>TE: applyToString(cappedLineText) TE->>RFP: rangeFromPositions(lastEditEnd, endPositionExclusive) Note over RFP: 💥 start > end
throws "start must be before end" ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/common/core/edits/textEdit.ts` | crash site | L781 (from stack): `throw new BugIndicatingError('start must be before end')` | | `src/vs/editor/common/core/edits/textEdit.ts` | throw path | L145-L146: `const r = rangeFromPositions(lastEditEnd, text.endPositionExclusive)` in `apply()` — `lastEditEnd` can be past `endPositionExclusive` when a replacement sits beyond the capped text | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/model/ghostText.ts` | root cause | L48: `const cappedLineText = lineText.substr(0, lastPart.column - 1)` — `substr` cannot lengthen a too-short line, leaving replacement columns out of range | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/controller/inlineCompletionsController.ts` | trigger | L331-L342: `await timeout(50, ...); await waitForState(...); ... renderForScreenReader(lineText)` — the delay is where the cached ghost text goes stale relative to the live line | ### Repro Steps This is a timing-dependent race between a pending delayed screen-reader announcement and a document edit, so it is non-deterministic. To increase likelihood: 1. Enable a screen reader (or `editor.accessibilitySupport: "on"`) and `editor.screenReaderAnnounceInlineSuggestion`. 2. Trigger an inline completion (ghost text) whose part column is near the end of a line. 3. Within the ~50ms announcement delay (`timeout(50)` + `waitForState` in `inlineCompletionsController`), delete characters on that line / replace the line with a shorter one (e.g. fast backspacing or an external edit) so the live line becomes shorter than the cached ghost-text column. 4. The delayed `renderForScreenReader` runs against the now-shorter line; the capped line is shorter than the last part's column and `TextEdit.apply` throws `start must be before end`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/model/ghostText.ts` → `renderForScreenReader()`: add a guard immediately after computing `lastPart`, before the capping/`TextEdit` construction. When `lastPart.column - 1 > lineText.length`, the cached ghost text is stale relative to the current line (it references columns that no longer exist), so the method returns `''` — the same benign empty-announcement result it already returns when there are no parts. This places the guard at the data producer of the invalid range (the stale snapshot), before the throwing code path is reached, rather than at the crash site in `textEdit.ts`. It does not add a `try/catch`, does not touch `TextEdit.apply`'s invariant (`rangeFromPositions` must keep throwing for genuinely inconsistent edits), and removes no `logService.error`/telemetry. The guard is correct because `GhostText`'s constructor asserts parts are ordered by non-decreasing column (`checkAdjacentItems(parts, (p1, p2) => p1.column <= p2.column)`), so `lastPart` holds the maximum column; if even that column fits within `lineText`, every replacement position is in range and `apply` cannot produce an inverted range. After this change, a stale ghost text can no longer reach `TextEdit.apply` with an out-of-range replacement, so `textEdit.ts:145`/`:781` cannot be driven to throw `start must be before end` from this call site. **Alternatives considered**: - Clamp each part's column to `lineText.length` inside `renderForScreenReader` — rejected: silently relocating the suggestion text produces a misleading screen-reader announcement, and the underlying snapshot is still stale; skipping is the honest result. - Wrap `applyToString` in `try/catch` — rejected: hides the `BugIndicatingError` from the telemetry pipeline and would also swallow genuinely inconsistent edits, masking real bugs instead of fixing the stale-data producer. - Guard inside `textEdit.ts` / `rangeFromPositions` — rejected: that is the crash site and a shared invariant relied on by many callers; weakening it would hide inverted-range bugs across the whole editor. ### Recommended Owner ``@hediet`` — area owner for inline completions (`editor/contrib/inlineCompletions`) and the `editor/common/core/edits` `TextEdit` data structures (authored the `TextEdit`-based ghost-text rendering and the `rangeFromPositions` invariant). Active in `microsoft/vscode` within the last 90 days.

pull_requests.title: fix: clamp stale inline-edit range in maxContentWidthInRange (fixes #339818)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary The editor throws `BugIndicatingError: Illegal value for lineNumber` from `TextModel.getLineMaxColumn` while measuring line widths for an inline-edit (NES) preview. During a synchronous `undo` the model shrinks, and the inline-edit width `derived` recomputes (it reads `editorObs.versionId`) while the edit's cached `displayRange` / `originalDisplayRange` still references the pre-undo line count. The shared helper `maxContentWidthInRange` then iterates those now-out-of-bounds line numbers against the current (shorter) model, hitting the line-count guard in `getLineMaxColumn`. Impact: a visible unhandled error affecting ~1,000 stable users on 1.140.0 whenever an inline edit is showing as the buffer shrinks underneath it. Fixes microsoft/vscode#339818 Recommended reviewer: ``@hediet`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not identified — pre-existing stale-range pattern | | Author | — | | PR | — | | Message | — | | Why | — | > No single regression commit was confirmed. The `maxContentWidthInRange` loop that dereferences stale line numbers dates to `f2c7116f8e19` (Feb 2025) and the `getWidthOfLine` call on line 42 to `461887743ad0` (Jan 2026); both predate the 1.140.0 window and pass the ancestry check against the shipped commit `07f806f9`. The bucket surfaced as a *new* stable anomaly in 1.140.0, but the throwing code path is pre-existing — the spike most plausibly reflects increased NES/inline-edit exposure rather than a change to this loop. Per the re-bucketing / pre-existing guidance, no speculative culprit is named; the owner is taken from the feature area. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Undo as TextModel undo participant Model as TextModel (content change) participant Derived as inlineEditsSideBySideView
_editorMaxContentWidthInRange participant Util as maxContentWidthInRange participant Crash as TextModel.getLineMaxColumn Undo->>Model: _applyUndo shrinks buffer Note over Model: line count decreases;
versionId increments Model->>Derived: synchronous layout cascade
recompute (reads versionId) Note over Derived: ⚠️ Root cause:
cached originalDisplayRange
still has pre-undo lines Derived->>Util: maxContentWidthInRange(editor, staleRange) Util->>Crash: getWidthOfLine(i) for out-of-bounds i Note over Crash: 💥 Illegal value for lineNumber ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts` | crash site | L900 (from stack): `throw new BugIndicatingError('Illegal value for lineNumber')` when `lineNumber > getLineCount()` | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/utils/utils.ts` | root cause | L41-L44: `for (let i = range.startLineNumber; i < range.endLineNumberExclusive; i++) { editor.getWidthOfLine(i, reader); }` iterates a range not reconciled with the current model | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/inlineEditsViews/inlineEditsSideBySideView.ts` | producer | L220-L227: `derived` keyed on `versionId` recomputes `maxContentWidthInRange(this._editorObs, originalDisplayRange, reader)` with the stale edit range after the model shrank | | `src/vs/editor/browser/observableCodeEditor.ts` | pass-through | L534-L539: `getWidthOfLine` forwards `lineNumber` to `editor.getWidthOfLine` | ### Repro Steps Non-deterministic timing-dependent race. To increase likelihood: 1. Enable inline suggestions / next-edit-suggestions (NES). 2. In a non-`file` scheme document (e.g. an untitled or notebook cell editor), trigger an inline edit preview whose `displayRange` extends to near the end of the buffer. 3. While the side-by-side inline-edit preview is visible, perform an `undo` (or any edit) that removes lines so the model becomes shorter than the preview's `displayRange`. 4. The synchronous content-change → layout cascade recomputes the width derived against the stale range, iterating a line number beyond the new line count and throwing `Illegal value for lineNumber`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/utils/utils.ts` → `maxContentWidthInRange()`: before iterating, clamp the incoming `range` to the current model's line count (`model.getLineCount()`), reading the authoritative line count in the same atomic section that already reads the model. The loop and the subsequent `mapToLineArray(l => model.getLineContent(l))` now use the clamped range, so no line number outside `[1, lineCount]` is ever passed to `getWidthOfLine` / `getLineContent`. This is the stale-cached-identifier lifecycle pattern: the consumer holds a range captured against an older model version and re-reads it after the producer (the undo-driven content change) shrank the model. The sanctioned fix for that pattern is to re-resolve the stale reference against authoritative state in the same read section, which is exactly what this utility — the single reconciliation point every inline-edit width call site routes through — is positioned to do. It fixes where the range meets the model, not at the crash site: `getLineMaxColumn`'s guard is left intact so it keeps feeding the telemetry pipeline for genuinely illegal callers, and no `logService.error`/throw is removed or wrapped in try/catch. After this change, `utils.ts:41` cannot pass an out-of-bounds line number to `getWidthOfLine` because every iterated value is bounded by `model.getLineCount()` read immediately above the loop. **Alternatives considered**: - Guarding at the crash site in `getLineMaxColumn` (e.g. returning a fallback instead of throwing) — rejected: it masks the real bug for every caller and removes a legitimate invariant check that feeds error telemetry. - Fixing each producer (`inlineEditsSideBySideView`, `inlineEditsDeletionView`, `inlineEditsCustomView`, `longDistancePreviewEditor`) to re-clamp its edit range before calling the utility — rejected: six-plus call sites all funnel the same edit-derived ranges through this one helper, so reconciling once at the shared reconciliation point is both minimal and complete; duplicating the clamp at every caller would be error-prone and easy to miss on future call sites. ### Recommended Owner ``@hediet`` — Henning Dieterichs owns the inline-edits / NES rendering area, authored `maxContentWidthInRange` (`f2c7116f8e19`) and the side-by-side view that produces the stale range, and is highly active in `microsoft/vscode` (148 commits in the last 90 days).

pull_requests.body:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

Release branch counterpart of #339820.

Enables the New Session View V2 onboarding tour by default for Insiders builds using the `workspaceAndModel` variant.

Non-Insiders builds retain the existing ExP gate and variation treatment. Developer-mode variation overrides continue to take precedence in every product quality.
