pull_requests.title: Agent Host: save requested files to the working directory by default
pull_requests.body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336442

- Add `chat.agentHost.copilot.requestedFileLocation`, an experimental application setting with two values: `workingDirectory` (default) and `sessionWorkspace`. It's mirrored to the Agent Host root config.
- Pass the setting to the Copilot SDK as the `requestedFileLocation` session option when the Agent Host creates or resumes a session. Unknown values fall back to `workingDirectory`.
- With `workingDirectory`, a file the user asks for without naming a path lands in the session's working directory (the open folder or worktree) and shows up in Changes, instead of in the session's storage folder. With `sessionWorkspace`, it goes to the session's `files/` folder.
- A path the user names always wins, and plan mode keeps its own rules.
- Depends on an SDK release with the new option (companion runtime/SDK PR: github/copilot-agent-runtime#24558) plus the matching `@github/copilot-sdk` bump. Against the pinned SDK 1.0.16, typecheck fails on the new `requestedFileLocation` property, so this stays a draft until the bump lands.

How to test (with an SDK that includes the companion change, or with `chat.agentHost.copilot.runtimePath` pointing at a runtime built from it):

1. Open a folder in the Agents window and start a Copilot session.
2. Ask for an analysis of a file, then send "Write the analysis into a markdown file."
3. With the default setting, the file appears in the folder and in Changes.
4. Set the setting to `sessionWorkspace` and repeat in a new session. The file is written to the session's `files/` folder and linked in the reply. A follow-up that names a path, such as `docs/analysis.md`, writes to the folder.

Validation:

- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`: 82 passing, including the new requested-file-location suite. It covers the default, `sessionWorkspace`, and invalid values on both create and resume.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passes against the SDK built from the companion PR; fails with 3 errors, all on the new property, against the published 1.0.16.
- ESLint on the changed files: passed.
- UI scenario on a dev build with the companion runtime: both runs passed.
  - Default setting: `greeting-analysis.md` was written to the folder, and the session's `files/` stayed empty.
  - `sessionWorkspace`: the file was written to `files/` and the folder was untouched. A follow-up naming `docs/greeting-analysis.md` wrote to the folder.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The default constant and `normalizeRequestedFileLocation` fallback follow [`DEFAULT_COPILOT_SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET` / `normalizeSkillCharBudget`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0fc14ed89479e0742c57d89590060f0e99ec3826/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/copilotCliConfig.ts#L91-L96).
- The setting registration and its declarative `agentHost: { key }` sync follow [`CopilotSkillCharBudgetSettingId`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0fc14ed89479e0742c57d89590060f0e99ec3826/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts#L1747-L1760). This setting uses the default sync scope because it's a behavior preference, not a local runtime knob.
- Reading the value from the Agent Host root config in `_buildSessionConfig` follows the existing [`getRootValue(copilotCliConfigSchema, …)` reads](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0fc14ed89479e0742c57d89590060f0e99ec3826/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts#L999). The option sits next to [`workingDirectory`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0fc14ed89479e0742c57d89590060f0e99ec3826/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts#L1133), so create, resume, and ephemeral sessions all get it.
- The test suite is modeled on the [`CopilotSessionLauncher canvas config`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0fc14ed89479e0742c57d89590060f0e99ec3826/src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts#L1044-L1121) suite.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: cap BYOK tools at 128 and warn when tools are dropped
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

BYOK turns in Copilot harness (Agent Host / Copilot SDK) sessions fail when more than 128 tools are enabled. OpenAI-compatible providers reject the request.

- **Every tool is forwarded.** Runtime tool search is never enabled for BYOK models. The launcher checks bare model ids (`claude-*`, `gpt-5-4`), but BYOK selections are vendor-qualified (`anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`).
- **Turning tool search on isn't a fix.** In a probe against the bundled runtime, Claude and custom models still sent every tool. gpt-5.4+ sent a native `{ type: 'tool_search' }` tool, which the BYOK proxy rejects (`Unsupported tools[0] type 'tool_search'`).
- **Neither does generic tool search yet.** The runtime has an undocumented `GENERIC_CLIENT_TOOL_SEARCH` flag. In the probe it only added a `generic_tool_search` tool and deferred nothing, so it doesn't help BYOK yet.
- **The local harness avoids this** with virtual `activate_*` tool groups. The Copilot harness has no equivalent.

## Change

- **Cap in the BYOK proxy** (`byokLmProxyService.ts`, `byokResponsesTranslation.ts`):
  - Requests are trimmed to 128 tools.
  - Tools the conversation already called are kept first, so their calls stay valid. The remaining slots follow the runtime's order, which lists built-ins first.
  - Kept tools stay in their original order, so the request looks the same from turn to turn.
  - The request is still sent. The run is never blocked.
  - The Agent Host log gets a warning with the counts. Names of dropped tools go to the trace log.
- **Warning in the chat:**
  - The proxy fires `onDidCapTools` with the session id from the bearer token. `CopilotAgent` sends it to that session.
  - The session adds a `SystemNotification` to the active turn, with a new `ByokToolLimitExceeded` kind and warning severity.
  - It's shown once per dropped-tool count, so it doesn't repeat every model call.
  - Text: "The model only supports 128 tools, 114 tools were not provided to the model."
- **Configure Tools link:** the workbench adapter appends a link that opens Chat Customizations on the Tools section.
  - Only that one command is allowed to run from this message.
  - Markdown in the host's text is escaped, so the host can't inject a command link.
  - The host sends plain text, so clients that don't know the new kind still show readable text.
- **The BYOK warning stays visible:** `IChatWarningMessage` gets an opt-in `keepVisibleWhenCollapsed` flag. The completed-response disclosure keeps flagged warnings out of "Completed N steps", and only the BYOK warning sets it. All other warnings collapse as before.
- **Host text can't inject command links:** angle brackets are escaped too, so `<command:…>` autolinks and raw `<a href>` in the host text stay plain text.
- **Accessible View:** `getChatResponsePlaintextParts` now includes `warning` parts as "Warning: {text}", with links shown as their labels. This applies to every warning, so they also show up in transcript Find.

## Notes for reviewers

- This is a stopgap that keeps BYOK runs working. The proper fix is runtime tool search for custom providers. That needs SDK work: the generic flag adds a search tool but defers nothing today.
- `IByokLmProxyService` gains `onDidCapTools`. `CopilotAgent` gains an `IByokLmProxyService` constructor dependency, and the test subclasses are updated for it.

## Testing

Unit tests added/updated:
- `capBridgeTools`: under the limit, trimming the end of the list, keeping already-called tools, and the default limit.
- Proxy: a 200-tool request succeeds, the model gets 128 tools, and one event fires with the right session id.
- Session: warning content and metadata, dedup by dropped count, no warning without an active turn.
- Agent: cap events go only to the matching session.
- Adapter: renders as a warning with the trusted Configure Tools link and escapes host markdown.
- Renderer: a flagged warning stays outside the collapsed steps and isn't counted, while an unflagged warning is still collapsed. This test fails without the fix.
- Adapter: host autolinks and HTML stay plain text, and the rendered warning's only link is Configure Tools. This test fails without the fix.
- Accessible View: warnings and their link text are included.

Commands run:
- `./scripts/test.sh src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokLmProxyService.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`: passed (106)
- `./scripts/test.sh src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts …`: passed (791, with the proxy and translation suites)
- `./scripts/test.sh src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts`: passed (188)
- `./scripts/test.sh src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts`: passed (610)
- `./scripts/test.sh src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`: the new test passes. 12 tests fail, the same 12 that fail on a clean `main` checkout (external chat discovery, state-file resolution, `collectDebugLogs`).
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in changed files. The remaining errors come from the local environment (missing electron types, and an installed SDK that's older than the bump).

Manual check: in a BYOK session with 242 tools, the turn completes, the warning stays visible above "Completed 2 steps", and the link opens Customizations → Tools.

pull_requests.body:

Refs #337478. **Part 1 of a planned PR stack implementing GitHub cloud automations**, rebuilt in small, independently reviewable slices from main. This PR targets main; subsequent PRs will layer discovery/provider integration and UI on top. It does not close or replace #337478 by itself.

### Scope
- Extend the Sessions GitHub API client with Copilot-gateway requests, stable account/session identity and provider/endpoint pinning, timeout/content-type options, pagination and Retry-After metadata, and structured API errors.
- Add the cloud automation API client: repository eligibility, list/detail, create/update/delete, dispatch, recent history, exact-task lookup and abort. Missing detail requests use bounded concurrency (five) and preserve list order.
- Distinguish definite pre-dispatch failures from uncertain mutation outcomes after request-service handoff.
- Add a shared request option to disable browser-to-remote fallback, enabled for Copilot mutations to prevent replay. Existing callers retain the default behavior.
- Add focused transport/client regression tests. Seven files; no provider registration, UI, polling, experiment gate, or automatic cloud requests.

### Review notes
- Requests currently use `https://api.githubcopilot.com/agents/...`, inherited from the full implementation. Earlier authenticated reads succeeded. Tim's API skill documents `https://api.github.com/cmc_internal/api/agents/...`; supported gateway parity and per-route integration-header requirements still need confirmation. The renderer CORS rationale comes from related task APIs, not a completed comparison of both automation routes.
- The three initial CCR findings (remote mutation replay, display-label credential matching, sequential missing-detail requests) are addressed in 4f1ba1a734b with regression tests.
- The browser request-service fixture is suite-scoped to isolate a pre-existing LogService/MultiplexLogger constructor lifecycle issue. Per-test request-path leak checks remain enabled; no logging implementation changes are included.

### Validation
Run from the repository root with Node 24.18.0:
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.

pull_requests.title: Extension host: use native source maps in development hosts
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Related to #145473 and #238469. This is a **local extension-development host** first step, not a claim to resolve the broader request for source-mapped crash reports from shipped extensions.

A bundled extension can ship a valid source map and still produce generated-file locations in its error stacks. There are two independent pieces to address:

1. Enable Node's native source-map support **before** importing the extension host and its extensions.
2. Keep the host's extension-attribution walk, but use the previously installed `Error.prepareStackTrace` formatter when native source maps are enabled. Building the stack from `CallSite.toString()` bypasses Node's mapped formatting.

This PR uses `module.setSourceMapsSupport(true)` and adds no dependency, `Module._load` interception, or extension API. The flag is set by `NativeLocalProcessExtensionHost` only for development hosts. With source maps disabled, the existing formatter and its tab indentation remain unchanged. Existing handling of formatters installed by extensions remains in place.

The formatter composition follows [Node's documented guidance](https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#--enable-source-maps) and the pattern used by [Babel](https://github.com/babel/babel/blob/main/packages/babel-core/src/errors/rewrite-stack-trace.ts). The captured hook is inferred, and the wrapper is contextually typed from `typeof Error.prepareStackTrace`, rather than asserting compatibility with a narrower call-site interface. Delegation preserves the `Error` receiver, and the native path skips unused fallback string rendering while retaining attribution.

## Before / after

The new isolated-process regression fixture has a real CommonJS module with an external source map. Paths below are shortened; this is a test fixture, not a screenshot from a fully launched editor.

Before (existing host formatter, even with native maps enabled):

```text
Error: source map probe
    at Object.createError (<fixture>/fixture.cjs:1:62)
```

After (native formatter preserved):

```text
Error: source map probe
    at Object.createError (<fixture>/fixture.ts:1:1)
```

The fixture deliberately uses a single mapping segment to make the expected source location deterministic. The test also verifies that the same error reaches `$onExtensionRuntimeError` and extension telemetry with the correct extension identifier and stack. It does not just assert a fabricated formatter string.

## Regression coverage

Nine new cases run in separate child processes because the host makes `Error.prepareStackTrace` non-configurable:

- Actual generated-to-source mapping using Node's formatter, with error and telemetry attribution preserved.
- Existing formatting and attribution with source maps disabled.
- Disabling source maps after handler installation.
- Custom formatters installed before and after the host handler, including their `Error` receiver.
- Zero fallback `toString()` calls when a formatter is selected, with attribution preserved.
- Bootstrap with the opt-in flag unset, `false`, and `true`.

I also ran the existing seven formatter-wrapping/re-wrapping tests for #184926.

To check the tests are sensitive to the change, I temporarily removed the proposed formatter delegation and bootstrap activation while retaining the original eight tests. Three cases failed: native mapping, the pre-installed formatter case, and bootstrap activation. Restoring the implementation made the suite pass.

For the review follow-up, I strengthened the custom-formatter cases to check the receiver and added an independently instrumented fallback-rendering case. Against the initial PR implementation, these exposed two failures: an incorrect receiver and one unnecessary fallback rendering call. Both pass after the revision.

## Local validation

Public `microsoft/vscode` source based on `1f6488722c942d1d7528a7d949769a69e4a557c3`, macOS arm64:

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- ESLint on all four changed files with `--max-warnings 0` — passed.
- Node 24.18.0: nine new cases and seven existing cases passed (the Node runner additionally reports its own unexpected-error checks).
- VS Code's pinned Electron 43.7.3 / embedded Node 24.21.0: nine new cases and seven existing cases passed via `scripts/test.sh`.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git-secrets` with AWS patterns on all four contribution files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Commands:

```sh
npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/node/extensionHostSourceMaps.test.ts
npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/common/extensionHostMain.test.ts
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/node/extensionHostSourceMaps.test.ts --grep 'Extension host native source maps'
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/common/extensionHostMain.test.ts --grep 'ExtensionHostMain#ErrorHandler'
```

The subprocess cases use Electron-as-Node when launched from the Electron test runner. A full UI/utility-process extension-host launch, Windows/Linux validation, and a representative startup/stack-formatting performance benchmark are **not yet completed**. Opening as a draft to make that validation scope explicit and discuss whether this is a useful first step.

## Scope and prior work

- This is an alternative native-runtime approach to #238469, not a continuation of that PR or a claim to its authorship.
- No new opt-in policy for release, remote, or web extension hosts is introduced. The shared handler respects native source-map support when it is already enabled, but only local development hosts are newly enabled by this PR.
- ESM `file:` URL error-attribution behavior is a separate concern and is intentionally not included.
- No internal repository files or patch files are included; this branch was prepared against public VS Code source.

Would the maintainers be open to this dev-host-only first step? Happy to adjust the scope based on guidance.

Prepared with AI assistance. The local automated checks are listed above; maintainer review is still required.

pull_requests.title: webview: Keep macOS Hide and Minimize shortcuts working in webviews
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #71800

## Problem

While a webview has focus, its window ignores native menu shortcuts (`setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(true)`). This prevents shortcuts from being handled twice, as in #82670 where Cmd+W closed both the editor and the window. Workbench keybindings still work because webview key events are forwarded to the keybinding service. On macOS, though, Hide (Cmd+H), Hide Others (Cmd+Alt+H) and Minimize (Cmd+M) are native-only menu items with no workbench command, so they did nothing while a webview had focus. This affects Markdown preview, release notes, the Markdown editor and extension webviews.

## Change

- `WebviewElement` now dispatches forwarded key events as cancelable, so it can tell whether the workbench handled them. Trusted key downs that nothing handled go to a new `handleUnhandledKeyDown` hook.
- On macOS, `ElectronWebviewElement` matches Cmd+H, Cmd+Alt+H and Cmd+M and calls a new `IWebviewManagerService.runMacOSMenuAction`. That method runs `Menu.sendActionToFirstResponder` with the same selectors Electron uses for the `hide`, `hideothers` and `minimize` menu roles. Only these three actions are accepted, and the method does nothing on other platforms.
- Workbench keybindings on these keys still take priority, as they do outside webviews. Menu shortcuts are still ignored while a webview is focused, so #82670 stays fixed.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Forwarded key events now set `defaultPrevented`** when a keybinding handles them. The only listener that checks this is the Alt-key mnemonics in the custom title bar (`menubar.ts`). An Alt+letter key press from a webview that runs a keybinding therefore no longer also opens a menu, which matches the text editor.
- **A webview's own `preventDefault()` is not forwarded.** A webview that handles Cmd+H or Cmd+M itself will also hide or minimize VS Code. Other forwarded shortcuts, such as Cmd+P, already behave this way.
- **Known gaps:**
  - The three shortcuts are hardcoded to match the defaults in `menubar.ts`.
  - Remapping Hide or Minimize in macOS System Settings > Keyboard > App Shortcuts isn't reflected inside webviews.
  - Other native-only menu shortcuts are still blocked while a webview has focus, such as App Shortcuts and Edit > Emoji & Symbols.
  - A more complete fix would decide key by key in the main process with `before-input-event`, letting through to the native menu every key the workbench doesn't own.
- **No extension API changes.** `vscode.d.ts`, the webview host page (`pre/index.html`) and the webview message protocol are unchanged.

## How to test (macOS)

1. Open a Markdown preview (or Help > Release Notes) and click inside it.
2. Press Cmd+H: VS Code hides. Press Cmd+M: the window minimizes. Press Cmd+Alt+H: other apps hide.
3. Bind Cmd+H to a command in `keybindings.json` and repeat step 2 inside the webview: the command runs and VS Code does not hide.
4. Press Cmd+W inside the webview: only the editor closes (#82670).
5. Press Cmd+P inside the webview: Quick Open opens.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/test/electron-browser/webviewElement.test.ts`: passed (5 passing). The new test fails when forwarded events are not cancelable.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npx eslint` on the changed files: passed.
- Pre-commit hygiene: passed.
- Not yet done: manual verification in a dev build on macOS (the steps above).

This is a standalone infrastructure change, separated from the accessibility fix in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339121. That PR's diff is back to the audio-error fix only.

## Evidence

The original PR failed twice with `[eslint] Killed` and `ERROR: "eslint" exited with 137`, while `core-ci` was bundling:

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36886697899/job/110455607266
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36886697899/job/110498856785

A bounded survey of 200 recent Code OSS runs on October 1 found the same signature on three other PRs:

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335978 - [failed job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36813221768/job/110212606489); still the latest failed Compile & Hygiene check when inspected.
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339105 - [failed job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36881600943/job/110434792012); subsequently passed and merged.
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339110 - [failed job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36884327836/job/110444324360); subsequently passed and merged.

These are SIGKILL/exit-137 observations, consistent with runner memory pressure. Kernel OOM diagnostics were not available, so this does not claim a proven kernel OOM cause or attribute unrelated CI failures to it.

## Impact

- No compiler settings, lint rules, target files, or validation gates change.
- ESLint remains mandatory and still checks the full repository.
- Lower overlapping resource demand, at the cost of losing lint/compile overlap.
- Applies to Code OSS pull-request builds; Azure Pipelines is unchanged.
- An equivalent scheduling canary [passed Compile & Hygiene](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36907047695/job/110520517941): 4m41s for parallel checks, then 2m09s for ESLint. These are observed step durations, not a measured before/after latency delta.

## Validation

- YAML assertions verify all seven other checks remain in the parallel group and full ESLint runs immediately afterward without conditional skipping or `continue-on-error`.
- All three existing ESLint-driver tests pass.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Precommit hygiene completes; it selects no files for this YAML-only change.
- [Exact-head Code OSS CI passes](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36924437179) on `bbe8269a1597633841e0cf6e0755ef14d5176977`, including all platform jobs. The Compile & Hygiene job ran parallel checks in 4m21s, then ESLint in 1m58s.
- All 34 completed PR checks pass; the separate VS Code PR Check approval gate is still pending.

pull_requests.title: chat: enable OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #338708. Supersedes #338709, retaining its OpenAI GPT-Live BYOK Voice Mode implementation and adding session, permission, transport, playback, and lifecycle hardening. Selectively incorporates compatible narration fixes from the already-closed #336640 rather than its older transport architecture.

## Summary

- Use the configured OpenAI provider credentials for WebRTC voice, with AI/preview-policy gating, credential invalidation, bounded connection attempts, and cancellation through the proposed speech API, RPC, provider request, response-body consumption, and ICE gathering.
- Bind speech to its originating chat input. Preserve ownership through welcome-composer preparation, draft replacement, and same-input session materialization; reject stale asynchronous completions.
- Route approvals and question answers deterministically to the exact session, request, pending occurrence, and schema. Accumulate multi-question forms and submit through normal validation. No additional reasoning-model request is introduced.
- Support regular workbench chat editor tabs and the sidebar as well as the Agents window. Use toolbar widget context or the focused input for keyboard invocation, and submit resident workbench input through its owning widget without depending on a rendered sidebar bridge.
- Fix speaking-state animation, transcript/delegation timing at final-fragment overlap, microphone mute/PTT synchronization, and autoplay-blocked remote audio using a disposable shared-WebAudio fallback.
- Distinguish request acceptance from coding completion. Request a brief, contextual acknowledgement from the existing voice model instead of repeatedly saying that it will report back.
- Update accessibility help and add focused regression coverage.

## When Voice Mode speaks

The following describes OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode in both Agents-window and regular editor-window chats. Model-generated acknowledgement examples are instructions, not guaranteed verbatim output.

| Event | Does voice speak? | What it says | Important guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Your coding request is accepted | Yes—a brief acknowledgement is requested from the voice model | Context-aware, e.g. “Okay, asking the agent to create that file.” | Only after successful submission. Acceptance does not mean execution or completion. Exact wording is model-generated. |
| An edited request is populated but not submitted | Yes—review/send guidance, not acceptance | “Your request was not sent. Please review the chat input and send it from there.” | The text remains in the input; populating an edit is not successful submission. |
| Session/worktree is being prepared | No automatic “done” announcement | No separate preparation acknowledgement | Setup and queuing must not be described as task completion. |
| Agent is working | Normally quiet; optional progress narration | Brief agent-provided progress updates when `agents.voice.agentProgress` is enabled | Only for the owning chat; superseded progress is cancelled. |
| Agent requires approval | Yes | Reads the current confirmation's available description | Must belong to the bound chat and current pending occurrence. |
| Agent asks a question | Yes | Reads the question and numbered choices | Uses the actual question schema, not invented choices or internal IDs. |
| You answer part of a multi-question form | Yes | Reads the next question and its choices | Answers accumulate; the form is submitted only when complete, or validly skipped. |
| Your approval, rejection, or completed form is successfully applied | Yes | “Your response was submitted.” | Acknowledgement follows confirmed application—not merely hearing your answer. |
| Consent or choice is ambiguous | Yes | Requests clarification, such as “Please say approve or reject…” or repeats the valid choices | Does not approve anything or turn that reply into a new coding request. |
| The pending prompt changed or became stale | Yes | Explains that the input/prompt changed and asks you to answer the current prompt | Never applies the captured answer to a replacement prompt. |
| Submission or prompt response fails | Yes | Explains that it could not be sent/applied and directs you to the chat input | No success acknowledgement. |
| Agent finishes its response | Yes | Narrates the completed response/summary | Separate from request acceptance; duplicate readings are suppressed. |
| Another chat needs approval or finishes | No, through this bound connection | Remains available visually in that chat | Background chats cannot borrow the active chat's voice connection. |
| You interrupt or deliberately hold push-to-talk | Current playback is stopped/suppressed | Listens to your new input instead | Passive hands-free listening can coexist with reply playback; deliberate held PTT cannot. |
| You switch the bound input or discard a recording | Voice Mode stops | Restart guidance is shown and announced through accessibility status | Restart in the intended input. Same-draft session creation preserves the connection. |
| Spoken responses are disabled | No audible output | — | `agents.voice.speakResponses: false` mutes remote playback. |

Accepted approval phrases: `approve`, `approved`, `accept`, `accepted`, `allow`, `yes`, `I approve`, and `I accept`. These must be complete, unqualified English replies. Tentative, qualified, negated, stale, and duplicate consent does not authorize anything. Rejection phrases remain `reject`, `deny`, and `no`.

Selection answers use exact displayed labels, numbers, number words, ordinals, or `option N`; opaque option values are not spoken identifiers. Multi-selection supports commas/`and`, custom answers require `other` when allowed, and skipping requires the form to permit it.

## Validation

### Initial publication

- `npm run compile` — passed earlier during the OSS launch/dependency repair; the subsequent publication build was stopped and is not counted as a successful final build.
- `npm run compile-client` — passed for the publication changes, with zero compilation errors.
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed, refreshing the JavaScript used by tests and the dev window.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --runGlob '**/chat/test/browser/voiceClient/*.test.js'` — passed with **283 tests**.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceBridge.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatVoiceTarget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/voiceClient/voiceLiveInputRouter.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/voiceClient/voiceQuestionAnswers.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/accessibility/chatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/test/browser/voiceModeActions.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/test/browser/voiceModeOnboarding.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/speech/test/browser/voiceLiveSession.test.ts` — passed with **107 tests**.
- `npm --prefix extensions/copilot run test:unit -- src/extension/byok/vscode-node/test/gptLiveSession.spec.ts src/extension/byok/vscode-node/test/openAIProvider.spec.ts` — passed again with 12 tests.
- `git diff --cached --name-only -z -- 'src/**/*.ts' | xargs -0 ./node_modules/.bin/eslint` — passed for all staged core TypeScript changes.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed.

Total focused regression coverage: **390 core tests plus 12 Copilot provider tests**. The complete repository test suite was not run.

### CI and selected-review follow-up

All six failed Browser/Electron jobs in run `36904688012` hit the same migration-test collision: importing the Voice Mode action registered the real voice migration alongside a synthetic test migration using the same production key. The test now uses an isolated synthetic key and retains its application/user target assertions. Compile & Hygiene reported five repository-formatting violations, which are corrected.

The five selected review issues are addressed:

- Composer submission awaits the real asynchronous send outcome through its interface and wrappers.
- Both edited-input paths report no submission and give review/send guidance rather than a success acknowledgement.
- WebRTC `disconnected` gets a 10-second recovery grace, cancelled on recovery/teardown. Repeated notifications do not extend the deadline; `failed` remains immediately terminal.
- Partial form answers retain their schema and are invalidated when the same pending IDs publish a different schema, preventing reuse of old opaque option values.

Local validation before the upstream merge:

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob '**/chat/test/**/voiceClient/*.test.js'` — **350 passed**.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatInput.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatVoiceTarget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceBridge.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/common/configuration.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/test/browser/voiceModeActions.test.ts` — **140 passed**, including migration and real-action registration in the same runner.
- `git diff --cached --name-only -z -- 'src/**/*.ts' | xargs -0 node build/lib/formatter.ts --verify` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --name-only -z -- 'src/**/*.ts' | xargs -0 ./node_modules/.bin/eslint` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed.

These are **490 core test executions** for this follow-up, not a complete repository or cross-platform test run. Remote CI must validate the pushed commit; recovery/edit guidance still needs live microphone verification.

### Upstream refresh and current-head validation

The fixes were pushed as `4895338c7e8`, but GitHub could not start the platform workflow because the branch conflicted with main. With maintainer approval, main snapshot `3daf19a04b5435718cd7291cd207815ec777abb4` was merged without rewriting published history. The single composer-test conflict was resolved by preserving both upstream tests and the four voice-submission regressions.

The resolved test file passed repository formatter verification, and `git diff --cached --check` passed. Post-merge dependency restoration via `npm run install-fast` was unsuccessful: the initial attempt hit `ENOTDIR`, and the retry was blocked by HTTP 401 from the Monaco/vscode Azure npm feed. The maintainer approved committing/pushing the merge with local validation pending and validating the merged head through CI.

The 490 passing tests and client type-check above apply to the pre-merge fixes, **not the merged head**. No post-merge local build/test success is claimed.

Remote CI has now verified all seven previously failing checks on merged head `fcd988900bb645dc182651d5040cb9c2d863b71b` in [Code OSS run 37026561920](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37026561920):

| Previously failing check | Merged-head result |
|---|---|
| [Compile & Hygiene](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37026561920/job/110902573726) | Passed |
| [Linux / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37026561920/job/110902574059) | Passed |
| [macOS / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37026561920/job/110902574137) | Passed |
| [Windows / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37026561920/job/110902574643) | Passed |
| [Linux / Browser](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37026561920/job/110902574049) | Passed |
| [macOS / Browser](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37026561920/job/110902574506) | Passed |
| [Windows / Browser](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37026561920/job/110902574799) | Passed |

At the last inspection, the overall workflow remained in progress for Linux Remote and the three Electron-Smoke jobs, with no failed jobs reported. Full-workflow completion and live microphone verification are not claimed.

## Live verification and remaining limits

An isolated OSS Agents window was fully compiled and launched. The user configured OpenAI through Models Management and confirmed a successful multi-turn run with speaking animation. Logs corroborated an initial composer submission and subsequent requests into the same concrete chat.

The final fragment-overlap, autoplay fallback, regular-workbench routing, natural-consent, and contextual-acknowledgement changes have not yet been reloaded and live-verified in that window. Regular editor-window microphone flows and cross-platform audio behavior still require live verification. Unit tests validate routing and protocol/instruction wiring, not ASR accuracy or model adherence to acknowledgement wording.

The branch retains the original feature's tested base rather than silently rebasing the entire implementation onto newer `main` commits. This is a draft; CI and base integration remain to be checked.

## How to test

1. Configure an OpenAI provider/API key in Models Management, enable Voice Mode, and select the BYOK voice model.
2. In the Agents window, start from the new-session input and send a voice request. Verify the resulting concrete chat remains the target for follow-up speech.
3. In a regular editor window, start Voice Mode from a chat editor tab and then from the sidebar. Verify the clicked input owns the request even if another widget was previously focused or the sidebar bridge was not rendered.
4. Exercise current approvals with “approved” and “I accept,” then test qualified consent, stale prompts, duplicate replies, and simultaneous prompts in another chat.
5. Exercise single/multiple selections, text answers, sequential forms, allowed custom responses, and permitted/forbidden skipping.
6. Verify acceptance gets a short contextual acknowledgement—not “done”—and actual completion is narrated separately. Optional progress should follow `agents.voice.agentProgress`.
7. Verify speaking animation, response-audio muting, autoplay fallback, barge-in, held PTT, and explicit-input-switch/discard restart behavior.

pull_requests.title: fix: assert configured Copilot integration ID in CloudSandboxApiService task deletion test (build fix for vscode-engineering#405
pull_requests.body:
## Build failure

Build 479434 (insider, `refs/heads/main`) failed the **Run unit tests (Electron)** job on Linux, macOS, and Windows with 3 failing tests in the new `CloudSandboxApiService task deletion` suite:

```text
actual Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat
expected Copilot-Integration-Id: code-oss
```

The failures covered the HTTP 200, 204, and 404 task-deletion cases.

## Root cause

`src/vs/platform/endpoint/common/licenseAgreement.ts` defines `COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID = 'code-oss'` for Code - OSS, but is explicitly "modified as part of the production build" (per the file's header comment), where product CI rewrites the value to `vscode-chat`.

The production code in `cloudSandboxApiService.ts` correctly sends the `Copilot-Integration-Id` header using the shared `COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID` constant. However, the task-deletion test in `cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts` asserted the header against a hardcoded literal `'code-oss'`. In the product build the constant becomes `vscode-chat`, so the assertion no longer matched the request the service actually made, failing the Electron unit tests on all three platforms.

## How the fix works

The test now imports and asserts against the same `COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID` constant that the production code uses to build the request header. The expectation therefore tracks whatever value the build configures — `code-oss` in OSS and `vscode-chat` in product — instead of a brittle literal. This verifies the real contract (the service sends the configured integration ID) without weakening the assertion.

## Rollback evaluation

- **Recommendation:** Do not roll back
- **Culprit:** `88349a27ead34c34511504a1d62906b0f2a84d7a`, microsoft/vscode#339042
- **Rationale:** The break is confined to a new test expectation that hardcoded the OSS integration ID. Aligning the assertion with the shared constant is a bounded, lower-risk fix-forward than reverting the larger session-deletion feature and its production code.
- Owners to consult: ``@roblourens``

## Validation

The TypeScript compiler (`tsc` / `npm run typecheck-client`) could not be run in this environment — the sandbox blocked invoking the compiler. The change is a minimal, localized test edit: it adds one import (verified that `src/vs/platform/endpoint/common/licenseAgreement.ts` exists at the computed relative path) and swaps a string literal for the already-exported `COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID` constant used by the production code. The resulting expectation matches the exact value the service sends in both OSS and product build configurations.

## Risk

Low. The change touches a single assertion in one test file, with no production code impact. It strengthens the test to match the production contract across build configurations.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: ``@roblourens``

Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#4050

pull_requests.title: agentHost: preserve legacy policy-required sandboxing
pull_requests.body:
Prevent a per-session Off selection from overriding the legacy VS Code `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` policy in Copilot Agent Host on macOS/Linux.

The policy already locked the global `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` setting, and sandboxing remained enabled for sessions following that setting. However, forwarding preserved only the resolved `on` value, not the fact that it was mandatory. Agent Host therefore treated the policy like a personal preference, allowing a session-level Off selection to override it.

## Scope

- **Affected:** Copilot Agent Host sessions on macOS/Linux governed by the legacy VS Code `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` policy, when a session selects or already has an Off override.
- **Not a general sandbox failure:** the sandbox implementation itself and the legacy Local harness are not changed. Runtime-managed `sandbox.enabled: true` already has enforcement and session controls from [#338172](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338172); that is a separate policy path.
- Personal sandbox preferences remain overridable. Windows continues to use its separate `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows` setting.

## Change

- Forward the legacy policy requirement separately from editable root settings. The host aggregates connection-owned contributions restrictively, so settings edits or another client cannot clear an active requirement.
- Combine that requirement with the host's existing runtime policy restrictions. Reconnect restores the contribution before authentication and session replay; withdrawal or disconnect-grace expiry removes only the owning client's contribution.
- Enforce the requirement in session configuration, not just the UI, and publish the effective policy to the existing session controls.
- Apply policy arrival and withdrawal to running sessions, including their peer chats and subagents. Preserve permitted SDK-approved bypasses without weakening runtime restrictions.

No SDK or runtime change is required. This addresses the legacy sandbox-enable gap described in [#339023](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339023), not its other policy-parity gaps.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

### Summary

Currently, custom editors (`contributes.customEditors`) and editor defaults (`workbench.editorAssociations` / `workbench.diffEditorAssociations`) only target `filenamePattern` glob patterns. However, many file types (such as `.md`, `.ipynb`, `.svg`, or custom domain languages) are associated with languages dynamically or via `files.associations`.

This PR implements language ID targeting for custom editors and editor defaults as requested in #335704:
1. Custom editors can now specify `language` in `contributes.customEditors[].selector`.
2. New settings `workbench.editorLanguageAssociations` and `workbench.diffEditorLanguageAssociations` allow users to configure language-wide default editors.
3. Precedence is strictly maintained: **explicit filename pattern > explicit language association > natural editor priority > default text editor fallback**.
4. Language default configuration is surfaced directly in the **Reopen Editor With...** QuickPick and the breadcrumbs/tab editor type menu.

---

### Key Changes

1. **Schema & Extension Point (`contributes.customEditors`)**:
   - Updated `customEditorsContributionSchema` in `extensionPoint.ts` to accept `language?: string`.
   - Updated `CustomEditorSelector` in `customEditor.ts`.
   - Implemented **AND** matching when both `filenamePattern` and `language` are specified within the same selector entry (e.g. `docs/**` AND `markdown`). Multiple array items remain **OR**.
   - Updated `contributedCustomEditors.ts` and `customEditors.ts` to register editors with their selector language.

2. **Effective Language ID & Dynamic Reactivity (`EditorResolverService`)**:
   - Injected `ILanguageService` and `IModelService` into `EditorResolverService`.
   - `getEffectiveLanguageId(resource)` resolves the language ID via the open text model first, and falls back to `languageService.guessLanguageIdByFilepathOrFirstLine(resource)` (which respects `files.associations`).
   - Wired listeners to `modelService.onModelLanguageChanged` and `configurationService.onDidChangeConfiguration` (for `files.associations`, `editorAssociations`, `editorLanguageAssociations`, etc.) to trigger dynamic cache invalidation and re-evaluation.

3. **Settings & Precedence Engine**:
   - Registered configuration schemas for:
     - `workbench.editorLanguageAssociations`
     - `workbench.diffEditorLanguageAssociations`
   - Updated `EditorResolverService`:
     - Filename associations take precedence over language associations (`getMatchingRawAssociationsForResource`).
     - `findMatchingEditors` checks both filename pattern and language (`matchesFilename && matchesLanguage`).
     - Fixed `isUnconfiguredUniversalOptionalEditorMatch` so language-targeted wildcard editors (`globPattern: '*'`) are not incorrectly treated as universal optional editors.
     - Implemented `setDefaultLanguageEditor(languageId, editorID, forDiffEditor?)` which writes to the appropriate setting and cleanly removes redundant overrides when restoring natural defaults.

4. **UI Surfacing**:
   - **Reopen Editor With... (`doPickEditor`)**: Surfaces `"Configure default editor for '{0}' (language)..."` (and diff-specific variant) alongside the pattern default option.
   - **Editor Type Picker (`editorTypePicker.ts`)**: Surfaces `"Set Default for '{0}'"` (with localized language name) in the breadcrumbs and editor tab dropdowns.

---

### Verification & Testing

#### Unit Tests Added
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/customEditor/test/common/customEditorInfo.test.ts`:
  - `matches with filenamePattern only`
  - `matches with language only`
  - `matches with combined filenamePattern and language (AND condition)`
  - `matches with multiple selectors (OR condition)`
- `src/vs/workbench/services/editor/test/browser/editorResolverService.test.ts`:
  - `Language-targeted custom editor resolves for matching resource`
  - `Selector with both filenamePattern and language matches with AND semantics`
  - `Precedence: explicit filename pattern overrides explicit language association`
  - `Language default setting overrides natural priority`
  - `Diff language association overrides general editor association for diffs`
  - `setDefaultLanguageEditor updates language association setting and removes redundant association`

#### Static Analysis & Architecture
- Verified clean TypeScript compilation (`tsc`) with **0 errors** across all modified files.
- Ran architecture layers checker (`build/checker/layersChecker.ts`): **passed with 0 layer violations**.
- Ran whitespace / hygiene check (`git diff --check`): **clean**.

## Description

Welcome phrases rendered over a custom chat background can lack contrast and become hard to read. This hides the new-session welcome phrases in the Agents window whenever a custom background (image or codicons preset) is active.

return derived(owner, reader =>

pull_requests.title: chat: Fix tabbed model picker for Free and Student plans
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

Fixes #338792
Fixes #338972

## What changed

Copilot Free and Student accounts only get Auto, and the tabbed model picker fell over for them:

- **Copilot harness (agent host):** the Copilot SDK lists **no models** for these accounts, so there was no Auto. The picker showed only the agent host's HydraFusion under an "Alternative routing" heading, followed by unexplained Upgrade rows (#338792). Once #338841 hid HydraFusion for Free users, the Copilot tab had nothing left and disappeared behind BYOK tabs (#338972).
- **Local harness:** Auto's tiers were followed by Upgrade rows with no heading.

This PR:

- **Agent host: offers Auto when the SDK lists nothing.** A successful but empty `models.list` now publishes Auto with its "Optimize for" tiers, the same way the Copilot CLI extension falls back to `buildAutoModel()`. Signed-out and failed refreshes are unchanged. Model validation treats a listing that returned nothing as an empty catalog, even with HydraFusion or BYOK models published beside the fallback Auto, so selections take the existing fail-open path.
- **HydraFusion is offered to Student plans only as an upgrade**, the same as Free. The six Free-only checks from #338841 now go through one helper, `isHydraFusionUpgradeOnly`. A previously selected HydraFusion switches to Auto.
- **Tabbed picker:**
  - When Copilot offers nothing to pick by hand, the locked models it lists sit under a new **"Upgrade for More Models"** heading. This only happens when every one of them is unlocked by upgrading; models that need an update or an admin stay unlabelled as before.
  - Free and Student plans keep the Copilot tab for these upsells even when Copilot relays nothing selectable.
  - A tab that only has upsells no longer sets the popup's height, which would otherwise squeeze BYOK tabs.
  - HydraFusion on its own still sits under the "Auto" tab.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Auto is added whenever the SDK lists no models, for any account.** Before, such an account saw an empty picker. Now it sees Auto, which works for Student (verified below). An account where Auto can't work would hit an error when sending instead.
- **HydraFusion is blocked for Student only in the picker**, the same as it already is for Free. The agent host still lists it; enforcing it on the server would be the real fix.

## How to test

1. Sign in with a Copilot Free or Student account and set `"chat.experimentalModelPicker": true`.
2. In the **Copilot** harness, open the model picker:
   - The tab is **Auto**, with the Efficiency / Balance / Intelligence tiers.
   - HydraFusion appears as an **Upgrade** row under "Alternative routing".
   - The plan's locked models appear under **"Upgrade for More Models"**.
3. Send a message with Auto. It should route to a model and reply.
4. In the **Local** harness, the picker shows Auto's tiers, then the locked models under "Upgrade for More Models".
5. With a BYOK provider added, the Copilot tab stays next to the BYOK tabs, and each BYOK tab sizes to its own models.

## Validation

- Manual: ran a dev build of this branch against a real Student (`free_educational_quota`) account.
  - Copilot harness: the SDK listed 0 models and the agent host offered Auto; the picker matched step 2.
  - Sending "Reply with OK" routed to gpt-5.6-luna and replied "OK".
  - Local harness: the picker matched step 4.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/*.test.js"`: **passed**, 369 passing.
- `npx mocha test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --timeout=10000 --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`: 462 passing, **12 failing**. The same 12 session-discovery tests fail locally without this change; the two new tests pass.
- `npx eslint <changed files>`: **passed**.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: 370 errors, the same count as without this change. They come from missing Electron typings in my local worktree, and none are in the changed files.
- New component fixtures (informational screenshots, not blocking): `PickerFreePlan`, `PickerFreePlanWithAddedModels`, `PickerFreePlanWithoutCopilotModels`, `PickerEduPlanCopilotHarness`.

pull_requests.title: Fix Git SCM perpetual scanning and extension activation deadlock
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
Fixes perpetual "Scanning folder for Git repositories..." hang after renderer SIGTERM (code 15) + extension host restart.

Field evidence (macOS Tahoe, VS Code 1.140.0):
- `main.log`: `CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: killed, code: 15)`
- `window2/exthost/exthost.log`: `Cannot activate the 'Git' extension because its dependency 'Git 基础' failed to activate` preceded by `Channel has been closed`
- `fileWatcher.log`: repeated `Events were dropped by the FSEvents client` for aggregate workspace
- `state.vscdb`: stale Agent worktree paths (e.g. `omni_panel_t544`) re-probed every scan

## Root causes verified in source
1. **SCM state machine has no failure state**: `extensions/git/package.json` welcome views match `git.state != initialized`; `APIState` is only `uninitialized|initialized`; `Model` constructor does `doInitialScan().finally(() => setState('initialized'))`. Any activation/scan failure leaves deceptive scanning UI forever.
2. **Transient dependency failure permanently cached**: `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostExtensionActivator.ts` wraps failed deps in `FailedExtension` in `_operations` with no retry. A transient channel close in `vscode.git-base` during host restart permanently poisons `vscode.git`.
3. **Ghost paths block @sequentialize queue**: `extensions/git/src/model.ts#openRepository` spawns `git rev-parse` for deleted worktree paths with no `fs.stat` fast-path.

Note: the draft snippet in the local bug report used `this._operations.delete` inside `ActivationOperation` (does not compile - map lives on `ExtensionsActivator`). This PR implements the compile-correct version.

## Changes (5 files, +118/-14)
- `extensions/git/src/api/git.d.ts`: `APIState` += `'failed'` (additive, backwards compatible).
- `extensions/git/src/model.ts`: 30s initial-scan timeout (`Promise.race` + `clearTimeout`); constructor `then(success->initialized, failure->failed)`; `isInitialized` resolves on `failed`; `openRepository()` `fs.stat` fast-path skips non-existent/non-directory paths.
- `extensions/git/package.json`: scanning views gated on `git.state == uninitialized`; new `scanFailed` welcome on `git.state == failed`.
- `extensions/git/package.nls.json`: `view.workbench.scm.scanFailed` message with Reload Window action (with Locked command comments per localization rules).
- `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostExtensionActivator.ts`: new exported `isTransientActivationError()` (CancellationError or channel/IPC-closed in message or `.detail/.cause` chain); transient dep failures do not cache `FailedExtension` (leave value null + warn); `_handleActivationRequest` drops null/transient cached ops for retry; `_initialize` opens barrier in `finally`.

## Verification
- `python3 -m json.tool` on both JSON files: OK
- `git diff --check`: clean (tabs in TS, 2-space in package.json per .editorconfig)
- `tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck` sweep: only pre-existing missing `vscode` module errors; no errors in edited hunks
- Isolated logic tests (6/6 PASS): transient classifier (direct/cancellation/detail-wrapped true; genuine missing false), ghost `stat` early-return, timeout race rejection
- Scope kept minimal; no formatting churn; no new Electron APIs; no API removal

## Follow-up / risk
- `failed` is additive; consumers checking `!= initialized` still treat it as not-ready, which is correct.
- 30s timeout value is conservative for 15+ repo aggregate workspaces; adjustable if maintainers prefer config.
- CLA will be signed on PR creation if required.

Fixes field report: `docs/2026-10-02-vscode-git-activation-deadlock-and-scm-hang-bug-report.md`.

pull_requests.title: Copilot setup: say where Copilot CLI was found
pull_requests.body:
Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#7531.

When Copilot CLI is already installed (for example WinGet's `C:\Program Files\WinGet\Links\copilot.exe`), setup skips its Copilot page by design. That looked like a missing page. Setup now says where it found Copilot CLI.

### Changes
- The shim's setup probe writes `cliPath`, the first Copilot CLI it found, next to `cliFound`. The result file is UTF-16LE, so any profile path works.
- Setup logs `cliPath` and, when it skips the page because Copilot CLI was found (and policy doesn't disable it), adds this to the Ready page:
  ```
  GitHub Copilot CLI:
        Already installed at <path>
  ```
  It shows no action line, because setup does nothing with Copilot in this case.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` documents `cliPath`.
- Separate commit: the ConPTY Ctrl+C test restores Ctrl+C before starting the shim. A test runner started in a new process group ignores Ctrl+C and the shim inherited that, so the test exited 1 instead of 130. Real interactive terminals aren't affected.

### How to test
1. Put any `copilot.exe` on PATH (or install Copilot CLI via WinGet, npm, or the MSI).
2. Run the user installer interactively and go to the Ready page.
3. Expect the "GitHub Copilot CLI: Already installed at …" section, and in the setup log (`/LOG=…`) a line `Copilot: probe … cliFound=true, cliPath=<path> …`.
4. Without a CLI on PATH, the Copilot page shows as before and the Ready page shows the chosen option.

### Validation
- `cargo fmt --check`: passed.
- `cargo test --locked` (Windows x64): passed (63 lib tests plus all integration tests).
- `cargo +1.88 clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`: passed.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Delegate Copilot plugin management to the SDK
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Addresses #338975.

## Summary

Introduces a provider-facing plugin-management protocol so the Customizations UI can delegate plugin inventory and mutation operations to a Copilot SDK-backed provider instead of maintaining its own parallel inventory and marketplace cache. This fixes the split-inventory issues reported against #338975 (install/uninstall ambiguity, enable/disable state not reflecting in the UI, duplicate/shadowed entries with inconsistent bare-vs-qualified plugin names).

## Changes

- **Protocol**: Added `vscode/plugins/v1/manage` (`ManageAgentHostPluginsExtensionMethod`) and `vscode/plugins/v1/changed` (`AgentHostPluginsChangedNotification`) to the Agent Host extension protocol, plus an `AgentHostPluginManagementCapabilityMetaKey` handshake flag so a provider can advertise which provider IDs support plugin management (`agentHostPluginManagement.ts`, `agentHostPluginManagementMeta.ts`, `agentHostExtensionProtocol.ts`).
- **Copilot provider implementation**: `copilotPluginManagement.ts` implements `IAgentHostPluginManagement` on the Copilot node agent host, routing `list`/`browse`/`install`/`uninstall`/`update`/`enable`/`disable` through the Copilot SDK's `session.rpc.plugins` API and emitting change notifications when SDK-side mutations happen out-of-band (e.g. via a `/plugin` slash command), so the UI stays in sync.
- **Browser-side consumer**: `AgentHostPluginManagementProvider` implements `ICustomizationPluginManagementProvider` and is wired into the Agent Host harness in `agentHostChatContribution.ts`. `pluginListWidget.ts` and `customizationMarketplaceInstallService.ts` now route list/browse/install/uninstall/toggle/update through this provider for any harness whose agent host advertises the new capability, instead of the legacy `IPluginInstallService`/file-based marketplace path.
- **Inventory de-duplication**: Tagged SDK-managed plugins in `agentPluginService`/`agentPluginServiceImpl` with `managedBy` so the legacy file-based plugin store excludes them from the merged list, fixing duplicate/shadowed entries between the two inventories.
- **Customization bundling**: `agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts`'s `resolveCustomizationRefs` now excludes SDK-owned plugin directories from the customization bundle sent back to capable Copilot hosts, since the SDK already owns that state.

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `npx eslint` on all changed/added files — passed, no warnings.
- `./scripts/test.sh` targeted runs — all suites touched by this change pass:
  - `copilotPluginManagement.test.ts` (new) — 7/7 passing
  - `agentHostPluginManagementProvider.test.ts` (new) — 5/5 passing
  - `copilotAgent.test.ts`, `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` — passing
  - `agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts` (electron-browser) — passing
  - `resolveCustomizationRefs.test.ts`, `customizationMarketplaceInstallService.test.ts` — passing
- Note: a broader `./scripts/test.sh` run across the agent host test folder surfaces ~134 pre-existing, unrelated failures caused by `@vscode/sqlite3` failing to resolve as an ESM module specifier in `sessionDatabase.ts` under the local test environment; these are unrelated to the files touched in this change (the failures originate in sessionDatabase.ts, which this PR does not modify) and appear to be a local environment setup issue (ESM resolution of @vscode/sqlite3).

## Stacked on

This PR is based on `main`, which already includes #338982 ("Add Copilot plugin slash commands to Agent Host").

pull_requests.title: fix: reject with proper Error on audio error event (fixes #339115)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary An accessibility signal sound fails to play, and the `error` event handler in `doPlayAudio` rejects the promise with `e.error` — but a DOM media `error` event is a plain `Event` that has no `error` property, so the promise rejects with `undefined`. That `undefined` then reaches the `catch (e)` block in `playSound`, which reads `e.message` and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'message')`. Impact: an unhandled error is logged to telemetry whenever an accessibility cue sound fails to load/play (e.g. missing/blocked media), affecting 425 users on stable 1.140.0. Fixes microsoft/vscode#339115 Recommended reviewer: ``@meganrogge`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | pre-existing — not a regression | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | The faulty `reject(e.error)` has existed since the file was created; no recent commit changed the triggering logic. This bucket is new on the 1.140.0 stable channel but the defect is long-standing (surfaced at stable scale / under conditions where a cue sound fails to play). This is best characterized as a pre-existing bug newly observed, not a code regression. | > No culprit commit identified: the defective line predates the available > history for this file and no commit in the regression window altered the > audio error-handling path. The fix targets the long-standing producer bug. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller as playSignal participant Sound as playSound participant Audio as doPlayAudio participant DOM as HTMLAudioElement Caller->>Sound: await playSound(sound) Sound->>Audio: await playAudio(url, volume) Audio->>DOM: new Audio(url)#59; audio.play() DOM-->>Audio: 'error' event (plain Event, no .error) Note over Audio: ⚠️ Root cause (L297):
reject(e.error) → rejects with undefined Audio-->>Sound: promise rejects with undefined Note over Sound: 💥 L211: e.message
Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'message') ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/platform/accessibilitySignal/browser/accessibilitySignalService.ts` | root cause (producer) | L297: `reject(e.error)` — the media `error` event is a plain `Event` with no `.error` property, so the promise rejects with `undefined` | | `src/vs/platform/accessibilitySignal/browser/accessibilitySignalService.ts` | crash site | L211 (from stack): `if (!e.message.includes(...))` reads `.message` on the `undefined` rejection value | ### Repro Steps 1. Trigger any accessibility signal that plays a sound (e.g. enable sounds via `accessibility.signalOptions`, then perform an action that plays a cue). 2. Cause the audio element to emit an `error` event — e.g. the media resource fails to load, is blocked, or is otherwise unplayable (the browser/Electron fires `error` rather than resolving `play()`). 3. The `error` handler rejects the play promise with `undefined`; the `catch (e)` in `playSound` reads `e.message` and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'message')`, which is reported as an unhandled error. Because `play()`'s own rejection path (L300) rejects with a real `Error`, the crash only manifests via the media `error` event path, which explains the intermittent, environment-dependent occurrence. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`accessibilitySignalService.ts` → `doPlayAudio`): fix the data producer, not the crash site. The `error`-event handler no longer rejects with the non-existent `e.error`. Instead it constructs a proper `Error`, enriched with the real failure details from `audio.error` (an `HTMLMediaElement`'s `MediaError`, carrying `.code` and `.message`) when available, and a generic `"Failed to play audio"` message otherwise. After this change the promise always rejects with a genuine `Error` instance, so the downstream `catch (e)` in `playSound` can always read `e.message` safely — the `TypeError` can no longer be produced. This keeps the existing `logService`/`console.error` telemetry path intact (the `catch` block still runs and still logs genuine failures), and it enriches the error with cross-boundary diagnostic context (`MediaError.code`) rather than swallowing it. **Alternatives considered:** - Guard at the crash site (`e?.message` or `if (!e) return` in `playSound`'s catch) — rejected: that is a crash-site guard that masks the producer bug, leaves every other consumer of `playAudio` receiving a meaningless `undefined` rejection, and discards the real failure cause. - Wrap the play call in try/catch that swallows the error — rejected: it would hide genuine audio failures from the telemetry pipeline. ### Recommended Owner ``@meganrogge`` — area owner of `accessibilitySignalService.ts`; authored the large majority of this file's history and is highly active in `microsoft/vscode` (hundreds of commits in the last 90 days). The culprit is pre-existing, so ownership falls to the feature-area owner. > Authored with Copilot

pull_requests.title: [Feature] Markdown Preview: Table of Contents with persistent visibility & Code block language labels
pull_requests.body:
This PR introduces two new features to the Markdown preview:

Table of Contents (TOC) — A navigable sidebar showing document headings with auto-scroll sync
Code Block Language Labels — Language badges (e.g., php, javascript, python) displayed on fenced code blocks
Both features are brand new and did not exist previously.

---

#### Features
1. Table of Contents

UI/UX:
- Collapsible sidebar on the left of the preview
- Shows all headings (h1–h6) with indentation by level
- Active heading highlighted based on scroll position
- Resizable width (drag handle), persisted in localStorage
- Toolbar toggle button with checkbox (synced to context key markdown.tocVisible)
- Persistence:
  - Visibility preference stored in extension globalState (markdown.preview.tocVisible)
  - Survives: tab close, VS Code restart, preview reopen
  - Default: visible (true)
Auto-scroll behavior:
- During document scroll: TOC panel scrolls minimally to keep active entry visible (with 4px edge gap)
- Manual click on TOC entry: Does not trigger TOC panel scroll — user stays at clicked position
- First/last headings can now reach true top/bottom of panel (no visual gap)

2. Code Block Language Labels
- Language identifier from fenced code blocks (php, js, python, etc.) displayed as a badge in the top-right corner of the code block
- Uses the existing tokenization from the markdown renderer
- Styled with theme-aware colors (uses `--vscode-editorCodeBlockLabel-background/foreground`)

#### Technical Implementation

TOC Architecture

```
MarkdownPreviewManager (owns globalState)
    ├── #tocVisible: boolean (persisted)
    ├── createPreview() / revivePreview() → passes tocVisible
    └── #setActivePreview() → sets context key 'markdown.tocVisible'

StaticMarkdownPreview / DynamicMarkdownPreview
    └── getAdditionalState() → includes tocVisible

Webview (preview-src/index.ts)
    ├── Reads State.TocVisible from vscode.getState() / data-state
    ├── Calls buildTableOfContents()
    └── If TocVisible === false → toggleTableOfContents()

tableOfContents.ts (webview module)
    ├── Module-level tocVisible (synced from State)
    ├── skipScrollActiveEntry flag (prevents auto-scroll on manual click)
    ├── scrollActiveEntryIntoView() (minimal scroll with edge gap)
    └── Resize handle → persists width to localStorage
```

Language Labels
- Injected during markdown rendering via markdown-it plugin
- Added as <span class="code-block-language-label"> inside code block wrapper
- CSS uses design tokens for theming consistency

#### Test

##### Test Workspace
Open the test workspace file:

```
extensions/markdown-language-features/test-workspace/e.md
```

This file contains:
- Multiple heading levels (h1–h6) for TOC testing
- Fenced code blocks with various languages (php, javascript, python, typescript, etc.)
- Enough content to trigger scrolling

##### Test Steps
Table of Contents:

1. Open e.md in VS Code
2. Open Markdown Preview (Ctrl+Shift+V / Cmd+Shift+V)
3. Verify TOC appears on the left with all headings
4. Scroll in the preview → verify active heading highlights in TOC
5. Click a heading in TOC → verify navigation works without scrolling the TOC panel
6. Scroll to first/last heading → verify TOC scrollbar reaches true top/bottom
7. Click toolbar toggle button → verify TOC hides/shows, checkbox matches
8. Close preview tab, reopen → verify TOC visibility persists
9. Restart VS Code → verify TOC visibility persists
10. Drag resize handle → verify width persists after reload

Code Block Language Labels:
1. In e.md preview, locate fenced code blocks
2. Verify each block shows a language badge (e.g., php, js, py, ts)
3. Switch themes (light/dark/high contrast) → verify badge colors adapt

Context Key:
1. Open Command Palette → Developer: Inspect Context Keys
2. Search `markdown.tocVisible` → verify it matches actual TOC visibility

---

Thank you very much for your time. Please let me know if there’s anything else I need to do.
