pull_requests.title: fix: guard against duplicate language model tool registration (fixes #339101)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary An extension can register a Language Model tool whose id was already registered in the same extension host. The extension-host `ExtHostLanguageModelTools.registerTool` / `registerToolDefinition` methods accepted the duplicate id, overwrote their own `_registeredTools` entry, and fired a second `$registerTool` across the ExtHost→MainThread RPC. On the main thread `registerToolImplementation` rejects the duplicate with `Tool "" already has an implementation.`, but because the ExtHost call is fire-and-forget the rejection surfaces as an unhandled error in telemetry. Impact: noisy unhandled errors on Mac/Windows/Linux; the second registration silently fails. Fixes microsoft/vscode#339101 Recommended reviewer: ``@roblourens`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not identified — pre-existing boundary throw | | Author | — | | PR | — | | Message | — | | Why | The main-thread throws in `registerToolImplementation` (`already has an implementation`) and `registerToolData` (`was not contributed`) have existed since `4ba135f7` (Oct 2024). No commit in the regression range `544a8291..73d5322b` touches the tool-registration files. The range commit `487a93be` ("extensions: serialize unexpected errors before forwarding") changed how unexpected ExtHost errors are serialized before `$onUnexpectedError`, which is the most plausible reason these pre-existing cross-process rejections began bucketing as new telemetry — i.e. re-bucketing of a pre-existing defect, not a behavioral regression. The underlying bug (missing producer-side duplicate guard) is pre-existing. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as Extension participant EH as ExtHostLanguageModelTools participant MT as MainThreadLanguageModelTools participant Svc as LanguageModelToolsService Ext->>EH: registerTool(id) Note over EH: ⚠️ Root cause:
no duplicate-id guard,
overwrites _registeredTools EH->>MT: $registerTool(id) [RPC, fire-and-forget] MT->>Svc: registerToolImplementation(id) Note over Svc: 💥 throw:
Tool "id" already has an implementation Svc-->>MT: rejection Note over MT: RPC reply rejected;
no ExtHost handler → unhandled error ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts` | crash site | L359 (from stack): `throw new Error(\`Tool "\$\{id}" already has an implementation.\`)` | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadLanguageModelTools.ts` | RPC boundary | L92-L109: `$registerTool` calls `registerToolImplementation(id, ...)`; rejection crosses back with no ExtHost handler | | `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts` | root cause (producer) | L344-L350: `registerTool` did `this._registeredTools.set(id, ...); this._proxy.$registerTool(id, ...)` with no guard against an already-registered id | ### Repro Steps 1. Author an extension that calls `vscode.lm.registerTool('myTool', impl)` twice for the same id (e.g. an activation path that runs registration more than once, or two code paths registering the same tool name). 2. Activate the extension. 3. The second call reaches the main thread and `registerToolImplementation` throws `Tool "myTool" already has an implementation.`; since the ExtHost did not await/handle the RPC rejection, it is reported as an unhandled error. The sibling bucket `Tool "" was not contributed.` (microsoft/vscode#339102) is the same boundary pattern when `registerToolImplementation` runs before the matching `registerToolData`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts`: add a synchronous duplicate-id guard at the top of both `registerTool` and `registerToolDefinition`, before mutating `_registeredTools` or sending the RPC: ```ts if (this._registeredTools.has(id)) { throw new Error(`Tool "${id}" is already registered.`); } ``` This fixes the data producer rather than the crash site. The duplicate is now rejected synchronously, in the extension host, on the caller's own stack — so the offending extension gets a normal thrown error from the API call it made (the same way `extHostDebugService`, `extHostCustomEditors`, `extHostFileSystem`, and many other extHost registries already reject duplicate ids), and no malformed second `$registerTool` ever crosses the RPC boundary to become an unhandled main-thread error. It also stops the ExtHost `_registeredTools` map from being silently overwritten, which previously detached the first registration's disposer from its entry. **Alternatives considered**: - Swallow or `try/catch` the throw in the main thread `registerToolImplementation` / `$registerTool` — rejected: that hides a real caller bug from telemetry and leaves the ExtHost map corrupted; the error pipeline depends on real defects being surfaced, just on the correct (caller's) stack. - Make `registerToolImplementation` idempotent (return the existing disposable) — rejected: it would mask double-registration and make tool ownership/disposal ambiguous across two different implementations sharing one id. **Lifecycle pattern**: external/untrusted boundary — the producer is an extension calling the public `lm` API across the extension-host RPC. The fix is placed at the first point inside `microsoft/vscode` that owns the contract (the extHost registry), converting an async unhandled rejection into a synchronous, attributable API error for the extension author. **Producer site**: `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts:344` (`registerTool`) and `:358` (`registerToolDefinition`). ### Recommended Owner ``@roblourens`` — owner of the chat language-model tools area (author of `languageModelToolsService` and its tests, 400+ commits to microsoft/vscode in the last 90 days).

pull_requests.title: fix: buffer LM tool implementations registered before their data contribution (fixes #339102)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary `unhandlederror-Tool "appmod-install-appcat" was not contributed.` is thrown on the main thread when an extension registers a language-model **tool implementation** (via `vscode.lm.registerTool(id, ...)`) before the matching **tool data** from that extension's `package.json` `languageModelTools` contribution has been registered by `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler`. This is an activation-ordering race: three App Modernization tools (`appmod-install-appcat`, `appmod-run-assessment`, `appmod-build-docker-image`) each hit it, affecting ~104 users across Linux, Windows and Mac. The fix buffers an early implementation and attaches it when the tool data arrives, so the race no longer throws. Fixes microsoft/vscode#339102 Recommended reviewer: ``@bhavyaus`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — see below | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | No commit in the regression range (`544a8291...73d5322b`) touches `languageModelToolsService.ts`, `languageModelToolsContribution.ts`, `mainThreadLanguageModelTools.ts`, or `extHostLanguageModelTools.ts`. This is **not** a code regression in those files. The bucket is a re-occurrence of the error family previously addressed by PR #326651 (*"register LM tools extension point handler at BlockStartup"*, milestone 1.131.0, owner ``@bhavyaus``). That fix moved the producer earlier but did not make the ordering impossible: the per-extension contribution *delta* for a newly-activated extension can still be delivered **after** that same extension's `activate()` has already called `vscode.lm.registerTool(...)`. The new bucket surfaced because the App Modernization extension began shipping `appmod-*` tools that activate through a non-tool path and register their implementations eagerly, re-exposing the latent race. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as App Mod extension
(activate) participant EH as extHostLanguageModelTools participant MT as mainThreadLanguageModelTools
$registerTool participant Svc as LanguageModelToolsService participant EP as ExtensionPointHandler
(registerToolData) Ext->>EH: vscode.lm.registerTool('appmod-install-appcat', impl) EH->>MT: $registerTool(id) MT->>Svc: registerToolImplementation(id, impl) Note over Svc: ⚠️ Root cause:
_tools has no entry yet —
data contribution not processed Note over Svc: 💥 Error thrown:
Tool "appmod-install-appcat"
was not contributed. EP-->>Svc: registerToolData(id) arrives later (too late) ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts` | crash site + root cause (fixed) | L384-L386 (pre-fix): `const entry = this._tools.get(id); if (!entry) { throw new Error(\`Tool "\$\{id}" was not contributed.\`); }` | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadLanguageModelTools.ts` | trigger (RPC) | L93: `$registerTool` calls `registerToolImplementation(id, ...)` from the fire-and-forget extHost RPC | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/languageModelToolsContribution.ts` | producer of tool data | L289: `languageModelToolsService.registerToolData(tool)` runs from the extension-point handler's `setHandler` delta | | `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts` | trigger origin | L344-L346: `registerTool` immediately calls `_proxy.$registerTool(id, ...)` during extension activation | ### Repro Steps 1. Install/enable an extension (e.g. App Modernization) that both declares tools in its `package.json` `languageModelTools` contribution and calls `vscode.lm.registerTool('appmod-install-appcat', impl)` early in `activate()`. 2. Cause the extension to activate through a non-tool path so its `activate()` runs before `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler` has processed that extension's contribution delta. 3. The main thread executes `registerToolImplementation('appmod-install-appcat', ...)` while `_tools` has no entry for the id, and throws `Tool "appmod-install-appcat" was not contributed.` into error telemetry. Note: this is an activation-ordering race, so it reproduces intermittently depending on extension activation timing relative to extension-point delta delivery. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts`: - `registerToolImplementation(id, tool)` no longer throws when `_tools` has no entry for `id`. Instead it buffers the implementation in a new `_pendingToolImpls` map and returns a disposable that cleans up whether the impl is still pending or has since been attached. A second pending implementation for the same id still throws `already has an implementation`, preserving the duplicate-registration signal. - `registerToolData(toolData)` now checks `_pendingToolImpls` after inserting the entry and attaches any buffered implementation to the newly created entry. This fixes the **data producer's ordering problem at the producer/consumer boundary in the service**, not at a crash-site guard: the two registration halves (data from the extension-point handler, implementation from the extHost RPC) can arrive in either order, and the service now makes the unsupported order representable and self-healing. This mirrors the invoke path, which already tolerates the reverse race (it activates the extension and re-reads `_tools` for the impl at `languageModelToolsService.ts:584`). The genuinely-missing-tool signal is still preserved everywhere it matters: `invokeTool` still throws `Tool was not contributed` when neither data nor impl ever arrives, so a typo'd id surfaces at invocation time via the existing telemetry path rather than being silently swallowed. **Alternatives considered:** - Re-adjusting the extension-point handler's lifecycle phase again (as PR #326651 did) — rejected because the handler is already at `BlockStartup` and the race is between a *per-extension* contribution delta and that same extension's activation, which phase ordering cannot serialize. - Wrapping the `$registerTool` RPC in try/catch at the main-thread boundary — rejected because it swallows the error at the crash site and hides genuine missing-contribution cases from telemetry instead of fixing the ordering. ### Recommended Owner ``@bhavyaus`` — owner of the language-model tools area and author of the prior fix for this exact error family (PR #326651). Active in `microsoft/vscode` within the last 90 days (commits through 2026-10-01) and holds write access.

pull_requests.title: Agent Host: replace unacknowledged send_message queued messages and keep the session model
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #339099

## Summary

When sessions talk to each other, the sender now reads the latest state and keeps one complete, up-to-date message in the target. Before, each `send_message` or `send_remote_message` call to a busy chat queued another unread message. Editing a queued cross-session message also shows the session's model in the picker instead of **Auto**.

### A follow-up replaces the sender's unacknowledged message

- If the target chat is busy and the sending chat already has a queued message there that hasn't started, the new message replaces it instead of queuing another turn. Both tool descriptions tell the model to write one complete message that reflects the current state, not only what changed.
- `get_session_context` returns the caller's undelivered message in full as `yourUndeliveredMessage`. Only the caller's own message is included; other senders' and user-queued messages are not.
- Both tools return the replaced text (`send_message` in its result text, `send_remote_message` as `replacedMessage` with status `replaced`), so the agent can see whether it dropped anything it still needs.
- The message keeps its ID, place in the queue, origin, model, and agent, and its delegation metadata points at the sender's latest turn. Attachments are kept, but their text ranges are removed because they pointed into the old text.
- **Fallback when the message already started:**
  - Local `send_message` reads and replaces in one synchronous host step, so it either replaces the waiting message or queues a new one.
  - Remote `send_remote_message` reuses the waiting message's ID. `ChatPendingMessageSet` is an upsert, so if the host started the earlier message before the replacement arrived, the replacement is queued as a new message. Nothing is lost or delivered twice, and the host needs no protocol change.
  - The router reports `replaced` only when the earlier message was still waiting. If it saw the message start or get removed first, it reports `queued`.
- **User edits:** editing a queued message in VS Code re-sends it as a new user message, so after a user edit the agent's follow-up queues separately instead of overwriting the user's change.

### Model handling

- Agent-sent queued messages carry no model, as before, so each runs on whatever model the target chat is using when it starts and never switches it. This matches the immediate-send path, which has never set a model. (An earlier revision of this PR filled in a model when the message was queued. That was removed because it could go stale: a reordered queue, a provider fallback, or a model becoming unavailable would make delivery switch models or fail the turn.)
- Inline-editing any request with no recorded model now starts on the conversation's current model and configuration, such as Opus 5.5 · xHigh · 1M, instead of the inline editor's default, Auto. Before, resubmitting that edit switched the chat to Auto and broke the prompt cache.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, start a long-running task in session **B** with a non-default model, for example Opus 5.5 · xHigh · 1M.
2. From session **A**, ask the agent to `send_message` session B, then send an update while B is still busy.
3. B shows one queued message from A containing only the latest complete message, and A's result includes the text it replaced.
4. From A, call `get_session_context` on B. The result includes `yourUndeliveredMessage`.
5. Edit that queued message (pencil icon). The model picker shows B's model, not Auto.
6. Let B finish. The message runs as one turn on B's model, and A's next message queues a fresh message.
7. Repeat steps 2–3 across hosts with `send_remote_message`. The second call reports `"status":"replaced"`.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/{sessionServerTools,serverToolGroups,agentService,agentSideEffects}.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/remoteSessions/test/{browser,common}/*.test.ts` (files listed explicitly): passed (1217 passing). The remote fallback test fails if the router's "earlier message already left the queue" detection is disabled.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWidget.test.ts`: passed (56 passing). The new inline-edit test fails without the `chatWidget.ts` change.
- `AGENT_HOST_UPDATE_AHP_SNAPSHOTS=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts`: regenerated the 19 Copilot prompt snapshots for the new `send_message` and `get_session_context` descriptions (description lines only). A plain replay run then passed (23 passing).
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/{copilot,claude,codex}AgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep "server tool"`: passed (Copilot 40, Claude 33 + 6 existing skips, Codex 40).
- `node build/checker/layersChecker.ts`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in changed files. The local run, like the type-check step of `valid-layers-check`, reports only pre-existing missing `electron` typings in this worktree.
- `npx eslint` on changed files: clean.
- **Live run with real models** (`validate-ui-scenario`, Code OSS dev build 1.141.0, macOS arm64, local agent host, Copilot): **passed, 7/7 steps**.
  - Session B: Claude Opus 5.5 · High · 1M, running `sleep 240`.
  - Agent A called `send_message` twice, 4 seconds apart, 17 seconds into B's sleep. The second call returned `Message replaced this chat's undelivered queued message (…). Replaced message: PLAN-V1: …`, and `get_session_context` returned `yourUndeliveredMessage: PLAN-V2: …`.
  - B's **Queued** section held exactly one message (PLAN-V2).
  - The inline editor for that message showed `Claude Opus 5.5 · Thinking Level: High, Context Size: 1M`, matching B's picker (not Auto).
  - After the sleep, PLAN-V2 was delivered exactly once ("Sent by another session") and answered. PLAN-V1 was never delivered, and B's model and configuration were unchanged (no model change in `agenthost.log`).
  - Not covered live: the cross-host `send_remote_message` path, which needs a second, remote agent host. It is covered by router tests that use the protocol reducer.

pull_requests.title: codex: avoid read-only flashes when switching chats
pull_requests.body:
Switching from a nested Codex chat to another session and back repeatedly showed “This chat is read-only” while reloading the conversation.

Session switching removes and restores client customizations, marking the native thread for reload. Chat preparation now checks whether the current app-server already owns a loaded thread and leaves pending launch changes for the next send. Unloaded threads still go through the existing writer-ownership check. The Agents window also waits for transcript loading to settle before displaying the generic read-only banner.

### Reproduction

1. Start a Codex workspace session and send a message.
2. Choose **New Chat in This Session** and send a message in that chat.
3. Switch to another session in the sidebar, then return to the nested chat. Repeat.

### Validation

- Added three regression tests; all failed before the fix and passed after it.
- Both affected unit-test suites: **194 passing**.
- Client compilation, TypeScript checking, and ESLint on the four changed files passed.
- Real Code OSS Agents window on macOS: **13 nested-chat switches and 3 main-chat switches**, with no read-only flash after the fix.
- Verified draft preservation, a successful follow-up send, and genuine second-instance writer-lock handling with Retry recovery.

auto_merge.commit_message: Keep an already-loaded Codex thread during readiness checks so switching chats does not apply pending customization reloads. Delay the generic read-only banner until transcript loading settles.

pull_requests.title: Fix reasoning replay for custom OpenAI models without IDs
pull_requests.body:
Custom OpenAI-compatible models that stream `reasoning_content` without a reasoning ID lose it on the next tool request. Preserve that text through language-model prompt grouping and BYOK Chat Completions serialization so each assistant message carries its accumulated reasoning when `thinking` is enabled.

There were two independent ID requirements: the prompt wrapper discarded ID-less thinking, and the endpoint callback required an ID before emitting reasoning. Keep empty completion markers excluded, retain supplied IDs, and preserve the existing non-thinking behavior.

Fixes #338819.

Validation on `909c7c164fcb20484b2aed66c1fb4c47a5937030`:

- **RED → GREEN:** the regression drives standard SSE parsing, the real CustomOAI provider, both language-model wrappers, prompt rendering, the real tool loop, and the next outbound request. Missing/empty-ID cases failed on the pinned base; a serializer-only fix still failed the full-route tests. All **43 focused tests** and **258 neighboring tests** now pass across 11 files. Controls cover early/late IDs, multiple deltas and tool rounds, per-assistant association, empty completion markers, no reasoning, and thinking disabled.
- **Real Code OSS runtime:** built and launched this exact checkout through the launch skill into isolated profiles with unique ports. Configured the legacy `github.copilot.chat.customOAIModels` setting and verified its migration into the real CustomOAI provider. Drove **Local / Agent** from the UI against a local streaming HTTP fixture: **21 requests**, **15 actual `read_file` calls**, six scenarios. The standard case emits `reasoning_content` without `cot_id`, `reasoning_opaque`, or `signature`. Baseline: 12 reasoning comparisons fail; fixed: **all 144 request assertions pass**, including exact accumulated Unicode/whitespace content on the assistant messages paired with the original tool calls.
- Extension TypeScript, changed-file ESLint, a fresh full product build, the normal commit hook, and independent standards/spec reviews passed. Runtime verification used clean production source without temporary probes.

Run the focused regression from the repository root:

```sh
npm --prefix extensions/copilot run test:unit -- \
  src/extension/byok/node/test/openAIEndpoint.spec.ts \
  src/extension/byok/vscode-node/test/customOAIProvider.spec.ts \
  src/extension/conversation/vscode-node/test/languageModelAccessPrompt.spec.ts
```

Runtime responses were scripted; live Kimi/SGLang inference was not performed. Historical replay policy, Messages signature ingestion, and retry lifecycle remain separate work. This PR is independent of #338874, #338878, and #338821.

pull_requests.title: Fix Local agent state after automatic stream retries
pull_requests.body:
When a Local agent response stream drops and the fetcher retries it, the tool-loop callback currently retains the abandoned attempt's reasoning and tool calls. The next request concatenates both attempts, and abandoned calls can execute alongside the successful retry.

Clear the current attempt's reasoning, tool calls, response marker, phase and compaction on `retryReason`. Completed earlier rounds remain intact.

Fixes #338821.

Validation:

- Added nine regressions through the real retry fetcher, SSE parsers, tool loop, tool execution, prompt renderer and outbound serializer. Original production code: eight failures, with the no-retry control passing. Fixed code: all nine pass. Covers repeated filter/network retries, omitted retry fields, cancellation/error and Responses metadata.
- **217 tests passed in 11 targeted/neighboring suites**; extension TypeScript, changed-file ESLint, full `npm run compile` and the normal commit hook passed.
- Launched this checkout using the launch skill in isolated Code OSS profiles. Actual Local/Agent + first-party Copilot/CAPI stack against a synthetic streaming endpoint with TCP disconnects: original `41 + 68 → 109` reasoning becomes exactly `68`; original `123 + 123 → 246` and four tool executions becomes exactly `123` and two successful executions. Completed prior rounds are byte-identical. Repeated retries, no-retry, terminal error and user cancellation controls pass; abandoned tools never execute on the fixed build.
- The runtime used the clean rebuilt production source without probes. Retained local evidence includes reproducible fixture/launch commands, sanitized lengths/SHA-256 hashes/call IDs, independent physical execution counts and an offline verifier.

Runtime limits: verified on macOS with a deterministic CAPI-compatible server and a synthetic execution-counting tool, not live Kimi inference. Responses metadata has real-parser regression coverage. BYOK reasoning ingestion (#338819) and other provider/transports are outside this change.

auto_merge.commit_message:
Reset Local agent attempt state on automatic retries

Clear streamed reasoning, tool calls, response markers, phase, and compaction when the fetcher restarts an attempt. Preserve completed rounds and cover the real retry callback, outbound history, and tool execution.

pull_requests.title: chat: offer Copilot continuation near ChatGPT limits
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Offer an experimental way for dual subscribers to continue existing Codex sessions through Copilot when their ChatGPT five-hour or weekly allowance is at least 90% used.

- Show a notice in the Agents session list or a normal notification in the editor, only in the active window.
- Reuse spotlights to guide users to the exact eligible session, then its model picker. Skip session navigation when it is already active; prefill the exact matching Copilot model without selecting it or sending a message automatically.
- Include externally discovered Codex sessions, exclude archived/Done sessions, and suppress suggestions when no exact selectable model or usable Copilot allowance exists.
- Keep quota eligibility live, including changes to additional-usage permission, managed pooled allowances, and session/weekly limits.

## Experiment and architecture

- Disabled without the `chatgptCopilotContinuation` treatment. The shared `experimentTrigger` event records eligibility before treatment-specific state is checked.
- Add bounded provider attribution to existing turn telemetry and correlate accepted provider switches, so converted sessions can be distinguished from sessions already using Copilot.
- Coordinate suppression across windows locally; permanently stop after a successful guided switch or Don't Show Again. No Settings Sync.
- Use existing Agent Host metadata slots; **no Agent Host Protocol schema changes**.
- The temporary developer command and all quota/experiment/suppression bypasses used for manual testing have been removed.
- Paid individual additional usage remains eligible; blocked managed allowances and Copilot session/weekly limits at 90% usage do not.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed.
- All 26 changed unit-test files — **2,050 passing, 17 pending**.
- ESLint across changed TypeScript files, layer checks, and full-branch whitespace checks — passed.
- Live Code OSS checks on macOS in both editor and Agents windows: row navigation, active-session shortcut, exact model search, explicit Copilot selection, keyboard navigation, Back, and cancellation. Also manually tested by the author.

The UI walkthrough was exercised using temporary instrumentation that is not included in this PR. Production quota and experiment gates are covered by unit tests; no real account was deliberately exhausted.

## Summary

Prevent filenames, configuration values, and error text from implicitly becoming executable notification links.

- Render core notification and progress strings/errors literally. Use nominal `NotificationText` builders for explicitly authored links, including mixed literal/link messages.
- Preserve extension notification behavior through an identity-checked compatibility capability in the two extension API bridges. Restrict access to that capability with ESLint and keep progress RPC DTOs string-only.

## Summary

Adds an experimental **Dev Container Sample** submenu to the Agents workspace picker.

- Offers Go, .NET, Node.js, PHP, Python, and Rust. C++ (Dockerfile) and Java (Feature image build) are deferred.
- Selecting a sample only creates a required-container draft. Trust, cloning, and container provisioning happen on the first prompt, without creating a local backend session.
- Clones directly into the final container's named Docker volume, then runs the sample's lifecycle commands. No bootstrap container is needed.
- Matches the Dev Containers extension's volume naming, legacy volume reuse, repository/container labels, and repository-in-volume editor authority.
- Displays and fetches lowercase `microsoft` URLs while retaining the extension's exact casing in Docker identity labels and volume hashes for compatibility.
- Preserves repository data through restart and container recreation, restores sample providers lazily, and keeps samples out of unsupported remote-host/worktree paths.
- Adds regression coverage and accessibility help. Detects configuration image changes and accepts containers rebuilt with the Dev Containers extension.

The new `chat.agentHost.devContainer.samples.enabled` setting is application-scoped, experimental, and off by default.

1. Start Docker Desktop and open the Agents window.
2. Enable:

   ```json
   {
     "chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled": true,
     "chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled": true,
     "chat.agentHost.devContainer.samples.enabled": true
   }
   ```

3. In the workspace picker, choose **Dev Container Sample**, then a sample.

5. Send the first prompt, accept the workspace trust request, and follow preparation in the Dev Container output channel.
6. Verify the session runs in the sample workspace and **Open in Editor** opens the same repository volume through the Dev Containers extension.
7. Restart/recreate the container and confirm workspace changes survive. Disabling the sample setting should hide the submenu and recent sample choices without stranding existing sessions. Disabling Dev Container hosts, remote hosts, or AI features should also hide sample choices and their accessibility help.
8. Cancel or fail sample preparation after the container starts. Verify the container is stopped without removing the repository volume. A container still used by another VS Code session must remain running.

- Real Docker validation for Node and Python - passed: lifecycle hooks as the configured remote user, exact volume/container labels, stopped-container reuse, recreation from the retained volume, and preservation of workspace edits. Test containers and sample volumes were removed afterward.

pull_requests.title: agent host: overlap provider session startup with the turn-start checkpoint (experiment)
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #339016

## TL;DR

- **What:** on a session's first turn, the provider's SDK session is now created *while* the turn-start checkpoint is captured, instead of after it. Dispatch still waits for both, so checkpoint behavior is unchanged.
- **Gate:** experiment-controlled setting `chat.agentHost.experimental.overlapProviderPreparation`, default **off**, for an ExP rollout. A trigger event marks exposure in both arms.
- **Measured (MSBench A/B, same build, setting off vs on):** time from turn start until the prompt is handed to the runtime drops by **160–240 ms (−20 to −27%) on Windows** and 60–180 ms on Linux.
- **Risk:** low. Providers opt in; a failed preparation falls back to the normal send path; checkpoint ordering is unchanged.

## Why

On a first turn, the agent host waits for the turn-start checkpoint (`git status` and a tree capture), then dispatches. Only then does the Copilot provider create the SDK session (client, customization snapshot, config, create/resume). On Windows each costs 0.3–1 s, and they ran back to back. They don't depend on each other: the provider can't touch the workspace before the prompt is sent, so session creation can run alongside the checkpoint.

## Changes

- **`IAgentChats.prepareTurn(chat, turnId, workingDirectories, context)`**: optional provider hook to set up session state before the send. It must not send a prompt or modify the working tree. Providers that don't implement it behave exactly as before.
- **`AgentSideEffects`**: when the setting is on, starts `prepareTurn` right after the turn's model and agent selection is applied. It runs alongside attachments, contributions and the checkpoint capture, and the dispatch waits for both.
  - A preparation failure is only logged; `sendMessage` then prepares as usual, so errors surface exactly as they do without the overlap.
  - A turn cancelled before dispatch takes the existing checkpoint-discard path.
- **Copilot provider**:
  - `prepareTurn` creates the session for a not-yet-started chat, or resumes the default or peer chat's session, if the chat has no live session. It runs on the same per-chat queue as `sendMessage` and retries a failed plugin sync first, as the send path does.
  - It records which turn it prepared the session for. That turn's `sendMessage` skips the snapshot-based configuration re-check: plugin-sync retry, customization snapshot, `getRestartReason`, disabled root MCP servers. The session was just created with that state. Explicit restart flags and additional-directory changes are still honored. Keying on the turn ID means a cancelled turn's leftover marker can never affect a later turn.
- **Setting**: `chat.agentHost.experimental.overlapProviderPreparation` (application scope, `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`), forwarded to the agent host as the root key `overlapProviderPreparation`. It's a rollout gate, not an enterprise control, so it has no policy entry.
- **Telemetry**:
  - New `sendStageProviderPreparationMs` in `agentHost.turnCompleted`, the OTel `turn_timing` span and `OTEL.md`: the time dispatch still waits for preparation after the overlap, not the preparation's total cost.
  - Provider stage marks made during preparation happen before dispatch, so they don't appear in `providerStage*Ms`.
  - The experiment trigger (`logSettingExperimentTrigger`) fires in both arms once a turn reaches a provider that implements `prepareTurn`. It waits until the workbench has forwarded the assignment context, like `AgentHostGitStateService`.

## Results

MSBench `say_hello` (Linux) and `say_hello_windows` (Windows Server 2022) containers. Both arms use the same build (Insiders `0d30d69` with #339016 and this change) and differ only in the setting. 4 runs per cell. Time from turn start until `session.send()` returns, p50:

| Variant | Off | On | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows, no repo | 611 ms | 449 ms | **−162 ms (−27%)** |
| Windows, large repo (VS Code, 19.6K files) | 1,180 ms | 940 ms | **−240 ms (−20%)** |
| Linux, no repo | 580 ms | 398 ms | **−182 ms (−31%)** |
| Linux, large repo | 710 ms | 650 ms | −60 ms (−8%) |

- Every "on" run reported `sendStageProviderPreparationMs`, so the treatment applied in all of them.
- Turn start → first model call moves the same way (−192 ms Windows no repo, −243 ms Linux no repo). End-to-end time to first progress also drops on Windows (−0.75 to −0.94 s p50), but model latency varies too much to separate at 4 runs per cell.
- **Dispatch happens later in the "on" arm** (+64 to +170 ms) because preparation moved before it, while the post-dispatch provider stages (`create`, `finalize`, `persist`, `snapshot`) disappear. Evaluate the experiment on time to first progress, not `timeToProviderDispatch`.
- **Without the redundant-refresh skip, the overlap gained nothing.** An earlier A/B, before that change, showed no improvement. `sendMessage` re-checked the configuration of the session `prepareTurn` had just created, which cancelled out the overlap.
- **Windows contention:** with a large repo, the checkpoint slows down when it runs alongside session creation (its remaining wait drops only 796 → 482 ms). The remaining checkpoint cost is the next thing to tackle.

pull_requests.body:
Fixes an issue that caused the overlay integration test to fail intermittently on macOS.

Copying Git’s index on macOS/Linux gives it a newer modification timestamp, defeating Git’s racy-clean detection and potentially omitting same-size working-tree edits from snapshots.

- Preserve the original index timestamps when copying to the temporary index.
- Add a deterministic regression test for same-size edits, verifying that the real index remains unchanged.
- Keep the existing overlay test enabled and retain the index-copy optimization.

## Summary

Fix three persistent chat-progress lifecycle issues:

- Do not show "This is taking a little longer than usual" while a foreground terminal, another tool invocation, or a progress task is still active. Preserve the existing background-work handling and restart the inactivity window when work finishes.
- Use the latest intersection entry when visibility changes are batched, preventing an outdated hidden state from leaving the Draw animation paused.
- Observe response completion directly so retained progress hides and its inactivity timer stops on completion or cancellation, without waiting for another render or hover.

Includes regression tests for the 90-second threshold, completion/cancellation, response reopening, batched visibility changes, and real DOM hide/show/remounts. Updates chat accessibility help to describe the corrected inactivity behavior.

## Validation

- Focused Electron tests below - **125 passed**.
- Changed-file ESLint below - passed.
- Commit hygiene hook - passed for all five changed files.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - attempted; blocked by existing Copilot SDK and local-transcription dependency type mismatches outside this change. No diagnostics in the changed files.

<details>
<summary>Exact focused test and lint commands</summary>

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWorkingLogo.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts \
  --grep 'ChatWorkingLogo|persistent progress|persistent footer|working progress|retained progress|working phrase' \
```

Result: all five files passed.

</details>

## Recorded UI verification

All six UI checks passed in an isolated macOS arm64 Code OSS 1.141.0 dev window, using the production chat renderer with a locally simulated terminal tool and real-time waits (no external model or terminal command):

1. Show the foreground terminal tool and verify the Draw SVG paths change.
2. Keep it active for **96.1 seconds**: 90 checks found no false inactivity warning.
3. Switch away from and reopen the chat editor three times: Draw resumes each time.
4. Complete the response with the pointer outside the response: progress clears without hovering.
5. Start an idle response with no active tools: the warning appears at **90.28 seconds**, while the previous completed response stays clear.
6. Complete the idle response: neither completed response retains progress or an active logo.

Captioned FFmpeg recordings and the per-step report were verified locally; the videos are not attached to this PR.

pull_requests.title: Engineering - Fix macOS CI build to run only ARM64 CLI job
pull_requests.body:
This pull request addresses a regression in the macOS CI build configuration by ensuring that only the ARM64 CLI job is executed. 

Changes made:
- Removed the x64 CLI job from the CI-only macOS stage in `product-build.yml`.
- Preserved the existing x64 and ARM64 CLI jobs for non-CI product builds.

The regression occurred due to the recent changes in the CI pipeline, which inadvertently included both architecture jobs in the CI stage. The fix has been validated, confirming that the CI `macOS` stage now correctly runs only the ARM64 CLI job, while the product stages retain their respective jobs.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: honor identity capture policy in host telemetry
pull_requests.body:
Admins can already control identity capture for the Local harness. This change applies the same policy to VS Code's own Agent Host telemetry, which is exported separately from the Copilot runtime.

- **Identity disabled:** omit governed identity fields before host storage and export.
- **Identity enabled:** include the OS username and hostname in host-generated telemetry, and preserve provider-supplied identity.
- **Enterprise policy wins** over personal configuration and inherited environment variables. Enabling identity capture does not enable telemetry or content capture.

**Existing-user impact:** identity capture is off by default. Explicitly supplied identity attributes that previously passed through the host are now removed unless capture is enabled.

Settled enterprise policy changes automatically restart the desktop Agent Host. Personal changes require a manual restart. Already stored or exported data is unchanged.

This covers the VS Code-owned pipeline, not every runtime's direct exports, and does not add authenticated account attribution ([copilot-agent-runtime#24299](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/24299)). Once the runtime fix lands and is bundled in VS Code, account attribution on runtime-generated spans should flow through automatically when both the runtime and host allow identity capture.

Refs #336814.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

pull_requests.title: sessions: hide stalled queued sandbox sessions
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Hide apparently never-started sandbox tasks from the core sandbox session lists using metadata already fetched during discovery. This is separate from #339031, which fixes sandbox/local task misclassification in the extension-based Cloud provider.

An entry is filtered only when all of these conditions hold:
- Its task title is exactly `New remote session` and its task state is `queued`.
- It has exactly one session, also still `queued`.
- The session has no reported `ahp_resource_uri`.
- Valid session creation and modification timestamps are identical.
- The session is at least one hour old, using the task-list response clock when available.

Missing or invalid evidence, a different title, multiple sessions, a reported AHP resource, or session progress keeps the entry visible. Offline status alone is not a filtering signal.

Cache the candidate creation time and reevaluate it on incremental scans even outside the update window, without additional detail requests. Report filtered task IDs as explicit removals for incremental/partial reconciliation. A later discovery update can restore a session that starts successfully. Existing reconciliation persists removals so filtered rows do not return from startup inventory; unverified cached rows remain until successful discovery confirms the filter. Connected and locally provisioning environments retain existing protections.

This does not connect to or wake sandboxes, read their histories, delete/archive service records, or change their service-reported activity state. It does not blanket-hide all generic titles or attempt to identify deleted compute. The two recent investigated stalled records match this heuristic; the older July records are not assumed to match.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed, including core TypeScript checking. Missing workspace dependencies were restored with `npm install`; no manifests or lockfiles changed. An initial compile identified a missing test import, which was fixed before the successful run.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts --grep "CloudSandbox"` — passed, 127 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed before committing; commit hygiene also passed.

Regression coverage includes the exact one-hour boundary, incomplete evidence, progressed sessions, server/local clock handling, cached incremental expiration, recovery, partial discovery, and removal across inventory restoration. No live UI verification was run.

(Written by Copilot)

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

All Cloud Sandbox sessions discovered through Mission Control should be non-external, including sessions created elsewhere and later discovered by VS Code.

This intentionally changes the sandbox-specific provenance policy introduced in [#338658](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338658). That policy classified sessions as external unless the current VS Code profile created, imported, or continued them. Mission Control discovery should instead surface these sessions as ordinary cloud sessions regardless of the creating client.

- Override Cloud Sandbox external-session classification with a constant non-external state across discovery, opening, host updates, disconnection, and cached restoration.
- Remove profile-local creation/adoption tracking and its request listeners and storage writes. Previously persisted provenance keys are no longer consulted.
- Preserve host-reported external-session classification for ordinary remote hosts.
- Update the provider contract documentation and regression tests, including cross-profile rediscovery and host metadata that reports a session as external.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep 'CloudSandboxSessionsProvider'` — passed, **30 tests**.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/cloudSandboxSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed before committing; pre-commit hygiene passed.
- `npm run compile-client` — blocked before source compilation by an existing dependency mismatch: the manifest declares Copilot runtime `1.0.90`, while the installed `@github/copilot-sdk` bundles `1.0.89-1`.
- Live Mission Control UI testing was not run.

## How to test

1. Discover a Cloud Sandbox session created outside the current VS Code profile. Verify it appears as non-external in the Agents Window sessions list.
2. Open and connect to the session; verify it remains non-external and does not show external-session onboarding.
3. Disconnect and reload; verify the cached session remains non-external.
4. Verify ordinary remote-host sessions still respect host-reported external-session classification.

(Written by Copilot)

## Summary

Enable the Agents Window to consume compatible VS Code Agent Host and copilotd metadata through host-neutral, domain-specific helpers.

- Separate host implementations into private `meta/vscode` and `meta/copilotd` folders, with public dispatch helpers and an ESLint import boundary.
- Integrate message, attachment, tool output, error, model, usage, and context metadata into the existing features. Preserve VS Code behavior, avoid mixing metadata sources, and emit compatible outgoing representations where an equivalent exists.
- Recognize host-advertised session/model schema keys for approval, workspace/worktree, base branch, reasoning, context, and Auto routing. Write the advertised keys rather than sending both aliases.
- Preserve expanded-prompt display metadata across ordinary retries, interrupted turns, steering, and restoration. Keep current occupancy separate from turn tokens and refresh the latest restored response while idle.

## Generated contracts and tests

Keep the generated declarations checked in, but do not vendor the schemas or a standalone license file. A small source pin records the upstream commit; explicit regeneration reads that commit from a supplied local checkout without fetching or changing it. The only retained upstream inputs are the conformance test fixtures, located beside the compiled tests and copied by the normal build. Ordinary builds and tests do not require the Copilot host checkout or network access.

Add a basic public-helper compatibility matrix, 24 controlled-peer wire-to-feature tests through the real protocol client and registered production handler, and regression coverage for the actual Chat retry/model paths and steering persistence. The upstream vector runner executes 109 client cases from 17 fixture files.

## Validation

- `env -u COPILOT_HOME ./scripts/test.sh --runGlob '{**/platform/agentHost/test/common/*.test.js,**/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.js,**/platform/agentHost/test/node/{copilotMetadataConformance,chatContributions,sessionDatabase,copilotAgentSession,copilotAgent,mapSessionEvents,copilotSlashCommand,copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider,proxyChatError,copilotSdkChatError,copilotToolDisplay,copilotNonPtyShellTerminals,copilotShellTools,copilotFailureTelemetry,localAgentHostMetadata}.test.js,**/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/*.test.js,**/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/{chatErrorMessages,chatService/chatService,model/chatModel,attachments/chatDraft}.test.js,**/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentHostUsageSidecar.test.js,**/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/**/*.test.js,**/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/{remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider,cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution}.test.js}'` — 6,181 passed, 17 existing pending.
- `npm run agent-host:check-copilot-meta -- --source "$COPILOT_HOST_CHECKOUT"` — passed against the pinned upstream checkout.

The test process omits the agent session's inherited `COPILOT_HOME` so mocked home directories remain isolated. Explicit override tests are included. Validation was on macOS; live two-host and Windows/Linux runs were not performed.

Latest `main` (`072617082f2`) has been merged in `b8d230a1138`, resolving the conflict-blocked checks. pull_requests.title: github: add explicit anonymous public reads
pull_requests.body:
Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678
Related issues: #174474, #205732, #283249

Adds explicit anonymous public reads to the reusable GitHub engine and migrates Issue Reporter similar-issue searches as the first consumer.

- `acquireAnonymousClient` exposes API-relative JSON GET requests for an approved HTTPS API base. It never selects an account, resolves `/user`, prompts for authentication, or falls back from an authenticated failure.
- Anonymous requests omit authorization, ambient credentials and referrers. Public caches and coalescing remain isolated from authenticated clients, while sharing the engine's admission limits, deadlines, bounded retries and anonymous-origin cooldowns.
- Reference-counted anonymous clients share the existing client-capacity bound. Disposal cancels their work without resetting a live server cooldown.
- Both wizard and legacy/web Issue Reporters use the client with ten-second search deadlines. The existing workbench engine registration is also loaded by the shared Agents entrypoint.
- Both legacy search backends share cancellation/generation ownership. Stale duplicate responses cannot cancel a newer GitHub query, Marketplace description edits do not start product duplicate searches, and failed searches cannot leave the previous query's results visible.

Cloud exports and the AHP log viewer now find the matching transcripts and locally forwarded host logs without assuming Copilot CLI's filesystem layout. Remote bundle collection remains best-effort when the host does not implement the VS Code-specific method.

Tests cover provider-neutral host matching, disconnected exports, reconnect/rotation history, excluding unrelated hosts, and complete bidirectional relay messages without framing or duplicate deliveries.

pull_requests.title: editor: align connected tab geometry across wrapped states
pull_requests.body:
Connected tabs drift between single-row, wrapped, pinned, and scrolled states: wrapped rows use different visible heights, shoulder/body joins can cross the separator, and the separate-row Unpin action sits closer to its pill edge than an ordinary Close action. This aligns those states around shared geometry while preserving each tab style's intended shape.

## Changes

- Keep wrapped tab hitboxes at the same height on every row, with upper rows remaining separate pills and only the bottom row joining the editor.
- Use the Inner radius tier for connected caps and upper pills, preserve the editor frame's Outer radius, and keep action controls on the Control tier.
- Share the separator slot and bottom-row connected geometry between wrapped and single-row tabs.
- Keep sticky/clipped viewport masks opaque and rounded without seams or content leaking behind compact pinned tabs.
- Share upper-pill action reservation and positioning across wrapped and separate pinned rows so Unpin, Close, and modified targets have matching clearance.
- Curate the production tab fixtures around layout/configuration contracts rather than transient hover/focus states.

## Testing

1. Enable Modern UI and select the Connected editor tab style.
2. Open enough editors to wrap. Verify every tab row has the same hitbox height, upper rows remain separate pills, and the bottom selected tab joins the editor with a continuous separator/shoulder tangent.
3. Switch between default and compact tab height. Verify close and modified targets remain centered without changing row height.
4. Enable normal pinned tabs and show Unpin actions. Compare inline, wrapped, and separate pinned rows; Unpin and Close use equal 20px targets with matching edge and vertical clearance.
5. Move tab actions to the left. Verify the same clearance contract on the leading edge.
6. Switch to Pill and Legacy tab styles. Verify their existing disconnected/legacy geometry is unchanged.
7. Exercise sticky compact tabs and horizontal scrolling. Verify the clipped selected cap is rounded and scrolled content does not leak through the sticky viewport.
8. Repeat in Dark, Light, Dark High Contrast, and Light High Contrast themes.

## Validation

- 119 targeted Modern UI and multi-editor tab tests
- ESLint, stylelint, and `git diff --check`
- 98 curated tab fixtures stable and error-free
- The targeted editor-tabs Playwright fixture spec passes all 3 interaction tests
- Expanded theme coverage is applied consistently to all three Tab Styles references and the Wrapped/Default density reference; other layouts use default Dark and Light
- Native Code OSS scenario covering wrapped upper/bottom rows, dirty state, and pinned action geometry

## Related work

- Addresses the unequal connected-tab height and outline feedback in #336320.
- Related to #336898, but does not change the Agents Window editor-toolbar/layout-action overlap described there.
- Coordinates with #338796, which owns legacy color customization and divider semantics in several of the same files. #338796 should land first; this PR should then be rebased while preserving its theme/divider ownership and applying these geometry/action changes on top.
- A read-only merge simulation against #338796 reports a content conflict in `connectedEditorTabs.css` and a rename/modify conflict on the former `editorTabBar.fixture.ts` path; the overlapping layout TypeScript and test files auto-merge.

pull_requests.title: chat: Enforce managed plugins and auto-install repository plugins
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #336858.

Companion runtime/SDK PR: github/copilot-agent-runtime#24246

## Summary

VS Code consumes one runtime-owned plugin preparation lifecycle with two distinct policy outcomes:

- **Managed `enabledPlugins: true`:** install automatically, enforce globally—even for workspaceless or untrusted sessions—and fail closed if the plugin cannot be installed and activated.
- **Trusted repository `enabledPlugins: true`:** auto-install for that workspace on a best-effort basis; warn and continue if installation fails.

Implementation details:

- Invoke `plugins.ensureRequired` once without a workspace to enforce managed requirements, then once per trusted active workspace/session root to apply repository settings.
- Keep settings precedence, managed composition, marketplace restrictions, installation, live source resolution, and final activation verification in the Copilot runtime.
- Publish exact persisted or live plugin roots consistently to Copilot, Claude, and Codex.
- Keep managed- and repository-only installations globally disabled in runtime state; managed provenance forces and locks effective enablement, while repository activation remains workspace-scoped.
- Keep managed plugins visible and locked even if the user disables ordinary plugin integration.
- Project repository `false` without mutating global state.
- Block initial customization resolution and later turns when managed requirements are unavailable; recover after a successful retry.
- Never block for repository auto-install failures; remove stale workspace publication and surface runtime warnings instead.
- Use the runtime snapshot fingerprint to suppress unnecessary plugin rediscovery and provider refreshes.
- Gate the optional namespaced Agent Host extension on `vscode.ensureRequiredPlugins` so non-VS Code hosts remain interoperable.

VS Code owns active roots, workspace trust, change triggers, user-facing errors, and cross-provider publication. It does not parse marketplace semantics or add another update scheduler.

## Dependency

- [ ] Bump `@github/copilot-sdk` after the companion `plugins.ensureRequired` API is published. Current VS Code `main` uses 1.0.16.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed against the declared SDK 1.0.16 after removing the validation overlay.
- Targeted ESLint — passed.
- Focused Agent Host/workbench suite — 418 tests passed.
- `npm run compile` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Cross-host recorded evidence: 11/11 scenarios and 18/18 steps passed on Code OSS Dev 1.141.0, macOS arm64.

pull_requests.title: Strip the command echo from scraped run_in_terminal output for multi-line commands
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #<issue>

## Problem

When `run_in_terminal` can't use `TerminalCommand.getOutput()`, it reads the buffer between its own markers with `getContentsAsText` and removes the echo with `stripCommandEchoAndPrompt`. That always happens without shell integration (`NoneExecuteStrategy`). With basic or rich shell integration it happens when there is no finished command, or when `getOutput()` returns `undefined`, for example because the command printed nothing ([terminalCommand.ts#L130](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f5f73df304d9c5eeab64d4d07eed57e007742a92/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/capabilities/commandDetection/terminalCommand.ts#L130)).

In that path a multi-line command such as a heredoc comes back with the prompt and its whole echo, and long lines are split at the terminal width. Chat tool terminals that were never shown use the [80x30 fallback size](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f5f73df304d9c5eeab64d4d07eed57e007742a92/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts#L711-L717), so lines wrap early. With bash 5.2 and shell integration off, this heredoc returns:

```
user@host:~/src $ cat > /tmp/hello.py <<'EOF'
import sys
print('hello from', sys.version_info[:2])
EOF
python3 /tmp/hello.py
hello from (3, 12)
```

With this change it returns `hello from (3, 12)`, and a heredoc that only writes a file returns `Command produced no output` instead of its echo. Seen on 1.139.1 with zsh on macOS and 1.133.0 with bash on Linux; the code is unchanged on `main`.

## Root cause

1. [`XtermTerminal.getContentsAsText`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f5f73df304d9c5eeab64d4d07eed57e007742a92/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/xterm/xtermTerminal.ts#L393-L408) joins every buffer row with `\n` and ignores `isWrapped`. `TerminalCommand.getOutput()` already joins soft-wrapped rows.
2. [`findCommandEcho`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f5f73df304d9c5eeab64d4d07eed57e007742a92/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/strategyHelpers.ts#L200-L209) removes the newlines from the output and looks for the command with `indexOf`. A multi-line command still contains its newlines, so it never matches.
3. A long command line can be broken into rows that aren't marked as soft-wrapped, and the space at the break can be dropped (zsh does this, and ConPTY appears to). The echo then doesn't contain the command verbatim.

## Fix

- `getContentsAsText` joins soft-wrapped rows, using the same approach as `getOutput()`. Its only production callers are the three execute strategies.
- When the exact match fails, `findCommandEcho` can match the echo ignoring whitespace. This covers multi-line echoes, row breaks that dropped a space, and the blank cell a wide character leaves when it doesn't fit at the end of a soft-wrapped row. The match must start on the first line, after the prompt, so it can't reach into the output: `ls -l` doesn't match `skills-lock.json` further down a listing. It is a single linear pass.
- This match is opt-in. The strategies enable it only for buffer contents read from a live start marker. Two cases keep the existing exact and suffix matching ([richExecuteStrategy.ts#L214](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f5f73df304d9c5eeab64d4d07eed57e007742a92/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/richExecuteStrategy.ts#L214), [basicExecuteStrategy.ts#L266](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f5f73df304d9c5eeab64d4d07eed57e007742a92/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/basicExecuteStrategy.ts#L266)):
  - `getOutput()` results, which start after the echo;
  - buffer contents read from line 0 because the start marker was trimmed or never created.

  The second pass, which looks for a re-echo, still requires an exact match.

If this match finds nothing, the output is the same as on `main`.

## Tests

- **`strategyHelpers.test.ts`:**
  - a multi-line echo is stripped, with and without output;
  - echoes whose row breaks dropped a space or added a wide-character padding cell are stripped;
  - no match is made outside the first line, or for `getOutput()` output.
- **`noneExecuteStrategy.test.ts`:** a multi-line echo is stripped end to end, and nothing is matched ignoring whitespace when the start marker was trimmed.
- **`xtermTerminal.test.ts`:** soft-wrapped rows are joined, and the join stops at an end marker.

On `main`, the stripped, end-to-end and join tests fail. With the fix:
- the `chatAgentTools` and `contrib/terminal` test globs pass;
- typecheck, eslint and hygiene are clean.

I also replayed bash 5.2 and zsh 5.9 pty captures through `@xterm/headless` to check the change.

## Known gaps (not in this PR)

- **Pastes taller than the terminal.** bash 5.2 draws the lines that don't fit over each other on the bottom row. zsh draws `>....` and then only the last lines. The echo is incomplete, so it still leaks as it does today. I can follow up with a fix.
- **A zsh right prompt drawn after the first line** of a multi-line command still splits the echo, so it leaks as it does today.
- **Trailing prompts** that the existing patterns don't know stay at the end of the output, for example zsh's `user@host dir %` and oh-my-zsh's `➜  dir git:(main) ✗`.
- **macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2** has no bracketed paste and echoes `> ` continuation prompts, so its echo still doesn't match. Output is unchanged.
- **No output with shell integration.** When the executed and end markers are on the same line, the strategies could return empty output without scraping. That needs care where markers misfire.
- **Untested locally:** fish, pwsh, and Windows/ConPTY.

pull_requests.title: chat: preserve enterprise controls during Agent Host migration
pull_requests.body:
The Local harness is being deprecated in favor of Agent Host, backed by the Copilot SDK. Rollout has started, but some existing VS Code enterprise policies need translation into the SDK's Unified Managed Settings so enterprise controls remain intact during the transition. ## What this PR does - **Enables supported legacy policy conversion by default.** Removes the separate bridge opt-in, `chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings`. When rollout or explicit selection chooses Copilot Agent Host, supported restrictions carry over automatically. Native terminal restrictions, including global user settings, still require approval under Allow All/assisted approval. - **Adds applied-policy readiness diagnostics.** Run **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** from the Command Palette to see conversion/enforcement coverage, source, impact, and remaining gaps. Separates unsupported requirements from source/path-dependent coverage needing verification; excludes unconfigured policies and preserves existing diagnostic sections. Policy gaps appear in diagnostics but do not block Agent Host rollout. Existing rollout behavior is unchanged, and supported policy restrictions remain enforced. Scope: Copilot Agent Host on this machine, not certification of remote hosts or other providers. Refs #332011, #337536, #337537. ## Accepted gaps (report-only) Accepted for this PR's rollout posture, not reclassified as enforced or treated as individual administrator consent. Source/path-dependent findings may already be enforced by runtime-native settings. OTel is implemented; its entries concern remaining forwarding, precedence, and runtime coverage. Its policies also reference `github.copilot.chat.otel.enabled`, `github.copilot.chat.otel.exporterType`, `github.copilot.chat.otel.captureIdentity`, and `github.copilot.chat.otel.headers`. **Merged identity fix:** Host identity capture is fixed by [#339045](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339045), merged into `main`. This is not a claim of release availability. **Sandbox scope update:** [#339396](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339396) proposes rolling back the mandatory legacy sandbox requirement added by [#339144](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339144), deprecating the legacy sandbox settings/device policies, and marking the four retired policies `notApplicable`. That follow-up is not yet merged. The supported Agent Host enterprise contract uses native Copilot managed settings; legacy sandbox lifecycle and auto-approval are no longer outstanding parity obligations. This is a scope retirement, not an enforcement fix: after the rollback, `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` can supply an overridable default but cannot guarantee sandboxing. Use managed `sandbox.enabled: true` for that guarantee. Local behavior and native managed enforcement remain unchanged. | Policy / setting | Remaining impact | |---|---| | `ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval` / `chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval` | Bypass is disabled for excluded tools, but per-tool confirmation is not guaranteed through other approval paths. | | `ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove` / `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove` | Native shell asks are covered; custom-terminal coverage is incomplete (`chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled`). | | `ChatMCP` / `chat.mcp.access` | Independent runtime discovery can escape workbench access filtering. | | `ChatAllowedMcpServers` / `chat.mcp.allowedServers`
`ChatDeniedMcpServers` / `chat.mcp.deniedServers`
`ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly` / `chat.mcp.allowManagedServersOnly` | VS Code-only restrictions do not reach every forwarded, discovered, or built-in server path. | | `McpEnterpriseManagedAuthIdp` / `mcp.enterpriseManagedAuth.idp` | Forwarded authentication lacks Local's enterprise IdP lookup; SSO may fail. | | `ChatPluginsEnabled` / `chat.plugins.enabled`
`ChatEnabledPlugins` / `chat.plugins.enabledPlugins` | Independent discovery and customization paths can bypass disablement or required-plugin decisions. | | `ChatExtraMarketplaces` / `chat.plugins.extraMarketplaces`
`ChatStrictMarketplaces` / `chat.plugins.strictMarketplaces` | Runtime-owned operations lack VS Code-only values; strict lists do not disable installed plugins. | | `ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization` / `chat.customizations.strictPluginOnlyCustomization` | Independent discovery, instructions, and selective lockdown lack equivalent coverage. | | `ChatHooks` / `chat.useHooks`
`ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly` / `chat.hooks.allowManagedOnly` | The Local switch does not disable runtime file hooks; managed-only file-hook/SDK-callback coverage is incomplete or unverified. | | `ChatAgentMode` / `chat.agent.enabled` | Agent Host targets can remain available when agent mode is disabled. | | `CopilotOtelEnabled` / `chat.agentHost.otel.enabled` | Separate destinations/recorders can override disablement. | | `CopilotOtelProtocol` / `chat.agentHost.otel.exporterType` | Inherited OTLP configuration can override exporter selection. | | `CopilotOtelCaptureIdentity` / `chat.agentHost.otel.captureIdentity` | Host identity capture is fixed ([#339045](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339045)); runtime account attribution awaits upstream merge, a bundled runtime roll, and end-to-end verification. No additional VS Code account-identity wiring is expected. | | `CopilotOtelHeaders` / `chat.agentHost.otel.headers` | Missing host forwarding can break authenticated export. | | `ChatAgentNetworkFilter` / `chat.agent.networkFilter`
`ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains` / `chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains`
`ChatAgentDeniedNetworkDomains` / `chat.agent.deniedNetworkDomains` | Legacy allowlists are not mandatory boundaries on native runtime URL/shell paths; supported URL denies and shared VS Code filtering remain. Domain `limitTo` integration is accepted follow-up work, not a landing prerequisite. | *🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

Fixes #338581

Treat full 40-character Git refs as immutable commit pins instead of passing them to `git clone --branch`. pull_requests.title: agent host: attribute provider send latency and trim host-side first turn overhead
pull_requests.body:
## TL;DR

- **New telemetry:** `providerStage*Ms` fields in `agentHost.turnCompleted` and the OTel `turn_timing` span break the time after dispatch into stages, from queue and client start through SDK create/resume to model response. The same breakdown appears in an `[AgentHostFirstProgress]` log line, and the renderer's `[ChatTTFP]` trace lines now carry `epochMs` so the two can be lined up. This is what will explain the Windows first-progress gap in production.
- **Faster first turns:** client startup, session config and project resolution now run in parallel instead of in sequence, and concurrent worktree-isolation git lookups for the same folder share one read.
- **Cheaper checkpoints:** clean repos skip the temp index entirely. Repos with uncommitted changes copy the existing index instead of running `git read-tree`, and fall back to the old path whenever that isn't safe.
- **Measured:** replay E2E TTFP p50 is about 30% lower. On Windows, host overhead before the model call drops about 190 ms. The end-to-end user-visible effect is small, because the larger Windows costs (MCP startup, runtime session creation) are outside this PR.
- **Risk:** low. The provider changes only run independent steps in parallel, and the checkpoint shortcuts produce the same tree or fall back to the old path. Turn ordering is unchanged.


## Why

Agent-host (Copilot CLI) sessions are 40–50% slower to first progress than extension-host sessions, and the gap is mostly on Windows. Today's telemetry stops at "dispatched to the provider", but most of the time is spent after that. So we can't tell how much of it is client startup, customization snapshot, SDK session create/resume, or model latency. This PR adds that breakdown and removes some serial host-side work from the first turn.

## Changes

### Instrumentation
- New `AgentHostProviderSendStage` / `IAgentProviderSendStageRecorder`. The turn tracker records provider stages between dispatch and first progress:
  - `queue`, `refresh`, `client`, `snapshot`, `config`, `create`, `finalize`, `persist`, `turnPrepare`, `modelResponse`
- The stages are emitted as `providerStage*Ms` in `agentHost.turnCompleted` and in the OTel `turn_timing` span, and are documented in `OTEL.md`.
  - A stage that never ran is omitted. A reported `0` means it ran within timer resolution.
- An `[AgentHostFirstProgress]` log line gives the same breakdown for local investigation.
- Copilot marks the stages on every launch path:
  - provisional materialization;
  - default-session resume;
  - peer-chat resume;
  - session launcher config, create and finalize.
- The renderer's `[ChatTTFP] start` / `end` trace lines include `epochMs` (wall-clock), so local traces can be lined up with the host's `[AgentHostFirstProgress]` breakdown. 

### Host-side latency
- **Copilot provider:** these steps now run in parallel:
  - the independent client-start lookups;
  - `_buildSessionConfig` (BYOK, shell tools and custom agents);
  - project resolution, alongside session launch;
  - reading the stored resume metadata, alongside client acquisition.
- **Checkpoint (`captureWorkingTreeAsTree`):**
  - `git status` and `HEAD^{tree}` run in parallel.
  - A clean working tree with a HEAD returns HEAD's tree directly, with no temp index or extra git processes. A clean repo with no commits still uses `write-tree`, so SHA-256 repos get their own empty tree.
  - With uncommitted changes, the temp index is seeded from a copy of the repo's index instead of `git read-tree HEAD`. The index path is resolved with `git rev-parse --git-path index`, so linked worktrees work.
  - The copy is used only when every `git status` entry can be restaged onto it (modified, added or untracked files, and deletions on disk). Staged deletions, renames, copies, conflicts, and files added then deleted (`AD`) fall back to `read-tree`, as does any failure.
- **Checkpoint service:** the baseline-exists check runs alongside the capture.
- **Worktree isolation:** concurrent `_getGitInfo` calls for the same folder share one in-flight read of repository root, current branch and default branch. Once it settles, the next caller reads git again, and a failed read isn't reused. This saves duplicate git processes when session config is resolved several times during startup

## Results

| Measurement | Before → After | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Local replay E2E (recorded model traffic, Windows), TTFP p50 | first turns and follow-ups | **~30% lower** |
| Checkpoint temp-index seeding, local dirty repo (Windows) | `read-tree` 148 ms → index copy 3–4 ms | **−98%** for that step (whole capture ~520 → ~380 ms, **−27%**) |
| Hello A/B, Windows, no repo: dispatch | 453 → 353 ms | **−22%** |
| Hello A/B, Windows, no repo: checkpoint | 406 → 316 ms | **−22%** |
| Hello A/B, Windows, no repo: host overhead before the model call | 1,315 → 1,124 ms | **−15%** |
| Hello A/B, turn start → `send()` returned | Windows 745 → 661 ms; Linux 631 → 439 ms | **−11%** / **−30%** |
| Hello A/B, large-repo variant, turn start → `send()` returned | Windows 1,348 → 1,301 ms; Linux 645 → 618 ms | **−3%** / **−4%** |
| Hello A/B, end-to-end UI TTFP | all variants | within model-latency noise at 3 runs per arm |

This PR is incremental. The larger Windows costs are MCP startup blocking the turn, per-session runtime work and SDK session creation on first send; these are tracked separately.
