pull_requests.title: Avoid unnecessary --numstat diff for incoming changes decorations
pull_requests.body:
## Problem and Context

`GitIncomingChangesFileDecorationProvider.getIncomingChanges()` (in
`extensions/git/src/decorationProvider.ts`) computes the "Incoming Changes"
file badges by calling `repository.diffBetweenWithStats()`. That method runs:

```
git diff --raw --numstat --diff-filter=ADMR -z --find-renames=<threshold>% <ref1>...<ref2> --
```

The only consumer of the result, `collectIncomingChangesFileDecorations()`,
reads only `change.status`, `change.uri`, and `change.originalUri` to pick a
badge glyph (added/deleted/renamed/modified). It never reads the
`insertions`/`deletions` stats that `--numstat` computes, so that work is
always discarded.

This code path runs automatically and without debounce whenever
`historyProvider.onDidChangeCurrentHistoryItemRefs` fires, which happens on
every git write operation and on every VS Code built-in auto-fetch tick
(`git.autofetch`, default every 180s) for any repository whose checked-out
branch has an upstream.

On a large repository backed by a partial-clone or virtualized-filesystem
remote (e.g. GVFS/VFS for Git), `--numstat` forces git to read full blob
content for every added/modified/deleted path in the diff range, and each of
those reads is a lazy network fetch rather than a local disk read. We
measured this directly: on such a repository, incoming ranges touching
several thousand files took 60-200+ seconds and pulled thousands of objects
over the network, purely to compute stats that are then thrown away. Because
the handler isn't debounced, repeated ref-change events can also stack up
multiple concurrent invocations of this work.

## Changes

- `getIncomingChanges()` now calls `repository.diffBetween()` instead of
  `repository.diffBetweenWithStats()`. `diffBetween()` already exists as a
  sibling method, already returns exactly the `Change[]` shape this caller
  needs (status + uri + originalUri), and builds a cheaper diff with no
  `--numstat` and no explicit `--find-renames` flag.
- No other call sites, types, or configuration (e.g. `git.similarityThreshold`,
  rename detection) are touched; `diffBetweenWithStats()` remains available
  and unchanged for its other callers.

## Known gaps and deliberate decisions

- **Rename badge may show as added+deleted instead of renamed, for non-default
  git config** — `diffBetween()` does not pass
  `--find-renames=<git.similarityThreshold>%` the way `diffBetweenWithStats()`
  did, so incoming-change rename detection now falls back to git's own
  `diff.renames` default instead of the user's configured threshold. With
  default git and VS Code settings (`diff.renames` on, 50% threshold on both
  sides) the output is identical either way. Only a repository with
  `diff.renames` explicitly disabled, or a `git.similarityThreshold` far from
  50%, would see a renamed file decorated as separate added (`↓A`) and deleted
  (`↓D`) badges instead of a single renamed (`↓R`) badge. The set of files
  decorated as "incoming changes" is unaffected either way; only the glyph
  choice for renames can differ, and only for non-default configs. This
  tradeoff was evaluated and accepted to avoid reintroducing the
  `--numstat`/blob-hydration cost this PR removes. No follow-up is planned; a
  full fix would mean plumbing `similarityThreshold` into `diffBetween()`,
  which is a separate, larger change.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: materialize draft sessions for the Customizations editor
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

When the Chat Customizations editor is open on a local, untitled Copilot CLI draft, the draft's Agent Host session now starts its provider runtime before the user sends anything. That makes the controls in the editor (MCP start/stop, sign-in, enablement) act on a real runtime instead of failing with "Cannot start an MCP server before the session runtime has been created".

On first send, that same session is promoted into the user's durable session instead of being replaced. Everything else keeps the existing deferred behavior.

## When it happens

The runtime starts only when **all** of these are true:

- The Customizations editor is visible and has an input.
- The active harness is the local Copilot CLI Agent Host (`agent-host-copilotcli`).
- The active session is an untitled draft (`/untitled-…`) on the local host.

It never starts from item queries, slash-command completion, slash-command resolution at send, Agents window sidebar counts, or the migration hint. When the editor hides, closes, or switches session, it cancels its request. Any in-flight creation still completes in the background.

## Draft lifecycle

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Deferred: chat input opens a draft
    Deferred --> Eager: Customizations editor shows the draft
    Deferred --> NewSession: first send (unchanged)
    Eager --> Promoted: first send
    Eager --> NewSession: first send, promotion not possible
    Deferred --> Disposed: draft closed
    Eager --> Disposed: draft closed
    Promoted --> [*]
    NewSession --> [*]
```

| State | Backend session | Runtime | Visible in session list |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deferred | Provisional | Not started | No |
| Eager | Ephemeral, marked as a promotable draft | Started (Copilot CLI) | No |
| Promoted | Same backend session, now durable | Reused | Yes |
| NewSession | New backend session with a fresh ID | Starts on send | Yes |

## Opening Customizations

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Editor as Customizations editor
    participant Custom as AgentHostCustomizationService
    participant Prov as ProvisionalSessionService
    participant Host as AgentService (host)
    participant Copilot as CopilotAgent

    Editor->>Custom: prepareSessionForManagement(draft, token)
    Custom->>Prov: getOrCreate(draft, provider, folder, eagerlyMaterialize)
    Prov->>Host: createSession(ephemeral _meta, eagerlyMaterialize)
    Host->>Host: mark session ephemeral + promotable draft
    Host->>Copilot: createChat (deferred)
    Host->>Copilot: chats.materializeDraft
    Copilot-->>Host: runtime started
    Host-->>Prov: backend URI
    Prov-->>Custom: onDidChange
    Custom-->>Editor: customizations refresh from the new session
```

If the draft already had a deferred session, that session is replaced with a new one (new backend URI). The old one is disposed.

Because the runtime is real, enabled MCP servers may start when the editor opens.

## First send

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[First send on draft] --> B{Draft promotable?}
    B -- yes --> C[Real chat resource reuses the draft's backend ID]
    C --> D[Host promoteSession]
    D --> E[Remove ephemeral and draft markers, register session, emit sessionAdded]
    E --> F[Turn runs on the existing runtime]
    B -- no --> G[Real chat resource gets a fresh ID]
    G --> H[Create durable deferred session]
    H --> I[Dispose draft backend]
    I --> J[Turn materializes the runtime as before]
```

A draft is promotable when its current backend session was created eagerly, still matches the draft's folder, doesn't select worktree isolation, and the host supports `promoteSession`.

In the fallback path, the new session is always created as a normal durable session. It never inherits the draft's ephemeral or eager flags, and the fallback never disposes the session it just created.

## Worktree isolation

Customizations always preview the picked folder. The worktree is always created and used on first send.

- An eager draft starts its runtime in the picked folder even when worktree isolation is selected. The host doesn't reserve a pending worktree for it.
- A draft that selects worktree isolation is never promoted. First send takes the fallback path: a fresh durable session is created with the worktree config, the worktree is created on send, and the draft's runtime is disposed.
- If worktree isolation is selected after the draft's ID was already reused for the send, the send fails instead of running in the folder.
- As a backstop, the host's `promoteSession` rejects sessions whose config selects worktree isolation.

The cost: for worktree drafts, anything started from Customizations (for example MCP servers) isn't reused by the real session.

## Ephemeral sessions vs. promotable drafts

Both are ephemeral on the host, so both stay out of the catalog. Only promotable drafts keep full capabilities, because the promoted session reuses their runtime.

| Behavior | Ephemeral session (inline, terminal) | Promotable draft |
|---|---|---|
| Hidden from the session list, no `sessionAdded` | Yes | Until promoted |
| Tombstoned in the registry, not persisted | Yes | Until promoted |
| Server tools (`create_session`, `send_message`, …) | Ephemeral-enabled only (none today) | Full set |
| Restricted capabilities (`hasRestrictedEphemeralCapabilities`) | Yes | No |
| `promoteSession` | Rejected | Allowed |

Only the host sets the promotable-draft marker (`vscode.chat.promotableDraftSession`), and only when a create request is both ephemeral and `eagerlyMaterialize`. Clients can't use it to opt a throwaway session out of its restrictions.

## API and contract changes

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `IAgentCreateSessionConfig` | `eagerlyMaterialize` (prototype-only): start the runtime during `createSession`. Uses the local extension path, not AHP. |
| `IAgentChats` | Optional `materializeDraft`. Implemented only by `CopilotAgent`. |
| `IAgentService`, `IAgentConnection`, `IAgentHostManagementService` | `promoteSession` (local host only). Returns without changes for durable sessions. Throws for ephemeral sessions that aren't drafts, and for drafts that select worktree isolation. |
| `AgentHostStateManager` | `hasRestrictedEphemeralCapabilities`, used by the server tool host and provider create options. |
| `IAgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService` | `getOrCreate(…, eagerlyMaterialize?)` and `getPromotableBackendSession`. `getOrCreate` now goes through the queue even when a mapping exists, so an existing draft can be upgraded. |
| `IAgentHostCustomizationService` | `prepareSessionForManagement`. No-op except in the editor window's `WorkbenchAgentHostCustomizationService`, which now also depends on `IAgentHostNewSessionFolderService`. |
| `IHarnessDescriptor` | Optional `managementSessionProvider`. Set only by the local Copilot CLI harness. Documented in `src/vs/sessions/AI_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md`. |

## Unchanged

- `whenCustomizationsReady` and `provideChatSessionCustomizations`.
- Drafts that are never shown in the Customizations editor.
- Claude, Codex, remote Agent Hosts, and cloud sandboxes.
- The Agents window, where `prepareSessionForManagement` is a no-op.
- Inline and terminal ephemeral sessions.

## Known gaps

- Opening Customizations while the draft's first deferred session is still being created skips the eager upgrade.
- Upgrading a deferred draft recreates the backend session instead of materializing it in place. The draft is briefly unmapped during the swap, so a send at that moment takes the fallback path.
- If `promoteSession` fails (for example after an Agent Host restart), the send fails rather than falling back.
- Abandoned eager drafts leave their `session.db` on disk.
- A model or custom-agent change between opening Customizations and first send restarts the SDK session inside the same host session.
- There's no capability negotiation: the client assumes a local host with `promoteSession`, and the host checks for `materializeDraft`.

## How to test

1. Launch `./scripts/code.sh --user-data-dir /tmp/code-oss-prototype --log trace` and open a folder.
2. Start a new Copilot CLI (Agent Host) chat, then open Chat Customizations without sending anything.
   - `agenthost.log` shows `[Copilot] Session materialized: copilotcli:/<id>`.
   - MCP server Start works before the first message.
3. Send a message. There's no new `Creating chat` for another ID, the turn runs on the same `<id>`, and the session appears in the session list.
4. Repeat with worktree isolation selected (before or after opening Customizations). The send creates the worktree, uses a new session ID, and the agent works in the worktree.
5. In a draft with Customizations closed, type `/`. There should be no early `Session materialized`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionServerTools.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostStateManager.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentMetaReaders.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostCustomizationService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/workbenchAgentHostCustomizationService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMigrationServiceImpl.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/remoteAgentHostCustomizationHarness.test.ts`: passed (1082 passing, 16 pending)
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts`: 531 passing, 2 failing. The two failures (`… Copilot CLI session reference becomes simple and trajectory attachments`) expect a stubbed home directory but get the real one. They fail the same way on the base commit and are unrelated to this change.
- Manual end-to-end testing in a running Code OSS window has not been done on the final version of this branch.

pull_requests.title: Agent Host: gate Copilot Memory (cloud and local) behind settings
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Adds opt-in [Copilot Memory](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory) for Copilot SDK (Agent Host) sessions.

### Settings (both off by default)
- `chat.copilot.memory.enabled`: enables cloud memory. Sent as `memory: { enabled }` on every session create and resume. Experiment-capable.
- `chat.copilot.memory.local.enabled`: with memory on, stores memories in `.github/copilot-memories.jsonl` via the runtime flag `copilot_swe_agent_memory_in_repo_store`. Changing it restarts the Copilot SDK client after active turns finish, because resident sessions don't reapply feature flags.

Both are forced off when the account disables preview features. Ephemeral sessions, and peer chats under them, never get memory.

### Known limitations (runtime-owned)
- Local memory isn't covered by GitHub's Copilot Memory policies, and doesn't support user-scoped memories or non-GitHub repos.
- The memory file can be included in agent or Agents window commits.
- There's no managed-settings policy key for memory yet.

### How to test
1. Enable `chat.copilot.memory.enabled` in a GitHub repo, ask the agent to remember a convention, and confirm the memory prompt appears.
2. Also enable `chat.copilot.memory.local.enabled` and confirm `.github/copilot-memories.jsonl` is written.

### Validation
- Launcher, settings, startup config and `agentService` unit tests: **passed** (748).
- New and updated `copilotAgent.test.ts` tests: **passed**. The suite's 12 other failures are pre-existing and environment-related.

auto_merge.commit_title: Agent Host: gate Copilot Memory (cloud and local) behind settings (#339005)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* Agent Host: gate Copilot Memory behind chat.copilot.memory.enabled

Adds an off-by-default, experiment-capable setting that controls whether
local Copilot SDK sessions enable Copilot Memory. The value is forwarded
to the agent host root config (like HydraFusion, honoring the preview
features policy) and passed explicitly as `memory: { enabled }` on every
session create and resume so the runtime default cannot enable it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: add chat.copilot.memory.local.enabled for in-repo Copilot Memory

Adds an off-by-default setting that, together with chat.copilot.memory.enabled,
switches Copilot SDK sessions to the runtime's local memory store
(.github/copilot-memories.jsonl) by passing the
copilot_swe_agent_memory_in_repo_store feature flag. The flag is always sent
explicitly so only the VS Code opt-in can switch memory to the local store.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: address Copilot Memory review feedback

- Keep local (in-repo) memory out of Stable and out of experiments: the local
  store skips GitHub's Copilot Memory policy checks, so the forwarder never
  enables it in Stable and the setting is no longer experiment-controlled.
- Skip memory for ephemeral (throwaway) chat sessions, like the other
  heavyweight features they omit.
- Clarify setting text: local memory needs a GitHub-hosted repo and the file
  can be included in agent/Agents window commits; drop the overstated
  "explicitly turned off" claim.
- Cover create, resume, and ephemeral launches and the Stable gate in tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: make local Copilot Memory a user-visible opt-in

Local memory is a Copilot SDK harness opt-in, so expose it in all qualities:
drop the Stable gate and the `advanced` tag from both memory settings so users
can find and enable them in the Settings editor. Both remain off by default,
local memory is not experiment-controlled, and the setting text calls out that
GitHub-configured Copilot Memory policies do not apply to the local store.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: restart for local memory changes and keep peer chats ephemeral

- The Copilot runtime does not reapply request feature flags when a resident
  SDK session resumes, so a toggled local memory store could be ignored for
  resident sessions and forks. Add the effective local memory value to
  CopilotAgentStartupConfig so changing it restarts the Copilot SDK client
  after active turns finish, like HydraFusion.
- Peer chats created under an ephemeral session now inherit its ephemeral
  state (AgentService passes isEphemeral to createChat and Copilot sets it on
  peer launch plans), so they skip memory like the owning session.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

pull_requests.title: standardize provider attribution on AH session telemetry
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Overview

### What

Identify the agent implementation associated with chat activity using `provider`: for example, `copilotcli`, `claude`, or `codex`. Local and remote sessions using the same implementation have the same provider, independently of the selected language model.

Adds attribution to workbench session invocation/opening, model-picker lifecycle and configuration changes, custom-agent mode changes, handoffs, instruction collection, and response code-block presentation/copy/insert actions. Workbench attribution reads the registered session contribution's `agentHostProviderId`, preserving hyphenated provider IDs and custom session types. Missing expected attribution is `unknown`; known non-Agent Host sessions and non-agent edit sources omit the field.

Edit-survival detail events replace their top-level `harness` field with `provider`, including the existing GitHub mirror. Internal source metadata, source keys, and protocol markers retain `harness`.

Also fixes `agentHost.instructionsCollected`: it now reads provider from the owning session, not the current chat resource scheme. A Copilot peer conversation whose resource is `ahp-chat://...` therefore reports `copilotcli`, not `ahp-chat`.

### Why

Tracked by the cross-cutting AH-filter item in [microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9096](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9096), alongside [microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9127](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9127). Consistent attribution reduces event-specific query logic and allows the metrics consumer to classify eligible Copilot AH edit reports as CopilotSDK instead of leaving them in N/A.

## Attribution contract

| Surface | Source of `provider` |
|---|---|
| Workbench invocation/opening, mode changes, handoffs, instruction collection | Registered session contribution's `agentHostProviderId` |
| Model-picker open/change/configuration/close | Registered provider captured at picker open |
| Response code-block presentation/copy/insert | Registered provider of the originating response session |
| Edit-survival details | Provider retained in the originating edit's source attribution |
| Host-native `agentHost.instructionsCollected` | Owning backend session's provider, not the conversation URI scheme |

Code-block `codeSuggested` means response text was presented; `codeAccepted` includes copying or inserting that text. These do not establish an Agent Host file-edit accept/reject workflow. `editTelemetry.codeRejected` and the traditional edit-hunk classes are unchanged by this PR; their additional constructor plumbing has been removed.

`copilotSDK/` events retain their namespace as the discriminator. Generic Git/workbench, install/authentication, and provider-agnostic events are not enriched. No `executionHost` field is introduced. This is not a claim that every existing telemetry event has provider attribution.

## Classification and remote privacy

Adds missing `isMeasurement: true` metadata to existing numeric/Boolean fields on touched events: invocation timings, citation/code-block counts, participant-detection flags, workspace/harness-setting flags, `isAgentHostSession`, and `isClaudeAgent`. These values serialize into Kusto `Measures`, not string `Properties`; the classification metadata now documents that distinction. The corrections do not add payload fields or change their values.

Workbench provider attribution is read from registered metadata rather than parsed from connection-specific session-type names. Remote invocation rows collapse connection-specific `sessionType` and `agent` values to `remote-agent-host`. Invocation and code-block telemetry use the existing authority-free session-ID projection. Tests cover a hyphenated canonical provider and check that the private remote hostname is absent from the invocation payload.

## Rollout and query compatibility

**Deploy [metrics compatibility draft 788309](https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/InternalTools/_git/VSCode_Copilot_Metrics/pullrequest/788309) before shipping the edit-field rename.** Consumers must read nonempty `provider` first and fall back to historical `harness` only when provider is absent/empty. Explicit `unknown` must not fall back to an older attribution. The companion also places historical `origin=agentHost, harness=copilotcli` edit reports in CopilotSDK.

This PR does not publish a live metric set or backfill telemetry. Provider segmentation does not repair statistics whose numerators and denominators use differently attributable Git/session/turn events. A regenerated scorecard still needs to verify meaningful CopilotSDK denominators for edit-only commit/focus measures with both historical and new schemas.

## How to test

Latest code follow-up (`2589c50fc90`):

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "instructionsCollected telemetry"
```

**Passed: 5 tests**, including owning-session and peer-chat provider attribution.

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\editTelemetry\test\browser\editTelemetry.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\actions\chatCodeblockActions.test.ts
```

**Passed: 25 tests**, preserving code-block actions and edit telemetry after removing rejection-specific additions. `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run transpile-client` also passed on this revision.

Browser CI-fixture follow-up (`31d27fb0958`, before the scope reduction):

```powershell
npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser webkit --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentSessionsControl.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts --sequential
```

**Passed: 667 tests.** An isolated Electron run covering the reported CI failures passed 136 tests. The broader local Electron run had 11 additional rendering geometry/timing failures; these are not claimed as passing or fixed by this PR.

Live metric publication and regenerated-scorecard validation have not been performed.

auto_merge.commit_title: standardize provider attribution on AH session telemetry (#339003)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* chat: add provider attribution to session telemetry

pull_requests.title: copilot shim: always explain why copilot stopped, and decide verbose mode
pull_requests.body:
@DonJayamanne, these are the decisions Karthik and I made on the open questions about verbose mode, and on the other items we found while combining `combined` and `combined-2`. Push back on anything you disagree with.

## Verbose-mode decisions (this PR)
| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Should outcomes that end `copilot` without running the CLI be silent without verbose? | No. Each prints one short line (`write_message`). This covers: the policy block (exit 10); no terminal (127); a CLI that can't start; ARMhf and musl; missing curl, wget, or brew; a failed install, including the reason from the Windows MSI install; and a shim that can't identify itself. |
| What stays verbose-only? | Troubleshooting detail (`write_diagnostic`): discovery errors, skipped candidates and interpreters, PowerShell probes, each installer attempt's result, and option errors. |
| How do users find verbose mode? | A failed install ends with `For details, run copilot --vscode-shim verbose, or set VSCODE_COPILOT_SHIM_VERBOSE=1.` Other messages don't need the hint, because they already give the reason. |
| Another way to turn it on? | Yes: `VSCODE_COPILOT_SHIM_VERBOSE`, set to anything other than empty or `0`, for scripts, aliases, and CI. Child processes inherit it, including the nested MSI install. |
| Should the extension pass verbose at trace log level? | No, for now. The environment variable covers support cases. |
| Should Windows setup pass verbose and log stderr? | No. The result file's `reason` is enough. |
| Malformed `--vscode-shim` options (exit 2)? | Stay quiet. Only VS Code passes them, and setup reports a missing result file. |
| Tests? | Messages are checked without verbose. The diagnostics tests also check the environment variable, and an integration test covers it end to end. |

`REQUIREMENTS.md` adds a **Messages and diagnostics** section with this rule and updates the outcome table.

## Other decisions, in their own PRs
- **#338927:** the extension uses the shim that ships next to `code` again. Your global-storage deployment of a local build now runs only when the build doesn't ship a shim, as in a build from source. The hard-coded Windows path in `LOCAL_SHIM_SOURCE_PATHS` is untouched. You may want it empty, or read from an environment variable, before this ships.
- **#338931:** the shim's folder is appended to the terminal `PATH` again, the same way Windows setup adds it, so a Copilot CLI the user already has is found first.
- **#338989:** `SHIM_POST_INSTALL.md` is updated to describe the current code: the installer-only `PATH` and the official-script install directory fallback. It keeps your investigation.
- **Translations:** out of scope for now.

## Validation
- Shim tests pass on Windows (63 unit, 4 app, 3 ConPTY) and on Linux in Docker (60 unit, 4 app, 3 PTY).
- clippy with Rust 1.88 passes for Windows x64 and arm64, Linux, and macOS; `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- Live check on Windows: with no terminal and no CLI, the shim prints the message with the documentation URL and exits 127.

pull_requests.title: automations: capture client customizations for offline runs
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Lets scheduled and manual automation runs use the client's plugins without the client being connected. This is a simpler replacement for #338777 and depends on microsoft/agent-host-protocol#474.

## How it works

- **Protocol**: syncs microsoft/agent-host-protocol#474, which adds `AutomationSessionTemplate.customizations`, `AutomationEntry.customizations`, and the `automations.customizations` capability.
- **Client**: when the host advertises the capability, the automation store sends the target scope's enabled plugins with the definition on create and when the target changes. It holds the scope until the host responds so the host can read client-served bundles. Ordinary edits resubmit the saved entries unchanged. A selected custom agent that lives in the synced bundle is sent as its bundled URI.
- **Host**: a new self-contained `AgentHostAutomationCustomizations` module copies new or changed entries into immutable directories under `agentPlugins/.host/automations/` and reuses copies whose `id`/`uri`/`nonce` are unchanged. Any capture failure rejects the mutation.
- **Runs**: each run session is created with a static, host-owned `vscode.automation` active client whose plugins point at the copies. Every provider (Copilot, Claude, Codex) already loads active-client plugins before the first turn, so there are **no provider, enablement-gate, or session-config changes**. The plugin manager uses `.host` directories in place.
- **Cleanup**: after each create, update, and removal, the host deletes copies that no automation references. Copies used by a run session in the current host process are kept until the next startup, because that session keeps using them for follow-up turns.

Compared with #338777, this drops plugin-cache holders and leases, per-run snapshots, session-deletion hooks, reattaching plugins on restore, provider-specific captured-plugin branches, and client bundle snapshots. Production code is about +320/−54 instead of +1,511/−266.

## MCP authentication in runs

Until the host can own MCP authentication, run sessions borrow existing sign-ins from connected windows. When an MCP server in a run session requires authentication, the host sends a VS Code-specific `vscode/requestMcpAuthentication` request to connected clients one at a time. A client never prompts: it reuses a sign-in the user already allowed for that server, pushes the token through the regular `authenticate` command, and reports success. The existing token fan-out then unblocks the run, so there are no provider changes. Each challenge is requested once per session and server; if no client can supply a token, the run continues without that server.

## Known limitations

- A run session restored after a host restart does not get the captured plugins back. Runs in flight during a restart are already failed as interrupted.
- If a customization is edited while the host is copying it, the copy could be inconsistent.
- MCP sign-in needs a VS Code window to be connected when the challenge happens; there is no retry when one connects later.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep 'AgentHostAutomationCustomizations|AgentHostAutomationService|AgentPluginManager|AgentHostAutomationStore|SyncedCustomizationBundler'`: 160 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/**/*.test.js'`: 7,862 passing, 72 pending
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/conformance/agentHostConformance.integrationTest.ts`: automation capability test passes; one changeset-discard test times out locally and fails identically on `main`
- ESLint on changed files and `git diff --check`: clean
- Manual, in Code OSS: created and edited automations and ran them 3 times with Copilot. All runs completed. The run sessions registered MCP servers from the captured plugins before any window client joined. Unchanged entries were reused on a second automation and on an ordinary edit, and the synced bundle was re-captured when its nonce changed.
- Manual MCP sign-in: a run with no prompts connected 7 MCP servers from existing sign-ins (and an 8th that shares a Slack resource) before its first model request, and the model successfully called `workiq-me-GetMyDetails`. Servers without a prior sign-in stayed unauthenticated as intended.
- Not run: real-provider integration tests.

pull_requests.title: sessions: center nested session connector lines on the status icon
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #338971

## What changed

In the sessions list, the nested-chat hierarchy guides are drawn as left borders. Each one was positioned at the icon's center x, so the 1px stroke spanned `[center, center + 1px]` and rendered half a stroke to the right of the status dot and twistie. On Retina that's one device pixel.

- Added three row-level custom properties: `--session-icon-start`, `--session-icon-size`, and a derived `--session-hierarchy-guide-left` (icon center minus half of `--vscode-strokeThickness`). The derived value is declared on `.monaco-list-row` so it resolves against the row's own overrides.
- The parent guide (`.session-item::after`, including its compact and phone `top` variants) and the child connectors (`.session-chat-item::before` / `::after`) now use `--session-hierarchy-guide-left`. The elbow's `width` grows by the same half stroke, so its right end doesn't move.
- The twistie position and size come from the same properties. The phone layout overrides only `--session-icon-start` and `--session-icon-size` (10px / 20px), keeping its existing twistie geometry.
- Registered the new properties in `build/lib/stylelint/vscode-known-variables.json`.

Phone layout keeps its existing status codicon sizing. On expanded phone rows the twistie always replaces the status icon, so the guide only needs to line up with the twistie. An earlier revision widened the phone codicon to 20px, which moved every phone session title 4px right, so it was reverted.

## Validation

Measured in the component explorer at DPR 1, with the codicon font loaded. The line center is `left + borderLeftWidth / 2`:

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Addresses #338063.

## Changes

- Preserve newer, validated local pending catalog state when applying passive archive/read updates, rather than rebuilding from a stale central payload. Respect generation/revision boundaries and fall back to central data if the pending payload is corrupt.
- Keep general catalog reconciliation cancelled during shutdown. After providers stop, replay only failed passive writes, once per session, within a shared 250 ms budget. Reuse the existing replay validation and CAS logic, without listing sessions or resolving provider metadata.
- Retain full available Agent Host logs from before and after restart, plus Copilot runtime logs, in the CI logs artifact before temporary-home cleanup.
- Add deterministic failure-injection tests for flag preservation, shutdown ordering, bounded retries, cancellation, corruption, deletion fencing, and a real SQLite close race.

## Investigation and limitations

Injected catalog-write failures reproduced two concrete problems: a subsequent flag update could overwrite locally pending flags, and cancelling scheduled reconciliation on shutdown could leave the first listing after restart stale. Regression tests failed before the fixes.

The original intermittent Windows failure mechanism is still unconfirmed because the failing jobs did not retain Agent Host logs. Windows/Linux and Azure validation remain outstanding; this draft adds defenses for the demonstrated failure paths and preserves evidence for another CI failure. No E2E assertions were weakened, tests skipped, or existing timeouts raised.

Latest `main` was merged without rewriting history.

## Validation

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Defer client restarts until background subagents settle
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Part of #338600

## Problem

A background subagent can still be finishing after its parent's root turn goes idle. The agent host deferred CopilotClient restarts only until every chat's root turn ended, so a restart requested in that window tore the SDK session down under the subagent. The subagent chat then never received its completion and stayed in progress.

One trigger matches the issue: another window signs in with a token whose expiry differs from the current one, which flips the Agent Host's GitHub credential mode and requests a restart. Proxy, startup-setting, GitHub Enterprise, Copilot Connector, and sign-out changes request the same restart.

## Changes

- `CopilotAgentSession.hasActiveSubagents` reports a subagent that started or resumed and has not yet been confirmed complete.
- Deferred client restarts now wait until no chat has an active turn or an in-flight subagent.
- When a chat's last in-flight subagent settles after its root turn already ended, the session calls `onTurnEnded` again, so a parked restart still runs instead of being stranded.

## Not covered here

The reported error, `GitHub token provider registration "…" is unavailable`, comes from the Copilot SDK runtime. Updating a live session's GitHub credentials retires the registration that its subagents still use. That needs a separate runtime fix, followed by an SDK update here, before #338600 can close. This PR prevents the stuck subagent chat on the client-restart path.

A long-running background subagent now also delays these restarts until it finishes. A retained subagent that is idle between follow-ups does not count as in flight.

## How to test

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "in-flight subagent settles|background subagent settles after its root turn"`: 2 passing. Both new tests fail without the source change.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "restart|subagent|Subagent|turn ending|failed send releases|BYOK|byok"`: 133 passing, 1 failing. The failure, `a marker written after an initial read miss is picked up without a restart`, also fails on unmodified `main` locally because it reads the real `~/.copilot` directory.
- Full runs of both files, before rebasing onto current `main`: 1220 passing, 12 failing; the same 12 tests fail on unmodified `main` locally, all in external chat discovery, state-file resolution, and debug-log collection.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep "subagent"`: 7 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in changed files. The only errors are existing `electron` module-resolution errors in this local worktree.
- Manual check, not committed: a temporary change to the retained background subagent E2E test held the child's model response, switched from an expiring token to a static token mid-subagent, and then released it. pull_requests.title: sessions: inherit the source chat's running model for side chats
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338867

## Problem

When signed out with BYOK models enabled (`chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled` + `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable`), `/btw` in the Agents window opens the "Sign in to use GitHub Copilot" dialog, even though normal messages in the same chat run on the BYOK model.

## Root cause

`BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.createSideChat` copies the source chat's model from the provider's per-chat record (`getChatModelSelection` / `getChatModelId`). That record can be empty while the chat is really running on a BYOK model. For example, a resumed chat whose persisted draft has no model: `_hydrateModelFromDraft` only reads `draft.model`. In that state the model picker is display-only. It shows the BYOK model and normal sends use it, but it never writes the model back to the provider.

As a result, the side chat is created with `model: undefined` and sent with `userSelectedModelId: undefined`. On the handler side, `_ensureRequiredAuthentication` → `modelRequiresAgentAuthentication` returns `true` for "no model" when signed-out BYOK is enabled. That is intentional, because an unknown model may be a Copilot one. So the handler calls `forceAuthenticationInteractively` (`forceSignInDialog: true`).

## Fix

When no model is recorded for the source chat, `createSideChat` now falls back to the model the host recorded that chat running on: its draft model, else its active turn's model, else its last turn's model. The side chat then runs on the same BYOK model as the source chat, and no sign-in is required.

## Notes for reviewers

- `forkChat` copies the model the same way and could hit the same gap. It is left unchanged to keep this PR focused; it would be a small follow-up.
- A broader follow-up would be to have `_hydrateModelFromDraft` also fall back to the last turn's model, so the main chat's recorded model is correct everywhere.

## Testing

- Added `createSideChat inherits the model the source chat last ran on when no model is recorded for it`. It fails before the change (`createdModel: undefined`, `sentModelId: undefined`) and passes after.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep "SideChat|forkChat"`: 10 passing.
- The full `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` suite has 3 failures in the resource-label tests; they fail the same way on `main` without this change.
- `npm run typecheck-client` reports no errors in the changed files. Its only errors are missing `electron` typings in this local worktree.

pull_requests.title: sessions: include Automations in Back/Forward navigation
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #328745

## What changed

In the Agents window, Back/Forward now include custom views such as **Automations**. Opening an automation run from the Automations page and pressing Back takes you back to Automations. Before this change, Back skipped the page and landed on whatever session was open before it.

## Why

`SessionsNavigation` only walks the session recency history (MRU `(session, chat)` entries). Custom views are shown by `ICustomViewService` and were never recorded, so Back went from the run straight to the previous session.

## How

- `SessionsNavigation` takes `ICustomViewService` and remembers one **custom view stop** next to the cursor: the view id, the entry that was current when the view opened (`beforeKey`), and the entry opened from the view (`afterKey`).
- `SessionsService._beginNavigation` calls a new `onWillNavigateExplicitly()` right before it hides the custom view.
  - If the user is leaving the custom view this way, the first entry recorded afterwards becomes `afterKey`.
  - Any other explicit navigation drops the stop.
- `goBack`/`goForward` step through the stop in this order: run ⇄ Automations ⇄ previous session. The `sessionsCanGoBack` and `sessionsCanGoForward` context keys follow the same rules.
- Custom views are **not** added to the recency history, so the recent-sessions picker is unchanged.

## Notes for reviewers

- The history stays MRU/Alt+Tab-style. Only the most recent custom view is remembered, and only next to the entries around it. Opening another session explicitly drops it from Back. This keeps the change small without turning navigation into a browser-style stack.
- Back from a custom view that was opened directly (not reached via Back) now returns to the session shown underneath it. Before, it went one entry further back.
- If the view is hidden without opening a session (the view gets disabled, or the mobile back gesture), the stop is dropped.

## Validation

All checks ran headlessly, with no Code OSS workbench window. Unit tests use the Electron test runner in `scripts/test.sh`.

**Bug reproduced on `main`.** I ran the new regression tests against the original `sessionNavigation.ts`/`sessionsService.ts`, with a temporary constructor adapter in the test that is not committed:

```
./scripts/test.sh src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionNavigation.test.ts --grep "custom view"
→ FAILED: 1 passing, 2 failing
  1) Back and Forward traverse a custom view left by opening a session
     step 2 (Back from the run): expected location "test.automations", actual "s1"
  2) Back from a custom view returns to the session it was opened from
     expected location "s2", actual "s1"
```

**With the fix:**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `./scripts/test.sh src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionNavigation.test.ts` | ✅ Passed: 21 passing, including 3 new custom view tests |
| `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/sessions/services/**/*.test.js"` | ✅ Passed: 594 passing, 2 pending |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | ✅ Passed (exit 0) |
| `npx eslint <3 changed files>` | ✅ Passed: 0 problems |
| `npm run valid-layers-check` | ✅ Passed (exit 0) |

The new tests use snapshot-style checks of `{ location, canGoBack, canGoForward }` after each step:

1. **Back and Forward traverse a custom view left by opening a session.** Covers the steps from the issue: s1 → Automations → open run, then Back ×2 and Forward ×2. The path is run → Automations → s1 → Automations → run.
2. **Back from a custom view returns to the session it was opened from.**
3. **Another explicit navigation drops the custom view from Back.** This checks that the MRU behavior is unchanged otherwise.

pull_requests.body:

Fixes #336858.

## Summary

- Read `enabledPlugins` and `extraKnownMarketplaces` from trusted `.github/copilot/settings(.local).json` and `.claude/settings(.local).json` files.
- Match Copilot CLI repository precedence: Copilot local, Copilot shared, Claude local, then Claude shared.
- Install `enabledPlugins: true` entries automatically with a disabled profile baseline, then activate them only for the repository.
- Install and enable the plugin from the current repository's exact marketplace source, even when another repository has already installed the same `plugin@marketplace` identity.
- Apply `false` as a repository-scoped disablement and preserve global state for absent entries.
- Skip the redundant marketplace confirmation because workspace trust already authorizes the repository configuration.
- Include repository-installed plugins in the existing automatic-update pipeline when user or managed settings authorize updates; repository `autoUpdate` cannot override global updates being off.
- Forward repository enablement to Agent Host as a workspace-scoped customization decision without changing managed-policy behavior.
- Keep settings keyed by their source folder in multi-root workspaces and publish only the primary session repository's overlay.
- Reconcile installs and current marketplace metadata before the initial Agent Host customization snapshot is published.

  - Added regression tests in `copilotAgent.test.ts`, `copilotAgentSession.test.ts`, and `copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` to verify the new behavior and ensure that the issue is resolved.

pull_requests.body:
Bumps [axios](https://github.com/axios/axios) from 1.18.1 to 1.20.0.
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.20.0 — August 19, 2026

This release hardens runtime option handling, adds RFC 9110 status-code aliases, fixes Node.js and XHR reliability issues, and refreshes project tooling and documentation.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • HTTP Status Naming: Added ContentTooLarge (413) and UnprocessableContent (422), while retaining PayloadTooLarge and UnprocessableEntity as backward-compatible deprecated aliases. (#11082)

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Runtime Option Handling: Hardened behavioral configuration reads against shared and foreign prototype pollution and normalized unsafe interceptor replacement objects. This also clarifies Fetch redirect and custom implementation behavior, HTTP/2 DNS and proxy handling, CIDR-based NO_PROXY matching, and malformed data URI rejection; see the PR for documented compatibility effects. (#11141)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Interceptor Lifecycle: Prevented unbounded handler-array growth by trimming trailing ejected interceptors without changing iteration semantics, and kept interceptor operations safe when the public handlers field is nullish. (#11087, #11118)
  • Request Error Preservation: Prevented custom Error.prepareStackTrace implementations that return non-string values from replacing the original request failure with an unrelated TypeError. (#11109)
  • XHR Reliability: Navigation-canceled requests now reject with ECONNABORTED instead of resolving with status 0, while successful downloads flush their final progress callback during the live loadend dispatch. (#11094, #11121)
  • Node.js Socket Memory: Removed request-context retention from per-socket error listeners, preventing completed response data from being pinned for the lifetime of pooled keep-alive sockets. (#11091)
  • Core Methods and HTTP Errors: Prevented structural method-header buckets from leaking into outgoing headers, standardized invalid DNS lookup and httpVersion failures as AxiosError.ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and corrected the timeoutErrorMessage merge strategy. (#11096)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Dependencies: Updated fast-uri, postcss, js-yaml, mocha, development-tooling groups, and GitHub Actions dependencies. (#11092, #11098, #11099, #11106, #11107, #11122, #11123, #11126, #11127, #11133, #11140, #11143, #11144)
  • Documentation: Applied the v1.19.0 documentation updates, added the missing fs import to the README stream example, introduced localized global search, and repaired the interceptor test link. (#11101, #11113, #11097, #11119)
  • Sponsorship: Updated sponsorship links and data and added ScrapingBee as a sponsor. (#11124, #11136, #11137)
  • CI and Release: Switched ESM smoke tests to locked dependencies and synchronized package and runtime version metadata for v1.20.0. (#11128, #11152)

🔒 Security Fixes

Changelog

v1.19.0 — July 22, 2026

This release raises the form-data security floor, adds configuration and type-system capabilities, and fixes NO_PROXY matching, interceptor errors, progress reporting, and serialization edge cases.

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Multipart Form Data: Raised the form-data dependency floor to ^4.0.6, preventing fresh installations from resolving versions affected by the CRLF injection vulnerability GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx). (#11028)

🚀 New Features

  • Configuration Extensibility: Preserved own-enumerable symbol-keyed fields through mergeConfig and added a generic params type across public TypeScript declarations, responses, errors, adapters, and serializers. (#11043, #11081)
  • Header Parameter Parsing: Added the opt-in AxiosHeaders.parseParameters() parser for quote-aware, RFC-style HTTP parameter parsing while preserving legacy parsing behavior. (#11051)
  • HTTP Status Codes: Added the missing Cloudflare 520 WebServerReturnsAnUnknownError status and matching ESM/CJS declarations. (#11067)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Form Data Conversion: Limited formDataToJSON path splitting to dot and bracket notation, preserving literal punctuation in keys, and removed browser-facing Buffer.from usage from toFormData to avoid unnecessary polyfills. (#11006, #11018)

  • Proxy Bypass: Canonicalized IPv4 shorthand, octal, and hexadecimal forms during NO_PROXY matching and honored * entries within comma- or space-separated bypass lists. (#11029, #11053)

  • Cancellation: Propagated already-aborted input signals immediately when composing abort signals. (#11035)

  • Header Handling: Preserved empty first values for duplicate singleton headers and made AxiosHeaders#getSetCookie() consistently return arrays for present values. (#11036, #11037)

  • URL Handling: Included normalized, safely redacted offending URLs in malformed-protocol errors and removed repeated trailing slashes when combining base URLs. (#11008, #11038)

  • Progress Events: Clamped malformed negative progress values to zero and ensured final Node.js download progress events are delivered before streamed responses close. (#11039, #11040)

  • Error and JSON Serialization: Serialized Set values as arrays in JSON-compatible snapshots and synthesized useful AxiosError messages from otherwise-empty AggregateError instances. (#11044, #11059)

  • Content-Length Enforcement: Corrected base64 data: URL size estimation so maxContentLength is enforced consistently by the HTTP and Fetch adapters. (#11061)

  • Synchronous Interceptors: Prevented requests from being dispatched after synchronous request interceptors fail unless their paired rejection handler resolves successfully. (#11071)

`b284dd5b991` changed the extension to put the Copilot shim's folder at the front of the integrated terminal `PATH` (`contributePath(..., true)`). The shim then came before the user's own `PATH` in every integrated terminal.

## Change
- **Append again:** the extension appends the shim's folder to the terminal `PATH` again, the same way Windows setup appends `{app}\bin\copilot-shim` to the user `PATH`.

  - The shim answers `copilot` only when nothing else on `PATH` does.
  - Copilot-created terminals are unaffected, because they run the shim by its full path.
- **Docs:** `REQUIREMENTS.md` now says the folder is appended.

## Merging with #338927
#338927, which makes the extension use the shipped shim, is independent of this PR. I merged both branches locally: they merge cleanly and the specs pass (40 tests).

pull_requests.title: copilot: use the shipped Copilot shim in terminals
pull_requests.body:
The extension stopped using the `copilot` shim that ships with VS Code. `b284dd5b991` replaced the lookup of `{app}/bin/copilot-shim/copilot` with a copy of a local development build, taken from `LOCAL_SHIM_SOURCE_PATHS`, into global storage. That path is set to a developer machine on Windows and is empty on macOS and Linux. So a shipped build never found its bundled shim, and integrated terminals fell back to `copilot` from `PATH`.

## Change
- **Shipped shim first:** the extension looks for the shim next to the `code` command again (`getNativeCopilotShimPath`, restored with its test). When it's there, the extension uses it and removes `<globalStorage>/copilotCli`. That folder held the script shims from earlier versions, which terminals restored with their old `PATH` could still run.
- **Development fallback:** when the build doesn't ship a shim (a build from source), the extension uses the development deployment in `copilotCLINativeShim.ts`, unchanged.
- **Docs:** `REQUIREMENTS.md` now describes the shipped shim as the default and the global-storage copy as the fallback.

## Not in this PR
- The terminal `PATH` order (the `prepend: true` argument) is left as is; #338931 changes it.
- The hard-coded `LOCAL_SHIM_SOURCE_PATHS` entry for Windows is untouched. It's only used when the build doesn't ship a shim.

## Validation
- `copilotCLITerminalIntegration.spec.ts` and `copilotCLINativeShim.spec.ts` pass (40 tests).
- New tests cover the shipped shim with cleanup, the development fallback, and the shim path on each platform.
- `tsc --noEmit -p extensions/copilot/tsconfig.json` and `eslint` pass on the changed files.

## Description

`code tunnel prune` skipped server folders named `Stable-<commit>`. It parses the folder name prefix with `Quality::try_from`, which only accepted lowercase values.

- `cli/src/options.rs`: `Quality::try_from(&str)` now lowercases its input before matching, so `Stable`, `Insiders` and `Exploration` parse the same as their lowercase forms.

pull_requests.title: Replace deprecated url.parse() with WHATWG URL in request service
pull_requests.body:
## What

Running `code --install-extension` prints this warning:

> (node:15706) [DEP0169] DeprecationWarning: `url.parse()` behavior is not standardized and prone to errors that have security implications. Use the WHATWG URL API instead. CVEs are not issued for `url.parse()` vulnerabilities.

It comes from `src/vs/platform/request/node/requestService.ts` and `src/vs/platform/request/node/proxy.ts`, which still used `url.parse()`. This PR switches both files to the WHATWG `URL` API.

## Changes

`URL` has different fields and error behavior than `url.parse()`, so these changes keep the old behavior:

- **`path`**: `URL` has no `.path`, so it's rebuilt from `pathname + search`.
- **IPv6 hosts**: `URL.hostname` keeps the brackets (`[::1]`), and Node's `http` module can't resolve a host with brackets. The brackets are removed.
- **Proxy `auth`**: `URL` has no `.auth`. It's rebuilt from `username` and `password`, which are URL-decoded to match what `url.parse()` returned.
- **Invalid input**: `new URL()` throws where `url.parse()` didn't. In `proxy.ts`, a small helper returns `null` on invalid input, so a bad proxy setting still falls back to no proxy instead of failing every request.

pull_requests.title: Don't cache prompt discovery results from a cancelled scan
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #338883, addressing the Copilot review comment on that PR.

### Problem

#338883 made the filesystem branches of `computeListPromptFiles` report cancellation as an error so a cancelled scan could not be cached as a permanent "no prompt files" answer.

That left one branch uncovered. `ExtensionPromptFileService._listFromProviders` bails out of its provider loop **without** throwing:

```ts
for (const providerEntry of providers) {
    if (token.isCancellationRequested) {
        break;              // returns a partial result, no throw
    }
```

So if cancellation lands while the extension-provider branch is running and the filesystem branches either already finished or are policy-blocked (`allowStandalone === false` makes them literal `[]`), the combined `Promise.all` resolves normally. The partial list is then stored in `cachedFileLocations[type]` and never evicted — the exact state #338883 set out to fix.

This is reachable in practice, not theoretical: extension activation (`activateByEvent`) is slow relative to the file scans, so the provider branch is often the last one outstanding.

### Change

Re-check the token after the combined computation, so no branch that swallows cancellation can have its result accepted and cached:

```ts
// A branch may stop early on cancellation without throwing (extension
// providers do), so re-check before this result is accepted and cached.
if (token.isCancellationRequested) {
    throw new CancellationError();
}
```

The guard is placed at the combined result rather than in `_listFromProviders`, because that loop's tolerance is intentional (it stops calling further providers without erroring), and a single choke point also covers any future branch that swallows cancellation.

### Testing

Added `does not cache a partial result when a provider swallows cancellation`. It enables the strict-plugin-only lockdown so the filesystem branches are literal `[]`, making the provider the only possible cancellation source — the test is therefore deterministic and specifically covers this gap rather than the path already fixed in #338883.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/contrib/chat/test/**/promptSyntax/**/*.test.js"` | passed (802 passing) |
| `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/contrib/chat/test/**/*.test.js"` | 11032 passing, 2 pre-existing failures |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | passed |

The new test was verified to fail without the guard (`AssertionError: Missing expected rejection (CancellationError)`) and pass with it.

The 2 remaining failures are pre-existing and unrelated — `agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` hardcodes `/home/test-user` as the home directory and fails identically on a clean checkout of `main`.

pull_requests.title: chat: continue terminal notifications within the current task
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338827.

A background terminal completion already carries `isSystemInitiated`, but Local chat treated the preceding task as earlier user history. Chat Completions then lost the task's reasoning even though the user had not sent a new message. History conversion also discarded the initiation flag, and terminal-first mixed steering could incorrectly mark genuine user input as system initiated.

Carry initiation provenance through the private chat history API and use the last genuine user request as the task boundary in both agent history renderers. System notifications preserve the current task's same-model Chat Completions reasoning. Historical tools retain their existing rendering, and genuine user input retains its turn boundary.

Extension-provided endpoints can omit `apiType` for either Chat Completions or Messages. The continuation condition now requires a known protocol from the endpoint, recorded round, or existing `vscode_thinking_origin_api` metadata. The wrapper retains this metadata on plaintext thinking and its completion marker. Unknown untagged transport fails closed, and budget-mode Messages is not classified from a model name such as `kimi-k3`. General historical replay opt-in remains separate; this PR does not depend on #338874.

### RED → GREEN

- Original full agent-prompt regressions failed in both history paths: expected current-task text/opaque reasoning, received `thinking: []`.
- Deterministic active/idle service tests exposed lost system provenance (2 failures); the private API test exposed the missing history property (1 failure); terminal-first mixed steering exposed a user request incorrectly marked system initiated (1 failure). All pass. Timing uses deferred promises rather than sleeps.
- The previous undefined-API continuation guard failed 2 real custom-provider/wrapper regressions: the actual Messages request body contained `signed-budget-state`. Plaintext Chat Completions provenance separately failed 2 cases before the wrapper fix.
- Final continuation suite: **16 passing cases**, covering both history paths, real custom provider/serializer paths, budget Messages with an opaque ID and Kimi alias, unknown transport, model switches, missing completed-tool results, repeated/restored notifications, exactly-once output, and genuine-user boundaries. The Chat Completions test endpoint has `supportsThinkingContentInHistory: false`.

From `extensions/copilot`:

```sh
npm run test:unit -- src/extension/prompts/node/agent/test/systemInitiatedHistory.spec.tsx src/extension/prompts/node/agent/test/summarization.spec.tsx src/extension/prompts/node/panel/test/toolCalling.spec.ts src/extension/prompt/test/node/conversation.spec.ts src/extension/byok/vscode-node/test/customEndpointProvider.spec.ts src/platform/endpoint/vscode-node/test/extChatEndpoint.spec.ts
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json
npm run compile
```

**6 files / 121 tests pass**, including a clean rerun after removing runtime probes. TypeScript, targeted ESLint, and the extension build pass.

From the repository root:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatService/chatService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/common/extHostChatAgents2.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/electron-browser/runInTerminalTool.test.ts
npm run compile
npm run vscode-dts-compile-check
```

**372 tests pass**, with 108 existing pending/skipped cases; product build and API checks pass. Those core sources are unchanged by the final protocol-provenance follow-up. Client output was regenerated after removing the probes.

### Final runtime verification

Verified source head **`fdadfd07810b889d91a376db7da8caff281e8128`** using the launch skill, this worktree's build/dependencies, and an isolated Code OSS Dev profile on macOS. Only that profile used `chat.tools.terminal.idleSilenceTimeoutMs: 1000`. Playwright and debug ports were isolated from the sibling launch. All **31 runtime assertions pass**.

| Scenario | Runtime evidence |
| --- | --- |
| **Live Local / Kimi K3 (GitHub) / High, idle completion** | Read the fixture file, ran the foreground command below, became idle, then received one automatic notification and one output line. Actual outbound payload retained the earlier **99-character `reasoning_text` and 36-character `reasoning_opaque` with identical SHA-256 hashes**; it also included the waiting response's **120/36-character** reasoning values. Core and extension system/history provenance matched. |
| **Controlled local Chat Completions, idle completion** | Actual workbench, extension, HTTP, and terminal paths. Prior reasoning byte-identical; one continuation/output; a subsequent genuine user message removed earlier reasoning. |
| **Controlled local Chat Completions, active completion** | Held the real provider HTTP response open until the terminal completion queued while the tool loop was active. Releasing it produced one system continuation with prior reasoning preserved. |
| **Controlled local Chat Completions, mixed steering** | Terminal notification queued first while active, then genuine input submitted using the UI's **Steer with Message** action. One merged request was user initiated, contained output once, and omitted earlier-task reasoning. |
| **Controlled custom budget Messages, model ID `kimi-k3`** | Actual transport was Messages, nonadaptive budget 4096. Signed thinking appeared within the original tool loop (`0 → 1 → 2` blocks), then was absent at notification (`0`). |

Live foreground command (`mode: sync`, `timeout: 60000`):

```sh
sleep 12 && echo TC338827-LIVE >> TC338827-LIVE.executions && echo TC338827-LIVE-DONE
```

Each scenario appended exactly one physical execution marker. The live continuation retained the original file/terminal tool history and issued no new tools. Deterministic tests additionally cover missing completed-tool results and restored sessions.

The active/mixed scenarios use a deterministic local model, **not live Kimi**. The budget fixture uses synthetic omitted-text signatures and a temporary fixture-specific `includeEncryptedThinking: true` option so signed state is observable before replay; real Messages-vendor signature acceptance is not claimed. A plaintext-plus-signature control with no observable signed state was excluded from passing evidence.

Sanitized comparisons retain lengths/hashes, tool IDs/names, flags, and counts without credentials or request headers. Reproduction scripts and the report are retained locally under `.build/338827-runtime-final`. All temporary production probes were removed, clean output rebuilt, and the isolated processes stopped. Combined validation with #338874 remains separate.

pull_requests.title: chat: preserve reasoning across turns and custom providers
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338820.

A genuine follow-up user message drops earlier Chat Completions reasoning while retaining the assistant messages and tool calls/results. Custom Responses and Messages endpoints also lose opaque reasoning state in the extension wrapper, including on a tool continuation within the first turn.

Preserve earlier reasoning for models that require it, and carry custom-provider reasoning state through the full response/request round trip:

- Recognized Kimi K3 IDs/families, including the documented `k3` and `k3-256k` aliases, opt in by default. `github.copilot.chat.modelCapabilityOverrides[modelId].thinkingInHistory` supports explicit opt-in or opt-out. Apply configured family aliases before selecting that default.
- Carry the provider's API type and adaptive-thinking capability through the proposed language-model capability API. Historical Chat Completions replay requires a declared Chat Completions API; unknown protocols fail closed. Responses and adaptive Messages retain their existing replay policy, budget Messages retains its safeguard, and the same-model guard remains mandatory. Feature-detect the new API enum for compatibility with older published hosts.
- Request encrypted reasoning from extension-contributed providers and prevent a later `vscode_reasoning_done` marker from replacing the saved signature/encrypted state. Declare the existing request option in the proposed consumer API.

The merge with main retains the now-upstream #338878 continuation behavior alongside this PR's separate historical replay policy. No additional system-notification/task-boundary changes are introduced here.

### Validation

Final head: `ed6699ad3496beba3b07f7e7bfc40508223ceae3`, following merge commit `7a68f86b3270bf197988d3bd3e484c813ebb3855` (main at `3a5dda6ed729e55a7e7b12dbaf0dab39d4703da0`). The committed source and compiled extension bundle hashes match the launch-validated build. The PR remains a draft.

- **Alias RED → GREEN:** 11 failures against the original matcher, then 102 passing tests with the correction. Coverage includes actual Copilot/custom request serialization through both history renderers, explicit overrides, family aliases and negative name boundaries.
- **Streaming RED → GREEN:** all 6 new Responses/Messages cases fail against the merged production behavior, then pass with the fix. Enabling the encrypted-state request option alone still fails the Responses regression because completion metadata overwrites the encrypted value. Tests stream tool-call and final-answer reasoning through the actual custom provider, outer endpoint, accumulator, full `AgentPrompt` and serializer in both history modes.
- **Final neighboring suite:** 675 tests pass in 18 files, including the upstream continuation tests, model-switch and opt-out guards, protocol distinctions and older-host compatibility.
- Full product compilation, all four extension TypeScript projects, API declaration compilation, changed-file ESLint, repository hygiene and normal commit hooks pass.
- The earlier CCR corrections were separately RED → GREEN: 4 wrapper-path failures on the previous implementation, then 4 passes for budget Messages protection and overridden Kimi family selection.

### Launch-skill runtime on the final source

Launched this worktree's freshly compiled Code OSS with an isolated profile, Playwright session `c338820-51247`, and unique ports: CDP `57962`, extension host `57963`, main `57964`, agent host `57965`.

A deterministic loopback HTTP provider returned SSE responses through the built-in custom provider, real language-model API and Copilot extension. Each UI scenario completed a tool-call round and final answer, then submitted a genuine follow-up user message. Outgoing request fields were compared with the emitted fields using exact values, lengths and SHA-256 hashes; UI snapshots/timestamps establish the completed-turn transition.

| Configured endpoint | First-turn tool continuation | Earlier reasoning on genuine follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| Responses, `store: false`, no `previous_response_id` | Original opaque state retained | Both reasoning IDs/encrypted values retained |
| Budget Messages | Original text/signature retained | Omitted intentionally |
| Adaptive Messages | Original text/signature retained | Both texts/signatures retained |
| Chat Completions `k3` | Original reasoning retained | Both text/ID pairs retained |
| Chat Completions `k3-256k` | Original reasoning retained | Both text/ID pairs retained |
| Explicit historical opt-out | Original reasoning retained | Omitted |

This is **scripted-provider validation, not real inference**. No production instrumentation was needed. The task-owned Code OSS process, HTTP server, Playwright session and throwaway profile have been cleaned up.

Earlier real inference at `f7c0a2a0d4ff4235bf619ccf75278412f3532f2d` used Local **Kimi K3 (GitHub), High**, model `kimi-k3-copilot-picker`. A completed first turn contained two tool-call rounds and a final answer. All three earlier `reasoning_text` and `reasoning_opaque` pairs were byte-for-byte identical in the actual follow-up request. Live opt-out and a switch to Gemini 3.5 Flash with replay enabled both excluded older Kimi reasoning. That live-model run predates the final alias/wrapper correction; the latest runtime coverage above uses deterministic HTTP providers.

### Limits

Standard Chat Completions deltas without an ID still reproduce independent #338819: plaintext reasoning is absent already on the first tool continuation. That separate serializer gate is outside this patch. Budget Messages intentionally does not replay thinking across genuine user turns (the #318076 safeguard). DeepSeek/model-quality and cache/cost gains were not benchmarked. CI results are tracked by the checks on this head.

pull_requests.body:
## Why

Fixes #338868.

The whole-side-pane toggle changes editor and auxiliary-bar visibility in separate steps. During the intermediate state, `SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator` could queue a detail-only collapse because the editor was hidden while the auxiliary bar was still visible. By the time that queued operation ran, the entire side pane had been hidden, but the stale collapse still closed non-managed editor tabs.

This was exposed while testing canvas editors, but it is a standalone Sessions layout bug and has no canvas dependency. This PR follows #338455 independently.

## What changed

- Centralizes the detail-only layout predicate in `_isDetailsOnly()`.
- Excludes the transient whole-side-pane toggle state via `togglingSidePane`.
- Rechecks the predicate when the queued collapse executes, preventing a stale visibility observation from closing editors.
- Adds a regression test that hides the editor and auxiliary bar through a whole-side-pane toggle and verifies the existing file editor remains open.

pull_requests.body:

Follow-up to #338666.

## Summary

Adds auxiliary windows containing independent Sessions grids to the Agents window.

- Add **Move Session to New Window**, **Move Session to Window…**, and **Return All Sessions to Main Window** actions.
- Support directional drops between grids and session-header tear-out, with Escape cancellation.
- Preserve session/chat models, inner chat groups, draft replies, attachments, and input undo history while reconstructing window-bound widgets in the destination document.
- Return an auxiliary window's sessions to main on close without stopping requests or rebalancing unrelated panes. Persist and restore each window's grid, bounds, selection, pins, and maximization.

## Design and scope

`SessionsService` remains the single membership/navigation owner. `SessionsParts` coordinates registered grids and retained-state transfers; `AuxiliarySessionsPart` owns one window's chrome, scoped services, and lifetime. Shared auxiliary-window infrastructure is reused without representing sessions as editor groups.

Header dragging uses pointer capture because native `dragend` does not reliably distinguish Escape from an unaccepted release. Existing sidebar drag payloads are handled by the destination grid.

The new-session composer and companion editor/details/terminal surfaces remain in main. Created sessions can move with their peer-chat composers. Finish or cancel an in-progress edit to an earlier request before moving its session or closing the auxiliary window, so that transient editing state cannot be discarded. Uncreated sessions and transfers between unrelated workbench instances are outside this change.

Includes owning-API regression tests and updated architecture/accessibility documentation. Existing fixtures only adapt to the connected-parent factory contract; no tests for fixtures were added.

The pre-publication review also added regressions for timed-out provider recovery, moving drop references, and delayed side-chat activation across windows.

- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed.

Before the refresh onto main, an isolated signed-out Code OSS instance was exercised with dbgjs and Playwright using real local chat models and widgets. Verified header commands, tear-out/Escape, all four drop directions, auxiliary-to-auxiliary/main transfers, streaming continuity, peer drafts with attachments and undo, sash resizing, maximize/restore, keyboard navigation, repeated native close/detach, and exact reload round-trips. Model-reference inspection returned one `ChatView` holder per displayed chat after transfers.

Physical OS-level mouse injection was unavailable because of macOS permissions. Header gestures used Playwright pointer input; the sidebar source's real payload and auxiliary drop receiver were verified separately.

## Manual testing

1. Open several created sessions, including one with multiple chat groups and unsent replies.
2. Use a session header's **Move Session to New Window** action. Add another session to that window and resize the splits.
