pull_requests.title: extensions: serialize unexpected errors before forwarding
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->
## Summary

Serialize unexpected extension-host errors before forwarding them to the main thread over JSON-RPC. This reuses `transformErrorForSerialization`, already used by adjacent error-reporting paths.

The raw forwarding path can fail when HTTP errors contain circular request/socket properties. It also loses non-enumerable error messages and stacks. The change preserves the existing serialized error contract, including causes, error codes, and telemetry suppression, while leaving non-Error values unchanged.

Observed in recent Insiders logs following an HTTP connection timeout:

```text
TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON
    --> starting at object with constructor 'TLSSocket'
    |     property '_httpMessage' -> object with constructor 'ClientRequest'
    |     property 'res' -> object with constructor 'IncomingMessage'
    --- property 'socket' closes the circle
```

This fixes the error-reporting failure, not the underlying network timeout. No linked issue; discovered through local log investigation.

## Validation

- Temporary regression tests reproduced the circular-JSON failure and loss of error details before the fix, and passed afterward. Those added tests and their supporting setup were subsequently removed at the maintainer's request; the final diff contains only the production fix.
- `npm run transpile-client` - passed after updating the branch to current `origin/main`.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\common\extensionHostMain.test.ts` - passed, 8 tests after removing the added tests and restoring the original suite.
- `node node_modules\eslint\bin\eslint.js src\vs\workbench\api\common\extensionHostMain.ts src\vs\workbench\api\test\common\extensionHostMain.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `npm run compile-client` - blocked before compilation by a local dependency mismatch: the manifest declared Copilot runtime `1.0.89-3`, while the installed SDK bundled `1.0.89-1`.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - failed with repository-wide dependency/type errors, including missing `electron` and `original-fs` declarations; no diagnostics reported in the production fix or the then-added tests. Shared installed dependencies were left unchanged.

## Summary

Retain the lightweight diagnostics used to investigate the recent macOS sanity-test slowdown:

pull_requests.title: sessions: Discover external Copilot sessions at runtime
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Discover newly used Copilot CLI/app sessions while Agent Host is running and publish them to the Agents Window through the existing incremental session notifications.

Copilot creates its session directory before the first request, but the SDK does not list the session until its journal exists. A root-only watcher would miss a request sent after the CLI has been idle.

## Implementation

- Separate directory membership, candidate readiness, and scan scheduling into provider-owned classes.
- Use one shallow root watcher and at most 32 temporary candidate watchers. Never recursively watch artifacts, tail transcripts, or watch database/WAL traffic.
- Coalesce SDK scans over 500 ms, limit filesystem concurrency to four, and classify only requested candidates after startup. Empty CLI folders do not trigger repeated catalog scans.
- Exclude Agent Host-created/resumed/imported sessions before persistence; guard forks until their SDK-generated IDs can be excluded.
- Preserve existing external-session visibility and legacy-adoption rules. Revalidate overflow candidates before publication, handle directory replacement, and retire terminally ineligible history.
- Add correlated `[CopilotDiscovery]` logs for discovery causes, session IDs, scan timings, catalog/candidate/watcher counts, exclusions, retries, and slow operations.

The SDK's provenance-complete listing still reads the full local catalog. These reads are event-driven and serialized; classification is candidate-scoped. Regression coverage with 5,000 historical sessions verifies that creating 100 host-owned sessions adds no catalog scans, directory enumerations, or discovery stat calls.

## Validation

Rebased onto `main` and validated the rebased commit:

- `npm run compile-client` — passed, zero compilation errors.
- Focused tests below — **118 passed**.
- ESLint command below — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Before rebase, the three host-ownership tests passed three additional isolated runs with no disposable leaks.

```sh
env -u COPILOT_HOME ./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotChatDiscovery.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts \
  --grep 'CopilotChatDiscovery|CopilotAgent (external chat discovery|listSessions legacy-CLI surfacing|createChat fork|createChat failure rollback|createChat exact-chat provisioning|provisional sessions|MCP authentication during session initialization|_resumeSession dedup|_resumeSession fallback)|external discovery|recent replaces the oldest visible external session|legacy migration and external discovery|identical session added notification|batches session added and removed notifications'

npm run eslint -- \
  src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotChatDiscovery.ts \
  src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionDiscoveryWatchers.ts \
  src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts \
  src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts \
  src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotChatDiscovery.test.ts \
  src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts \
  src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts
```

### Manual test

Full Agents Window interaction was not exercised. To verify:

1. Enable external-session visibility and leave the Agents Window running.
2. Open a Copilot CLI using the same Copilot home, wait before sending its first request, then send it.
3. Verify the session appears without a reload.
4. Create a session in Agent Host and verify discovery does not scan or publish a duplicate.
5. Inspect `[CopilotDiscovery]` logs for the discovery cause and scan timings; transcript appends should not trigger further catalog scans.

pull_requests.title: github: bind workbench requests to a single-attempt executor
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Make the workbench GitHub engine use VS Code's existing proxy/authentication/certificate infrastructure without moving retry, redirect, cancellation, or response-size policy out of the engine.

- Add a reusable platform `IFetchService`: desktop delegates individual wire attempts through pull-based IPC to a Node executor in the main process; web retains a browser-only binding with no remote fallback.
- Reuse `@vscode/proxy-agent` and the native host's proxy/PAC, Basic/Kerberos, and certificate lookups. Enable the existing network-interface-change cache invalidation setting.
- Use lower-level Undici `request`, not fetch, so HTTP 421 is returned instead of transparently redispatching even POST requests. Disable connection-level replay as well.
- Return headers before consuming the body, pull at most 64 KiB per IPC read, decode compressed bodies incrementally, and preserve abort through body consumption. Sanitize executor/proxy diagnostics.
- Release IPC requests when renderers crash or are destroyed. Cancel discarded GitHub REST redirect/retry bodies rather than leaving them open.

The portable engine still owns admission, cooldowns, read coalescing/ETags, application retries, deadlines, and byte limits. This PR does not add the broader REST/GraphQL lifecycle limits from the consolidation work.

## Scope and integration

Related work: #338831 and #338842. This is an independent prerequisite: no client migrations, account-client refactors, Agent Host executor changes, shared-process engine relocation, endpoint extraction, CAPI, or extension API changes are included.

The branch starts at the requested local-main snapshot `301c31b679b3313439f01cdf9cd1d6c63d70d34b`. Current upstream main has advanced; this draft still needs reconciliation with current main before merging. At integration, preserve the endpoint import introduced by #338842 and the telemetry opt-out wiring from #338831 alongside this fetch-service injection.

## Compatibility boundaries

This reuses the shared Node networking helper rather than promising full Chromium proxy parity. As agreed during review, SOCKS4/SOCKS4a, native NTLM/Negotiate-to-NTLM fallback, and ordered PAC failover lists remain documented limitations of the reused helper. A connection failure is not replayed on another route or machine.

Certificate verification and hostname checks remain enabled. There is no new trust store, OS certificate modification, or automatic insecure fallback; `http.proxyStrictSSL: false` is not translated into a verification bypass. Web retains browser/OS trust, CORS, opaque manual redirects, and browser-internal networking limitations. See `src/vs/platform/request/README.md` for the precise settings and lifetime contract.

pull_requests.title: Agent Host: prompt for scoped, targeted workspace search
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Evals showed Copilot Agent Host sessions spending time and tokens on search/discovery. #337342 addresses this by injecting a first-turn workspace file-name tree. This PR is a lightweight alternative to evaluate first: a scoped prompt change only, with no new host plumbing.

- Adds an unconditional, model-agnostic `tool_instructions` line (`COPILOT_AGENT_HOST_TARGETED_SEARCH_TOOL_INSTRUCTION`) in `toolInstructions.ts`. It asks the agent to first take a quick, shallow look at the workspace layout (e.g. top-level directories) unless it already knows it, then use that structure to run targeted searches for the concrete names/symbols/strings/paths in the request, scoped to the most relevant directories, batching independent searches and reads in parallel. It avoids recursively listing the entire workspace and stops once it has enough context. This lets the agent orient itself, which is what the injected tree provides, without new host plumbing. It is intentionally neutral on subagent delegation so explore/search subagents are not suppressed.
- Composes with per-model `tool_instructions` overrides and is appended after `replace`-mode prompts, like the other universal lines.
- Updates unit tests, the prompts `AGENTS.md`, and the Copilot e2e prompt baselines (each baseline diff only inserts the new sentence).

The recorded LLM replay fixtures are unaffected because the replay request matcher asserts only that a system prompt was sent, not its text.

## How to test

- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/{toolInstructions,agentHostPromptRegistry,copilotAgent}.test.js"`: all prompt-related tests pass. The 3 `copilotAgent` failures (`collectDebugLogs…`, and two others) also fail on `main` without this change.
- `AGENT_HOST_UPDATE_AHP_SNAPSHOTS=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts`: baselines regenerated tokenlessly, then re-run in strict replay: 23 passing.
- Eval: compare search/discovery tool-call counts and tokens against `main` and against #337342.

Currently stacked on #338836 for review; the UI fix also applies independently to current `main`. Together these two PRs cover background-refresh policy continuity and selection preservation. Only affects configurations where `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` is effective and `true`. Preserve the Chat composer's Agent selection while startup policy is pending or a failed fetch awaits retry, rather than persisting a temporary Ask/Edit fallback. 1. **Background policy refresh:** After a successful fetch, keep the last accepted policy active while refreshing for the same account, authentication provider, and endpoint. pull_requests.title: Pet: manual-first Interactions and Sprites pages, pets.md, one sprite per event
pull_requests.body:
Builds on #338664 and targets its branch (`fbrancasi/pet-moves`), so it can be reviewed and merged into that PR rather than into `main`.

## What this adds

**Manual first, agentic second.** Everything an agent can teach the pet with `/pet` can now be seen and changed by hand, in the pet's modal or as text, and both paths write to the same store — so agent edits show up in the UI and in `pets.md`, and manual edits are what `petGuide` reports back to the agent.

- **Interactions tab** (*when* the pet plays a sprite, and the one place sprites are assigned)
  - Every built-in event — request finished, confirmation needed, shaken, falls asleep, typing, responding — plays **one** sprite, picked from pictured tiles (*Pet's Own · Taught · Built-in Moves · Pet Animations · Nothing*). A pick applies at once; a taught move replaces the pet's own animation, held while the event lasts. The pet's own reactions can be held too, so every event offers the same sprites.
  - **Clicked** keeps a pool: the pet's own reactions plus sprites added to it, one at random, each with an on/off checkbox.
  - **Text interactions** (phrases → sprite) are written in a form in the pane; chips pick the event when a sprite is handed over from the Sprites page.
  - **Restore Defaults** puts the pet's own animation back on every event (two-click confirm) and leaves text interactions alone.
- **Sprites tab** (*what* the pet can show): taught moves, built-in moves and the pet's own animations, with what uses each (links only). New sprites are made here — *New Move* starts one in `pets.md`, *Import from Clipboard* teaches a move someone shared, *Customize* copies a built-in move to edit. *Use in an Interaction…* hands a sprite to the Interactions page.
- **`pets.md`**: a virtual file (`vscode-chat-pet:/pets.md`) serving moves and reactions as text; saving it teaches the pet and plays the changed move.
- **Model changes**: reactions lose `chance` (a phrase alone always plays; several take turns at random); reactions can be turned off (`enabled`); a new reaction on a single-sprite event replaces the previous one; stored data migrates. The stage in the modal now plays the pet's own animations from their sheets.
- Agent-facing text (tool schema, `petGuide`, `pets.md` help, pet skill) and the accessibility help describe the new model; three review comments on #338664 are addressed (whole-number loop iterations, sheet cache kept on replay, request dedupe by id).

## How to test

1. Show the pet (`/vscode-pet`), open its context menu → **Interactions…**.
2. Select *Request finished*, pick a tile (e.g. `yes-sir` or *Love*), then finish a request: the pet plays it instead of the button press. Pick *Nothing*: the pet does nothing. Pick *Button press*: back to default.
3. Select *Clicked*: turn sprites off/on, *Add Sprite…*, click the pet a few times.
4. *New Text Interaction*: phrases `ship it, do it`, pick a sprite, save; send a message containing one of them.
5. **Sprites** tab: *Play*, *Copy*, *Import from Clipboard* (paste a copied move), *Use in an Interaction…* → lands in the Interactions form with the sprite set.
6. *Edit as Text*: change a move or reaction in `pets.md`, save; the pet plays the change and both pages update.
7. Ask the agent: `/pet when a request finishes, do the SHIP IT move` — the Interactions row updates and `pets.md` shows the reaction.
8. *Restore Defaults* on Interactions: events go back to the pet's own animations; text interactions stay.

Validation run locally: `npm run typecheck-client` (clean), `scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/chat/test/browser/**/*chatPet*.test.js"` (236 passing), `npm run eslint` on touched files, `npm run stylelint`, `npm run gulp hygiene` (clean); all 22 Sprites/Interactions component fixtures render.

pull_requests.title: Agent Host: distinguish human and automatic tool permission decisions
pull_requests.body:
## What

Distinguish explicit human tool-permission decisions from automatic host and assisted-approval decisions in Copilot Agent Host telemetry.

Previously, an SDK approval could be reported as `userAction` even when the host automatically approved a sandboxed command or an internal file read. With this change, those replies carry their actual decision source; only explicitly human-attributed approvals become `userAction`. Denials retain both their SDK result category and responder source, so a human rejection can be separated from policy decisions, cancellation, and unavailable responders.

## Concrete data examples

These are AH `chat.toolApproval` payloads. Previously the event had `confirmKind` but neither `decisionSource` nor `permissionResult`. All new rows have `approvalTelemetryVersion: 2`. An absent source means attribution was not supplied; it is not evidence of a human decision.

| Activity in VS Code / the SDK | Before: `confirmKind` | After: `confirmKind` / `decisionSource` / `permissionResult` |
|---|---|---|
| A terminal command asks for permission and the user clicks **Allow in this Session**. The host remembers the grant and answers this SDK request with an approval. | `userAction` | `userAction` / `human_response` / `approved` |
| The user clicks **Skip** on a terminal confirmation. The command does not run. | `denied` | `denied` / `human_response` / `denied-interactively-by-user` |
| **Assisted permissions** evaluates a command and approves it without a user click. | `userAction` for the ordinary, non-hook SDK approval | `confirmationNotNeeded` / `assisted_approval` / `approved` |
| The host automatically approves a command because terminal sandboxing is enabled, or approves a read of its own internal session resources. | `userAction` for the ordinary, non-hook SDK approval | `confirmationNotNeeded` / `host_policy` / `approved` |
| An SDK permission rule blocks an operation without asking the user. | `denied` | `denied` / source absent if not supplied / `denied-by-rules` |
| The host cannot complete a response (for example, the turn ended or the pending request expired) and the SDK records its attributed fallback rejection. No user clicked Deny. | `denied` | `denied` / `unattended_fallback` / `denied-interactively-by-user` when the SDK converts the host's `reject` reply |
| The user cancels the turn while a confirmation is pending, and the SDK completes that permission request as cancelled. | `denied` | `denied` / source absent if not supplied / `cancelled` |
| An older or unmarked responder returns an SDK approval without identifying who decided. | `userAction` for a non-hook, unscoped approval | `unknown` / source absent / `approved` |

`unattended_fallback` describes an unavailable or interrupted response path, not a permission mode and not a user rejection. The SDK can normalize a programmatic `reject` to `denied-interactively-by-user`, so use `decisionSource` together with `permissionResult`. SDK-originated cancellation can instead emit `cancelled` without a source, as observed in the smoke test. `approvalTelemetryVersion` is a numeric measurement; `confirmKind`, `decisionSource`, and `permissionResult` are event properties.

For example, `confirmKind == "denied"` alone still means a denied resolution. To identify a human rejection, also require `decisionSource == "human_response"` and the appropriate rejection result; a policy denial or cancellation is not a user rejection.

## How

- Carry validated decision provenance from the workbench confirmation flow through the host's permission-response context and the SDK's existing attributed-result API.
- Preserve a typed denial/skip source (`user`, `hook`, or `riskAssessment`) through invocation state and local serialization, instead of a human-only boolean. Explicit UI/voice decisions remain human; known automatic decisions map to host policy at the AH boundary; missing source stays unattributed.
- Stamp hook denials and local Autopilot risk skips at their producers. The workbench risk gate remains local-only; this does not enable it for AH sessions or reconstruct actors from historical protocol metadata.
- Treat working-directory and stored path-allowlist matches as automatic approvals, preserving session/workspace grant scope rather than labelling them human responses.
- Attribute cancelled/stale sandbox-disable requests to unattended fallback. Unclassified SDK failures stay unattributed instead of being guessed policy refusals.
- Preserve existing tool metadata when forwarding attribution, and classify subsequent voice-session auto-approvals as automatic rather than human responses.
- Add `decisionSource`, `permissionResult`, and `approvalTelemetryVersion: 2` to AH `chat.toolApproval`. Missing-source approvals are `unknown`, not guessed human.

This preserves the permission verdicts, rules, and existing per-tool event cadence. It does not add a prompt counter or a scorecard metric. Older/unmarked client decisions remain unattributed, and version 2 should be queried separately from the historical classification.

## Built-product smoke validation

On Windows, Code OSS Dev 1.141.0 at `ba45fb0b4b5`, using the real Copilot SDK provider, verified the UI action, emitted telemetry, and file-system effects for manual allow, explicit Skip, turn cancellation, Allow All, and assisted approval. pull_requests.title: github: harden request execution and add client attribution
pull_requests.body:
Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678.

Harden the existing reusable GitHub engine ahead of the broader request-consolidation work:

- Bound retained requests, coalesced waiters, response sizes, and end-to-end request lifetimes; add caller fairness and reserved admission capacity for interactive/mutation work.
- Preserve rate-limit cooldowns across invalidation and identity-bootstrap failures, classify bounded download diagnostics, and recheck cooldowns before authenticated redirect hops. Keep writes non-retrying except for existing operation-specific reconciliation.
- Add privacy-safe request health summaries and sampled timings using product telemetry, with bounded categories and no request/account/repository content.
- Add binding-supplied product/component identification and per-attempt retry headers. Node egress sends all four headers; browser fetch (including desktop renderers) sends only the CORS-allowed `X-Client-Application` to `api.github.com`. Enterprise browser identification remains disabled until its header contracts are confirmed. Storage redirects receive no identification or retry headers.
- Add deterministic regression coverage and source-adjacent architecture/behavior documentation.

pull_requests.title: chat: offer Microsoft sign-in when an Entra account links to GitHub
pull_requests.body:
## What

Sign-in surfaces now offer **"Continue with Microsoft"** to users who can actually use it: users with a Microsoft work or school account on the device that GitHub links to a GitHub account (for example an Enterprise Managed User). VS Code finds this out silently in the background, so no dialog ever waits for it.

The check chains three silent steps:

1. **Broker accounts:** `microsoft-authentication` returns silent tokens (GitHub Entra audience) for the native broker's work and school accounts. That includes accounts not yet approved for VS Code, capped at 5, with personal Microsoft accounts excluded.
2. **Exchange:** `github-authentication` exchanges each token for a `read:user` GitHub token and reads the linked account with `GET /user`, stopping at the first link.
3. **Result:** core offers the option for that GitHub host.

## Why only the workbench can run it

Getting tokens for accounts the user hasn't approved for VS Code is something no extension should be able to request. So the check uses two provider options that **only the workbench can set**:

- `_workbenchIncludeUnapprovedAccounts` (Microsoft provider)
- `_workbenchEntraExchangeProbe: { subjectTokens }` (GitHub provider)

`prepareSessionRequest` in `mainThreadAuthentication.ts` strips every `_workbench*` option from extension `getSession` requests before they reach a provider. The core probe calls `IAuthenticationService.getSessions` directly.

## Nothing left behind

- **Microsoft:** with the native broker, the probe uses a separate in-memory `PublicClientApplication`. It doesn't approve accounts, touch the cached-account list, write secret storage or fire session events, and the sessions it returns have no ID token. Without the broker, it only reads already-approved accounts from existing clients and never creates one.
- **GitHub:** nothing is linked, persisted, published or confirmed, and the session core gets back has an empty access token. The minted `read:user` token is revoked with `DELETE /applications/{client_id}/token` when the host supports it and the build has a client secret. Otherwise it's left to expire (Code - OSS; see #338555).

## Setting and rollout

`chat.microsoftAuthentication.enabled` changes from a boolean to `auto` / `always` / `never`:

- **Default:** `never`, rolled out through experimentation with `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`, so pulling a treatment also stops probing in running windows. The treatment is `config.chat.microsoftAuthentication.enabled` with string values.
- **Legacy values:** `true` means `always` and `false` means `never`; anything unrecognized means `never`.
- **Experiment trigger:** `experimentTrigger` is logged in every arm while the assigned default is in effect (no user or policy value) and the option can matter (AI features shown, and the product has a Microsoft provider).
- **Telemetry:** `chatSetup.microsoftSignInProbe` reports the outcome (`linked` / `notLinked` / `noMicrosoftAccounts` / `error`), the account count and the duration.

## Where the option shows up

- **`IChatMicrosoftSignInProbeService`** (new, in `chatSetupMicrosoftProbe.ts`) owns the decision. In `auto` it probes in the background as soon as it exists, signed in or not, so forced sign-in dialogs for signed-in users (Agents window, agent host re-sign-in) are ready too. It runs at most one probe per GitHub host with `ThrottlerByKey`, never abandons a running probe, and probes again after Microsoft sign-in changes.
- **Chat setup dialog:** reads the answer without waiting.
- **First-run onboarding ("Welcome to VS Code"):** now has a Microsoft icon button after Apple. It stays hidden until the service offers it and can appear while the step is showing. Before this change, onboarding had GitHub, Google, Apple and GHE hard-coded.

## Reviewer notes

- **Probe cost in `auto`:** probing signed-in users means every signed-in user gets the check in each window. For users with a linked work account, that's a non-interactive Microsoft sign-in record and a short-lived GitHub token per window.
- **"Error" vs "not linked":** any failure in the GitHub step is reported as `notLinked`, so telemetry can't tell a broken exchange from a real "no link".
- **Slow extension start:** how fast the probe finishes depends on how fast `microsoft-authentication` activates. In one cold debug launch that took about 19 seconds, and a forced dialog opened sooner lacked the button; the next one had it.
- **Duplicated names:** the option names and the Entra audience GUID are duplicated between core and the two extensions. Each copy has a comment pointing at the other.

## Validation

- **Unit tests:** chat setup, probe service, onboarding, `MainThreadAuthentication` (stripping `_workbench*` options end to end through `$getSession`), `EntraTokenExchange.probe`, the GitHub provider's probe routing, and `workAccounts` selection.
- **Code - OSS on Windows with the native broker**, via `experiments.override.config.chat.microsoftAuthentication.enabled: "auto"`:
  - **Fresh profile:** the Microsoft icon appears on the onboarding screen about 7 seconds after launch, and the title-bar Sign In dialog offers it on the first try.
  - **Signed-in profile:** the first forced sign-in dialog offers it once the background probe has finished.
- **Not yet tested:** completing an actual sign-in by clicking the new button; macOS or Linux brokers; revocation against a real host with the client secret, which is covered by unit tests only.

pull_requests.title: Mark virtual tool groups as used when they are activated
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338818

## Problem

When more than 128 tools are enabled, Copilot puts extension and MCP tools behind `activate_*` virtual tools. After each change it trims expanded groups back under `HARD_TOOL_LIMIT`, collapsing the group with the lowest `lastUsedOnTurn` first.

Activating a group never updates that group's own `lastUsedOnTurn`. `ToolGrouping.didCall` only updates the groups on the path to the called item, and when the item is a group, that path is just the root. Groups are created with `lastUsedOnTurn = 0`, so a group the model has just activated ranks as the least recently used one.

If the activation pushes the total over the limit, the trim collapses that same group before the request is sent. `runOne` recomputes the tool list right after `_handleVirtualCalls`, so the model gets "Tools activated: …" but the next request contains only the `activate_*` entry again.

Activating again doesn't help. A group only counts as used when one of its tools is called, and that can't happen while it's collapsed.

Fallback groups hit this easily. The first `slots - 1` tools of a server are exposed directly and the rest go into the group, so calling the server's direct tools never refreshes the group.

## What we saw

A session had the Slack and Notion MCP servers enabled. Notion's fallback group, which contains `notion-fetch`, was activated repeatedly. Each time, the older Slack group stayed expanded, because one of its tools had been called earlier. The Notion group was collapsed again every time. The model never received `notion-fetch` and looped on the directly exposed `notion-create-attachment` instead.

## Fix

Set `lastUsedOnTurn` to the current turn when `didCall` expands a group. `ensureExpanded` already does this for `#`-referenced tools. The trim then collapses the group that really is least recently used.

## Test

Added a case to `virtualToolGrouping.spec.ts`:
- Setup: 80 standalone tools, a 20-tool group and a 40-tool group.
- The first group is activated and one of its tools is called.
- The second group is then activated, bringing the total to 140, over `HARD_TOOL_LIMIT`.

On `main`, the newly activated group is collapsed (101 tools). With the fix, the older group is collapsed (121 tools).

`npx vitest --run src/extension/tools/test/node/virtualTools/`: 45 passed.

## Known gaps and follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Same-turn tie.** If the model activates one group and calls a tool from another expanded group in the same response, both get the same `lastUsedOnTurn`. If they're the last groups left to collapse and together exceed the limit, the trim collapses whichever comes first in the tree, which can be the one just activated. One option is to skip groups activated in the current response unless nothing else can be collapsed. I have that change and a test ready if you'd like it here or in a follow-up. It favors the model's explicit request over a tool it used on the same turn, which seemed worth discussing rather than bundling.
- **The trim counts duplicate tools.** The trim loop counts `this._root.tools()`, which includes duplicates: `activate_embeddings` holds copies of tools that are also listed directly or in their home group. `compute()` removes the duplicates from what it returns, so trimming can fire even when the list actually sent is under the limit. Counting unique names would avoid needless collapses, but it changes when trimming happens for everyone, so it should be a separate change.
- **The activation message is built before the trim.** `didCall` returns "Tools activated: …" before the trim runs. If the activated group still can't fit, it's collapsed after the model has been told it's active. If a group is collapsed on a later turn, the old message stays in history. The result should reflect what the trim actually did, and ideally the model should be told when a group is collapsed. Doing that would also settle the same-turn tie above.
- **Misleading error for hidden tools.** Calling a tool from a collapsed group returns "Tool X is currently disabled by the user, and cannot be called.", which is misleading when grouping hid the tool, not the user.

auto_merge.commit_title: Mark virtual tool groups as used when they are activated (#338812)
auto_merge.commit_message:
Activating a virtual tool group never updated the group's own
lastUsedOnTurn, so a just-activated group ranked as least recently used.
When the activation pushed the tool count over HARD_TOOL_LIMIT, the trim
collapsed that same group before the request was sent, and the model
could never reach the tools it was told were activated.

#336628 moved Agent Host to the SDK-owned Copilot runtime, which is where the reported regression began. The bundled runtime update in #338512 (`@github/copilot-sdk@1.0.15-preview.4`, runtime `1.0.89-7`) already restores native execution for file-backed plugins such as those installed through `chat.plugins.marketplaces`.

The remaining gap on `main` was deterministic coverage of the exact reported shape. This test publishes a `ClientPluginCustomization`, exercises `AgentPluginManager` synchronization into Agent Host storage, and uses a plugin containing only `plugin.json`, `hooks.json`, and its hook script. It waits for the native callback because hook execution can finish asynchronously after the provider turn.

No production behavior changes are included in this PR.

## Validation

- [Azure pipeline 478985](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=478985) — passed on commit `8cacf92eb96` across Windows, Linux, and macOS x64
- [Azure pipeline 479012](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=479012) — second Windows and macOS Electron runs passed; Linux was canceled by infrastructure
- [Azure pipeline 479042](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=479042) — Linux-only replacement passed

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotCustomizations.integrationTest.ts` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- managed-plugin UI validation scenario on macOS arm64 with the repository-locked Copilot SDK/runtime and mocked LLM — passed

The SDK-owned runtime does not invoke plugin hook callbacks on Windows. The managed hook execution assertion remains platform-gated and the limitation is documented in `e2e/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`.

The scenario verifies that VS Code synchronizes the plugin, `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `cwd` point at the Agent Host copy, and native `userPromptSubmitted` runs exactly once with `hello`.

pull_requests.title: editor: restore connected tab border and divider customizations
pull_requests.body:
Connected editor tabs still suppressed legacy border customizations after #337986. This restores those colors while preserving the height, wrapping, and corner geometry introduced by #339028.

Fixes #325250.
Fixes #336377.

## Changes

- Restore active top/bottom, hover, selected, modified, and unfocused border customizations. Explicit selected-top colors remain the fallback when the active-top color is absent, without exposing the default theme accent.
- Add `tab.divider`, inheriting `tab.border` unless customized separately. Legacy keeps its existing separators; Pill shows dedicated dividers at every adjacency; Connected shows them only between inactive neighbors. High Contrast retains theme-owned boundaries without redundant dividers.
- Keep the connected cap, curved shoulders, and body separator continuous in default/custom colors and High Contrast. Reserve wrapped action space before assigning row markers so compact tabs do not lose their left boundary.
- Preserve Modern action-background customization on ordinary, upper wrapped, and separate pinned tabs. Color fixtures use isolated customized themes and production-generated CSS, including derived colors.

## Visual evidence

Current production fixtures in Dark: yellow is `tab.border`, white is `tab.divider`, cyan is the active-top accent, and red is the active-bottom accent. Top to bottom: Legacy, Pill, Connected. The linked issue contains the original missing-customization state.

![Current Legacy, Pill, and Connected fixtures with matched custom colors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d469a612-0c31-4d97-b9aa-29ea88e52009)

Compact wrapped tabs in Dark High Contrast, without color overrides. Before/after detail shows the active left boundary and shoulder restored by correcting row classification; the updated tab height is unchanged.

![Compact wrapped HC tab before and after restoring its left contour](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18429c93-ddea-4c61-a950-3c05f95ceca9)

The **Screenshots & Tests** check supplies the broader component-fixture theme report.

## Testing

1. Enable Modern UI and select Connected tabs. Assign distinct colors to `tab.border`, `tab.divider`, `tab.activeBorder`, and `tab.activeBorderTop`. Verify the active contour and accents, with dividers only between inactive neighbors.
2. Switch to Pill, then disable Modern UI for Legacy. Verify rounded Pill outlines and independent dividers; Legacy must not gain a second separator.
3. Wrap enough tabs to select a bottom-row tab with neighbors on both sides. Switch between default and compact tab height. Verify both shoulders meet the body border, row markers remain correct, and Close/Unpin controls stay aligned.
4. Repeat in Dark and Light High Contrast with no overrides. Verify continuous theme-owned outlines and no dedicated dividers.
5. Customize `modernEditorTab.hoverActionBackground` differently from `modernEditorTab.hoverBackground`. Hover ordinary, upper wrapped, and separate pinned tabs in focused and unfocused groups.
6. With Dark+, customize only `tab.selectedBorderTop` and multi-select tabs. Verify the active tab retains the selected-color fallback. In a theme with an active-top color, confirm that fallback does not override it.
7. Customize only `tab.border` and verify `tab.divider` inherits it. Check modified, multi-selected, action-left, clipped, and unfocused states, then clear all overrides and verify the default appearance.

## Validation

Production tab/color regression tests, existing tab fixture behavior checks, render/remount checks, ESLint, stylelint, and staged hygiene pass. Component Explorer validation includes full-folder views and matched physical-pixel shoulder checks.

fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338495

Populate the Copilot MCP customization view before the first message, using the bundled runtime's existing discovery RPCs rather than creating a dummy SDK session.

## Changes

- Query `client.rpc.mcp.discover({ workingDirectory, includeEffectiveSource: true })` through the existing provisional session customization controller. For no-folder browsing, use `mcp.config.list()` without a fabricated discovery directory.
- Combine the primary runtime catalog with the existing ordered, exact-root workspace declarations. Keep workspace-specific results out of provider-global inventory and retain MCP-only plugin ownership.
- Preserve declaration identity, scoped enablement, and real session status across materialization and subsequent refreshes. Runtime-discovered enablement is a default beneath explicit host/client decisions; pending resolution still fails closed at SDK handoff.
- Share host-side user-config invalidation and call `mcp.config.reload()` before querying after external edits. Reuse existing workspace watchers, watch returned source files, and discard stale/disposed responses.
- Add `[Copilot:McpDiscovery]` debug diagnostics for queries, refresh reasons, result counts, publication, and materialization state. Do not log raw configuration, launch arguments, credentials, or RPC error payloads.
- Cover the provider snapshot and both editor/Agents Window adapters without adding provider logic to shared widgets.

This is VS Code-only. It adds no runtime subscription, SDK API, authentication flow, server-control feature, or dependency upgrade.

- Persist revision holder IDs for automation definitions and retained runs. Register holders before saving automation state, release obsolete holders after successful persistence, and reconcile only after successfully loading authoritative automation storage.
- Use atomic cache-manifest writes and preserve captures across restarts, definition edits/deletion, and session unloading. Permanent session deletion releases run holders.

Includes the imported AHP update to `0d9ec389` and documentation of capture and retention semantics.

pull_requests.title: Copilot Chat OTel: emit github.copilot.auto_mode when Auto model selection is used
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338748

## What

When **Auto** is selected in the model picker, the extension routes the turn through `POST /auto` and wraps the selected model in an `AutoChatEndpoint`. The OTel spans then report the concrete model in `gen_ai.request.model`, so there is no way to tell an auto-routed (discounted) request from one where the user pinned the same model. Copilot CLI already reports `gen_ai.request.model = "auto"`, so the two clients currently disagree.

This PR adds a new canonical attribute, **`github.copilot.auto_mode`** (boolean). It is set to `true` on auto-routed spans and left out otherwise:

| Span | Where | How auto is detected |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | `prompt/node/chatMLFetcher.ts` | `isAutoModel(chatEndpointInfo)` |
| `invoke_agent` (agent / ask / edit / subagents) | `intents/node/toolCallingLoop.ts` | `isAutoModel(endpoint)` |
| `invoke_agent Inline Chat` | `inlineChat2/node/inlineChatIntent.ts` | `isAutoModel(endpoint)` |
| `invoke_agent copilotcli` + synthesized per-turn `chat` spans | `chatSessions/copilotcli/node/copilotcliSession.ts` | session model id is `auto` |

The attribute is also documented in `docs/monitoring/agent_monitoring.md` (`invoke_agent` and `chat` tables).

The routing tier (optional in the issue) is not included, to keep this change small. It can be a follow-up.

## How to test

Unit tests, each of which fails without the change:

```
npx vitest --run --pool=forks \
  src/extension/prompt/node/test/chatMLFetcherResponseApiTelemetry.spec.ts \
  src/extension/intents/test/node/toolCallingLoopAutoMode.spec.ts \
  src/extension/inlineChat2/test/node/inlineChatIntent.spec.ts \
  src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/node/test/copilotcliSession.spec.ts -t "auto_mode"
```

Manual check: enable `github.copilot.chat.otel.enabled`, select **Auto** in the model picker, send a chat request, and confirm that the `invoke_agent` and `chat` spans carry `github.copilot.auto_mode: true`. With a pinned model, the attribute should be missing.

`preserves order of edit toolCallIds and permissions for multiple pending edits` in `copilotcliSession.spec.ts` fails for me on `main` without this change as well, so it is unrelated.

## Summary

Tool-call titles can render file links through the generic markdown renderer, which adds a native `title` attribute. When `InlineAnchorWidget` subsequently installs its managed hover, this triggers the repeated "HTML element already has a title attribute" warning.

- Add regression coverage for local and agent-host links, including title rerenders, and verify ordinary links retain their native tooltips.

Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.0

What's Changed

  • [Backport v7.x] fix: selectively re-enable SIMD for ppc64 by @​github-actions[bot] in nodejs/undici#5794
  • Backport upgrade diagnostics lifecycle fixes to v7.x by @​BridgeAR in nodejs/undici#5783
  • [Backport v7.x] fix: honor backpressure in decompression interceptor by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5837
  • fix: close rejected HTTP/2 WebSocket streams on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5876
  • test(fetch): make pull-dont-push exceed any socket buffer by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5889

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.29.1...v7.30.0

v7.29.1

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-w293-vg96-wgc3: BalancedPool could drop function-valued connection options while cloning its configuration, including custom TLS certificate validation callbacks. Undici now preserves connect and legacy tls options when creating upstreams. Fixed by f690157d.
  • GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5: a WebSocket server could select a subprotocol when none was requested, causing an uncaught TypeError that could terminate the process. Undici now rejects the handshake with protocol error 1002. Fixed by 6615e017.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v: a malformed permessage-deflate payload exceeding the configured decompression limit could emit an unhandled zlib error and terminate the process. Undici now destroys the inflater after reaching the limit. Fixed by 63cf698b.
  • GHSA-rx4f-c7p8-82vq: an unclean WebSocketStream close could create an unobserved rejected promise when its writable stream was locked, potentially terminating the process. Undici now propagates the failure through the retained writable stream controller. Fixed by 1858656e.
  • GHSA-2jfj-6hjv-fm6j: shared caches could store and replay responses containing Set-Cookie, disclosing one user's cookies to another caller. Undici now excludes these responses from shared caches, including existing entries and revalidation paths. Fixed by b6c5a002.
  • GHSA-3xpg-4rpp-hhhm: the decompression interceptor did not bound decoded output, allowing compressed responses to consume excessive memory. Undici now limits every decompression stage to 64 MiB by default and supports a configurable maxSize. Fixed by 2c7d7e12.
  • GHSA-pmjh-fq2x-6v4x: a terminal retry failure after response headers were exposed could orphan the original response body, causing consumers to hang indefinitely. Undici now propagates the terminal error to the exposed body. Fixed by 3c672659.

Low severity

  • GHSA-8436-99hf-9mmv: cache interceptors could store and replay responses to unsafe HTTP methods such as POST or DELETE. Undici now restricts cache reads and writes to safe methods while preserving invalidation by successful unsafe requests. Fixed by b61d9432.
  • GHSA-2gqq-gqf2-x968: the dump interceptor could treat an oversized chunked response as successfully truncated when no Content-Length was present. Undici now enforces maxSize against received bytes and aborts oversized responses. Fixed by 21693f40.
  • GHSA-r53p-7pc4-xj5r: the retry interceptor could concatenate a resumed response with inconsistent framing into downstream output, enabling response splitting or corruption. Undici now validates Content-Range against the original response framing before resuming. Fixed by cd8af90b.

What's Changed

  • [v7.x] drop: remove Node.js 26 from shared-builtin CI build by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5592
  • fix(h2): honour headersTimeout by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5604
  • fix(h2): keep the connection ref'd while requests are outstanding by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5605
  • ci: increase Windows workflow timeout on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5621
  • fix(h2): retire the request that completed, not the head of the queue by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5618
  • fix(h2): settle a request whose stream is cancelled by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5607
  • perf: reduce EventSourceStream parser allocations (#5032) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5646
  • fix(h2): handle GOAWAY for CONNECT streams by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5640
  • [v7.x] perf(h1): drop idle-socket timer floor with a ref'd setImmediate (#5707) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5769

pull_requests.title: agentHost: deduplicate native MCP server publication
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

fixes microsoft/vscode#338716. **Migration and disabled-state preservation through migration are explicitly out of scope**, so this PR does not close the issue.

Workspace MCP discovery and live runtime tracking can publish the same server with the same customization ID. Concatenating those records duplicates the Agent Host inventory. The UI then sees ambiguous matches and retains a local row plus both runtime rows, producing three rows for one server.

Merge discovered declarations and live MCP customizations by stable ID at the Copilot publication boundary:
- Preserve declaration identity, source URI, range, and enablement.
- Prefer live connection state and channel, and live MCP App capabilities when present.
- Combine metadata with declaration values taking precedence on conflicts.
- Keep different IDs separate, even when server names match; retain runtime-only servers.

No changes to server launching, migration, or protocol behavior.

## Regression coverage

- Actual Copilot discovery plus live native-server publication produces one record per ID.
- Declaration metadata and enablement survive; stale runtime decisions do not reappear.
- Distinct source identities and runtime-only servers remain present.
- Local-row matching yields 13 rows rather than the reported 17, and 11 enabled servers when the two workspace servers are disabled.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed immediately before commit.
- Focused controller, Copilot publication, and MCP list-widget tests — **133 passing** after compilation:
  ```sh
  ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/mcpListWidget.test.ts --grep 'McpCustomizationController|mcpListWidget|CopilotAgent.*(getChatCustomizations|getSessionCustomizations)'
  ```
- Reduced patch also passed `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run transpile-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, ESLint on all five changed files, and `git diff --check`.
- Repository pre-commit hygiene checks passed.

Tests use mocked SDK boundaries; no live-provider or visual end-to-end test was run.

pull_requests.title: ci: add a Linux unit test job with stable product quality
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #338506 (native GitHub stack; merge bottom-up). Tracking: microsoft/vscode-engineering#4016. Incident: #338418, fixed by #338463.

#338506 runs PR unit tests with `insider`. This PR adds `stable` coverage, so tests that break only in stable builds are also caught in PR CI.

This job would **not** have caught #338418; that was an `insider` failure, and #338506 covers it. It closes a gap that #338506 opens: with no quality, PR CI happened to take the `stable` side of `product.quality === 'insider'` checks (that is how #336700's test, which expected the Stable icon, passed in PR CI). With `insider`, no PR job takes any `stable` path, so a stable-only break would first fail in the stable ADO build on release day. Example: `sessionsApplicationBadge.test.ts` expects `[1]` under `insider` and `[]` under `stable`.

1. Adds a `test_quality` input to `pr-linux-test.yml` (default `insider`) and passes it to the Electron and node.js unit test steps. Artifact names get a `-<quality>` suffix when it isn't `insider`.
2. Adds a separate, parallel `Linux / Electron-Unit (Stable)` job that runs those suites with `VSCODE_TEST_QUALITY=stable`.
3. Updates the docs to mention the extra job.

| Quality tested | Jobs | Change | CI cost delta per PR run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `insider` | `Linux / Electron-Unit`, `macOS / Electron-Unit`, `Windows / Electron-Unit` | Unchanged (from #338506) | 0 |
| `stable` | `Linux / Electron-Unit (Stable)` (`ubuntu-24.04`) | Added | +1 job, 7m42s in [run 36612752313](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36612752313/job/109558044771): +3.6% of the ~218 job-min median. $0, because standard GitHub-hosted runners are free for public repos. Wall-clock unchanged: it runs in parallel, and the slowest path is Electron-Smoke at ~21 min. |

<details>
<summary>Why Linux only</summary>

`product.quality` comes from `product.json` and is the same on every OS, so quality-dependent tests fail the same way everywhere:

- Official ADO builds run the same Electron, node.js and browser unit tests on Windows x64, Linux x64 and macOS arm64 for every quality (`product-build.yml`, unless `VSCODE_STEP_ON_IT`). None of the `product-build-*-test.yml` steps branch on quality.
- `src/vs` has only one expression that combines quality with a platform check: the `window.menuStyle` default in `desktop.contribution.ts` (`native` on macOS stable). No unit test loads that file.
- Only 3 test files read the global `product.quality`: `agentSessionsDraftHandoff.test.ts`, `chatConfiguration.test.ts` and `sessionsApplicationBadge.test.ts`. None of them is platform-gated. The other quality-related tests stub `IProductService` with an explicit quality.
- The quality failures we know of failed identically on all OSes: ADO builds 477897, 477908 and 477916 (Linux, macOS, Windows), and #336700 ("fails identically across platforms").
- `stable` already passes the full suites on macOS arm64 (locally) and Linux (this job). Windows is the only OS never run with `stable`, and nothing in `src/vs` couples `stable` with Windows.

| Alternative | Added job-min per PR run | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| All 3 OSes | +24 (+11%), including ~$0.82 on `macos-26-xlarge` (`macos_xl`, $0.102/min) and ~9.5 min of the self-hosted Windows 1ES pool | No evidence of OS-specific stable failures |
| Fold into the required `Linux / Electron-Unit` job | +6.0; blocking without a required-check change | Keeps jobs parallel and short instead of doubling that job to ~14 min |
| `stable` for node.js tests only | ~+2.8 | All 3 tests that read the global quality run in the Electron runner (`browser/`, `electron-browser/`) |
| `stable` only for PRs into `release/*` | ~0 on `main` | Stable-only breaks land on `main`; they would first fail on unrelated cherry-pick PRs during endgame |
| Path filter | varies | 83 quality checks across 57 files; no path predicts which change matters |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Related</summary>

| | |
|---|---|
| Tracking issue | microsoft/vscode-engineering#4016 |
| `insider` coverage | #338506 (base PR) |
| `stable` coverage | #338728 (this PR) |
| Stack | Native GitHub stack: #338506 (bottom) → #338728 (top) |
| Incident | #338416 (`main`, setting and test), #338418 (`release/1.140` cherry-pick, setting only), #338463 (test fix) |
| Earlier quality failure | #336700 (`insider`-only, all OSes) |
| Same pattern elsewhere | #338290 (`product.quality === 'insider' ? Draw : Off`) |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Example breakage (why quality coverage matters)</summary>

#338416 changed `chat.agentsParallelWorkBanner.enabled` from `product.quality === 'insider'` to `false` on `main`, together with its test. The `release/1.140` cherry-pick #338418 took only the setting. Its PR CI passed because, with no quality, both sides of the assertion were `false`. Official insider builds then failed until #338463.

| ADO build (`release/1.140`) | Commit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [20260928.37](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477897) | `c2eef65426f` (#338418) | ❌ Electron unit tests failed on Linux, macOS and Windows |
| [20260928.40](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477908) | `a78e233e81e` | ❌ Same failure |
| [20260928.42](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477916) | `ce814adc30a` | ❌ Same failure |
| [20260928.44](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477925) | `acbb06ed809` (#338463) | ✅ Fixed |

#338506 alone catches this breakage. Under `stable` the assertion expected `false` and got `false`, so this job would have passed. This job covers the opposite case: expectations that break only under `stable`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

- **Split out of #338506**: #338506 only runs the existing unit test jobs with `insider`, at no extra cost. This PR is the separate decision about paying for `stable` coverage.
- **Runs on every PR, not only `release/*`**: release branches are cut from `main`. With a `release/*`-only gate, a stable-only break from `main` would first show up on unrelated cherry-pick PRs during endgame.
- **Separate job, not folded in**: kept as its own parallel job so the existing unit test jobs stay short.
- **Not blocking yet**: to block merges, `Linux / Electron-Unit (Stable)` must be added to the required status checks for `main` and `release/*`. That needs repo admin.
- **Native GitHub stack**: this PR sits on top of #338506 in a native GitHub stack. `Code OSS` CI runs on this layer too, including the new job (run [36612752313](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36612752313)). When #338506 merges, this PR retargets to `main` automatically.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- The full local suites pass with `VSCODE_TEST_QUALITY=stable` on macOS arm64: node.js unit 19,599 passing, Electron unit 44,352 passing, 0 failing.
- `Linux / Electron-Unit (Stable)` passed in 7m42s in [run 36612752313](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36612752313/job/109558044771).
- `go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.7 -shellcheck= -pyflakes= -ignore 'is unknown. available labels' .github/workflows/pr.yml .github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml`: no findings.
- Costs: job medians from 20 green `Code OSS` PR runs on 2026-09-29, and per-minute rates from the [GitHub Actions runner pricing reference](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing).

</details>

pull_requests.title: chat: share complete status pill rows across windows
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follow-up to #332982.

## Summary

The Agents Window and editor/panel inputs already shared the pill-row renderer, but the editor's Agent Host adapter used a reduced catalog that omitted **Subagents** and **Customizations**. This completes that wiring without adding a second implementation.

- Use the complete shared pill catalog in editor and panel Agent Host inputs.
- Share subagent grouping, newest-first ordering, status filtering, and customization parsing/presentation between windows.
- Share issue-state icons and single-entry context-menu actions so those presentations do not drift either.
- Add regression coverage for live updates, chat switching, filter recovery, navigation dispatch, focus restoration, and subscription disposal; update accessibility help and the existing visual fixtures.

Existing application-wide visibility preferences are preserved. Subagents and Customizations remain hidden by default and can be enabled from the pill-row context menu. Non-Agent Host Local chat behavior and each window's navigation/compact-layout behavior remain unchanged.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed, zero compilation errors.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed, including after updating the branch to current `main`.
- `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR -z -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 npm run eslint --` — passed for all 20 changed TypeScript files before committing.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed.
- Normal pre-commit hygiene hook — passed.
- Six dark/light component fixture renders — passed. Verified visible Subagents/Customizations controls, ARIA labels, matching row/pill heights, and loaded icon fonts.

Focused Electron tests — **130 passed**, including on current `main`:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentHost/agentHostSessionInputPills.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatInputPills.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionBackgroundActivitiesControl.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionCustomizations.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostSessionCustomizations.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/accessibility/chatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/sessionChatPills.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/test/common/chatIssue.test.ts
```

The three per-item action regressions also pass independently under name filtering:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatInputPills.test.ts --grep 'shares single-entry'
```

## How to test

1. Open an Agent Host session in the editor window's Chat panel or chat editor, and compare with the Agents Window.
2. Use the pill-row context menu to enable **Subagents** and **Customizations**.
3. Run a task that delegates to subagents and uses a known skill or instruction. Confirm the pills appear, their entries navigate correctly, and the customization list includes only items used by that chat.
4. Switch Subagent Options between **Show All** and **Show In Progress**. Confirm completed entries are filtered, options remain reachable when everything is filtered out, and preferences carry across windows.
5. Compare issue-state icons and single-item removal actions, then use keyboard navigation and switch chats to check focus and scoping.

Live-provider end-to-end and screen-reader testing were not run; UI validation used the component fixtures and browser/Electron regression tests above.

pull_requests.title: Publish chat background work and show background shells above the chat input
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Depends on: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/482
Replaces: #338713
Related: #336348, #337684

- Publish Copilot's background work into AHP chat state with `chat/backgroundWorkSet` and `chat/backgroundWorkRemoved`: shells that keep running after their tool call returns (attached or detached), and running background subagents with their chat. Copilot only for now; Claude and Codex can follow.
- Keep the list out of `ChatSummary`, so it isn't broadcast to every session subscriber. Both pills read `ChatState.backgroundWork`: the Agents window through the chat subscription it opens while the session is active, and the editor window from the chat it shows.
- Read `session.rpc.tasks.list()` on `session.background_tasks_changed` and when a client starts watching the chat, and poll `tasks.refresh()` every 5 seconds while a watched chat has detached shells.
- Keep the list independent of turns, reconcile it when a replacement session starts, and read again after an abort so finished shells don't linger.
- Show shells in a new **Background Shells** pill above the chat input, in both the Agents window and the editor window, with elapsed time and the shell ID from `_meta`. Only detached shells carry a **Detached** label, so an unlabeled shell is attached, matching the GitHub app. Rows are keyed by the protocol `id`, and other kinds, subagents included, aren't shown yet.
- Leave `terminal` unset until shell output streaming lands, and leave turn completion and Stop unchanged.
- Sync the protocol with `scripts/sync-agent-host-protocol.ts` at `dc9ff6b0`, the head of microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482, so the two PRs can merge back to back. `main` already has microsoft/agent-host-protocol#484 from #339007, so the only protocol changes here are #482's background work. Once #482 merges, `.ahp-version` should point at its merged commit.

Still to do: clear a chat's background work when its session is disposed.

How to test:

1. Ask Copilot to run `sleep 120` with its shell tool in async mode.
2. A **1 Background Shell** pill appears above the input. Its details show the shell ID and elapsed time, with no Attached label.
3. Ask for another `sleep 120` with `detach: true`: the pill reads **2 Background Shells**, and only the new row shows **Detached**.
4. Send another message or press Stop: the shells stay listed until their commands exit. Repeat in an editor-window Agent Host chat.

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

- After merging `main` in `fa17532f`: `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and ESLint on the 37 changed `.ts` files passed. `npm run test-node` on the Agent Host session, service, state manager, and agent tests: 2022 passing; on the protocol server handler: 164 passing; on the Agent Host `common` tests: 931 passing. `./scripts/test.sh` on the pill, accessibility help, and sessions provider tests: 584 passing. The full Copilot E2E suite passed in replay mode with `main`'s Copilot SDK 1.0.16: 233 passing.
- The protocol folder is synced from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482 at `dc9ff6b0`; compared with `main`, it only adds background work types, actions, and reducer cases.

</details>

-----------------------------------------

<details>
<summary>Inspirations from</summary>

- Listing tasks on `session.background_tasks_changed` with a revision counter extends [`_reconcileSubagentTaskStatuses`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a0c82f9df6268b5d35d109254b995190b02d2aa5/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L1814-L1853).
- What gets listed follows what starts a Copilot turn: [shell completions and background agents finishing](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a0c82f9df6268b5d35d109254b995190b02d2aa5/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSystemNotification.ts#L81-L113).
- Keying rows by the entry `id` follows the protocol's rule that [`id` is opaque](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/dc9ff6b0c404f35edefd1ab2d16422be64f0a0b7/types/channels-chat/state.ts#L229-L236).
- Reading the Agents window list from `ChatState` follows [`_createChatCurrentTurnChangesObservable`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/14b9d22f9a980b451aacff4b0ed3864ca2a1b7c4/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L2467-L2485), which subscribes to the chat through [`createActiveSessionSubscriptionObs`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/14b9d22f9a980b451aacff4b0ed3864ca2a1b7c4/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/agentHostSessionChangesets.ts#L240-L267) only while the session is active.
- Watching only while a chat has subscribers comes from [`AgentService._watchChatHistory`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a0c82f9df6268b5d35d109254b995190b02d2aa5/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L6355-L6364).
- Sharing one pill between both windows follows [`createSessionPullRequestPillData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a0c82f9df6268b5d35d109254b995190b02d2aa5/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/sessionPullRequestPill.ts#L24).
- Syncing from the AHP PR head, then recording the merged commit, follows [#338952](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/5470377e71f72089f2bbd5eb8aeb862892f78b31).

</details>

pull_requests.title: Fix timeout issue for remote agent host connection
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #338665

## Problem

The agent host client treats a remote connection as dead if no complete message arrives for 25 seconds. Over SSH and dev tunnels, the WebSocket lives in the shared process, which only forwards complete messages to the window. A large message on a slow link, like the 94 MB snapshot the host sends after a reconnect, looked like silence. The client dropped the connection, reconnected, received the same message again, and looped.

## Approach

Count incoming bytes, not just complete messages, as proof the connection is alive. The regular remote extension host already works this way. A dead connection still sends nothing, so it's still detected within 25 seconds.

- Transports can report that data is still arriving through a new optional `onDidReceiveData` event. The client restarts its liveness timer when it fires.
- **SSH and desktop tunnels:** the shared process watches the raw bytes and sends the window at most one activity event per second per connection. An SSH relay that's being replaced stops reporting immediately, so it can't make its replacement look alive.
- **Browser tunnel and Web PubSub:** these already see partial data in the window and report it directly. Web PubSub counts only chunks from the host, not relay acknowledgements, and reports per chunk (up to about 900 KB) rather than per byte.
- **WSL and dev containers:** these are local links, so they report nothing.

## Not in this PR

- Very large messages. Reconnects still resend every open chat's full history, and messages over 100 MiB (32 MiB on Web PubSub) still fail. That needs host changes, such as paging chat history.
- Dev containers behind a remote agent host, and the editor-remote and embedder web tunnel connections.

## Testing

New unit tests cover the client's liveness check, including a reconnect whose response takes 60 seconds to download. They also cover each transport's reporting, and run the SSH and desktop tunnel relays over real loopback sockets.

To try it manually, connect to an SSH agent host with several large sessions, slow the network (for example with Network Link Conditioner), and reconnect. Before this change the connection drops about every 25 seconds. With it, the reconnect completes.

<details>
<summary>Test run: 21 suites, 867 passing</summary>

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/relayActivity.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/relayTransport.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/reconnectingTransport.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/tunnelAgentHostConnector.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/webSocketOverDuplex.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sshRemoteAgentHostService.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/tunnelAgentHostService.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/wslRemoteAgentHostService.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/devContainerAgentHostProtocol.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/sshRemoteAgentHostService.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/wslRemoteAgentHostService.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/browserTunnelAgentHostService.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/devContainerAgentHostService.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/electron-browser/devContainerAgentHostConnector.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/electron-browser/tunnelAgentHostServiceImpl.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/workbench/services/agentHost/test/browser/editorRemoteAgentHostServiceClient.test.ts \
 --run src/vs/workbench/services/agentHost/test/common/editorRemoteAgentHostTransport.test.ts
```

Result: 867 passing, 0 failing. `npm run typecheck-client` and ESLint on the changed files are clean.

</details>

pull_requests.title: Show active background shells in agent chats
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Depends on: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/475
Related: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336348

- Add a **Background Shells** pill above the Agents window chat input. It lists the chat's background shells with running or waiting status, attached or detached mode, and live elapsed time, and opens a list even for a single shell.
- Publish shells from the Copilot Agent Host: whenever `session.background_tasks_changed` fires or a client starts watching the chat, read `session.rpc.tasks.list()` and dispatch the new AHP `chat/backgroundShellSet` and `chat/backgroundShellRemoved` actions.
- Keep the list independent of turns. Shells survive steering and turn completion, and leave the list only when they complete, fail, or are cancelled.
- Reject superseded task-list reads, and keep the last known list when a read fails.
- While a client watches a chat that has detached shells, call `session.rpc.tasks.refresh()` before listing, every 5 seconds.
- Watch shells only while a hydrated chat has subscribers: `AgentService._watchChatHistory` becomes `_watchChatUpdates` and also calls the new optional `IAgent.watchChatBackgroundShells`.
- Mirror each chat's list into its session chat summary through `session/chatUpdated`. Lists are per chat, so the same shell ID in two chats doesn't collide.
- Open a shell's details on row activation (`openHoverOnSelect`), move keyboard focus into them, and pin them to the bottom of the picker (`alignToParentBottom`) so they stay above the input.
- Use the shared chat-input pill placement, which prefers opening above the input.
- Hand-apply the protocol changes from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#475 without bumping `.ahp-version`, as d1fdacc1767 did. A full AHP sync can follow once #475 merges.
- Leave turn completion alone: an attached shell still keeps the turn active (#336348).

Still to do in this draft:

- Show the pill in the editor window's chat too, not only the Agents window.
- Fix a race where aborting a turn can drop an in-flight shell-list refresh, leaving the list stale until the next task change.

How to test:

1. In the Agents window, ask Copilot to run `sleep 120` with its shell tool in async mode, without detaching.
2. A **1 Background Shell** pill appears above the input. Open it and select the shell to see its status, mode, and elapsed time.
3. Send another message or let the turn finish: the shell stays listed. When the command exits, it leaves the list. The turn stays active until then, which is existing behavior (#336348).

Validation on this branch:

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npx eslint --max-warnings=0` on the 31 changed `.ts` files: passed.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: retry permission mode rejected before managed settings resolve
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Pragmatic mitigation for the intermittent `Copilot SDK rejected permission mode 'allow-all'` error on the first turn of a session. Users with Auto Approve and enterprise managed settings hit it and have to resend the message.

**Cause:** the Copilot runtime resolves managed settings (including `permissions`) in the background. VS Code doesn't wait for `session.managed_settings_resolved` before calling `permissions.setMode`, and the runtime rejects bypass mode until settings finish loading. In the reported logs, the rejection came about 57ms before settings resolved with `bypassPermissionsDisabled=false`.

**Change:** in `CopilotAgentSession.syncPermissionMode`, if `setMode` is rejected before this session has seen a top-level `session.managed_settings_resolved`, wait up to 3s for that event and retry once.

**Safety:**
- The retry is the same SDK call with the same mode. The runtime still enforces managed policy, so a real policy block is rejected again and fails as before.
- It retries at most once. If settings had already resolved before the first call, a rejection fails immediately as today.
- If the event never arrives, or it fired before the session subscribed, the worst case is a 3s delay followed by the existing error.
- The launcher and wrapper are unchanged.

This doesn't replace a more fundamental fix, such as waiting for managed settings before the first turn.

**Testing:**
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts`: passed (737 tests). New tests cover retry-then-success and still-rejected-after-one-retry.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/agentHost/test/node/**/*.test.js"`: 3 failures, all in `copilotAgent.test.ts`. The same 3 fail on the base commit without this change.

(Written by Copilot)
