Fixes #338708

## What changed

- add the experimental `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceModel` setting, whose string value is the OpenAI live model ID Voice Mode should use
- keep OpenAI API-key entry in Models Management and confirm the configured model when a GPT-Live session connects
- use OpenAI GPT-Live over WebRTC only when client BYOK is allowed, an OpenAI key exists, and that key can access the configured model
- read the active OpenAI provider configuration only inside the Copilot extension host and preserve the complete SDP offer during session exchange
- preserve the hosted MAI Voice Mode backend when the setting is empty, the key is missing, or the configured model is unavailable
- keep the API key in the built-in Copilot extension host and exchange only the SDP offer/answer with the workbench
- route GPT-Live client delegations through the existing VS Code/Copilot coding-agent flow
- synchronize direct WebRTC audio and microphone state with the existing Voice Mode UI, push-to-talk lifecycle, and `agents.voice.speakResponses`

## Reviewer notes

The configured live model is intentionally not added to Models Management or chat model pickers. Models Management remains the place to securely add the OpenAI key; the new setting only stores a model ID.

The existing `isClientBYOKAllowed` policy remains authoritative. The proposed speech-provider bridge retains extension identity so only the configured Copilot Chat extension can use the stored key to create a live session. The extension host returns only the OpenAI session ID and SDP answer, never the API key.

Once BYOK has been selected, a live-session failure is surfaced instead of silently switching billing paths. Availability failures before selection continue through the existing hosted MAI backend.

## How to test

1. Open **Models Management**, choose **Add Provider** → **OpenAI**, and enter an OpenAI project API key.
2. Set `"agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceModel": "<live-model-id>"`.
3. Start Voice Mode. With access to that model, verify that VS Code confirms it is using the model from the OpenAI provider, then verify that speech input, remote audio, and coding-agent delegation work.
4. Clear the setting or use a model ID that the key cannot access. Verify that Voice Mode uses the existing hosted backend.
5. Toggle `agents.voice.speakResponses` while connected and verify that remote audio follows the setting.

pull_requests.title: Modern UI: Fix compact status bar item spacing
pull_requests.body:
Fixes the compact-density status bar gaps reported in #334933 while preserving the established spacing of ordinary status bar items. The change restores the semantic margin exceptions for joined and colored items and adds production-component fixture coverage.

Fixes #334933

## What was broken

Modern UI's compact-density rule reapplied a 2px margin to every status bar label. That overrode the status bar's narrower semantic rules:

- joined split-button edges reopened into a visible gap;
- colored labels no longer covered their complete item background;
- middle segments of three-part controls could gain unintended spacing.

## What changed

- Restore zero margins only on joined and colored edges in compact density.
- Preserve the existing compact spacing for ordinary items.
- Add a computed-style regression matrix for default and compact density.
- Add real `StatusbarEntryItem` fixtures for simple, colored, two-part split, three-part split, and colored split controls.
- Exercise Dark, Light, and Dark High Contrast themes using production status bar heights and platform typography.

## Visual audit

**Result: 6/6 density and theme variants pass.**

The fixture captures below use the production `StatusbarEntryItem`, production CSS, the macOS workbench system font, and identical dimensions and zoom.

### Simple button — matched before and after

![Simple status bar button before and after in default and compact density](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e97a3d1f-be75-4f72-b5bb-5818f0b4ca89)

The simple button is intentionally unchanged: default density retains 3px margins and compact density retains 2px margins.

### Branch + sync split button — matched before and after

![Branch and sync split status bar button before and after in default and compact density](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40d40b2e-2384-4092-81fe-13fcdafd41e1)

Default density remains unchanged. In compact density, the pre-fix 4px visual gap closes to a 0px seam while the outer compact spacing remains intact.

### Native Code OSS context

| Default density | Compact density |
|---|---|
| ![Code OSS default-density status bar validation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a91cade3-a87f-4a14-a1cf-96a58cc07adb) | ![Code OSS compact-density status bar validation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4612b43d-da38-41e7-a5e6-dfd7b7f9f552) |
| Split seam: **0px** · colored insets: **0/0px** | Split seam: **0px** · colored insets: **0/0px** |

## Coverage matrix

| Area | Scenarios | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary items | Simple text, icon + text, hovered fill | Existing spacing preserved |
| Colored items | Warning, error, remote, colored split | 0/0px label-to-item insets |
| Two-part split | Branch + sync, primary + dropdown | 0px joined seam |
| Three-part split | Left, middle, and right segments | 0px at both seams |
| Density | Default and compact | 2/2 |
| Theme | Dark, Light, Dark High Contrast | 3/3 |

The `Screenshots & Tests` report provides the complete fixture theme sweep.

## Testing

1. Enable `workbench.experimental.modernUI`.
2. In default density, hover ordinary, colored, and joined status bar items and verify the existing spacing is unchanged.
3. Switch `window.density.layout` to `compact`.
4. Verify ordinary controls retain compact spacing.
5. Verify branch + sync and other split controls have no gap at joined edges.
6. Verify colored hover surfaces cover their complete item backgrounds.

Validation completed locally:

- `npm run transpile-client`
- Modern UI browser unit suite: **82 passing**
- ESLint on the changed TypeScript files
- Stylelint on the changed CSS
- Component Explorer render/dispose sweep: **14/14 variants passed**
- Code OSS Dev 1.141.0 on macOS arm64 in isolated default- and compact-density profiles

The local ffmpeg build lacks the `drawtext` filter, so the raw scenario videos could not be captioned; screenshots and independent DOM geometry assertions are unaffected.

pull_requests.title: ci: allow 30 minutes for Windows Electron integration tests
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
Raise only the GitHub Actions **Windows / Electron integration-test step** timeout from 20 to 30 minutes, matching the equivalent Azure pipeline budget introduced in #338685.

## Investigation
The [reported failure on #338698](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36589259095/job/109477742532?pr=338698) is an aggregate step timeout, not an individual test assertion failure:

- The step started at 15:21:53 UTC and GitHub Actions cancelled it at 15:41:53 UTC: `The action 'Run integration tests (Electron)' has timed out after 20 minutes.`
- All four parallel Agent Host E2E groups passed; the last finished at 15:35:00 (about 13m07s into the step).
- The remaining node.js integration tests passed at 15:38:27. Extension suites then continued passing through Git at 15:41:45; cancellation occurred during Git Base startup.
- A [nearby successful Windows run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36589686489/job/109480046973) needed 16m52s for the same integration step. Linux and macOS passed in the reported run.
- #338685 raised the Azure test budgets but did not change the GitHub Actions workflows.

This is targeted CI-budget hardening, not a claim that a test race or the underlying runtime variability has been fixed. No test assertions, per-test timeouts, retries, skip conditions, commands, or other job budgets change.

## Other occurrences in the past 24 hours

Reviewed **346 Code OSS workflow runs created between 2026-09-28 15:59:34 UTC and 2026-09-29 15:59:34 UTC**, including earlier attempts of rerun workflows (so a later green result does not hide the original failure). Each job below was checked against its downloaded log, not inferred from duration: all contain `The action 'Run integration tests (Electron)' has timed out after 20 minutes.`

Found **15 additional Windows / Electron job attempts across 14 runs**, beyond the originally reported #338698 job. The table records the last suite/progress visible before cancellation; it does not identify that suite as faulty.

pull_requests.title: editor: hide text drop feedback over rejected targets
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #103487.

Implements the [reporter's accepted alternative](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/103487#issuecomment-768375221): hide the insertion marker when releasing the dragged text would be rejected. This is a conservative alternative to #338027; it does not broaden drop acceptance.

## Changes

- Resolve captured-pointer drag movement and release through the same mouse-handler path, retaining release hit-test classification and checking actual editor-widget bounds.
- Forward invalid/no-position movement and share drop eligibility between preview and release, clearing the marker without ending the drag so reentry still works.
- Keep out-of-bounds scrolling separate from drop feedback. General selection projections and native external `DragEvent`/`dataTransfer` behavior are unchanged.
- Add 28 rendered-editor regressions covering content/gutter move and copy, undo, rejected surfaces and releases, rendered marker disappearance and reentry, scaled bounds, wrapping, RTL gutters, endpoint copying, Escape, and scrolling.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed on both the unmodified starting commit (`db46a82c4f4`) and the final changes.
- ESLint on all seven changed files and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Focused Electron suites — **310 passing**:
  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\editor\contrib\dnd\test\browser\dnd.test.ts --run src\vs\editor\test\browser\view\viewController.test.ts --run src\vs\editor\test\browser\widget\codeEditorWidget.test.ts --run src\vs\editor\test\browser\controller\cursor.test.ts --reporter dot
  ```
- Chromium regressions — **28 passing**:
  ```powershell
  npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --run src\vs\editor\contrib\dnd\test\browser\dnd.test.ts --reporter dot
  ```
- Negative control: restoring only the original mouse handler while keeping the contribution fix produced **19 regression failures**, including missing no-position notifications and incorrect gutter feedback. The handler fix was restored before the final green runs.

The new tests exercise `MouseHandler`/`MouseDownOperation`, real hit testing, view-to-model conversion, and rendered feedback; they do not directly fire downstream editor emitters. Pointer events are synthetic and target the captured view-lines element. Native OS-level dragging beyond a real VS Code window has not been manually verified; negative client coordinates cover its target-resolution behavior.

pull_requests.title: test: tolerate slow disk I/O in agent host persistence tests
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
Give only the two disk-backed Agent Host tests that timed out in [build 478269, Windows Electron unit tests](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=478269&view=logs&j=7d207509-2e04-5536-0391-4ea7561cdba7&t=bb369bd4-5e7c-56c7-c55a-10dafdd2b656) a bounded 60-second timeout:

| Test | Previous budget | Unchanged Windows rerun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `real v1 registry rows retain undefined provenance until service migration` | 10 seconds | Passed in 227 ms |
| `external session adoption survives closing and reopening the database` | 30 seconds in Electron CI (inherited) | Passed in 161 ms |

Both tests create real SQLite files and close/reopen database connections. Keep their persistence coverage, assertions, cleanup, and production code unchanged; do not add retries or change suite-wide timeouts.

## Investigation
- The original job reported only these two timeout failures; the same source passed both tests in Linux and macOS Electron jobs.
- The existing Windows rerun passed both tests without code changes. Other filesystem/database tests were also much slower in the failed attempt.
- Both tests passed 20 consecutive local Windows Electron runs in CI mode before the change, and all 697 related tests passed together.

The evidence is consistent with transient Windows CI I/O latency, but the original logs do not identify the stalled operation and no deterministic race was reproduced. pull_requests.title: Remove unsolicited MCP authentication hint and add tool routing cache
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

This change makes MCP authentication contextual instead of prompting about unrelated servers at the start of a conversation.

It adds an experimental, default-off setting, `chat.agentHost.experimental.mcpToolRouting`, that replaces the proactive authentication hint with deferred server-level routing tools. These routing tools let the model decide whether an unavailable MCP server is relevant before VS Code starts or connects to it and potentially asks the user to authenticate.

Cached metadata is used only as a routing index. It is never treated as an authoritative execution contract: current tools are always discovered from the live server before any MCP tool can be used.

The targeted authentication card also gains **Disable for This Session**, allowing the user to decline authentication and prevent that server from being offered again during the current session.

## Why

Previously, an MCP server in `AuthRequired` state could cause a generic authentication hint even when the user's task had nothing to do with that server. This was disruptive and gave the model no way to first determine whether authentication was actually useful.

The new approach keeps unavailable servers discoverable while deferring startup and authentication until the model has evidence that a server is relevant.

## Flow

When MCP tool routing is enabled:

1. VS Code creates one deferred routing tool for each configured MCP server whose live tools are not currently available to the model.
2. The routing tool description always includes the configured server name and explains that:
   - it represents an MCP server that is not currently available to the model;
   - selecting it starts or connects to the server;
   - the user may be asked to authenticate;
   - it should be selected only when the current task clearly needs that server, never speculatively.
3. If cached tool metadata exists, the description also includes the previously observed tool names and descriptions. The description explicitly identifies this data as a potentially stale routing hint.
4. If no cached tool metadata exists, the routing tool is still available. The model uses the server name to judge relevance.
5. If the model does not select the routing tool, no live tool discovery or targeted authentication is triggered by this routing path.
6. If the model selects it, VS Code performs a live `mcp.listTools` request. Starting or connecting to the server may trigger the existing targeted authentication flow.
7. The authentication card lets the user choose:
   - **Authenticate** to continue;
   - **Cancel** to decline this attempt;
   - **Disable for This Session** to cancel the attempt and write a session-scoped MCP disable decision.
8. After successful connection, VS Code refreshes the routing cache and asks the model to search tools again. Only the server's current live tools can then be selected and executed.
9. Once live tools are available, or if the server is disabled for the session, its deferred routing tool is hidden from tool search.

With `chat.agentHost.experimental.mcpToolRouting` disabled, the existing proactive authentication-hint behavior remains unchanged.

## Implementation Notes

- The persistent cache is keyed by a hash of the server name and stable configuration fingerprint.
- Cached entries contain bounded tool names and descriptions; raw server configuration, headers, environment variables, and credentials are not persisted or exposed to the model.
- A changed server configuration produces a cache miss.
- Live discovery remains authoritative before execution.
- Session disablement uses the existing customization enablement mechanism rather than introducing a second source of truth.
- The setting is synchronized through the typed Agent Host configuration bridge and defaults to `false`.

## Validation

Passed after merging the latest `origin/main`:

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "MCP.*routing proxy|MCP tools add a routing proxy|configured MCP server adds|tool-triggered MCP auth"` — 6 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatToolAuthenticationSubPart.test.ts` — 2 passing
- `git diff --check`
- Pre-commit hygiene check — passed

pull_requests.title: automations: fix timestamp placement in session history list
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337064

## Description

In the automations history list, failed automations rendered with their timestamp pushed to the far right of the row, instead of appearing inline as `<workspace> - Failed - <time ago>` like other statuses (e.g. Completed).

### Root cause

`.session-title` and `.session-description` shared a single `flex: 1` CSS rule (intended to push trailing items, like the timestamp, to the end of the row). `.session-description` is only rendered when `getSessionStatusMessage()` returns a non-`undefined` message, which is the case for the `Error` (Failed) status but not for `Completed` (returns `undefined`, so no description element exists) or `InProgress`/`NeedsInput` (the whole details row is hidden via `hideDetails`). So Failed was the only status where the description element existed *and* the details row was shown, causing its `flex: 1` to expand and push `.session-time` all the way to the end of the row.

### Fix

Split the shared rule in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/sessionsList.css` so `.session-description` no longer has `flex: 1` — it now sizes to its own content (still truncating with ellipsis if needed), while `.session-title` keeps `flex: 1` to push the timestamp to the end.

## How to test

1. Trigger or view an automation run that fails.
2. Open the session history list (Agents / Automations view).
3. Confirm the failed item's row reads `<workspace> - Failed - <time ago>` with the timestamp immediately following the status text, matching the layout of other statuses, instead of being pushed to the far right of the row.

This is a CSS-only change; no other statuses (Completed, InProgress, NeedsInput) are affected.

- **POSIX process-name map** (`terminalProcess.ts`): `['abacusai', GeneralShellType.AbacusAI]`, matching the native binary name.
- **Windows node.exe command-line pattern** (`windowsShellHelper.ts`): `/[\\/]@abacus-ai[\\/]cli[\\/]/i` → `abacusai.exe`, matching the npm package directory (`node_modules/@abacus-ai/cli/scripts/npm-wrapper/shim.cjs`).
- `TerminalLabelComputer.agentCliShellTypes` and the setting description updated accordingly.

Tests mirror the existing coverage: OSC-title shell-type detection for the CLI's default title, and a `TerminalLabelComputer` case asserting `${sequence}` is used for `GeneralShellType.AbacusAI` when `allowAgentCliTitle` is enabled.

## Summary

- Support four-edge drag/drop, directional opening, keyboard navigation/movement/resizing, and an explicit balanced-grid arrangement.
- Persist actual split geometry, pins, active selection, composer placement, and maximization, with compatibility for legacy ordered-session state.
- Keep desktop geometry intact while maximized or in phone layout, including viewport transitions in both directions.
- Resolve and prepare external sessions before changing visibility, revalidate asynchronous openings, and retain unresolved geometry during partial restoration.
- Add realistic workbench-framed fixtures for nested splits, maximization, and multiple chats within one session, using production titlebar/header menus and deterministic account/workspace data.

`ISessionsService` continues to own visible/active sessions and persisted bindings; the Sessions Part owns canonical geometry and live views. The session grid remains separate from the chat-group grid within each session.

Ordinary opening retains its replacement behavior. Structural edits preserve unaffected panes and useful sizes; balanced tiling is an explicit operation, not a persistent mode.

pull_requests.title: pet: teach the VS Code pet new moves and reactions from chat
pull_requests.body: Describe a move and the agent draws it for the VS Code pet, or tell the pet when to play it. ## Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f29f3bc2-4008-458a-b870-08a106865f12 1. `/pet an ANGRY move: it gets furious and turns red, steam puffs out of its antennae, then it cools down back to normal`: the agent draws the move, previews every frame, fixes a mistake and saves it. The pet plays it. 2. `/pet-play angry`: the pet plays it right away, without the agent. 3. `/pet-play the mad one`: that isn't a move's name, so the agent finds the one meant. 4. `make it angrier`: the agent changes the move. 5. `/pet whenever I say bugs or broken, play ANGRY`: the agent adds a reaction. 6. `Check the vscode repo it's full of bugs!!!!!`: the pet gets angry as the message is sent. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/186ccabe-b742-4619-8a12-7f05b6a6d64f Four more moves, each drawn from a one-line request: FROZEN, SLEEPY, YAY and PIZZA. ## What's new - **`/pet `** in the Agents window: describe a move and the agent draws it, or ask for a change ("make it angrier"). It uses two tools: - `petGuide` gives the pet's poses, its art style and what it knows; - `teachPet` previews every frame, then saves. - **Moves are drawn in layers**: the pet's real poses and expressions, props, and shaded pixel text. - **Reactions** tell the pet when to play a move, such as `/pet whenever I say bug or broken, play ANGRY`. After that, any message you send with one of those words plays the move. Matching runs locally. - **`/pet-play `** plays a move right away, without the agent. If the name isn't exact, as in `/pet-play the mad one`, the agent finds the move you meant and plays it. - **Taught Moves**, in the pet's context menu, lists moves and reactions to play, copy or forget. ## Built-in moves The pet knows these out of the box, and agents study them as examples: ## Notes for reviewers - The tools appear only while AI features are on and the pet is shown. - Agent input is untrusted. A lesson is validated whole, and nothing is saved until it's valid. Moves are limited to 24×24 pixels, 16 frames and 5 s. - Moves and reactions are stored per user in `APPLICATION_SHARED`, so both windows share them. - The pet announces what it plays, and reduced motion shows a still frame. - Known limitations: - two windows saving at the same moment can overwrite each other; - the preview shows only the right-facing pet. ## How to test In the Agents window with Copilot CLI, show the pet with `/vscode-pet`. Then send the six messages from the first demo, in order.

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] Handle settled blocked policy in Local OTel recovery
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #338645 from `main`.

## Summary

Follow-up to #338623; addresses https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338640#discussion_r4131931927 and relates to #338630.

The original `isPolicyRefreshPlaceholder` heuristic mistook a permanently blocked restriction (`enabled=false`, `exporterType=''`) for pending policy. A Pending -> Blocked transition leaves the same settings and need not emit another configuration event, leaving a stale running exporter silently unhandled.

This correction adds the private `_workbench.whenAccountPolicySettled` command. It awaits **the gate service's own post-account initialization update**, including asynchronous native managed-settings processing, before inspecting gate settlement. Merely waiting for `getDefaultAccount()` can observe stale Inactive/NoAccount gate state; the review correction in `2339e9484d86e7581c43aebf751b887e6187c1c9` fixes that ordering. Initialization completes even without a gate-change event, cannot be completed by an overlapping update, and logs failures while preserving rejection for callers.

Pending and PolicyNotResolved defer recovery; Blocked and other settled restrictions resume it even when policy values are identical. The monitor reads configuration after the wait and reaches the existing opt-in reload behavior when disabling or restricting a running exporter.

Disabled restricted-startup recovery eligibility, restart budgets, and user-consent semantics are preserved. The monitoring documentation describes the private readiness dependency.

## Scope

- Does **not** implement live exporter reconfiguration or automatically shut down the exporter.
- Does **not** change the Agent Host pipeline or implement the full coordinator idea from microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9778.
- The analogous account-only initialization wait in `createAgentHostOTelPolicyReadiness` remains **unresolved and outside this Local OTel follow-up**. This is not a release-wide readiness fix.
- Release cherry-pick #338640 is intentionally untouched pending review.

## Regression coverage

Real `DefaultAccountService` and `AccountPolicyService` tests hold the gate's post-account native managed-settings update while account initialization completes. They cover pending/unresolved policy, unchanged Inactive/NoAccount terminal gates with zero gate-change events, an overlapping update that must not release initialization, and account/native initialization failures logged before any command caller awaits them.

The real Pending -> Blocked transition still resumes with zero policy-value changes. Existing extension coverage exercises monitor and contribution wait completion without a second configuration event, restricted startup, and success-path recovery.

## Validation

Review correction `2339e9484d86e7581c43aebf751b887e6187c1c9`:

- **Before production fix:** all four new delayed-gate initialization regressions failed because the waiter resolved while the gate still held its pre-initialization state (Inactive or NoAccount).
- **After fix:** `npm run transpile-client`, then `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/policies/test/browser/accountPolicyService.test.ts` — **43 passing** (42 account-policy tests plus the registry-cleanliness harness check).
- Root `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Focused ESLint on all three changed core TypeScript files, `git diff --check`, and commit hygiene hooks passed.
- No extension implementation/test files changed in the review correction; extension tests/typecheck were not rerun.

Prior validation by the creator session on source commit `007e5b8c1fb0c0979b2da16f7ac039b30d589815`, transferred without conflicts or implementation changes as `1db016f91d868b47da4ba5121faab9f71fa401ba`:

- 78 focused Local OTel extension tests in `otelConfigResolution.spec.ts`, `otelStaleConfigMonitor.spec.ts`, and `otelContrib.spec.ts`.
- 40 core tests reported by the original account-policy run; the current run above supersedes this count.
- Extension `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json`, root `npm run typecheck-client`, ESLint on all changed TypeScript files, `git diff --check`, and commit hooks.

### Scoped live validation on macOS

The creator session completed live validation using **Code OSS Dev 1.140.0 / Copilot 0.68.0**, in the prepared original worktree at `93272735cd26b56684db3e5675989f957908ae04`. The OTel implementation directories, `accountPolicyService.ts`, and `accountPolicyGate.contribution.ts` were verified byte-identical to reviewed PR head `2339e9484d86e7581c43aebf751b887e6187c1c9`. **This was not an exact main 1.141 / Copilot 0.69 product build**: the fresh PR checkout's full build was blocked by disk/dependency constraints. The run reused an authenticated throwaway profile, a mock through the existing proxy, and a local summary-only OTLP receiver.

The final five-step live scenario **passed**:

1. Unchanged-policy synchronization preserved Extension Host PID 10173 without an OTel reload prompt.
2. A synthetic Local span attributed to `copilot-chat` arrived at `/v1/traces`.
3. A forced nonresponding refresh entered Pending with restrictive `enabled=false` / empty exporter values and no premature OTel reload prompt.
4. Pending (`1790677470512`) -> Blocked (`1790677475941`) preserved those values and emitted no new OTel configuration event, yet the actual **Reload Window** action appeared.
5. Successful policy was restored (`enabled=true`, `exporterType=otlp-http`) without accepting reload.

Earlier attempts passed the regression assertions but failed harness cleanup on native/queued dialogs. The corrected harness handled the actual custom error dialogs, and the final all-pass report was retained.

The initialization race was also exercised live using a **temporary generated-JavaScript-only timing hold** after `getDefaultAccount()` and before `initialize()`'s awaited post-account update. The real initialization promise and private command were unmodified. For over three seconds, the account was ready and the gate remained Inactive: the old account-only predicate would have settled, but the real `_workbench.whenAccountPolicySettled` command stayed pending. Releasing the hold at `1790677561757` completed initialization and then the command at `1790677561758`. **This is runtime timing instrumentation, not a natural unmodified slow-native-service run.**

The probe was removed from compiled output, the source worktree was clean, and implementation equivalence was rechecked. The final live window had an inactive gate and no dialogs/notices; the mock was restored to JSON/200. Screenshots, Playwright traces, and HTML reports are retained locally by the validating session, **not uploaded to this PR**. No video was produced (missing ffmpeg/ffprobe and a custom attached runner).

**Remaining validation gaps:** an exact PR product build, a natural unmodified slow-native-service run, cross-platform, multi-window, and repeated-authentication checks. These tests do **not** validate or fix the separate Agent Host account-only initialization race.

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.

Fixes #338441

## Changes

- Default external-session visibility to the last 7 days.
- When the Agents Window's External section is enabled, replace the filter-setting prompt with an informational banner explaining that the session was picked up from another application and can continue here. Codex mentions ChatGPT or Copilot subscriptions and the model picker; Claude mentions the Copilot subscription.
- Preserve permanent, profile-wide dismissal through the Close action and keep the existing visibility-setting banner when external sectioning is disabled.
- Mark GitHub Sandbox sessions as external unless this VS Code profile created or adopted them. Persist that state locally, independently of host metadata and discovery refreshes; accepting a user message or importing a session adopts it.
- Add Codex, Copilot, and Claude fixtures in dark/light themes, regression tests, and updated accessibility help.

Sandbox provenance is deliberately scoped to this local VS Code profile, not to creation by any VS Code client: the discovery API currently does not expose creation-app metadata.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` - passed.
- Targeted tests below - **173 passed**, rerun after branching from the latest `origin/main`.

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/externalSessionBanner.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep 'Sessions - External Session Banner|RemoteAgentHostSessionsProvider|CloudSandboxSessionsProvider|LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider.*external'
```

- ESLint below - passed for all eight changed TypeScript files.

```sh
npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/externalSessionBanner.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/externalSessionBanner.fixture.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/externalSessionBanner.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/cloudSandboxSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts
```

- Component Explorer: all 12 external-session banner fixtures rendered without errors; all six new provider/theme variants passed screenshot stability checks. Visually inspected Codex, Copilot, and Claude.
- `git diff --cached --check` - passed.
- `npm run compile-client` - blocked before compilation: the manifest declares Copilot runtime `1.0.89-7`, while the installed `@github/copilot-sdk` bundles `1.0.87-unstable.r35651157977.g1aacd25`.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - failed on unrelated Copilot SDK API/type mismatches; no diagnostics in the changed files after correcting the new tests.
- Expanded provider test run below - 473 passed, 11 pending, and 3 unrelated local-provider resource-label failures (`registers provider-neutral resource label homes for quick chats and provider state`, `shares one resource label formatter across session state homes`, and `registers the SDK session state home from recorded artifacts`).

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/externalSessionBanner.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts
```

## How to test

1. With `sessions.list.groupExternalSessions` enabled, open external Codex, Copilot, and Claude sessions. Check the informational copy, subscription guidance, and absence of the visibility picker/Save button.
2. Close the banner, open another external session, and reload. It should remain dismissed. Keyboard dismissal should return focus to the chat input.
3. Disable external sectioning and verify the existing visibility-setting banner remains available in a profile where it has not been dismissed.
4. Discover a GitHub Sandbox session created elsewhere. It should be external, including after connecting and reloading. A session created in this profile, or continued here with an accepted user message, should be internal after reload.
5. Without an explicit visibility override, confirm `chat.agentSessions.showExternal` defaults to `last7Days`.

pull_requests.title: Engineering - decompose macOS build stage
pull_requests.body:
This pull request implements a decomposition of the macOS product build process into dedicated jobs for compiling, testing, and packaging/signing/notarizing. The changes include:

- **Job Structure**: Created separate jobs for Compile, Test, and Sign, allowing for parallel execution of Test and Sign jobs that consume the compilation artifact.
- **Reusable Steps**: Extracted common steps into reusable templates for setup, compilation download, CLI mix-in, local entitlement signing, and packaging/signing/notarization.
- **Checkpoint Updates**: Enhanced the test checkpoint helper to support macOS-specific test IDs and updated related YAML files to ensure compatibility.
- **Naming Consistency**: Renamed the terminal job to "Sign" for consistency with other platforms, while maintaining the underlying functionality.

Validation checks for YAML syntax and TypeScript typechecking have passed successfully.

pull_requests.title: Handle settled blocked policy in Local OTel recovery
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #338623; addresses https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338640#discussion_r4131931927 and relates to #338630.

The original `isPolicyRefreshPlaceholder` heuristic mistook a permanently blocked restriction (`enabled=false`, `exporterType=''`) for pending policy. A Pending -> Blocked transition leaves the same settings and need not emit another configuration event, leaving a stale running exporter silently unhandled.

This correction adds the private `_workbench.whenAccountPolicySettled` command. It awaits **the gate service's own post-account initialization update**, including asynchronous native managed-settings processing, before inspecting gate settlement. Merely waiting for `getDefaultAccount()` can observe stale Inactive/NoAccount gate state; the review correction in `2339e9484d86e7581c43aebf751b887e6187c1c9` fixes that ordering. Initialization completes even without a gate-change event, cannot be completed by an overlapping update, and logs failures while preserving rejection for callers.

Pending and PolicyNotResolved defer recovery; Blocked and other settled restrictions resume it even when policy values are identical. The monitor reads configuration after the wait and reaches the existing opt-in reload behavior when disabling or restricting a running exporter.

Disabled restricted-startup recovery eligibility, restart budgets, and user-consent semantics are preserved. The monitoring documentation describes the private readiness dependency.

## Scope

- Does **not** implement live exporter reconfiguration or automatically shut down the exporter.
- Does **not** change the Agent Host pipeline or implement the full coordinator idea from microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9778.
- The analogous account-only initialization wait in `createAgentHostOTelPolicyReadiness` remains **unresolved and outside this Local OTel follow-up**. This is not a release-wide readiness fix.
- Release cherry-pick #338640 is intentionally untouched pending review.

## Regression coverage

Real `DefaultAccountService` and `AccountPolicyService` tests hold the gate's post-account native managed-settings update while account initialization completes. They cover pending/unresolved policy, unchanged Inactive/NoAccount terminal gates with zero gate-change events, an overlapping update that must not release initialization, and account/native initialization failures logged before any command caller awaits them.

The real Pending -> Blocked transition still resumes with zero policy-value changes. Existing extension coverage exercises monitor and contribution wait completion without a second configuration event, restricted startup, and success-path recovery.

## Validation

Review correction `2339e9484d86e7581c43aebf751b887e6187c1c9`:

- **Before production fix:** all four new delayed-gate initialization regressions failed because the waiter resolved while the gate still held its pre-initialization state (Inactive or NoAccount).
- **After fix:** `npm run transpile-client`, then `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/policies/test/browser/accountPolicyService.test.ts` — **43 passing** (42 account-policy tests plus the registry-cleanliness harness check).
- Root `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Focused ESLint on all three changed core TypeScript files, `git diff --check`, and commit hygiene hooks passed.
- No extension implementation/test files changed in the review correction; extension tests/typecheck were not rerun.

Prior validation by the creator session on source commit `007e5b8c1fb0c0979b2da16f7ac039b30d589815`, transferred without conflicts or implementation changes as `1db016f91d868b47da4ba5121faab9f71fa401ba`:

- 78 focused Local OTel extension tests in `otelConfigResolution.spec.ts`, `otelStaleConfigMonitor.spec.ts`, and `otelContrib.spec.ts`.
- 40 core tests reported by the original account-policy run; the current run above supersedes this count.
- Extension `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json`, root `npm run typecheck-client`, ESLint on all changed TypeScript files, `git diff --check`, and commit hooks.

### Scoped live validation on macOS

The creator session completed live validation using **Code OSS Dev 1.140.0 / Copilot 0.68.0**, in the prepared original worktree at `93272735cd26b56684db3e5675989f957908ae04`. The OTel implementation directories, `accountPolicyService.ts`, and `accountPolicyGate.contribution.ts` were verified byte-identical to reviewed PR head `2339e9484d86e7581c43aebf751b887e6187c1c9`. **This was not an exact main 1.141 / Copilot 0.69 product build**: the fresh PR checkout's full build was blocked by disk/dependency constraints. The run reused an authenticated throwaway profile, a mock through the existing proxy, and a local summary-only OTLP receiver.

The final five-step live scenario **passed**:

1. Unchanged-policy synchronization preserved Extension Host PID 10173 without an OTel reload prompt.
2. A synthetic Local span attributed to `copilot-chat` arrived at `/v1/traces`.
3. A forced nonresponding refresh entered Pending with restrictive `enabled=false` / empty exporter values and no premature OTel reload prompt.
4. Pending (`1790677470512`) -> Blocked (`1790677475941`) preserved those values and emitted no new OTel configuration event, yet the actual **Reload Window** action appeared.
5. Successful policy was restored (`enabled=true`, `exporterType=otlp-http`) without accepting reload.

Earlier attempts passed the regression assertions but failed harness cleanup on native/queued dialogs. The corrected harness handled the actual custom error dialogs, and the final all-pass report was retained.

The initialization race was also exercised live using a **temporary generated-JavaScript-only timing hold** after `getDefaultAccount()` and before `initialize()`'s awaited post-account update. The real initialization promise and private command were unmodified. For over three seconds, the account was ready and the gate remained Inactive: the old account-only predicate would have settled, but the real `_workbench.whenAccountPolicySettled` command stayed pending. Releasing the hold at `1790677561757` completed initialization and then the command at `1790677561758`. **This is runtime timing instrumentation, not a natural unmodified slow-native-service run.**

The probe was removed from compiled output, the source worktree was clean, and implementation equivalence was rechecked. The final live window had an inactive gate and no dialogs/notices; the mock was restored to JSON/200. Screenshots, Playwright traces, and HTML reports are retained locally by the validating session, **not uploaded to this PR**. No video was produced (missing ffmpeg/ffprobe and a custom attached runner).

**Remaining validation gaps:** an exact PR product build, a natural unmodified slow-native-service run, cross-platform, multi-window, and repeated-authentication checks. These tests do **not** validate or fix the separate Agent Host account-only initialization race.

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] Fix managed OTel restart recovery
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #338623 from `main`.

## Summary

- automatically restart the shared local Agent Host when settled enterprise OTel policy changes after startup
- forward policy readiness alongside the renderer snapshot: pending refreshes and windows still resolving their initial account cannot overwrite the running host's policy or cause redundant restarts
- preserve settled fail-closed restrictions and policy withdrawal, and coalesce changes while a replacement host is pending
- bound Local Copilot Chat automatic recovery to prevent restart loops; record a managed window reload only after the user accepts it
- ignore transient fail-closed policy placeholders so stale reload notifications do not survive an otherwise successful Extension Host recovery
- carry the reload guard into only its immediate successor: failed recovery remains visible without another reload action, while successful recovery and dismissed prompts do not block later launches
- cover policy readiness, multi-window forwarding, process replacement with the latest environment, fresh-launch recovery, and notification/user-consent behavior
- update both monitoring guides

This is a VS Code-only release mitigation discovered while validating #338234. It does not require changes to `github/copilot-agent-runtime`.

## Validation

- 84 core tests passed across `agentService.test.ts`, `agentHostService.test.ts`, `localAgentHostService.test.ts`, and the workbench Agent Host service tests
- 75 focused extension tests passed across `otelConfigResolution.spec.ts`, `otelStaleConfigMonitor.spec.ts`, and `otelContrib.spec.ts`
- `cd extensions/copilot && npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files and pre-commit hygiene

Live validation in an authenticated OSS window with Proxyman, an isolated managed-settings mock, `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true`, and a privacy-safe OTLP receiver confirmed:

- late settled policy automatically replaced both the Extension Host and shared Agent Host without either developer restart command
- transient fail-closed refresh values did not leave a stale **Reload Window** notification
- the successor Extension Host initialized Local OTel as `otlp-http` at `http://localhost:4318/` and acknowledged successful recovery
- Local Copilot Chat exported a `copilot-chat` trace to `/v1/traces`
- the native Agent Host exported metrics to `/v1/metrics`
- an unchanged policy sync kept both replacement process IDs stable, with no restart loop

Fixes #338630.

Related test plan items: #337818 and #338234.

pull_requests.title: sessions: Preserve Dev Container draft isolation during startup
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338533

## Summary

The first Dev Container connection can advertise agents before authentication finishes. The replacement draft then has no resolved configuration schema, but the previous handoff only waited for an in-flight resolution. It skipped copying the source draft's `isolation: folder` and sent the container provider's default `worktree` instead.

- Wait for draft authentication and configuration resolution before transferring settings, without waiting for required configuration values to be populated.
- Finish source-side configuration operations before taking the handoff snapshot.
- Reject unavailable configuration and preserve cancellation, draft-disposal, and connection-release behavior.
- Add real-provider regression tests for delayed/already-settled authentication, missing required values populated by the handoff, cancellation, draft disposal (including during configuration writes), provider disconnect, and configuration-resolution failure.
- Explicitly enable the experimental worktree setting in existing tests that exercise detached Dev Container worktrees.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` - passed.
- Focused local and remote provider tests with `--grep "Dev Container"` - 59 passed.
- ESLint on all five changed files - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

A fresh Docker/UI reproduction has not been rerun; regression coverage exercises the actual provider handoff with mocked connections.

Review follow-up: client type-checking and targeted lint also passed after the lifecycle fix.

pull_requests.title: Fix breadcrumb picker focus for webview editors
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338120.

Opening a breadcrumb picker currently focuses the owning editor first. For webview editors, the delayed focus message can arrive after the picker takes focus and immediately dismiss it.

## Changes
- Activate the owning editor group without focusing its editor when opening file, outline, or quick-access pickers.
- Preserve editor focus for actual file/symbol navigation, including opening to the side. Revealing a folder only opens the next picker.
- Dispose the file picker's filter, fixing a leak exposed by the new tests.
- Add 17 regression tests covering controlled focus-delivery orderings, mouse/keyboard opening, group activation, selection, Escape, outside dismissal, and repeated opening.

No additional timeout, DOM-selector workaround, or change to the picker's blur-to-close behavior.

## Validation
- All 33 breadcrumb browser tests pass in Chromium.
- Regression tests reproduced focus loss before the fix and pass afterward.
- Targeted TypeScript dependency-graph check, ESLint, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full client type-check is blocked by missing Electron typings in the existing local dependencies.
- Live Windows Agents/image-preview validation was not performed; the browser tests model delayed editor-focus delivery deterministically.

pull_requests.title: Fix managed OTel restart recovery
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- automatically restart the shared local Agent Host when settled enterprise OTel policy changes after startup
- forward policy readiness alongside the renderer snapshot: pending refreshes and windows still resolving their initial account cannot overwrite the running host's policy or cause redundant restarts
- preserve settled fail-closed restrictions and policy withdrawal, and coalesce changes while a replacement host is pending
- bound Local Copilot Chat automatic recovery to prevent restart loops; record a managed window reload only after the user accepts it
- ignore transient fail-closed policy placeholders so stale reload notifications do not survive an otherwise successful Extension Host recovery
- carry the reload guard into only its immediate successor: failed recovery remains visible without another reload action, while successful recovery and dismissed prompts do not block later launches
- cover policy readiness, multi-window forwarding, process replacement with the latest environment, fresh-launch recovery, and notification/user-consent behavior
- update both monitoring guides

This is a VS Code-only release mitigation discovered while validating #338234. It does not require changes to `github/copilot-agent-runtime`.

## Validation

- 84 core tests passed across `agentService.test.ts`, `agentHostService.test.ts`, `localAgentHostService.test.ts`, and the workbench Agent Host service tests
- 75 focused extension tests passed across `otelConfigResolution.spec.ts`, `otelStaleConfigMonitor.spec.ts`, and `otelContrib.spec.ts`
- `cd extensions/copilot && npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files and pre-commit hygiene

Live validation in an authenticated OSS window with Proxyman, an isolated managed-settings mock, `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true`, and a privacy-safe OTLP receiver confirmed:

- late settled policy automatically replaced both the Extension Host and shared Agent Host without either developer restart command
- transient fail-closed refresh values did not leave a stale **Reload Window** notification
- the successor Extension Host initialized Local OTel as `otlp-http` at `http://localhost:4318/` and acknowledged successful recovery
- Local Copilot Chat exported a `copilot-chat` trace to `/v1/traces`
- the native Agent Host exported metrics to `/v1/metrics`
- an unchanged policy sync kept both replacement process IDs stable, with no restart loop

Fixes #338630.

Related test plan items: #337818 and #338234.

pull_requests.title: terminal: bound aggregate terminal image previews
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #332145

## Summary

- Bound automatic terminal image previews to 10 images and 5 MiB of total encoded image-file data per result.
- Keep original stdout and exact image bytes/MIME/User-only image audience; surface a localized omission notice through the existing terminal result banner.
- Keep that UI notice separate from tool content rather than relying on text-audience propagation through extension-host or Agent Host transports.
- Use cancellable streamed reads with the remaining size budget, retain final byte checks, and preserve existing per-file/regex behavior.

The aggregate/count limits were explicitly approved for this fix. They are not decoded-pixel or whole-session memory limits.

## Validation

- Original baseline regression: 2 passing, 3 failing. The additional real-invocation regression for notice isolation fails before the follow-up and passes after it.
- Current targeted terminal-tool suite: 229 passing, 107 existing pending. Client type checking, targeted ESLint, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Actual credential-free Code OSS with synthetic local PNGs and real `vscode.lm.invokeTool('run_in_terminal')`: unchanged 151-character stdout previously attached 8 images / 6,298,016 file bytes / 8,397,376 base64 characters; candidate attaches 6 / 4,723,512 / 6,298,032 with a visible omission notice.
- Live count, small image, text/nonimage, historical long-line regex, nonzero exit, cancellation, and large-output controls; byte/hash-exact valid PNGs at 5 MiB - 1 and exactly 5 MiB, verified to decode in Chromium.
- Post-GC inspection confirmed the actual invocation retains binary image data and base64 result details.
- Follow-up live checks confirm unchanged stdout and image hashes, with the notice absent from extension-host tool-result content and from the actual Agent Host converter's content. It remains visible in the terminal UI and in the protocol UI message.
- The original aggregate-limit implementation received two independent read-only full-diff reviews (gpt-6-astra and claude-opus-5.5, default effort), with findings addressed and same-reviewer follow-up. The later notice-isolation fix received the regression and live validation described above; no additional independent agent review is claimed.

No intentional OOM was attempted. Windows/local-disk validation only; authenticated providers and other platforms were not exercised. Whole-file-only/atomic file providers retain their existing fallback behavior.

pull_requests.title: Mitigate managed Local OTel reload loops with extension restart
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Mitigation for #338597, not the complete startup-readiness fix.

When enterprise OTel settings arrive after the Copilot Chat extension constructs its Local telemetry service, the existing informational recovery path offers **Reload Window**. With `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`, reloading the window can recreate the same startup ordering.

This change offers **Restart Extensions** for recognized managed-policy changes and the fallback after unsuccessful automatic recovery. It uses the existing extension-host restart command and lifecycle-bound progress rather than reloading the renderer.

- Names **Local Copilot Chat** in policy notifications and explains that other extension work may be interrupted.
- Preserves automatic-recovery eligibility, its persisted one-attempt guard, and notification deduplication. Explicit user retries do not reset or consume that automatic-recovery guard.
- Rechecks configuration drift and contribution disposal before acting on a notification.
- Reports command failures or a host that remains alive, without automatically retrying or falling back to another window reload.
- Leaves personal-setting changes and policy withdrawal on the existing **Reload Window** action.
- Logs changed field names only for the informational policy path; no endpoint or header values.
- Documents the mitigation and its limits.

## Scope and limitations

No Copilot Runtime or Agent Host changes. This does not weaken `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`, add a policy-readiness API, reconfigure OTel in place, or claim collector delivery. The underlying startup race remains; recovery may be needed again after a subsequent window reload or application restart. Keeping this draft pending real-window validation of the extension-host/authentication restart sequence.

## Validation

- 76 tests passed across `otelContrib.spec.ts`, `otelStaleConfigMonitor.spec.ts`, `otelConfigResolver.spec.ts`, and `otelConfigResolution.spec.ts` using the existing Vitest configuration.
- Added coverage for provisional restricted startup values with personal OTel both on and off, explicit restart acceptance, dismissal, settled-policy reconstruction, failed/vetoed restart behavior, stale notification choices, automatic-recovery fallback retries, and unchanged personal/withdrawal behavior.
- ESLint passed for all three changed TypeScript files.
- Commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Manual validation still required

- [ ] Reproduce with `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true` and managed OTel on Windows Insiders.
- [ ] After policy settles, choose **Restart Extensions** and verify that Local OTel uses the managed configuration and delivers spans to the collector without a window reload.
- [ ] Exercise cancellation/confirmation with active extension work.
- [ ] Confirm native Agent Host telemetry remains independent of this notification.

Related coverage: #336872, #337818, #338234.

pull_requests.title: Set TERM_PROGRAM for Agent Host terminals created by VS Code clients
pull_requests.body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338608

- Add a `vscodeTerminalIdentity` option to `AgentHostTerminalManager.createTerminal` that sets `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode` and `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` to the agent host's product version.
- Pass the requesting connection's `AgentHostClientType` from the `createTerminal` protocol handler to `IAgentService.createTerminal`.
- Enable the identity only for known VS Code clients (Editor Window or Agents Window), as identified by `clientInfo` at `initialize`.
- Keep the inherited environment for unknown clients, and for agent tool shells and `!` commands, which call the terminal manager directly.
- Leave attach, reconnect, and ownership transfer unchanged, since they don't spawn a process.
- Keep the protocol, generated AHP files, and workbench code unchanged; the host decides from existing connection state.

### Validation

- After a one-shot `npm run transpile-client`, `agentHostTerminalManager.test.ts` and `protocolServerHandler.test.ts` pass (192 tests), both with `TERM_PROGRAM`/`TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` unset and with conflicting inherited values.
- Targeted ESLint on the changed files passed with no warnings.
- Full typechecking is left to CI.

### Manual test

1. Start the updated build, open the Agents Window, and create a **new Agent Host terminal**.
2. Run `printf 'TERM_PROGRAM=%s\nTERM_PROGRAM_VERSION=%s\n' "$TERM_PROGRAM" "$TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION"`.
3. Verify the output is `vscode` and the build's version.
4. Ask the agent to run `echo "$TERM_PROGRAM"` and verify the tool shell keeps the inherited value.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Terminal identity variable names and values come from [`addTerminalEnvironmentKeys`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/terminalEnvironment.ts#L62-L71). Only the identity is shared, not the full workbench environment or extension-collection pipeline.
- The `vscodeTerminalIdentity` option shape and placement follow the existing per-request `preventShellHistory` and `nonInteractive` environment options in [`AgentHostTerminalManager.createTerminal`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L313-L336).
- Passing per-connection client identity from the protocol handler to the agent service follows how `dispatchAction` passes [`client.telemetryContext`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts#L556) to [`IAgentService.dispatchAction`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentService.ts#L979). Only its `clientType` is passed here, since terminal creation needs nothing else.
- Gating host behavior on the client type follows the Editor Window check for [session working-directory actions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L7230-L7235), with clients identified by [`getAgentHostClientType`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostClientInfo.ts#L27-L36).
- Using the host's product version follows [`RemoteTerminalChannel`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/server/node/remoteTerminalChannel.ts#L242-L249), which passes the server's `productService.version` when creating remote terminals.
- The protocol handler test's client-type assertion is copied semantically from [`session working-directory actions reach the agent service`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts#L1812-L1835).

pull_requests.title: terminal: release consumed shell execution output
pull_requests.body:
Refs #256854.

## Change

Replace replaying terminal shell-execution streams with an independent, single-consumption producer per reader.

- Flush follows actual reader progress without consuming the reader's queue or treating producer completion as delivery completion.
- Preserve trailing-output ordering, separate readers, and streams subscribed before command end but consumed afterward.
- Release abandoned queues on early return and complete active/pending readers when a terminal closes.
- Add ten regression tests and document the independent, single-consumption `read()` contract.

The change is limited to terminal stream ownership; generic async primitives are unchanged. Unread output remains buffered intentionally.

## Validation

- Client type-check and targeted ESLint passed.
- Repository Electron-Mocha: 19 passing checks (18 terminal tests plus the clean-state guard), including the existing multiline regressions.
- Recorded Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev scenarios on Windows x64: core stream suite 12/12 passed; native PowerShell/Git Bash, real heredocs, argument quoting, interruption, cwd, independent/delayed readers and terminal recreation exercised.
- Two matched live baseline/fix runs delivered 7,987,208 byte-identical output bytes each. Actual extension-host snapshots after GC showed baseline consumed-string retention growing from approximately 2 MB to 8 MB; the fixed producer queues had zero unconsumed entries at both checkpoints. This is stream-owner evidence, not a global leak-free or performance claim.

Two additional scenario failures reproduced on the unchanged baseline and are tracked separately in #338609 and #338610; this PR does not address them. Native macOS/Linux and remote WSL/fish cases were not run.

pull_requests.title: Add ARM64 Linux Snap builds with selectable core22/core24 bases
pull_requests.body:
Build ARM64 Linux Snap artifacts from native-architecture staged libraries, keeping core24 as the default and offering core22 for unpublished validation builds.

## Changes
- Use pinned amd64/arm64 Snapcraft 8 builders with matching Ubuntu package mirrors; reject mislabeled executable architectures before packing.
- Render base-specific Snapcraft architecture syntax, desktop libraries, and RPATH. The launcher reads the installed snap's base rather than hard-coding core20/core24.
- Wire the ARM64 product artifact and sanity target, add focused packaging tests, and document native install and release gates. Core26 can be packed locally on native Ubuntu 26.04 with Snapcraft 9+, but is not enabled in product CI without a verified multiarch builder.

## Related
Refs microsoft/vscode#125120 and microsoft/vscode#269552. Related to base/runtime report microsoft/vscode#241636. This is a follow-up/alternative to microsoft/vscode#298237 and microsoft/vscode#271464; please coordinate overlapping changes rather than merging both independently. It does not claim to fix their separate alternatives-registration or terminal-environment work. Do not close the ARM64 issues until snaps are available in the Store.

## Validation and remaining work
- Merged upstream microsoft/vscode#338552 in signed commit 31aa2557dc9; the Snap package step now runs in the split Linux Sign job, and the x64/ARM64 stages receive the Snap base and build flags. GitHub reports the PR as mergeable.
- `node --test build/lib/test/buildSnap.test.ts`: 35 passing after resolving the Linux-stage split conflicts.

v7.30.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.29.1...v7.30.0

v7.29.1

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-w293-vg96-wgc3: BalancedPool could drop function-valued connection options while cloning its configuration, including custom TLS certificate validation callbacks. Undici now preserves connect and legacy tls options when creating upstreams. Fixed by f690157d.
  • GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5: a WebSocket server could select a subprotocol when none was requested, causing an uncaught TypeError that could terminate the process. Undici now rejects the handshake with protocol error 1002. Fixed by 6615e017.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v: a malformed permessage-deflate payload exceeding the configured decompression limit could emit an unhandled zlib error and terminate the process. Undici now destroys the inflater after reaching the limit. Fixed by 63cf698b.
  • GHSA-rx4f-c7p8-82vq: an unclean WebSocketStream close could create an unobserved rejected promise when its writable stream was locked, potentially terminating the process. Undici now propagates the failure through the retained writable stream controller. Fixed by 1858656e.
  • GHSA-2jfj-6hjv-fm6j: shared caches could store and replay responses containing Set-Cookie, disclosing one user's cookies to another caller. Undici now excludes these responses from shared caches, including existing entries and revalidation paths. Fixed by b6c5a002.
  • GHSA-3xpg-4rpp-hhhm: the decompression interceptor did not bound decoded output, allowing compressed responses to consume excessive memory. Undici now limits every decompression stage to 64 MiB by default and supports a configurable maxSize. Fixed by 2c7d7e12.
  • GHSA-pmjh-fq2x-6v4x: a terminal retry failure after response headers were exposed could orphan the original response body, causing consumers to hang indefinitely. Undici now propagates the terminal error to the exposed body. Fixed by 3c672659.

Low severity

  • GHSA-8436-99hf-9mmv: cache interceptors could store and replay responses to unsafe HTTP methods such as POST or DELETE. Undici now restricts cache reads and writes to safe methods while preserving invalidation by successful unsafe requests. Fixed by b61d9432.
  • GHSA-2gqq-gqf2-x968: the dump interceptor could treat an oversized chunked response as successfully truncated when no Content-Length was present. Undici now enforces maxSize against received bytes and aborts oversized responses. Fixed by 21693f40.
  • GHSA-r53p-7pc4-xj5r: the retry interceptor could concatenate a resumed response with inconsistent framing into downstream output, enabling response splitting or corruption. Undici now validates Content-Range against the original response framing before resuming. Fixed by cd8af90b.

pull_requests.title: SCM - Avoid redundant refreshes of the Repositories view for child repositories
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338547

When the Source Control Repositories view isn't in explorer mode (`scm.repositories.explorer: false`, the default), child repositories such as worktrees are nested under their parent repository row. With many worktree repositories open (for example, `git.detectWorktrees: true` with 50 worktrees), the view refreshes the whole tree and collapses/re-expands the parent row about twice per worktree during startup.

There are two causes in `scmRepositoriesViewPane.ts`:

- **`updateRepository()` falls through to a full refresh.** For a child repository, it refreshes the parent via `updateParentRepository()` and then falls through to `updateChildren()`, a full recursive refresh of the tree.
  - In non-explorer mode, the root's children are only repositories without a `parentId`, so a child repository change can't change them.
  - `updateChildren(parent)` already re-evaluates the parent's `hasChildren`.
  - This change returns after refreshing the parent.
- **The `historyItemRef` subscription isn't gated on explorer mode.** Every history item ref change triggers `updateRepository()`, even though outside explorer mode there are no artifact groups for a ref change to affect.
  - This change gates the subscription on `explorerEnabledConfig`, the same way the artifact-group subscription right above it already is.

### Verification

MutationObserver on `.scm-repositories-view` in Insiders 1.140.0, 50 worktree repositories. The fixed versions of the two methods were applied at runtime to `SCMRepositoriesViewPane.prototype` before the view initialized:

| | DOM mutations | Parent collapse/re-expand cycles |
|---|---|---|
| Before (2 runs) | 114,308 / 114,991 | 99 / 99 |
| After (2 runs) | 54,522 / 53,691 | 1 / 1 |

Explorer mode (`scm.repositories.explorer: true`) is unchanged.

pull_requests.title: Fix middle click paste over text in terminal on Linux
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #157233

## Problem

On Linux, middle click pastes the selection clipboard (the X primary selection) into the terminal only when clicking empty terminal space. Clicking on text does nothing. This affects both `terminal.integrated.middleClickBehavior` settings.

## Cause

- xterm.js activates a link on `mouseup` of any mouse button, not just the primary one (xtermjs/xterm.js#4052).
- `TerminalWordLinkDetector` makes every word in the terminal a link, so a middle click on text always lands on a "link".
- `TerminalLinkManager`'s activation handler calls `preventDefault()` on the event before it checks the modifier key.
- Chromium skips its built-in paste of the selection clipboard when the middle-button `mouseup` is default prevented. No `paste` event ever reaches xterm's textarea.

I confirmed this in a running Code OSS instance by hooking `Event.prototype.preventDefault`. Over text, the `mouseup` was prevented from `TerminalLink.activate` → `terminalLinkManager.ts`. Over blank space, nothing prevented it.

## Fix

Ignore link activations from non-primary buttons before calling `preventDefault()`. Nothing changes for left-click activation, Ctrl/Alt+click behaviour, or links opened from the quick pick (`TerminalLinkQuickPickEvent` reports button 0).

A matching upstream fix for xterm.js is in xtermjs/xterm.js#6194. I've kept the guard here as well, because extension-provided link handlers also go through this code path.

## How to test

On Linux:

1. Open a terminal and run `echo alpha beta gamma` a few times.
2. Select a word anywhere, in the terminal, the editor or another app. Don't copy it.
3. Middle click over text in the terminal. The selection is pasted at the prompt. Before this change, nothing happened.
4. Middle click on empty terminal space. It still pastes.
5. Ctrl+click (or Alt+click, depending on `editor.multiCursorModifier`) on a URL or file link. It still opens.

A unit test in `terminalLinkManager.test.ts` checks that only primary-button activations are default prevented.

---

> [!NOTE]
> This PR was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding agent (Claude Code). The agent did the investigation (reproducing the bug in a live Code OSS instance and tracing the `preventDefault()` call), the fix and the test. I've reviewed the change and tested it locally.

pull_requests.title: Fix plugin custom-agent hooks in Agent Host
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338177

Related to #337388 and #332083.

## Summary

- parse hooks declared in plugin custom-agent frontmatter in the Agent Host plugin pipeline
- scope those hooks to the selected root agent or spawned subagent at invocation time
- preserve the original plugin root across Agent Host materialization, including `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` in commands, environment values, and working directories
- preserve shell provenance and execute `powershell` hooks with Windows PowerShell instead of `cmd.exe`

## Root cause

#337388 wired custom-agent hooks into the local workbench Chat path, but Agent Host has a separate parser and session-launch path. That path dropped `hooks` from agent frontmatter. Once parsed, two additional Agent Host boundaries also broke the exact issue scenario: selected-agent URIs referred to the original plugin while Agent Host parsed a synchronized copy, and the `powershell` field was flattened to a generic Windows command that was launched through `cmd.exe`.

The combined result was that this valid hook never ran against the source plugin root on Windows:

```yaml
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - type: command
      powershell: "echo hi > ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hello.out"
```

## Before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1b55a44-8f7c-416a-9fb7-0a22cff652bf

The `asparagus` agent invokes `glob`, but the marker is absent from the source plugin's `scripts` directory.

## After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8605d0de-801b-4de5-a6bb-3ffe05f29989

The same agent and hook invoke `glob` and create `scripts/hello.out` with content `hi` under the source plugin root, including when its path contains spaces.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint on all 10 changed TypeScript files
- 918 passing tests across the complete plugin parser, hook converter, session launcher, and Agent Host session suites
- targeted Agent Host plugin materialization test: 1 passing
- focused Windows PowerShell execution test: 1 passing
- `git diff --check`
- before/after UI recordings on Windows with a deterministic mock model and the exact hook from #338177

## Overlap

#338476 is changing the same SDK hook-dispatch area for hook aggregation. Whichever PR lands second will need a small rebase in `toSdkHooks`.
