pull_requests.title: Engineering - split Windows stage into multiple stages/jobs
pull_requests.body:
This pull request enhances the Windows x64 build pipeline by implementing a mechanism to reuse compilation artifacts, thereby optimizing the build process. The key changes include:

- **Artifact Management**: Introduced a mapping of job names to their respective artifacts in `publish.ts`, allowing artifacts to be published only if their gating job has completed successfully.
- **New YAML Files**: Created several new YAML files for managing test checkpoints and restoring artifacts, ensuring that the pipeline can efficiently handle retries without recompiling.
- **Updated Build Steps**: Modified existing build YAML files to integrate the new artifact management logic, ensuring that compilation steps are skipped if artifacts are available from a previous successful run.
- **Testing Enhancements**: Added unit tests to validate the new artifact handling logic, ensuring that the system behaves correctly under various scenarios (e.g., job success, failure, and retries).

These changes aim to reduce build times and improve reliability by preventing unnecessary recompilation, especially in the presence of flaky tests or external dependencies.

auto_merge.commit_title: Engineering - split Windows stage into multiple stages/jobs (#338404)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* Engineering - Reuse Windows compilation outputs on job retries

Windows product build jobs can fail for reasons unrelated to compilation
(flaky tests, codesigning dependencies), and retrying them used to compile
everything again. The x64 and arm64 jobs now publish their compilation
outputs as a pipeline artifact before the CLI is added and codesigning
runs. On a retry, the job restores that artifact and skips all
compilation steps.

A temporary step fails the first job attempt after the artifact is
published so that the retry path can be validated. It must be removed
before merging.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Split Windows product build into compile, test and sign jobs

Retrying a failed Windows product build job used to repeat all of its work,
even when only a flaky test or an external code signing dependency failed.
The Windows x64 and arm64 product jobs are now split into three jobs:

- Compile: compiles the client, server and web server builds and publishes
  them as the compilation_win32_<arch> pipeline artifact.
- Test (x64 only): downloads the compilation artifact and runs the tests.
- Sign: downloads the compilation artifact, adds the CLI, code signs and
  packages the builds, and publishes the product artifacts.

The test and sign jobs both depend on the compile job and run in parallel,
so retrying a failed job never repeats the work of a job that succeeded.
This replaces the in-job reuse of the compilation outputs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Sign the Windows CLI in the Windows sign job

The Windows CLI job built the CLI and signed it, while the Windows sign job
polled for the unsigned CLI and signed the same executable again as part of
the client build. A code signing failure in the CLI job also meant building
the CLI again on retry.

The CLI job now only builds the CLI and publishes the unsigned artifact. The
Windows sign job depends on both the compile and the CLI jobs instead of
polling for the CLI artifact, signs the CLI once as part of the client build,
and publishes the standalone vscode_cli_win32_<arch>_cli artifact from that
signed executable.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Skip passed test tasks when retrying the Windows x64 test job

Retrying the Windows x64 test job ran every test task again, even when only
one of them failed. Each test task now records a checkpoint artifact as soon
as it passes, and retries of the job skip the test tasks that already passed
in an earlier attempt of the same pipeline run. The WSL Dev Container setup is
skipped together with the Electron smoke tests it serves.

This ports the test checkpoints from #334926 to the Windows x64 test job. The
VSCODE_SKIP_SUCCESSFUL_TEST_TASKS queue parameter (default true) enables them;
all other jobs are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Always skip passed Windows test tasks and align Windows job names

- Remove the VSCODE_SKIP_SUCCESSFUL_TEST_TASKS parameter: the Windows test
  steps always record checkpoints and skip the test tasks that already passed
  in an earlier attempt of the job. This also applies to the Windows CI test
  jobs, which share the same test steps. All test tasks, including the unit
  tests, now use the run-test-with-checkpoint template.
- Rename the Windows CLI job to Windows_<arch>_CLI ("Windows (<ARCH>) - CLI")
  to match the compile, test and sign jobs.
- Order the Windows jobs by architecture: the x64 jobs first, then the arm64
  jobs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Temporarily fail the Windows x64 test job to validate retries

Fails the first attempt of the product test job after the unit tests and
the second attempt after the integration tests, so that "Rerun failed jobs"
exercises the test checkpoints. The Windows CI test jobs are not affected.

Revert this commit before merging.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Split the Windows stage into Windows X64 and Windows ARM64

Azure DevOps lists the jobs of a stage by dependency level, so with all
Windows jobs in one stage the x64 test and sign jobs were listed after the
arm64 CLI and compile jobs. The arm64 jobs now run in a separate WindowsARM64
stage ("Windows ARM64"), next to the Windows stage ("Windows X64"), so each
stage lists its jobs in build order. Both stages start right away and run in
parallel. CI builds keep a single Windows stage.

- VSCODE_BUILD_STAGE_WINDOWS now tells whether the Windows stage exists, and
  the new VSCODE_BUILD_STAGE_WINDOWS_ARM64 whether the WindowsARM64 stage does.
- publish.ts waits for both stages and matches stages by their identifier,
  since the timeline record name is the stage's display name when one is set.
- The Windows artifact sanity tests depend on the stages that exist.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Revert "Engineering - Temporarily fail the Windows x64 test job to validate retries"

This reverts commit e67375dd0b99d96ff992a3a2cca6db565aa4006b.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Refactor publish script and remove obsolete documentation

- Update publish.ts to improve functionality and performance.
- Delete test-checkpoints.md as it is no longer relevant.
- Make minor adjustments to product-build-win32.yml for consistency.

* Engineering - Publish test checkpoints whenever their test runs

The checkpoint publish step now reuses the condition of the test step it belongs to, instead of additionally requiring the READY variable set by the record command. A test that runs and passes always publishes its checkpoint, while a failed or reused test does not.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Record test checkpoints in a dedicated step

Step template parameters reach templates normalized (e.g. powershell: as task: PowerShell@2), so the wrapper never appended the record command to the test script. No checkpoint file was created, and the checkpoint publish either never ran or failed to resolve the checkpoint path. The test step is now copied as is, and a separate step records the checkpoint before it is published, using the same condition as the test step.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Ref #305961 (related: #305967)

## Problem

`workbench.action.files.newFile` (used by the "New File..." quick pick, e.g. "Create New File (foo.ts)") calls `fileService.createFile` without handling errors. 1. Run "New File..." and type a name that can't be created (e.g. pick a read-only folder in the save dialog, or on Windows use a name containing `:`).
2. Before: nothing happens. After: an error notification explains why the file couldn't be created.
3. Normal file creation still works and opens the new file.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Keep remote hosts alive while agents are running
pull_requests.body:
Remote agent hosts started with `--idle-timeout` (managed SSH, WSL, and dedicated tunnel hosts) shut down 300 seconds after the last client disconnected, even while an agent was still running, which killed the in-progress turn.

The CLI supervisor now counts the agent host server process as activity. The server already stays up while a turn is running and exits on its own once idle, so running agents no longer count as idle. Server exit is now detected from the process itself instead of its output closing, so a leftover child process can't keep the supervisor alive.

Notes for reviewers:
- An idle host frees the server on the same schedule as before. Only the small supervisor process stays up about 5 minutes longer.
- A turn waiting for approval also keeps the host alive, with no upper limit.

pull_requests.title: Fix notification Accessible View close listener lifetime
pull_requests.body:
Refs #293200

Addresses only the unchecked `notificationAccessibleView.ts:69` direct event subscription (`notification-accessible-view-69`, queue ID47).

### Change

Opening a notification in Accessible View subscribed to the notification's close event, but closing Accessible View left that listener attached until the notification itself was dismissed. Repeatedly reopening a surviving notification accumulated listeners.

Return this subscription from the provider's `onOpen` hook and register it in Accessible View's existing per-show disposable store. The optional `onOpen` return contract is documented. Each showing owns exactly its subscription, including same-provider re-shows and providers copied/restored through accessibility help.

### Validation

|---|---:|---:|

| Closed after 21 cycles | 24 | 3 |
| Open before help | 25 | 4 |
| In help | 25 | 3 |

Original successful and unsuccessful raw results are preserved in the local task evidence.

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] test: validate Windows Agent Host cleanup process ancestry
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #338316 from `main`.

## Summary
- Validate creation times at every Windows parent/child edge and when checking descendant identity, preventing stale parent PIDs or reused process identities from authorizing cleanup.
- Use the same verified descendant cleanup for graceful and forceful shutdown; avoid `taskkill /T` traversing stale Windows ancestry.
- Record timestamped runner/server PIDs, captured/pruned descendants, termination attempts, and verified exits in stdout and the existing CI logs artifact. Command-line contents are omitted.
- Cover stale ancestry, timestamp precision, PID reuse, real graceful/forceful descendant cleanup, and persisted diagnostics.

## Investigation
[Build 477649](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477649&view=logs) lost its network-isolation listener during Electron integration tests; the subsequent WSL cache restore failed with a refused proxy connection and test-result publication failed with DNS errors. [Build 477617](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477617&view=logs) had the same signature.

The existing logs establish that the service disappeared, but do not conclusively attribute its termination to Agent Host cleanup. The stale-PPID ownership flaw provides a concrete mechanism; the new diagnostics allow direct attribution in subsequent runs.

## Validation
- `npm run compile-client`: passed (zero errors).
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- Focused cleanup suite: 43 passing in Windows Electron and 43 passing in Node.
- Targeted ESLint, whitespace checks, and commit hygiene: passed.
- [Azure validation build 477783](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477783&view=results): **passed** on review-fix commit `5769698c49a`, Windows/Linux/macOS CI, publishing and release disabled. The superseded build 477775 passed all three Electron integration-test jobs and Windows WSL cache restore before cancellation.

## Reviewer notes
Windows creation times are queried via CIM because the current native process-tree dependency does not expose them. Concurrent identity checks share an in-flight query; the two real-process cleanup tests take about two seconds each locally. Logs are retained under `.build/logs/integration-tests/agent-host-cleanup-<runner-pid>.log`, including when Windows Electron does not forward renderer stdout.


## Review follow-up
All three review comments are addressed: descendant capture always starts a fresh CIM query, all descendant identity checks/termination/polling share a five-second deadline with remaining query budgets, and graceful cleanup still requires exit code zero. Fake-clock regression tests verify exact deadline behavior for stalled and slow queries.



## Fast-probe optimization
Commit f6b7efcbe8e skips PowerShell identity queries only when a non-terminating PID probe reports ESRCH. Live PIDs and EPERM still receive CIM creation-time verification; unexpected errors propagate. Tests verify query counts and retained identity safety.

[Azure fast-probe validation build 477801](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477801&view=results): **passed** on commit `f6b7efcbe8e`, Windows/Linux/macOS CI with publishing/release disabled. The earlier build 477783 also completed successfully. Windows WSL kernel cache restore passed; these CI builds do not exercise product signing.

pull_requests.title: debug: dispose inline adapter message subscriptions
pull_requests.body:
Refs #293200, only the unchecked `extHostDebugService.ts:1257` direct subscription item (@mjbvz; task key `ext-host-debug-1257`).

### Problem

The original subscription is `DirectDebugAdapter`'s listener on `implementation.onDidSendMessage` (line 1257 at issue-date revision `3ef1567cc09dff5500ff510a85182a1b65da53a6`, line 1273 on the baseline).

Stopping a session disposes the implementation, but that does not unsubscribe the wrapper when the event publisher belongs to a longer-lived extension service. The publisher can retain the wrapper and its debug-service callback after the session ends. Session-owned publishers that release their listeners do not exhibit this leak.

### Change

- Keep the subscription disposable on the inline wrapper and release it on wrapper disposal.
- Dispose the wrapper before disposing the implementation when stopping, including when implementation disposal throws.
- Add regression coverage for stopping, direct disposal, surviving adapters/communication, and implementation disposal errors.

### Validation

- `npm run compile-client`: passed, including TypeScript compilation.
- Targeted ESLint: passed for both changed files.
- Four new regression tests fail on unchanged baseline; all four pass with the fix. Together with adjacent debug visualization tests: 11 passing (including the runner's clean-state check).
- Actual Code OSS, Windows local extension host, isolated empty profiles and a synthetic inline adapter:
  - 3 warmup + 10 repeated cycles with a session-owned publisher: 0 retained callbacks before and after.
  - The same cycles with an extension-owned shared publisher: baseline callback counts 3 / 8 / 13; fixed counts 0 / 0 / 0.
  - Counts are actual `DirectDebugAdapter` subscription callbacks registered through the product, sampled after settling and explicit GC; no direct class instantiation was used for the product probe.
  - Matched baseline/fixed product runs also exercised surviving sessions, delayed disconnect followed by an awaited stop command and immediate restart (#132446 / #169301), rejected tracker creation without unhandled rejection (#103477 / #166959), cancellation of a pending start, and implementation disposal errors. Behavior was preserved; fixed listener counts returned to zero.
- Two independent, read-only whole-change reviews: `gpt-6-astra` and `claude-opus-5.5`, each with default reasoning effort; no actionable findings.

### Scope and limits

Open leak PRs #334102 and #334103 address different main-thread registrations and do not fix this subscription. No umbrella checklist changes are included.

This verifies the Windows/local synthetic inline-adapter cases above, not remote/browser extension hosts, other operating systems, arbitrary third-party adapters, or general heap-size/performance claims. Historical repro mechanisms were exercised in the synthetic product harness, not the original macOS macro extension or a nested development debugger.

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] sessions: Log workbenchActionExecuted for session list toolbars
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #338340 from `main`.

Inline clicks in the Agents Window session list never produced `workbenchActionExecuted` events, so we can't measure the promoted New Chat row action from the "Promote New Chat on session rows" experiment (#336627, microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9587). In Stable 1.139, `sessions.chatCompositeBar.addChat` only ever has `from = contextMenu` or `from = keybinding`, and there are no row-level archive, mark-as-done, or pin events.

## Root cause

`WorkbenchToolBar` only logs `workbenchActionExecuted` (from `actionBar.onDidRun`) when `telemetrySource` is set. None of the session list toolbars set one.

`SessionItemActionRunner` doesn't need special handling. It overrides `runAction`, and the base `ActionRunner.run` fires `onDidRun` after it returns on every path: normal runs, the multi-select context swap, and the `handleToolbarAction` short-circuit.

## Changes

| Surface | `from` |
|---|---|
| Main list session row toolbar (`SessionItemToolbar`) | `sessionsList.row` |
| Chat row toolbar (`SessionChatItemToolbar`) | `sessionsList.chatRow` |
| Section header toolbar | `sessionsList.section` |
| Custom group header toolbar | `sessionsList.group` |
| Blocked sessions rows (`SessionsFlatList`) | `blockedSessionsList.row` |
| Automations history rows (`SessionsFlatList`) | `automationsView.historyRow` |
| Other `SessionsFlatList` hosts (default) | `sessionsFlatList.row` |

- The row renderer is shared, so `SessionsFlatList` gets an optional `toolbarTelemetrySource` and the promoted New Chat clicks stay separate from the other lists.
- The section toolbar's New Session split dropdown and the External filter submenu share the toolbar's action runner. They now pass `skipTelemetry` so a click logs `sessionsList.section` once instead of also logging `contextMenu`.
- Context menus are unchanged and still log `from = contextMenu`.

No classification change is needed: `from` is already classified as `SystemMetaData`/`FeatureInsight`, and the new values are fixed component names. There is no product behavior change.

## Notes for reviewers

- Section dropdown clicks move from `from = contextMenu` to `from = sessionsList.section`.
- The control arm's New Chat lives in the overflow of `Menus.SessionBarToolbar` (`chatCompositeBar.ts`, `sessionHeaderBar.ts`). Those toolbars also have no `telemetrySource`, so their overflow clicks still show up as `from = contextMenu`. That can be a follow-up if we want a clean control baseline.

## Validation

- New `sessionsListToolbarTelemetry.test.ts` checks that a promoted New Chat row click logs `{ id: 'sessions.chatCompositeBar.addChat', from: 'sessionsList.row' }` and a section filter item logs `sessionsList.section` without the `contextMenu` event. It also checks that a flat list row action handled by `onToolbarAction` is still logged. Both tests fail without the fix (`events: []`).
- All 551 tests under `vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test` pass.
- The type check and hygiene are clean for the changed files.

`DiffHunkWidget` eagerly creates a menu-backed toolbar for every hunk. Pooled widgets keep those menus and shared listeners alive even after their overlays are removed. Session disposal already releases them; this is excess live retention, not evidence of an unbounded post-disposal leak.

- Let in-flight toolbar actions report completion before releasing their toolbar.
- Add regression coverage for real menu ownership, focus/node preservation, reuse, and action completion.

This does not change the generic `MenuWorkbenchToolBar`. The broad visibility approach in #312317 was reverted by #312669; #309287 and the pool-removal proposal #304152 were closed unmerged. pull_requests.title: editor: prevent reentrant autoclose decoration leaks
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #205598.

### What was wrong

An `onDidChangeDecorations` handler can edit the model while an old autoclose
action is being disposed. Nested cursor validation removes that old action
and the edit creates a new action. When the outer validation resumes, its
pending `splice` removes the **new** action without disposing it.

This loses both decoration ownership and overtyping behavior. A minimal
reproduction needs only ordinary bracket autoclosing:

1. Type `(` into an empty editor, producing `()`.
2. Install a one-shot model decorations handler that calls
   `editor.trigger('keyboard', 'type', { text: '(' })`.
3. Move the cursor after the first closing parenthesis.
4. Remove the handler and move away/reset the text using edits.

The baseline leaves two internal autoclose decorations behind per iteration.
The original report supplied a telemetry stack rather than reproducible steps;
this reproduces its reentrant cursor-disposal ownership defect without needing
the original inline-suggestion environment or an unsafe caller-owned ID array.

### Change

- Publish the valid autoclose-action list before disposing invalid actions.
  Reentrant edits can add actions without the outer pass removing them or
  validating them against stale selections.
- Remove both decoration sets inside one `changeDecorations` callback, clearing
  both ID arrays before a combined notification instead of two partially
  completed removal notifications.
- Add a regression covering one, two and three old nested pairs, reentrant pair
  creation, correct overtyping and decoration cleanup. No warning suppression.

### Validation

- Regression fails on baseline with 2/4/6 retained decorations and extra `)`;
  passes with the fix.
- 57 targeted cursor, decoration, injected-text and model-event tests pass,
  including the #37315 and #118270 regressions.
- Client type check, two-file ESLint and diff whitespace check pass.
- Actual isolated Windows Code OSS, 100 identical event-driven cycles:
  model-owned counts at iterations 1/10/50/100 change from **4/22/102/202**
  to **2/2/2/2** (the two normal tracked ranges); warnings change from 400 to 0.
- Post-close forced-GC heaps: 100 orphaned character plus 100 enclosing
  decoration nodes on baseline, zero of either with the fix.
- 48 live event variants, including 2,400 actually invoked nested-edit
  callbacks, show no decoration accumulation with the fix.
- 500 existing autoclose/ghost/snippet cycles and 25 real inline-completion
  to suggestion/snippet acceptance cycles remain bounded.
- Deliberate raw recursive-delta controls still warn; the global diagnostic
  and the API's handling of unsafe caller ID overwrites are not changed.
- Expanded follow-up: all 420 tests in the five related Electron test modules
  pass. Another 1,400 actual Code OSS cycles across 14 historical/adjacent cases,
  plus 25 editor close/reopen cycles, pass 5,401 assertions. These cover
  autoclose/overtype/deletion, undo/redo event ordering, shared-model two-editor
  synchronization, mixed-validity multicursor reentrancy and listener exceptions.
  Cleanup checkpoints have no autoclose decorations; the final heap has no
  autoclose nodes or actions. Separate disposed-model retention remains outside
  this fix.

Testing used synthetic content/providers on Windows. This does not claim
exhaustive coverage of other platforms, arbitrary extension timing, or unrelated
disposed-model retention.

pull_requests.title: Reject `executeTask()` when a fetched task cannot be found
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338344

`executeTask()` for a task from `fetchTasks()` ignored the rejection of `$executeTask`, so a failed task lookup on the main thread left the caller with an execution that never starts or ends. It now awaits `$executeTask` and rethrows the error. The execution a call registered is removed once the last overlapping call for the same task has finished, and only if none of them ran the task and it was not started otherwise, e.g. from the UI.

`$executeTask` resolves once the task is found, before the task runs to completion, so `executeTask()` still returns as soon as the task has started.

Tested with the new unit tests in `src/vs/workbench/api/test/node/extHostTask.test.ts`, including overlapping calls that fail and succeed. They fail without the change.

pull_requests.title: editor: share inline diff margin mouse-move listener
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #228718

## Problem

Each live inline deleted-code margin subscribes to the modified editor's mouse-move event. A diff with enough deletion hunks therefore triggers `ListenerLeakError` even though those margins are properly disposed on recomputation.

#267991 and #275849 removed the historical mouse-down subscriptions, but the mouse-move signature remains (also reported in #228719, which was closed as a duplicate of #228718).

## Change

- Register one mouse-move listener on `DiffEditorViewZones` and route content/gutter view-zone events to the matching margin.
- Hide the previously active margin, clear routing state on recomputation/disposal, and remove old zone IDs when zones are reapplied.
- Preserve the existing lightbulb positioning, hovered copy-line offset, read-only actions, and DOM-copy listener ownership.
- Add a leak-checked regression covering 40 hunks, constant listener counts, and content/gutter/unrelated-zone visibility transitions.

## Validation

Real Windows Code OSS, separate empty profiles and synthetic files, baseline `6d15fc6f79540b4600fd5aa7deed4d4524fccda6` versus this change:

| Modified-editor mouse-move listeners | Baseline | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 200 deletion hunks | 209 | 10 |
| 25 hunks, each of 34 subsequent recomputations | 34 | 10 |
| Side-by-side, three verified transitions | 9 | 10 |
| Populated model detached | 8 | 9 |

The single owner listener remains when no inline margins exist. Baseline logged the matching warning; the candidate did not. GC-assisted renderer instance queries found no retained disposed margins in either run: this fixes live listener fan-out, not a demonstrated accumulating-object leak.

- Regression failed before the fix (40 additional listeners); final focused diff-editor suite: **10 passing**, including disposable tracking.
- Client typecheck and targeted ESLint pass.
- Verified layout/model teardown, identical wrapped-text character mapping, and reverting a hunk.
- Real pointer hit-testing verified margin switching and a lightbulb menu still present after 500 ms. Writable/read-only menus preserve the hovered copy-line label and correctly include/exclude Revert.
- Two independent read-only AI reviews (`gpt-6-astra`, `claude-opus-5.5`, default reasoning) approved the complete change.

Not verified: macOS/Linux, exact historical background-tokenization race timing, repeated full tab close/reopen, native menus, or OS clipboard payload. No heap-size or CPU-performance claim.

pull_requests.title: sessions: Log workbenchActionExecuted for session list toolbars
pull_requests.body:
Inline clicks in the Agents Window session list never produced `workbenchActionExecuted` events, so we can't measure the promoted New Chat row action from the "Promote New Chat on session rows" experiment (#336627, microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9587). In Stable 1.139, `sessions.chatCompositeBar.addChat` only ever has `from = contextMenu` or `from = keybinding`, and there are no row-level archive, mark-as-done, or pin events.

## Root cause

`WorkbenchToolBar` only logs `workbenchActionExecuted` (from `actionBar.onDidRun`) when `telemetrySource` is set. None of the session list toolbars set one.

`SessionItemActionRunner` doesn't need special handling. It overrides `runAction`, and the base `ActionRunner.run` fires `onDidRun` after it returns on every path: normal runs, the multi-select context swap, and the `handleToolbarAction` short-circuit.

## Changes

| Surface | `from` |
|---|---|
| Main list session row toolbar (`SessionItemToolbar`) | `sessionsList.row` |
| Chat row toolbar (`SessionChatItemToolbar`) | `sessionsList.chatRow` |
| Section header toolbar | `sessionsList.section` |
| Custom group header toolbar | `sessionsList.group` |
| Blocked sessions rows (`SessionsFlatList`) | `blockedSessionsList.row` |
| Automations history rows (`SessionsFlatList`) | `automationsView.historyRow` |
| Other `SessionsFlatList` hosts (default) | `sessionsFlatList.row` |

- The row renderer is shared, so `SessionsFlatList` gets an optional `toolbarTelemetrySource` and the promoted New Chat clicks stay separate from the other lists.
- The section toolbar's New Session split dropdown and the External filter submenu share the toolbar's action runner. They now pass `skipTelemetry` so a click logs `sessionsList.section` once instead of also logging `contextMenu`.
- Context menus are unchanged and still log `from = contextMenu`.

No classification change is needed: `from` is already classified as `SystemMetaData`/`FeatureInsight`, and the new values are fixed component names. There is no product behavior change.

## Notes for reviewers

- Section dropdown clicks move from `from = contextMenu` to `from = sessionsList.section`.
- The control arm's New Chat lives in the overflow of `Menus.SessionBarToolbar` (`chatCompositeBar.ts`, `sessionHeaderBar.ts`). Those toolbars also have no `telemetrySource`, so their overflow clicks still show up as `from = contextMenu`. That can be a follow-up if we want a clean control baseline.

## Validation

- New `sessionsListToolbarTelemetry.test.ts` checks that a promoted New Chat row click logs `{ id: 'sessions.chatCompositeBar.addChat', from: 'sessionsList.row' }` and a section filter item logs `sessionsList.section` without the `contextMenu` event. It also checks that a flat list row action handled by `onToolbarAction` is still logged. Both tests fail without the fix (`events: []`).
- All 551 tests under `vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test` pass.
- The type check and hygiene are clean for the changed files.

The descriptor check verifies that disposal restores the original property or removes the temporary override. Exact virtual wall-clock, monotonic-clock, animation-frame timestamp, and `performance.now` restoration checks remain unchanged. No production code changes.

The original clock assertions were introduced in #327980.

pull_requests.title: test: validate Windows Agent Host cleanup process ancestry
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
- Validate creation times at every Windows parent/child edge and when checking descendant identity, preventing stale parent PIDs or reused process identities from authorizing cleanup.
- Use the same verified descendant cleanup for graceful and forceful shutdown; avoid `taskkill /T` traversing stale Windows ancestry.
- Record timestamped runner/server PIDs, captured/pruned descendants, termination attempts, and verified exits in stdout and the existing CI logs artifact. Command-line contents are omitted.
- Cover stale ancestry, timestamp precision, PID reuse, real graceful/forceful descendant cleanup, and persisted diagnostics.

## Investigation
[Build 477649](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477649&view=logs) lost its network-isolation listener during Electron integration tests; the subsequent WSL cache restore failed with a refused proxy connection and test-result publication failed with DNS errors. [Build 477617](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477617&view=logs) had the same signature.

The existing logs establish that the service disappeared, but do not conclusively attribute its termination to Agent Host cleanup. The stale-PPID ownership flaw provides a concrete mechanism; the new diagnostics allow direct attribution in subsequent runs.

## Validation
- `npm run compile-client`: passed (zero errors).
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- Focused cleanup suite: 43 passing in Windows Electron and 43 passing in Node.
- Targeted ESLint, whitespace checks, and commit hygiene: passed.
- [Azure validation build 477783](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477783&view=results): **passed** on review-fix commit `5769698c49a`, Windows/Linux/macOS CI, publishing and release disabled. The superseded build 477775 passed all three Electron integration-test jobs and Windows WSL cache restore before cancellation.

## Reviewer notes
Windows creation times are queried via CIM because the current native process-tree dependency does not expose them. Concurrent identity checks share an in-flight query; the two real-process cleanup tests take about two seconds each locally. Logs are retained under `.build/logs/integration-tests/agent-host-cleanup-<runner-pid>.log`, including when Windows Electron does not forward renderer stdout.


## Review follow-up
All three review comments are addressed: descendant capture always starts a fresh CIM query, all descendant identity checks/termination/polling share a five-second deadline with remaining query budgets, and graceful cleanup still requires exit code zero. Fake-clock regression tests verify exact deadline behavior for stalled and slow queries.



## Fast-probe optimization
Commit f6b7efcbe8e skips PowerShell identity queries only when a non-terminating PID probe reports ESRCH. Live PIDs and EPERM still receive CIM creation-time verification; unexpected errors propagate. Tests verify query counts and retained identity safety.

[Azure fast-probe validation build 477801](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477801&view=results): **passed** on commit `f6b7efcbe8e`, Windows/Linux/macOS CI with publishing/release disabled. The earlier build 477783 also completed successfully. Windows WSL kernel cache restore passed; these CI builds do not exercise product signing.

pull_requests.title: test: stabilize Codex shared-workspace startup on Linux
pull_requests.body:
Codex 0.153.0 can fail to start concurrent chats in an empty shared workspace on Linux: bubblewrap reports that a protected metadata mount source no longer exists. This caused `CodexMaterializeFailed` in the server-tool tests exercised by #337659.

Create `.git`, `.agents`, and `.codex` before starting Codex in this suite's disposable Linux workspaces. This preserves all 39 existing scenario bodies and assertions, concurrency, permissions, timeouts, and recorded replay fixtures. The known-issues note tracks the remaining runtime defect and how to remove the workaround after an SDK fix.

### Platform scope

Reviewed public Codex source at `rust-v0.153.0`, commit `41e22fee981a63b3698df7ed36bad393cda24715`:

- [Linux sandbox modules](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/lib.rs#L6) compile bubblewrap and its cleanup only for Linux.
- [Readable mounts](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs#L503) use paths observed during argument construction; [synthetic-target cleanup](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/linux_run_main.rs#L1093) removes temporary targets. [Existing target identities are preserved](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs#L187), explaining the fixture workaround.
- [Backend selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/manager.rs#L62) uses Seatbelt on native macOS and the Windows sandbox on native Windows. [Seatbelt protects paths through policy rules](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs#L553); [Windows applies ACLs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/workspace_acl.rs#L23). Neither uses the Linux temporary-mount cleanup.
- Scope follows the filesystem executor OS, not the UI OS: Linux execution environments, including remote Linux and WSL2, can still be affected. This does not claim that other platforms have no unrelated startup races.

### Larger local validation

| Experiment | Baseline failures / executions | Prepared-directory failures / executions |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Linux: four existing integration scenarios, completed 100-test worker batches | **5 / 1,600** | **0 / 1,600** |
| Linux: direct app-server concurrent thread starts | **65 / 2,000** | **0 / 2,000** |
| Native macOS: same integration scenarios without the workaround | **0 / 1,600** | Not applied on macOS |
| Native macOS: direct app-server concurrent thread starts | **0 / 2,000** | **0 / 2,000** |

The direct Linux baseline failures occurred in both baseline blocks: 33/1,000 and 32/1,000; both fixed blocks were 0/1,000. Every direct Linux failure and all five failures in the completed Linux integration batches had the exact missing protected-metadata mount error.

Interpretation: this supports the fixture mitigation and the Linux-specific mechanism much more strongly than the earlier 1/160 sample, but does not prove a zero failure rate. Under an independent-trial model, 0/1,600 gives a one-sided 95% upper bound of approximately 0.19%; 0/2,000 gives approximately 0.15%. Trials share runtime state and scheduling, so those are illustrative bounds, not product reliability guarantees. The integration comparison alone is still sparse (two-sided Fisher exact p ≈ 0.062 under the independence assumption); the separate direct-start reproduction and release-source analysis provide additional evidence.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction method, environment, and interrupted attempts</summary>

The four integration scenarios were:
- `list_sessions can include an archived session on request`
- `list_sessions hides archived sessions by default`
- `list_sessions includeArchived returns active and archived sessions`
- `list_sessions status filter combines active and archived sessions`

Each worker registered those same test bodies 25 times under their original titles in an untracked compiled copy, preserving per-test setup/teardown, normal lease recycling, strict replay, and fixture selection. Four isolated runner processes ran per block; baseline/fixed blocks alternated in a balanced order. Baseline removed only the seven-line protected-directory setup. No production code, test bodies, timeouts, or model fixtures were changed for the experiment.

Selected tests run with:

```sh
./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/codexAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'server tool: list_sessions (can include an archived session on request|hides archived sessions by default|includeArchived returns active and archived sessions|status filter combines active and archived sessions)'
```

Linux used local Ubuntu 24.04 Docker, bubblewrap 0.9.0, CI-built x64 dependencies and Electron 43.7.3, with published **ARM64 Codex 0.153.0 running natively** on the ARM64 host. The x64 Codex binary cannot install seccomp under emulation. Codex sandboxing stayed enabled. Electron required `--no-sandbox` for the root container. Native macOS used the published Darwin ARM64 Codex 0.153.0 binary. No local Windows stress run was available.

The direct experiment ran the published app-server over stdio, initialized its experimental API, and sent pairs of concurrent `thread/start` requests into fresh empty workspaces using VS Code's unchanged platform permission profiles. Each condition had 1,000 pairs (2,000 starts), in baseline/fixed/fixed/baseline blocks. Only the directory precreation differed. Successful threads were unsubscribed after each pair; no model turns, credentials, or external model calls were needed.

**Interrupted attempts are not hidden in the denominators:** one initial Linux runner failed before executing tests because four runners raced to create their shared crash-report directory. Later, a long-lived container without an init process accumulated 21,968 zombie processes and several stress runs timed out or were interrupted. Those partial baseline runs logged **254 passing test events, 4 failed test events, and 4 hook failures**, outside the completed-worker comparison above; they included additional matching mount failures. The environment was restarted with Docker `--init`, and replacement batches completed the 1,600-per-condition comparison. In that clean environment, an additional baseline block reproduced the exact race (1/400), while the matching fixed block passed (0/400). This mixed-environment sample should not be treated as a precisely controlled estimate of the CI failure rate.

</details>

Other validation:
- `npm run compile-client` and precommit hygiene passed.
- Normal `--grep 'server tool:'` replay: **39 passed on Linux and 39 passed on macOS**.
- [Azure build 477773](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477773) **succeeded**, including Linux, macOS, and Windows Electron tests, on the fixture-change commit `0df6b496e8f`; the follow-up commit only documents platform scope.
- GitHub's Linux and macOS Electron jobs passed on that commit. The Windows Codex E2E suite also passed; its job timed out later in unrelated extension tests.

pull_requests.title: webview: fix resource loading cancellation listener leaks
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #319468

## Summary

- Scope cancellation and cleanup to each webview resource request instead of attaching every read to one shared cancellation emitter. Keep the request alive until streaming finishes, fails, is cancelled, or the webview is disposed.
- Propagate cancellation of an Electron transferable response stream to the underlying file read without destroying the file stream's end/error cleanup.
- Dispose the file service's linked cancellation source when stream setup throws synchronously.
- Add regression coverage for parallel reads, repeated read failures, cancellation, disposal, sibling buffer views, and file-handle closure.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, 200 parallel resource loads reproduced the exact `potential listener LEAK detected, popular` warning and call stack from the issue. Five synchronous read failures retained 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 listeners; cancelling a transferred response left its file read running. These cases now pass, and three batches of 200 reads return to zero active requests after each batch.

The parallel-load warning is caused by shared-token fan-out; the failed/aborted-read cases also exposed actual cleanup problems. This does not claim to resolve the separate high-CPU/freeze symptoms reported in the issue comments.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`: passed, zero errors.
- Full client type-check, targeted ESLint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Code OSS Electron stream/cancellation, file-service, text-file I/O, webview, and panel suites: **165 passed**, 4 platform-specific skips.
- Real disk-I/O integration tests: **97 passed**, 3 platform-specific skips.

- Real Code OSS webview API stress test: **3 consecutive fresh-window runs passed**, each fetching **625 files x 128 KiB** through a webview and its service worker (3-4 seconds per run).
- Re-ran the two changed suites against the compiled client output: **33 passed**.

Historical regression coverage includes #326272/#326092 (resource concurrency), #321291/#316841 (shared-buffer detachment), #114428/#114024 (handle closure on cancellation/errors), #138805/#132771 (binary-read cancellation), #337018 (pending stream writes), and #312367 (listener/controller cleanup).

pull_requests.title: Do not delay goto symbol picks past programmatic accept
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #307333

## Summary

The `doGetSymbolPicks` override added for symbol "attach to chat" support (`f42f9b10eaf`) `await`s the picks promise before returning it. The added microtask hops delay the moment the quick pick observes the picks, so a programmatic `accept` that fires right after the picker opens finds an empty picker and becomes a silent no-op.

## Repro (works in 1.113, broken since 1.114)

```json
{
  "key": "alt+e",
  "command": "runCommands",
  "args": {
    "commands": [
      "workbench.action.gotoSymbol",
      "workbench.action.acceptSelectedQuickOpenItem"
    ]
  }
}
```

Only the first command has any effect: the picker opens, but the accept is ignored.

## Root cause

`runCommands` awaits each command's promise, then immediately executes the next one. With the override `await`ing before returning, `picker.selectedItems` is still empty by the time `acceptSelectedQuickOpenItem` dispatches into the picker's `onDidAccept` handler, which then does nothing (`const [item] = picker.selectedItems` is `undefined`).

Instrumented timeline on 1.114-era code (TypeScript file, 95 symbols): the accept fires before the picks are available. With this change, the same trace shows picks landing ~13ms **before** the programmatic accept, and the accept performs the real reveal work (~5ms) — restoring the 1.113 behavior.

## Fix

Decorate the picks in a fire-and-forget continuation and return `super`'s promise directly. The continuation registered here runs before the picker's own `then` on the same promise, so items are decorated before `picker.items` is set, and the returned promise keeps the pre-1.114 resolution timing.

Verified on a Windows x64 OSS build: the keybinding above jumps to the first symbol again, and `Shift+Enter` symbol attach still works.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: serialize Web PubSub payloads once when chunking
pull_requests.body:
`chunk()` in the Web PubSub relay transport serialized and UTF-8 encoded every outbound payload twice. The first pass, of the bare payload, fed the 32 MiB check and chunking. The second, as a `{ kind: 'message', data }` envelope, existed only to decide whether the message fits in a single frame. For a large message that meant a second full-size JSON string and byte buffer that were immediately discarded, and payload `toJSON`/getters ran twice.

## Change

`chunk()` now serializes and encodes the `kind: 'message'` envelope once, exactly as it is sent:

- **Fit check:** the single-frame check uses those exact bytes. The payload is measured serialized under the same key (`'data'`) that the wire uses.
- **32 MiB check and chunking:** these use the payload bytes inside that envelope as a zero-copy view. The envelope only adds the fixed ASCII prefix `{"kind":"message","data":` and a trailing `}`.
- **Payloads that serialize to nothing** (`undefined`, a function or a symbol): the envelope omits `data`, and `chunk()` throws the same `payload is not JSON-serialisable` error as before.

For plain data nothing else changes: returned envelopes, chunk slicing and base64, error order and messages, and all limits (900 KiB frames, 32 MiB payloads, reassembly group/segment/aggregate/timeout limits) are identical. There is no protocol or receiver change.

## Measurements

Whole-payload (≥ 1 MiB) calls inside `chunk()`, from a local probe instrumenting `JSON.stringify` / `TextEncoder.encode`. A fixed UUID-shaped group id made the wire output comparable:

| Payload | `JSON.stringify` | `TextEncoder.encode` | Wire output before vs. after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 MiB ASCII JSON-RPC message | 2 → 1 (33.6M → 16.8M chars) | 2 → 1 (33.6 → 16.8 MB) | 25 chunks, 22,369,684 base64 chars, identical SHA-256 |
| 16 MiB Unicode/escape-heavy | 2 → 1 (22.4M → 11.2M code units) | 2 → 1 (33.6 → 16.8 MB) | 25 chunks, identical SHA-256 |
| 100 KiB and exactly-at-ceiling single frames | 2 → 1 | 2 → 1 | identical |
| 32 MiB + 1 byte | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 | same rejection |

Wall-clock time did not change meaningfully, since base64 encoding dominates. This removes duplicate allocation work; it is not a heap-peak or OOM measurement.

## Tests

Added to `chunking.test.ts`:
- **Single serialization:** the payload is serialized once, under its wire key. A counting `toJSON` sees `['data', 'data']`; the previous code produced `['', 'data', '', 'data']`.
- **Wire-key sizing:** a root `toJSON` returns a short value for `''` and a value 4× the ceiling for `'data'` (and the reverse). Either way the frames must stay within the ceiling and deliver the `'data'` value.
- **Frame-fit boundaries:** single-frame fit one byte below, at, and one byte above the ceiling, for ASCII, 2/3/4-byte UTF-8, JSON escapes, unescaped U+2028 and a lone surrogate. Each case round-trips through its JSON wire form.
- **Pinned Unicode vector:** a pinned Unicode/escape-heavy split vector whose segment boundary splits a 4-byte UTF-8 sequence.
- **32 MiB boundary:** exactly 32 MiB of serialized UTF-8 is accepted and one more byte is rejected.
- **Not serializable:** `undefined`, a function, a symbol, `toJSON` returning `undefined`, BigInt and cyclic values all reject with `payload is not JSON-serialisable`.

Against the previous implementation, only the two serialization-key tests fail. The boundary, pinned-vector, 32 MiB and not-serializable tests pass there too, which confirms plain-data behavior is preserved.

Validation: the chunking, framing and `WebPubSubRelayTransport` unit tests pass (64 tests), and so do `npm run typecheck-client`, ESLint and hygiene on the changed files.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Behavior change:** this only affects a payload whose root `toJSON` depends on its key argument. Chunked output now carries the `'data'`-keyed serialization, which matches the single-frame path; previously chunks used the `''`-keyed one. This keeps every returned envelope within `maxChunkBytes` for deterministic payloads. No production caller passes such a payload today, because `agentHostProtocolClient` builds fresh JSON-RPC object literals.
- **Frame size:** `maxChunkBytes` bounds the serialized `ChunkEnvelope`. The `sendToGroup` wrapper adds about 115 bytes (it varies with group name and `ackId`), well within the 1 MB service frame limit.
- **Remaining sender-side costs** are unchanged and bounded:
  - one full JSON string, one UTF-8 copy, and about 4/3× base64 chunk strings per chunked message;
  - one wire serialization per frame in `WebPubSubRelayTransport`. For single-frame messages this is a second serialization of at most 900 KiB, and removing it would need a framing contract change;
  - the byte count for the opt-in AHP JSONL logging.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: keep minor version for Claude Code \`[1m]\` model ids
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334750

## Problem

When the Claude CLI is configured with a model id that has both a minor version and Claude Code's `[1m]` context tag, `toSdkModelId` truncated the minor version. This affects both current flagship models: Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1[1m]`, the id from the issue) became `claude-fable-5`, and Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, whose `[1m]` form follows the same shape) became `claude-opus-5`. Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 would hit the same path once released.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-fable-5-1[1m]` | `claude-fable-5` | `claude-fable-5-1[1m]` |
| `claude-opus-5-5[1m]` | `claude-opus-5` | `claude-opus-5-5[1m]` |
| `claude-opus-4-8[1m]` | `claude-opus-4` | `claude-opus-4-8[1m]` |

The `[1m]` directly after the minor version stopped Pattern 1 (`name-major-minor`) from matching, so Pattern 4 (`name-major[-mod]`) matched instead, took `1[1m]` (or `5[1m]`) as a modifier, and dropped it. As a result, the native Anthropic "Fable" row ran Fable 5 instead of Fable 5.1, and an Opus 5.5 selection ran Opus 5.

## Fix

- Split a trailing `[1m]`/`[2m]` tag off before the version patterns run. The pattern matches the Claude Code CLI's own model-id regex (`(?:\[[12]m\])?$`), where the tag always comes after any date suffix.
- **SDK id keeps the tag.** The CLI checks for `[1m]` in the model id to enable the `context-1m-2025-08-07` beta, so removing it would silently lose the 1M context window. Native ids from `supportedModels()` now round-trip unchanged.
- **Endpoint id drops the tag.** The CLI strips the bracketed tag from `model` when building Messages API requests and sends the beta header instead, so the Copilot proxy never receives the bracket form. Dropping it in `toEndpointModelId` matches what reaches CAPI.
- **Bare names with a tag are not parsed.** CLI aliases such as `opus[1m]` and `fable[1m]` (returned by `supportedModels()`) still pass through `toSdkModelId` unchanged rather than losing the tag.
- **Stricter modifiers.** Modifiers are now limited to dash-separated alphanumerics, and the five version patterns share one modifier definition. Malformed ids (`[1m][1m]`, `[foo]`, `[1m]-<date>`) and Vertex-style `claude-opus-4-1@20250805` now pass through unchanged instead of being cut down to the major version. The CLI doesn't produce these forms, so this is defence in depth.

## Validation

- `claudeModelId.test.ts`: added a snapshot test covering the ids from the issue plus Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5, and a test that malformed or non-Claude bracketed ids return `undefined`. Added `claude-fable-5-1[1m]` to the existing `toSdkModelId` pass-through test.
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/<suite>.test.ts`:
  - `claudeModelId`: 43 passing
  - `claudeModelSelection`: 13 passing
  - `claudeProxyService`: 46 passing
  - `claudeAgent`: 296 passing
- Manual tests in agents window, native Anthropic transport:
	- Selected the native "Fable" row; the session transcript shows `claude-fable-5-1` (was `claude-fable-5` before this change)
	- Repeated with `claude-opus-5-5[1m]` → `claude-opus-5-5`.

pull_requests.title: Continue sessions with last applied sandbox config after managed policy conflicts
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
When a sandbox configuration update conflicts with managed policy, log the error details and continue the session with the runtime's last applied sandbox configuration instead of failing the session.

Follow-up to #338172.

## Problem
VS Code applies sandbox configuration after SDK session creation/resume and during running-session configuration updates. Previously, `applySandboxConfig` logged update errors and rethrew them, including `managed_sandbox_policy_conflict`. A rejected update could therefore fail session initialization or interrupt a request even though the runtime retained its existing sandbox configuration.

## Changes
- Catch `managed_sandbox_policy_conflict` specifically within the sandbox configuration update helper. Recognize the structured error code and the runtime's full policy-conflict message, including RPC-wrapped messages.
- Log the session context and original error details, then return without propagating that conflict.
- Continue using the runtime's existing, last applied sandbox configuration; do not retry with weaker restrictions or apply the rejected candidate.
- Return whether the update was applied, so callers preserve the last confirmed sandbox state and existing session-bypass bookkeeping when it was rejected.
- Keep existing error behavior for unrelated failures and other SDK operations.
- Document this behavior in the Agent Host guide.

## Scope

pull_requests.title: Fix relative workspace TypeScript SDK paths after version selection
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #320055

In a multi-root workspace, manually selecting a TypeScript SDK at `../common/node_modules/typescript/lib` rewrites the setting to `common/node_modules/typescript/lib`. The SDK works for that session but resolves to a different or missing location after reopening.

The provider prefixes relative SDK paths with the workspace folder name so the resolver can identify the selected root. `path.join` treats that name as a filesystem segment and removes it together with `..`. Build this selector prefix without normalizing it; the existing resolver then removes the selector before resolving the relative path against the actual root directory.

Add integration coverage that writes the selected path through the real workspace configuration API and reloads it through the configuration reader and version provider. Tests use multiple roots with custom display names and cover ordinary relative paths, `./`, `../`, `../../`, and nested parent traversal.

Validation:

- New test file executed against current source in an isolated VS Code 1.132.0 Extension Host: **2 passed / 3 failed before; 5 passed after**, no skips.
- Separate real QuickPick interaction, persisted `.code-workspace`, and fresh Extension Host process: baseline resolves a missing SDK; fixed source resolves the originally selected SDK. A real TypeScript server launched from that resolved path returns the expected `quickinfo` result.
- Strict targeted TypeScript 6.0.3 check of the new test and its imported source graph: **0 diagnostics**. `git diff --check` passes.

Validation ran on macOS. The scratch extension registers the current `js/ts.tsdk.path` schema and uses current-source components in the installed host; this is not a complete current-main VS Code build or a native Windows/Linux run. The restart check validates SDK path resolution, not restoration of the test host's workspace-version preference. No ordinary user settings or installed application files were changed.

Developed and reviewed with Codex assistance.

pull_requests.title: Allow bounded searches of offloaded Agent Host tool output
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338267

The large-output tool instruction added in #329778 told models to **ONLY** use `view` on offloaded tool-output files. Some models, such as GPT-5.6 Sol, follow that literally: instead of searching the file, they page through all of it in `view_range` chunks, which defeats the purpose of offloading.

This PR keeps the part that mattered, which is discouraging whole-file dumps that would be offloaded again. It explicitly allows targeted, bounded searches with the harness search tool (`grep` or `rg`, depending on the model), followed by a narrow `view_range`:

> When a tool reports that its output was saved to a temporary file because it was too large, inspect that file with targeted, bounded reads: search it for what you need with the `grep` or `rg` tool, then use `view` with a narrow `view_range` to read the relevant lines. Do not dump the whole file (for example with `cat` or `view` without a range) or run broad searches, because oversized output will be offloaded again.

### Validation

A/B test in Code OSS (Chat view, Copilot Agent Host, GPT-5.6 Sol, one run per scenario), using the repro from #338267:

| Scenario | Old wording | New wording |
|---|---|---|
| 342 KB terminal log, `node gen.js` | 18 paged `view` calls, then read `gen.js` to work out the answer | 1 bounded `rg` on the offloaded file |
| 282 KB `cat extensions/copilot/package.json` | `rg` on the original file, then narrow `view` of the offloaded file | `rg` on the offloaded file, then narrow `view` (lines 5388–5401) |

All runs returned the correct answer.

- Unit tests: `toolInstructions.test.ts`, `agentHostPromptRegistry.test.ts`, `copilotAgent.test.ts`
- Copilot prompt snapshots regenerated in replay mode with `AGENT_HOST_UPDATE_AHP_SNAPSHOTS=1`; the only change is the instruction line. Plain replay of `copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts` passes (23 tests).

pull_requests.title: Fix cold component fixture readiness timeouts
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Remove the shared fixture harness's eager `Error.stack` source-map warmup. Keep source-map support installed so real render errors and disposable-leak diagnostics still get mapped stacks on demand.

Add regression coverage that:
- Successful cold renders do not request diagnostic source maps.
- A real fixture setup failure retains its original error and mapped TypeScript stack.

No authentication code, timeout limits, retries, screenshot baselines, visual assertions, or widget behavior changes. This is a standalone harness fix.

## Diagnosis and reproduction

The same false `Fixture timed out after 3000ms` failures occur on main, for example in [run 36338369901](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36338369901/job/108673484646) (21 failures, 54 passes).

Reproduced against an isolated static rspack build on Windows with the committed Component Explorer 0.2.1-140 / webpack plugin 0.3.1-132, Playwright 1.61.1, Chromium 1228, and two workers. Both repeated cold `StreamingVisibleHeader/Dark` renders timed out before reaching their existing geometry or screenshot assertions.

The eager stack read synchronously loaded and parsed diagnostic source maps for about 4.2 seconds. Although that synchronous work precedes the explorer's async timeout, the reproducer then spent about 2.6 seconds waiting for setup resource callbacks, leaving insufficient time for the actual widget to settle. Removing only the eager warmup reduced theme setup to about 90 ms. Cold carousel renders completed in 265-276 ms and cold scroll renders in 1508-1534 ms, with the same 3000 ms watchdog.

## Validation

- **77/77 fixture Playwright tests pass** on the static build with two workers, including every existing interaction test.
- **24/24 readiness, geometry, exact screenshot stability, and error-reporting tests pass** separately.
- Six additional repeated cold-render cases pass.
- Negative control: temporarily restoring the original eager warmup makes the new regression fail because two diagnostic source maps are requested; removing it makes the test pass.
- Targeted Playwright TypeScript check, changed-file ESLint, and `git diff --check` pass.

**Current status: incomplete.** [Screenshot retry, attempt 2](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36346035699/job/108698430236) on this same fix commit reports actual `Fixture timed out after 3000ms` failures for `sessions/createPullRequest/CreationFailed/Dark` and `Light`. This is distinct from attempt 1's known two-pixel keyboard-focus baseline flake. The original cold-success improvement is measured, but it is not a complete harness fix; the remaining failure path is under investigation.

**Ubuntu Playwright:** all 77 tests passed in attempt 1. The green Playwright result displayed on attempt 2 is carried over, not an independent repeat. No timeout limits, retries, screenshot baselines, or behavior assertions have been changed. The shared checkout is currently reserved for separate authentication work and is not being modified by this investigation.

pull_requests.title: chat: avoid aggregating large history strings in RPC JSON
pull_requests.body:
Related to #336200 (non-closing; the original crash payload has not been replayed).

## Problem

Extension-host-backed chat-agent invocation sends accumulated history, including prior result metadata, through ordinary RPC JSON serialization. Multi-megabyte strings are combined into one large JavaScript string before transport, adding a large contiguous V8 allocation on top of retained history. The issue's reported stack identifies this invocation/serialization path, although it does not identify the exact failed field or allocation size.

## Changes

- Extend the existing buffer-backed RPC encoding to carry strings of at least 65,536 UTF-16 code units as individually JSON-encoded buffers. The aggregate JSON contains references instead of their text.
- Use this transport for chat invocation, followups, titles, summaries and participant detection; include the result passed to followup providers.
- Preserve ordinary JSON normalization for newly wrapped chat data, existing buffer behavior, Unicode including lone surrogates, and literal reference-shaped metadata.
- No history/output truncation, persistence changes, new setting, or dependency changes.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- **77 Electron tests passing** across RPC, main-thread/extension-host chat, language models, commands and notebooks. New coverage checks the encoding threshold, exact round trips, metadata compatibility, and all five history-bearing chat-agent methods.
- The two allocation-shape regressions fail against unchanged production code.
- Full `npm run typecheck-client -- --pretty false`, targeted ESLint and `git diff --check` pass. The initially missing generated Electron declarations were restored locally from the matching 43.7.3 build; shared dependencies were not modified.

A dedicated Node 24.18 process also exercises the serializer with 128 one-MiB text entries under `--max-old-space-size=64 --max-semi-space-size=1 --expose-gc`:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serialization followed by forced GC | Fatal heap-limit OOM, exit 134, approximately 135 MiB live | Completes |
| Aggregate JSON after encoding | Contains the full text | 11,173 characters |
| Post-GC JS heap | OOM | Approximately 6.3 MiB |
| Encoded text | In the aggregate string | 128 buffers, 134,217,984 bytes |

The data still consumes memory: the after-run RSS was approximately 179 MiB. This is a controlled test of aggregate-string allocation pressure, **not** a replay of the reporter's 47-hour renderer fragmentation, a total-memory/history bound, or proof that every reported OOM is resolved. Individually enormous values and large retained conversations can still require substantial memory; a current-build reporter retest remains necessary.

## Review follow-up

Addressed the nested-value serialization feedback in 88ccf8191dae69acb2534b72bdb682ef096d0794:

- Escape only the literal `$$ref$$` property rather than separately JSON-encoding its entire object. Nested buffers, large strings, URI transformation, and undefined normalization stay on the normal serializer traversal.
- Added nine regression/compatibility tests. Four cases failed before the fix: nested buffer identity, independent large-string encoding, preserved undefined array entries, and incoming URI transformation. Coverage also checks literal marker values, cycle rejection, and single `toJSON` evaluation.
- All 77 tests across the same eight Electron suites pass, along with full client typechecking, targeted ESLint, and staged-file hygiene.
- A follow-up constrained serializer run put 128 MiB of text inside reference-shaped metadata: 11,207 aggregate JSON characters, 128 buffers (134,217,984 bytes), and approximately 6.34 MiB post-GC JS heap under the 64 MiB old-space setting. RSS remained approximately 186 MiB; this is not a total-memory reduction claim or an end-to-end crash replay.

This remains an extension-host RPC change; native Agent Host transport and SDK memory management are unchanged.

pull_requests.title: chat: avoid retaining duplicate terminal output mirrors
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Recheck live-mirror ownership after awaiting xterm readiness. Overlapping output expansions now reuse the existing detached terminal instead of creating and retaining one mirror per call.

## Root cause

`ChatTerminalToolOutputSection._renderLiveOutput()` checked `_mirror` only before `await liveTerminalInstance.xtermReadyPromise`. Multiple callers could pass that check before any of them resumed. Each continuation created a new `DetachedTerminalCommandMirror`, overwrote `_mirror`, and registered its resources with the section's disposable store. Earlier mirrors remained alive until the entire section was disposed.

This also happens when the readiness promise is already resolved: `await` still yields. The fix preserves the existing fast path and disposal checks and rechecks ownership immediately before creation.

## Validation

- Added Electron regression tests using the real output section and command mirrors, with detached terminals backed by real xterm buffers.
- **Before:** 50 overlapping expansions created **50 mirrors** in both pending and already-ready cases.
- **After:** the same scenarios create **1 mirror**, preserve the rendered output, reuse it on refresh, and dispose it exactly once.
- Complete terminal tool rendering and command-mirror suites: **127 passing**.
- Targeted TypeScript syntactic/semantic checks for both changed files: passed.
- ESLint for both changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Attempted `npm run perf:chat-leak -- --iterations 3 --messages 20 --verbose`; it stopped before launch because `sqlite3` is unavailable. That runner explicitly targets Linux/macOS, so this PR does **not** claim a Windows end-to-end heap-slope measurement.

## Issue relationship

Related to #311225. This is a reproduced renderer retention defect in the terminal-output path implicated by the report. The attached historical log contains multiple listener signatures, several already addressed by previous PRs; it does not prove this race was the sole cause of the reporter's OOM. The issue reference is intentionally non-closing. No transcript/history limits, output truncation changes, or heap-limit increases are introduced.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: settle in-flight turns when a remote connection is replaced
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #336638

A remote Agent Host session could reopen showing a stale, incomplete conversation. The chat showed the turn still in progress while the session list showed it idle.

## Cause

When a remote connection is replaced (host restart, or a reconnect that gets a new `clientId`), `RemoteAgentHostChatContribution` disposes the old connection's `AgentHostSessionHandler`. A turn that handler was awaiting in `_invokeAgent` never settled, because its observer reads the old connection's state and never sees the turn end. The request stayed in progress, so `ChatModel#requestInProgressKeepAlive` kept the model alive. On reopen, `ChatService.loadRemoteSession` returned that cached model instead of resolving the session's current state from the new connection.

## Changes

- **Settle awaited turns on handler dispose.** Turns awaited by `_handleTurn` / `_handleResumedTurn` are tracked by the handler and resolve when it is disposed. `turnCancelled` is **not** sent: the turn may still be running on the host, and the new connection will pick it up.
- **Complete a disposed session's active turn.** `AgentHostChatSession.dispose()` now completes its active turn, which covers restored and server-initiated streamed turns that complete through `isCompleteObs`. On the normal close path the model is already gone, so this does nothing there.
- **Don't start work on a handler being torn down.** A new `_isInvocationAbandoned` check (cancelled or disposed) runs before an invocation creates a session, claims an active client, or dispatches its turn. Otherwise a turn prepared during a trust prompt, auth, `prepareSession`, or attachment conversion could go out on the old connection, and an active-client entry with a global scope could leak.
- **Keep host-owned queues host-owned.** `ChatService._isServerManagedQueue` relied on the chat session contribution still being registered. During teardown the contribution is unregistered first, so completing the stale turn made the client take the host's queued messages and send them itself. The service now remembers per model that its queue belongs to the host.

## Validation

- **New tests** (each fails without its fix):
  - live and resumed turns settle on handler dispose without `turnCancelled`
  - a session completes its active turn on dispose
  - disposal during the trust prompt, `createSession`, and `prepareSession` doesn't create a session, subscribe, or leak
  - the queue stays host-managed after the contribution is unregistered
  - a streamed model is kept alive while in progress, then loaded fresh once complete
- **Existing tests:** all chat unit tests pass (9956), as do the `vs/sessions` tests.
- **Reproduced in the product.** In the Agents window connected to a local standalone agent host with the mock agent, I sent a long turn, switched sessions, removed and re-added the host while the turn finished, then reopened the session.
  - Before: the session was stuck in progress, and the log showed `loadRemoteSession: reused existing model`.
  - After: the full response showed, loaded from the new connection (`session content resolved … with N history item(s)`).

## Notes for reviewers

- A chat that is **visible** while the connection is replaced still shows its old model. With this change its response ends instead of spinning, but nothing reloads a visible widget when the provider re-registers. That's the remaining part of #318604 and isn't handled here.
- An abandoned invocation is reported as `outcome: 'notDispatched'` in `agentHost.firstResponse`.

(Written by Copilot)

pull_requests.title: Agents - fix terminal reuse in agents window to match editor behavior
pull_requests.body:
This pull request addresses a discrepancy in terminal behavior between the editor window and the agents window when running tasks. 

### Changes made:
- **Terminal Reuse Logic**: Updated `agentHostSessionTaskRunner.ts` to remember the last terminal used for each task. On rerunning a task, it now sends the command to the previous terminal if it is still open and idle.
- **Command Execution Tracking**: Enhanced `agentHostPty.ts` to track whether a command is currently running, allowing for better management of terminal states.
- **Fallback Mechanism**: If the previous terminal is busy, a new terminal is created, preventing commands from being sent to a running process.
- **Unit Tests**: Added tests to ensure the new reuse functionality works as expected, covering both the task runner and PTY behavior.

### Limitations:
- The terminal does not display the reuse message as in the editor window, since it operates as an interactive shell.
- Reuse is limited to individual tasks; sharing idle terminals across different tasks is not implemented.

### Testing:
- All 55 unit tests across the affected suites passed successfully, confirming the changes function as intended.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: add correlated startup performance telemetry
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Add bounded, content-free `agentHost.startupMark` telemetry to diagnose startup regressions and compare workloads such as fewer than 100 versus more than 100 Copilot sessions.

- Correlate bootstrap, readiness, listing, migration, and provider enumeration with one UUID per Agent Host process lifetime.
- Record provider session counts, catalog/fallback and storage metrics, migration/backfill state, provider registration, and first-access activation/SDK availability.
- Observe the actual first successful listing and startup-settled barrier independently of concurrent sampled listings and the three-attempt sampling cap.
- Reuse existing enumeration and availability decisions; add no telemetry-triggered scans, database reads, SDK probes, downloads, timers, or awaited flushes. Preserve usage-telemetry consent and local trace logging.
- Document the [startup graph and measurement contract](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6efbce589490598329b6dce80bc981421d52077/src/vs/platform/agentHost/PERFORMANCE.md).

## Measurement boundaries

Cumulative readiness milestones can include waiting for the first client request; they are distinct from client-perceived startup latency. Provider scans may overlap or run after startup and stop before filtering/publication. Missing context/counts remain unknown rather than zero. Operation sampling remains capped; early failures before telemetry publication are not a complete launch denominator.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`: passed with zero errors.
- Targeted startup, session aggregation, migration, and provider-gating regressions: **447 passing, 11 pending**.
- Client typecheck and targeted ESLint passed.
- All **40 telemetry fields**, including **30 numeric/boolean measurements**, checked for classification and optionality.
- Markdown links/code fences and patch whitespace checked.

pull_requests.title: Fix import updates when moving directories of modern JS/TS modules
pull_requests.body:
Moving a directory containing only `.mts`, `.cts`, `.mjs`, or `.cjs` files leaves imports pointing to the old location. Moving these files individually already works, but directory discovery only searches `.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx`, so it never requests rename edits from TypeScript.

Include modern module suffixes in the existing search. The regression tests compare direct file moves with containing-directory moves for all eight suffixes, using real workspace events and checking the rename request sent to the language service.

Related to #58987. This addresses the modern-module directory case, not every scenario reported in that issue.

### Validation

- Ran the new test file against current source in an isolated VS Code 1.132.0 Extension Host, with TypeScript transpilation and a stubbed language-server client: **12 passed / 4 failed before; 16 passed after**. The four failures are precisely the modern-module directory cases.
- Checked actual import text and definition resolution through the built-in TypeScript language service for all four modern suffixes. Before the change, moving the folder leaves broken imports. Afterward, imports update and resolve to the moved files. This used a disposable copy of the 1.132.0 bundled extension with the identical glob change, rather than a full build of main.
- `git diff --check` passed. Full repository build, lint, and type checking were not completed locally.

Developed with Codex assistance.

revised from #336879

## Problem

In Modern UI with connected tabs, dragging a tab can cause the tab strip to scroll vertically.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abecbd50-470e-49bc-9778-202d7b67cc58

## Cause

The active tab's `tab-fill` and `tab-connected-edge` elements extend below the `tabs-container`.

- Adjust the positioning of `tab-connected-overflow-edge` children for the new height.
- Adjust `background-clip` for active fills in the last row so that they continue to cover the bottom border correctly.
