pull_requests.title: fix: await connector record persistence before asserting in WebKit test (build fix for vscode-engineering#3992)
pull_requests.body:
## Build failure

The macOS WebKit browser unit test suite failed on a single assertion in `CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService`:

```text
CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService > Copilot connectors > records a connector that was already connected outside this workbench
actual: recorded=[]; expected: recorded=["mail"]; both state.kind="installed"
```

The browser exited cleanly (code 0); the runner returned 1 solely for this assertion.

## Root cause

The test (`records a connector that was already connected outside this workbench`) marks a connector as connected, fires the change event, then waits only `await timeout(0)` before asserting that a record was persisted.

The listener registered in `updateEnablement()` responds by calling `void this.synchronizeConnectedConnectorRecords()`. That method computes the record id via `createConnectorRecord()`, which awaits `createInstallationRecordId(...)` — an async `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', ...)` — before calling `recordStore.upsert()`. A single macrotask (`timeout(0)`) does not guarantee that the digest promise has resolved and the upsert has run, so on slower/async digest completion the recorded-resource list is still empty when the assertion runs. `getInstallState()` can return `installed` directly from the connector's connection status without a stored record, which is why the state assertion passed while `recorded` was empty. This is a test synchronization defect, not a product regression.

## How the fix works

Instead of a fixed timer, the test now waits deterministically for the persistence to complete using the same pattern already established throughout this file (`Event.toPromise(Event.filter(service.onDidChange, ...))`):

```ts
const recorded = Event.toPromise(Event.filter(fixture.service.onDidChange, () => fixture.service.getRecordedResources().some(resource => resource.identifier === 'mail')));
fixture.connectedConnectors.add('mail');
fixture.connectorChanges.fire();
await recorded;
```

`recordStore.upsert()` triggers `recordStore.onDidChange`, which fires the service's `onDidChange`. The test therefore proceeds only once the connector record is actually persisted, regardless of how long the SHA-256 digest takes. Both original assertions (recorded resources and installed state) are preserved unchanged.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back.** Public culprit: not confirmed (strong suspect: the commit that introduced the timer-based assertion and async persistence path, microsoft/vscode#337649, but not verified by reproduction or bisect). Rationale: only one CI assertion is affected and no product data loss is established; a bounded, forward test-synchronization fix is far lower risk than reverting a broad feature with runtime integration. Owners to consult: `@pwang347`.

## Validation

Change is a focused edit to a single test. Repository dependencies were not installed in this environment, so `npm`-based typecheck/test runs could not be executed here. The edit uses `Event`/`Event.toPromise`/`Event.filter`, all already imported and used repeatedly in this file, and preserves the existing assertions. Recommended local validation: run this suite under WebKit, e.g. `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --build --browser webkit` filtered to `CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService`.

## Risk

Low. Test-only change; no production code touched. The deterministic wait matches the file's existing idiom and cannot mask a real failure because it still requires the record to be persisted before asserting.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@pwang347`

pull_requests.title: [3/4] authentication: canonicalize enterprise credential storage
pull_requests.body:
## Review stack

**#338149 (merged) -> #338150 (merged) -> #338151 (canonical credential storage) -> #338080 (multi-host enablement)**

This PR targets `main`; #338080 remains stacked on this branch. The provider lifecycle and core registration buffering are already on main through #338150.

## Stack 3/4: Canonical credential storage

Derive enterprise credential keys from normalized instance URIs instead of maintaining a persistent canonical-to-storage registry.

- Remove `github-enterprise.storageKeys`, namespace claims, and the host/storage planning layer. No migration marker or replacement bookkeeping key is added.
- Normalize hostname casing and trailing slashes while preserving scheme, deployment path case, and ports.
- Locate existing legacy token and Microsoft account-link stores through their existing storage keys, then move the selected data to the canonical credential keys before creating the engine.
- Preserve native session/account fields and token payloads. Canonical credentials, including signed-out state, remain authoritative.
- Keep legacy data until destination writes succeed; propagate write/cleanup failures and retry without a completion marker.
- Recheck canonical credentials around asynchronous legacy reads/copies so a newer sign-in is not overwritten.
- Keep public GitHub available if enterprise migration fails. Token-only migration does not add a dependency on global-state writes.

This remains a working **single-host** provider. It adds no plural setting, host picker, host-qualified identities, or workbench changes. Ambiguous legacy aliases require selecting the original URI rather than silently choosing a store.

## Validation

Full-suite baseline: `f3150bec6a5`.

- **128 GitHub authentication extension tests passed** independently on this layer.
- Coverage includes alias changes, restarts, Microsoft-only consent, canonical sign-out, read-only state for token-only migration, escaped paths, every migration write/cleanup failure, and newer canonical credentials appearing during migration.
- The stale-canonical-read regression was verified to fail before the fix and pass afterward.
- Extension compilation, browser-target type checks, scoped lint, hygiene, and diff checks passed.

Tests use fake storage and isolated test profiles; no actual user credentials or settings were modified. The follow-on #338080 uses the same deterministic keys and handles ambiguous legacy HTTP/HTTPS ownership without a persistent registry.
## URI helper consolidation

URI-consolidation checkpoint: `8bb82878fe5`.

Removed the tiny single-host `enterpriseConfiguration.ts` module: its URI identity helper and legacy setting constant now live in `enterpriseStorage.ts`. Hostname lowercasing is left to `Uri.toString()`; explicit scheme and trailing-slash normalization remain. Added coverage for uppercase schemes, explicit default ports, root paths, repeated trailing slashes, and escaped deployment paths.

Fresh validation for this behavior-preserving follow-up: **51 targeted GitHub Enterprise tests passed**, plus extension compilation, browser-target type checking, scoped lint, hygiene, and diff checks. The 128-test full-suite result above is the prior baseline.
## Selected canonical-precedence feedback

Current head: `4ee145bdaef`.

Canonical tokens and Microsoft account links are authoritative independently. Alias selection is required only for a component still missing from the canonical destination; already-authoritative components can clean up their redundant aliases. Signed-out empty values remain authoritative. Unresolved ambiguity for missing data still fails before mutation.

Added explicit user-info casing coverage for the already-simplified URI helper. Seven migration regression cases were verified failing before the fix and passing afterward. **58 targeted GitHub Enterprise tests passed**, with fresh extension compilation, browser-target type checks, scoped lint, hygiene, and diff checks. Earlier full-suite counts above are historical baselines. The migration-only region remains scheduled for removal in 1.144.

pull_requests.title: [2/4] authentication: separate enterprise provider lifecycles
pull_requests.body:
## Review stack

**#338149 (merged) -> #338150 (provider lifecycle) -> #338151 (credential storage) -> #338080 (multi-host enablement)**

This PR targets `main`. Review and merge the remaining layers in order.

## Stack 2/4: Single-host authentication lifecycle

Can registration and host-bound session work be owned separately without changing the existing single-host account-selection contract?

- Keep `github-enterprise.uri` as the only host setting and preserve native account/session IDs and labels.
- Make `GitHubSessionEngine` explicitly host-bound: it owns token flows, persistence, broker restore/renewal, and a cached session inventory that does not restore or renew tokens.
- Construct engines directly. Remove the production factory/interface and the extension-side registration wrapper; engines do not register themselves.
- Buffer initial session events in the extension host with the existing `Event.buffer`, forwarding only after the main-thread registration RPC acknowledges registration. No microtask-based readiness inference or extension-side readiness API.
- Keep configuration updates and their failure states in the same queue. Reconcile preparation-time session deltas before publishing replacements, without generation counters.
- Isolate OAuth callbacks by host and clean up retired engines, output channels, and listeners. Public GitHub remains available if enterprise initialization fails.

No plural host setting, host picker, credential namespace mapping, platform account-identity migration, or enrollment changes are enabled here.

## Validation

Full-suite baseline: `8cfd8eadb62`.

- **103 GitHub authentication extension tests passing**, including broker compatibility, cached-inventory behavior, consecutive initialization failures, A-to-B-to-A updates, and preparation-time session changes.
- **65 core authentication RPC integration tests passing**, including six registration-boundary regressions: immediate initial events, actual acknowledgment ordering, queued disposal, failure/retry cleanup, replacement during pending registration, and duplicate-disposer ownership.
- Extension compilation, core and browser-target type checks, scoped lint, staged hygiene, and diff check passed.

The previously reported component-fixture failures are being addressed separately in #338259. This auth stack changes no fixtures, screenshot baselines, or timeout thresholds.

The next layer adds credential-namespace compatibility to this same single-host runtime.
## Selected review follow-up

Current head: `d1098c9d042`.

- Keep the bundled documentation user-facing; remove implementation and proposed-API provenance sections.
- Make disposal cancellation explicit in naming and cover disposing a preparing engine with another update queued.
- Clarify why core captures events before queueing and forwards only after the registration acknowledgment; no session-selection behavior change.

Fresh verification for this follow-up: **14 lifecycle tests** and **65 core authentication RPC tests** passed. Extension compilation, browser-target type check, scoped lint, hygiene, and diff checks passed. The full-suite figures above refer to the prior baseline. Both downstream PRs have been restacked and their lifecycle suites passed independently.

pull_requests.title: [1/4] authentication: refresh Copilot on session issuer changes
pull_requests.body:
## Review stack

**#338149 (1: Copilot identity) → #338150 (2: provider lifecycle) → #338151 (3: credential storage) → #338080 (4: multi-host enablement)**

Each PR targets the preceding branch. Review and merge in numbered order. After squash-merging a layer, rebase and retarget the next layer onto `main` before merging it.

## Stack 1/4: Copilot identity refresh

Base: `main`.

## Review question

Does changing a GitHub session's account or authorization server refresh Copilot authentication and identity-dependent repository state, even when its token and session ID are unchanged?

- Reuse the existing account/issuer comparison when publishing authentication changes.
- Update the code-search subscriber to invalidate repository authorization/index status for the same identity changes, while preserving existing session-ID invalidation.
- Avoid redundant repository refreshes for token-only changes or equivalent session objects.

This is an independent bug fix using the session-provenance API already on main. It adds service and subscriber regressions without changing providers, configuration, credential storage, or enrollment.

## Validation

- 48 targeted authentication/session/code-search tests passing; 1 existing skip.
- Four same-ID account/issuer cases reproduced stale repository status before the subscriber fix; all nine subscriber tests pass afterward.
- Copilot type check, scoped lint, staged hygiene and diff check passed.
- Full-stack follow-up: 105 authentication/code-search/domain/MCP tests passing, 1 existing skip.

The next layer (#338150) separates enterprise registration from host-bound engines while keeping current single-host behavior.

## Screenshot CI follow-up

The earlier one-time screenshot override was explicitly approved by the maintainer, who reported that its two-pixel difference was not noticeable to their human eye. After rebasing onto the newer upstream fixture code, both captures in [run 36328148644](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36328148644) matched the original upstream baseline instead. Commit `fc3e05b83c2` removes the now-obsolete override; this PR **no longer changes screenshot baselines**.

The new Playwright fixture tests initially hit render timeouts, but all **75 passed on an unchanged-head retry**. No fixture implementation, UI, timeout threshold or authentication code was changed for this CI repair. Final fixture CI passed: all 75 Playwright tests, Screenshots, and Screenshots & Tests succeeded on run 36334957548 attempt 2. This PR merged on 2026-09-27.

| `user_message` | `monacoworkbench/agenthost.usermessagesent` | Strong equivalent |
| `assistant_usage` | `monacoworkbench/agenthost.requesttokenusage` | Strong for request-level tokens |
| `assistant_usage` cost | `monacoworkbench/agenthost.turncompleted` using `Measures.billednanoaiu` | Turn-level equivalent |
| `assistant_turn_end` | `monacoworkbench/agenthost.turncompleted` | Strong equivalent |
| `session_idle` with abort | `agenthost.turncompleted` where `Properties.result == "cancelled"` | Approximate |
| `loop_detected` | `monacoworkbench/agenthost.turnhung` | Health proxy, not exact loop detection |

### Existing intentional forwarding

| Runtime event | VS Code Kusto event | Why retained |
|---|---|---|
| `response.success` | `monacoworkbench/copilotsdk/response.success` | Exact model-call, network, and correlation details |
| `response.error` | `monacoworkbench/copilotsdk/response.error` | Exact model-call failure details |
| `tool_call_executed` | `monacoworkbench/copilotsdk/tool_call_executed` | Runtime tool outcome, safe arguments, result size, and token counts |
| `task_complete_todo_state` | `monacoworkbench/copilotsdk/task_complete_todo_state` | No equivalent native todo-state event |
| `model_call_cancelled` | `monacoworkbench/copilotsdk/model_call_cancelled` | No equivalent native cancellation event |

Native Agent Host queries should currently filter with:

```kusto
| where tostring(Properties.provider) == "copilotcli"
```

Forwarded HydraFusion queries should select the standard copy:

```kusto
| where coalesce(tolong(Measures.restricted), 0) == 0
```

### Summary

Fixes #337848 by preventing small Agent Host session-list fallback sets from repeatedly scanning the entire Copilot SDK session store.

In the reported case, 47 fallback sessions among approximately 4,858 SDK sessions now require 47 exact lookups—with at most four active concurrently—instead of repeatedly enumerating the entire SDK store.

This does not change the separate one-time provider catalog migration or background external-session discovery scans.

pull_requests.title: Fix platform-specific extension updates and package reinstallation
pull_requests.body:
Addresses #306702.

Extension update checks can reuse a universal gallery result for an installation on another platform even when a platform-specific build is available. A universal installation also cannot recover to a native build at the same version. If a same-version platform change does reach the installer, it only updates metadata and leaves the previous package's files in place.

This change:

- Resolves gallery results for the installation server's target platform before offering an update, including remote installations.
- Offers same-version updates from universal to native packages while preventing native-to-universal replacements at the same version. Newer universal releases remain eligible when they are the latest compatible choice.
- Uses the full extension key, including target platform, before reusing an installed package. Platform changes now extract the correct package instead of relabeling the old files.

Validation:

- Added 22 regression cases covering platform selection, remote installations, fallback behavior, update eligibility, and package extraction. The affected cases fail against the original behavior.
- 275 tests pass across ExtensionsWorkbenchService, Extension Gallery Service, InstallExtensionInProfileTask, and ExtensionDownloader.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, targeted ESLint, and pre-commit hygiene pass.
- Ran Code - OSS on macOS with an isolated profile, a local gallery, and real test extension packages. The original build left the universal package installed and reported all extensions up to date. The fixed build downloaded the native package at the same version; after restart, the native extension activated and no further update was offered.

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

Fixes #338125

Switching input sources through GNOME Shell's switcher on Wayland can close the Explorer rename input and accept a valid pending filename. The blur handler checks `document.hasFocus()` first, so losing page focus finishes editing even when the input remains the document's active element.

Check the input's own `ownerDocument.activeElement` before deciding to finish editing. This preserves the input, pending text and selection when the page loses focus. Moving focus to another element in the document still finishes editing, and the existing context-menu handling is retained.

This intentionally also preserves rename across window switches such as Alt+Tab, provided the input remains its document's active element.

Adds two Electron tests using the real `FilesRenderer`: preserving rename on page blur, and finishing it when focus moves to another input. A test-only IPC helper focuses a second `WebContentsView` to produce page blur without changing the original document's active element.

Validation (rechecked after rebasing onto `c94d3d7ed24`, with Electron 43.7.3):

- Before rebasing, the preservation test was verified to fail without the fix. Both new tests pass with the fix after rebasing, using the Wayland backend.
- TypeScript checking, ESLint on the changed files, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Manually verified on GNOME Shell 46.0 / Wayland: switching input sources preserves rename with the fix and closes it without the fix. Enter, Escape and dismissing the input context menu before continuing to type also work.

To reproduce: select a file in Explorer, press F2, edit the name without confirming, then switch input sources using the configured shortcut (for example, Super+Space). The input should remain open. The GNOME switcher scenario was verified manually; the automated tests cover page-focus handling.

Run the tests after compiling:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --ozone-platform=wayland --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/test/electron-browser/explorerRename.test.ts
```

pull_requests.title: agentHost: an automatic rename_chat keeps a title the user set
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338122

An automatic `rename_chat` (one fulfilling the host's title reminder) no longer replaces a title the user chose. Before this, `applyRenameChatTool` read `automatic` only to run the rename in the background, and `_renameChatFromTool` then wrote the agent's title with source `agent` regardless of where the chat's title came from. An agent that followed the reminder after the user renamed the chat overwrote the user's title, live and in the persisted metadata.

**Changes**

- `sessionServerTools.ts`: `ISessionServerToolAccessor.renameChat` takes `{ automatic }`, and `applyRenameChatTool` passes it on.
- `agentServiceFoundation.ts`: the forwarding accessor passes the new argument through.
- `agentService.ts`: `_renameChatFromTool` leaves the title alone when the rename is automatic and the chat's persisted title source is `user`. That source is `customChatTitleSource:<chat>`, or for the default chat the session's `customTitleSource`. It returns the user's title as the result.

An explicit rename, where the user asks the agent to rename the chat and `automatic` is omitted, still replaces a user title. The existing `rename_chat replaces live and persisted default and peer chat titles` test covers that and is unchanged.

**Tests**

- `sessionServerTools.test.ts`: *rename_chat tells the accessor whether the rename is automatic*.
- `agentService.test.ts`: *an automatic rename_chat keeps a title the user set, which an explicit rename_chat still replaces*.

Without the fix, both new tests fail; the second shows the user's title replaced by the automatic one. With it, `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/*.test.ts` passes: 6401 passing, 70 pending.

pull_requests.title: telemetry: log experiment triggers for triggered scorecards
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Adds a shared `experimentTrigger` telemetry event so that ExP triggered scorecards can be limited to users who reached the moment where an experiment's control and treatment behavior diverge. Without a trigger, assigned users whom an experiment never affects dilute its scorecard.

- `logExperimentTrigger` / `logSettingExperimentTrigger` (`src/vs/platform/telemetry/common/experimentTrigger.ts`) log `experimentTrigger { treatmentName }` at most once per window or process for each treatment. `treatmentName` is the ExP variable: `config.<setting id>` for experiment-controlled settings (via the new `getConfigurationExperimentName`, now also used by the configuration service), or the assignment-service treatment name.
- Each trigger is logged where the behavior is decided, under a condition that is computed identically in every experiment arm. Where only the treatment renders UI, the condition is evaluated as if it were enabled.

| Experiment | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `sessions.list.groupExternalSessions` | An external session that isn't pinned, done, or in a custom group is listed |
| `sessions.list.showUnreadInCollapsedSections` | A collapsed section header (any header, for screen-reader users) contains a session that needs input, is unread, or has a PR |
| `sessions.list.showArchivedByDefault` | No Done filter is chosen yet, and done content is listed, the Filter Sessions dropdown opens, or a session's context menu opens |
| `sessions.markAsDoneConfetti` | Mark as Done is clicked, except with reduced motion |
| `chat.agentSessions.archiveNudge.enabled` | The viewed session is idle with all its PRs merged, even if the nudge is off or dismissed |
| `chatSessionArchiveNudgeTitle` / `…Icon` | The nudge renders |
| `chat.experimental.openInAgentsWindow.transferDraft` | The Agents window opens from a new chat draft with content |
| `chat.agentsParallelWorkBanner.enabled` | The invitation would show, or would replace the empty-workspace handoff tip |
| `chatAgentsParallelWorkBannerTitle` / `…Description` | The invitation is shown |
| `chat.agentsHandoffTip.delaySeconds` | The handoff countdown starts |
| `chatAgentsHandoffTipTitle` / `…Description` | The tip is shown |
| `chat.agentHost.experimental.autoAttachPullRequests` | The agent host looks up a PR on a feature branch, or with PRs that restricted mode would drop; held until the assignment context arrives |

There is intentionally no trigger for `chat.agentMerge.enabled`, which changes agent tools and commands before any single visible moment, or for onboarding experiments, whose assignment context is already filtered out of telemetry until the tour would show.

Also adds an `experiments` skill that covers experiment-controlled settings, assignment-service treatments, and when and where to fire trigger events.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Archive nudge:** until a window has reported its trigger, eligibility and PR merged state are resolved even when the nudge is disabled or dismissed. Afterwards, disabled or dismissed nudges release their PR models again.
- **Draft handoff:** the chat widget is resolved before the transfer setting is checked.
- **New view items:** `SessionArchiveActionViewItem` for the Mark as Done button, and a Filter Sessions dropdown view item that reports when it opens.
- Experiments should start a new iteration once this ships, because earlier exposures have no trigger events.

## Validation

- Type check, ESLint, and layer checks report no new errors for the changed files.
- Unit tests for sessions, workbench chat, onboarding, telemetry, configuration, and agent host: 24,214 passing. New tests cover each trigger in every experiment arm.

pull_requests.title: Git: preserve FETCH_HEAD during automatic fetches
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #158309.

Background fetches can overwrite `FETCH_HEAD` while `git pull` is preparing its merge, causing `fatal: Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches.` Pass `--no-write-fetch-head` for silent/background fetches on Git 2.29 and newer. This covers both `git.autofetch: true` and `"all"`; manual fetches and the command used with older Git versions keep their existing behavior.

Adds five integration tests using local Git repositories to cover preservation of an existing `FETCH_HEAD`, an absent `FETCH_HEAD`, remote-tracking ref updates, manual fetching, and the compatibility fallback when Git reports version 2.28.

Validation on macOS ARM64 with Git 2.50.1:

- `npm run compile-client` and `npm run compile-copilot` passed.
- `node build/hygiene.ts extensions/git/src/git.ts extensions/git/src/test/fetch.test.ts` passed.
- `scripts/test-integration.sh --suite git`: 65 passed, 2 existing skipped tests. With the fix removed, the three new `FETCH_HEAD` protection tests fail; the other two pass.
- Launched Code OSS from this checkout with an isolated profile. For both autofetch settings, incoming commits appeared, the expected remote-tracking refs advanced, and `FETCH_HEAD` stayed byte-for-byte unchanged. Clicking the status-bar Sync action then successfully fast-forwarded the checkout.
- A local concurrent `git fetch` / `git pull --tags origin main` reproduction with `pull.ff=only` produced the reported error in 60/60 trials without the flag and 0/60 with it.

To verify manually, configure a local repository with `git.autofetch: true`, save its current `FETCH_HEAD`, and add a commit to its remote. Wait for the incoming change indicator, confirm that `FETCH_HEAD` is unchanged, and sync. Repeat with `git.autofetch: "all"` and a second remote.

## Summary

Adds a host-owned GitHub pull-request artifact integration, independently of Agent Merge, reusing the shared GitHub subscriptions, credentials, and mutations.

pull_requests.title: Webview: settle only a frame's own load fallback
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338084

The webview host keeps a frame's 200ms load fallback in `loadTimeout`, a variable shared by every frame, and each frame's `load` listener cleared whatever timer it held. When a frame shown by its fallback finished loading late, inside the next frame's window, it cleared the next frame's timer. That frame's own `load` then found nothing to settle, so it stayed `pending-frame` for good: the old content stayed on screen, and every message to the webview stayed queued.

Each frame now settles only its own timer. A frame's `load` listener and its fallback clear `loadTimeout` only while it still holds that frame's timer. Nothing else changes: whichever of a frame's own `load` and its fallback comes first still activates it, and the later one still does nothing.

The CSP hash for the inline script is updated to match the new script.

## How I tested

I drove this branch's `index.html` from an embedding page in Chromium, loading it from its `<parentOriginHash>.localhost` host with `disableServiceWorker`, using the sequence in #338084. Each page holds its own `load` with an open inner document until the test releases it. 5 runs of each scenario:

| Scenario | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| A's late `load` inside B's fallback window | 0 of 5: B stuck pending, message lost | 5 of 5: B active, message delivered |
| Control: A finishes loading before B is sent | 5 of 5 fine | 5 of 5 fine |

The page ran under its CSP with the new hash: the inline script executed and signaled `webview-ready`.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: harden sandbox connection and recovery
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Consolidates the sandbox reliability chain into one PR targeting `main`, avoiding repeated retargeting and CI runs between dependent PRs. There are six separate review commits: the connection-lifetime change, its provider-removal fix, and one commit for each of the four former dependent PRs, including their review fixes.

## Review by change

| Change | What it fixes | Original PR / commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connection lifetime and cancellation | Cancel address-owned attempts on removal, account changes, and disposal; clean up staged credentials; prevent late factory results or disconnect cleanup from affecting a replacement. Preserve concurrent-open coalescing. | Original scope of this PR: [`8ee94e5a06f`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/8ee94e5a06f30c3b11f1a80cc33deefab10a9ac6), with provider-removal fix [`3019094d951`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3019094d95122870d2cca314df0ed33b5133ee3e) |
| Admission and authentication recovery | Keep the first cached reconnect fast, share bounded credential renewal, and require a genuinely new sealed token for expired authentication. Preserve initial state if authentication is interrupted. | #338086 -> [`8d308a58394`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/8d308a583945a2472e7bdb43a862b395220f9ee2) |
| Deadlines and retry ownership | Bound attachment and recovery, use one automatic retry owner, honor server pacing, and prevent a late authentication resolver from overwriting a newer connection's credentials. | #338090 -> [`a35c4876953`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/a35c4876953cd598b9716f1d468e88379a87587e) |
| Connection diagnostics | Extend the existing scorecard with actual product-surface attribution, credential-request counts, phase timings, and the first post-readiness session request, without issuing probes. | #338092 -> [`2830df6a0d7`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/2830df6a0d72d5ac1f58334d67066029a7b7defd) |
| File watches and continuity | Restore file watches after logical reconnect, reject stale watch-setup results, and regression-test existing accepted-turn and lost-reply behavior without adding mutation replay. | #338093 -> [`1672b3e3dc4`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/1672b3e3dc492c09c55dba4622ac67df2a54a368) |

The original PRs retain their review discussions and are superseded by this combined PR. Startup client-identity handling in #338073 has merged into `main` and is included in this branch's base.

## Behavior and scope

- Shared browser-compatible services cover the desktop Agents Window, Editor existing-session connections, and `vscode.dev/agents`.
- Ordinary relay renewal retains its existing fallback, in-flight sharing, failure limits, permanent stops, and the 30-second authentication/repair floor. A relay-only credential update does not count as renewed authentication.
- Ten-minute attachment and five-minute automatic-recovery ceilings are safety bounds, not measured warm/cold latency targets. Existing task-creation/per-request timeouts and non-sandbox host defaults remain unchanged.
- No automatic replay of prompts, session creation, file writes, or other mutations. File-watch restoration does not recover every event missed during an outage.
- Diagnostics are supporting measurement, not a direct performance fix. They export bounded labels/numeric measurements, not credentials, identifiers, URLs, bodies, or error/detail text. Existing telemetry opt-out remains authoritative. Phase durations can overlap; created/existing caller context does not establish warm/cold compute.

## Validation

- The original consolidation exactly preserved the former cumulative PR tree; all 628 focused tests across twelve suites passed on that pre-main-update tree.
- Rebased onto `main` at `74c6c00f970f4f34a92e1ab83fb0f810974e1e1d` after #338073 merged. Conflict resolution preserves same-client credential polling together with retry pacing, cancellation, deadlines, and request diagnostics.
- All 161 focused service, API, credential-refresh, and remote-provider unit tests passed after the main integration, along with targeted TypeScript, ESLint, hygiene, and whitespace checks. The final linear rebase has exactly the same source tree as that tested integration.
- Regression tests reproduced provider cleanup, stale/reused authentication, late authentication resolution, and watch-restoration failures before their respective fixes.
- The new head requires fresh CI and team approval; earlier CI results and dismissed approvals are not substitutes.
- No local full product build, live sandbox/end-to-end validation, deployment, or measured production improvement is claimed.

## Merge strategy

Keep the per-change commits separate both during review and on `main`. Use **rebase and merge**, not squash, after required CI and team approvals pass. The four former dependent PRs remain one commit each, alongside the two connection-lifetime commits. The PR is ready for review with rebase auto-merge enabled, gated on fresh required CI and renewed team approval.

pull_requests.title: [4/4] authentication: enable multiple configured enterprise hosts
pull_requests.body:
## Review stack

**#338149 (merged) -> #338150 (merged) -> #338151 (merged) -> #338080 (multi-host enablement)**

This final layer targets `main`, building on the landed session-provenance API (#337846), distro enablement (#337882), provider lifecycle (#338150), and canonical credential storage (#338151). Part of #277435.

## Multi-host authentication

- Add unordered `github-enterprise.uris`, taking precedence over deprecated `github-enterprise.uri`, including explicit `[]`. No first-host default.
- Keep one `github-enterprise` provider and a separate public `github` provider. Return all eligible sessions, filtering scopes, account and issuer inside the provider/host engine.
- Preserve native session and account IDs. There are no host prefixes or ID-unwrapping transformations; `authorizationServer` remains the session's provenance.
- Construct session/account presentation in the host engine rather than rewriting every result/event in the facade. Enterprise account labels always use `username - host`, under the stable `GitHub Enterprise` provider label, even with one configured host. Ports and deployment paths remain visible when present.
- Keep account labels stable as other hosts are added or removed. There is no mutable suffix setter, cached relabeling pass, or host-count presentation flag. Native IDs and stored usernames remain unchanged.
- Resolve sign-in through explicit issuer/account hints, the sole host, or the extension-owned native picker. Preserve cancellation and platform preferences, permissions, silent/passive behavior and complete candidate lists.
- Remove a native session ID through cached ownership. In the rare case that the same session ID belongs to multiple hosts, report ambiguity instead of selecting an arbitrary host.

## Copilot enrollment

Copilot setup and onboarding accept **GHE.com instance names or HTTPS GHE.com URLs only**. General GitHub Enterprise authentication and configured-host validation still support GHES.

Invalid configured URI entries are prefilled for correction, one at a time, without replacing unrelated hosts. If only GHES is configured, Copilot enrollment prompts for a cloud instance and retains the existing server. Cancellation does not save the current prompt's proposed correction or start authentication.

The browser product-default fallback uses `github-enterprise.uri`, not an empty setting key. The prior Linux, macOS and Windows Browser CI failures were fixed and all three Browser jobs passed in run `36638660666`; that old run's remaining failure was unrelated WSL preparation/cleanup in Windows Electron-Smoke.

## Storage and compatibility

Canonical URI-derived credential storage comes from #338151: no storage-key registry or migration-completion flag. The temporary legacy migration remains marked for removal in 1.144, four releases after 1.140.

Legacy keys omitted the scheme. Ambiguous HTTP/HTTPS ownership requires an explicit original instance when migration is needed; already-authoritative canonical credentials are preserved. Native tokens and Microsoft account-link usernames remain intact.

The platform-wide structured-account identity migration remains deferred. This update may require one explicit account selection/consent for the new enterprise display labels. Adding or removing other hosts no longer changes an existing account's label. GitHub Pull Requests and GitHub Repositories should adopt session-derived routing before broad rollout.

## Latest validation

Rebased onto `origin/main` at `c46161fa184`, including the Microsoft sign-in probe from #338823. Current head: `a3f9a6f0af8`.

The onboarding conflict resolution preserves both the new Microsoft probe service/button behavior and trust-aware multi-host enrollment. The remaining commits replayed without conflicts; range-diff confirms no unrelated patch changes.

| Area | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Authentication extension, persistence and Microsoft broker/probe tests | **206 passing** |
| Core authentication RPC/selection, with native colliding account IDs | **66 passing** |
| Enrollment, parser, setup and onboarding in Chromium | **70 passing** |
| Enrollment, parser, setup and onboarding in WebKit | **70 passing** |
| Microsoft probe and external sign-in regressions | **23 passing in each of Chromium and WebKit** |

All counts are fresh runs after the rebase. Core and extension output was refreshed. Core and extension-browser type checks, scoped lint/hygiene and diff checks passed. Tests use fake services and isolated profiles, not user credentials. No fixture baselines, timeout thresholds, provider-level silent ambiguity policy, or test-only production APIs were added.

## Remaining validation

- [ ] Live sign-in/account switching across two real enterprise instances, including relevant brokered-account scenarios.
- [ ] Confirm downstream consumer releases are ready for rollout.

- Added a regression test to cover scenarios involving significant wall-clock jumps, such as an eight-hour hibernation.

### Validation
- The changes have been validated with a dependency-free timing probe, confirming that the new implementation behaves as expected.
- Full transpilation and tests could not be executed due to authentication issues with Azure Artifacts, but no dependency manifests were altered.

pull_requests.title: Keep customization migration inside the originating workspace folder
pull_requests.body:
## Description

In a multi-root workspace, migrating a prompt to a SKILL deleted the prompt from its own repo and wrote the skill into the first workspace folder. Migration targets were resolved only per `(target type, storage)`, and the default selection for workspace-local customizations was simply the first available source folder — which is always the first root.

### Changes

- **`customizationMigration.ts`**
  - `resolveClosestMigrationTargetFolder(customizationUri, targetFolder, availableFolders)`: picks the available folder sharing the most path segments with the source customization, preferring one with the same layout (e.g. `.github/skills`) as the selected destination so an explicit `.github` vs `.claude` choice survives the root correction.
  - `ICustomizationMigrationOptions.resolveTargetFolder(customization, targetType)`: optional per-customization override, consulted before the `(type, storage)` map, so a single migration run can write into several roots.
- **`aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts`**
  - `getEffectiveCustomizationMigrationTargetFolder()` applies the above to workspace-local customizations; folders chosen through "Choose another folder…" (not part of the discovered source folders) are used verbatim.
  - The confirmation dialog destination label is now computed from the effective per-file destinations instead of the type/storage map.

```
/workspace-a/.github/skills           <- selected target (first root)
/workspace-b/.github/prompts/review.prompt.md

before: /workspace-a/.github/skills/review/SKILL.md
after:  /workspace-b/.github/skills/review/SKILL.md
```

pull_requests.title: Fix manual slash invocation of Agent Skills with disable-model-invocation
pull_requests.body:
In the Agents window, an Agent Skill with `disable-model-invocation: true` shows up in the `/` completion menu, but manually invoking it via `/name` silently fails — no skill instructions load and the trailing text is treated as an ordinary prompt.

## Root cause

- `CopilotAgentSession._send` special-cased runtime slash commands of `kind === 'skill'` to skip `commands.invoke` and pass the raw prompt straight to `session.send`, relying on the model to notice the leading `/name` token and invoke the skill tool itself.
- `disable-model-invocation` is a client-parsed SKILL.md frontmatter flag (not part of the Copilot SDK's `Skill` RPC schema), and skills with this flag are intentionally excluded from the model's own skill catalog.
- Result: for those skills, passthrough silently does nothing — the model never learns the skill exists, and the `/name` text is just handled as an ordinary message.

## Fix

- Route skill-kind runtime slash commands through `commands.invoke`, the same host-directed path already used for builtin/client commands, instead of passing the prompt through as-is.
- This deterministically loads the skill (via the `agent-prompt` result) regardless of whether the model is allowed to invoke it autonomously.

```ts
// before
if (runtimeSlashCommand && runtimeSlashCommand.kind !== 'skill') { ... commands.invoke(...) ... }

// after
if (runtimeSlashCommand) { ... commands.invoke(...) ... }
```

## Tests

- Added a regression test in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` covering `/wait-what` invoking through `commands.invoke` and its `agent-prompt` result being sent as the turn's prompt.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #331477

pull_requests.title: editor: ignore stale multi-diff document resolutions
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #307899 (the stale-refresh corruption path described below).

## Summary

- Invalidate an asynchronous multi-diff document batch when its observable evaluation is replaced or disposed.
- Prevent an older SCM resource snapshot from publishing references that have already been released.
- Add deterministic regression tests for resource replacement, removal, and editor input disposal.

## Reproduction and scope

The original issue reports repeated file headers. Ordinary scrolling, collapse/expand, and Git refresh did **not** reproduce that literal symptom on current main.

A delayed SCM document provider did reproduce a related corruption path in Code OSS:

1. Open a multi-diff containing an existing resource.
2. Start a resource refresh containing that resource and a slow-resolving document.
3. Replace the resource list before the slow document finishes.
4. Let the obsolete refresh finish.

Before this fix, the obsolete batch republishes the removed resource, attempts to attach its disposed text models, reports `Model is disposed!`, and blanks the multi-diff. The same scenario passes with this fix. This PR targets that reproducible race; it does not claim that every historical repeated-header cause was reproduced.

## Validation

- The new replacement regression failed on the baseline: the published sequence incorrectly returned to `removed.ts` after `current.ts`, with a disposed-model error.
- All **21 targeted tests** pass across multi-diff input, SCM resolution, widget behavior, and template virtualization, including the three new regression cases.
- `npm run compile-client` completed with zero compilation errors; the remaining built-in Copilot extension was also built.
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check` pass.
- **11 Code OSS UI scenario steps pass** on Windows x64, Code OSS **1.140.0 Dev**:
  - Delayed document resolution, replacing the SCM resource list, completing the obsolete refresh, and scrolling the surviving diffs.
  - Built-in Git Open Changes, repeated scrolling, collapse/expand, staging/unstaging, keyboard change navigation and collapse, inline/side-by-side layouts, and closing/reopening the editor.
- Independent **GPT-6 Astra / max** and **Claude Opus 5.5 / max** reviews: no findings.

The large collapse/expand stress run also emits development listener-count warnings. The baseline and fixed builds emitted the same eight warnings with the same listener counts; those pre-existing warnings are outside this patch's scope.

## Baseline reproduction recording (before the fix)

Recorded in Windows x64 Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev at baseline `d912aa0ec55e578a95a65b39e7fd112d317dfdc6`, before the production fix. A test SCM provider deliberately holds one document resolution while newer changes replace the resource list. Releasing the obsolete refresh causes a `Model is disposed!` error and blanks the multi-diff; the failed final validation is expected in this before-fix recording.

This demonstrates the stale-refresh race addressed by this PR, **not the historical repeated-header symptom**. It is the original baseline recording, not a result from the ongoing independent investigation.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4fac7fd-8e31-43e5-b6d6-002aa7c613cd

## Fixed-version recording

The captioned recording below shows the delayed-SCM reproduction with the fix.

pull_requests.title: browser: reconcile popup state missed before the renderer subscribes
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

`Integrated Browser › preserves native page lifecycle across editors, popups, and restart` fails intermittently on Linux and macOS ([run 36120855518, job 108025747044](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36120855518/job/108025747044)):

```
locator.waitFor: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for locator('.tab').filter({ hasText: 'Browser Smoke Popup Child' }) to be visible
```

In the failure screenshot the popup page has rendered, but its tab still shows the host name (`127.0.0.1:41045`), which is the fallback label used when the model has no title.

## Root cause

This is the race described in #335987:

1. When a page opens a popup, the main process creates the child view and starts loading it immediately.
2. The renderer builds its `BrowserViewModel` from a state snapshot taken when the view was created, and only then subscribes to the view's dynamic IPC events.
3. Events fired before the subscription reaches main are lost. A fast page can commit and set its title in that gap, so the model keeps an empty title.

It happened in 4 Electron-Smoke jobs in the last ~15h of PR runs, 2 on Linux and 2 on macOS: 108025747044, 107951348615, 107885059240 and 108087350213.

## Fix

This PR takes the popup-reconciliation part of #335987, without its favicon-loader changes (those are in #336077) and without its per-event version numbers.

- **Platform:** a new `getNavigationState(id)` returns a lightweight `IBrowserViewNavigationState`: URL, title, back/forward, loading, favicon and errors. `IBrowserViewState` extends it. No screenshots or session data go over IPC.
- **Renderer model:** navigation, loading, title and favicon events are relayed through the model's own emitters, so the model's state is updated before consumers see an event. After subscribing, the model reads the navigation state once and applies only what changed. A snapshot that changes only the title fires a title event, not a navigation.
- **Seeded state:** URL, title and favicon from the snapshot are applied only once a navigation has committed. Until then the model keeps what it was seeded with: the requested URL, or a restored editor's title and favicon.

**Why no versions are needed:** the events and `getNavigationState` use the same ordered main-process channel. `ChannelServer` subscribes as soon as each `listen` request arrives and forwards events as they fire. It builds the snapshot synchronously and sends the reply on the microtask queue, so no Electron event can run in between. Any event the model received was therefore fired before the snapshot, and is already reflected in it. Anything fired later arrives after the reply.

#336077 is stacked on this PR. It scopes main's favicon state to the current page, so the favicon replayed here is the current page's too.

## Validation

- **Unit test:** a new test covers a popup that loaded before subscribing, a restored page that hasn't navigated yet, and a live event that arrived before the snapshot and isn't repeated. All 180 tests under `**/browserView/**` pass.
- **Smoke test:** the `Integrated Browser` suite passes 7/7, three times in a row.
- **Delay experiment:** I added a temporary 2s delay before the renderer creates the model for a new view. Without the fix, the test fails with the CI error. With the fix, the whole suite passes.
- **Static checks:** `npm run typecheck-client`, eslint and `build/hygiene.ts` pass on the changed files.

When this test runs alone (`-g "preserves native page lifecycle"`), its `afterEach` times out waiting for the restored page to close. That also happens on `origin/main`, so it isn't related to this change. The full suite, as CI runs it, passes.

pull_requests.title: test: retry transient WSL2 import failures in Windows smoke setup
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

`Windows / Electron-Smoke` fails before any smoke test runs, in **Prepare WSL Dev Container smoke tests** ([run 36120855518, job 108025747515](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36120855518/job/108025747515)):

```
Import exit code: -1
Import output:
The virtual machine or container with the specified identifier is not running.
...
Explicit WSL2 import failed with exit code -1. WSL1 is not supported by this test.
```

## Root cause

This is a transient failure of the inbox WSL on the hosted Windows Server 2022 image (`wsl.exe 10.0.20348`, kernel 5.10.16). It is not caused by a code change. The diagnostics added in #337242/#337438 show the sequence:

- The WSL2 kernel MSI installs with exit code 0.
- `Microsoft-Windows-Hyper-V-Worker-Admin` logs the WSL utility VM as `started successfully` at 09:59:56 and `connected to virtual network` at 09:59:59.
- In the same second it logs `'Virtual Machine' was shut down by the guest operating system`.
- `wsl --import` then returns `-1` with the HCS error above.
- No distribution or files are left behind. LxssManager, vmcompute and hns are running, both optional features are enabled, and no reboot is pending.

So the machine is set up correctly; the first utility-VM boot just died. The PR that surfaced this (#337895) only touches chat code.

## Frequency

These counts come from the last 400 runs of `pr.yml` (about 15 hours; 222 Windows Electron-Smoke jobs that completed as success or failure). 9 of those jobs failed in the WSL setup step:

| Failure mode | Jobs |
|---|---|
| `wsl --import` exit -1, `The virtual machine or container ... is not running.` | 3 (108025747515, 108029388564, 108027000353) |
| `wsl --import` exit -1, `0x80041001` | 1 (108008742001) |
| step timed out after 15 min while importing | 1 (107934540288) |
| Docker/apt crashed inside the distro (containerd panic, apt segfault) | 2 |
| `curl: (18)` partial download of the pinned server | 2 |

This PR targets the first two rows: the import fails fast with -1, which accounts for about 1.8% of Windows smoke jobs. The same class of failure was earlier reported with `The interface is unknown` (#337242).

## Fix

- Retry `wsl --import` up to 3 times.
- After each failed attempt, keep writing the full diagnostics. They now go to `import-<distro>-attempt-<n>.log`, so the logs artifact shows whether a retry on the same host helps.
- Before retrying, reset the host: `wsl --unregister` any partial distro, run `wsl --shutdown` so the next attempt boots a fresh utility VM, recreate the empty install directory, and back off 10s then 20s.
- If the third attempt fails, throw the same error as before.

`wsl --shutdown` stops every distro on the host. That is safe here because CI agents are dedicated to the job and the distro is created by this script. The script is shared by GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines, so both get the retry. The step normally takes about 80s and has a 15-minute timeout, so there is room for the retries.

Not addressed here, since they are different failure modes:
- **Import hangs:** the import can still hang until the step times out.
- **Crashes inside the distro:** the containerd panic and apt segfault happen after import.
- **`curl: (18)` partial downloads:** curl's `--retry` does not retry exit code 18 unless `--retry-all-errors` is passed.

## Validation

- The PowerShell parser reports no errors.
- I extracted the import loop and the diagnostics functions and ran them against a fake `wsl.cmd` that fails the import N times. With 0 failures it imports on attempt 1. With 2 failures it retries twice (unregister, shutdown, 10s then 20s backoff) and succeeds on attempt 3. With 3 failures it throws after 3 attempts. Each failed attempt writes its own diagnostics log.
- I did not run a real WSL import locally, because it would change the host's WSL state. This PR's Windows Electron-Smoke job covers the success path on a hosted agent.

pull_requests.title: sessions: add worktree cleanup flow
pull_requests.body: Fixes #338039 ## Summary - add the opt-in `sessions.chat.experimental.worktreeLimitPrompt` setting, disabled by default and configured with automatic experiment metadata - check once after startup and show a cleanup dialog when there are at least 20 unique, non-archived session worktrees and at least one recommended cleanup candidate - persist a seven-day cooldown as soon as the automatic dialog is shown, preventing repeated prompts across window reloads - add **Agents: Clean Up Session Worktrees...** so users can review cleanup manually at any time - measure Agent Host worktrees and show estimated reclaimable storage without delaying the manual picker - show additional recent and pinned candidates in the picker with an explanation, without selecting them automatically ## Candidate model The unique-worktree threshold counts all non-archived session worktrees, including active, running, recent, and pinned sessions because they still occupy capacity. Shared worktree URIs count once. A session is available in the cleanup picker only when it: - has a worktree; - is completed and not archived; - is not the active session; and - exclusively owns every worktree it references among non-archived sessions. Available sessions are then classified as: - **Recommended:** unpinned and last updated at least 14 days ago. These are selected by default. - **Recent:** updated within 14 days. These are visible but not selected automatically. - **Pinned:** pinned by the user. These are visible but not selected automatically. Each picker row explains its classification. This keeps automatic cleanup conservative while allowing an intentional manual cleanup to include more completed sessions. Active, running, archived, and shared-worktree sessions are never offered. ## Automatic startup prompt The contribution performs one delayed check after startup. It prompts only when: 1. `sessions.chat.experimental.worktreeLimitPrompt` is enabled. 2. No automatic cleanup prompt has been shown in the previous seven days. 3. There are at least 20 unique non-archived worktrees. 4. At least one recommended candidate exists. The cooldown is recorded when the dialog is shown, regardless of whether the user reviews candidates, dismisses it, or completes cleanup. Session catalog changes, configuration changes, and cooldown expiry do not independently open another dialog in the running window; the next automatic check happens on a later startup. The initial estimate covers the recommended candidates. ## Manual command and cleanup flow - **Agents: Clean Up Session Worktrees...** bypasses the count threshold and automatic-prompt cooldown while retaining all safety rules. - If no safe candidates exist, the command explains why instead of silently doing nothing. - Worktrees are measured through an optional provider capability with bounded concurrency. The manual picker opens before measurement and only selected sessions are measured. - Complete measurements are described as “about”; partial measurements are described as “at least”; unavailable measurements are omitted. - The picker groups shared guidance under Recommended and Additional headings, shows concise per-session differences, and updates Calculating… placeholders with measured sizes in place. The final confirmation reports the selected total. - The final confirmation reports the estimate for the selected sessions. - Archive success announcements count only sessions whose archived state actually changed; partial and total failures are reported explicitly. ## Validation - `npm run compile` - `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorktreeLimitContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/worktreeDiskUsage.test.ts` (15 tests) - `npx eslint src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/sessionWorktreeLimitContribution.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorktreeLimitContribution.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/chat.contribution.ts`

pull_requests.title: fix: absorb browser horizontal reveal into editor scroll
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #336539

## Problem

With the secondary side bar open, a side-by-side diff of a long line would not scroll horizontally. End and the arrow keys left the rest of the line and the cursor out of view. Closing the side bar made the pane wider, so it was easier to miss, but the same path is what actually breaks.

Pressing End asks the browser to reveal the editor textarea. The browser sets `scrollLeft` on `.monaco-scrollable-element.editor-scrollable`. That node's scroll listener already folds a surprise `scrollTop` back into the editor, but it ignored `scrollLeft`. Monaco's scrollbar stayed at 0 while the text jumped.

## Fix

Treat horizontal movement on that scrollable the same way vertical movement is already treated: add the delta to the editor `scrollLeft` and clear the native value. The view node already did this. The lines-content and overflow-guard listeners are unchanged, because those nodes were not the ones receiving `scrollLeft`.

## Tests

pull_requests.body:
Refs #337602

Explicit Responses API prompt caching (#336967) is on by default for gpt-5.6 and gpt-6. For client-side BYOK endpoints, requests go to gateways such as LiteLLM. These can forward `prompt_cache_options: { mode: 'explicit' }` but drop the per-part `prompt_cache_breakpoint` markers, which results in 0% cache hits.

- Adds tests in `responsesApi.spec.ts` and `openAIEndpoint.spec.ts`.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: refresh expired sandbox credentials before reconnect
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Refresh expired sandbox relay credentials before constructing a replacement transport. Previously, reconnect rebuilt the relay using cached credentials, while the background refresher was only created after the first successful connection. Recovery could therefore retry with credentials already known to be expired.

- Add an optional protocol-client preparation callback and await it before rebuilding the transport, including retries during initial establishment.
- Own the sandbox credential refresher for the connection lifetime and share in-flight work between recovery and background refresh.
- Keep still-valid credentials on the fast path: no extra refresh request or wait for an unrelated background refresh.
- Preserve existing refresh backoff, permanent-error handling, and failure limits. Cancel recovery waits on disposal and ignore late results.
- Cover callback ordering, initial-establishment retries, failure and disposal, sandbox factory wiring, expiry handling, shared refreshes, and retry bounds.

## Scope

The first socket dial remains unchanged. This does not add recovery for still-valid but unusable admission tickets or host-lane failures, and does not change the wire protocol. No production performance improvement is claimed from unit tests alone.

Builds on the merged credential guards in #337836 and #337851.

## Validation

Rebased onto current `main` and reran the focused checks:

- Focused TypeScript compilation of the affected tests and dependencies: passed.
- 97 focused unit tests: passed, including the merged host-credential consistency tests.
- ESLint for all six changed files: passed.
- Commit hygiene and whitespace checks: passed.
- No full product build, workbench launch, live sandbox test, or end-to-end test was run.

Unit-test selection:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxCredentialRefresh.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.test.ts \
  --grep 'soft reconnect|CloudSandboxCredentialRefresher|credentialRefreshDelayMs|CloudSandboxAgentHostService|Errors|Tests are using suiteSetup'
```

auto_merge.commit_message:
* agentHost: refresh expired sandbox credentials before reconnect

Refresh expired or unusable relay credentials before constructing a replacement transport. Share in-flight refreshes with the background timer while preserving valid-ticket reuse, bounded retries, and cancellation on disposal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: preserve sandbox refresh limits across client redials

Retain refresh failure counts, permanent-stop state, and absolute retry deadlines on the staged logical sandbox connection. Keep timers and in-flight requests owned by each protocol client so replacing a client still cancels its work without resetting the refresh budget.

## Summary

Agent Merge turns blocked MCP in general, not just GitHub. #333872 enforced "use only the Agent Merge GitHub tools" by treating every external MCP server as a GitHub fallback:

- **Copilot** denied tools from every registered server (root config, workspace `.mcp.json`, and plugins).
- **Claude** denied every `mcp__*` tool except the host server tools, including the workbench client tools (`mcp__client__*`).
- **Codex** dropped all configured MCP servers from the thread.

Unrelated local servers such as Component Explorer were therefore rejected with a GitHub-specific denial, and the agent stopped the turn.

## Changes

- Add `isAgentMergeRestrictedMcpServer`, which identifies a GitHub MCP server by its name, a GitHub-hosted endpoint (`github.com`, `githubcopilot.com`, `ghe.com`), or a command that runs `github-mcp-server` or `@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`.
- Copilot and Claude now deny tools only from those servers and the built-in `github-mcp-server`. Codex omits only those servers during Agent Merge turns.
- The GitHub CLI, direct GitHub API, and GitHub tool-name restrictions are unchanged.

## Notes for reviewers

- The Copilot and Claude pre-tool hooks receive only a tool name. Servers the SDK loads without the host seeing their configuration (for example Claude user-level config) are therefore matched by name only.
- Non-GitHub MCP servers are usable again during Agent Merge turns, including a custom server that could itself reach GitHub. The Agent Merge prompt still requires the dedicated tools for CI details, review threads, and workflow reruns.

## Validation

- Added tests for the shared classifier and for each provider. The provider tests fail against the previous implementation.
- The related agent host unit suites pass (1370 tests), and eslint and hygiene are clean on the changed files.

## Description

Clicking "Don't Show Again" on the customization migration hint took effect (no hint on the next message), but gave no visible confirmation — the hint stayed in the transcript with its links still clickable, making it unclear the action worked.

```ts
response?.updateContent({
	kind: 'systemNotification',
	id: options.notificationId,
	content: new MarkdownString(localize('customizationMigrationHint.dismissed', "Customization migration hints are hidden for this workspace.")),
	icon: Codicon.info,
}, true);
```

pull_requests.title: sessions: Fix Stop and Mark as Done while a new session is being created
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337984

## The problem

When you send the first message of a new session, the session isn't ready right away. The agent host sets it up first, which takes a few seconds with worktree isolation. During those seconds:

- **Stop** left the session at "Working…" forever, until you reloaded the window.
- **Mark as Done** did nothing.

The window only has a draft of the session until the host tells it about the real session. The host did that only after the agent received the first message.

## What this fixes

### Stop

If the first message is stopped before the agent gets it, the host now tells the window about the session anyway. The session shows up as a normal, idle session with the stopped message, instead of spinning forever.

The host also includes the worktree it just created, so your next message runs in that worktree, not in your main folder. Without this, the next message would have run in the original folder, because the worktree is no longer marked as pending once it exists.

### Mark as Done

If you mark a new session as done before the host has told the window about it:

- The draft is marked as done right away, so it moves to Done immediately.
- The real session is marked as done as soon as it arrives.
- If that step fails (for example the Dev Container worktree step in the remote provider), the error is logged. Before, a failure there would have thrown away a session that had already been created.

The remote and cloud sandbox providers get the same handling.

## Tests

New regression tests:

- `agentSideEffects.test.ts`: a first message stopped during working-directory resolution announces the session, doesn't send the message to the agent, and doesn't mark creation as failed.
- `agentService.test.ts`: the announced session has the worktree, project and branch, and the next message runs in the worktree.
- `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`:
  - marking as done before the host announces the session archives the draft, then the real session;
  - an unarchive after the host announced the session but before commit isn't undone at commit.
- `remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`: a failing Dev Container archive at commit doesn't break the new session.

## Known limitations

- The session still shows "Working…" until the worktree is ready, then it becomes idle.
- If Stop is clicked before the window has even sent the message to the host, the session can still stay at "Working…". This window is usually very short, but it includes the workspace-trust prompt, and declining trust has the same effect.
- A session whose first message was stopped can disappear after the agent host restarts, just like sessions whose creation failed.

pull_requests.title: session: Improve reference popup placement consistency
pull_requests.body:
Short reference collections could open below the input pills and immediately show a wide detail card over the list and its actions. This change makes collections prefer above and keeps secondary details beside their row where space allows, using shared ActionWidget behavior rather than feature-specific positioning CSS.

## Changes

- **Consistent collection placement:** add optional `preferredAnchorPosition` to `IActionListOptions` and `IChatDropdownPillOptions`. Chat-input PR, Issue, Reference, Artifact, Customization, Browser, and Subagent collections prefer `ABOVE`, with fallback when space is insufficient. The existing forced `anchorPosition` takes precedence; unrelated dropdown defaults are unchanged.
- **Reveal details on intent:** the initially highlighted row no longer opens a detail card. Pointer movement uses the existing hover delay; deliberate keyboard navigation, Tab, and ArrowRight can reveal details. Row actions and persistent model-picker previews retain their existing behavior.
- **Responsive, row-relative details:** secondary previews use right/left space and can narrow to a readable width before resorting to overlap. Oversized content scrolls, and content growth/collapse recomputes placement without losing keyboard focus.

## Before / after

Matched **headless component** captures: dark theme, three PRs, first row selected, identical 720x800 viewport and trigger position, with the same crop. The before rendering loads the unmodified shared ActionList from base `d0a02edd39b`; the after rendering uses this PR at `c0c074666db`. These are controlled component comparisons, not native-window screenshots.

### Opening the collection

| Opens below; the initial highlight immediately reveals a card that obscures the collection. | Opens above; the initial highlight stays quiet and all rows/actions remain visible. |
| ![Before: collection opens below with an automatic overlapping preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6777f6b9-2a34-4194-aca3-5f4b856fa274) | ![After: collection opens above without an automatic preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5e6a2f4-32a3-48a9-978f-9312ef3e4a7b) |

### Deliberately entering the first item's details with ArrowRight

| --- | --- |
| The full-width card overlaps the rows even though usable space exists to the left. | The card narrows into that space, stays aligned with its row, and leaves the list and Copy action visible. |
| ![Before: keyboard-invoked detail card overlaps the collection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97ffef33-be3c-49f5-b229-c2b995566049) | ![After: keyboard-invoked detail card fits beside its row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb105f03-ee4c-425d-b478-051fce8fc19b) |

<details>
<summary>Native Code OSS context: short PR collection</summary>

Dark theme, 968x859 native window, second PR selected. The collection is above the input pills and the card sits to its left; Copy and Remove remain visible. This is an in-context after view, not a matched native before/after pair.

![Native Code OSS: second PR details beside an above-opening collection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b8dbf26-8b77-4c8b-bd06-0e7d2b43bf37)

</details>

The component theme sweep is available in [Screenshots & Tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36155006807/job/108143573933).

## Testing

1. In an existing **local** Copilot session, prepare a short collection of three PRs/issues and mixed References. Open each collection: it should prefer above and remain quiet until intentional interaction.
2. Move over a row and wait for the hover delay, then exercise Arrow keys, Tab/Shift+Tab, ArrowRight, and Escape. Verify detail links and Copy/Remove remain reachable and dismissal restores focus.
3. Narrow the window so only a reduced-width card fits to one side. Verify row-relative placement and readable reflow. Also check a trigger near the top, where the collection should fall back below, and an extremely narrow window where overlap is unavoidable.
4. Repeat with long PR/Issue, References, and Artifacts collections. Navigate to lower rows, scroll into and out of details, and expand/collapse a long title by focusing its link. Verify viewport containment, row alignment, and retained focus.

Local validation passed for placement, reveal timing, keyboard traversal, scrolling, content resizing, and existing persistent-preview behavior. Client transpilation/type checking, targeted lint, and ActionWidget/chat-pill/hover tests passed; the resize correction was additionally verified with grow/overflow/shrink regressions and a headless rich-card reproduction. Four local Copilot scenarios were exercised in native Code OSS.

**Limits:** overlap remains possible when neither side meets the readable-width floor. VoiceOver announcements and physical macOS Split View transitions still need manual validation.

pull_requests.title: Keep picker changes made while a new session is starting
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337981

In the Agents window, if you changed a picker right after sending the first message of a new session, the change was lost once the session finished starting. This affected the permission level, mode, sandbox, model and agent pickers. With this fix, the session keeps what you picked.

## What the fix does

While a new session is starting, picker changes only update a local draft. The fix passes the draft's latest picks on to the session once it is ready:

- **Model and agent:** the session now gets the draft's latest model (including its model settings) and agent, instead of the ones from before the first message. Both are sent with every message, so follow-up messages use them. If you switch back to the default agent while waiting, that is kept too.
- **Permission level, mode, sandbox and other session settings:** the fix compares the draft's settings with the ones sent with the first message. It then sends the agent host one update containing only the settings that changed and that a running session is allowed to change.

These settings are sent once the session is ready, not right away. Just after the first message goes out, the original settings are sent to the host again, and that would overwrite an earlier update.

The code that sends a settings update to a running session is now a small shared helper, `_dispatchRunningSessionConfig`, used by both the existing picker path and this one.

## Tests

Four new tests in `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` change a picker while a new session is starting, then check that the session and follow-up messages use the new value:
- the permission level;
- the model and its settings;
- the custom agent;
- switching back to the default agent.

All four fail without the fix. The local and remote Agent Host provider test suites pass.

## Not included

Other actions taken while a new session is starting (rename, mark unread, delete, archive, stop, Agent Merge, sending a second message) fail for related reasons, but need separate fixes.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: discover a peer chat's pull request in its own folder
pull_requests.body:
When a peer chat works in its own worktree and creates a pull request outside the Agents Window's Create PR operation (for example with `gh pr create`), the pull request showed on the session's main chat instead of on the peer chat.

## Why

At turn end the host looks up the pull request of the current branch. `GitHubReferencesContribution` passed the owning session (`turn.session`) for every turn, so a peer chat's turn only looked up the session folder's branch. The peer worktree's folder was never looked up, so its GitHub state never got the pull request. The client only knew about it from the recorded artifact, and recorded artifacts carry no folder, so they attach to the session folder.

The other lookup triggers don't cover this case:
- Session restore looks up the session folder only.
- A peer chat's Git refresh looks up its folder only when the branch changes.
- Agent Merge looks up per folder, but only while it is on.
- The Create PR operation records the pull request on its folder directly, but `gh` bypasses it.

## Change

A turn that ends in a peer chat whose folder isn't the session folder now looks up that chat's folder, which runs the existing per-folder lookup (`_attachFolderGitHubPullRequest`). The default chat, peer chats in the session folder, and sessions without a folder keep looking up the session folder. Once the peer folder has the pull request, the client already moves the recorded artifact from the session folder to that folder, so no client change is needed.

## Notes for reviewers

- Session restore still looks up only the session folder, so an existing session's pull request moves to the peer chat after that chat's next turn, not on restart. That could be a follow-up.
- Test: `chatContributions.test.ts` covers turn ends from the session, the default chat, a peer chat in the session folder, and a peer chat in its own folder. Without the fix it fails on the last case.
- Validated with `typecheck-client`, the Agent Host node tests (8,303 passing), the sessions unit tests (4,794 passing), and eslint.

pull_requests.title: Agents - keep chat git state when the git probe fails
pull_requests.body:
Sessions could suddenly lose their Git-backed changesets (Branch, Uncommitted, Compare) mid-session, leaving only Session Changes and This Turn until a later Git refresh succeeded.

## Cause

Since #331792, `_computeSessionGitState` returns `undefined` when `git status` fails or times out (5 s default), with the contract that callers keep the last known state. The session-keyed refresh honors that. When changesets moved to chats (#337263, #337594), the chat-keyed refresh started clearing the chat's Git state on `undefined`. The default chat writes through to the session's persisted Git state, so one transient probe failure during a turn also wiped the session's Git state. `buildDefaultChangesetCatalog` then published a Git-less catalogue.

No Git service change makes `git status` fail more often; what changed is how a failure is handled.

## Fix

Keep the last known Git state when the Git probe returns nothing, matching the session-keyed behavior. Explicit clears (no resolvable working directory, chat removal) are unchanged.

## Validation

- Updated the peer-chat folder-scope test to expect retained state after a failed probe.
- Added a default-chat regression test.
- All agentHost node tests pass.
