pull_requests.title: agentHost: mark external sessions in ~/.copilot/chats as workspace-less
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

Sessions that the GitHub Copilot app creates without a workspace run in a folder under `~/.copilot/chats`, nested by date (e.g. `~/.copilot/chats/2026-09-23/congenial-happiness-c052778d`). When Agent Host discovered these as external sessions, it reported that folder as a regular working directory without the workspace-less marker. The Agents window therefore showed the internal chats folder as the session's workspace instead of treating the session as a workspace-less (quick) chat.

## Changes

- **Copilot discovery and `getChatMetadata`** mark a chat workspace-less when its working directory is inside `~/.copilot/chats` (case-insensitive on Windows and macOS). `getChatMetadata` does this only when the host has not recorded its own `agentHost.workspaceless` marker, so host-created sessions keep their persisted value. Covering `getChatMetadata` keeps the marker when the session is restored or its catalog entry is rebuilt.
- **`workspacelessChatsRoot`** defines the `~/.copilot/chats` path in one place; `workspacelessScratchDir` builds on it.
- **Catalog resolver** no longer persists the `agentHost.workspaceless` marker for external sessions. That marker also identifies host-created sessions (`_readSessionRegistrationFacts`), so persisting it made a pruned-then-rediscovered external session register as internal. `_buildImportedCatalogSyncRequest` now passes the external flag so the resolver can tell.

## Notes for reviewers

- Detection is one path comparison per chat, with no extra file-system, database, or Git access.
- Like `workspacelessScratchDir`, detection uses `~/.copilot/chats` and ignores `COPILOT_HOME`.
- External sessions discovered before this change get the marker when they are next opened or their catalog entry is rebuilt.
- No Agents window changes: it already hides the workspace for sessions marked workspace-less.

## Tests

- `copilotAgent.test.ts`: discovery marks a `github/autopilot` chat under the chats folder as workspace-less but not a chat in a regular folder; `getChatMetadata` infers the marker only when the host recorded none.
- `agentService.test.ts`: a workspace-less external session stays external after it is pruned and rediscovered, and the host marker is not persisted.

pull_requests.title: Terminal: Sanitize trailing/leading newlines when mutating environment variables
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337937

### Summary
When extensions contribute to environment variables (such as `PATH`) using `EnvironmentVariableMutatorType.Append` or `Prepend`, the existing environment variable value is concatenated directly via string addition (`+`).

If the existing environment variable happens to have a trailing carriage return (`\r`) or newline (`\n`)—which can happen via manual environment variable configuration, batch files, or external tools/installers—appending an extension path produces a string with an embedded `\r`. 

On Windows integrated terminals:
1. Printing `$env:Path` causes the cursor to return to the beginning of the line upon hitting `\r`, overwriting earlier characters with the appended path and visually truncating the line.
2. The path entry containing the trailing `\r` becomes an invalid filesystem path on Windows, breaking command resolution.

### Proposed Changes
- In `MergedEnvironmentVariableCollection.applyToProcessEnvironment`:
  - `EnvironmentVariableMutatorType.Append`: Trim trailing `[\r\n]+$` from `env[actualVariable]` before appending.
  - `EnvironmentVariableMutatorType.Prepend`: Trim leading `^[\r\n]+` from `env[actualVariable]` before prepending.
- Restricted the sanitization strictly to `[\r\n]` so that full-width Unicode characters (e.g., Japanese directory paths with full-width spaces `\u3000`) and standard spaces/symbols remain completely intact.
- Added comprehensive unit test cases to `environmentVariableCollection.test.ts` covering CR/LF sanitization and full-width multi-byte paths.

### Verification Done
- Verified with unit tests covering trailing `\r`, `\r\n`, `\n`, multiple newlines, and Japanese characters with ideographic spaces.
- Verified that trailing newlines are safely stripped while paths and full-width spaces remain intact.

pull_requests.body:

  - `sessions`, with chats, status, pins and CI state
  - custom `groups`
  - `view`: grouping, sorting, compact or phone layout, and which rows are collapsed or expanded

  - `settings`

- **Hover without a pointer** — `DefaultStyleController` and `sessionsList.css` pair every row `:hover` rule with a `.hovered` class, using `:is(:hover, .hovered)` to keep specificity. Hover-only actions and backgrounds now render in fixtures. `sessionsList.css` documents the convention.

pull_requests.title: sessions: rebind agent feedback to the provider's current connection
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

On a remote agent host (dev tunnel), a feedback comment submitted via **Submit Feedback** was not visible to the agent: `listComments` and `viewUnreviewedComments` returned `[]` even though the turn attachment referenced the comment id.

From the server-side AHP wire logs and the client window log:

- The agents window reconnected to the tunnel host as a **new client** (fresh `initialize`, new client id), so the remote provider's `IAgentConnection` was replaced via `setConnection`.
- `AnnotationsAgentFeedbackItemsBackend` caches one channel per session and kept returning the one bound to the **old, closed** connection.
- The comment was added to the local cache (so it rendered in the editor) and dispatched on the dead connection, where `_sendNotificationMessage` silently drops it. The new connection never subscribed to `<session>/annotations`, and the server never received an `annotations/set`.

## Fix

`_ensureChannel` now remembers the provider/session it resolved the channel from and, on reuse, checks that the provider still reports the same connection. If the connection changed, the stale channel is released and re-subscribed on the current connection. If the provider has no connection (offline), the existing channel is kept so cached comments stay visible.

The check is a cheap provider cache lookup; it deliberately avoids `ISessionsManagementService.getSession` (linear scan) on the hot path. After a rebind, the new subscription's first snapshot fires the existing "loaded" change event, so consumers (editor comments, PR review seeder) refresh on their own.

## Notes for reviewers

- Comments that were already dropped on a dead connection are not replayed; the server stays the source of truth.
- The rebind happens lazily on the next read/write (every feedback access goes through `_ensureChannel`), since the provider has no public connection-change event.

## Testing

- Added `moves to the provider's new connection after a reconnect` to `agentFeedbackItemsBackend.test.ts` (fails without the fix).
- `agentFeedbackItemsBackend`, `agentFeedbackService` and `agentFeedbackPRReviewSeeder` suites pass (71 tests).

pull_requests.title: chat: Keep incremental rendering stable when inline references stream in
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #336883

## Problem

With incremental rendering enabled, every inline file reference that streams into the main response replays the entrance animation for the whole response.

`ChatMarkdownContentPart.tryIncrementalUpdate` rejected any update whose `inlineReferences` differed from the previous one. A streamed reference appends `[label](http://_vscodecontentref_/N)` to the markdown and adds key `N` to `inlineReferences`. That failed the equality check, so the renderer disposed the part and created a new one. The new part seeds the morpher with `animateInitial: true`, which re-animates every block.

## Fix

Accept the update when the new `inlineReferences` keeps every existing entry unchanged and only adds entries. A changed existing entry, such as a reference resolving to a symbol, still forces a full re-render. The morpher's render callback reads the updated `this.markdown`, so appended references resolve in place.

## How to test

1. Set:
   - `chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.enabled`: `true`
   - `chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.animationStyle`: `blur`
   - `chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.buffering`: `off`
2. Open a workspace and ask for a response that mentions existing workspace files (for example `` `src/example.ts` ``) and keeps streaming after each one.
3. Before: earlier paragraphs animate again each time a reference appears. After: only new content animates.

I checked this with the chat simulation mock server driving the in-repo Copilot extension. The response streamed two existing file paths; the control run named missing files so they stayed plain text.

| Run | Markdown parts created | Earlier paragraph animated again |
|---|---|---|
| Before, with references | 3 (one per reference) | Yes, when each reference arrived |
| Before, control | 1 | No |
| After, with references | 1 | No; animation counts match the control |

Both reference widgets still render after the fix. The existing tests in `chatMarkdownContentPart.test.ts`, `chatListRenderer.test.ts`, and `annotations.test.ts` pass.

pull_requests.title: sessions: leave peer-discovered recorded pull requests to their folder
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #337694. In a multi-folder Agents Window session, a pull request created with the Create PR button from a peer chat on its own worktree showed on the session row and on every session-folder chat.

## Cause

Create PR saves the new pull request in two places: the session's recorded artifacts, which carry no folder, and the GitHub state of the folder it was created from. #337694 promotes every recorded pull request of the repository into the session folder's GitHub info. So a peer worktree's pull request also counted as a session-folder pull request. An open pull request's icon outranks merged ones, so the session row and the session-folder chats showed it.

## Change

In `toGitHubInfo`, the session folder skips a recorded pull request that another folder discovered for its own working directory (`githubData`), unless the session folder discovered it too.
- Recorded pull requests that no folder discovered still go to the session folder, as with #337694.
- Folders other than the session folder are unchanged: they report only their own discovered pull requests.
- The lookup reads `githubData` directly rather than the host-published working-directory keys, which list metadata can lack.

## For reviewers

- A pull request that a peer chat's agent records with `add_artifact_or_reference` isn't discovered for the peer's folder, so it still goes to the session folder. Placing it correctly would require recording the folder on the artifact, which this change deliberately avoids.

pull_requests.title: test: fix Codex sandbox fixtures on Azure macOS
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337861.

The Codex Sandbox tests create their fixtures under `os.tmpdir()`. On Azure macOS that resolves to shared system temp, which Codex intentionally permits command processes to read and write. The tests therefore put their supposedly protected files inside an allowed area.

Use `AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY`, then `RUNNER_TEMP`, then the local temp fallback, matching the correction already made to the neighboring permission suite in #337826. Remove the Azure-only quarantine and its known-issues entry so all five tests run normally again. Every test assertion and the production permission profiles remain unchanged.

### Validation

- **RED:** current main with `TF_BUILD=1`, `TMPDIR=/tmp`, a private `AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY`, and the quarantine opt-in reproduces all five assertion failures.
- **GREEN:** changing only fixture placement makes the same five tests pass under the identical environment.
- After removing the quarantine, the Azure-like environment passes all **19 Codex sandbox, permissions, and customization cases**, plus the clean-state guard, with `AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES` unset.
- The GitHub temp-root fallback also passes all **13 sandbox and permissions cases**, plus the guard, with `TMPDIR=/tmp`.
- `npm run compile-client`, targeted ESLint/hygiene, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [GitHub macOS Electron](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36108322851/job/107985845794) passed; its job log confirms all five sandbox and eight permission cases execute and pass.
- [Azure build 477196](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477196) passed the macOS Electron integration-test task. Log 1594 confirms all five sandbox and eight permission cases execute and pass, including the disabled-plugin assertion from the reported failure.
- A second Azure macOS run, [477200](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477200), is in progress on the same commit. This PR remains a draft.

### Reproduce locally on macOS

With the normal macOS private `TMPDIR` available, preserve it as the CI-owned directory while making the system temp fallback point at shared temp:

```sh
env -u AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES \
  TF_BUILD=1 AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY="$TMPDIR" TMPDIR=/tmp \
  ./scripts/test-integration.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/codexSandbox.integrationTest.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/codexPermissions.integrationTest.ts
```

All five sandbox and eight permission cases must execute and pass; skipped tests do not establish recovery.

pull_requests.title: Auto indent on paste when the first line is already indented
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #285222

### The problem

With `editor.autoIndentOnPaste` enabled, pasting several lines at a position that is already correctly indented leaves every line but the first flush left:

```ts
{
	const a = 4;
const b = 4;
const c = 4;
const d = 4;
}
```

Breaking the indentation of the first line first makes it work, which is the clue: the adjustment is being skipped precisely when the first line needs no adjustment.

### The cause

`AutoIndentOnPaste.trigger` computes the indent for the first pasted line. When that indent already matches and the line matches no indentation rule, it returns from the whole method — which also skips the block below it that re-indents the remaining pasted lines.

### Why the guard cannot simply be removed

The early return was added in e77b196c269 for #38833. The remaining lines are shifted by the difference between the good indent of the second line and its actual indent, and the good indent does not account for continuation lines. Without the guard, blocks like these are outdented:

```ts
type T =
	| number
	| string;

const x = foo
	.bar()
	.baz();
```

Limiting the guard to pastes that start at column 1 is not enough either. A continuation block copied from its first non-whitespace character and pasted at an indented position is outdented the same way.

### The change

In the case the guard covers — the first line is already correctly indented and matches no indentation rule:

- **The paste starts at column 1:** return early, as before. The pasted block carries its own indentation.
- **The paste starts after existing indentation:** that indentation belongs to the document, and the following lines did not get it. Indent them to match, but never outdent them.

Every other path is unchanged: when that case does not apply, the new condition reduces to the previous `!==`.

### Tests

- `issue #285222` reproduces the bug. It fails without the change.
- `issue #38833: preserve the internal indentation of a pasted block` covers the original case at column 1. The nearest existing test (`issue #167299`) starts with a blank line, which leaves the second line unindented and hides the regression, so this behaviour was effectively uncovered.
- `issue #38833: preserve continuation lines when pasting at an indented position` pastes a method chain inside a function. It fails if the guard is only limited to column 1.

Removing the guard outright fails both `#38833` tests and the existing `issue #29753: incorrect indentation of header comment`.

### Behaviour change to be aware of

A multi-line template literal pasted at an indented position now has its second line indented, which changes the string. The same text pasted at column 1 of an empty line in a block is already indented this way today, so this makes the two cases consistent rather than introducing new behaviour for the feature. `editor.autoIndentOnPasteWithinString` does not apply because the pasted range starts and ends outside the string.

### Verification

- `vs/editor/contrib/indentation/test/**` — 63 passing
- `vs/editor/**` — 5429 passing, 0 failing

pull_requests.title: fix(glob): keep path separator in negated bracket ranges
pull_requests.body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #322331

A `files.exclude` pattern like `"Source[^M/]*": true` was excluding far more than it should: everything under `Source/` disappeared from the Explorer, even though `/` was explicitly listed in the negated character class.

## Root cause

In `src/vs/base/common/glob.ts`, `parseRegExp` silently dropped any `/` found inside a bracket expression when compiling the glob to a regular expression. So `Source[^M/]*` compiled to `Source[^M]*`, and the negated class happily matched `/` too. I confirmed this against current `main` with a small repro before changing anything:

- `Source[^M/]*` matched `Source/` and `Source/sub` (wrong, both)
- after the fix it matches neither, while `SourceX` / `SourceXyz` still match and `SourceM` still doesn't

## The change

In a *negated* bracket range the separator is now kept as a literal, so it stays excluded from matching (`[^/]` no longer matches `/`). Positive ranges are untouched: `foo[/]bar` still does not match `foo/bar`, which the existing test suite asserts.

## Tests

- Added regression cases to the `brackets` test in `src/vs/base/test/common/glob.test.ts` covering the exact pattern from the issue.
- Ran the full `src/vs/base/test/common/glob.test.ts` suite standalone on Linux (node, no display needed): **51 passing, 0 failing** with the fix; with the fix reverted the new assertions fail as expected (`Source[^M/]* should not match Source/`), so the test genuinely guards the regression.

Only the two files above are touched. Nothing else in the repo depends on the old drop-the-slash behavior; I checked the existing suite for any `/`-in-bracket expectations and the only one is the positive-range case, which still passes.

pull_requests.title: Ensure the database directory exists before opening the database.
pull_requests.body:
Fixes issue#337873

### Problem

`ExternalIngestIndex` opens its local index DB at `joinPath(context.storageUri, 'codebase-external.sqlite')`. `vscode.d.ts` guarantees only that storageUri's parent exists , and nothing creates the extension's own folder. So on a fresh workspace the folder is missing, `new DatabaseSync(path)` throws `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` (errcode 14), and the code falls back to `:memory:`. But an in-memory index can never be reused, so the whole workspace is re-ingested on every extension-host start. On a large workspace that pinned the extension host for minutes per reload — all other extensions in the process unresponsive — with nothing surfaced in the UI; the only trace is `Failed to create database. Falling back to in memory db` in the Copilot Chat output channel.

### Fix

Create the folder (recursively) immediately before opening the DB — the same pattern `_ensureDb()` /
`openDb()` already use elsewhere in this extension, and the placement suggested in the issue thread.

```diff
 import * as fs from 'node:fs';
+import * as path from 'node:path';
 import sql from 'node:sqlite';
@@
 			return this.createFreshDatabase(dbPath);
 		}
 
+		// VS Code only guarantees that storageUri's parent exists, this folder is created by the extension.
+		// node:sqlite cannot create a file inside a folder that does not exist.
+		fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(dbPath), { recursive: true });
+
 		// Try to open existing database and check cache version
```

Placed after the `:memory:` early-return, so no extra guard is needed, and it covers both the "open existing" and "create fresh" paths.
Failure behaviour is unchanged: if this still fails (read-only mount, permissions, …), the existing `catch` still falls back exactly as before.

### Test plan

- Field-verified on a Remote-SSH setup: with the folder missing, `codebase-external.sqlite` was never created and the ingest re-ran on every reload (extension host pinned ~1 core for minutes). After creating the folder by hand, the DB is created once (2,789,376 B), kept current, and reloads no longer re-ingest.
- Independent standalone reproduction (in the issue thread): the real directory layout plus the twofunctions mirrored from the bundle, on Node 24 / SQLite 3.53 — without the mkdir every start throws errcode 14 and re-ingests; with it, the second open reuses the existing rows and skips the ingest.
- No new test added: I'm contributing from the browser without a local checkout, so I can't iterate against the Vitest harness.
### Notes

- Deliberately out of scope: 
  (1) the fallback semantics — retrying once and then marking the codebase index unavailable instead of picking `:memory:` would be better
  (2) the synchronous ingest holding the extension host — need tracked separately.
- Credit: the `vscode.d.ts` / `extHostStoragePaths` reading that makes the root cause airtight, and the standalone reproduction, come from @aron-intframe in issue#337873.

pull_requests.title: Release inline request edit input and listeners when editing finishes
pull_requests.body:
Related to #146841

With the default `chat.editRequests: inline`, clicking a request creates an inline `ChatInputPart` through `ChatWidget.createInput`. `createInput` registers about 10 listeners and autoruns on the widget's own store (`onDidLoadInputState`, `onDidFocus`, `onDidAcceptFollowup`, `inputEditor.onDidChangeModelContent`, `chatAgentService.onDidChangeAgents`, `input.onDidChangeCurrentChatMode`, `contextKeyService.onDidChangeContext`, two autoruns, and the scoped instantiation service), and `clickedRequest` adds 3 more listeners. They were only released when the whole widget was disposed, so every edit left them behind:

- the autoruns read the inline input's `selectedToolsModel.entriesMap` / `selectedLanguageModel`, keeping them subscribed to the global `LanguageModelToolsService.toolSets`, and through them the disposed input part, its `CodeEditorWidget`, `TextModel` and DOM;
- listeners accumulated on global emitters (`chatAgentService.onDidChangeAgents`, `contextKeyService.onDidChangeContext`);
- the edit listeners captured the edited request view model, so the replaced `ChatRequestModel`/`ChatResponseModel` stayed alive too.

Edit-only disposables now go into a per-edit `DisposableStore` (`_editingDisposables`), which `createInput` receives for the inline input and which is cleared in `finishedEditing`. The main input keeps using the widget's store. `createInput` subscribes to the input part it created rather than the active one (`this.input`), so the main input's autoruns can't switch to the inline input while an edit is open. `finishedEditing` clears the inline input and paste-target holders instead of only disposing the input, and only the main input gets the getting-started tip presenter (the tip only applies to the empty state; previously an edit replaced the main input's presenter and left it bound to the disposed inline input).

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`LanguageModelToolsService.toolSets._observers → Derived (ChatSelectedTools.entriesMap) → AutorunObserver (ChatWidget._store)`, and `ObservableValue (owner ChatInputModelSelectionController) → ChatInputPart.container → <div class="chat-edit-input-container">`

### Measurement

| Per inline edit (send + edit) | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| CodeEditorWidget / TextModel | **+1 / +1** | flat |
| ChatRequestModel / ChatResponseModel | **+2 / +2** (replaced request kept) | +1 / +1 (the new request) |
| Detached DOM | **+36 nodes**, +19 roots | flat |
| Emitter / DisposableStore instances | **~+265 / ~+260** | +4 / +5 (the new request) |
| Heap after GC | ~+1 MB | ~+0.1 MB |

### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) with the mock LLM server from `scripts/chat-simulation` (no sign-in), driven over CDP with Playwright. After a warm-up round and after each of 4 rounds: 4× forced GC, live instance counts via `Runtime.queryObjects` on the class prototypes, and `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (descendants of every detached root, queried from a throwaway CDP session). "Without this change" means only this fix reverted. The retainers were identified from heap snapshot retainer paths.

Added a `ChatWidget` test for the inline edit path: it creates the main input, starts and finishes an inline edit, and checks that the inline input, its scoped instantiation service, listeners and autoruns are released, and that the main input keeps its tip presenter (fails without this change).

pull_requests.title: Release previous chat models when the chat view switches sessions
pull_requests.body:
Related to #146841

`ChatViewPane.showModel` defers marking the previous session as read with `this._register(disposableTimeout(..., 0))`. That adds one disposable to the view pane's store on every model switch (New Chat, picking another session), and it is only removed when the view is disposed. The timeout closure shares the `showModel` scope, which holds `model`, so every previous `ChatModel` stayed alive.

The timeout now gets the store as its third argument, so it removes itself from the store once it fired (and is still cleared if the view is disposed first).

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`ChatViewPane._store → FunctionDisposable._fn → closure → Context(showModel) → model → ChatModel`

### Measurement

| Scenario (per round) | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| New chat + 4 messages (text, markdown, code blocks) | **+1 ChatModel**, +3 Emitters | flat |
| Switch between 3 sessions in the sessions list | **+3 ChatModels**, +9 Emitters | flat |

One retained `ChatModel` per session switch for the lifetime of the Chat view.

### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) with the mock LLM server from `scripts/chat-simulation` (no sign-in), driven over CDP with Playwright. After a warm-up round and after each of 4 rounds: 4× forced GC, live instance counts via `Runtime.queryObjects` on the class prototypes, and `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (descendants of every detached root). "Without this change" means only this fix reverted. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

No new test: the change relies on the `disposableTimeout(handler, timeout, store)` contract that is covered in `async.test.ts`, and `ChatViewPane` has no unit test harness.

pull_requests.title: sessions: fix renderer OOM from workspace file count telemetry
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #325919

## Problem

`SessionsTelemetryContribution` computes the `workspaceFileCount` telemetry measurement with `ISearchService.fileSearch({ filePattern: '' })` and no `maxResults`. The extension host streams every matching file URI to the renderer, and `SearchOperation` in `mainThreadSearch.ts` keeps all of them until the search completes. The scan was also restarted on every send: the `onWillSendRequest` prewarm bypassed the per-session cache, and the in-flight entry was deleted once the scan finished. It ran even with telemetry turned off.

When a session's workspace is a very large folder, such as the home directory, the renderer V8 heap runs out. This matches nine crash dumps from 1.140 Insiders (`eb1f2bba`):
- **Heap:** every dump is a renderer V8 OOM at the 4 GB pointer-compression cage limit.
- **Running JS:** crash keys name `$handleFileMatch` / `SearchOperation.addMatch`, and most main-thread stacks are parsing extension host search results.
- **Timing:** every crash came 1–5 minutes after a send to a session whose workspace was the home folder.
- **Crash loop:** the last four crashes repeated the cycle reopen → send → OOM.

This was introduced in #318435 and moved to its current location in #319019. The Copilot review on #318435 flagged the per-session caching, but it wasn't addressed.

## Fix

- **Bounded count:** the count is capped at 20,000 files. Folders are searched one at a time with the remaining budget, because providers apply `maxResults` per scheme or per folder. Only one bounded result list is in memory at a time.
- **One scan per folder set:** a single cache keyed by workspace URI plus folder roots holds the pending or completed count. The prewarm and the logging paths share it, so each set of folders is scanned at most once per window. A session that gains folders under the same URI gets a fresh scan.
- **No scan without usage telemetry:** the scan is skipped when the telemetry level is below usage, since the event wouldn't be sent.
- **Field descriptions:** the `workspaceFileCount` descriptions now state the cap.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Telemetry meaning:** a `workspaceFileCount` of 20000 now means "20,000 or more files".
- **Staleness:** counts are computed once per window for each folder set, so they can go stale if a workspace's file count changes a lot.
- **Not addressed here (pre-existing):**
  - Remote agent host sessions (`vscode-agent-host:`) have no file search provider, so their count likely never resolves and their `requestSent` / session action events never fire.
  - Command telemetry is dropped when a command runs without arguments, for example from the title-bar button bar (flagged in the #319019 review).

## Testing

- Two new unit tests:
  - The scan is bounded and runs once per folder set, including the same URI with different folders.
  - No scan runs without usage telemetry.
  - Both fail without the fix.
- `scripts/test.bat --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsTelemetry.contribution.test.ts`: 12 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client` and eslint on the changed files pass.

auto_merge.commit_title: sessions: fix renderer OOM from workspace file count telemetry (#337889)
auto_merge.commit_message:
SessionsTelemetryContribution computed workspaceFileCount with an unbounded
file search and restarted it on every send, because the prewarm bypassed the
per-session cache. When a session's workspace is a very large folder such as
the home directory, every file URI was materialized in the renderer until the
V8 heap ran out, and the next send after reopening crashed it again.

- Cap the count at 20,000 files, searching one folder at a time with the
  remaining budget so the cap holds across folders and schemes.
- Cache the pending or completed count per workspace URI and folder roots so
  each set of folders is scanned once per window.
- Skip the scan when usage telemetry is off, since the event is not sent.

Fixes #325919

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

pull_requests.title: Stop chat progress signals once the request settles
pull_requests.body:
Related to #146841

## Leak

`ChatAccessibilityService.acceptRequest()` stores an `AccessibilityProgressSignalScheduler` in `_pendingSignalMap`. It was removed only by `acceptResponse()` or `disposeRequest()`. Some callers never report a response. For example, the `ChatWidget.viewModel` setter calls `acceptRequest(uri, true)` when it attaches to a request that is already in progress. That happens for every session created from the Agents window new-session composer. Each such session left a scheduler behind, and its `playSignalLoop` setTimeout chain ran every 5 s forever. The map was also keyed by URI object identity, so `acceptResponse` with an equal but different URI instance never removed the entry.

Retainer: `ChatAccessibilityService._pendingSignalMap` → `Map` → `AccessibilityProgressSignalScheduler` (+ the signal loop timer).

## Fix

- Key the map with `ResourceMap`.
- Each entry now lasts until the chat model's `hasActiveRequest` settles as false or the model is disposed. The scheduler pauses while `requestInProgress` is false (tool confirmation or elicitation) and restarts when processing resumes.
- Reruns call `acceptRequest` and then `resendRequest`, which synchronously cancels the active request and adds its replacement. So the entry is only removed once `hasActiveRequest` is still false after that call (a 0 ms `RunOnceScheduler`).
- `ChatWidget` passes the model it displays. Models that aren't registered with `IChatService` still clean up when disposed, such as the Agents window preparation transcript (`sessions/contrib/chat/browser/chatView.ts`).

## Measurement

Code OSS `--agents` against the local mock agent host (`--enable-mock-agent`). 6 rounds of "new session → send prompt", with live instance counts from heap snapshots after forced GC. Leave-one-out: only this change was reverted.

| | AccessibilityProgressSignalScheduler | RunOnceScheduler |
|---|---|---|
| before | 5 → 11 (+1 per session) | 165 → 184 |
| after | 0 → 0 | 160 → 173 (unchanged after each review revision) |

## Tests

New `chatAccessibilityService.test.ts`. Covers: settling without a reported response, pausing and resuming around a confirmation (true → false → true), a rerun that cancels the active request before its replacement, model disposal (registered and unregistered models), and matching of equal URIs.






## Known pre-existing issue (out of scope)

On `main` too, "rerun without" (participant detection) while the original request is still streaming loses the rerun's progress sound. The original request's `ChatWidget` chain later calls `acceptResponse` for the same session, which deletes the rerun's entry. That stale call also plays "response received" and announces the rerun's partial text. This isn't a leak and this PR doesn't change it, so I'm leaving it for a separate fix.

pull_requests.title: agents: Let Toggle Block Comment keep Ctrl+Shift+A on Linux
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #321321

## What

On Linux, `Ctrl+Shift+A` is the default keybinding for **Toggle Block Comment** (`editor.action.blockComment`), but **Open Agents Window** (`workbench.action.openAgentsWindow`) registered the same key at a higher weight (`WorkbenchContrib` vs `EditorContrib`), so pressing it in the editor opened the Agents window instead of commenting.

Both `Ctrl+Shift+A` window-switching keybindings now defer to the editor on Linux when a writable editor in the editor area has focus:

- `OpenAgentsWindowAction` (VS Code → Agents window)
- `OpenVSCodeWindowAction` (Agents window → VS Code), for consistency

New `when` clause component: `!isLinux || !editorAreaFocus || editorReadonly`

## Notes for reviewers

- **Linux only.** On Windows/macOS, Toggle Block Comment is `Shift+Alt+A` / `⇧⌥A` and Toggle Line Comment is `Ctrl+/` / `⌘/`, so there is no default conflict there; behavior is unchanged on those platforms. The issue says "All OS", but all duplicates (#326962, #328272, #333341) were reported on Linux.
- **Read-only editors** still get the Agents shortcut, since Toggle Block Comment's keybinding requires `!editorReadonly` and would not fire anyway.
- Non-text editors in the editor area (e.g. image preview, settings editor) don't set `editorReadonly`, so on Linux the shortcut is inert while one of those has focus. The Command Palette entry still works.
- The screen-reader variant (`Ctrl+Shift+Alt+A`) is unchanged.

Related to #146841

## Leak

`Delayer.cancel()` cleared the timeout and rejected the pending promise, but it kept `this.task`. `dispose()` calls `cancel()`, so it had the same problem. The last task closure stayed on the delayer until the next `trigger()`. `ThrottledDelayer` wraps a `Delayer`, so it kept the closure too.

`QuickInputList._registerHoverListeners` uses a `ThrottledDelayer`. Its `onMouseOver` task closes over the tree mouse event `e`. When the mouse leaves, `onMouseOut` calls `delayer.cancel()`, but the task and its `MouseEvent` stay alive. When the pointer moves from editor text into a Quick Open row, the event's `relatedTarget` is an editor token span. After the editor view is detached, for example by switching tabs, the canceled task keeps that old view DOM alive. At most one view is retained this way, and only until the next hover.

Retainer path seen in a heap snapshot:

```
QuickInputService._controller → QuickInputController.ui.list → QuickInputList._store → DisposableStore
  → ThrottledDelayer.delayer → Delayer.task → closure (promiseFactory) → closure scope { e }
  → Object.browserEvent → MouseEvent → <span class="mtk22"> → … → <div class="monaco-editor">
```

## Fix

- `Delayer.cancel()` (and so `dispose()`) now clears `task`. A canceled trigger still rejects with `CancellationError` and doesn't run its task, and a later `trigger()` works as before.
- A `cancel()` can happen after the delay has elapsed but before the queued `.then` runs the task. Before this change, the task still ran in that case. Now it rejects with `CancellationError`, which matches a normal cancel.
- Each round's `.then` now checks that it still owns `completionPromise`. Before, a `cancel()` in that window followed immediately by `trigger()` let the stale round run the new task as the canceled promise's result and clear the new round's promise, so the new promise never settled. This was already the case before this PR (found in review); the stale round now rejects with `CancellationError` and leaves the new round alone.
- `Throttler.dispose()` now clears `queuedPromiseFactory`. After dispose, the queued factory never runs, but the throttler used to keep a reference to it.
- `ThrottledDelayer` needs no separate change because it uses these two classes. `Throttler` already clears finished tasks: `activePromise` holds only the promise, and `queuedPromiseFactory` is cleared once it has been queued.

## Tests

New tests in `src/vs/base/test/common/async.test.ts`:

- Delayer: `cancel` / `dispose` release the pending task. The pending promise rejects with `CancellationError`, the task doesn't run, and a later trigger works.
- Delayer: a cancel after the delay elapsed doesn't run the task.
- Delayer: a cancel and retrigger after the delay elapsed rejects the canceled promise and settles the new one with its own task.
- ThrottledDelayer: `cancel` releases the pending task.
- Throttler: disposal releases the queued factory.

The unit test runner doesn't expose `gc()`, so a `WeakRef` or `FinalizationRegistry` check isn't reliable here. The tests read the private field directly instead. All 6 new tests fail without the fix and pass with it. The full async suite passes.

## Measurement (Code OSS, Windows)

Scenario, driven with Playwright over CDP (`--remote-debugging-port`):

1. Open two files and press Ctrl+P.
2. Move the mouse onto an editor token span below the widget, then straight onto a Quick Open row, then back to the span within the hover delay. This makes `mouseover` fire with `relatedTarget` = the editor span, followed by `mouseout` → `cancel()`.
3. Press Escape, then Ctrl+PageDown to switch tabs so the previous editor view is detached.
4. Run `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage` 5 times, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes`. Count detached roots whose subtree contains `view-lines` / `overflow-guard`.

Each variant got 3 fresh launches with 5 iterations each. The build was the same apart from `out/vs/base/common/async.js`:

| | detached editor views after each iteration | nodes in those roots (`retainedNodeIds`) | total detached nodes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 1 in 15/15 iterations | 154 | ~260–275 |
| After | 0 in 15/15 iterations | 0 | ~106–111 |

The retained view is bounded (always exactly 1), as expected, because the delayer holds only the latest task. `retainedNodeIds` counts are smaller than the ~1,057 nodes seen in the original heap snapshot. The count depends on file contents and window size, and CDP only reports nodes that JS retains.

pull_requests.title: Release accessible view listeners per show instead of on dispose
pull_requests.body:
Related to #146841 (replaces the `AccessibilityHelpWidget` item of the issue, which became `AccessibleView`)

`AccessibleView` is a long-lived singleton, but `show()` registered per-provider listeners into its own `_store` on every call:
- `provider.onDidChangeContent` listener
- `provider.onDidRequestClearLastProvider` listener
- a code block context provider registration (chat)

and `_render()` returned a new listener store on every content refresh, which was dropped when refreshing an already visible view. So every provider ever shown was retained for the lifetime of the window — for the terminal that is the whole `TerminalInstance`, xterm and DOM of every terminal whose accessible view was ever opened, even after the terminal was killed.

Now listeners of a `show()` are released when the view hides, render listeners replace the previous set, the clear-last-provider listener lives as long as that provider is remembered, and the code block context provider is registered once.

Retainer path (heap snapshot, before):
`AccessibleViewService → AccessibleView._store → FunctionDisposable → listener closure → TerminalAccessibleBufferProvider._instance → TerminalInstance._wrapperElement → <div class="terminal-wrapper">`

The clear-last-provider listener now uses the structural provider contract, so providers implementing `IAccessibleViewContentProvider` directly (like `TerminalAccessibleBufferProvider`) are honored. The terminal provider's clear notification is tied to the terminal instance instead of the provider, because the accessible view disposes the provider on hide while it may still remember it. Copies of the provider made for Accessibility Help (and restored when it closes) forward the clear request too.

### Measurement

| Scenario | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| 5× (create terminal, `echo hello`, *Open Accessible View*, Escape, kill terminal) | **5** `TerminalInstance`, **5** `XtermTerminal`, **5** `TerminalAccessibleBufferProvider`, **5** `BufferContentTracker` alive; 5 detached terminal DOM trees (+26 detached roots / +96 nodes) | **0** of each |

This is unbounded: it grows by one terminal per terminal whose accessible view was opened (live object counts from heap snapshots after GC).
### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. "Without this change" means all other fixes from this series applied and only this one reverted, so the number shows what this retainer alone keeps alive. Each scenario was run 3 times with identical results. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

Added a unit test that provider listeners don't accumulate across show() calls and are released when the view hides.

Related to #146841

`ContextKeyService.updateInputContextKeys` creates a focus tracker for the focused input on every `focusin`. When the input blurred, the tracker was disposed, but the disposed tracker and the `Event.once` listener stayed in the per-focus `DisposableStore` until the next `focusin`. The store is now cleared once the input blurs.

pull_requests.title: Release widget DOM nodes when an editor view is disposed
pull_requests.body:
Related to #146841

Content, overlay and glyph margin widgets outlive the editor `View`: `CodeEditorWidget` keeps them and re-adds them to the next view once a model is attached. When a model is detached without a new one (e.g. all editors of a group are closed, the editor stays around without a model), the widgets' DOM nodes stayed parented in the disposed view — or in its `overflowingContentWidgets`/`overflowingOverlayWidgets` containers, which live outside the view's DOM. Since the widgets are referenced by live contributions (rename, suggest, hover, sticky scroll, …), the entire previous view DOM stayed alive.

`ViewContentWidgets`, `ViewOverlayWidgets` and `GlyphMarginWidgets` now remove the DOM nodes of their widgets on dispose. Attaching a new model adds them to the new view as before.

Retainer path (heap snapshot):
`StickyScrollController → StickyScrollWidget._rootDomNode → <div class="sticky-widget"> → overlayWidgets → overflow-guard → <div class="monaco-editor">` (same for `RenameWidget`, `SuggestWidget`, `HoverWidget` via the overflowing containers)

### Measurement

| Scenario | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| Open a file, show rename (F2) and suggest widgets, run *Close All Editors* | 1 detached editor view, **1,402 DOM nodes** + **95 nodes** of overflowing widget containers | 0 |
| Same, closing the group's editors with Ctrl+K W | **1,443 + 95 nodes** | 0 |

One retained view per editor control that is left without a model (e.g. per empty editor group), until a model is attached again.
### How this was measured

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. "Without this change" means all other fixes from this series applied and only this one reverted, so the number shows what this retainer alone keeps alive. Each scenario was run 3 times with identical results. The retainer was identified from a heap snapshot retainer path.

Added a CodeEditorWidget test with a real view: widget nodes (incl. an overflowing content widget) are released on setModel(null) and reattached on the next setModel.

Related to #146841

`ModifierKeyEmitter` stored the last modifier `KeyboardEvent` in its (singleton) key status. A `KeyboardEvent` references its target and event path, so the DOM that received the last Ctrl/Alt/Shift/Meta key stayed alive until the next modifier key press — e.g. the complete view DOM of an editor whose model changed or which was closed, or a killed terminal.

| Show rename + suggest widgets (Ctrl+Space), close all editors of the group | 1 detached editor view, **1,385 nodes** | 0 |
| Close all editors of the group with Ctrl+K W | 1 detached editor view, **1,426 nodes** | 0 |

Bounded to one retained tree at a time (replaced on the next modifier key press), but it's the most common way an old editor view stays alive — any keyboard-driven tab switch or close.

Code OSS (Electron, dev build) driven over CDP with Playwright. After each scenario: 4× forced GC, then `DOM.getDetachedDomNodes` (the data behind Edge's *Detached Elements* tool), counting the descendants of every detached root. pull_requests.title: agentHost: keep refreshed sandbox credentials bound to the host
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Prevent a sandbox credential refresh from combining new host-key metadata with a cached token encrypted for a different key.

Previously, a refresh that omitted the sealed token also replaced any newly reported host key with the cached key. That could hide a host-key change while accepting the new relay credentials.

- Check that the sealed token names the refreshed host key, and that cached key metadata has not changed when reusing a sealed token.
- Keep the entire previous credential bundle on mismatch, log a warning without credential contents, and retry using the existing 30-second schedule and 10-consecutive-failure cap.
- Install matching credentials together while preserving the existing optional-key behavior and leaving the current socket untouched.

This is a defensive correctness fix for host/key changes, not a measured performance improvement. It does not add recovery-time admission refresh or change connection retry policy.

## Validation

- Reproduced the host-key mixing regressions before the fix.
- Focused TypeScript check passed after rebasing onto main.
- All 22 focused credential-refresh and scheduling unit tests passed.
- Targeted ESLint, whitespace checks, and pre-commit hygiene passed.

Coverage includes key changes, matching replacement credentials, omitted key metadata, preservation of the complete previous bundle, and exact retry timing and limits.

Focused unit-test command after compiling the test output:

```sh
npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxCredentialRefresh.test.ts
```

Live sandbox and end-to-end validation have not been established. No application was launched as part of these checks.

pull_requests.title: Fix Agent Host sandbox path normalization on Windows
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fixes #337171.

- Resolve sandbox configuration in a shared, provider-neutral Agent Host accessor before SDK or host-terminal policy mapping.
- Normalize Windows filesystem path separators using the executing Agent Host's OS, independently of whether its client is local or remote.
- Apply the resolver at session launch/resume, per-turn SDK updates, and host-terminal settings reads.
- Preserve stored configuration, client forwarding, POSIX paths, and session/managed-policy overrides.
- Reuse the platform normalization helper in the existing Windows MXC terminal path.

## Validation

- 74 targeted sandbox, session, launcher, and Windows terminal tests passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- ESLint passed for all 11 changed files.
- `npm run compile` completed with zero errors.
- Pre-commit hygiene passed.
- Launched Code OSS and attached the Agent Host debugger with a breakpoint after normalization. End-to-end access-denial enforcement has not been verified.

## Compatibility / follow-up

No persisted schema or wire-format migration is required. Existing sessions receive normalized policy on resume or the next policy application. Windows paths that previously failed to match may now enforce their intended restrictions.

The runtime filesystem schema still accepts generic objects; this change assumes the documented string-array fields. Malformed persisted configuration is not covered by the new normalization tests and may throw earlier during resolution, including with sandboxing disabled.

pull_requests.title: automations: support scheduled end dates
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339011

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Adds **scheduled end dates only** to AHP-backed automations: run on the configured schedule until a date/time, then stop scheduling. This PR does **not** ship run-count limits, Run once, allowance counters, or a Run until field in the automation dialog.

- Ask an agent in chat to create or update an automation with one `afterDate` condition. New or changed end dates must be valid future timestamps, including after tool approval.
- The Agent Host persists the cutoff and stops scheduled/catch-up admission at or after it, including when a provider is unavailable. Already-admitted runs are not cancelled; manual runs remain available.
- Show the saved end date on enabled automation cards. **Remove end date** clears it without enabling a disabled automation. Unrelated dialog edits preserve host-owned enabled state and the existing end date.
- Export end-date blueprints as version 2. Retain the original strict version-1 parser and version-1 exports for definitions without conditions.
- Restore historical run-count definitions safely: strip obsolete caps/counters, preserve dates and history, and leave formerly capped automations disabled pending explicit re-enable.

The expandable Advanced Settings / Run until editor is a separate UX follow-up, not part of this shipping MVP.

## Protocol source

Related: microsoft/agent-host-protocol#461.

Merged main through `e6c5367ae8d`, including the canonical AHP sync in `5470377e71f` (#338952). Main now supplies the automation disable-condition/end-date contract. **There are no generated protocol-file changes relative to main in this PR.**

The upstream protocol still declares run-count conditions, but this implementation accepts only scheduled end dates. Run-count support is out of scope.

## CCR follow-up

- Removed the count-only and combined count/date confirmation/card wording, making the two run-count pluralization findings obsolete.
- Kept `scheduleChanged` trigger-only; added a separately classified boolean `disableConditionsChanged` measurement without recording dates.
- Base completion announcements on the authoritative returned automation state, including "remains disabled" when an expired end date prevents enabling.
- Versioned the extended blueprint schema instead of adding fields to strict version 1.

## Validation

Run from the VS Code repository root:

- `npm run typecheck-client` - passed.
- `npm run transpile-client` - passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --runGlob '**/{automationDisableConditions,agentHostAutomationService,automationDialog,automationTools,agentHostAutomationStore,automationsView,automationBlueprint}.test.js'` - **330 passing**.
- `$files = @(git diff --name-only 7b232e8b044 3bbcd0a435c -- '*.ts'); npm run eslint -- @files` - passed for all seven TypeScript files in the CCR fix.
- `node build\lib\formatter.ts --verify` on those seven files - passed.
- Pre-commit hygiene - passed for both the main merge and the CCR fixes; `git diff --check` - passed.

The focused tests cover deadline boundaries, provider-unavailable/active-run behavior, persistence and migration, manual-run exemptions, post-approval validation, card removal, hidden dialog controls, versioned blueprint compatibility, trigger-versus-condition telemetry, and authoritative accessibility announcements.

Before this final main merge, a real Code OSS + Copilot recording verified the MVP (not a mock): send "Create an hourly automation named Morning check that says hello, running until October 1, 2026 at 8 AM Pacific," open Automations, verify "Runs until Oct 1, 2026, 8:00 AM," and click **Remove end date**. The demonstration automation was disabled afterward. The final review fixes were validated by the tests above; the UI recording was not repeated after them.

### Manual verification

1. With Automations enabled and an available Agent Host, ask an agent in chat to create an hourly automation until a specified future date/time.
2. Open Automations and verify the card's end date.
3. Open Edit automation: there is no Run until field; save an unrelated change and verify the end date is retained.
4. Choose **Remove end date** from the card's More menu. Verify the cutoff disappears and a disabled automation is not re-enabled.
5. Use a near-future cutoff to verify scheduling stops while manual Run now remains available.

pull_requests.title: mcp: make assisted setup destination-aware
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Choose the destination before package-assisted MCP setup, including Copilot Global.
- Preserve the server's stdio, HTTP, or SSE configuration and use package manifests when available.
- Keep collected values out of generated files and require explicit approval before falling back to VS Code configuration.

Stacked on #337838. The base is `agents/p3-copilot-global-manual`; main integration is intentionally deferred.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Package setup previously generated a stdio-shaped configuration before choosing its destination. That prevented the prompt and input handling from matching the destination, excluded Copilot Global, and overwrote remote transport intent.

### Implementation

Core selects the destination using the existing install-target service, global picker, and workspace-file defaults. It supplies a destination schema to the extension. The extension validates and extracts exactly one named server without partially converting its dialect; core then normalizes through the shared converters, and the existing scanner owns the final file representation and safe write.

Usable package manifests still bypass the model. Their inputs and unsupported fields remain intact so core can offer a safe destination instead of stripping metadata. Workspace-root generation can retain required VS Code fields or SSE intent, but those configurations require explicit approval to use the legacy workspace file.

### Behavior and constraints

- Manual setup retains its question order and the existing global labels and path descriptions.
- VS Code input answers become opaque references before reaching the model, including when embedded inside URLs, arguments, or headers. Values go through the existing saved-input path rather than the configuration file.
- Copilot Global prompts request uppercase environment-variable names, not values. Generated references are retained, and the completion notification explains that variables must be set on the agent-host machine before a new session.
- Validation rejects malformed or ambiguous output, missing or altered input references, and mismatched command output formats without logging sensitive payloads. Older callers without a destination format retain the VS Code default; incompatible extension output produces an explicit error.
- Explicit file targets are never silently redirected. Cancellation and policy rejection occur without writes, and package configurations requiring unresolved inputs cannot be handed to the current agent session.
- Existing Copilot-home lookup, authority-scoped discovery behavior, shared workspace eligibility, and scanner concurrency protections remain unchanged. No agent-host protocol or general destination framework is added.

</details>

pull_requests.title: Close the promo hover when Try is clicked
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #331588.

### Problem
When a user clicks the Copilot status entry, the closed-chat promo tooltip is pinned. Clicking **Try <model>** in that tooltip leaves the hover open, and it switches to the Copilot usage dashboard.

Here's why: the Try command opens Chat synchronously. This withdraws the offer, so `ChatStatusBarEntry` swaps the tooltip back to the dashboard. The status bar item then calls `hover.update(...)`, and the pinned managed hover re-renders in place with the new content, keeping its focus, before the hover action gets a chance to dispose it.

### Fix
In `ChatStatusPromo`, the `_chat.tryPromoModel` command now calls `hoverService.hideHover(true)` before it opens Chat.

### Testing
- New regression test in `chatStatusPromo.test.ts`: "Try closes the pinned offer instead of swapping in the dashboard". It drives a real `StatusbarEntryItem` and `HoverService`: it pins the offer, clicks Try, and asserts that no hover remains.
  - It fails without the fix (the hover shows `Dashboard`) and passes with it. All 37 tests in the file pass.
- `npm run typecheck-client` is clean.
- I checked it manually in Code OSS with a GPT-5.5 sale fixture. After clicking Try, no hover is left and Chat opens.

### Proof
Both clips use Code OSS with a GPT-5.5 sale fixture and the `copilotIconPopup` treatment, with Chat collapsed. The mouse moves to the status bar pip, clicks it to pin the offer, then clicks **Try GPT-5.5**.

**Before** (`a6e06b5`, main): Chat opens, but the pinned hover stays open and switches to the Copilot dashboard.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fb0abd4-b2f2-4da2-8194-8ff004f53d54

**After** (`1c1477e`, this PR): the hover closes and Chat opens with the input focused.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37636950-a6ca-4db2-b6b7-a8b976a48718

pull_requests.title: sessions: keep new-session controls opaque over dark chat backgrounds
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337721

With a chat background configured, the new-session composer's bottom-row controls, including the combined Mode + Permissions picker, were transparent in the default dark themes, so the background showed through them. Light themes were unaffected.

### Root cause

`chatView.css` repeated the `chatWidget.css` surface rule for `.new-chat-bottom-container .action-label` with higher specificity (it adds `.chat-view`), so it always won. Its base color is `var(--vscode-chat-list-background, var(--vscode-button-secondaryBackground))`:

- The new-session view has no chat list, so `--vscode-chat-list-background` is never set there and the fallback always applies.
- `button.secondaryBackground` is transparent (`#00000000`) in 2026 Dark and Dark Modern and opaque in the light themes, hence dark-only.

The in-session toolbar isn't affected because `ChatWidget` sets `--vscode-chat-list-background`.

### Fix

Remove the duplicate new-session selectors (resting, hover, and open) from `chatView.css`, so the existing `chatWidget.css` rule, which falls back to the opaque `--session-view-background`, applies. A short comment explains why they shouldn't come back. The in-session rules are unchanged.

The issue calls out the combined picker, but every bottom-row control used this rule; the Worktree | Branch group only looked right because its action bar paints its own surface. The other session controls and status actions are now opaque in dark themes too.

### Testing

- `keeps background-image composer controls on complete opaque surfaces` (`chatView.test.ts`) never exercised the winning rule because its new-session DOM was missing `.chat-view`. It now uses the real ancestry, a transparent `button.secondaryBackground` like the dark themes, and a combined picker. It fails on `main` with `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` and passes with this change.
- The chat view, new-chat widget, and agent host picker suites pass; `typecheck-client`, eslint, and stylelint are clean.

### Screenshots

The real `AgentHostModePicker` in the new-session bottom row, rendered in the Component Explorer over a gradient standing in for the chat background. Captions come from the picker's computed styles. The Light Modern crops are byte-identical before and after.

![Before and after: the combined picker is transparent over the chat background in 2026 Dark and Dark Modern before the fix, and opaque after it; Light Modern is unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16b41e67-bfde-44d6-a4c0-da3cbc97efad)

### Notes for reviewers

- This PR updates the `NewSessionChatBackground/Dark` blocks-ci baseline. The only pixels that change are inside its bottom-row status controls, which now hide the part of a faint wallpaper icon that used to show through the Status control (70 pixels, max delta 9/255). That fixture's expected description already says these controls have opaque surfaces.
- The `chat/scrollAnchoring` entries in the bot's screenshot diff report are unrelated. They're workbench chat fixtures, which none of the removed selectors can match, and the two Light entries just trade hashes with each other, which points to timing-dependent rendering (they run with virtual time disabled) rather than a real change.

pull_requests.title: terminal: dispose auto responders when a persistent process is reattached
pull_requests.body:
## What

`AutoRepliesPtyServiceContribution.handleProcessReady` now disposes any existing `TerminalAutoResponder`s for a persistent process id before installing fresh ones.

## Why

`handleProcessReady` runs again for the same persistent process id whenever the workbench reattaches to it (e.g. on window reload): `attachToProcess` → `start()` takes the already-started path in `PersistentTerminalProcess`, which calls `triggerReplay()` → `onPersistentProcessReady` → `handleProcessReady`. The old responder map was replaced without disposing its entries, so each responder kept its `onProcessData` listener on the long-lived child process. After N reloads with one configured auto reply, a terminal held N+1 responders and a matched prompt was answered N+1 times (the throttle is per responder).

Disposal is done in place rather than via `handleProcessDispose`, so `_terminalProcesses` is never briefly missing the process. On first start there is no existing map, so behaviour is unchanged.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: keep Codex permission tests out of /tmp
pull_requests.body:
## What changed

- Create Codex permission-boundary fixtures under the CI runner's private temp root instead of relying on `os.tmpdir()`.
- Keep the fixture-local `TMPDIR` used to verify Codex's private temporary-directory access.
- Make Azure DevOps validation a non-negotiable requirement for every new Agent Host E2E or real-provider integration test.

## Why

[Azure build 476995](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=476995&view=logs&j=e352877c-ff47-5dec-32e2-b206099d9704&t=b83513b4-f303-5ddc-d18a-1b47c02d8dad) failed six macOS Codex permission integration tests because that worker resolved `os.tmpdir()` to `/tmp`. Codex intentionally grants macOS processes access to system scratch roots, so the test's supposedly external fixtures were actually allowed.

The same test passed in PR CI because the GitHub runner provided a private temp directory. The initial fix placed fixtures under `.build`, but GitHub's macOS Electron job then exposed a second invalid assumption: Codex discovered repository-level `AGENTS.md` instructions outside the test workspace and correctly denied access while materializing the session. Preferring `AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY` on Azure and `RUNNER_TEMP` on GitHub keeps fixtures outside both system scratch roots and the source tree.

## Validation

- Reproduced the original six failures with `TMPDIR=/tmp`.
- Reproduced and diagnosed the GitHub macOS `CodexMaterializeFailed` failure from the completed job log.
- Azure-like environment (`TMPDIR=/tmp` plus private `AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY`): 9 passing.
- Focused [Azure DevOps build 477038](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477038): succeeded, including Electron integration tests on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- Earlier forced-temp verification of the sandbox-boundary fix: 36/36 cases passing.
- `npm run compile-client`
- Targeted ESLint
- Pre-commit hygiene
- `git diff --check`

(Written by Copilot)

pull_requests.title: agentHost: handle relay publish acknowledgement failures
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Relay publish acknowledgements were requested but ignored. A rejected or unacknowledged publish could leave a request pending even while unrelated traffic kept the connection looking healthy.

- Track acknowledgement IDs for every published chunk. Accept successful and `Duplicate` acknowledgements; fail through the existing handshake or transport-close path on rejection.
- Give each publish a 30-second acknowledgement deadline, sharing the existing handshake timeout constant. Use one scheduler per transport, preserve older deadlines when newer traffic arrives, and clear tracking and timers on settlement or close.
- Preserve chunk ordering and do not automatically resend publishes. Relay acceptance is not a guarantee that the host executed the request.

Follow-up to #337778.

## Validation

- Targeted TypeScript check passed.
- All 58 focused relay transport, framing, and chunking unit tests passed.
- Targeted ESLint and whitespace checks passed.

Regression coverage includes rejected and missing acknowledgements, out-of-order and `Duplicate` acknowledgements, chunked publishes, exact timeout boundaries, handshake transitions, failed socket writes, and timer cleanup.

Focused unit-test command (after compiling the test output):

```sh
npm run test-node -- \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/webPubSub/framing.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/webPubSub/chunking.test.ts
```

Live relay and end-to-end testing have not been run and remain pending manual validation. This PR does not claim measured production reliability or performance improvements.

auto_merge.commit_title: agentHost: handle relay publish acknowledgement failures (#337819)
auto_merge.commit_message:
Track relay acknowledgements per published chunk and fail the transport on rejection or after 30 seconds without acceptance. Share the handshake timeout constant and use one scheduler without extending older publish deadlines.

Cover successful, Duplicate, rejected, missing, and out-of-order acknowledgements, including chunked sends and handshake and cleanup behavior. Do not automatically replay publishes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

pull_requests.title: Track customization marketplace installation records
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Follow up to #337110 by separating marketplace installation provenance from local-item discovery.

- Persist machine-local profile installation records after successful marketplace installs. Each record keeps the source/identifier/version identity, validated installation descriptor, and exact installed URI or MCP server ID.
- Derive `checking`, `installed`, and `missing` state by reconciling records with the owning skill, plugin, or MCP implementation. Same-name and same-repository local items no longer imply marketplace installation or hide an available entry.
- Add **Repair** for missing recorded installations. Skill repair restores only recorded files that are missing, preserving edited and additional files.
- Route skill uninstall through the existing confirmed deletion/Trash flow. Cancelling keeps both the target and its record; already-absent targets can drop their record cleanly.
- Keep exact association and repair state available to keyboard and screen-reader users, including Accessibility Help and Accessible View.

## Model

This follows the extension installation model: durable profile metadata owns marketplace identity/version/location while reconciliation observes the local installation. Customization records use the same record-versus-local separation. One deliberate difference is that customization resource identity still includes version because this marketplace does not yet expose an update flow.


## Production hardening review

A line-by-line architecture, correctness, lifecycle, accessibility, and test review found and resolved 12 initial issues before this draft is ready for review. Five additional inline review findings were also fixed and resolved:

- Split persistence/validation and complete skill package operations into focused internal modules; the public install service now owns orchestration and reconciliation.
- Store each deterministic SHA-256 installation slot independently, avoiding cross-window lost updates and bounding record count, individual/aggregate bytes, fields, and skill manifests.
- Persist immutable skill and plugin Git revisions. Repair uses the existing commit-aware source adapter and rechecks revisions before restoring content.
- Reconcile only relevant owner records and affected skill files; unrelated plugin/MCP events no longer rescan every skill manifest.
- Distinguish missing files from verification errors, keep uninstall available, and make Repair eligibility respect source enablement, AI disablement, and plugin policy.
- Preserve destination-group identity, rebase exact targets when provider URIs move, and expose recorded resources even when a catalog entry disappears.
- Fix stale target notifications, plugin uninstall races, incomplete-repair success, accessible state announcements, picker documentation, and the prior formatter CI failure.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- full repository hygiene
- changed-file ESLint
- Discover CSS Stylelint
- 131 focused marketplace installation and Discover tests
- Dev-build UI scenario on macOS arm64 covering public-feed search, exact install, same-name separation, missing-file detection, non-destructive repair, and confirmed uninstall

## Video evidence

Captioned Dev-build scenario (VS Code 1.140.0, macOS arm64): 5/5 steps passed.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ad1837e-d415-4d7e-890b-c6932c5ee92a

The recording demonstrates public-feed search, independent same-name entries, exact install association, missing-file detection through VS Code’s Explorer deletion path, immutable repair preserving an extra local file, and confirmed uninstall.

## Follow-ups addressed

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337110#discussion_r4089215563
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337110#discussion_r4089215561
