pull_requests.title: test: cache WSL kernel installer for Windows smoke jobs
pull_requests.body:
## Why
Windows Electron smoke jobs repeatedly fail before WSL import when the WSL kernel MSI host cannot be resolved (for example, [476491](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=476491), [476726](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=476726), [476731](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=476731), and [476751](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=476751)). Nearby [476742](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=476742) downloaded it successfully, so a warm cache can avoid this intermittent dependency.

## What
- Restore the latest verified WSL kernel installer from a daily Azure Pipeline or GitHub Actions cache before WSL setup.
- On a cold cache, download the MSI normally; with an older cache, install the cached MSI and refresh it concurrently with WSL setup. Verify Microsoft Authenticode signatures before use or cache replacement.
- Keep the cache outside the run-owned WSL directory so cleanup does not remove it. New daily entries save after a successful job; stale Azure cache entries expire after inactivity.

## Validation
- PowerShell parser and both YAML files parse; `git diff --check` passed.
- Local isolated checks covered cold cache, exact hit, previous-day refresh, offline refresh with cached install, and invalid cache fallback.
- Did not run hosted WSL import or full smoke tests locally. The first cold build still requires network access; cache upload requires a successful job.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/issues/3925

Restore a verified installer across builds, refresh it when a new daily cache key is created, and keep the per-run WSL cleanup separate from cached downloads. This lets warm jobs proceed when the installer host intermittently fails DNS resolution.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: show live HydraFusion phase work in its phase chat
pull_requests.body:
Shows live HydraFusion phase work in each phase's chat. Needs runtime [github/copilot-agent-runtime#21218](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/21218), which `main` now has via SDK `1.0.15-preview.3` (#337821).

## Background

While a phase runs, #21218 sends a provisional copy (`ephemeral`, no `commitId`) of each `assistant.message`, `tool.execution_start`, and `tool.execution_complete`. The winning phase then replays with a `commitId` and the same ids. A losing phase never replays. Rendering every event naively shows a rejected draft as the response and duplicates the winning phase's text and tool rows.

## Changes

- **Live:** provisional messages and tool calls go to their phase chat as they happen, including the phase's own answer. Review phases still show their critique on completion.
- **Commit:** routed per model call. A call that ends in tool requests is phase work, and anything already shown is skipped. A call that ends without them is the answer and becomes the response. Only the winning phase commits.
- **Chunks:** earlier chunks of a model call wait for its last chunk. This also fixes text before a reasoning boundary leaking into the response.
- **Unchanged:** approvals and client tools are raised inside the phase chat, and accounting still counts committed work only.

## Testing

- Unit tests (1063) and Copilot Agent Host E2E (198) pass. New tests cover live streaming, a rejected phase, chunk routing, review phases, and approvals.
- Manual, in Code OSS on runtime `1.0.89-3`: Single and Cascade runs with file edits and terminal commands. Phase pills streamed live, approvals appeared inside the phase, each tool row showed once, and only the winning answer reached the response.

## Known limitations

- A losing phase's chat is gone after a reload, because provisional copies aren't saved.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: expand E2E workspace and lifecycle coverage
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Expand meaningful bundled-provider E2E coverage without changing production behavior:
- Multi-root peer folder scoping, runtime working-directory execution, restart persistence, delegated folders, and additional worktree ownership/cleanup.
- Automation cancellation, durable failed runs, request deduplication, and new-run definition updates across providers.
- Synchronized input draft clearing, explicit answer replacement, cancellation, and follow-up turns.
- Real Git checkout safety: dirty-worktree errors, stash/commit preservation, index-lock recovery, and deleted target branches.
- MCP application side channels through real Copilot/Codex runtimes: tool schemas, structured arguments, concurrent clients, binary/HTML resources, errors, and stop/start.

pull_requests.title: chat: add user-perceived time to first progress telemetry
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Add `chat.userPerceivedTimeToFirstProgress` to measure UI submission entry to first meaningful progress while continuously visible, including Agents window new-session and new-chat composers.

- Qualifying progress is non-whitespace markdown/reasoning or a visible tool invocation (live or serialized).
- Hiding the widget/document ends measurement as `hidden` without stopping the request. Initially hidden/background submissions are ineligible, showing again never resumes timing, and focus loss alone does not end it.
- Agents composers hand off the original timer to the exact created response; session preparation and navigation are included without restarting the clock.
- Completion waits two animation frames and rechecks visibility/session identity. This is a render-boundary approximation, not a physical input or paint timestamp. Fork navigation is not measured.
- Queued sends are excluded from latency samples in both submission paths. Measurement has no duration cap and ends on progress or lifecycle events; provider/request timeouts are unchanged.
- Optional `[ChatTTFP] start` / `end` diagnostics use trace-level window logs.

## Event schema

Kusto: `monacoworkbench/chat.userperceivedtimetofirstprogress`. Ingested field names are lowercase.

### Measures

| Field | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timeToFirstProgress` | ms | Duration to the render boundary; success only. |
| `timeToTermination` | ms | Duration until an unsuccessful observation ends; absent on success. |
| `windowVisible` | 0/1 | Source window visibility when the observation ends. |
| `windowFocused` | 0/1 | Source window focus when the observation ends. |

Missing timings are omitted, not zero. There is no full-response-duration measure.

### Properties

All properties are strings; context fields are omitted when unavailable.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | `success`, `cancelled`, `error`, `completedWithoutProgress`, `notDispatched`, `queued`, `navigated`, `hidden`, or `disposed`. |
| `requestPhase` | `first`, `followup`, or `unknown`, from this request's position in chat history; not a cold/warm process indicator. |
| `firstProgressKind` | `text`, `reasoning`, or `tool`; present only on successful observations. |
| `interactionKind` | `turn` (chat submission). |
| `requestId` | Submitted request ID. |
| `chatSessionId` | Session/peer-chat ID, excluding remote Agent Host connection authorities. |
| `agent` | Chat agent/participant ID. |
| `agentExtensionId` | Contributing extension ID. |
| `location` | Chat surface. |
| `model` | Selected model ID; Auto is not replaced with the resolved model. |
| `permissionLevel` | Selected tool-approval level. |
| `chatMode` | Telemetry mode name or ID. |
| `sessionType` | Normalized session type. |
| `harness` | Provider for remote Agent Host sessions; otherwise omitted. |

Unlike `agentHost.firstResponse` (#336704), this starts in the shared UI path and includes a render boundary rather than stopping at first response text.

## Validation

Client typecheck, transpilation, targeted ESLint, and whitespace checks passed. **141 focused tests per browser engine** (Chromium/WebKit/Firefox) and **138 Electron tests** cover queue exclusion, request phase, progress kind, continuous visibility, composer handoff, attribution, and cleanup.

For harness comparisons, use successful observations and compare matching request phases, progress kinds, and selected models. See the Checks tab for live CI status.

ref: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/266055

## Summary

Render native Copilot and Codex image generation through the shared Chat image presentation.

- Map Copilot's runtime-owned `image_generation` events into existing AHP tool-call actions, preserving embedded image results and optional image-engine attribution across live and restored history.
- Reuse the renderer for Codex's native `imageGeneration` items, including its final revised prompt. Codex generation, authentication, and provider-enablement logic are unchanged.
- Keep image generation standalone and chronological, outside thinking/tool groups. The expandable prompt/model row stays above the loading band and completed image, aligned with the tool icon.
- Use the selected Glyph Wave loading band and ASCII Resolve reveal. Honor reduced motion and high contrast, skip the reveal on restore, and reserve the adjacent Save action's space throughout the transition.
- Cache only natural dimensions to preserve row height and scroll position across virtualized remounts; the cache retains neither image bytes nor DOM. Embedded images use browser-native decoding.
- Handle overlapping generations, out-of-order completions, failure, cancellation, and restored galleries. Ordinary non-image tools retain their existing presentation.

No client-side image generator or development-only image tool is registered. Rendering can be tested with provider-shaped unit tests and Component Explorer fixtures; their sample PNG is a test asset, not a runtime asset. The unrelated extension whitespace change and test README expansion have been removed.

For a preview without model access:

```sh

npm run serve-out-rspack
```

Choose **Copilot** or **Codex** in the fixture properties, then **Complete Generation**. The fixture also supports delayed referenced images and follow-up turns. The other `chat/generatedImages` fixtures cover completion, failure, galleries, narrow layouts, and reduced motion.

Actual generation remains provider-owned and requires a compatible runtime/SDK and provider access. Codex retains its existing OpenAI/ChatGPT-sign-in gate.

- Copilot runtime counterpart: [github/copilot-agent-runtime#22394](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/22394), merged.

- No canonical AHP schema change is required. Image-engine metadata is an optional, validated extension; other hosts retain baseline rendering without it.

pull_requests.body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8971

## Problem

Responses on the HydraFusion model sometimes appeared stuck. Client tools (including tool search) invoked during a *provisional* Fusion phase never ran: the SDK handler awaited the client, the client waited for a `ChatToolCallStart`/`Ready` it never received, because the runtime held the phase's `tool.execution_start` back until commit. Only permission-gated tools escaped this (the permission path already surfaced them), so skip-permission / auto-approved client tools hung the turn.

Separately, phase tiles showed only a status pill — a phase's tool calls, intermediate text and review critique were invisible, so users couldn't tell what each phase actually did.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: fix background subagent lifecycle and recipient labels
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337339
Refs #335292

## Summary

- Preserve reusable child routing when a parent turn is cancelled, while keeping final chat/session disposal destructive and scoped to the correct parent.
- Retire execution-scoped Copilot child state through the existing completion cleanup so reuse works without a child-completed event and cannot inherit cancelled usage or Auto routing.
- Settle orphaned approvals rather than buffering indefinitely. Bound startup buffers to 1,000 signals or 30 seconds, keep failed-route suppression in a separate 1,000-entry LRU, and surface failed routing on the active parent. Correctly routed, displayed approvals are **not** timed out.
- Preserve reordered child signals when a background launch returns before child startup.
- Restore normal **inline subagent pills** with live observation: resumed activity, new tools and approvals stay attached to the original parent response after reopening the chat. Adopt existing tool snapshots without duplication and keep settled child history lazy until activity resumes.
- Show readable **write-agent recipient names**, including multi-recipient writes. Reuse names from lifecycle events, completion notifications and runtime task metadata in live/restored chats. Preserve raw routing IDs and the unknown-ID fallback.

The optional Subagents summary above the prompt and approval policy are unchanged.

## Why

Parent cancellation removed the host's routing identity while the SDK retained the reusable agent, stranding later progress and approvals. Restored inline pills also did not reactivate idle children or append newly emitted tools. The recipient-name lookup only learned names from start events, and multi-recipient writes had no targeted display label.

Focused regressions reproduced these failures before the corresponding fixes. The inline change targets the restored/reused cases of #335292 rather than introducing another surface.

## Live Copilot / AHP validation

Built with `npm run build-fast` and launched through `./scripts/code.sh` on macOS arm64 using Code OSS 1.140.0 dev, the real Copilot harness, GPT-5.4 mini, and AHP 0.9.0. No model or protocol responses were mocked.

- Created **Label Alpha** and **Label Beta** using `task` with **`mode: "background"`**.
- Verified `Write to agent Label Alpha` and `Write to agents Label Alpha, Label Beta` in both AHP ready/completed actions and the rendered accessible chat buttons.
- Verified write arguments still contain the exact SDK-generated IDs.
- Verified readable labels and both ordinary inline subagent links remain correct after renderer reload.
- The inline pill's **Validate Alpha label** is the task description of the background agent named **Label Alpha**; this was not a foreground-only test.

Screenshot caption: *Real background agents shown as ordinary inline subagent pills, with readable single- and multi-recipient write labels.*

## Automated validation

- Core lifecycle follow-up: 909 host/provider tests and 242 focused Chromium history/rendering/reconnect tests passed after syncing main.
- Recipient-label update: 880 focused display, history-mapper and provider tests passed. These counts overlap and should not be summed.
- Current development build, changed-file ESLint, commit hygiene and `git diff --check` passed.
- The latest full client type-check reports two existing `SinonFakeTimersConfig` errors in unchanged MCP/sticky-scroll test files; no changed-file diagnostics.
- Earlier CI failures were stabilized with a test-only pet-frame assertion matching elapsed-time frame skipping and the existing `deferPaint` option on the MCP provenance fixture. Code OSS and Component Fixtures passed at `68b72bf3de1`; CI for the new recipient-label commit is pending.

## Validation limits

The successful live scenario was submitted through the normal authenticated AHP endpoint and verified in the actual rendered window. An additional direct UI-send attempt was blocked by GitHub Copilot sign-in in the cloned test profile. Renderer reload was tested, not an Agent Host process restart. Notification-only name recovery is covered by automated tests.

This PR remains a draft.

pull_requests.title: Avoid diff editor work while scrolling collapsed multi-diff files
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337614

## Reproduction

Open `wangnan0916/ssh-forward` commit `c1798f2d3bc9055f864e1e8270b798fa836d4469` (58 changed files) from Source Control commit history. Collapse every file in the multi-diff view and scroll up and down through the file headers. The renderer stutters even though no diff content is open. Turning off `workbench.list.smoothScrolling` did not change the behavior. We reproduced this in the stable build and in an unpatched local source build.

## What the profile showed

The source-mapped renderer profile led to `DiffEditorItemTemplate` / `DiffEditorWidget` construction while scrolling collapsed headers. There were three related costs:

1. Acquiring a row template eagerly constructed a full `DiffEditorWidget`, bound its diff model, and performed editor layout/scroll work, including for a collapsed file. The collapsed header did not need any of that editor work.
2. `CompressedVirtualizedScrollView._render` visited items in list order. During a fast upward scroll it could acquire templates for newly visible rows before releasing rows that had left the viewport, so reuse was missed within that render pass.
3. The shared template pool retained only five unused templates. A full viewport of lightweight collapsed headers can contain roughly 26 rows in this reproduction, so moving between distant positions repeatedly rebuilt headers and toolbars. Disposed template roots also remained in the DOM.

## Change

- Construct `DiffEditorWidget` when an expanded file actually needs it. Collapsed and binary rows skip diff model binding and editor layout/scroll work. A reveal with a range on a still-collapsed file also avoids creating a hidden editor.
- Release invisible row bindings before acquiring templates for newly visible rows, allowing reuse in the same scroll update.
- Allow the multi-diff view to retain up to 30 unused lightweight header templates and up to five templates that have allocated diff editors. Reuse an idle editor template for an expanded file before allocating another editor. The default limit for other `VirtualizedItemManager` users remains five.
- Remove a disposed template's root from the DOM and preserve selections when an expanded file is collapsed and recycled.
- Restore the current horizontal offset after a lazily created or rebound editor has been laid out.

## Local evidence

| Manual scroll capture, 58 files collapsed | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread long tasks during span | 13 | 0 |
| Longest long task | 642 ms | none |
| Largest `requestAnimationFrame` interval | 649 ms | 17.7 ms |
| Wheel-to-zero-delay-timer scheduling delay, p95 | 992 ms | 9.5 ms |

Both recordings were made with a trackpad. These are two individual manual captures, not controlled benchmark averages: the before recording spans 4.3 seconds and 28 wheel events, while the after recording spans 7.2 seconds and 185 wheel events. Those spans describe how long each manual scroll recording lasted, not how long the UI took to complete the same work. The timer delay and animation-frame interval are responsiveness proxies, not presentation latency. The after capture was taken after the primary collapsed-scroll fix and before the follow-up changes for expanded-editor reuse and horizontal offset. In that capture, all files remained collapsed, zero diff editor DOM nodes were allocated, and the user confirmed that scrolling felt smooth.

Supporting files:

- [Sanitized renderer trace (JSON.gz)](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32593143/Trace-collapsed-commit-renderer-sanitized.json.gz): a renderer-only excerpt of the original source-mapped recording. Source maps remain available for stack attribution; embedded source text, local paths, email addresses, and unrelated processes were removed.
- [Before and after scroll captures (JSON)](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32593145/Scroll-captures-before-after.json): relative event timings behind the table above.

## Before / after videos

Both videos show commit `26aad04d5a878596983c9b695b67d291b2554a42` in `wangnan0916/ssh-forward` (95 changed files), with all file diffs collapsed. These are visual demonstrations recorded separately from the 58-file performance captures above; their durations and manual scroll gestures differ.

### Before — `vscode-collapsed-scroll-before.mov`

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d0fd282-34ad-412f-aa02-0d59157ae4bb

### After — `vscode-collapsed-scroll-after.mov`

Recorded in the local Code - OSS build with this PR's fix.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f3029ea-dade-4054-a2ba-92917268a77d

Related: #240181 tracks lazy text-model loading, a broader concern. This change addresses renderer work while scrolling fully collapsed file headers.

pull_requests.title: chat: check nested subagent calls against the caller's allowlist
pull_requests.body: Fixes #335257 ## Problem Custom agents can limit which subagents they call with the `agents:` frontmatter list. #331442 (fixing #331002) enforced that list in `runSubagent`, but it always resolved the "current agent" from `model.getRequests().at(-1)`. That is the top-level request, because subagent requests reuse the session and are never added to the chat model. So in a chain A → B → C, B's call to C was checked against **A's** list and rejected with `Requested agent 'C' is not allowed by the current agent.` Any nested call two or more levels deep failed. Enabling `chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents` doesn't help, since it only limits nesting depth. ## Fix - **Identify the caller.** Tool invocation tokens now carry the id of the request they were issued for (`IToolInvocationContext.requestId`, set in `ChatAgentRequest.to`). The token is opaque to extensions (`ChatParticipantToolToken` is `never`) and is passed back unchanged on every `vscode.lm.invokeTool` call, so each subagent's tool calls carry its own request id. `prepareToolInvocation` receives it as `IToolInvocationPreparationContext.invocationRequestId`. There are no API changes. - **Track running subagents.** `RunSubagentTool` keeps a map of the subagents it started, keyed by their request id (the `callId` of the `runSubagent` call that started them). An entry is added right before `invokeAgent` and removed in the same `finally` that decrements the nesting depth. - **Validate against the caller.** Both `prepareToolInvocation` and `invoke` use the calling subagent's instructions and allowlist. Calls made in the top-level request fall back to the previous behavior. - **Why the request id.** The caller is identified by request id rather than `subAgentInvocationId`. That id comes from the model's tool call id, which is not guaranteed to be unique (some models reuse tool call ids), so parallel subagents could resolve to the wrong caller. Unchanged from #331442: top-level enforcement in both `prepareToolInvocation` and `invoke`, each subagent carrying its own `agents:` list, and passing the allowlist to automatic instruction collection. ### Behavior change for nested calls without `agentName` When a nested subagent calls `runSubagent` without `agentName`, the new subagent is now a copy of the **calling subagent**: its instructions, allowlist, model, tools and frontmatter hooks. Previously it silently became a copy of the top-level agent. That let a subagent step outside its own allowlist, and with only the allowlist fixed, the copy would have run on a model that is neither the subagent's own nor the Auto default from #333663. An explicit `model` still goes through the usual checks. ## Tests 7 new tests, all of which fail without the fix: - `runSubagentTool.test.ts`: - 3 and 4 levels of nesting. - The caller's allowlist decides, not the top-level agent's. - Parallel subagents started by tool calls with the same id each resolve their own caller. - What a copy inherits: instructions, allowlist, model, tools and hooks. - A finished or failed subagent is no longer treated as the caller. - `languageModelToolsService.test.ts`: the invocation request id reaches `prepareToolInvocation`. - `extHostTypeConverter.test.ts`: the tool invocation token carries the request id. The 3 suites (205 tests) pass, as do the broader chat tools (455), API chat and language model (87), and chat model and service (457) tests. `npm run typecheck-client` and ESLint are clean. The change was reviewed iteratively with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5. Their findings are addressed: colliding tool call ids, copies running on the wrong model, and copies losing hooks. Both final passes found no significant issues. ## Manual validation in Code OSS Agents: Coordinator (`agents: [Worker]`) → Worker (`agents: [Specialist]`) → Specialist, plus a Forbidden agent, with `chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents` enabled. | Scenario | Result | |---|---| | Without the fix: Coordinator → Worker → Specialist | ❌ `Requested agent 'Specialist' is not allowed by the current agent.` (the bug reproduces) | | With the fix: same chain | ✅ `SPECIALIST_OK`, 3 nested levels | | Worker → Forbidden | ✅ rejected; Forbidden never ran | | Coordinator → Forbidden or Specialist directly (the #331002 check) | ✅ rejected | | Worker copies itself (no `agentName`) → Specialist, 4 levels | ✅ the copy runs as Worker; `SPECIALIST_OK` | | Final build smoke test with a different model | ✅ | ## Not changed - A copy of the **top-level** agent (no `agentName` and no calling subagent) still doesn't get that agent's frontmatter hooks. That was already the case before this change, so it's left for a follow-up. - A copy reports its caller's model selection source in the `chat.subagentModelSelection` telemetry event. ## Functional Subagents

auto_merge.commit_title: chat: check nested subagent calls against the caller's allowlist (#337611)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* chat: check nested subagent calls against the caller's allowlist

RunSubagentTool resolved the current agent from the session's last
request, which is always the top-level agent because subagent requests
are not added to the chat model. A subagent's calls were therefore
checked against the top-level agent's `agents:` allowlist, so calls
two or more levels deep were rejected (regressed by #331442).

Tool invocation tokens now carry the id of the request they were issued
for. RunSubagentTool tracks running subagents by request id, and uses
the calling subagent's instructions and allowlist for nested calls. A
subagent that runs the tool without agentName now gets a copy of
itself, with its model, tools and hooks, instead of a copy of the
top-level agent.

Fixes #335257

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: model real tool enablement in the nested subagent copy test

The fake tools service only returned the tools an agent lists, while the
real service also returns every other known tool as disabled. Because
RunSubagentTool keeps an explicit `runSubagent: false`, the copy test
exercised a subagent calling runSubagent without having the tool, which
production does not allow. Mirror the real enablement map and list
runSubagent in the calling subagent's tools.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: fix chat-folder separation review findings
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #337594. It fixes the Copilot review comments on that PR and the findings from a full review of the chat-folder separation feature (steps 1–7). Chats in one session can work in different folders; these fixes keep each chat's surfaces and host work scoped to its own folders.

## Agent Merge and folder keys
- **Host folder keys:** the host publishes its folder keys and scope ids (`workingDirectoryKeys` / `workingDirectoryScopeIds` in session `_meta`) for every session and chat folder. The client uses them instead of recomputing keys with its own path-case rules. This fixes a Linux remote host used from a macOS or Windows client, where per-folder GitHub info, Agent Merge settings and restored Git state were lost, or distinct folders were merged. State persisted in the old format still resolves through the local fallback.
- **Older hosts:** a host that doesn't publish the keys doesn't support per-folder Agent Merge. For it, the client writes the legacy session-folder setting and rejects peer-folder writes.
- **Peer chats:** the Agent Merge changeset is advertised on the chat that owns the folder's Agent Merge, with a chat-owned Compare template, and the client follows that chat's turns. The session-level reader no longer returns another folder's state.
- **Folder loading:** Agent Merge state observables react when a peer chat's folder finishes loading, and change events fire after the full state snapshot is applied.
- **Session folder identity:** the session folder resolves to the session's own GitHub info, so single-folder main chats keep the session workspace.

## Changesets, checkpoints, Git and PR state
- **Session Changes:** always computed over all session folders, whatever supplies the list summary. Lifecycle refresh schedules it only for session owners.
- **Checkpoints:** history is tracked per repository. Turn and Compare lookups use the chat's own checkout, so terminal-only changes in another folder are captured.
- **Pull request attachment:** repository and branch come from the same folder-scoped owner.
- **Stale branch state:** the default chat's Git state is cleared, live and persisted, when its repository goes away.
- **PR status:** a reused status watch updates its folder descriptor when the representative chat changes.

## Session and chat lifecycle
- **Pinning a peer:** keeps the peer's provider backing data.
- **Forks:** copy the source chat's own folders.
- **Removing a folder:** rejected while a chat is still scoped to it.
- **Resume:** resuming an additional checkout uses that checkout's own worktree record.
- **Quick chats:** `create_session` with the current session and a workspace is rejected from a quick chat, with an actionable error. The model-facing descriptions are unchanged.
- **GitHub state migration:** the legacy row is deleted only once its state is migrated, and one removal mechanism is used. Persisted `__proto__` keys are rejected.

## Agents Window
- **Chat actions:** input banner actions (Fix Checks, comments) go to the chat that shows the pull request. Tasks run, and are added and configured, in the active chat's folder.
- **Session Changes:** available again in multi-folder sessions, rendered with the whole session workspace.
- **Terminal:** visibility and active terminal follow the active chat's folder.
- **Sessions list:** peer chat rows and hovers no longer take the main worktree's pending state. The hidden folder row takes no space. Height reconciliation no longer loads detailed state for offscreen chats.

## Not changed
- The old `github` session meta key isn't restored for mixed client/host versions, as the plan decided.
- The two definitions of "session folder" (the default chat's first folder vs the session summary's first folder) stay as they are; they only differ in rare cases.
- Other folders keep baselining pre-existing pull requests regardless of isolation. This is now documented and tested as intended.

## Validation
- Typecheck and eslint are clean.
- 7,917 Agent Host tests, 4,505 sessions tests and 1,728 workbench agent-session tests pass.

pull_requests.title: customEditor: forget failed documents so they can be opened again
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #250622 Fixes #268301 Fixes #231231 ### Problem When creating a custom editor document fails, the resource is stuck until the window is reloaded. This happens when an extension's `openCustomDocument` throws, or when the text model of a custom text editor can't be loaded (for example, the file doesn't exist or `FileSystemProvider.readFile` fails). - `CustomEditorModelManager` kept the rejected model promise. Reopening the resource, even after closing the tab, replayed the same error without asking the extension again. - **Try Again** in the error placeholder, and the automatic reload of the "file not found" placeholder once the file exists, reopen the *same* editor input. Its webview resolution was `@memoize`d, so those could never work either. ### Fix - **`CustomEditorModelManager`** - Forgets a model when its promise rejects, but only if the map still holds that entry. - `getAllModels` skips models that fail to resolve, and `disposeAllModelsFor*` no longer causes unhandled rejections for pending models. - Releasing a reference only disposes and forgets the model if its entry is still the current one. Before, releasing a reference to a model that `disposeAllModelsForResource` had already disposed (after its file was deleted) disposed it a second time. That sent another `$disposeCustomDocument`, which could dispose the replacement document, and it also dropped the replacement from the map. - **`MainThreadCustomEditors`** - The resolver rethrows document creation failures instead of swallowing them, so the editor shows the real error, for example "The editor could not be opened because the file was not found." Before, the error only reached the editor because `CustomEditorInput.resolve()` re-read the cached rejected promise. Only evicting the failed model would turn that into a generic `Assertion Failed` error and lose the file-not-found handling. - The webview handle is kept per input, so resolving the same editor again doesn't register its webview twice. - Failures of the extension's `resolveCustomEditor` are handled as before. - **`LazilyResolvedWebviewEditorInput.resolve()`** - Replaced `@memoize` with an explicitly shared resolve promise that is reset after a failure, so Try Again and the placeholder reload resolve the editor again. - Only the cancellation caused by disposing the input is ignored. Other cancellations are retryable failures, for example a shared document canceled by closing another editor, or the extension host going away. - The webview panel serializer resolver never rejects, so restored webview panels behave as before. ### Behavior | Scenario | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Open fails, close the tab, open again (issue steps) | Same error; extension not called | Extension asked again; editor opens | | Open fails, click **Try Again** | Error dialog; extension not called | Extension asked again; editor opens in place | | Markdown preview editor on a missing file, create the file, close and reopen (#268301) | Still "file not found" | Preview shown | | Markdown preview editor on a missing file, create the file (placeholder auto-reload) | Still "file not found" | Preview shown | ### Tests I wrote the baseline tests first, against the unchanged code; they pass before and after. The `#250622` tests fail without the fix. - `customEditorModelManager.test.ts`: reference counting, lookups, and dispose-all (baseline). Failed models are forgotten, everyone waiting on a pending model sees its failure, and a stale failure or reference doesn't remove a newer model. `getAllModels` skips failed models. - `webviewWorkbenchService.test.ts`: `LazilyResolvedWebviewEditorInput` resolves once for concurrent and later calls, and ignores the cancellation from disposing it (baseline). It resolves again after a failure or after a cancellation that didn't come from disposing it. - `mainThreadCustomEditors.test.ts`: runs `MainThreadCustomEditors` with `CustomEditorInput` and `CustomEditorDiffInput` against a fake extension host. - Baseline: the document is created before the editor is resolved, and the `$resolveCustomEditor` failure path is unchanged. - After a failure, a new editor and Try Again both ask the extension again, and Try Again reuses the webview handle. - An editor whose shared document was canceled by closing another editor can be retried, and so can an inline diff whose original document failed to open. `npm run typecheck-client` and eslint are clean, and the 1139 unit tests in the related suites pass (`api/test/browser`, `customEditor`, `webview`, `webviewPanel`, `webviewView`, `services/editor`, `sessions/contrib/layout`). ### UI validation I ran a UI scenario against the dev build of this branch (Windows x64, VS Code 1.140.0 Dev). It uses a repro extension whose custom editor's `openCustomDocument` throws on the first attempt for each file, and the built-in Markdown preview custom editor (`vscode.markdown.preview.editor`) on files that don't exist yet. All 10 steps pass. On `main`, the same scenario fails at the reopen, Try Again, and both Markdown steps.
Repro extension (flaky provider) ```js const attempts = new Map(); vscode.window.registerCustomEditorProvider('repro250622.flaky', { async openCustomDocument(uri) { const attempt = (attempts.get(uri.toString()) ?? 0) + 1; attempts.set(uri.toString(), attempt); if (attempt === 1) { throw new Error(`Simulated failure while opening ${uri.path}. The next attempt will succeed.`); } return { uri, dispose() { } }; }, async resolveCustomEditor(document, webviewPanel) { webviewPanel.webview.html = `

${document.uri.path} opened

`; } }); // Built-in custom text editor on a file that does not exist yet: vscode.commands.executeCommand('vscode.openWith', vscode.Uri.joinPath(workspaceFolder, 'missing.md'), 'vscode.markdown.preview.editor'); ```
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26ca0e8b-744e-4363-b510-37a39d2fd19c ### Known follow-ups (not changed here) - **The extension's `resolveCustomEditor` throws.** The resolver disposes the only model reference, so `CustomEditorInput.resolve()` hits an assertion and shows the generic placeholder. Closing and reopening the editor works; Try Again doesn't. This PR doesn't change that path. - **Retrying in place after the extension host restarts.** The per-webview listeners that the previous extension host's `MainThreadWebviews` registered are not disposed with it, so a retried editor gets a second set; for example, a link click is handled twice. For side-by-side custom diffs, a side still waiting in the previous extension host can make the retry hang until the diff is closed. Closing and reopening works in both cases. A fix would make `MainThreadWebviews` own its per-webview subscriptions, and settle pending side-by-side resolutions when `MainThreadCustomEditors` is disposed.

auto_merge.commit_title: customEditor: forget failed documents so they can be opened again (#337607)
auto_merge.commit_message:
When creating a custom editor document failed (an extension's openCustomDocument threw, or the text model of a custom text editor could not be loaded), CustomEditorModelManager kept the rejected model promise. Every later attempt to open the resource got the same error back without asking the extension again, until the window was reloaded (#250622, #268301).

- CustomEditorModelManager forgets models that fail to resolve, skips them in getAllModels, and only lets an entry remove itself from the map so that stale references no longer dispose or drop a newer model.
- The custom editor resolver rethrows document creation failures so the editor shows the error, and reuses the webview handle when the same editor is resolved again.
- LazilyResolvedWebviewEditorInput resolves again after a failed resolve instead of memoizing the failure, so Try Again and the file-not-found placeholder reload work in place. Only the cancellation caused by disposing the input is ignored.

Part of #337536.

Adds `agentHostPolicySupport`, which gives every enterprise policy an Agent Host status: `enforced`, `partial`, `notEnforced`, or `notApplicable`. The export writes this status into `policyData.jsonc` as `agentHost.status`, and gaps link to their tracking issues. This list is the burndown for Local → Agent Host parity. It will also drive the Local fallback in #337537.

| Status | Count | Policies |
|---|---:|---|
| `enforced` | 21 | `BrowserChatTools`, `ChatAgentExtensionTools`, `ChatAgentHostCustomTerminalTool`, `ChatAgentSandboxAllowNetwork`, `ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands`, `ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations`, `ChatDefaultModel`, `ChatEditorPreferCopilotHarness`, `ChatToolsAutoApprove`, `Claude3PIntegration`, `Codex3PIntegration`, `CopilotOtelCaptureContent`, `CopilotOtelEnabled`, `CopilotOtelEndpoint`, `CopilotOtelOtlpProtocol`, `CopilotOtelOutfile`, `CopilotOtelProtocol`, `CopilotOtelResourceAttributes`, `CopilotOtelServiceName`, `CopilotSessionSync`, `TelemetryLevel` |
| `partial` | 14 | `ChatAgentMode`, `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled`, `ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly`, `ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly`, `ChatAllowedMcpServers`, `ChatDeniedMcpServers`, `ChatEnabledPlugins`, `ChatExtraMarketplaces`, `ChatPluginsEnabled`, `ChatStrictMarketplaces`, `ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization`, `ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove`, `CopilotOtelCaptureIdentity`, `CopilotOtelHeaders` |
| `notEnforced` | 8 | `ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains`, `ChatAgentDeniedNetworkDomains`, `ChatAgentNetworkFilter`, `ChatAgentSandboxAllowAutoApprove`, `ChatHooks`, `ChatMCP`, `ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval`, `McpEnterpriseManagedAuthIdp` |
| `notApplicable` | 15 | `AgentsVoice`, `AllowedExtensions`, `CopilotNextEditSuggestions`, `CopilotReviewAgent`, `CopilotReviewSelection`, `DictationEnabled`, `DictationLLMCleanup`, `DictationModel`, `EnableFeedback`, `ExtensionGalleryAuthProvider`, `ExtensionGalleryServiceUrl`, `ExtensionsAutoUpdate`, `ExtensionsAutoUpdateDelay`, `McpGalleryServiceUrl`, `UpdateMode` |
| **Total** | **58** | |

- `npm run export-policy-data` fails if a policy has no status. Unit and build tests fail if the list and `policyData.jsonc` don't match.
- Statuses are for the Copilot agent on a local host. When enforcement depends on how the policy is delivered (VS Code policy vs. Copilot managed settings), the weaker status is used. Comments on each entry note differences for Claude, Codex, and remote hosts.
- No behavior changes. The generated ADMX/ADML, macOS, and Linux policy files are byte-identical with and without the new field, and the docs generator reads only the fields it needs.
- Also fixes the merge step so that the field order in `policyData.jsonc` no longer depends on which entrypoint (Workbench or Agents window) declares `referencedSettings`. Without this fix, the export's check mode failed.

pull_requests.title: linux: add launcher migration notices and shortcut sanity checks
pull_requests.body:
Related to #337589.

## Problem

#332935 renamed the DEB/RPM desktop entry IDs in 1.139.0. Existing favorites, pinned launchers, and saved desktop/MIME references can still point at the removed filenames.

## Changes

- Keep only the canonical reverse-DNS application entry and hidden URL handler. **Do not ship legacy desktop files or an additional application shortcut.** Saved references require manual migration.
- Add a compressed Debian `NEWS.Debian` notice and RPM `%doc` NEWS, both linking to the release-note migration guidance. Debian frontends using apt-listchanges can display NEWS; this depends on the user's installation/configuration. RPM NEWS is packaged documentation, not a guaranteed upgrade notification.
- Use a fixed Debian NEWS version newer than the affected Stable package (`1.139.0-1790100840`), rather than generating a new entry for every build.
- Keep desktop generation shared within the existing Linux packaging gulpfile. Snap packaging is unchanged.

## Release sanity coverage

- **DEB/RPM:** validate the canonical application and hidden URL-handler entries, executable targets, application window identity, handler arguments/MIME type, and visibility. Exercise the one application entry's parsed `Exec` command by opening a unique file in the isolated test window. These container checks do not require GTK/GIO or a full desktop shell and do not simulate saved favorites.
- **Windows installers:** explicitly request the Desktop shortcut, validate Start Menu and Desktop `.lnk` targets in the appropriate user/common folders, and exercise the shortcuts through ShellExecute.
- **macOS bundles:** validate executable/type metadata and exercise LaunchServices with the exact downloaded ZIP/DMG bundle.
- Preserve download-only behavior and archive/server exclusions. Snap retains direct-launch coverage. Keep installer/DMG cleanup on failures.

## Companion release notes

microsoft/vscode-docs#10378 documents the breaking change and manual migration. **Publish it before packages containing the notices ship**, so their link resolves:
https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_139#_linux-desktop-launcher-names

## Validation

- Build tooling typecheck, sanity compile, targeted ESLint, and whitespace checks passed.
- Exercised the actual desktop/NEWS generation streams for Stable, Insiders, and OSS: two canonical desktop entries and the expected notice paths.
- Parsed rendered Debian NEWS and verified version ordering and matching release-note links.
- Built and inspected a minimal DEB fixture with native `dpkg-deb`, confirming the generated compressed NEWS and exactly two canonical desktop files survive packaging.
- Previously verified Windows shortcut argument forwarding and uninstall cleanup for all four installer registrations when post-install validation fails.

Full installed-product sanity runs across Linux, Windows, and macOS, native RPM packaging, and a real KDE upgrade remain release/CI validation; they were not run locally.

pull_requests.title: chat: Add Copilot connectors as an authenticated customization source
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #337110. Adds an independently gated, authenticated Copilot Connectors source to the unified customization marketplace and MCP management. This replaces the closed #337372, whose designer-branch base was deleted when #337347 merged. The branch incorporates the current marketplace base; with both feeds off, the original Overview and legacy management catalogs remain available. Enabling either feed shows Discover.

- Keep connector discovery and sign-in separate from anonymous GitHub Feed IPC. Desktop connector requests use a scoped native channel with typed operations, bounded responses, cancellation, and per-request credentials; web retains the workbench request path.

pull_requests.title: sessions: run Agent Merge per chat folder and present multi-folder sessions
pull_requests.body:
Continues chat-folder separation in the Agents Window: chats in one session can work in different folders, and everything a chat shows or does is scoped to its own folders.

## Agent Merge per folder

Agent Merge now runs separately for each folder a chat works in, instead of once per session.

- **Host:** runs Agent Merge separately for each folder, each with its own settings, bound pull request, feedback watermark and repair budget. Repair turns and notices go to the chat that turned Agent Merge on (else the first chat in that folder; the default chat for the session folder). Repairs run concurrently per chat, and elevated approvals stay applied while any folder runs. Settings from earlier versions are read as the session folder's and migrated on first write.
- **Client:** Agent Merge actions, context keys and the chat input's pull request pill follow the folder the active chat works in. Session-wide surfaces (sessions list, blocked sessions) keep the session folder, matching the pull request they show.
- **Hardening (from reviews):**
  - **Client writes:** a client writes only the folder it changes, by working directory. The host merges the write into the other folders and derives the key itself, so a stale client copy can't undo host changes, and keys match across platforms. The host drops entries for folders or chats outside the session.
  - **Host writes:** lifecycle writes re-read current state and write only host-owned state. A config replacement no longer overwrites Agent Merge settings.
  - **Tool authorization:** Agent Merge tools act for the invoking chat, and only the chat running a repair turn can use its authorization.
  - **Lifecycle:** turning a folder off, or creating a pull request with Agent Merge, starts fresh. A folder no chat works in any more turns Agent Merge off with a reason. Removing a chat ends its repair turn and moves its pending notices to the default chat.

## Multi-folder presentation and restore

- **Restore:** the host persists the latest Git state for each chat's working-directory scope, so chats in other folders show their own branch state right after a restore.
- **Session hover:** in a multi-folder session, it summarizes every workspace, its changes and pull requests. A chat's hover shows its own folder, branch changes and pull requests, and the sessions list shows chat rows accordingly.
- **Changes view and banners:** the Changes view hides Session Changes in multi-folder sessions, and the input banners follow the active chat's folder.

## Notes for reviewers

- Mixed client and host versions are not handled for the new per-folder Agent Merge settings. An older remote host ignores them, and an older client stops seeing Agent Merge once the host migrates the old format.
- Follow-ups:
  - Session creation still copies Agent Merge keys from the client request. The old host-owned key was already copied before this change.
  - Folders that differ only in path case on a Linux host collide on the client.

## Validation

- Typecheck, eslint and hygiene are clean.
- 7,816 Agent Host tests, 4,499 sessions tests and 1,714 workbench agent-session tests pass.
- New tests cover per-folder reads and writes, host-side merging, tool authorization per chat, chat removal, lifecycle resets, and folders without chats.

pull_requests.title: managed settings: keep policy through transient refresh failures
pull_requests.body:
Copilot's OTel reload notification (reworked in #336701) exposed a managed-settings refresh regression from #330896. Enterprise users see "Copilot OTel endpoint will change to http://localhost:4318 after reload." every few hours, especially after idle, and reloading clears chat.

## Cause

Since #330896, a cached server-managed-settings response expires one hour after the last successful fetch. If a refresh fails after that (no response, 401/403, 429, 5xx, malformed), the policy is dropped rather than kept. A policy-backed OTel endpoint then reverts to its default and the notification appears. The next successful fetch restores the policy, so it keeps switching back and forth. Every other server-managed control switches back and forth in the same way, so for the length of the gap their restrictions are silently lifted.

## Change

Keep the policy unless the service answers affirmatively that it should change. A failed refresh without `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` now keeps the last successful response, however old, with its original timestamp. The failure therefore doesn't count as a refresh, and the next poll or focus retries. A 401/403 is treated as a failure because it can be temporary, for example while a token refreshes.

This keeps #330896's fix that a failure never renews the cache timestamp, and reverts only its dropping of stale policy. Before #330896, failures also kept the previous policy, but they renewed the timestamp.

These still behave as before:
- A 200 replaces the policy; a 404 or 466 clears it.
- Sign-out, or an account or scope change, clears or stops reusing the policy.
- `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` still fails closed.

## Follow-up

- A thrown session lookup error still makes `getDefaultAccountForAuthenticationProvider` return `null`, so `setDefaultAccount(null)` clears the policy without applying this retention. This path predates #330896 and changes account availability, so it needs a separate PR.
- `managedSettingsActive` (set when the server returns settings that no VS Code policy uses) is never cleared once set. This bug existed before this PR and will be fixed separately.

## Validation

- `defaultAccount.test.ts`: 49 passing. The updated test fails without this change.
- Account and policy suites: 250 passing.

pull_requests.title: Add configured Plugin marketplaces to Discover
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Show the existing configured Plugin marketplaces in unified Discover when `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled` is enabled.
- Preserve the feature-off behavior exactly: the original Overview and legacy Plugins **Available** section remain, and Discover does not start catalog or installation work.
- Align the implementation with #337574's MCP Gallery architecture instead of adding a parallel Plugin-specific marketplace stack.
- Keep installed Plugin management, updates, trust, create, and install-from-source actions in the Plugins page. Marketplace deep links route to plugin-filtered Discover only while Marketplace visibility is enabled.
- Do not add a Plugin-specific feature flag. The existing Marketplace visibility setting is the only switch for moving configured Plugin discovery into Discover.

## How it works

- The workbench marketplace service composes renderer-owned Plugin providers with the existing platform-owned MCP Gallery and public GitHub Feed providers.
- Configured Plugin marketplaces expose separate custom and default providers behind one logical `pluginMarketplaces` source, matching MCP Gallery's custom/default provider structure.
- `IPluginMarketplaceService` remains the native owner of effective marketplace references, enterprise-policy filtering, text/type filtering, opaque pagination, invalidation, and partial marketplace errors. The Discover adapters only select a provider partition and map Plugin metadata.
- The default Awesome Copilot provider returns no content while the public GitHub Feed is enabled, avoiding duplicate public entries. Custom and workspace marketplaces remain available and take priority over equal-relevance public results.
- Installation re-fetches the exact opaque Plugin identity through the policy-aware Plugin marketplace service, delegates trust and installation to the existing Plugin installer, verifies that the installer registered the expected URI, and persists that exact URI for reconciliation, repair, and uninstall.
- Configuration and workspace/trust changes invalidate in-flight queries and installs. Recoverable native-marketplace warnings remain visible while healthy marketplaces continue paging.

## Behavior matrix

- **Marketplace off:** original Overview; default, custom, and workspace Plugin marketplaces remain in Plugins → Available; no Discover catalog work.
- **Marketplace on, public GitHub Feed off:** Discover shows custom/workspace Plugin marketplaces first, followed by Awesome Copilot.
- **Marketplace on, public GitHub Feed on:** Discover shows custom/workspace Plugin marketplaces and public results; the Plugin source omits duplicate Awesome Copilot content.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Fix Agent Merge startup and configuration
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Agent Merge could capture stale session Git metadata immediately after an agent created a branch and pull request, then incorrectly disable itself when the metadata caught up. Enabling monitoring also did not make the effective automatic-merge policy clear.

- Capture the checked-out branch with a lightweight local Git query before the enablement tool returns, and include the target branch, effective configuration, and monitoring status in its response. Autonomous work still waits until the foreground turn ends.
- Allow the tool to configure `addressReviews`, `fixCI`, `resolveConflicts`, and `mergePullRequest`. Repeated calls update only supplied options without resetting an active target; global defaults and GitHub auto-merge settings remain unchanged.
- Revalidate stale, missing, or detached Git metadata before accepting or rejecting a target. Failed or interrupted branch reads do not silently enable monitoring, and genuine branch changes still stop it safely.
- Show the effective merge policy in collapsed notices and accessible labels, describe requested authority in confirmations, and provide clear branch-specific recovery guidance when monitoring stops.

## Validation

pull_requests.title: agents: preserve session identity on first send
pull_requests.body:
agents: preserve session identity on first send

The first-send path could replace a new remote session with an unrelated archived session.
A catalogue refresh could discover that old session before the requested session appeared.
The novelty fallback then selected the old session as the committed draft. The message still
ran in the requested session, but the visible conversation switched to the wrong session.

- Require the requested raw session ID and resource scheme in both the cache and session-added
  notification paths. Do not select a session only because it was absent from the earlier cache.
- Remove the novelty snapshot, in-flight own-ID set, and committed-ID claim set. Keep cancellation
  and connection-loss handling.
- Add tests for newly discovered archived and unarchived sessions in both matching paths.
- Update first-send test mocks to materialize the requested session ID.

Why the fallback and in-flight bookkeeping can be removed safely:

- The original novelty matcher came from #307732, when drafts used temporary untitled URIs.
  #313622 later made the client create the session URI and added a guard that rejects a backend
  URI different from the requested URI. First-send commitment therefore preserves identity.
- Commit 87d66b3a18fecc3f134f57467466203abee4e704 (#324792) preferred the own ID but retained a
  novelty fallback "for backends that assign a fresh id." That rationale does not match the
  first-send creation contract now enforced by the handler.
- The in-flight own-ID set protected the fallback from selecting another concurrent draft's
  session. Exact matching removes that possibility: send A accepts only A, even when B appears
  first. The claim set is also unnecessary for distinct drafts because their matches cannot
  overlap. Backend identity remapping would require an explicit mapping, not a novelty guess.
- The existing concurrent-send regression remains and passes: B materializes before A, and
  each send commits to its own session. Cached own-session and delayed-materialization tests
  also pass.

Validation:

- Client transpilation passed.
- Complete local and remote provider suites: 392 passing, 11 pending.
- ESLint passed for all three changed files.
- git diff --check passed.
- No live remote UI end-to-end validation was performed.

pull_requests.title: chat: Keep search intent parameters literal in markdown table
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #316997

## What

The `/search` intent renders search parameters parsed from the model's own response into a markdown table in the chat panel. `jsonToTable` wrapped each value in single backticks and escaped only `|`, so model-authored content could break out of the table cell:

- **A backtick closed the code span early.** The rest of the value then rendered as markdown. For example, ``a` [click](https://evil.example) `b`` produced a live `<a href>`.
- **A line break ended the row**, which let the model inject extra table rows.
- **Keys were not escaped at all.**

The inline `CodeQL [SM02383]` justification ("only a `|` pipe character would interfere") was therefore incorrect.

## How

- Values are wrapped with the existing `appendEscapedMarkdownInlineCode` helper. Its backtick fence is one longer than the longest backtick run in the value, so the whole value stays literal.
- Line breaks, including U+2028/U+2029, are collapsed to spaces.
- Each `|` is handled together with the run of backslashes before it, in one pass. Backslashes themselves are not escaped, because they display literally inside a code span.
  - **Even run (including none):** one extra backslash is added. marked removes it again, so the pipe stays in the cell and the common `a|b` regex renders exactly as before.
  - **Odd run:** marked checks backslash parity, so a pipe here would split the cell even with an extra backslash. The code span is closed before it, and the pipe is emitted as `|`.
- Only the six parameters defined by the search prompt are shown (`query`, `replace`, `filesToInclude`, `filesToExclude`, `isRegex`, `isCaseSensitive`). These are the only ones the Search follow-up button uses, and their fixed names need no escaping.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Behaviour change:** parameters the model invents beyond those six no longer appear in the table. Previously they were shown even though the Search button ignored them.
- **Found by review:** the first version of this fix rendered correctly in markdown-it but still allowed link injection in marked via `[evil](https://evil.example)\|`. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 reviews both caught it; the second fix addresses it.
- Severity is low. This is formatting and link injection in chat output, with no code execution.

The /search intent renders search parameters parsed from the model's own

only `|` escaped, so a backtick closed the code span early and the rest of

ended the row and let the model inject table rows. Keys were not escaped.

Values now use a backtick fence longer than any run in the value, collapse
line breaks (including U+2028/U+2029), and pad only where CommonMark would
strip spaces. Pipes that follow an odd run of backslashes cannot be kept
inside a code span in marked, so the value is split around them and they are

pull_requests.title: copilot: fix shell argument injection in generated commit messages
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #316995
Fixes #316996

## The bug

`github.copilot.terminal.generateCommitMessage` types `git commit -m <message>` into the active terminal. It is the terminal quick fix offered after a successful `git add`. The old sanitizer escaped `"` before `\`, so its second `replace` re-escaped the backslash the first one had just added, and the message could end its own `-m` argument. Backticks were never escaped either, so command substitution still worked.

It is worse than typed-but-not-run. `Terminal.sendText` turns every line break into an Enter key press, and generated messages are usually multi-line. So a message that breaks out of its quotes **runs without the user pressing Enter**, even though the command is sent with `shouldExecute: false`.

## The fix

`buildGitCommitCommand` builds the command for the terminal's detected shell (`TerminalState.shell`):

| Terminal | Command |
|---|---|
| bash, zsh, sh, ksh, Git Bash | `-m '…'` with POSIX single quotes. The message is kept intact, line breaks included. |
| fish | `-m '…'`, with `\` and `'` escaped, because fish treats both as escapes inside single quotes. |
| PowerShell | `-m '…'`, doubling `'` and the typographic single quotes PowerShell also treats as delimiters (U+2018, U+2019, U+201A, U+201B). `"` becomes `'`, and a trailing `\` gets a space after it, which git's message cleanup removes again. Without this, Windows PowerShell 5.1's legacy native argument passing splits the argument at a `"` and lets a trailing `\` escape its closing quote. PowerShell 5.1 and 7 both report `pwsh`, so they can't be told apart. |
| cmd, nu, csh, WSL, other or undetected shells | One `-m "…"` per paragraph, reduced to characters every shell treats literally inside double quotes. `$`, `!` and `%` are removed; `"`, backticks and typographic quotes become `'`; `\` becomes `/`; the lines of a paragraph are joined. This is needed because cmd runs each line as soon as it's entered and expands `%VAR%` inside quotes, and the quoting rules of an unknown shell are unknown. |
| An agent CLI running in the terminal (Copilot CLI, Claude, Codex, Gemini and so on) | Nothing is typed, because the text would be a prompt to another agent. |

Control characters are removed for every shell, and a tab becomes a space. Typed control characters are commands to the shell's line editor. For example, a Backspace can erase the opening quote, and a following line break then runs the rest; that was reproduced in Git Bash and pwsh 7.6.

Agent Host terminals never report a shell type, so they always get the one-line form. That includes the Agents window, which has no Source Control view that a fallback could use.

The inline `// CodeQL [SM02383]` suppression is removed, since the double-escaping pattern it covered is gone.

## Validation

- **Unit tests:** 9 tests in `shellQuoting.spec.ts` (vitest).
- **Real shells:** every form was run through real shells into a native program and compared byte for byte. That covered Git Bash, pwsh 7.6, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and cmd.exe; the single-quote rules were also run through WSL bash, fish 4.9.3, and pwsh 7.6 in `Legacy` argument-passing mode. The inputs included the payloads from both issues and from review.
- **PowerShell parser:** the real parser in 5.1 and 7.6 read the single-quoted form of every BMP character, and of 20,000 random hostile strings, as a single literal equal to the input.
- **Interactive terminals:** real `git commit` commands were typed into interactive cmd, pwsh 7.6, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and Git Bash sessions through a pty, exactly as `sendText(text, false)` sends them. Nothing committed or ran before Enter, each produced exactly one commit, and `git log` showed the expected message.

## Known limitations

- The one-line form is lossy: the lines of a paragraph are joined, and `` `$var` `` becomes `'var'`. If Agent Host terminals reported a shell type, they could use the lossless forms instead.
- These predate this PR and are not injection paths:
  - Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops typed characters outside the console code page, such as `’`, `✓` and emoji. Git Bash turns a typed emoji into `�`.
  - Git Bash's MSYS runtime rewrites an argument that starts with `/` as a Windows path.
  - For remote Agent Host sessions the command does nothing, because `vscode.git` only opens `file:` repositories.

`copilotCLITerminalIntegration.ts` has a separate `quoteArgsForShell` for Copilot CLI paths and arguments. It is intentionally left unchanged here.

auto_merge.commit_title: copilot: fix shell argument injection in generated commit messages (#337547)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* Fix shell argument injection in generated commit messages

The commit-message sanitizer escaped `"` before `\`, so the second replace
re-escaped the backslash the first one had just added and turned `"` into
`\\"`. Inside a double-quoted shell string that reads as an escaped backslash
followed by a closing quote, ending the `-m` argument early and leaving the
rest of the message to be parsed as separate shell tokens. Backticks were not
escaped at all, so a message containing `cmd` in backticks still triggered
command substitution.

Quote the message with single quotes instead, which suppress expansion and
substitution outright rather than depending on every metacharacter being
escaped individually. Quoting is shell-aware because `'` is not a quote
character in cmd.exe and PowerShell escapes an embedded `'` by doubling it
rather than with the POSIX `'\''` idiom. This also fixes the previous `\`
doubling silently corrupting backslashes under PowerShell.

The helper lives in its own module so it is covered by the fast unit suite
and can be reused by the other terminal sendText call sites.

Fixes #316995
Fixes #316996

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Harden commit-message quoting per shell, else use the commit box

The first fix still let a generated message break out of its quoted
argument in several shells. Because sendText turns every line break into an
Enter key press, a breakout in a multi-line message ran without the user
pressing Enter.

- PowerShell also ends a single-quoted string at the typographic single
  quotes U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B, which are common in generated
  text.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not escape an embedded double quote when it
  builds git's command line, so the quote split the argument. PowerShell 5.1
  and 7 both report the shell as pwsh, so a double quote is refused.
- fish treats \' and \\ as escapes inside single quotes, so a backslash
  defeated the POSIX '\'' idiom.
- nu has no escape for a single quote. cmd.exe expands %VAR% inside double
  quotes and runs each line as soon as it is entered. csh expands ! inside
  single quotes and cannot continue them onto a new line.

Typed control characters are also commands to the shell's line editor; for
example, a Backspace can erase the opening quote. A message containing one
is refused for every shell.

quoteShellArgument now uses an allowlist of shells whose quoting rules are
known, and returns undefined when a value cannot be quoted safely. The
command then puts the message in the Source Control commit box instead of
typing it into the terminal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Shorten comments in commit-message shell quoting

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Strip or replace unsafe characters instead of refusing them

Refusing a message sent it to the Source Control commit box. The Agents
window has no Source Control view, though, and Agent Host terminals never
report a shell type, so there every message was refused and then lost.

buildGitCommitCommand now always builds a command, except for agent CLIs:

- Control characters are stripped for every shell.
- PowerShell gets ' in place of ", and a space after a trailing \. Git's
  message cleanup removes that space again.
- cmd.exe and other or undetected shells get one -m per paragraph, reduced
  to characters that every shell treats literally inside double quotes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

pull_requests.title: agentHost: let chats work in their own folder, and show it
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #337263 and #337499. In the Agents Window, chats in one session can work in different folders, but until now nothing let an agent create such a chat: `create_session` rejected `workspace` and `worktree` for the current session, so every chat it started shared the session's workspace.

## What changes

- **`create_session` can start a chat in its own folder.** With the current-session relationship, `workspace` names the folder for the new chat. The host adds it to the session, preparing a worktree when requested or inherited, and assigns the resulting checkout only to the new chat. Existing chats keep their folders. Without `workspace`, the chat shares the session workspace as before.
- **How the folder is prepared.** An explicit `worktree` wins, otherwise the creating session's isolation, otherwise the folder itself. `worktree: true` always creates a fresh worktree; otherwise a checkout of that repository already in the session is reused. `worktree` requires `workspace`.
- **`relationship` is optional and defaults to a chat in the current session.** Agents use `independent` only for work unrelated to the current session's plan or deliverable; work in the current session can also be in a different workspace.
- **The chat shows its project.** A folder that is a VS Code-created worktree (`<repo>.worktrees/<name>`) reports its repository as the folder's project, so a chat in such a worktree shows that project. The path helper moves to the shared `worktreePaths.ts` and the host reuses it.
- **Chat folders survive a restart.** Providers only persist the folders a session started with, so restoring a session dropped a folder added later for a chat, and the client then built no workspace for that chat. Restore now adds every chat's persisted folders back to the session's working directories.
- **The Changes view follows the active chat's folder.** Its tree root and relative file paths now come from the active chat's workspace instead of the session's first folder, and update when switching chats.
- **The sessions list and command center show a chat's folder.** In the compact sessions list, a chat row shows the folder its chat works in (on hover or focus) when the session spans more than one project and the chat works in exactly one folder; screen readers hear it too. The command center's project, icon, path, and branch follow the active chat's workspace instead of the session's.

## Notes for reviewers

- No protocol change: chats already carry their own working directories.
- If the provider doesn't support multiple working directories, or the session has no workspace, the tool fails before creating the chat.
- If the chat cannot be created after its folder was prepared, the host removes the folder that call added (and deletes a worktree it created), unless a chat uses it by then.
- Agent Merge and pull request lifecycle actions still follow the session folder's pull request; making them per folder is a follow-up.
- The Copilot prompt snapshots are regenerated from replay; only the `create_session` schema text changed.

## Validation

- Agent Host unit tests and Sessions unit tests pass. New tests cover the folder and worktree choices, failed preparation, releasing a prepared folder or worktree when the chat cannot be created, restoring a folder added for a chat, the chat folder label in the sessions list, the command center's workspace, the default relationship, the tool running end to end in the Agent Service, the worktree path helper, and a worktree folder's project in a chat workspace.
- Agent Host end-to-end replay for session and chat tests passes on Copilot, Claude, and Codex.
- Type-check, layer, and hygiene checks pass.

pull_requests.title: Agent host: adopt runtime-managed model defaults from managedSettings.get
pull_requests.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Draft: depends on an unpublished runtime/SDK change.** This shows the VS Code side of github/copilot-agent-runtime#22675, which adds a sessionless `managedSettings.get` returning `modelPolicy`. The method is declared locally and called defensively, so this compiles against today's `@github/copilot-sdk` and is a no-op on runtimes without it. CI may still fail until a runtime with the method is published and bundled, which is why this stays a draft.

Refs microsoft/vscode#336829. The runtime/SDK proposal is in https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/18968#issuecomment-5798731740.

## Problem

The agent host builds its picker from `client.rpc.models.list`, which carries catalog facts only:

- The Auto tier default is hardcoded to `balance`.
- No model is marked as the default.

The workbench separately re-resolves Copilot managed settings to overlay a managed Auto tier, and that resolver disagrees with the runtime on:

- strict versus overridable `autoTier`;
- channel precedence;
- the policy helper.

## Changes

- **`copilotAgent.ts`.** After each successful model refresh, fetch `managedSettings.get({ gitHubToken })` in the background.
  - The model list is published first, so the picker never waits on managed policy. Resolving policy can hit the network.
  - When the policy changes, the list is republished with it applied.
  - Runtimes without the method reject the call, which is ignored.
  - A policy resolved for another account is never applied.
- **`copilotManagedModelDefaults.ts` (new).** A defensive reader for `modelPolicy`: `{ model?, autoTier? }`, each `{ value, overridable, source }`. It applies the policy to this provider's models:
  - The managed Auto tier becomes the "Optimize for" default, marked `readOnly` when policy locks it.
  - The model whose id equals `modelPolicy.model.value` is marked as the default.
- **`common/meta/agentModelDefaultMeta.ts` (new).** A validating reader for the well-known `_meta.isDefault` key. The AHP `SessionModelInfo` is generated from the upstream protocol ("DO NOT EDIT"), so a first-class field would be an upstream protocol change. `_meta` is the protocol's extension bag.
- **`agentHostLanguageModelProvider.ts`.** Publishes a host-reported default as `isDefaultForLocation[Chat]`, which `chatInputPart.ts` already uses for `getDeclaredDefaultModel`.

Without a managed model policy (older runtimes, or no policy), the published models are identical to today's.

### Not in this draft (follow-ups)

- **Enforcing `readOnly` in the picker.** The model-picker controls (`modelPickerConfiguration.ts`, `modelPickerCard.ts`, `modelPickerAutoRow.ts`, `createModelConfigurationActions`) don't disable read-only properties yet. Separately, `ChatModelConfigurationStore` lets a saved preference win over a locked default.
- **Retiring the workbench's managed Auto tier overlay for agent-host sessions.** It should be gated off once `managedSettings.get` is available. It stays for the Copilot extension vendor, which does not use the runtime.
- **`chat.defaultModel` precedence.** A configured or policy-backed `chat.defaultModel` still wins over the declared default.
- **Workspace-scoped policy.** This covers the policy helper and model alias resolution, both deferred in the runtime as well.

## How to test

- **Unit tests** (`copilotManagedModelDefaults.test.ts`, `copilotAgent.test.ts`, `agentHostLanguageModelProvider.test.ts`) cover:
  - reading a well-formed `modelPolicy`;
  - ignoring malformed results and entries (`null`, arrays, wrong types, empty values);
  - applying the policy only to this provider;
  - leaving the tier unlocked when overridable;
  - skipping tiers the picker doesn't offer;
  - the no-policy passthrough;
  - SDKs without the method;
  - the agent applying the policy after publishing the list;
  - keeping built-in defaults when the call fails or reports no policy;
  - `isDefaultForLocation` mapping.
- **End to end, once a runtime with github/copilot-agent-runtime#22675 is bundled:** set a managed `model` and `"autoTier": "efficiency"`. The picker loads as today and then:
  - preselects the managed model;
  - defaults "Optimize for" to Efficiency, marked read-only.

These changes were authored in a sparse checkout without dependencies installed. I checked that the files parse, but did not type-check or run the tests locally, so I'm relying on CI for that.

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- reject host-key algorithm changes for previously known SSH hosts instead of treating them as first contact
- use `HostKeyAlias` consistently for `known_hosts` lookup, stored trust, and `UpdateHostKeys`, including safe migration of existing trust

The previous algorithm-specific lookup could classify a previously verified host as unknown when a different host-key algorithm was presented. pull_requests.title: Git - sort repository picker by workspace folder order
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #186549

In a multi-root workspace, the "Choose a repository" picker (used by Undo Last Commit, Push, etc.) listed repositories in an unpredictable order. Two things caused it:

- The initial scan opens repositories in parallel (`Promise.all` over workspace folders), so `openRepositories` ends up in whatever order they finish opening.
- `getOpenRepository()` sorts `openRepositories` in place by root path length each time it looks up a repository by Uri.

This change sorts the picker items by workspace folder index, then by repository path. Repositories outside every workspace folder go last. It sorts the filtered copy, not `openRepositories`. The existing behavior of moving the active editor's repository to the top is kept.

### How to test

1. Open a multi-root workspace with 3+ folders, each a git repository, in a non-alphabetical order (e.g. `c`, `a`, `b`).
2. Close all editors, then run **Git: Undo Last Commit** (or any command that asks for a repository).
3. The picker lists the repositories in the same order as the Explorer: `c`, `a`, `b`.
4. Open a file from `b` and run the command again: `b` comes first, then `c`, `a`.
