pull_requests.title: agentHost: scope pull requests to chat repositories
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #337263. In the Agents Window, chats in one session can work in different folders. Until now, pull requests were tracked once per session, from the session's first folder, so a chat working in another repository could not create or see its own pull request.

## What changes

- **Pull requests are tracked per folder.** A pull request belongs to a checkout and its branch, so every folder, including the session's first, keeps its own GitHub and pull request state. That state lives in session metadata (`githubData`, keyed by folder) and is persisted with the session. There is no protocol change.
- **The original single-folder entry (`github`) is retired.** It is no longer written, and every reader now uses `githubData`. Clients can still pass `github` when creating a session (for example, a session started from a pull request); it seeds the session folder. Existing sessions are migrated: persisted and cached `github` entries become the session folder's state on list, restore and catalog read, and restore deletes the old entry. Older clients and downgraded hosts no longer see pull request state.
- **State follows the checkout.** When a new session's folder moves into a worktree, its pull request state moves with it.
- **Create PR works from any folder.** Create PR is offered on each folder's Branch changes and targets that folder's own repository and branch. The created pull request is recorded for that folder. The form's "send to chat" option now goes to the chat whose changes are shown.
- **The host finds pull requests for other folders.** When a chat's folder refreshes, the host reads the folder's GitHub repository from its checkout and looks up the pull request for its current branch.
- **The UI shows each chat's own pull requests.** Every folder in a chat's workspace reports its own pull requests, so the chat's pull request pill shows pull requests for all of its folders. Chats sharing a folder share its pull requests. Recorded pull request artifacts from other repositories stay in the artifacts list, and artifacts themselves remain session-wide.
- **Auto-archive** re-checks pull requests from every folder. Folder records are kept as session history when a chat is removed or changes folders.

## Intentionally not included yet

- Agent Merge, and pull request lifecycle actions (Mark Ready, Merge, auto-merge), stay tied to the session's pull request. They are unavailable for other folders, so those chats can't act on the session's pull request. Per-folder status tracking and Agent Merge are the next step.
- Session-wide surfaces (sessions list, hover, banners) show the session folder's pull request.
- When automatic pull request attachment is disabled, only the session folder's pull requests are reconciled from recorded artifacts.

## Validation

- Agent Host and Sessions unit tests pass. New tests cover:
  - per-folder state and persistence
  - offering pull request actions per folder
  - Create PR from another folder
  - each folder of a chat reporting its own GitHub info
  - pull request pills combining a chat's folders
  - sending the chat request to the active chat
  - migrating the original entry on restore, list and catalog read, and moving state with a replaced checkout
- The recorded end-to-end tests for artifacts and pull request creation, and the Sessions component fixtures, passed before the `github` key was retired.
- Type-check, layer, and hygiene checks pass.

pull_requests.title: fix: iterate grid-installed groups in applyContentRightInset (fixes #337477)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary `EditorPart.applyContentRightInset()` iterates every group in the `groupViews` map and asks the grid for each group's right-hand neighbors. During grid reconstruction (state restore / layout apply), `doCreateGroupView()` inserts freshly-created group views into `groupViews` *before* the rebuilt `SerializableGrid` is installed via `doSetGridWidget()`. A re-entrant active-editor-change event fired from inside the deserialize callback flows through the Agents-window single-pane layer back into `applyContentRightInset()`, which then queries the still-old `gridWidget` for a group it does not contain, so `Grid.getViewLocation()` throws `Error: View not found`. Impact: an unhandled error is reported on Windows and Mac during Agents-window working-set / grid restore. Fixes microsoft/vscode#337477 Recommended reviewer: `@sandy081` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`7317e60f`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7317e60fe47b) | | Author | `@sandy081` | | PR | #324257 | | Message | sessions: single-pane detail-panel layout for the Agents window (#324257) | | Why | This commit introduced `applyContentRightInset()`, which iterates `this.groupViews.values()` and calls `gridWidget.getNeighborViews(group)` for each. `groupViews` can transiently hold group views that are not yet part of the current `gridWidget` during reconstruction, and the neighbor query throws for those groups. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Restore as applyWorkingSet / doApplyState participant Deser as SerializableGrid.deserialize participant Part as EditorPart participant Sessions as singlePane layer participant Grid as Grid Restore->>Deser: doCreateGridControlWithState() Note over Part: ⚠️ Root cause:
doCreateGroupView adds new
groups to groupViews before
doSetGridWidget installs new grid Deser->>Part: fromJSON -> doSetGroupActive(newGroup) Part->>Sessions: fire active editor change (re-entrant) Sessions->>Part: setEditorContentRightInset -> applyContentRightInset() Part->>Grid: getNeighborViews(newGroup, Right) Note over Grid: 💥 Error thrown:
View not found ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/base/browser/ui/grid/grid.ts` | crash site | L708 (from stack): `throw new Error('View not found')` in `getViewLocation` | | `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorPart.ts` | root cause | L263-L271: `for (const group of this.groupViews.values()) { ... this.gridWidget.getNeighborViews(group, Direction.Right) }` iterated groups not present in the grid | | `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorPart.ts` | producer | L1346-L1379: `doCreateGridControlWithState` populates `groupViews` and fires `doSetGroupActive` before `doSetGridWidget` installs the new grid | | `src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/singlePaneEditorPart.ts` | trigger | L156: `setEditorContentRightInset: (px) => this.setContentRightInset(px)` re-enters the editor part from the docked aux-bar layout path | ### Repro Steps 1. Enable the experimental `sessions.layout.singlePaneDetailPanel` setting (Agents window single-pane layout). 2. Set a non-zero content right inset (docked detail panel visible) so `_contentRightInset > 0`. 3. Trigger a grid state restore that rebuilds the editor grid (restore a working set / apply a saved editor layout) while the active group changes during deserialization. 4. The re-entrant active-editor-change event calls `applyContentRightInset()` mid-reconstruction, querying the not-yet-installed grid and throwing `View not found`. The race is timing-dependent; it surfaces when the deserialize callback activates a group before `doSetGridWidget` runs. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorPart.ts` → `applyContentRightInset()`: iterate `this.getGroups(GroupsOrder.GRID_APPEARANCE)` instead of `this.groupViews.values()`. `GroupsOrder.GRID_APPEARANCE` derives its list directly from `gridWidget.getViews()`, so it only ever yields groups that are actually installed in the current grid. This removes the transient group views from the iteration entirely, so `getNeighborViews` is never called for a group the grid does not know about. This fixes the bug at the code that produces the invalid input to the grid query (the over-broad iteration), not at the crash site inside `Grid`. **Alternatives considered**: guarding the crash site in `Grid.getViewLocation` or wrapping the neighbor query in try/catch — rejected because that hides a real re-entrancy/ordering bug from the telemetry pipeline instead of only inspecting groups that legitimately belong to the grid. ### Recommended Owner `@sandy081` — author of the culprit commit #324257 that introduced `applyContentRightInset()`; active VS Code core team member (multiple commits in the last 90 days). > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/35876628522) · opus48 · 412.4 AIC · ⌖ 10.4 AIC · ⊞ 18.3K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

pull_requests.title: automations: feat: support GitHub cloud automations
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in GitHub cloud automations to the existing Agents Window Automations UI. Users can create, edit, enable, disable, delete, and manually run automations for private GitHub.com repositories, then open their runs in VS Code or on GitHub.

The preview is **off by default** behind `chat.automations.cloud.enabled`. This builds on the browser-execution removal in #337334.

## Architecture

- **Local and remote automations remain Agent Host-owned and use AHP.** Cloud automations use GitHub's automation and task APIs; they do not require AHP or a synthetic Agent Host.
- `CloudAutomationApiClient` supplies typed definition/task operations through existing GitHub authentication and Copilot API transport, with account pinning, cancellation, timeouts, private-repository checks, pagination, and structured errors.
- `CloudAutomationStore` lives on the default Copilot sessions provider, not its sandbox-creation variant. `ProviderAutomationService` combines its optional catalogue with existing host catalogues. Only the cloud session type is eligible; local CLI sessions do not regain browser execution support.
- GitHub owns definitions, schedules, and execution. VS Code stores account-scoped repository discovery references, not an execution ledger. Closing VS Code, signing out, or disabling cloud management does **not** disable an existing cloud schedule.

## Behavior and safeguards

**Creation and editing** reuse the existing dialog and repository/model selection. Cloud configuration adds tool review, paused-by-default creation, and manual/hourly/daily/weekly schedules. Daily and weekly times are explicitly UTC, with quarter-hour minutes. Unsupported server triggers remain visible but read-only; unsupported local configuration and UTC-to-local blueprint export fail rather than silently changing meaning.

The dialog now keeps its draft while the actual save is pending. Definite failures preserve inputs; uncertain remote outcomes block blind resubmission. Guarded edits read the current definition before a targeted PATCH and preserve unknown trigger fields. This is **optimistic preflight, not atomic server-side compare-and-swap**. Retargeting requires duplication.

**Manual runs** report acceptance when GitHub returns `202` without a task ID. The UI neither fabricates a run nor assumes that the latest task belongs to that request. History independently discovers real tasks and retains the 50 most recent runs per automation plus previously observed active runs. Read concurrency is bounded, refresh is observation-driven, and failures retain existing data while surfacing an error.

**Opening runs** uses the existing `copilot-cloud-agent:/task/<id>` conversation viewer. The provider resolves an exact task missing from cached/paged discovery and waits for session-model publication before opening it. Its bounded explicit-task cache is invalidated on account/API-domain changes.

GitHub links use `/{owner}/{repo}/tasks/{taskId}?author={creator}`, with the signed-in account as fallback. **Open on GitHub** survives the transition from an unhydrated run to a session-backed row, in both the row toolbar and context menu; local rows do not acquire it. Opening failures are logged and reported visibly. Existing AI-disable behavior, availability messaging, refresh, and accessibility help are wired through the shared UI.

## Validation

Focused coverage includes account isolation, repository eligibility, schedule serialization, sparse responses, guarded edits, accepted/uncertain dispatch, AHP routing, dialog persistence, provider/type selection, tools, and history.

- Latest task-opening checks: **248 root tests passed**, with four platform-specific skips, and **71 Copilot extension tests passed**.
- Subsequent history-action checks: **248 tests passed** across the history widget and shared session lists. These suites overlap with the task-opening checks; the counts are not additive.
- Client and extension type checks, targeted ESLint, layer/CSS checks, diff checks, and commit hygiene passed during implementation.
- Five cloud fixtures rendered cleanly across dark/light/high-contrast and narrow layouts. The mixed fixture includes a hydrated cloud run and verifies that its GitHub action does not appear on the local row.
- Authorized private-repository probes verified native VS Code authentication, disabled-definition CRUD, and no-op manual execution/history retrieval. Temporary resources were cleaned up.

**Still needed before removing the preview gate:** a complete automated, signed-in workbench create/edit/run scenario. API probes and component coverage are not a substitute for that end-to-end UI exercise.

## How to try it

1. Enable `chat.automations.enabled` and `chat.automations.cloud.enabled`, and sign in with repository access.
2. Open **Automations → New Automation** in the Agents Window. Select a private GitHub repository and the Cloud target; review model, tools, and UTC schedule.
3. Create it paused and exercise edit, enable/disable, and refresh. Use an authorized test repository before enabling a schedule or running it, since execution may consume credits.
4. Verify acceptance feedback, actual run history, and opening a task not yet present in the session catalogue.
5. Verify **Open on GitHub** before and after session hydration, while running and after completion. Loaded rows expose the external-link toolbar action and right-click menu entry.
6. Confirm local/remote automations still use their original providers and disabling AI features hides cloud management.

## Deliberate limits

Private GitHub.com repositories only. Discovery covers selected/recent repositories, not an exhaustive account-wide catalogue. Enterprise hosts, arbitrary cron/event-trigger editing, infrastructure selection, unlimited history, and cross-provider history transfer are out of scope. GitHub remains authoritative for effective permissions; an omitted tools array is not proof of a no-tools guarantee.

pull_requests.body:
This pull request addresses the performance issue when switching sessions in the Agents window, specifically regarding the delay in displaying changeset statistics and file lists. 

### Changes made:
- Removed the readiness gate that previously required a fresh recomputation of changeset data before rendering statistics and file lists.

- Added regression tests to verify the behavior when switching sessions.

### Rationale:
This change aims to improve the responsiveness of the Changes editor by utilizing cached data more effectively, thereby enhancing the user experience during session switches.

pull_requests.title: fix: only show banner message hover when truncated (build fix for vscode-engineering#3943)
pull_requests.body:
## Build failure

The `Run Sanity Tests` task timed out on every platform during the `installExtension` step. Playwright reported the Extensions view **Refresh** button as visible, enabled, and stable, but every click was blocked because the Restricted Mode banner's tooltip overlay intercepted the pointer events:

```
locator.click: Timeout 180000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Refresh' })
  - attempting click action
    - Restricted Mode is intended for safe code browsin...
      from ... subtree intercepts pointer events
    - retrying click action ...
```

## Root cause

`src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/banner/bannerPart.ts` was recently updated to attach a delayed hover to the banner message container:

```ts
this.itemDisposables.add(this.hoverService.setupDelayedHover(messageContainer, { content: ariaLabel }));
```

Because the banner code is shared, this also applies to the existing Restricted Mode banner. The hover fired unconditionally on mouse-over, popping a hover overlay even when the message was not truncated. That overlay is positioned over the workbench and intercepts pointer events on controls directly below the banner — including the Extensions **Refresh** button — so clicks never land.

The `.message-container` already truncates overflowing text (`text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden`), so revealing the message on hover is only meaningful when the message is actually clipped.

## How the fix works

The hover options are now provided lazily and only supply content when the message container is actually truncated (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`):

```ts
this.itemDisposables.add(this.hoverService.setupDelayedHover(messageContainer, () => ({
    content: messageContainer.scrollWidth > messageContainer.clientWidth ? ariaLabel : '',
})));
```

When the message fits, the content resolves to an empty string, and `HoverService` short-circuits empty-content hovers (`_createHover` returns early for `content === ''`), so no overlay is created and pointer events pass through to controls below. When the message is truncated, the full text is still revealed on hover as intended. This preserves the accessibility/reveal behavior while removing the unconditional overlay.

## Rollback evaluation

- Recommendation: **Do not roll back.**
- Public culprit commit/PR: commit `d65936c590d70e1bd142bcdc4a718d04cc4d1f3d` (PR microsoft/vscode#337151).
- Rationale: The impact is bounded to Insider sanity tests. The culprit PR also lands unrelated enterprise `minVersion` UI across many areas (policy, chat, sessions, welcome views), so reverting it is riskier and broader than this targeted, fix-forward change to the banner hover. A scoped fix in `bannerPart.ts` lands quickly and safely.
- Owners to consult: `@rwoll`

## Validation

Added a focused regression test in `bannerPart.test.ts` asserting the banner hover resolves to empty content when the message fits and to the full message only when truncated. Dependencies were not installed in this environment, so the unit test and typecheck could not be executed here; the change is source-reviewed and matches the established `scrollWidth > clientWidth` truncation pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.

pull_requests.title: sessions: fix: preserve hidden Chat on editor handoff
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Preserve a user's hidden Chat state when **Open in Editor** returns an Agents session to an editor window that is already open.

- Track successful external session handoffs for the lifetime of each editor window.
- Suppress only a repeated handoff whose existing Chat widget is hidden.
- Restrict suppression to the Chat view, excluding inactive Chat editor tabs.
- Coalesce concurrent handoffs for the same session.
- Gate preservation behind the false-by-default ExP setting `chat.experimental.openInEditor.preserveHiddenChat`.
- Preserve the existing first-open, visible-widget, missing-widget, and retry behavior.
- Add focused regression coverage for the window-local lifecycle.

## Motivation

The Agents window hands a session to the regular workbench through `vscode:openChatSession`. Opening the same workspace again correctly reuses and focuses its existing editor window, but the IPC listener previously reopened Chat every time. That overrode the user's deliberate choice to hide Chat while continuing to work in the editor.

The hidden state should be remembered only for that editor window's lifetime. It should not become profile or workspace state, and a newly created or reloaded window must still open the handed-off session.

For an initial A/B experiment, the setting is application-scoped, tagged
`experimental`, and registered with `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`:

- **Control (`false`)** retains the previous behavior and reopens Chat.
- **Treatment (`true`)** preserves the hidden Chat view.

## Implementation

`ChatSessionHandoffController` records sessions only after their first handoff opens successfully. For later handoffs it checks the current widget:

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| First handoff in this editor window | Open Chat |
| Existing widget is hidden after a previous handoff | Keep Chat hidden |
| Only an inactive Chat editor exists | Open/reveal the session normally |
| Existing widget is visible | Use the normal open/reveal path |
| Widget no longer exists | Open the session again |
| Different session | Open that session |
| Open fails | Leave it unrecorded so a later handoff retries |
| Concurrent handoffs for one session | Share one pending open |
| Chat becomes hidden during a pending open | Keep waiting for the pending result |

`ChatCommandLineHandler` owns one controller per renderer contribution, which naturally scopes this memory to one editor window without adding storage or provider-specific behavior.

## Validation

- Focused configuration and `ChatSessionHandoff` tests: **14 passing**
  - registration verifies the false default and automatic ExP metadata;
  - control verifies that hidden Chat reopens;
  - treatment verifies that hidden Chat stays hidden.
- ESLint on all changed TypeScript files: **passed**
- Full client type check: no diagnostics in changed files; existing Agent Host SDK dependency mismatches remain outside this change
- Code OSS Dev UI scenario on Windows x64, VS Code 1.139.0: **5/5 steps passed**
  - first handoff created an editor window and displayed Chat;
  - hiding Chat left that editor window open;
  - the second handoff reused and focused the same window;
  - the window count stayed unchanged;
  - Chat remained hidden.

### UI evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae0d3a50-fd13-4129-b639-f4648f9dc8ea

pull_requests.title: Respect editor font family for inline code in rendered Markdown

## Problem

Inline code rendered using `DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_STYLES` uses a hard-coded monospace font stack and ignores `editor.fontFamily`.

This affects extension README pages and other workbench views that consume these shared Markdown styles.

## Fix

Use `--vscode-editor-font-family` for inline code while retaining the existing monospace stack as a fallback.

This aligns inline code with fenced code blocks and the Markdown preview.

## Testing

1. Set `editor.fontFamily` to a visibly distinct monospace font.
2. Open an extension README containing inline code.
3. Confirm that inline and fenced code use the configured editor font.
4. Confirm the existing monospace fallback remains available.
5. Set `editor.fontFamily` to a nonexistent font and confirm inline code remains monospace.

## Related

PRs #325629 and #326118 address missing-font fallback behavior, but do not make inline code in `DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_STYLES` respect `editor.fontFamily`.

pull_requests.title: build: extend Windows Electron CI timeout
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Increase the Windows Electron CI job timeout from 50 to 70 minutes while preserving the existing 50-minute timeout for Browser and Remote suites.

The node_modules cache result is only available after the job starts, so Azure Pipelines cannot dynamically extend the current job timeout on a cache miss. A suite-level template condition is known before job creation and lets us give only the longer Electron workload enough cold-cache headroom.

## Evidence

Cold node_modules cache misses add roughly 14–17 minutes of dependency installation and archive creation. The Electron workload then reaches smoke tests with too little of the 50-minute budget remaining:

- [build 475824](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475824&view=logs&j=15ec5277-fdc6-550c-b203-acb65f44f31c&t=19c87eee-4f28-5155-a71e-4ac992305659): cache miss, smoke tests canceled at 50 minutes
- [build 475850 attempt 1](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475850&view=logs&j=15ec5277-fdc6-550c-b203-acb65f44f31c&t=19c87eee-4f28-5155-a71e-4ac992305659&s=27eddb93-7805-576c-c80f-37b2176e40f7): cache miss and timeout; retry succeeded after the cache became available
- [build 476029](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=476029&view=logs&j=15ec5277-fdc6-550c-b203-acb65f44f31c&t=19c87eee-4f28-5155-a71e-4ac992305659): cache miss, normal smoke progress, canceled at 50 minutes

A timeout is only a ceiling; cache-hit jobs continue to finish at their normal duration. Existing task-level timeouts continue to bound individual test commands.

## Validation

- Azure pipeline queue dry-run
- `git diff --check`

Give cold node_modules cache runs enough headroom while preserving the existing 50-minute limit for Browser and Remote suites.

pull_requests.title: test: Harden Windows Agent Host descendant cleanup
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- capture the name and command line of Windows Agent Host test-server descendants before graceful shutdown
- prune inaccessible process branches that stale Windows parent PIDs can attach to a reused server PID
- after a failed `taskkill`, suppress the error only when the captured process identity is no longer present
- add focused coverage for stale-PPID branches, exited or reused PIDs, and genuine kill failures

## Context

The Windows Electron integration run in Azure build 475775 passed the `Protocol WebSocket - Session Config` test body, then failed during suite teardown after `taskkill` raced with descendant exit and the fallback `process.kill(pid, 0)` returned `EPERM`.

A subsequent 20x flaky run in Azure build 476056 reproduced both variants of the lifecycle race:

- exit code 128 when the captured PID no longer existed
- exit code 255 when stale Toolhelp parent-PID metadata attached a protected critical-system branch to the reused Agent Host PID

The previous fallback could not distinguish these cases reliably. Signal zero requests termination access on Windows, while a numeric PID alone does not preserve process identity across reuse.

## Validation

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/serverIntegrationTestHelpers.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/serverIntegrationTestHelpers.test.ts`
- `npm run compile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/serverIntegrationTestHelpers.test.ts` — 5 passing, 1 Windows-only pending on macOS
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocol/sessionConfig.integrationTest.ts` — 6 passing

(Written by Copilot)

pull_requests.title: Retain full Codex shell output across chat reloads
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338051
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328596
Follow-up to: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335016

- Keep Codex command output up to 80,000 UTF-16 code units inline, using a Codex-owned character limit.
- Retain larger output in the owning chat's session database within the existing 10 MiB UTF-8 limit. Show the first 400 characters unchanged with **Open Full Output (Read-Only)**, without keeping a terminal alive.
- Wait for storage before publishing ordinary or recovered command completions. Preserve per-chat signal order, keep full inline output if storage fails, and suppress queued publication after disposal.
- Preserve tool-call identity across live events and replay. Coalesce sandbox pre-flights only when raw command invocations match, including shell flags. Unwrap Bash/zsh and PowerShell/pwsh scripts for display and existing script inspection, not identity.
- Restore retained resources on initial history reads and incremental refreshes, even when native replay output is short, empty, or null.
- Share the recovery eligibility check between retention and completion mapping. Remove retained output when rollback or revert removes its turn; session deletion removes the remaining database.
- Leave subagent output, unretained output, and output above 10 MiB unchanged. Reject obviously oversized strings before UTF-8 allocation and check exact byte size for multibyte output.

This is a Codex Agent Host adapter change. It does not change AHP, Copilot/Claude retention, workbench rendering, or approval policy.

### Validation

Verified at `2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124`:

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Focused Codex suites — **307 passing**:

  ```sh
  npm run test-node -- --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/codex/{codexPrewarmEviction,codexMapAppServerEvents,codexReplayMapper,codexShellCommand,codexTerminalOutput,codexChatDiscovery,codexCreateChat}.test.js'
  ```

- `./node_modules/.bin/eslint $(git diff --name-only c364cc986a3..HEAD -- '*.ts')` — passed.
- `git diff --check c364cc986a3..HEAD` — passed.

Regression coverage includes delayed/rejected writes, missing turn rows, disposal, recovered completions, ASCII/UTF-8 size boundaries, raw PowerShell identity, rollback cleanup, and short or missing native history output. Failure, size-guard, identity, and restore regressions were observed failing against the preceding implementation before passing with the fixes.

The PowerShell identity and shorter-history cases use synthetic protocol payloads; they do not claim a captured reproduction from the pinned Codex runtime. Live manual verification of this head is pending. GitHub currently reports a conflict with `main`; these review fixes intentionally do not include an upstream merge.

### Manual verification

In a Codex Agent Host chat, ask the agent to run this exact shell command:

```sh
node -e "process.stdout.write('FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN\n' + 'x'.repeat(131072) + '\nFULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE\n' + 'y'.repeat(131072) + '\nFULL_OUTPUT_END\n')"
```

Verify:

- The card starts with `FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN`, shows the raw 400-character prefix and truncation indicator, and offers **Open Full Output (Read-Only)**.
- The read-only editor contains the beginning, middle, and end markers.
- Closing and reopening the editor, then restarting the Agent Host and reloading the window, still opens the full retained output.
- Short output, such as `node -e "console.log('short output')"`, remains inline without a truncation indicator or full-output action.

On Windows or where PowerShell is available, repeat with:

```powershell
$x = 'x' * 131072; $y = 'y' * 131072; [Console]::Out.Write("FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN`n$x`nFULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE`n$y`nFULL_OUTPUT_END`n")
```

Verify that the card shows the script rather than the PowerShell wrapper, with the same retention and restore behavior.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Write-before-publication and fallback behavior follow [`CopilotAgentSession`'s stored shell output capture](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L5965-L5982).
- Restore-by-tool-call-id follows [`_restoreStoredShellOutputsForChat`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3745-L3771).
- Serving completed output without a live terminal uses the existing [`AgentService._resolveRetainedTerminalState`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L5834-L5898).
- Storage ownership, turn-row requirements, and the 10 MiB limit come from [`SessionDatabase.storeTerminalOutput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionDatabase.ts#L918-L937).

pull_requests.title: Retain full Claude Bash output across chat reloads
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338050
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328596
Follow-up to: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335016

- Copy complete output that Claude saves for a top-level `Bash` result into the owning chat's session database before publishing completion, within the existing 10 MiB limit.
- Attach an exited non-PTY terminal resource so the existing card provides a preview and **Open Full Output (Read-Only)**, both live and after history restore, without keeping a terminal alive. Restore attaches the resource only when its stored output exists.
- Cover `pwsh` invoked through `Bash`, but leave Claude's separate native `PowerShell` tool, background commands, subagent shell calls, inline results, and results without saved output unchanged.
- Extract the preview from Claude's `<persisted-output>` notice. If the format is unrecognized, trace the tool-call ID without logging output or paths, and preserve the raw result and access to retained output. Successful results retain the existing exit-code-0 behavior.
- Propagate cancellation to the file read and recheck before mapping completion, including the microtask gap after capture. Cancelled captures clear staged content and mapper tracking, suppress completion, and attempt to delete the retained row without recreating missing session storage. Read/store failures without cancellation preserve the original text result; persistent deletion failures are logged rather than reported as successful cleanup.
- Keep retained rows owned by their turn and session so existing truncation and session-deletion paths clean them up. Leave the shared database API and existing per-call restore lookup pattern unchanged.

### Validation

Re-run at `318b82831c3a44c5e9cba5228907f212428e0314`:

- `scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/agentHost/test/node/claude{SdkMessageRouter,TerminalOutput}.test.js"`: **23 passing**. Covers capture ordering, cancellation before/during/after reading and storing, transient and persistent deletion failures, text fallback, missing storage, preview-format fallback, and restore filtering.
- `scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/claudeAgent.test.ts --grep "getMessages restores retained Bash output from the chat database"`: **1 passing**.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**. This feedback pass made no source changes; no new full build, typecheck, or live Claude run was performed.

Earlier manual verification at `80f1b4b9a43` confirmed that a 262,199-character Claude Haiku 4.5 result opened in full and read-only, both live and after **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host** followed by **Developer: Reload Window**. That evidence predates the cancellation follow-ups and is not a new end-to-end result for the current head.

Current blockers: the branch conflicts with `main`. The [macOS / Electron job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36070313679/job/107869494363) failed in the Copilot E2E test `runtime MCP: plugin tools remain callable after a built-in subagent` (expected `MCP_PROBE:before`, received no probe output); its Claude, Codex, and Conformance E2E suites passed. This review did not change the Copilot MCP path or establish the cause of that failure.

### Manual check

1. In a local Agent Host Claude session, ask Claude to run this command once using `Bash`, without redirecting its output:

   ```sh
   node -e 'console.log("FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN"); console.log("x".repeat(131072)); console.log("FULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE"); console.log("y".repeat(131072)); console.log("FULL_OUTPUT_END")'
   ```

2. Open **Open Full Output (Read-Only)** from the completed card. Check that the editor contains all three markers, Select All reports 262,199 characters, and typing cannot modify the document.
3. Run **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host**, then **Developer: Reload Window**. Reopen the same card's full output and check the markers, length, and read-only behavior again.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

Allow the web Agents window to create a GitHub sandbox session from a repository, without requiring an existing sandbox connection.

- The creation provider owns drafts only; existing sandbox sessions remain owned by their connection-backed providers.

- Preserve the existing unscoped authentication fallback for other GitHub callers; only explicit repository access requests can initiate scoped sign-in.
- Observe entitlement-based AI hiding as well as settings, tearing down sandbox hosts/providers when hidden and rediscovering when restored.

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] agentHost: keep the default chat title in sync with a session rename
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #337308 from `main`.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336995
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326054

Renaming a session from the **sessions list** left the **session header** showing the old title. Worse, clicking into that header and pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> renamed the default chat, which mirrors back onto the session and overwrote the rename — silent data loss.

## Why it happened

A session whose only chat is its default chat has no independently titled chat: the header renders the session title. But the default chat still owns persisted title metadata, written whenever something renamed it directly — the `rename_chat` tool, the chat header, or an automatic title.

A session-scoped rename (the sessions list path) updated only the session, so that chat metadata went stale. On restore it was seeded back as the chat's *own* title, making the divergence sticky: the list showed the new name, the header showed the old one, and committing the header handed the stale title back to the session.

This regressed in #331509 (commit 771cd9d5d75), which removed the `isDefaultChat && _isOnlySessionChat(session)` guard from `_renameChatFromTool` — after that, a single-chat session could get an independent title stamped onto its default chat.

## What changed

`SessionTitleContribution._retitleSoleDefaultChat` mirrors a session rename down onto the sole default chat, updating both live state (so the open header updates immediately) and persisted metadata (so it survives restore).

Restoring the old guard alone would **not** have been sufficient: it only covers the `rename_chat` tool path, while the UI header rename flows through `onDidApplyClientAction`. Handling it in `onDidApplyClientAction` covers every session-channel rename — sessions list, tool, or header — and repairs sessions already broken on disk the next time they are renamed.

Sessions that own peer chats are skipped: their default chat is independently titled by design.

## Notes for reviewers

- The four metadata writes are two pairs — the title plus a companion `…SOURCE` key marking it user-set — written to both the chat's own database and the session's database keyed by chat. `onHydrateChat` reads them in that order on restore, so writing only one would leave the other as a stale fallback.
- `state.defaultChat ?? buildDefaultChatUri(session)` covers state where `defaultChat` is not yet populated.

## Validation

- New test `a session rename retitles the sole default chat in the live session and across restore` covers live state, persisted metadata, and restore.
- Confirmed falsifiable: removing only the `_retitleSoleDefaultChat` call makes the new test fail with exactly the bug signature (`defaultChatTitle: 'Agent title'` instead of `'User title'`).
- `agentHost/test/node`: 5678 passing, 0 failing.
- `agentHostChatContribution`: 439 passing, 0 failing.
- `eslint`, `hygiene` and `typecheck-client` all clean.

pull_requests.title: chat: Add Copilot connectors to the customization marketplace
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #337347 and based on the Agent Host connector support from #334141. The MCP management presentation adopts the connector treatment from `agents/connectors-in-mcp-alternative`, without its duplicate Available marketplace section.

This connector branch currently targets the designer branch (#337347), not the marketplace base (#337110). Accordingly, it keeps installed-only Discover with both feeds off; #337110 restores Overview in that state. The home-surface difference must be reconciled when these stacks are combined.

- port the connected Copilot connector MCP discovery service to the current Agent Host and keep connector definitions below user/workspace MCP configuration for Copilot, Claude, and Codex
- retain the default-off, automatically assignable `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled` experiment and forward its effective application-scoped value to Agent Host
- compose independently enabled public and authenticated sources into Discover, with lazy source initialization and source-specific cancellation/installation eligibility
- install supported GitHub Feed MCP servers from their version-pinned feed records through the existing policy-enforced MCP installer; unsupported local prerequisites offer publisher setup instructions when a link is available
- keep healthy feeds visible when another source fails, with named warnings and explicit retry actions; missing connector access instead uses a neutral **Sign in to view connectors.** prompt and primary **Sign In** button in Discover and MCP management
- route desktop connector HTTP through a dedicated, cancellable native channel instead of renderer fetch, which was blocked by CORS
- keep normal default-account sign-in scopes **unchanged regardless of the connector experiment**; request connector permission separately after an explicit connector sign-in or connection action
- rank the cached connector catalog locally with bounded, field-weighted VS Code fuzzy matching instead of assigning every match a constant score
- consume one globally paginated marketplace stream with a 24-entry page size, opaque retryable continuations, and round-robin interleaving for queryless browsing
- install and disconnect connectors through the existing GitHub account and Copilot consent flow, with bounded validation, pagination, cancellation, and connection polling
- show connected connector MCP servers under **Installed** and connector products in a separate **Connectors** section with status-aware Connect, Retry, Review, and overflow actions
- show connector metadata, contained MCP servers, external information, and lifecycle actions in a dedicated connector detail page
- keep the MCP page's duplicate **Available** marketplace section removed; available MCP servers and connectors remain owned by Discover

## Source settings

```json
{
  "chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled": true,
  "chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled": true
}
```

Either source can be enabled independently; both default to disabled. There is no global marketplace switch. The former `agentFinderPublicFeed` and `publicGitHubFeed` setting names do not enable the GitHub Feed; use `publicFeed` instead. With neither source enabled, Discover still searches installed customizations without catalog or marketplace-installation work.

Disabling a source cancels its in-flight discovery/consent work and prevents joining a disabled-source installation. Other enabled sources remain available. Disabling connectors also removes connector rows from MCP management and clears connector MCP servers in Agent Host. Unchanged effective enablement does not cancel an in-flight connector request.

## Ranking and pagination

- The workbench fetches `/plugins` using the current default GitHub account and uses the existing 60-second catalog cache. Search introduces no additional search API or model requests.
- Exact complete names score 100. Otherwise, every search word must match and its best field match contributes to an average: names 70-95, keywords/capabilities/tags 40-65, descriptions/representative queries 10-35. Within a field band, exact, prefix, substring, and compact fuzzy matches descend in that order.
- These 0-100 scores are **heuristic relevance**, not trust/quality and not calibrated equivalents to AgentFinder semantic scores. Queryless connector results remain unscored and retain native catalog order within the interleaved list. Connector search results are stably sorted into source-owned snapshots before native pagination. Continuations retain those entries, scores, and totals instead of rereading the catalog after its 60-second refresh.
- Queries are bounded to 256 characters and 16 words. Matching covers complete validated metadata with overlapping 128-character fuzzy windows; longer words must match contiguously in full, never through a truncated fuzzy prefix.
- The aggregator fills short native pages and merges enabled search sequences into one global page. Equal search scores retain source-registration order and each source's native ties. Queryless browsing interleaves enabled feeds round-robin, preserving each feed's native order and the rotation across page boundaries. When one feed exhausts, remaining feeds fill the available slots.
- Public continuations are only `{ token: string }`. Source cursors, buffered entries, and browse rotation remain service-side in the bounded 32-entry, 30-minute cache; cancellation and rejected pages do not consume the prior continuation. Cursor contents are not installation provenance.
- A native fetch failure suspends only that source for the continuation. Healthy sources keep supplying results, warnings persist across subsequent pages, and the combined total stays unknown. Source retry or successful authorization starts a new combined query to preserve ranking. All-source failure is not presented as a successful empty result.
- Native connector continuations are also opaque, source-owned references in a 32-entry LRU with 30-minute expiry, scoped to the issuing source, query, type, and page size. Valid replay and caller cancellation preserve the snapshot. Expired, evicted, and mismatched cursors require a new search.
- Default-account changes, sign-out, active-session authentication changes, and source lifetime changes invalidate the catalog and its snapshots. An in-process validity token also invalidates aggregator buffers, including exhausted sources, so a continuation cannot quietly mix accounts even without another native fetch. Unchanged identity notifications and unrelated sessions preserve valid pages; public-only continuations are unaffected. No validity token or authentication data is added to IPC.
- Discover forwards a single continuation, including for combined type filters. When multiple native formats are selected, it filters presentation without concatenating or re-sorting independent pages. It backfills bounded pages to find visible matches and offers Load More if the remaining result list cannot scroll; Accessible View applies the same filters.

## Authentication and native transport

Connector account/session selection remains in the workbench. Desktop HTTP uses a separate, narrowly scoped shared-process channel; it does not send credentials through the anonymous public-feed catalog channel. The native service accepts only typed catalog/connect/disconnect operations against the product-defined HTTPS endpoint, not caller-selected URLs or bodies. Credentials are supplied per request; there is no native credential store. Requests disallow redirects/cache, forward cancellation, enforce a 5 MiB response limit before IPC, and have a 30-second deadline covering headers and body. Both the editor workbench and Agents Window register the native service. Web retains the workbench request path and remains subject to API CORS/remote availability.

- Normal default-account sign-in never automatically adds connector scope, including when `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled === true`. Unset/false, enabled, public-feed-only, and GitHub Enterprise keep their ordinary scope bundles. Existing explicitly requested additional scopes and social sign-in options are preserved and deduplicated.
- Browsing checks existing sessions silently. Signed-out users and accounts lacking connector permission see **Sign in to view connectors.** and a primary **Sign In** button in Discover and the MCP Connectors section. There is no warning icon, failed/empty-result message, or incomplete-results hint solely because sign-in is needed. Healthy public results remain available; genuine source failures retain warning/retry behavior.
- Explicit **Sign In** first performs ordinary default-account sign-in with no additional scope options when needed, then separately requests connector permission for that account through the standard authentication service. Browsing and ordinary retries never initiate OAuth. The flow is cancellable and single-flight, rejects wrong-account/missing-grant results, and retains healthy results on cancellation or denial. MCP section rerenders preserve pending sign-in; hiding the page or disabling MCP access cancels it. Explicit connect/disconnect actions may also request the write-scope upgrade.
- A separately stored, suitably scoped session for the same account is reused even if the default account still references an older narrow session. Related session changes invalidate connector snapshots; an already-scoped token rejected by the API produces an HTTP error, not a consent loop.
- With the experiment enabled, Agent Host silently prefers an already-authorized same-account connector session that still satisfies the original Copilot scopes. Otherwise normal Copilot authentication is retained. This does not broaden Agent Host required-resource scopes, request background consent, or bypass rejected-session quarantine.

**Live verification succeeded after explicit GitHub consent in an isolated native profile.** The real catalog displayed Work IQ Copilot, Calendar, Mail, and Teams interleaved with public-feed entries. The existing Work IQ Mail connection was recognized as **Installed**, and the source warning disappeared. This verifies real catalog loading and existing connection state; no new third-party connector connection was created during this check.

## Validation

- Local focused suites for feed-backed MCP installation, Discover, source gating, connector behavior, and MCP management passed; client typecheck, layer check, changed-file lint, and formatting checks passed on the fork branch. Earlier isolated UI and consent checks are described above.
- CI and Linux screenshot hashes have not been used to validate this update; do not regenerate screenshot hashes on macOS.

## How to test

1. Exercise connectors-only, public-only, both, and neither using the source settings above, then run **Chat: Open Customizations**. Installed Discover must remain available with both sources disabled.
2. Search using exact connector names, prefixes, abbreviations, mixed-case multi-word queries, and metadata terms. Browse without a query and verify each feed retains its native order while the combined list interleaves the enabled feeds.
3. With both sources enabled, scroll to load results and combine type filters; use Load More only if bounded filtered backfilling leaves no scrollable matches. Verify a single continuation, preserved search order or browse rotation, and no duplicates or missing entries. Cancellation or rejected pages must leave the prior continuation replayable.
4. Fail one source during browsing/search or a later page. Healthy results continue with a named warning and unknown total; source retry starts a fresh combined query. All-source failure must show warnings and recovery, not an empty-success message.
5. Start normal public GitHub sign-in with the connector experiment unset/false, public-feed-only, and enabled. None of these cases adds connector permission to the default scopes. GitHub Enterprise also keeps its original scopes.
6. Start signed out, then repeat with an existing session lacking connector permission. Discover and MCP management show a neutral **Sign in to view connectors.** prompt and primary **Sign In** action, without warning or false empty/failure presentation. No browsing/retry action opens consent. Choose **Sign In**: a signed-out user first completes ordinary sign-in without extra scopes, then grants connector permission separately; an existing account goes straight to missing connector consent. Verify connector cards join public results. Cancellation/denial retains healthy cards, and leaving the MCP page cancels pending authorization. An already-scoped token rejected by the API must show an HTTP error rather than a consent loop.
7. Choose **Install** for a connector, complete its browser connection consent, and verify it becomes installed only after the connected catalog confirms success.
8. Open **MCP Servers**. Connected connector MCP servers appear under **Installed**, connector products appear under **Connectors**, and no **Available** marketplace section is shown.
9. Exercise Connect, Retry, Review, Disconnect, and pending states, including keyboard navigation and accessible labels.
10. Open a connector and verify its detail shows status, metadata, contained MCP servers, external information, and lifecycle actions rather than raw MCP configuration.
11. Start fresh Copilot, Claude, and Codex sessions and verify connector MCP servers are available unless overridden by a same-name user/workspace server.
12. Toggle each source during discovery and authorization. Only the disabled source's work should stop; re-enabling should fetch fresh results rather than restore cancelled work. Disabling connectors removes its management rows and prevents fresh Agent Host sessions from receiving connector servers.
13. Start a multi-page connector search, then refresh the catalog after 60 seconds with changed membership and relevance. Existing continuations keep their original snapshot and do not fetch the catalog again; a new search sees the refreshed data. Repeat in browsing mode.
14. Switch the default account, sign out, or change the active or related scoped authentication session between pages. Old native and globally buffered continuations must explicitly require a new search, and late responses from the old account must not replace the new catalog. Public-only pages and unrelated-session notifications remain unaffected.

pull_requests.title: agent-host: preserve identity and actor of admitted turns
pull_requests.body:
## What and why

Make accepted Agent Host turns identifiable and distinguish human input from generated work so downstream scorecards can count user-initiated turns without relying on response completion.

The Microsoft `agentHost.userMessageSent` event currently lacks the turn/chat key needed for deduplication. Its `inline` origin classification also hides whether a human or a system produced the message. In addition, the workbench adapter currently stamps system-initiated requests as user messages.

Part of [microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9130](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9130).

## Changes

- Add `turnId` and telemetry-safe `chatSessionId` to the Microsoft send event, alongside its owning `agentSessionId`.
- Add `messageActorKind` independently of the existing origin classification: a human inline request reports actor `user`, while a system-generated inline request reports `systemNotification` even though both have origin `inline`.
- Recognize both modern subagent chat URIs and legacy subagent sessions.
- Keep remote-only pending messages on their session's Agent Host participant when sent immediately, rather than silently routing them through the legacy default participant.
- Preserve the original actor, metadata, and system label for direct, queued, and steering workbench requests. A system notification queued by another client stays system-generated when choosing **Send Immediately**, after a reload, or when a rejected resend is requeued. Explicit system initiation cannot be overwritten by an older `user` classification.

## Scorecard contract and rollout boundary

These fields support **admitted explicit-human turns**, not successful responses. Queue entries qualify when admitted, including subsequent execution failures; an entry removed before admission does not qualify. Steering and resuming the same turn do not introduce a new admitted send.

Consumers must deduplicate using the approved user identity plus owning session, chat, and turn, and require an explicitly human actor and non-subagent flag. Inline is not itself proof of human initiation. Rows from older builds missing these fields must not be silently classified.

This is the producer-side prerequisite, not the scorecard deployment. The existing legacy panel/inline metric observes responses, so it is only a close analogue of accepted starts. Managed input mapping, population/trigger validation, and a versioned or aligned local metric are separate downstream work. Do not add overlapping core completion events to this numerator or silently substitute a remote host's machine identity for the initiating user's assignment unit.

## Manual verification

Exercised an isolated, signed-in Code OSS build and checked its local telemetry log. Direct human sends carried the human actor and correlation identifiers; a queued system notification emitted only on admission and retained its non-human actor.

A synthetic automation message from a second loopback AHP client exposed the participant-routing gap through the real **Send Immediately** UI. After the correction, the same scenario created a new Agent Host turn with actor automation and preserved metadata, rather than a legacy Ask request. Confirmed the completed host turn, the visible response, and absence of a legacy panel.request event in the post-fix probe window.

These checks validate local production-code logging, not production ingestion or downstream scorecard deployment. Also verified reload/reconnection with a remote automation message still pending: reopened the session, chose **Send Immediately**, and confirmed a new completed host turn with actor automation and preserved metadata/label, one matching host send event, and no legacy panel.request. Full-host-restart disk-only recovery, queue deletion, and inline/subagent cases were not live-verified.

pull_requests.title: automations: fix: distinguish run admission from session creation
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

**Draft — not merge-ready.** This follow-up to #337334 contains an operation-ordering optimization and accepted/pending manual-run feedback. The result-contract migration, status-query output, and session-start accessibility feedback are implemented and covered by focused regressions. Cancellation ownership for tool-launched pending runs still needs a decision and follow-through.

## Background

The Agent Host owns Automation admission, session creation, execution, and terminal outcomes. The Agents Window requests runs and observes authoritative state; it does not execute Automation sessions itself.

Host admission and session creation are distinct events. A manual run can be accepted while credentials or another execution prerequisite are unavailable. That run remains pending and occupies the Automation's active-run slot even though no session exists yet.

The removal PR already removed the client's premature deadline while waiting for an admitted run to acquire a session or reach a terminal state. This follow-up acknowledges admission without waiting for session creation, while continuing to observe the host.

## Changes

### 1. Stable operation ordering

`AgentHostAutomationService.withOperation` reconstructs the existing operation set in canonical `Update`, `Remove`, `Run` order instead of appending a restored operation. After run completion, restoring `Remove` no longer leaves a different order that an unrelated configuration refresh would treat as a meaningful catalogue change.

The regression extends the existing host run-lifecycle test: after completion, an unrelated configuration change must cause zero additional storage writes, zero catalogue publications, and preserve canonical operation order.

### 2. Admission-first manual-run feedback

- The shared request result carries the admitted `runId`, allows its initial run snapshot to be absent, and resolves `whenCompleted` with the terminal run snapshot.
- `AgentHostAutomationStore` returns after admission, starts deadline-free terminal observation, and retains cancellation observation until that observation ends.
- The shared runner result adds `kind: 'accepted'`. The Sessions runner reports `started` when a session is already known and `accepted` while the run is pending or has not yet appeared in the catalogue.
- Tool results and card accessibility announcements distinguish acceptance/waiting from an actually started session. The run tool's past-tense message becomes "Requested automation".
- The architecture specification separates admission, session creation, completion, and observation failure.

Elapsed renderer waiting time must never turn a host-accepted pending run into failure or `notStarted`. Observation loss cannot undo admission or synthesize a terminal result; the runner retains acceptance and warns that the host may still execute the run.

### Review fixes

**Result-contract consumers and regressions:** Dispatched fixtures now provide `runId` and terminal snapshots, optional initial snapshots are narrowed, and store tests await observations instead of leaving them open. Pending cancellation tests distinguish admission feedback from authoritative termination: a previously accepted result stays accepted while cancellation is observed. Coverage includes admission before catalogue publication and observation loss.

**Actionable status queries:** `listAutomations` includes each definition's available run snapshots. Match the returned run ID against `runs[].id` to inspect status, session resource, completion time, and errors. Session URIs are serialized as strings or `null`; runs belonging to other definitions are excluded. The descriptions clarify that these snapshots are not complete history and that an accepted run's temporary absence is not proof of failure.

**Session-start accessibility feedback:** After a card reports acceptance, it observes the run's authoritative session resource and announces "Started automation" once linkage appears. The observer disposes itself after that announcement, and its enclosing lifetime ends on operation completion, card removal, or widget disposal. No additional shared runner or execution contract is needed for this view-owned feedback.

## Remaining work before merge

- [ ] Decide cancellation ownership for tool-launched accepted runs that do not yet have a session. The tool still detaches its linked token on admission; retaining it blindly would also forward tool-framework cleanup cancellation.
- [ ] Complete the remaining cancellation cleanup and error handling, including simplifying duplicated cancellation catch logic, and validate the chosen ownership behavior.

These cancellation changes remain separate from the three approved review fixes; this PR is still a draft.

## Validation

- **197 passing** focused unit tests across `automationRunner.test.ts`, `automationTools.test.ts`, `agentHostAutomationStore.test.ts`, and `automationsView.test.ts`, including disposable tracking.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes.
- `git diff --check` and repository pre-commit hygiene pass.
- Test output was regenerated with `npm run transpile-client`. The independent ordering regression was previously validated and is unchanged by these review fixes.

## Scope

Thirteen files differ from the main-branch merge base: the original nine follow-up files plus four focused test files. The ordering change, initial feedback draft, and approved review fixes are separate commits. No browser-owned execution is reintroduced. Cloud automations, hover explanations, and the separately deferred Claude-readiness changes are excluded.

pull_requests.title: build: harden Linux product signing resilience
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Why

Linux product jobs have a 90-minute timeout, but ESRP signing can take up to its configured 120-minute limit. That leaves the job vulnerable to cancellation before it can finish signing, scan the packages, and upload artifacts.

This PR gives the job enough headroom and fixes misleading or missing output from the shared signing helper. It does not change signing policy or skip release checks.

## Changes

- Increase the **Linux product-job timeout to 180 minutes**. ESRP stays at 120 minutes; CI job limits are unchanged.
- Start Debian/RPM signing **before Snap packaging**, keeping both signers parallel and overlapping signing with tests.
- Preserve each signing process's stdout, stderr, exit result, and elapsed time. Observe failures immediately so a later parallel signer cannot terminate Node before ordered output consumption; the original promise still rejects. This also fixes Windows/macOS callers of the shared helper.
- Add a **20-minute slow-signing warning** for Linux. Detached output still appears at the existing post-test attach step, not live during tests.

## Validation

The final diff contains four signing-related production files and no added test files. Existing repository tests, test discovery, and CI/release checks are unchanged. YAML parsing, scoped hygiene, and whitespace checks passed for the final edits.

**Real-signing Product validation passed on the earlier revision `ef6b22a44af`:** all ten stages succeeded with tests and artifact sanity enabled. This is historical signing evidence; **the final revision has not had a live pipeline run**.

| Platform | Live validation at `ef6b22a44af` |
| --- | --- |
| **Linux x64, including Snap** | Both DEB/RPM signing operations, seven artifacts, six product SBOMs, and six artifact-sanity tests passed. The scratch-directory cleanup test passed unskipped. The DEB signature and its SPDX hash were independently verified. |
| **Windows x64** | All seven signing operations, six artifacts, five product SBOMs, and six artifact-sanity tests passed, including signature and installer checks. |
| **macOS ARM64** | All four signing and four notarization operations, five artifacts, four product SBOMs, and five artifact-sanity tests passed, including strict signature/notarization checks. One desktop case recovered from an extension-install timeout using the existing test retry. |

All three CLI SBOMs also succeeded. Artifacts from that run were uploaded privately.

## Limits

- RPM signing and artifact upload passed, but RPM installation and independent RPM signature verification were not tested.
- Existing Linux/Windows binary-scan findings remain; passing the configured security tasks does not mean zero findings. The macOS template does not run BinSkim or antimalware scans.
- The live run did not inject signing failures or independently compare exact output bytes. The PR-added regression tests are no longer included.
- Neither Linux signer reached the 20-minute warning, and the 180-minute job limit was not exercised. macOS notarization exceeded 20 minutes but is outside the Linux-only warning.
- Existing individual test skips remain, including Windows scratch-directory cleanup. Unpublished artifact tests do not compare against update-service hashes.

This PR targets `main`; applying it to stable requires a separate backport. No production release or public artifact publication was tested.

pull_requests.title: sessions: Restore sandbox sessions promptly on reload
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Restore sandbox providers and cached session rows from a minimal, account-scoped inventory before awaiting network discovery on reload. The inventory stays in machine-local profile storage, contains no credentials or chat transcripts, and restoration does not connect to or wake environments.
- Refresh discovery incrementally with cached task details, coalesced requests, staleness checks, and failure backoff. Preserve existing rows after failed or partial discovery, and use full scans for authoritative reconciliation.
- Publish cached session additions when providers arrive. Provider disappearance refreshes the list without reporting session deletion or triggering deletion-style cleanup.
- Add regression coverage for discovery, provider lifecycle, metadata updates, reload restoration, account isolation, cancellation, provisioning, and cross-window inventory writes. The earlier telemetry fixture correction adds its required steering fields without changing production telemetry.

## Review feedback addressed

- **Provider lifecycle:** unregistering a provider now emits a catalog refresh with no removed sessions. Actual provider-reported removals still follow the existing deletion path; the extra removal-membership tracking is gone.
- **Metadata:** opt-in discovery updates refresh existing row titles, timestamps, repository metadata, and provider labels without replacing adapters. Per-field discovery baselines survive reload and protect fields subsequently changed by the host. Live status remains host-owned. Missing discovery timestamps do not manufacture new session activity.
- **Inventory writes:** entries are stored separately by account, environment, and session. Windows write only their local changes and remove only previously known entries, rather than replacing an account-wide snapshot. Legacy snapshots migrate during restoration.
- **Lost bindings:** confirmed disappearance of a previously discovered environment binding emits an explicit task removal. Failed requests retain the last known binding and remain queued for retry, so a later successful response can still report the removal.

Restoration requires account identity and an inventory previously populated by discovery or provisioning. Account changes stop listing the previous account's providers without erasing its saved inventory; same-account credential refreshes preserve providers. Legacy provider summaries without discovery baselines conservatively preserve mismatched fields whose ownership is unknown.

## Validation

- **643 passing tests, 13 existing pending** across six focused Electron unit suites: session management, sandbox API, sandbox contribution, remote providers, local provider, and tunnel contribution.
- Passed: client type checking (`npm run typecheck-client -- --pretty false`).
- Passed: targeted ESLint for all 11 review-fix TypeScript files, whitespace checks, and pre-commit hygiene.
- Cross-window regression tests use independent storage caches and delayed external visibility; they cover an older scan completing after another window provisions a session, plus unchanged stale writes after metadata updates/removals.
- The earlier test-runner startup blockers did not recur. Real-window reload/account-switch checks and multi-window E2E verification remain human validation tasks; the unit tests are not a claim that those scenarios have been exercised.
