pull_requests.title: agentHost: opt-in subagent model guidance for Claude Opus sessions
pull_requests.body:
Adds an opt-in prompt experiment for Copilot agent host sessions running a Claude Opus model: guidance on which lighter model to run a subagent on. It is off by default and registered for experiment rollout.

This replaces what the PR did before. The earlier version ported the Copilot Chat Opus prompt behind one switch (`chat.opusAltPrompt.enabled`): about ten removals and five additions together, so its result could not be attributed to any one of them. That commit is still in the branch history; the tree no longer contains it. A second experiment that removed three "verify before you finish" sentences was in this PR until 5 October; benchmark runs showed no measurable effect from it, and it has been taken out so the PR is about one thing.

Draft. Benchmark results are in "What the benchmark showed": the current wording does not yet show a saving for a whole task, and a second wording is being screened. See "Not checked" before relying on it.

## The setting

| Setting | Values | What it changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.agentHost.subagentModelGuidance` | `off` (default), `sameProvider`, `crossProvider` | Tells the agent which lighter model to run a subagent on |

It applies only when the session's model id starts with `claude-opus`.

### Subagent model guidance

Today the prompt tells the agent, in two places, to leave the `task` tool's `model` parameter unset, and in ten nightly benchmark runs the agent never named a model. With the setting on:

- The host's two "leave `model` unset" lines are replaced by guidance: a lightweight model for searching, reading and run-and-report work; a mid-sized model for a well-defined piece of implementation; unset (the session's model) for work that needs the agent's own judgment.
- The foundation prompt's "Trust the harness defaults for subagents" rule is narrowed to `reasoning_effort` and `context_tier`, so the prompt does not say both "choose a model" and "leave it unset".

| Value | Lightweight | Mid-sized |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sameProvider` | `claude-haiku-4.5` | `claude-sonnet-5.5` |
| `crossProvider` | `gpt-6-luna` | `gpt-5.6-terra` |

The two mixes are alternatives, so this is one setting with three values and not two switches.

## What the benchmark showed

Two sets of runs on an internal 13-task agent benchmark with Opus 5.5, on one VS Code build. First, three full runs of each variant against three of the unmodified prompt. Then 29 further attempts at the two long tasks, which are the only ones where the agent delegates, planned from the first set's results before they were run. The variants were delivered as a prompt override with the same wording as these settings (see "Checked"), not through this code path.

**Subagent model guidance: a named model is honored and the delegated work is cheaper, but the agent follows the guidance unevenly, and no saving for a whole task is shown.**

Delegations on the two long tasks, both sets:

| | Unmodified | `sameProvider` wording | `crossProvider` wording |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Delegations | 81 | 71 | 76 |
| Named a model | 0 | 26, all `claude-sonnet-5.5` | 34: 29 `gpt-5.6-terra`, 1 `gpt-6-luna`, 4 `claude-sonnet-5` |
| Subagent ran only on the model named | n/a | 26 of 26 | 34 of 34 |

- **Cheaper per piece.** One component is delegated in nearly every attempt at one of the tasks. It cost a median of $1.26 on Opus (20 times), $0.41 on Sonnet 5.5 (5) and $0.45 on GPT-5.6 Terra (4), with ranges that do not overlap.
- **Not cheaper per task.** Cost per attempt overlapped between every variant and the unmodified prompt on both long tasks (six attempts each, ten for the unmodified prompt on one). After the first set the `crossProvider` wording looked cheaper; on the second set it was not.
- **The reason is uneven adherence.** With the same prompt and build, the agent named a model for most delegations in some attempts and for none or one in others (4 of 6 `crossProvider` attempts in the second set). The attempts that named models were the cheap ones. Wording alone does not make the choice reliable.
- **It chose a model the guidance does not name.** Four delegations in one `crossProvider` attempt asked for `claude-sonnet-5`, which the `task` tool lists and the prompt does not mention.
- The lightweight model was chosen once in 147 delegations, for reading-and-summarizing work as intended. The agent rarely delegates that kind of work on this benchmark.
- Work the guidance reserves for the session's model mostly stayed there: one delegation for hardening tests named the mid-sized model, of 60 that named any.
- Pass rates did not drop with either wording, and no delegation appeared on the eleven tasks where the agent does not delegate today.

Limits that apply to all of it: few attempts per arm, so no cost difference here is beyond chance; one model; a prompt override also changes the prompt's layout and caching, which these settings do not.

## How it is built

- Section transforms in `customize` mode (`promptExperiments.ts`, applied by the contributor in `anthropicPrompt.ts`). The foundation prompt, its guardrails and its per-session content are untouched; only the named sentences change.
- Each edit matches a whole sentence or bullet. If the foundation rewords one, the edit leaves the text alone. That also means it stops applying without an error; the end-to-end test below fails when that happens.
- `composeToolInstructions` now appends the host's tool lines after a transform override's output. It used to return a transform untouched, which dropped the host's lines. No existing contributor used a transform on `tool_instructions`.
- The tool-instruction line context gains `modelId`, so the subagent line can be gated on the session model.
- **Model switches.** A session keeps the prompt it launched with. A model change that crosses the Claude Opus boundary while the guidance is on now restarts the session, the same way a switch to or from HydraFusion does. Without that, a session switched from Opus to Haiku would stay told to delegate to models heavier than its own.

## Also removed

The Opus 4.8 prompt and `chat.agentHost.opus48Prompt.enabled`, with their config key, forwarding and tests. If that setting is referenced by a running experiment, that needs handling before this merges.

## Checked

- **Against the real runtime.** A new case in `copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts` replays an Opus 5.5 turn through the bundled Copilot runtime with the guidance off and then on, and asserts the two system prompts differ by exactly the intended edits. It fails if an edit lands in the wrong section, changes more than its sentence, or stops matching. It passes locally. Its replay fixture is the existing Opus 5.5 exchange twice, written by hand, not recorded.
- That test found two things unit tests could not, one fixed here and one that cannot be:
  - Host tool lines appended after a transform lost the blank line they normally have. Restored.
  - **One side effect remains.** When the `tool_instructions` group is transformed, the runtime renders the group's intro sentence ("You have access to several tools. ...") inside `<tools>` instead of before it. A transform cannot avoid that. It happens only with subagent model guidance on, and the test pins it.
- Unit tests: 82 pass across `promptExperiments.test.ts`, `toolInstructions.test.ts` and `agentHostPromptRegistry.test.ts`; 7 pass in `agentHostCopilotCliSettingsContribution.test.ts`; the model-switch test in `copilotAgent.test.ts` passes.
- ESLint and the pre-commit hygiene check on the changed files.
- **CI on the pinned SDK.** My checkout has an older `@github/copilot-sdk` preview than `main` pins, so locally the existing prompt snapshots do not match and some unrelated tests fail with and without this change. CI is the run that counts: all jobs pass on the latest commit, including the new end-to-end test (macOS job). "Linux / Electron" failed once in an existing test this PR does not touch ("client tool reaches ready after start and completes", one extra event in a traffic snapshot) and passed when re-run. That was on the commit before the verification experiment was removed; CI on the latest commit is the one to read.
- An independent code review of the first commit; its three findings (the model-switch case, an undocumented dropped sentence, and tests that pinned copies of the foundation text) are addressed in the second commit.
- **Same wording as the benchmark variants.** Applied to a system prompt captured from a real Opus 5.5 request, these edits give the prompt text used for benchmark runs of each variant, character for character. The product's real output differs from that text only by the intro-sentence side effect above, and only for subagent model guidance.

## Not checked

- **Not run in a VS Code window or on a benchmark through this code path.** The benchmark runs deliver the same wording through the `promptOverrideString` debug setting, which replaces the whole prompt. A benchmark run of a build that contains this PR, with the settings on, is the missing confirmation.
- **The restart on a model switch** is covered by a unit test with a fake session. Whether a restart mid-conversation is an acceptable cost for users in the experiment is a product call.

## Known limits

- **A sentence about `/subagents` preferences is dropped with the narrowed rule.** The foundation rule ends "The runtime resolves `/subagents` preferences when these fields are omitted; do not copy them merely because they appear in `<subagent_model_preferences>`". Narrowing the rule removes it. It concerns the model preference, which the guidance overrides; the `task` tool's parameter descriptions still carry it.
- **One contradiction remains.** The `task` tool's `model` parameter has its own description saying to set it only when the user asks. That text belongs to the runtime and cannot be changed from here, so the guidance ends by saying it takes precedence. The clean fix is in the runtime.
- **Model names are literals in this PR and will go stale.** They are also not checked against what the user's plan offers. They do not need to be: the agent host already holds each model's category (`lightweight`, `versatile`, `powerful`) and billing from the models list, so the names can be filled in from that when the session starts, with nothing fixed here or in the runtime. That is the next change to this PR once the wording is settled.
- **User preferences.** When the agent sets `model`, the user's own `/subagents` preference is bypassed. That needs a product decision before any rollout beyond an experiment.
- **Scope.** Gated on any `claude-opus` model. The benchmark evidence is from Opus 5.5 only.

pull_requests.title: Add initial workspace context to Copilot Agent Host chats
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Gives the first turn of a new Copilot Agent Host chat a small file-name tree of its working directories, so the model can orient itself without listing the workspace first.

- Behind `chat.experimental.workspaceSnapshot` (off by default, experiment-controlled). While off, nothing is read, no prompt changes, and no telemetry is sent.
- `WorkspaceContextContribution` walks the turn's working directories through `IFileService`, names only, capped at 2,000 characters. It skips hidden entries, common dependency and build folders, and Git storage directories. Like the classic Copilot Chat workspace structure, it does not apply `.gitignore`.
- The walk starts when the turn is accepted, and the send waits at most one second for it. Measured at 1–4 ms on this repository.
- The tree is added as an ordinary host instruction (a `<workspace_info>` block); the user's message is unchanged and no provider code changes.
- Sent once per chat: not on later turns, restored chats, forks, side chats, or tool-spawned chats. A first turn that never reaches the provider leaves it for the next one.
- Reports `agentHost.workspaceSnapshot` telemetry when the turn is handed to the provider.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/platform/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js"`: passed (9,272 passing, 72 pending, 0 failing).
- `npm run typecheck-client`, ESLint on the changed files, and hygiene: passed.
- Code OSS from sources, first turn in a small folder:
  - Setting off: no `[WorkspaceContext]` log lines and no `<workspace_info>` in the prompt.
  - Setting on: `included 1/1 roots, 133 characters (prepared, waited 0ms)`, the prompt carries `<workspace_info>`, and the model lists the files without a tool call.

pull_requests.title: voice: mark numeric telemetry fields as measurements
pull_requests.body:
## What

Adds `isMeasurement: true` to every emitted `number` and `boolean` field in the Voice Mode telemetry classifications in `voiceTelemetry.ts`.

## Why

VS Code's telemetry convention (and the repo's telemetry instructions) require that every emitted `number` and `boolean` declare `isMeasurement: true`. Telemetry serialization is runtime-type-driven, so these values already land in `Measures` at runtime — but the GDPR classification metadata was incomplete and inconsistent with every other chat telemetry file (e.g. `chatSpeechToTextService.ts`, `chatEditingSession.ts`), which all follow the rule. The voice file was the sole outlier.

All of these events are actively emitted via `publicLog2` in `voiceSessionController.ts` and `agentsVoice.contribution.ts`.

## Changes

Marked 13 numeric/boolean fields across 9 classifications:

- `voiceDisabled.daysActive`
- `voiceFirstConnect.timeToConnectMs`
- `voiceSessionStarted.sessionIndex`
- `voiceSessionEnded.turnCount`, `.durationSec`, `.reconnectCount`
- `voicePtt.holdDurationMs`
- `voiceTtsListenThrough.listenedToEnd`, `.listenedPct`
- `voiceToolApproval.approved`
- `voiceReconnect.timeSinceLastConnectSec`
- `voiceLatency.timeToFirstTranscriptionMs`, `.endToEndTurnMs`

## Notes for reviewers

- Metadata-only change on TypeScript classification literals — no runtime behavior changes.
- String fields (`source`, `toolName`, `kind`, `reason`, `rejectionReason`) are correctly left unmarked.

pull_requests.title: automations: refactor: remove browser-owned automation execution
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Why

Automations should have one execution authority rather than a browser executor alongside the Agent Host. This makes AHP the only execution path for both local and remote-host Automations. Local Automations remain supported through the local Agent Host.

The Agents Window continues to manage definitions, request manual runs, and observe results. It no longer evaluates schedules, elects a leader, claims browser-ledger executions, creates run sessions, sends their first prompts, or recovers their lifecycle.

## Approach

- Remove browser scheduling, leadership, execution/storage services, fallback paths, their registrations/settings, and obsolete tests.
- Retain the provider-neutral management and manual-dispatch APIs over AHP projections. Definition and run identities include the concrete host and complete resource URI, preventing collisions and wrong-host routing.
- Apply host availability and operation checks across authoring, tools, templates/imports, catalogue, and history. Update-only hosts remain editable; unavailable selections stay visible, while unsupported host/workspace/session-type combinations cannot be saved. Missing support or connectivity never falls back to local execution.
- Initialize host authority without a browser migration-completion handshake. Restore existing enablement/timeout configuration and consult optional provider-owned execution readiness. Copilot preserves catch-up work while its required credentials are unavailable.
- Keep Run Now as dispatch and observation, including cancellation during admission/session creation. An already-admitted run no longer hits the browser's 30-second mutation deadline while waiting for its session.

The ownership and lifecycle contract is documented in `src/vs/sessions/AUTOMATIONS.md`.

## Compatibility and retained data

Clients require standard AHP Automation support plus `vscode.autonomousAutomations` in initialize metadata. Older hosts receive upgrade guidance, including hosts whose previous migration already completed. Ordinary AHP sessions are unaffected.

**The transition assumes users have already moved to host-owned definitions.** Obsolete browser definition ledgers are left untouched, but are no longer loaded, migrated, displayed, or executed. There is no legacy-specific warning. Existing AHP definitions/history remain authoritative, and already-migrated historical run archives remain readable without becoming an execution authority.

## Scope

No cloud Automations implementation or UI redesign. **Claude and Codex readiness fixes belong together in a separate provider-readiness PR.** Both providers' implementations and tests remain unchanged in this removal PR.

Richer early accepted/pending run feedback, independent operation-order optimization, and disabled-card hover explanations are also deferred to follow-up work.

## Validation

- Latest validation after rebasing onto current main: **326 dialog/local Agent Host provider tests passing**, with **11 pending tests**.
- Earlier focused validation of retained changes includes host-authority, AHP store, manual-runner, tool, Copilot readiness, and session-picker suites.
- `npm run typecheck-client -- --pretty false` passes.
- Regression coverage includes provider-readiness-gated catch-up, Copilot credential readiness, effective first-turn model selection, incompatible targets, cancellation during admission, and cancellation after waiting more than 30 seconds for a session.
- Claude and Codex source/test files match the removal branch's merge base; provider-specific readiness validation belongs to their combined follow-up.

No live GitHub Automation mutations or cloud compute were exercised.

pull_requests.title: Make removal of many decoration subtypes linear instead of quadratic
pull_requests.body:
### Problem

When an extension passes per-option `renderOptions` to `TextEditor.setDecorations` (Error Lens does this for its inline messages), `CodeEditorWidget.setDecorationsByType` registers one decoration subtype per distinct render-options hash, and each subtype's `DecorationCSSRules` inserts up to three rules into the editor stylesheet.

Tearing those subtypes down is quadratic. `DecorationCSSRules.dispose` calls `removeCSSRulesContainingSelector`, which scans every rule in the sheet and reads `selectorText` off each one, and the widget does that once per subtype that is no longer used. I profiled the renderer main thread on a file with ~11k diagnostics (a NativeScript `android.d.ts`): the extension host was idle, but the renderer was blocked for 66 s, of which 45 s was the scan loop in `removeCSSRulesContainingSelector` and 15 s its `isCSSStyleRule` helper. Inserting the same 36k rules cost 0.4 s.

### Fix

- `createCSSRule` now returns the `CSSRule` it inserted, and `DecorationCSSRules` keeps those handles. Disposal removes them by identity through a new `domStylesheets.removeCSSRules(Set<CSSRule>)`, a single pass with an O(1) membership test per rule and no `selectorText` reads. Cloned global stylesheets (auxiliary windows) hold their own rule objects, so those are matched by `cssText`, read before the source rules are detached.
- The stylesheet wrappers in `abstractCodeEditorService.ts` share a new `DecorationStyleSheet` base with `beginRemovalBatch` / `endRemovalBatch`. A new **optional** `ICodeEditorService.removeDecorationTypes(keys)` opens a batch on every sheet, removes all keys, and flushes once. The four widget loops that drop many subtypes and `MainThreadTextEditors.dispose` go through it, falling back to per-key `removeDecorationType` when an implementation does not provide it. Existing implementations of `ICodeEditorService` are unaffected.
- Identity matching is also stricter than the old substring match: removing type `x` no longer removes the rules of an unrelated type `x-1`.

`removeCSSRulesContainingSelector` is untouched and still used by `zoneWidget.ts` and `decorationsService.ts`.

Not covered here: `DecorationCSSRules` still re-inserts its own rules per instance on color theme change, so that path stays quadratic with a smaller constant. That seemed better handled separately (probably by rewriting `style.cssText` in place).

### Tests

- New `src/vs/base/test/browser/domStylesheets.test.ts`: `createCSSRule` return value, identity removal, idempotent removal, identity vs. two rules with the same selector, and a regression test that `removeCSSRulesContainingSelector` still matches substrings.
- `decorationRenderOptions.test.ts`: new `removeDecorationTypes removes exactly the given types`. `TestGlobalStyleSheet` now stores rule handles.
- `npm run compile` (0 errors), `npm run eslint` and hygiene on the touched files, and `./scripts/test.sh` for `domStylesheets`, `Decoration Render Options`, `CodeEditorWidget` and `MainThreadEditors` all pass (33 tests).

### How to test manually

Install Error Lens, open a `.d.ts` with thousands of diagnostics (e.g. `@nativescript/types-android/lib/android/android-platform-35.d.ts`, which triggers ~11k "namespace declared with module keyword" diagnostics), then close the tab or edit the file. Before: multi-second to minute-long UI freeze. After: no freeze.

I could not find an existing issue for this; happy to file one if you want it tracked separately.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: keep the default chat title in sync with a session rename
pull_requests.body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336995
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326054

Renaming a session from the **sessions list** left the **session header** showing the old title. Worse, clicking into that header and pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> renamed the default chat, which mirrors back onto the session and overwrote the rename — silent data loss.

## Why it happened

A session whose only chat is its default chat has no independently titled chat: the header renders the session title. But the default chat still owns persisted title metadata, written whenever something renamed it directly — the `rename_chat` tool, the chat header, or an automatic title.

A session-scoped rename (the sessions list path) updated only the session, so that chat metadata went stale. On restore it was seeded back as the chat's *own* title, making the divergence sticky: the list showed the new name, the header showed the old one, and committing the header handed the stale title back to the session.

This regressed in #331509 (commit 771cd9d5d75), which removed the `isDefaultChat && _isOnlySessionChat(session)` guard from `_renameChatFromTool` — after that, a single-chat session could get an independent title stamped onto its default chat.

## What changed

`SessionTitleContribution._retitleSoleDefaultChat` mirrors a session rename down onto the sole default chat, updating both live state (so the open header updates immediately) and persisted metadata (so it survives restore).

Restoring the old guard alone would **not** have been sufficient: it only covers the `rename_chat` tool path, while the UI header rename flows through `onDidApplyClientAction`. Handling it in `onDidApplyClientAction` covers every session-channel rename — sessions list, tool, or header — and repairs sessions already broken on disk the next time they are renamed.

Sessions that own peer chats are skipped: their default chat is independently titled by design.

## Notes for reviewers

- The four metadata writes are two pairs — the title plus a companion `…SOURCE` key marking it user-set — written to both the chat's own database and the session's database keyed by chat. `onHydrateChat` reads them in that order on restore, so writing only one would leave the other as a stale fallback.
- `state.defaultChat ?? buildDefaultChatUri(session)` covers state where `defaultChat` is not yet populated.

## Validation

- New test `a session rename retitles the sole default chat in the live session and across restore` covers live state, persisted metadata, and restore.
- Confirmed falsifiable: removing only the `_retitleSoleDefaultChat` call makes the new test fail with exactly the bug signature (`defaultChatTitle: 'Agent title'` instead of `'User title'`).
- `agentHost/test/node`: 5678 passing, 0 failing.
- `agentHostChatContribution`: 439 passing, 0 failing.
- `eslint`, `hygiene` and `typecheck-client` all clean.

pull_requests.title: sessions: add image previews to reference hovers and align all artifact type behavior better
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Chat session references currently make image files difficult to identify without opening them, and reference behavior differs between the Agents window and editor Chat. This change adds on-demand image previews to reference hovers and aligns rich metadata, actions, layout, and lifecycle behavior across both surfaces.

The references list remains compact: visual detail and additional actions appear only in the existing hover or secondary panel.

## Changes

### Image reference previews

- Shows a bounded thumbnail and supporting path when an image-file reference is hovered or keyboard-selected.
- Reuses the attachment image-preview component, thumbnail cache, and workbench hover styling.
- Reads local, remote, and Agent Host resources through the file service on first hover, with a 20 MB safety limit.
- Keeps the path visible and shows a localized unavailable state when an image cannot be read, decoded, or previewed.
- Cancels obsolete reads and disposes object URLs when hovers or references leave their visible lifetime.
- Leaves produced image artifacts and generic URL resources on their existing behavior.

### Consistent reference cards and actions

- Uses the same rich GitHub card for issues, pull requests, and commits in the Agents window and editor Chat.
- Lazily resolves commit metadata and preserves the newest metadata when duplicate references are merged.
- Adds capability-gated removal actions to editor Chat and announces successful removal to screen readers; backend failures use the notification service.
- Adds the appropriate copy action for each resource type:
  - website URL
  - file path or relative path
  - generic resource URI
  - non-GitHub issue or pull-request URL
  - GitHub URL or commit hash
- Keeps row actions concise and shows only incremental actions in collection hover footers.

### Layout, theming, and accessibility

- Shares responsive location and action layouts across file, image, and GitHub hovers, including narrow viewports.
- Uses workbench theme colors for links and hover actions instead of browser-default anchor colors.
- Keeps row accessible names, path descriptions, list navigation, and focus behavior unchanged.
- Gives preview images localized alternative text without adding a tab stop.
- Supports keyboard access to hover links and actions, with Escape returning focus to the references list.

## How to test

1. Open an Agents window or editor Chat session containing an image-file reference, a regular file reference, a website, and GitHub issue, pull-request, and commit references.
2. Open the **References** list and move through its rows with the pointer and with Up/Down.
3. Verify that an image row shows a bounded preview with its path beneath it, while the list itself remains compact.
4. Verify that unreadable, invalid, and oversized images retain the path and show the unavailable state instead of a broken image.
5. Verify that issue, pull-request, and commit rows show the same rich metadata hierarchy in both chat surfaces.
6. Exercise copy and removal actions from singleton hovers and collection rows; verify collection footers do not duplicate actions already available on the row.
7. Tab through rich-hover links and actions, then press Escape and confirm focus returns to the references list.
8. Resize the window so the hover is narrow and confirm long locations, titles, metadata, and actions wrap without horizontal overflow.
9. Confirm the negative cases: non-image file and URL references do not receive image previews, and produced image artifacts retain their existing **Images Preview** affordance.

## Screenshots

There is no natural before/after image pair for the new preview state: before this change, the secondary hover contained only the resource path.

- [Automated dark/light screenshot report for image previews and GitHub hover layouts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337303#issuecomment-5781001958)
- [Captioned reference-hover walkthrough](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c49ce60-340d-44c5-a311-e3ed84bf30fd) (1:50)

<details>
<summary>Walkthrough chapters</summary>

| Time | State |
|---|---|
| 00:00 | Landscape and portrait image-reference traversal |
| 00:11 | Collection row actions and incremental hover-footer actions |
| 00:15 | Keyboard list navigation and Escape return |
| 00:21 | Singleton file and image-artifact action footers |
| 00:33 | Rich pull-request, issue, and commit metadata |
| 00:48 | Tab navigation through rich-hover links |
| 00:53 | Website URL and generic-resource actions |
| 01:00 | Reference removal with the fixture image still readable |
| 01:07 | Light-theme image previews, pull-request checks, and commit details |
| 01:25 | GitHub cards and long titles at 320 CSS pixels |

![Contact sheet showing image previews, action footers, GitHub cards, and narrow-viewport layouts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5de3aa34-426b-4076-9fca-d2482e9b9914)

</details>

The walkthrough uses production toolbar, list, hover, image-preview, and GitHub-card components with deterministic fixture services; it is not a live-workbench end-to-end recording.

## Validation

- Client transpilation and type checking pass.
- Targeted unit tests cover image-hover rendering and cancellation, reference actions and removal, GitHub metadata resolution and retries, duplicate-reference metadata, subscription disposal, and stable hover lifetimes.
- Targeted linting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Dark and light component fixtures cover landscape and portrait previews, production reference toolbars, GitHub metadata cards, action footers, keyboard traversal, and narrow layouts.
- The PR's **Compile & Hygiene**, Electron unit, browser, remote, smoke, CodeQL, telemetry, and **Screenshots & Tests** checks pass on the current head.

Live GitHub authentication, backend removal persistence and failure handling, and unavailable or oversized image states are covered by implementation and automated tests rather than the fixture walkthrough.

<!-- reference-hover-related-prs -->
## Related reference-hover work

This PR is part of the reference-hover UI work originating in [#335448](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335448) (Henning's issue to show rich GitHub issue previews with title and rendered body). [#336500](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336500) tracks accumulated references lacking per-item cleanup, and [#337045](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337045) tracks editor-window parity for rich issue and pull-request previews. The related implementation and refinement PRs are:

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Keep external Codex sessions and transcripts live
pull_requests.body:
Codex conversations created or updated in the ChatGPT app now stay current in the Agents Window after explicit Codex activation. This covers both newly discovered list rows and messages sent externally after the conversation is already open in VS Code.

- Watch the app-server's resolved `codexHome` and nested session directories. Coalesce catalog invalidations, share scans with migration, retain trailing invalidations, and retry failures. After initial native legacy repair, use `thread/list` with `useStateDbOnly` and reuse unchanged metadata.
- Refresh subscribed transcripts through the provider-owned history API without `thread/resume` or taking the external writer lock. Reads coalesce at one second with a five-second fallback; paginated histories read the recent tail with overlap. Unchanged native turns retain mapped identity. Watching ends with the chat subscription, release, or shutdown.
- Route passive snapshots through the host hydration path, preserve local turns and drafts, and defer across local execution. Existing AHP truncation/load actions refresh the retained snapshot without invoking provider truncation or turn execution. A provider-neutral contributed-session history event updates the open workbench model while retaining unchanged requests and unsent input.
- Publish metadata/recency updates through the existing root-summary path; keep internal backing suppression, visibility filters, host title overrides, and `ISession.isExternal` grouping. Refresh the list on host reconnect and reject stale responses.

**Activation:** enabling/listing Codex alone does not activate it or download its SDK. Discovery starts after explicit session creation/restoration. The existing startup account probe is unchanged.

**Native limits:** live viewing follows persisted items/turns. Codex 0.153 does not expose another process's unpersisted token deltas through its history API and can report an unfinished external turn as interrupted. Simultaneously sending from VS Code while ChatGPT owns the thread still obeys Codex's single-writer rule; passive viewing never acquires that lock.

**Validation**

- Red regressions first for catalog creation/updates and the follow-up sequence: open a conversation, send another turn externally, remain selected or reselect.
- `npm run compile-client`: passed with zero errors.
- Codex unit suites: **580 passed**.
- Agent Service, state manager, local Sessions provider: **932 passed**, 27 existing skips.
- Agent Host chat handler and Chat Service: **552 passed**.
- Targeted ESLint, layering check, diff checks, and commit hygiene: passed.
- Real native probe with two pinned app-server 0.153 processes and an isolated home/local mock model endpoint: catalog creation/rename and observed transcript updates passed for both `legacy` and `paginated` histories. The production Codex provider opened one turn, then published two turns after a later external message, without resuming the writer.
- Rebuilt Code OSS opened on the user's example conversation and displays its previously missing exchange. The user's final live retest is pending.

[Manual cross-app scenario](src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/chatDiscovery.manual.md). Agent Host living architecture and code-local contracts are updated; high-level Sessions specifications and generated protocol are unchanged.

Watch the resolved Codex home after explicit activation, coalesce native catalog invalidations, and publish changed metadata without reloading Agent Host or the Agents Window. Preserve cold-provider policy, internal backing suppression, external visibility, and host title overrides.

* agentHost: Refresh observed Codex transcripts from external writers

Keep an opened Codex chat current through passive native history reads and a provider-neutral history update seam. Coalesce invalidations, preserve host turns and unsent input, avoid native writer locks, and update the existing workbench model without reselection.

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fixes #130053.

The find widget sometimes shows `? of N` instead of `1 of N` right after switching editors (e.g. clicking a different tab and back), even though there clearly is a current match. Several users confirmed the repro in the issue thread, and @hediet traced it to `FindModelBoundToEditorModel.research()` in `findModel.ts`: when the editor's selection is restored, it's briefly reset to the very start of the document (`(1,1)`), which doesn't overlap any match decoration.

`research()` already has a fallback for exactly this case — when the current selection isn't on top of a match, it looks for the nearest match at or after the selection and uses that as the current position. However the fallback is gated by:

```ts
currentMatchesPosition = matchAfterSelection > 0 ? matchAfterSelection - 1 + 1 /** match position is one based */ : currentMatchesPosition;
```

`matchAfterSelection` is the 0-based index (from a binary search) of the nearest match at or after the selection, or `findMatches.length` if there is none. The `-1 + 1` cancels out, so this is equivalent to `matchAfterSelection > 0 ? matchAfterSelection : currentMatchesPosition`. That means the fallback only fires when the nearest match is *not* the first one in the document (index > 0). When the nearest match *is* the first one — which is exactly what happens when the selection resets to the top of the file — `matchAfterSelection` is `0`, the condition is false, and `currentMatchesPosition` stays at its unresolved value of `0`, which the find widget renders as `?`.

## Fix

Check against `findMatches.length` (whether a match was actually found) instead of `> 0`, and use `matchAfterSelection + 1` to convert the 0-based index to the 1-based position:

```ts
currentMatchesPosition = matchAfterSelection < findMatches.length ? matchAfterSelection + 1 /** match position is one based */ : currentMatchesPosition;
```

This makes the fallback also cover the case where the nearest match is the first one in the document.

## Test plan

- [x] Added a regression test in `findModel.test.ts` (`issue #130053: ...`) that sets the selection to `(1,1)-(1,1)` in a document whose first match is not at that position, and asserts `matchesPosition` resolves to `1` instead of `0`.
- [ ] CI unit tests

pull_requests.title: agentHost: preserve Codex replacement turns after cancellation
pull_requests.body:
Cancelling a Codex turn and immediately submitting a replacement can let the interrupted turn's completion arrive after the replacement has claimed the host turn ID. The completion handler then cancels the replacement and clears its correlation, so the replacement's response finishes under a native Codex turn ID and the E2E test times out.

Establish the Codex-to-host turn mapping on turn start, reuse that mapping on completion, and preserve the replacement's active state and timer when an older turn completes. Add a deterministic regression for this ordering and keep the existing paused-input cancellation E2E test enabled.

Observed in [ADO build 475992 on macOS ARM64](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475992&view=logs&j=e352877c-ff47-5dec-32e2-b206099d9704&t=b83513b4-f303-5ddc-d18a-1b47c02d8dad) and [GitHub Actions on Linux](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35707049762/job/106693351073). The same GitHub commit passed this test on its first two attempts before failing on the third. Codex 0.153.0 source confirms that interrupt acknowledgement precedes the completion notification.

Validation on macOS ARM64:

- `npm run gulp compile-client`.
- Codex unit suites: 567 passing, including the new regression (which failed before the fix).
- Full Codex E2E replay: 102 passing, 28 existing pending tests.
- Temporarily delaying cancellation notifications by 500 ms reproduced the original timeout before the fix; 9/9 focused replays passed afterward. Temporary instrumentation was removed; fixtures and test timeouts are unchanged.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: avoid recomputing unchanged turn diffs
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337256.

## Summary

Stop streamed tokens in the active Agent Host turn from reprocessing every historical request's file changes.

- Share lazy, bounded session/chat sources and index completed turns only when the history array changes. Project history, active-turn ID, and active-turn contents at the event boundary so token updates do not invalidate historical observers.
- Separate host-notice detection from file-edit parsing. Only observe the response-edit fallback when authoritative changesets cannot supply the result.
- Normalize and aggregate response edits only when the relevant edit objects or workspace roots change, and reuse unchanged changeset entries.
- Preserve source precedence, authoritative-empty results, migration fallbacks, live edits, and retained summaries across recomputes/reconnects.
- Preserve retry-on-acquire for failed shared subscriptions: a new/restarted request observation can replace the failed source, and existing observers follow the replacement. No polling or automatic retry loop.

This fixes the upstream provider work; it does not include the separate timeline-rendering changes tracked in #337244.

## Performance comparison

Measured with a temporary, uncommitted harness using the **actual provider, chat reducer, URI helpers, and observable implementation**, with a synthetic connection and deterministic streamed updates. Each workload observes the historical requests and active turn. Numbers below are **median synchronous stream-processing time across three runs**, excluding setup, on macOS arm64 / Node 24.18.0.

These are isolated component timings, **not end-to-end workbench frame timings or real token-delivery duration**.

| Workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 200 historical turns, 5,000 updates, authoritative changesets | 43,584.42 ms | 7.04 ms |
| 200 historical turns, 5,000 updates, response fallback | 25,139.13 ms | 18.42 ms |
| 800 historical turns, 2,000 updates, mixed sources | 49,078.28 ms | 2.49 ms |
| 30 historical turns, 50,000 updates plus 50 actual file-edit additions | 48,667.70 ms | 69.05 ms |

A separate timing-only control with provider/history instrumentation disabled confirmed the first workload: **42,481.68 ms before -> 5.64 ms after**.

Work avoided and correctness checks:

- In the 200-turn / 5,000-update workload, historical response reads and notifications drop from **1,000,000 to 0**, and historical turn visits drop from **100,500,000 to 0**.
- Historical diff arrays retain reference identity, and all paired runs produce identical complete file-change payload hashes.
- The 50-edit live workload produces exactly **50 active-turn notifications**, rather than 50,050, while preserving the resulting changes.
- Five larger stress runs each used **2,000 historical turns and 100,000 updates plus 40 actual file-edit additions**: zero historical lookup/parsing/notifications during streaming, exactly 40 active updates, and all subscription references released afterward.

## Validation

- **43 tests pass**: 42 provider tests and the related changes-opening service test.
- Ten repeated suite runs: **430 passing test executions**, with disposable-leak checking.
- **14 tests use the real AgentSubscriptionManager**, covering initial/repeated failures, explicit/discovered chats, existing observers following replacement, external replacement, cached request reobservation, the file-edits API, pending hydration, and disposal. Eight recovery regressions were demonstrated failing before the recovery fix.
- Targeted compilation and TypeScript checks, repository ESLint for both changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The requested Astra code review of the complete diff found no significant issues.

The checkout did not have an Electron build, so the actual component suites were bundled and run through Node/Mocha; full Electron/workbench UI validation was not performed. The performance harness, logs, and temporary toolchain are intentionally excluded from this PR.

For UI verification, use a long Agent Host chat with the timeline enabled, stream text/reasoning and file edits, and check that historical change counts stay stable while actual edits update. Confirm completed-response summaries and per-turn diff opening still work, including after reconnect/reobservation.

This PR allows chats created within an Agent Host session to use folders or worktrees that differ from the session's original workspace. Those locations become part of the containing session while repository state and operations remain scoped to each chat's effective folder set.

pull_requests.title: mcp: enforce destination policy and contain redirected credentials
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337194
Fixes #336293

## Changes

- Check current MCP policy against every data-request destination before dispatch, retaining the configured server identity and deny-list precedence. Stop active transports when a contacted destination is revoked.
- Confine configured and standard credential headers across origins while preserving generated protocol headers, same-origin requests, and ordinary OAuth metadata discovery.
- Keep the caller's headers, method, and body intact for authentication retries. This covers the header-preservation fix proposed in #336295 and extends it to redirect method/body changes.
- Validate server-selected first destinations as well as redirect hops. Preserve explicitly configured IPC transports using their decoded socket endpoint, rather than treating opaque URL origins as equivalent.
- Report and dispose failed background legacy-SSE sends, and update the configuration/API documentation.

## Validation

- Regression-first unit coverage: 32 initial failures, a separately caught protocol-header compatibility regression, and 16 additional first-destination failures before their respective fixes. Existing assertions were not weakened.
- 284 focused Electron tests and 71 Node tests pass.
- Client transpilation, full `npm run typecheck-client`, targeted hygiene, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Real Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev / Electron 43.7.3 on Windows: 16 functional scenarios plus setup passed through the editor MCP pipeline. The independent fixture ledger recorded 74 requests; all four blocked destinations received zero.
- Real scenarios cover start/stop and tool invocation, redirects, header confinement, policy revocation/recovery, legacy SSE failure/recovery, an owned named pipe, and a synthetic authentication retry preserving the original POST/body.

## Validation scope

Fixtures use only task-owned loopback/pipe endpoints and synthetic credentials. The real MCP, configuration, policy, and tool services are used; no model or real account is required. Browser OAuth/token exchange, remote TLS endpoints, Linux sockets, and IPC JSON-schema diagnostics were not exercised.

Cached tool metadata can remain listed after a redirected destination is revoked. The connection errors, the active target stream closes, and invocation is rejected before any further request reaches that target; this change does not purge cached metadata.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: fix account-scoped Copilot SKU telemetry for Codex
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fix Codex Agent Host `copilotSku` attribution at the authentication/telemetry lifecycle, without dashboard imputation.

- Read the raw entitlement SKU from the existing token-scoped `/copilot_internal/user` cache. Codex no longer depends on Copilot initializing a process-wide common property.
- Capture account context for turns at provider dispatch (including authentication that finishes during host preparation), and retain that guarded context for completion, failure, hang, usage, tool, and forwarded SDK telemetry.
- Keep unchanged-credential and proactive refreshes from erasing valid metadata, while distinguishing rejected credentials. Retry failed discovery on reauthentication; omit unknown, malformed, expired, invalidated, or superseded metadata.
- Prevent older authentication completions from replacing replayable credentials, and make late provider initialization wait for the current authentication request.
- Scope discovery to its original GitHub endpoint and prevent old failures from evicting newer cache entries. Retire Copilot and Claude credentials/proxy handles when the endpoint changes; this is necessary because they share the corrected CAPI cache. Codex already retired its credential on that transition.

## Root cause and ownership

Previously, only `CopilotAgent` published `copilotSku` through `setCommonProperty`. Codex independently fetched CAPI metadata, so its first turns could be missing a SKU; another provider's authentication could also clear or overwrite the shared value.

The replacement is explicit provider/account context, not another shared mutable SKU. Point-in-time events read their provider's current account; delayed events carry a captured, invalidatable context. Unattributed events no longer borrow another provider's account. The field remains optional, preserving historical and legitimately missing-SKU compatibility.

## Privacy

The existing `copilotSku` GDPR classification remains unchanged: a string, `SystemMetaData` / `FeatureInsight`. No tokens, account identities, new telemetry fields, settings, or policy controls are added. There is no guessed SKU, historical backfill, or change to dashboards, notes, OTel configuration, or telemetry consent gates.

## Red → green evidence

The first regression used real Codex authentication, `CopilotApiService`, `AgentHostAuthenticationService`, the turn tracker/reporter, and the real telemetry service/appender merge; only external HTTP/SDK boundaries were controlled.

```sh
npm run transpile-client
TMPDIR="$PWD/.r" ./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexSkuTelemetry.test.ts \
  --grep 'authenticated CAPI account SKU'
```

Before implementation: **0 passing, 1 failing**, actual `[undefined]` versus `['copilot_for_business_seat']`. After the first fix: **1 passing**.

Further observed assertion-red/green slices cover account replacement/removal, out-of-order resolution and replay, late provider initialization, unchanged credentials, failed discovery/retry, dispatch-time authentication, old-endpoint discovery/401 responses, expired-cache endpoint races, non-string SKUs, and delayed tool events. Real Copilot/Codex service tests cover independent provider initialization/clearing; real Claude proxy/API tests ensure the shared cache change cannot send retired credentials to a newly configured endpoint.

## Validation

A short workspace-local scratch directory was used for `TMPDIR` and removed afterwards.

- `npm run compile` — **passed**, including client and built-in extension compilation.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — **passed**; the final compile also typechecked the subsequent source changes.
- Targeted ESLint on all changed TypeScript files — **passed**.
- `git diff --check` — **passed**.
- Related unit suites below — **1,055 passing, 1 pending**.

```sh
TMPDIR="$PWD/.r" ./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexSkuTelemetry.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexAgent.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexModelRefresh.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexProxyService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/copilotApiService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/claudeAgent.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotGitHubTelemetryForwarder.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostTelemetryService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostTelemetryReporter.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostTurnTelemetry.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostTurnHangTelemetry.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostToolCallTelemetry.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostProviderService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostServices.test.ts

TMPDIR="$PWD/.r" ./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts \
  --grep 'AgentService.*[Aa]uthenticat'
```

The separate authentication selector passed **12 tests**: **1,067 passing total**, plus the one pending test.

## Real launch verification

Used the launch skill's prelaunch, settings, and CDP-readiness helpers with workspace-local isolated user-data, extension, shared-data, `HOME`, `COPILOT_HOME`, and `CODEX_HOME` directories. The agent did not extract, inspect, or print credential values or copy another profile's credential store. The existing in-app GitHub authentication path supplied authentication.

Two real Codex turns, including one after rebuilding/restarting the host and replaying authentication, returned the requested smoke-check replies:

- provider `codex`
- model `@provider=vscode-proxy:gpt-5.3-codex`
- result `success`
- the same nonempty raw `copilotSku` on both runs
- real CAPI `responses` HTTP **200**
- unchanged source worktree and unchanged Git worktree list

The payload was observed at the real `AgentHostTelemetryReporter.turnCompleted` boundary using a non-pausing debugger logpoint; this does **not** claim verification of remote telemetry ingestion. The launch also ran the real Codex app-server/account probe. Cropped screenshots and bounded, non-identity evidence were retained locally; debug probes, runtime profiles, helper scripts, and task-owned processes were removed.

Live account switching, credential invalidation, and configured enterprise-host switching were not performed against the user's accounts; those cases are covered by the deterministic service/lifecycle regressions. The opt-in external CAPI integration test was updated for disposal ownership but was not run separately.

## Baseline

Started from freshly fetched `origin/main` at `f2375bfd46fb664b40159f09f9e4727f20f1f8c8`, with a clean isolated worktree on `agents/codex-sku-lifecycle-20260922`.

pull_requests.title: sessions: fix: reveal Find matches in collapsed branches
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

The Sessions sidebar's native Find widget scores descendant labels inside collapsed branches, but those matching rows are not in the rendered list. Its initial focus/reveal pass therefore cannot expose them reliably in either Filter or Highlight mode.

For example, searching for a peer-chat title can leave the result hidden behind its collapsed session and workspace or custom group.

## Fix

After native refiltering, a coalesced, disposable scheduler traverses the tree once and expands only collapsed ancestors of actual matching descendants. It collects each ancestor once, visits every sibling subtree, and expands inner branches before outer branches. Matching uses the existing native scores, including fuzzy/contiguous matching; there is no separate search engine or transcript search.

After expansion, the list repeats the logical focus pass without moving DOM focus out of the Find input. Enter still returns focus to the tree. The focused match is scrolled into view only when it is not already entirely within the viewport.

## Collapse preferences and lifecycle

Automatic expansion does **not** overwrite saved user collapse choices. The deferred reveal reuses the existing persistence-suppression flag and restores its previous value. A microtask-bounded guard also covers the native controller's synchronous reveal when applying, clearing, or closing Find; otherwise clearing Find can reopen the focused branch and accidentally persist that expansion.

Explicit user expansion and collapse still persist, including while Find is open. There is no pre-search snapshot or special restore-on-clear mechanism: normal native in-memory layout and focus behavior remain intact, while saved choices survive list recreation.

Pending reveals are coalesced and cancelled when Find is cleared/closed or the list is disposed. Find-state callbacks stop rebuilding rows during list teardown.

This is a standalone fix on `main` for existing workspace, custom-group, and peer-chat branches. It does not change Show More/reveal capping, generic tree infrastructure, storage formats, settings, or session nesting.

## Validation

**55 focused Electron tests passed:** 15 new Find regressions and 40 existing peer-chat/selection regressions.

New coverage includes both Find modes; matching workspace/group/session ancestors; parent-only and unrelated matches; empty Find; deduplication across 5,000 matching siblings; uninterrupted typing and Enter-to-tree; viewport stability for an already visible result; native fuzzy/contiguous matching; coalescing; cancellation on clear, close, and dispose; unchanged persisted preferences through clear/close and recreation; and direct user persistence while searching.

```sh
npm run transpile-client
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListFind.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --grep 'Sessions - SessionsList Find|session chat rows'
npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListFind.test.ts
```

Validation used the macOS Electron unit harness; full workbench end-to-end and Windows/Linux runs were not performed.

pull_requests.title: sessions: fix: reveal sessions hidden by sidebar limits
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

The Agents Window sidebar applies two presentation limits: sessions beyond the per-workspace/custom-group limit and inactive workspaces are omitted until Show More is selected. These sessions can pass every filter without having a row in the tree.

Previously, `reveal(sessionResource)` returned `false` for those eligible sessions because it only handled existing tree rows. Active sessions could remain behind either cap as well. This affects ordinary, single-chat sessions; no nested-session hierarchy is needed to reproduce it.

Activating an offscreen main-session row also updated selection without scrolling it into view. Already-visible rows should stay stationary when activated.

## Changes

Record eligible session IDs after the existing filters and active/onboarding exceptions, before applying presentation caps. An explicit reveal resolves the catalog session using the URI identity service and temporarily includes an eligible capped target before revealing and selecting its row.

Both cap paths now preserve the active session, explicit reveal target, and archive-onboarding target simultaneously. The per-section helper keeps the normal prefix and includes additional targets in their original order, without duplicates. Show More counts reflect only the sessions or workspaces still omitted.

Temporary explicit-reveal state is cleared on active-session/chat changes, host/filter changes, catalog removal, and subsequent filter mismatch. An unchanged refresh retains it, and releasing onboarding does not discard the other inclusion reasons. Main-session activation scrolls only when the row is not entirely visible, preserving DOM focus and avoiding recentering visible rows.

Explicit reveal does **not** disable saved filters or expose otherwise-filtered sessions. Existing active/onboarding filter exceptions and automation exclusion are preserved. This is a standalone change against `main`, with no Find, hierarchy, drag-and-drop, settings, or collapse-persistence changes.

## Validation

Fresh output from `npm run transpile-client`; **91 focused Electron tests passed**:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsRename.test.ts \
  --grep "Sessions - SessionsList (limitSessionsForList|capped session reveal|session toolbar keyboard focus|session chat rows)|Sessions rename list interaction" \
  --reporter dot
```

New coverage includes one multi-target cap-helper regression and 25 rendered-list cases for simultaneous inclusion beyond both caps, ordering/uniqueness/counts, filtered-out targets, URI identity, temporary-state cleanup, onboarding release, and offscreen-versus-visible activation without stealing DOM focus. The run also covers existing onboarding, toolbar, chat-selection, and rename interactions. Capped reveal and offscreen activation failures were reproduced before the production fix.

Targeted ESLint and commit hygiene passed for both changed files; `git diff --check` passed. No full provider-backed UI scenario or broad repository typecheck was run.

pull_requests.title: build: clarify Linux diagnostic failures
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #337218 (microsoft/vscode-engineering#3362 remains closed).

In [build 475879](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475879), the Linux pre/post-smoke diagnostic steps finished in 43.90s and 3.26s with exit 1, not a timeout. Tests and publication succeeded, but the combined "failed or exceeded the 60s limit" warning was ambiguous. Suppressed `du` stderr and aggregate-only status made the failing command impossible to identify from those logs.

- Share the pre/post collector so both use identical command/error reporting.
- Log each diagnostic command and retain its stderr, while streaming stdout through the existing disk/handle summaries.
- Treat `du` exit 1 as informational partial output only when every stderr line is a recognized C-locale permission-denied or missing-entry error. Mixed errors, unexpected errors, other statuses and unexplained exit 1 still warn and fail the optional step. No blanket suppression of `lsof` failures.
- Keep the 60-second process-group deadline, but treat confirmed budget expiry as warning-only truncation. Require timeout's own isolated stderr to confirm the deadline; unrelated SIGKILL and monitor errors remain failures.
- Persist unexpected command/pipeline failures outside the killed process group, so a later timeout cannot hide an earlier error. Preserve each command's actual exit status in its warning.

[Build 475949](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475949) confirmed that both root scans reached the deadline while required Linux tests and results publication succeeded. This update prevents that optional truncation alone from making the Linux job partially successful. The separate Copilot NOTICE-generation failure is outside this PR.

Validation: 80 controlled native-Linux scenarios passed, including earlier errors followed by timeouts, same-pipeline errors plus a hung consumer, unrelated SIGKILL, and lookalike timeout text from child stderr. Actual 60-second deadline checks completed in 60.252s/60.246s with warning plus exit 0. Owned children were terminated, unrelated siblings survived, required-step structure was unchanged, and YAML/Bash/whitespace checks passed. Temporary fixtures were removed; no live ADO validation was queued.

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] agentHost: retract stale sessions when a provider catalog becomes readable
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #337214 from `main`.

Fourth and final cause of the "zombie" agent sessions — empty rows titled `Session` that cannot be opened. Follows #336480, #336806 and #336979.

## What happens

Suppression bails out while a provider's catalog is unreadable, which is deliberate: a provider that cannot answer is not evidence that a session is absent, so the row stays visible (#331648). The gap is that **nothing refreshes the list once the provider becomes readable**, so a list computed during that window stays stale for the rest of the session.

From a reporter's log, where the Claude SDK had not been downloaded:

```
22:27:08.871  Agent Host process started
22:27:11.182  [Claude] SDK not downloaded yet; deferring passive chat metadata   (x317, through 22:46)
22:27:11.445  listSessions computed 645 of 668     <- claude unreadable, suppression skipped
22:27:13.372  listSessions computed 645 of 668     <- same
22:27:27.189  listSessions computed 645 of 668     <- same
22:46:17      user clicks the row; restore forces the SDK download
22:47:05.859  sessions_v2 import for provider claude: ... marker set   <- claude becomes readable
22:47:06.007  restore fails: "Session was never created on the backend"  (marker present, correct)
```

The import was deferred for twenty minutes. No listing ran after readability arrived, so the unsuppressed list stayed on screen.

**Invalidating the list is not sufficient**, and this is the part worth knowing: that import reported `19 excluded`, so `_invalidateSessionList()` already fired at 22:47:05 on current `main` — and the row still did not disappear. Bumping the epoch only affects the *next* listing; nothing requests one, and the client keeps the sessions it was already told about.

## The change

On a genuine readable transition, recompute the list and **retract** any published session that is no longer visible, through the existing surfaced-session removal path. The retraction is what reaches the client.

Scoped to provisional sessions of the transitioning provider, so an ordinary re-import does no work and nothing else is disturbed.

The fail-open behaviour is unchanged: while a provider is unreadable its sessions stay visible, exactly as before.

## Reproduction

A marked, empty, undescribable orphan of a provider that is unreadable at first listing: it is listed (fail-open, correct), the provider then becomes readable, and on `main` the orphan **remains on screen**. With the change it is retracted. Neutralising the fix reproduces the failure precisely — `after: []` but no `root/sessionRemoved`, so the client keeps the row.

Guards: a provider that never becomes readable keeps failing open; an already-readable provider re-importing queues no refresh; a session with conversation turns is never retracted.

5,581 passing across the agentHost node suites, typecheck and eslint clean.

## Note on the invalidation condition

An earlier revision of this change also removed `report.skipped` from the import invalidation condition, on the reasoning that a skipped candidate performs no writes. That is not true: a candidate whose stale exclusion is cleared still reports `skipped`, and clearing an exclusion makes a previously hidden session eligible again — so dropping it would have introduced the mirror image of this bug. The condition is left untouched, and the repro passes with it intact.

pull_requests.title: Wait for installed plugins before updating
pull_requests.body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330090
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8462

- Expose readiness only after the file-backed installed-plugin manifest and current plugin metadata hydration complete.
- Serialize hydration runs so updates observe a stable installed-plugin snapshot after restart.
- Wait for readiness before periodic update checks and manual or automatic bulk updates.
- Re-check cancellation after manual update readiness without changing per-marketplace policy, strict marketplace enforcement, metered-connection behavior, or the 24-hour interval.

## Reproduction

The reported failure was reproduced on the August 10, 2026 main commit `ff64ebf41766298a17e1a1c5150e92aad530cad3` with:

- an installed v1 plugin restored from `installed.json`;
- the marketplace remote advanced to v2 before window startup;
- managed marketplace `autoUpdate: true`;
- global extension auto-update disabled;
- a disposable profile, plugin home, local Git remote, and temporary file policy.

Computer Use confirmed the managed `autoUpdate: true` value in the real Settings UI. The installed clone remained on v1 while the remote was v2.

The periodic check was reading `installedPlugins` before asynchronous metadata hydration completed. It observed an empty list, recorded the check time, and deferred the next attempt for 24 hours. Manual Update Plugins had the same early-read window.

An automated timing bisect reinforced the race diagnosis:

- `a06d01ff8fbb8ab45882d09c31a14b6003dd6e94` still failed.
- Its child `ff155aaf5624b3c77933073841294f41ad9b1acc` first passed despite changing only Agents application badges.

The unrelated timing change masked the race on newer builds without establishing an update-readiness contract.

## Verification

The exact readiness patch was applied to the historically failing August 10 source and the unchanged scenario was replayed:

- the installed clone advanced from v1 to v2;
- clone HEAD matched remote HEAD;
- the plugin manifest reported `2.0.0`;
- the plugin skill marker changed from `version-one` to `version-two`;
- global auto-update remained disabled and managed `autoUpdate: true` remained active.

Automated validation on current `upstream/main`:

```text
npm run transpile-client
npm run typecheck-client
npm run eslint -- <6 changed TypeScript files>
node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts <7 changed files>

npm run test-browser-no-install -- \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/plugins/pluginMarketplaceService.test.ts \
  --browser chromium
```

pull_requests.title: Install required plugins and show policy-blocked recovery UI
pull_requests.body:
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8906

Last reconciled with PR head `26f22e1d1c06722cf0d4786c9dadfc212eb1ec65` on September 22, 2026.

- Install plugins explicitly required by enterprise `enabledPlugins` policy and restore removed entries in the existing `installed.json` manifest.
- Keep policy-false and policy-omitted plugins out of background acquisition, preserve managed marketplace identities, and honor strict marketplace policy.
- Align unavailable-plugin presentation with the merged minimum-version UI from #337151: a shared read-only Chat view, the existing Agents policy overlay, and a neutral editor banner that remains visible when Chat is closed.
- Offer **Retry** for required plugins and **Open Editor Window** from Agents. Keep version requirements and their native update actions distinct, with minimum-version restrictions taking precedence.
- Block chat submission through the same availability state. Require a recorded installation before clearing it, including when an installer returns normally after failing.
- Preserve the user's draft through blocking and recovery, skip conflicting required identities sharing an install location, and abandon stale policy/entitlement reconciliation passes.

The enablement and uninstall UI locks from #337209 are already in `main`. This branch incorporates #337151's merged implementation rather than maintaining a separate copy of its policy-blocked components.

## Reproduction

1. Launch Code OSS with a disposable profile, shared-data directory, and agent-plugins directory.
2. Enable repository-supported temporary file policy. Configure a reachable local marketplace named `policy-ui-local`, and require `required-demo@policy-ui-local: true`.
3. Leave `required-demo` out of the marketplace. Open a synthetic text file and Chat.
4. Close Chat and confirm the editor still explains the organization requirement.
5. Add the required catalog entry, but point it at a missing plugin directory. Select **Retry**. The failed installation must not clear the block.
6. Remove the requirement and confirm normal Chat returns. Enter a draft, reapply the requirement, then remove it again; the draft must survive.
7. Repeat the unavailable-plugin and policy-removal cases in an isolated Agents window.

This uses actual file-policy ingestion, marketplace lookup, installation failure, and live recovery. No normal profile, real account, system proxy, certificate trust, native machine policy, or runtime policy was changed.

## Verification

Local verification used macOS 26.6.2 arm64 and Code OSS Dev 1.140.0. The code is published through `26f22e1d1c0`; capture commits and test commits are recorded separately below.

| Evidence | Tested commit | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full initial Editor and Agents scenarios | UI candidate committed as `4a328ef94d89` | Read-only Chat, persistent banner, failed-install blocking, policy-removal recovery, draft preservation, and Agents overlay passed. |
| Integrated Chat screenshot and shared policy-UI tests | `7b13c2f3ba7` | Chat recaptured after #337151 integration; 167 focused Chromium tests passed. |
| Latest-main merge validation | `21ac5618bd6` | 296 focused Chromium tests passed, including the policy UI and managed Auto-tier/model-selection paths; scoped hygiene passed. |
| Compile-fixture correction | `26f22e1d1c0` | Original overload stub reproduced `TS2322`; corrected overloads passed a focused semantic TypeScript check. Both overlay suites passed: 21 tests; scoped hygiene passed. |

**Screenshot currency:** the relevant Chat policy view, plugin presentation, Agents overlay, and banner code is unchanged between the integrated Chat capture at `7b13c2f3ba7` and current head `26f22e1d1c0`. The latest commit changes only a screenshot fixture's layout-service overloads. The images show the aligned UI, but they are not all captures of the current commit.

**Remaining capture limitation:** Computer Use still cannot arm its physical Escape handler, rechecked on September 22, 2026. Agents and banner-only recapture on the current head remain blocked. Their earlier captures are labelled below rather than presented as current-head verification.

- **Editor / Chat:** one read-only policy explanation, plugin identity and Retry; no composer or old inline plugin notification.
- **Editor / Chat closed:** the policy banner remains while ordinary editing is available.
- **Failed install:** the catalog resolves but its directory is absent; Retry leaves the required plugin uninstalled and Chat blocked.
- **Recovery:** removing the requirement clears the banner and blocked view without restarting; an existing draft is retained through a block/recovery cycle.
- **Agents:** one policy overlay with Retry and Open Editor Window, no redundant banner; removing the requirement clears it.
- **Shared minimum-version behavior:** regression tests preserve update actions, focus restoration, narrow-view wrapping, and update precedence when both requirements exist.

### Editor with Chat open

Captured at `7b13c2f3ba7`; the relevant product UI is unchanged at `26f22e1d1c0`.

![Required-plugin policy explanation in Chat beside the editor and its persistent banner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a84675b0-5f1e-4a87-bf67-f4b9893b4131)

These are unedited product captures. Unlike the earlier install/restore evidence, they do not display harness-generated JSON reports.

### Validation

- **296 focused Chromium tests passed** after merging latest `main` at `21ac5618bd6`. This includes the earlier 167-test policy-UI coverage plus managed Auto-tier and model-selection regressions.
- **21 overlay tests passed** after the fixture compile fix at `26f22e1d1c0`. A focused semantic TypeScript check reproduced the original `TS2322` and passed with the corrected overloads.

- A broad local client typecheck and full layer checks were not run because the shared machine remained heavily loaded and approval was unavailable. The focused overload check is not a full compile.

</details>

Historical successful acquisition/restoration evidence is retained in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337221#issuecomment-5782538168, explicitly tied to its older tested commit. Its original failed-install finding is fixed in the published code; those historical test failures are not current-head results.

## Debugging and Retry

- Set **Developer: Set Log Level... > Window > Debug**, reproduce with **Retry**, then open **Developer: Show Window Log**. Search for `[ManagedPluginInstall]`, `[PluginMarketplaceService]`, `[AgentPluginRepositoryService]`, or `[FileBackedInstalledPluginsStore]`.
- If the Agents overlay prevents reading Output, use **Developer: Open Logs Folder** and inspect that window's `windowN/renderer.log`. A newly opened editor window has a different Window log.
- Retry queues reconciliation using the currently loaded policy, checks installed identities, and attempts missing required installs. It does not restart the app, sign in, refresh server policy, or bypass the normal marketplace cache, whose TTL is eight hours.
- There is currently no dedicated **View Logs** action in the blocked UI. A forced fresh catalog fetch on manual Retry is also not implemented.

## Scope

- `installed.json` is VS Code's existing installed-plugin inventory, not a new enterprise-policy format. The earlier `01-install.json` and `02-restore.json` screenshots showed verification-only reports, not product files.
- Restoration here concerns removed manifest entries. Physical deletion of plugin content while leaving its manifest entry intact is not claimed to self-heal.
- This does not change Agent Host wire contracts, the public SDK, or runtime-owned plugin enforcement. It changes VS Code acquisition, availability, and presentation.
- An already-started install may finish; queued policy changes stop subsequent work and stale presentation.

-----------------------------------------

pull_requests.body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3362
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337227

In [build 457583](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=457583), the optional pre-smoke root `du | sort | head` pipeline took approximately 27 minutes. Browser unit, integration, and smoke tests passed, but the 50-minute job deadline canceled results publication. `continueOnError` did not bound diagnostic runtime. The underlying scan delay remains undiagnosed.

- Bound each complete pre/post-smoke collector to 60 seconds using GNU timeout and an isolated process group, including pipeline children that ignore TERM. Handle its exit in the outer shell instead of requesting Azure task cancellation.
- Collect process, disk, inotify, handle, and narrower directory information before scanning `/`.
- Warn explicitly and retain a nonzero status for diagnostic errors or truncation; keep the existing `continueOnError` behavior for downstream execution.
- Preserve top-30 output without pipefail/SIGPIPE false failures and handle absent smoke-directory matches safely.

- Try native Git credentials first, then retry canonical `https://github.com/` marketplaces with an existing VS Code GitHub session whose scopes include `repo`.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and verification</summary>

### Reproduction

1. Configure a server-managed private GitHub marketplace and expose a VS Code GitHub session whose scopes include `repo`.
2. Disable ambient native Git, Git Credential Manager, environment-token, and `gh` authentication paths.
3. On base `39f91b155cb34b670a38a4fe5f1bbdaa8aa972c9`, Local Plugins shows **Available 0** because native Git cannot authenticate to the private repository.
