pull_requests.title: agentHost: retract stale sessions when a provider catalog becomes readable
pull_requests.body:
Fourth and final cause of the "zombie" agent sessions — empty rows titled `Session` that cannot be opened. Follows #336480, #336806 and #336979.

## What happens

Suppression bails out while a provider's catalog is unreadable, which is deliberate: a provider that cannot answer is not evidence that a session is absent, so the row stays visible (#331648). The gap is that **nothing refreshes the list once the provider becomes readable**, so a list computed during that window stays stale for the rest of the session.

From a reporter's log, where the Claude SDK had not been downloaded:

```
22:27:08.871  Agent Host process started
22:27:11.182  [Claude] SDK not downloaded yet; deferring passive chat metadata   (x317, through 22:46)
22:27:11.445  listSessions computed 645 of 668     <- claude unreadable, suppression skipped
22:27:13.372  listSessions computed 645 of 668     <- same
22:27:27.189  listSessions computed 645 of 668     <- same
22:46:17      user clicks the row; restore forces the SDK download
22:47:05.859  sessions_v2 import for provider claude: ... marker set   <- claude becomes readable
22:47:06.007  restore fails: "Session was never created on the backend"  (marker present, correct)
```

The import was deferred for twenty minutes. No listing ran after readability arrived, so the unsuppressed list stayed on screen.

**Invalidating the list is not sufficient**, and this is the part worth knowing: that import reported `19 excluded`, so `_invalidateSessionList()` already fired at 22:47:05 on current `main` — and the row still did not disappear. Bumping the epoch only affects the *next* listing; nothing requests one, and the client keeps the sessions it was already told about.

## The change

On a genuine readable transition, recompute the list and **retract** any published session that is no longer visible, through the existing surfaced-session removal path. The retraction is what reaches the client.

Scoped to provisional sessions of the transitioning provider, so an ordinary re-import does no work and nothing else is disturbed.

The fail-open behaviour is unchanged: while a provider is unreadable its sessions stay visible, exactly as before.

## Reproduction

A marked, empty, undescribable orphan of a provider that is unreadable at first listing: it is listed (fail-open, correct), the provider then becomes readable, and on `main` the orphan **remains on screen**. With the change it is retracted. Neutralising the fix reproduces the failure precisely — `after: []` but no `root/sessionRemoved`, so the client keeps the row.

Guards: a provider that never becomes readable keeps failing open; an already-readable provider re-importing queues no refresh; a session with conversation turns is never retracted.

5,581 passing across the agentHost node suites, typecheck and eslint clean.

## Note on the invalidation condition

An earlier revision of this change also removed `report.skipped` from the import invalidation condition, on the reasoning that a skipped candidate performs no writes. That is not true: a candidate whose stale exclusion is cleared still reports `skipped`, and clearing an exclusion makes a previously hidden session eligible again — so dropping it would have introduced the mirror image of this bug. pull_requests.title: Enforce managed plugin enablement in the model and UI
pull_requests.body:
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8906

- Apply managed `enabledPlugins` `true` and `false` entries as an immutable overlay on VS Code's plugin enablement model.
- Keep the user's profile and workspace choice stored underneath policy, restoring it when the managed entry is removed.
- Ignore local enablement writes and removal-state cleanup for managed identities.
- Give a policy-required plugin priority over unmanaged duplicates in the same collision group.
- Lock managed switches and enablement actions, and hide uninstall for policy-required plugins across every existing plugin management surface.
- Leave policy-omitted plugins user-controlled, preserving additive behavior rather than turning `enabledPlugins` into an allowlist.

## Reproduction

Using an isolated Code OSS profile, fixture plugins, and a temporary `ChatEnabledPlugins` policy:

- `required-demo@repro-8906-local: true`
- `blocked-demo@repro-8906-local: false`
- `unmanaged-demo`: omitted from policy

Before this change, `blocked-demo` was disabled and locked, proving the policy was active. `required-demo` remained user-toggleable; disabling it removed its contributed skill and persisted a local `false` decision while policy still required it.

Reproduction details: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8906#issuecomment-5771771859

## Verification

The same isolated scenario was replayed with `required-demo` pre-seeded as locally disabled:

- `required-demo` stayed checked and locked by managed `true`.
- `blocked-demo` stayed unchecked and locked by managed `false`.
- `unmanaged-demo` remained enabled and user-toggleable.
- The fixture skill count remained `2`, confirming required and unmanaged contributions were active.
- The stored local `false` decision remained unchanged underneath the effective managed `true`.

A clean negative control applied the managed-precedence behavior test to the unmodified base; it failed on the expected policy assertion.

```text
npm run transpile-client
npm run typecheck-client
npm run eslint -- <9 changed files>
node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts <9 changed files>

npm run test-browser-no-install -- \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/plugins/agentPluginEnablement.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentPluginActions.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/embeddedAgentPluginDetail.test.ts \
  --browser chromium
# 29 passing

npm run test-browser-no-install -- \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/pluginListWidget.test.ts \
  --browser chromium
# 7 passing

npm run test-browser-no-install -- \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsService.test.ts \
  --grep "managed-only hooks preserve frontmatter hooks from force-enabled plugin agents" \
  --browser chromium
# 1 passing
```

## Evidence

### Before

![Managed required plugin can be disabled before the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa2b8783-6502-4bc0-bc7a-e571daa50279)

### After

![Managed true and false plugin controls after the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b22f8e64-dd78-4a2a-9054-5b036b9cc38f)

## Scope

- This PR enforces effective enablement and user controls for plugins that are already discovered.
- Managed acquisition and restoration of a missing plugin are handled separately by #337221.
- Fail-closed behavior when a required plugin cannot be resolved remains a product decision.
- This does not change Agent Host wire contracts or runtime-owned enforcement.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Managed `true`/`false` and additive semantics come from [`ChatConfiguration.EnabledPlugins`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/62c8ac8ac5e0feaba1fa728fa48b10403f96ccab/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts#L1365-L1372).

pull_requests.title: github-authentication: prevent sessions returning after sign-out
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Keep session publication and sign-out ordered so in-flight work cannot recreate removed sessions or overwrite newer accounts.

```text
sign-in:  login + identity lookup -> queue(read latest sessions + update + store + notify)
restore:  exchange token -> queue(recheck link + publish)
sign-out: queue(remove local session + account link + notify) -> remote revoke
```

- Use the existing Sequencer pattern for persisted sign-in, Microsoft-backed restoration, and local sign-out mutations.
- Discard renewal results when the original session was removed or replaced.
- Keep authentication and remote OAuth revocation outside the queue. Local removal is announced even if remote revocation later fails. GitHub sign-out does not remove the Microsoft account.

## Validation

- GitHub authentication extension compilation/typecheck passed.
- 29 focused tests passed: blocked reads/writes, concurrent restores, stale snapshots during login/identity lookup, delayed/failed revocation, account links, and sequencer failure recovery.
- Three persisted sign-in races reproduced before the follow-up fix; existing account/scope replacement behavior remains covered.
- ESLint and pre-commit hygiene passed. Tests use fake accounts and credentials.

## Scope

Only four GitHub authentication files (implementation, utility, and tests). No runtime/protocol, subagent, or development-probe changes. Based on `main`, independently of #337188.

pull_requests.title: Copilot Chat: expose the chat session id to language model request middleware
pull_requests.body:
Stacked on #337130 and depends on it. Only the last two commits, `copilot: expose the chat session id to language model request middleware` and `copilot: only trust the conversation id from the chat participant`, belong to this PR; the rest is the base PR.

## Summary

- The request middleware context from #337130 now carries `sessionId`, the chat session a request belongs to, so an extension can tag every request of one chat with the same id and let a gateway group them. A new chat gets a new id, and separate VS Code windows have separate sessions.
- `sessionId` is `undefined` for requests that are not made from a chat session, such as an extension calling `vscode.lm` directly.
- To make the id available to the provider, the proposed `chatProvider` API gains `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions.sessionId` (one d.ts field), and core forwards it along the chat path. That part needs API owner sign-off and can be reshaped independently of the rest.

## Why

Gateways such as LiteLLM attach requests to a session through a request header (`x-litellm-session-id`), which is what makes per-chat grouping and cost views work. With `customendpoint` the extension does not control the network request, so the only way to send such a header is through the middleware, and the middleware had no way to tell which chat a request came from. It could tell the vendor, model, URL and provider group apart, but two chats on the same model looked identical.

```ts
copilot.registerLanguageModelRequestMiddleware({
	selector: { vendors: ['customendpoint'] },
	provideRequestHeaders: async ({ sessionId }) =>
		sessionId ? { 'x-litellm-session-id': sessionId } : {},
});
```

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Previous behavior

The session identity existed on both chat paths but never reached the provider. On the agent host path, the loopback proxy in `byokLmProxyService.ts` authenticates every request with a bearer of the form `<nonce>.<sessionId>` and then discarded the session id after the check. On the Copilot participant path, `extChatEndpoint.ts` passes the conversation id to the provider inside `modelOptions._conversationId`, which the BYOK providers did not read for the middleware context.

### Implementation

The proxy sets the authenticated session id on the bridge request (`IByokLmChatRequest.sessionId`). `AgentHostByokLmHandler` copies it onto `ILanguageModelChatRequestOptions.sessionId`, and `extHostLanguageModels.ts` forwards it to the provider as `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions.sessionId`. `AbstractOpenAICompatibleLMProvider.applyRequestMiddleware` puts it in the middleware context, taking the option from core first and the participant path's `_conversationId` as fallback. The fallback is only used when the request was initiated by the Copilot Chat extension itself (`requestInitiator` equals `IEnvService.extensionId`) and the value is a string, because `modelOptions` is caller-controlled on `vscode.lm` requests. `LanguageModelRequestContext.sessionId` is documented in the Copilot extension API together with the LiteLLM example above.

### Behavior and constraints

- The id is the chat session id that core already uses for the session, not a new identifier. It is stable for the lifetime of a chat and differs between chats and between windows.
- The id is only exposed to middleware; it is not added to any request by default.
- Requests from `vscode.lm` callers outside a chat carry `undefined`. Another extension cannot attribute its request to a chat session by putting `_conversationId` in its model options: the fallback ignores it for every initiator other than Copilot Chat.

</details>

## Validation

- Unit tests: the proxy test asserts the authenticated session id reaches the bridge request, and the agent host handler test asserts it reaches the language model request options. The custom endpoint provider test asserts the id reaches the middleware context, and a new test covers the fallback: the core option wins, `_conversationId` is used for requests initiated by this extension, and it is ignored for other initiators, for non-string values and when absent. The Azure Entra test and the registry fixture include the field.
- `vitest` for `src/extension/byok` and `src/extension/api`, `tsc --noEmit` for the Copilot extension, `npm run typecheck-client` at the repo root, `scripts/test.sh --grep "ByokLmProxyService|AgentHostByokLmHandler"`, `eslint` on changed files and `npm run hygiene` pass.

pull_requests.title: Fix terminal sticky scroll header positioning
pull_requests.body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335193

- Anchor the sticky header to the main terminal's actual top instead of deriving a bottom offset from its padded height.
- Use xterm's CSS cell height when pushing a multiline header out at the next command boundary.
- Create and position the overlay before its first reveal, keeping the existing 100 ms delay and cancellation behavior.
- Forward terminal layout changes to the overlay so it stays aligned even when the row count does not change. Keep Modern UI padding and command detection unchanged.
- Add browser regression coverage for Classic and Modern UI, including split-view ancestry, sidebar/editor/fixed-dimension geometry, layout forwarding, multiline push-off, pending-show cancellation, alternate-buffer return, UI toggling, and fractional font/zoom geometry.

**Validation**

- 26 Chromium browser tests pass. Five of six selected geometry tests fail against the unmodified implementation, on alignment assertions rather than missing methods.
- Client TypeScript checking and ESLint on the three changed files pass.

```sh
npm run transpile-client
npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/stickyScroll/test/browser/terminalStickyScrollOverlay.test.ts --browser chromium
npm run typecheck-client
npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/stickyScroll/browser/terminalStickyScrollContribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/stickyScroll/browser/terminalStickyScrollOverlay.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/stickyScroll/test/browser/terminalStickyScrollOverlay.test.ts
```

**Local reproduction**

Verified on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 with Code OSS Dev 1.140.0, comparing base `597d6c38f750` with PR head `0931ff1544e`.

1. Open a shell-integrated Bash terminal with Modern UI and terminal sticky scroll enabled. Set `terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration` to `on` and `terminal.integrated.fontSize` to `22`.
2. Keep the terminal in the normal bottom panel with automatic dimensions, not Set Fixed Dimensions. The recorded run used a 1920x1080 workbench viewport and an automatically fitted 95-column, 11-row terminal. The displacement depends on the pane's remaining space below the terminal grid.
3. From the VS Code checkout, use a short single-line prompt, generate substantial output, then scroll up, down, and up again with the mouse wheel:

```sh
PS1='\[\e[32m\]bash\[\e[0m\] \[\e[34m\]\W\[\e[0m\] $ '; clear
git --no-pager log --oneline --no-decorate -n 500 597d6c38f750
```

Before the fix, scrolling moves the sticky command down and exposes clipped terminal output above it. After the fix, the same content and scroll positions keep the sticky command aligned at the top, with no output above it.

[Before/after screenshots and verification results](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337192#issuecomment-5770598518)

The screenshots are cropped to the terminal pane, with no injected labels or guide lines. The comparison checks both the live terminal geometry and the actual output pixels exposed above the header.

The browser tests use real xterm and SplitView with mocked command detection; this UI reproduction uses real Bash shell integration and WebGL. The reporter's devcontainer environment and sash-drag performance were not tested.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Top anchoring preserves the existing alignment rules in [`terminal.css`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/597d6c38f75065e71b49006710d80e8c1def87db/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/media/terminal.css#L88-L105) and [Modern UI terminal padding](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/597d6c38f75065e71b49006710d80e8c1def87db/src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/browser/media/padding.css#L342-L350).
- CSS cell-height measurement follows the renderer-metric semantics used by [`TerminalLinkManager`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/597d6c38f75065e71b49006710d80e8c1def87db/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/links/browser/terminalLinkManager.ts#L163-L167).
- Layout forwarding uses the existing [terminal contribution layout dispatch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/597d6c38f75065e71b49006710d80e8c1def87db/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts#L2039-L2049).
- The geometry fixture uses the same [`SplitView` ancestry as terminal groups](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/597d6c38f75065e71b49006710d80e8c1def87db/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalGroup.ts#L55-L59).

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] [1.139] Fix Agent Host sandbox settings forwarding and deprecate stale SDK settings
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #337183 from `release/1.139`.

## Summary

Cherry-pick of #337181 into `release/1.139`.
Original commit: 74246652a293292da01d8a82079b2564550755bb.

Fixes #337113.
Related to #337152.

Use the standard `chat.agent.sandbox.*` settings for both the Copilot SDK built-in shell and the Agent Host custom terminal tool, instead of overriding sandbox enablement with the stale `chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.*` settings.

- Remove the terminal-implementation-dependent enablement overrides and configuration listeners from `AgentHostSandboxForwarder`.
- Deprecate the SDK-specific sandbox enablement settings, remove their experimentation hooks, and document that they no longer have an effect.
- Remove the obsolete SDK sandbox settings from the permissions settings query and update the session-toggle description.
- Update regression tests to verify the standard settings are forwarded regardless of terminal implementation or deprecated SDK settings.

## Bug fixes and scope

### #337113: Linux filesystem sandbox settings appear to have no effect

Previously, when using the SDK built-in shell, the forwarder replaced the standard sandbox enablement values with the separate SDK settings, which defaulted to `off`. This could leave sandboxing disabled even when the standard sandbox setting was enabled, making the configured Linux filesystem restrictions appear ineffective. The forwarder now preserves the standard enablement settings alongside the filesystem policy.

### #337152: Separate Windows sandbox setting

This PR removes the SDK-specific settings split, but does **not** eliminate the OS-specific split: Windows still uses `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows`, while macOS/Linux use `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled`. Making `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` enable sandboxing on Windows as well remains a follow-up.

The runtime behavior change applies to the Copilot Agent Host harness. This does not change Claude or Codex sandbox implementations or global sandbox defaults.

## Backport validation

- Applied cleanly to `release/1.139`, with no conflict resolutions or release-specific code changes.
- Stable patch ID matches the original commit exactly.
- Restored release-branch dependencies with `npm ci` and compiled fresh output with `npm run transpile-client`.
- Ran all 17 sandbox-cleanup-related unit-test files on the release branch with `--force-device-scale-factor=1`: **981 passing, 4 pending, 0 failing**.

pull_requests.title: authentication: Preserve session request context end to end
pull_requests.body:
## Stack

Follow-up to merged #337185. Rebased onto `main`; this draft contains only the remaining request-context change, with the test-reliability improvements already in the base.

## Summary

Preserve the complete authentication request through coalescing, provider lookup/creation, account selection, deferred Accounts-menu sign-in, and MCP background revalidation.

- Share typed internal provider options and the RPC DTO instead of maintaining divergent copies; retain proposal gates for existing proposed fields.
- Key requests by actual account, authorization-server, client, resource, and audience values. Preserve scope-array boundaries and coalesce equivalent option/scope orderings.
- Strip platform interaction controls before forwarding provider options. Silent and default/passive lookups do not permit interactive provider recovery.
- Carry the context into account pickers and deferred commands, including MCP and agent-host MCP account selection.
- Keep pending-request completion scoped to its context and lifetime, while preserving account-wide extension consent.
- Surface provider failures separately from cancellation. Unrelated pending revalidation does not delay a successful sign-in.

No stable `vscode.d.ts` changes, credential-storage migration, or new dependencies.

## Concrete behavior

These requests must not share one in-flight result:

```json
[
  { "scopes": ["read"], "resource": "https://api.example/orders" },
  { "scopes": ["read"], "resource": "https://api.example/calendar" }
]
```

Previously the coalescing key reduced these resource values to `true`, and the API bridge dropped resource/client/audience values before calling the provider.

Likewise, a silent lookup receiving `{ "error": "invalid_client" }` during refresh must not open a client-registration prompt.

Deferred sign-in retains its target:

```text
pending: sign in for orders, sign in for calendar
complete orders sign-in
remaining: sign in for calendar
```

If both targets already have sessions for the same account, account-wide extension consent can clear redundant access prompts. It must not clear a third target's sign-in request when that target still needs a token.

## Review and complexity

A focused review found four pending-request edge cases, now fixed and covered by deterministic tests:

1. Default-context requests also require provider revalidation; a resource-bound token does not satisfy them automatically.
2. Queued and in-flight work cannot cross a provider/request generation or continue making lookups after disposal.
3. Another extension joining an in-flight request preserves its identity and is included in completion.
4. A successful Accounts-menu command completes its originating request without waiting for unrelated lookups.

Cognitive complexity is addressed by separating request preparation, generation ownership, session satisfaction, and completion. The coordinator captures ownership before queueing; completion verifies it again after asynchronous work.

Measured using the existing ESLint classic cyclomatic-complexity rule, without changing lint configuration:

| Method | Base | Final |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `MainThreadAuthentication.doGetSession` | 35 | 30 |
| `AuthenticationExtensionsService.requestNewSession` | 12 | 8 |

The pre-review revalidation callback measured 16; its final coordinator callback measures 2, with per-request revalidation at 5 and satisfaction/completion helpers at 3 each. The extracted request-preparation helper measures 8. These are per-function decision counts, not a claim that the overall feature has fewer required behaviors or a numeric cognitive-complexity score.

## Validation

- 149 related unit checks passed: authentication service/query, extension-host/main-thread authentication, MCP, and agent-host authentication.
- 51 authentication in-process integration checks passed.
- Five targeted ownership/default-context/subscriber regressions failed before their fixes and passed afterward.
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Installed ESLint CLI using repository rules for every changed TypeScript file.
- Signed commits with normal pre-commit hooks; `git diff --check` clean.

Integration selection:

```powershell
.\scripts\test-integration.bat `
  --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\browser\extHostAuthentication.integrationTest.ts `
  --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\browser\mainThreadAuthentication.integrationTest.ts
```

Local tests used `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1` and installed Electron 42.10.0. The pinned Electron 43.6.0 runtime remains for CI validation. Tests use controlled providers and HTTP responses, not live OAuth services.

## Scope

Account identity/storage redesign and the separately identified granted-scope/refresh-token durability issues are intentionally excluded.

Related regression history: #273176 and #324925 were previously fixed; they illustrate the request-identity/context contract, not issues this PR claims to close again.

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Strengthen existing authentication tests before changing request handling. This PR contains no production or public API changes.

- Replace four negative tests that caught their own `assert.fail()` with awaited `assert.rejects()` assertions and relevant error matchers.
- Await the authorization-server rejection assertion before checking that the provider was not called.
- Verify that a failed provider lookup does not poison a subsequent identical session request.

The previous pattern could pass when the operation unexpectedly succeeded:

```ts
try {
    await getSession(incompatibleOptions);
    assert.fail("Expected rejection");
} catch (error) {
    assert.ok(error); // Also accepts the assertion error above.
}
```

The retry regression exercises real in-process extension-host/main-thread authentication services with a controlled provider:

```text
same request -> provider rejects
same request -> provider returns an existing session
assert: two provider lookups and the expected token
```

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Cherry-pick of #337181 into `release/1.139`.
Original commit: 74246652a293292da01d8a82079b2564550755bb.

Fixes #337113.
Related to #337152.

Use the standard `chat.agent.sandbox.*` settings for both the Copilot SDK built-in shell and the Agent Host custom terminal tool, instead of overriding sandbox enablement with the stale `chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.*` settings.

- Remove the terminal-implementation-dependent enablement overrides and configuration listeners from `AgentHostSandboxForwarder`.
- Deprecate the SDK-specific sandbox enablement settings, remove their experimentation hooks, and document that they no longer have an effect.
- Remove the obsolete SDK sandbox settings from the permissions settings query and update the session-toggle description.
- Update regression tests to verify the standard settings are forwarded regardless of terminal implementation or deprecated SDK settings.

## Bug fixes and scope

### #337113: Linux filesystem sandbox settings appear to have no effect

Previously, when using the SDK built-in shell, the forwarder replaced the standard sandbox enablement values with the separate SDK settings, which defaulted to `off`. This could leave sandboxing disabled even when the standard sandbox setting was enabled, making the configured Linux filesystem restrictions appear ineffective. The forwarder now preserves the standard enablement settings alongside the filesystem policy.

### #337152: Separate Windows sandbox setting

This PR removes the SDK-specific settings split, but does **not** eliminate the OS-specific split: Windows still uses `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows`, while macOS/Linux use `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled`. Making `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` enable sandboxing on Windows as well remains a follow-up.

The runtime behavior change applies to the Copilot Agent Host harness. This does not change Claude or Codex sandbox implementations or global sandbox defaults.

## Backport validation

- Applied cleanly to `release/1.139`, with no conflict resolutions or release-specific code changes.
- Stable patch ID matches the original commit exactly.
- Restored release-branch dependencies with `npm ci` and compiled fresh output with `npm run transpile-client`.
- Ran all 17 sandbox-cleanup-related unit-test files on the release branch with `--force-device-scale-factor=1`: **981 passing, 4 pending, 0 failing**.
- Coverage includes configuration forwarding, settings reading, session overrides, SDK sandbox configuration, permission pickers, session launching, and terminal sandbox behavior.
- `git diff --check` and the commit hygiene hook passed.

The original main-branch validation reported 987 passing and 4 pending. Fixed display scaling avoids the exact CSS measurement failures seen at the default Windows display scale.

### Manual verification

1. Enable `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` on macOS/Linux, or `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows` on Windows, and configure the applicable filesystem restrictions.
2. Create a new Copilot Agent Host session and verify the permissions picker reflects sandboxing as enabled and terminal commands honor the configured restrictions.

Add temporary cloud-sandbox repository preparation using the currently advertised host capability. This PR is independent of the unsettled protocol proposal in microsoft/agent-host-protocol#451 and client draft #336361; it does not adopt their request shape.

- Keep legacy cloning behind a connection-owned session-start callback in the existing cloud connection customization. The cloud service API and transport factory remain unchanged.
- Read sandbox-specific metadata, reuse a ready checkout or join an existing clone, and request host-side cloning only when needed.
- Require a ready checkout before creating the session and binding directory-scoped customizations.
- Share simultaneous preparation for the same repository while allowing each caller to cancel its own wait. Preparation waits are bounded to five minutes; cancellation does not delete the host checkout.
- Surface failed clone replies immediately and preserve existing sessions and hosts without the capability.

The standalone resolver class and service plumbing have been removed. The legacy callback, metadata reader, and tests carry removal TODOs for adoption of released repository-backed creation. No protocol mirror/version changes, draft protocol fields, new settings, or repository picker.

## Scope

The protocol-client change is only a five-line host-extension request entry point using existing dispatch. Generic cancellation, reconnect, request tracking, and outgoing queue behavior remain unchanged. Improving the lifetime of unanswered RPCs is deliberately outside this PR; stopping a preparation wait does not abandon its underlying RPC tracking.

## Validation

After removing generic request-cancellation changes:

- **65 focused unit tests passed**: 35 legacy startup tests, two extension-request tests, and the affected session-customization suite.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Changed-file ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed; normal signed commit hooks passed.

Unit tests used the available cached Electron 42.10.0 test runtime. Only selected test dependencies were transpiled. No application build or live sandbox/end-to-end flow was run.

## Manual verification still needed

1. Start a cloud sandbox session for a GitHub repository on a host advertising project management; confirm the first turn runs in the prepared checkout.
2. Repeat with an existing checkout and with a clone already in progress; confirm reuse and readiness before the first turn.
3. Check clone failure, cancellation, and explicit retry, plus unchanged behavior on a host without the capability.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: manage additional chat workspaces
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the Agent Host infrastructure for sessions that own multiple repositories and detached worktrees, without changing `create_session` behavior yet.

### Additional worktree ownership

- persist each session-owned detached worktree by opaque handle, effective checkout URI, and authoritative source repository-root URI
- validate malformed metadata, invalid URIs and handles, and duplicate ownership records
- keep repository inference through Git for new records; the path-based convention remains private legacy-metadata recovery only

### Lifecycle integration

- archive, unarchive, automatic cleanup, automatic-deletion eligibility, and permanent deletion now cover every session-owned worktree
- resolve deletion cleanup against persisted source repository roots even when an additional checkout has disappeared from live session `workingDirectories`
- delete detached worktrees before dropping their ownership records so failed cleanup remains retryable
- synchronize archive state through an ordered, failure-isolated chat contribution backed by an injected lifecycle service

### Chat workspace preparation

- add an internal operation that prepares a folder or detached worktree for a chat and returns the effective directory for explicit chat assignment
- resolve repositories authoritatively through Git, reuse an existing owned checkout by default, and support explicitly creating another worktree
- pin chats that inherit the aggregate session workspace before expanding it, preserving their previous effective folders
- persist and claim newly created worktrees, with rollback that deletes successful creations or retains ownership when deletion itself fails
- expose the operation through the internal session-server-tool accessor so the follow-up can wire it without duplicating repository logic

## Scope boundary

This PR intentionally does **not** change the `create_session` schema, descriptions, argument parsing, relationship semantics, or execution behavior. The follow-up only needs to parse the requested folder/repository options, call the preparation operation, and pass its returned URI as the new chat's explicit `workingDirectories`.

Chat-scoped changesets, repository operations, artifacts, pull requests, Agent Merge ownership, and final multi-project presentation remain separate follow-ups.

## Validation

- 301 Agent Host contribution, side-effect, lifecycle, and disposal tests
- all 87 session server-tool unit tests
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `git diff --check`

pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337097.

## Summary

A same-name MCP server in another workspace folder can hide or collision-disable an enabled configuration. That also prevented the Customizations editor from offering to migrate it.

- Track migration eligibility separately from live MCP delivery, allowing supported workspace configurations to migrate without incorrectly reporting them as enabled or forwarded.
- Read and observe the stored profile/workspace enablement before runtime name-collision suppression. Enrich registered as well as missing installed entries while preserving explicit disablement and MCP access restrictions.
- Revalidate the same migration configuration throughout the file move, without invalidating the operation when its own destination is discovered.
- Fix JSON editing to consume the trailing comma when deleting the last object property. Migrating every entry from the repro previously wrote invalid source JSON, triggered rollback, and retained duplicate entries in the destination.
- Add regressions for real collision-aware enablement, complete migrations, retries against equivalent existing destinations, and both removal orders. Update the Settings Sync assertion that expected the old dangling-comma output.

Live forwarding and runtime duplicate-name precedence are unchanged.

- Initial full `Compile` task passed after updating to `main`; client transpilation and type-check passed for the follow-ups.
- Latest focused suites: 157 Electron tests passed; 156 tests each passed in Chromium and WebKit. These include Settings Sync, JSON editing, the real MCP service, support assessment, migration service, and migration writer.

pull_requests.title: minVersion: UI when enforced by Enterprise
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #337086

Enterprise Managed Settings `minVersion` lets administrators block AI features on outdated VS Code clients until users update—for example, to require newer sandboxing protections.

This PR explains that existing restriction without changing enforcement. Chat shows an update notice. **Agents shows one blocking overlay, without a redundant banner.** The editor retains a Workspace Trust-style banner even when Chat is closed, because other editing features remain available.

Native update actions are offered when available. If enterprise policy disables built-in updates, the notice directs users to their administrator for an approved update. Other unavailable-updater states do not imply administrator management, and **no generic fallback link is shown**. **Open Editor Window** opens a fresh editor window, preserving the existing recovery behavior.

## Screenshots

**Controlled simulations, real rendered UI.** Code - OSS Dev, isolated HTTP 466 requirement (installed 1.140.0; required 1.141.0), with the existing updater service temporarily set to `Idle` or `Disabled(Policy)` and then restored to `Disabled(NotBuilt)`. Agents captures were regenerated at the final review-fix head and matched the published PNGs byte-for-byte; unchanged Editor captures are retained. No DOM/text substitution, composites, shipping test switches, or actual update installation. Editor captures exclude the account area and show only a synthetic example file.

### Native updater available — simulated `Idle`

**Chat closed: the editor banner remains visible, with Check for Updates.**

![Editor with a synthetic text file and Chat closed, retaining the organizational update banner and Check for Updates action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc6d41c6-1f90-4f3c-ab21-35bedc4db4ce)

**Chat open: the same requirement and native update action appear beside the editor.**

![Editor showing the Chat update notice and persistent banner with Check for Updates](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9587a5b5-24f0-42f4-a7e2-c5860c573ea0)

**Agents: overlay only, with Check for Updates and Open Editor Window.**

![Agents update-required overlay with Check for Updates and Open Editor Window, without a window banner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eec22c2-4aa5-493a-bedb-67e0b45d280d)

### Enterprise-managed updates — simulated `Disabled(Policy)`

**Chat closed: the editor banner explains that an administrator manages the update path; no generic link.**

![Editor with Chat closed and a text-only banner explaining that built-in updates are disabled by the organization](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0999d027-f53c-4192-9337-4bda4355bf10)

**Chat open: administrator guidance, without a misleading fallback action.**

![Chat notice showing the required and installed versions and administrator guidance, with no update button or generic link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec6b9776-6351-429b-b107-bcb2cefbb414)

**Agents: administrator guidance and Open Editor Window; no redundant banner or generic link.**

![Agents overlay showing administrator-managed recovery guidance and only Open Editor Window as an action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/feb3a981-0d5d-45b3-8ca5-67cab57ad988)

<details>
<summary>Validation and remaining checks</summary>

- 158 focused tests passed in **each of Chromium and WebKit**, including focus ownership/restoration, startup fallback, long tokens and viewport resizing, available-action help, all disabled-updater reasons, and the unchanged fresh-editor-window action.
- Before the final push, all eight Compile & Hygiene scripts passed across documented runs: `core-ci`, `hygiene`, `eslint`, `valid-layers-check`, `define-class-fields-check`, `vscode-dts-compile-check`, `tsec-compile-check`, and `test-build-scripts`. The original aggregate hit environment blockers; it is not claimed as one successful unmodified run. The same `core-ci` command passed after GitHub's rate-limit reset. Build-script tests passed 462/462 with command-scoped empty Git configuration for synthetic fixture repos and canonical `/private/tmp`; the other checks used normal Git configuration. User signing settings were unchanged.
- Build-tool typecheck, Markdown manifest checks, conditional Codex protocol check (no changed inputs), and cyclic-dependency check (9,174 files) passed or correctly skipped before that push.
- Real Electron checks covered both updater states and editor-banner independence from Chat. A long version token at a 600×320 renderer viewport wrapped without horizontal overflow, and the focused recovery action remained visible after shrinking the viewport. Mock settings, updater state, and viewport were restored afterward.
- Earlier validation covered actual 320/480/900px Chat widths and HTTP 466 → `200 {}` → 466 recovery in both windows. All three Copilot review threads have concise inline replies and are resolved.
- Presentation consumes the existing compatibility signal; it does not invent extension/runtime-specific metadata. VoiceOver and full light/dark/high-contrast coverage remain pending.
- Draft review and a trusted signed approval checkpoint at the new head remain outstanding. No automatic merge.

</details>

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] test: isolate CopilotAgent proxy environment
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #337119 from `main`.

## Summary

- Clear inherited `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` variants for every `CopilotAgent` test.
- Restore the original proxy environment after each test, preserving the runner's original key casing and values.
- Leave production proxy precedence and the 1ES Network Isolation configuration unchanged.

## Root cause

1ES Network Isolation began injecting `HTTPS_PROXY` into the Windows Electron test process. `CopilotAgent._resolveProxyForSdk` intentionally skips system-proxy resolution when a proxy environment variable is already present, while `_createCopilotCliEnvironment` forwards the inherited environment to the SDK client. That correct production behavior made 11 tests non-hermetic: their `TestProxyResolver` was never called and the runner proxy replaced the test fixtures.

The failure reproduces across Insider builds 20260921.32, 20260921.33, and 20260921.34. The preceding green build had `SetUpHttpProxy:false`; the failing builds had `SetUpHttpProxy:true` without a relevant VS Code source change.

#337114 addresses the nested `restart on startup config change` suite, but does not cover the two top-level `defers a proxy-change restart...` failures. This change isolates the outer `CopilotAgent` suite so all affected tests start from the same proxy-free environment. It also snapshots the actual environment key casing before restoration, avoiding uppercase/lowercase alias issues on Windows.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- Ran the affected tests with all eight uppercase/lowercase proxy variables injected: **55 passing, 1 Windows-only pending**.
- The full test file was also exercised; current `main` has unrelated pre-existing filesystem-state failures both with and without proxy injection.

Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3914

pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #337080 from `main`.

## Summary

Minimal, **test-harness-only** follow-up to the Windows Codex E2E teardown failure on #337043 ([failed job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35611851264/job/106372674062)). Replaces my overly broad adaptation in #337070; Dmitri's provider-lifecycle work remains in #335992 and is not taken over here.

`stopServer` waits for the agent-host parent to exit. On Windows, descendants can remain alive after that clean exit and retain resources under the test home; `taskkill /T` cannot discover them through a parent that has already exited.

- Record the running test server's Windows descendants before sending EOF.
- Preserve existing graceful shutdown and fallback behavior, then await cleanup of the recorded descendants using the existing `killTree` helper.
- Ignore termination errors only when the recorded process has already exited; otherwise propagate them. A failed descendant lookup is reported after still stopping the server.
- Bound descendant enumeration and graceful exit with one shutdown deadline; preserve EOF and forced cleanup even if enumeration stalls.
- Add Windows orphan-cleanup and cross-platform stalled-snapshot regressions, and document the cleanup boundary.

**No production code, shared process utilities, Codex provider behavior, shutdown budgets, SDK versions, replay fixtures, or retry policies change.** The changes remain confined to test-server cleanup, its regression tests, and documentation.

This targets the test-server cleanup boundary, not every possible provider shutdown race. The archived CI error does not identify its exact locking process, so the synthetic reproduction establishes the orphan-cleanup gap rather than conclusively identifying the handle owner in that run.

## Validation

- New regression fails on unchanged main: the parent exits with code 0, but the recorded descendant is still running.
- After the fix: cleanup and host-shutdown unit suites **6 passing**.
- Strict tokenless Codex replay across common and Codex-specific suite lifetimes: **3 passing**, teardown successful.

fix https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337317

## Summary

Keep the remote host selector usable while hosts connect, reconnect, or refresh discovery in web Agents.

Previously, the bottom-left host dropdown could disappear a few seconds after opening without another click. The phone host sheet could also close during background updates. After this change, those updates leave the picker open so the user can finish choosing a host.

## Implementation

Fix both dismissal paths found during reproduction:

- Stop rebuilding the host toolbar on host/discovery changes. The existing view items already update in place; retain the one-time refresh that replaces the default toolbar item at startup.
- Only reset the web workspace selection when the selected host or its provider membership changes. Status-only notifications were resetting an empty workspace and moving focus into the composer, closing the menu even after the toolbar lifetime fix.
- Use immutable host menu actions to avoid undisposed action objects exposed by the new lifecycle tests.

Add regression coverage for desktop menu and mobile sheet lifetime, startup registration, continued host selection, and workspace scope changes.

## Product verification

Reproduced the original dismissal in the deployed Insiders web app and captured the toolbar-disposal call stack. Exercising the first fix in the actual local Agents workbench exposed the second, focus-stealing path.

Verified the complete fix in Chromium desktop and iPhone-emulated layouts using controlled host entries in the real host-filter service: the picker remains visible through eight connection-status transitions and discovery start/finish, selecting another host works, and reopening/Escape dismissal works. Inspected the rendered UI screenshots.

This local verification uses controlled host transitions, not live tunnel reconnections; phone coverage is browser emulation, not a physical device.

pull_requests.title: Editor: Refine connected tabs UI
pull_requests.body:
Connected editor tabs and the editor surface should read as one document well. Today the seam between them breaks down: wrapped rows leave gutters, selection shifts tab geometry, the strip repaints the whole theme's tab palette, and close targets move as a tab is selected, hovered, or focused. This PR refines that boundary so the tab strip, editor frame, and close affordances stay visually and physically stable.

Classic tabs, the `pill` tab style, and the Agents window are unchanged.

Refs #336320. Consolidates the close-spacing work from #336791.

## Changes

**Theming — the strip no longer repaints the whole palette**
- Adds `editorGroupHeader.connectedTabsBackground` (defaults to `editorGroupHeader.tabsBackground`), so connected strips get their own restrained neutral fill without rewriting each theme's global `editorGroupHeader.tabsBackground` and `tab.inactiveBackground`. Classic tabs keep their original colors.
- The outside stroke, shoulders, and strip separator now use `editorGroupHeader.tabsBorder` (falling back to `tab.border`) instead of `editor.background`, so the seam is a real border rather than a coincidence of matching fills.
- Inactive labels use `tab.inactiveForeground` instead of dimming `foreground` to 50%, keeping at least 4.5:1 contrast, including in inactive editor groups.

**Frame — one continuous boundary instead of stacked edges**
- First tabs and wrapped-row starts drop their own left stroke and outside shoulder; the editor frame paints that edge once.
- An active tab on the outermost row reuses the editor frame's top stroke rather than drawing a second line beside it.
- In high-contrast themes, a single rounded editor-group frame encloses the title and editor surface on all four sides, including breadcrumbs.
- Free corners stay rounded; only corners adjoining the frame are squared.

**Layout — geometry stops depending on selection**
- Wrapped rows lose their horizontal gutters, so painted row surfaces meet edge to edge; spacing remains only between rows.
- Selecting a tab no longer changes its width or margin, and row classification no longer triggers a second fit-tab reflow.
- Shoulder space is reserved only after the final tab; intermediate shoulders paint over adjacent surfaces instead of inserting a gap.

**Close targets — stable across every state**
- Close-action clearance is derived from tab height and row gutters rather than the shoulder radius, and is reserved on inactive tabs too, so selecting a tab never moves its close target.
- The 20px hover target keeps even inset spacing on all sides and stays clear of the terminal shoulder in wrapped rows, single rows, and separate pinned rows.
- High-contrast hover and focus indicators belong to the close target itself, not to a second border around its container. Disabled Close Others (Alt) no longer shifts the target.

**Structure**
- The connected root marker now lives with the editor control constants and is shared by editor layout, the Modern UI contribution, and theming.
- `connectedEditorTabs.css` owns marker-gated geometry; `connectedEditorTabs.ts` owns marker-gated theme derivations. Core editor-tab code keeps only what CSS cannot express: row classification, label compression, shoulder-aware reveal, and viewport clipping.

## How to test

1. Run Code OSS and set `"workbench.experimental.modernUI": true` (`modernUIEditorTabStyle` defaults to `connected`).
2. Open about eight editors and narrow the window until tabs wrap onto two rows. Confirm rows meet without horizontal gutters and no gutter appears below the last row.
3. Select tabs on both rows. The selected tab must not change width or shift its neighbours, and its close button must not move.
4. Hover a clean inactive tab, then Tab into its close action. The hover or focus indicator should sit on the close target with even inset spacing.
5. Hold `Alt` to turn the close action into a disabled Close Others action; the target must stay in place.
6. Switch to **Dark High Contrast** and **Light High Contrast**. The editor group should have one continuous rounded frame, with tabs sharing its strokes rather than doubling them.
7. Turn Modern UI off and confirm Classic tabs are visually unchanged.

## Screenshots

The [automated screenshot report](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337126#issuecomment-5766493535) is the primary visual evidence for this PR. It compares the base and current implementations across all bundled themes and fixture states.

When reviewing the report, focus on:

- connected versus Classic tab colors, especially inactive labels and editor-group backgrounds;
- single-row, wrapped-row, and separate pinned-row geometry;
- shared frame edges, shoulders, and corner treatment in default and high-contrast themes;
- close-action position and indicators across inactive, selected, hover, focus, and disabled states.

## Validation

- Targeted unit tests cover row geometry, viewport clipping, connected-theme derivation, and high-contrast frame behavior.
- Component fixtures cover default and compact density, single and wrapped rows, separate pinned rows, action placement, and bundled themes.
- A Playwright fixture test asserts that close-target position remains stable across selection, hover, and focus.
- Client compilation, ESLint, Stylelint, and hygiene checks pass.

## Root cause

1ES Network Isolation began injecting `HTTPS_PROXY` into the Windows Electron test process. `CopilotAgent._resolveProxyForSdk` intentionally skips system-proxy resolution when a proxy environment variable is already present, while `_createCopilotCliEnvironment` forwards the inherited environment to the SDK client. That correct production behavior made 11 tests non-hermetic: their `TestProxyResolver` was never called and the runner proxy replaced the test fixtures.

The failure reproduces across Insider builds 20260921.32, 20260921.33, and 20260921.34. The preceding green build had `SetUpHttpProxy:false`; the failing builds had `SetUpHttpProxy:true` without a relevant VS Code source change.

Supersedes #337114, which addresses the nested `restart on startup config change` suite, but does not cover the two top-level `defers a proxy-change restart...` failures. This change isolates the outer `CopilotAgent` suite so all affected tests start from the same proxy-free environment. It also snapshots the actual environment key casing before restoration, avoiding uppercase/lowercase alias issues on Windows.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- Ran the affected tests with all eight uppercase/lowercase proxy variables injected: **55 passing, 1 Windows-only pending**.
- The full test file was also exercised; current `main` has unrelated pre-existing filesystem-state failures both with and without proxy injection.

Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3914

pull_requests.title: fix: isolate ambient proxy env in CopilotAgent proxy tests (build fix for vscode-engineering#3914)
pull_requests.body:
## Build failure

The `Run unit tests (Electron)` task on `main` failed deterministically on the Windows Electron run with five failing assertions in `vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`, all under `CopilotAgent > restart on startup config change`. In every failure the mocked proxy resolver was never invoked (`resolveProxyCalls: 0`) and a real system proxy address leaked in instead of the test's configured fixtures.

## Root cause

The affected tests assert how `CopilotAgent` resolves and forwards the CAPI proxy, but the production code paths read ambient proxy environment variables:

- `_resolveProxyForSdk(env = process.env)` short-circuits and returns early when any of `HTTPS_PROXY`/`https_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`http_proxy`/`ALL_PROXY`/`all_proxy` is already set (`COPILOT_PROXY_ENV_KEYS.some(key => env[key])`), deliberately leaving proxy configuration to the environment. This is why the injected resolver is never called (`resolveProxyCalls: 0`).
- `_createCopilotCliEnvironment` reads `process.env` and forwards the ambient proxy into the created client env, so the runner's real `HTTPS_PROXY` replaced the test's configured value.

The tests did not isolate ambient proxy environment variables, so when the Windows CI agent had an `HTTPS_PROXY` set in its environment, that value leaked into the production resolver and broke the assertions. The failure is a test-isolation gap, not a product defect: the same suite already saves/clears/restores `COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN` for the same reason, but the proxy env vars were never isolated. No suspect commit in the build touched the proxy code.

## How the fix works

Added `setup`/`teardown` hooks scoped to the `restart on startup config change` suite that save, clear, and restore the ambient proxy env keys (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `ALL_PROXY`, `all_proxy`, `NO_PROXY`, `no_proxy`) around every test. This gives each test a known, proxy-free `process.env`, so the injected `TestProxyResolver` is exercised as intended and the runner's real proxy can no longer leak in. This mirrors the existing Kerberos SPN save/clear/restore pattern already used in this suite. Production code is unchanged.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**.

- Public culprit commit/PR: **not confirmed**. The commits associated with the failing build touch unrelated MCP-lifecycle code in `vs/platform/agentHost`, not the proxy-resolution path or its tests; the failure is ambient-environment leakage on the CI agent surfaced by a test-isolation gap.
- Rationale: The failure is confined to unit tests on insider CI with no shipped user impact, and the fix is a bounded, test-only isolation change. There is no confirmed culprit to revert, and reverting the unrelated agentHost commits in this window would risk more than it fixes.
- Owners to consult: not determined

## Validation

The change is test-only and does not touch product code. Node modules and compiled output are not available in this environment, so `scripts/test.sh --grep "restart on startup config change"` could not be executed here. The fix follows the established `COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN` save/clear/restore pattern already present in the same suite.

## Risk

Low. The change only adds `setup`/`teardown` env isolation scoped to the affected suite and restores prior values afterwards; it does not alter production behavior or other suites.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: not-determined

Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3914

pull_requests.title: chat: Add a unified customization marketplace
pull_requests.body: ## Summary Build a source-neutral customization marketplace using the designer's unified Discover experience from #337347. When no marketplace feed is enabled, Agent Customizations keeps its original Overview and management pages. Enabling any marketplace source replaces Overview with Discover; changing the enabled sources updates the home surface and cancels stale requests. Individual management pages retain their existing Available catalogs until those catalogs are added as separate feeds. The default-off GitHub Feed is enabled by `chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled`. The visible name is **GitHub Feed**; `agentFinder` remains an internal source ID and the existing API endpoint is unchanged. - Discover combines installed agents, skills, instructions, prompts, hooks, MCP servers, and plugins with available catalog results. The designer's responsive, accessible UI provides browse cards, source selection, a flat virtualized search list, and type filters. Search normally paginates on scroll; a bounded Load More fallback remains when filtering leaves no scrollable matches. - Independent source gates lazily construct only selected feeds. Global pages contain at most 24 entries. Search merges descending optional relevance scores; browse interleaves sources. Source-owned cursors and buffered entries stay behind bounded opaque continuations. - A failed source does not hide healthy results. Named warnings, neutral explicit sign-in prerequisites, Accessible View/Help, and retry restart the combined query from page one. No browsing action starts OAuth. - Installation uses existing VS Code destinations and policies: skills are imported as complete packages with no overwrite, plugins retain trust and managed-marketplace checks, and MCP servers resolve version-pinned GitHub Feed MCP records through the existing policy-enforced installer. Resources without validated installation information remain discoverable without an install action; MCP entries with unsupported local prerequisites offer publisher setup instructions when a link is available instead of Retry Install. Cursor-format plugins are omitted from browse and search until supported. - Desktop public-feed requests use a lazy shared-process channel; web uses the workbench request service and its remote fallback. The feed API response is validated and bounded before exposing installation provenance. The designer's latest refinement (`26035c4`) is incorporated where safe: the Discover migration warning is removed, browse section actions align with headings, and fallback artwork respects theme/high-contrast borders. Its unconditional removal of the MCP and Plugin pages' Available sections is deferred until their respective catalogs are actually available in Discover, each in a separate draft PR. Backend context: [catalog onboarding guide](https://github.com/github/copilot-ecosystem/discussions/1452). Related to #333757 and #336202. Discover searches installed agents, skills, instructions, prompts, hooks, MCP servers, and plugins; Tools and direct enable/disable from global results remain outside this PR. ## Validation - Focused marketplace/provider, install, editor, Overview, Discover and source recovery tests pass locally. - Full client typecheck, module layer check, changed-file ESLint and repository CSS Stylelint pass. - Eight light/dark component fixture cases verify disabled Overview, Discover with an alternate source only, and both live enable/disable transitions. - Ten additional designer Discover browse/search fixtures were visually inspected and rendered without errors after the integration. - The committed blocks-ci hashes still name MarketplaceTab while the blocking fixture is DiscoverSearchResults. This remains a screenshot-baseline follow-up using hashes from Linux CI; I have not regenerated them on macOS or waited for CI. ## Manual test 1. With all marketplace sources disabled, open Customizations and verify the original Overview, migration card and management pages remain; no feed requests occur. 2. Enable `chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled`: Discover replaces Overview, shows public browse/search, and the home button reads Discover. Disable it again and confirm Overview returns and stale requests are cancelled. 3. Search with type/installed filters, switch sources, clear search to restore Featured, and scroll to load the next bounded global page (or use Load More when a filtered page has no scrollable matches). 4. Fail a feed while another succeeds, retry and verify ranked results restart; review inaccessible/unavailable and installation states with keyboard and Accessible View/Help. 5. Exercise skill destination/cancellation, plugin trust, feed-backed MCP install and policy, manual setup for unsupported packages, and uninstall. When the independent MCP or Plugin feeds are disabled, their legacy Available sections remain accessible on their management pages.

pull_requests.title: Agent Host: apply supported legacy policy restrictions by default
pull_requests.body:
Supported legacy VS Code restrictions now reach local Agent Host Copilot sessions by default. This removes the experimental `chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings` opt-in; stale `true`/`false` entries are ignored and cannot disable a mapped restriction. Existing host permission enforcement remains in place. The Local harness, remote hosts, and other agents are unchanged.

| Legacy control | Before (bridge off) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Global auto-approve disabled by policy | Allow All blocked | Allow All blocked, also enforced in the runtime |
| Terminal auto-approve off / `false` rules | Enforced only when the host layer handles the approval | Also enforced in the runtime; matching commands require approval |
| Network deny list, or filter on with empty lists | Not enforced for fetch/URL requests | Matching domains denied |
| Network allowlist | Not enforced | Not enforced; unlisted domains prompt instead of being blocked |
| Tools ineligible for auto-approval | Not enforced; Allow All approves them | Allow All disabled for the session (coarser than Local); assisted approval can still approve them |
| MCP allow/deny | Not enforced | Unchanged; tracked in #333291 |
| Remote hosts, Claude, Codex | Not covered | Unchanged |

This is not full Local → Agent Host policy parity; MCP, network allowlist, and per-tool approval remain separate work.

**Validation:** A new bundled-runtime integration test covers no restriction, a denied domain, and a terminal ask across new session, cold resume, and removal, checking that unrelated requests keep baseline approval behavior. Added coverage for deferring the managed-permission restart until an active turn ends; unit tests updated for the removed gate. CI passes at `8c6df6e`.

Supersedes #333290. Refs #332011; the first released default-on build remains an open criterion.

pull_requests.title: Preserve selected provider for voice-created worktree sessions
pull_requests.body:
## Description

Voice-created worktree sessions could switch from the selected provider to **Local** when the active session type was no longer advertised for the folder. This change keeps the active session’s selected provider authoritative while allowing that provider to choose its current default session type.

### Root cause

`prepareNewVoiceSession` used `inheritableSessionTarget`, which intentionally drops both `providerId` and `sessionTypeId` when the exact provider/type pair is unavailable. With no provider specified, shared new-session resolution selected the first provider by order, causing Local Agent Host (`order = -1`) to win.

### Fix

- Preserve both the selected provider and session type when the exact target remains available.
- When only the previous session type is unavailable, preserve the selected provider and omit the stale type so that provider chooses its current default.
- Leave shared provider ordering and `_resolveProviderForNewSession` unchanged.

pull_requests.title: Add prioritized Sessions Inbox notifications view
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
- add a new `inboxOne` Sessions contribution with a dedicated **Inbox** custom view for prioritized, actionable notifications
- introduce `IInboxNotificationsService` to aggregate notifications from session lifecycle state (`NeedsInput`, unread `Completed` sessions)
- add session-linked PR notifications using existing client-side GitHub models:
  - failing required CI checks
  - passing required CI checks (merge-ready signal)
  - unresolved Copilot review comments
  - **merged pull requests** (session cleanup signal)
- for the CI / review / merge PR notifications, add one-click actions that submit the matching agent skill to the session's chat **in the background** — the same universal mechanism as the in-session **Fix Checks / Address Comments** — so they work for **cloud and agent-host sessions alike** and never open or navigate to the session:
  - **Fix CI Failures** → `/fix-ci`
  - **Address Reviews** → `/act-on-feedback`
  - **Merge Pull Request** → `/merge`
  - failing CI **and** unresolved Copilot comments on the same session are addressed together in one turn (`/fix-ci and /act-on-feedback`)
- show an inline progress spinner on the action while the request is submitting, and surface an error notification if the submission fails
- for merged pull request notifications, add direct actions to:
  - **Archive Session**
  - **Delete Session**
  - optional **Always {Action}** dropdown behavior wired to existing merged-session lifecycle settings
- keep a provider-neutral external publish seam (`publishExternalNotification`) for additional integrations
- integrate an **Inbox** shortcut section in the Sessions list that opens the custom view directly
- add accessibility support for the Inbox surface (focus context key, accessible help + view providers, and `accessibility.verbosity.inboxNotifications`)
- gate the whole feature behind an experimental setting `chat.agentSessions.inbox.enabled` (off by default, `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`), mirrored into a `ChatInboxEnabledContext` context key; the Inbox section, view, and Show Inbox command are hidden unless the setting (or an experiment) enables it
- add focused unit tests for notification derivation/persistence, PR/CI/comment/merged signal derivation, and accessible-content output

## Intentional Scope
This change does not add new agent-host async event contracts. PR/CI/comment signals are derived from existing client-side session-linked GitHub models for MVP, and can later switch to unified async triggers with minimal churn. The CI / review / merge actions reuse the existing in-session skill-submission path (`IChatService.acquireOrLoadSession` + `sendRequest` with `agentIdSilent`), so they run identically on cloud and agent-host sessions without opening the session.

## Enablement
The Inbox is experimental and off by default. It is gated by the machine-scoped setting `chat.agentSessions.inbox.enabled` (tags: `experimental`, `advanced`; `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`), mirrored into the `ChatInboxEnabledContext` context key. When disabled, the Inbox shortcut section in the Sessions list, the Inbox custom view (restore + auto-hide), and the **Show Inbox** command/keybinding are all hidden. Toggling the setting updates the Sessions list reactively without a reload. This mirrors the Automations enablement pattern (`chat.automations.enabled`).

## Testing
- `npx eslint src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/browser/inboxNotificationsView.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/browser/inboxNotificationsService.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/test/browser/inboxNotificationsService.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/test/browser/inboxNotificationsService.test.ts`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/inboxOne/test/browser/inboxNotificationsAccessibility.test.ts`

## Inbox Event → Actions (Now/Next/Later Order)

| Priority Tier | Event | Actions Offered |
|---|---|---|
| Now | Needs input | Open Session · Done |
| Now | Failing CI on linked PR | Open Session · Fix CI Failures · Done |
| Now | Unresolved Copilot review comments | Open Session · Address Reviews · Done |
| Next | Passing CI on linked PR | Open Session · Merge Pull Request · Done |
| Next | Pull request merged | Open Session · Archive Session · Delete Session · Done |
| Later | Completed session (unread) | Open Session · Mark as Read · Done |

The CI / review / merge actions submit their agent skill to the session in the background — `Fix CI Failures` → `/fix-ci`, `Address Reviews` → `/act-on-feedback`, `Merge Pull Request` → `/merge` (and `/fix-ci and /act-on-feedback` when the session has both failing CI and unresolved Copilot comments). A spinner shows on the button while the request submits; an error notification is shown if it fails.

## Inbox PR Action Mechanism (Cloud vs Agent-Host)

All three CI / review / merge actions run through one code path — `IChatService.acquireOrLoadSession(session.resource)` then `sendRequest(session.resource, query, { agentIdSilent: session.resource.scheme })` — so the Inbox behaves the same regardless of provider and never navigates to the session.

| Session kind | Routing key (`agentIdSilent` = `resource.scheme`) | Where the skill runs |
|---|---|---|
| Agent-host (local / remote) | `agent-host-*` | Local/remote agent-host process runs the skill against the PR |
| Cloud Copilot | `copilot-cloud-agent` | Cloud coding-agent task runs the skill server-side |

## Agent Merge "Always" Opt-In Prompt Behavior

The immediate action always submits the agent skill (above). Separately, the Inbox tracks usage of these actions globally (profile-scoped, per action) and offers a milestone-based opt-in to enable the corresponding **Agent Merge** default. Because those defaults only take effect for **agent-host** sessions, the **Always {Action}** dropdown (and its opt-in prompt) is shown only on agent-host session notifications and is hidden on cloud sessions.

| Tracked event in Inbox | Action being tracked | "Always" dropdown action | Prompt cadence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Failing CI on linked PR | Fix CI Failures | Always Fix CI Failures | On 10th use, then every +10 (20, 30, …) |
| Unresolved Copilot review comments | Address Reviews | Always Address Reviews | On 10th use, then every +10 (20, 30, …) |
| Passing CI on linked PR | Merge Pull Request | Always Merge Pull Request | On 10th use, then every +10 (20, 30, …) |

Prompt details:
- shown only for agent-host sessions, and only when that action is not already globally enabled
- primary action: **Always {Action}**
- secondary action: **Not Now**
- checkbox: **Don't ask again for this action** (suppresses future prompts for that action)
- opting in writes global Agent Merge defaults, so the auto-behavior applies to future agent-host sessions

## Merged PR "Always" Cleanup Behavior

For merged PR notifications, selecting **Always Archive Session** or **Always Delete Session** writes existing lifecycle settings (`ConfigurationTarget.USER`) to enable automatic merged-session cleanup:

- `chat.agentSessions.autoMarkAsDoneMergedSessionsAfterDays = 15`
- `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteMarkedAsDoneMergedSessionsAfterDays = 15` (for Always Delete)

## Inbox Telemetry (Privacy-Constrained)

This PR adds inbox-surface telemetry specific to actions taken in the Inbox view (`agents/inboxInteraction`) and keeps payloads bounded to interaction metadata.

### Logged interaction coverage
- toolbar interactions (sort mode changes, completed visibility toggle)
- section interactions (expand/collapse)
- list/update interactions (deferred update banner actions)
- card-level actions and dropdown actions
- inline needs-input submissions (confirmation, tool confirmation, question carousel)
- detail-pane interactions (open full session, open PR/evidence links)
- selection lifecycle and dwell timing (select/deselect)

### Logged metadata
- interaction name and trigger surface
- outcome (`attempt`, `success`, `failure`, `skipped`)
- duration (for async actions and dwell)
- bounded notification/action kinds
- whether a session is associated
- command id for command-backed actions
- per-view trajectory fields (`viewInstanceId`, monotonic `sequence`)

### Explicitly not logged
- session titles
- AI-generated summaries, responses, or request/response snippet text
- typed inline-answer text
- command arguments or tool payload content
- hashed per-notification identifiers
- inline answer-shape/length/count metadata

## Follow-up (not included in this PR)
- add an explicit **"Inbox was useful"** feedback affordance to collect direct user sentiment on Inbox usefulness.

pull_requests.title: test: clean up Windows agent-host descendants after shutdown
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Minimal, **test-harness-only** follow-up to the Windows Codex E2E teardown failure on #337043 ([failed job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35611851264/job/106372674062)). Replaces my overly broad adaptation in #337070; Dmitri's provider-lifecycle work remains in #335992 and is not taken over here.

`stopServer` waits for the agent-host parent to exit. On Windows, descendants can remain alive after that clean exit and retain resources under the test home; `taskkill /T` cannot discover them through a parent that has already exited.

- Record the running test server's Windows descendants before sending EOF.
- Preserve existing graceful shutdown and fallback behavior, then await cleanup of the recorded descendants using the existing `killTree` helper.
- Ignore termination errors only when the recorded process has already exited; otherwise propagate them. A failed descendant lookup is reported after still stopping the server.
- Bound descendant enumeration and graceful exit with one shutdown deadline; preserve EOF and forced cleanup even if enumeration stalls.
- Add Windows orphan-cleanup and cross-platform stalled-snapshot regressions, and document the cleanup boundary.

**No production code, shared process utilities, Codex provider behavior, shutdown budgets, SDK versions, replay fixtures, or retry policies change.** The changes remain confined to test-server cleanup, its regression tests, and documentation.

This targets the test-server cleanup boundary, not every possible provider shutdown race. The archived CI error does not identify its exact locking process, so the synthetic reproduction establishes the orphan-cleanup gap rather than conclusively identifying the handle owner in that run.

## Validation

- New regression fails on unchanged main: the parent exits with code 0, but the recorded descendant is still running.
- After the fix: cleanup and host-shutdown unit suites **6 passing**.
- Strict tokenless Codex replay across common and Codex-specific suite lifetimes: **3 passing**, teardown successful.
- `npm run gulp compile-client`: 0 errors.
- ESLint, diff checks, and commit hygiene: passed.

Local validation is Windows-only. The previous head passed three-platform [Azure build 475551](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475551). The review follow-up in `62e8628b8fe` passes local compile, lint, hygiene, 6 unit tests, and 3 focused Codex replay tests; removing its snapshot bound makes the new regression fail. Fresh PR CI and [Azure build 475625](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475625) are running on the updated head with publishing and release disabled; results remain pending.
