pull_requests.title: Fix Copilot CLI plugin updates on Windows
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- use the Copilot runtime's persisted `installedPlugins` records in `~/.copilot/config.json` as the authoritative installed-plugin inventory
- observe only the state file through a correlated non-recursive watcher; never watch the CLI cache recursively or open handles inside plugin directories
- validate committed `cache_path` records stay under the runtime-owned install root, preserve the last good inventory when state is malformed, and suppress unchanged state
- ignore redundant `chat.pluginLocations` entries into the CLI-owned cache and apply managed enablement to the authoritative discovery result instead of rediscovering cache folders
- leave live/local development plugins to configured, extension, and VS Code marketplace discovery, which retain in-place component watching
- remove VS Code's direct-delete action for CLI-owned plugins because CLI install/update/uninstall are lock-coordinated state transactions
- rebind MCP collections when a committed update rebuilds a plugin object at the same URI

Fixes #334391

Addresses the watcher trigger in #336864.

## Cross-client contract

This follows the same ownership model used by Copilot CLI and GitHub Copilot App:

- Copilot runtime persists a typed `installedPlugins` global-state array, writes it atomically under a per-file lock, and holds a cross-process plugin mutation lease across cache promotion/removal and dependent state writes.
- Cache replacement rolls back if the state transaction fails.
- Real installs persist `cache_path`; legacy records are accepted from the original snake-case `installed_plugins` key and resolve through both historical cache layouts when `cache_path` is absent.
- Live directory/local marketplace plugins are a separate non-persisted tier and are resolved per session.
- GitHub Copilot App asks runtime `plugins.list`, consumes stable plugin identities, and reacts to explicit `plugins_changed` invalidation; it does not enumerate cache directories.

## Automated validation

- 238 related plugin discovery, format, enablement, settings, installed-store, marketplace, install-service, and MCP discovery tests passed
- focused transaction tests cover committed versus uncommitted cache trees, config-only update signals, unchanged-state suppression, malformed-state retention, ancestor bootstrap/recreation, path confinement, and legacy fallback
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint for all changed implementation and test files
- Windows x64 assertion-backed UI scenarios using VS Code Dev 1.139.0 and the official Copilot CLI
- WSL 2 Ubuntu source-workbench validation using the official Linux Copilot CLI

## Original Windows reproduction

The unmodified build fails during the exact command `copilot plugin update spark@copilot-plugins` with `Access is denied. (os error 5)` while VS Code is open.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bceebba2-9f91-45fe-ab4c-162d20b8a126

## Final-head verification matrix

All 24 recorded Windows final-head steps passed with no skips and no window reloads. The additional WSL lifecycle passed 4/4 assertions without reloading.

### Official Copilot CLI lifecycle — 7/7 passed

Starts before `.copilot/config.json` exists, then verifies official CLI install, config-backed discovery, update, post-update discovery, uninstall, and UI removal.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e719ebe-df54-43bb-9b98-284a837b7601

### WSL 2 source-workbench lifecycle — 4/4 passed

Launches the Code OSS source build connected to Ubuntu, proves the remote filesystem provider is active, discovers `spark` from the Linux `~/.copilot` state and cache path, runs the official CLI update successfully, then observes official CLI uninstall remove the plugin without a window reload.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57ec7608-f3cb-45c2-b298-5fe02adc57ab

### Committed transaction behavior — 6/6 passed

Verifies uncommitted valid cache trees stay invisible, committed promotion appears, committed atomic replacement refreshes, committed removal clears inventory, and recreated state/cache recover without reload.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f10174c-c14f-448e-b8a8-7ef088a3abb1

### Managed plugin overlap — 3/3 passed

Verifies a CLI plugin also enabled by managed `chat.plugins.enabledPlugins` is discovered once from authoritative state, updates successfully with exit code 0, and remains visible.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7879fe8-c695-4b32-9256-bc8d33c23f7f

### Non-CLI live discovery regressions — 8/8 passed

Verifies configured Copilot and Claude plugins, extension-contributed Open Plugins, and VS Code-installed Agent Plugin marketplace sources retain live in-place component refresh, install, uninstall, and configured-location removal behavior.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d14eb12-c4fa-4123-b565-a98f60495a6c

pull_requests.title: Keep synchronized plugin paths alive for active sessions
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #328464

Synchronized plugin revisions could be evicted or overwritten while an active session still retained their concrete paths. A later skill invocation then failed because its advertised `SKILL.md` no longer existed.

Each Agent Host now materializes plugins under a runtime-isolated directory. Returned paths carry reference-counted leases owned by the Copilot, Claude, or Codex session, so runtime eviction skips paths an SDK may still read. Released revisions remain bounded by the existing per-plugin and global limits, nonce-less syncs use unique immutable revisions, and dead runtime directories are reclaimed by later hosts.

## Video evidence

- [Before fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/336641#issuecomment-5722086570)
- [After fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/336641#issuecomment-5722087681)

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentPluginManager.test.ts` (21 passing)
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/capiReplayProxyPathNormalization.test.ts` (3 passing)
- Claude and Codex customization store suites (28 passing)
- Focused Copilot, Claude, and Codex sync/rebind/teardown tests (12 passing)
- Targeted ESLint for all changed files

pull_requests.title: agentHost: reduce artifact tool overhead with a prompt experiment
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Add the experiment-configurable `chat.artifactTools.compactPrompts` setting, defaulting to **false** (verbose/control). The treatment key is `config.chat.artifactTools.compactPrompts`. Compact prompts reduce repeated classification prose and first-turn guidance while retaining the full eligibility contract in the Add tool description for restored chats.
- Keep List/Remove deferral **independent of the prompt experiment**. Typed per-tool metadata keeps Add eager, uses Copilot discovery when its existing search gate is active, and uses Claude's native MCP loading metadata. Codex stays eager because the host cannot reliably determine native search support.
- Make Add idempotently promote references in place, preserve IDs and atomic batches, and return concise per-item mutation results. Preserve actual tool names, legacy aliases, feature gating, explicit removal, and user-visible labels. The existing authoritative PR-creation registration path remains unchanged.

## Experiment and measurement

Start a new chat after changing the prompt setting. Both variants use the same deferral behavior and shared eligibility/discovery clarifications; the control retains the original verbose format rather than reproducing the old payload byte-for-byte.

Local `o200k_base` measurements of serialized tool-definition arrays plus the first-turn reminder, with List/Remove deferred in both variants:

| Artifact-specific payload | Control | Compact |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial tool definitions | 568 | 500 |
| First-turn reminder | 218 | 46 |
| Total | 786 | 546 |

This is **240 fewer initial artifact-specific tokens** from prompt compaction. The eager fallback also saves 240 tokens (888 to 648). Measurements exclude provider framing and later discovery overhead and do **not** establish total-session cost or AIU savings.

## Validation

- 83 targeted Electron tests and 8 Node checks passed, including native Claude SDK/MCP invocation.
- Coverage includes experiment defaults/overrides and host sync, both prompt variants, discovery and invocation, restored/legacy compatibility, gate off/on, first-turn reminders, multi-item adds, duplicate/promotion behavior, atomic failures, URI validation, persistence, and removal.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, changed-file ESLint, `npm run gulp compile-client`, `npm run precommit` (23 staged files), and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full Copilot E2E replay could not complete: the standalone agent host timed out during startup before the scenario ran. No replay recordings were changed; the existing batch-result assertion was updated for the compact success response.

Query parser reads parameters after the URL fragment, causing cache-key and proxy interpretation differentials

Affects: Cache Middleware and applications behind a proxy, WAF, or logging layer that inspects query strings. pull_requests.title: Fix Copilot reasoning replay using API provenance instead of ID prefixes
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fixes the reasoning replay regression introduced by #320199: Responses-compatible endpoints can issue valid encrypted reasoning with IDs that do not start with `rs`.

- Record the producing API type (`responses`, `messages`, or `chatCompletions`) on the local tool-call round and thinking envelope.
- Carry API provenance through `vscode.lm` thinking-part metadata.
- When API provenance is present, include encrypted reasoning in Responses requests only for `responses`, regardless of ID format. Explicit `messages` and `chatCompletions` origins are excluded even when the ID starts with `rs`.
- When API provenance is absent, fall back to the old behavior: require a string ID starting with `rs`.
- Require encrypted content in both cases. Preserve the existing local same-model history gate and the original reasoning ID/payload; no new model identity check is added.

## Compatibility

The new API provenance property is optional. Existing persisted history and extensions that do not supply it retain the previous ID-prefix-based replay behavior. Explicit API provenance takes precedence over ID shape. No public VS Code API signature changes are introduced. Compaction and stateful-marker behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- Latest compatibility fallback change: **64 Responses request serialization tests passed**, including legacy untagged replay and missing encrypted payload coverage; no editor diagnostics in the changed files.
- Before the fallback change: **66 focused tests passed** across Responses request serialization and language-model access prompt tests.
- Earlier API-type-only version: **1,460 tests passed**, 52 skipped across affected endpoint/prompt/conversation/intents suites; extension TypeScript check passed.
- `git diff --check` passed; commit hooks completed successfully.

Regression coverage checks tagged Responses reasoning with and without `rs` IDs, exclusion of Messages/Chat Completions reasoning with `rs`-looking IDs, legacy prefix behavior for untagged reasoning, missing encrypted payloads, and metadata-to-envelope provenance preservation.

auto_merge.commit_title: Fix Copilot reasoning replay using API provenance instead of ID prefixes (#336626)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* Track reasoning provenance instead of inferring it from ids

Responses API reasoning was only round-tripped when its id began with `rs`.
That treated one provider's id convention as a protocol guarantee: CAPI's
production /responses endpoint issues reasoning ids that are long opaque blobs
with no `rs` prefix, so valid reasoning was silently dropped from the next
stateless tool continuation and the model re-derived work it had already done.

Record the producing API and model on the thinking envelope when a round is
created, and gate the round-trip on that origin. The envelope tag lives inside
the same opaque value as its payload so prompt pruning cannot separate them, and
it is carried across the vscode.lm boundary as part metadata since that API has
no envelope of its own. The model check also gives the vscode.lm path the gate
it never had.

History persisted before provenance tracking carries no origin and keeps the
previous `rs` prefix behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: d8a292b0-2f13-45cf-bfcc-8e808833b4a0

* Identify reasoning by API type only, dropping the model dimension

Provenance now records just the producing API (responses/messages/chatCompletions),
which is what decides whether an encrypted reasoning payload can be replayed.
The model is already gated separately by the same-model check in toolCalling, so

pull_requests.title: Fix active-view picker visibility for new-session onboarding
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fix the new-session onboarding scope regression introduced by #335080.

That change correctly gave new-session composers the session view's scoped instantiation service. However, the workspace/harness/isolation visibility keys were then written only into child contexts, while the workbench-level onboarding trigger and spotlight step conditions still read the root context. Child updates do not propagate upward, so a visibly rendered workspace picker never satisfied V2/V3 readiness.

- Keep picker rendering state in observables owned by the composer, and project it into each session view's own context with explicit false values for absent/hidden pickers.
- Let the Sessions Part alone publish the active view's picker visibility globally. Detach the old view during reconciliation so inactive updates and disposal cannot overwrite the active view's values; publish all three keys together.
- Include the empty new-session composer in active-slot selection and keyboard/pointer activation, even beside an existing session and without an active session object.
- Reset visibility when a composer is hidden, sent, rebound, replaced by the no-agent-host state, or disposed.

The scoped DI for session-specific actions is retained. No onboarding eligibility guards, experiment assignments, rollout conditions, or onboarding-engine behavior are changed. Both the trigger and per-step conditions now observe the same active-view state.

## Validation

Validated on refreshed `origin/main` at `671bc162f3558e2a7e333e92db4bcd2d1eac76e4`; the latest upstream changes did not already address this regression.

- `npm run transpile-client` - passed.
- Focused Electron unit tests below - **350 passing, 2 pre-existing pending tests**.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - passed on the refreshed base.
- `npm run eslint -- <all 21 changed TypeScript files>` - passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - passed.
- `npm run precommit` - hygiene passed for all 21 staged file versions.

pull_requests.title: github-authentication: skip education.github.com check for EMU accounts
pull_requests.body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327377

Reopens #327379, which GitHub auto-closed when its head fork was deleted — the head repository no longer resolves, so that PR can't be reopened. Same commit, rebased onto current `main`.

Enterprise Managed User (EMU) accounts can't access `https://education.github.com/api/user`, so `checkUserDetails` always fails that fetch for them and falls through to `edu = 'unknown'` after a wasted network round trip and a log line on every sign-in.

The EMU signal was already computed in this method — `session.account.label.includes('_')`, used for the `isManaged` telemetry property. This hoists it above the fetch and skips the request entirely for managed accounts, setting `edu = 'none'`, then reuses the same value for telemetry instead of recomputing it.

Telemetry schema is unchanged: `isEdu` and `isManaged` are still reported with the same values for non-managed accounts.

### How to test

- Sign in with a regular github.com account — EDU status still resolves as before (`student` / `faculty` / `none`, or `unknown` when the endpoint errors).
- Sign in with an EMU account (login shaped `<idp-username>_<shortcode>`) — no request to education.github.com, log shows `Skipping optional EDU details check for a managed account.`, telemetry reports `isEdu: none`, `isManaged: true`.

auto_merge.commit_title: github-authentication: skip education.github.com check for EMU accounts (#336608)
auto_merge.commit_message:
Managed (EMU) accounts can't access the education.github.com endpoint, so
evaluate the EMU heuristic up front and skip the fetch entirely for them,
setting edu to 'none'. Telemetry schema is unchanged.

copilot: fix slow content exclusion filtering of large search results
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #335194

## What was wrong

Copilot checks every file that a search returns against the content exclusion rules. Since #332368, that check put every result into a `Limiter`. The `Limiter` takes work off its queue with `Array#shift`, which gets slower as the queue gets longer. With a queue of a few hundred thousand files, the whole thing became quadratic. On a big workspace this kept the shared extension host busy for minutes, and other extensions stopped responding.

On top of that, `findFilesWithDefaultExcludes` ran the check twice on the same results, because its override filtered again after the base class had already gone through the filtering `findFiles` override.

## What this change does

- `filterIngoredResources` now uses a fixed pool of 20 workers. Each worker takes the next file when it is free. Nothing is queued up front, so the work is linear. The concurrency bound, the order of results and the set of files that get checked are all the same as before.
- The redundant `findFilesWithDefaultExcludes` override in `SearchServiceImpl` is removed. The base class already routes through the filtering `findFiles`, so every result is still checked, just once.

The reporter's benchmark (100,000 files with an instant check) went from about 14 seconds to about 15 milliseconds. Locally, 200,000 files went from 12.5 seconds to about 40 milliseconds.

## Tests

- New `ignoreService.spec.ts`: results stay in order even when checks finish out of order, at most 20 checks run at once, and 200,000 files are filtered in linear time.
- `searchServiceImpl.spec.ts`: `findFilesWithDefaultExcludes` checks each result exactly once and still passes the exclusion glob to the search, and the `maxResults: 1` path still withholds an excluded file.

Against the old code, the linear-time test takes over 12 seconds and the "checks each result once" test fails.

BYOK models can report only `maxContextWindow`, but the workbench model adapter ignored that field and exposed zero input/output limits. The context usage widget consequently had no usable window and stayed hidden, even when token usage was available.

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Chat tab labels in the agents window sat 2px left of the tab pill's center because the tabs inherited the shared modern tab padding, which is asymmetric (8px right, 6px left).

- exposes the shared tab left padding as the `--modern-ui-tab-padding-left` custom property, mirroring the existing `--modern-ui-tab-action-padding` hook, so consumers can restore symmetric padding without another `!important`
- sets `--modern-ui-tab-padding-left` to `--vscode-spacing-size80` for the agents window chat tab strip (`chatCompositeBar.css`), matching the padding the shared styles use for icon-less editor tabs; regular editor tabs are unchanged (they fall back to `--vscode-spacing-size60`)
- adds a regression test that asserts the computed horizontal padding of chat tabs is symmetric; it fails without the fix

pull_requests.title: Draft: Search Editor: Allow choosing whether context lines appear before or after matches
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Related to #336570

> This PR is currently a draft to validate the proposed UX and implementation approach.

## Summary

This PR allows Search Editor context lines to be displayed:

- Around a match
- Before a match
- After a match

The existing context line count is reused for all three modes. **Around** remains the default and preserves the current behavior.

## Changes

- Adds a compact context-placement menu to the Search Editor
- Adds **Around**, **Before**, and **After** options
- Keeps the existing context toggle and context line count behavior
- Persists the selected placement in saved Search Editors
- Preserves **Around** as the default for existing saved Search Editors
- Supports `contextLinesMode` in Search Editor command arguments

## Implementation notes

The search service currently supports only `surroundingContext`, so this PR does not modify the search query or search-provider contracts.

The Search Editor continues to request surrounding context from the search service and filters the displayed context while serializing Search Editor results.

This may retrieve context from both sides when only one side is displayed, but it keeps the change scoped to the Search Editor and avoids affecting the Search view, search providers, remote search, and notebook search contracts.

## How to test

1. Open a new Search Editor.
2. Enter a query that produces matches with surrounding context.
3. Set the context line count to a value greater than zero.
4. Open the context-placement menu next to the context toggle.
5. Select **Around** and verify that context appears on both sides.
6. Select **Before** and verify that only preceding context appears.
7. Select **After** and verify that only following context appears.
8. Save and reopen the Search Editor and verify that the selected mode is restored.
9. Open an existing Search Editor without a `ContextLinesMode` header and verify that it uses **Around**.

pull_requests.title: sessions: fix: scope send message limit per turn
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Retain the 50-message `send_message` runaway guard while scoping its allowance to the originating chat and current source turn.
- Track only the latest observed turn/count for each source chat, so historical turns do not accumulate entries.
- Reserve capacity before awaiting a send and refund failures against the captured turn record. Parallel calls cannot overbook, and delayed completions cannot overwrite a newer turn budget.

## Problem

The server-tool group is long-lived. Its previous process-lifetime counter combined successful sends from unrelated chats and earlier turns. Legitimate cross-session coordination could therefore exhaust the shared budget and cause a later terminal report to be rejected even though that reporting turn was not running away.

One originating turn is the appropriate boundary for this fan-out guard: later turns and other chats are independent work. This is not a global orchestration budget and does not claim to stop every cross-turn feedback cycle.

## Behavior

- One source turn may successfully send or queue 50 messages; its next call is rejected.
- In-flight sends reserve slots synchronously, so the same limit holds for concurrent tool calls.
- A later turn in the same source chat receives a fresh allowance.
- Another source chat has an independent allowance.
- Failed sends refund their reservations without changing a newer turn record.
- Existing immediate-start behavior, FIFO queue behavior, target resolution, self-loop prevention, and delegation metadata are unchanged. No dispatch serialization is introduced.
- Session/chat creation limits remain process-wide.
- No report-specific handling, FIFO steering, or Agent Host Protocol changes are introduced.

## Validation

- Added deterministic regressions for 51 concurrent sends, a failed parallel send releasing its slot, and delayed success/failure from an older source turn. The original implementation failed three of these cases.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionServerTools.test.ts --grep send_message` (11 passing)
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/sessionServerTools.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionServerTools.test.ts` (passed)

pull_requests.title: Make deepFreeze worklist traversal linear (O(n²) → O(n))
pull_requests.body:
### What

`deepFreeze` walks an object graph with a worklist, draining it via `Array.shift()`.

```diff
 	const stack: any[] = [obj];
-	while (stack.length > 0) {
-		const obj = stack.shift();
+	for (let index = 0; index < stack.length; index++) {
+		const obj = stack[index];
+		stack[index] = undefined;
 		Object.freeze(obj);
```

### Why

`shift()` re-indexes the whole array on every call, so once the queue is large the bookkeeping dominates and freezing a wide graph degrades to **O(n²)**. An index cursor makes it **O(n)**. `stack[index] = undefined` releases the processed reference so those objects can still be collected.

`pop()` would be linear too, but `deepFreeze` reads properties with `for...in`, which invokes enumerable getters — so traversal order is externally observable, and `pop()` would silently reverse sibling order. The cursor preserves it exactly.

### Performance

Node 24, wide graph of n sibling objects. Speedup spans two independent benchmark runs on different harnesses; `before` is the slower run.

| n | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10,000 | 1.4 ms | 0.6 – 1.1 ms | 1.3× – 1.6× |
| 30,000 | 74 ms | 3.3 – 5.4 ms | 14× – 19× |
| 50,000 | 202 ms | 5.6 – 10 ms | 20× – 31× |
| 100,000 | 1.4 s | 10 – 11.2 ms | **64× – 137×** |

Both runs used a same-vs-same control arm to establish the measurement floor. Graphs below ~1,000 objects are within noise — this is not a small-input optimization, and I'm making no claim about startup or user-visible latency.

Tradeoff: the worklist array is no longer shrunk as it drains, so peak transient memory is ~1 MiB per 100,000 enqueues, released when the call returns.

Verified with 30,000 randomized differential cases (cycles, shared references, typed arrays, symbols, throwing getters, graph mutation mid-traversal) checking return identity, frozen set, getter invocation order and exception signature: 0 mismatches.

pull_requests.title: fix: allow workbench origin for remote resources
pull_requests.body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336527

Electron 43 migrated `vscode-remote-resource` from the deprecated `registerHttpProtocol()` API to `protocol.handle()` backed by `net.fetch()`. The new handler preserves the request method, headers, and body. This is intentional, it keeps HTTP behavior intact and allows Electron to relay untouched `net.fetch()` responses without copying the response body through JavaScript.

Unlike the old protocol API, `net.fetch()` applies normal CORS validation. The renderer correctly sends:

```text
Origin: vscode-file://vscode-app
Sec-Fetch-Mode: cors
```

The remote server did not authorize that origin in its response, so Chromium rejected the resource.

## NetLog evidence

The net log capture shows that the remote file was found and returned successfully:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: image/svg+xml
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000
Vary: Origin
```

The response was missing:

```text
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: vscode-file://vscode-app
```

Chromium then ended the request with `CORS_REQUEST` followed by `CANCELLED`, which surfaced as `net::ERR_FAILED`.

## Why WSL and Dev Containers failed

WSL and Dev Containers use a direct host-and-port connection:

```text
vscode-remote-resource
→ protocol.handle()
→ net.fetch()
→ forwarded loopback HTTP endpoint
```

SSH uses `vscode-managed-remote-resource`, which reads through main process IPC and the remote file service. It does not use the affected HTTP fetch path.

## Why this is different from previous regressions

Earlier fixes covered `vscode-managed-remote-resource`:

- #319834 registered the managed scheme as CORS capable.
- #335241 fixed managed workbench request identification and response handling.

Those fixes remain valid and explain why SSH continues to work. The direct `vscode-remote-resource` path did not have equivalent end-to-end coverage. The remote resource endpoint now authorizes the exact native workbench origin

```text
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: vscode-file://vscode-app
Vary: Origin
```

Existing configured web endpoint origins remain supported. The fix does not use a wildcard and does not authorize `vscode-webview://` origins. Webviews use the HTTPS virtual resource pipeline and should not get direct access to token protected remote files.

## Test coverage

The new tests cover both sides of the failure:

1. A server test verifies that native workbench and configured web origins are allowed, while webview and arbitrary origins are rejected.
2. An Electron integration test loads a real SVG from `vscode-file://vscode-app` through `vscode-remote-resource` and verifies that the server receives the expected CORS headers.

pull_requests.title: Fix `code-import-patterns` not checking dynamic imports
pull_requests.body:
### The bug

`createImportRuleListener` in `.eslint-plugin-local/utils.ts` selects dynamic imports with:

```js
['CallExpression[callee.type="Import"][arguments.length=1] > Literal']
```

typescript-eslint emits an **`ImportExpression`** node for `import('module')`. The installed `@typescript-eslint/types` (8.66.0) contains no `"Import"` node type at all, so that selector matches nothing and dynamic imports are never checked.

Every rule built on this listener is affected — `code-import-patterns` and `code-layering` among them. A layering violation written as a static import is reported; the identical violation written as `import('...')` is not.

### Reproduction

Using `ESLint.lintText` on a file whose layer forbids the target:

| form | reported |
| --- | --- |
| `import { x } from '<forbidden>'` | `local/code-import-patterns` |
| `export { x } from '<forbidden>'` | `local/code-import-patterns` |
| `import('<forbidden>')` | *(nothing)* |

With this change, all three report.

### The fix

Adds an `ImportExpression > Literal` selector and **keeps** the existing `CallExpression[callee.type="Import"]` one, so the listener keeps working if the plugin is ever run against an older parser. One file, additive.

I noticed this while reading the layering rules and was surprised a dynamic import wasn't flagged; happy to adjust the approach if you'd prefer the old selector dropped outright.

pull_requests.title: fix: guard Explorer focus until tree is initialized
pull_requests.body:
Summary
This PR fixes a focus-related issue in the Explorer view. When focus is requested before the Explorer tree has been fully initialized, the code can call into the tree while it has no input set. That can result in invalid focus state or unexpected reveal behavior during early lifecycle and command-triggered transitions.

Problem
The Explorer view exposes a focus() method that immediately calls this.tree.domFocus(). However, there are scenarios where this method can be invoked before the tree is fully created or before it has received an input. In those cases, the tree is not ready to handle focus operations, and the code path can behave incorrectly.

Fix
This change adds a guard in ExplorerView.focus() to ensure:

the tree exists
the tree has an input before attempting to focus it
If the tree is not ready yet, the method falls back to the default super.focus() behavior instead of calling into an uninitialized tree.

The existing auto-reveal flow remains unchanged once the tree is initialized and ready to operate.

Files Changed
src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/views/explorerView.ts
Why This Matters
This avoids edge-case failures in the Explorer when focus is requested during view activation, restoration, or command-driven navigation. It keeps the Explorer behavior stable without changing the normal user-facing flow once the view is initialized.

Validation
Reviewed the focus implementation in the Explorer
Confirmed the guard prevents focus access before tree initialization
Confirmed normal focus and auto-reveal behavior still runs once the tree is ready

pull_requests.body:
Codex's `request_user_input_async` emits an `agentMessage` with `delivery: "async"` and structured questions. The current adapter treats that item as ordinary Markdown, leaving the question and suggested answers as text with no answer controls. This reproduces with the original VS Code 1.137.0 bundle and is independent of the feedback-review patch.

Route these items to the existing question carousel, including free-text answers. Codex continues working while the controls are open. If its native turn completes first, retain the host turn until the user answers or skips. Explicit answers use native `turn/start`, which steers active work or starts a continuation using the thread's existing settings. Ordinary messages and synchronous input requests keep their existing paths.

Interactive controls are restricted to owned sessions with an answer route; isolated subagent messages retain their existing text path. The acknowledged continuation ID is recorded before answer delivery resolves, with live-session and host/native ownership checks, so Stop targets it before its notification arrives.

The controller deduplicates items, reopens questions on delivery failure, cancels stale controls on replacement/disposal, and handles Stop during an in-flight answer. It also handles an answer RPC response arriving before the native turn-start notification. No suggested answer is automatically submitted. Late answer acknowledgements are ignored after cancellation or question replacement.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: prevent silent reconnects from hanging session requests
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

The protocol client disables its liveness watchdog throughout `Reconnecting`, including after the replacement transport is established. If a recovery RPC (`reconnect`, fresh `initialize`, or subscription restoration) stops receiving traffic without a transport-close event, recovery never completes. New session subscriptions stay behind the reconnect gate, and chat requests can wait indefinitely for their first snapshot.

This was found while investigating a remote tunnel session that remained unhydrated until cancellation. The supplied client logs also showed host replacement and session restore rejections, but did not contain enough server-side diagnostics to identify the exact stalled recovery RPC or explain the missing session registration. This PR fixes the independently reproduced client-side liveness gap, not the registration issue.

## Changes

- Start the existing liveness watchdog after a reconnect transport is established, not during transport establishment or retry backoff.
- Let watchdog pings bypass the reconnect gate.
- Stop the attempt's timers when recovery fails or the transport closes, allowing the existing retry path to continue.
- Preserve the existing 25-second silence window and load/reverse-request deferrals.

The underlying gap predates tunnel soft reconnect; #333655 exposed it to tunnel connections, and #334003 added subscription restoration within the same recovery phase.

## Validation

- Reproduced silent reconnect/initialize failures before the fix.
- Full `AgentHostProtocolClient` suite: **137 passing**.
- Four regression tests cover silent reconnect, initialization, subscription restoration, and slow-but-responsive recovery, including the liveness window and subsequent session hydration.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Targeted hygiene/ESLint and `git diff --check` passed.

(Written by Copilot)

pull_requests.title: fix: drop obsolete arm64/aarch64 GLIBC 2.27 deps after Copilot runtime bump (build fix for vscode-engineering#3887)
pull_requests.body:
## Build failure

The scheduled insider build of `main` failed the Linux ARM64 packaging stage:

```
'vscode-linux-arm64-prepare-deb' errored
Error: The dependencies list has changed.
  Old: ... libc6 (>= 2.27) ...
  New: ... libc6 (>= 2.25) ...
    at getDependencies (build/linux/dependencies-generator.ts:93:10)
```

`build/linux/dependencies-generator.ts` regenerates the shared-library dependency set from the packaged binaries and fails the build when it no longer matches the checked-in reference in `build/linux/debian/dep-lists.ts` (and the RPM equivalent).

## Root cause

The Copilot runtime package bump to `@github/copilot` `1.0.86-0` changed the generated Linux shared-library dependency set, dropping the previously required `libc6 (>= 2.27)` / `libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.27)` entry. The reference dep-lists were updated to match — but only for the `amd64` (deb) and `x86_64` (rpm) architectures. The symmetric `arm64` (deb) and `aarch64` (rpm) entries were left in place, so the generated set for ARM64 no longer matches the checked-in reference and the packaging guard fails.

These `GLIBC_2.27` reference entries had originally been added to **both** the amd64/x86_64 and arm64/aarch64 sections; the runtime bump only removed the amd64/x86_64 side, leaving the arm64/aarch64 side stale.

The source-issue narrative attributed the break to a different head commit and to a missing `darwin-arm64` `runtime.node` prebuilt. Inspection of the current source does not support that: the referenced session commit only adds a configuration setting and does not touch the Copilot version or native packaging, and the `1.0.86-0` bump lives in the root `package.json` (Agent Host), not the built-in extension. The reproducible, repository-local defect on `main` is the asymmetric dep-list update described above.

## How the fix works

Remove the obsolete `libc6 (>= 2.27)` entry from the `arm64` Debian reference and the `libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.27)(64bit)` entry from the `aarch64` RPM reference, mirroring the change already applied to `amd64`/`x86_64`. The `arm64`/`aarch64` references now match the dependency set generated after the Copilot runtime bump, so `getDependencies` no longer throws and the ARM64 deb/rpm prepare tasks succeed. The resulting reference blocks are identical to the pre-bump baseline, preserving the packaging guard's protective behavior for every other dependency.

## Rollback evaluation

- Recommendation: **Do not roll back**
- Public culprit commit/PR: `6e9cf0e4adeb6d7a04d2a2dc0d64ebc5365cd175` (microsoft/vscode#336360, "agentHost: bump Copilot SDK to 1.0.14"), which removed the `GLIBC_2.27` reference for `amd64`/`x86_64` only.
- Rationale: The fix-forward is a two-line, data-only correction that simply completes the change the culprit commit already made for the other architectures. Reverting #336360 would also revert the intended Copilot runtime SDK bump and unrelated Agent Host work, which is far more disruptive than this bounded reference update.
- Owners to consult: `@roblourens`

## Validation

Change is limited to the checked-in reference dependency data in `build/linux/debian/dep-lists.ts` and `build/linux/rpm/dep-lists.ts`. The updated `arm64`/`aarch64` reference blocks are byte-identical to the pre-#336227 baseline for those entries, confirming they match the dependency set generated after the runtime bump. Full deb/rpm packaging validation runs only in the Linux ARM64 build stage, which is not reproducible in this environment; no automated unit test exists for these reference lists (the packaging guard itself validates them at build time).

## Risk

Very low. The change only removes two stale reference entries for ARM64 packaging and does not alter build logic, other architectures, or runtime behavior. If the generated set still diverged, the guard would continue to fail loudly rather than ship an incorrect package.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@roblourens`

pull_requests.title: agentHost: add remote Agent Host federation
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Adds Remote Agent Host federation so an Agent Host can connect to admitted downstream Agent Hosts and expose their providers as ordinary, non-default `IAgent` implementations.

- extracts a browser-independent AHP client core and transport-neutral remote-target boundary
- adds default-off runtime/managed controls, host-feature authentication, and authenticated tunnel discovery
- projects remote provider/model catalogs without recursively re-exporting proxies
- supports workspace-less remote chat creation, streaming, history, cancellation, backing restoration, and reconnect recovery
- adds brokered `create_remote_session` delegation for the A -> B -> C flow with durable deduplication, depth/breadth limits, and cleanup recovery
- relays parameter confirmations, result confirmations, and user input with chat/turn-scoped ownership and outage-safe delivery

## Why

This enables Host A to broker work requested by Host B onto Host C while keeping the resulting session in A's normal session catalog. B never receives C's credentials or address, and C remains responsible for its own execution environment.

Refs #336199

## Security and scope

- outbound federation and tunnel discovery are separately controlled and disabled by default
- endpoint credentials, provider credentials, and delegation authorization remain separately scoped
- remote providers are not selected as defaults
- remote proxies are not automatically re-exported
- arbitrary upstream tools, customizations, credentials, and local paths are not forwarded
- the initial chat capability is intentionally workspace-less; broader workspace authority remains follow-up work

## Validation

- RemoteAgent: 29 passing
- RemoteSessionDelegation: 35 passing
- AgentSideEffects: 206 passing
- packaged be1514c851 validation: A -> B passed; live confirmation projection defect reproduced and fixed with live/snapshot regressions
- full affected TypeScript matrix during implementation: 1,898 passing, 16 pending
- Rust CLI suite during implementation: 179 passing
- TypeScript typecheck passed
- targeted ESLint passed
- layer validation passed
- diff whitespace checks passed
- repeated code-style and code-review loops completed; final focused passes were clean

## Reviewer notes

The implementation is split into roadmap-sized commits covering the client core, controls, target boundary, provider federation, authentication, tunnel discovery, delegation, and interaction relay.

For standalone custom-build testing, set `VSCODE_CLI_INITIAL_AH_VERSION` to the build commit before running `code-insiders agent host`; otherwise the packaged CLI may download the latest stock Agent Host server.

pull_requests.title: sessions: show pending automatic host connections on web
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Keep web `/agents` hosts visibly **Connecting** while automatic connection setup is still in progress, even after discovery finishes and before a protocol connection entry exists.

Previously, discovery could finish and the indicator turn idle while transport setup continued. The passive indicator and modal host summary now reflect actual pending setup, and captured diagnostics include the attempt's start time, elapsed time, automatic/manual trigger, and whether a protocol connection entry exists.

On phones, Connection Information is also accessible beside the **Hosts** sheet title. Opening it dismisses the picker first; closing the report restores the originating control, or its workbench toolbar if the control was replaced while the host connected.

## Implementation and boundaries

- Expose actual in-flight attempts through a read-only catalog and dedicated invalidation event, rather than inferring activity from discovery or historical log events.
- Preserve established, reconnecting, and incompatible states. Completed attempts clear by identity; removed, disabled, and disposed hosts are excluded from the catalog.
- Preserve connection scheduling, retry policy, and native UI status behavior. The connection indicator remains passive.
- Rebased onto main including #336443. Pending state now coexists with its asynchronous snapshot capture, connection-stage history, and Window-log excerpt. Tests verify that a historical start event does not keep a completed attempt marked pending.
- Tighten notification regression tests, use one numeric snapshot timestamp for elapsed calculations, and document the pending-state contract.

## Product validation

Used standalone Chromium against the local `/agents` build with deliberately delayed mock transport setup. Desktop and phone-emulated runs verified pending status in the indicator and modal, combined pending/stage/log evidence, Copy/Download equivalence allowing Windows clipboard line endings, and transition to Connected. The phone Hosts-sheet information entry was activated using actual Playwright touch taps.

This uncovered a focus loss when the mobile toolbar replaced the original host control while diagnostics was open. The toolbar fallback now passes both the targeted regression test and the completed desktop/phone-emulated end-to-end rerun, including replacement of the original mobile control. Device emulation is not physical-phone/PWA or real-tunnel validation.

Additional manual-connection validation caught a staging race: clearing suppression before staging could start an automatic dial first. Suppression now clears as part of staging, and the pending catalog reads the factory’s effective initiation mode. Held both automatic and manual attempts pending in Chromium and verified their respective triggers in downloaded diagnostics, equivalent copied evidence, eventual Connected state, and phone touch/focus recovery.

pull_requests.title: chat: Add experiment-backed MCP authentication hints setting
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Recurring proactive MCP authentication reminders can interrupt otherwise unrelated conversations. Add a way to suppress only these reminders so we can evaluate their effect on retention without disabling MCP or bypassing authentication.

- Add application-scoped `chat.mcp.authenticationHints.enabled`, defaulting to `true`, with `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`. The shared registration covers editor chat and the Agents Window.
- Gate new proactive reminders and update existing reminders when the setting changes. Suppression does not mark a server as authenticated or a reminder as actioned.
- Preserve silent authentication, manual sign-in, authentication prompts blocking actual tool calls, and progress for user-initiated authentication already in flight.
- Record `chat.mcp.authenticationHintEligible` once per open conversation in both variants. Its only event-specific property is the effective `hintsEnabled` boolean; it records no server names, URLs, credentials, or conversation content.

## Experiment / rollout

Treatment variable: `config.chat.mcp.authenticationHints.enabled`

- Control: `true` (existing behavior)
- Treatment: `false` (suppress proactive reminders)

Explicit user settings take precedence over experiment defaults. The eligibility event supports identifying the affected population in either arm instead of selecting only users who saw a reminder. Review the new telemetry event before rollout, and target only builds containing this change. This PR does not create or enable a remote experiment and does not change the default experience.

## Validation

Rebased onto current `main` (`de1a430a2f3`).

- `npm run gulp compile-client` — passed, including client type-checking.
- Hygiene and lint on all six changed files — passed.
- 16 focused Electron unit tests — passed, covering default/enabled/disabled behavior, eligibility deduplication, live configuration changes, preserved silent and tool-call authentication, and existing reminder rendering.

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatMcpAuthenticationContentPart.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts \
  --grep 'mcp auth prompt|ChatMcpAuthenticationContentPart|authentication-required invocation'
```

## Try locally

Set `"chat.mcp.authenticationHints.enabled": false` to suppress reminders. Toggle it while a reminder is visible to verify that hiding it does not authenticate the server, and that authentication required by an actual tool call is still actionable.

To exercise experiment assignment instead, leave the setting unset and use:

```json
"experiments.override": {
  "config.chat.mcp.authenticationHints.enabled": false
}
```

pull_requests.title: agentHost: recognise a crash-orphaned provisional session
pull_requests.body:
Fixes a session that can never be opened after a crash, reported by @roblourens after his OS crashed:

> `Provider copilotcli could not describe copilotcli:/229963e7-9163-452a-a2a6-34913a560315 yet`

## What actually happened

A new chat reserves a backend session before the user sends anything. That reservation is **durably registered**, and — this is the part worth being precise about — its provider data, including the SDK backing id, is persisted too. The identity survived the crash intact.

What it recorded was a pointer to **an SDK session that was never created**: `_reserveChatBacking` only mints a UUID, and the real SDK session first exists at `_materialize`. So the host durably recorded a promise that was never fulfilled.

That matters because the widely-repeated explanation — "creation state is in-memory only until materialization" — is wrong, and it points at the wrong fix. No recovery path can exist for these rows, which is why `yet` was categorically wrong rather than merely imprecise, and why suppressing them is correct rather than a workaround.

The row stayed visible because the guard that hides idle provisional sessions, `isIdleProvisionalSession`, is in-memory: after a restart there is no tracked state, so it returns `false` and stops hiding the registration (#321269).

## The fix

Record the provisional fact **durably**, as a host-owned `sessionProvisional:` metadata key, and clear it at materialization. Listing then drops a session only when **both** hold:

1. it is still marked provisional, and
2. its provider cannot describe it.

Both clauses are required, and the second is what protects real user content: clearing the marker is best-effort, so a materialized session whose clear never landed keeps a stale marker — and stays visible, because its provider vouches for it. An unregistered or erroring provider is likewise never treated as evidence of absence.

### Rejected: deferring durable registration until materialization

The obvious fix — don't register until the session materializes — was tested and **discarded**. Probed by execution, a materialized session whose registry row is missing does not recover after a restart, even when the provider relists it under the correct URI:

```
materialize → drop registry row → restart
sameId:      recoveredAfterRestart: FALSE
divergedId:  recoveredAfterRestart: FALSE
```

The registry is the sole durable index. Deferring its write trades a cosmetic empty row for **permanent silent loss of a session with real user content**, in exactly the crash window this bug occupies.

## Scope: prevention only

Existing orphaned rows are not cleaned up; they stay until deleted. **Deleting one works today** — `_doDisposeSession` needs no provider metadata, and the SDK call is skipped when there is no live backing — so anyone hitting this has a working recovery path now and need not wait for this change. Nothing already on disk can carry the marker, so a retroactive sweep would need a different, evidence-based discriminator; that deserves its own design rather than being smuggled in here.

## Second commit: the error message

`yet` told the user to wait for something that could never happen. Now: *"Provider X is not ready to open Y; it may still be starting, so try again shortly"*.

Wording only. The `catalogReadable && !knownToRegistry` classification is deliberately untouched — turning borderline cases into sticky `AHP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` is the regression #331721 exists to prevent.

## Implementation note

The suppression check cannot `await` inside `_computeSessions`. Doing so shifts when `_retryInitialProviderMigrationsInBackground` fires and produces a second provider-absent exclusion pass, breaking `provider-absent stale exclusion withholds migration completion`. That is why the marker is mirrored in memory and read synchronously, with the call site skipping the await entirely when nothing is provisional. It looks like gratuitous complexity otherwise, and simplifying it reintroduces the regression.

## Independent verification

The fix was verified by a second implementation built against the same behaviour, not a re-reading of this code. Both orphan shapes were run with the session catalog on and off:

| shape | catalog | marker | visible | restore |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vouches-while-live | on | true | **false** | `Session was never created on the backend` |
| vouches-while-live | off | true | **false** | same |
| never-vouches | on | true | **false** | same |
| never-vouches | off | true | **false** | same |

**Suppression holds with the catalog disabled**, though not via this filter. With the catalog off every row resolves through `_legacyRegisteredSessionMetadata`, which returns `undefined` for a session its provider cannot describe, so the row is dropped before the provisional filter runs — the same behaviour these sessions had before this PR. The filter itself now fails open in that mode, because the readability signal it consults is only populated by the catalog import.

The point that matters for reading this PR is unchanged: the fix lives at the registration layer, not in the catalog, so it is not a narrowing of what the catalog will show.

The *vouches-while-live* shape is the valuable half: a catalog row written from real provider metadata that later outlives the provider's memory. That is the reported shape, and it was the route least covered by the tests in this PR.

The inverse-orphan case — a materialized session with real content — was probed under four interleavings (clean, stale marker, stale marker with a throwing provider, stale marker with no provider). All keep the session visible. No interleaving was found that hides real content.

### If you write your own probe: vouch via `getChatMetadata`

Suppression consults `getChatMetadata`. A double that vouches only through `getSessionMetadata`/`listSessions` is not vouching on the path under test, and will appear to show real content being wrongly hidden. That false positive occurred during verification before being traced to the mock.

Nothing here required instrumenting inside `_computeSessions`: the behaviour is observable from `listSessions()` plus `listProvisionalSessions()`.

## A rejected robustness change, recorded so it is not re-added

The marker mirror loads asynchronously while listing reads it synchronously, so a listing during that window fails open. Two mitigations were considered; **only one was shipped**.

`whenDeferredWorkSettled()` now joins the marker load, so a settled listing cannot miss suppression. This was the load-bearing half — the observed "still visible when settled" behaviour was a settle-semantics gap, not a caching one.

Re-verified against a 250 ms delayed marker read: `visibleWhenSettled` flipped `true → false`, while `visibleOnFirstListingWithSlowRead` stayed `true` (fail-open, by design) and `visibleAfterLoadCompletes` was already `false` beforehand. The change moved exactly the one cell it was meant to move.

An epoch bump on load completion was **implemented and then dropped as a no-op**:

1. A settled entry is evicted from `_inFlightListSessions` on `clear()`, so the next listing recomputes regardless.
2. Suppression runs after the provider phase, so a computation still in flight when the markers land consults the mirror anyway.
3. A changed epoch only forces recomputation when `_sameSessionRegistrations` also reports a change. Markers are not registrations, so that branch never fires for this case.

No test could be written that fails without it. Shipping it would have added a dead line plus an unfalsifiable test, both of which would read as covering the race. The loader carries a comment explaining this so it is not re-added.

## Review round

Two defects found in review, both fixed in `a9e97aabf9a`.

**Suppression could hide real user content.** The check treated any metadata miss as proof the backing was never created. But a provider whose catalog is not yet readable returns `undefined` *without throwing*, and the `catch` only covered providers that throw. Combined with a materialized session whose best-effort marker-clear never landed, listing would hide a real session and restore would report it as never created — worse than the bug being fixed.

Both sites now require the provider's catalog to be readable this run before classifying a miss as authoritative. The listing path reads that signal synchronously, so no `await` enters `_computeSessions`; with no signal the session stays visible. Under-suppressing costs a junk row, over-suppressing costs a user's work.

This gate is not a no-op. In the reported logs the owning provider became readable four seconds after start:

```
09:43:03.246  sessions_v2 import for provider copilotcli: … marker set in 375ms
09:43:03.156  [Claude] SDK not downloaded yet; deferring the migratable chat list
```

The same log shows both sides working: `copilotcli` readable and eligible for suppression, `claude` deferred and therefore protected — the #331648 shape.

**The marker was written in a second transaction.** A crash between registering the session and marking it provisional — the exact failure this PR addresses — left an unmarked orphan. The marker is now written inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`COMMIT` as the registration.

Added test: `keeps a materialized session whose provider catalog is not readable yet`. It fails with either gate removed.

## Validation

The new test reproduces the reported symptom exactly when the fix is neutralised:

```
listed: ['copilot:/crashed-provisional']   restoreCode: -32603   saysYet: true
```

With the fix: `listed: []`, `restoreCode: -32001`, `saysYet: false`. Falsifiability was verified twice — on the initial shape and again after the design changed.

Three regression guards alongside it: a merely-unavailable provider stays listed; a provisional session the provider *can* describe stays listed (the failed-promotion case); deletion clears the marker.

5,389 passing across the agentHost node suites, typecheck and lint clean.

pull_requests.title: editor: integrate optional editor-view GPU renderer
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Integrate the experimental `@vscode/editor-view` Rust/WASM renderer as an optional desktop distro dependency, alongside the existing DOM and TypeScript GPU renderers.

- Add the editorView rendering mode with incremental text/token/model synchronization and measured layout/hit testing.
- Move supported text, selections, carets, current-line highlights, whitespace, indentation guides, line numbers, folding-control paint, and decorations to the GPU; retain DOM input and unsupported surfaces.
- Detect the application-owned package at desktop startup, including ASAR builds. Hide the editorView choice when absent and validate saved editorView settings to off.
- Restore DOM rendering and report the error if package import or initialization fails, without rewriting user settings.
- Keep OSS/Monaco builds independent of the npm package through a host-owned type contract.
- Mirror the full document without the prototype's 20,000-view-line cap. Text, decorations, guides and coordinate queries share the full range; ordinary edits remain incremental even in large or soft-wrapped documents.

## Distro follow-up

The distro must add `@vscode/editor-view: 0.0.1` to its npm manifest and lockfile. No source dependency or product.json opt-in flag is needed. Web/server builds are not enabled by this change.

Setup and behavior are documented in src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/editorViewGpu/README.md. The editor-view package itself is not changed by this PR.

## Validation

- Monaco compile check, generated declaration check and staged-file hygiene pass.
- Monaco editor-distro, ESM loading, webpack bundling and Chromium integration tests passed after the CI repairs. Local Firefox startup timed out before running tests; no Firefox pass is claimed.
- 63 related Electron unit tests pass, including uncapped model synchronization, decorations and configuration; the six package-detection tests also passed.
- Full client type-check passes; optional-package validation also passed with the npm package physically absent.
- Electron smoke checks verified installed WebGPU rendering, absent-package DOM rendering with no package requests, and missing-WASM error reporting with DOM recovery.
- Detection verified against a real Electron ASAR archive.
- DOM/GPU comparisons for tabs, Unicode and selection passed; largest measured pixel difference was 0.057%.
- New package-side comparison regressions reproduced truncation before the cap fix (8.461% for a 30K-line document, 4.349% for the wrapped fixture), then passed after it (0.038% / 0.000%).
- Local behavioral comparisons verify visible tails, edits/inserts/deletes/undo/redo, EOL measurements and pointer hit testing in 30,000- and 100,010-line documents, growth/shrinkage across 19,999 and 20,001 lines, and 12,000 model lines wrapping to 60,000 view lines. pull_requests.title: build: restore a shared NLS catalog across targets
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #299425.

## Why

The old build assigned core NLS IDs before target bundling. The esbuild migration instead assigns IDs from each target's dependency graph, while browser localization still selects a CDN catalog by commit/version/locale, without a target identity.

This is a verified cross-target mismatch, not merely a suspected write race: the official 1.110.0 server-web bundle expects 16,545 entries, but its same-commit localized CDN supplies standalone web's 16,421-entry table. Fresh-browser reproduction matches the original `NLS MISSING: 16444` exception and stack. Materializing the same language pack with server-web's ordered keys restores localized startup.

## Changes

- Extract a deterministic, source-wide core catalog before target bundling, independently of entry points. Exclude declarations and test sources, preserve translator comments and separate `localize`/`localize2` slots, and reject conflicting default messages.
- Prepare one manifest before parallel `core-ci` bundles. Targets consume its index map and write only their own catalogs, rather than overwriting shared metadata.
- Prepare the same source-wide catalog for standalone-web packaging and CDN metadata upload. Direct/local bundles without a supplied manifest extract that catalog in memory without publishing to `out-build`.
- Fail on missing, malformed, non-canonical, or source-stale manifests, changed entries, and unresolved placeholders. Publish the manifest only after metadata writes succeed.
- Preserve ASCII serialization, source maps, and the native/remote cache identity protections from #336109. Update related build documentation.

## Validation

- 34 focused NLS tests pass, covering cross-target semantic lookups, repeated keys/comments, translation export, source drift, LF/CRLF portability, failed publication, source maps, ASCII serialization, and cache identities.
- `npm run typecheck --prefix build -- --pretty false` passes.
- Staged repository hygiene (`npm run precommit`), explicit changed-file ESLint with `--max-warnings 0`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Real `bundle --minify --nls` runs succeed for server, server-web, and standalone web. All four catalog files are byte-identical across those outputs, including the server's independent extraction path.
- Both browser bundles emit the original profile-icon key at index **25,094** in a **25,216-slot** catalog.
- Independent extraction produces byte-identical manifests/metadata. The real XLF exporter emits **168 files covering all 25,165 distinct keys**.

## Reviewer / rollout notes

The correctness trade-off is shipping the complete catalog in smaller targets. On the validated source snapshot, the English JSON is **1,238,251 bytes / 319,198 bytes gzip**; these are total sizes, not per-target increases. Source-wide extraction took about **23 seconds**, and loading plus full-source validation about **2 seconds**, locally on Windows.

Reindexed bundles and catalogs must ship together under a new build identity; existing published commit catalogs must not be replaced with reordered arrays. This does not change browser fallback behavior, language-pack formats, or the CDN URL contract. Full signed release packaging and live CDN deployment have not been exercised.

pull_requests.title: performance: reduce URI-to-string conversion overhead
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Reduce overhead when converting URIs into strings, with approximately
52% lower execution time on VS Code's existing URI corpus in a controlled
local benchmark using Electron's V8 runtime.

A URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) identifies a file or other resource.
URI formatting converts its components—such as the scheme, host, path,
query, and fragment—into a string, escaping reserved characters where
required. For example, a literal `#` inside a file path becomes `%23`
rather than being interpreted as the start of a fragment.

The existing minimal encoder scans every character in JavaScript, even
when no escaping is needed. After encountering a delimiter, it appends
unchanged characters individually.

This change uses native string searches to locate the first `?` or `#`,
returns delimiter-free components unchanged, and copies subsequent safe
runs as substrings.

## Behavior

- Preserves existing minimal-encoding output, including delimiter order
  and repeated delimiters.
- Preserves Unicode and surrogate code units in unchanged runs.
- Leaves normal encoding, raw-fragment handling, and URI caching unchanged.
- Adds no caches, retained state, dependencies, or public API changes.

Regression tests cover delimiter boundaries, unchanged prefixes and tails,
component encoding, and both normal/minimal serialization call orders.
The new tests also pass against the unchanged upstream implementation.

## Performance

Measured on an Apple M3 Pro, macOS arm64, using the existing URI corpus:

| Runtime | Baseline median | Candidate median | Time reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Electron 43.6.0 | 346 ns/operation | 166 ns/operation | 52.2% |
| Node.js 24.18.0 | 394 ns/operation | 230 ns/operation | 41.8% |

### Measurement scope

The comparison used:
- The same 105,025 corpus entries, including the trailing empty entry.
- Actual baseline/candidate URI modules built with identical tooling.
- Fresh URI construction, minimal formatting, and output-content
  consumption inside each measured operation.
- Warmups followed by alternating baseline/candidate samples.
- Separate repeat runs, including reversed first-arm order in Electron.
- An unchanged full-encoding control and matching output checksums.
- Correctness checking in a separate process to avoid preconditioning
  the benchmark's JIT.

Electron was run in Node mode. These are component-level measurements,
not workbench startup or renderer-latency measurements. Results are
corpus-specific; some very short delimiter-heavy inputs can be slower.

## Validation

- 131 targeted URI and consumer tests passed on both baseline and candidate,
  with the same four pending tests.
- Full client TypeScript checking passed.
- Changed-file ESLint and whitespace checks passed.
- 387,209 exact public-API comparisons completed without mismatches.
- Validation was performed on macOS; Windows/Linux CI remains necessary.

Only two source/test files are changed: 19 production lines added and
9 removed, plus 52 regression-test lines. Benchmark instrumentation and
raw reports are not included in the production patch.

pull_requests.title: Add main-process startup perf marks between didStartMain and willOpenNewWindow
pull_requests.body:
## Why

There is currently **nothing** marked between `code/didStartMain` and `code/mainAppReady`, and nothing between `code/mainAppReady` and `code/willCreateCodeWindow`. On an empty window that is ~200 ms of main-process startup sitting in two opaque buckets.

## What

Marks around the top-level work in `src/main.ts`:

| mark pair | covers |
|---|---|
| `willConfigureCommandlineSwitches` / `did…` | `configureCommandlineSwitchesSync` |
| `willGetUserDataPath` / `did…` | `getUserDataPath` + UNC allowlist + `app.setPath` |
| `willRegisterSchemesAsPrivileged` / `did…` | `protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` |
| `willRegisterListeners` / `did…` | `registerListeners` |
| `willGetPreferredSystemLanguages` / `did…` | `app.getPreferredSystemLanguages` |
| `willWaitForAppReady` / `didWaitForAppReady` | waiting for Electron's `ready` event |
| `willResolveNlsConfiguration` / `did…` | `resolveNlsConfiguration` |
| `willBootstrapESM` / `did…` | `bootstrapESM` |
| **`willRunMainBundle` / `didRunMainBundle`** | **`import('./vs/code/electron-main/main.js')`** |

and around the electron-main work:

| mark pair | covers |
|---|---|
| `willCreateMainServices` / `did…` | `CodeMain.createServices` |
| `willInitMainServices` / `did…` | `CodeMain.initServices` |
| `willStartCodeApplication` | entry of `CodeApplication.startup` |
| `willResolveMachineId` / `did…` | machine / sqm / devDevice id |
| `willInitAppServices` / `did…` | `CodeApplication.initServices` |
| `willInitChannels` / `did…` | `initChannels` |
| `willSetupProtocolUrlHandlers` / `did…` | `setupProtocolUrlHandlers` |
| `willOpenFirstWindow` / `did…` | `openFirstWindow` |

### The important one

`code/willRunMainBundle` → `code/didRunMainBundle`.

`out/main.js` is a single bundle that is **already compiled** by the time that import runs — esbuild lowers `await import(...)` to a call to the module's initializer — so the pair isolates *execution of our own electron-main module graph*, cleanly separated from Electron/Chromium cost. That is the distinction that could not be made before.

## Behavior note for whoever watches startup telemetry

`timers.ellapsedRunMainBundle` previously measured `code/didStartMain` → `code/didRunMainBundle`, i.e. essentially all of main-process startup, despite its name and despite the perf view rendering it in a row labelled **"run main.js"**. Now that a real start mark exists it is pointed at `code/willRunMainBundle`.

**Expect this metric to step down** — roughly 405 ms → 175 ms on the 1.139 build measured here. That is a definition fix, not a perf win. The previous quantity remains derivable from `ellapsedAppReady` plus the new phase marks.

auto_merge.commit_title: perf: add main-process startup marks between didStartMain and willOpenNewWindow (#336450)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* perf: add main-process startup marks between didStartMain and willOpenNewWindow

Nothing is marked today between `code/didStartMain` and `code/mainAppReady`, nor
between `code/mainAppReady` and `code/willCreateCodeWindow`. On an empty window
that leaves ~200ms of main-process startup in two opaque buckets, which is why a
large regression in this area went unnoticed for a long time.

Add marks around the top-level work in `src/main.ts` (commandline switches,
userDataPath, privileged schemes, app listeners, preferred system languages, the
wait for `app.ready`, NLS resolution and `bootstrapESM`) and around the
electron-main work (`CodeMain` service creation/init, `CodeApplication.startup`,
machine id resolution, the app service graph, IPC channels, protocol URL handlers
and the first window).

The most valuable pair is `code/willRunMainBundle` -> `code/didRunMainBundle`
around `import('./vs/code/electron-main/main.js')`. `out/main.js` is a single
bundle that is already compiled by the time that import runs, so the pair isolates
execution of our own electron-main module graph from Electron/Chromium cost -
a distinction that previously could not be made from the marks we had.

Two measured results are recorded as comments so they are not re-investigated:
`app.getPreferredSystemLanguages()` is expensive only because it forces Chromium's
locale subsystem to initialize (deferring it past `app.ready` relocates the cost
rather than removing it), and the `willWaitForAppReady` gap is Electron's own
readiness rather than our work.

No behavior change.
