pull_requests.title: sessions: feat: support nested session drag-and-drop
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
Allow meaningful drag-and-drop ordering within the new independent-session hierarchy, including siblings working in different repositories and sessions moving into or out of custom groups.

This draft is part 4 of 4 and is based on #336447. It contains only the drag-and-drop increment; the preceding draft introduces the tree with conservative root-only reorder guards.

## Reorder siblings without changing their creator
Require dragged sessions to share the target's displayed parent. Preserve the existing pin and group restrictions, and retain workspace scoping for ungrouped roots. Nested siblings can be reordered even when their own repositories differ.

Apply ordering through the existing list-owned sort-key service. This does not rewrite provider timestamps or creator references, move files, change repositories, or permit arbitrary reparenting.

## Make group-drop feedback describe the resulting tree
Joining or leaving a custom group can change whether a session appears beneath its creator. Build a hypothetical hierarchy for that membership change before deciding whether a before/after position is valid. Joining a group also models the unpinning performed by the real operation.

If the dragged sessions and target will be siblings, permit positional insertion. Otherwise, retain the valid group-membership operation but omit the positional cue rather than promising an impossible placement. Drag feedback and the drop use the same target-resolution rules.

Reuse the hypothetical hierarchy while the current hierarchy, dragged session objects/order, and destination group remain unchanged. Normal list updates invalidate this short-lived preview cache; it is not persisted parent state.

## Preserve requested positions through presentation limits
A newly grouped, older session may initially sort behind Show More before its new position is assigned. Include the explicitly dragged sessions alongside visible candidates, then restrict them to the applicable sibling/pin/group/workspace scope. Preserve the dragged block's relative order when assigning sort keys, rather than silently skipping an incoming session hidden by the cap.

## Coverage
Regressions cover cross-repository sibling reorder, rejected cross-branch reorder, prospective sibling versus parent/unrelated group-drop outcomes, and an incoming root whose old sort key places it beyond the destination cap. After the review fix and restack, the complete stack's 228 focused tests and client typecheck pass on Electron 43.6.0.

For manual review, reorder two children of the same parent, try a cross-branch reorder, move creator-linked sessions between groups, and move an older session before a visible row in a capped group. The drop cue should agree with the resulting position; unsupported positions must remain membership-only.

## Stack
**Part 4 of 4. Base: #336447.** All PRs are drafts; review and merge bottom-up. Original commit labels are retained below; PR 1 also contains its test-only review follow-up.

| Order | PR | Original commits | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #336444 | 1 + regression-test follow-up | Repository action boundaries |
| 2 | #336446 | 2-4 | Session state, Find, and reveal |
| 3 | #336447 | 5 | Independent-session hierarchy |
| 4 | #336448 | 6 | Nested session drag-and-drop |

pull_requests.title: sessions: feat: show independent sessions beneath their creators
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
Display independently managed, agent-created sessions recursively beneath their creator in the Agents Window, including children working in different repositories. Extend the existing WorkbenchObjectTree rather than introducing a second tree implementation.

This draft is part 3 of 4, based on #336446. The existing nested chat rows are conversations within one session; the new rows are full sessions with their own workspace, execution state, capabilities, and actions. The provider-neutral `createdBySession` reference already exists, so this PR does not add an AHP parent field or a new session-creation tool.

## Visual example
![A parent session in alpha, its child in beta, and a grandchild back in alpha](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6eb6e81c-6ea9-4ba8-be2d-01e4aa7dda27)

Earlier live Code OSS capture using disposable test repositories. It illustrates the actual hierarchy and each session's repository label, not a new live-UI run on this rebased commit. Unrelated window content was excluded from the crop.

## Placement and ownership
- Resolve creator references using URI identity and build a full-session forest before workspace/date grouping. Assign each branch to its root's section, while preserving each descendant's own repository. Section roots remain distinct from full membership, so descendants are counted once and do not gain duplicate primary workspace entries.
- Nest only when both sessions are unarchived, unpinned, non-quick-chat sessions with matching rendered custom-group placement. Preserve existing pin/group priorities and saved membership; do not migrate them to force nesting.
- Re-root a child when its creator is missing, filtered out, or incompatible. Remove malformed cycle edges so every session stays reachable. Recompute when creator metadata and other structural inputs arrive or change.
- Keep lifecycle ownership independent: archiving, deleting, stopping, or opening a parent does not implicitly perform the same operation on its children. Flat-list consumers remain flat.

## Tree interaction and rendering
Compose existing peer chats before recursively composed full-session children. Apply presentation caps to root branches, map descendant reveal requests to those roots, and keep native expansion, selection, keyboard navigation, and tree levels aligned with the actual structure.

Render depth-aware guides in normal, compact, and phone layouts. Reuse the ancestor list for body indentation, reset recycled root rows to depth zero, and keep guide emphasis tied to hover/focus/selection. A child retains its own repository hint while running or awaiting input; accessible labels identify its creator and repository rather than implying it works in the section root's repository.

Observe semantic creator URI changes and other structural inputs, coalescing synchronous updates and replacing observer stores when the catalog refreshes.

## Deliberate boundaries
This PR keeps drag-and-drop conservative: ordinary root reorder remains available, but nested-session reordering waits for the following draft. Creator-linked group moves use membership-only feedback instead of promising an unsupported before/after position.

There is no independent-child activity roll-up on a collapsed parent. A completed parent can still contain a hidden working or input-blocked child; users expand the branch, search, or navigate directly to that session. This is separate from existing status aggregation within a session's own chats. No cross-host scheduler, automatic cloning, reparenting API, or implicit agent coordination is added.

## Coverage and review

pull_requests.title: sessions: fix: persist and reveal session tree state
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
Complete existing collapse, Find, and reveal behavior in the Agents Window before adding recursive independent-session nesting. Expand/collapse, stored section/group state, and Find already exist; this PR addresses individual session branches and targets hidden by collapse or presentation limits.

This draft is part 2 of 4 and is based on #336444, not directly on main. It contains three focused commits and does not create parent/child relationships between independent sessions.

## 1. Remember individual session branches
Persist each session's collapsed or expanded choice across list recreation and grouping changes. Retain it when a provider temporarily removes the session from its catalog, and remove it only on definitive deletion. Validate stored values and read one snapshot per update. Collapse All includes section, group, and session branches while preserving stored choices for temporarily absent sessions.

## 2. Expose matches behind collapsed branches
Wait for native tree refiltering to populate match scores, then expand only collapsed ancestors of actual matching descendants. A matching parent alone does not open nonmatching children. Reconcile result focus and visibility without stealing DOM focus from the find input. Generalize the existing Collapse All write suppression into reusable batching, so opening many matching branches saves their state once rather than once per ancestor.

Search expansion uses the normal persisted branch state; this does not add a separate temporary find-expansion state. Opening an empty Find widget does not open unrelated branches.

## 3. Reveal sessions omitted by Show More
Distinguish sessions excluded by filters from sessions omitted only by sidebar limits. Include the active session, an explicitly requested session, and the archive-onboarding target simultaneously beyond session/workspace caps, without rewriting saved filters. Clear temporary explicit reveal state when its context changes. Preserve existing conditional scrolling for explicit reveal and add offscreen reveal to main-session selection without recentering an already-visible row.

## Coverage
The shared state suite uses existing peer-chat branches, independently of the later nested-session feature. Regressions cover storage read/write counts, invalid saved state, grouping/recreation, true and false deletion entries, hidden matches in both Find modes, typing focus, viewport stability, and simultaneous cap exceptions. pull_requests.body:
## Summary
Keep repository-specific Agents Window actions tied to the repository represented by the section roots, and recognize existing pull-request sessions by repository identity rather than sidebar placement.

This is the first part of a four-PR stack. Later parts improve tree state/search, add recursive independent-session nesting, and add sibling/group drag-and-drop. This PR does not render nested sessions yet.

## Why
A session in a frontend repository can create an independent session in a backend repository. Once the latter is displayed beneath its creator, it must not become the repository chosen by New Session or New Session from Pull Request on the frontend heading. Conversely, checking for an existing PR must find sessions in other worktrees of the same repository without treating an unrelated repository's equal PR number or branch name as a duplicate.

## Changes
- Centralize section construction in `createSessionSection` without changing the existing section shape or behavior.
- Separate `ISessionSection.rootSessions` from complete `sessions` membership. Repository creation actions and capability checks use roots; counts and membership-based bulk actions keep the complete list. These arrays still contain the same sessions at this stage of the stack.
- Resolve PR creation from a non-cloud root folder, retaining its actual `ISessionFolder`. Keep the working folder URI separate from the source repository URI, and skip missing workspace/repository/GitHub metadata while preserving the existing fallback priority.
- Deduplicate across the session catalog by case-normalized GitHub owner/repository identity. While GitHub metadata is pending, compare source repository URIs with the URI identity service, not ancestry, display labels, or checkout paths.

## Commit Order
1. `70b22845447` — Extract `createSessionSection` as a behavior-preserving refactoring. The helper initially returns the original section shape.
2. `24d600d7d91` — Introduce `rootSessions`, initialize it alongside complete membership, and update section fixtures and documentation. Repository-action behavior is still unchanged.
3. `fbadd8296fc` — Switch repository actions and capability checks to roots, improve repository resolution and PR deduplication, and add focused regressions. The previous test-only review follow-up is included in this commit rather than a separate commit.

## Coverage
Focused regressions cover root-only action selection, metadata-pending sibling worktrees, URI case and authority handling, unrelated repositories, and worktree/source-folder fallback. This PR introduces no new visual surface.

The New Session action fixture places a different-workspace descendant first in `sessions`, while `rootSessions` contains only the intended root. This detects a regression to choosing `sessions[0]`; folder/provider and composer-timing assertions remain intact. A mutation check confirmed that the strengthened test fails for the old lookup.

This PR's 175 focused tests and client typecheck pass on Electron 43.6.0 after the three-commit split. The final source tree is unchanged. Before this commit-only reorganization, the complete stack's 228 focused tests and client typecheck also passed.

pull_requests.title: sessions: Add connection-stage diagnostic evidence
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Make failed or stalled remote connection attempts diagnosable from Connection Information, including setup that happens before a connection entry exists.

Previously, a host could show **No connection entry** without revealing whether authentication or tunnel setup had started. The snapshot can now show the last observed stage and its timestamp—for example, `relay.connect: started` or `relay.connect: failed` with a redacted error—and a chronological history of the recorded stages.

- Capture discovery, authentication, tunnel/relay/gateway setup, protocol initialization, transport closure, watchdog, and reconnect evidence at their owning boundaries.
- Include operation/attempt identifiers, durations, and available error codes, HTTP status, request IDs, and nested causes.
- Include a collapsed, bounded excerpt of connection-related messages from the current local Window log. Snapshot text, Copy, Download, and Accessible View share the captured evidence; missing logs are reported explicitly.
- Bound retained events and exported messages, redact known credential formats, and exclude protocol bodies. Reports still require review before sharing because names, addresses, and messages can contain personal information.

## Integration

Builds on the connection-management UI merged in #336328 rather than introducing another restore flow. The added instrumentation observes existing operations without changing authentication or retry policy.

These are client observations, not server logs or an inferred diagnosis. A start without a completion is not treated as proof that the operation is still running.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: park catalog sessions whose source cannot resolve
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #332410, which shipped the session catalog. Background reconciliation was repeatedly opening session storage for sessions whose provider cannot vouch for them, and retrying them forever.

## The problem

On an idle host with ~640 sessions, reconciliation ran at roughly **170 session-database opens per minute**, and in an 8-minute observation window **every single outcome was a retry** — 1,317 attempts, none successful. 69 sessions accounted for 1,343 of 1,957 opens.

The cause is one outcome label covering two different conditions:

- **provider not registered** — transient, clears when the provider arrives, and already guarded cheaply by `isSourceAvailable`.
- **provider registered but cannot resolve this session** — does not clear on its own, and was unguarded.

Both returned `providerUnavailable`, so both got the same retry policy. The second kind re-attempted on every pass forever: the guard passed, `runMigrationExclusive` opened the session database, the source then failed to resolve, `payloadDirty` stayed set, and the session was re-listed on the next pass.

The affected sessions here were genuine orphans — provider-side state pruned while the registry still listed them.

## The change

1. **Split the outcome.** `sourceUnresolvable` is now distinct from `providerUnavailable` all the way through to the retry policy.
2. **Park unresolvable sessions.** Parked sessions are filtered out of the dirty list, so later passes open nothing. Parking never tombstones and never clears `payloadDirty` — the rebuild is still owed. It wakes on provider registration, session mutation, and periodic verification.
3. **Lazy chat-backing check**, so a doomed path no longer performs it.
4. **Coalesce `schedule()`.** A request arriving mid-pass sets one follow-up taken after a 30s floor, replacing back-to-back chaining. User activity was driving ~9 passes/minute.

**Parking never tombstones, by design.** A single failed lookup is not proof of absence — a provider whose SDK is still downloading looks identical to an orphan. Only enumeration proves absence, which is what the existing `providerAbsent` exclusion already relies on.

## Measurement

| | session-dir opens | default-chat-dir opens | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 1,311 | 19 | 1,330 |
| After | 69 | 1 | 70 |

**94.7% reduction**; ~170 opens/min → ~9/min, with hourly verification as the safety net.

> The before/after figures come from driving the real reconciliation service at the observed profile's parameters (69 unresolvable sessions across 19 passes) with a refcounting fake that mirrors `SessionDatabaseCollection`'s open-on-cache-miss semantics; they are not an end-to-end measurement of a running host, and the only variable between the two arms is the outcome the source resolver returns. The before-arm's 1,311 session-dir opens agree with the 1,343 observed in logs to within 2.4%, which is the basis for trusting the after-arm's 69; the default-chat-dir column is the weaker of the two, because the one session that has such a database on disk was also the session actively being chatted in, so its 45 logged opens include listing-fallback and chat traffic this change does not affect — 19 is the reconciliation-only contribution the simulation isolates, and 45 should be read as an upper bound rather than a baseline.

**The parking set is deliberately in-memory**, so on a frequently-restarting host the steady state is one open per orphan per host lifetime rather than zero. That is the explicit trade that stops parking from becoming hidden permanent state — the 94.7% should not be read as "never opens again".

## Validation

Three tests written failing first (parking, wake-and-resume, coalescing). 8,128 passing across the agentHost suites, `typecheck-client` clean.

The one failing test in that run, `AgentHostModePicker > new-chat controls keep the same padding…`, is a pre-existing failure on `main`: this branch is `main` plus one commit touching only agentHost platform files, so it is unrelated to this change.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`runMigrationExclusive` acquires the database handle eagerly, before its callback can decide it has nothing to do — so every early-bail path pays an open. Making that lazy would help more than this one case, but the ref is taken inside the sequencer slot and holding it is part of what makes the operation exclusive against concurrent mutation. Reordering that deserves its own change with its own concurrency tests.

pull_requests.title: fix(media-preview): support untitled audio documents
pull_requests.body:
## Description

Fixes support for opening and previewing untitled audio documents in the Media Preview extension.

Previously, `AudioPreviewProvider` did not preserve the contents of untitled documents when VS Code created the custom document. As a result, the audio preview could not reliably access the in-memory data for an untitled audio document.

This change updates the custom document lifecycle to carry the untitled document data through to the audio preview.

## Changes

- Added `AudioPreviewDocument` extending `vscode.CustomDocument`.
- Added `untitledDocumentData` to preserve in-memory audio content.
- Updated `openCustomDocument` to receive and store `CustomDocumentOpenContext`.
- Passed `untitledDocumentData` from the custom document into `AudioPreview`.
- Updated the `resolveCustomEditor` typing to use the new `AudioPreviewDocument`.
- Preserved the existing document URI and dispose lifecycle.

## Technical Details

The implementation uses VS Code's `CustomDocumentOpenContext.untitledDocumentData` to retain the contents of untitled audio documents.

This allows `AudioPreview` to receive the in-memory `Uint8Array` data directly instead of relying only on a URI, which is important for documents that have not been saved to disk.

## Validation

- ESLint passed for the modified file.
- The change was committed and pushed successfully.

## Related

This addresses the handling of untitled audio documents in the Media Preview extension.

pull_requests.title: Prevent extension manifest cache thrashing across scan languages
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

The renderer's extension-host startup scan passes `platform.language` (for example, `en`), while shared-process scans can omit the language. Both previously used the same manifest cache file even though `ExtensionScannerInput.equals` compares the language, so they overwrote each other's cache and forced repeated scans.

Reproduced in Code OSS: across three launches/reloads, the built-in cache alternated between `en` and an omitted language, with its modification time changing on each cycle.

## Changes

- Prefix language-specific cache filenames with the encoded language ID, e.g. `en.extensions.builtin.cache`. Language-unspecified scans retain the original filename and remain distinct from English scans.
- Lowercase the language before translation lookup and scanner-input construction. `zh-cn` and `zh-CN` therefore share both the filename and cached input, preventing collisions/thrashing on case-insensitive filesystems.
- Invalidate all language variants of the user cache on extension changes, respecting filesystem casing rules and preserving other profiles and built-in caches.
- Add regression coverage for language isolation, casing variants, invalidation, and genuine manifest changes.

The existing three-second delayed cache validation remains enabled, including for built-in extensions.

## Measured performance on this branch

Fresh A/B measurements on Windows 11 Enterprise x64, AMD EPYC 7763 (32 logical processors exposed), Code OSS 1.139.0 / Electron 42.10.0:

- **Before:** parent revision `a8f49160195`.
- **After:** this PR's revision `793a97fa19d`.
- Same local build, same 96 built-in extensions, `--disable-extensions`, `--locale=en`, and identical settings. Each variant used its own isolated profile/extensions/shared-data directories.
- A pilot was followed by two excluded warm-up launches per variant and **five measured warm process starts per variant**. Before/after execution order was reversed on alternating pairs; launches were sequential.
- Timed the renderer's initial `scanDefaultSystemExtensions` with `performance.now()`, from immediately before `Started scanning system extensions` through `Scanned system extensions`. This is the initial system-extension scan, **not total application startup**.
- Both variants retained identical delayed-validation behavior. Each process remained open for ten seconds after its initial scan to allow shared-process activity and delayed validation to finish before the next launch.

| | Initial scan samples (ms) | Median | Built-in cache hits |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Without this fix | 383.6 / 401.2 / 421.8 / 408.9 / 488.7 | **408.9 ms** | **0/5** |
| With this fix | 73.1 / 74.7 / 73.7 / 73.9 / 79.0 | **73.9 ms** | **5/5** |

**335.0 ms lower median initial scan duration (~82% reduction)** in this local experiment. In every measured before run, the shared cache ended with its language omitted. After the fix, the `en` and language-unspecified caches coexisted.

### Delayed validation is still real work

The fixed revision performed a successful delayed built-in validation in all five measured runs. Its elapsed durations were **302.8 / 300.1 / 304.3 / 316.0 / 295.7 ms**, median **302.8 ms**, after the three-second delay. The before revision had no renderer-side built-in delayed validation during these samples because its initial scans missed the cache. This does not imply the shared process performed no validation.

The improvement above is therefore on the initial scan path; it is **not** a claim of 335 ms less total CPU/I/O work or total startup duration. Timing later validation separately confirms it was not disabled to obtain the result.

### Measurement limitations

This was a local source-build experiment on a shared development machine, not a shipped-product or end-to-end startup benchmark. Development-mode Code OSS normally bypasses these caches, so both variants temporarily enabled the production cache path in generated output. The two changed runtime modules were transpiled from their respective Git revisions; identical lightweight timing/cache-hit instrumentation was used in both. Original generated output was restored afterward, and no benchmark instrumentation is included in this PR.

## Correctness validation

### Final revision in Code OSS on Windows

Using an isolated profile and monitoring filesystem cache events plus creation/modification timestamps:

- After warm-up, **three reloads and two warm restarts produced zero cache creations, deletions, or writes**, with unchanged timestamps.
- **Twelve alternating `zh-cn` / `zh-CN` scans through the live renderer scanner** produced zero cache changes and reused one cache with stored language `zh-cn`.
- English and language-unspecified built-in caches remained separate and stable.

These checks used the same temporary production-cache override described above; the casing check also temporarily exposed the live scanner. All verification hooks were removed and isolated instances/profiles cleaned up.

### Automated checks

- `npm run compile`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- Extension scanner suite: **37 tests passed**.
- Targeted ESLint: passed.
- Staged-file hygiene (`npm run precommit`): passed for all three changed files.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Full `npm run gulp hygiene` was attempted but stopped before file checks due to an existing Windows path-conversion error in `build/gulpfile.hygiene.ts` (`C:\C:\...\remote\package.json`). The staged-file hygiene entry point passed; no unrelated build-tool changes are included.

pull_requests.title: build: separate artifact processing from producer validation
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Separate retryable artifact processing from the final producer-stage result check.

- `Process artifacts` uses `publish.ts --process-artifacts` and retains its existing task/per-operation retries.
- Processing still waits for every enabled producer to finish, discovers later artifacts, and drains publication workers. Downloads/extraction stay serial; publication remains concurrent; successful outputs retain the existing checkpoint behavior.
- A following `Validate producer stages` task re-reads the timeline and fails once for missing, incomplete, or unsuccessful producers. It has no task-level retry or continue-on-error bypass. Scheduled release remains gated on the whole job succeeding.
- Running `publish.ts` without arguments still performs both operations. A drained coordinator exits naturally to avoid the Windows Node async-handle assertion exposed by the new CLI tests; publishing workers and interrupted processing retain forced shutdown.

The regression covered explicitly is: **Windows fails -> Mac artifacts arrive later -> Mac artifacts finish publishing -> producer validation fails -> no final build release.**

Refs microsoft/vscode-engineering#3710. This removes useless terminal-stage retries; it does not implement artifact reuse or change signing, SBOM, canonical artifact identity, or security gates. Independent of #336389; the two branches merge cleanly.

## Validation

- `node --test build/lib/test/artifactProcessing.test.ts` — 17 passed, covering late-Mac publication, draining, serial preparation/concurrent publication, checkpoint reuse, failed publication, and actual CLI exit behavior for all three modes.
- Targeted TypeScript check using `build/tsconfig.json` for changed build entry points and imports — passed.
- Existing hygiene checks on all five changed paths — passed.
- Azure DevOps definition 111 **preview-only** expansion — passed. Verified retryable processing followed by non-retrying validation. A scheduled-path preview (in-memory scheduled-flag override only) also verified release remains behind `succeeded()` and the processed-artifact checkpoint retains `always()`.
- Three-way merge check with #336389 — clean.

No build was queued, no production artifacts were published, and no infrastructure/storage changes were made during validation.
## Combined verification

Validated together with #336389 in a temporary local merge: all **37 focused tests**, targeted build type checking, standalone ESLint (including both new test files), and eligible hygiene checks passed. The temporary merge was discarded without changing either independent PR branch tip. The late-Mac regression passes with both improvements applied.

pull_requests.title: Fix built-in extensions manifest cache never being hit
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

Built-in extension scanning is on the `code/willLoadExtensions` critical path, and **the window re-scans all ~96 built-in extensions on every startup** even though a manifest cache already exists.

`CachedExtensionsScanner` keys its cache on `ExtensionScannerInput`, which includes `language` — but the cache *file name* did not. Two callers scan built-ins with different languages against the same file:

| caller | language | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| window — `cachedExtensionScanner.ts` | `platform.language` (e.g. `'en'`) | **missed every startup** |
| shared process — `extensionManagementService.cleanUp()` via IPC `getInstalled` | `undefined` | wrote last, 9–15×/startup |

Each overwrote the other's entry, so `ExtensionScannerInput.equals` always failed on the `language` comparison and neither side ever got a hit.

A second cost sits on top: on every cache *hit*, `validateCache()` runs a **full re-scan** 3s later to diff the result. For built-ins of an installed product that work is pure waste — they are replaced wholesale by an update, and `productCommit` is already part of the cache key.

This is long-standing (1.105 has it too); it simply got more expensive as built-ins grew 93 → 97 and the `extensions/` folder grew 47 MB → 269 MB.

## Change

- `getManifestCacheFileName(type, language)` in `platform/extensions/common/extensions.ts` — the cache file name now carries the scan language (`extensions.builtin.en.cache`). The language is lowercased and reduced to `[a-z0-9-]` because it can originate from a remote client. Also fixes remote servers serving clients with different locales, which had the same collision.
- `CachedExtensionsScanner.shouldValidateCache()` — skips the throttled re-scan for system extensions in built products. User extensions and dev mode are unchanged.
- `ExtensionsManifestCache` now deletes **all** per-language user cache files on install/uninstall, so invalidation keeps working.

## Measurements

1.139.0-insider win32-x64, `--disable-extensions`, fresh user-data dir, warm starts, window-side `Started scanning system extensions` → `Scanned system extensions`:

| | median scan | cache hits |
|---|---|---|
| before | 372 ms (398/405/347/332) | 0/5 |
| after | 41 ms (36/63/41/41) | **5/5** |

**~330 ms off every startup**, on the window that regressed 273 ms → 435.5 ms between 1.105 and 1.139.

The "after" numbers were produced by patching the shipped shared-process bundle to use a distinct cache file name, which reproduces exactly what this change does; the build was restored afterwards.

auto_merge.commit_title: Fix built-in extensions manifest cache never being hit (#336383)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* extensions: fix built-in manifest cache never being hit

The manifest cache key includes the scan language, but the cache file name did
not. The window scans built-in extensions with a language while the shared
process scans without one, so both wrote the same file and the window missed
the cache on every startup, re-scanning every built-in extension on the
`code/willLoadExtensions` critical path.

Name the cache file after the scan language so the two callers stop clobbering
each other, and skip the throttled full re-scan that validated the built-in
cache on every hit: built-ins of an installed product cannot change behind our
back, and the product commit guarding them is already part of the cache key.
Invalidation now clears every per-language user cache file.

Measured on 1.139.0-insider (win32-x64, --disable-extensions, n=5 warm starts):
median built-in scan in the window 372ms -> 41ms, cache hits 0/5 -> 5/5.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: address review feedback on manifest cache fix

Inline the cache validation check at its only call site, tighten the user
cache file filter to require the .cache suffix, and document why install and
uninstall invalidation has to clear every per-language file.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: condense inline comments to single lines

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: make the cache file name identify the language exactly

The readable part of the name is lossy and file names are compared case
insensitively on some platforms, so languages differing only in case or in
separators mapped to one file while ExtensionScannerInput compared them
strictly - reintroducing the eviction loop this change fixes. Identify the
language by a hash of its exact value as well.

Also cover the skipped validation scan: a built-in cache hit must not scan
again, while a user cache hit still must.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: respect path casing when matching cache file names

Matching the file name with a plain string prefix ignored that file names are
compared case insensitively on some platforms. Move the predicate next to the
name generator so the two conventions cannot drift, and pass the extUri path
casing of the cache location so a differently cased name is recognized only
where it refers to the same file.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: identify the cache language with a digest, not a 32 bit hash

hash() is dense for short strings - 6016 of 9025 two character ASCII pairs
collide - so languages that also sanitize to the same readable part shared a
cache file and kept evicting each other. The unbounded readable part could
also push the name past the length a path component may have, which made the
cache write fail outright.

Use a truncated SHA1 of the exact language, which collides on none of those
pairs, and bound the readable part so the name stays short.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* extensions: drop the validation skip and validate every cached language

Skipping validation for built-in extensions was not worth its risk. It made an
incomplete scan - a built-in whose manifest failed to read is silently dropped -
stick permanently, since nothing else in the cache key changes when the read
recovers. It also removed the only in-session detection of built-ins changing
under a running window, which a product update does. None of the measured win
came from it: the gain is entirely from giving each language its own file.

Validation also kept a single mutable input, so with per-language files two
scans within the throttle window validated only the last language. Track a
pending input per cache file and validate each of them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

This is a rollback, not a DNS fix. It restores navigation to Google, so the original external-DNS failure tracked in microsoft/vscode-engineering#3817 remains a separate follow-up.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Preserve prepared repository directory state
pull_requests.body:
## Summary and dependency

Implement the rich working-directory contract from [microsoft/agent-host-protocol#451](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/451), pinned to **`0ceeb99be0ac7821d1f4ca887ed5771a6e15391a`**.

Repository selection is creation input; session state describes the actual result:

```json
{
  "repositories": [
    {
      "source": "https://git.example.org/team/app.git",
      "revision": "main",
      "subdirectory": "packages/api"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "workingDirectories": [
    {
      "uri": "file:///worktrees/topic/packages/api",
      "repo": "https://git.example.org/team/app.git",
      "origin": {
        "kind": "worktree",
        "mainWorktree": "file:///checkouts/app"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Directory URIs are the keys. Repository sources can repeat and are not checkout identities. A selected subdirectory is not assumed to be the repository root, and metadata does not expand tool-access roots.

## Changes

- Keep optional, nonempty `repositories` on creation/configuration requests; remove the immutable input echo from session metadata. Forward and validate repository-relative `subdirectory` selection.
- Preserve repository associations and preparation origin through native canonical state, directory actions, listings, cached Sessions workspaces and per-chat directory subsets. Existing SDK/provider APIs still receive URI-only views.
- Advertise `workingDirectoryInfo` as a client. Project URI-only snapshots, summaries, notifications, live/replayed actions and reconnect state for clients without it. Filesystem URI mapping changes `uri` and `mainWorktree`, never `repo` or opaque user content.
- Validate client directory inputs before side effects. Only authoritative preparation records establish worktree provenance; merely finding a linked Git worktree does not. Metadata does not grant workspace trust or cleanup authority.
- Reject duplicate repository creation, including after authentication retry. Do not send the queued first prompt or attach customization reconciliation; the user must explicitly reopen the existing session. No creation token or idempotent-success fallback.
- Wait for repository preparation and resolved directories before sending. Preserve ordinary native sessions' lazy first-turn materialization and known-session reconnect behavior.
- Add **Sessions: New Repository Session...** using existing host selection and input dialogs. It collects an HTTPS source, supported revision and optional subdirectory, then opens a draft without preparing a checkout. The command is scoped to the Agents window and hidden when AI is disabled.

Host-level `repositoryPreparation` discovery and existing primary-directory capability rules remain unchanged. Multiple inputs still require `multipleRepositories`; the picker selects one repository. Native VS Code does not add a repository-preparation engine.

Supersedes closed #336294; no vendor clone adapter, arbitrary RPC dispatch, token change or new lifecycle state.

## Validation

For VS Code commit **`c76463ab9b729044ea3213cb892372d7706117cb`**:

- Client typecheck and changed-file hygiene/ESLint passed; normal signed commit hooks passed.
- Eight native/protocol suites: **1,045 passed**, **16 existing pending**. The final mixed-client projection rerun passed all **10** cases.
- Chromium and WebKit each passed **672** main migration/chat-lifecycle tests and **111** additional directory-consumer tests.
- Main through `39bc32738a7` is included by normal merge. Tests used isolated output; the running development build was not replaced.

The four existing VS Code review threads are resolved. This PR remains draft for coordinated review and interoperability verification. Current-head [Code OSS CI](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35668314091) passed; all 32 completed checks passed. Only the external VS Code PR Check remains in progress.

## Verification limits

No full application build, live UI/sandbox or end-to-end scenario was launched. Earlier manual tests used older builds and do not validate this contract. The local-only temporary command remains outside this PR. These unreleased drafts require coordinated host/client updates; released-binary compatibility is not claimed.

pull_requests.title: Retry Snap Store 429s before snap lifecycle
pull_requests.body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3831
Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3193

## Summary

Snapcraft 7.5.3 can abort on HTTP 429 while querying `core20` required-grade metadata, before any snap part runs. The existing apt retries do not cover this Store request, and pre-extracting the base snap does not remove the metadata lookup.

- Retry only the observed 7.5.3 initialization failure: exit 1, exact terminal Store-429 message, and no saved lifecycle state.
- Limit execution to four attempts with 30/60/120-second backoff plus 0-29 seconds of jitter (at most 297 seconds of added sleep).
- Preserve live logs and failure exit codes. Do not retry part hooks, packaging failures, cancellation, or failed output capture. Setup and output naming remain outside the loop.
- Fail closed for other Snapcraft versions; review the version/state boundary when upgrading the pinned image.

## Evidence

Build 472713 at `7f59d5e0` failed in Linux attempts 1 and 2 with the same Store 429 ([attempt 1](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_apis/build/builds/472713/logs/1769), [attempt 2](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_apis/build/builds/472713/logs/2509)). The publishing failure is a cascade. Green build 472717 was BatchedCI with no snap task, so it does not establish recovery.

The [upstream lifecycle ordering](https://github.com/canonical/snapcraft/blob/7.5.3/snapcraft_legacy/internal/lifecycle/_runner.py#L121-L145) saves global state after the metadata query and before executing parts. This is the retry boundary used here.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: recheck Codex hook trust before the first turn
pull_requests.body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3840

## Summary

- Track the hook trust applied when a fresh Codex thread starts.
- Recheck before the first turn and reuse the existing pre-turn restart path if newly discovered hook hashes require a different grant.
- Carry successful discovery into the replacement without a redundant lookup, revalidate workspace and hook-source trust before startup, and rediscover if the working directory changed.
- Preserve existing grants on a failed recheck, log the failure, and keep Workspace Trust/revocation checks intact.
- Add seven regression cases and document the fresh-workspace requirement. No timeout increase, quarantine, or persistent hook grants.

## Root cause and evidence

In a fresh workspace, `hooks/list` can return no project hooks before `thread/start` establishes native project trust. The thread then starts without `hooks.state`, and a model turn can finish successfully without running the synchronous `SessionStart` marker hook. Incidental pre-turn restarts can mask this ordering problem.

The [original failure in build 473136](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=473136&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=8211513&resultId=100220) took 30.450 seconds. Checkout logs confirm the failed attempt and existing passing retry both used `d550ca3ed31712f730403f337ce7bcae62aadf1b`; the retry is not evidence of a resolving change.

Reproduced with the locked Codex 0.153.0 SDK on main `aa513800f750ab6a2edf90d45fa28bfe7e411749`. Native controls returned zero hooks before startup and one afterward; restarting with the discovered hash produced the marker in 3/3 controls. The original integration assertions remain unchanged and pass with this fix.

Original provider-internal CI logs were not published, so the historical restart trigger is inferred; the failure mechanism and fix were reproduced locally. This does not claim a common cause for the other timeouts aggregated in the tracker.

## Overlapping work

- **Overlapping/alternative product fix: #336306.** It addresses the same cold-start hook discovery problem and additionally changes cold-resume handling. These PRs should be reconciled rather than merged independently; this draft is the narrower first-turn fix from the build 473136 investigation.
- **Quarantine-only alternative: #336297.** This PR keeps the trusted integration case active.
- **Related history: #334063, #331733, and #331285.** The latter two issues are already closed; #334063 introduced the pre-start hook lookup and test. They are context, not additional closing targets.

Searches of open VS Code hook, Codex, Workspace Trust, and exact-marker reports found no additional open issue that this patch can confidently close.

## Validation

Windows, Electron 42.10.0, locked Codex 0.153.0:

- Targeted transpilation and scoped TypeScript checking of changed modules/dependencies: passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\codex\codexCreateChat.test.ts`: **98 passing**.
- `scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\providerIntegration\codexCustomizations.integrationTest.ts`: **6 passing** (five provider cases plus the harness check).
- Repository hygiene on changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.

No full build, CI rerun, or Linux/macOS validation was performed.

pull_requests.body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3817

## Summary

- Replace the live Google URL in `chat - browser tools > Open a page from the web` with an ephemeral loopback HTTP fixture.
- Exercise the real `open_browser_page` tool and assert both its Page ID and the rendered fixture heading, rather than only tab creation.
- Register an owned tunnel in remote workspaces so existing remote proxying or forwarded-localhost rewriting can reach the fixture.
- Close browser tabs, dispose the tunnel, and close the HTTP server and lingering connections, including on failure.

No test skips, mocks, file/data navigation, or additional permission/network-policy overrides.

## Evidence

The original [472458 Electron log](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/a6d41577-0fa3-498e-af22-257312ff0545/_apis/build/builds/472458/logs/1585?api-version=7.1) and [470936 log](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/a6d41577-0fa3-498e-af22-257312ff0545/_apis/build/builds/470936/logs/1584?api-version=7.1) show navigation to Google rejecting with `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED (-105)`. This test does not need external DNS or internet access to cover HTTP navigation.

Although ADO reports zero changes between green 472452 and failing 472458, their source commits differ by unrelated #335290; the browser-test contents are identical. This fixes the latent test dependency, not an established product DNS defect. #335368 addressed a separate storage-test cleanup timeout.

## Validation

- API-test extension compilation and scoped single-file hygiene passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Ran the exact test on Windows using an existing older Code OSS runtime with external DNS deliberately failing (`--host-resolver-rules="MAP * ~NOTFOUND, EXCLUDE 127.0.0.1, EXCLUDE localhost"`): the original test reproduced `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED (-105)`; the fixed test passed, including the rendered-content assertion.

pull_requests.title: Give telemetry build extraction a measured 4 GiB heap budget
pull_requests.body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#3836

## Summary

- Give both telemetry-extractor subprocesses an explicit `--max-old-space-size=4096` budget.
- Preserve extraction scope, declaration validation, endpoints, output handling and hard failures.
- Refine the earlier, still-unmerged proposal #335527: measured validation supports 4 GiB rather than its proposed 8 GiB.

## Evidence

[Build 472879, log 1185](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_apis/build/builds/472879/logs/1185?api-version=7.1) shows the first/core child exhausting its V8 heap around 2052 MB under Node 24.18.0 arm64. The helper/config child never started.

The substantial working set is the extractor's TypeScript compiler program, not the emitted telemetry JSON. Local instrumentation observed 336 selected project files, 5,402 compiler-program files and approximately 2.2 GiB of heap after type resolution; the core output was only 740 KiB.

This does **not** establish deterministic source-tree growth or a specific culprit commit. Both sibling macOS extractions succeeded on their first attempts on the failing build's SHA. A bounded, attempt-level audit of 24 builds found 203 successful extractor steps and this one OOM; all task/job/phase/stage attempts were 1, with no previous-attempt pointers.

## Validation

Real extraction using Node 24.18.0, extractor 1.20.4, ts-morph 25.0.1 and Windows x64, on baseline `aa513800f750ab6a2edf90d45fa28bfe7e411749`:

| Input | Old-space limit | Result | Peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Core | 2048 MiB | V8 OOM, exit 134 | - |
| Core | 4096 MiB | Pass | 2430 MiB |
| Core | 8192 MiB | Pass | 2434 MiB |
| Extension/helper config | 4096 MiB | Pass | 126 MiB |
| Extension/helper config | 8192 MiB | Pass | 125 MiB |

Both core and extension outputs were byte-identical between 4096 and 8192 MiB, including 481 core events and 72 extension events.

- Five isolated checks executed the actual wrapper and real Node children: explicit heap settings override inherited settings, CI/local paths and output handling are preserved, child failures propagate, and missing output remains a hard failure.
- Focused TypeScript check: zero diagnostics.
- Targeted repository hygiene, `node --check` and `git diff --check`: pass.

- keep executable proxy configuration inside the shared process and bridge proxy stdio into the existing `ssh2` final-host connection

- proxy directives never cross renderer IPC or enter persisted connection metadata
- `ProxyCommand` substitutions are validated and expanded in one pass
- `ProxyJump` uses an absolute OpenSSH executable, `shell: false`, and an argument array
- proxy failures never fall back to direct DNS/TCP dialing

pull_requests.title: Add Copilot setup dialog impression telemetry
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Add `chatSetup.dialogShown` to measure displayed Copilot setup/sign-in dialogs rather than infer impressions from login attempts or setup outcomes.

Related to #333139 and #335403. This adds diagnostic coverage; it does not claim to fix repeated sign-in prompting or establish credential loss.

## Implementation

- Emit from the shared dialog presentation path, after `show()` is invoked and before waiting for dismissal. Skipped/pre-cancelled setup does not emit; concurrent setup requests sharing a dialog count once, and a later redisplay counts again.
- Record five categorical/boolean fields: allowlisted `source`, sign-in/setup `kind`, current `accountAvailable`, the `ChatEntitlement` enum name, and `forceSignInDialog`. Reuse the existing `common.isAgentsWindow` property to distinguish Agents windows from the regular workbench.
- Attribute setup commands, Accounts/title bar/URL entry points, chat and inline rename, Agents onboarding, Agent Host authentication, SCM, and code review. Other callers of the general setup command remain in the `command` category; unspecified or unrecognized sources are `unknown`.
- Use the existing synchronous account snapshot. A missing account may still be initializing, so the event deliberately does not call it a confirmed sign-out or await account readiness.
- Reuse the existing telemetry service and common correlation fields. Do not collect raw command arguments, dialog text, scopes, URLs, credentials, or account identifiers.

No authentication, entitlement, dialog presentation, or accessibility behavior is intentionally changed. No new setting or telemetry infrastructure is introduced.

## Event schema

`chatSetup.dialogShown` registers the following five fields. All are classified as `SystemMetaData`; event owner: `jruales`. Boolean fields are serialized as numeric measures (`true` = `1`, `false` = `0`). The event does not register a separate impression-count measure: count event rows.

| Field | Property / measure | Possible values and meaning | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | String property | One of the 13 allowlisted values below. Identifies the attributed setup entry point, not necessarily the original UI action or extension. | `FeatureInsight` |
| `kind` | String property | `signIn`: the displayed buttons offer provider authentication. `setup`: no provider-authentication button; the dialog offers AI feature setup. Determined from button strategies, not localized/custom dialog text. | `FeatureInsight` |
| `accountAvailable` | Boolean measure: `0` or `1` | `1`: `currentDefaultAccount` is non-null when the impression is recorded. `0`: no current default account, which can include pending initialization. Neither value establishes credential persistence, token validity, or interactive sign-in success. | `PerformanceAndHealth` |
| `entitlement` | String property | A `ChatEntitlement` enum **name**, listed below, taken from the setup context used to construct the dialog. This may be cached/last-known state, not a fresh server result. | `PerformanceAndHealth` |
| `forceSignInDialog` | Boolean measure: `0` or `1` | `1`: the caller explicitly set `forceSignInDialog: true`. `0`: the option was absent or not strictly `true`. This describes the request, not the displayed buttons; use `kind` to identify provider-sign-in dialogs. | `PerformanceAndHealth` |

### `source` values

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unknown` | Source is unspecified or fails the runtime allowlist. Arbitrary caller strings are not logged. |
| `command` | General `workbench.action.chat.triggerSetup` command without more specific attribution; includes UI/API callers that do not supply a source. |
| `anonymousCommand` | Anonymous-capable setup command (`workbench.action.chat.triggerSetupSupportAnonymousAction`) without more specific attribution. Does not mean the user is anonymous. |
| `forcedSignInCommand` | Explicit `workbench.action.chat.triggerSetupForceSignIn` command. |
| `accounts` | Workbench Accounts-menu setup action. |
| `titleBar` | Workbench title-bar setup action. |
| `url` | Chat setup extension URL handler. The URL, referrer, and input text are not logged. |
| `chat` | Setup agent invoked from a chat request. |
| `inlineRename` | AI new-symbol-name provider invokes setup. |
| `sessionsSetup` | Agents window onboarding/setup sign-in flow, including redisplays/retries. |
| `agentHost` | Interactive Agent Host authentication through the product sign-in flow. |
| `scm` | SCM setup actions for generating a commit message or resolving merge conflicts. |
| `codeReview` | Setup requested by the `chat.internal.review` command. |

Concurrent callers sharing an open dialog do not emit additional impressions or replace the first caller's source. These values are caller attribution, not proof that a prompt was automatic or unwanted.

### `entitlement` values

| Value | Meaning in the setup context |
| --- | --- |
| `Unknown` | Signed-out entitlement state. This is not proof that stored credentials are absent. |
| `Unresolved` | Signed in, but entitlement has not yet resolved. |
| `Available` | Signed in and eligible to sign up for Copilot Free. |
| `Unavailable` | Signed in but not eligible for Copilot Free. |
| `Free` | Signed up for Copilot Free. |
| `EDU` | Education entitlement. |
| `Pro` | Copilot Pro entitlement. |
| `ProPlus` | Copilot Pro Plus entitlement. |
| `Business` | Copilot Business entitlement. |
| `Enterprise` | Copilot Enterprise entitlement. |
| `Max` | Copilot Max entitlement. |

### Existing common window indicator (not newly registered)

The telemetry pipeline already adds `common.isAgentsWindow = true` for Agents windows (serialized as measure `1`); it is **omitted**, rather than explicitly `false`, for other windows. It provides the workbench/Agents split without an event-specific `surface` field. Existing common session/device correlation and timing fields are also reused, not registered again by this event.

## Interpretation and review

Filter `kind == 'signIn'` to count provider-sign-in dialog displays in the telemetry-reporting population. This does not cover generic extension authentication permission dialogs, and an impression is not an interactive login attempt or success.

The event includes typed privacy classifications with `jruales` as owner. Please review the new telemetry schema before merging.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- ESLint on all 11 changed TypeScript files — passed.
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- 27 targeted tests passed across chat setup and affected Agent Host authentication tests, including 10 new tests covering payloads, untrusted source values, concurrency, redisplay, skipped setup, and cancellation.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

pull_requests.title: Optimize chat window resizing performance
pull_requests.body:
This pull request addresses performance issues related to resizing the chat window in the agents interface. The changes focus on reducing redundant style recalculations and layout measurements that were identified as the primary cause of slow resizing.

### Key Changes:
- **Terminal Resizing Optimization**: Layout now runs once after terminal reflow, reducing DOM scans from 4 to 1 per resize.
- **Background Replicas Improvement**: Hidden backgrounds no longer measure geometry, eliminating unnecessary reads.
- **Queued Terminal Layouts**: Duplicate frame requests are coalesced, and pending work is canceled upon disposal.

### Testing:
- Added eight regression tests; all 59 targeted tests were executed and passed.
- Full TypeScript and hygiene checks have passed.

These optimizations aim to enhance the user experience by providing smoother resizing without altering any visual or accessibility aspects of the chat interface. Further profiling is recommended to quantify the performance improvements.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Avoid repeated sign-in for stale sessions
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #336407

## Summary

- retry one other matching authentication session from the same account before showing sign-in after the preferred session is rejected repeatedly
- quarantine the rejected session in the existing connection-scoped token cache, whether it was an exact scope match or the narrowest matching superset
- apply the quarantine consistently to background authentication and session creation; prevent delayed lookups from restoring a quarantined credential
- release the account constraint when the quarantined session is removed or replaced
- preserve the existing interactive sign-in behavior when no same-account alternative exists
- add bounded product telemetry for recovery decisions and interactive sign-in results

## Context

Agent Host prefers an exact scope match, then the narrowest matching superset. The Copilot extension normally prefers the broader `read:user,repo,user:email,workflow` session, and the product sign-in flow refreshes that broader session. If Agent Host's preferred credential is stale, startup can repeatedly select it and open sign-in even though another matching session for the same account remains usable.

This covers both an exact `read:user,user:email` session being rejected and the no-exact-match case seen in #336407, whose stored scope inventory includes both `read:user,repo,user:email` and `read:user,repo,user:email,workflow`.

The Agent Host/renderer export supplied for #336407 captures GitHub `401 Bad credentials` failures during model discovery, two `auth/required` notifications, and the resulting `workbench.action.chat.triggerSetup` invocation while the window has an active account/entitlement. The [reporter's earlier authentication and successful-chat logs](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336407#issuecomment-5698946047) provide supporting context.

This change keeps the existing resend-once recovery behavior, then tries one same-account alternative without silently switching accounts. The rejected session is remembered only for that resource/scope pair so subsequent authentication does not immediately put it back.

The prompting path is confirmed by the new logs, but the alternative credential's validity and same-account eligibility are not established by the redacted export. Verification of this fix against the affected profile is still required.

Central tracker: #336407. Matching repeated-dialog reports #331773 and #333139 are consolidated there. BYOK-specific and other authentication failures are not assumed to share this cause.

## Suspected introducing change

#330556, "agentHost: recover from expired GitHub credentials" ([`670963f9037`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/670963f9037ad055b21b16de2457d0d23e055015)), merged on 2026-08-13 and first included in stable 1.134.0, added:

- [model-list 401 failures becoming authentication challenges](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/670963f9037ad055b21b16de2457d0d23e055015/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts#L1530);
- [interactive sign-in on a repeated challenge with the same resolved token](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/670963f9037ad055b21b16de2457d0d23e055015/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostAuth.ts#L226).

That is the likely regression trigger for the repeated-dialog behavior. Exact/narrowest-superset selection predates that PR; this attribution does not claim that the PR caused the underlying credentials to become invalid.

## Telemetry

Two typed `ITelemetryService.publicLog2` events use the existing VS Code telemetry consent:

| Event | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `agentHost.authRecovery` | `trigger` (host challenge/session creation), `action`, `initialSessionMatch`, `quarantinePresent`, `windowAgeMs` |
| `agentHost.authSignInResult` | `trigger`, `result`, optional `credentialChanged` and `sessionMatch`, `durationMs` |

Recovery actions distinguish no session, provider deferral, forwarding the current credential, forwarding an alternative, and requesting sign-in. Interactive results distinguish cancellation, failure, no resolved session, token forwarding, deduplication, and superseded work.

- Scope matching is classified from the actual session scopes, without sending scope strings or performing extra authentication lookups.
- Credential comparison happens locally; only the boolean result is emitted, and it is omitted when there is no prior credential or no selected session.
- No tokens, token hashes, session/account IDs, account names, raw errors, resource URLs, or remote host names are included in these event payloads.
- Ordinary background authentication emits neither event. Concurrent recovery notifications are coalesced by the existing recovery logic, and repeated cached forwarding does not produce another forwarding event.
- `prompt` means setup was requested, not that a distinct dialog was displayed. `tokenForwarded` does not claim the service accepted that credential; host-confirmed recovery is not measured here.
- No new settings, extra authentication requests, or persistent journey state were added.

## Earlier recovery simplification

The recovery refactor in `0a526826aae` removed the mutable prompt/fallback flags, consolidated alternative lookup and forwarding, and removed 27 production lines relative to the preceding revision without adding helpers or persistent state.

At that revision, measured against `c8d95a6f2fc` with ESLint 10.8.0 classic complexity and SonarJS 4.2.1 cognitive complexity, `_recover` decreased from 27 to 24 cyclomatic and 28 to 18 cognitive complexity. These measurements predate the later type cleanup and telemetry instrumentation; they are not scores for the current PR head.

## Validation

- 81 focused shared/local/remote authentication tests passed, including 16 telemetry tests
- telemetry tests cover exact payloads, duplicate notifications, quiet background authentication, actual scope classification, changed/unchanged credentials, user cancellation, superseded work, failed setup/forwarding, and missing sessions
- the decision telemetry tests and broader-scoped return classification test were verified failing before instrumentation/fix
- characterization tests passed before and after the earlier control-flow refactor
- targeted ESLint, `git diff --check`, and commit hygiene passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` reports only the same three existing Copilot SDK type mismatches for `clientInfo` and `autoTier`, with no errors in changed files

The earlier full `npm run compile` reached those same SDK type mismatches. Full repository hygiene also passed during initial PR preparation.

pull_requests.title: Ensure test diagnostic artifact directories exist
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #272563.

## Why

In [build 366411](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=366411), attempt 1 failed first in WebKit unit tests. Integration/smoke tests were then skipped, and the subsequent 1ES checks and artifact publication failed again because `.build/logs` and `.build/crashes` did not exist. The successful second attempt did not fix this failure path.

## Changes

- Add one shared, inline PowerShell template for the two optional diagnostic directories. Use explicit source-directory paths and the agent build directory as the working directory so initialization does not depend on successful checkout or dependency installation.
- Opt in test-enabled macOS, Linux, and Windows jobs after checkout and the credential-sensitive LFS cache fetch, but before tool/dependency setup. Jobs without tests remain unchanged.
- Reuse the helper in the flaky build and unit/integration/smoke job templates. Preserve the flaky build's existing post-compile placement and `always()` condition.
- Use `System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory` to preserve existing contents and fail explicitly on file/directory collisions. Local validation caught that `New-Item -Force` silently accepts those collisions.

Test exit codes, artifact publication conditions, and 1ES non-production validation remain unchanged. This addresses the secondary diagnostic-collection errors, not the unrelated historical WebKit test failures.

pull_requests.title: chat: Keep Mermaid diagrams mounted while a response streams
pull_requests.body:
Mermaid diagrams render into a webview `<iframe>` inside a chat output code block. While a response was still streaming, every markdown update re-rendered the whole markdown part and reset its container, which detached and reinserted that iframe. Detaching an iframe destroys its browsing context, so the diagram reloaded on every token and flickered heavily.

Measured on a streaming response containing a diagram:

| | Webview reloads during 14s of streaming |
|---|---|
| Before | **84** |
| After | **0** |

> [!NOTE]
> A side-by-side before/after screen recording is attached in a comment below.

In the "before" state the diagram never even finishes drawing — it reloads faster than Mermaid can render, so it sits on *"Rendering code block…"*. The recording harness initially failed outright with `Frame was detached`, which is the bug itself.

## Approach

Reconcile the rendered markdown in place instead of clearing it, so a reused code block and its matching ancestors stay connected to the document.

- **`markdownRenderer`** — add a reconciling replacement that keeps reused sync code blocks and their ancestor chain in the DOM, falling back to the previous reset when nothing can be preserved.
- **`chatMarkdownContentPart`** — re-render in place and reuse the part across streamed updates so the diagram survives. Read the layout width through a delegate so a resize is picked up by later renders.
- **`chatListRenderer`** — notify reused parts when their row is remounted after virtualization, keep code block registrations in sync as the part re-renders, and stop the progressive renderer from rewinding past a closing fence that was already rendered.

## Testing

- New coverage in `markdownRenderer.test.ts`, `chatMarkdownContentPart.test.ts` and `chatListRenderer.test.ts` for iframe document preservation (top-level, blockquote and list nesting), remount after virtualization, resize during streaming, and rendering a diagram once its fence closes.
- Full chat browser suite (5577) and base markdown suite (173) pass, plus `typecheck-client` and ESLint.
- Verified end to end in a real Code OSS window in both streaming modes, and confirmed the new remount tests fail when the fix is disabled.

## Notes for reviewers

- This reuse path previously sat behind the `chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.enabled` flag. That gate is removed so the fix applies by default, but the non-experimental path only engages for an append-only update to a part that already contains a rendered output code block. **This is the part most worth a close look.**
- Known pre-existing limitations, not addressed here: collapsing a completed response re-parents (and so reloads) a diagram in the collapsed range, and reordering two diagrams reloads them.

auto_merge.commit_message:
* chat: Keep Mermaid diagrams mounted while a response streams

Mermaid diagrams render into a webview iframe inside a chat output code
block. While a response was streaming, every markdown update re-rendered
the whole markdown part and reset its container, which detached and
reinserted that iframe. Detaching an iframe destroys its browsing
context, so the diagram reloaded on every token and flickered heavily.

Reconcile the rendered markdown in place instead of clearing it, so a
reused code block and its matching ancestors stay connected:

- markdownRenderer: add a reconciling replacement that keeps reused sync
  code blocks and their ancestor chain in the DOM, falling back to the
  previous reset when nothing can be preserved.
- chatMarkdownContentPart: re-render in place and reuse the part across
  streamed updates, so the diagram survives. Read the layout width
  through a delegate so a resize is picked up by later renders.
- chatListRenderer: notify reused parts when their row is remounted after
  virtualization, keep code block registrations in sync as the part
  re-renders, and stop the progressive renderer from rewinding past a
  closing fence that was already rendered.

Measured on a streaming response containing a diagram: 84 webview
reloads before, 0 after.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Restore code block registrations when a row is remounted

disposeElement drops a row's code block registrations when it is
virtualized. The remount paths only told the retained parts that they
were back in the DOM, so a response whose markdown had not changed was
left out of getCodeBlockInfosForResponse: Next/Previous Code Block could
reveal the row and then find nothing to focus until another token
triggered a re-render.

Re-apply the existing registrations when a retained part is remounted,
reusing the registration callback rather than subscribing again. Only the
template that currently owns the element may rewrite them, so a stale row
cannot clobber the entries of the template that replaced it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Only let the owning template write code block registrations

A retained markdown part can re-render after its row was virtualized, and
with incremental rendering that render is deferred to an animation frame.
If the response was re-rendered into another cached template in the
meantime, the detached part's registration listener overwrote the
response's navigation entries with its own blocks. Recycling the stale
template then deleted those entries - they now looked like its own - so
Next/Previous Code Block targeted detached output, or did nothing, while
the replacement response was still visible.

Check template ownership inside the registration callback, so it covers
the initial registration, the change listener and the remount refresh
alike, and drop the narrower check that remounting did itself.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Enforce fresh remote transport lifecycle
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- separate ordinary remote-host ensure/open operations from explicit recovery reconnects
- require every factory-created protocol client to receive a fresh, uninitialized transport
- make SSH and WSL relay reuse, relay replacement, and full connection replacement explicit across IPC
- preserve desktop, browser, and web tunnel reconnect/location behavior while refreshing cached metadata
- add regression coverage for repeated connects, in-flight and queued races, incompatible transports, and relay handle ownership

## Architectural invariant

A newly constructed AgentHostProtocolClient must never be bound to a transport already initialized by another client. An already-live transport instead retains its protocol client. Ordinary ensure/open operations preserve connected, connecting, reconnecting, and incompatibly-live clients; explicit recovery and preferred-location changes serialize behind in-flight work and replace the connection. Protocol soft recovery retains the client and replaces only its relay.

This fixes the repeated SSH picker flow where a new renderer client sent a second initialize over the shared process's retained relay and received Method not found: initialize.

## Validation

- targeted remote lifecycle suite: 322 passing
- npm run transpile-client
- npm run typecheck-client
- targeted ESLint for all changed TypeScript files
- git diff --check
- two independent Claude Opus 5 code reviews; all valid findings addressed

A real repeated-picker run against a dedicated SSH host or WSL was not available in this environment. The renderer/shared-process lifecycle is covered with focused transport tests. Config-less SSH recovery continues to use existing agent-auth fallback because credentials are intentionally not persisted.

Fixes #335919.

(Written by Copilot)

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Make host connections in web `/agents` understandable and recoverable, particularly on phones. Disconnecting a host no longer makes it disappear from the picker, and the information button works with touch as well as mouse and keyboard input.

### Connection controls

- Keep the connection indicator passive, with a separate information button that opens Connection Information and exposes the selected host status to assistive technology.
- Put labeled **Disconnect** (prohibited icon) and **Connect** (plug icon) actions beside the existing host summaries, without a duplicate normal-host list. On web, Disconnect keeps the host selectable and pauses automatic connection; explicit Connect resumes it.
- Show previously dismissed hosts in a separate **Hidden Hosts** section with a labeled **Restore** action. Restore clears dismissal and reruns discovery. Failures or hosts not found are reported without claiming that a connection succeeded. Explicit removal remains in host management.
- Use live status for host summaries and controls. Expanded diagnostic details and exports use the captured snapshot, with that distinction stated in the modal.

### Diagnostics presentation

- Group Copy, Download, Refresh, and Close in the header. On web, Refresh combines rediscovery and snapshot capture.
- Describe picker membership as **selectable / not selectable**, independently of connectivity.
- Center the modal in wide layouts and retain the phone bottom sheet. Use workbench scrolling, keyboard focus containment/restoration, and 44px minimum phone host-action targets.
- Keep diagnostic content factual, activity chronological, and client details collapsed. Copy and Download include the complete captured snapshot, including collapsed content.

## Scope and desktop compatibility

The connection-management changes target web `/agents`. Shared native tunnel behavior is preserved: native disconnect/removal retains persistent dismissal, and native reconnect does not acquire the web-specific suppression-clearing behavior. A separate permanent-removal operation prevents recoverable web Disconnect from changing the existing Remove Host flows.

The new diagnostics modal may share presentation and scrolling improvements with the native Agents window. Native diagnostics remain read-only, Refresh captures local state without rediscovery, and accessibility help describes that native behavior. This is not a general native Agents window or regular VS Code redesign. Authentication and CORS work are outside scope.

## Product validation

Tested the actual local `/agents` build using standalone Chromium on the development machine, with desktop and iPhone device emulation:

- Reproduced the top information button's touch-only failure before fixing it: mouse click and keyboard activation worked, but a touch tap did nothing. After the fix, Playwright touch taps, mouse clicks, Enter, and Space opened diagnostics; the adjacent host picker also remained touch-operable.
- Exercised Connect/Disconnect beside collapsed host summaries, live status updates, replacement-action focus, and existing host removal followed by Hidden Hosts recovery.
- Checked desktop centering, phone action-target height, wheel scrolling, narrow desktop layout, and phone portrait/landscape adaptation. Captured empty/failed discovery and multiple-host scenarios as well.

Phone results are Chromium device emulation, not verification on a physical phone or installed PWA. Real-tunnel network-failure behavior and the full incompatible-host scenario have not been validated end to end.

pull_requests.title: Make hover mouseout dismissal tests deterministic
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #313831

## Summary
- Re-enable both skipped hover layout/dismissal regression tests (including the related re-entry coverage from #314025).
- Use text content with `hideOnHover: false` to preserve the same mouse tracking without creating a native `ResizeObserver`.
- Dispatch non-bubbling `mouseleave` events on the tracked hover container, and verify dismissal at the existing 200 ms debounce boundary with no intervening layouts.

The HTML fixture registered a native `ResizeObserver`, which is not controlled by the fake timer scheduler. The original WebKit failure was reproduced locally, with a spy recording two unexpected layouts while the pointer was outside and the hover remained undisposed in the DOM. The historical change in #313832 only skipped the test.
