pull_requests.title: agentHost: finish foreground turns independently of background work
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fix the Copilot parent turn remaining **Working** after its foreground response has finished while an intentional background shell or agent is still running. The SDK defines `session.idle` as whole-session quiescence, including background agents and attached shell commands; it is not the foreground request completion boundary.

This is independent of the subagent-rendering work in #335899 and is based directly on main, not on that PR.

## Changes

- Await request-scoped foreground completion for sends and zero-message continuations; use root `assistant.idle` for SDK-initiated turns without a host request promise.
- Preserve request identity through steering and reject stale completion after cancellation, failure, disposal, or replacement. Drain pending host-side tool persistence before finalizing.
- Keep background-child Markdown, reasoning, and tool-input streams intact after parent completion.
- Protect active background agents and attached/detached shells from automatic session release and deferred client restarts; recheck restart eligibility when session idle eventually arrives.
- Add native attached-shell regression coverage and extend lifecycle and restart-race tests. No UI, protocol, or permission-setting changes.

## Reproduction and validation

Checked against freshly fetched main `3e8601c5f63f5b2358e0fbbfb825fbbfd72cbe2b`: a real attached asynchronous shell waits for a test-controlled release file. After the final foreground Markdown arrives, main retains the active parent and `InProgress` state. Releasing the shell unblocks parent completion. The identical probe passes with this change while the shell remains running.

Local macOS validation:
- 879 Copilot provider unit tests passed, with 1 existing skipped test.
- Four persistent real-provider/mock-model integration cases passed: hello, attached shell, detached shell, and idle release/resume.
- Two strict SDK replays passed: simple message and repeated retained-background-child follow-ups.
- The independent before/after native-shell probe failed on unmodified main and passed with this patch; temporary probe removed.
- Client type-check, scoped ESLint, repository formatting, hygiene hooks, and full `npm run build-fast` passed.

One replay attempt timed out at test-server startup before either scenario began; both passed on a standalone rerun without code or timeout changes. Tests use isolated temporary state and local synthetic/captured model responses, with no real model requests. Cross-platform CI is still to be validated.

The original symptom was observed in Autopilot, but the reproduced host completion-boundary issue is not Autopilot-only. The historical export cannot identify every native-runtime condition in that particular run.

pull_requests.title: workbench: keep startup regex literals ASCII
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Spell five characters in two regular-expression literals as equivalent Unicode escapes:

- The em dash accepted after `Goal` in goal summaries.
- The four chevrons accepted in interactive terminal prompts.

Matching behavior is unchanged. Add hyphen/em-dash goal-prefix coverage; existing terminal tests cover all four chevrons, ANSI prefixes, and negative cases. Replace the now-unnecessary Unicode exemption on the terminal regex with a short explanation.

## Why

These were the only non-Latin-1 characters in the measured 19.4 MB workbench bundle. The existing esbuild ASCII/minification configuration retains raw characters inside these regex literals, whereas the escaped spellings remain ASCII.

A character above `0xff` makes Chromium widen the accumulated decoded script from 8-bit to 16-bit. The decoder also resets SHA-256 and rehashes the preceding content in the wider representation ([matching Chromium implementation](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/148.0.7778.280/third_party/blink/renderer/bindings/core/v8/script_decoder.cc#L22-L41)). In an observed loading sequence, that means about 47.1 MB of digest-update input instead of 19.4 MB.

The escaped bundle grows by just 15 UTF-8 bytes but avoids widening. No code splitting, service deferral, initialization-order changes, or integrity-check bypass is involved.

## Measurement

Same-installation-path control using the change in official Windows x64 Insiders `b065ad9cd83dae266607baf77f10c1fbf0330fba`, Electron 42.10.0 / Chromium 148.0.7778.280:

- Two warmups and six alternating measured pairs; separate isolated profiles.
- No debugger/tracing in headline timings; GPU and user extensions disabled.
- Only the five regex spellings and the actual integrity checksum differ.

| Median | Original | Escaped |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Perf-bot startup | 1,486 ms | 1,394 ms |
| Main-time-origin to workbench ready | 1,602 ms | 1,509.5 ms |
| Workbench import | 309 ms | 244.5 ms |
| Workbench initialization | 631.5 ms | 600.5 ms |

Paired mean startup change: **-91.33 ms**, 95% bootstrap interval **[-114.17, -67.33] ms**. The standard-interval median improves by approximately **6.2%**.

Three separate diagnostic traces per variant all accept the same-sized code cache. Decoder worker-task time drops from approximately **100-101 ms to 51-54 ms**. These are task-level measurements, not per-function allocations of hashing versus copying time.

These measurements are from the matching change in a private copy of the official artifact, not a rebuilt PR-head package. They describe one Windows VM and are not a cross-platform performance guarantee.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- Targeted goal-summary and terminal-output suites: **64 passing**
- Repository hygiene for all three changed files
- Existing esbuild 0.27.2 transform emits ASCII for both modified modules
- Separately, **917,504 regex-equivalence cases per runtime** pass on the exact Electron 37.5.1 and 42.10.0 runtimes

Only the focused source fix and goal-prefix coverage are included; the experimental delayed-loading prototype is not part of this PR.

pull_requests.title: Batch SVG whitespace markers in the editor per line
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #201123.

## Summary

- Batch SVG whitespace dots and tab arrows into one path per line containing markers instead of creating a separate DOM element for every character.
- Preserve marker geometry, theme colors, whitespace visibility modes, and the font/legacy rendering paths.
- Add 12 focused whitespace-overlay regression tests, including a constant SVG element-count assertion for a line containing 1,000 spaces.

Whitespace shares per-line HTML with selection highlights. Changing a selection replaces that line's overlay subtree, rebuilding otherwise unchanged SVG markers. Drag auto-scroll also forces the pending style/layout work when reading geometry for hit testing. The attached issue profile shows this DOM/style cost; enabling SVG whitespace by default also matches the reported 1.74.3 -> 1.75.1 regression boundary.

## Performance evidence

Measured in an isolated Code OSS 1.139.0 / Electron 42.10.0 window on Windows, with extensions disabled, the historical 1,992-line Rust file near line 140, `editor.renderWhitespace: all`, and 6x renderer CPU throttling. Selection used 90 real mouse updates ending in the same 2,109 selected characters. Scrolling used 120 wheel updates, 150 lines down and back.

| Metric | Original | Batched SVG | Original restored |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Glyph elements in the initial viewport | 778 | 49 | 778 |
| Selection: renderer task time | 16.48 s | 12.51 s | 17.51 s |
| Selection: style recalculation | 6.33 s | 3.35 s | 6.68 s |
| Selection: p95 inter-frame interval | 250 ms | 150 ms | 250 ms |
| Scrolling: style recalculation | 2.76 s | 1.91 s | 2.73 s |

All 778 whitespace markers remain present. Restoring the original implementation restores the style cost. Without CPU throttling, selection style time fell from 599 ms to 306 ms. An editor-content screenshot comparison found a maximum RGB-channel difference of 1/255 (antialiasing).

These are controlled local measurements with automation/recording overhead, not a claim to reproduce the reporter's exact Linux/Wayland hardware or physical battery-saver mode. Other renderer work remains; the change does not make every 6x-throttled frame meet a 60 Hz budget.

## Validation

- [x] `npm run gulp compile-client` (zero compilation errors)
- [x] Targeted hygiene, including formatting and ESLint, for both changed files
- [x] `scripts\test.bat`: 190 passing tests across whitespace overlay, view layer, and line renderer suites
- [x] Real Code OSS drag-selection, wheel-scrolling, and drag-auto-scroll scenarios
- [x] Live checks for spaces, tab arrows, all/boundary/trailing/none modes, partial selection and Select All

## Visual validation (Windows)

Ran the pre-PR whitespace renderer and the current implementation in the same Code OSS 1.139.0 / Electron 42.10.0 build, using fresh profiles and identical inputs/settings. Captured and visually reviewed all eight before/after image pairs. Used native Chromium viewport screenshots so non-default zoom is captured correctly; AI affordances were disabled in both test profiles to avoid transient selection-toolbar icons.

| Case | Markers before / after | Paths after | Maximum RGB-channel difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original Rust file, zoom -1 (~83%) | 927 / 927 | 58 | 4/255 |
| Original Rust file, zoom 0 (100%) | 778 / 778 | 48 | 1/255 |
| Original Rust file, zoom +1 (120%) | 662 / 662 | 40 | 4/255 |
| Original Rust file, zoom +2 (144%) | 543 / 543 | 32 | 9/255 |
| Wrapped Hebrew/Arabic/Latin with tabs | 191 / 191 | 20 | 2/255 |
| Wrapped RTL with a multi-line selection | 191 / 191 | 20 | 2/255 |
| Consolas with mixed fallback fonts and styled tokens | 210 / 210 | 20 | 2/255 |
| Proportional Georgia with fallback fonts and ligatures | 210 / 210 | 15 | 6/255 |

Every pair has matching marker counts, SVG glyph geometry, text-line bounds, selections, font styles, and actual platform-font sets. No missing/misaligned markers or new text shifts/clipping were observed. Images are not pixel-identical: remaining differences are small rasterization/antialiasing changes, at most 9/255 per RGB channel.

Zoom factors were checked in the renderer. Chromium's platform-font API confirmed real fallback fonts in the mixed-font cases, including Yu Gothic, Segoe UI Emoji, Courier New, Noto Sans KR, and Tahoma where needed, alongside regular/bold/italic Consolas or Georgia. Wrapping was also checked to produce more visual lines than model lines.

The review follow-up skips empty paths on marker-free lines. Consequently, the final default-zoom screenshot has **48 paths for all 778 markers**; the earlier timing runs above used 49 paths, including one empty path. Compilation, targeted hygiene, and **190 focused editor tests** pass on the follow-up commit.

This verifies the local Windows setup, not macOS/Linux or every font/display-scaling configuration. The PR remains a draft.

### Original file with rendered whitespace

The historical `adapter.rs` near line 140, in the patched Code OSS window at 100% zoom with `editor.renderWhitespace: all`:

![Code OSS showing the original Rust file near line 140 with whitespace markers visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b86edba3-8ce2-46e8-a00d-cc97c536c18c)

<details>
<summary>Wrapping/RTL and mixed-font screenshots (cropped editor views)</summary>

Wrapped Hebrew, Arabic, and Latin with tabs and a multi-line selection:

![Wrapped RTL text with preserved whitespace markers and selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8335693d-fab8-4aef-b68f-26396a511177)

Proportional Georgia with bold/italic syntax tokens and real CJK/emoji/RTL fallback fonts:

![Mixed proportional and fallback fonts with whitespace markers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edd77c82-c245-4287-9817-ddce5dff449d)

</details>

## Before marking ready

- [x] Local Windows visual validation at zoom levels -1/0/1/2, with wrapping/RTL and mixed font families
- [ ] Cross-platform visual validation on macOS and Linux

pull_requests.title: Escape theme icons in Quick Search result labels
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #336076

## Problem

Quick Search (`workbench.action.quickTextSearch`) shows file contents as quick pick labels. Quick pick labels are rendered with icon support, so text like `$(copy) foobar` in a file shows up as the copy codicon instead of the literal text.

## Fix

Add `escapeIconsWithHighlights` to `vs/base/common/iconLabels` and use it for the preview text of Quick Search results. It escapes icon syntax in arbitrary text and shifts the match highlights to the escaped text.

Differences from the existing `escapeIcons`:

- Icons that already have a leading backslash (`\$(copy)` in the file) are escaped again, so the backslash stays visible.
- Icons split by a highlight boundary (for example, searching for `copy` inside `$(copy)`) are not changed. `HighlightedLabel` renders each highlight segment separately, so these icons never render as icons. Escaping them would leave a visible backslash.

| File text | Highlight | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$(copy) foobar` | `foobar` | 📋 **foobar** | `$(copy)` **foobar** |
| `a $(copy) b` | `$(copy)` | a **📋** b | a **`$(copy)`** b |
| `\$(copy) foo` | `foo` | `$(copy)` **foo** | `\$(copy)` **foo** |
| `$(copy) foobar` | `copy` | `$(`**copy**`) foobar` | unchanged |

## Tests

Added unit tests for `escapeIconsWithHighlights` in `src/vs/base/test/common/iconLabels.test.ts`.

pull_requests.title: browser: isolate favicon state by document
pull_requests.body:
> **Stacked on #338048.** Review this PR's own commits only. When #338048 merges, rebase this branch onto `main` and retarget it.
Keep favicon work with its committed native document until that document is actually replaced.  - Preserve the outgoing page's updates, in-flight requests, and history across aborted or diverted navigation. - Reject stale work after replacement, failure, or disposal. - Reacquire current-document candidates through the existing preload/frame helper when Electron suppresses unchanged favicon URL sets, including back/forward navigation. - Cover ownership, shared icons, candidate filtering, and history with focused unit/API tests and controlled Code OSS scenarios.  Favicon-only extraction from #335987, redesigned rather than copied. Based directly on `main`; no popup snapshot/version protocol or native-close cleanup from #336075.
## Compatibility with #338048

In this stack, both `getNavigationState` and `getState` read the favicon from `BrowserFavicon`, which tracks the current page. pull_requests.title: chat: preserve environment-hidden setup state
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

In the classic no-remote web workbench, `ChatEntitlementService` intentionally hides chat setup and returns before creating the entitlement context and request services.

`setForceHidden(false)` could later clear that environment-owned hidden state. When no `ChatEntitlementContext` exists, `setForceHidden` falls back to updating `chatSetupHidden` directly, without preserving the fact that setup was already disabled by the current environment.

This could expose **Use AI Features** even though `ChatSetupContribution` never registers `workbench.action.chat.triggerSetup`, leaving the UI pointing to a command that does not exist.

This change keeps track of whether setup was hidden by the environment and preserves that state when the policy-level forced-hidden state is cleared.

The existing fallback behavior remains unchanged for environments where setup is not explicitly hidden.

## Testing

Added a browser regression test covering the failing sequence:

1. Create `ChatEntitlementService` in the classic web environment.
2. Verify that setup is hidden and no entitlement context is created.
3. Call `setForceHidden(false)`.
4. Verify that the environment-owned hidden state remains set.

Before the fix, the final assertion fails because `sentiment.hidden` becomes `false`.

Validated with:

- `npm run build-fast`
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatEntitlementService.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

This does not register the chat setup command in classic `vscode.dev`; it keeps the setup UI consistent with the existing environment restriction instead of exposing an action whose command is not registered.

Refs #335708

pull_requests.title: sessions: address #335583 review feedback on ActionList hover panels
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #335583, addressing the review threads that were left unresolved when that PR merged.

## What's fixed

- **Focus lost on live refresh**: `chatDropdownPill` now preserves the focused dropdown entry (and its open hover) across `updateItems()` refreshes triggered by live PR/CI/issue updates, instead of dropping focus back to the trigger control.
- **Narrow/phone viewport overflow**: `ActionListWidget`'s submenu-panel layout now clamps panel width and position to the viewport, so the hover panel stays fully on-screen even when neither side has room next to a narrow dropdown anchor (tested at 320px/375px).
- **Modified Tab captured**: the panel keydown handler now ignores `Tab` when `Ctrl`/`Meta`/`Alt` is held, so shortcuts like editor-group navigation bubble to the keybinding service instead of being treated as panel traversal.
- **Issue entries missing lifecycle state**: issue reference entries now get an `ariaDescription` with their lifecycle state (Open/Closed/Duplicate/Not planned), matching the existing behavior for pull requests.
- **Stale panel position after content grows**: `tabThroughPanel` hovers (used by GitHub reference cards) now also participate in resize observation, so the panel repositions itself (not just the focused row) when focusing a control reveals bounded text and grows the panel's height.
- **Draft PR CI over-polling**: `GitHubPullRequestPollingContribution` now only continuously polls CI checks for a draft pull request while its session is active; other open drafts refresh once instead of polling every 60 seconds.

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/test/browser/githubContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/chatPills.test.ts` — 138 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean

New regression tests cover: modified-Tab bubbling, panel width/position clamping at 320px/375px, panel repositioning when tabThroughPanel content grows (including near the viewport bottom), issue `ariaDescription` per lifecycle state, focus/hover preservation across dropdown refresh, and draft PR CI polling scoped to the active session.

pull_requests.title: Agent Host: Forward Git identity to Dev Containers
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Forward the host Git author identity to Dev Container Agent Host sessions so baseline checkpoints and requested commits can succeed without manual repository configuration.

Fixes #335761

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Use the existing post-`devcontainer up` configuration hook**: The recent `safe.directory` fix established this as the shared-process boundary where container Git setup must occur before Agent Host startup and its baseline checkpoint.
- **Forward only author identity**: Only host-global `user.name` and `user.email` are copied. Copying the full host Git configuration could leak or break credential helpers, signing configuration, filters, and host-specific paths.
- **Preserve container configuration**: Effective identity already available in the container is retained; only missing values are written to the container user global configuration.
- **Keep startup best-effort**: Identity forwarding follows the `safe.directory` behavior by logging failures without preventing the Dev Container Agent Host from starting.

</details>

## Changes

- Read host-global Git author name and email after starting the Dev Container.
- Populate only missing identity fields for the container user.
- Add regression coverage for forwarding, preserving container identity, and absent host identity.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/devContainerAgentHostService.test.ts` (27 passing)

pull_requests.title: agentHost: render the context-usage widget for Claude sessions from SDK usage and model limits
pull_requests.body:
Ref #322617
Fixes #328844

Renders the context-usage widget for Claude agent sessions in the agent host, including native Anthropic account sessions and the editor-window chat.

Two changes:

1. After each successful `result`, the Claude pipeline calls the SDK's `getContextUsage({ detail: 'summary' })` and re-emits the turn's usage with `_meta.contextAttribution`, the same key the Copilot harness fills. The widget hover now shows the System / User Context breakdown for Claude sessions. The enriched emission also reports the SDK's in-window token estimate as `inputTokens`, so cached conversations no longer undercount. The call is bounded by a 2s timeout and any failure leaves the base usage untouched.

2. The SDK's `supportedModels()` catalog carries no token limits, so native Claude models were published without a context window and the widget hid itself. Every `result` names the serving model with `contextWindow` and `maxOutputTokens` in `modelUsage`. The pipeline now raises those as `onDidObserveModelLimits`, the agent records them per model id (matching aliases like `sonnet` through `resolvedModel`), and re-publishes the catalog with the limits folded in. The widget renders on the same turn that produced the first usage report.

Tests added in `claudeContextUsage.test.ts`, `claudeSdkPipeline.test.ts`, `claudeAgent.test.ts`, and `claudeModelSelection.test.ts`.

pull_requests.title: Fix large Agent Host snapshots over tunnel gateway
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #335232.

Opening a large Agent Host conversation over a tunnel can leave Agents web reconnecting with stale progress and a terminal transport error. The browser accepts WebSocket messages up to 8 MiB but limits each frame to 1 MiB. The protocol-v6 gateway reads an assembled Tungstenite message and sends it as a single frame, so a chat snapshot just over 1 MiB disconnects the client.

Split large outgoing text messages into 512 KiB WebSocket continuation frames in the gateway. This preserves the existing browser limits and protocol message contents.

The regression test runs the actual gateway between in-memory WebSocket peers with the browser's limits. It checks a 1.5 MB Unicode snapshot whose characters cross frame boundaries, a following server update, and a subsequent client request.

Manual verification used a local build based on VS Code 1.137.0 on Linux with Chrome on iPhone: a 1,302,977-byte live chat snapshot was fragmented successfully, the connection continued receiving updates, and the user confirmed current progress appeared in Agents view.

Validation:

- The new test fails on unchanged `main` with `Capacity(MessageTooLong { size: 1500000, max_size: 1048576 })`, and passes with the fix.
- `cd cli && cargo test --locked`: 172 library tests and 5 CLI tests passed.
- Changed-file `rustfmt --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings` under Rust 1.98.1 reports the same 11 diagnostics on unchanged `main` and this branch, all in untouched files (`useless_borrows_in_formatting` and `manual_clear`). Clippy passes when only those two existing lint categories are allowed. The repository CI pins Rust 1.88.

pull_requests.title: Make the empty Explorer view movable
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #335217

### The problem

With a folder open, the Explorer's **Folders** view can be dragged into any other view container — for example into a Panel container shared with Terminal, Source Control and Search.

With no folder open, that is not possible. The Explorer shows **No Folder Opened** (`workbench.explorer.emptyView`) instead, and that view cannot be dragged at all. A layout built with a folder open therefore cannot be reproduced in an empty window, and the Explorer jumps back out into its own container whenever the last folder is closed or a new empty window is opened.

### The cause

`createEmptyViewDescriptor()` does not set `canMoveView`. Its two siblings in the same file do:

| descriptor | `canMoveView` |
| --- | --- |
| `createOpenEditorsViewDescriptor()` | `true` |
| `createExplorerViewDescriptor()` (Folders) | `true` |
| `createEmptyViewDescriptor()` (No Folder Opened) | *(missing)* |

`canMoveView` is optional and `undefined` is falsy, so both the drag source and the drop targets in `viewPaneContainer.ts` reject the view.

This looks like an oversight rather than a deliberate restriction: 6ee9724963d ("Explore making the explorer a moveable view") added the flag to the Folders descriptor and did not touch the empty view, even though the two views are swapped in and out by the same code path in `ExplorerViewletViewsContribution.registerViews()`.

### The change

Add `canMoveView: true` to `createEmptyViewDescriptor()`.

The empty view is registered and deregistered as the workbench state changes, but that is already handled: `regroupViews()` in `viewDescriptorService.ts` consults each view's persisted custom location on both register and deregister, so a moved empty view is removed from — and later restored to — wherever the user put it. The Folders view already relies on this same machinery. View welcome content is registered against `EmptyView.ID`, so it travels with the view.

### Note for reviewers

This also makes the Explorer **container** draggable in an empty window. Container-level drag is gated on every view in the container being movable (`viewPaneContainer.ts`), which the empty view's missing flag currently blocks. After this change an empty window behaves like a window with a folder open, where Folders and Open Editors are both movable. That seems desirable and consistent, but it is a second behavioural effect and is not mentioned in the issue.

### Verification

- `vs/workbench/services/views/test/**` — 37 passing
- `vs/workbench/contrib/files/test/**` — 125 passing
- `vs/workbench/**` — 15207 passing

(`ModernUIContribution > pane composite actions fill regular and Agents headers` fails in the full workbench run, but it fails identically on an unmodified `main` and is unrelated to this change.)

`createEmptyViewDescriptor()` was missing `canMoveView: true`, which its

Opened" view could not be dragged into another view container, so a

pull_requests.title: Move to the next match when replacing with a multiline string
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #248209

### The problem

The replace input accepts newlines (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd>, or `\n` in regex mode). When the replacement string contains one, clicking **Replace** repeatedly does not advance through the matches — it keeps replacing the text it has just inserted.

Using the steps from the issue (search `text`, replace with `⏎text1`, click Replace three times) the document becomes `text111 text text` instead of advancing to each match in turn. Clicking **Replace All** is unaffected.

### The cause

After applying the edit, `replace()` recorded the position to resume searching from by offsetting the start column by the length of the replacement:

```ts
new Position(selection.startLineNumber, selection.startColumn + replaceString.length)
```

That assumes the replacement never contains a newline. When it does, the end of the inserted text is on a later line, so the recorded position pointed *before* it. The subsequent search then matched the freshly inserted text and replaced it again.

The expression predates multiline find/replace, when the replace input was a single-line field and a newline was not possible.

### The change

`ReplaceCommand.computeCursorState` returns the end of the inverse edit range — that is, the end of the inserted text — so the editor cursor is already the position to resume from. Read it instead of recomputing it:

```diff
-this._decorations.setStartPosition(new Position(selection.startLineNumber, selection.startColumn + replaceString.length));
+this._decorations.setStartPosition(this._editor.getPosition());
```

For a single-line replacement the cursor lands on exactly the column the old expression computed, so existing behaviour is unchanged. The `else` branch immediately below already reads the position the same way.

### Tests

Two regression tests are added to `findModel.test.ts`, covering both branches of `_getReplacePattern()` — a literal newline in the replacement, and a `\n` escape in regex mode (which goes through `parseReplaceString`).

Both fail without the change, selecting `[12, 1, 12, 4]` — the match inside the text that was just inserted — instead of `[12, 5, 12, 8]`.

### Verification

- `vs/editor/contrib/find/test/**` — 79 passing
- `vs/editor/**` — 5348 passing, 0 failing

pull_requests.title: agentHost: await Codex process shutdown before directory cleanup
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Add awaitable Codex app-server shutdown, including persistent, transient, cancelled, and late-ready startup paths. Release sandbox/proxy resources after process shutdown; keep synchronous disposal as a bounded forceful fallback.
- Reuse `killTree` through a shared shutdown helper that records owned Windows descendants before EOF, awaits process/stdio closure, and reaps remaining descendants with a bounded fallback. Treat `EPERM` liveness probes conservatively rather than assuming the process is gone.
- Await the same boundary in Agent Host E2E server teardown before removing suite homes. Preserve nested cleanup errors and filesystem errno/leaf-path diagnostics; failed shutdown remains a failure.
- Adjust host shutdown budgets to cover provider cleanup and ensure a stalled protocol drain cannot skip provider shutdown.

## Why

Windows Codex E2E test bodies can pass while their `after all` hook fails to remove the isolated suite home. Representative evidence from #335240: [failed execution](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34341159122/job/102432009032) and [same-source successful rerun](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34341159122/job/102579889438).

A controlled native Windows reproduction demonstrated a file-holding descendant surviving direct-child termination and host exit code 0, blocking directory removal. Awaited shutdown released the holder and allowed removal. This establishes the lifecycle mechanism; the archived CI logs do not identify their exact handle owner.

This is not an SDK upgrade: Codex 0.153.0 was already present in a later failing execution. SDK versions, turn-state mapping, replay fixtures, and terminal retention policy are unchanged. No tests are quarantined and the directory-removal retry budget is not increased.

## Review follow-up

- Distinguish raw startup cleanup failures from expected account-probe/request failures, so cleanup errors escape the real probe's inner catch and remain visible to provider shutdown. The regression now exercises real raw-startup cleanup with failing proxy disposal, rather than replacing the probe with a throwing stub.
- Derive the test-server grace period from all three shared 4.5-second shutdown phases plus a 2-second cleanup margin: 15.5 seconds for local non-Windows runs, with a 30-second minimum for CI/Windows/coverage.
- Add regressions for expected probe errors, ordinary request aggregates, cancellation, and the complete local shutdown budget. The budget regression uses virtual time on Windows; it is not packaged Linux/macOS qualification.

## Validation

Local Windows x64, Electron 42.10.0 / Node 24.18.1, Codex CLI 0.153.0:

- `npm run transpile-client` - passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - passed.
- `npm run precommit` - passed for the staged changes.
- Initial implementation (`6b488c79daa`): 296 focused Electron unit tests passed, covering client/provider/host shutdown, delayed and ignored EOF, detached descendants, startup failures and races, repeated disposal, sequential lifetimes, `EPERM`, and nested filesystem diagnostics. Strict tokenless replay passed twice serially with 3 selected tests per execution.
- Seven-file review follow-up: 88 affected lifecycle/shutdown unit tests passed, plus a fresh strict tokenless replay execution with 3 selected tests spanning the common Codex and Codex-specific suite lifetimes. Transpilation, type-check, and staged hygiene were revalidated before publication.

For every local replay execution, recording/snapshot-update flags were disabled and test-process credentials cleared.

Replay selection:

```powershell
.\scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\e2e\providers\codexAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep "sends a simple message and receives a response|materialized provider exposes its supported management artifacts|secondary workspace skill reaches the Codex model request"
```

No owned reproduction processes or directories remained. These local results do not qualify packaged Windows/Linux/macOS or the full Agent Host E2E matrix. CI results are checked separately for the exact PR head; checks on the initial commit do not establish the follow-up's qualification.

## Related issues

- Related to #329893: Agent Host worktree-removal races and cleanup ordering. Its read-only Git locking cause is separate and is not addressed here.
- Related to #329316: retained Agent Host shell processes after worktree removal. Archived-terminal retention is outside this change.

These are contextual links, not closing references.

- Ask once before running `worktreeCreated` tasks from the worktree's own `.vscode/tasks.json`, since that file comes from the checked-out branch.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: prevent phantom custom-subagent turns
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #335458
Related to #326710 (the broader SDK event-safety audit is not completed by this PR).

## Summary

- Keep a child execution's stable identity across completion. Only an explicit new user/provider boundary can resume a retained child; late message, tool, usage, and bookkeeping events no longer manufacture a successor turn.
- Preserve genuine second/third follow-ups, early discovery boundaries, and originating ownership for delayed tool-display callbacks.
- Publish available authoritative `latestResponse`/`result` text before completion, including a missing streamed suffix, without duplicating final text or moving it before a tool round.
- Keep cumulative child-message rendering independent of root-turn parts and retain old identity tombstones when an SDK agent ID receives a new task mapping. Transient rendering buffers clear on execution completion/remapping; the identity ledger clears on session disposal and is history-proportional, not fixed-bounded.
- Preserve accepted edit invalidation through a small internal `file_edits_applied` notification when the stale child tool response itself must be rejected. The host forwards it to the existing changeset refresh service; no client protocol action or additional scheduler is added.

The exact failure in #335458 has correct response text but two completed child turns instead of one. The new deterministic regression failed on unchanged main with `started -> completed -> resumed -> completed` after an idle status overtook the final message. The three existing replay scenarios also passed on unchanged main, so those green baseline samples are not presented as a deterministic reproduction of the CI flake.

## Validation

Windows source Electron 42.10.0, Copilot SDK 1.0.13 / runtime 1.0.84-4:

- **517 related unit tests passing**, covering the full `CopilotAgentSession` suite, host changeset forwarding, and observed non-Git Session Changes refresh. Coverage includes all 720 completion-event permutations in virtual time, explicit second/third executions, root replacement between deltas, partial post-tool final messages, generation-preserving remapping, delayed accepted edits, and 21,000 repeated events checking identity retention.
- **9 strict tokenless child/subagent replay scenarios passing**, including the three exact custom-agent cases and retained background subagent repeated follow-ups.
- Targeted TypeScript dependency-graph check, ESLint, repository hygiene, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Existing E2E assertions, fixtures, and snapshots are unchanged. No response padding, retries, or global snapshot reordering.

Focused test commands:

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentSideEffects.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostChangesetService.test.ts --grep "CopilotAgentSession|changeset forwarders|non-git folder summaries|late applied edits refresh observed" --reporter dot
& $env:ComSpec /c '.\scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\e2e\providers\copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep "subagent|child" --reporter spec'
```

## Draft / remaining qualification

- **Not a blanket lossless late-final guarantee:** genuinely unseen valid text arriving after completion without an authoritative result is still an unresolved case. The passing tests cover the authoritative-result path and duplicate/stale events, not that unresolved case.
- Explicit acceptance of the private identity contract and combined validation with the independently developed retained-child task-status refresh fix are still pending. This PR does not include that scheduler patch. The existing genuine-resume freshness increment remains; no competing query scheduler or public protocol/routing API is introduced.
- When combining, the guarded successful task-completion application supplies `latestResponse ?? result` as the optional final-text argument. Both owners' regressions and the exact custom/retained E2E scenarios must run on the assembled change.
- Safe general child retirement/pruning semantics, packaged Windows/Linux/macOS qualification, and longer runtime stress runs remain outstanding.

## CI / review follow-up

- The original macOS unit failure was the 720-order test timing out while waiting on real timers, followed by its still-running loop reaching disposed test state. The same exhaustive scenarios now run in virtual time without raising the timeout (about 2.5 seconds locally).
- Guard task completion against an obsolete `agentId`/tool mapping, preserve the originating root ID on child result/usage signals after parent completion or replacement, and allow authoritative results to fill empty final-message placeholders. The new regressions demonstrated five failures before these fixes.
- The original [macOS integration failure](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34722651797/job/103631217144) was the separate browser-tools test failing to load Google with `ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED`; all four targeted Copilot scenarios passed in that job. No browser test skip or retry was added.
- Further selected review cases reproduced missing post-tool text, duplicated text across a parent rollover, lost identity tombstones on remapping, and a missing changeset refresh after delayed accepted edits. Cumulative rendering now belongs to the child message, final-message state is set only after the current message is represented, and accepted edits refresh the owning session without emitting a stale tool action. An observed non-Git changeset regression verifies updated files/counts while the parent turn remains active.

pull_requests.title: Preserve browser popup state across IPC handoff
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fixes a race where a popup finishes loading before the workbench subscribes to its events, leaving the tab's title or loading state stale ([smoke failure](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/33958583544/job/101286291586)).

- Reconcile state after subscribing with a lightweight, versioned navigation snapshot.
- Prevent out-of-order events and stale favicon fetches from overwriting newer state.
- Preserve editor identity and native-page/editor closure coupling.

Initial navigation and `ERR_ABORTED` handling are unchanged.

## Validation

- Regression coverage for delayed handoff, snapshot/event ordering, favicon races, and editor lifecycle.
- Windows Code OSS: build, **221 browser unit tests**, **24 API/CDP/tool tests** (2 existing skips), and **7 integrated-browser smoke tests** passed.
- Native negative controls confirm the intended fixes. Full lifecycle and cross-platform stress qualification remain pending.

Fixes #320443.

pull_requests.title: chat: defer noncritical model configuration startup work
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Move noncritical model-configuration work out of the blocking startup path without delaying early UI context keys:

- Register `ChatLanguageModelsDataContribution` at `AfterRestored` instead of `BlockRestore`.
- Read the schema association URI from the current user-data profile rather than resolving the configuration service solely for that path.
- Request BYOK configuration readiness only once the existing feature-enabled predicate is true. Keep context-key binding, persisted-state restoration, and the extension/configuration readiness checks unchanged.
- Add coverage for pre-existing model schemas, schema updates/disposal, zero forced readiness requests while BYOK or AI is disabled, and exactly one readiness request on enablement.

Deferring the schema contribution alone shifted some initialization into `HasByokModelsContribution`, which still accessed `whenReady` even with the feature disabled. The guarded readiness request addresses that additional eager access. Other consumers or ordinary DI idle initialization can still instantiate the configuration service.

Agent prewarming/experiment-context forwarding and the early debug usage/customization recorders are deliberately unchanged. This PR is independent of #335977 and contains no picker or activity-bar changes.

## Performance evidence

**This is a small startup-work cleanup, not a demonstrated overall startup speedup.**

Six alternating paired warmed runs of the same local Code OSS dev build (two warmups per variant; isolated profiles):

| Metric | Before median | After median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 4,393 ms | 4,392 ms |
| Blocking contributions | 47.5 ms | 47 ms |

The paired-mean startup difference was -0.17 ms, with a 95% bootstrap interval of approximately [-70.3, +70.0] ms. Four separately collected runtime traces confirm that the roughly 1 ms schema contribution moved after workbench restoration. Regression tests verify that the disabled-feature readiness request changes from one to zero.

These are unbundled dev-build measurements on one Windows VM, not a claim about published-build startup latency.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run typecheck-client -- --pretty false`
- Targeted hygiene, including ESLint and formatting, on all five changed files
- Language-model configuration, BYOK, and contribution-lifecycle suites: **33 passing in Chromium and 33 passing in WebKit**
- Real before/after Code OSS probes verified schema availability and associations after startup
- The new regression tests were confirmed failing against their respective baseline implementations before the fixes

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Preserve denied permission results across async checks
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Preserve the originating permission request's result and feedback when a decision races asynchronous preview or sandbox preparation.
- Bind post-await work to the exact pending registration, so reused tool-call IDs cannot let stale callbacks publish a preview or authorize a replacement request.
- Give previews request-specific storage and retire superseded content without deleting the replacement's preview.
- Carry a host-only permission-request handle through asynchronous host policy checks, bind confirmation publication in the final AHP dispatch block, and apply policy decisions to that exact request.
- Add deterministic regressions and strengthen the denied-create E2E scenario to require one interactive denial, complete rejection feedback, no file mutation, exactly one final denied response/completion, and no active turn.

## Why

A missing pending-registry entry was treated as cancellation, replacing an already-settled user denial with a bare rejection. A bounded tokenless reproduction through the actual preview branch showed that losing the feedback suppresses this scenario's continuation request and final response. The same key-only checks could also affect a replacement request while older work was awaiting.

This is a permission-result/ownership fix, not a terminal-ownership change. Provisional-ready UX, session terminal/cancellation ownership, authorization defaults, SDK versions, fixtures, and snapshots remain unchanged.

## Validation

- 233 targeted unit tests passed, including existing successful approvals, ordinary denials, duplicate-approval compatibility, managed permissions, errors, abort/disposal, and the new races.
- Exact Copilot and Claude denial scenarios passed in each of two consecutive strict tokenless replay runs. Each uses one denial and asserts the final response/completion and absence of mutation or an active turn. Copilot's full feedback-bearing rejection is asserted explicitly.
- Also replayed `creates a new text file` for both providers to verify the host auto-approval path.
- Scoped transpilation and TypeScript diagnostics for the 19 changed TypeScript files passed.
- Staged repository hygiene and ESLint passed; temporary reproduction gates and tracing were removed.

Replay command (Windows, recording and snapshot updates disabled):
```powershell
.\scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\e2e\providers\copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\e2e\providers\claudeAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep "declining a file creation tool prevents the mutation and completes the turn$"
```

Local validation used Windows source-based Electron 42.10.0, Copilot SDK 1.0.13, and runtime 1.0.84-4. Packaged Linux/macOS/Windows qualification remains outstanding. The controlled local defect is reproduced; definitive attribution of every historical CI failure remains unconfirmed.

## Scoped confirmation identity and compatibility

Scoped prompts carry an immutable `agentHost.confirmationId` in the existing AHP tool-call `_meta`. Clients echo the ID captured from the prompt; the host validates it and captures the exact live handle **before** reducer, routing, or tracking changes. Both stale approvals and stale denials are rejected rather than applied to a replacement with the same tool-call ID. Cancellation-token renewal cannot reactivate an old handle.

Legacy unscoped providers keep their existing behavior without the new stale-decision guarantee. Missing or malformed IDs fail closed for scoped prompts, so older clients that do not echo the ID cannot answer those prompts. No generated protocol schema, SDK, setting, fixture, or snapshot changes are included.

## Combined cancellation validation

Pinned cancellation revision: `4714761993cddc0608ec870303effbd5db8eba62` (#335981). Temporarily overlaid only its Copilot production diff and adapted the gated tests to create a fresh SDK system turn and deliver a late aborted idle before the old policy decision returns. The combined overlay passed 233 targeted tests, type checks, hygiene, and two strict replay runs (4 denied/allowed Copilot/Claude cases each). The overlay and temporary test edits were removed; no cancellation ownership changes are shipped in this PR. This does not qualify the separate Codex changes or packaged platform jobs.

After restoration, the PR-only candidate passed 233 tests and two strict replay runs (7 cases each, including client-tool readiness/disconnect/result confirmation). Client tests cover prompt-captured identity through late callbacks and late dispatch. The earlier 120-test results alone are not the qualification for this new contract.

## Related issues

Related to #330899 and #333174. These describe the broader readiness/SDK ordering area; this narrower Copilot fix does not claim to close either issue.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Preserve turn ownership after cancellation
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334431
Fixes #334016

## Summary

- Keep every outstanding Copilot abort owner in terminal order, so late aborted-idle notifications cannot complete or clear a replacement, including after successive cancellations. Renew the cancellation token when a system notification starts a fresh turn. Preserve the existing abort serialization from #335343 and normal matching completion behavior.
- Map Codex completion through the established provider-to-host turn identity without rebinding it to the current turn. Ignore unmapped/duplicate terminals before they can create mappings or clear replacement streams, timing, or steering state. Clear completed provider IDs independently of replacement host state, and defer cancellation until the replacement has its own provider interrupt target. Capture start/compact RPC owners in order so delayed or duplicate starts cannot consume another host turn's queued cancellation.
- Capture guardian requests' originating host/provider turn IDs and guard cleanup by request-record identity. Old completion and delayed callback cleanup cannot resolve or remove a newer execution's request.
- Add deterministic ordering/callback regressions and strengthen the existing tokenless cancellation scenarios to require a cancelled original, a complete replacement with the expected text, no pending interactions, and no cancelled file mutation.

## Root cause

The host can admit a replacement after protocol cancellation while provider terminal events from the original are still arriving. Copilot previously completed a running replacement on the original's aborted idle; its old regression test incorrectly expected that premature completion. Codex used the mutating turn-start mapper for completion, reassigning the old terminal to the replacement and clearing its state.

This is a provider-local cancellation/ownership fix. Authorization decisions, ordinary permission-denial behavior, shared APIs, fixtures, retries, and timeouts are unchanged. The independently investigated lost-denial-feedback race is not part of this PR.

pull_requests.body:

- Preserve fully quoted Bash wildcard filenames as literal destinations; require confirmation for PowerShell wildcard destinations even when quoted.
- Keep existing quote stripping for non-glob destinations so Bash quote concatenation and PowerShell escaped apostrophes do not make absolute paths look workspace-relative.

- Cover destination classification and session permissions, including confirmation-rule eligibility.

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/commandAutoApprover.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/commandAutoApprover.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionPermissions.test.ts`
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/commandAutoApprover.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionPermissions.test.ts` (102 passing)
- Verified both new quote-handling regression tests fail on the previous PR head and pass with the fix.

Manual checks:

- In an Agent Host session with default permissions, verify unresolved wildcard redirects and quoted destinations outside the workspace require confirmation; cancel rather than approving.
- Verify normal workspace destinations, null sinks, and file-descriptor redirects retain their existing approval behavior.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Safe-sink ordering and existing quote stripping come from [`classifyFileRedirect`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9b46b4eb4fe899d4c28da3c595b6018b5ca1f265/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/commandAutoApprover.ts#L73-L92).
- Workspace containment and destination policy remain owned by [`SessionPermissionManager`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9b46b4eb4fe899d4c28da3c595b6018b5ca1f265/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionPermissions.ts#L565-L618).

pull_requests.title: Trust only nonce-verified terminal cwd for command approval
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

- Send the shell integration nonce with `OSC 633 ; P ; Cwd` from the bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell scripts, so the cwd they report is trusted. The parser already accepts this optional nonce and marks a cwd without it as untrusted.
- Make the fish script's nonce global so its functions can send it.
- Drop the trailing nonce in the Agent Host OSC 633 parser, as it already does for `E`.
- When preparing a terminal command, treat an untrusted cwd as unknown instead of using it, so relative writes require confirmation instead of being resolved against a cwd that terminal output reported.

Testing:

- `npm run transpile-client` (passed)
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/electron-browser/runInTerminalTool.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/xterm/shellIntegrationAddon.test.ts` (289 passing, 108 pending); the new test fails without the change
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/osc633Parser.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostTerminalManager.test.ts` (57 passing); the updated parser test fails without the change
- `bash -n`, `zsh -n`, and `fish -n` on the changed scripts (passed); the bash and fish forms emit `ESC ] 633 ; P ; Cwd=/x ; <nonce> BEL`
- `npm run eslint -- <4 changed TypeScript files>` (passed)
- `npm run typecheck-client` (no errors in changed files; the remaining errors are in Agent Host Copilot and local transcription files and come from locally linked packages that differ from the versions pinned on `main`)

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The trust flag comes from the existing nonce check for `Cwd` in [`ShellIntegrationAddon`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/35c9fdad14f2b2a4ffc318bf5a337527b6316597/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/xterm/shellIntegrationAddon.ts#L583-L591).
- The PowerShell script sends the nonce the same way it already does for [`EnvJson`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/35c9fdad14f2b2a4ffc318bf5a337527b6316597/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.ps1#L132-L144) in the same prompt.
- The Agent Host parser mirrors its existing [`E` nonce handling](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/35c9fdad14f2b2a4ffc318bf5a337527b6316597/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/osc633Parser.ts#L122-L131).
- The cwd check is in [`RunInTerminalTool.prepareToolInvocation`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/35c9fdad14f2b2a4ffc318bf5a337527b6316597/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/runInTerminalTool.ts#L969-L974).

pull_requests.title: chat: reduce picker layout measurement work
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Reduce repeated DOM measurement in the chat picker responsive-layout path identified during startup profiling:

- Reject rendered overflow/overlap before cloning the lane for preferred-width measurement.
- Capture each visible item's bounds once per snapshot rather than rereading geometry while sorting.
- Prepare all measurement styles on the detached clone, then attach it and read geometry without interleaved style writes.
- Add regression tests for measurement count, detached preparation, reverse visual order, hidden pickers, and non-picker contents. Preserve the measurement clone's `aria-hidden`/`inert` behavior and cleanup.

This is based on current `main` and preserves its newer shrinkable-picker, compact/minimal-state, and overflow restoration behavior. No activity-bar changes, persistent sizing cache, or observer-scheduling changes.

## Performance

Component microbenchmark against current `main`, Windows + Chromium 149: 12 alternating before/after pairs of 80 calls per scenario, excluding two warmup pairs. All compact-state sequences matched.

| Scenario | Before, ms/call | After, ms/call |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Three pickers, narrow | 1.076 | 0.414 |
| Three pickers, resizing | 0.689 | 0.287 |
| Three pickers, wide | 0.248 | 0.173 |

For the narrow case, measurement clones drop from **5 to 2** and Chromium layout count from approximately **21 to 7** per call. These are synthetic component measurements, **not an end-to-end startup improvement claim**.

## Validation

pull_requests.title: feat(save): Opening a non-existent file should not trigger "save file"
pull_requests.body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327076

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Add a setting `workbench.editor.untitled.dirtyWhenEmpty` that prevents a newly created, empty and untouched file from being treated as "dirty," so that closing it does not trigger a "Do you want to save?" prompt.

In Microsoft VSCode, if you open a new file ("code doesnotexist.txt` from the Terminal), make no changes, then try to exit, it asks if you want to save the file. Other editors, such as Vim and Emacs, do not ask to save the file. This feature gives users the option to emulate that behavior.

The default setting for `workbench.editor.untitled.dirtyWhenEmpty` retains the current behavior. The setting must be disabled to get the new behavior.

pull_requests.title: Add `workbench.editor.tabHoverInformation` to customize editor tab hover
pull_requests.body:
**Fixes #163166**

Adds `workbench.editor.tabHoverInformation`, which controls the information shown when hovering over an editor tab:

- `short`: the name of the file
- `long` (default): the absolute path of the file — exactly what is shown today
- `detail`: the name of the file on the first line and its absolute path on the second line

The values come straight from the issue body. `long` is the default, so the current behaviour is unchanged for anyone who does not set the option.

The colour half of the request is already available through the existing `tab.hoverBackground` / `tab.hoverForeground` colors, so this only covers the information part.

### Implementation notes

- `getHoverTitle()` in `editorTabsControl.ts` used to hardcode `Verbosity.LONG`. It now resolves the verbosity from the new option via a small `getHoverTitleText()` helper: `Verbosity.SHORT` is the file name and `Verbosity.LONG` is the absolute path, so `short` and `long` need no new label logic.
- `detail` builds `name + '\n' + path`. `MarkdownString.appendText()` turns the `\n` into a paragraph break and escapes markdown tokens, so a single string produces both the markdown hover and the `markdownNotSupportedFallback`. Preview tabs keep their existing `(_preview_ …)` decoration in every mode.
- The option reaches `IEditorPartOptions` through the existing generic `Object.assign(options, config.workbench.editor)` in `getEditorPartOptions()`.
- Both tab controls redraw when the option changes, mirroring what `workbench.editor.labelFormat` already does, so the setting applies to already-open tabs without a reload.

### Verification

- 4 new unit tests in `multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` (default, `short`, `detail`, and preview-tab decoration).
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium` → 28271 passing, 133 pending, 2 failing; both failures reproduce on a clean tree and are unrelated (`AutomationsCardsWidget`, `ChatStatusDashboard`).
- `MultiEditorTabsControl` suite: 26 passing, 0 failing.
- `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck`, `npm run valid-layers-check` and `eslint` on the changed files are all clean.
- Only Chromium was run locally (Firefox/WebKit builds not installed); CI covers the rest.

pull_requests.title: [WIP] Add canvases to saved chats in the Agents window
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Adds a **default-off, source-built local desktop preview** of runtime-owned canvases in the Agents window. Existing Copilot canvas extensions keep their original source directories, runtime, HTTP/SSE interaction and provider-owned data; VS Code supplies exact-chat ownership and isolated native editor presentation.

The first release is intentionally limited to **existing, persisted chats**. The user sends a normal first request before canvases become available. Canvas-first/zero-turn chat creation is deferred.

This is the original-directory compatibility implementation, separate from #335902. It does not modify or supersede that parallel implementation's PRs.

## First-release scope

- Untitled sessions and untitled peer chats do not expose a canvas facet or command target.
- The Agent Host rejects initialize, open, action and provider-restart effects for an unused draft.
- Initial SDK session creation does **not** request extensions. After the first request makes the chat durable, explicit canvas initialization starts extensions on the resident session. A cold resume may request them during resume.
- The integration no longer calls `session.retain`, stores retained execution intent, or promotes a draft from canvas membership.
- Canvas membership recorded in an already-persisted chat can still restore after restart. Restoring an editor remains metadata-only and obtains a fresh source without replaying the open or an action.

Canvas-first creation, durable zero-turn owners and their automatic recovery can be designed separately using host-owned persistence. They are not silently preserved through another API in this PR.

## Included

- Canonical AHP canvas state, discovery, lifecycle and action routing, with separately negotiated explicit provider initialization.
- Host-approved extension launch using exact `sessionId` and the runtime's original `defaultLaunch`, strict version-1 negotiation, cancellation/disconnect fencing and no fallback after denial.
- Deterministic extension/readiness handling and resident-session contribution attachment for persisted chats.
- Workspace Trust as a hard prerequisite for project-extension execution, with separate approvals preserved for user/plugin/session sources, credentials and recovery.
- Provider-neutral Sessions projection and native canvas editors. Tab close, hiding and owner switching detach presentation; logical close and provider restart remain separate explicit operations.
- User-only native isolation, separate browser permissions and file trust, cancellation-safe choosers, accessibility/help and theme integration. Canvas pages do not become ordinary browser/model automation targets.
- A guarded backport over SDK `1.0.15-preview.2` / CLI `1.0.89-1`. The current-main package is patched as a complete image; the obsolete public-1.0.13/B3 transition route has been removed.

The presentation setting `sessions.experimental.canvases.enabled` defaults to false. Actual canvas support additionally requires a non-built development environment and an explicitly selected compatible runtime through `VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_CANVAS_RUNTIME_PATH`.

## Persisted-chat startup flow

For a new chat, the SDK session starts without extensions. The normal first request creates durable user/assistant history. When the user later selects **Initialize Canvas Providers** or opens a canvas, VS Code:

1. rechecks the owning session and Workspace Trust;
2. attaches the existing runtime session to the canvas launch context;
3. explicitly reloads extensions;
4. applies source approval and the launch-v1 callback;
5. waits for complete extension and canvas registry readiness;
6. exposes/open the requested canvas.

For a cold existing chat, resume can request extensions during resume. Neither path fabricates a chat turn or calls `sessions.save` during admission.

## Workspace Trust execution boundary

Workspace Trust is owned by VS Code, not by the Copilot runtime:

- New folder-backed sessions and first/follow-up sends already use the normal session trust gates.
- Canvas initialize, open, action and provider restart re-enter `ISessionsService.canExecuteSession`, including when trust was revoked from an already-active session.
- Every execution workspace folder is checked, including VS Code-created worktrees. Missing workspace metadata blocks execution until it hydrates.
- Catalog refresh and source resolution remain non-starting. Logical close remains available for cleanup after trust is removed.
- Immediately before launch, the Copilot adapter also rechecks the actual working directory plus the original and canonical extension entrypoint, preventing a changed symlink or late revocation from authorizing execution.

Workspace Trust is not a Node sandbox, content-bound package approval or replacement for extension/credential/browser/file/recovery permissions.

## Dependency alignment

- Runtime stack 1/4: github/copilot-agent-runtime#22702, head `31879439` — generic numeric schema-constant generation. Its repository CI is green.
- Runtime stack 2/4: github/copilot-agent-runtime#22714, head `b6467d5e` — launch-v1 contract, exact owner/default recipe, fail-closed resolver, exact upstream native resume lock-order fix `8f00ab12`, and deterministic CI fixtures. This is the direct SDK wire dependency. Public runtimes `1.0.89-0` and `1.0.89-1` predate the native fix.
- Runtime stack 3/4: github/copilot-agent-runtime#22718, head `b5526e14` — resident attachment, deterministic readiness, privileged-callback ordering and initial script safety.
- Runtime stack 4/4: github/copilot-agent-runtime#20368, head `e6668e8b` — the two-file persisted-chat integration proof plus a test-only background-interrupt routing precondition.
- Node SDK: github/copilot-sdk#2637, head `82916669`. All 93 current-head checks pass (78 existing path-selected skips, zero failures/pending). CI fixes are limited to test/fixture ownership and strict replay history; production SDK, generated schemas, pins and carrier bytes are unchanged.
- AHP: microsoft/agent-host-protocol#447, canonical revision `cd05c63c`. No persisted-chat scope change was required.
- VS Code carrier: SDK `1.0.15-preview.2` / CLI `1.0.89-1`, patch SHA-256 `987c431f47a68ba6c10d20223405223ac745e4bcad00df62d0c450fdab16a6f9`. Final integrated qualification requires a newly published runtime that contains `8f00ab12`; the later publication timestamp of `1.0.89-1` does not imply that it contains the fix.

These are candidate contracts, not published SDK/runtime releases. Aligned review and releases remain required before replacing the private carrier or enabling the feature by default.

## Validation

The current VS Code head `adefbd95` is reconciled with current main and passed:

- all 35 repository-native hosted checks, including compile/hygiene, all platform Electron/browser/remote lanes, Copilot tests, screenshots, Monaco, CodeQL, metadata, dependency and license checks;
- client and build-tool typechecking plus valid-layers;
- hygiene, changed-file ESLint/stylelint and normal signed commit hooks;
- focused unit selections with 494, 1,051, 1,211, 562, 828 and 1,096 passing tests;
- provider integration selections with 7, 11 and 5 passing tests;
- 30/30 carrier tests plus root and remote installation verification.
- the runtime MCP E2E replay 4/4 twice after adding deterministic warm-up turns and re-recording four Copilot fixtures.

Runtime and SDK PRs have their own focused generation/build/test evidence. SDK's previously failing freshness, macOS Node and macOS Rust jobs are repaired; its full current-head matrix is green.

Runtime CI is not uniformly green and is not represented as such. Layer 1 and the top are terminal green. Layer 2 has zero native/test failures; its only two reds are a GitHub HTTP-500 review-dispatcher reconciliation and its aggregate. Layer 3 has two unresolved root failures plus aggregates: a pending-work handoff result and one extension-environment permission prompt attempt. The one authorized pending-work proof compiled and ran but was inconclusive because its warm assertion misread `sessionWasActive` and its cold fixture was not persisted. The environment-access failure cannot be assigned because the CI artifact omits the terminal resume/peer-exit/extension-launch witness. No failure is waived.

No Code OSS/Electron/native application qualification was rerun for this scope change.

## Historical qualification boundary

Earlier native qualification belongs to older heads that supported canvas-first retention and used older runtime/SDK images. It remains useful evidence for native presentation, isolation, reload, close and restoration mechanics, but it does **not** qualify this persisted-chat head or its new B4/runtime pair.

## Draft gates and limits

- All four runtime stack PRs, SDK and AHP review/release alignment are still required.
- The feature remains default-off and development-runtime-only.
- VS Code, SDK, runtime layer 1 and the runtime top are green. Runtime layer 2 retains only an infrastructure review-dispatcher failure; runtime layer 3 remains red and needs separately authorized corrected diagnostic proofs before further evidence-backed source work. No baseline or failing check is waived.
- A newly published runtime containing `8f00ab12` is required before final consumer qualification; neither public `1.0.89-0` nor `1.0.89-1` contains it.
- Application qualification against the aligned persisted-chat runtime/SDK is still required.
- Other native platforms, all source scopes, physical assistive technology, every model/resume combination, remote/Web execution and native Office built-ins are not qualified by this preview.

pull_requests.title: Speed up component fixture execution
pull_requests.body:
Speed up the full Component Fixtures workload without skipping checks, fixtures, or leak detection.

- Capture allocation and timer-scheduling errors immediately, but defer expensive stack formatting and source-map expansion until diagnostics need the stack.
- Initialize source maps once, before asynchronous fixture-render timeouts start, so cold-cache error fixtures still render successfully.
- Distribute independent Playwright tests within files across the existing worker pool.
- Add regression tests for lazy stack formatting, leak reporting, and preservation of original allocation/scheduling locations.

## Motivation and measurements

The Component Fixtures job on #335932 took 20m17s, including 13m05s capturing screenshots and 5m44s running interaction tests. Profiling identified eager source-mapped diagnostic stack formatting as a major rendering cost.

Local before/after measurements used the same Windows checkout, Chromium version, complete fixture list, two Playwright workers, and an already-running fixture server:

| Workload | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All 1,765 fixture screenshots | 589.74s | 332.82s | 43.6% |
| All 15 interaction tests | 82.79s | 76.42s | 7.7% |
| Combined | 672.53s | 409.24s | 39.1% |

## Summary

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42182471-09a8-46b9-b2e5-a9480c932864

Add `/sandbox-policy` to Copilot agent-host sessions. The VS Code command invokes the SDK's existing `/sandbox policy` command and presents its effective policy as a persisted Markdown report, without starting a model turn or changing sandbox enforcement.

## User experience

- Offer `/sandbox-policy` in slash-command completion while keeping native `/sandbox` subcommands hidden.
- Show an **Open Sandbox Policy** link in the response that opens the formatted report in Markdown preview.
- Use normal theme-aware chat link colors, including hover and active states.
- Support mouse, Enter, and Space activation, with accessible-help guidance.
- Save a unique report for each invocation so earlier links continue to show their original snapshots.

## Implementation

- Introduce optional host-side `getInvocation` and `getOutput` hooks on resolved slash commands, separate from SDK catalog metadata. Omitted hooks or hooks returning `undefined` preserve the existing SDK invocation and output behavior.
- Support structured text and link output with optional Markdown and preview flags. Keep command lifecycle, mode handling, and runtime-settings invalidation in the session.
- Keep sandbox-specific argument validation, SDK mapping, policy formatting, and report persistence in `CopilotSandboxPolicyDisplay`.
- Strip ANSI styling, preserve SDK Markdown, format recognized terminal policy reports, and safely fence unrecognized plain text. Propagate invocation and file-write failures instead of emitting broken links.
- Preserve preview metadata across local and remote Agent Host URI rewriting without passing it to filesystem providers.
- Extract a reusable single-anchor rendering helper to avoid a second anchor scan. Repeated decoration does not register duplicate widgets or listeners.
- Reuse the shared SDK command type in completion handling.

## Compatibility

- Existing commands retain their default invocation and rendering when no custom behavior applies.
- Preserve native sandbox aliases and raw SDK input; do not format unrelated sandbox subcommands or client commands as policy reports.
- Reserve the host alias against runtime name collisions and keep it discoverable when SDK command discovery fails.
- No SDK dependency changes, new permissions, or sandbox-policy enforcement changes.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: isolate CopilotAgent tests from ambient COPILOT_HOME
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #335887

## Problem

Three `CopilotAgent` tests fail on a clean checkout when `COPILOT_HOME` is set:

| Test | Line |
| --- | --- |
| `resolves state files from the default and peer chat SDK backings` | 1323 |
| `a marker written after an initial read miss is picked up without a restart` | 8549 |
| `collectDebugLogs includes persisted events for a closed session` | 11419 |

They inject `userHome: URI.file('/home/test')`, but `getCopilotHomePath` prefers the ambient variable, so session-state lookups resolve outside the test sandbox and return `undefined`. CI never sets `COPILOT_HOME`, so CI stays green.

## Change

Clear `COPILOT_HOME` in a suite-level `setup` and restore it in `teardown`, so every test under `suite('CopilotAgent')` sees the injected home. This is the same save/delete/restore already used by one test in this file and six in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts`; the per-test copy is now redundant and removed.
