pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Add a default-off local canvas development preview to the Agents Window, backed by approved Copilot SDK extension packages and source-resolved native browser surfaces.

This is a work-in-progress integration PR, not a request to enable the feature generally or publish the companion SDK/runtime changes.

### Included

- Canonical AHP canvas state and operations, generation/revision guards, bounded operation deduplication, and exact owning-chat routing.
- Inert package preparation, immutable reviewed snapshots, explicit revision/workspace or shared-host approval, revocation, and document data kept outside code.
- Canvas-first session retention, provider lifecycle/disposal fixes, explicit restart versus page reload, and stable restoration without persisting live endpoint authority.
- Provider-neutral Sessions controls, authoring starter, visible/removable request-frozen canvas context, automatic active-chat reveal, and inert hidden/restored instances.
- Native Integrated Browser app policy, semantic themes, permissions/navigation controls and ownership/lifecycle handling.
- Genuine joined-SDK user-message projection so canvas-originated requests appear in chat with normal tool confirmation and cancellation. The host does not resend the prompt.
- Focused unit/integration coverage and isolated developer launch/runbook support.

The five JavaScript allowlist additions are executable extension/browser fixtures and the no-build authoring starter; those files intentionally run as delivered rather than requiring TypeScript transpilation. The allowlist still requires normal CODEOWNERS review.

## Validation

- Latest affected Copilot live-session/history selection: **492 passing**, with targeted typecheck and uncached lint clean.
- Automatic presentation/facade selection: **99 passing**, plus actual native model-driven reveal and hidden-tab refresh checks.
- Earlier scoped native/lifecycle/load qualification is documented in the implementation runbooks. Counts from overlapping runs are not added together.
- Real macOS arm64 native chess exercised actual model actions, explicit per-call approval, denial, cancellation, a permission wait beyond 120 seconds, reload, and provider restart while preserving data and the complete approved snapshot.
- The standalone repaired chess ZIP is a separate local deliverable, not included in this source PR; its 125 packaged core/browser tests passed.
- With the corrected companion runtime, the complete opt-in public SDK integration file is now **3 passing**, including the formerly failing package-approval-after-an-existing-turn case.
- Final commit preparation passed the normal VS Code pre-commit hygiene hook (181 checked files). Its formatting findings were fixed without changing behavior; protocol braces were corrected in the canonical AHP source and re-synced, not patched in generated copies.

## Public companion drafts

- github/copilot-sdk#2630 — public Node SDK launch authorization and retention.
- microsoft/agent-host-protocol#443 — canonical renderer-neutral canvas contract and complete native-client generation at `46a47524`.

The compatible runtime change is tracked separately in its existing private repository.

## Remaining WIP gates

- The separately reproduced `Hook processor is not configured` resume failure was fixed in the companion runtime's lifecycle handling, without a VS Code workaround. Repeated unchanged SDK reproductions and actual native existing-chat package approval now pass. Consuming released dependency versions is still separate from the isolated development-build validation.
- The normal-workspace execution route is qualified only for the local macOS arm64 development setup with explicitly selected compatible SDK/runtime artifacts. Other native platforms, built-product enablement and normal dependency-release integration remain gated.
- Real assistive-technology qualification remains outstanding.
- Coordinated dependency releases remain separate from this draft. AHP's seven language/check jobs now pass without a provisional version bump.

## Review and verification follow-up (2026-09-13)

- All reported inline review threads are addressed: resource trust is requested unconditionally for the captured effective worktree, and package selection/approval use that same directory.
- Native testing exposed and fixed first-worktree materialization revoking a newly bound launch lease, and immediate opening after approval failing to refresh an already initialized empty catalog.
- Windows failures are repaired without weakening package quotas or execution authority: platform-correct file identity, verified immutable-snapshot reuse, and actual process termination rather than Unix signal-handler breadcrumbs. The deliberately large 2,048-file quota test has an explicit filesystem I/O budget.
- Local validation: 20 tests across the three real canvas integration files, final 17-test lifecycle and 32-test package selections, client typecheck, scoped lint, and normal commit hygiene pass. These are overlapping selections, not an additive total.
- Real macOS arm64 OSS: a first worktree turn succeeded; approval/open worked immediately afterward; two independent chess documents and the public greeting package worked in one retained conversation. A canvas-originated model request appeared in chat and waited for explicit tool approval. A rejected invalid move input caused no mutation; the legal retry moved exactly one piece.
- Package refresh and explicit provider restart preserved documents and replaced origins. The old origin was explicitly CSP-blocked. Hide/reveal, attaching/removing/submitting a URL-free canvas reference, and closing just one logical instance passed. All 18 captured owned process-tree PIDs exited afterward.
- All 32 executable checks pass at final head `5d9864b8adb`, including compile, unit, browser, integration and smoke checks across Windows, macOS and Linux.
- The screenshot failure was an actual fixture setup regression: `NewChatView` required the view-state service but the new-chat fixture did not register it. Signed follow-up `5d9864b8adb` adds that real fixture-local service. All 42 affected Dark/Light fixtures render and dispose without errors; representative composers and attachment controls render again. All 16 blank-image baseline replacements were rejected, and no blocking hashes were changed. [Exact-head screenshot/fixture CI passes](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34776003713), as does [exact-head platform CI](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34776003863). ## sdk-vscode-bump-fix status

**Validation stage:** `pr-checks` (cycle 1) — **blocked, escalated**

### SDK+CLI correlation & compatibility
- **CLI-only** bump: `@github/copilot` `1.0.84-4` → `1.0.84-5`; `@github/copilot-sdk` stays `1.0.13` (root + `remote/`). Pins verified; `extensions/copilot` untouched.
- Published package layout diff shows **no path changes** for the CLI or any platform payload — the delta is runtime behavior only. The installed CLI `changelog.json` for `1.0.84-5` names the exact drivers: **"Subagent launches honor explicit model, reasoning effort, and context tier preferences from applicable global and custom instructions"** (`copilot-agent-runtime#20004`) and **"Streaming responses preserve message chunk ordering before final output."**
- Slack canary insights reference a **different** pair (`sdk=1.0.14-canary.*`, `cli=1.0.84-canary.*`), so they are not exact-pair evidence. The SDK-compatibility digest shows SDK `1.0.13` is published and consumable, so **no SDK bump is required**. This is a genuine VS Code-side integration signal for the exact pinned pair.

### Root cause (from the authoritative PR-check failure + installed CLI changelog; local E2E replay is unavailable — the sandbox has no network and the Electron download fails by design)
- PR checks: every job green **except** the three `*/ Electron` jobs, which fail **identically** — one cross-platform Agent Host E2E integration failure, not compile/hygiene/product-code (Compile & Hygiene, Electron-Unit/Smoke, Remote, Browser, CLI, Copilot-Test all pass; core `compile-src` reproduced locally with **0 errors**).
- The Copilot Agent Host E2E suite reports **194 passing / 18 pending / 2 failing**, both in `suites/subagentSuite.ts`:
  1. **`custom subagent permits requested file output in its system instructions`** (the `discover`-mode variant only; the two `scan`-mode siblings sharing the same `childTurns: [Complete]` assertion still pass) — the child chat now reports **two** `TurnState.Complete` turns instead of one. Child/parent response contents are unchanged (`CUSTOM_AGENT_CHILD_OK` / `PARENT_DONE`); only the child turn *count* differs.
  2. **`retained background subagent completes repeated follow-up turns`** — an AHP-traffic snapshot mismatch. Every functional assertion passes (child/parent contents, counts, states); only the *ordering* of one out-of-band `session/chatAdded` catalog event differs (now emitted at the later `read_agent` tool-call instead of at the `task` spawn call, within the same parent turn).
- Mechanism: CLI `1.0.84-5` changed subagent-launch behavior (honoring custom/global instruction preferences — active in `discover` mode) and message/event ordering. VS Code faithfully reflects the runtime's new subagent turn/spawn timing via the task-status reconciliation added in #335361 (`copilotAgentSession._reconcileSubagentTaskStatuses`, throttled off `onBackgroundTasksChanged`). **No VS Code product code is provably wrong**, and there is no compile/type/packaging change to make.

### Why no edit was pushed this cycle
- **Failure 2 is the hard blocker:** the only fix is regenerating the committed Agent Host fixture `providers/__snapshots__/Agent_Host_E2E___Copilot_retained_background_subagent_completes_repeated_follow-up_turns.traffic.ahp.yaml`. This workflow is **not permitted** to regenerate or edit committed `*.traffic.ahp.yaml` fixtures, and a harness "normalization" would wrongly mask a deliberately-retained catalog-event signal.
- **Failure 1 is not a safe assertion edit:** although `subagentSuite.ts` is test code (not a fixture), the intended contract is **not established**. The prior cycle's reported local replay showed this test *passing* (`1 failing`) while CI shows it *failing* (`2 failing`) on the identical commit `39076f5`, and the captured Copilot runtime log shows the child ran only **one** turn — consistent with a **non-deterministic reconciliation race** (real, unmocked subagent task-status polling), not a clean deterministic new turn. Baking `childTurns: [Complete, Complete]` into the assertion would risk **masking a regression**, which is disallowed, and cannot be confirmed without running the real Agent Host E2E (impossible in this sandbox). Even a correct failure-1 fix cannot turn the stage green while failure 2 blocks it.

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Keep late-discovered background agents from remaining generic tools or disappearing into completed-step disclosures, including when a nested worker is still active after its parent finishes.
- Preserve sibling tool content, keyboard focus, and observer cleanup when a completed tool is promoted to the shared subagent pill.
- Show the child's known model at startup rather than waiting for usage or completion. Carry canonical model identity through live progress and restored history so matching models, including BYOK display-name variants, do not produce redundant labels. Preserve Auto routing on configuration-only updates.
- Make synchronous/background progress and navigation parity inspectable with 27 interactive lifecycle fixtures (58 themed variants), using real chat models, pills, child transcripts, and session/chat result links.

## Intended behavior and scope

The clickable pill remains in the response to the request that spawned the child and updates there through startup, follow-ups, and completion. A child first discovered after parent completion is appended to that original response; an existing launch that is reclassified is promoted in place. No pinned activity area or duplicate launch pill is added to later turns. Peer chats and independent sessions retain their structured link presentation.

The separate Autopilot case where task_complete succeeds but the SDK idle/parent turn-complete handoff is missing is not addressed here.

## Validation

- 289 focused cross-layer subagent/background regression tests passed before commit.
- ESLint passed for all 23 changed TypeScript files.
- All 58 themed component captures passed their assertions and disposal checks.
- Browser interaction checks verified pointer/keyboard opening and changing progress in parent and child views, including completed-parent, nested, and retained-worker cases.
- The broader client type check has three previously reproduced SDK baseline errors involving clientInfo and autoTier; no new fixture diagnostics.
- Additional local testing is in progress; this PR is intentionally a draft.

Start the Component Explorer Server and filter for agent-lifecycle. pull_requests.title: mcp: stabilize discovery and coalesce migration refreshes
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Stop migration-panel refresh loops when multiple workspace roots define the same MCP server names.
- Collapse duplicate MCP notifications and migration refresh bursts instead of repeating discovery for every event.
- Cancel obsolete migration discovery when a newer refresh supersedes it or the editor closes, while preserving genuine updates and error reporting.

Fixes #335820

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Installed MCP discovery selected duplicate-name winners from the runtime-dependent display order. Publishing a winner moved it ahead of the other root's entry, which made the other entry win the next discovery pass. Replacing the runtime servers repeated this cycle.

Overlapping workbench subscriptions amplified each replacement into multiple notifications. The migration editor also observed several related inputs and started a computation for each notification. Its sequence guard discarded stale results only after the work had already happened.

### Implementation

- Discovery sorts a copy of the installed inventory by name and ID before applying existing scope precedence. Display ordering remains independent of discovery selection.
- One workbench observer handles runtime inventory and per-server enablement changes, re-sorts the display inventory, and emits the change notification.
- A zero-delay delayer coalesces migration refresh requests within a burst. The generation advances when a refresh is requested, immediately invalidating older work rather than waiting for the replacement computation to start.
- Each active refresh owns a cancellation token. It reaches file and MCP migration computation, destination-folder discovery, and MCP source-file reads. Cancelled planning stops before reading additional roots.
- Closing, recreating, or disposing the editor cancels pending work; reopening requests fresh migration information. Generation, session, harness, and cancellation checks prevent late results from being applied, including results from providers that do not cooperate with cancellation.

### Behavior and constraints

- Real configuration, enablement, and policy changes still trigger refreshes. This does not disable discovery or cache migration results indefinitely.
- Expected cancellation is not reported as a failure. Genuine computation errors remain visible and retryable.
- Scope precedence, display ordering, policy filters, workspace-root discovery exclusions, and guarded migration writes remain unchanged.
- The cross-root duplicate-name migration restriction tracked by #335884 is intentionally unchanged; this change fixes refresh behavior, not which same-name entries may migrate.

</details>

pull_requests.title: Validate OSC 633 CWD reports with shell integration nonces
pull_requests.body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335858

- Require process-terminal OSC 633 CWD updates to carry the terminal's exact, non-empty shell integration nonce; ignore missing, empty, or mismatched reports while preserving the prior CWD.
- Keep nonce-less CWD reports working for extension-owned and custom pseudoterminals, while marking those updates as untrusted.
- Keep nonce-less reports from manually integrated nested or relayed process shells rejected because the nonce is intentionally removed from the environment; those shells may retain the parent CWD until a trusted report resumes.
- Update the compatibility policy when a terminal is reused, so process and custom-PTY tasks cannot inherit each other's behavior.
- Carry extension ownership through remote launch transport and persistent process details.
- Apply the same compatibility policy in the PTY-host recorder so completed and partial command CWD metadata survives replay.
- Restore extension ownership through an ownership-only process property before persistent replay, without overwriting the restored executable, arguments, environment, or CWD.
- Append the same nonce to serialized CWD reports from Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, and task startup.
- Keep the Fish nonce in global shell scope so prompt hooks can include it after initialization.
- Emit the PowerShell CWD nonce as prompt output, matching the existing nonce-bearing `EnvJson` report; Windows 10 prompt rendering still requires manual verification.
- Rewrite task `initialText` to the live or persisted terminal nonce during reuse and reconnection for both string and object forms.
- Keep Agent Host property parsing compatible with the optional nonce without including it in the decoded CWD or changing terminal-management policy.
- Keep OSC 7, OSC 9;9, OSC 1337, and Agent Host CWD trust policy unchanged; this PR is scoped to Workbench OSC 633 handling.

## Testing

- Passed 57 targeted Node tests with 9 expected platform skips, covering PTY-host recorder metadata, reattach/revive ordering, remote server transport, Agent Host parser compatibility, and shell emitters.
- Passed 188 targeted Electron tests with 2 existing pending cases, covering strict process-terminal validation, live reuse transitions, remote client transport, persistent extension-terminal reconstruction, old editor-state hydration, serialized delimiters, task startup, and reused-terminal nonce rewriting.
- Passed Bash, Zsh, and Fish syntax and runtime checks.
- Passed `transpile-client`, targeted ESLint, full repository hygiene, and diff checks.
- PowerShell runtime was unavailable on macOS. Its source emission is covered by the terminal environment test suite, but visible prompt rendering on Windows 10 has not been manually verified.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- OSC 633 CWD argument framing comes from [`ShellIntegrationAddon` property handling](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/xterm/shellIntegrationAddon.ts#L571-L590); this keeps the serialized property in the first argument and the terminal nonce in the second.
- Separate nonce framing follows the existing shell command reports in [Bash](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration-bash.sh#L350-L356), [Zsh](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration-rc.zsh#L256-L260), [Fish](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.fish#L104-L119), and [PowerShell](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.ps1#L134-L145).
- Task CWD serialization and nonce placement follow [`taskShellIntegrationStartSequence`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/browser/terminalTaskSystem.ts#L182-L201).
- Reconnection handling builds on the existing task-terminal reuse flow in [`terminalTaskSystem.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/browser/terminalTaskSystem.ts#L1592-L1603).
- PTY-host command metadata persistence follows the existing [`XtermSerializer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L1033-L1059) and process-detail reconstruction path in [`PtyService`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L638-L664).
- Remote ownership transport follows the existing client mapping in [`RemoteTerminalBackend`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/remoteTerminalBackend.ts#L184-L197) and server mapping in [`RemoteTerminalChannel`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/server/node/remoteTerminalChannel.ts#L193-L211).
- Ownership-only editor hydration follows the existing process-property dispatch in [`TerminalInstance`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts#L1558-L1583).
- Agent Host compatibility parsing follows the existing command-line nonce separation in [`Osc633Parser`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/osc633Parser.ts#L122-L138).

issues.title: Very slow interactions between chats
issues.body:
Testing #339594

I had one interaction where I asked a chat to reach out to two other side chats, just to ask for a code word that I had shared with those chats and it took 5 minutes to get through.

1. establish 3 chats within one session
2. give the two side chats a code word to share with other agents that ask for it.
3. have the main chat session ask for code words from the side chats

copilot's analysis:

## Actual latency breakdown

| Inbound reply | Registered as main-chat turn | Reached SDK agent | Model response | Pre-agent delay |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Waterfall | 11:32:40.088 | 11:33:29.101 | 5.7 s | **49.0 s** |
| Terminal confirmation | 11:33:35.062 | 11:35:19.966 | 5.4 s | **104.9 s** |
| Quick confirmation | 11:35:25.512 | 11:36:06.713 | 4.1 s | **41.2 s** |
| Tacos | 11:36:11.913 | 11:36:31.804 | 4.6 s | **19.9 s** |

Across those four turns:

- Total elapsed turn time: approximately **237 seconds**
- Actual model-response time: approximately **20 seconds**
- Time before the agent received the messages: approximately **215 seconds**

So about **91% of the delay was not model inference**.

## What happened during the delay

For every inbound cross-chat reply, the pattern was:

1. Agent Host registered the new main-chat turn.
2. The current SDK session shut down.
3. The SDK session resumed.
4. There was a long silent interval.
5. Only then did the session log record the inbound message as `user.message`.
6. The model answered normally in 4–6 seconds.

For example, the Terminal confirmation:

- 11:33:35.062 — new main-chat turn registered
- 11:33:36.549 — session shut down
- 11:33:37.062 — session resumed
- 11:35:19.966 — SDK finally received the user message
- 11:35:25.345 — model response completed

That is a **103-second resume-to-delivery gap**, followed by a normal five-second model call.

issues.title: Agents: #339409 peer-chat recovery is undone when the phantom comes from a never-sent peer chat
issues.body:
Follow-up to #339409 / #339476.

The recovery in #339476 can restore a session's peer chats and then lose them again within a second. This happens when the phantom registration was created by a peer chat that never sent a message. The phantom is never unregistered, its restore erases the recovered catalogue, and the recovery is already marked `completed`, so it never runs again.

- VS Code Version: 1.141.0-insider, commit `ae1080a9ed1098a8b532c6cfd50977d784b29e6d` (contains #339476)
- OS Version: macOS
- Feature: Agents Window, local Agent Host / Copilot CLI, multi-chat sessions

## Steps to Reproduce

Session state before updating to a build that contains #339476 (all of it produced by the #339409 regression):

1. Parent session `copilotcli:/P` had 10 peer chats. One of them, `C0`, was created but **never sent a turn**.
2. Phantoms `copilotcli:/P#C0`, `copilotcli:/P#C1` and `copilotcli:/P#C2` were registered with `source = restore`. The parent's `peerChats` metadata had been erased to `[]`.
3. Update to the build above and launch.

## Expected

All recoverable peer chats are restored. Every phantom is unregistered so it cannot run the #339409 erase path again.

## Actual

```text
12:08:36.923 [info]    [AgentHostPeerChatStore] Recovered 8 peer chats affected by #339409 for copilotcli:/P
12:08:37.587 [warning] [AgentService] Skipping peer-chat catalog entry 0 that is not owned by copilotcli:/P#C0
   … entries 1-7 …
12:11:34.434 [info]    [AgentService] Restored session copilotcli:/P#C0 with 15 turns
```

- The two phantoms of chats that had sent turns (`C1`, `C2`) were unregistered. The phantom for `C0` stayed registered.
- About 0.7 s after recovery, the `C0` phantom was restored. It rejected all 8 entries and wrote `peerChats = []` to the parent again, so the sidebar again shows the parent with no peer chats.
- The parent's `agentHost.peerChatRecovery339409` marker already reads `{"recovered":[…8 chats…],"completed":true}`, so later launches never retry.
- Later in the same run, selecting the parent restored the phantom again (`Restored session copilotcli:/P#C0 with 15 turns`), followed by `Catalog synchronization for copilotcli:/P#C0 remains pending: acknowledgementSuperseded`. The phantom stays registered.

The other two affected sessions on this machine had only sent-to peer-chat phantoms. Both recovered correctly and stayed recovered.

## Root cause

In [`recoverChatSelectionCorruption`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ae1080a9ed1098a8b532c6cfd50977d784b29e6d/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostPeerChatStore.ts#L87), a selected phantom is verified only if its chat backing database has `agentHost.chatProviderData`:

```ts
if (!await backing.object.getMetadata(CHAT_PROVIDER_DATA_METADATA_KEY)) {
    continue;           // never reaches verifiedPhantomChatIds.push(chatId)
}
```

A peer chat that never sent a turn has no `agentHost.chatProviderData`: its backing DB has 0 rows in `turns`. An SDK session was created for it, but its storage has 0 turns too. As a result:

1. `C0` is not added to `verifiedPhantomChatIds`.
2. [`_recoverChatSelectionCorruption`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ae1080a9ed1098a8b532c6cfd50977d784b29e6d/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L3357) unregisters only verified phantoms, so the `C0` phantom stays registered.
3. The recovery still completes, because the other phantoms were verified, and it writes `completed: true`.
4. Startup restores the remaining phantom. It hits the original #339409 path ("Skipping peer-chat catalog entry N that is not owned by …#C0") and erases the parent catalogue that was just recovered.

After that the session cannot recover by itself:
- `completed: true` blocks any further recovery.
- With the marker removed but the phantom still unverifiable, `if (verifiedPhantomChatIds.length === 0) return;` exits before doing anything. The `C0` phantom is now the only one left.

## Manual workaround (confirmed)

With VS Code quit:
1. Delete `agentHost.peerChatRecovery339409` from the parent's `session.db`.
2. Add `agentHost.chatProviderData` to the `C0` chat's backing `session.db`.

On the next launch, the recovery verified the `C0` phantom, logged `Recovered 8 peer chats…`, and unregistered the phantom. There were no further `not owned by` warnings, and the catalogue has stayed intact since.

## Suggested fix

Something along these lines:

- Verify a *selected* phantom from evidence that does not depend on the chat having sent a turn. For example: the backing chat dir resolves to the parent (the path check that already exists), plus the phantom's own `restore` registration.
- Or always unregister restore-created, fragment-bearing `copilotcli` registrations whose parent is registered. A fragment-bearing session URI is never valid once #339074 is reverted, and unregistering does not touch shared storage.
- Avoid writing `completed: true` while an unverified fragment phantom of the same parent is still registered, so a later launch can retry.

issues.title: ChatGPT sidebar header controls become unclickable in Integrated Browser at wider viewport widths
issues.body:
Type: Bug Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.140.0 - OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (build 26200) Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open VS Code's Integrated Browser and navigate to `https://chatgpt.com/`. 2. Sign in with a ChatGPT Plus account. 3. Make the Integrated Browser editor area relatively wide. 4. Try clicking the controls at the top of the ChatGPT sidebar: - ChatGPT / Codex selector - Search button - Sidebar toggle button 5. The controls remain visible, but do not respond to mouse clicks. 6. Resize the Integrated Browser to a narrower width. 7. Try the same controls again. They become clickable. Additional observations: - The issue is dependent on the Integrated Browser viewport width. - Other parts of the ChatGPT page remain interactive. - The issue reproduces when signed in with a ChatGPT Plus account. - The issue does not reproduce when logged out. - The issue does not reproduce when signed in with a ChatGPT Free account. - Other ChatGPT plans have not been tested. - ChatGPT works normally in a regular desktop browser. - The issue still reproduces when VS Code is launched with `code --disable-extensions`. - The issue also reproduces in the latest VS Code Insiders build. This appears to depend on both the viewport width and the ChatGPT account state/plan. One possibility is that a UI element present for Plus accounts overlaps these sidebar controls or otherwise affects hit testing at certain responsive-layout widths, but I have not identified the exact cause. issues.title: MCP resource URI templates incorrectly encode non-ASCII variable values
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Reproduced against `main` at `3d5764c14dea123b0fd50fb61788328c33c076b8` on Linux with Node.js 22.22.1, using the actual `UriTemplate` source. This is a source-level reproduction, without extensions or a live MCP server session.

`UriTemplate` percent-encodes UTF-16 code units instead of UTF-8 bytes. This affects non-ASCII values entered for an MCP resource template: `mcpResourceQuickAccess.ts` collects the variable text and calls `resolveURI`, and `mcpServer.ts` resolves it through this helper.

To reproduce in the existing `UriTemplate` unit suite:

```ts
const template = UriTemplate.parse('resource://docs/{name}');
template.resolve({ name: 'café' });
// Actual:   resource://docs/caf%E9
// Expected: resource://docs/caf%C3%A9

template.resolve({ name: '中文' });
// Actual:   resource://docs/%4E2D%6587
// Expected: resource://docs/%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87

template.resolve({ name: '🚀' });
// Actual:   resource://docs/%D83D%DE80
// Expected: resource://docs/%F0%9F%9A%80
```

The accented and emoji results fail `decodeURIComponent`; the Chinese result decodes to different characters. Prefix expansion also counts UTF-16 units: `{name:1}` should retain the whole first emoji, rather than splitting its surrogate pair.

[RFC 6570](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6570.html#section-3.2.1) specifies UTF-8 percent-encoding and Unicode-character prefix lengths. The previous low-control padding fix in #323012 does not address these non-ASCII values.

A focused correction and regression tests are prepared: UTF-8 encoding while preserving ASCII punctuation escaping, plus code-point prefix slicing. I plan to submit the linked fix. AI assistance was used for the investigation; the reported outputs were reproduced against the actual source.

issues.title: Copilot agent host (Copilot CLI) sessions load no user or workspace instruction files on macOS
issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version:
- VS Code: 1.140.0 (commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74)
- OS: macOS 26.6.2
- Feature: agent mode, regular ole' honkin chat UI panel, both in 'Autopilot' mode and 'Interactive'
- Selected model: Sonnet 5.5
- Logs: couldn't find any major logs that I felt comfortable sharing. 

Custom instructions I have used for years are not included in the system prompt of agent host sessions. The editing UI still lists and edits them, and the Local agent still loads them. After the latest update, none of them reach the agent.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/prompts/general.md (or whatever filename of your choiuce) and fill with instructions.
2. Also create ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md with the same rule, and .github/copilot-instructions.md in the open workspace, just for good measure.
3. Start a new Copilot agent host session in that workspace and ask along the lines of "Do you see any custom instructions?"
4. Inspect the system.message event in ~/.copilot/session-state/<session file id thing>/events.jsonl and the agent host log.

None of them are seemingly getting to the agent, and this symptom started with the "new" experience (some popup about Copilot is different now; I dismissed it and promptly forget what it was talking about. whoops.)

## Notes

- Checked in new sessions started after the files were created, as well as existing sessions. No diff.
- The system.message in events.jsonl contains none of the text from any of the three files. 
- The agent host log shows the same customization every time, before and after the files existed: Resolved system message: mode=customize sections=[identity:replace, tool_instructions:append] +content(length 1178)
- The files are valid and the VS Code UI lists them. The same files worked in earlier versions.
- No setting in settings.json disables or relocates them.
- I can Cmd+P and `> Conf` and get to the UX to change my old instruction files. If this is expected to be discontinued, that UX shouldn't be there. But, I assume that's not what's happening seeing as the other copilot.md files are being ignored too.

issues.title: fix: guard stale ghost text screen reader rendering (fixes #339819)
issues.body:
### Summary While rendering ghost text (inline completions) for the screen reader, `GhostText.renderForScreenReader` builds a `TextEdit` whose replacement positions are taken from the cached ghost-text part columns. When the current editor line has become shorter than the cached ghost text expects (the document was edited during the deliberate `timeout(50)` + `waitForState` delay before the delayed screen-reader announcement), the line-capping step is a no-op and a replacement lands past the end of the capped text. `TextEdit.apply` then calls `rangeFromPositions(lastEditEnd, endPositionExclusive)` with `start > end`, which throws `BugIndicatingError: start must be before end`. Impact: an unhandled error is logged (921 users on stable 1.140.0) and the screen-reader announcement is lost; it does not crash the editor. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339819 Recommended reviewer: ``@hediet`` ### Culprit Commit Not identified — pre-existing. The `renderForScreenReader` capping logic (`cappedLineText = lineText.substr(0, lastPart.column - 1)`) dates back to the original ghost-text implementation (`7ec64f0dad5d`, 2021) and the `TextEdit`-based rendering (`a9cd99e83e03`, 2024); neither assumes `lineText` may be shorter than the cached part column. The issue itself records a prior occurrence (microsoft/vscode#287069) tracked since 1.97-era builds and anomaly hits in multiple releases, so this is a long-standing latent race re-bucketed for stable 1.140.0, not a new regression from a specific commit. | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — pre-existing | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | Capping logic never handled the case where the live line is shorter than the cached ghost-text columns; surfaced as a new stable bucket, not introduced by a recent change. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ctrl as inlineCompletionsController participant GT as GhostText.renderForScreenReader participant TE as TextEdit.apply participant RFP as rangeFromPositions Ctrl->>Ctrl: timeout(50) + waitForState (document may change) Note over Ctrl: Cached ghost text now stale
vs. current (shorter) line Ctrl->>GT: renderForScreenReader(lineText) Note over GT: ⚠️ Root cause:
substr cannot lengthen lineText;
lastPart.column-1 > lineText.length GT->>TE: applyToString(cappedLineText) TE->>RFP: rangeFromPositions(lastEditEnd, endPositionExclusive) Note over RFP: 💥 start > end
throws "start must be before end" ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/common/core/edits/textEdit.ts` | crash site | L781 (from stack): `throw new BugIndicatingError('start must be before end')` | | `src/vs/editor/common/core/edits/textEdit.ts` | throw path | L145-L146: `const r = rangeFromPositions(lastEditEnd, text.endPositionExclusive)` in `apply()` — `lastEditEnd` can be past `endPositionExclusive` when a replacement sits beyond the capped text | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/model/ghostText.ts` | root cause | L48: `const cappedLineText = lineText.substr(0, lastPart.column - 1)` — `substr` cannot lengthen a too-short line, leaving replacement columns out of range | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/controller/inlineCompletionsController.ts` | trigger | L331-L342: `await timeout(50, ...); await waitForState(...); ... renderForScreenReader(lineText)` — the delay is where the cached ghost text goes stale relative to the live line | ### Repro Steps This is a timing-dependent race between a pending delayed screen-reader announcement and a document edit, so it is non-deterministic. To increase likelihood: 1. Enable a screen reader (or `editor.accessibilitySupport: "on"`) and `editor.screenReaderAnnounceInlineSuggestion`. 2. Trigger an inline completion (ghost text) whose part column is near the end of a line. 3. Within the ~50ms announcement delay (`timeout(50)` + `waitForState` in `inlineCompletionsController`), delete characters on that line / replace the line with a shorter one (e.g. fast backspacing or an external edit) so the live line becomes shorter than the cached ghost-text column. 4. The delayed `renderForScreenReader` runs against the now-shorter line; the capped line is shorter than the last part's column and `TextEdit.apply` throws `start must be before end`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/model/ghostText.ts` → `renderForScreenReader()`: add a guard immediately after computing `lastPart`, before the capping/`TextEdit` construction. When `lastPart.column - 1 > lineText.length`, the cached ghost text is stale relative to the current line (it references columns that no longer exist), so the method returns `''` — the same benign empty-announcement result it already returns when there are no parts. This places the guard at the data producer of the invalid range (the stale snapshot), before the throwing code path is reached, rather than at the crash site in `textEdit.ts`. It does not add a `try/catch`, does not touch `TextEdit.apply`'s invariant (`rangeFromPositions` must keep throwing for genuinely inconsistent edits), and removes no `logService.error`/telemetry. The guard is correct because `GhostText`'s constructor asserts parts are ordered by non-decreasing column (`checkAdjacentItems(parts, (p1, p2) => p1.column <= p2.column)`), so `lastPart` holds the maximum column; if even that column fits within `lineText`, every replacement position is in range and `apply` cannot produce an inverted range. After this change, a stale ghost text can no longer reach `TextEdit.apply` with an out-of-range replacement, so `textEdit.ts:145`/`:781` cannot be driven to throw `start must be before end` from this call site. **Alternatives considered**: - Clamp each part's column to `lineText.length` inside `renderForScreenReader` — rejected: silently relocating the suggestion text produces a misleading screen-reader announcement, and the underlying snapshot is still stale; skipping is the honest result. - Wrap `applyToString` in `try/catch` — rejected: hides the `BugIndicatingError` from the telemetry pipeline and would also swallow genuinely inconsistent edits, masking real bugs instead of fixing the stale-data producer. - Guard inside `textEdit.ts` / `rangeFromPositions` — rejected: that is the crash site and a shared invariant relied on by many callers; weakening it would hide inverted-range bugs across the whole editor. ### Recommended Owner ``@hediet`` — area owner for inline completions (`editor/contrib/inlineCompletions`) and the `editor/common/core/edits` `TextEdit` data structures (authored the `TextEdit`-based ghost-text rendering and the `rangeFromPositions` invariant). Active in `microsoft/vscode` within the last 90 days. --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. The changes have been pushed to the branch [`fix/ghost-text-screen-reader-stale-range-339819-3e7877f43890bd9b`](https://github.com/vscodebot-pr/vscode/tree/fix/ghost-text-screen-reader-stale-range-339819-3e7877f43890bd9b). > > **Original error:** ERR_API: [2026-10-05T15:52:24.217Z] create pull request in microsoft/vscode failed (attempt 1) Original error: Validation Failed: {"resource":"PullRequest","code":"custom","field":"fork_collab","message":"fork_collab Fork collab can't be granted by someone without permission"} - https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#create-a-pull-request Retryable: false Suggestion: This error cannot be resolved by retrying. issues.title: fix: clamp stale inline-edit range in maxContentWidthInRange (fixes #339818)
issues.body:
### Summary The editor throws `BugIndicatingError: Illegal value for lineNumber` from `TextModel.getLineMaxColumn` while measuring line widths for an inline-edit (NES) preview. During a synchronous `undo` the model shrinks, and the inline-edit width `derived` recomputes (it reads `editorObs.versionId`) while the edit's cached `displayRange` / `originalDisplayRange` still references the pre-undo line count. The shared helper `maxContentWidthInRange` then iterates those now-out-of-bounds line numbers against the current (shorter) model, hitting the line-count guard in `getLineMaxColumn`. Impact: a visible unhandled error affecting ~1,000 stable users on 1.140.0 whenever an inline edit is showing as the buffer shrinks underneath it. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339818 Recommended reviewer: ``@hediet`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not identified — pre-existing stale-range pattern | | Author | — | | PR | — | | Message | — | | Why | — | > No single regression commit was confirmed. The `maxContentWidthInRange` loop that dereferences stale line numbers dates to `f2c7116f8e19` (Feb 2025) and the `getWidthOfLine` call on line 42 to `461887743ad0` (Jan 2026); both predate the 1.140.0 window and pass the ancestry check against the shipped commit `07f806f9`. The bucket surfaced as a *new* stable anomaly in 1.140.0, but the throwing code path is pre-existing — the spike most plausibly reflects increased NES/inline-edit exposure rather than a change to this loop. Per the re-bucketing / pre-existing guidance, no speculative culprit is named; the owner is taken from the feature area. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Undo as TextModel undo participant Model as TextModel (content change) participant Derived as inlineEditsSideBySideView
_editorMaxContentWidthInRange participant Util as maxContentWidthInRange participant Crash as TextModel.getLineMaxColumn Undo->>Model: _applyUndo shrinks buffer Note over Model: line count decreases;
versionId increments Model->>Derived: synchronous layout cascade
recompute (reads versionId) Note over Derived: ⚠️ Root cause:
cached originalDisplayRange
still has pre-undo lines Derived->>Util: maxContentWidthInRange(editor, staleRange) Util->>Crash: getWidthOfLine(i) for out-of-bounds i Note over Crash: 💥 Illegal value for lineNumber ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts` | crash site | L900 (from stack): `throw new BugIndicatingError('Illegal value for lineNumber')` when `lineNumber > getLineCount()` | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/utils/utils.ts` | root cause | L41-L44: `for (let i = range.startLineNumber; i < range.endLineNumberExclusive; i++) { editor.getWidthOfLine(i, reader); }` iterates a range not reconciled with the current model | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/inlineEditsViews/inlineEditsSideBySideView.ts` | producer | L220-L227: `derived` keyed on `versionId` recomputes `maxContentWidthInRange(this._editorObs, originalDisplayRange, reader)` with the stale edit range after the model shrank | | `src/vs/editor/browser/observableCodeEditor.ts` | pass-through | L534-L539: `getWidthOfLine` forwards `lineNumber` to `editor.getWidthOfLine` | ### Repro Steps Non-deterministic timing-dependent race. To increase likelihood: 1. Enable inline suggestions / next-edit-suggestions (NES). 2. In a non-`file` scheme document (e.g. an untitled or notebook cell editor), trigger an inline edit preview whose `displayRange` extends to near the end of the buffer. 3. While the side-by-side inline-edit preview is visible, perform an `undo` (or any edit) that removes lines so the model becomes shorter than the preview's `displayRange`. 4. The synchronous content-change → layout cascade recomputes the width derived against the stale range, iterating a line number beyond the new line count and throwing `Illegal value for lineNumber`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/utils/utils.ts` → `maxContentWidthInRange()`: before iterating, clamp the incoming `range` to the current model's line count (`model.getLineCount()`), reading the authoritative line count in the same atomic section that already reads the model. The loop and the subsequent `mapToLineArray(l => model.getLineContent(l))` now use the clamped range, so no line number outside `[1, lineCount]` is ever passed to `getWidthOfLine` / `getLineContent`. This is the stale-cached-identifier lifecycle pattern: the consumer holds a range captured against an older model version and re-reads it after the producer (the undo-driven content change) shrank the model. The sanctioned fix for that pattern is to re-resolve the stale reference against authoritative state in the same read section, which is exactly what this utility — the single reconciliation point every inline-edit width call site routes through — is positioned to do. It fixes where the range meets the model, not at the crash site: `getLineMaxColumn`'s guard is left intact so it keeps feeding the telemetry pipeline for genuinely illegal callers, and no `logService.error`/throw is removed or wrapped in try/catch. After this change, `utils.ts:41` cannot pass an out-of-bounds line number to `getWidthOfLine` because every iterated value is bounded by `model.getLineCount()` read immediately above the loop. **Alternatives considered**: - Guarding at the crash site in `getLineMaxColumn` (e.g. returning a fallback instead of throwing) — rejected: it masks the real bug for every caller and removes a legitimate invariant check that feeds error telemetry. - Fixing each producer (`inlineEditsSideBySideView`, `inlineEditsDeletionView`, `inlineEditsCustomView`, `longDistancePreviewEditor`) to re-clamp its edit range before calling the utility — rejected: six-plus call sites all funnel the same edit-derived ranges through this one helper, so reconciling once at the shared reconciliation point is both minimal and complete; duplicating the clamp at every caller would be error-prone and easy to miss on future call sites. ### Recommended Owner ``@hediet`` — Henning Dieterichs owns the inline-edits / NES rendering area, authored `maxContentWidthInRange` (`f2c7116f8e19`) and the side-by-side view that produces the stale range, and is highly active in `microsoft/vscode` (148 commits in the last 90 days). --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. issues.title: Bundled /create-* customization slash commands are not registered in Copilot SDK harness sessions
issues.body:
### Type: Bug

The bundled `/create-prompt`, `/create-instructions`, `/create-skill`, `/create-agent` and `/create-hook` slash commands are not available in Copilot SDK harness sessions (the agent-host sessions used by the Agents window / Copilot SDK harness). They are still available in regular Copilot Chat.

The skills are still shipped and still referenced by other built-in customizations, so this looks like a gap in how the harness builds its slash-command catalog rather than an intentional removal.

### Evidence that the commands still exist in the installed build

All paths below are inside the installed app at `/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app`.

The skill definitions are present and are all marked user-invocable (`disable-model-invocation: true`, no `user-invocable: false`):

```
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-agent/SKILL.md
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-hook/SKILL.md
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-instructions/SKILL.md
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-prompt/SKILL.md
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-skill/SKILL.md
```

They are documented as a shipped feature in `extensions/copilot/changelog.md:73` (0.38):

> **Create agent customizations from chat** — New `/create-prompt`, `/create-instruction`, `/create-skill`, `/create-agent`, and `/create-hook` slash commands to generate customization files directly from a conversation.

Other bundled customizations actively depend on them:

- `extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/init/SKILL.md:48` tells the agent to recommend them:
  > Once finalized, propose related agent-customizations to create next (`/create-(agent|hook|instruction|prompt|skill) …`)
- `extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/agent-customization/SKILL.md:3` hides itself *because* they are expected to exist:
  > `user-invocable: false # don't show as slash command, we have sepcialized create-agent, create-instructions, create-hook prompts for that`

### Current behavior

In a Copilot SDK harness session, the available skill catalog contains user-level skills (`~/.copilot/skills`) and plugin skills, but none of the bundled `create-*` skills — and `init` is missing as well. The `agent-customization` skill correctly stays hidden, so the net effect is that **no** built-in entry point for creating customization files is reachable from the harness.

Because `agent-customization` deliberately hides itself in favor of the `create-*` commands, the result is a discoverability dead end: `/init` recommends commands the user cannot invoke.

### Expected behavior

Bundled user-invocable skills shipped with the Copilot extension (`create-agent`, `create-hook`, `create-instructions`, `create-prompt`, `create-skill`, `init`) should be registered as slash commands in Copilot SDK harness sessions, the same way they are in Copilot Chat.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Agents window and start a session on the Copilot SDK harness.
2. Type `/` in the chat input.
3. Observe that `/create-agent`, `/create-hook`, `/create-instructions`, `/create-prompt`, `/create-skill` and `/init` are absent, while user-level and plugin skills are listed.
4. Start a regular Copilot Chat session and type `/` — the `create-*` commands are listed there.

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.140.0 (stable), commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`, 2026-09-30
- GitHub Copilot extension: 0.68.0
- `@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-arm64`: 1.0.15-preview.4
- OS: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64

### Notes

If this is intentional and the harness is meant to rely on natural-language requests instead, then `init/SKILL.md` and the `user-invocable: false` rationale in `agent-customization/SKILL.md` should be updated, since both currently point users at commands that do not exist in this surface.

issues.title: fix: register extension install commands in Agents window (fixes #339804)
issues.body:
### Summary The Agents (sessions) window throws `command 'workbench.extensions.installExtension' not found` whenever code paths that are shared with the main workbench try to install an extension. The sessions window loads chat UI contributions (via `chat.shared.contribution.js`) and the extension URL handler — both of which call `commandService.executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', ...)` — but it never loads `workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts`, the only place that registered that command. So the command is missing in the sessions window and `_tryExecuteCommand` rejects. Affected 25 users on the current build across Windows, Linux, and Mac. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339804 Recommended reviewer: ``@sandy081`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not identified — pre-existing architectural gap | | Author | — | | PR | — | | Message | — | | Why | No single commit in the regression range introduced the defect. The producers (`chatAgentRecommendationActions.ts`, `aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts`, `extensionUrlHandler.ts`) and the command registration are both long-lived. The bucket became "new" because the sessions window progressively adopted the shared chat contribution that reaches these producers, while the extensions contribution that registers the command was never added to the sessions bundle. The fix therefore closes the registration gap rather than reverting a commit. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User (Agents window) participant Producer as Chat/URL contribution participant CmdSvc as CommandService participant Registry as CommandsRegistry Note over Registry: ⚠️ Root cause:
workbench extensions.contribution
not loaded in sessions window,
so installExtension is never registered User->>Producer: Trigger install (recommendation / customization / URL) Producer->>CmdSvc: executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', id) CmdSvc->>Registry: getCommand(id) Registry-->>CmdSvc: undefined Note over CmdSvc: 💥 Error thrown:
command 'workbench.extensions.installExtension' not found ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/services/commands/common/commandService.ts` | crash site | L93-L95 (from stack): `if (!command) { return Promise.reject(new Error(\`command '\$\{id}' not found\`)); }` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts` | root cause | L437-L582 (pre-change): the sole registration of `workbench.extensions.installExtension`, only loaded in the main workbench bundle, not in the sessions window. | | `src/vs/sessions/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts` | root cause | Sessions-window extensions contribution registered only a config setting and never registered the install/uninstall commands. | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatAgentRecommendationActions.ts` | producer | L89-L91: `await commandService.executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', recommendation.extensionId, ...)` — loaded in sessions via `chat.shared.contribution`. | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts` | producer | L471: `await accessor.get(ICommandService).executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', CHAT_CUSTOMIZATION_EXTENSION_ID, { enable: true })`. | | `src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/browser/extensionUrlHandler.ts` | producer | L276: `await this.commandService.executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', extensionId, ...)` — loaded in sessions via `sessions.common.main.ts`. | ### Repro Steps 1. Open the Agents (sessions) window. 2. Invoke any flow that installs an extension from shared chat UI — e.g. click an "Install Chat Customization Extension" / agent-recommendation install action, or open a `vscode:extension/` URL that the extension URL handler resolves in that window. 3. The command dispatch reaches `CommandService._tryExecuteCommand`, which cannot find `workbench.extensions.installExtension`. 4. Observe the unhandled error `command 'workbench.extensions.installExtension' not found`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** - **New `src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsCommands.ts`**: extracted the `workbench.extensions.installExtension`, `workbench.extensions.uninstallExtension`, and `workbench.extensions.search` command registrations verbatim into a dedicated, idempotent `registerExtensionsCommands()` function. This module only touches `CommandsRegistry` and resolves its services lazily via the accessor, so it pulls in no editor panes or view containers and is safe to load in a lightweight window. This is the data-producer fix location: the command must exist wherever its producers run, so registration is made shareable rather than guarding each call site. - **`src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts`**: replaced the inlined registrations with a single `registerExtensionsCommands()` call and removed the now-unused imports. Behavior in the main workbench is unchanged — the same commands are registered through the shared module. - **`src/vs/sessions/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts`**: call `registerExtensionsCommands()` so the Agents window registers the same install/uninstall/search commands it already has services for (`IExtensionsWorkbenchService`, `IWorkbenchExtensionManagementService`, and `IExtensionGalleryService` are all registered in the sessions bundle). The command now resolves in that window instead of rejecting. This fixes the defect at its source — the missing registration — rather than suppressing the symptom at the crash site in `commandService.ts` (which must keep throwing for unknown commands so telemetry stays accurate). No `logService.error`/telemetry path is removed, and no `try/catch` masks the error. **Alternatives considered** - Guarding each producer with a "command exists?" check before calling — rejected: it scatters duplicated lifecycle checks across unrelated features and silently drops a capability the sessions window actually supports, rather than fixing the single missing registration. - Importing the whole workbench `extensions.contribution.ts` into the sessions window — rejected: it registers extension editor panes and view containers that do not belong in the Agents window and would bloat/alter that window's UI. **Why this fix**: after this change, `src/vs/sessions/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts` calls `registerExtensionsCommands()` at load time, so `CommandsRegistry.getCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension')` returns the handler in the Agents window and `commandService.ts:94` can no longer reject with "command not found". ### Recommended Owner ``@sandy081`` — owns extension management (dominant author of `extensions.contribution.ts`) and is actively working on the Agents/sessions window (agentHost) integration, making him the right owner for a fix that bridges both areas. --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. issues.title: fix: wrap agent-host URIs with rootless paths (fixes #339802)
issues.body:
### Summary The Agent Host URI wrapper (`wrapAgentHostUri` in `agentHostUri.ts`) builds a `(redacted) URI that **always** carries a connection authority, but sets its path to `originalUri.path || '/'`. That expression only repairs an *empty* path; it does not repair a non-empty, **rootless** path (one that does not begin with `/`), as opaque URIs such as `untitled:Untitled-1` (path = `Untitled-1`) have. RFC 3986 requires an authority-bearing URI's path to be empty or begin with `/`, so `URI.from`/`_validateUri` throws `[UriError]: If a URI contains an authority component, then the path component must either be empty or begin with a slash`. The throw surfaces as an unhandled error while mapping session customization resources into client space (168 users, 742 hits on `429a4ec7`). Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339802 Recommended reviewer: @aeschli ### Culprit Commit No regression-range commit touched the failing code path. The bug is **pre-existing** in `wrapAgentHostUri`: the `originalUri.path || '/'` guard was written to cover empty paths only and never handled rootless opaque paths. The bucket is classified `new` because the surrounding customization-mapping feature (which first routes opaque URIs through this wrapper) reached the `429a4ec7` build, not because a commit in the range introduced the faulty line. | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — pre-existing latent bug in `wrapAgentHostUri` | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | The path-validity guard at the producer only handled empty paths; a rootless path combined with the always-present agent-host authority violates RFC 3986. No range commit changed this line. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Pills as agentHostSessionInputPills participant Map as agentHostSessionCustomizations.mapHostUri participant Wrap as wrapAgentHostUri participant URI as URI.from / _validateUri Pills->>Map: map customization resource to client space Map->>Wrap: toAgentHostUri(originalUri, connectionAuthority) Note over Wrap: ⚠️ Root cause:
path = originalUri.path || '/'
leaves a rootless path (e.g. 'Untitled-1') unrepaired
while authority is always set Wrap->>URI: URI.from({ scheme, authority, path: 'Untitled-1', ... }) Note over URI: 💥 Error thrown:
[UriError]: authority present but path
does not begin with '/' ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/base/common/uri.ts` | crash site | L40 (from stack): `throw new Error('[UriError]: ...')` in `_validateUri` | | `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostUri.ts` | root cause (producer) | L124: `path: originalUri.path \|\| '/'` — repairs only empty paths, not rootless opaque paths, while L123 always sets a non-empty `authority` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/agentHostSessionCustomizations.ts` | trigger | L247: `mapHostUri(originalUri)` routes customization URIs through the wrapper | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionInputPills.ts` | trigger | L783/L789: builds the `CustomizationIndex` with a `fromAgentHost` mapper | ### Repro Steps 1. Open an Agent Host session connected to a remote connection (non-`local` authority). 2. Surface a customization (or any resource) whose URI is **opaque** — its path is non-empty and does not begin with `/` (e.g. an `untitled:Untitled-1` resource). 3. The input-pills derived chain builds a `CustomizationIndex` whose `mapHostUri` calls `toAgentHostUri` on that URI. 4. `wrapAgentHostUri` constructs `URI.from({ scheme: 'vscode-agent-host', authority, path: 'Untitled-1', ... })`, which throws the `[UriError]` because the authority-bearing URI has a rootless path. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostUri.ts`): fix the data producer, not the crash site. In `wrapAgentHostUri`, detect a non-empty rootless path (`originalUri.path.length > 0 && originalUri.path.charCodeAt(0) !== CharCode.Slash`). When present, synthesize a leading slash for the wrapped path (`/${originalUri.path}`) so the authority-bearing URI satisfies RFC 3986, and record a `rootlessPath: true` marker in the `_ah` metadata. `fromAgentHostUri` reads that marker and strips the synthesized slash (`agentHostUri.path.slice(1)`), so the original opaque path round-trips losslessly. Empty paths keep the existing `'/'` behavior, and already-rooted paths are unchanged, so existing wrapped URIs and their stored metadata are unaffected. This is correct because it repairs the invalid value where it is produced (the wrapper that pairs a mandatory authority with the original path), rather than widening `URI`'s validation at the crash site or suppressing the throw — the telemetry pipeline and `_validateUri` contract both stay intact. **Alternatives considered**: - Guard/try-catch at the `URI.from` crash site in `uri.ts` — rejected: masks the symptom, weakens a shared base-layer invariant for every caller, and loses the original resource identity. - Drop the authority for rootless paths — rejected: the agent-host filesystem provider relies on the connection authority to resolve the resource, so dropping it would break resolution. A round-trip unit test (`round-trips an opaque URI with a rootless path`) is added to `agentHostFileSystemProvider.test.ts` to lock in both the synthesized wrapped path and the lossless unwrap. ### Recommended Owner ``@aeschli`` — Martin Aeschlimann authored the Agent Host customization URI-mapping code (`fc358ad`, "Add remote URI transformations for customizations" #335324) and the surrounding `agentHostUri.ts` transformations, and is highly active in `microsoft/vscode` (82 commits in the last 90 days). Best-placed to review the producer-side URI fix. --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. issues.title: fix: validate chat participant declaration regardless of when clause (fixes #339803)
issues.body:
### Summary `MainThreadChatAgents2.$registerAgent` throws `chatParticipant must be declared in package.json: copilot-cloud-agent` when an extension registers a chat participant whose chat-session contribution is declared in `package.json` but is currently gated off by its `when` clause. The declaration check used `getAllChatSessionContributions()`, which filters out any contribution whose `when` condition is not currently satisfied, so a *declared-but-disabled* participant was treated as *not declared* and the registration threw. Impact: an unhandled error is reported to telemetry (and registration fails) whenever the `copilot-cloud-agent` participant registers while `config.github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.enabled` is false. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339803 Recommended reviewer: ``@joshspicer`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`548e73f30b8`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/548e73f30b8015c51ba993a9d0085ff3aff537fe) | | Author | ``@joshspicer`` | | PR | #275918 | | Message | check chatSessionService in $registerAgent (#275918) | | Why | It added `const chatSessionRegistration = this._chatSessionService.getAllChatSessionContributions().find(...)` to gate the throw. `getAllChatSessionContributions()` filters by `_isContributionAvailable` (the `when` clause), so a contribution declared in package.json but disabled by its `when` condition is excluded, making the "declared in package.json" check fail and throw. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as Copilot extension participant EH as ExtHost participant MT as MainThreadChatAgents2.$registerAgent participant CS as ChatSessionsService Ext->>EH: register "copilot-cloud-agent" participant EH->>MT: $registerAgent(id="copilot-cloud-agent") MT->>CS: getAllChatSessionContributions() Note over CS: ⚠️ Root cause:
filters out contributions whose
`when` clause is currently false CS-->>MT: list WITHOUT copilot-cloud-agent Note over MT: 💥 Error thrown:
chatParticipant must be
declared in package.json ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadChatAgents2.ts` | crash site | L351 (from stack): `throw new Error(\`chatParticipant must be declared in package.json: \$\{id}\`)` | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadChatAgents2.ts` | root cause | L343: `const chatSessionRegistration = this._chatSessionService.getAllChatSessionContributions().find(...)` — availability-filtered lookup used as a declaration check | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatSessions/chatSessions.contribution.ts` | producer | L874-L878: `getAllChatSessionContributions()` applies `.filter(entry => this._isContributionAvailable(entry.contribution))` | ### Repro Steps 1. Ensure `github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.enabled` is set to `false` (so the `copilot-cloud-agent` chat-session contribution's `when` clause — `config.github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.enabled` — evaluates to false). 2. Load the Copilot extension so it calls `vscode.chat.createChatParticipant`/registers the `copilot-cloud-agent` participant. 3. During `$registerAgent`, the declaration check calls `getAllChatSessionContributions()`, which omits the disabled contribution. 4. Observe the thrown error `chatParticipant must be declared in package.json: copilot-cloud-agent` reported to error telemetry. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatSessionsService.ts` + `.../chatSessions/chatSessions.contribution.ts`: add a new `isChatSessionContributionDeclared(chatSessionType)` method that reports whether a contribution (by primary `type` or `alternativeIds`) was *declared*, independent of its `when` clause. It consults `_contributions`/`_alternativeIdMap` directly rather than the availability-filtered `getAllChatSessionContributions()`. - `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadChatAgents2.ts`: replace the availability-filtered `getAllChatSessionContributions().find(...)` with `isChatSessionContributionDeclared(id)`. This fixes the check at the place where the wrong data source was consumed: the guard is meant to assert the participant is *declared in package.json*, which is a declaration fact, not a runtime-availability fact. A `when`-gated-off contribution is still declared, so registration must be allowed. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/mockChatSessionsService.ts`: implement the new interface method in the mock. **Alternatives considered** - Add a `?.` / early-return guard at the `throw` crash site in `$registerAgent`: rejected because it suppresses the symptom at the crash site rather than correcting the declaration check that produced the wrong decision. - Make `getAllChatSessionContributions()` stop filtering by `when`: rejected because many other callers rely on it returning only currently-available contributions; changing it would regress those consumers. ### Recommended Owner ``@joshspicer`` — author of the culprit commit #275918, active in `microsoft/vscode` within the last 90 days. --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. issues.title: API: expose selected SCM resources to extension commands invoked by keybindings
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Feature request

Provide a supported way for an extension command invoked by a keyboard shortcut to obtain the currently selected file resources in the built-in Source Control Changes view, including multi-selection.

This request is about extension access to SCM resource selection. It does not request a global Ctrl+C override or an integration with a particular chat product.

## Problem and use case

I am developing a local extension that copies selected file references for use in a coding assistant. Users select several staged or unstaged files in the existing Source Control view, press Ctrl+C, then paste those references into the assistant.

The selection works when the command is invoked from `scm/resourceState/context`: the command receives the selected resource states. Invoking the same command through a keybinding does not supply those arguments. Falling back to the active editor URI is incorrect: in our test, seven SCM files were selected but only the active editor file path was copied.

The context-menu workaround works, but does not provide the requested keyboard workflow.

## Minimal reproduction

Register an extension command and contribute it to both a menu and a keybinding:

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "command": "example.inspectScmSelection", "title": "Inspect SCM Selection" }
    ],
    "menus": {
      "scm/resourceState/context": [
        { "command": "example.inspectScmSelection", "group": "navigation" }
      ]
    },
    "keybindings": [
      {
        "command": "example.inspectScmSelection",
        "key": "ctrl+alt+c",
        "when": "focusedView == workbench.scm && listFocus && !inputFocus"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```js
vscode.commands.registerCommand('example.inspectScmSelection', (...resources) => {
  const paths = resources.flat().map(resource => resource?.resourceUri?.toString());
  console.log('SCM command arguments:', resources, paths);
});
```

1. Open a Git workspace with several changed files.
2. Select multiple file rows under Staged Changes or Changes.
3. Invoke Inspect SCM Selection from a selected row's context menu: selected resources are supplied.
4. Invoke it with the keybinding while the SCM list has focus: the same selection is not supplied as command arguments.

## Requested capability

A supported query API or command returning selected SCM resource URIs would unblock this. An opt-in mechanism to forward resource context to keybinding commands could also address the use case. I am not requesting a change to existing command argument behavior by default.

Design considerations include selection versus focused item, staged and unstaged entries for the same URI, multiple repositories, tree-view folders, and empty selection. The implementation should not silently substitute the active editor URI for SCM selection.

## Existing implementation

The selection is already available internally in `SCMViewPane.getSelectedResources()`. `RepositoryPaneActionRunner.runAction()` reads that selection and supplies it to menu actions:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmViewPane.ts

SCM menu argument behavior is documented here:

https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/scm-provider#menus

## Related issues

- #24916: broader SCM keyboard-shortcut support. This request specifically concerns extension access to the current SCM multi-selection.
- #207066: Git staging shortcut and focus behavior; related discussion of SCM list context.
- #3553 and #316820: access to built-in Explorer selection; this request concerns the built-in SCM view.
- #72442 (closed as duplicate of #170248): keyboard commands on tree items. #170248 concerns focused items in extension-owned TreeViews, rather than querying built-in SCM selection.

If this SCM API request is already covered by an existing issue, please point me to the preferred tracking issue; I am happy to consolidate there.

## Environment

Observed locally on Windows, VS Code 1.139.1 (x64), commit 04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1, with a local helper extension and the built-in Git provider.

I would be interested in contributing an implementation once the desired scope and API shape are agreed on.

issues.title: Markdown Preview local file links fail in vscode-file provider with JSON parse error
issues.body:
## Description
Clicking relative Markdown Preview links to ordinary local `.txt` or `.ps1` files can fail with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` in VS Code's internal `vscode-file` text content provider.

## Reproduction
1. Open a workspace with non-empty `file_structure.txt` and `file_structure.ps1` files.
2. Add links such as `[map](./file_structure.txt)` and `[generator](./file_structure.ps1)` to Markdown.
3. Open Markdown Preview and click either link.

## Expected
The linked file opens as text in the editor.

## Actual
The window logs a JSON parse error in `provideTextContent` for a `vscode-file://vscode-app/...` URI. The files are valid and non-empty; adding `./` did not help.

## Environment
- VS Code 1.140.0
- Windows desktop
- Markdown Preview

## Workaround
Adding `workbench.editorAssociations` entries mapping `*.txt` and `*.ps1` to `default`, then reloading the window, allowed both links to open. This suggests an issue in the editor/provider routing; root cause is unconfirmed.

instead of the older VS Code location:
`%APPDATA%\Code\User\workspaceStorage\...\chatSessions\`

The new session format uses:

- workspace.yaml for session metadata
- events.jsonl for user, assistant, tool, and model events
- client_name: vscode-agent-host
- producer: copilot-agent
