issues.title: Agent sessions with BYOK models: tool-result images (e.g. `view` tool) are silently dropped before reaching the model — source-level root cause, regression shipped in 1.132.0

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: bundled (VS Code 1.140.0)
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (also source-verified on current `main`, commit `24a4117`)
- OS Version: Windows 10 (protocol-agnostic; reproduces on any OS)
- Feature: agent mode — tool result pipeline for BYOK (OpenAI-compatible) models
- Selected model: any BYOK vision-capable model via custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (verified via a local logging proxy against DeepSeek / StepFun / Mimo endpoints)
- Logs: outgoing request bodies captured at a local OpenAI-compatible proxy — the tool message contains only a 31-char text receipt, no image part (details below)
- Relates to #339439 (same symptom reported from a CLI agent session with black-box evidence; this report adds the source-level root cause and the git-verified regression window)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a BYOK provider with an OpenAI-compatible base URL, model declares image input support (a request-logging proxy makes the evidence visible).
2. Start an agent session with that model.
3. Ask the model to look at an image file — it invokes the `view` tool.
4. Inspect the outgoing request body: the tool result is only `"Viewed image file successfully."` — no image content part anywhere.
5. Contrast: attach the same image directly to the user prompt → the request contains a proper image part.

## Actual result

The model receives a 31-character text receipt instead of the image. It correctly reports it received no pixels. The image bytes exist in agent-host session state (base64 payload present), so the loss happens between the agent host and the model request.

## Expected result

Tool-result images are forwarded to the model as image content parts — as the legacy in-extension path still does, and as the Claude-bridge path does. If a model cannot consume images, degrade explicitly with a visible notice instead of silently sending a text receipt.

## Root cause (source-verified on `main` @ `24a4117`): the BYOK LM bridge has no image channel for tool results

The image survives deep into the pipeline — `handleClientToolCallComplete` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts` ~line 2910) correctly extracts `EmbeddedResource` blocks into `binaryResultsForLlm` — then hits **three consecutive drop points**:

1. **Bridge DTO has no image field** — `IByokLmFunctionCallOutputItem.output` is `string` only:
   `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostByokLm.ts` (~line 59)
   ```ts
   export interface IByokLmFunctionCallOutputItem {
       readonly type: 'function_call_output';
       readonly callId: string;
       readonly output: string;   // ← no image channel
   }
   ```
   Compare `IByokLmMessageItem.content: IByokLmContentPart[]` (text | image) — the user-message path *does* have an image channel.

2. **Responses→bridge translation takes text only** — `output: item.output ?? ''`:
   `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/byokResponsesTranslation.ts` (~line 179)

3. **Renderer-side conversion emits text-only LM parts** — `agentHostByokLmHandler.ts` (~line 289):
   ```ts
   case 'function_call_output':
   case 'custom_tool_call_output':
       return {
           role: ChatMessageRole.User,
           content: [{ type: 'tool_result', toolCallId: item.callId,
               value: [{ type: 'text', value: item.output }] }],  // ← no image branch
       };
   ```
   while the user-message conversion **in the same file** (`_toChatMessageParts`, ~line 313) has a full `image_url` branch — this asymmetry is exactly why attaching images to the prompt works while tool-result images do not.

**This is a capability regression of the agent-host bridge**, not a new-code typo:

- The legacy in-extension path still forwards tool-result images today (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts` ~line 514):
  ```ts
  input.push({ type: 'function_call_output', call_id: message.toolCallId, output: asText });
  if (asImages.length) {
      input.push({ role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'input_text', text: 'Image associated with the above tool call:' }, ...asImages] });
  }
  ```
- The Claude-bridge path converts them too (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/clientTools/claudeClientToolResult.ts` ~line 52). Only the OpenAI-compatible BYOK LM bridge lacks the channel.

## Regression window (git-verified)

- `26b7c6b` (2026-06-23): bridge born text-only ("agentHost: add opt-in BYOK language-model bridge") — opt-in, no user impact.
- `2c549ee` (2026-07-29): "Enable Agent Host migration settings by default" flips `chat.agentHost.enabled` to `true`.
- Verified by diffing the actual tag sources:
  - **1.131.0** (2026-07-27): default `!isWeb && product.quality !== 'stable'` → stable users on legacy path, tool-result images work.
  - **1.132.0** (2026-08-04): default `true` → stable users moved to the bridge → tool-result images dropped.
- **Last good stable: 1.131.x. First broken: 1.132.0.** Insiders affected earlier (~late June builds).
- On current `main` the `chat.agentHost.enabled` setting is gone (`agentHostEnablementService` enables the host unconditionally on desktop), so recent builds have **no configuration fallback**.

## Workaround

Attach the image directly to the user prompt instead of letting the model call `view`.

issues.title: Test: Send messages between chats
issues.body:
Refs: [#339298](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339298), [#335540](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335540)

- [x] anyOS @aiday-mar
- [x] anyOS @amunger

Complexity: 4

Authors: @sandy081


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339594%0A%0A&assignees=sandy081)

---

The existing `send_message` tool has been enhanced to give agents more control over messages sent to another chat.

## What the tool supports

- **Queue:** send a message as a separate turn. It starts immediately if the receiving chat is idle; otherwise it waits. Multiple queued messages run in order.
- **Steer:** send a correction to the receiving chat's active turn, rather than queue a separate turn.
- **Replace:** change a message the sending chat queued while it is still pending, keeping its place in the queue.
- **Cancel:** remove a message the sending chat queued while it is still pending, without stopping the current task.

A message that has started processing can no longer be replaced or cancelled as a pending message. Already-delivered steering cannot be retracted. Sending is asynchronous: the tool does not wait for the receiving chat's reply.

## Set up

In the Agents Window, create a session on a workspace. In that session, send this prompt to create a peer chat:

> Create another chat in this session, in the same workspace, and say hi.

Open the main chat and the peer chat side by side. Use the first to send instructions and watch what happens in the second.

The following scenarios are suggestions. Feel free to follow your own scenarios to exercise these behaviors.

## Send work and queue a follow-up

In the first chat, ask:

> Use send_message to ask the other chat to wait for 30 seconds, then write the alphabet from a to z.

While the second chat is waiting, ask the first:

> After that, queue another message asking it to write the alphabet in reverse.

Check that the second chat receives the first request and runs the follow-up as a separate turn afterward, rather than interrupting the first request.

## Replace a queued message

Repeat the waiting task and queue the reverse-alphabet follow-up. Before it starts, tell the first chat:

> Replace that queued message: ask it to write a to u instead of the reverse alphabet.

Check that the pending message is replaced, not duplicated, and only the replacement runs in the original queue position.

## Cancel a queued message

Repeat with a fresh waiting task and queued follow-up, then tell the first chat:

> Cancel that queued follow-up.

Check that the follow-up disappears and never runs, while the current task continues.

For replacement and cancellation, expand the tool result to confirm the outcome rather than relying only on the agent's reply. If the follow-up has already started, it is too late to mutate it as a pending message; repeat with a fresh wait to exercise the pending case.

## Steer work already in progress

Start another waiting task that will write ten lines. While the second chat is working, tell the first:

> Use send_message to steer the other chat's current work: write fifteen lines instead of ten. Do not queue a separate follow-up.

Check that the correction reaches the current work rather than waiting as another queued turn. The second chat should take the correction into account before answering. Do not expect a running wait command to stop instantly.

Feel free to try your own scenarios, such as counting numbers, listing animal names or coordinating small disposable workspace tasks. Check that messages reach the intended chat, queued work stays in order, and the tool clearly reports when a message has already started and cannot be replaced or cancelled.

issues.title: Test: Read and last-modified state in Agents Window
issues.body:
Refs: [#339500](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339500), [#338969](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338969)

- [x] anyOS @justschen
- [x] anyOS @houghj16

Complexity: 3

Authors: @sandy081


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339593%0A%0A&assignees=sandy081)

---

Each chat, including the main chat, shows its own read status and last-modified time.

## Set up

In the Agents Window, have different kinds of sessions available, including single-chat and multi-chat sessions. Include both new and existing sessions.

## Read one chat without reading another

Send prompts in different chats and switch away while they respond. Check that the chats show unread responses. Open one chat: it should become read without marking other chats read.

Repeat with the main chat and peers in a multi-chat session. Each chat should show its own read status independently. An unread peer must not make the main chat appear unread.

## Mark the whole session as read

With unread responses in the main chat and multiple peer chats, use Mark as Read on the session. Check that the main chat and all its peer chats become read, while chats in other sessions remain unchanged. This is a session-level action, not an action on individual chats. Also check it on a single-chat session.

## Keep last-modified times independent

Send prompts in different chats at distinguishable times. Check that each chat's last-modified time updates for its own conversation, not when another chat changes.

Repeat with the main chat and peers. The main chat must not inherit a peer's last-modified time, and peers must not inherit each other's times. Also check single-chat sessions.

## Leave and return

Switch between chats, reload the Agents Window, then restart after the conversations finish. Check that each chat retains its own read status and last-modified time. Include previously read existing chats: they should not unexpectedly become unread after reload or restart.

Keep testing focused on these two fields.

issues.title: Expose the chat permission level (Default / Allow all / Autopilot) in agent hook input
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
### Problem

A `PreToolUse` hook can return `allow`, `deny` or `ask`. We verified on all three permission levels (Default, Allow all, Autopilot) that:
- a hook `allow` skips VS Code's own confirmation;
- a hook `ask` always shows a confirmation, even under Allow all and Autopilot.

That is a safe default, but a policy hook cannot adapt to the level the user chose, because the hook input (`timestamp`, `hook_event_name`, `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`, `cwd`) does not include it.

Our use case: a security hook asks for confirmation on operations that are risky but legitimate, such as a command outside a per-agent allowlist, and denies operations that must never run. Under Default, `ask` is what we want. Under Allow all or Autopilot, the user has explicitly chosen to skip confirmations, and the hook's `ask` prompts become the main source of interruptions. We would like to turn those `ask` into `allow` in these modes, while keeping every `deny`.

### Why the workaround is not safe

VS Code records the level for each request in the chat session file (`modeInfo.permissionLevel`). We tried reading it from the hook, but writes to that file are deferred and batched. We observed a request made under Allow all and the next request made under Default appended in a single write, after the second request had started. A hook reading the file during a request can therefore see a stale level. When the user switches from Allow all back to Default, the hook would relax its checks right after the user turned confirmations back on. Reading undocumented internal storage is also fragile across versions.

### Proposal

Add the effective permission level of the request to the common hook input, using the value VS Code already records, for example:

```json
"permission_level": "default" | "autoApprove" | "autopilot"
```

For tool calls made inside a subagent, the value should be the level actually applied to that call (see #329564 on subsessions inheriting the parent level).

### Alternative

Let the hook delegate the decision instead of exposing the level: a hook result meaning "ask only if the current permission level would ask anyway", for example `"permissionDecision": "ask"` with a `"respectAutoApprove": true` flag. VS Code keeps the logic, and the hook never needs to know the level.

### Security considerations

The field only lets a hook relax its own `ask` in modes where the user already chose to skip confirmations. It cannot override a `deny`, and VS Code remains the source of truth for the level.

### Related

- #293631 - agent identifier in hook input
- #301152 - `model` field in hook input
- #297815 - Allow all and Autopilot behavior
- github/copilot-sdk#2810 - same request for the Copilot SDK, where hooks are moving

### Environment

VS Code 1.140.0 (07f806f), Windows x64.

issues.title: Incorrect handling of completions in the Debug REPL

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.141.0 (run from source code, commit 5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35)
- OS Version: Windows 11

The debug console has some bugs and deviations from the DAP w.r.t. the replacement range of a completion item:

**1. Bug: Debug REPL ignores `item.start` from DAP completions.**

The [replacement range calculation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/repl.ts#L282) always replaces `length` characters immediately before the cursor. An explicit `item.start` is used for filtering, but not for the edit itself.

This makes it impossible to consume/overwrite text behind the current cursor, even though this should be possible according to the DAP.

Expected behavior: when `item.start` is provided, replace from `item.start` to `item.start + item.length`. I implemented this [here](https://github.com/ManuelHentschel/vscode/blob/621f9ec3b8f0c6342dedf7091647476e20e31ee8/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/repl.ts#L301-L305) and can provide a PR.

**2. Bug: Multiline history completions duplicate preceding lines.**

This is a separate bug in VS Code's own history suggestions, rather than a DAP adapter issue.
The [history replacement range](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/repl.ts#L319) is limited to the current line by `position.delta()`, while the inserted text contains the entire history entry.

To reproduce: With a Python debug session active and `debug.console.historySuggestions` enabled, execute in the REPL:

```python
if True:
    print(0)
```

Then enter the following, with `|` marking the cursor:

```python
if True:
    pr|
```

Accept the history suggestion for the previously executed command. The resulting input is:

```python
if True:
if True:
    print(0)
```

Expected behavior: complete the command once, or withhold the suggestion if its replacement range is unsupported. Accepting a history suggestion should not duplicate preceding lines.

**3. Clarification needed: deviations from the DAP**

Some behavior w.r.t. replaced ranges deviates from the DAP but is consistent otherwise.
This should be clarified or the DAP should be adapted accordingly:

1. Vscode uses zero-based indexing for `item.start`, but advertises `columnsStartAt1: true`,
which implies 1-based indexing for `item.start` according to the [DAP definition](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/621f9ec3b8f0c6342dedf7091647476e20e31ee8/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/common/debugProtocol.d.ts#L2326).


2. If `item.start` is omitted, vscode replaces `length` characters up to the cursor.
The [DAP definition](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/621f9ec3b8f0c6342dedf7091647476e20e31ee8/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/common/debugProtocol.d.ts#L2326) specifies that it should instead default to the cursor position.

3. Vscode only handles single-line replacement ranges correctly. Being single-line is required for [internal completion representations](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35/src/vs/editor/common/languages.ts#L615-L616), but not stated in the DAP. The [related code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/repl.ts#L282-L322) mixes offset- and position-based range computations, which leads to messy behavior for multi-line ranges. A clean implementation should either filter out multi-line ranges early, or handle them correctly, leaving them to be filtered out later.

As far as I'm aware, these deviations do not cause problems most of the time, since existing debug adapter implementations seem to work around them. However, they make implementing a new adapter unnecessarily confusing, and should be explicitly stated somewhere or updated in the DAP itself.

Related topics:
- https://github.com/microsoft/debug-adapter-protocol/issues/138 (`start`/`length` interpretation)
- https://github.com/microsoft/debug-adapter-protocol/issues/285 (0- vs 1-based indexing)
- https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-dap/pull/1507 (similar discussion for nvim-dap)

issues.body:
Refs: #339067, #317380

- [x] windows @cwebster-99 (Node.js and .NET)
- [x] macOS @Giuspepe (Python and Rust)
- [x] linux @rzhao271 (Go and PHP)

Complexity: 3

Authors: @chrmarti

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+Dev+Container+samples%0A%0A&assignees=chrmarti)


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339581%0A%0A&assignees=chrmarti)

---

Test starting an Agent Host session from a Dev Container sample without first cloning a repository or creating a configuration. **Use local Docker; remote hosts are out of scope.**

## Set up

1. Use latest Insiders, sign in to Copilot, and verify `docker ps` works.
2. Enable:
   - `chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled`
   - `chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled`
   - `chat.agentHost.devContainer.samples.enabled`

   Set these explicitly so the test does not depend on experiment assignment.

3. Open the Agents Window. Prefer samples you have not previously tried: existing sample volumes and checkouts are reused. Do not delete unrelated containers, existing work, or the shared `vscode` volume.

## Test

### 1. Pick a sample without starting it

1. Open the workspace picker and verify **Dev Container Sample** offers Go, .NET, Node.js, PHP, Python, and Rust.
2. Select your first assigned sample. Verify:
   - It becomes the selected workspace without asking for a local clone folder.
   - No sample container or repository volume is created yet. Compare `docker ps -a` and `docker volume ls` before and after selection.
   - Worktree isolation cannot be selected for the sample.
3. Switch to the other assigned sample before sending. Verify this also does not start provisioning.
4. Check that the submenu can be opened and a sample selected using only the keyboard.

### 2. Start and use the sample

0. Disable sandboxing for this session, this is a known limitation.
1. Send:

   > Run `hostname` and `pwd`. Identify this sample's language/runtime, run its version command, and create `sample-test.txt` containing a short greeting.

2. Accept any trust or approval prompts. Verify:
   - Preparation starts only after sending.
   - Progress and **Show Log** are available.
   - The workspace is `/workspaces/vscode-remote-try-<sample>`.
   - The expected runtime is available and the file is created successfully.
   - The submitted prompt is sent once and the session remains usable.

3. Check the sample is usable.

## Finish and report

For failures, include the OS, Insiders build, sample, whether its volume already existed, the action taken, and Docker state. Attach the relevant **Agent Host** and **Dev Container** output channels after checking them for private content. Remove only disposable test files/resources that you created.

issues.title: High CPU feedback loop between prompt discovery and Open Editors view when Copilot is enabled

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (`07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`)
- OS Version: Windows client, Remote WSL2 / Linux

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a VS Code Remote WSL workspace with the bundled GitHub Copilot extension enabled.
2. Open at least one normal file/editor.
3. Switch to the **Explorer** Activity Bar view so that the Explorer/Open Editors UI is active.
4. Observe sustained high CPU in the remote extension-host process while VS Code is otherwise idle. In my reproduction the extension host remains at approximately **45–55% CPU**.
5. Switch from Explorer to another Activity Bar view, for example **Extensions**, while leaving the editor open. The CPU churn stops.
6. Switch back to Explorer. The CPU churn returns.
7. Alternatively, while Explorer remains visible, close all open editors. The CPU churn stops. Open an editor again and it returns.
8. Disabling GitHub Copilot and reloading also drops the extension-host CPU to approximately 1%.

## Summary

This appears to be a feedback loop involving prompt-provider discovery, readonly-state updates, the Open Editors view, and the `resourceExtname` context key.

The high CPU initially appears in the remote extension host inside GitHub Copilot, but tracing both the extension-host and renderer/application sides shows that VS Code core continuously invalidates and re-enumerates prompt providers.

The observed loop is approximately:

```text
ExtensionPromptFileService._listFromProviders()
    ↓
FilesConfigurationService.updateReadonly(readonlyUris, true)
    ↓
onDidChangeReadonly
    ↓
ResourceEditorInput capability change
    ↓
OpenEditorsView refresh / focusActiveEditor
    ↓
ResourceContextKey.reset() / set()
    ↓
resourceExtname: undefined ↔ ""
    ↓
ExtensionPromptFileService context-key invalidation
    ↓
prompt caches invalidated
    ↓
prompt discovery runs again
    ↓
ExtensionPromptFileService._listFromProviders()
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────↻
```

## Measurements

A CPU profile of the remote extension host showed the active path dominated by:

```text
onStreamRead
  → extension-host RPC
  → $providePromptFiles
  → GitHub Copilot provideCustomAgents
  → buildCustomizedConfig / _buildCustomizedConfig
  → getNonExtensionConfig
```

`onStreamRead` itself has negligible self-time and appears to be the IPC entry point rather than the expensive operation.

Instrumentation showed:

- `provideCustomAgents()`: **more than 1,000 calls in less than 10 seconds**
- extension-host `$providePromptFiles`: **more than 1,000 calls in less than 5 seconds**
- application-side `$providePromptFiles` also increments at a very high rate
- four separate `agent` provider handles advance almost in lockstep
- an `instructions` provider is also repeatedly invoked

The extension-host `$onDidChangePromptFiles` callback does **not** fire at this rate, so the storm does not appear to originate from `onDidChangeCustomAgents`.

## Context-key invalidation

The application-side `ExtensionPromptFileService.onDidChangeContext` callback also fires hundreds of times per second.

The tracked provider `when` keys at the time included:

```text
editorLangId
notebookType
resourceExtname
config.jsts-chat-features.skills.enabled
github.copilot.sessionSearch.enabled
config.github.copilot.chat.newWorkspace.useContext7
config.github.copilot.chat.installExtensionSkill.enabled
config.github.copilot.chat.newWorkspaceCreation.enabled
```

Instrumenting which key was changing identified `resourceExtname`.

In one short capture:

```text
resourceExtname = "":         20700
resourceExtname = undefined:  20699
```

The nearly exact 1:1 ratio suggested repeated `ResourceContextKey.reset()` / `ResourceContextKey.set()` calls.

## Captured call stacks

For `resourceExtname = ""`:

```text
ContextKeyService.setContext
→ ContextKey.set
→ ResourceContextKey.set
→ openEditorsView.ts
→ editor group/model change
→ ResourceEditorInput
→ FilesConfigurationService.updateReadonly
→ ExtensionPromptFileService._listFromProviders
→ getExtensionPromptFiles
→ PromptsService.computeListPromptFiles
→ computeAgentDiscoveryInfo
→ getCustomAgents
→ $provideCustomAgents
```

For `resourceExtname = undefined`:

```text
ContextKeyService.removeContext
→ ContextKey.reset
→ ResourceContextKey.reset
→ openEditorsView.ts
→ focusActiveEditor / list update
→ editor group/model change
→ ResourceEditorInput
→ FilesConfigurationService.updateReadonly
→ ExtensionPromptFileService._listFromProviders
→ ...
```

Specifically, the SET path reaches `openEditorsView.ts:382`, while the REMOVE path reaches `openEditorsView.ts:372`.

## Relevant source behavior

In VS Code 1.140, `ExtensionPromptFileService._listFromProviders()` ends by marking provider resources readonly:

```ts
void this.filesConfigService.updateReadonly(readonlyUris, true);
```

The array form of `FilesConfigurationService.updateReadonly()` fires `onDidChangeReadonly` whenever the array is non-empty:

```ts
if (Array.isArray(resource)) {
    for (const r of resource) {
        this.applyReadonly(r, readonly);
    }

    if (resource.length > 0) {
        this._onDidChangeReadonly.fire();
    }

    return;
}
```

This appears to happen even when the effective readonly state has not changed.

`ResourceEditorInput` listens for this global event and fires an editor capabilities change.

`OpenEditorsView` handles `EDITOR_CAPABILITIES` by replacing the list entry and calling `focusActiveEditor(true)`. Its focus-change handler performs:

```ts
resourceContext.reset();
...
resourceContext.set(resource ?? null);
```

For the resource in this reproduction, this changes:

```text
resourceExtname: undefined → "" → undefined → "" → ...
```

`ExtensionPromptFileService` tracks `resourceExtname` because it occurs in a prompt-provider/contribution `when` clause. Each context-key transition therefore invalidates prompt discovery, causing another provider enumeration and another `updateReadonly()`.

## UI dependency

The Explorer/Open Editors view is an important part of the reproduction.

With an editor open:

```text
Explorer visible
→ high CPU / continuous provider calls

Extensions pane visible
→ CPU churn stops

Explorer visible again
→ CPU churn resumes
```

Closing all editors also stops the loop.

This provides a reliable workaround without disabling Copilot.

## Expected behavior

Prompt-provider discovery should settle when neither the provider resources nor their effective readonly state has changed.

Displaying the Explorer/Open Editors UI should not cause continuous prompt-provider re-enumeration or sustained extension-host CPU usage while idle.

## Actual behavior

Readonly-state notification causes an editor-capability update, which causes Open Editors focus/context churn. The resulting `resourceExtname` changes invalidate prompt discovery, which invokes the providers again, producing a self-sustaining feedback loop and hundreds of `$providePromptFiles` RPC calls per second.

## Workarounds

Any of these stops the problem in this reproduction:

- switch away from Explorer to another Activity Bar pane, such as Extensions
- close all open editors
- disable GitHub Copilot

## Related issues

This appears related to the broader prompt/customization churn reported in:

- #304857
- #304858
- #305545

However, the mechanism observed here is different from a provider `onDidChangeCustomAgents` / `$onDidChangePromptFiles` feedback loop.

The measured path here is:

```text
updateReadonly
→ editor capability change
→ OpenEditorsView
→ resourceExtname context change
→ prompt cache invalidation
→ provider enumeration
```

I searched for an existing report describing this specific `updateReadonly → OpenEditorsView → resourceExtname → prompt discovery` loop and did not find an exact duplicate.

## Additional information

The problem was reproduced in a Remote WSL window. I have not yet verified whether the same feedback loop occurs in a local (non-remote) workspace or whether it is already fixed in the latest Insiders build.

issues.title: Insiders 1.141.0: "Cannot find package 'koffi'" - build/.moduleignore strips koffi now required by @microsoft/mxc-sdk 0.9.0
issues.body:
- VS Code Version: 1.141.0-insider
- OS: Windows 11 x64

### Steps to Reproduce

Run any agent shell tool (e.g. the Copilot run_in_terminal / run command tool).

### Expected

The command executes.

### Actual
Cannot find package 'koffi' imported from C:\Users<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\429a4ec703\resources\app\node_modules.asar@microsoft\mxc-sdk\dist\bindings\run.js

`koffi` is missing from both `node_modules.asar` and `node_modules.asar.unpacked` in the installed product.

### Cause

`build/.moduleignore` strips `koffi/**` and `@koromix/koffi-*/**` from product builds:

> `@github/copilot-sdk` uses Koffi only for its in-process FFI transport.
> VS Code uses RuntimeConnection.forStdio.

However, PR #338828 (milestone 1.141.0) bumped `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` from 0.8.0 to 0.9.0, whose `dist/bindings/run.js` does `import koffi from 'koffi'` at runtime (the PR description notes "MXC 0.9.0 adds koffi"). The `.moduleignore` exclusion was not updated, so every build >= 1.141.0 ships an mxc-sdk whose bindings cannot load.

### Suggested fix

Drop or narrow the koffi exclusion in `build/.moduleignore` (it targets the copilot-sdk transport, but mxc-sdk 0.9.0 needs koffi at runtime), or have `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` bundle its own koffi copy.

issues.title: [chat-perf] layoutDurationMs regressed 20–33% in 10 chat scenarios
issues.body:
### Summary
:rotating_light: New regression: layoutDurationMs increased 20–33% in 10 chat scenarios (text-only, tool-terminal, large-codeblock, file-links, thinking-response, many-small-chunks, tool-read-file, multi-turn-user, mixed-content, tool-edit-file). This is a broad and sustained regression not present in the prior 6-night window, which was stable.

### Evidence
- *text-only*: 162.73ms ±8.85ms → 208.3ms ±5.44ms (+28.0%)
- *tool-terminal*: 243.36ms ±6.54ms → 303.7ms ±4.84ms (+24.8%)
- *large-codeblock*: 183.62ms ±9.23ms → 232.4ms ±10.75ms (+26.6%)
- *file-links*: 229.29ms ±3.75ms → 275.43ms ±8.01ms (+20.1%)
- *thinking-response*: 169.14ms ±5.4ms → 225.58ms ±9.06ms (+33.4%)
- *many-small-chunks*: 190.25ms ±12.15ms → 239.69ms ±7.01ms (+26.0%)
- *tool-read-file*: 206.96ms ±8.45ms → 263.85ms ±11.19ms (+27.5%)
- *multi-turn-user*: 220ms ±5.45ms → 277.1ms ±13.65ms (+26.0%)
- *mixed-content*: 134.57ms ±3.51ms → 177.78ms ±8.09ms (+32.1%)
- *tool-edit-file*: 167.21ms ±6.63ms → 201.39ms ±7.85ms (+20.4%)

All p-values = 0 (statistically significant). No similar regressions in the previous 6-night window; all layoutDurationMs changes were within noise or improved.

#### Trend
- The regression is abrupt and present in all scenarios above, not a gradual drift.
- All prior baselines (last 6 runs) show layoutDurationMs within ~10% of previous values; this run jumps 20–33% across the board.

#### Suspect Commits
- Regression window: b10961b (last good) → 64a666e (current)
- 64a666e is a version bump; the bulk of changes are in the preceding commits.
- Several large merges affecting chat/session/layout code landed: e.g., 5270ba6 ("sessions: Stabilize docked side pane sizing"), 1f3057f ("sessions: Preserve workbench-level pane sizing"), 4ccdb71 ("sessions: Synchronize live last turn changes").
- These touch layout/session infrastructure and could plausibly impact layout counts/duration.

### Suggested Action
- Bisect between b10961b and 64a666e, focusing on session/layout-related changes (esp. 5270ba6, 1f3057f, 4ccdb71).
- Review for any changes that could increase layout churn or trigger extra layout passes in chat scenarios.
- Consider reverting or optimizing the responsible change(s) to restore previous layout performance.

issues.title: No way to open a single-file diff from the chat "N Files +X -Y" summary — only the combined multi-file diff opens
issues.body:
# No way to open a single-file diff from the chat "N Files +X -Y" summary — only the combined multi-file diff opens

## Version

- VS Code: `1.140.0` (commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`), `x64`
- OS: Windows

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In the Chat view, start an Agent-mode request that edits/creates multiple files (e.g. "create 3 new files for testing").
2. Wait for the request to complete. A compact summary bar appears under the response, showing `N Files` and `+<insertions> -<deletions>` counts (the "pills" style summary).
3. Click directly on the `+X -Y` counts / the file-changes bar.

## Expected Behavior

Previously (and as still documented in [Review and revert agent changes](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits)), clicking the summary should expand a disclosure list of the individual changed files, and clicking one of those files should open **that file's own diff** — not a combined multi-file diff.

## Actual Behavior

Clicking the `+X -Y` counts always opens the combined "View All File Changes" multi-file diff editor (`multi-diff-editor:`), with no way to review a single file's diff from this chat summary. This appears to be because, for this chat session type, the summary is rendered via the `chat-turn-pills-part` component, where the counts element is implemented as a `<button>` wired directly to `openChangesForRequest(...)` (always opens the combined diff), rather than the `checkpoint-file-changes-summary` component used elsewhere, which renders an expandable per-file list.

Relevant settings investigated and found **not** to control this:
- `chat.checkpoints.showFileChanges` — only toggles whether the summary bar is shown at all, not which component variant renders it.
- `sessions.changes.openSingleFileDiff` — only affects the separate **Agents window**, not the docked **Chat view**.
- `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled` — toggling this off/on does not change which summary component is used; the pills/combined-diff-only behavior persists either way.

## Impact

Users with many changed files in one turn can no longer inspect individual file diffs directly from the chat summary; they must fall back to the Source Control / Changes view to get a per-file diff.

## Suggested Fix

Either:
- Make the counts/`+X -Y` element in `chat-turn-pills-part` open the per-file disclosure list (like the `checkpoint-file-changes-summary` component) instead of always jumping to the combined diff, or
- Add a dedicated setting (e.g. extend `sessions.changes.openSingleFileDiff` or add a new `chat.checkpoints.openSingleFileDiff`) that also applies to the docked Chat view's pills summary.

## Screenshot

(Attach screenshot showing the "2 Files +42 -2" pill bar from the chat response — see session attachment.)

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0
- OS Version: Windows 11; WSL: Ubuntu 22.04

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a VS Code window connected to WSL and open a Python file from the WSL workspace Explorer.
2. Use Ctrl+I to request a simple change, such as adding `print("Hello, World!")` at the end of the file.
3. Let Copilot generate and apply the edit.

Expected behavior:
Copilot applies the generated change to the open file in the WSL workspace.

Actual behavior:
Copilot generates a response, but fails to apply the edit. Inline Chat reports that the requested change could not be applied and eventually aborts after repeated attempts.

Relevant versions:
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.68.0
- Models observed: mai-code-1.1-flash and gpt-6-luna

Relevant error excerpts:

`Invalid input path: home/<user>/.../hello.py. Be sure to use an absolute path.`

`Healed error: Error: File not found: \home\<user>\...\hello.py, original error: Error: File not found: \home\<user>\python-tutorial\guidelearn\hello.py`

The logs also show:
`Aborting inline chat edit: too many failed edit attempts`
`[InlineChat], BAIL_OUT because of needsExitTool`

The GitHub Copilot Chat extension can be found through Extensions search, but does not appear under either “Local - Installed” or “WSL: Ubuntu-22.04 - Installed”. Its details page shows “Disable AI Features”; the extension installation location is unclear.

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74)
- OS Version: Windows 11

With `diffEditor.hideUnchangedRegions.enabled`, unchanged regions sometimes show up partially or fully expanded. Toggling the setting off and on again collapses them.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Set `"diffEditor.hideUnchangedRegions.enabled": false`.
2. Open a diff of a long file with a single change in the middle.
3. Click or Go to Line into unchanged lines in both editors.
4. Turn on collapsing unchanged regions (diff editor toolbar or setting).
5. :bug: The unchanged regions are expanded (partially or fully).

The same happens without step 4 when reopening a diff whose view state was saved while the setting was off. It also happens when reopening a diff that changed since it was last viewed, e.g. the SCM diff of a file that was edited in the meantime.

Fixed by #339567.

issues.title: Agent Host: search_code_subagent child turns never complete and are reported as cancelled

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.139 and 1.140 (seen on both)
- OS Version: All

Found while investigating the "possibly related" items in #339326.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In an Agent Host Copilot session, send a request that makes the agent call the `search_code_subagent` tool.
2. Let the tool call finish, and let the parent turn finish.
3. With telemetry output logging on, look for the `agentHost.turnCompleted` event of the subagent chat whose `parentToolCallId` is that tool call.

### What's happening

The child turn that the host opens for a `search_code_subagent` call is not completed when the search finishes. It stays open until something cancels it, such as the user cancelling a later turn or the session being disposed.

In telemetry, for subagent turns whose spawning tool call is `search_code_subagent`:

- Nearly all end with `result: cancelled`, a small share end with `error`, and practically none end with `success`.
- The spawning `search_code_subagent` tool call itself reports `success`.
- The cancelled turns stay open for a long time: the median is tens of minutes, against a few minutes for `task` subagents.
- Each such subagent has exactly one turn.

The same pattern is present on 1.139 and 1.140, so this is not a 1.140 regression. It is more visible on 1.140 because `search_code_subagent` makes up a larger share of subagent turns there.

### Likely cause (not confirmed)

The host completes a subagent turn in two places only: when the SDK's task list reports the agent task as idle, completed, failed or cancelled ([`_reconcileBackgroundTasks`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0227a45005a/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts)), and on abort. The SDK's `subagent.completed` and `subagent.failed` events are only logged. If the `search_code_subagent` child never appears in the task list as an agent task, nothing closes its turn. I have not confirmed that it is absent from the task list.

### Impact

- **Subagent outcome metrics:** these turns count as cancelled subagent turns with very long durations, which skews cancellation rates and duration percentiles for subagents.
- **`subagentTaskModelSource` coverage:** `search_code_subagent` is not a `task`-tool subagent, so its turns never carry `subagentTaskModelSource`. Because they almost all end as cancelled, they look like "cancelled subagent launches missing `subagentTaskModelSource`". `task`-tool subagent turns themselves do not miss the source. This explains that item in #339326.
- **Open turn state:** the subagent chat keeps an active turn in host state long after its work is done.

### Suggested fix

- Complete the child turn when the SDK reports `subagent.completed` or `subagent.failed` for it, or when its spawning tool call completes and no agent task exists for it.
- Until then, analysis of `task`-tool subagents can exclude subagent turns whose `parentToolCallId` belongs to a `search_code_subagent` tool call.

issues.title: Extension host crash-loops on every startup after Microsoft account sign-in (fixed only by clearing microsoft-authentication session state)

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **Yes** — verified with `code --disable-extensions`: the extension host still terminated 3 times within 30 s. `vscode.microsoft-authentication` is a built-in extension that stays enabled even with `--disable-extensions`, and its activation is the last thing logged before every crash (zero third-party extensions were activated in that test run). Also reproduces with all installed extensions disabled via the Extensions view.

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`, x64), **portable mode** (Scoop install; user data under `<install>/data`)
- OS Version: Windows 10 Pro, version 26H2 (build 26300)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On VS Code 1.140.0 (portable mode), install the *C# Dev Kit* extension and complete the Microsoft account sign-in it requests (personal `@outlook.com` account). This persists a Microsoft session into `state.vscdb` (`secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"accounts-AzureCloud"}` and `…publicClients-AzureCloud`, the MSAL token cache).
2. Open any window (even an empty folder). The extension host dies within ~5 s of startup, auto-restarts, dies again → dialog: *"Extension host terminated unexpectedly 3 times within the last 5 minutes."* This repeats on **every** startup.
3. Uninstalling C# Dev Kit does **not** stop the crashes; disabling all extensions does **not** stop them.
4. Close VS Code and delete the `vscode.microsoft-authentication` session keys from `data/user-data/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb` (equivalent to signing out) → startup is stable again.

Caveat: the sign-in step itself was observed once and not re-tested from a clean profile; the session data being the trigger is verified by add/remove experiments (below).

## Evidence

**Every crash's last logged activity is the activation of the built-in auth extension.** `exthost.log` ends abruptly ~0.2–2 s after this line, with no error of any kind (no JS stack, no OOM message; no WER/Application Error event for `Code.exe` either):

```
12:40:25.583 [info] ExtensionService#_doActivateExtension vscode.microsoft-authentication, startup: false, activationEvent: 'onAuthenticationRequest:microsoft'
… (only harmless i18n warnings) …
<end of file — process died silently>
```

`renderer.log` (repeats every few seconds, 8+ times across two sessions; note the running-list tail):

```
12:40:26.146 [error] Extension host (LocalProcess pid: 52620) terminated unexpectedly. The following extensions were running: …, ivnjey.ai-translator, vscode.microsoft-authentication, johnny-zhao.oai-compatible-copilot
12:40:26.147 [info] Automatically restarting the extension host.
```

**Controlled experiments** (empty temp workspace, 30 s observation per launch, VS Code otherwise closed):

| Launch | `state.vscdb` | Exthost crashes | `microsoft-authentication` activated |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal | Microsoft session present | 2–3 (every run) | yes |
| `code --disable-extensions` | Microsoft session present | 3 | yes (built-in stays enabled; 0 third-party activations in log) |
| normal | session keys deleted | **0** (stable >60 s) | — |

## Workaround / Fix Applied

With VS Code closed, delete from `ItemTable` in `state.vscdb` (i.e. sign out):

```sql
DELETE FROM ItemTable WHERE key IN (
  'secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"accounts-AzureCloud"}',
  'secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.microsoft-authentication","key":"publicClients-AzureCloud"}',
  'vscode.microsoft-authentication',
  'microsoft-<account>',
  'microsoft-<account>-usages'
);
```

Suspect: the MSAL token cache (`publicClients-AzureCloud`) fails hard (rather than gracefully) while the session is restored, killing the extension host process. Expected behavior: a bad persisted session should surface a recoverable error (discard + re-authenticate), never a silent process exit on every startup.

## Additional Context

- Portable-mode detail that may or may not be relevant: this is a Scoop-managed install whose `data/` directory is moved between versioned install dirs on updates (e.g. `…\vscode\1.140.0\data`).
- Locale: `zh-cn`; ~45 extensions installed (list available on request; irrelevant per the `--disable-extensions` test).
- I preserved a backup of the pre-fix `state.vscdb` containing the offending session blob. It holds live auth tokens, so it will not be attached publicly, but I can provide it privately or run further diagnostics on request.
- Not yet tested on an Insiders build (no Insiders portable setup at hand).

issues.title: Copilot Chat `copilot_sessionStoreSql` tool blocks read-only queries whose string literals contain SQL keywords, with a misleading error message

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
- **Copilot Chat Extension Version:** @github/copilot 1.0.89-7 (@github/copilot-sdk 1.0.15-preview.4)
- **VS Code Version:** 1.140.0 (system setup), Commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74
- **OS Version:** Windows_NT x64 10.0.19045 (VS Code Remote — WSL2 Ubuntu)
- **Feature:** Agent mode — `copilot_sessionStoreSql` tool (chronicle session store), `/chronicle search`
- **Selected model:** Z.ai GLM 5.3 Flash via OpenRouter
- **Logs:** Attached `blocked-sql-evidence.json` — 4 consecutive `copilot_sessionStoreSql` tool-call records from Chat Debug View showing identical read-only queries blocked with the misleading "Only SELECT or WITH" error (the retry loop). Request-level logs and successful-query responses omitted as they contain conversation content and session history snippets.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Enable the session index (`github.copilot.chat.localIndex.enabled`) and ask the agent to search session history, or run `/chronicle search` with a term containing a SQL keyword.
2. The agent sends the tool a read-only query such as:

```sql
SELECT session_id FROM turns
WHERE user_message ILIKE '%memory create%'
```

3. The tool returns: `Error: Blocked SQL statement. Only SELECT or WITH queries are allowed.` — even though the query **is** a SELECT. The actual trigger is the substring `create` inside the `ILIKE` string literal. The agent retried the identical query 4+ times (see attached log) before the cause was diagnosed manually.

**Expected:** the read-only query executes (or a blocklist rejection names the actual reason).

**Actual:** rejected with a message asserting the query is not a SELECT/WITH statement, which is false.

## Analysis

The blocklist in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/sessionStoreSqlTool.ts` is applied to the raw SQL string, including quoted literals:

```ts
const BLOCKED_PATTERNS = [
    /\b(INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|DROP|CREATE|ALTER|TRUNCATE|REPLACE)\b/i,
    ...
];
for (const pattern of BLOCKED_PATTERNS) {
    if (pattern.test(sql)) { ... }  // tests raw sql — literals included
}
```

Any search term containing `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `drop`, `alter`, `replace`, `vacuum`, `begin`, etc. false-positives. Conversation-text search is a primary use case of this tool, so such terms are common.

**Impact:**

1. False positives on legitimate queries.
2. The blocklist check and the allowlist check return the *identical* message string, so the model is told its query isn't a SELECT/WITH when it is — this directly caused an extended identical-retry loop in a real session.
3. Telemetry already distinguishes `blocked_mutating_sql` vs `blocked_not_select_or_with` — the information exists but isn't surfaced to the model.

## Suggested fixes (in order of value)

1. **Distinct error messages per check**, mirroring the telemetry discriminators. Trivial change.
2. **Include the matched pattern category + remediation hint**, e.g. *"Blocked keyword `CREATE` detected. Keywords inside string literals (e.g. ILIKE patterns) also trigger this check — rephrase the search term if your query is read-only."* Keep it to the pattern category, not raw matched text — enough to recover, not enough to probe the filter.
3. **Fix the false positive — but not with a naive literal-stripping regex.** A regex must agree with the engine tokenizer on `''` doubling, backslash escapes, DuckDB dollar-quoting, and quotes inside comments; any divergence in the over-strip direction hides a real `DROP` and becomes a bypass. Prefer parser-based classification (local SQLite `prepare()`/`setAuthorizer` already enforces at the engine level; enforce read-only server-side for cloud DuckDB), or fail-closed literal stripping where ambiguity means *reject*. Note the blocklist is belt-and-suspenders on top of engine enforcement, so (3) is heuristic correctness, not the primary boundary.

## Relation to existing issues

- #317358 (error rate trending up) counts blocked calls in the error budget and notes "blocked is a success, not a failure" — this issue shows a class of blocks that are *false positives*, i.e. the guardrail misfiring on valid read-only queries, which inflates that error rate and wastes model retries.
- #317355 (schema hallucination, closed) addressed wrong-column errors; this is a different failure class (valid schema, valid SELECT, rejected by the keyword blocklist).
- No existing issue found describing the blocklist scanning string literals.

issues.title: Test: Agent Host Copilot background shell tracking
issues.body:
Refs: #338723, #339220, #339345

- [x] macOS @pwang347
- [x] Linux @rzhao271
- [ ] Windows @connor4312 

Complexity: 3

Authors: @anthonykim1

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339555%0A%0A&assignees=anthonykim1)

---

Verify that background shells are tracked above the chat input and removed when they finish.

## Setup

Use a build containing the referenced PRs and a local **Agent Host Copilot** session. Keep `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` set to `false`.

Test in both the **Agents window** and an **editor-window Agent Host chat**.

## Attached shell

Ask Copilot:

> Use your shell tool to run `sleep 120` in async mode, without detaching. Don't wait for it to finish.

Verify:

- A **1 Background Shell** pill appears above the input.
- Open the pill. The row shows elapsed time without a **Detached** label.
- The details show the command and running status. Because `sleep 120` is silent, the output area shows **No output yet.**
- Try another attached command that prints periodically. Its details show the output streaming in the small read-only terminal.
- The turn stays active until the command exits, which is existing behavior.
- The shell disappears when it finishes, and the pill disappears when the list is empty.

## Detached shell

After the attached shell finishes, ask Copilot:

> Use your shell tool to run `sleep 120` in async mode with detach set to true.

Verify:

- A **1 Background Shell** pill appears above the input.
- The row shows **Detached** and elapsed time. Its details show the command, shell ID, and start time.
- The response can finish while the detached shell continues running.
- The shell disappears after it exits and the list refreshes.

## Exploratory checks

**Be creative with attached and detached scenarios; don't limit testing to these two examples.** Try development servers, builds, test runs, and commands with or without output.

- Start multiple shells and confirm the count updates as individual commands finish.
- Switch sessions or reload VS Code. The list should reflect the correct session's currently running shells.
- Try an attached build or test command that prints output. Check that new output appears in both the shell details and the original terminal preview.
- Ask Copilot to stop a test shell and confirm it leaves the list.

Stop any remaining test commands when finished.

issues.title: Background task completion error event omits the final resource
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Reproduced in core unit tests without extension activation; an installed-app reproduction was not run.

- VS Code Version: 1.141.0 development, source commit 0817aaa824590067854c361e77eb973a08b3cf48
- OS Version: macOS arm64, Node 24.18.0; source-level reproduction

WatchingProblemCollector emits onDidFindErrors before flushing markers for its current resource when a background end pattern matches. With one file, the completion event is empty even though the MarkerService subsequently contains its diagnostics. With multiple files, the completion event omits the last file. Repeated cycles can expose markers from the previous cycle in that final-resource slot.

Expected behavior: the completed-cycle error snapshot includes diagnostics for the final resource before consumers are notified.

Reproduced on main commit 0817aaa824590067854c361e77eb973a08b3cf48 using WatchingProblemCollector and the real MarkerService, an active-on-start matcher with begin/end patterns, and one-file and two-file cycles. Tests await the public BackgroundProcessingEnds event and inspect the onDidFindErrors payload. They also cover repeated and empty cycles.

The narrow correction is to flush the current resource before reading MarkerService for the completion error event. This report concerns completion-event contents; it does not establish that historical Problems-panel issue #179361 is resolved.

Steps to reproduce in the repository test runner:

1. Use the focused [regression tests](https://github.com/rksharma-owg/vscode/blob/751432217953b83e4a0993702e46890f4c4a5fac/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/test/common/problemCollectors.test.ts) with problemCollectors.ts from the baseline commit.
2. Process begin, two matching diagnostic lines for a.ts, and end through the watcher.
3. Await BackgroundProcessingEnds and inspect the captured onDidFindErrors snapshot: expected both errors, observed an empty snapshot.

issues.title: Task problem monitor drops distinct errors on the same file
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Reproduced in core unit tests without extension activation; an installed-app reproduction was not run.

- VS Code Version: 1.141.0 development, source commit 0817aaa824590067854c361e77eb973a08b3cf48
- OS Version: macOS arm64, Node 24.18.0; source-level reproduction

When a completed task reports two distinct errors for the same resource, TaskProblemMonitor.getTaskProblems() retains only the last error. For example, an event containing errors on lines 1 and 2 of /a.ts returns one marker rather than two. Errors on different resources are retained.

The per-owner marker map is keyed only by the resource URI, so later markers for the same file overwrite earlier markers. This affects the diagnostics available to task tools that consume getTaskProblems().

Expected behavior: retain distinct errors and their resource associations while deduplicating identical markers.

Reproduced on main commit 0817aaa824590067854c361e77eb973a08b3cf48 with the actual TaskProblemMonitor and its public event input. A focused regression test exercises same-file errors, different files, owners, identical repeats, cycle replacement, invalidation, and terminal disposal.

A minimal fix can combine the resource URI with the project's existing marker identity key. No change to warning filtering or task-output formatting is needed.

Steps to reproduce in the repository test runner:

1. Use the focused [regression test](https://github.com/rksharma-owg/vscode/blob/42bcbc3eb3a79b9dccb836eaec4a1a649b694595/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/test/browser/taskProblemMonitor.test.ts) with TaskProblemMonitor from the baseline commit.
2. Fire the collector error event with two markers for the same resource, at different lines.
3. Read getTaskProblems(1): expected two distinct markers, observed only the last.

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: A synthetic task-provider extension is required to exercise the real `vscode.tasks` API. The otherwise-unreachable callbacks are retained by VS Code's extension-host cache.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev, `dcb81648f8a8f1863d2577f8fec98e805e5f95a0`; affected source files are unchanged on checked main `6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4`.
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise x64.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Register a task provider returning one `Task` with a `CustomExecution`. Its callback captures a deterministically filled 2 MiB buffer.
2. Successfully discover it through `vscode.tasks.fetchTasks`, checking its definition and execution type.
3. Dispose the provider registration and drop the fixture's strong references to the task, callback, and payload.
4. Verify discovery returns no tasks and there are no active task executions or terminals. Force extension-host GC twice at a settled boundary.
5. Repeat with distinct task identities, using one warmup and five measured cycles.
6. Compare with register/dispose without discovery and with discovery using the same task identity.

**Expected:** Otherwise-unreachable custom-execution callbacks and captured data are released, rather than accumulating indefinitely under obsolete task identities.

**Actual:** Five measured discovery/disposal cycles retain **10 MiB** of native buffer backing storage in all four fresh windows.

| Scenario | Additional retained payload after five cycles |
|---|---:|
| Distinct task identities, discover then dispose | **10 MiB** |
| Register then dispose without discovery | **0 bytes** |
| Discover then dispose, reusing the same identity | **0 bytes** |

No task callback is executed. No task process or terminal is created.

### Root cause

[Provider disposal](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTask.ts#L452) removes its handler but leaves successful entries in `_providedCustomExecutions2`.

Native heap ownership:

`ExtHostTask -> _providedCustomExecutions2 -> CustomExecution -> callback closure -> Buffer -> ArrayBuffer -> native backing storage`

### Scope

The **2 MiB payload is synthetic** to make ownership measurable; it is not a typical task-size or user-frequency estimate. External memory, weakly observed live payloads, and native snapshot sizes agree. The `arrayBuffers` counter stays zero in this Electron runtime and is not used as the proof.

This is distinct from #338231: that PR handles failed provider/task-ID promises and pending RPC replies. Here discovery succeeds, registration is disposed, and obsolete callback-cache entries remain.

The installed Insiders comparison was blocked by a pending-update guard; the shared installation was left untouched.

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: The built-in Markdown extension is required. No third-party renderer is used; a development fixture opens the built-in preview.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev, `dcb81648f8a8f1863d2577f8fec98e805e5f95a0`; affected source files are unchanged on checked main `6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4`.
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise x64.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a built-in preview for generated Markdown containing 16,000 ordinary numbered paragraphs separated by blank lines: 32,000 source lines and 944,000 bytes.
2. Capture its rendered HTML.
3. Invoke the existing preview `updateContent` handler with that HTML and no line changes as a control.
4. Invoke the same unmodified handler with identical HTML and valid added-line metadata covering source lines 0 through 31,999.
5. After a warmup, measure five updates per mode. Verify all paragraph text and every added paragraph marker.

**Expected:** Marking a bulk addition should not repeatedly rescan the entire document for each changed source line.

**Actual:** Every large marked sample blocks the preview handler for more than 200 ms.

| Fresh window | Marked handler median | Same-HTML unmarked control |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | **709.1 ms** | 41.8 ms |
| 2 | **607.2 ms** | 43.6 ms |
| 3 | **676.5 ms** | 44.2 ms |

At 8,000 paragraphs, marked medians are approximately 273 ms versus 24 ms for controls. Exact paragraph text and marker counts pass in every promoted sample.

### Root cause

[`markChangedLines`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4/extensions/markdown-language-features/preview-src/index.ts#L444) calls [`getElementsForSourceLine`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4/extensions/markdown-language-features/preview-src/scroll-sync.ts#L87) for every changed line. Each lookup restarts at the beginning of the mapped element array, even for monotonically increasing lines.

### Scope

This isolates the **real production preview handler with synthetic valid diff metadata**. It is not a claim that full rendered-diff opening takes exactly these times. HTML generation, diff calculation, and additional inline highlighting are not included in the promoted measurement.

The installed Insiders comparison was blocked by a pending-update guard; the shared installation was left untouched.

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. The reproduction disables extensions and supplies synthetic diagnostics directly to the workbench marker service.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev, `dcb81648f8a8f1863d2577f8fec98e805e5f95a0`; affected source files are unchanged on checked main `6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4`.
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise x64.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open Problems in tree mode. Publish four error diagnostics for each of 500 resource URIs: 2,000 current diagnostics in total.
2. Update diagnostics for just one existing resource while Problems remains visible. This invalidates the marker model's sorted-resource cache.
3. Hide Problems using the panel toggle.
4. Replace all diagnostics while hidden, changing their messages but preserving resource URIs, ranges, and counts.
5. Show Problems again. It correctly displays 2,000 current diagnostics.
6. Repeat steps 2-5 seven times, collecting garbage at settled measurement boundaries.

**Expected:** Obsolete per-marker view models are released. Only state for the current diagnostics remains.

**Actual:** The Problems view strongly retains 15,976 marker view models, including **13,976 obsolete models**.

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---:|
| Median retained renderer heap per cycle, four fresh windows | **20.02-20.10 MiB** |
| Same diagnostic updates with Problems kept visible | **0.046-0.052 MiB/cycle** |
| Current diagnostics after seven cycles | **2,000** |
| Obsolete view models after seven cycles | **13,976** |

Clearing diagnostics while Problems is visible releases all accumulated view states. Backing storage remains approximately constant; the reported growth is renderer JavaScript heap.

### Root cause

[Visibility cleanup](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4/src/vs/workbench/contrib/markers/browser/markersView.ts#L558) resets the marker model before enumerating its resources to remove per-resource view states. When the sorted-resource cache is invalid, that enumeration sees an empty model and skips cleanup.

The snapshot retainer is `MarkersView -> markersViewModel -> markersViewStates Map -> obsolete MarkerViewModels`.

### Scope

Real Problems UI and production classes, with synthetic diagnostics: 77-character messages and a 1,478,001-byte serialized payload. This is not a language-server or typing-latency measurement. A single-resource update before hiding and changed diagnostic identities while hidden are required; plain hide/show is not sufficient.

Installed-release regression status was not tested. This is distinct from the typing-update issue #109406 and the broad, closed 18,000-error report #125929.

Currently, unit tests for `toCodeReviewResult` in the review command cover successful/resolved promise-based suggestions, but there is a lack of test coverage for handling rejected or failed promise-based suggestions (`Promise.reject`).

issues.title: Add version validation check in CopilotExtensionApi.getContextProviderAPI
issues.body:
## Problem Statement
In `extensions/github-copilot/src/extensionApi.ts`, the `getContextProviderAPI` method accepts a version parameter (currently typed as `'v1'`), but it uses an underscore prefix (`_version`) and lacks runtime validation. If future versions are introduced or unsupported versions are requested, there is no explicit validation or safeguard.

## Proposed Solution
Add a runtime check inside `getContextProviderAPI` to explicitly validate the requested API version, ensuring that unsupported versions throw an informative error (e.g., throwing an error if the version is not `'v1'`).

## Benefits
- Improves API robustness and future-proofing.
- Prevents unhandled fallback behaviors when dealing with extension API versions.

issues.title: Enhance resilience and debugging context in chat input focus automation script
issues.body:
## Overview
The chat input focus helper script (used in Playwright CLI automation) occasionally encounters timing or visibility hurdles in complex UI states or CI/CD pipelines. Currently, when it fails to find or focus a visible chat input, the thrown error lacks detailed diagnostic context.

## Proposed Improvements
1. **Richer Error Context:** When `throw new Error` is triggered (e.g., after shortcut and command palette fallback attempts), include more diagnostic details such as the current platform, evaluated selectors, and whether the command palette fallback was invoked.
2. **Resilience & Debugging:** Make the failure logs more informative to quickly trace flaky test behavior in automated environments.

## Benefits
This will drastically reduce debugging time for flaky UI tests and improve the overall reliability of chat-related automation workflows in VS Code.

issues.title: Codex agent: overlapping thread restarts before the first turn lose the conversation
issues.body:
**What goes wrong**

Before a Codex session's first turn, the agent host restarts the session's app-server thread whenever client tools, MCP servers, customizations, hook trust or the selected agent change, since Codex only takes these at `thread/start`. Several of these triggers can restart the same session at once. Each restart unsubscribes the current thread, clears it and starts a new one, so overlapping restarts each start a thread.

The first turn then runs on one of those threads while the restart that finishes last persists another as the session's thread. The turn's history is on a thread the session no longer points to, so the next time the session is resumed (window reload, agent host restart) it opens the other thread and the conversation is gone.

Two related failures:

- A first send that reads the session's thread while another restart is in flight fails with `Cannot use Codex session <id>: no backing thread`.
- A restart that begins after the turn is claimed but before `turn/start` returns unsubscribes the thread the turn runs on and starts a new one.

**Steps to reproduce** (timing-dependent)

1. Open a new Codex chat in a folder and let the agent host prewarm its thread.
2. Before the first message, trigger a thread restart (change the selected agent, push new client tools, MCP servers or customizations, or complete MCP auth for a server the session uses), trigger a second one while it is in flight, and send the first message.
3. In the agent host log, two `thread/start` requests overlap, the first restart's thread is never unsubscribed, and `turn/start` names a thread other than the `threadId` persisted for the session.
4. Reload the window and reopen the chat: the first exchange is missing.

**Expected**

Restarts of one session run one at a time, the first turn runs on the thread the session persists, and a restart requested once the turn is claimed resumes the thread with the new settings on the next turn instead of replacing it.

**Cause**

In `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/codexAgent.ts`, nothing serializes `CodexAgent._restartThreadWithCurrentTools` per session. Each call unsubscribes `session.threadId`, sets it to `undefined`, drops `session.materializePromise` and calls `_materializeIfNeeded`, which starts another `thread/start`. It is called from `_sendMessage` (the pre-turn restart), `_ensureCurrentLaunchBeforeTurn`, `_doReconcileMaterializedCustomizations`, `_changeAgent` and `_reconnectSessionsForMcpAuth`. `_sendMessage` reads the thread through `_ensureThreadConnection` and claims the turn regardless of a restart in flight, and the restart path checks only `firstTurnSent` (set after `turn/start` returns), not whether a turn has been claimed (`currentTurnId`).

A fix with tests follows in a PR.
