issues.title: Agent-host sessions switch model after their first turn because no agent-host model is declared default
issues.body:
A new agent-host session (seen with Codex) that is started without picking a model runs its first turn on the agent's own default model, and from the next turn on the chat input sends a different one: the first non-BYOK model of the session's list sorted by name. Codex compacts the context to switch model; when the account cannot use that other model, the turn fails.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Sign in so the Codex agent host lists its models.
2. Start a new Codex agent-host session without choosing a model.
3. Send a message: it runs on the model Codex reports as its default (`isDefault` in `model/list`).
4. Send a second message.

**Expected**

The second turn runs on the same model as the first: the chat input selects the agent's default model.

**Actual**

The chat input selects the alphabetically first non-BYOK model, so the second turn switches model (with a context compaction), or fails when that model is not available to the account.

**Cause**

- `AgentHostLanguageModelProvider.provideLanguageModelChatInfo` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostLanguageModelProvider.ts`) publishes every model with `isDefaultForLocation: {}`.
- With no declared default, `ChatInputModelSelectionController._defaultModel` falls back to the first non-BYOK model of the pool from `ChatInputPart.getModelsForSessionType`, which sorts by `metadata.name`.
- The agents publish their default first — `CodexAgent` sorts `model/list` by `isDefault` (and CAPI models by `is_chat_default`) and itself falls back to `models[0]` when no model is sent; `ClaudeAgent._fetchProxyModels` sorts by `is_chat_default` — but `SessionModelInfo` carries no default flag, so that order is lost once the chat input sorts by name. (The Agents window's own pool keeps publication order, so its fallback already lands on the first model.)

A fix with a test follows in a PR.

issues.title: Agent-host chats welcome with "Delegate to @agent-host-codex" and say the chat is forwarded to a coding agent
issues.body:
An empty chat of an agent-host session shows the generic coding-agent welcome:

- Title: **Delegate to @agent-host-codex** (for an agent on a remote agent host, **Delegate to @remote-<authority>-codex**)
- Message: *This chat session will be forwarded to the @agent-host-codex coding agent where work is completed in the background.*

Neither is accurate: an agent-host chat runs the agent directly, on this machine or on the named remote host — nothing is forwarded or done in the background — and the title shows the session type's internal id instead of the agent's name.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. With the agent host enabled, open the Agents window and start a new session with an agent-host agent (e.g. Codex).
2. Watch the chat before the first request renders: the welcome above appears, briefly on a new session and for longer when a session's earlier turns load slowly.
3. Or, in the Chat view, choose an agent-host session type (local, or an agent on a remote agent host) and leave the chat empty: the welcome stays.

**Expected**

The welcome names the agent by its display name (e.g. "Codex", or "Codex [my-host]" for a remote host) and says where it runs, without delegation wording.

**Cause**

When a chat is locked to a coding agent, `ChatWidget.getWelcomeViewContent` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts`) uses the chat session contribution's `welcomeTitle` / `welcomeMessage`, and otherwise falls back to `"Delegate to {0}"` and the "forwarded to the … coding agent" message with the locked agent's `@name` — for agent-host sessions, the session type id. Neither `AgentHostContribution._registerAgent` (`agentHostChatContribution.ts`) nor `RemoteAgentHostContribution._registerAgent` (`remoteAgentHostChatContribution.ts`) sets `welcomeTitle` or `welcomeMessage`. The widget locks to these session types from `chatView.ts` (Agents window), `chatViewPane.ts`, `chatEditor.ts` and `chatInputPart.ts`.

A fix with tests follows in a PR.

issues.title: Removing several remote agent hosts at once briefly renames the remaining ones to their address
issues.body:
When one change to the configured remote agent hosts removes two or more connected hosts, each removal fires `IRemoteAgentHostService.onDidChangeConnections`, and those events list the hosts still waiting to be removed under their **address** instead of their configured name (and without their `operatingSystem`). Consumers that compare names treat that as a rename.

In the Agents window, `RemoteAgentHostContribution` (`remoteAgentHostChatContribution.ts`) then tears down each such host's agent registrations (chat session type, customization harness, session handler, language model provider) and registers them again as `<agent> [<address>]`, re-authenticates and re-subscribes to the host's logs — only for the next removal event to dispose all of it.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In the Agents window, configure two named hosts in `chat.remoteAgentHosts`, e.g. `[{ "name": "Host A", "address": "hosta:8080" }, { "name": "Host B", "address": "hostb:8080" }]`, and wait until both are connected.
2. Remove both entries in one edit (e.g. set `chat.remoteAgentHosts` to `[]`).
3. The window log shows, for the second host, `[RemoteAgentHost] Reconnecting contribution for hostb:8080: ... nameChanged=true`, then `Registered agent ... from hostb:8080 ...` for each of its agents, then `Removing contribution for hostb:8080`.

The same happens in the editor window when a connection factory stops exposing several cloud sandbox hosts at once.

**Expected**

Every `onDidChangeConnections` names each listed connection by its configured name; removing hosts never reads as a rename of the ones that remain.

**Cause**

`RemoteAgentHostService._reconcileConnections` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/remoteAgentHostServiceImpl.ts`) clears and rebuilds `_names` from the desired entries, then drops the label formatters and `_operatingSystems` of addresses no longer configured, and only then runs the "Remove connections no longer exposed by a factory" loop. Each `_removeConnection` fires `onDidChangeConnections`, and the `connections` getter names each entry `this._names.get(address) ?? address` — so the connections not yet removed have already lost their names.

A fix with a test follows in a PR.

issues.title: Agents window: Claude Agent SDK is never downloaded for sessions on a remote SSH host (download offer is local-only), Claude target silently does nothing

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74), same version for the client and the server installed on the remote host
- OS Version: client Windows 11 Enterprise, build 26200.9445; remote host Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-1064-aws, x64

**Summary**

In the Agents window, a Claude harness session on a **remote SSH host** can never download the Claude Agent SDK. The "Download the Claude Agent" chat-input notification is only shown for sessions on the *local* Agent Host, and the remote Agent Host never downloads lazily either. The remote Claude provider therefore stays in `notDownloaded` state forever: the model picker is empty, pressing Enter in the chat does nothing, and `createSession` fails with "Authentication is required to use Claude" even though a native Claude setup (BYOK via Amazon Bedrock) is configured on the remote host and `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable` is enabled.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On a Linux host reachable over SSH, configure Claude Code for a third-party provider, here Amazon Bedrock, in `~/.claude/settings.json` (`env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`, `AWS_REGION`, credentials from the EC2 instance role). The CLI works on that host. The host has never had the Claude Agent SDK downloaded (`~/.vscode-server/data/agent-host/sdk-cache/claude/<version>` does not exist).
2. On the client, do not sign in to GitHub. Set `"chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable": true`. Leave `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled` at its default (true).
3. Open the Agents window (`code --agents`), **New**, **Remote**, **SSH**, connect to the host, pick a folder.
4. Open **Session Target** and choose **Claude**.
5. Type a prompt and press Enter.

**Actual**

- Nothing happens. The model picker for Claude is empty. No "Download the Claude Agent" notification appears above the chat input.
- Choosing **Copilot** instead sends the prompt and then asks to sign in, as expected while signed out.
- On the remote host, `~/.vscode-server/data/logs/<timestamp>/agenthost.log` shows the Claude provider waiting for an SDK that is never requested; there is no `[AgentSdkDownloader]` line at all:

```
[info] [Claude] SDK not downloaded yet; deferring chat discovery
[info] [Claude] Models refreshed (merged). Count: 0,
[info] [Claude] SDK not downloaded yet; deferring the migratable chat list
[error] [ProtocolServer] Request 'createSession' failed Authentication is required to use Claude
```

- `agent-host-config.json` on the remote confirms the setting arrived: `"allowSignedOutWhenUsable": true`. `agent-host-storage.json` contains no `agentSdkDownloadConsent` entry, so the provider publishes `download: "notDownloaded"`.

**Expected**

Either the SDK download offer appears for remote sessions as it does for local ones, or the remote Agent Host downloads the SDK when a Claude session is created, so that the native account check runs and Claude BYOK models appear. If remote execution of the Claude harness is intentionally unsupported, the Session Target or the chat input should say so instead of silently ignoring Enter.

**Analysis (from the 1.140.0 sources)**

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSdkSetupNotification.ts`: `createAgentSdkSetupNotification` sets `sessionTypes: [agentSdkSetupSessionType(setup.agent)]`, and `agentSdkSetupSessionType` returns `LOCAL_AGENT_HOST_SCHEME_PREFIX + agent`. The notification can therefore only ever match a local Agent Host session type; a remote session never sees the `downloadOffered` state and never gets the **Download** action that writes `vscode.agentSdkSetup.downloadRequest`.
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/...` (Claude provider, as bundled in `agentHostMain.js`): `_refreshModels` only calls `_fetchNativeModels` when `canLoadWithoutDownload()` is true, and `createSession` goes through `_ensureAuthenticated`, which throws before any SDK call. The lazy download inside `loadSdkRoot` is therefore never reached. The only unconditional `ensureAvailable()` call is in `getChatMetadata` for `activation === 'restore'`, which a fresh remote host never hits.
- Net effect: on a remote host the Claude provider cannot leave `notDownloaded` through any UI path. Once the SDK is present, everything else works (see workaround), so the remote account check and BYOK detection themselves are fine.

**Workaround that confirms the diagnosis**

On the remote host, place the SDK where the downloader would and restart the Agent Host:

```bash
# version and URL come from <server>/product.json -> agentSdks.claude
VER=0.3.281
DEST=~/.vscode-server/data/agent-host/sdk-cache/claude/$VER/linux-x64
mkdir -p "$DEST"
curl -fsSL "https://main.vscode-cdn.net/agent-sdk/claude/$VER/linux-x64.tgz" | tar xz -C "$DEST"
: > "$DEST/.complete"
pkill -TERM -f 'bootstrap-fork --type=agentHost'   # ServerAgentHostManager relaunches it
```

After the restart the log shows the provider working with the third-party setup, and the Agents window lists the models and runs sessions:

```
[info] [Claude] Native account check: setUp=true, provider=bedrock, tokenSource=absent, apiKeySource=absent
[info] [Claude] Models refreshed (merged). Count: 16, ...
```

The workaround has to be repeated after every VS Code update because each release pins a different SDK version.

**Additional notes**

- The docs' harness table lists the Claude harness execution environment as "On your machine" only. If remote Claude is meant to be supported (the server bundle ships the full Claude provider and the remote account check works), the download path is the missing piece; if not, the UI should not offer Claude as a Session Target for remote sessions.
- Related: the Codex harness shows the same `SDK not downloaded yet` state on a remote host, but it was not investigated further because its model sources (Copilot or ChatGPT sign-in) do not apply to this setup.

issues.title: Agent Host chat: responses render only after the turn completes, no streaming deltas

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.68.0 (bundled)
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0
- OS Version: Windows 11
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window / Agent Host chat (`chat.agentHost`, provider `copilotcli`)
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): BYOK custom endpoint (OpenAI chat-completions API, `"streaming": true`)
- Logs: in any affected chat, `%APPDATA%\Code\logs\<session>\window1\renderer.log` shows `_invokeAgent called for resource: copilotcli:/<id>`; the session event log at `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl` shows the problem (see below)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In the Agents window, open an Agent Host chat using a BYOK custom-endpoint model whose `chatLanguageModels.json` entry has `"streaming": true`, and send a message. Server-side logs confirm SSE chunks are streamed token-by-token, but nothing renders until the whole turn finishes — then the full text appears at once.
2. When the turn completes, count event types in `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`: in my session (68 turns) there were 76 × `assistant.message` and **0** × `assistant.message_delta` / `assistant.streaming_delta`. Each turn records exactly one full message snapshot, timestamped ~0.5 s before its `assistant.turn_end` — no events exist during generation.

Root cause: `SessionOptions.streaming` in the Copilot SDK defaults to `false`; deltas are only emitted when it's enabled (contract confirmed in github/copilot-cli#4677). The extension enables streaming on the `copilot-cli` session-provider path, but sessions created via the Agent Host path don't set it, so the runtime buffers chunks and emits a single final `assistant.message` per turn.

Expected behavior: Agent Host sessions should create the underlying session with streaming enabled (or expose a setting), so `assistant.message_delta` events reach the renderer incrementally.

issues.title: WTF is this "Changes" pill supposed to be??

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled? Yes, I'm not even going to bother checking because this is core chat UI garbage, not an extension problem. - VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74) - OS: Linux --- Okay I need to vent before I even get to the bug report because I am genuinely pissed off right now. I open VS Code today after an update and the chat input box has this new pill thing sitting above it: `📄 13 Files +29 -19`. Cool, looks like a diff summary. Except it's NOT. I have made ZERO changes in this session. Nothing staged, nothing unstaged, git status is clean. And this thing is STILL showing me a diff. So I go dig into it and it turns out it's not showing my working tree, not showing my index, it's diffing against the BRANCH MERGE-BASE, i.e. some commit from god knows when that has literally nothing to do with what I'm doing right now in this chat session. So the one piece of information this pill is supposed to give me — "what did this session change" — is just factually wrong. It's lying to my face about what changed. So fine, annoying but whatever, I'll just turn it off. NOPE. Can't. I went and read the source because I didn't believe it, and sure enough someone hardcoded this: ```ts // src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/sessionChatPills.ts export function isSessionChatPillHideable(kind: SessionChatPillKind): boolean { return kind !== SessionChatPillKind.Changes; } ``` Every other pill in that same row (Artifacts, PRs, Issues, Customizations, Subagents, whatever) you can right click and hide. This one specific pill, the one that's actively showing me WRONG information, is the one you decided I'm not allowed to hide. Why? Who decided this? What meeting happened where someone said "yes, let's show users a misleading diff and also not let them turn it off"? Genuinely asking because I cannot comprehend the logic here. If it was at least correct I'd just be mildly annoyed, but it's wrong AND mandatory, that's a hell of a combo. And the baseline itself (`ChangesetKind.Branch` in `changesetUri.ts` / `selectDefaultChangeset`) is just hardcoded per provider, not exposed as a setting anywhere. So there isn't even a `settings.json` escape hatch. Nothing. I checked every chat.* setting I could find. Dead end. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a fresh agent chat session on a branch that has commits ahead of its base, with a totally clean working tree (nothing staged/unstaged). 2. Look above the chat input. 3. See a "Files changed" pill showing a non-zero diff that corresponds to your branch's history, not your session, not your working tree, not your index. 4. Try to right-click it to hide it. There's no option. Try literally any setting. There isn't one. ### Expected Either: - The pill reflects the actual session's changes (what the agent touched this conversation), or at minimum actual git working tree / staged state, OR - It's hideable like literally every other pill in the same component, OR - The baseline (`Branch` / `Uncommitted` / `Session`) is a user-facing setting instead of hardcoded. Preferably all three because right now it fails on every count. --- ON TOP OF THAT, same update: **"Ask" mode is just gone.** The mode dropdown used to have Ask/Edit/Agent, now it's just Agent. No popup, no release note I saw in-app, no "hey we moved this to custom agents now" prompt. It just disappeared. I used Ask mode constantly for quick read-only questions without giving the model free rein to run tools and touch my files. Now apparently I have to go hand-write a `.agent.md` file to get equivalent behavior? That's not a reasonable replacement for a built-in mode that existed for ages. **My own custom agents are gone too.** I had set up a couple of agents through VS Code's own UI, and the files are ``` /home/shyeyian/.config/Code/User/prompts/music-file-manager.agent.md /home/shyeyian/.config/Code/User/prompts/knowledge.agent.md ``` After this update: gone. No error. No "couldn't load N agents" warning. No migration notice. They just don't exist anymore like I never made them. I don't know if the storage format changed, if the discovery path changed, or if something just silently failed, because VS Code gave me ZERO indication anything went wrong. I only noticed because I went to use one and it wasn't there. So to summarize this absolutely fantastic release: you shipped a UI element that lies about what it's showing and refuses to be turned off, you removed a mode I used every day with no warning and no equivalent, and you silently deleted things I built through your own UI without so much as a log line. That's three separate ways my workflow got wrecked in one update, and I only found out by actually using the product, not from any changelog or in-app notice. I get that "implicit context" and "agent everything" is the direction the team wants to go. Fine, your product, your call. But FORCING new always-on UI (that's also just incorrect) with no opt-out, and silently dropping user-created config in the same breath, is not an acceptable way to ship this. At minimum: 1. Make the Changes pill hideable, or fix what it shows, or both. 2. Don't remove a mode without an equivalent built-in replacement and an actual heads-up. 3. If a custom agent/chat mode fails to load or its format changed, LOG IT somewhere visible instead of just dropping it on the floor.

Allow text zoom to be configured independently for each editor group/view.

For example:

1. Focus the left editor.
2. Press `Ctrl` + `+`.
3. Only the text in the focused editor/group increases.
4. Focus the right editor.
5. Press `Ctrl` + `+`.
6. Only the right editor/group increases.

This could work similarly to browser zoom, where the zoom level is associated with the currently focused view.

issues.title: Add a dedicated link color token for hover/widget/tooltip content
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

When customizing `editorHoverWidget.background`/`editorHoverWidget.foreground`  any links rendered inside the hover still use the global `textLink.foreground` / `editorLink.activeForeground`. In the case user/theme creator want to have light-themed hover for generally dark theme or the other way around, the link text color (which usually set for the general theme) inside it would have a low contrast.

There's currently no way to override link colors scoped to the hover widget without changing the link color globally, which would break links color everywhere else.

Suggestion: Introduce a widget-scoped link color, for example:

`editorHoverWidget.linkForeground` — foreground color for links rendered inside the editor hover widget, falling back to `textLink.foreground` if not set.

(If this is approved I can try to work on this and write a PR)

labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:

<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->

<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No (not tested; the failure is in the Agents window agent host, not in an extension)

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (stable)
- OS Version: Windows 10.0.26200 host, project in WSL 2 (Ubuntu, kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2); Dev Container is Debian 13 (trixie)
- Dev Containers CLI 0.88.0, Docker 29.8.1, Compose 5.5.1

## Summary

In the Agents window, a Claude session in a Dev Container (project folder on WSL) fails with `Authentication is required to use Claude`, and a GitHub sign-in (Copilot-routed Claude) is requested. I want to use my Anthropic subscription via `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (the native path from #323037 / workaround from #333738). Claude Code CLI is authenticated in the very same container, so the credentials are not missing there.

## Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create a compose-based Dev Container (`remoteUser: appuser`) with Claude Code installed via `ghcr.io/anthropics/devcontainer-features/claude-code:1`. A `postCreateCommand` copies the host's `~/.claude/settings.json` (containing `"env": {"CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN": "<token from claude setup-token>"}`) to `/home/appuser/.claude/settings.json`, and exports the same token in `~/.bashrc`.
2. In the Agents window, start a session with "Use Dev Container".
3. Start a new Claude session.

## Expected

The Claude agent authenticates with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, without a GitHub sign-in.

## Actual

The session fails and a GitHub sign-in prompt appears. Agents window log:

[ERROR] [ProtocolServer] Request 'createSession' failed Authentication is required to use Claude
[ERROR] [ProtocolServer] Request 'subscribe' failed Session not found on backend: claude:/<session-id>
[ERROR] [ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' failed Resource not found: file:///workspace/.vscode/settings.json


(The `.vscode/*.json` errors are harmless; those files do not exist.)

## Checked inside the container (as `appuser`)

- `claude -p "say ok"` returns `ok`, so the CLI is authenticated.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set in the environment of `devcontainer exec` processes.
- `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.claude.json` exist and are writable.

## Questions

- Does the agent host inside a Dev Container resolve Claude credentials natively? Are `~/.claude/settings.json` `env` or the process environment used there?
- Is the Copilot-proxy vs. native choice made on the host side only? If so, how can a Dev Container session select native mode?

Related: #323037, #333738, #314952, #317380

issues.title: Workspace Trust prompt shown on every restore/reopen/reconnect of an already-trusted Remote-SSH folder
issues.body:
## Environment

- VS Code 1.140.0 (commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74), Windows 11 x64 client
- Remote - SSH 0.128.0
- Remote host: Windows 11, built-in OpenSSH server
- `security.workspace.trust.enabled`: true (default); no profiles; Settings Sync off

## Steps to reproduce

1. Remote-SSH: Connect to Host, open folder `C:\Project` on the remote, click "Yes, I trust the authors".
2. Confirm in *Workspaces: Manage Workspace Trust* that the row `SSH: <host>  C:\Project` is listed under Trusted Folders.
3. Close the window, then reopen `Project [SSH: <host>]` from File > Open Recent (or restart VS Code with that window open so it is restored).

## Expected

No trust prompt; the folder is already trusted.

## Actual

The Workspace Trust modal appears every time (step 3), even though the folder is still listed as trusted once connected. It also appears every time the SSH connection drops and is re-established in an open window. A fresh "Connect to Host" (no folder) never prompts.

Setting `"security.workspace.trust.startupPrompt": "never"` does not suppress it.

## Observations

- In 1.140 the trust list is stored in `%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\agent-host-config.json` → `workspaceTrust.trustedUris`. On the client this list contains only `file:///` URIs.
- The trust for the remote folder is persisted on the **remote**, in `~/.vscode-server/data/User/globalStorage/agent-host-config.json`, as `"file:///c%3A/Project"`. The remote server's agent-host protocol logs (`data/logs/*/ahp/*.jsonl`) show it present in every session after it was first granted.
- Adding `"vscode-remote://ssh-remote%2B<host>/c%3A/Project"` by hand to the client's `trustedUris` (with VS Code closed) does not help: on next start VS Code rewrites the file and drops the entry, and the prompt still appears.
- The old `content.trust.model.key` entry in `globalStorage/state.vscdb` no longer exists (only a deleted remnant remains in the file).

## Likely cause (inferred, not verified in source)

On restore/reopen, trust for the `vscode-remote://` folder is evaluated before the remote authority has resolved. At that point only the client's list is available, and it can never contain remote URIs, so the folder is treated as untrusted and the startup prompt is shown. The remote's list, which does contain the folder, is only consulted after the connection is established.

## Possibly related

With `remote.SSH.useLocalServer: false`, reopening/restoring the same window frequently failed to connect at all: Remote-SSH logged `Running script with connection command: ... ssh.exe ...` but ptyhost never spawned the hidden terminal (no `ssh.exe` process was created, nothing reached the host's sshd), and the resolver timed out after `remote.SSH.connectTimeout`. A fresh "Connect to Host" spawned it immediately. `remote.SSH.useLocalServer: true` avoids this. The failure and the trust prompt occurred in the same reopen/restore scenarios; whether one causes the other was not established.

issues.title: Copilot Chat shows "Please try again" for a deterministic 400, and the image-specific error branch misses "unsupported image"
issues.body: ## What happens With a BYOK `customendpoint` provider (OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions`, DeepSeek), a request that carried an attached file failed with: ``` Sorry, your request failed. Please try again. Client Request Id: 942f0d74-96e2-46fe-83a3-783f9d00f2cf Reason: Request Failed: 400 {"error":{"message":".messages[32].image[0]: You have uploaded an unsupported image. Please make sure your image is valid and has one of the following formats: webp, png, jpeg, and gif. (request_id: 4e81c613-fe29-493c-afe4-f6965e3d7477)","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"invalid_request_error"}} ``` The actual cause was that the attached file had a `.png` extension but its bytes were not any image format. The provider identified it by content and rejected it. This is a **deterministic** failure: replaying the same request reproduces it every time, so retrying cannot help. ## Code paths I verified Everything below is read from `resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js` in the bundled extension 0.68.0, at the call site that produces this message (the stack points at `extension.js:1614:15814`). **1. The message comes from the `badRequest` / `failed` branch, taking the template that has no GH Request Id** — which matches the output above, where that field is absent: ```js case "badRequest": case "failed": { OIt(t) ? a = /* image-specific message */ : a = t.serverRequestId ? { message: Fi.t(`Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.\n\nClient Request Id: {0}\n\nGH Request Id: {1}\n\nReason: {2}`, ...) } : { message: Fi.t(`Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.\n\nClient Request Id: {0}\n\nReason: {1}`, ...) }; break; } ``` **2. `OIt()` is very narrow, and our reason matches none of it:** ```js function OIt(t) { if (t.type !== "badRequest" && t.type !== "failed") return false; let e = `${t.reason ?? ""} ${t.reasonDetail ?? ""}`.toLowerCase(); return e.includes("vision_attachment_not_accessible") || e.includes("attachment") && e.includes("not accessible"); } ``` Our reason contains `image` and `unsupported`, but neither `attachment` nor `not accessible`, so it falls through to the generic branch. Among image-related 400s, only `vision_attachment_not_accessible` reaches a dedicated message. **3. In the same classification, `badRequest` is grouped with transient failures:** ```js case "badRequest": case "notFound": case "failed": case "networkError": case "unknown": return new Ir.FetchFailure(yi.fromUnknown(t)) ``` ## Requests 1. **Do not append "Please try again" to every failure.** It currently lives in a single template shared by all of them, regardless of error class. For 5xx responses and network interruptions the advice is right; for a deterministic 4xx (a malformed request body) it is wrong, because replaying the identical request cannot succeed. Consider wording that follows the error class — for 4xx, something actionable such as "check the attachment and try again". 2. **Widen the image-specific branch.** It keys off one reason substring, so a clear image validation failure such as `You have uploaded an unsupported image` never reaches the dedicated message. Rather than enumerating more substrings, classify on structured fields; text matching drifts away from the message it is meant to detect. 3. **As the root cause, sniff attachment bytes locally.** Here the client sent a non-image file whose name ended in `.png`, and the request travelled all the way to the provider before being rejected. A magic-number check before sending would let the client report "this file is not a valid image" without a round trip. ## Why this is not a duplicate of #253136 #253136 is the meta thread that collects chat request failures; it is about **requests failing**. This report is about **how a failure is classified and worded**: the generic branch gives advice that cannot work for deterministic 4xx errors, and the image-specific branch's matching is too narrow to cover clear image validation failures. I searched for `"your request failed" misleading` (5 results) and did not find this raised on its own. ## Environment - VS Code: 1.140.0 (commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74) - GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.68.0 (bundled) - OS: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26300) - Provider: BYOK / customendpoint, OpenAI-compatible, DeepSeek ## Not verified I did not verify whether the generic message is accompanied by a "Try Again" button in the UI — searching the workbench bundle for `FetchFailure` and `Try Again` returned no matches. Request 1 therefore rests on the mismatch between wording and error class, not on a retry affordance existing in the UI.

Type: Feature Request Summary   VS Code Profiles currently separate settings, extensions, themes, and other configuration, but authentication remains global across all profiles.   Requested Feature   Allow each VS Code Profile to maintain its own authentication state for GitHub, Microsoft, GitHub Copilot, and other identity providers.   Example   I use a single Mac for both work and personal development.   Work Profile: - Work GitHub account - Work GitHub Copilot license - Work repositories   Personal Profile: - Personal GitHub account - Personal GitHub Copilot subscription - Personal repositories   Today, signing into or out of one account affects all profiles because authentication is shared globally.   Expected Behavior   Each profile should be able to maintain its own authenticated accounts. When switching profiles, VS Code should automatically use the accounts associated with that profile.   Business Impact   I would like to purchase a personal Copilot subscription while continuing to use my employer-provided Copilot subscription for work.   However, because profiles do not isolate authentication, I would need to constantly manage account switching or maintain separate VS Code installations.   If profile-specific authentication were supported, I would immediately subscribe and maintain both work and personal Copilot accounts on the same machine.   Additional Note   Authentication isolation is the missing piece that would make Profiles function as complete identity boundaries. issues.title: Agent Host permission picker exposes Configure Keybinding, but command implementation is a no-op

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0
- OS Version: Linux / Kubuntu

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Copilot Chat / Agent Host session where the permission picker is visible.
2. Right-click the permission picker and select **Configure Keybinding**.
3. Assign a keybinding to `workbench.action.chat.openAgentHostAutoApprovePicker`, for example:

```json
{
    "key": "ctrl+shift+.",
    "command": "workbench.action.chat.openAgentHostAutoApprovePicker",
    "when": "chatIsAgentHostSession"
}
```

4. Press the configured keybinding while in the Agent Host session.
5. Observe that nothing happens.
6. Enable **Developer: Toggle Keyboard Shortcuts Troubleshooting** and press the keybinding again.

The troubleshooting log confirms that the keybinding is resolved and the command is invoked:

```text
[KeybindingService]: matched workbench.action.chat.openAgentHostAutoApprovePicker
[KeybindingService]: + Invoking command workbench.action.chat.openAgentHostAutoApprovePicker.
```

However, the permission picker does not open.

Clicking the permission picker directly with the mouse still works.

## Expected Behavior

Invoking:

```text
workbench.action.chat.openAgentHostAutoApprovePicker
```

should open the Agent Host permission picker, especially since the picker itself exposes **Configure Keybinding**.

Alternatively, if the command is not intended to be invoked directly, the control should probably not expose **Configure Keybinding**.

The preferred behavior would be for the command to open the picker, since keyboard access to the permission picker is useful and this workflow was possible with the previous chat permission UI.

## Additional Information

The current source appears to explain the behavior.

`OpenAgentHostAutoApprovePickerAction.run()` is intentionally empty:

```ts
override async run(): Promise<void> {
    /* the action view item handles interaction */
}
```

The picker appears to be opened directly by the rendered action view item's interaction handler via `_showPicker()` instead of through the registered command.

This means the keybinding system successfully invokes the command, but the command itself performs no action.

This is particularly confusing because the UI exposes **Configure Keybinding** for the permission picker, which creates a valid keybinding for a command that does nothing when invoked independently.

issues.title: Allow configuring the default search mode of the Command Center
issues.body:
I'd like an option to configure which search mode opens when I click the Command Center in the title bar.

I mainly use it to find functions, classes, and other symbols across my workspace. Currently, I have to type # each time to switch to Workspace Symbols search.

It would be helpful to have a setting that makes Workspace Symbols the default mode, so I could click the Command Center and immediately start typing a symbol name.

Possible options could include:

Files (current default)

Workspace Symbols (#)

Current File Symbols (@)

I prefer using the mouse, and the Command Center is a large, easy-to-find target. A keyboard shortcut or a separate extension button doesn't provide the same workflow.

Would it be possible to support this through a built-in setting?

issues.title: Update Electron to include the WASM exception-handling crash fix

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No. It is triggered by an extension running WebAssembly code with WASM exception handling.

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0
- OS Version: Windows 10 x64, build 19045
- Bundled Electron: 43.7.3

The extension host repeatedly crashes with `0xC0000005` when V8 optimizes WebAssembly code using exception handling.

This matches a confirmed Electron regression:
https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/54203

The fix shipped in Electron 43.7.6:
https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/54235

The recently merged Electron update, #339260, targets 43.7.5 and still misses this fix.
Could VS Code update to 43.7.6 or later, or backport the patch?

Steps to Reproduce:

No standalone reproduction attached; please see the upstream report and fix above. Locally, the same workload crashes on the bundled Electron 43.7.3 but succeeds on Electron 44.5.1. Launching VS Code with `--js-flags="--liftoff-only"` also prevents the crash.

VS Code Insiders has not been tested.

- VS Code Version: 1.139.1 (System Installer)

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Arrange workspace into three side-by-side editor groups, one group holding the built-in browser panel for mobile development.

Clicking the browser panel should only focus the panel, preserve the three-column split layout, and not maximize it to full viewport.

issues.title: Agent Host: pluggable session isolation (non-Git VCS and custom worktree providers)
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->

## Problem

Agent Host sessions support two isolation modes: `folder` and `worktree`. The `worktree` mode is hard-coded to Git (`git worktree add` / `git worktree remove`, Git branches). There is no way to supply a different isolation mechanism.

This blocks two groups:

- **Non-Git version control.** Mercurial (`hg share`), Sapling, Jujutsu (`jj workspace add`), Perforce, and similar users get no per-session isolation. They can only use `folder` mode on a shared checkout.
- **Custom isolation in Git repos.** Some setups isolate work differently, for example a copy-on-write overlay (overlayfs) per session with a container per workspace, pre-warmed clones, or a remote build sandbox. Today these must be created by hand before each session and then opened in `folder` mode, losing the one-click "new session in isolation" flow and automatic cleanup.

The agent itself is VCS-agnostic (it only needs a working directory). Only workspace creation and cleanup are tied to Git.

## Proposal

Make session isolation pluggable, with Git worktrees as the built-in default.

A provider would supply:

- **create**: input is the source folder and session ID (optionally a base revision and a name hint); output is the directory the session should work in, plus optional display metadata (label, branch or bookmark name).
- **remove**: called when the session is archived or deleted, to clean up.
- Optional **status / changes**: so the session list can show changed files without assuming Git.

This could be exposed as:

1. A setting that points to commands or scripts, for example:
   ```jsonc
   "chat.agentHost.isolationProviders": {
     "overlay": { "label": "Overlay", "create": "my-isolate create", "remove": "my-isolate remove" }
   }
   ```
   with the session directory read from the command's stdout (JSON). This works for remote hosts (SSH, tunnels, WSL) because it runs where the Agent Host runs.
2. And/or an extension API, so SCM extensions (for example Mercurial) can contribute isolation the same way they contribute SCM providers.

Custom providers would appear next to "Folder" and "Worktree" in the isolation picker, and be usable from `create_remote_session` (`workspace.isolation`).

## Related

- #334727 (sessions without a Git worktree, i.e. `folder` mode)
- #337350 (pre-warming agent worktrees)
- #321685 (customizing worktree branch names)

issues.title: [chat-perf] layoutDurationMs regressed 21–47% in 6 chat scenarios
issues.body:
### Summary
:rotating_light: New regression: `layoutDurationMs` increased by 21–47% in 6 chat scenarios (text-only, tool-terminal, many-small-chunks, tool-read-file, multi-turn-user, mixed-content). This is a clear, sudden step outside the prior window's noise, not seen in the last 6 baselines.

### Evidence
- *text-only*: 213.3ms (±2.5) vs baseline 169.4ms (±12.6) — +25.9%
- *tool-terminal*: 316.4ms (±12.1) vs baseline 260.8ms (±15.3) — +21.3%
- *many-small-chunks*: 182.9ms (±2.7) vs baseline 126.6ms (±12.3) — +44.5%
- *tool-read-file*: 208.1ms (±12.0) vs baseline 141.3ms (±10.2) — +47.2%
- *multi-turn-user*: 217.7ms (±15.9) vs baseline 167.0ms (±12.4) — +30.4%
- *mixed-content*: 183.9ms (±4.8) vs baseline 146.6ms (±8.4) — +25.4%

All affected metrics were stable in the previous 6 runs, with no sign of drift or prior outliers. The current values are well outside the baseline spread.

#### Trend
- All affected scenarios show a sudden jump in layoutDurationMs in this run, not a gradual drift.
- No similar regressions reported in prior Slack threads or open issues.

#### Suspect Commits
- The regression appeared in this run, after a long period of stability. The window contains a large batch of merges, but the following are most suspicious due to their direct relevance to chat layout, session, and chat rendering:
  - `5270ba6` (sessions: Stabilize docked side pane sizing, sandy081)
  - `1f3057f` (sessions: Preserve workbench-level pane sizing, sandy081)
  - `4ccdb71` (sessions: Synchronize live last turn changes, sandy081)
  - `38220ea` (Improve agent feedback workflows and persistence, benibenj)
  - `d9a8a27` (Share one model-selection policy between Workbench chat and the Agents Window, lramos15)

### Suggested Action
- Bisect or revert recent changes to chat/session layout and sizing logic, especially those in the above commits. Investigate for accidental extra layout passes or inefficient layout invalidations.
- If a root cause is found, file a PR to address the regression and link this issue.

---
*Please triage and assign to the chat/session layout owners for investigation. This regression is new and not covered by any open tracking issue or prior alert.*

Integrated Browser blocks Encrypted Media on every page; videos won't play

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (user setup), commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74, 2026-09-30
- Electron: 43.7.3, Chromium: 150.0.7871.250
- OS Version: Windows 11 (Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200)

**Summary:** The Integrated Browser blocks Encrypted Media (EME) on every page, and video playback fails on YouTube and Instagram.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Launch with `code --disable-extensions`.
2. Open the Integrated Browser (View > Browser) and go to https://example.com
3. Open DevTools and run in the Console:
   `navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess('com.widevine.alpha', [{initDataTypes:['cenc'],videoCapabilities:[{contentType:'video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E"'}]}]).then(() => console.log('widevine: yes'), () => console.log('widevine: no'))`
4. Open any YouTube video in the Integrated Browser.

Expected: Encrypted media is available, or at least video plays, as in a normal Chromium browser.

Actual:
- Console shows "[Violation] Permissions policy violation: encrypted-media is not allowed in this document" and prints "widevine: no".
- YouTube videos do not play.
- Instagram Reels show "Sorry, we're having trouble playing this video." and `document.querySelectorAll('video').length` returns 0.

Additional info:
- `document.createElement('video').canPlayType('video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E, mp4a.40.2"')` returns `'probably'`, so H.264/AAC decoding is available.
- The same violation happens on youtube.com, so it is not specific to one site.

issues.title: Agent host: skill argument-hint is not shown as inline placeholder text

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: polish
labels.description: Cleanup and polish issue

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
In agent-host chat sessions (the Agents window, and agent-host sessions in the chat view), a skill's `argument-hint` frontmatter is not shown as inline placeholder text after its slash command. Built-in runtime commands such as `/review` do show their hint, and local (non agent-host) chat shows prompt and skill `argument-hint`s too.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create `~/.copilot/skills/design-prep/SKILL.md`:
   ```md
   ---
   name: design-prep
   description: Prep a design
   argument-hint: "<problem and repo> [offline]"
   user-invocable: true
   ---
   ```
2. Open a Copilot CLI session in the Agents window.
3. Type `/review ` and note the grey hint text.
4. Type `/design-prep ` and accept the completion.

**Expected:** `<problem and repo> [offline]` appears as placeholder text.
**Actual:** no placeholder is shown.

**Cause:** the hint is dropped at every layer of the agent-host skill path:
- the skill frontmatter parser does not read `argument-hint`;
- `SkillCustomization` and the skill completion `_meta` do not carry it;
- both hint renderers only accept command references, not skill references.

The runtime's own hint for skill commands is also discarded when skill completions are de-duplicated. This affects personal, repo and plugin skills.

**Related changes and intended behavior**

The merged changes below support treating this as a missing propagation path for existing behavior, rather than a new feature:

- #273011, **Use argument-hint for prompt placeholders**, established that explicit `argument-hint` text should guide users about expected input after a slash command.
- #293173, **Add skill frontmatter fields for slash command support**, explicitly added `argument-hint` as a supported skill attribute, documented it as a hint about expected arguments, and added validation tests for it.
- #324009, **Showing skill description in chat input is noisy**, intentionally removed the **description fallback**, not explicit argument hints. Its diff changes the workbench placeholder from `argumentHint ?? description` to `argumentHint`, and the Agents-window prompt placeholder from `description` to `argumentHint`. The proposed fix preserves that distinction: skills without an explicit hint still show no placeholder.
- #330178, **agentHost: fix duplicate skill completions and the "VS Code Synced Data:" prefix**, explains why runtime skill completions are suppressed in favor of the generic skill provider. This is relevant to the loss: a runtime hint cannot compensate when the generic skill completion does not carry it. That PR concerns completion identity and de-duplication, not removing argument hints.

These changes are evidence of an apparent omission in the agent-host skill metadata/completion path; they do not establish the authors' intent conclusively. Restoring explicit skill hints aligns agent-host sessions with existing skill and prompt behavior without bringing back noisy description placeholders.

Low priority: this is a discoverability polish issue, and skills without a hint are unaffected.

issues.title: Settings Sync: user settings unexpectedly reduced from 148 entries to 3; first reduced remote revision shows "Current"
issues.body:
My user settings were unexpectedly reduced from 148 top-level entries to just 3. I discovered this when Chat's default permissions reverted from **Allow All** to **Default**.

I have experienced apparent settings/sync inconsistencies more than once, but the evidence below concerns one specific occurrence.

### Environment

- VS Code: **1.140.0 Stable**
- Commit: `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`
- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise, x64, build `26100`
- Settings Sync: enabled in the main installation
- Reproduces with extensions disabled: **not tested**
- Deterministic reproduction: **not available**

### Observed behavior

Local History shows that the user settings file changed from approximately **11.6 KB / 148 top-level entries** to **236 bytes / 3 entries**.

Only these keys remained:

```text
terminal.external.windowsExec
terminal.integrated.shell.windows
workbench.colorTheme
```

The two terminal paths were retained. The theme changed from `GitHub Light High Contrast` to `Light 2026`.

The missing entries included:

- `chat.permissions.default: "autoApprove"`
- Chat model and agent configuration
- `settingsSync.ignoredSettings` and `settingsSync.ignoredExtensions`
- Editor, autosave, formatting, terminal, and Git customizations

This was not an intentional reset of my user settings.

### Evidence collected

1. **Settings Sync wrote to the local settings file.**
   A preserved log excerpt contains:

   ```text
   [AutoSync] Triggered by Interval
   Sync started.
   Settings: Updated local settings
   Settings: Updated last synchronized settings
   ```

   A local sync backup contains the earlier, full settings.

2. **The earliest reduced revision I found in Sync Activity (Remote) is marked "Current".**
   This identifies the current installation's sync machine identity, but does not establish which process or operation originally produced the reduced settings.

3. **The settings were still intact after upgrading.**
   Verified timestamps, normalized to UTC:

   | Event | UTC |
   |---|---|
   | Installation of 1.140.0 succeeded | 2026-09-30 23:19:45 |
   | Local History snapshot still contains 148 entries | 2026-10-01 02:11:04 |
   | First reduced Local History snapshot contains 3 entries | 2026-10-01 06:28:46 |

   These are snapshot times, not necessarily the exact write times. The raw sync-log timezone has not yet been reconciled with this timeline.

4. **A separate portable 1.140.0 test installation was also checked.**
   It had separate user data and shared storage, a different machine ID, and its retained startup logs consistently report `[AutoSync] Disabled`. There is currently no evidence that this portable instance uploaded the reduced settings.

### Expected behavior

Existing user settings should remain intact unless explicitly changed. An unexpected near-empty settings state should not silently replace the established configuration through synchronization.

### Investigation status

I cannot yet determine whether the initial loss originated in local configuration writing, sync merging/state handling, or another component. The evidence does **not** establish that the installer directly deleted the settings, or that this matches a particular known regression.

Could you advise which targeted diagnostics would identify the original writer or sync operation? Local settings history, a pre-change sync backup, and some preserved sync-log excerpts are available. Full configuration files and logs are omitted here for privacy.

issues.title: Allow configuring which terminal profiles are elevated into the AI group
issues.body:
### Problem

Since 1.111 the terminal `+` dropdown elevates "AI" profiles into a dedicated group at the top. Which profiles qualify is decided by a hardcoded substring match on the profile **name**, in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalMenus.ts`:

```ts
function isAiProfileName(name: string): boolean {
	const lowerCaseName = name.toLowerCase();
	return lowerCaseName.includes('copilot') || lowerCaseName.includes('claude');
}
```

`splitProfiles()` feeds that into `getTerminalActionBarArgs()`, and `isAiContributedProfile()` additionally hardcodes the `github.copilot-chat` and `anthropic.claude-code` extension ids.

The recognised vocabulary is two vendors. Users who run other agent CLIs get an inconsistent dropdown: two structurally identical user-defined profiles land in different groups purely because of the words in their names.

### Steps to reproduce

These two profiles differ only in name, path and icon:

```jsonc
"terminal.integrated.profiles.linux": {
  "Claude Code":  { "path": "/home/user/.npm/bin/claude", "icon": "claude" },
  "OpenAI Codex": { "path": "/home/user/.npm/bin/codex",  "icon": "openai" }
}
```

Open the terminal `+` dropdown:

```
New Terminal / New Terminal Window / Split Terminal
──────────────────────────────────
Claude Code                          ← elevated AI group
──────────────────────────────────
Zsh (Default)
Bash
OpenAI Codex
Split Terminal with Profile
```

Neither `path`, `args`, nor `icon` affects the outcome — only the name. Renaming the profile to anything still containing `claude` keeps it elevated; renaming it to drop the word moves it down.

### Request

Make the set of elevated profiles configurable. Either a list of matchers:

```jsonc
"terminal.integrated.profiles.aiGroupMatchers": ["copilot", "claude", "codex", "gemini"]
```

or a per-profile opt-in/out in the existing profile schema:

```jsonc
"OpenAI Codex": { "path": "...", "group": "ai" }
```

The second mirrors the `terminalProfileGroup` proposed API added in #293569, which already lets *contributed* profiles declare `group: "ai"`. Profiles defined in `terminal.integrated.profiles.*` have no equivalent, which is the gap here.

### Alternative solution

If a user-facing setting isn't wanted, extending the hardcoded list to cover other widely used agent CLIs — Codex, Gemini CLI, Aider, opencode, and similar — would resolve the inconsistency for most users. That keeps the zero-config behaviour, at the cost of ongoing maintenance as new CLIs appear, and it still wouldn't help anyone whose profile has a custom name.

### Relationship to #332673

#332673 asks for a way to turn the grouping **off**. This issue asks for control over **which** profiles are elevated, which matters for users who want the group but want it to contain every agent they actually use. Happy for the two to be merged if the team would rather treat them as one request.

### Notes

Original feature: #293554 / #293569, milestone 1.111.0. The `terminal.integrated.experimental.aiProfileGrouping` setting referenced in the 1.111 release notes no longer exists — `splitProfiles()` reads no configuration, so the grouping is currently unconditional with no opt-out.

VS Code version: 1.139.0, commit `2242ebbb54efeeb0129e08e919e7e8d43033cd83`
OS: Windows client, dev container remote (Linux x64)

issues.body:
Type: Bug **Describe the bug** In a Copilot CLI agent session (VS Code 1.140.0), viewing an image file only returns a 31-character text receipt to the language model. The image bytes never reach the model. **To Reproduce** 1. Start a Copilot CLI agent session. 2. Select a BYOK language model provider that declares image input support (tested with the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash provider from the "DeepSeek V4 for Copilot Chat" extension, `capabilities.imageInput: true`). 3. Ask the model to view any image file (the model calls the `view` tool), e.g. `/tmp/probe_red_8x8.png` (a 75-byte 8x8 solid-color PNG), a 1.5 MB PNG, or a ~875 KB screenshot. 4. Observe that the tool result handed to the model is only: `content: "Viewed image file successfully."` with `detailedContent: "Viewed image file at path ..."`, and telemetry reports `metrics.resultLength = 31` and `resultForLlmLength = 31` — no image content part. **Actual result** All three images produce the identical text-only result. The model correctly reports that it received no pixels, only a file path. The same images can be described correctly when attached directly to the user prompt. **Expected result** The `view` tool result for an image should be delivered to the model as an image content part (or, when the model does not support images, degrade explicitly with a visible notice instead of silently sending a text receipt). **Additional evidence** - `~/.copilot/session-state//events.jsonl` contains `session.binary_asset` records with the full base64 payload of the very same images (e.g. 75-byte PNG, 1.5 MB PNG), so the image data does exist in the session and is only lost on the way to the model request. - The provider request logs never contain an image part for these requests. - Same images work through the classic Chat view with the `view_image` tool, which returns an image content part. This suggests a regression/limitation specific to the Copilot CLI agent session tool-result path. - Workaround that works: attach the image directly to the prompt instead of using `view`. issues.title: Test: Agent Host full output for Claude, Codex, and Copilot
issues.body:
Refs: #338053, #339410, #337389, #337390

- [x] macOS @Giuspepe
- [x] Linux @eleanorjboyd
- [x] Windows @benvillalobos

Complexity: 3

Authors: @anthonykim1

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339432%0A%0A&assignees=anthonykim1)

---

Verify that large shell output has a truncated terminal preview and can be opened in full in a read-only editor, both live and after reloading or restarting VS Code.

**Repeat the checks with Claude, Codex, and Copilot.**

## Setup

1. Use a build containing #339410.
2. Start a local Agent Host session with the provider being tested.
3. For Copilot, keep `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` set to `false`.


Ask the agent to run this as a normal foreground shell command, without redirecting or filtering its output:

```text
node -e "process.stdout.write('FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN\n' + 'x'.repeat(131072) + '\nFULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE\n' + 'y'.repeat(131072) + '\nFULL_OUTPUT_END\n')"
```

**Please don't limit testing to this command.** Also try realistic large output from builds, test runs, or printing a large file.

## Open the full output

1. Run the large-output command and expand the completed terminal card.
   - The preview shows **Output truncated. View Full Output**.
2. Click **View Full Output**.
   - A read-only editor opens with the complete output, including all three markers.
3. Close the editor, then use **Open Full Output (Read-Only)** in the command header.
   - The same output opens.
4. Click ordinary preview text, select and copy text, and scroll the preview.
   - These interactions work normally and do **not** open the full-output editor.

## Reload and restart VS Code

1. Close the output editor and reload VS Code using **Developer: Reload Window**.
2. Return to the same session, navigate back to the earlier terminal card, expand its preview, and click **View Full Output**.
   - The complete output opens again without rerunning the command.
3. Close the output editor, fully quit VS Code, then reopen VS Code and the same workspace.
4. Return to the same session, navigate back to the earlier terminal card, expand its preview, and click **View Full Output** again.
   - The complete output still opens without rerunning the command.

After both the reload and the restart, confirm all three markers remain present, the editor is read-only, and no terminal appears in the Terminal panel.

## Regression and exploratory checks

- **Short output:** Run `node -e "console.log('short output')"`. The complete output stays inline without a truncation message or full-output action.
- **Failed command:** Run a large-output command that exits with an error. The card reports failure, and retained full output still opens.
- **Running/background commands:** Confirm their existing behavior is unchanged.
- **Multiple commands:** Run commands with different output and confirm each card opens its own result.
- **Everyday use:** Watch for missing output, unexpected editor openings, broken selection or scrolling, or output disappearing after reload.

issues.title: fix: gate unbundled Copilot OTel exporter E2E as a known issue (build fix for vscode-engineering#4077)

labels.name: vscode-build
labels.description: VS Code build process issues

issues.body:
## Build failure

The Linux X64 Integration Tests (Electron) job fails on the Agent Host E2E suite `Copilot OTel`:

```text
FAIL Copilot OTel
provider turn exports SDK spans through the Agent Host file exporter
Error: OTel spans have not reached the file exporter
```

The export file contains the Agent Host session spans but not the Copilot SDK `invoke_agent` span (`service.name: github-copilot`) the test requires. The failure reproduces across consecutive `main` builds after the suite was registered.

## Root cause

The `provider turn exports SDK spans through the Agent Host file exporter` test was added together with the registration of the `Copilot OTel` suite in `scripts/test-agent-host-e2e.ts`. It asserts that the file exporter receives a Copilot SDK `invoke_agent` span whose `service.name` is `github-copilot`. That span is produced only by an upstream copilot-agent-runtime file-exporter fix that is **not yet bundled** into this repository. The runtime currently bundled emits the Agent Host spans (so the exporter path and polling window work) but not the SDK inference span, so the polling assertion can never be satisfied on CI.

This is a test/runtime-version mismatch, not a product regression: the host, SDK wrapper, and exporter plumbing are correct, and the missing span is a property of the bundled native runtime. The suite's sibling test (`new sessions honor changed managed telemetry without restarting`) already handles an equivalent unbundled-runtime dependency by gating on `AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1`.

## How the fix works

The file-exporter test is gated behind `AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1` using the exact `(process.env['AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES'] === '1' ? test : test.skip)` pattern already used by the sibling test in the same file. The desired-behavior assertions are preserved verbatim, so the test still runs — and must pass — when the environment flag is set and once the runtime that emits the `invoke_agent` span is bundled. A matching entry in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` records the user-facing gap, scope, expected/observed behavior, gate, and focused reproduction, and notes that the gate and entry must be removed together when the runtime fix lands. No production code, telemetry, or error reporting is changed, and no error is suppressed: the gap is surfaced as a documented, reproducible known issue rather than hidden.

## Rollback evaluation

- Recommendation: **Do not roll back**.
- Public culprit: commit `52347f5223fb35fced93431e890ab99516558f23` (microsoft/vscode#339315), which registered the `Copilot OTel` suite and added this test.
- Rationale: The fix-forward is bounded and test-only, matching an established in-repo pattern for unbundled-runtime coverage. A revert would remove the already-passing managed-telemetry coverage added by the same PR and discard the file-exporter specification that should run once the runtime is bundled. Gating the single unbundled-dependent test restores build signal with lower risk than reverting the whole change.
- Owners to consult: ``@rwoll``

## Validation

Local build/typecheck and test execution could not be run in this environment: Node.js and `tsc` invocations are blocked by the sandbox (`Permission denied`). The change is a mechanical, syntactically-identical application of the existing `AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES` gate already present on line 176 of the same file, plus a documentation entry. `git diff --check` passes. The gated test still executes and asserts the full span contract under `AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1`:

```bash
AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run \
  src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotOtelAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts \
  --grep "provider turn exports SDK spans through the Agent Host file exporter"
```

## Risk

Minimal. The change is test-only and documentation-only: it skips one integration test in default CI and runs it under an existing opt-in flag. No shipping behavior, telemetry, or runtime code is affected. The only risk is that the gap could be forgotten; `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` documents removal criteria to mitigate this.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: ``@rwoll``

Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering\#4077

issues.title: Test: Marketplace missing-target cleanup and isolated skill repair
issues.body:
PRs: #338781, #339020

- [ ] anyOS @ulugbekna

Complexity: 3

Authors: @pwang347


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339417%0A%0A&assignees=pwang347)

---

## Context

Marketplace installation state must follow the exact installed target. Externally deleted plugin targets should become Missing and remain safely uninstallable, while skill repair staging must never appear as a user customization inside the scanned skills root.

Related focused reports: #338582 and #338584.

Use a disposable profile, workspace, and plugin directory with the Customization Marketplace enabled.

## Missing plugin target cleanup

1. Install a configured-Marketplace plugin and verify its exact entry is Installed.
2. Create or retain an unrelated local plugin with the same display name.
3. Outside Discover, delete only the recorded Marketplace plugin target. Leave its installation record intact.
4. Return to Discover. Verify the entry refreshes to a missing/error state rather than remaining Installed or binding to the same-name plugin.
5. Invoke **Uninstall**. Verify the stale installed-plugin entry, enablement, source metadata, and Marketplace record are removed without touching the unrelated plugin.
6. Reload the window and verify Discover offers **Install** again with no stale Retry Uninstall state.

## Isolated skill repair

1. Install a multi-file Marketplace skill to a disposable target.
2. Edit one recorded file, add an extra file, and delete a different recorded file.
3. Return to Discover and verify the skill reports **Missing files**. Start **Repair** while keeping the installed Skills list visible.
4. Verify no `.customization-marketplace-<uuid>` staging item appears in the list or exposes an Uninstall action.
5. After repair, verify the missing recorded file returns while the edited file and extra file remain unchanged.
6. Reload the window and verify only the real skill target is discovered and remains associated with its Marketplace record.

**Expected:** Missing exact targets transition to a recoverable state and can be cleaned up safely, while skill repair stages outside discovery and restores only missing recorded content.

issues.title: Test: Marketplace-indexed and SHA-pinned plugin installs

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

issues.body:
PRs: #338794, #339021, #339022

- [x] anyOS @federicobrancasi
- [ ] Windows @kycutler

Complexity: 5

Authors: @pwang347


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339416%0A%0A&assignees=pwang347)

---

## Context

Configured repository Marketplaces can declare plugins through an index, including sources pinned to a full commit SHA. Installation must validate the exact repository, revision, and relative path, and failed or cancelled ref clones must not poison another cache variant.

Related focused reports: #338581, #338583, and #338775.

Use a disposable profile and isolated plugin directory. Enable `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled` and `chat.plugins.enabled`. Configure a repository Marketplace that currently declares an installable plugin through its index, plus a full 40-character commit-pinned variant of that source.

## Indexed plugin installation

1. Open **Chat: Open Customizations** > **Discover** and find the indexed plugin.
2. Verify **Install** is enabled, accept the source trust prompt, and install it.
3. Verify the installed files come from the indexed repository, resolved revision, and exact relative path. The plugin should appear in the installed Plugins list and remain associated after reload.
4. Verify an index without a resolved revision, a path outside the repository, or an ambiguous path match is rejected rather than recorded with guessed provenance.

## Full-SHA installation

1. Install the same or another indexed plugin from a source pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA.
2. Verify installation checks out that exact commit in detached state instead of passing the SHA to `git clone --branch`.
3. Verify named branches and tags continue using the established clone path.
4. Cancel or fail a pinned clone, then retry. Verify the incomplete clone is removed and Retry starts cleanly.

## Cache recovery and isolation

1. In the disposable plugin cache, leave an empty or invalid unpinned repository cache, or reproduce one through a deliberately failed ref clone.
2. Install from the unpinned source and verify the cache is validated and recovered automatically.
3. Verify recovery does not delete a valid sibling ref cache, follow symbolic links, or mutate anything outside the expected repository-cache root.
4. Start two installation attempts close together if practical. Verify cache recovery remains serialized and both operations settle into a valid installed or actionable error state.

**Expected:** Indexed and commit-pinned plugins install only from verified provenance, retries clean up incomplete work, and invalid cache variants recover without damaging sibling or external paths.
