issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 and later. It starts with #337621 and is not present in 1.139.
- OS Version: All

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In an Agent Host Copilot session, select the HydraFusion model and send a request that runs a multi-phase Fusion workflow.
2. With telemetry output logging on, look at the `agentHost.turnCompleted` events.
3. Each Fusion phase that gets a child chat produces a `turnCompleted` event with:
   - `isSubagentSession: true`
   - `parentToolCallId: fusion:<fusionId>:<phaseId>`
   - no `subagentTaskModelSource`
   - no `model`

### What's happening

Since #337621, each HydraFusion phase opens its child chat by firing a synthetic `subagent_started` signal ([`_openFusionPhaseChat`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L7531)). The phase's tool call id is [`fusion:<fusionId>:<phaseId>`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotFusionProgress.ts#L29). Real `task`-tool subagents get `taskModelSource` from the SDK's `subagent.started` event ([here](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L6403)). The synthetic signal carries neither a source nor a model.

The host handles it like any other subagent start. [`_handleSubagentStarted`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentSideEffects.ts#L1184) starts a tracked subagent turn on a subagent chat URI. When that turn completes, `agentHost.turnCompleted` reports it as a subagent turn with `subagentTaskModelSource` and `model` unset ([reporter](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTelemetryReporter.ts#L1440)). No `ChatUsage` action carrying a model is routed to the phase chat, so `model` stays empty.

Telemetry confirms this: on 1.140, these `fusion:` phase chats are most of the subagent turns that lack both `subagentTaskModelSource` and `model`. They do not appear on earlier versions.

### Impact

- **Inflated subagent numbers:** phase chats are presentation-only and are not `task`-tool subagents, but they count as subagent launches. That inflates subagent reach and launch counts on 1.140 and later.
- **Lower per-subagent rates:** they lower the share of subagents with a known model and with a reported model source. That breaks before/after comparisons across the 1.140 boundary.
- **Other events are affected too:** many Agent Host events decide `isSubagentSession` from the chat URI, including `agentHost.requestTokenUsage` and the tool-call events. Any activity routed into a phase chat is classified as subagent activity there as well.
- **Manual filtering:** analyses of subagent model selection, like the investigation for #333947, have to filter on the `parentToolCallId` prefix by hand.

### Suggested fix

- Distinguish phase chats from `task`-tool subagents in telemetry. For example, add a bounded `subagentKind` property (`'task' | 'fusionPhase'`) to `agentHost.turnCompleted` and the other events that report `isSubagentSession`. Or skip turn telemetry entirely for presentation-only phase chats.
- If phase chats keep reporting turns, fill in `model` from the Fusion phase's model where it's known.
- Until this is fixed, analysis can exclude subagent turns whose `parentToolCallId` starts with `fusion:`.

### Possibly related (not investigated yet)

Even after excluding phase chats, 1.140 shows two other differences from 1.139 over the same days:
- Cancelled `task`-tool subagent launches are missing `subagentTaskModelSource` somewhat more often.
- Noticeably more subagent turns have a `parentTurnId` that doesn't match any parent turn in the same session.

These may have separate causes, such as #337620, #337584 or the SDK update to `1.0.15-preview.4`.

issues.title: ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations (chat.approvedAccountOrganizations) policy never recognized via macOS managed preferences, confirmed on 1.137.0-1.140.0
issues.body:
## Description
The `ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations` managed policy (`chat.approvedAccountOrganizations`) does not appear to be read/recognized by VS Code when delivered via macOS Managed Preferences (.mobileconfig, deployed through MDM), even though the value is confirmed present on disk with correct permissions, and the general managed-preferences mechanism is independently confirmed working on the same machine/session via two other policies.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On a macOS device enrolled in an MDM (tested with Jamf Pro), deploy a Configuration Profile targeting the `com.microsoft.VSCode` managed-preferences domain, setting:
   - `ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations`: `["your-org-name"]`
2. Confirm the value is actually delivered to disk:
   `sudo plutil -p "/Library/Managed Preferences/<user>/com.microsoft.VSCode.plist"`
   Correctly shows: `{ "ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations" => [ 0 => "your-org-name" ] }`
3. Launch VS Code, run `Developer: Policy Diagnostics` from the Command Palette.
4. Check the **Account Policy Gate** section of the report.

## Expected Behavior
Per the policy's own description ("Setting this policy to a non-empty list activates the Approved Account gate..."), the gate should become active — `State` should be `restricted` or `satisfied` depending on the signed-in account, and `ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations` should reflect the configured list.

## Actual Behavior
`Account Policy Gate` consistently reports:
```
State: inactive
Reason: n/a
ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations: not set
```
— VS Code does not recognize the policy value at all, despite it being correctly present in the managed-preferences file.

## Isolation / why this doesn't look like an environment issue
- Verified file content, permissions (644), and that the delivering profile is `Verified`/MDM-sourced (not a local unsigned install).
- Verified on a fully fresh session: force-killed VS Code, cleared `cfprefsd`, logged out and back in, relaunched.
- **Control fields, delivered via the exact same profile/session**: `ChatMCP` (`chat.mcp.access`) and `DictationModel` (`dictation.model`) are correctly recognized and show up as applied in the same `Developer: Policy Diagnostics` report. This isolates the gap specifically to `ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations`.
- **Not a recent regression**: reproduced identically on both current stable and `1.137.0`, with the same control-field comparison holding on both — `ChatMCP`/`DictationModel` work, `ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations` doesn't, on either version.

## Environment
- VS Code versions tested: 1.137.0 and 1.140.0 (both stable, both exhibit the same behavior)
- OS: macOS (Jamf Pro-managed/supervised Mac)
- Delivery: macOS Configuration Profile (.mobileconfig, Custom Settings payload) pushed via Jamf Pro, confirmed `Verification State: Verified` / `Source: MDM`

issues.title: fix: guard multi-diff item clearBinding against re-entrant disposal (fixes #339312)
issues.body:
### Summary The multi-diff editor throws `BugIndicatingError: Cannot unbind a diff editor template from a different item` when a `ManagedVirtualizedItem` disposes a binding. Clearing a binding synchronously disposes the diff editor, which fires editor model-change events that drive the item's own `autorun`; that autorun re-enters `_clearBinding()` and disposes the same binding a second time, so `unbind()` finds `_viewModel` already cleared (`undefined !== item`) and throws. Impact: unhandled error surfaced to telemetry when closing/switching multi-diff editors (e.g. the Agent Sessions diff view) on all platforms. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339312 Recommended reviewer: ``@hediet`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`10de1b93436`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/10de1b93436) | | Author | ``@hediet`` | | PR | n/a | | Message | Refactor multi-diff virtualized scrolling | | Why | This change introduced the `ManagedVirtualizedItem` lifecycle where `_clearBinding()` disposes a binding whose `dispose()` synchronously re-enters the same item's `autorun` via editor events; the clear path has no re-entrancy guard, so the nested dispose runs against already-cleared state. Subsequent commits (`98e228b47bc`, `519f5fa46f0`) refined the same lifecycle but kept the re-entrant clear path. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Autorun as ManagedVirtualizedItem.autorun participant Clear as _clearBinding() participant Binding as DiffEditorItemBinding.dispose() participant Unbind as DiffEditorItemTemplate.unbind()/setItem() participant Editor as DiffEditor events Autorun->>Clear: item hidden, not kept alive Note over Clear: ⚠️ Root cause:
no re-entrancy guard Clear->>Binding: binding.dispose() Binding->>Unbind: _template.unbind(item) (before super.dispose) Note over Unbind: setItem(undefined)
_viewModel = undefined
editor.setDiffModel(null) Unbind->>Editor: synchronous model-change event Editor->>Autorun: re-enters autorun Autorun->>Clear: _clearBinding() again Clear->>Binding: binding.dispose() again Binding->>Unbind: unbind(item) Note over Unbind: 💥 _viewModel (undefined) !== item
Cannot unbind a diff editor template from a different item ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/diffEditorItemTemplate.ts` | crash site | L539 (from stack): `throw new BugIndicatingError('Cannot unbind a diff editor template from a different item')` | | `src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/diffEditorItemTemplate.ts` | re-entrant trigger | L592-L593: `dispose()` calls `this._template.unbind(this.item)` before `super.dispose()`, so `currentBinding`/`_store` are still live; `unbind` → `setItem(undefined)` fires editor events synchronously | | `src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/virtualizedItemManager.ts` | root cause (producer) | L228-L247: `_clearBinding()` disposes the binding with no guard; the autorun at L149-L155 re-enters it during that synchronous dispose | ### Repro Steps This is a timing-dependent re-entrancy, reproduced by closing/hiding a multi-diff item whose diff editor fires a synchronous model-change event during disposal. 1. Open a multi-diff editor (e.g. a source-control / Agent Sessions diff view) with at least one visible diff item that has loaded its diff model. 2. Trigger disposal of a bound, visible item — close the editor, switch the active editor, or scroll the item out while it is being cleared. 3. During `_clearBinding()`, `binding.dispose()` → `unbind()` → `setItem(undefined)` → `editor.setDiffModel(null)` fires an editor event that re-enters the item's `autorun`, calling `_clearBinding()` a second time on the same binding. 4. The nested `unbind()` sees `_viewModel === undefined`, `undefined !== item`, and throws `BugIndicatingError`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/virtualizedItemManager.ts`, `ManagedVirtualizedItem._clearBinding()`: add an `_isClearingBinding` guard flag. On entry, if a clear is already in progress the method returns immediately; otherwise it sets the flag, performs the unbind/dispose/reset sequence inside a `try`, and resets the flag in `finally`. This fixes the bug at the data producer — the clear path that initiates the re-entrant disposal — rather than at the crash site. The outer `_clearBinding()` invocation still completes the full clear atomically (it sets `_templateReference` to `undefined` and disposes the reference after the binding dispose returns), so the nested call being a no-op does not leave the item half-cleared. The throw inside `unbind()` is preserved as a genuine invariant check for other callers; it is simply no longer reached on this re-entrant path because the duplicate dispose never starts. **Why this is correct**: the guard makes the unsupported "dispose during dispose" ordering unrepresentable at the producer, which is the lifecycle-fix priority (reorder/serialize the producer's state mutations), instead of teaching the consumer `unbind()` to tolerate inconsistent state. No `logService.error` or telemetry path is removed, and no `try/catch` swallows the error. **Alternatives considered**: - Guard inside `unbind()` / `DiffEditorItemBinding.dispose()` by comparing `_viewModel` and returning early — rejected: that is a crash-site guard that silently tolerates double-dispose and would mask the same re-entrancy for every other binding type, hiding the producer bug. - Defer `editor.setDiffModel(null)` to a microtask so events do not fire synchronously — rejected: broader behavioral change to editor teardown timing with higher regression risk than serializing the clear. ### Recommended Owner ``@hediet`` — author of the multi-diff virtualization refactor (`10de1b93436`) and the follow-up lifecycle fixes; active `microsoft/vscode` core team member (write access, multiple commits in the last 90 days). --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. The changes have been pushed to the branch [`fix/multidiff-clearbinding-reentrancy-339312-b812a85b6a26bdc1`](https://github.com/vscodebot-pr/vscode/tree/fix/multidiff-clearbinding-reentrancy-339312-b812a85b6a26bdc1). > > **Original error:** ERR_API: [2026-10-02T16:28:40.131Z] create pull request in microsoft/vscode failed (attempt 1) Original error: Validation Failed: {"resource":"PullRequest","code":"custom","field":"fork_collab","message":"fork_collab Fork collab can't be granted by someone without permission"} - https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#create-a-pull-request Retryable: false Suggestion: This error cannot be resolved by retrying. Please check the error details and fix the underlying issue. To create the pull request manually: ```sh gh pr create --title "fix: guard multi-diff item clearBinding against re-entrant disposal (fixes #339312)" --base main --head vscodebot-pr:fix/multidiff-clearbinding-reentrancy-339312-b812a85b6a26bdc1 --repo microsoft/vscode ```

issues.title: fix: guard webview find against disposed frame subtree (fixes #339314)
issues.body:
### Summary `WebviewMainService.getFrameByName` (electron-main) reads `getWebContents(id).mainFrame.framesInSubtree.find(...)` unconditionally. When a find / stop-find IPC request is handled against a webContents whose render frame has already been torn down (window closed, navigated away, or detached editor window disposed), `mainFrame.framesInSubtree` is `undefined`, so `.find(...)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')` in the main process. This new-in-1.140.0 bucket affects 566 users / 736 hits across Mac, Windows, and Linux. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339314 Recommended reviewer: ``@dmitrivMS`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`9cc2a44b`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9cc2a44bf20ac6f4badef53bc9f33dfdb5803378) | | Author | ``@dmitrivMS`` | | PR | #337403 | | Message | webview: Fix find in detached editor windows (#337403) | | Why | The commit reworked `getFrameByName` to resolve the frame via the shared `getWebContents(id)` helper and routes stop-find/find requests through auxiliary web-contents IDs (detached editor windows) as well as main window IDs. This widened the set of webContents the find path runs against — including auxiliary/detached contents that can be disposed between request and handling — so `mainFrame.framesInSubtree` can now be `undefined` at the dereference, which the prior window-only path did not expose. Verified ancestor of shipped commit `07f806f9` (first appears in `1.140.0~389`, matching the "new in 1.140.0" anomaly). | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Renderer as Webview (renderer) participant IPC as ipcMain / ChannelServer participant Service as WebviewMainService participant Electron as Electron WebContents Renderer->>IPC: stopFindInFrame(id, frameName) IPC->>Service: call stopFindInFrame Service->>Service: getFrameByName(id, frameName) Note over Electron: ⚠️ Root cause:
render frame already disposed,
framesInSubtree is undefined Service->>Electron: getWebContents(id).mainFrame.framesInSubtree Note over Service: 💥 TypeError: Cannot read
properties of undefined (reading 'find') ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/platform/webview/electron-main/webviewMainService.ts` | crash site & fix | L96 (from stack): `getWebContents(id).mainFrame.framesInSubtree.find(...)` dereferences `undefined` when the webContents' render frame is disposed | ### Repro Steps The error is a timing-dependent race on the main process; it fires when a stop-find/find reply is handled after the target render frame is gone: 1. Open a webview-backed editor (e.g. Markdown preview, Simple Browser, or a detached editor window) and start Find (Cmd/Ctrl+F) inside it. 2. Close the webview / window (or navigate it away) while a find or stop-find request is in flight. 3. The in-flight `stopFindInFrame` / `findInFrame` IPC call reaches `getFrameByName`, whose `webContents.mainFrame.framesInSubtree` is now `undefined`, throwing the `TypeError`. - Detached editor windows (added in #337403) increase the likelihood because stop-find is now routed through auxiliary web-contents IDs that are disposed independently of the main window. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `webviewMainService.ts` → `getFrameByName()`: the producer of the invalid state is Electron's render-frame disposal, which lives outside `microsoft/vscode` and cannot be reordered or awaited, so a consumer-side guard at this external boundary is the correct fix. `getFrameByName` now returns `WebFrameMain | undefined`: it checks `contents.isDestroyed()` and `contents.mainFrame?.framesInSubtree` before calling `.find(...)`, returning `undefined` when the frame subtree is gone. The two callers (`findInFrame`, `stopFindInFrame`) already treat a missing frame as a no-op, so they early-return on `undefined`. This mirrors the existing disposed-frame guards already in this codebase: the `contents.isDestroyed()` check in `setIgnoreMenuShortcuts` (same file) and the `frame.isDestroyed()` guard in `app.ts`'s `isSafeFrame`. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. The chat extension is needed to reproduce this workflow.

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74), x64
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.22621, x64
- Chat extension installed: openai.chatgpt 26.930.21537

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a chat inside VS Code.
2. Continue the conversation with more than one image in the chat.
3. Try to read or continue the conversation.

Expected behavior: The chat remains responsive with multiple images in the conversation.

Actual behavior: The chat becomes very slow and sometimes appears to freeze, interrupting work. The problem has happened repeatedly. I have not established whether the entire VS Code window becomes unresponsive or only the chat pane, nor measured the delay.

I am reporting the observed behavior without attributing it to VS Code core or an extension yet. No chat content or raw logs are attached.

issues.title: Claude agent host: between-turn 'resume rebuild' kills subagents and drops replies
issues.body:
<!-- Observed on VS Code 1.139.1 (04c0d99f4fb0) on Linux, with anthropic.claude-code 2.1.284. The mechanism is in core (vs/platform/agentHost), not the extension. -->

**Summary.** The agent host sometimes discards a healthy, live Claude SDK session *between turns* and rebuilds it from transcript on the next turn. Any in-process background subagents (Agent tool tasks) are killed mid-flight by the rebuild, and the assistant's reply is sent but not rendered to the Agents Window.

**Mechanism** (read from the minified `out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js`): `ClaudeSdkPipeline` attaches a "rematerializer" which `_rebindQuery(reason)` invokes whenever desired state drifts from applied state — `rebindForRestart()`, `rebindForClientTools()` (client tool-set changes mark `toolDiff.markDirty()`), MCP launch-enablement revision changes, additional-directory changes, and transport switches. The rematerializer starts a fresh SDK session with `isResume: true` and the live one is discarded, logging `[Claude] session <uuid>: resume rebuild agent=(none)`.

**Consequences observed** (agenthost.log, 2026-10-02, hostProcessAgeMs continuous across the event — i.e. no host restart):

1. Seven running background subagents died and reported on the next turn as "didn't finish before the previous session ended".
2. Their stopped-notices ran as their own tiny turn (`queue yielded` → `result` 23 ms later), which closed the pending user turn; the assistant's actual reply then logged as `result for sdkUuid=undefined` and was never rendered to the user.
3. Related variant: a user message sent mid-turn is folded in as steering (`injectSteering: enqueued id=…`, `queue yielded … steeringPendingId=…`); the turn again closes on the first `result`, dropping the reply to the second message.

Log signature sequence for one occurrence:

```
11:03:42 [Claude:<session>] result for sdkUuid=request_49dfe40f-…        ← turn ends normally, 7 subagents still running
11:06:01 [Claude] session <session>: resume rebuild agent=(none)         ← between turns; kills the subagents
11:06:03 [Claude:<session>] queue yielded sdkUuid=request_26892093-…
11:06:03 [Claude:<session>] result for sdkUuid=request_26892093-…       ← 23 ms stopped-notice turn
11:08:56 [Claude:<session>] result for sdkUuid=undefined                 ← the real reply, never rendered
```

**Expected behavior.** A between-turn rebind should be deferred while background subagents are running (or hand them off to the new session), and an SDK-initiated notice turn must never consume the pending user turn's result slot.

**Environment.** VS Code 1.139.1, Linux; anthropic.claude-code 2.1.284. The 1.140 release notes mention no fix, and no `chat.agentHost.*` setting governs rebind behavior.

**Related, but distinct:** #332073 (replies lost after background subagents complete — analyzed there as a `turnId === undefined` discard), #337904 (mid-turn steering messages never shown), PR #326270 (removes the rematerializer pattern; does not claim to preserve running subagents across a rebuild), PR #336753 (renders SDK-initiated turns when the prompt queue is empty).

issues.title: Copilot token refresh that finishes after an account switch is adopted for the new account

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
Found while fixing #339239.

## Problem

A Copilot token fetch that started for one GitHub account can finish after the user has switched accounts, and the result is then stored as the current token for the new account.

The post-fetch guard in `VSCodeCopilotTokenManager.getCopilotToken` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/authentication/vscode-node/copilotTokenManager.ts`) only checks that the auth provider and the GitHub Enterprise URI haven't changed. It doesn't check that the GitHub account is still the same. `BaseAuthenticationService.getCopilotToken` then stores the result and fires `onDidCopilotTokenChange`.

## Sequence

1. Account A is signed in, and its Copilot token refresh is in flight.
2. The user switches to account B. B's token mint fails (network error, `EnterpriseManagedError`, ...), and `onDidAuthenticationChange` fires with no token.
3. A's refresh finishes. Its token is stored and `onDidCopilotTokenChange` fires while the session is B.

## Impact

- Requests made while signed in as B use A's Copilot token until it expires or the identity changes again.
- Anything that evaluates policy from the current token reads A's entitlements for B. One example is BYOK provider registration (`BYOKContrib`), which re-applies policy on `onDidCopilotTokenChange`.

## Suggested fix

Tie each token result to the account (or an identity generation) that started the fetch. Discard stale results before they update the token store or fire token change events.

Last iteration we have made it possible to define the case sensitivity of selection matching with `cmd+d` independently of the Find widget. I have added a setting called `editor.selectedTextMatchMode` which takes three values `findOptions`, `caseSensitivity` and `caseInsensitivity`. The default value is `findOptions` and it ties the case sensitivity of occurrence matching with the Find widget. To test do the following: 

- Set `editor.selectedTextMatchMode` to `findOptions`. Verify the selection matching follows the case sensitivity of the Find widget.
- Set `editor.selectedTextMatchMode` to `caseSensitivity`. Verify the selection matching follows case sensitivity.
- Set `editor.selectedTextMatchMode` to `caseInsensitivity`. Verify the selection matching follows case insensitivity.
- Verify the above works correctly with different cursor interactions.

For an internal drag originating in the VS Code Explorer, the webview never gets re-enabled, so the webview's dragover/drop handlers never fire.

For comparison, in the same build:

Dragging a file from the Windows Explorer (OS) into the same webview works — dragover/drop fire as expected.
The internal Explorer drag does not work in either a sidebar webview (WebviewView) or an editor-tab webview (WebviewPanel).

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: VS Code 1.140.0
- GitHub Copilot extension 0.68.0 (bundled)
- OS Version: mac Golden Gate 27.0

Steps to Reproduce:

1. it's a Copilot Chat / `chat-ext-issue` scoped problem 
What happened
An MCP server exposes a tool whose input schema has an array-typed parameter with no items key (e.g. ```
{"type":
"array"}
```). This is valid JSON Schema — items is optional, an array without it is simply unconstrained — but Copilot's tool-list validation rejects it outright:

Error: tool parameters array type must have items at `extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1725:74 `at `RS.runWithToolCalling` (`extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:2807`)

Impact
The failure isn't scoped to the one malformed tool — it blocks registration of every tool from that MCP server, and the chat agent loop (`runWithToolCalling`) throws before any tool call can proceed, for any tool from any server, not just the offending one.

Expected behavior
Either (a) treat a missing items as "unconstrained array" per the JSON Schema spec rather than rejecting it, or (b) if Copilot wants to enforce a stricter profile, fail registration of only the one non-compliant tool and keep every other tool (from that server and others) available.

Repro
Register any MCP server (`stdio` or `streamable-http`) exposing a tool whose `inputSchema` contains a property declared {`"type": "array"`} with no items. Open Copilot Chat in that workspace. Tool registration throws the error above and the error shows as a generic chat failure, not attributed to the specific tool/server.

Happy to share a minimal repro MCP server if useful.

issues.title: Copilot Chat retains stale latest-chat content after switching to a previous chat

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
Type: Bug Description When switching from the currently active/latest Copilot Chat session to a previous chat session, content/state from the latest chat remains visible in the chat interface instead of being cleared or replaced correctly. The stale content remains visible even though a different previous chat has been selected. It only disappears/reset correctly after I open a new chat. Steps to Reproduce 1. Open GitHub Copilot Chat in VS Code. 2. Start or continue a chat session and send prompts so that it becomes the current/latest chat. 3. Without creating a new chat, navigate back to and open a previous chat session. 4. Observe the Copilot Chat interface after the previous session is loaded. 5. Content/state belonging to the latest chat remains visible instead of being removed when the previous chat becomes active. 6. Open a new chat. 7. The stale content is then cleared/reset. Actual Result After switching from the latest chat to a previous chat, UI state/content from the latest chat remains visible. The selected previous conversation and the latest conversation appear to have stale/mixed UI state. The stale state remains until a new chat is opened. Expected Result When I select a previous chat session, Copilot Chat should immediately update the UI to represent only that selected session. Any UI state/content belonging exclusively to the previously active/latest chat should be cleared or replaced. Opening a new chat should not be required to reset the interface. Reproducibility The issue can be reproduced by switching from the current/latest chat to an older chat without first opening a new chat. Impact This is confusing because the interface visually suggests that content from the latest conversation still belongs to the previously selected conversation. It can also make it unclear which chat session is currently active. Workaround Opening a new chat clears/resets the stale state, but this should not be necessary. issues.title: Copilot agent host: every ~/.copilot/instructions file is in the system prompt twice

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: built into VS Code 1.140.0 (bundled `@github/copilot` 1.0.73, `@github/copilot-sdk-win32-x64` 1.0.15-preview.4)
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`, x64)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise 26200
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent mode, agent host session (Copilot CLI in VS Code)
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): claude-sonnet-5
- Logs: not attached; `events.jsonl` holds the full private instructions. The relevant `system.message` excerpt can be shared on request.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Put user instruction files in `~/.copilot/instructions/`, e.g. `a.instructions.md`:
   ```markdown
   ---
   name: 'Rule A'
   description: 'Test rule A'
   applyTo: '**'
   ---

   # Rule A

   Always say MARKER-A when asked for the marker.
   ```
2. Optionally add a project instruction in `.github/instructions/p.instructions.md` of the open folder, same format.
3. Quit VS Code completely, start it, open the folder, start a new Copilot CLI session and send any prompt.
4. Open `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl` and look at the content of the `system.message` event.

**Expected:** each instruction file once.

**Actual:** every file from `~/.copilot/instructions` appears **twice**, byte-identical including its frontmatter: first together with the project instruction files, then again on its own, directly after. `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` and the project's `.github/instructions` files appear once. The model notices it too ("some instructions appear twice in the prompt"). The Local agent loads each file once.

Things that do **not** change it:
- `chat.instructionsFilesLocations` with `"~/.copilot/instructions": false` (the Local agent stops loading the files; the agent host session still has them twice)
- `~/.copilot/instructions` as a real folder instead of a symlink
- a full restart of VS Code (rules out the instruction cache)

**Likely cause (from the bundled, minified code):**

1. The runtime reads `<config>/instructions/**/*.instructions.md` itself and merges the files into **one** source: `{ id: "user-copilot-instructions", label: ".copilot/instructions", type: "vscode", location: "user" }`.
2. The agent host (`out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js`) runs its own customization discovery: `discoverRules` calls `rpc.instructions.discover`, turns the sources into `rule` customizations, and `lme` turns those into a plugin. Only rules that are `alwaysApply` **and** whose name ends in `.md` are skipped (which is why `copilot-instructions.md` appears once). `_buildSessionConfig` then passes `instructionDirectories: Lz(snapshot.plugins.flatMap(p => p.instructions))`, i.e. the **folders** of those rule files, which includes the user instructions folder.
3. The runtime loads each file of an `instructionDirectories` entry as a separate source: `type: "vscode"`, `id: "vscode-instructions/external/<path>"` (outside cwd / git root), `label: "<file> [external]"`.
4. The final dedup hashes content only for `type` `home`, `repo` and `model`, and otherwise dedups by `id`. The merged user source and the per-file sources are both `vscode` and have different ids, so both are kept. Project files get the same id `vscode-instructions/<path>` on both paths and are deduped.

I could not confirm from the minified code which discovery source makes the agent host include the user folder in step 2; steps 1, 3 and 4 are in the `@github/copilot` JS bundle, and the same ids (`user-copilot-instructions`, `vscode-instructions/external`) are in the SDK's `runtime.node`.

**Impact:** about 9 KB of duplicated context per request with ~12 small instruction files; no functional error.

**Possible fixes:**
- Agent host: do not pass folders the runtime already discovers itself (user `<config>/instructions`) as `instructionDirectories`.
- Runtime: dedup `vscode` sources by resolved file path or content as well, or skip files of an additional directory that are already part of `user-copilot-instructions`.

<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->

<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0
- OS Version: Windows 10

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Enable the `git.worktreeSymlinkFolders` setting:
2. Create a Git worktree for a repository.
3. Verify that the configured folder inside the worktree is a symbolic link pointing to the corresponding folder in the main worktree.
4. Remove the worktree using VS Code's Git worktree UI/command.
5. Observe that the target directory pointed to by the symbolic link is deleted instead of the symbolic link itself.

Expected Behavior:

When removing a worktree, VS Code should remove the symbolic link created by `git.worktreeSymlinkFolders`, leaving the target directory and its contents untouched.

Actual Behavior:

VS Code follows the symbolic link during worktree removal and deletes the contents of the target directory instead of removing only the symbolic link.

This can result in data outside of the worktree being unintentionally deleted.

Additional Information:

The issue appears to be specific to the handling of symbolic links created by `git.worktreeSymlinkFolders` during worktree cleanup/removal.

The symbolic link itself should be removed using an operation that does not follow the link.

issues.title: Test: Agents window session filters
issues.body:
Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339245

- [x] anyOS @federicobrancasi
- [x] anyOS @vijayupadya

Complexity: 3


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339261%0A%0A&assignees=benibenj)

---

The Agents window's **Filter Sessions** menu now separates where a session runs (**Environment**), the application that created it (**Created In**), and its agent (**Harness**).

![Filter Sessions menu with its Ordering, Grouping, Show, Environment, Created In, Harness, and Created Externally submenus](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2db7953-a997-496f-9cc3-49c3f050d66c)

## Set up

Open the Agents window. Start with default settings, ideally in a fresh profile.

- Create Local sessions in VS Code and in another application, such as Copilot CLI or Copilot App. Add Cloud sessions, and try different harnesses where available.
- Make sure you create at least one Cloud session from another application — for example, Slack, by sending a DM to the GitHub bot. Use a connected GitHub account and repository whose sessions you can see in the Agents window.
- If available, connect a remote agent host and create a session there.

## Explore the filters

Open **Filter Sessions** in the sidebar.

- Combine **Environment**, **Created In**, and **Harness** selections. Only sessions matching all three should remain visible. The creating application and harness are independent: a Claude session created in VS Code should still be listed under VS Code.
- **Created In** should list applications observed in your sessions, separated into environment groups. Try the same application in Local and Cloud where supported; changing one selection should not change the other.
- By default, Local has only **VS Code** selected. Cloud **Slack** and **Teams** are excluded. Enable **Slack (Cloud)** and confirm your DM-created session appears, then disable it again.
- Disable Cloud in **Environment**. Its application choices should disappear from **Created In**. Re-enable Cloud and check that the previous application selections return.
- If testing a remote host, rename it and disconnect/reconnect it. Environment choices should show connected hosts by name, without losing selections when the name or connection changes.

Reload the window and check that your selections persist. Try **Reset Filters**. Open and continue an externally created session in VS Code; its original **Created In** application should not change.

## Created externally and list presentation

- **Created Externally** defaults to **Last 7 Days**, with **Show in External Section** off. Explore the time options and the section checkbox. Eligible external sessions should either follow normal workspace/time grouping or appear in their own External section. Changing the time range should not change the grouping choice, or vice versa.
- Try **Ordering**, **Grouping**, and **Show**. Single-choice submenu titles should reflect the selected value; Show is available for Workspace grouping.
- Check that **Show Done**, **Compact View**, and **Collapse All Groups** still work.

Explore a few combinations rather than exhaustively testing every option. Are the menu organization, names, and interaction between Environment and Created In easy to understand?

issues.title: Git: Stash messages appear garbled when i18n.logOutputEncoding is set

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 / main
- OS Version: Windows / macOS / Linux

In `extensions/git/src/git.ts`, `Repository.getStashes()` runs `git stash list` without forcing the output encoding to UTF-8. If a repository or global gitconfig sets `i18n.logOutputEncoding` (or `i18n.commitEncoding`), non-ASCII stash messages appear as corrupted characters (Mojibake) in the Source Control Stashes view and related QuickPicks.

This is a follow-up to #331086 / PR #331087, which added `-c i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8` to `log`, `logFile`, `blame2`, `getCommit`, and `showChanges`, but missed `getStashes`.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Initialize a repository with non-UTF-8 encoding configured:
   ```sh
   git init test-repo
   cd test-repo
   git commit --allow-empty -m "initial"
   echo "sample" > file.txt
   git add file.txt
   git config i18n.commitEncoding EUC-JP
   git config i18n.logOutputEncoding EUC-JP
   ```
2. Create a stash with a non-ASCII message (e.g., EUC-JP text):
   ```sh
   git stash push -m "$(printf '\xa5\xc6\xa5\xb9\xa5\xc8 stash')"
   ```
3. Open the folder in VS Code with extensions disabled (`code --disable-extensions .`).
4. Inspect the stash in the Source Control panel or via `Git: Pop Stash...`.

Expected Behavior:
The stash message is decoded and displayed as `On master: テスト stash`.

Actual Behavior:
The stash message displays as `On master: ƥ stash`.

Direct CLI comparison:
```sh
# Current git.ts behavior (garbled output)
$ git stash list
stash@{0}: On master: ƥ stash

# Expected git.ts behavior (with -c i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8)
$ git -c i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8 stash list
stash@{0}: On master: テスト stash
```

Cause:
In `extensions/git/src/git.ts:3022`:
```typescript
async getStashes(): Promise<Stash[]> {
	const result = await this.exec(['stash', 'list', `--format=${STASH_FORMAT}`, '-z']);
	return parseGitStashes(result.stdout.trim());
}
```
Because `this.exec()` decodes stdout using `bufferResult.stdout.toString('utf8')` (line 657), `git stash list` needs `-c i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8` prepended to ensure Git converts the commit message to UTF-8 before writing to stdout:
```typescript
const result = await this.exec(['-c', 'i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8', 'stash', 'list', `--format=${STASH_FORMAT}`, '-z']);
```

issues.title: [chat-perf] layoutDurationMs regressed >20% in multiple chat scenarios (first run)
issues.body:
**Summary:**
New regression detected: layoutDurationMs increased by 21–38% in text-only, tool-terminal, large-codeblock, file-links, thinking-response, and tool-read-file chat scenarios. This is the first run, so no prior baseline exists, but the magnitude and consistency across scenarios indicate a real regression.

**Evidence:**
- *text-only*: 126.34ms ±1.82ms → 166.63ms ±6.81ms (+31.9%)
- *tool-terminal*: 177.62ms ±3.32ms → 220.3ms ±9.02ms (+24.0%)
- *large-codeblock*: 167.31ms ±4.46ms → 216.57ms ±9.64ms (+29.4%)
- *file-links*: 211.82ms ±3.7ms → 261.71ms ±2.17ms (+23.6%)
- *thinking-response*: 154.67ms ±3.84ms → 212.82ms ±6.57ms (+37.6%)
- *tool-read-file*: 213.62ms ±7.18ms → 258.39ms ±4.69ms (+21.0%)

All p-values are 0, indicating high statistical significance.

**Suspect commits:**
- 3b1bd0b (justschen): "make sure layout accounts for agents window padding" — src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.ts, src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts, src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts
- aaf5994 (justschen): "fix editor container overflow" — src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chat.css
- 33a3fa9 (justschen): "use plan widget instead of questions carousel when exiting plan mode" — src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts, src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts

**Suggested action:**
- Investigate recent changes to chat widget rendering/layout logic, especially those affecting chatListRenderer, chatWidget, and chat.css.
- Roll back or optimize the affected code to restore layoutDurationMs to prior levels.
- Monitor subsequent nightly runs for confirmation and further trend analysis.

issues.title: Selected custom endpoint can silently auto-route to another paid model

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body: - Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.66.0 (GitHub Copilot extension: 1.388.0) - VS Code Version: 1.138.0 (`7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda`, x64) - OS Version: Linux x64 under WSL2 - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode with a custom endpoint - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Custom endpoint model `azure-gpt-56-sol` - Logs: Attached. The available logs contain session metadata and the public model catalog, but do not appear to record the selected custom endpoint or automatic-routing decision. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Select the custom endpoint model `azure-gpt-56-sol` and use it in an existing chat. 2. Intermittently, a later request reports `Auto routed to ...`, although the custom endpoint still appears selected. I do not currently have reliable reproduction steps or enough evidence to identify the trigger. It may coincide with degraded connectivity or an unavailable custom endpoint, but this is unconfirmed. ## Actual behavior Copilot Chat can automatically route a request to a different GitHub-hosted model while `azure-gpt-56-sol` remains visibly selected. Observed routing targets include Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna. Therefore, the problem does not appear specific to one destination model. The automatic-routing notice is easy to overlook. This behavior can consume premium or paid requests even though the user did not knowingly select the model that processed the request. It also leaves the selected model shown by the UI inconsistent with the model that handled the request. ## Expected behavior When a specific custom endpoint is selected, no request should be sent to another model unless the user has explicitly enabled or approved automatic routing. If the selected model cannot handle the request, Copilot Chat should stop and clearly report the problem rather than silently falling back. The displayed selection must match the model that processes the request. Please provide a setting or policy that completely disables automatic model routing and fallback, especially fallback that can consume premium requests. ## Frequency Intermittent, but observed multiple times. ## Attachments [12ed51c2-f015-4922-b315-a259e933ce9f.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32947345/12ed51c2-f015-4922-b315-a259e933ce9f.zip)

issues.title: # DocumentDB for VS Code Extension v0.11 📈
issues.body:
# DocumentDB for VS Code Extension v0.11 📈 We are excited to announce **DocumentDB for VS Code Extension v0.11**. Explore your databases at a glance with the new **Cluster Dashboard**, work faster in a more helpful **Interactive Shell**, connect from Azure VMs with **Managed Identity authentication**, and carry indexes along when you **copy and paste** collections. Local setup is more dependable, too. ## What's New in v0.11 ### ⭐ Cluster Dashboard We are introducing a major new feature: the **Cluster Dashboard**. Opened from a cluster tree node, it gives you a focused inventory of everything a cluster holds, without leaving VS Code. The dashboard shows an overview with cluster identity, connection status, round-trip time, and Azure high-availability facts, plus a details view with server and other metadata you can copy directly.

Below the header, a database and collection inventory reports storage, data, index, collection, and document statistics where the server provides them, with sorting, filtering, drill-in, refresh, create, and delete actions. Open Shell and Copy Connection String are one click away, and a failed or partial read shows a clear retry state instead of a guessed number. Use the dashboard to get oriented and navigate your cluster on demand. It presents a snapshot of your data rather than a live view of running operations. ### ⭐ A More Helpful Interactive Shell The **Interactive Shell** now helps you find your way from the first prompt, with more context up front and useful guidance as you type. #### Know where you are The new connection header shows your saved connection name, host, authentication method, active database, and identity when available. For example: ```text Connected to: Local development (mycluster.example.com) Identity: admin | Authentication: Username and Password (SCRAM) | Database: myDatabase ``` With Microsoft Entra ID account sign-in, the header makes your signed-in identity just as clear: ```text Connected to: Production (prod.example.com) Identity: alex@contoso.com | Authentication: Microsoft Entra ID (Account) | Database: inventory ``` #### Discover as you type After connecting or switching databases, collection suggestions are prepared for you. Type `db.` to see how many collections are available in the current database; press **Tab** to browse their names and the database methods. Once you finish typing a method, the shell explains it before you run it: ```text myDatabase> db. 🛈 7 collections myDatabase> db.restaurants.countDocuments 🛈 Counts documents matching a filter (uses aggregate) ``` Complete the query with `({})` to count documents. Previously entered commands can also appear as inline history suggestions, and terminal resizing or narrow widths no longer disrupt your input and cursor. #### Let Tab handle tricky names For a collection named `restaurants-something`, the shell previews the bracket notation it needs. Press **Tab** to replace the dot notation with valid syntax: ```text myDatabase> db.rest 🛈 ['restaurants-something'] myDatabase> db['restaurants-something'] ``` Need to change how the shell behaves? Run `help` and follow the clickable link directly to the Interactive Shell settings. Learn more in the [Interactive Shell user manual](https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/interactive-shell). ### ⭐ Managed Identity Authentication We've added **managed identity authentication** for Azure DocumentDB (vCore) connections from VS Code running on Azure VMs. Connect with a system-assigned or user-assigned identity, and keep using it across the Collection View, Query Playground, and Interactive Shell. Your choice is remembered when you save, reconnect, or update a connection, with guidance when an identity endpoint is unavailable or a cross-tenant configuration is unsupported. Signing in is easier to navigate, too. Choose Username and Password, Microsoft Entra ID, or No Authentication first; if you choose Microsoft Entra ID, you can sign in with your account, use a managed identity from the connection string or current machine, or enter a user-assigned identity's client ID. You can return to the authentication choice at any step. Learn more in the [Managed Identity user manual](https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/connect-with-managed-identity). ### ⭐ Copy and Paste Indexes We've extended **Copy and Paste Collections** with full support for indexes, so you no longer have to recreate them by hand, whether you're copying an entire collection or just moving index definitions on their own. - **Indexes with your collection**: When you paste a collection, choose whether to recreate eligible secondary indexes on the target. To protect the data being copied, TTL and unique indexes are not included in this option; copy the documents first, then apply those indexes with the dedicated workflow below. - **Indexes on their own**: Use **Copy Index…**, **Copy Selected Indexes…**, or **Copy Indexes…** on a collection's Indexes node, then **Paste Indexes…** into a target collection, database, or another connected cluster. This workflow can include TTL and unique indexes without moving any documents. Existing equivalent indexes are skipped, conflicting names are handled automatically, and vector options and hidden-index state carry over. Your copied selection stays ready for the next target, making it easy to apply the same indexes across collections. Learn more in the [Copy and Paste user manual](https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/copy-and-paste). ## Key Fixes and Improvements - **DocumentDB Local Quick Start Reliability** - Set up or start fresh with greater confidence: Quick Start checks that setup can proceed before removing an existing data volume. - See useful Docker errors promptly and catch unsupported credentials or empty ports during configuration. - Pick up where you left off after an interrupted setup or external container or data removal. Your instance password stays out of the setup output channel, and temporary credentials are cleared as soon as the container starts. - **Settings Organization** - Find settings in eight expandable sections: General, Connections & Discovery, Queries & Results, Copy & Paste, Query Playground, Interactive Shell, AI Assistant, and Accessibility. - Shell and Query Playground connection timeouts now share `documentDB.connectionTimeout`. Nine settings have been renamed; if you customized any of the old settings, set their new equivalents again because previous values are not migrated. - **Azure Discovery Connections** - Connect more reliably to Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (RU) clusters from the Azure Resources view. Azure VM Discovery also shows VMs without a reachable address as unavailable, so you can see them without attempting a connection that cannot succeed. - **Connection Startup Diagnostics** - See whether a slow connection is waiting on Microsoft Entra ID authentication or the database, with separate timing information across Collection View, Interactive Shell, and Query Playground. - **Completion and UI Polish** - Field completions and Collection View now show document fields instead of internal BSON properties, including `MinKey` and `MaxKey` fields in completions. - Keyboard focus remains visible on the Create Index drawer's Standard and Vector tabs. When you select multiple connections, the deletion command clearly says **Delete Selected Connections**. ## Changelog See the full changelog entry for this release: ➡️ [CHANGELOG.md#0110](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-documentdb/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#0110) _Originally posted by @tnaum-ms in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-documentdb/discussions/982_

issues.body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.140.0 - OS Version: Windows 11 25H2 arm64 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Download VS Code Windows arm64 installer from the VS Code website 2. Start the installer 3. Notice it takes _much_ longer to install than a x64 machine, because the Inno Setup installer runs as a x86 executable: x86 emulation on Windows arm64 is much slower than x64 emulation. Inno Setup introduced a new field called [`SetupArchitecture=x64`](https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/index.php?topic=setup_setuparchitecture) in [7.0.0](https://jrsoftware.org/files/is7-whatsnew.htm), which is opt-in and still defaults to `SetupArchitecture=x86`. Please update the VS Code installer on Windows to also use `SetupArchitecture=x64` on Windows x64 and arm64. [Here's a PR](https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/pull/732) of how we did it in Git for Windows for inspiration. Given that VS Code doesn't seem to support 32-bit Windows anymore, just setting `SetupArchitecture=x64` in [`code.iss`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/build/win32/code.iss) should be enough, but I'm not sure if VS Code is already on Inno Setup v7.

issues.body:
Type: Bug ### Brief Description The model picker in VS Code Copilot Chat gets visually stuck on "Auto" / "HydraFusion" and does not allow manual model selection. Changing the session target to "Local" and then back to "Copilot" forces the UI to re-render, unfreezing the dropdown and leaving the manually selected model active. ### VS Code Version / Extension Version - VS Code: Latest (September 2026 Release) - GitHub Copilot Chat: Latest (Post-September 2026 update introducing HydraFusion) - OS: Windows/macOS/Linux ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open VS Code with an active Copilot Pro subscription. 2. Open the Copilot Chat view. 3. Observe the model picker at the bottom right stuck on "Auto" / "HydraFusion" with no ability to open the dropdown or change the model. 4. Attempting `Developer: Reload Window` or signing out/in does not resolve the UI lock. ### Workaround Found (UI State Reset) 1. Change the **session target** from `Copilot` to `Local` (or any local MCP agent). 2. Select the desired model while in the local session context. 3. Switch the session target back from `Local` to `Copilot`. 4. Result: The model picker unfreezes, and the manually selected model remains active and functional. ### Expected Behavior The model picker dropdown should always be interactive for Copilot Pro users, allowing manual model switching without requiring a session target toggle to force an interface re-render. ### Actual Behavior The UI state freezes on the automated router ("HydraFusion"), hiding or disabling the model selection list until the chat instance is destroyed and recreated via a session target switch. issues.title: Saving an open file after an ancestor directory is renamed externally silently recreates the old directory tree.

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
Type: Bug ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a directory structure such as: ``` A1/B/C/file.txt ``` 2. Open `A1/B/C` as a folder in VS Code and open `file.txt`. 3. Outside VS Code, rename the ancestor directory: ``` A1 → A2 ``` At this point the file is at `A2/B/C/file.txt`, and `A1` no longer exists. 4. Return to the still-open `file.txt` editor in VS Code, make an edit, and save. ### Actual behavior VS Code silently recreates the old directory tree and saves the edited file as: ``` A1/B/C/file.txt ``` The file at: ``` A2/B/C/file.txt ``` is left unchanged. There are now two versions of the file in different directory trees, with no warning that editing is continuing at the obsolete path rather than the user-intended path. ### Expected behavior I do not expect VS Code to follow an externally renamed directory automatically. However, if a file was opened from an existing path and then that path or one of its parent directories disappeared, I would expect the save to fail or VS Code to prompt before recreating the missing directory hierarchy. For example, VS Code could report that the original path no longer exists and ask whether the user wants to recreate it. ### Why this is different from #20071 #20071 requests that VS Code follow an externally renamed project folder. This report is narrower. Even if VS Code continues to identify the open file by its old path, silently recreating that path on the next save can cause the user to continue working in a new, obsolete copy of the directory tree without realizing it. This is especially easy to encounter when the rename happens while VS Code is open but unattended. For example, a user may leave a project open on one machine, later rename an ancestor directory on another machine with the same folder synchronized through Dropbox, and then return hours later to the first machine. Seeing the file still open in VS Code, the user may simply resume editing and saving, without realizing that VS Code is still using the old path and will recreate it. issues.title: Claude-format .claude/settings.json hooks enforced fail-closed on Windows; useClaudeHooks/useHooks/hookFilesLocations disables ignored

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
**VS Code version:** 1.140.x (Windows 11 Pro, no WSL distributions installed)
**Area:** agent hooks (Local harness), Claude-format hook discovery

## Summary

A workspace containing a Claude Code `.claude/settings.json` with `PreToolUse` hooks causes **every** Copilot agent tool call to be denied with:

```
Denied by preToolUse hook from "repo settings" (hook errored)
```

The hooks are un-executable on this platform, every hook error is treated as a denial, and every documented opt-out setting is ignored. Renaming the file is the only working mitigation.

## Root causes (each independently fatal on Windows)

1. **Wrong shell.** Hook `command` strings are bash syntax. On Windows they are either handed to PowerShell (parse error on `||`, `[ -f ... ]`, `case ... esac`) or dispatched via a bare `bash`, which resolves to `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` — the WSL launcher — regardless of `PATH` (`CreateProcess` system-directory precedence, microsoft/WSL#13277). With no WSL distribution installed, that exits immediately with "Windows Subsystem for Linux has no installed distributions."
2. **`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is never set** in the hook process, so every path reference (`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/...`) collapses to `/.claude/hooks/...` — a nonexistent path. (Same gap as #337374 measured for `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`.)
3. **Matchers are ignored.** The hooks use Claude tool-name matchers (`Bash`, `Edit|Write`, `Read|Glob|Grep`). Per the docs, "Local parses nested commands but ignores matcher values, so every command for the event runs" — so once any PreToolUse hook is registered, every tool call (including file views and greps) triggers every hook, and every hook errors.
4. **Fail-closed.** A hook error is treated as a denial of the tool call — so even advisory hooks that only emit `additionalContext` become fatal gates for the entire session.

## All documented opt-outs are ignored

Each of the following was set in the workspace settings, the window fully reloaded, and every tool call was still denied:

```jsonc
{
  "chat.useHooks": false,               // no effect
  "chat.useClaudeHooks": false,         // no effect — despite docs saying it gates .claude discovery and is off by default
  "chat.hookFilesLocations": {          // no effect
    "~/.claude/settings.json": false,
    ".claude/settings.json": false,
    ".claude/settings.local.json": false
  }
}
```

Notably, the docs say `chat.useClaudeHooks` is **off by default** and required for `.claude/settings.json` discovery — yet the hooks were enforced with no such setting present anywhere in user or workspace settings.

Also verified: the same enforcement applies to `.claude/settings.local.json` (moving the hooks there did not help), which the docs list as a Claude-format hook location gated by the same setting.

## Only working mitigation

Rename `.claude/settings.json` to any other name (e.g. `.disabled`) and reload the window. This also disarms the hooks for Claude Code itself, which honors the file correctly — so teams using both hosts cannot currently have Claude Code hooks and a functional Copilot agent in the same workspace.

## Verification that the hooks themselves are sound

The same hook commands execute correctly under Git Bash (exit 0, valid JSON output) — the failure is entirely in harness execution/discovery, not in the hook content.

## Related

- #337374 — Claude-format plugin hooks on Windows: WSL bash, mangled paths, unset env var. This report reproduces on a machine with **no WSL distributions installed**, removing the WSL-interop variable from that diagnosis.
- github/copilot-cli#4001 — same fail-closed symptom and error string in Copilot CLI ("repo settings", PowerShell execution, unset `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`).
- #312314 — hookExecutor hardcodes the Windows shell.

issues.title: BackgroundDownload leaves a ~118 MB installer copy in %TEMP% on every failed run (337 copies, 39.8 GB), which fills the disk it is checking for space

labels.name: bug

labels.name: install-update

labels.name: windows
labels.description: VS Code on Windows issues

issues.body:
Type: Bug Summary The scheduled task \Microsoft\VisualStudio\Updates\BackgroundDownload fails its disk-space pre-check when C: has less than 10 GB free. Every run, including the failed ones, extracts a full copy of the Visual Studio Installer into a randomly named folder in %TEMP% and never deletes it. Because the task keeps retrying, these copies pile up, use up the free space the pre-check requires, and turn into a self-reinforcing loop. Environment Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (10.0.19045) Visual Studio Community 2022: 17.14.36623.8 Visual Studio Community 2026: 18.0.11222.15 Both installed side by side on C: (465 GB drive) What happens Free space on C: drops below 10 GB. BackgroundDownload runs. The log shows: Error: Pre-check verification: Visual Studio needs at least 10737418240 of disk space. Try to free up space on C:\ or change your target ... Precheck: Failure in checking if the drive exists: Value cannot be null. Error: Pre-check verification failed with error(s) : BackgroundDownloadPrecheck. The task exits with last result 0x1F42. A folder such as %TEMP%\bzs3zla1.ecc is left behind. It contains setup.exe, vs_installer.exe, vswhere.exe, feedback.exe, InstallCleanup.exe, localized resource folders, PrecheckTools\, ProxyStub\, and so on, about 118 MB per folder. The task runs again a few minutes later (consecutive logs at 21:46 and 21:53 on the same evening) and leaves another copy. Result 337 folders in %TEMP% contain vs_installer.exe, totalling 39.8 GB. The drive reached less than 1 GB free. This blocked the update permanently and affected the rest of the system. Expected behavior The installer deletes its extracted temp copy when a run finishes, whether it succeeds or fails. After a failed disk-space pre-check, it backs off or notifies the user once, instead of retrying every few minutes and using more disk on each attempt. The pre-check doesn't throw Value cannot be null when it checks whether the drive exists. Impact On machines that are already low on space, the updater silently uses tens of gigabytes. It's hard to diagnose because the space is spread across hundreds of randomly named Temp folders with no obvious link to Visual Studio. Workaround Disable the BackgroundDownload scheduled task. issues.title: Managed OTel policy changes break new chats until the Agent Host restarts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: otel
labels.description: OTel (OpenTelemetry)

issues.body:
## Error

```text
Error: (sendFailed) Request session.create failed with message: Standalone managed telemetry preparation failed: Managed telemetry conflicts with the already selected OTel configuration
```

## Summary

Changing managed telemetry policy between sessions on a running Agent Host can break new chats. We reproduced the exact error by changing only `telemetry.serviceName`; restarting the host with the new policy unchanged restored chat. Policy requests returned HTTP 200.

## Environment

- Reproduced: macOS, Code OSS `1.141.0` at `c2f1ef2d05c`, SDK `1.0.16`, runtime `1.0.90`.
- Originally reported: Windows, Insiders `1.141.0` at `ec2e580674cdb512aa9b2a9596ab35d8a9590f1e`, same SDK/runtime. The original policy-change sequence is unverified.

## Reproduction

1. From a built VS Code checkout, start the mock server:

```sh
npm run mock-policy-server
```

2. Open <http://127.0.0.1:3000>, follow **Setup > System proxy**, and enable Proxyman's platform proxy. Set VS Code's `http.proxy` to `http://localhost:9090` (Proxyman), **not port 3000** (the mock server).

3. Mock Managed Settings with HTTP 200 / JSON and the following body. Leave other endpoints on passthrough:

```json
{
  "forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": false,
  "telemetry": {
    "enabled": true,
    "endpoint": "http://localhost:4319",
    "captureContent": true,
    "lockCaptureContent": true,
    "serviceName": "testtesttest"
  }
}
```

This disables the unrelated startup refresh gate. Use harmless prompts because content capture is enabled.

4. Fully quit Code OSS, then launch from the checkout root with an isolated policy cache:

```sh
COPILOT_CACHE_HOME="$PWD/.build/otel-repro-cache" ./scripts/code.sh --log trace
```

Run **Developer: Sync Account Policy**, then **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host**. Create a new Agent Host chat and send `Hi`. **It succeeds.**

5. Change only `telemetry.serviceName` to `testtesttest-warm-change`. From the checkout root, clear only the isolated policy cache:

```sh
rm -r -- .build/otel-repro-cache/managed-settings
```

Without syncing policy, reloading, or restarting, create another new Agent Host chat and send `Hi`. **It fails with the exact error above.**

6. Keep the changed policy. Run **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host**, create a new chat, and send `Hi`. **It succeeds again.**

## Scope

`serviceName` is the minimal verified reproduction, not a reason to scope the fix to that field. Please also cover changes to collector endpoints, headers/credentials, resource attributes, protocols, content-capture policy, and telemetry enablement. Those transitions were not individually live-tested here.

## Expected behavior

Coordinate safe recovery, or offer an explicit restart-and-retry action, preserving the message and history. Recovery must continue to enforce the required exporter and privacy policy.

## Version context

Related runtime PR: [github/copilot-agent-runtime#22864](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/22864) (repository access required).

Relevant dependency updates: [#338512](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338512) adopted SDK `1.0.15-preview.4` / runtime `1.0.89-7`; [#339018](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339018) upgraded to the reproduced SDK `1.0.16` / runtime `1.0.90`. Earlier builds were not live-tested in this reproduction.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

issues.title: Improve build/agentHost metadata generation script with pre-flight Git commit verification
issues.body:
## Summary
The Copilot metadata generation script (`build/agentHost/generateCopilotMetadata.ts`) currently relies on running `git show` directly with the configured `sourceCommit`. If an invalid repository path or a non-existent commit SHA is provided, it fails later in the execution flow with obscure or deeply nested errors.

## Proposed Enhancement
Add an early validation check (fail-fast principle) to verify that the provided `--source` path is a valid Git repository and that the target `sourceCommit` exists and is reachable before attempting schema extraction. 

## Benefits
* **Better Developer Experience (DX):** Provides clear, immediate error messages when incorrect commit hashes or paths are supplied.
* **Robustness:** Prevents partial execution and unnecessary build friction.

issues.title: Add integrated browser support for new permissions-based Domain rules (Local and Agent Host)
issues.body:
The integrated browser reads legacy network-filter settings, but not runtime-managed Domain rules. An enterprise restriction that blocks native `web_fetch` therefore does not necessarily block the same destination in the browser. This shared-browser gap affects both Local and Agent Host.

## Examples

**1. Managed blocklist only**

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "deny": ["Domain(blocked.example.com)"]
  }
}
```

With no legacy browser restriction, this rule does not configure the browser filter. Expected: agent-driven access to `https://blocked.example.com` is blocked in both harnesses.

**2. Mixed legacy and managed policies**

Keep the managed deny above and also apply these legacy policies:

```json
{
  "ChatAgentNetworkFilter": true,
  "ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains": ["*.example.com"],
  "ChatAgentDeniedNetworkDomains": []
}
```

The browser filter permits `blocked.example.com` through the legacy safelist without applying the managed deny. Expected: the managed deny wins, while `docs.example.com` remains permitted.

## Requested behavior

Apply effective managed Domain restrictions to agent-controlled browser navigation and network requests, alongside existing legacy restrictions. Cover both harnesses and policy changes. This should not impose blanket restrictions on manual browsing or reinterpret `permissions.allow` as a mandatory safelist.

Evidence: the [shared browser filter reads only legacy settings](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d89944204d3fce23e43270c27c0099e13509d879/src/vs/platform/networkFilter/common/networkFilterService.ts#L96). Examples are source-derived, not a fresh end-to-end reproduction.

**Related:** Once [Domain `limitTo` support](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/23922) lands, also include those restrictions in the integrated browser's policy enforcement.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

issues.title: macOS: Remote status bar corner is clipped with Modern UI enabled
issues.body: ### Description There appears to be a visual issue with the Remote SSH UI on recent versions of macOS when the experimental Modern UI is enabled: ```json "workbench.experimental.modernUI": true ``` With Modern UI enabled, the Remote SSH/status bar area at the bottom-left of the window is rendered as a rounded rectangle. However, its corner radius is noticeably smaller than the native VS Code window corner radius on macOS 26/27. As a result, the rounded edge of the Remote SSH area intersects with / gets clipped by the outer macOS window corner, producing an awkward cut-off appearance. ### Screenshots **Modern UI enabled — issue present:** The inner rounded corner has a significantly smaller radius than the macOS window corner, so part of the UI appears clipped. **Modern UI disabled — looks correct:** Without Modern UI, the Remote SSH/status bar area follows the window edge normally and does not have this visual mismatch. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run VS Code on macOS 26 or macOS 27. 2. Install/use the Remote - SSH extension. 3. Enable: ``` "workbench.experimental.modernUI": true ``` 4. Connect to a remote machine using Remote SSH. 5. Look at the bottom-left corner of the VS Code window. ### Actual behavior The Remote SSH/status bar container uses a relatively small corner radius. Because the macOS window itself now has a substantially larger corner radius, the two curves do not align and the Remote SSH area appears visually cut off at the window edge. ### Expected behavior The bottom-left Modern UI container should visually follow the native macOS window corner. Ideally, its corner radius could either: - match the effective macOS window corner radius, or - be clipped/inset in a way that follows the outer window shape correctly. The non-Modern UI layout already looks correct in this respect. ### Additional note This seems primarily to be a Modern UI styling/layout issue rather than an SSH functionality issue. It is especially noticeable on newer macOS versions because of the larger native window corner radius. Would it be possible to adjust the corner radius or clipping behavior for this element on macOS? ``` Version: 1.140.0 Commit: 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74 Date: 2026-09-30T10:38:38+02:00 Electron: 43.7.3 ElectronBuildId: 15386805 Chromium: 150.0.7871.250 Node.js: 24.21.0 V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0 @github/copilot: 1.0.89-7 @github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.15-preview.4 OS: Darwin arm64 27.0.0 ```

Configured/built-in MCP servers that support remote usage remain available in remote windows, and the built-in GitHub MCP server behavior is consistent with the setting.

issues.title: Agent turn should not end while background commands are still running
issues.body:
**Searched existing issues:** yes — no open feature request matches this (checked 2026-10-01).

## Problem

In agent mode, a turn can end — and its reply read as "done" — while the chat's **"Waiting for x background commands"** indicator is still live. The count is also opaque: a **crashed** session is indistinguishable from a **slow** one, and over a working day the background-task count only grows, with nothing ever inspected or cleaned up.

## What I see locally (setup + observed facts)

- Setup: a local **OpenCode** instance configured as a custom endpoint for GitHub Copilot Chat, with the LLMs it serves declared as agents in VS Code's `chatLanguageModels.json` custom-models file. I observe this notably with LLMs managed by agents defined as custom endpoints in that file. Every fact below is observed with this configuration.
- A sync command that exceeds its timeout is moved to the background **silently**.
- Session state is known to the runtime (completion is reported, if at all, in the *next* turn) but is not available when the agent finalizes a turn — so a truthful end-of-turn evaluation is hard to produce.
- Background sessions **survive window reloads and new chat sessions**, which can neither see nor stop them: a concrete source of the daily accumulation.
- Observed today: a test-suite command exceeded its sync timeout and moved to the background; the next turn ended and read as "done" with the indicator still live; and a session whose stdout had gone silent was impossible to distinguish from one still producing results.

## Proposal

- End-of-turn rule: every background session started for the task is **finished**, or the agent has **explicitly evaluated** each pending one (keep running / stop / stop and relaunch) and says so in the final reply (which session, why, how to stop it).
- Surface session state (running / finished / failed, exit code) to the agent at turn finalization — it is already tracked, just not visible at that moment.
- Give the agent those sessions as **one grouped, machine-readable inventory** (single call) — the precondition that makes the evaluation above applicable.
- Make the indicator honest and actionable: per-session state, expansion into a list, a stop action per session — stale sessions become stoppable without the agent.
- Announce the sync→background switch; report a session's completion and keep its output retrievable, so nothing is lost when a command times out to background.
- On chat-session end, offer to stop the sessions it started; leftovers from previous windows stay visible and stoppable.
- Optionally a setting for the preferred end-of-turn behavior (wait / evaluate / allow detached).

## Why

- **Performance**: fewer follow-up round-trips caused by continuing with steps that depend on results the background sessions had not produced yet.
- **Coherence**: the "done" state always reflects reality; the "Waiting for..." indicator no longer appears on a reply that claims completion.
- **Hygiene**: crashed or stale sessions become visible instead of silently accumulating over the day.
- **Recoverability**: background-session results are not lost when a sync command moves to the background after a timeout.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.140.0 (stable), bundled GitHub Copilot extension
- Windows 11 + WSL (Fedora 44) remote workspace
- Custom endpoint: local OpenCode instance serving the LLM models to Copilot Chat
