issues.body:
Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338666

- [x] anyOS @roblourens
- [x] anyOS @houghj16

Complexity: 2

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/925f18dd-e6c5-4980-a7f9-3a9673de8ad3

## Arrange sessions in a grid

The Agents window previously supported showing sessions side by side. Sessions can now be arranged in a two-dimensional grid, with nested horizontal and vertical splits that persist across reloads.

Open the Agents window and create or open at least three sessions with some conversation history. Include an unsent draft in one of them.

### Drag and drop

- Drag sessions from the sidebar onto different edges of an open session. Verify the drop indicator makes the resulting placement clear.
- Build a layout containing both rows and columns, then move sessions between different positions.
- Resize the panes using their sashes. Make sure the layout remains usable at different window sizes.
- Close and reopen a session from the grid. Existing conversations and unsent drafts in the other panes should remain intact.

### Layout actions

Explore the related commands in the Command Palette:

- Move focus between sessions in each direction.
- Move sessions around the grid and resize panes with the keyboard commands.
- Arrange the sessions into a balanced grid.
- Maximize one session and restore the full grid.

Do the actions, labels, and resulting layouts feel predictable?

### Restore

Reload the Agents window and verify the grid arrangement, pane sizes, active session, and maximized state are restored. Resize the window between narrow and wide layouts and confirm returning to the wide layout restores the desktop grid.

issues.title: Test: GHES with GitHub Pull Requests and GHE.com with Copilot, side by side

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

issues.body:
Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/277435, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github/issues/9003

- [x] anyOS @bhavyaus
- [x] anyOS @sandy081

Complexity: 5


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339182%0A%0A&assignees=TylerLeonhardt)

---

## Context

`github-enterprise.uri` only held one instance, so you couldn't use Copilot with a GHE.com account and GitHub Pull Requests with a GHES account in the same VS Code (#277435). The new `github-enterprise.uris` setting takes a list:

```json
"github-enterprise.uris": [
  "https://github.ghe.com",
  "https://ghe.io"
]
```

There's still one **GitHub Enterprise** provider. It holds accounts from every configured instance, and each account is labeled `username - host` so you can tell them apart.

## Setup

You need:

- a GHE.com account (https://github.ghe.com works)
- an account on https://ghe.io (a GHES instance), and a repo there with a pull request or two

Run `code-insiders --transient` so you start signed out with empty settings. Then install the pre-release of GitHub Pull Requests:

1. Open the Extensions view (`Cmd+Shift+X` on macOS, `Ctrl+Shift+X` on Windows and Linux).
2. Search for `GitHub Pull Requests`, select it, and click **Install**.
3. On the extension's page, click **Switch to Pre-Release Version**.
4. Check the version next to the extension name on that page. You need 0.167.2026100118 or newer.

## Copilot on GHE.com

On the welcome screen, click **GHE**, enter `github`, and sign in. Use Copilot for a bit so you know it works.

## Pull Requests on GHES

Clone your repo from ghe.io. GitHub Pull Requests should notice it and offer to set up GitHub Enterprise. Go along with it, then sign in from the GitHub Pull Requests view.

- With both instances configured, sign-in asks which instance you want. Is it clear which to pick?
- Check `github-enterprise.uris`. Is your GHE.com entry still there next to the new one?
- Do the repo's pull requests and issues show up?
- Is Copilot still signed in to GHE.com, with no new prompts?

## Telling accounts apart

Open the Accounts menu. You should see two GitHub Enterprise accounts, one ending in `github.ghe.com` and one ending in `ghe.io`.

- Can you tell at a glance which account is which?
- Open **Manage Extension Account Preferences...**, either from the Accounts menu or by running **Accounts: Manage Extension Account Preferences...** from the Command Palette. Does it show which account each extension uses?

## Things to poke at

- Reorder the entries in `github-enterprise.uris`. Nothing should change.
- Remove the `https://ghe.io` entry, then add it back. The account should go away and come back without signing in again.
- Reload the window. Both accounts should stay signed in, with no prompts.
- Sign out of your GHE.com account and sign in to Copilot again. Now that both instances are configured, the picker lists your GHES instance too, even though Copilot only works with GHE.com. Does that trip you up?

## Known limitations

Please don't file these:

- GitHub Pull Requests uses one GitHub Enterprise account at a time. Using GHES and GHE.com repos in GitHub Pull Requests at the same time is microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github#9004. Multiple accounts on one instance is microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github#9005.
- Copilot only supports GHE.com, not GHES.
- Upgrading from `github-enterprise.uri` and Copilot's instance validation are covered by #339160 and #339161. You don't need to retest them here.

issues.title: MCP migration picker: clicking a server row or checkbox does not reliably toggle selection

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6af0ab1-0341-4fef-a48a-ae04955d3a6a

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an MCP server available to migrate.
2. Open **Agent Customizations → Migrations → Migrate MCP Servers**.
3. With the server unchecked, click its row/name and then its checkbox to select it.
4. Observe the checkbox, selected count, and **Migrate** button.

## Actual Behavior

In the observed recording, the row responds visually with hover/focus feedback, but clicks on the row and checkbox do not reliably change the selection. The checkbox remains unchecked, the footer still reads **0 selected**, and **Migrate** remains disabled.

Later in the recording, the item becomes selected: the footer reads **1 selected**, **Select all** is checked, and **Migrate 1** is enabled. Further row clicks appear not to deselect it. The recording does not establish which interaction caused selection to succeed.

## Expected Behavior

Clicking the server row or its checkbox should toggle selection exactly once and immediately update the checkbox, selected count, **Select all** state, and migration button.

## Scope

This report describes the selection interaction observed in a screen recording, not a failure of migration execution. The underlying cause has not been investigated.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

issues.title: Keep default chat input permissions in sync across chat surfaces
issues.body:
When a user changes the default chat input permission in one chat surface, the choice should carry over to the others.

For example, choosing **Allow All** in the Agents Window currently does not persist as the default in the Editor chat input. Users have to select the same permission again when moving between surfaces.

**Expected behavior**

Default chat input permissions are shared and kept in sync between the Agents Window and Editor chat, including changes made from either surface.

Type: Feature Request ### Problem I want to run AI agents like Claude Code in the integrated terminal, but VS Code intercepts shortcuts they rely on ( like Ctrl+P and Ctrl+Shift+P ) instead of passing them to the terminal application. VS Code currently handles some of these shortcuts instead of passing them to the terminal application. The workaround, terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell, also disables the corresponding VS Code shortcuts globally. For example, allowing Ctrl+P in the terminal disables Quick Open. ### Expected behavior When a terminal application is using the alternate buffer, keyboard shortcuts should be passed through to it, while continuing to work normally in VS Code outside the terminal. ### Alternative considered `terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell` works, but changes VS Code shortcut behavior globally. labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

labels.name: authentication-github
labels.description: Issues with the GitHub Authentication extension

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Work not yet planned for a specific release.

issues.body:
GitHub sessions only expire today when they're brokered through Microsoft Entra (#335183). Those sessions report `expiresAfter` and renew themselves before they run out. Ordinary GitHub OAuth sessions are stored in the keychain with no known expiry, and nothing ever renews them.

The GitHub Authentication extension should support expiring GitHub tokens for those sessions too, by requesting the `offline_access` scope. With `offline_access`, sign-in returns an access token that expires plus a refresh token. The extension would:

- store the refresh token next to the session
- report the access token's remaining lifetime through `expiresAfter`
- renew the access token before it expires, the same way Entra-brokered sessions renew today

The renewal path in `extensions/github-authentication/src/github.ts` (`stillGood`) only handles transient Entra-brokered sessions. It will need to give persisted sessions their own expiry and branch on how a given session renews.

Related: #335183, #335184

issues.title: Test: "Continue with Microsoft" only when your Microsoft account links to GitHub
issues.body: Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338823 - [x] windows @dmitrivMS - [x] macOS @ulugbekna Complexity: 3 [Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339157%0A%0A&assignees=TylerLeonhardt) --- ## Context Last round (#333246) put **Continue with Microsoft** in sign-in dialogs behind a setting. Turning it on for everyone would show the button to people it can't help, like anyone whose Microsoft account isn't linked to a GitHub account. So now VS Code checks first. The check runs silently in the background. It asks the OS broker for the work and school accounts on your machine, trades each one for a short-lived GitHub token, and asks GitHub who that is. If one of them is linked to a GitHub account (for most of us, an EMU), you get the button. Nothing is saved, and the GitHub token used for the check is revoked. `chat.microsoftAuthentication.enabled` now takes three values: - `auto`: run the check, and offer the button only if it finds a link - `always`: offer the button without checking - `never`: don't offer it, and don't check The button also shows up in a new place: the "Welcome to VS Code" screen a fresh install opens on, as an icon next to Apple. ## Setup Use a work machine where your Microsoft work account is signed in to the OS. Everything here runs in `code-insiders --transient`, which uses throwaway data and extension folders, so you start signed out of everything. ## `auto` Run `code-insiders --transient`. The welcome screen opens with GitHub, Google and Apple. After a short delay, the Microsoft icon should join them. You don't need to change any settings, since Insiders already has `auto`. - How long did it take? Did the icon popping in feel natural or jarring? - Skip the welcome screen and click **Sign In** in the title bar. Is the option in that dialog too? ## `always` Start another `code-insiders --transient` and add this to your settings: ```json "microsoft-authentication.implementation": "msal-no-broker" ``` Click **Reload** when VS Code asks. Without the broker, the check can't see the accounts on your machine, so `auto` has nothing to find. Run **Developer: Welcome Onboarding 2026** to reopen the welcome screen. The Microsoft icon should stay away this time. Now set `"chat.microsoftAuthentication.enabled": "always"`. The icon and the dialog option should come back. ## `never` Set it to `never`. The option should be gone from both the welcome screen and the **Sign In** dialog. ## Then sign in When you're done with the settings, set it back to `auto` or `always`, click **Continue with Microsoft**, and go through sign-in. - The confirmation shows your GitHub handle and nothing else. Is that enough to decide? - Once you're signed in, does Copilot work like it normally does? - Did anything along the way confuse you or feel broken? ## Notes - `auto` depends on the OS broker. Windows on ARM and Linux don't have it yet, so `auto` won't find anything there. - `msal-no-broker` sends Microsoft sign-in through the browser instead of the OS prompt. That's expected. ## Known issues - #333501: signing in with a personal Microsoft account ends at an unhelpful error. `auto` skips personal accounts but `always` doesn't, so you might hit this one. - #333492: you get your EMU account, not your personal GitHub account. That's by design. - If the Microsoft authentication extension is slow to start, a dialog you open early can be missing the option because the check hasn't finished. Dialogs you open after that should have it.

issues.title: Dictation intermittently omits word spaces and inserts literal <en-US> tags
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested.

- VS Code Version: Code - Insiders 1.141.0-insider
- Commit: ec2e580674cdb512aa9b2a9596ab35d8a9590f1e
- Build date: 2026-10-01T04:00:54Z
- OS Version: macOS 15.6.1, Apple silicon (arm64)
- Input method: VS Code's built-in microphone button in the chat input, not macOS system dictation
- Spoken language: English

## Description

Dictation intermittently omits spaces between words and sometimes inserts the literal language tag `<en-US>` into the chat input. This seems to have started recently, but I have not identified the first affected build. I do not know whether the two symptoms share a cause.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start dictation using the microphone button in the VS Code chat input.
2. Dictate ordinary English sentences, stop recording, and inspect the resulting text.
3. Repeat over multiple dictation sessions. Missing spaces occur repeatedly; the extra language tag is intermittent. I have not isolated a reliable trigger for the tag.

## Actual results

Examples copied from affected dictated messages:

```text
What iswrong with thetext tospeech?<en-US> Therearenospaces, andit'sadding extrastuff like

<en-US>
```

```text
I'm now testing the dictation Are thespaces beingentered properly andare there extra tags beingadded
```

```text
Is thisworthfiling issuereporton the GitHubrepo
```

A later message also contained the tag between sentences:

```text
I liked having the live preview it's too bad it went away. <en-US> Will it come back in the future
```

## Expected result

Preserve spaces between spoken words and do not insert language metadata such as `<en-US>` into the transcript unless it was actually dictated as text.

## Troubleshooting and limits

- Temporarily set `dictation.experimental.llmCleanup` to `false`. Missing spaces still occurred.
- Also temporarily set `dictation.showTranscript` to `false`. Subsequent samples had normal spacing, but there were too few controlled samples to establish a reliable fix or a causal relationship.
- The literal `<en-US>` tag appeared again while both of those overrides were disabled. Its absence in earlier samples was not evidence of a fix.
- Both overrides have now been removed, restoring the original/default behavior. Missing spaces have appeared again after restoration.
- I have not yet tested with all extensions disabled or compared with a known-good older build.

## Relevant log observation

Before AI cleanup was disabled, the renderer log repeatedly recorded:

```text
[chat-stt] selecting language model cleanup model (vendor=copilot, id=copilot-utility-small)
[chat-stt] language model transcript cleanup failed (reason=error, phase=consumeResponse, elapsedMs=6); using raw transcript Unknown tokenizer: undefined
```

This is an additional observation, not a confirmed explanation: the spacing problem also occurred with cleanup disabled.

## Related issue

#332324 concerns replacement/deletion of a visible transcript after stopping. It may be useful background, but I have not established that this report has the same cause or that its fix introduced these symptoms.

issues.title: fix: assert configured Copilot integration ID in CloudSandboxApiService task deletion test (build fix for vscode-engineering#405

labels.name: vscode-build
labels.description: VS Code build process issues

issues.body:
## Build failure

Build 479434 (insider, `refs/heads/main`) failed the **Run unit tests (Electron)** job on Linux, macOS, and Windows with 3 failing tests in the new `CloudSandboxApiService task deletion` suite:

```text
actual Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat
expected Copilot-Integration-Id: code-oss
```

The failures covered the HTTP 200, 204, and 404 task-deletion cases.

## Root cause

`src/vs/platform/endpoint/common/licenseAgreement.ts` defines `COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID = 'code-oss'` for Code - OSS, but is explicitly "modified as part of the production build" (per the file's header comment), where product CI rewrites the value to `vscode-chat`.

The production code in `cloudSandboxApiService.ts` correctly sends the `Copilot-Integration-Id` header using the shared `COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID` constant. However, the task-deletion test in `cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts` asserted the header against a hardcoded literal `'code-oss'`. In the product build the constant becomes `vscode-chat`, so the assertion no longer matched the request the service actually made, failing the Electron unit tests on all three platforms.

## How the fix works

The test now imports and asserts against the same `COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID` constant that the production code uses to build the request header. The expectation therefore tracks whatever value the build configures — `code-oss` in OSS and `vscode-chat` in product — instead of a brittle literal. This verifies the real contract (the service sends the configured integration ID) without weakening the assertion.

## Rollback evaluation

- **Recommendation:** Do not roll back
- **Culprit:** `88349a27ead34c34511504a1d62906b0f2a84d7a`, microsoft/vscode#339042
- **Rationale:** The break is confined to a new test expectation that hardcoded the OSS integration ID. Aligning the assertion with the shared constant is a bounded, lower-risk fix-forward than reverting the larger session-deletion feature and its production code.
- Owners to consult: ``@roblourens``

## Validation

The TypeScript compiler (`tsc` / `npm run typecheck-client`) could not be run in this environment — the sandbox blocked invoking the compiler. The change is a minimal, localized test edit: it adds one import (verified that `src/vs/platform/endpoint/common/licenseAgreement.ts` exists at the computed relative path) and swaps a string literal for the already-exported `COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID` constant used by the production code. The resulting expectation matches the exact value the service sends in both OSS and product build configurations.

## Risk

Low. The change touches a single assertion in one test file, with no production code impact. It strengthens the test to match the production contract across build configurations.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: ``@roblourens``

issues.title: Feature Request: Privacy-focused built-in coding time tracking
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

I’d like to propose an optional, privacy-focused coding time tracker built
directly into VS Code.

Today, users who want to understand their actual coding time generally need
third-party extensions and external services. A lightweight built-in solution
could provide this functionality without requiring an account or sending any
activity data outside VS Code.

The initial version could:

- Track active editor time and automatically pause during inactivity.
- Show daily, weekly, monthly, and lifetime coding time.
- Provide basic statistics per workspace and programming language.
- Display the current session/time through the status bar.
- Store all statistics locally.
- Avoid recording keystrokes, source-code contents, or file contents.

The feature could be opt-in and disabled by default, with settings to control
tracking and idle timeout.

I believe this could provide a useful zero-configuration alternative for users
who only want basic coding-time statistics while keeping their activity
private.

I’d be happy to investigate the existing VS Code architecture and contribute
an initial implementation if the team considers this suitable for VS  #Code.

issues.title: Investigate Agent Host enforcement of content exclusions

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
Agent Host sessions currently do not appear to enable content exclusions, even though the underlying SDK supports them. This is still required by customers and has blocked CLI rollout.

Investigate whether this is intentional or a gap, and ensure Agent Host sessions enforce the configured content exclusion policy where applicable.

### Questions to resolve
- How content exclusion policy is propagated to Agent Host sessions today
- Whether all supported Agent Host providers enforce it consistently
- What validation or tests are needed to prevent regressions

issues.body:

issues.title: fix: reject with proper Error on audio error event (fixes #339115)
issues.body:
### Summary An accessibility signal sound fails to play, and the `error` event handler in `doPlayAudio` rejects the promise with `e.error` — but a DOM media `error` event is a plain `Event` that has no `error` property, so the promise rejects with `undefined`. That `undefined` then reaches the `catch (e)` block in `playSound`, which reads `e.message` and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'message')`. Impact: an unhandled error is logged to telemetry whenever an accessibility cue sound fails to load/play (e.g. missing/blocked media), affecting 425 users on stable 1.140.0. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339115 Recommended reviewer: ``@meganrogge`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | pre-existing — not a regression | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | The faulty `reject(e.error)` has existed since the file was created; no recent commit changed the triggering logic. This bucket is new on the 1.140.0 stable channel but the defect is long-standing (surfaced at stable scale / under conditions where a cue sound fails to play). This is best characterized as a pre-existing bug newly observed, not a code regression. | > No culprit commit identified: the defective line predates the available > history for this file and no commit in the regression window altered the > audio error-handling path. The fix targets the long-standing producer bug. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller as playSignal participant Sound as playSound participant Audio as doPlayAudio participant DOM as HTMLAudioElement Caller->>Sound: await playSound(sound) Sound->>Audio: await playAudio(url, volume) Audio->>DOM: new Audio(url); audio.play() DOM-->>Audio: 'error' event (plain Event, no .error) Note over Audio: ⚠️ Root cause (L297):
reject(e.error) → rejects with undefined Audio-->>Sound: promise rejects with undefined Note over Sound: 💥 L211: e.message
Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'message') ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/platform/accessibilitySignal/browser/accessibilitySignalService.ts` | root cause (producer) | L297: `reject(e.error)` — the media `error` event is a plain `Event` with no `.error` property, so the promise rejects with `undefined` | | `src/vs/platform/accessibilitySignal/browser/accessibilitySignalService.ts` | crash site | L211 (from stack): `if (!e.message.includes(...))` reads `.message` on the `undefined` rejection value | ### Repro Steps 1. Trigger any accessibility signal that plays a sound (e.g. enable sounds via `accessibility.signalOptions`, then perform an action that plays a cue). 2. Cause the audio element to emit an `error` event — e.g. the media resource fails to load, is blocked, or is otherwise unplayable (the browser/Electron fires `error` rather than resolving `play()`). 3. The `error` handler rejects the play promise with `undefined`; the `catch (e)` in `playSound` reads `e.message` and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'message')`, which is reported as an unhandled error. Because `play()`'s own rejection path (L300) rejects with a real `Error`, the crash only manifests via the media `error` event path, which explains the intermittent, environment-dependent occurrence. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`accessibilitySignalService.ts` → `doPlayAudio`): fix the data producer, not the crash site. The `error`-event handler no longer rejects with the non-existent `e.error`. Instead it constructs a proper `Error`, enriched with the real failure details from `audio.error` (an `HTMLMediaElement`'s `MediaError`, carrying `.code` and `.message`) when available, and a generic `"Failed to play audio"` message otherwise. After this change the promise always rejects with a genuine `Error` instance, so the downstream `catch (e)` in `playSound` can always read `e.message` safely — the `TypeError` can no longer be produced. This keeps the existing `logService`/`console.error` telemetry path intact (the `catch` block still runs and still logs genuine failures), and it enriches the error with cross-boundary diagnostic context (`MediaError.code`) rather than swallowing it. **Alternatives considered:** - Guard at the crash site (`e?.message` or `if (!e) return` in `playSound`'s catch) — rejected: that is a crash-site guard that masks the producer bug, leaves every other consumer of `playAudio` receiving a meaningless `undefined` rejection, and discards the real failure cause. - Wrap the play call in try/catch that swallows the error — rejected: it would hide genuine audio failures from the telemetry pipeline. ### Recommended Owner ``@meganrogge`` — area owner of `accessibilitySignalService.ts`; authored the large majority of this file's history and is highly active in `microsoft/vscode` (hundreds of commits in the last 90 days). The culprit is pre-existing, so ownership falls to the feature-area owner. --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. issues.title: [Feature] Markdown Preview: Table of Contents with persistent visibility & Code block language labels
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
This issue tracks the implementation of two new features for the Markdown preview. **A PR has already been created implementing these features.**

Features Requested  

**1. Table of Contents (TOC) Sidebar**  

Requirements:  
- Display a collapsible sidebar on the left of the Markdown preview showing all document headings (h1–h6)
- Indent entries by heading level
- Highlight the active heading based on scroll position in the preview
- Toolbar button to toggle TOC visibility with checkbox state
- Persistence: Remember visibility preference across:
   - Preview tab close/reopen
   - VS Code restart
- Resizable sidebar width (drag handle), persisted across sessions
- Context key `markdown.tocVisible` for keybinding/menu integration

Auto-scroll behavior:
- When scrolling the document, the TOC panel should scroll minimally to keep the active entry visible (with small edge gap)
- Clicking a TOC entry manually should navigate without scrolling the TOC panel
- First/last headings should be able to reach the true top/bottom of the TOC panel (no visual gap when selected)

**2. Code Block Language Labels**  

Requirements:
- Display a language badge in the top-right corner of fenced code blocks
- Theme-aware styling using design tokens (`--vscode-editorCodeBlockLabel-background/foreground`)
- Works in light, dark, and high contrast themes

#### Related PR
PR #339113

When `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` is enabled and the user has configured a custom Agents chat background, the new-session prompt stack needs an opaque main session-surface base. Without it, the configured background can show between translucent input elements and make the composer feel visually fragmented.

The prompt stack should use `--session-view-background` only when a custom chat background is active. The legacy composer and sessions without custom backgrounds should remain unchanged.

Implemented in #339110.

issues.title: fix: guard against duplicate language model tool registration (fixes #339101)
issues.body:
### Summary An extension can register a Language Model tool whose id was already registered in the same extension host. The extension-host `ExtHostLanguageModelTools.registerTool` / `registerToolDefinition` methods accepted the duplicate id, overwrote their own `_registeredTools` entry, and fired a second `$registerTool` across the ExtHost→MainThread RPC. On the main thread `registerToolImplementation` rejects the duplicate with `Tool "" already has an implementation.`, but because the ExtHost call is fire-and-forget the rejection surfaces as an unhandled error in telemetry. Impact: noisy unhandled errors on Mac/Windows/Linux; the second registration silently fails. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339101 Recommended reviewer: ``@roblourens`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not identified — pre-existing boundary throw | | Author | — | | PR | — | | Message | — | | Why | The main-thread throws in `registerToolImplementation` (`already has an implementation`) and `registerToolData` (`was not contributed`) have existed since `4ba135f7` (Oct 2024). No commit in the regression range `544a8291..73d5322b` touches the tool-registration files. The range commit `487a93be` ("extensions: serialize unexpected errors before forwarding") changed how unexpected ExtHost errors are serialized before `$onUnexpectedError`, which is the most plausible reason these pre-existing cross-process rejections began bucketing as new telemetry — i.e. re-bucketing of a pre-existing defect, not a behavioral regression. The underlying bug (missing producer-side duplicate guard) is pre-existing. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as Extension participant EH as ExtHostLanguageModelTools participant MT as MainThreadLanguageModelTools participant Svc as LanguageModelToolsService Ext->>EH: registerTool(id) Note over EH: ⚠️ Root cause:
no duplicate-id guard,
overwrites _registeredTools EH->>MT: $registerTool(id) [RPC, fire-and-forget] MT->>Svc: registerToolImplementation(id) Note over Svc: 💥 throw:
Tool "id" already has an implementation Svc-->>MT: rejection Note over MT: RPC reply rejected;
no ExtHost handler → unhandled error ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts` | crash site | L359 (from stack): `throw new Error(\`Tool "\$\{id}" already has an implementation.\`)` | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadLanguageModelTools.ts` | RPC boundary | L92-L109: `$registerTool` calls `registerToolImplementation(id, ...)`; rejection crosses back with no ExtHost handler | | `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts` | root cause (producer) | L344-L350: `registerTool` did `this._registeredTools.set(id, ...); this._proxy.$registerTool(id, ...)` with no guard against an already-registered id | ### Repro Steps 1. Author an extension that calls `vscode.lm.registerTool('myTool', impl)` twice for the same id (e.g. an activation path that runs registration more than once, or two code paths registering the same tool name). 2. Activate the extension. 3. The second call reaches the main thread and `registerToolImplementation` throws `Tool "myTool" already has an implementation.`; since the ExtHost did not await/handle the RPC rejection, it is reported as an unhandled error. The sibling bucket `Tool "" was not contributed.` (microsoft/vscode#339102) is the same boundary pattern when `registerToolImplementation` runs before the matching `registerToolData`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts`: add a synchronous duplicate-id guard at the top of both `registerTool` and `registerToolDefinition`, before mutating `_registeredTools` or sending the RPC: ```ts if (this._registeredTools.has(id)) { throw new Error(`Tool "${id}" is already registered.`); } ``` This fixes the data producer rather than the crash site. The duplicate is now rejected synchronously, in the extension host, on the caller's own stack — so the offending extension gets a normal thrown error from the API call it made (the same way `extHostDebugService`, `extHostCustomEditors`, `extHostFileSystem`, and many other extHost registries already reject duplicate ids), and no malformed second `$registerTool` ever crosses the RPC boundary to become an unhandled main-thread error. It also stops the ExtHost `_registeredTools` map from being silently overwritten, which previously detached the first registration's disposer from its entry. **Alternatives considered**: - Swallow or `try/catch` the throw in the main thread `registerToolImplementation` / `$registerTool` — rejected: that hides a real caller bug from telemetry and leaves the ExtHost map corrupted; the error pipeline depends on real defects being surfaced, just on the correct (caller's) stack. - Make `registerToolImplementation` idempotent (return the existing disposable) — rejected: it would mask double-registration and make tool ownership/disposal ambiguous across two different implementations sharing one id. **Lifecycle pattern**: external/untrusted boundary — the producer is an extension calling the public `lm` API across the extension-host RPC. The fix is placed at the first point inside `microsoft/vscode` that owns the contract (the extHost registry), converting an async unhandled rejection into a synchronous, attributable API error for the extension author. **Producer site**: `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts:344` (`registerTool`) and `:358` (`registerToolDefinition`). ### Recommended Owner ``@roblourens`` — owner of the chat language-model tools area (author of `languageModelToolsService` and its tests, 400+ commits to microsoft/vscode in the last 90 days). --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. The changes have been pushed to the branch [`fix/lm-tool-duplicate-registration-339101-99cc1ecba207c6d9`](https://github.com/vscodebot-pr/vscode/tree/fix/lm-tool-duplicate-registration-339101-99cc1ecba207c6d9). > > **Original error:** ERR_API: [2026-10-01T15:15:08.464Z] create pull request in microsoft/vscode failed (attempt 1) Original error: Validation Failed: {"resource":"PullRequest","code":"custom","field":"fork_collab","message":"fork_collab Fork collab can't be granted by someone without permission"} - https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#create-a-pull-request Retryable: false Suggestion: This error cannot be resolved by retrying. Please check the error details and fix the underlying issue. issues.title: fix: buffer LM tool implementations registered before their data contribution (fixes #339102)
issues.body:
### Summary `unhandlederror-Tool "appmod-install-appcat" was not contributed.` is thrown on the main thread when an extension registers a language-model **tool implementation** (via `vscode.lm.registerTool(id, ...)`) before the matching **tool data** from that extension's `package.json` `languageModelTools` contribution has been registered by `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler`. This is an activation-ordering race: three App Modernization tools (`appmod-install-appcat`, `appmod-run-assessment`, `appmod-build-docker-image`) each hit it, affecting ~104 users across Linux, Windows and Mac. The fix buffers an early implementation and attaches it when the tool data arrives, so the race no longer throws. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339102 Recommended reviewer: ``@bhavyaus`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — see below | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | No commit in the regression range (`544a8291...73d5322b`) touches `languageModelToolsService.ts`, `languageModelToolsContribution.ts`, `mainThreadLanguageModelTools.ts`, or `extHostLanguageModelTools.ts`. This is **not** a code regression in those files. The bucket is a re-occurrence of the error family previously addressed by PR #326651 (*"register LM tools extension point handler at BlockStartup"*, milestone 1.131.0, owner ``@bhavyaus``). That fix moved the producer earlier but did not make the ordering impossible: the per-extension contribution *delta* for a newly-activated extension can still be delivered **after** that same extension's `activate()` has already called `vscode.lm.registerTool(...)`. The new bucket surfaced because the App Modernization extension began shipping `appmod-*` tools that activate through a non-tool path and register their implementations eagerly, re-exposing the latent race. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as App Mod extension
(activate) participant EH as extHostLanguageModelTools participant MT as mainThreadLanguageModelTools
$registerTool participant Svc as LanguageModelToolsService participant EP as ExtensionPointHandler
(registerToolData) Ext->>EH: vscode.lm.registerTool('appmod-install-appcat', impl) EH->>MT: $registerTool(id) MT->>Svc: registerToolImplementation(id, impl) Note over Svc: ⚠️ Root cause:
_tools has no entry yet —
data contribution not processed Note over Svc: 💥 Error thrown:
Tool "appmod-install-appcat"
was not contributed. EP-->>Svc: registerToolData(id) arrives later (too late) ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts` | crash site + root cause (fixed) | L384-L386 (pre-fix): `const entry = this._tools.get(id); if (!entry) { throw new Error(\`Tool "\$\{id}" was not contributed.\`); }` | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadLanguageModelTools.ts` | trigger (RPC) | L93: `$registerTool` calls `registerToolImplementation(id, ...)` from the fire-and-forget extHost RPC | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/languageModelToolsContribution.ts` | producer of tool data | L289: `languageModelToolsService.registerToolData(tool)` runs from the extension-point handler's `setHandler` delta | | `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts` | trigger origin | L344-L346: `registerTool` immediately calls `_proxy.$registerTool(id, ...)` during extension activation | ### Repro Steps 1. Install/enable an extension (e.g. App Modernization) that both declares tools in its `package.json` `languageModelTools` contribution and calls `vscode.lm.registerTool('appmod-install-appcat', impl)` early in `activate()`. 2. Cause the extension to activate through a non-tool path so its `activate()` runs before `LanguageModelToolsExtensionPointHandler` has processed that extension's contribution delta. 3. The main thread executes `registerToolImplementation('appmod-install-appcat', ...)` while `_tools` has no entry for the id, and throws `Tool "appmod-install-appcat" was not contributed.` into error telemetry. Note: this is an activation-ordering race, so it reproduces intermittently depending on extension activation timing relative to extension-point delta delivery. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts`: - `registerToolImplementation(id, tool)` no longer throws when `_tools` has no entry for `id`. Instead it buffers the implementation in a new `_pendingToolImpls` map and returns a disposable that cleans up whether the impl is still pending or has since been attached. A second pending implementation for the same id still throws `already has an implementation`, preserving the duplicate-registration signal. - `registerToolData(toolData)` now checks `_pendingToolImpls` after inserting the entry and attaches any buffered implementation to the newly created entry. This fixes the **data producer's ordering problem at the producer/consumer boundary in the service**, not at a crash-site guard: the two registration halves (data from the extension-point handler, implementation from the extHost RPC) can arrive in either order, and the service now makes the unsupported order representable and self-healing. This mirrors the invoke path, which already tolerates the reverse race (it activates the extension and re-reads `_tools` for the impl at `languageModelToolsService.ts:584`). The genuinely-missing-tool signal is still preserved everywhere it matters: `invokeTool` still throws `Tool was not contributed` when neither data nor impl ever arrives, so a typo'd id surfaces at invocation time via the existing telemetry path rather than being silently swallowed. **Alternatives considered:** - Re-adjusting the extension-point handler's lifecycle phase again (as PR #326651 did) — rejected because the handler is already at `BlockStartup` and the race is between a *per-extension* contribution delta and that same extension's activation, which phase ordering cannot serialize. - Wrapping the `$registerTool` RPC in try/catch at the main-thread boundary — rejected because it swallows the error at the crash site and hides genuine missing-contribution cases from telemetry instead of fixing the ordering. ### Recommended Owner ``@bhavyaus`` — owner of the language-model tools area and author of the prior fix for this exact error family (PR #326651). issues.title: Agent Host: send_message should replace its unacknowledged queued message with an up-to-date one

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

When one session messages another with `send_message` and the target chat is busy, every call adds another queued message. If the sender follows up before the target has started the first one, the target ends up with a stack of separate, unacknowledged messages from the same sender. Each becomes its own turn, and the earlier ones are usually out of date by the time they run.

## Proposal

When sessions talk to each other, the sender should read the most up-to-date state and keep one complete, current message in the target, not a stack of unread updates:

- The sender can read its own undelivered message, including any edits made to it while it waited, before sending again (for example, through `get_session_context`).
- Sending again before the target has started that message replaces it with one complete message that reflects the current state, not just what changed. The message keeps its ID, its place in the queue, and its model.
- The `send_message` result returns the text that was replaced, so the sender can tell whether anything it still needs was dropped.
- Once the target has started the message, which acknowledges it, the next message is queued as a new one.

## Related: queued cross-session messages show "Auto" in the model picker

When you edit a queued message that another session sent, the model picker shows **Auto** instead of the target session's model. It should show that session's model, so if the session's picker shows Opus 5.5 · xHigh · 1M, the edit should show Opus 5.5 · xHigh · 1M too.

This is more than a display problem. Saving the edit as Auto switches the chat's model when the message is delivered, and switching models breaks the prompt cache. Queued messages from other sessions should run on whatever model the target chat is already using, without switching it, and editing a request that has no recorded model should start on the conversation's current model.

Related: #334459 (queue messages sent to a busy chat), #335540 (use steering for inter-session messages)

issues.title: Agents window: Subagents menu replaces the active chat while subagent pills open to the side

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
In the Agents window, opening a subagent chat behaves differently depending on the entry point:

- **Subagent pill** in a response (`MenuId.ChatSubagentContent`): opens the subagent chat **to the side** of the current chat.
- **Subagents menu** in the chat input pills ("Subagents: In Progress" / "Subagents: Completed"): **replaces** the active chat with the subagent chat.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In the Agents window, start a session that runs a subagent.
2. Click the subagent pill in the response. The subagent chat opens to the side.
3. Close it, then open the Subagents menu in the chat input and select the same subagent. The subagent chat replaces the active chat.

### Expected

Both entry points open the subagent chat to the side, so the parent chat stays visible.

### Notes

The two paths use different `ISessionsService` methods:

- Pill: the opener registered in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/openSubagentChat.ts` calls `sessionsService.openChatToSide(...)` and passes the parent as `referenceChatResource`.
- Menu: `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/sessionBackgroundActivitiesControl.ts` sets each entry's `open` to `this._sessionsService.openChat(currentSession, subagent.resource)`.

issues.title: Agent fails to execute known tool operations, enters planner livelock, and generates synthetic failures instead of performing tool dispatch

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
# Title

Agent fails to execute known MCP tool operations, substitutes unrelated actions and synthetic failures, and never attempts dispatch

- Copilot Chat Extension: GitHub Copilot Chat (Built-in)
  - Extension Identifier: github.copilot-chat
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (x64)
  - Commit: b6c7324cedb6fc4ed639e3c7e1d4b233a09df8bc
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise 64-bit
  - Version: 10.0.26200
  - Build: 26200
- Feature: Agent Mode (MCP tools enabled)
- Selected model:
  - Initially: GPT-6.1 Sol
  - Switched to: GPT-6 Astra at approximately 09:31 on October 1, 2026
  - Failure continued after the model switch.
- Logs: Attached

## Summary

While attempting to create an Azure DevOps User Story through an MCP-backed Azure DevOps tool, the agent identified the correct operation, tool, and arguments but never performed the requested dispatch.

The same configured MCP server successfully executed equivalent Azure DevOps operations from a different chat session, including successful invocation of `wit_work_item`, successful invocation of `wit_work_item_write`, and creation of work item 67722.

The failing chat never produced either:

- a successful Azure DevOps response; or
- a genuine MCP dispatch failure.

Instead, it repeatedly performed unrelated actions and eventually generated a synthetic PowerShell exception.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Copilot Agent Mode with MCP tools, including Azure DevOps work-item operations.
2. Successfully use MCP tools or establish a valid MCP connection.
3. Encounter a tool availability concern, authentication issue, or tool catalog refresh.
4. Reload the VS Code window.
5. Allow MCP discovery to complete.
6. Request an Azure DevOps work-item operation whose tool name and arguments are already known.
7. Continue instructing the agent to execute the operation instead of researching it.
8. Observe the agent repeatedly perform planning activity rather than dispatching the MCP tool.

## Requested Operation

Tool:

```text
azure-devops-wit_work_item
```

Arguments:

```json
{
  "action": "get",
  "project": "Development",
  "id": 67705,
  "expand": "Relations"
}
```

## Expected Behavior

The agent should do one of the following:

1. Resolve the tool binding and execute the requested operation.
2. Attempt dispatch and return the actual MCP/tool error.
3. Report that binding resolution could not be completed.

The agent should not substitute unrelated actions for execution.

## Actual Behavior

Observed behavior:

- Another chat successfully invoked `wit_work_item` against the same MCP server.
- Another chat successfully invoked `wit_work_item_write` against the same MCP server.
- Another chat successfully created Azure DevOps work item 67722.
- The affected chat repeatedly failed to invoke the requested MCP operation.
- The issue persisted after window reload.
- The issue persisted after tool rediscovery.
- The issue persisted after changing models.
- Searches for the requested tool returned unrelated capabilities.
- The agent repeatedly substituted instruction-file reads, agent actions, tool discovery, and unrelated tool calls for the requested operation.
- No fresh Azure DevOps tool response was produced.
- No genuine MCP dispatch rejection was produced.

Representative sequence:

```text
Operation selected
        ↓
Binding uncertainty
        ↓
Instruction reads
        ↓
Tool discovery
        ↓
Unrelated tool calls
        ↓
Additional instruction reads
        ↓
Availability claims
        ↓
Synthetic terminal failure
        ↓
No dispatch attempt
```

## MCP Discovery Evidence

MCP log:

```text
2026-10-01 09:17:10.899 [info] Discovered authorization server metadata at https://login.microsoftonline.com/72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration

2026-10-01 09:17:11.510 [info] Discovered 43 tools
```

Despite successful rediscovery, the agent continued behaving as though tool availability could not be verified.

## Synthetic Failure Example

After being explicitly instructed to either execute the operation or return a real dispatch error, the agent executed:

```powershell
throw 'Cannot dispatch azure-devops-wit_work_item: it is not registered in this terminal executor.'
```

This was not a tool-dispatch result.

The assistant later acknowledged that the error was authored by the assistant itself and executed through PowerShell rather than being returned by the MCP runtime.

## Agent Self-Reported Findings

The assistant later acknowledged:

- The operation was known.
- The tool name was known.
- The required arguments were known.
- No actual dispatch attempt occurred.
- The PowerShell exception was synthetic and authored by the assistant.

## Impact

This failure prevents valid MCP-backed operations from completing even when:

- The operation is known.
- The tool is known.
- The arguments are known.
- User authorization is present.
- MCP discovery completed successfully.
- Equivalent operations can be executed successfully in another chat against the same MCP server.

The conversation remains active and continues generating activity, but no execution progress occurs.

## Why This Appears To Be A Product Issue

Evidence suggests this is not an Azure DevOps issue and not an MCP server issue:

- The same configured MCP server was successfully used from another chat session.
- Successful `wit_work_item` and `wit_work_item_write` operations were observed during the same investigation.
- The failing chat never produced an Azure DevOps tool response.
- The failing chat never produced an MCP dispatcher rejection.
- The failing chat instead produced planning activity and a synthetic PowerShell exception.

## Suggested Investigation Areas

- Planner-to-executor transition logic
- MCP tool binding resolution
- Tool availability invalidation after catalog refresh
- Handling of rediscovery events
- Prevention of synthetic execution receipts
- Prevention of repeated instruction-reading loops after execution has been selected
- Cases where one chat can execute MCP operations while another chat attached to the same server cannot

## Description
An extension can be activated through an implicit `onLanguage:<languageId>` event while VS Code is restoring the previously opened editor after **Developer: Reload Window**. 
At that moment: 
* `vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders` is already populated and contains the correct workspace folder;
* `vscode.workspace.getConfiguration(...).get(...)` returns the default value instead of the value from `.vscode/settings.json`;
* `vscode.workspace.getConfiguration(...).inspect(...)` reports the workspace value as `undefined`;
* the workspace configuration becomes available only later, after activation has already completed.

The same problem does not occur when the extension is activated later through `onStartupFinished`. In that case, the value from `.vscode/settings.json` is already available when `activate()` is called.

## Steps to Reproduce:
Reproduced in an Extension Development Host launched with --disable-extensions. The only active extension required for reproduction is the minimal development extension itself.
1. Create a `package.json` file, specify the new language, and set `activationEvents` to `onStartupFinished`.
```

    "displayName": "VS Code Configuration Repro",
    "description": "Minimal repro for workspace configuration loading",
    "version": "0.0.1",
    "engines": {
        "vscode": "^1.100.0"
    },
    "main": "./extension.js",
    "activationEvents": [
        "onStartupFinished"
    ],
    "contributes": {
        "languages": [
            {
                "id": "reprolang",
                "aliases": ["Repro Language"],
                "extensions": [".repro"],
                "configuration": "./language-configuration.json"
            }
        ],
        "configuration": {
            "title": "Configuration Repro",
            "properties": {
                "configRepro.testPath": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "default": "",
                    "scope": "window"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```
2. Create an empty language-configuration.json.
3. Create the extension.js file:
```

function dumpConfiguration(label) {
    const configuration =
        vscode.workspace.getConfiguration("configRepro");

    console.log(`\n========== ${label} ==========`);

    console.log("time:", new Date().toISOString());

    console.log(
        "workspaceFolders:",
        vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders?.map(
            folder => folder.uri.fsPath
        )
    );

    console.log(
        "activeTextEditor:",
        vscode.window.activeTextEditor?.document.uri.fsPath
    );

    console.log(
        "testPath:",
        configuration.get("testPath")
    );

    console.log(
        "inspect:",
        configuration.inspect("testPath")
    );

    console.log("==============================\n");
}

function activate(context) {
    dumpConfiguration("ACTIVATE");

    setTimeout(() => {
        dumpConfiguration("AFTER 0 MS");
    }, 0);

    setTimeout(() => {
        dumpConfiguration("AFTER 100 MS");
    }, 100);

    setTimeout(() => {
        dumpConfiguration("AFTER 500 MS");
    }, 500);

    setTimeout(() => {
        dumpConfiguration("AFTER 1000 MS");

}

function deactivate() {}

module.exports = {
    activate,
    deactivate

```
4. The workspace configuration where we will test the extension: `.vscode/settings.json`
```

    "configRepro.testPath": "/THIS/IS/WORKSPACE/VALUE"
}
```
5. Run Extension
6. Open the .c file and run **Developer: Reload Window**.
7. In OUTPUT - Extension Host the line was displayed:
`[info] ExtensionService#_doActivateExtension undefined_publisher.vscode-config-repro, startup: false, activationEvent: 'onStartupFinished'`

10. In OUTPUT - Extension Host the line was displayed:
`[info] ExtensionService#_doActivateExtension undefined_publisher.vscode-config-repro, startup: false, activationEvent: 'onLanguage:reprolang'`
11. The `Debug Console` shows that `testPath` is unavailable during activation and remains unavailable even after the active editor has been restored. It becomes available only on a subsequent `onDidChangeConfiguration` event:

issues.title: Tool grouping/virtual tools broken for custom endpoints
issues.body:
### Summary
VS Code Insiders 1.140/1.141 virtual tool optimization engine fails to initialize when starting a new session with custom endpoints (OpenRouter, custom DeepSeek extensions).  
Error: "You may not include more than 128 tools in your request"`
Currently the only way around it is to manually disable built-in tools and mcp servers to get below the 128 threshold

### Workspace & Environment Details
- **VS Code Version:** Insiders 1.140.0 / 1.141.0
- **Custom endpoint:** OpenRouter and DeepSeek

### Precise Replication Steps
1. **Scenario A (Fails - Expected Bug Context):** Start a brand-new chat session (`+` icon) with the BYOK/OpenRouter endpoint explicitly selected as the primary provider. 
   - *Result:* Chat fails with the 128-tool hard limit constraint error before any input prompt is sent.

2. **Scenario B (Succeeds temporarily):** Start a fresh session using an official hosted Copilot model (e.g., Sonnet 5.5). Send a prompt, copilot is able to discover all tools dynamically selects relevant ones and defers irrelevant ones. Then, switch mid-session to a custom endpoint.
   - *Result:* Prompting works perfectly fine for the first few turns.

3. **Scenario C (Native Control):** Run the official hosted Copilot model on the paid tier.
   - *Result:* Works flawlessly; virtual tool threshold optimization is presumably able to successfully group tools.

### Logs

Agent debug logs is not showing logs beyond the initial loading of instructions

issues.title: Explorer: add "Collapse All" and "Expand All" to the folder context menu
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
## Problem

In the Explorer, the only way to collapse folders is the "Collapse Folders in Explorer" button in the view title bar, which collapses the entire tree. There is no way to collapse or expand just one folder together with all of its subfolders. In large projects this means:

- Collapsing one deeply nested folder requires clicking each subfolder individually, or collapsing the whole tree and losing my place.
- Expanding a folder's full structure at once is not possible without expanding each level by hand.

## Proposal

Add two items to the Explorer context menu when right-clicking a folder:

- **Collapse All**: collapses the selected folder and all of its descendant folders.
- **Expand All**: expands the selected folder and all of its descendant folders.

Behavior details:

- The actions apply only to the selected folder's subtree. The rest of the tree is untouched.
- They appear only on folders, not on files.
- Expand All should be safe on very large trees (for example `node_modules`). I'd suggest it respects `files.exclude` and `explorer.excludeGitIgnore`, and I'm open to guidance on whether a depth or item limit is needed.
- Both would be registered as commands so they can be bound to keyboard shortcuts and used from the Command Palette.

## Alternatives considered

- The existing "Collapse Folders in Explorer" title-bar button only works on the whole tree.
- Keyboard shortcuts for expanding or collapsing a recursive subtree are not discoverable and are not available for all cases.

## Additional context

I'm willing to implement this and open a PR. I'd appreciate guidance from the team on the preferred menu group and placement, command naming, and any performance concerns with recursive expansion.

issues.title: Recursive watcher deduplication lets narrow same-root request replace broad workspace watcher

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: Code - OSS 1.141.0, 98f79f78c81
- OS Version: macOS 15.8.1 arm64

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Register a normal uncorrelated recursive watcher for a workspace root, without an `includes` filter.
2. Register another uncorrelated recursive watcher for the same root with a narrow filter such as `includes: ['mcp/*.mjs']`.
3. Ensure the narrow request occurs later in the request list.
4. Change a file outside the narrow pattern, for example `.custom/agents/example.agent.md`.

Expected:

The broad workspace watcher continues reporting the change through `IFileService.onDidFilesChange`.

Actual:

No change is reported. The later narrow request replaces the broad request during Parcel watcher deduplication, so the effective watcher only reports `mcp/*.mjs`.

## Root cause

`ParcelWatcher.removeDuplicateRequests()` groups uncorrelated requests by path. For duplicate paths it logs that the duplicate request is being ignored, but then unconditionally overwrites the existing map entry:

```ts
if (requestsForCorrelation.has(path)) {
	this.trace(`ignoring a request for watching who's path is already watched: ${this.requestToString(request)}`);
}

requestsForCorrelation.set(path, request);
```

For equal paths, behavior therefore depends on request ordering and the last request wins even when it is narrower than the request it replaces.

## Live-debug evidence

The failure was diagnosed with two requests for the same workspace root:

- the normal recursive workspace watcher with no `includes` filter;
- an MCP dev-mode watcher with `includes: ['mcp/*.mjs']`.

While the narrow watcher was active, saving `.custom/agents/custom-planner.agent.md` produced no workspace resource event and downstream customization discovery remained stale. Temporarily separating the narrow request with a correlation ID immediately restored the `.custom` event. After restart, with the narrow watcher absent, the same save produced the complete expected chain:

1. `FileOperation.WRITE`;
2. uncorrelated `internalOnDidFilesChange`;
3. global `onDidFilesChange`;
4. the configured `.custom/agents` root matched via `e.affects(searchRoot)`.

The deduplication should preserve the union of uncorrelated watch interests, or otherwise ensure a narrow same-root request cannot replace a broader request.

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. Reproduced with the Arm Debugger extension in an Extension Development Host; the evidence below captures the state being removed inside VS Code's workbench, rather than a missing debug-adapter event.

- VS Code Version: 1.138.0, commit `7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda` (Linux snap)
- OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, x86_64; Linux 6.8.0-139-generic
- Debug extension: Arm Debugger 2.0.0 development checkout
- Latest stable / Insiders: Not yet tested. Latest stable is 1.140.0 at reporting time. The affected `stoppedDetails` push/filter logic is also present in upstream `main` at `d547327fc4b6721ccf340c95b73bd6bffd708a78`; this is a source check, not a claim of reproduction on that build.

### Steps to reproduce (observed)

1. Start a single-thread debug session that initially stops, then resumes and quickly hits an entry-point breakpoint (`main` in our case).
2. Inspect the Call Stack after the entry-point breakpoint is hit.
3. Stop and start the session again if needed; the problem is intermittent.

**Expected:** The Call Stack shows "Paused on breakpoint" when the target stops at the breakpoint.

**Actual:** The target is paused at `main`, and the stack frame/source location are correct, but the Call Stack pause-reason header is absent. There is no subsequent `continued` event in the failing session.

### Captured workbench evidence

These are JSON snapshots from DevTools logpoints in the failing session, in execution order. `JSON.stringify` was used so these are not lazily evaluated object references.

Immediately before `this.stoppedDetails.push(event)` in `DebugSession.handleStop`:

```json
{"point":"stop-before-push","incoming":{"allThreadsStopped":true,"hitBreakpointIds":[1],"preserveFocusHint":false,"reason":"breakpoint","threadId":2},"existing":[{"preserveFocusHint":false,"reason":"stopped","threadId":2}]}
```

Immediately before the continued-event handler's `stoppedDetails.filter`, with `remaining` calculated using that same filter:

```json
{"point":"continued-cleanup","threadId":2,"before":[{"preserveFocusHint":false,"reason":"stopped","threadId":2},{"allThreadsStopped":true,"hitBreakpointIds":[1],"preserveFocusHint":false,"reason":"breakpoint","threadId":2}],"remaining":[]}
```

The older continued-event cleanup therefore removes the newer breakpoint-stop record as well as the initial stop record.

Adapter logs independently show this order:

```text
stopped   {"preserveFocusHint":false,"reason":"stopped","threadId":2}
continued {"threadId":2}
stopped   {"allThreadsStopped":true,"hitBreakpointIds":[1],"preserveFocusHint":false,"reason":"breakpoint","threadId":2}
threads responses: thread 2 is present
stackTrace responses: top frame is main, line 26
```

### Small regression-test scenario (no Arm target required)

The observed ordering suggests this focused test with a fake debug adapter:

1. Establish thread 2 and its initial stopped state.
2. Deliver `continued` for thread 2 and let its cleanup be scheduled but not executed yet.
3. Deliver the breakpoint `stopped` event above, allowing `handleStop` to append the new record.
4. Allow the earlier continued cleanup to execute before the new stop's asynchronous thread lookup completes; then resolve that lookup with thread 2 and a valid stack frame.
5. Assert that the thread is stopped **and** `session.getStoppedDetails()?.reason` is `"breakpoint"`.

This is a proposed deterministic regression test, not a standalone full-workbench reproduction we have already run. The real-session logpoints above confirm the record-removal ordering.

### Relevant source

- Continued cleanup: [`debugSession.ts`, line 1153](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/debugSession.ts#L1153)
- New stop is recorded before asynchronous thread lookup: [`debugSession.ts`, line 1353](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/debugSession.ts#L1353)
- Scheduler awaits thread IDs before applying cleanup: [`debugSession.ts`, line 1634](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/debugSession.ts#L1634)
- Single-thread Call Stack header reads session stop details and hides when absent: [`callStackView.ts`, line 187](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/callStackView.ts#L187)

It appears the continued cleanup needs to invalidate only the older stop state, without removing a stop received after that continued event. No raw debugger logs, local file paths, or target binaries are needed to demonstrate the captured state mutation.

- VS Code Version: current `main` (`d547327fc4b6721ccf340c95b73bd6bffd708a78`)
- OS Version: macOS

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open the Agents Window and create a custom session group.
2. Use the **New Session** action on that custom group's header.
3. Select a workspace if needed, enter a prompt, and send it.
4. Observe where the newly created session appears in the Sessions list.

**Expected:**

The new session is placed in, and remains in, the custom group from which it was created.

**Actual:**

The new session appears outside the custom group under the normal workspace/date grouping instead of retaining the selected custom-group placement.

## Suspected regression

This appears to have been exposed by `dd3b04daa8a3dfaa41bafec47ac0b381b0521e1d` (#337741), specifically the change that publishes in-flight new sessions through `ISessionsManagementService.getSessions()` and fires `onDidChangeSessions` for the provisional session.

The custom-group intent is currently captured by `SessionGroupsService` on `onWillSendRequest`, but durable membership is not applied until `onDidStartSession`. Publishing the provisional session before that point lets the Sessions list place it using the normal workspace/date rules. There is no integration test covering custom-group placement during this new provisional-publication interval.

- `src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/browser/sessionGroupsService.ts`: pending/in-flight group handling

issues.title: Code Review: Session Timeout Handler - Edge Case Analysis
issues.body:
## PR Review: Game Session Timeout Handler
**Reviewer:** Data Cohen, Senior Software Engineer
**Author:** Chunk Cohen
**Repository:** athena-casino-platform
**Focus:** Edge case handling around session limit enforcement

---

### Overview

Thanks for the PR, Chunk. I've done a thorough pass focusing on the session limit enforcement logic - there are some solid patterns here, but a few architectural concerns and edge cases we should address before merging. Let me walk through my findings systematically.

---

### Architecture Concerns

**[CRITICAL] Race condition in session limit check**

```python
# Current implementation (problematic)
def enforce_session_limit(user_id, max_sessions=3):
    active_sessions = db.query_active_sessions(user_id)  # READ
    if len(active_sessions) >= max_sessions:
        raise SessionLimitExceeded()
    session = create_new_session(user_id)  # WRITE
    return session
```

The read-check-write pattern here is a classic TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) race condition. If two requests arrive simultaneously, both could pass the `len(active_sessions) >= max_sessions` check before either creates a session. In a gaming context with concurrent connections, this *will* happen under load.

**Suggested fix:** Use a database-level atomic operation or distributed lock:

```python
def enforce_session_limit(user_id, max_sessions=3):
    with distributed_lock(f'session_limit:{user_id}', timeout=5):
        active_sessions = db.query_active_sessions(user_id)
        if len(active_sessions) >= max_sessions:
            raise SessionLimitExceeded(
                current_count=len(active_sessions),
                limit=max_sessions
            )
        session = create_new_session(user_id)
    return session
```

Alternatively, a database-level `INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ?) < ?` with proper transaction isolation would be even cleaner.

---

### Edge Case Issues

**[HIGH] Expired sessions not excluded from limit count**

What happens when a session exists in the DB but the timeout has already elapsed? If `query_active_sessions()` doesn't filter on `last_activity_at + timeout_duration > NOW()`, you'll block users who technicallyve active sessions - they just have stale records pending cleanup.

This is especially problematic during the cleanup grace period. A user could be locked out even though all their sessions have timed out.

**[HIGH] Timeout handler not idempotent**

If the timeout job fires twice for the same session (network retry, scheduler quirk), does it handle that gracefully? I don't see any guard against:
- Double-expiry events
- - Expiring an already-expired session
- - - The audit log getting duplicate entries
Idempotency is non-negotiable for timeout handlers. Add a check:

```python
def expire_session(session_id):
    session = db.get_session(session_id)
    if session is None or session.status == SessionStatus.EXPIRED:
        logger.info(f'Session {session_id} already expired or not found - skipping')
        return  # Idempotent - already done
    # ... proceed with expiry
```

**[MEDIUM] No handling for sessions crossing midnight/DST boundaries**

Game sessions that span daylight saving time transitions could have incorrect timeout calculations if using `datetime.now()` without timezone awareness. Use `datetime.utcnow()` or `datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)` consistently throughout.

---

### Security Concerns

**[HIGH] Session tokens not invalidated server-side on timeout**

Are session tokens being invalidated in the token store (Redis/DB) when a session times out, or just marked as expired? A user with a token that's marked 'expired' in the DB but still valid in the token validation cache could continue making authenticated requests for the duration of the cache TTL.

For a gambling platform, this is a compliance risk - session limits exist for regulatory reasons.

**[MEDIUM] Session limit bypass via rapid reconnection**

If the session cleanup is asynchronous (batch job vs. real-time), is there a window where a user could disconnect-reconnect rapidly and create more sessions than the limit allows? Need a synchronous limit check *at connection time*, not just relying on the cleanup job.

---

### Error Handling

**[MEDIUM] Overly broad exception catching**

```python
# What I'm seeing (pattern to avoid)
try:
    session = create_session(user_id)
except Exception as e:
    log.error(f'Failed: {e}')
    return None  # <- Silently returns None?
```

Returning `None` on failure is dangerous - callers have to remember to null-check. Prefer:
1. Raise specific, typed exceptions (`SessionCreationError`, `SessionLimitExceeded`)
2. 2. Let them propagate to a centralized error handler
3. 3. Never swallow exceptions silently in security-critical code paths
**[LOW] Missing structured logging context**

For compliance auditing, session lifecycle events need structured fields:

```python
logger.info('session_expired', extra={
    'session_id': session_id,
    'user_id': session.user_id,
    'duration_seconds': elapsed,
    'expiry_reason': 'timeout',
    'ip_address': session.ip_address
})
```

---

### Code Quality

**[LOW] Magic numbers need constants**

I see `3`, `1800`, `300` scattered through the timeout logic. These should be:

```python
class SessionConfig:
    MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS = 3
    SESSION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800  # 30 minutes
    INACTIVITY_WARNING_SECONDS = 300  # 5 min warning
```

**[LOW] Missing type hints**

For a codebase this critical, type hints + mypy would catch a class of bugs at dev time rather than prod. Worth the investment.

---

### What's Working Well

- The session activity heartbeat mechanism looks solid
- - Separation of timeout detection vs. cleanup is a good architectural call
- - - Test coverage on the happy path is good
---

### Summary

The TOCTOU race condition and the server-side token invalidation gap are the two items I'd consider blockers for merge - especially given the regulatory context of session limits in gaming. The others are important but could be tracked as follow-up issues.

Happy to pair on the distributed lock implementation if that's new territory. It's a really common pattern once you've done it once, and the athena-casino-platform is going to see enough concurrent load that it matters.

Good work overall on the structure - the timeout handler architecture is clean. These edge cases are the hard part of session management, and they're easy to miss.
