issues.title: Dictation cleanup: allow any chat model available to the user/organization instead of a hard-coded model ID

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

milestone.title: Backlog Candidates
milestone.description: Work that is not yet accepted for the Backlog. We wait for the community to weigh in.

issues.body:
**Use case**
In organizations on Copilot Business/Enterprise, admins decide which models are available, and users only get that subset. Dictation cleanup, however, can only use one hard-coded "good" model (`gpt-5.6-luna`). If that model is not offered to an organization, every user there silently falls back to `copilot-utility-small`. There is no way to choose another model that the organization *does* allow and that the same user already uses in chat every day.

**What happened to us**
Between 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-28, dictation cleanup stopped using Luna, although `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` is still `gpt-5.6-luna`. `gpt-5.6-luna` is no longer offered to my account/organization (Copilot Business). Our model list now contains `gpt-6-luna` instead. I cannot tell whether the model was retired globally or is just not enabled for our organization. Either way, the result for the user is the same.

```
[chat-stt] selecting language model cleanup model (vendor=copilot, id=gpt-5.6-luna)
[chat-stt] gpt-5.6-luna cleanup model unavailable; falling back to copilot-utility-small
[chat-stt] applied language model cleanup (model=copilot-utility-small, ...)
```

**Why settings cannot fix it:** `gpt-5.6-luna` is hard-coded in three places:
- the setting enum (`auto | copilot-utility-small | gpt-5.6-luna`)
- `LLM_CLEANUP_LUNA_MODEL_ID` in `chatSpeechToTextService.ts`
- the Copilot alias `copilot-dictation-cleanup-luna`, which resolves the CAPI family `gpt-5.6-luna`

Any other value is silently replaced with `copilot-utility-small`.

**Request:** allow `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` to take the ID of any chat model that is user-selectable for the current user, i.e. what their organization has enabled, for example `gpt-6-luna`. From #332969 I understand that the dedicated cleanup aliases are intentionally core-only. This request leaves them as they are. It only asks to accept models the user is already allowed to use in chat. This would also respect organization model policies by design, and model retirements would no longer need a code change.

**Nice to have:** when the configured model is unavailable, show a visible hint, not only an info line in the log.

**Environment:** VS Code 1.139.1 (04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1), built-in Copilot extension 0.67.0, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Copilot Business, `dictation.model` = Nemotron (local), `agents.voice.language` = `de`.

issues.body:
### Summary
:rotating_light: New regression detected: `layoutDurationMs` increased by 26.5% in the *text-only* scenario and 33.0% in the *tool-terminal* scenario, both well outside the baseline window's normal spread.

### Evidence
- *text-only*: Baseline 113.96ms ±4.4ms → Current 144.13ms ±3.15ms (+30.17ms, +26.5%)
- *tool-terminal*: Baseline 167.28ms ±1.96ms → Current 222.56ms ±10.84ms (+55.28ms, +33.0%)
- Both metrics were stable in the last 3 baselines (no prior runs near these values).
- No open tracking issue or prior Slack thread covers this regression in these scenarios.

#### Trend (last 3 runs):
- *text-only* layoutDurationMs: 166.3ms → 140.9ms → 144.1ms (current)
- *tool-terminal* layoutDurationMs: 230.8ms → 188.5ms → 222.6ms (current)

### Suspect Commits
- The regression appears after a large set of agent host and chat-related changes, especially `bf87d75` ("Merge pull request #330566 from microsoft/connor4312/agents-enablement-2"), which touched chat session, layout, and agent host logic.

### Suggested Action
- Investigate recent changes to chat layout/session/agent host logic, especially in `bf87d75` and related commits.
- Profile layoutDurationMs in the affected scenarios to identify the cause of the increased layout time.
- Consider reverting or optimizing the relevant changes if a root cause is confirmed.

issues.title: Insiders 1.141.0 .deb: chrome-sandbox lost setuid bit, app aborts with SUID sandbox FATAL on Ubuntu
issues.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (crash happens before any extension loads)

- VS Code Version: Insiders 1.141.0 (`1.141.0-1790789516`, commit `0d30d69c8e18b8413dd7292edb51a30cda1403fb`; also `1.141.0-1790832227`)
- OS Version: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic, `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`
- Package: `.deb` from packages.microsoft.com

## Problem

After updating to Insiders 1.141.0 via apt, `code-insiders` exits immediately:

```
FATAL:sandbox/linux/suid/client/setuid_sandbox_host.cc:166] The SUID sandbox helper binary was found, but is not configured correctly. Rather than run without sandboxing I'm aborting now. You need to make sure that /usr/share/code-insiders/chrome-sandbox is owned by root and has mode 4755.
```

## Regression: the setuid bit is missing from `chrome-sandbox` inside the 1.141.0 .deb

Comparing the packages in `/var/cache/apt/archives` with `dpkg-deb -c <pkg> | grep chrome-sandbox`:

| Package | chrome-sandbox mode in .deb |
|---|---|
| code 1.139.1-1790309529 | `-rwsr-xr-x` ✅ |
| code 1.140.0-1790759618 | `-rwsr-xr-x` ✅ |
| code-insiders 1.140.0-1790583587 | `-rwsr-xr-x` ✅ |
| code-insiders 1.140.0-1790633624 | `-rwsr-xr-x` ✅ |
| code-insiders 1.140.0-1790715083 (commit b6c7324ced) | `-rwsr-xr-x` ✅ |
| code-insiders 1.141.0-1790789516 (commit 0d30d69c8e) | `-rwxr-xr-x` ❌ |
| code-insiders 1.141.0-1790832227 | `-rwxr-xr-x` ❌ |

On Ubuntu with `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, Ubuntu's `apparmor` package only ships a userns profile for stable (`/etc/apparmor.d/code` → `/usr/share/code/code`), so Insiders falls back to the SUID sandbox and aborts.

## Suspected cause

The range `b6c7324ced...0d30d69c8e` includes da67ddb87d "Engineering - decompose Linux stage" (#338552). After that change, the package job gets the client build by downloading the `compilation_linux_$(VSCODE_ARCH)` artifact and running `tar -xzf builds.tar.gz` (`product-build-linux-download-compilation.yml`) instead of packaging the in-job build directory. Non-root GNU tar does not restore setuid bits by default, and the deb build (`gulpfile.vscode.linux.ts`, `fakeroot dpkg-deb`) takes file modes as-is, with no `postinst` fixup. The rpm spec sets `%attr(4755, root, root)` explicitly, so the rpm is probably not affected.

I haven't verified this against the CI logs; it's inferred from the commit range and the pipeline files. If it isn't fixed, stable 1.141 will likely ship with the same problem.

## Workarounds

- `sudo chmod 4755 /usr/share/code-insiders/chrome-sandbox` (lost again on every update), or
- add an AppArmor profile for Insiders, mirroring the stable one:

```
abi <abi/5.0>,
include <tunables/global>

profile code-insiders /usr/share/code-insiders{/bin,}/code-insiders flags=(unconfined) {
  userns,
  include if exists <local/code-insiders>
}
```

issues.title: Codex conversation repeatedly locks after every laptop sleep and Remote SSH reconnect
issues.body:
**Environment**

- VS Code 1.139.1
- Linux remote host accessed through Remote SSH
- Codex extension: `openai.chatgpt` 26.917.62051

**Reproduction**

This happens every time I follow this sequence:

1. Use a Codex conversation in a Remote SSH workspace.
2. Close my laptop.
3. Reopen the laptop and reconnect to the remote workspace.
4. Try to continue the same conversation.

**Actual behavior**

The conversation is blocked by:

> This is open in another app. Close it there to continue here.

From my perspective, I am returning to the same workspace and conversation—not intentionally opening another concurrent session. The message does not identify the owning window or provide a way to recover ownership. Normal laptop sleep and reconnection repeatedly require manual process cleanup.

**Diagnostic evidence**

After reconnection, two separate VS Code extension hosts have Codex `app-server` processes on the remote machine. The older server retains a kernel `FLOCK` on:

```text
~/.codex/thread-writer-locks/<redacted>.lock
```

The newer server cannot resume the conversation:

```text
codex_core::session: Failed to create session:
thread-store conflict: thread <redacted> already has an active writer

method: thread/resume
error code: -32600
message: thread <redacted> already has an active writer
```

On September 29, we confirmed that the older server’s recorded tasks had completed, then terminated only that Codex server. This released the locks. The issue returned September 30, with another older server holding the conversation lock.

These observations suggest that conversation ownership is not recovering properly across disconnect/reconnect cycles. They do not establish whether the underlying defect is in VS Code’s extension-host lifecycle or Codex’s ownership management.

**Expected behavior**

Laptop sleep, network interruption, and Remote SSH reconnection should be handled automatically and robustly:

- Reattach to the existing session when possible.
- Distinguish a disconnected client from a genuinely active competing client; a surviving server process alone should not leave the user permanently blocked.
- Safely recover ownership when the prior client is gone, while preserving running work and preventing concurrent writers.
- If automatic recovery is unsafe, identify the owning session and offer an explicit recovery or takeover action with clear consequences.
- Make **Retry** re-evaluate ownership and recover when possible.

Users should not need to find and terminate remote processes after every laptop sleep. The current workaround is disruptive and risks interrupting legitimate work.

**Routing**

The banner and backend error originate in Codex. Please investigate whether VS Code’s Remote SSH/extension-host lifecycle contributes, or route this to the Codex extension maintainers if appropriate.

issues.title: xtension host crashes (0xC0000409) after Copilot Chat activates; Copilot CLI fails with "HW capability requested" on CPU without AVX-512 (i5-12500H)
issues.body:
**Title:** Extension host crashes (0xC0000409) after Copilot Chat activates; Copilot CLI fails with "HW capability requested" on CPU without AVX-512 (i5-12500H)

## Description
The Copilot CLI server (AgentHost) fails at every VS Code start on my machine with:

`Fatal Error: HW capability found: 0xFFCBFBFF 0xFFFAF38B, but HW capability requested: 0x200000 0x00.`

and exits with code 3221226505 (0xC0000409). This alone does not break VS Code: the extension host stays stable for minutes. But once GitHub Copilot Chat activates (after signing in with GitHub), the extension host itself crashes with the same exit code, in a loop ("Extension host terminated unexpectedly 3 times within the last 5 minutes"). Code Runner and other extensions then stop working.

I suspect the bundled Copilot CLI binary requires a CPU feature (possibly AVX-512) that my processor lacks. I cannot confirm whether the host crash is caused by that same requirement, but the exit code is identical and the timing matches Copilot Chat activation.

## Environment
- VS Code: 1.140.0 (commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74, x64), user installer
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.68.0
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, build 26200, 64-bit
- CPU: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12500H (Alder Lake)
- AVX2: present. AVX-512F: not present (IsProcessorFeaturePresent)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Fresh install of VS Code (removed %APPDATA%\Code and %USERPROFILE%\.vscode), only Code Runner installed, not signed in.
2. Extension host is stable, but agenthost.log already shows the CLI server failing with the HW capability error.
3. Sign in with GitHub.
4. GitHub.copilot-chat activates (`onStartupFinished`, then `onChatSession:copilotcli`) and the extension host crashes within ~2 seconds, repeatedly.

## Expected behavior
The extension host should not crash. If the Copilot CLI cannot run on this CPU, it should fail gracefully or ship a compatible binary.

## Logs
agenthost.log:
```
[info] [Copilot] Client unavailable while listing chats to migrate: CLI server exited with code 3221226505
stderr: Fatal Error: HW capability found: 0xFFCBFBFF 0xFFFAF38B, but HW capability requested: 0x200000 0x00.
```
main.log:
```
[info] Extension host with pid 10556 exited with code: 3221226505, signal: unknown.
[error] [UtilityProcess id: 1, type: extensionHost, pid: 10556]: crashed with code -1073740791 and reason 'crashed'
```
renderer.log:
```
[error] Extension host (LocalProcess pid: 10556) terminated unexpectedly. The following extensions were running: ... GitHub.copilot-chat, vscode.microsoft-authentication
```
The GitHub.copilot-chat output log file is empty (0 bytes).

## Workaround
`code --disable-extension GitHub.copilot-chat`, or `"chat.disableAIFeatures": true` in settings.json.

issues.title: Crash reports on Windows include the full process environment (incl. user env-var secrets); please document this and revisit the default
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Summary

On Windows, the Crashpad minidumps that VS Code uploads contain the whole environment block of the crashed process. Anything a user keeps in User environment variables, such as API keys and tokens, can therefore be sent with a crash report. Crash reporting is on by default (`telemetry.telemetryLevel: all`). The telemetry docs do not mention this, and an older, still-published instruction for turning crash reporting off (`enable-crash-reporter` in `argv.json`) is silently rewritten after one launch.

The capture itself happens in Crashpad; this issue covers the parts that belong to VS Code.

I searched this repo and found no existing issue about the environment block in crash dumps. Related but different: #107945 (2020, `enable-crash-reporter: false` not honoured, closed) and #159775 (the 2022 change discussed below).

## What I observed

- Source of the capture: Crashpad always adds the PEB environment block to the minidump on Windows. https://github.com/chromium/crashpad/blob/ce308a86daa85e65df219ff5fb385095b0a1c467/snapshot/win/process_snapshot_win.cc#L439-L442
- On one developer workstation with default telemetry, Code's local Crashpad database recorded crash reports as uploaded, each with a server report ID. Crashpad sets that mark only after an HTTP 200-203 response. The configured destination was App Center (`appcenter://`; `in.appcenter.ms` is in Code.exe). Every dump in that set contained the environment block (I checked this with a variable that is not a secret), and the dumps from one day also contained multiple API keys and tokens taken from the user's User environment variables. I have not seen the server side, and I withhold names, counts and services.
- These dumps confirm that shipped builds behave as the source says. If you want to check it yourself, in outline: use a throwaway environment that holds no real secrets, clear the environment before launch and set only a canary variable, disable crash uploads before crashing the process, then search the local dump for the canary.
- **Safety:** if you try this, do it in a disposable user account or VM whose environment holds nothing real, and turn uploads off first. Treat any dump produced during the test as something that could be uploaded.

## Requests

1. **Document what a crash report contains, where it goes, and how long it is kept.** https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/telemetry says crash reports "collect diagnostic information" and that there are "valid data retention policies ... for example crash dumps". Please state that on Windows the minidump includes the process environment variables, name the destination (App Center), and give the retention period. For comparison, App Center's retirement page says Analytics & Diagnostics runs until the end of March 2027 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/appcenter/retirement), Mozilla lets only people who have been granted access view minidumps, and they agree to delete a dump (within 30 days) when finished with it (https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/documentation/protected_data_access/), and the Edge privacy whitepaper says crash dumps are kept on Microsoft servers for up to 30 days (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/privacy-whitepaper/).

2. **Fix the instructions for turning crash reporting off.**
   - First, fix the comment that VS Code writes into the generated `argv.json`: "Allows to disable crash reporting." Changing that value by hand does not keep crash reporting disabled, because the value is overwritten from the telemetry level.
   - Since #159775 (2022-09, "More tightly couple crash reporter and telemetry level"), `updateCrashReporterEnablement()` in `src/vs/code/electron-main/app.ts` writes `enable-crash-reporter` as `telemetryLevel >= TelemetryLevel.CRASH`. As a result, `"enable-crash-reporter": false` set by hand is silently rewritten after one launch unless `telemetry.telemetryLevel` is `off`.
     https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/11e39c07900133ada310c017b2e72fc86ce8d014/src/vs/code/electron-main/app.ts#L1846-L1890
   - The first launch after changing only `telemetry.telemetryLevel` to `off` still has crash reporting on. `src/main.ts` reads `argv.json` and starts the crash reporter before `app.ready`, but `argv.json` is written back only later, from `afterWindowOpen()`. So users need both settings, followed by a restart.
     https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/11e39c07900133ada310c017b2e72fc86ce8d014/src/main.ts#L85-L98
   - The 1.49 release notes (https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_49) say crash reporting is controlled by the `enable-crash-reporter` runtime argument, while the FAQ (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/supporting/faq, "How to disable crash reporting") points to `telemetry.telemetryLevel`. Please add a note to the 1.49 notes that points to the current method, and mention the first-launch gap in the FAQ.

   The documentation parts of 1 and 2 can be moved to microsoft/vscode-docs if that is a better place.

3. **Revisit the default.** Some options: keep uploading crash metadata by default but upload the minidump only after a clear opt-in; or, once Crashpad offers it, exclude the environment block or allowlist variable names.
   For comparison, a user report on OpenAI's Codex desktop app (also Electron) shows the Sentry scope tag `minidumpAttachmentUploadEnabled: false` (openai/codex#46808).

## Workaround for users (today)

- Set `"telemetry.telemetryLevel": "off"` in `settings.json` **and** `"enable-crash-reporter": false` in `argv.json`, then restart VS Code. Setting only `argv.json` is rewritten after one launch; setting only `settings.json` leaves crash reporting on for one more launch.
- Delete the existing dumps under `%APPDATA%\Code\Crashpad`. Dumps written before the change still hold the old environment values.
- Avoid keeping long-lived secrets in User environment variables. Inject them only into the process that needs them, for example with a secret manager's `run` wrapper.

## Notes

- I have not verified what App Center keeps on its side or for how long.
- Every dump the crash reporter writes on Windows contains the environment block. The telemetry level decides whether the crash reporter runs at all (`src/main.ts` calls `configureCrashReporter()` only when `enable-crash-reporter` is true or `--crash-reporter-directory` is given); when it runs, dumps are uploaded unless VS Code was started with `--crash-reporter-directory`.

issues.title: Automations: let an automation stop after an end date

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

labels.name: automations
labels.description: Issue for the sessions window automation feature

issues.body:
Telling an automation to stop itself is inherently non-deterministic. We should support automations stopping by a specified date so users can be confident that an overnight automation will stop exactly when it's told to.

The end date condition was added to the agent host protocol in microsoft/agent-host-protocol#461.

Implemented in #337847.

issues.title: Copilot coding agent cannot run commands in an already open terminal session and always creates a new terminal context
issues.body:
Type: Bug Summary When using the Copilot coding agent in Visual Studio Code, command execution does not attach to an already open terminal session. Instead, it creates a separate terminal execution context. This breaks workflows that must stay in one live terminal. Environment Visual Studio Code version: [fill in] GitHub Copilot extension version: [fill in] GitHub Copilot Chat extension version: [fill in] Operating system: Linux Remote mode: [Local or WSL or SSH, fill in] Workspace type: Multi-repository workspace Problem I have one terminal session already open and in use. I ask Copilot coding agent to run a command. Copilot runs the command in a different terminal context instead of the already open one. This behavior breaks strict single-terminal workflows and interactive hardware flows where continuity in one exact terminal session is required. Expected Behavior Copilot should allow selecting an existing terminal and running commands in that exact terminal. Copilot should support a setting or mode to force reuse of one terminal. Copilot should not create a new terminal execution context when an explicit existing session is required. Actual Behavior Copilot command execution creates a separate terminal execution context. Copilot cannot target the user’s already open interactive terminal session. Workflow continuity is broken for long-running interactive tasks. Reproduction Steps Open Visual Studio Code. Open an integrated terminal and run any command so the session is clearly active. In Copilot Chat, request a command run, for example: cd /home/cornelius/KYANITE/tools/ci && ./test_boot_phase_1_firmware_security.py Observe that Copilot executes in a different terminal context instead of the already open terminal session. Frequency Always reproducible in my setup. Impact Breaks single-terminal workflow discipline. Interferes with interactive command sequences and hardware test flows. Causes context fragmentation and operator confusion. Why this matters Some workflows require one continuous terminal session for correctness, auditability, and operator safety. If agent execution cannot reuse that session, the coding agent is not safe for those workflows. Requested Fix Add ability to run commands in a specific existing terminal tab. Add a user setting to enforce terminal reuse only. Add a visible warning and cancel option if Copilot is about to open a different terminal context while reuse-only mode is enabled. Diagnostics to include Screenshot or short recording showing: Existing terminal already open Copilot command creates separate terminal context Output panel logs: GitHub Copilot GitHub Copilot Chat Extension Host Additional Notes This is not a shell script issue. The issue is at Copilot agent command execution routing layer, where execution context is not attachable to an existing user terminal session. issues.title: Claude Agent native model picker should show the concrete model version behind aliases such as `Opus`
issues.body:
## Claude Agent native model picker should show the concrete model version behind aliases such as `Opus`

### VS Code version

```text
Version: 1.140.0
Commit: 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74
Date: 2026-09-30T10:38:38+02:00
Electron: 43.7.3
ElectronBuildId: 15386805
Chromium: 150.0.7871.250
Node.js: 24.21.0
V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0
@github/copilot: 1.0.89-7
@github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.15-preview.4
OS: Darwin arm64 25.5.0
```

### Summary

When using the Claude Agent harness with native Anthropic authentication, the Anthropic model group exposes models using unversioned Claude Code aliases:

```text
Anthropic

Fable
Haiku
Opus
Opus (1M context)
Sonnet
```

This makes it impossible from the VS Code UI to determine which concrete model version will actually serve the request.

For example, the Claude Agent SDK bundled with VS Code 1.140.0 is `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.281, which is at parity with Claude Code 2.1.281. In Claude Code 2.1.280, Anthropic changed the default Opus model to Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`).

Therefore the picker entry:

```text
Opus
```

currently means Claude Opus 5.5, but there is no indication of that in the VS Code UI.

This is particularly confusing because the Copilot-backed models shown by the same Claude harness are explicitly versioned, for example:

```text
Claude Fable 5.1
Claude Fable 5
Claude Opus 5
Claude Sonnet 5
Claude Haiku 4.5
```

So the picker can contain both:

```text
Anthropic → Opus
Copilot   → Claude Opus 5
```

without explaining that the Anthropic `Opus` entry currently resolves to a different concrete model, namely Opus 5.5.

### Authentication / model discovery evidence

Native Anthropic authentication is working correctly in this case:

```text
[Claude] Native account check: setUp=true, provider=firstParty, tokenSource=CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, apiKeySource=absent
```

The native catalog is then published using the unversioned names:

```text
[Claude] Models refreshed (merged). Count: 5, Sonnet, Fable, Opus, Haiku, Opus (1M context)
```

After Copilot authentication completes, the merged catalog becomes:

```text
[Copilot] Found 13 models: Auto, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Haiku 4.5, ...

[Claude] Models refreshed (merged). Count: 10, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet, Fable, Opus, Haiku, Opus (1M context)
```

### Expected behavior

The alias semantics should ideally be preserved, since aliases such as `opus` are intentionally moving targets.

However, VS Code should also show the concrete model that the alias currently resolves to.

For example, the picker could display:

```text
Opus
Currently resolves to Claude Opus 5.5
```

or:

```text
Opus (5.5)
```

A hover/details view could expose both values explicitly:

```text
Selector: opus
Resolved model: claude-opus-5-5
```

The important part is that users should be able to tell which concrete model version will actually serve the request without inspecting the Claude transcript manually.

### Why keeping both alias and resolved model matters

Simply renaming `Opus` to `Claude Opus 5.5` would lose useful information.

`opus` is a moving Claude Code selector. Anthropic can change which concrete model it resolves to in a future Claude Code / Agent SDK version.

So ideally VS Code should expose both:

- the selected alias (`opus`)
- its current concrete resolution (`claude-opus-5-5`)

That would make it clear whether a user selected a moving alias or a fixed model ID.

### Relevant VS Code implementation

The native Claude model projection currently takes the SDK's `ModelInfo` essentially as follows:

```ts
export function fromSdkModelInfo(m: ModelInfo, provider: AgentProvider): IAgentModelInfo {
    return {
        provider,
        id: m.value,
        name: m.displayName,
        supportsVision: false,
        ...
    };
}
```

So the SDK-provided display name such as `Opus` becomes the picker label directly.

File:

```text
src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeAgent.ts
```

The same file already references `ModelInfo.resolvedModel` when discussing the SDK's synthetic `default` model:

```ts
/**
 * Whether `m` is the SDK's SDK_DEFAULT_MODEL_VALUE alias rather than a
 * real model. The alias resolves to a concrete model (`ModelInfo.resolvedModel`)
 * ...
 */
```

If `resolvedModel` is populated for family aliases such as `opus`, it seems like that information could potentially be projected into the model metadata used by the picker.

If the SDK does not expose the concrete resolution at catalog-enumeration time, it would still be useful to show the actual resolved model after a turn, since the concrete model ID is present in the Claude transcript / turn metadata.

### Related issue

Possibly related, but not a duplicate:

- #337653 — Claude agent host: model picker shows the first native model after restart while turns still run on the saved model

That issue also demonstrates that the displayed native Claude model label and the concrete model actually serving the request can diverge.

### Requested improvement

Please expose the concrete model version behind native Anthropic aliases such as `Opus`, `Sonnet`, `Fable`, and `Haiku` in the model picker or its hover/details UI while preserving the alias itself.

issues.title: Notify when sandboxing dependencies are not present for windows

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
### Problem

When sandboxing is enabled on Windows but the host lacks the required sandboxing support or dependencies, the Agent Host chat input does not show the SDK's explanation. Sandbox diagnostics are currently gated to Linux, so Windows users do not get the existing warning or remediation guidance.

For example, the SDK can report that PowerShell sandboxing requires Process Security Environment 1.1 filesystem enumeration support and provide https://aka.ms/ghcp-sandbox-os-support.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an Agent Host Copilot session on a Windows host that the SDK reports as unsupported for sandboxing.
2. Enable Windows sandboxing and send a message to initialize the session.
3. Observe the chat input notifications.

### Expected behavior

Show the session-scoped "Sandboxing is unavailable in this environment" warning with the SDK's explanation. The warning text should be selectable/copyable, and HTTP/HTTPS remediation URLs should be clickable with mouse and keyboard.

### Actual behavior

The Linux-only diagnostic gate suppresses the warning on Windows.

### Scope

Keep existing sandbox enforcement, session scoping, dismissal, and custom-terminal behavior. Showing a warning in the empty new-session composer before SDK session initialization is a separate follow-up.

issues.title: Agents: support additional skill folders
issues.body:
# Agents: support additional skill folders (reuse VS Code's `chat.agentSkillsLocations`)

## Current behavior

- VS Code finds skills from all configured extra folders.
- **Agents** app ignores those folders. The same skills don't show up there, even though VS Code shows them.

## Expected behavior

- By default, Agents App uses the **same skill folders as VS Code**. It reads `chat.agentSkillsLocations` from the user settings, and from workspace settings where they apply.
- If there are separate settings, they should be optional overrides. The default should be the VS Code setting.

## Why this matters

- the possibility to enable additional folders in VS Code is extremely helpful!
- In Agens App ,with the current behavior, skills have to be copied or configured twice, and the two copies drift apart.
- Users expect a skill that works in VS Code to also work in Agents.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A skill in a folder listed in `chat.agentSkillsLocations` shows up in Agents without any extra setup.
2. (optional) Agents can show which folders it loaded skills from, so users can troubleshoot missing skills.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- VS Code: 1.140.0

issues.title: Delegate Copilot plugin installation to the Copilot SDK

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Problem

The Chat Customizations UI currently installs Copilot plugins through VS Code's `IPluginInstallService`, while Agent Host `/plugin` commands use the Copilot SDK's `session.rpc.plugins` API.

This creates two independent plugin inventories and two implementations of source parsing, repository cloning, manifest validation, persistence, update, and uninstall behavior.

For example:

1. Install the `dotnet` plugin from the Chat Customizations UI.
2. The plugin is recorded in VS Code's `agent-plugins/installed.json` and becomes available as a session customization.
3. Completion suggests `dotnet` for `/plugin uninstall` because it sees the VS Code customization.
4. `/plugin uninstall dotnet` calls `session.rpc.plugins.uninstall({ name: 'dotnet' })`.
5. The SDK responds that plugin `dotnet` is not installed because it is absent from the SDK's installed-plugin inventory.

The same split prevents `/plugin list`, enablement, update, and uninstall from consistently reflecting plugins installed through the customization UI.

## Proposal

For Copilot plugins, make the Copilot SDK the canonical owner of plugin installation state and mutations. The customization UI should retain responsibility for catalog browsing, confirmation/trust UI, progress, accessibility, and error presentation, but delegate the actual operation to the SDK:

- `plugins.install`
- `plugins.uninstall`
- `plugins.update`
- `plugins.enable` / `plugins.disable`
- marketplace operations where applicable

Do not add synchronization between two persistent installation databases as the long-term solution.

Because the SDK API is currently session-scoped while the customization UI can operate without an active Agent Host session, introduce a provider-facing plugin-management boundary that can acquire the correct SDK context, preserve account/policy/configuration context, perform the mutation, and refresh affected Agent Host sessions.

Non-Copilot providers without a provider-owned plugin API can continue using a separate implementation where necessary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Plugins installed from the customization UI appear in the SDK's authoritative plugin inventory.
- `/plugin list`, completion, enablement, update, and uninstall use the same inventory as the customization UI.
- Installing a plugin in the UI and then running `/plugin uninstall <name>` succeeds.
- Account, managed-policy, working-directory, remote, and profile context are preserved.
- Active Agent Host sessions refresh after plugin mutations.
- The UI exposes delayed, accessible progress and actionable SDK errors.
- Existing VS Code-installed Copilot plugins have a migration path to SDK-owned state.

## Description

The customization migration banner in the editor window chat panel should be reconsidered and redesigned.

When switching workspaces, the banner can flicker in and out as migration availability changes for the selected workspace. It can also stack with the new harness banner, resulting in a banner-heavy experience.

The customization migration message is intended to communicate a needs-attention state rather than a did-you-know message, so its treatment may appropriately differ from other informational banners.

issues.title: Emojis disappear from unselected in-progress session titles
issues.body:
## Type of Bug

Rendering

## Description

Emoji characters in an in-progress session title disappear when the session row is not selected. Selecting the row makes the emoji render again.

This makes otherwise equivalent session titles look inconsistent based only on selection state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Agents window.
2. Start a session whose title contains one or more emoji characters.
3. While the session is in progress, select a different session.
4. Observe that the emoji characters are missing from the unselected session title.
5. Select the affected session and observe that the emoji characters reappear.

## Cause

The in-progress title shimmer in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/sessionsList.css` applies a clipped gradient and `-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent` to `.session-title` for unselected rows:

```css
.monaco-list-row:not(.selected) .session-item.in-progress .session-title {
	background-clip: text;
	-webkit-background-clip: text;
	-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent;
}
```

Chromium color emoji glyphs do not render through this text-clipped background, so they become transparent. The selector stops matching selected rows, which explains why selection restores them.

## Suggested Fix

Keep the real title as the solid, semantic base layer and apply the shimmer to a separate `aria-hidden` visual clone/overlay. The overlay can retain the existing clipped-gradient animation while the base layer preserves color emoji (and provides a fallback for any glyph the clipped background cannot paint). The clone should mirror truncation/highlight markup, be ignored by pointer events and accessibility, and be refreshed when the title or filter highlights change.

A focused component/fixture regression should cover an in-progress title containing a color emoji in both selected and unselected states, plus reduced-motion behavior.

issues.title: Unicode highlight boxes outlive their highlighter when the worker result arrives after dispose
Agent Host resumes a completed Copilot turn after state divergence, causing assistant-prefill 400
issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Agent Host integration (no separately listed Copilot extension)
- VS Code Version: 1.141.0-insider (`73d5322bb28c1a3c449fcee6c3869af33fad5027`, arm64)
- OS Version: macOS 27.0 (26A428)
- Feature: Agents window / Copilot CLI Agent Host / failed-turn recovery
- Selected model: Claude Opus 5.5
- Logs: AHP JSONL logging and the runtime event transcript were captured. The relevant sequence is summarized below; local paths and session IDs are omitted.

## Summary

After an `ENOSPC` failure during an active Copilot Agent Host turn, the UI/AHP turn state and the runtime transcript diverged:

- AHP retained the turn as `Error` with `resumable: true`.
- The Copilot runtime continued after space was freed, produced a final assistant response, and ended the session with reason `complete`.
- Selecting **Try Again** later caused VS Code to dispatch `chat/turnResume` for that stale errored turn.
- The runtime then attempted a zero-message continuation of a transcript that already ended with an assistant message. The provider rejected it with HTTP 400:

> This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.

Each subsequent Try Again repeated the same failure.

This may affect interruptions other than disk-full whenever AHP's persisted turn state remains resumable after the underlying runtime has already completed the interaction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Copilot CLI Agent Host session with a sufficiently long-running turn.
2. While the turn is active, exhaust writable disk space so a tool/build receives `ENOSPC`.
3. Free disk space and allow the runtime to continue to a final assistant response.
4. Reopen the session after AHP has retained the affected turn as a resumable error.
5. Select **Try Again**.

## Actual behavior

VS Code dispatches `chat/turnResume`. The provider returns HTTP 400 because the restored runtime conversation already ends with the assistant's completed response. The turn remains resumable, allowing the failure to loop.

Observed timeline:

- `16:48:13`: tool reports `No space left on device (os error 28)`.
- Runtime continues after cleanup.
- `16:58:18`: runtime records the final assistant message and `sessionEnd` with reason `complete`.
- `18:32:20`: client dispatches `chat/turnResume` for the stale resumable turn.
- `18:32:22`: provider rejects the request as unsupported assistant-message prefill.
- Ten retry attempts produced the same 400 response.

The runtime transcript itself remained valid JSON and ended cleanly; the failure was the mismatch between that completed transcript and AHP's stale resumable turn state.

## Expected behavior

A completed runtime interaction should not remain retryable as an errored AHP turn. Before dispatching `chat/turnResume`, VS Code should reconcile the turn against the runtime's durable completion state. If the runtime already completed, the UI should adopt that completion rather than attempt a zero-message continuation.

At minimum, a stale resume should become a non-resumable/already-completed result instead of calling the model and presenting an endlessly retryable 400.

## Relevant implementation

[`_handleResumedTurn`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e418d6d41f448c56ab7210f2a66a55b4916ab93/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts#L3321-L3403) dispatches `chat/turnResume` whenever the latest AHP turn is `Error` and its error part is resumable. It trusts that AHP state without checking whether the runtime transcript subsequently completed.

The failed-turn recovery path was introduced in [`ea7ede57`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/ea7ede57fb2d943c86c31520c28ab06f0c547cf1) (`agentHost: recover failed Copilot turns in place`).

issues.title: MCP: Allow users to disable all workspace servers while keeping user servers enabled
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Problem

VS Code can discover MCP servers from workspace/repository configuration (`.mcp.json` and `.vscode/mcp.json`) as well as user-level configuration. I want a user-controlled way to disable every workspace-origin MCP server while keeping my user/global MCP servers available.

Today, I can disable workspace servers individually or disable MCP access entirely, but I cannot exclude the workspace configuration source as a class. This is useful when I want my trusted personal MCP set without automatically adding tools declared by each repository.

## Proposed behavior

Add a user-controlled setting or enablement action that:

- Excludes all workspace/repository MCP servers.
- Keeps user/global MCP servers enabled.
- Can default workspace MCP servers off globally, with explicit opt-in for trusted workspaces.
- Is stored outside repository-controlled settings, so a workspace cannot re-enable its own MCP servers.
- Applies consistently to both the local harness and Agent Host-based harnesses.
- Is visible and reversible in the MCP/Agent Customizations UI.

For example, this could be represented as a user preference such as `chat.mcp.workspaceServersEnabled`, or as a scoped enablement decision in the existing MCP enablement model. The exact setting shape is not important.

## Related work

- #329475 requests the inverse: a workspace can exclude all user-level MCP servers and keep only workspace servers.
- #329478 proposes `chat.mcp.userServersEnabled` for that inverse case.
- #254931 tracks per-server enable/disable at user/workspace scope, but not bulk exclusion by configuration origin.
- #330566 introduced scoped MCP enablement decisions (`session > workspace > global > enabled`) that may provide a foundation.
- #337335 requests all MCP servers default-off with per-workspace opt-in; this request is narrower because user/global MCP servers should remain enabled.
- github/copilot-cli#3380 requests an analogous `--disable-repo-mcps` option for Copilot CLI.

issues.title: VoiceOver typing echo is silent on first launch, and speech stops after Command+Down Arrow in VS Code Insiders
issues.body:
VoiceOver does not announce typed characters or words when VS Code Insiders first opens, even with typing echo enabled and all extensions disabled. This makes it difficult to confirm what I am entering while editing.

Reloading the window restores typing echo. It then continues working after switching to another app and back. This corrects my earlier report that app switching caused the silence.

There is also a navigation issue: after pressing **Command+Down Arrow** to move to the end of the document, VoiceOver stops speaking in the editor. Setting `"editor.editContext": false` resolves that problem, but typing echo remains silent on first launch.

The regular VS Code release also exhibits this behavior, but the detailed reproduction steps and testing below were carried out in Insiders.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable VoiceOver with character and word echo.
2. Open VS Code Insiders and type in the editor: typing echo is silent.
3. Reload the window and type again: echo works, including after switching apps.
4. With EditContext enabled, press Command+Down Arrow: VoiceOver stops speaking in the editor.
5. Set `"editor.editContext": false` and repeat the navigation test: speech continues.

### Findings

The initial typing-echo issue also reproduces in ordinary HTML inputs in Electron. Our tests place its introduction between **43.0.0-beta.3** and **43.0.0-beta.4**. It persists in **43.7.3** and **44.5.1**, but was absent in the **45 alpha builds tested**, starting with **45.0.0-alpha.1**. This is consistent with [Chromium’s VoiceOver regression](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/534441751).

IntelliSense works with VoiceOver when using Trigger Suggest. The earlier missing Python suggestions were due to missing Python/Pylance extensions.

### Environment

macOS 27.0 (26A428), VS Code Insiders 1.141.0-insider, commit `9666ca8ea7a0ac0d0ce4e661c19f8a05d5d7ad79`, built September 30, 2026.

issues.title: Custom agent model pin is overridden by the model selected in Copilot chat or the GitHub cloud window
issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in (version not captured in the original report)
- VS Code Version: current stable / insiders as of 2026-09-30 (exact build not captured)
- OS Version: not captured
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): custom agent selection in Copilot chat, and in the GitHub cloud / Cloud session window
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): whichever model is already selected in the chat or cloud window; it differs from the model pinned in the custom agent
- Logs: not attached. Chat debug view should show the request model matching the window picker, not the `.agent.md` `model` field.

## Summary

Selecting a custom agent does not honor the model pinned in that agent's frontmatter. The model already selected in the Copilot chat window, or in the GitHub cloud window, overrides the pin. The agent then runs on the window's model.

This is not the same as frontmatter failing to load. Instructions and tools can still come from the agent file. Only the pinned model loses to the window selection.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a custom agent, for example `.github/agents/reviewer.agent.md`, with a model pin that is **not** the model currently selected in the window. Use the qualified name:

```yaml
---
name: reviewer
description: Review-only agent that must run on the pinned model
tools: [search/codebase]
model: Claude Haiku 4.5 (copilot)
---

You are a review agent. When asked which model you are using, answer with the model that actually served this request.
```

2. In the Copilot chat window, select a different model in the model picker (for example a GPT model, or Auto).
3. Select the `reviewer` custom agent from the agent dropdown.
4. Send a prompt. In the chat debug view, check the model on the request.
5. Repeat from the GitHub cloud window (Cloud session target / agents panel): leave a different model selected in that window, select the same custom agent, and start a task.

## Expected

Selecting the custom agent uses the model pinned in frontmatter (`Claude Haiku 4.5 (copilot)` in the example). The model selected in the chat or cloud window is only the fallback when `model` is omitted.

That matches the docs:

- VS Code custom agents: "`model` — The AI model to use when running the prompt. … If not specified, the currently selected model in model picker is used."
- GitHub custom agents configuration: "`model` — Model to use when this custom agent executes. If unset, inherits the default model."

A set `model` should win. The window selection should not override it.

## Actual

The model selected in the Copilot chat window, or in the GitHub cloud window, overrides the frontmatter pin. The custom agent's model selection is not honored. There is no warning that the pin was ignored.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #321765 is a startup load bug: after restart, some agents do not load frontmatter at all (empty description, tools not applied, `user-invocable: false` agents still listed). This report is precedence, not a cache miss: the window's selected model wins over a pin that is present in the agent definition. It also happens in the GitHub cloud window, which #321765 does not cover.
- #338489 / #338629 updated guidance to say the Copilot harness supports `model` (single value and ordered list) and removed the old "unsupported" hover warning. That docs fix does not stop the window selection from overriding the pin at runtime.
- #291883 (subagent `model` not respected) was fixed in 1.109. This is the parent-session / cloud-window case.
- github/copilot-cli#2950 is the same class of bug on the CLI prompt-invocation path, not the Copilot chat or GitHub cloud window.

## Notes

- Reproduced with the qualified `Model Name (vendor)` form, not a bare API id, so this is not the unknown-model fallback in #319709 / #319131.
- An array pin (`model: [A, B]`) has the same result: the window selection is used instead of the first available entry in the list.

## Summary

On the first launch after installing the current Insiders build, VS Code successfully retrieved the managed settings and enabled managed sandboxing, but an existing GitHub Copilot Chat session remained on Local.

The session remains usable on Local until the user manually selects Agent Host.

- Current VS Code Insiders
- Managed settings successfully retrieved
- Managed sandbox shown as enabled
- Existing session created on Local before the first launch

## Related

#338570 tracks a different selection problem specific to dev containers, where Local is used even though Agent Host is selected in the Agents window.

issues.title: Agent Host: reused multi-turn subagent remains running after child turn completes
issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Agent Host/Copilot provider
- VS Code Version: Code - Insiders, 2026-09-30
- OS Version: macOS
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode, background multi-turn subagents
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Parent GPT-5.6 Sol, research subagent Claude Sonnet 5
- Logs: Agent Host debug bundle available locally. The relevant sanitized timeline is included below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Start a background multi-turn subagent with the `task` tool and let its initial turn complete.
2. Reactivate the same subagent with `write_agent`.
3. Send one or more follow-up messages while that subagent is active.
4. Wait for the final child turn to complete.
5. Observe that the child chat has completed, but the parent still reports that the subagent is running.

Expected:

The parent receives a new `subagent_completed` signal after each completed turn of a reused multi-turn subagent and clears its running state.

Actual:

The child emits `assistant.turn_end`, the `subagentStop` hook succeeds, and the child AHP channel emits `chat/turnComplete`. The parent does not receive a matching `subagent_completed` signal, so its running state remains stale.

## Timeline from the debug bundle

All timestamps are UTC.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 05:35:56 | The outer research subagent started. |
| 05:37-05:41 | Three nested subagents started and completed. |
| 05:44:00 | The outer subagent's initial turn completed. |
| 15:33:49 | `write_agent` reactivated the same outer subagent. |
| 15:47-15:50 | More follow-up messages were delivered to the same subagent. |
| 15:50:04.040 | The final child `assistant.turn_end` was recorded. |
| 15:50:04.045 | The `subagentStop` hook completed successfully. |
| 15:50:04.305 | The child AHP channel emitted `chat/turnComplete`. |
| After 15:50:04 | No parent `subagent_completed` signal appeared before the log export. |

## Suspected cause

The child turn and the parent's subagent state use separate completion paths.

`CopilotAgentSession._reconcileSubagentTaskStatuses()` calls `tasks.list()` and emits completion only when the SDK task reports `idle`, `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. If the check triggered by `turn_end` still reports `running`, the host removes the completion scheduler and waits for a later `session.background_tasks_changed` event.

In this trace, the child completed normally, but that later status transition did not produce `subagent_completed`. `AgentSideEffects.completeSubagentSession()` therefore never cleared the parent state.

This looks like a lifecycle reconciliation race or missing transition at the Copilot SDK and Agent Host boundary. The model call and child chat did not hang.

## Suggested regression coverage

Add a test for this sequence:

1. Complete a multi-turn subagent.
2. Resume it with a follow-up.
3. Queue additional follow-ups.
4. End the final child turn while the first `tasks.list()` response still says `running`.
5. Verify that the parent eventually receives exactly one new `subagent_completed` signal without requiring another user action.

The host could keep reconciling after a subagent `turn_end` until the task becomes idle or a newer child turn begins. The SDK could also guarantee `session.background_tasks_changed` after the task status changes.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

issues.title: Markdown links drop non-line fragments like #page=3 when opening files (PDF links always open on page 1)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested end to end. The drop happens in the built-in Markdown extension, so it does not depend on third-party extensions. Seeing the effect on a PDF needs a PDF viewer extension (see below).

- VS Code Version: VS Code main as of 2026-09-30
- OS Version: macOS

Following a markdown link to a non-text file with a non-line fragment, such as `[pdf](file.pdf#page=3)`, opens the file without the fragment, so a PDF viewer always starts on page 1. Only `L<line>`-style fragments survive.

Code path, from reading `extensions/markdown-language-features/src/util/openDocumentLink.ts` on main. The bundled `vscode-markdown-languageservice` 0.5.0 is the version pinned in `package.json`:

1. `MdLinkOpener.openDocumentLink` calls `resolveDocumentLink`, which sends `resolveLinkTarget` to the language server.
2. In the language service, `resolveLinkTarget` → `#resolveInternalLinkTarget` gets the fragment `page=3`. It is not a line/position fragment (`parseLocationInfoFromFragment` returns nothing) and the target is not a markdown document with a matching header, so it returns `{ kind: 'file', uri: target }`. `target` has no fragment.
3. `openResolvedDocumentLink` sees `resolved.kind === 'file'` and no `rangeSelection`, and `uri.fragment` is empty. So it calls `getLocationFragmentFromLinkText(linkText)`. That only accepts `^L?\d+(?:,\d+)?(?:-L?\d+(?:,\d+)?)?$`, so `page=3` returns `undefined` and the URI is left unchanged.
4. It then runs `vscode.commands.executeCommand('vscode.open', uri, { selection: undefined, viewColumn })` with a URI that has no `#page=3`.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Open a folder containing `doc.md` and any multi-page `file.pdf`.
2. In `doc.md` add `[pdf](file.pdf#page=3)`.
3. Install a PDF viewer extension that opens `.pdf` files in VS Code, for example "vscode-pdf" (`tomoki1207.pdf`). VS Code has no built-in PDF viewer. Whether a given viewer honors a URI fragment is up to that viewer.
4. Open the Markdown preview (`Markdown: Open Preview to the Side`) and click the link. Alternatively, Cmd+click the link in the editor.
5. To see the dropped fragment without any PDF viewer: open the repo in VS Code, run the "Run Extension" launch config, and set a breakpoint on the `vscode.open` call in `openResolvedDocumentLink` (`openDocumentLink.ts`). Repeat step 4 in the Extension Development Host and inspect `uri`. Expected per the code above: `uri.fragment` is `''`, and `uri.toString()` ends in `file.pdf` with no `#page=3`.

**Expected:** the URI passed to `vscode.open` keeps the fragment (`file:///.../file.pdf#page=3`), so an editor or viewer that understands it can open at page 3. Line fragments such as `#L10` should keep working as before.

**Actual:** the URI passed to `vscode.open` is `file:///.../file.pdf` and the fragment is lost, so the PDF opens at its default position (page 1).

A fix is proposed in #332661.

issues.title: "This is taking a little longer than usual" shows while a foreground terminal command is running
issues.body:
When `chat.experimental.persistentProgress` is enabled, the chat working footer switches to **"This is taking a little longer than usual"** after 90s without any change to the response model. This fires while the agent is running a long foreground terminal command (e.g. a long test run), even though the agent is working fine and simply waiting on the command.

The message should only appear when the agent is truly not responding, not while a tool (such as a foreground terminal command) is actively executing.

### Why it happens

- `ChatWorkingProgressContentPart` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatProgressContentPart.ts`) schedules the message via `DELAYED_PROGRESS_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000` and only resets the timer on `response.model.onDidChange`.
- For tool invocations, `Response` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/model/chatModel.ts` only fires a change when the invocation's `state` transitions or `toolSpecificDataKind` changes. Terminal output and the executing state's `progress` observable do not fire a change, so a running command looks idle until it exits.
- `getPersistentWorkingProgress` in `chatListRenderer.ts` sets `showDelayedProgressMessage: !activityLabel`. `getPersistentActivityLabel` only produces a label for background terminals (`isActiveBackgroundTerminalToolInvocation` requires `isBackground` or `didContinueInBackground`), active subagents, or blocking `get_terminal_output`/`read_bash`/`read_powershell`/`read_agent` calls. A foreground `run_in_terminal` call gets no label, so the delayed message is allowed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `chat.experimental.persistentProgress` to a value other than `off`.
2. Ask the agent to run a command in the foreground terminal that takes more than 90s (e.g. a long test suite).
3. After ~90s the footer reads "This is taking a little longer than usual" while the command is still running normally.

### Expected

No "taking longer" message while a foreground terminal command (or any executing tool) is running. Only show it when the agent/model has genuinely stopped producing activity.

### Possible fixes

- Treat an executing foreground terminal invocation as activity (e.g. give it an activity label / suppress `showDelayedProgressMessage`, like the background terminal case).
- More generally, don't arm the delayed-progress timer while any tool invocation is in the `Executing` state, and/or reset it on tool `progress` updates.

issues.title: Hide Migrations from the Customizations sidebar when no migrations are pending
issues.body:
## Description

The Customizations pane continues to show a **Migrations** entry with a warning icon after all migrations have been completed. The warning suggests that action is required, but opening the entry shows that there is nothing left to do.

## Expected behavior

Hide the **Migrations** sidebar entry when there are no pending migrations. If migrations later become available, show the entry again.

## Current behavior

The warning-marked **Migrations** entry remains visible even when the user is fully migrated, creating a misleading action-needed state.

issues.title: MCP tools silently dropped when tool IDs collide after trancation to 64 chars
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.139.1
- OS Version: mac tahoe 26.7.1
- Transport: Streamable HTTP, via MCP gateway litellm that adds server name prefix to each tool name

# Summary

VS code builds each MCP tool ID as McpPrefixGenerator prefix + tool name, then custs it to 64 chars. The 64 chars length limit is correct, because model provider APIs cap function names at 64. But VS code doesn't keep the IDs unique after the cut. When 2 different tool names end up with the same ID, the second registration throws "Tool... is already registered" inside Mcp[LanguageModelToolContribution._syncTools. That aborts the deferred registration loop, and all tools after it in alphabetical order are siliently dropped.

No useful info tells:
- The MCP output log says Discovered N tools
- MCP Inspector shows all tools correctly.
- Only the tool picker and agent model are missing the tools

This is increasingly common behind MCP gateways that add <servername>- prefix to every tool. The MCP spec allows tool names up to 128 chars, so a server can follow the spec and still hit this.


# Steps to Reproduce:

1. Connect to a mcp server via litellm.
2. mcp server is registered in litellm with a relatively long name
3. mcp tools has a relatively long name
4. 2 mcp tools has the same prefix before the cutting length
5. the following mcp tools are not showing up in the tool picker.

Or reproduce it from local
1. Run below server

```python
  from fastmcp import FastMCP
  
  mcp=FastMCP(name="Long_Server_Name_For_Gateway")
  P = "Long_server_Name_For_Gateway-"
  
  for tool in ["get_resource_details", "get_resource_stats", "get_resource_status", "list_resources", "list_zones"]:
      mcp.tool(name=P+tool, description=tool)(lambda: "ok")
  mcp.run(transport="streamable-http", port=8000)
```
2. Add it to mcp.json
3. open chat tool picker.
Expected: all 5 tools are listed.
Actual: only 2 are listed, list_resources and list_zones are missing, even though their names are short.

# Root cause
How the ID is built (mcpserver.ts)
```python
this.id=(idPrefix + _definition.name).replaceAll('.','_').slice(0, McpToolName.MaxLength);
```
The 18 chars prefix plus the 29 chars gateway prefix leaves 17 chars for the tool name.

# Proposed change
1. Make IDS unique when they are cut short
When prefix+name is longer than 64, replace the end of the id with a short hash of the full tool name
2. Handle each registration on it's own mcpLanguageModelToolContribution.ts
Even with unique IDs, one bad registration shouldn't drop every tool after it

issues.title: Chat sessions are not shared between VS Code clients connected to the same Remote SSH host
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested

- VS Code Version: 1.139.1
- OS Version: macOS 27.0.1 (Golden Gate)
- Remote OS: Linux
- Remote connection: VS Code Remote SSH

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Connect from **Machine A** to a remote Linux host using VS Code Remote SSH.
2. Open a workspace/folder on the remote host.
3. Create and use a VS Code Chat session in that remote workspace.
4. Connect from **Machine B** to the **same remote host** using VS Code Remote SSH.
5. Open the **same remote workspace/folder**.
6. Open the Chat session history.

### Expected behavior

Chat sessions associated with the remote workspace should be available from both clients, allowing the same session to be resumed regardless of which machine connects to the remote host.

### Actual behavior

Machine A and Machine B have independent chat histories. A chat session created from Machine A is not visible from Machine B, despite both clients being connected to the same remote host and workspace.

This is **not about Copilot cloud session synchronization**. The use case is VS Code Chat with a remote workspace, without relying on cloud synchronization. Ideally, the chat session state for a remote workspace should be persisted on the remote side or otherwise be accessible to clients connecting to that workspace.

### Related issue

This appears to be exactly the same problem described in #307885 ("Share chat session across machines").

That issue was closed as a duplicate, but the canonical issue it duplicates does not appear to be linked or publicly visible. The issue is also locked, so it is not possible to ask there which issue is currently tracking this problem.

If this is still a duplicate, could you please point to the canonical issue where this is being tracked?

issues.title: Subagent invoked by a custom agent reports `tool_search` unavailable and cannot load deferred tools
issues.body:
Subagent invoked by a custom agent reports `tool_search` unavailable and cannot load deferred tools

Copilot Chat Extension Version: 1.0.85
VS Code Version: 1.139.1
OS Version: Windows 11
Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Custom agent invoking subagents
Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-6 Astra
Logs: `Blocked: execution did not start. The delegated security worker also lacked tool discovery, XXX`
Steps to Reproduce:

Use a custom agent that delegates execution to a subagent via runSubagent.
Ask it to execute a task requiring a deferred tool, such as the version-control tool for creating a branch.
The subagent reports that tool_search is unavailable, preventing it from loading the required tool.
Retry execution. In this session, the delegated worker reported the same limitation.
Expected Behavior:

Subagents should have access to the tool-discovery capability needed to load their permitted deferred tools, or receive those tools directly.

Actual Behavior:

The parent session has access to tool_search, but the subagent reports that it does not. Execution stops before the required tool can be invoked.

Example response:

Your authorization is valid, but the required branch tool is deferred and this session exposes no tool_search to load it.

A subsequent retry reported:

The delegated security worker also lacked tool discovery.

Additional Context:

This occurred in an execution coordinator → security worker delegation flow. Branch creation had already been authorized. No branch creation or code changes occurred.

These messages are agent-reported failures; debug logs are needed to confirm whether the cause is tool exposure, agent configuration, or tool-discovery behavior.

issues.title: Can not install local MCP server from MCP registry by Azure API Center when allowlist is enabled as enterprise policy.
issues.body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No - VS Code Version: 1.140.0-insider - OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise - More details for VS Code version. ``` Version: 1.140.0-insider (user setup) Commit: b6c7324cedb6fc4ed639e3c7e1d4b233a09df8bc Date: 2026-09-29T20:21:41Z Electron: 43.7.3 ElectronBuildId: 15386805 Chromium: 150.0.7871.250 Node.js: 24.21.0 V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0 @github/copilot: 1.0.89-7 @github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.15-preview.4 OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 ``` Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create MCP registry from Azure API Center by following the [blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/all-things-azure/locking-down-mcp-create-a-private-registry-on-azure-api-center-and-enforce-it-in-github-copilot-and-vs-code/#step-1:-create-your-azure-api-center-instance) 2. Register a local MCP server by following [the doc](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-center/register-discover-mcp-server), e.g. [Playwright using npm](https://playwright.dev/docs/getting-started-mcp#installation) as package manager. The entry from the endpoint https://mcp-registry.data.eastus.azure-apicenter.ms/workspaces/default/v0.1/servers/ should look like the follows. ``` { "server": { "$schema": "https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json", "name": "playwright", "title": "Playwright", "description": "UI test automation", "version": "2026-09-29", "packages": [ { "registryType": "npm", "version": "latest", "runtimeHint": "npx", "transport": { "type": "stdio" }, "identifier": "@playwright/mcp", "runtimeArguments": [], "packageArguments": [], "environmentVariables": [] } ] }, "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/official": { "status": "active", "createdAt": "2026-09-29T13:45:57.1982055+00:00", "updatedAt": "2026-09-29T14:38:12.9076165+00:00", "isLatest": true }, "x-ms-id": "cde131c6-7998-4e37-a1ec-378ef3c3071d" } } ``` 3. Configure custom registry MCP server for the proper GitHub Enterprise or GitHub organization where the test user gets GitHub Copilot license from 4. Create allowlist in local file at `%ProgramFiles%\GitHubCopilot\managed-settings.json` with below sample content. ``` { "allowedMcpServers": [ { "serverUrl": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/*" }, { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/sse" }, { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp" }, { "serverCommand": ["npx", "@playwright/mcp@latest"] }, { "serverCommand": ["npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]}, { "serverCommand": ["cmd", "/c", "uvx", "markitdown-mcp"] } ], "deniedMcpServers": [ { "serverUrl": "https://learn.microsoft.com/*" } ] } ``` 5. Browse the MCP server with `@mcp` from extension panel 6. The Playwright MCP server from the UI above can not be installed with the reason `This mcp server cannot be installed because This Model Context Protocol server is not in the list of servers allowed by your organization. Please contact your administrator for more information.` 7. If no allowlist configured, above Playwright MCP server can be installed from the MCP server catalog in the UI from MCP registry hosted by API Center 8. If manually editing the mcp.json file with the following entry, with above allowlist, the Playwright MCP server can be started successfully. ``` "playwright": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": [ "@playwright/mcp@latest" ], "gallery": "https://mcp-registry.data.eastus.azure-apicenter.ms/workspaces/default", "version": "2026-09-29" } ```

issues.title: Agents Window exposes never-materialized provisional sessions as "Session" after restart

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: papercut :drop_of_blood:
labels.description: A particularly annoying issue impacting someone on the team

issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not collected; affected sessions use the Agent Host Copilot provider (`copilotcli`).
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0-insider, commit `b6c7324cedb6fc4ed639e3c7e1d4b233a09df8bc`, build date 2026-09-29T20:21:41.
- OS Version: Windows, 10.0.26200.
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents Window, local Agent Host session discovery/restoration.
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not applicable; these sessions have no persisted conversation turns.
- Logs: Relevant excerpts and protocol/storage findings below. Raw logs are not attached because they contain unrelated conversation and workspace data.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Have an idle Copilot session allocated locally but never materialized on the backend. The two affected entries were allocated on September 29.
2. Update/restart VS Code Insiders and open the Agents Window. This occurred on September 30 immediately after updating.
3. Observe two recent entries named only **Session**.
4. Open one: it fails with `Session was never created on the backend: copilotcli:/d95942c4-3f31-4d30-9229-143453048ac5`.

This is the observed sequence, not yet a clean-room deterministic reproduction. No crash is established by the available evidence.

### Expected

Never-materialized provisional sessions should not appear as ordinary, reopenable sessions after restart.

### Actual

The initial session list includes the two abandoned placeholders. Opening the first produces an authoritative session-not-found error. A later full list excludes both, but the initial exposure already leaves the user with broken entries.

### Affected sessions

| Session ID | Creation time (UTC) | Initial title | Initial status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `d95942c4-3f31-4d30-9229-143453048ac5` | 2026-09-29T17:43:30.299Z | Session | 1 |
| `92b0c9e0-7e6c-4937-8d0b-4fc818ebbde9` | 2026-09-29T20:58:20.154Z | Session | 1 |

These IDs existed before the update/restart; they were not newly allocated during startup.

### Log timeline

Plain host log timestamps below are local time (UTC+02:00). AHP wire timestamps are UTC.

**Startup lists persisted catalog entries:**

```text
2026-09-30 10:56:05.282 [info] [AgentService] listSessions computed 772 of 793 session(s) for mode 'last7Days' in 3629ms (catalog enabled, 792 catalog-served, 4 provider fallback, resolve 2660ms, 11 db opens, 25 db stats, 0 state-manager fallback)
2026-09-30 10:56:08.003 [info] [AgentService] listSessions computed 731 of 752 session(s) for mode 'last7Days' in 2463ms (catalog enabled, 792 catalog-served, 4 provider fallback, resolve 262ms, 100 db opens, 116 db stats, 0 state-manager fallback)
```

The Agents Window AHP connection (`clientInfo.name = vscode-agents-window`) receives two initial `listSessions` results at **08:56:05.535Z** and **08:56:05.619Z**. Both contain 772 items and include both affected session IDs with `title: "Session"`, status 1, project/working-directory metadata, and zero changed files.

**Opening the first entry fails:**

```text
2026-09-30 10:57:24.059 [trace] [AgentService] restoreSession start: copilotcli:/d95942c4-3f31-4d30-9229-143453048ac5
2026-09-30 10:57:24.071 [trace] [AgentService] restore: catalog and registry resolved for copilotcli:/d95942c4-3f31-4d30-9229-143453048ac5 (registered=true, external=false)
2026-09-30 10:57:24.072 [trace] [AgentService] restore: reading provider metadata for copilotcli:/d95942c4-3f31-4d30-9229-143453048ac5
2026-09-30 10:57:25.193 [error] [ProtocolServer] Request 'subscribe' failed Session was never created on the backend: copilotcli:/d95942c4-3f31-4d30-9229-143453048ac5
```

The matching AHP response at **08:57:25.567Z** has error code **-32001** and the same message. Subsequent subscriptions fail with the same error, including at 10:57:35 and 10:58:11 local time.

Only the first entry was verified by opening it; the second has the matching storage characteristics below.

**Later full listing excludes both:**

```text
2026-09-30 10:59:37.200 [trace] [AgentService] listSessions computed 731 of 749 session(s) for mode 'last7Days' in 239ms (catalog enabled, 789 catalog-served, 4 provider fallback, resolve 16ms, 88 db opens, 96 db stats, 0 state-manager fallback)
```

The matching Agents Window AHP response at **08:59:37.528Z** contains 731 items and neither affected ID.

### Read-only storage verification

Both IDs have:

- A `sessions` registration with `provider = copilotcli`, `external = 0`, and `registration_source = explicit`.
- A durable metadata marker `sessionProvisional:copilotcli:/<id> = true`.
- A `sessions_v2` catalog row with `verified = 1`, `payload_version = 1`, and `is_chat_backing = 0`.
- Catalog payloads containing project/working-directory, Git, and default-chat metadata, but **no title**.
- Zero rows in each of the local `turns`, `local_turns`, and `chat_drafts` tables.
- No `events.jsonl` at the normal Copilot SDK session-state location for either ID.

The first row has catalog `source_revision = 2`; the second has `source_revision = 1`. Thus, persisted catalog metadata exists even though the durable provisional markers remain set and there is no conversation history.

### Relevant code / investigation lead

@sandy081: This appears closely related to #336480, **agentHost: recognise a crash-orphaned provisional session**.

Relevant paths in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts`:

- `_whenProvisionalSessionKeysLoaded`: asynchronously loads the durable markers.
- `_withoutUnmaterializedProvisionalSessions`: suppresses marked sessions only when the provider catalog is known readable and the provider cannot describe the session.
- `_computeSessions`: serves eligible central catalog records and then applies provisional filtering.
- `_restoreSessionState`: emits the exact observed error when the catalog is readable, the session remains marked provisional, and provider metadata is absent.

The evidence establishes an **initial-list versus later-list inconsistency**: persisted provisional catalog rows are exposed at startup, while restoration correctly rejects the first one and later listing removes both. A startup readiness/ordering gap between catalog-backed listing and provisional filtering is a likely investigation lead, **not a proven exact interleaving**. In particular, the logs do not establish whether marker loading or provider-catalog readability was the late prerequisite.
