<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes — the underlying issue also affects normal non-managed editor tabs; the recording uses a project canvas to make the closure visually clear.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: Code - OSS Dev 1.141.0 (`2044f65df4a2`)
- OS Version: macOS 26.7 (25G229)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open the Agents window in single-pane layout with the Side Panel visible.
2. Open a non-managed editor tab in the Side Panel, such as a file editor or a canvas editor.
3. Run **Toggle Side Panel** (`workbench.action.agentToggleSidePanel`, Option+Command+B) to hide the editor area and Session Details together.
4. Run **Toggle Side Panel** again to restore it.

### Expected behavior

The editor tabs that were open before hiding the Side Panel remain open when it is shown again.

### Actual behavior

The open non-managed editor is closed. In the canvas reproduction, the Chess canvas tab disappears and the editor area falls back to the Files tab.

[Watch the canvas reproduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/1d695535509bff366c3e0492cb06e6d078db6b00/attachments/2026/09/30/35b55d26-2970-4bbf-a800-fff98fb45e51-side-panel-toggle-closes-canvas.mp4)

The video shows the Chess canvas before the toggle, followed by the restored Side Panel where the Chess tab is gone.

### Confirmed root cause

`SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator` observes the intermediate toggle state where the editor area is hidden while the auxiliary bar is still visible and queues a detail-only collapse. The queued operation runs after the whole Side Panel has finished hiding, but it does not revalidate that the layout is still detail-only, so it closes non-managed editors based on stale state.

### Additional context

A focused fix and regression test are available in #338863. The fix ignores detail-only collapse while the whole Side Panel is toggling and rechecks the layout predicate when the queued operation executes.

- VS Code Version: 
- OS Version: 

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install VS Code 1.139.1 stable (x64) on Windows 11 using the User Setup (`VSCodeUserSetup-x64-1.139.1.exe`).
2. Make sure no VS Code instance is running.
3. Double-click the "Visual Studio Code" shortcut in the Start Menu or on the Desktop (target `Code.exe`, **no arguments**, working directory = install folder).
   - Nothing happens: no window appears, no `%APPDATA%\Code\logs\<timestamp>` folder is created, and no `Code.exe` process is left behind.
4. From a terminal, run the installed `Code.exe` directly:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Code.exe` (no arguments), cwd = install folder | exit code **0** in ~90 ms, starts nothing |
| `Code.exe "C:\path\to\folder"` | exit code **1** in ~50-200 ms, starts nothing |
| `Code.exe "C:\path\to\file.txt"` | exit code **1** in ~100 ms, starts nothing |
| `Code.exe --new-window "C:\path\to\folder"` / `Code.exe -n "C:\path\to\folder"` | exit code **9** in ~70 ms |
| `& "<install>\bin\code.cmd" "C:\path\to\folder"` | **works** - VS Code starts and opens the folder |

5. The same failure occurs when an instance is already running (started via `bin\code.cmd`).

### Expected

- The Start Menu / Desktop shortcut starts VS Code.
- `Code.exe <folder>` opens that folder.
- The file association `HKCU\Software\Classes\Applications\Code.exe\shell\open\command` (`"<install>\Code.exe" "%1"`) opens the file.

### Actual install layout (after a clean reinstall)

```
<install>\                                  (= C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code)
├─ 04c0d99f4f\                              directory name = first 10 chars of the commit
│  ├─ resources\app\                        full application payload (out\, extensions\, node_modules.asar ...)
│  ├─ locales\  policies\  tools\  appx\
│  └─ *.dll  *.pak  icudtl.dat  snapshot_blob.bin  version (43.6.0)
├─ bin\code.cmd                             points at 04c0d99f4f\resources\app\out\cli.js
├─ Code.exe                                 237 MB, FileVersion 1.139.1
├─ Code.VisualElementsManifest.xml
└─ unins000.exe / unins000.dat / unins000.msg
```

`resources\app\product.json` contains `"win32VersionedUpdate": true`. There is **no `resources\` directory next to `Code.exe`**, and no marker file at the install root that identifies the versioned folder.

`bin\code.cmd` contents:

```cmd
@echo off
setlocal
set VSCODE_DEV=
set ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1
"%~dp0..\Code.exe" "%~dp0..\04c0d99f4f\resources\app\out\cli.js" %*
IF %ERRORLEVEL% NEQ 0 EXIT /b %ERRORLEVEL%
endlocal
```

### VS Code version

1.139.1 (stable, x64), commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`

### OS version

Windows 11 (x64)

### Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?

Yes. The application never initializes - no log folder is created at all, with or without extensions installed.

### Additional information

- A silent in-place reinstall of the official `VSCodeUserSetup-x64-1.139.1.exe` (222 MB, Authenticode status Valid, signer CN=Microsoft Corporation, installer exit code 0) does **not** change any of the above; the layout and the symptoms are identical before and after.
- Nothing is written to `%APPDATA%\Code\logs\`, i.e. the failure happens before application initialization.
- Installer log tail (`/LOG=...`), note the helper failure:

```
KillContextMenuComSurrogate: stopping COM surrogate(s) hosting context-menu DLL (1C6DF0C0-192A-4451-BE36-6A59A86A692E)
KillContextMenuComSurrogate: PowerShell exited with non-zero code 1
Invoking inno_updater to remove previous installation folder
inno_updater completed gc successfully
Need to restart Windows? No
```

- Related: #263998 (create versioned resources for windows setup)
- I can provide any further diagnostics on request (`--verbose` output, Process Monitor traces, process/exit-code logging).

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

When editing a previously sent message that is **not the last message in the queue**, there should be an additional **"Save Changes"** option.

Currently, the available options (**Send and Stop**, **Add to Queue**, and **Direct with...**) move the edited message to the **end of the queue**.

It would be useful to have a **"Save Changes"** action that updates the message while **preserving its current position in the queue**.

### Expected behavior

1. Edit a queued message.
2. Select **"Save Changes"**.
3. The message is updated in place.
4. Its position in the queue remains unchanged.

This would make it possible to correct or refine a queued message without unintentionally changing the execution order.

issues.title: Copilot Chat PATH contribution breaks zsh startup on macOS
issues.body:
This is likely the same issue as https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/280448, but that issue was closed.

# Copilot Chat PATH contribution breaks zsh startup on macOS

## Description

Opening a new VS Code integrated terminal with zsh on macOS prints an `export` error when the GitHub Copilot Chat extension is enabled. The extension contributes PATH entries located under `~/Library/Application Support/Code/...`; the space in `Application Support` appears to be mishandled when the environment is applied to the shell.

This then results in some kind of background process-spawning loop which eventually reaches the thread limit on my system, causing further forks to fail (essentially rendering the entire laptop useless). Closing the terminal kills all the runaway processes.

Disabling VS Code shell integration prevents the error, which suggests the failure is in how the contributed environment is applied.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, use zsh as the integrated terminal profile.
2. Enable the GitHub Copilot Chat extension.
3. Leave `terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled` enabled.
4. Open a new integrated terminal.

## Actual behavior

The terminal prints an error similar to:

```text
(eval):export:1: not valid in this context: Support/Code/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/copilotCli:...
```

The **Terminal: Show Environment Contributions** command reports this PATH contribution from `GitHub.copilot-chat`:

```text
PATH=/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/Code/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/copilotCli:/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/Code/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/debugCommand:${env:PATH}
```

The unescaped space in `Application Support` appears to split the `export` command, leaving the terminal with an invalid PATH.

## Expected behavior

The Copilot Chat PATH entries should be applied without breaking shell startup, including when the VS Code user-data directory contains spaces.

## Workaround

Setting this in User Settings avoids the error:

```json
"terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled": false
```

This disables VS Code shell integration features such as command detection. I still get the export warning when I open an integrated terminal (see bellow), but processes don't run away uncontrollably. This is the only way I've found to keep Copilot working and still be able to have a terminal open in VSCode.

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- Shell: zsh
- VS Code version: 1.139.1 
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension version: 0.41

issues.title: Agent Host: prune old Claude/Codex SDK versions from sdk-cache
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Description

Agent Host downloads versioned copies of the Claude and Codex SDKs into its SDK cache.

When the required SDK version changes, a new version is downloaded into a separate directory, but older versions appear to remain in the cache indefinitely.

For example, over several VS Code updates, the cache may end up containing directories like:

```text
agent-host/sdk-cache/
  ...
  0.3.220/
  0.3.239/
  0.3.258/
```

Only the currently requested SDK version is normally used, so these older versions gradually become unused files consuming disk space.

This affects both Claude and Codex SDK downloads.

## Current behavior

When Agent Host requires a new SDK version:

1. The new version is downloaded.
2. It is extracted into a version-specific cache directory.
3. Previously downloaded SDK versions remain in the cache.

There does not appear to be any cache pruning or eviction policy for old SDK versions.

Since the SDK packages themselves are relatively large, the cache can grow noticeably over time as VS Code updates its pinned SDK versions.

## Expected behavior

Agent Host should clean up SDK versions that are no longer needed.

For example, one of the following strategies could work:

- Remove older SDK versions after a newer version has been downloaded successfully.
- Keep only the current version and the immediately previous version.
- Keep the most recent N versions.
- Apply a size- or age-based cache eviction policy.

Keeping one previous version may be useful in case VS Code is downgraded or rolled back, while still preventing the cache from growing indefinitely.

## Possible implementation

After successfully installing the requested SDK version, Agent Host could enumerate sibling version directories for the same SDK/package/target and remove versions that are outside the retention policy.

Cleanup should probably happen only after the new SDK has been downloaded and installed successfully, so that a failed update does not remove a working cached version.

It may also be worth avoiding deletion of SDK versions that are currently in use by another running Agent Host process.

## Why this matters

Claude and Codex SDK distributions can be fairly large, and Agent Host updates may introduce new pinned versions over time.

Without cleanup, users can accumulate multiple SDK installations that are no longer referenced by the current VS Code version.

A small retention policy would keep the convenience of the SDK cache while preventing unnecessary disk usage.

issues.title: Background terminal completion notification starts a new turn, dropping the model's reasoning mid-task

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When a `run_in_terminal` command prints nothing for `chat.tools.terminal.idleSilenceTimeoutMs` (5 minutes by default), it is moved to the background. When it finishes, VS Code sends `[Terminal … notification: command completed …] Terminal output: …` as a new chat request with `queue: Steering` and `isSystemInitiated: true` ([runInTerminalTool.ts#L3226](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4f5c0700138956542ba70734adb986801c463222/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/runInTerminalTool.ts#L3226)).

Because it is a new request, every earlier round of the task is rendered as history. For Chat Completions models, that strips the reasoning from all of them (#338820). The user never sends a message, but the model loses its reasoning partway through the task.

Kimi K3 in the Local agent, running a task that reads a file and then runs `sleep 320 && echo NOTIFY-DONE`:

```
requests 2-4 (task tool loop):   each earlier assistant message has reasoning_text and reasoning_opaque
request 5 (notification turn):   the same assistant messages are sent without either (1,089, 291 and 1,051 chars dropped)
```

Nothing else in those messages changes. The final message before the notification, which had 1,520 characters of reasoning, is also sent without it.

### Affected version

1.139.1. The code is unchanged on `main`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In the Local agent, select Kimi K3
2. Ask it to run a command that prints nothing for more than 5 minutes as a normal foreground command, for example `sleep 320 && echo done`
3. After 5 minutes the command moves to the background; when it finishes, VS Code sends the notification
4. Compare the raw request bodies before and after the notification: the earlier assistant messages lose `reasoning_text` and `reasoning_opaque`

### Expected behavior

A system-initiated notification continues the current task rather than starting a new user turn, so the model's reasoning from that task is kept.

issues.title: [Regression] Extension Development Host fails to start because js-debug connects to IPv6 localhost on VS Code 1.139.1
issues.body:
## Type of issue

Bug / Regression

## Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?

Yes. The issue still occurs after adding `--disable-extensions` to the Extension Development Host arguments.

## VS Code version

```text
Version: 1.139.1 (Universal)
Commit: 04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1
Date: 2026-09-25T03:40:57Z
Electron: 43.6.0
ElectronBuildId: 15274685
Chromium: 150.0.7871.250
Node.js: 24.20.0
V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0
@github/copilot: 1.0.85.r35379093703.g3514c9a
@github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.15.35393089353.gfc44743
OS: Darwin arm64 23.6.0
```

The bundled JavaScript Debugger version is `1.117.0`.

## Regression

This issue is reproducible in VS Code 1.139.1. The same repository and debug configuration work correctly in VS Code 1.138.0 on the same machine.

## Reproduction repository

https://github.com/onlymisaky/vscode-proxy-switch

Debug configuration:

https://github.com/onlymisaky/vscode-proxy-switch/blob/master/.vscode/launch.json

## Steps to reproduce

1. Clone and prepare the reproduction repository:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/onlymisaky/vscode-proxy-switch.git
   cd vscode-proxy-switch
   npm install
   ```

2. Open the repository in VS Code 1.139.1.
3. Press `F5` and select `debug proxy switch`.
4. Wait for the Extension Development Host window to open.

The issue can also be reproduced after adding `--disable-extensions` to the `args` array in `.vscode/launch.json`.

## Expected behavior

The debugger attaches to the Extension Development Host. The extension activates, its commands are registered, and the controls in the `Proxy Switch` view can be used normally.

This is the behavior observed with VS Code 1.138.0.

## Actual behavior

The Extension Development Host window opens and the extension's declarative UI contributions are visible, including its Activity Bar icon, view title, and welcome button.

However:

- The extension never finishes loading.
- None of its commands or buttons work.
- The debug toolbar appears briefly and then disappears.
- After approximately 10 seconds, the Extension Development Host reports:

  ```text
  Extension host did not start in 10 seconds (debugBrk: true)
  ```

- In some attempts, it eventually also reports:

  ```text
  The local extension host took longer than 60s to send its ready message.
  ```

Using `Ctrl+F5` / Run Without Debugging avoids the debugger attachment and can be used as a temporary workaround.

## Relevant logs

The parent VS Code extension host log repeatedly reports that the bundled `ms-vscode.js-debug` extension cannot connect to the debug port through the IPv6 localhost address:

```text
ExtensionService#_doActivateExtension ms-vscode.js-debug,
activationEvent: 'onDebugResolve:extensionHost'

RequestError: connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:53447
    at ClientRequest.<anonymous>
    (.../extensions/ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js:23:14613)
    ...
    at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete]
    (node:net:2017:16)
```

The same error occurs repeatedly with different dynamically allocated ports:

```text
ECONNREFUSED ::1:53219
ECONNREFUSED ::1:53328
ECONNREFUSED ::1:53447
ECONNREFUSED ::1:53451
ECONNREFUSED ::1:55376
ECONNREFUSED ::1:55499
```

The Extension Development Host renderer log contains:

```text
[LocalProcessExtensionHost]: Extension host did not start in 10 seconds (debugBrk: true)

Error received from starting extension host (kind: LocalProcess)
The local extension host took longer than 60s to send its ready message.
```

On this machine, `localhost` resolves to IPv6 first:

```text
::1
127.0.0.1
```

This looks similar to the previously reported IPv4/IPv6 debugger connection problem in microsoft/vscode#140536. That issue was addressed in js-debug by falling back to `127.0.0.1` when a request to `localhost` fails.

In VS Code 1.139.1, the logs show repeated attempts against `::1`, but no successful IPv4 fallback.

## Additional information

- The extension builds successfully before the Extension Development Host is launched.
- The generated extension entry point exists at `dist/extension.js`.
- The problem happens before the extension's `activate()` function can run.
- No equivalent failure occurs in VS Code 1.138.0.
- The behavior is reproducible across multiple launches and dynamically allocated debug ports.

issues.title: Agents window: colored session groups and collections

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

issues.body:
## Problem

The Agents window sessions list is hard to scan. Custom groups, workspace sections, Pinned, and Chats all render as the same grey text, so with a lot of sessions it reads as a wall of grey and groups don't stand out.

To work around this today, I create empty custom groups named `===================== ENG`, `===== PRIV`, and `===== MISC` as visual dividers between engineering, personal, and miscellaneous work.

Browsers already solve both problems:
- **Colored tab groups:** a solid colored header, and a colored rail on the tabs inside. A collapsed group is a small color pill.
- **Workspaces:** separate sets of groups and tabs (for example, personal vs. two work contexts) that you switch between with an icon strip.

This exploration brings both ideas to the sessions list.

## Exploration

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Interactive mockup** | https://yoyokrazy.github.io/agents-window-color-groups-mockup/ (Dark, [Light](https://yoyokrazy.github.io/agents-window-color-groups-mockup/?theme=light), [High contrast](https://yoyokrazy.github.io/agents-window-color-groups-mockup/?theme=hc)) |
| **Walkthrough video** | https://yoyokrazy.github.io/agents-window-color-groups-mockup/walkthrough.mp4 |
| **Mockup source** | https://github.com/Yoyokrazy/agents-window-color-groups-mockup (a Component Explorer fixture built from real VS Code components) |
| **Implementation branch** | [`agents/agents-window-color-grouping-mockup`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/agents/agents-window-color-grouping-mockup) ([compare](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/compare/main...agents/agents-window-color-grouping-mockup)) |

![Interactive mockup: colored groups and collections in the Agents window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yoyokrazy/agents-window-color-groups-mockup/main/media/demo-dark.png)

## Proposal

| Area | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Colored groups** | Every custom group has a color: a named palette color (grey, blue, red, yellow, green, pink, purple, cyan, orange) or a custom hex. New groups get the next unused color. The default **Rail** style shows a colored header pill, plus a colored rail next to the group's sessions. |
| **Readable labels** | The label color on a colored header is picked automatically (light or dark, whichever has the higher WCAG contrast), and can be forced to light or dark. |
| **Collapsed groups** | A collapsed group is a compact pill with a session count and its most urgent status: needs input, then in progress, then unread. |
| **Workspace and built-in sections** | Workspace sections, **Pinned**, and **Chats** can optionally be colored too. Uncolored sections look the same as today. Pinned and Chats can only be recolored: they keep their names and their place in the list. |
| **Collections** | User-defined sets of groups, workspaces, and sessions, like browser workspaces, for example Engineering / Personal / Misc. Each has a name, a codicon, and a color, and the list shows only the active collection. You switch collections with an icon strip or the Sessions header menu; each collection remembers its last open session. To move sessions, groups, or workspaces to another collection, drag them onto its icon or use **Move to Collection**. With a single collection, the list works as it does today. The name "Collections" avoids a clash with the existing meaning of "workspace" in VS Code. |
| **Editing** | Hover actions, F2, and context menus open an editor with a name field, color swatches, an optional custom color picker, the text color (Auto / Light / Dark), and a live contrast preview. Every change can be undone. |
| **Theming** | Palette colors are theme tokens with dark, light, and high contrast defaults, and only standard codicons are used. The window frame doesn't change color with the collection. |

The mockup also compares other group styles (**Outline**, **Tint**, **Dot**), a compact density, and other places for the collection switcher (sidebar tabs, or the header menu only).

## Status

The mockup is complete and published. The implementation branch is in progress and not ready for review yet. So far it has:
- services for header colors and collections, with profile-scoped persistence;
- colored groups and sections in the sessions list;
- the collection switcher and navigation;
- a `SESSIONS_LIST.md` update covering the new list state.

## Open questions

- [ ] Rail as the default group style, or one of the alternatives?
- [ ] Where the collection switcher lives: the title bar strip, sidebar tabs, or only the Sessions header menu?
- [ ] "Collections" as the name.
- [ ] Should Pinned and Chats allow more than a color change (rename, move between collections)?
- [ ] Should collections ship behind a setting at first?

issues.title: Local agent: automatic retry after a dropped stream keeps the abandoned attempt's reasoning and tool calls

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When a streamed response fails partway through and the Local agent retries it automatically, the reasoning and tool calls already received from the failed attempt are kept. The retry's reasoning is appended to them, and the next request sends both as a single assistant message.

`_retryAfterError` signals the retry with `retryReason` and calls `fetchMany` again with the same callback ([chatMLFetcher.ts#L902](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4f5c0700138956542ba70734adb986801c463222/extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompt/node/chatMLFetcher.ts#L902)). The chat UI clears its partial response on that marker, but the tool loop's callback ignores it and keeps accumulating into the same `thinkingItem` and `toolCalls` ([toolCallingLoop.ts#L1911](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4f5c0700138956542ba70734adb986801c463222/extensions/copilot/src/extension/intents/node/toolCallingLoop.ts#L1911)).

Kimi K3 through Copilot, with the connection reset after the first reasoning deltas of one response:

```
abandoned attempt:  41 chars of reasoning, then connection reset
automatic retry:    68 chars of reasoning, then read_file
next request:       {"role": "assistant", "reasoning_text": "<109 chars: the abandoned 41 followed by the retry's 68>", "tool_calls": [read_file]}
```

The same run without the reset sent back exactly the 134 characters it received. Replaying recorded responses through the same code:
- A disconnect after reasoning, followed by a retry with the same response, sends that reasoning twice (123 → 246 chars).
- A disconnect after two tool calls leaves four tool calls recorded on the round.

### Affected version

1.139.0-insider (also present in 1.133.0). The code is unchanged on `main`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Point `github.copilot.advanced.debug.overrideCapiUrl` at a local relay that forwards to the Copilot API and resets the connection once, after the first reasoning deltas of a response
2. In the Local agent, select Kimi K3 and send a prompt that reads a file
3. Let VS Code retry automatically
4. Compare the retry's reasoning with `reasoning_text` in the next request: it also contains the abandoned attempt's reasoning

### Expected behavior

A retried request discards the abandoned attempt's state, and the round records only the successful attempt's reasoning and tool calls. Resetting the tool loop's per-attempt state (`toolCalls`, `thinkingItem`, `statefulMarker`, `phase`, `compaction`) when `delta.retryReason` arrives fixes it in our replay.

issues.title: Chat Completions models lose reasoning from earlier user turns (breaks Kimi K3 preserved thinking)

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

For models on the Chat Completions API, reasoning from earlier user turns is dropped from the prompt. Within one turn, assistant messages keep their reasoning across tool calls. Once the user sends another message, the same assistant messages are resent without it.

The history renderer only replays reasoning from earlier turns for Responses, or for Messages models with adaptive thinking ([toolCalling.tsx#L141-L143](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4f5c0700138956542ba70734adb986801c463222/extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/panel/toolCalling.tsx#L141-L143)). Earlier turns are rendered as historical ([agentConversationHistory.tsx#L117](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4f5c0700138956542ba70734adb986801c463222/extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/agent/agentConversationHistory.tsx#L117)), so for Chat Completions their reasoning is removed. This applies to both Copilot-provided and custom Chat Completions models. The same assistant message from Kimi K3 in the Local agent:

```
last request of turn 1:  {"role": "assistant", "reasoning_text": "<1,819 chars>", "reasoning_opaque": "<36 chars>", "tool_calls": [...]}
first request of turn 2: {"role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [...]}
```

Everything else in the message and its tool results is identical.

[Kimi K3](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) is trained with its reasoning preserved across tool calls and user turns, and expects `reasoning_content` passed back unchanged. Its chat template renders an empty thinking block for any assistant message without reasoning, so after a few user turns K3 sees a long history of empty reasoning.

### Affected version

1.139.0-insider (b040d43). The code is unchanged on `main`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In the Local agent, select Kimi K3 with High thinking effort
2. Send a prompt that makes a few tool calls, for example reading two files
3. Send a second message
4. Compare the raw request bodies for the last request of turn 1 and the first request of turn 2: the turn-1 assistant messages lose `reasoning_text` and `reasoning_opaque`

### Expected behavior

Models that expect preserved thinking, such as Kimi K3, get their reasoning back on every earlier assistant message, as Responses models already do. A per-model opt-in would keep the protection for models that reject replayed thinking (#318076).

issues.title: Custom OpenAI-compatible models: `reasoning_content` is never sent back when the provider streams it without an id

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With a custom Chat Completions model (`github.copilot.chat.customOAIModels`, `"thinking": true`), VS Code parses streamed `reasoning_content` but never sends it back on later requests.

`OpenAIEndpoint.getCompletionsCallback` only echoes reasoning `if (data?.id)` ([openAIEndpoint.ts#L160](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4f5c0700138956542ba70734adb986801c463222/extensions/copilot/src/extension/byok/node/openAIEndpoint.ts#L160)). The id comes only from `cot_id`, `reasoning_opaque` or `signature` ([thinkingUtils.ts#L30](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4f5c0700138956542ba70734adb986801c463222/extensions/copilot/src/platform/thinking/common/thinkingUtils.ts#L30)). Standard OpenAI-compatible servers (SGLang, vLLM and similar) stream `reasoning_content` with no id, so every later request carries the assistant message's `content` and `tool_calls`, but no reasoning.

Models that expect their reasoning back on every assistant message degrade badly. With Kimi K3 served by SGLang, the model reasoned for 68 tokens on the first step and exactly 3 tokens on every later step. After six steps it repeated the same turn until cancelled. Replaying the second request with the first step's reasoning added back gave 175, 303 and 244 reasoning tokens, versus 3, 3 and 3 without it. Adding a `cot_id` to each reasoning delta in a proxy fixes it.

### Affected version

1.138.0 and 1.139.1. The code is unchanged on `main`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Serve a reasoning model behind an OpenAI-compatible server that streams `reasoning_content`, for example SGLang with `--reasoning-parser`, and log the requests it receives
2. Add it under `github.copilot.chat.customOAIModels` with `"thinking": true` and `"toolCalling": true`
3. Run an agent request that makes a few tool calls
4. The responses stream `reasoning_content`, but the assistant messages in later requests have no `reasoning_content`

### Expected behavior

With `"thinking": true`, reasoning received as `reasoning_content` is sent back on its assistant message, whether or not the provider supplied an id.

issues.title: Activated tool group is collapsed again when over 128 tools

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
- Copilot Chat: 0.67.0 (also on `main`)
- VS Code: 1.139.1
- Feature: Agent mode

With more than 128 tools enabled, a virtual tool group the model activates can be collapsed again before the next request. The model is told "Tools activated: …" but never receives those tools, and keeps re-activating the group.

Seen with the Slack and Notion MCP servers: the model activated Notion's group repeatedly and never got `notion-fetch`.

Cause: `ToolGrouping.didCall` doesn't update the activated group's `lastUsedOnTurn`, so the trim treats it as least recently used. Fix and test in #338812.

issues.title: Feature Request: Enhance CLI and Bootstrap Module Logging/Extensibility for Developer Tools
issues.body:
Summary
As a developer working closely with VS Code architecture and custom extension tooling, I would like to propose an enhancement to the core initialization and bootstrap processes (src/main.js / CLI bootstrap flow).

Specifically, providing cleaner extension hooks or enhanced diagnostic logging during the ESM bootstrap and NLS configuration phase (resolveNLSConfiguration) would greatly help developers debug startup behaviors and integrate custom CLI workflows.

Details / Use Case
Current Behavior: The core bootstrap cleanly initializes portable support, NLS configurations, and hands over to the CLI server (cli.js), but offers limited flexibility for external monitoring or safe injection of custom diagnostic layers during startup.

Proposed Feature: Introduce cleaner extension points or structured telemetry/logging hooks right after await bootstrapESM(); to allow developers to track startup performance and CLI launch flags (VSCODE_CLI) more transparently.

Does this issue relate to any existing documentation?
No

issues.title: Copilot Chat OTel: set service.instance.id on the resource

labels.name: otel
labels.description: OTel (OpenTelemetry)

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

The Copilot Chat OTel resource has `service.name`, `service.version` and `session.id`, but no `service.instance.id`:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/bdc5ebe5a7df49696921f75726fb51b3871b0b28/extensions/copilot/src/platform/otel/node/otelServiceImpl.ts#L135-L139

The metrics are cumulative and exported every 10 seconds. Prometheus-compatible backends (Prometheus, Mimir, Grafana Cloud) map `service.name` to `job` and `service.instance.id` to `instance`. Other resource attributes such as `session.id` only end up in `target_info`. So the metrics from every VS Code window and every user go into the same series, and counters like `copilot_chat.lines_of_code.count` or `gen_ai.client.token.usage` can't be summed correctly.

Please also set `service.instance.id`, for example to the same value as `session.id` or to a random UUID per window. The [semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/service/) recommend generating one. Each window then gets its own series, and `sum()` across instances gives the right result.

Related: open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification#4577

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A (Agent Host)
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 source build
- OS Version: Windows
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode sandbox permissions
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Agent Host logs show `session.options.update` disabling sandboxing, followed by `session.sandbox.disableForSession` failing with `sandbox is already disabled`.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Start a sandboxed agent turn and leave a Run Outside Sandbox permission request pending.
2. Turn sandboxing off, then select **Allow in this Session** on the pending request.

The sandbox configuration update and approval are serialized. After the Off update completes, the approval redundantly calls `disableForSession`. The SDK throws because sandboxing is already disabled, so VS Code rejects the approved operation and can overwrite the synchronized sandbox state with the stale enabled value.

Expected: skip the redundant disable call and approve the pending operation once when synchronized session state is already disabled.

issues.title: Agents Window: stacked Changes toolbars make Toggle Details look duplicated
issues.body:
## Description

In the Agents Window's single-pane **Changes** editor, the narrow side pane shows two stacked icon-only action rows. The **Toggle Details** button in the tab/title row sits directly above a second ellipsis button in the Changes editor header, followed by another horizontal divider. This makes the lower ellipsis and divider look like duplicated or detached parts of **Toggle Details**.

The composition does not feel calm or self-explanatory: two visually equivalent action clusters are stacked without enough hierarchy to show that they belong to different surfaces.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Agents Window using the single-pane detail layout.
2. Open a created session that has changes.
3. Select the **Changes** tab.
4. Make the side pane narrow enough that the header actions are predominantly icon-only.
5. Observe **Toggle Details** in the editor title row, then the code-review action and ellipsis directly beneath it, plus the additional divider above the first file card.

## Expected

The title/layout actions and Changes-specific actions have a clear visual hierarchy. The Changes overflow should not look like a second control attached to **Toggle Details**, and adjacent section boundaries should not read as redundant dividers.

## Actual

The stacked icon-only rows and nearby separators make the lower ellipsis appear to be another part of **Toggle Details**.

## Cause

This is not one button rendering twice; it is two independent toolbar surfaces stacked together:

- `Toggle Details` is contributed to `MenuId.EditorTitleLayout` and rendered in the editor title/tab row (`singlePaneExistingSessionStrategy.ts`).
- `SinglePaneMainEditorPart` always enables a separate full-width editor-group header using `Menus.SessionsEditorHeaderPrimary` and `Menus.SessionsEditorHeaderLayout` (`singlePaneEditorPart.ts`).
- In the Changes editor, that lower header contributes **Run Code Review** as a primary action, while collapse/expand and diff-view actions are secondary items that render behind the toolbar's ellipsis (`codeReview.contributions.ts`, `changesViewActions.ts`).
- The tab/header boundary and the first multi-diff card border add closely spaced horizontal strokes, reinforcing the impression that the second row is an accidental duplicate.

The full-width header was introduced/aligned in #335336. The issue is the resulting narrow-width composition and hierarchy, rather than duplicate command registration.

## Related

- #336898 concerns overlapping title actions when tab wrapping is enabled; this report is about the separate stacked Changes header and overflow even without action overlap.

![Stacked icon-only toolbars beneath Toggle Details in the Agents Window Changes editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8911dfd7-0b75-4c63-a59b-d03397add267)

issues.body:
## Copilot Chat: screenshot tool requests fail with upstream file-download 404 on GPT models

### Environment
- OS: Windows
- VS Code: 1.139.1
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.67.0

### Description
Using the browser screenshot tool (`screenshot_page`) with GPT models fails consistently with a 400 response stating that an upstream file download returned 404. Clicking `Retry` succeeds for some snapshots but also fails consistently for others.  Reproduced with an internal page, a locally hosted site page, and the publicly accessible https://www.kernel.org/, so it does not appear specific to one website.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In VS Code Copilot Chat, select a GPT-5.4 or GPT-6 model, using either the Luna or Sol variant.
2. Make a browser page available in the shared Browser Pages context.
3. Ask Copilot to take a snapshot of the page and describe it.
4. Observe the request failure.
5. Pressing “Try Again” succeeds for some snapshot images, may failed consistently / repeatedly.

### Expected
Copilot captures the shared page and responds with a description.

### Actual
Copilot displays an error similar to:

> Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.  
> Reason: Request Failed: 400  
> `{"error":{"message":"Error while downloading file. Upstream status code: 404.","code":"invalid_request_body"}}`

### Model comparison
- Affected: GPT-5.4 and GPT-6, both Luna and Sol.
- Not affected in my testing: Grok 4.7 and local models with vision enabled.

issues.title: Improve type safety and future-proofing in IToolResultContentRenderer
issues.body:
The `IToolResultContentRenderer` service currently handles rendering tool result content parts (such as `LanguageModelTextPart`, `LanguageModelPromptTsxPart`, and `LanguageModelDataPart`) into human-readable strings. 

To improve robustness on the hot path and ensure long-term maintainability as new language model part types are introduced, we should enhance the underlying implementation with stricter type narrowing and defensive handling for edge cases (e.g., unexpected or unhandled part types, `null`/`undefined` iterables).

### Proposed Changes
* Introduce exhaustive type checking (using `never` type assertions) within the content rendering logic to catch unhandled part types at compile time.
* Add defensive programming guards to gracefully handle edge cases in `Iterable<unknown>` without triggering runtime panics or expensive performance penalties on the hot path.

issues.title: Copilot edit-agent request stays active for about five minutes; cancelling reports "patch cancelled"
issues.body:
### Description

While asking Copilot Agent to add tests in an existing JavaScript project, the chat UI displayed “This is taking longer than usual.” After about five minutes, I clicked Cancel and the UI reported “patch cancelled.”

The Copilot Chat extension log contains a matching cancelled edit-agent request:

```text
2026-09-29 15:45:49.809 [info] ccreq:993f3a7a.copilotmd | cancelled | gpt-6-luna | 310172ms | [panel/editAgent]
```

The request appears to have started around 15:40:39 and was cancelled at 15:45:49. This matches the delay shown in the UI. A later request in the same session logged editing activity with `apply_patch`, but available logs do not reveal what operation was active during the cancelled request or why it took so long. The session-specific debug log contains only a `session_start` record.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Copilot Agent edit mode, ask it to add tests to an existing source file.
2. Wait while the UI displays “This is taking longer than usual.”
3. After about five minutes, click Cancel.

### Actual behavior

The request remains active for about five minutes. Cancelling it displays “patch cancelled.” The extension log records the edit-agent request as cancelled after 310172 ms, but does not show the cause or the operation that was running.

### Expected behavior

The edit should complete or report a useful error without an unexplained multi-minute wait. If cancellation is necessary, the UI should clearly indicate which operation was cancelled and return promptly.

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.140.0-insider
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.68.2026092802
- OS: Linux
- Model: `gpt-6-luna`

This report describes the observed behavior and available log evidence; it does not assume that `apply_patch` itself was the source of the delay.

issues.body:

<!-- Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->

<!-- Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No

<!-- If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.139.1 (Universal)
- OS Version: Tahoe 26.6.2
- GitHub Copilot extension version: N/A
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension version: N/A
- Environment: Local
- VS Code channel: Stable

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure more than 100 valid and uniquely named GitHub Copilot custom agents.
2. Open the **Agent Customizations** view in VS Code.
3. Select **Agents**.
4. Observe that the total number of agents stops at exactly 100.
5. Search for one of the omitted agents by its exact name.
6. Observe that the omitted agent cannot be found.
7. Move or temporarily remove one or more agents that are currently visible.
8. Reload the VS Code window and reopen Agent Customizations.
9. Observe that previously omitted agents now appear, while the total remains exactly 100.

## Expected Behavior

Agent Customizations should discover and display all valid custom agents.

If 100 agents is an intentional supported limit, the UI should clearly communicate that limit and indicate that additional agents were omitted.

## Actual Behavior

Agent Customizations reports exactly 100 agents:

- Workspace: 0
- User: 98
- Local: 2
- Total: 100

There are 128 agents available, so 28 agents are omitted.

The omitted agents cannot be found using the search field, even when searching by their exact names.

## Validation Performed

I have reproduced this behavior consistently and performed the following checks:

- Confirmed that all 128 agents have unique names.
- Confirmed that the omitted agents cannot be found through exact-name search.
- Validated and revalidated the agent files and YAML frontmatter.
- Moved agents between locations to test the 100-agent boundary.
- Confirmed that removing or moving visible agents causes previously hidden agents to appear.
- Confirmed that the displayed total remains exactly 100.

The most significant result is:

> Removing or moving displayed agents causes previously omitted agents to appear, while the total remains exactly 100.

This indicates that the missing agents are valid and discoverable, but the Agent Customizations collection appears to be truncated at 100 entries.

## Additional Comparison

The classic VS Code Chat experience can access my 128 agents:

- 128 total agents

By comparison, Agent Customizations reports exactly 100 agents and does not provide pagination, a continuation control, a warning, or a "load more" action.

I understand that the MCP catalog and Agent Customizations may use different discovery mechanisms. However, the remove-and-replace boundary test demonstrates that valid omitted agents become visible when other agents are removed.

## Possible Cause

The behavior appears consistent with one of the following:

- A fixed discovery limit or page size of 100.
- A paginated query where only the first page is processed.
- A continuation token that is not handled.
- A collection that is truncated to 100 before being passed to the UI.
- A UI-side limit applied before search and filtering.
- An intentional but undocumented maximum.

## Impact

Users with more than 100 custom agents cannot:

- Discover all configured agents in Agent Customizations.
- Find omitted agents using the search field.
- Inspect or manage omitted agents through the UI.
- Reliably determine which agents are available.
- Know that results have been truncated.

The UI displays `100`, rather than `100+` or `100 of 128`, and does not warn that additional valid agents were omitted.

## Documentation

I could not find a documented maximum of 100 custom agents in the VS Code documentation for:

- Custom agents
- Agent Customizations
- The Agents Window
- GitHub Copilot custom-agent configuration

If the 100-agent limit is intentional, could the supported maximum and truncation behavior be documented?

## Request

Could the VS Code team confirm whether 100 is an intentional limit?

If it is not intentional, Agent Customizations should retrieve and display all valid custom agents. If pagination or another limit is required, the UI should indicate that the results were truncated and provide a way to access the remaining agents.

issues.title: Support versionless model-family aliases that select the newest model in custom agents
issues.body:
## Feature request

Support versionless model-family names in the `model` frontmatter of custom agent files (`.agent.md`) so they resolve to the newest available model in that family.

For example, a setting such as:

```yaml
model: GPT Luna (copilot)
```

would mean "use the newest available GPT Luna model from Copilot" instead of requiring the agent author to update a version-specific name after each model release. This is illustrative syntax; the request is for documented versionless aliases, not a claim about current resolution behavior.

## Motivation

Maintaining multiple custom agents requires repeated edits when newer model versions become available. A stable family alias would let agent authors opt in to new versions without changing every agent file.

## Suggested behavior

- A documented model-family name without a version number resolves to the newest stable version available to the current user from the specified provider.
- An explicitly versioned name continues to pin that version.
- Resolution stays within the selected model family and provider, rather than switching to an unrelated model.
- Preview models are excluded unless explicitly requested.
- The UI shows the concrete model selected by the alias.
- If no matching model is available, show a clear message instead of silently selecting an unrelated model.

## Related request

#297210 requests latest-model selection for prompt files. This request proposes versionless family aliases specifically for custom agent model configuration; the same convention could serve both file types.

issues.title: Copilot Chat OTel: emit github.copilot.auto_mode on chat/invoke_agent spans when Auto model selection is used

labels.name: otel
labels.description: OTel (OpenTelemetry)

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Feature request

Please add an OTel attribute to Copilot Chat's `chat` (and `invoke_agent`) spans that says whether the model was picked by **Auto** model selection. Using the canonical `github.copilot.*` namespace:

- `github.copilot.auto_mode` (boolean): `true` when the request went through an `AutoChatEndpoint`
- optionally `github.copilot.auto_mode.tier` (string): the routing tier sent to `POST /auto` (`efficiency` / `balance` / `intelligence` / `fast`)

## Why

When a user picks **Auto** in the model picker, the extension calls `POST /auto`, wraps the selected model in an `AutoChatEndpoint`, and the backend bills the request at the auto discount (`discounted_costs` / `billing.auto_discount`, currently 10% on paid plans).

In the exported OTel data, though, `gen_ai.request.model` is set from `endpoint.model`, which for an `AutoChatEndpoint` is already the concrete model:

- `src/extension/prompt/node/chatMLFetcher.ts` (`[GenAiAttr.REQUEST_MODEL]: chatEndpointInfo.model`)
- `src/extension/intents/node/toolCallingLoop.ts` (`span.setAttribute(GenAiAttr.REQUEST_MODEL, endpoint.model)`)

So an OTel consumer can't tell an auto-routed request from one where the user explicitly picked the same model. The only way to infer it is to divide `copilot_chat.copilot_usage_nano_aiu` by tokens × list price and look for the discount. That's fragile: it needs a price table kept in sync, and it breaks if the discount changes.

Copilot CLI already reports `gen_ai.request.model = "auto"` for these requests, so today the two clients disagree.

The extension already computes this flag. `isAutoModel(endpoint)` is sent to the internal telemetry events (`chatMLFetcherTelemetry.ts`, `chatParticipantTelemetry.ts`, `automode.autoV2Decision`), but it never reaches the OTel spans.

## Use cases

- Cost attribution and chargeback: explaining why the same model has different effective per-token rates for different users or sessions.
- Adoption reporting: how much traffic uses Auto vs. a pinned model.
- Consistency between the VS Code and CLI OTel data.

## Suggested implementation

In `src/platform/otel/common/genAiAttributes.ts` (`GitHubCopilotAttr`):

```ts
/** True when the model was selected by Auto model selection. */
AUTO_MODE: 'github.copilot.auto_mode',
/** Auto routing tier requested from `POST /auto`. */
AUTO_MODE_TIER: 'github.copilot.auto_mode.tier',
```

In the `chat` span attributes in `chatMLFetcher.ts`:

```ts
...(isAutoModel(chatEndpointInfo) === 1 ? { [GitHubCopilotAttr.AUTO_MODE]: true } : {}),
```

and the same (`isAutoModel(endpoint) === 1`) on the other spans that report `gen_ai.request.model` from a chat endpoint:

- `src/extension/intents/node/toolCallingLoop.ts`: `invoke_agent` span (agent / ask / edit, including subagents)
- `src/extension/inlineChat2/node/inlineChatIntent.ts`: `invoke_agent Inline Chat` span

For Copilot CLI sessions hosted in VS Code (`src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/node/copilotcliSession.ts`), `AutoChatEndpoint` isn't used. The `invoke_agent copilotcli` span already carries `gen_ai.request.model = "auto"`, but the synthesized per-turn `chat` spans (`_emitChatSpan`) use the resolved `turn.model`. Setting `github.copilot.auto_mode = true` there when the session's model id is `auto` would keep those spans consistent too.

The tier is already stored in the automode cache entry, so it could be exposed on `AutoChatEndpoint` and emitted the same way.

issues.title: Sessions: Hide other controls while editing a session name
issues.body:
When editing a session name, the other session controls remain visible. The nearby **Mark as Done** checkmark can be mistaken for the control that saves the edited name, making it easy to complete the session accidentally.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session.
2. Start editing the session name.
3. Observe that the other session controls, including **Mark as Done**, remain visible next to the name editor.

## Expected behavior

While the session name is being edited, hide unrelated session controls. Only the controls for confirming or cancelling the name edit should be visible.

## Actual behavior

Unrelated controls remain visible and can be confused with the save action.

issues.title: Show file paths in customization page list items
issues.body:
Customization page list items should show their source file paths again. The paths are useful for understanding where customizations are defined, diagnosing different setups, and interpreting screenshots without opening every item.

## Expected behavior

- Show the source file path on customization page list items.
- Sanitize long or intimidating paths where possible, for example by replacing the user data directory with a readable variable.
- Ensure the full path is available in the item hover.
- Keep the path available in the details view as well.

issues.title: Stale Local OTel reload notification remains after managed policy recovers

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: candidate
labels.description: Issue identified as probable candidate for fixing in the next release

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

labels.name: otel
labels.description: OTel (OpenTelemetry)

issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.68.2026092904
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0-insider (commit f9bb522f5746a56791aa4407a3db5c1b5cd3ad04)
- OS Version: macOS
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Enterprise-managed Local Copilot OTel policy recovery
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): N/A
- Logs:
  - Before the repro, Local OTel was healthy: `[OTel] Instrumentation enabled — exporter=otlp-http endpoint=http://localhost:4318/ captureContent=false`.
  - The failed refresh settled the account policy gate as restricted with reason `managedSettingsRefresh`.
  - The retry applied the same managed settings and the gate settled inactive.
  - After accepting the stale reload action in an earlier run, the successor Extension Host logged: `[OTel] Telemetry policy is still not applied after reloading. Not prompting for another window reload.`

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure an enforced managed policy with `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true` and Local Copilot OTel enabled at `http://localhost:4318` using `http/json`.
2. Start VS Code Insiders and confirm Local Copilot OTel initializes successfully at that managed endpoint.
3. Make the managed-settings endpoint unavailable, then run **Developer: Sync Account Policy**. Wait for the refresh to fail and the policy gate to settle Blocked/restricted.
4. Restore the managed-settings endpoint with the exact same successful OTel policy as in step 1.
5. Select **Retry** and wait for managed settings to be applied and the policy gate to return to inactive.
6. Open Notification Center (bell on bottom right).

Expected: The Local Copilot OTel reload notification created for the temporary Blocked state is cleared because the restored settled policy matches the exporter already running in the Extension Host. No reload is required.

Actual: **Copilot OTel settings changed - a reload is required for the change to take effect** remains actionable after the identical policy is restored. Accepting it causes an unnecessary window reload and can then produce the warning that the telemetry policy is still not applied after reloading.

This reproduced twice from a known healthy Local exporter on port 4318. Agent Host correctly restarted fail-closed on the failed refresh and restarted again when policy was restored; this issue is specifically about the Local Copilot OTel reload notification/recovery record. Related changes: #338623 and #338645.

issues.title: Chat: Sticky user prompt background covers its border while scrolling
issues.body:
When a user prompt becomes sticky while scrolling through chat, its background covers the prompt border. The overlap changes as the conversation scrolls.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open Chat with enough conversation history to scroll.
2. Scroll until a user prompt becomes the sticky item.
3. Observe the edge of the sticky prompt.

**Expected**
The sticky prompt preserves a visible border and does not cover it with its background.

**Actual**
The sticky prompt background overlays the border while scrolling.

Reported from a visual review with screenshots showing the border before and after the sticky state.

This would preserve the motion while making the animation feel calmer and less visually prominent.

issues.title: AI Customization does not refresh newly added MCP servers until restart
issues.body:
## Type of Bug

Bug

## Description

AI Customization does not refresh when a new MCP server is added to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`. The server appears only after restarting VS Code.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code and the AI Customization editor.
2. Add a new MCP server to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`.
3. Return to or reopen the AI Customization editor.

## Expected Behavior

The newly added MCP server appears without restarting VS Code, consistent with newly added skills.

## Actual Behavior

The server is not shown until VS Code is restarted.

Related to #338614.

issues.title: AI Customization does not show the source of built-in MCP servers
issues.body:
## Type of Bug

Bug

## Description

The AI Customization MCP server details do not identify the source of built-in MCP servers. For file-backed MCP servers, the configuration file can be opened from the details page or through **Show Configuration**, but built-in servers provide no equivalent source information.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the AI Customization editor.
2. Select a built-in MCP server.
3. Inspect its details and the `...` menu.

## Expected Behavior

The details page clearly identifies that the MCP server is built in and shows its source or provider.

## Actual Behavior

No source information is shown for built-in MCP servers.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (core Agents window / Agent Host code path; reproduced in a unit test)

<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0-insider (e741ab1c964b9fbb11bffed2c0a145af22dad54f, 2026-09-29)
- OS Version: macOS 27.0

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In the Agents window, run a Copilot CLI (local Agent Host) session that spawns subagents, so the session has more than one chat in its catalog.
2. Send another request in that session, then switch to a different session (or the new-session view) and wait more than 30s.
3. Have the session's **main** chat ask for input.
4. 🐛 The title bar shows the session as requiring input, but its row in the sessions list keeps showing the in-progress state instead of needs-input.

### Root cause

- The title bar indicator (`BlockedSessions`) reads the aggregate `session.status`, which stays fresh via the root `sessionSummaryChanged` notification.
- The sessions list row reads `session.mainChat.status` (`getSessionRowStatus` with `deriveStatusFromMainChat`, since #332931).
- When a session has surfaced peer chats (tool-origin subagents count), the main chat status is `_defaultChatStatusOverride`, which is only refreshed from `SessionState` snapshots in `_applyChatCatalog`. The provider's session-state listener is idle-released 30s after the session leaves the viewport (`_keepSessionStateAlive`), after which the override is frozen.
- #333804 re-acquires session state on `ChatTurnComplete`, but an input request does not complete the turn. It arrives as `session/chatUpdated` + `session/inputNeededSet` + root `sessionSummaryChanged`, none of which refresh the override. In the observed case the wire subscription was still held by another owner, so the `session/chatUpdated` action reached the client, but the provider's `onDidAction` handler does not process it.

### Evidence (AHP log, UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 15:53:54 | Default chat status → `8` (InProgress) while the session is visible → override = InProgress |
| — | User navigates away; the provider's session-state listener is idle-released |
| 15:59:56 | Default chat status → `24` (InputNeeded), `session/inputNeededSet` (kind `chatInput`, on the default chat), root `sessionSummaryChanged` status → `56` (IsRead \| InputNeeded) |

Result: `session.status` = NeedsInput (title bar), `mainChat.status` = InProgress (sessions list).

A focused test in the `multi-chat catalog` suite of `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` reproduces it: after the 30s idle release, pushing an InputNeeded default-chat state plus a `SessionSummaryChanged` notification yields `{ session: NeedsInput, mainChat: InProgress }`.

### Suggested fix

Generalize #333804: in `_handleSessionSummaryChanged`, when the mapped aggregate status changes for a session whose default-chat status is overridden (multi-chat), re-acquire the session state (`_keepSessionStateAlive`) after the transaction so `_applyChatCatalog` refreshes the override. The root notification always arrives, so this also works when no wire subscription exists.

### Related

When a hidden subagent or side chat needs input, the aggregate is NeedsInput while the main chat is genuinely InProgress. `getSessionListChats` filters those chats out and `getSessionRowStatus` only promotes InProgress from the aggregate, so the sessions list shows no needs-input state in that case either. Possibly related: #338320.

issues.title: Add an Agent Host URI layer to the layer checker
issues.body:
Following #337859 and #337263, add an Agent Host-specific layer to the layer checker so URI handling that is shared across local and remote/cloud Agent Host implementations cannot accidentally depend on VS Code-specific URI shapes.

The Agent Host Protocol treats host-advertised chat URIs as opaque identifiers. A recent regression rebuilt an advertised cloud sandbox URI using the local default URI format, which caused the Changes view to stop resolving the session.

The layer checker should make this class of regression harder to introduce by isolating Agent Host URI handling and flagging imports or helpers that assume a particular host-specific URI structure.

Acceptance criteria:
- Define an Agent Host-only layer (or equivalent layer-check rule) for shared URI handling.
- Prevent code in that layer from depending on local-only/default chat URI construction.
- Cover the rule with a layer-check fixture/test that demonstrates host-advertised URIs remain opaque.

issues.title: Expose Modern UI / layout density state to webviews

labels.name: ux
labels.description: User experience issues

issues.body:
With `workbench.experimental.modernUI` on by default (eaeb8d9be23), native views change noticeably: sentence-case 12px/semibold pane headers, inset rounded list rows, and compact density via `window.density.layout`. Webview views that sit next to native views have no way to follow along from CSS.

What webviews get today:
- The size tokens (`--vscode-cornerRadius-*`, `--vscode-spacing-size*`, `--vscode-fontSize-*`, `--vscode-fontWeight-*`), via `WebviewThemeDataProvider` in `contrib/webview/browser/themeing.ts`. Their values are identical whether Modern UI is on or off, so they can't be used to tell the two apart.
- Theme kind classes on `<body>` (`vscode-light`, `vscode-dark`, …).

What they don't get: the `.modern-ui`, `.modern-ui-compact` and `.modern-ui-uppercase-view-headers` markers. `ModernUIContribution` puts these on the workbench containers only.

Extensions can work around this by reading the settings through `workspace.getConfiguration` and relaying them into the webview. But every extension has to rebuild that plumbing. It can also drift from what the workbench actually applies, for example during an experiment rollout or when later versions add rules on top of the setting.

**Proposal:** add the Modern UI state to the webview `<body>` alongside the theme kind class. For example `data-vscode-modern-ui`, `data-vscode-layout-density="default|compact"` and `data-vscode-uppercase-view-headers`, kept in sync with `ModernUIContribution`. Alternatively, export density-aware size tokens, so values like the pane header size or list row inset differ between default and compact.

**Why it matters:** extensions with rich webview views (for example GitLens's Commit Graph and Inspect views) can match native pane chrome under Modern UI without guessing.

issues.title: Agents window connected-tabs border does not follow the macOS corner radius

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
## Type of Issue

Bug

## Description

After #337972 makes the Agents window card radius concentric with the native macOS window corner, the visible inner border can narrow or disappear at the bottom corner. The outer `.agents-part-card` gets the derived `--agents-window-corner-radius`, but connected tabs paint their visible border on `.session-view::after`; `.session-view` still uses the fixed `calc(var(--vscode-cornerRadius-large) - var(--vscode-strokeThickness))` radius.

This leaves the inner border curve out of sync with the outer card curve.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Agents window on macOS with Modern UI connected tabs enabled.
2. Use a layout where the sessions card reaches a bottom native-window corner, such as hiding the panel and editor area.
3. Inspect the bottom corner of the sessions card.

## Expected

The visible inner border remains uniformly inset from the outer card edge and follows the native window curve.

## Actual

The inner border uses the normal card radius, so it pinches or disappears at the corner.

## Suggested Fix

Apply the same corner-ownership conditions used in `src/vs/sessions/browser/media/workbench.css` to the nested `.session-view`, using an inner radius derived from the exposed card radius:

```css
max(0px, calc(var(--agents-window-corner-radius) - var(--vscode-strokeThickness)))
```

Only override the exposed bottom-left and/or bottom-right corners; keep the existing `calc(var(--vscode-cornerRadius-large) - var(--vscode-strokeThickness))` radius for internal corners. Add a focused regression assertion for the connected-tabs `.session-view` radius in the macOS corner geometry test.

issues.title: Agent Host (Copilot): hooks from marketplace-installed agent plugins are never invoked since 1.139
issues.body:
## Summary

Since VS Code 1.139, hooks declared by an agent plugin installed from a marketplace (`chat.plugins.marketplaces`) never run in Copilot sessions on the Agent Host. The plugin is synced to the Agent Host and loaded by the Copilot runtime, and its skills work, but none of its hooks (`userPromptSubmitted`, `preToolUse`, `postToolUse`) are executed. The same plugin worked on 1.138.0.

This matches the root cause described in #337811 ("the plugin and its hook are still discovered, but the native hook is not invoked"). That PR was closed without merging, and I couldn't find an open issue tracking it. #338571 changes custom-agent frontmatter hooks, not plugin-level `hooks.json`.

For security/compliance plugins this is a silent failure: the guardrail stops running without any error or warning.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.139.1 (worked on 1.138.0)
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.67.0 (worked on 0.66.0)
- OS: macOS (arm64)
- Session type: Copilot on Agent Host (`agent-host-copilotcli`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a marketplace with a Copilot-format plugin (`plugin.json` + `hooks.json` at the plugin root), e.g.:
   ```json
   {
     "version": 1,
     "hooks": {
       "userPromptSubmitted": [
         { "type": "command", "bash": "sh \"${PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/log.sh\" userPromptSubmitted", "timeoutSec": 30 }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```
   where `hooks/log.sh` appends a line to a file.
2. Install and enable the plugin, then reload the window.
3. Send a prompt in a Copilot chat session.

**Expected:** the hook command runs (a line is appended), as on 1.138.
**Actual:** the command is never spawned.

## Evidence (trace log level)

- The plugin is delivered to the Agent Host:
  `[AgentPluginManager] Nonce match for file:///…/.vscode/agent-plugins/github.com/<org>/<repo>/<plugin>, skipping copy`
- The runtime loads the plugin: `session.skills_loaded` includes the plugin's skill with `"source": "plugin"` and a path inside `…/Code/agentPlugins/<plugin copy>/skills/…`.
- In the session events, `hook.start` / `hook.end` for `userPromptSubmitted` only show the built-in VS Code hooks. A wrapper placed in front of the plugin's command logs no invocation at all.
- The plugin's copy under `~/Library/Application Support/Code/agentPlugins/…` is byte-identical to the source.

## Workaround

Registering the same command as a user-level hook in `~/.copilot/hooks/<name>.json` (absolute paths, `PLUGIN_ROOT` set via `env`) works: the command is invoked for `userPromptSubmitted`, `preToolUse` and `postToolUse`. So only the plugin → hook path is broken, not hook execution itself.

The workaround means plugin authors will get duplicate invocations once this is fixed, so it would help to know whether a fix is planned for a 1.139.x recovery or for 1.140.

issues.title: Agents Window: side-by-side sessions show a distracting full-height divider

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body: ## Type of issue Bug ## Reproduction 1. Open the Agents Window. 2. Open two sessions so they are displayed side by side in the Sessions Part. ## Actual behavior A prominent full-height vertical line is drawn between the two session views. It visually cuts the shared floating card into two hard-edged panels and is much stronger than the otherwise quiet session chrome. ## Expected behavior Side-by-side sessions should read as views within one shared card. The resize boundary should stay quiet at rest and reveal itself on hover/drag, while remaining visible in high-contrast themes. ## Analysis `SessionsPart` passes `agentsPanelBorder` to `SerializableGrid` as its `separatorBorder` in `src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/sessionsPart.ts`. `SplitView` renders every non-transparent separator as a 1px pseudo-element spanning the full height of the second grid leaf. Reusing the outer card border token for this internal resize boundary creates the line shown in the screenshots. ## Proposed fix - Make the Sessions Part grid separator transparent in normal themes so the sash itself provides the resize affordance on hover/drag. - Preserve `contrastBorder` for high-contrast themes. - Add a two-visible-sessions component fixture/screenshot assertion so the resting-state divider does not regress. The surgical implementation is to have `SessionsPart._gridSeparatorBorder` return `contrastBorder` when defined and otherwise `Color.transparent`, instead of falling back to `agentsPanelBorder`. This keeps the outer `agentsCard.border` unchanged and does not affect the separate side-by-side chat-group grid.

issues.title: Remote agent host over SSH keeps reconnecting while a large message is still downloading
issues.body:
After my laptop slept, VS Code reconnected to a remote agent host over SSH. The host replied with the state of every open session in one message (about 94 MB), which took 25 seconds or more to download.

VS Code drops the connection if no complete message arrives within 25 seconds, even while one is still downloading. So it dropped the connection and reconnected, and the host sent the same large message again. It took 7 tries to get through.

It happened again when I opened the laptop: 12 drops in about 40 minutes, most of them about 25 seconds after the host started sending a large message (8–33 MB). Clicking Reconnect just started the same download again.

The host was fine the whole time. In the first loop it sent each reply within a second, and after reconnecting VS Code received dozens of late replies to requests from the connection it had just dropped.

**Expected:** a connection that's still receiving data isn't treated as dead.

VS Code Insiders 1.140.0 (fee7930e)

Type: Bug **Title:** Python environment auto-activation unreliable in multi-root workspace **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Create a multi-root VS Code workspace with two project folders, each using a different Conda environment. 2. In each folder, set `python.defaultInterpreterPath` and `"python.terminal.activateEnvironment": true` in `.vscode/settings.json`. 3. Select the correct Conda interpreter for the second workspace folder. 4. Restart VS Code and open a `.py` file from that folder. 5. Click **Run Python File**. VS Code correctly runs the script using the selected environment’s full Python path, but the newly created integrated terminal does not automatically run `conda activate `. 6. In some cases, selecting the interpreter for one workspace folder also appears to update the status-bar interpreter only when selecting through the other workspace folder. Expected: a newly created terminal for the project should automatically activate its selected Conda environment. issues.title: Queued messages are never sent while a background subagent is running
issues.body:
In an Agent Host Copilot CLI session, the agent handed work to a background subagent and finished its reply. The chat stayed in progress while the subagent worked, so the two messages I sent were queued. Both were queued while the agent had already replied and was only waiting. Neither was ever sent.

When the subagent finished, its notification restarted the agent in the same request, and it carried on without seeing my messages. They sat in the queue for about 3 and 5 hours until I removed them.

**Expected:** once the agent finishes its reply, queued messages are sent, even if a background subagent is still running.

Possibly related: #337684

VS Code Insiders 1.140.0 (4a6a3612), @github/copilot-sdk 1.0.15-preview.3

issues.title: Multi-agent debate (adversarial agent workflow)
issues.body:
I would low for it to be a built-in way to have a multi-agent debate to reach a solution. There are already suggestions for a complete "team" of agents taking on all kinds of roles, but I would prefer a simpler approach first.

It would work something like this:
- I ask e.g. chatgpt to solve a problem.
- I have then set up a claude model to be the reviewer of the solution. It finds bugs or suggests changes back to the chatgpt agent.
- They continue doing this back-and-forth till they both agree.

This can be done manually in various ways, but being able to set this up easily would be a great, first start.

A solution could be to have two personas only, "The Writer" and "The Editor", and you just select the models for both. Nothing else. The entire workflow is then automated with just this in mind: to iterate on the solution till both think it is good.

I think this would improve solutions by a large margin. It should also be fairly easy to implement compared to other more advanced solutions.
