issues.title: Managed OTel policy arriving after startup requires manual Agent Host restart and can repeat Local reload prompts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: otel
labels.description: OTel (OpenTelemetry)

issues.body:
Enterprise OTel settings arriving after initialization do not reliably take effect without manual recovery. Agent Host can keep its startup exporter configuration, while Local Copilot Chat can repeatedly offer **Reload Window** for the same policy.

Proposed fix: #338623. Found while validating #338234.

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

**Setup:** Use a local OTLP/HTTP collector and a managed-settings mock. Include **`forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true` in the managed-settings response**, not in `settings.json`. Complete one successful sync to seed the cached refresh requirement before testing subsequent reloads.

Steps to Reproduce:

**Agent Host: late policy does not update the exporter**

1. Initially serve `{"forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": true}` without a telemetry block. Start Insiders, sync account policy, then open an Agent Host session and send a short prompt so the host has initialized.
2. Switch to the OTel-enabled response below. Run **Developer: Sync Account Policy** and dismiss its confirmation. Do not restart Agent Host.
3. Send another prompt and inspect the collector.

**Actual:** The running host does not begin exporting to the managed collector. Manually running **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host**, then sending another prompt, applies the policy and produces exports.

**Local Copilot Chat: repeated reload prompt** *(timing-dependent)*

1. Successfully sync the OTel-enabled response below, including `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true`. Use the **Local** harness.
2. Reload the window, delaying the required fresh managed-settings response until after the extension telemetry service initializes. Then let the same response complete.
3. When the OTel **Reload Window** prompt appears, accept it. Repeat the response delay after the reload, without changing the policy.

**Actual:** The same OTel reload prompt can return, leading the user through repeated reloads without resolving the initialization race.

**Expected:** VS Code recovers when settled enterprise OTel policy arrives or changes, without requiring knowledge of a developer restart command. Recovery should be bounded; if it still fails, show that policy remains unapplied rather than repeatedly offering reloads. Temporary refresh states should not restart an otherwise correctly configured shared Agent Host.

<details>
<summary>Mock response, refresh behavior, and environment</summary>

OTel-enabled managed-settings response (HTTP 200):

```json
{
  "forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": true,
  "telemetry": {
    "enabled": true,
    "endpoint": "http://localhost:4318",
    "protocol": "http/json",
    "captureContent": false,
    "capture": { "identity": false }
  }
}
```

`forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` requires a fresh successful server response rather than satisfying startup from cached managed settings. While the refresh is pending, the account-policy gate temporarily applies restrictive values; successful completion restores the managed values. This timing matters for the repeated Local reload prompt and for avoiding redundant Agent Host restarts during an unchanged-policy refresh. The flag is not required for every possible late-policy race, but it is part of this refresh-based reproduction. A failed refresh must remain fail-closed.

Testing used a local OTLP/HTTP collector at `http://localhost:4318` and a managed-settings mock routed through Proxyman. Use `npm run mock-policy-server` and its [proxy setup instructions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/101c86fe138844c24b14ccb1a6636986f68e9bd2/scripts/mock-policy-server/README.md). Leave unrelated endpoints on passthrough. Do not configure personal OTel settings or inherited OTel environment variables.

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not recorded.
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0-insider, commit `2dfd3b41fbc30a7270f0b84db51d67ab7568ebe3`.
- OS Version: macOS / Darwin arm64 27.0.0.
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent Host sessions and the separate Local Copilot Chat harness; enterprise-managed OTel export.
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not recorded for the original reproduction; the issue concerns exporter initialization rather than a specific model.
- Logs: No raw logs attached. Use the OTLP collector, Agent Host log, and GitHub Copilot Chat output to distinguish actual export from merely accepting policy.

</details>

issues.title: Please provide supported Copilot Chat / VS Code commands or agent tools to initialize, refresh, inspect, and configure the semantic code index for an open workspace.
issues.body:
I work in a large multi-root workspace containing SQL, PHP, Perl, shell, XML, and configuration files. Before making a change, an agent needs to locate relevant files across workspace roots without the user repeatedly supplying full paths.

The desired index scope is explicit:

- Include active text-based source and configuration files, including:
  `*.sql`, `*.ddl`, `*.dml`, `*.dat`, `*.php`, `*.pl`, `*.sh`, `*.ctl`, `*.xml`, `*.conf`, and `*.properties`
- Exclude:
  `.git/**`
  `legacy-production-copy/**`

### Current limitation

The semantic-search operation accepts a broad query but can return no results, without diagnostics to clarify whether the workspace has not been indexed, indexing is in progress, or indexing is unavailable.

Available file discovery can enumerate matching files, but cannot reliably apply required exclusions. For example, a search can still return files under `legacy-production-copy/**`.

There is no exposed mechanism to:

1. Initialize or rebuild the semantic index.
2. Configure include and exclude path patterns.
3. Inspect index status, progress, or file count.
4. List files or paths that could not be indexed.
5. Confirm which workspace roots were indexed.

### Requested functionality

Please expose commands and/or agent APIs such as:

- `Copilot: Build Workspace Semantic Index`
- `Copilot: Configure Semantic Index Scope`
- `Copilot: Show Semantic Index Status`

The status should report indexed workspace roots, included and excluded patterns, indexed file count, skipped or unreadable files, and actionable error details.

This would make Copilot more dependable for large multi-root repositories while allowing users to control scope and avoid repeatedly providing file locations.

issues.title: Terminal shell integration: leading comment ends multiline execution before its output

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: terminal-shell-integration
labels.description: Shell integration infrastructure, command decorations, etc.

labels.name: terminal-shell-bash
labels.description: An issue in the terminal specific to bash, including shell integration

issues.body:
## Problem

A comment-leading multiline Bash command can end the `TerminalShellExecution` returned by `executeCommand()` before any of the script's output reaches its `read()` stream. The following commands are then reported as separate executions.

This reproduced in Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev on Windows x64, baseline `c05a76bd8fd5f91727709685be99d80f64aa1784`, using `bash.exe` from Git with an isolated HOME/startup file and VS Code's Bash shell-integration script. The installed Bash reports `5.3.15(2)-release (x86_64-pc-cygwin)`. It also reproduces with an independent terminal-stream retention fix applied, so that change is not the cause.

## Reproduction

In an extension development host, create a Bash terminal and wait for `terminal.shellIntegration`. Register execution start/end listeners, then immediately read the execution returned for:

```ts
const command = [
	'# leading comment',
	'printf "Q74_QUOTED_FIRST\\nQ74_QUOTED_LAST\\n"',
	'{',
	'printf "Q74_BLOCK\\n"',
	'}',
].join('\n');

const execution = terminal.shellIntegration!.executeCommand(command);
let output = '';
for await (const chunk of execution.read()) {
	output += chunk;
}
console.log(JSON.stringify(output));
```

When inspecting end events, match `event.execution === execution`, rather than accepting any end event from the terminal.

**Expected:** The returned execution covers the complete script. Its stream contains all three output markers and completion reports exit code `0`.

**Actual:**

- The original execution starts with the complete requested command line.
- Its end event fires with `exitCode: undefined`, and its stream resolves to `""`.
- The `printf` and compound block subsequently appear as separate executions.
- The output is visible in the terminal, but missing from the originally returned stream.

## Controls / related issues

Recorded baseline/fix runs reproduced the same failure, including a focused run matching the exact execution identity. Ordinary six-command multiline scripts and a long second-command heredoc both passed.

Related to #243442 / #237208. Also related to open reports #250764, #316556 and #324392, but this repro differs: the original end event **does fire prematurely** and the stream **closes empty**, rather than remaining permanently silent/open. No claim depends on including the final OSC 633 D sequence in the data stream.

issues.body:
<!-- bug_report_template -->

New Agent Host terminals opened from VS Code can print a blank `TERM_PROGRAM`, while workbench terminals explicitly set it to `vscode`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch VS Code without an inherited `TERM_PROGRAM` value, for example from the desktop rather than another terminal.
2. Open the Agents Window and create a new Agent Host terminal.
3. Run `echo "$TERM_PROGRAM"`.
4. Compare with a workbench terminal in the editor window.

**Actual:** The Agent Host terminal can print an empty value. It inherits the host process's environment rather than setting its own terminal identity, so an unrelated inherited terminal name can also carry through.

**Expected:** When VS Code requests creation of a new Agent Host terminal, set `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode` and the creating client's `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`. Do not force VS Code identity on terminals created by other clients or relabel an existing terminal when VS Code attaches to it.

### Source context

- Workbench terminals set the identity explicitly in [`addTerminalEnvironmentKeys`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/terminalEnvironment.ts#L62-L71).

Reported on macOS in the Agents Window. The source gap is present on `main` at `4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811` (1.140.0). Other platforms and an extensions-disabled UI reproduction have not been separately tested.

issues.title: [chat] Renderer crashes with -36861 while restoring large Copilot editing session
issues.body:
## Summary

VS Code Stable repeatedly crashes the local window renderer with:

```
The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'crashed', code: '-36861')
```

The crash occurs while restoring a large persisted Copilot chat editing session. The extension host is not the crashing process in the latest reproductions; it exits cleanly after the renderer closes its MessagePort.

## Environment

- VS Code Stable `1.139.0`
- Commit `2242ebbb54efeeb0129e08e919e7e8d43033cd83`
- Windows x64 `10.0.26200`
- Microsoft Dev Box
- GitHub Copilot Chat `0.67.0`
- Local workspace; no Remote-SSH required

## Reproduction

1. Use a long Copilot chat with agent edits and persisted chat editing state.
2. Leave the session open in VS Code.
3. Continue working or allow the session to be restored after a renderer crash.
4. Observe repeated renderer termination and automatic window recreation.

## Observed evidence

The same VS Code log session recorded renderer crashes at:

- 2026-09-28 12:20:30
- 2026-09-28 17:59:29
- 2026-09-29 08:41:56
- 2026-09-29 09:05:37
- 2026-09-29 09:16:50

Each event is recorded as:

```
CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: crashed, code: -36861)
```

The paired extension host exits with code `0`, and its log reports that the renderer closed the MessagePort. This distinguishes the current failure from an extension-host crash.

Immediately after the 09:16:50 crash, the replacement window restored Copilot session `6884b9c4-8e0a-4d46-8835-5c39b61498d9`:

- Chat JSONL: approximately `437.4 MiB`
- Chat editing state: approximately `135.6 MiB` across `564` files
- Combined persisted state: approximately `573.1 MiB`

During restore, the renderer logged repeated failures through the chat editing restore path:

```
ChatEditingSession._initEntries
_getOrCreateModifiedFileEntry
_createModifiedFileEntry
createTextModel
```

The active renderer reached approximately `3.12 GiB` private/working memory while the machine still had approximately `83 GiB` free. No system-wide memory exhaustion was observed.

The latest crashed and replacement extension hosts contain no MAI AI Telemetry activation reference. The earlier MAI extension-host crashes are a separate issue.

## Expected behavior

Restoring a large Copilot session should never crash the VS Code renderer. The session should open using bounded resources, with a recoverable warning or partial/read-only fallback when the persisted state is too large.

## Proposed direction

- Load only a bounded initial transcript and hydrate older messages on demand.
- Do not create text models for every persisted editing entry during session startup.
- Apply size/count budgets to persisted chat and editing state.
- Preserve the session and offer an explicit recovery path when state exceeds the budget.
- Add diagnostics showing the session size and restore phase before failure.

## Related issues

- #332725: Renderer and extension host OOM with multiple concurrent Copilot sessions.
- #324809: Copilot Chat renderer OOM in Remote-SSH sessions.

This report is a local, non-Remote-SSH reproduction focused on eager restoration of persisted chat editing state and the `-36861` renderer crash signature.

`-36861` is the Crashpad handler-disconnected fallback; no dump was retained, so the final native exception is unavailable.

issues.title: claude harness not showing up
issues.body:
## Summary

The Claude harness does not show up in VS Code Insiders. The agent host registers the Claude provider and receives authentication, but the Claude SDK never becomes available during the captured session. As a result, Claude reports zero models and existing Claude sessions remain unavailable.

## Current state from the logs

- The Agent Host starts successfully.
- Providers `copilotcli`, `claude`, and `codex` are registered.
- Claude model refresh completes with `Count: 0`.
- The Claude proxy starts listening and the Claude auth token is updated.
- Claude repeatedly logs `SDK not downloaded yet` and defers migratable chat loading, passive chat metadata, and chat discovery.
- Three existing Claude sessions are repeatedly left for retry with `providerUnavailable`.
- This persists from approximately 16:42 through at least 16:57; there is no later indication that the Claude SDK downloaded or became ready.

Representative log lines:

```text
2026-09-28 16:42:55.622 [info] Registering agent provider: claude
2026-09-28 16:42:55.729 [info] [Claude] Models refreshed (merged). Count: 0,
2026-09-28 16:42:55.969 [info] [Claude] SDK not downloaded yet; deferring the migratable chat list
2026-09-28 16:42:59.948 [info] [ClaudeProxyService] listening on http://127.0.0.1:62500
2026-09-28 16:42:59.948 [info] [Claude] Auth token updated
2026-09-28 16:43:00.358 [info] [Claude] SDK not downloaded yet; deferring chat discovery
2026-09-28 16:43:21.978 [info] [AgentHostCatalogReconciliation] claude:/7697e119-b529-4344-bc7a-79fcb8939488 will be retried: providerUnavailable
2026-09-28 16:57:37.670 [info] [AgentHostCatalogReconciliation] claude:/fefe45d7-6da6-40a7-b1f7-1a56fe77d595 will be retried: providerUnavailable
```

## Expected behavior

The Claude harness should appear and expose available models. If the SDK is not installed, VS Code should trigger/download it and surface a clear actionable error if that download cannot start or fails.

## Actual behavior

The harness does not appear. Claude stays in an SDK-not-downloaded/provider-unavailable state, with zero models and no logged download attempt or direct download failure explaining why it remains unavailable.

## Other errors/warnings present in the same capture

These may be unrelated, but were logged concurrently:

- `No harness descriptor found for session type file` and `agent-host-copilotcli`.
- `github.copilot-chat` requests more proposed APIs than are enabled in `product.json`.
- Tunnel relay connection attempts time out after 30 seconds.
- Installed MCP server configuration parsing fails (`Invalid symbol` / `Colon expected`).
- Some Copilot requests fail with `Response contained no choices.`
- One GitHub MCP server instance fails because its Authorization header is missing the `Bearer ` prefix; another instance subsequently connects successfully.
- OTEL forwarding to `http://localhost:4319/v1/traces` fails.

## Environment

- Windows x64
- VS Code Insiders
- Captured installation/build directory identifier: `fee7930e95`
- Log date: 2026-09-28

## Related issues

- #334077 reports Claude models not loading and similar SDK-not-downloaded messages.
- #334170 reports a discovery race where the SDK becomes available later. In this capture, the SDK does not become ready at any point during the observed interval.

issues.title: Copilot OTel reload prompt loops when managed settings resolve after activation

labels.name: otel
labels.description: OTel (OpenTelemetry)

issues.body:
## Summary

Copilot Chat can show an OTel reload notification after every window reload or full application restart when managed settings resolve after the extension has already constructed its OTel service.

The confirmed notifications were:

- `Copilot OTel settings changed - a reload is required for the change to take effect.`
- after changing the local endpoint for diagnosis: `Copilot OTel endpoint will change to … after reload.`

Selecting **Reload Window** reproduces the same startup ordering, so the notification loops instead of applying the managed configuration.

## Environment

- VS Code Insiders, `release/1.140`
- Commit `2dfd3b41fbc30a7270f0b84db51d67ab7568ebe3`
- Copilot OTel was already explicitly enabled locally
- Managed Copilot settings were applied through the account-policy path

## Runtime evidence

### Initial run

```text
18:12:05.453  Extension host starts, PID 9104
18:12:15.957  [DefaultAccount] Managed settings applied
~18:12:16.5  OTel stale-config check shows the generic reload notification
18:12:26.562  Window reload begins
18:12:27.630  New extension host starts, PID 18296
18:12:30.313  [DefaultAccount] Managed settings applied again
~18:12:30.8  The notification appears again
```

### After a full application restart

```text
18:45:42.181  Fresh Agent Host process starts
18:45:42.254  Fresh extension host starts, PID 14988
18:45:46.594  [DefaultAccount] Managed settings applied
~18:45:47.1  OTel shows the reload notification again
```

For the second run, the local OTel endpoint had intentionally been changed. The endpoint-specific notification proves that the managed endpoint became visible only after OTel initialization.

The Agent Host process itself started once per application run and was not the source of the notification.

## Root cause

The Copilot extension constructs `IOTelService` once from `IOTelConfigResolver.activeResolution`. `OTelStaleConfigMonitor` later compares the current resolution with that startup snapshot.

When managed settings arrive late, the effective configuration drifts. Because OTel was already explicitly enabled locally, this branch applies:

```ts
if (active.hasEnterpriseSettings || active.config.enabledExplicitly || !isPolicyEnabledOtlp(current)) {
    // promptReload(...)
}
```

This occurs before the guarded automatic extension-host recovery path. The prompt offers `workbench.action.reloadWindow`, but reloading the window restarts account-policy initialization, causing managed settings to arrive late again.

The per-session automatic-restart guard is therefore not involved in this loop.

## Relationship to previous work

- #336102 identified the managed OTel initialization race.
- Draft #336156 / commit `bea10f45f67` attempted to stabilize startup using the early core policy owners, but was closed as superseded.
- #336701 added restart-based late-policy recovery and closed #336102.

#336701 intentionally routes already-enabled OTel configurations to an opt-in reload. The logs above show that a window reload is not a successful recovery action when the account-managed settings pipeline resolves after extension activation on every launch.

## Expected behavior

Once managed OTel settings resolve, Copilot should apply them without entering a reload loop. No telemetry-producing Copilot work should continue indefinitely with the stale startup configuration.

## Potential directions

Any complete fix should cover managed-settings data that arrives after service construction, not only late registration of extension policy references. Options include:

1. await an account-managed-settings readiness barrier before constructing OTel;
2. make the extension and embedded runtime OTel pipeline safely reconfigurable/lazily initialized; or
3. restart only the extension host after policy settles, preserving the renderer's resolved account-policy state, instead of reloading the window.

At minimum, the informational drift path should not offer a recovery action that deterministically recreates the same race.

## Diagnostics gap

The informational prompt path does not log `describeOTelConfigDrift(active.config, current.config)`. Logging bounded field names only—not values—would make future incidents diagnosable without exposing collector URLs, headers, or other sensitive configuration.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
The artifact tools guidance (`ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION`) is injected as a `<system_reminder>` in the user message by [`ArtifactToolsContribution`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/chatContributions/artifactTools/artifactToolsContribution.ts). It's gated to the first turn, but because it lives in the conversation it's re-sent with every model request for the rest of the session.

**Impact (from AHP token-usage evals):**
- It prompts `add_artifact_or_reference` calls even in headless sessions where nothing surfaces the artifacts: about 0.5 per task, each one a full-context request.

**Suggested fix:**
- Don't send the instruction or register the tool when there's no artifacts UI (headless/automation sessions).
- Otherwise, move the guidance into the tool description or system prompt, and shorten it.

Testing #338175, related to #337816.

## Environment

- Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev, commit `9ae5e965fdd41026cd7bb60f232a339ea3c61761`
- Windows x64, disposable profile/workspace, no sign-in
- Marketplace enabled; `chat.plugins.enabled: true`
- Configured marketplace: `microsoft/skills`
- Plugin: `microsoft-foundry`, version `1.0.0`
- An explicit isolated `--agent-plugins-dir <test-directory>` was used.

## End-to-end reproduction

1. Set `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled` to `true` and `chat.plugins.marketplaces` to `["microsoft/skills"]`.
2. Open Agent Customizations > Discover. Install **microsoft-foundry** from **Configured Plugin Marketplaces - microsoft/skills**, accepting the trust prompt.
3. Verify Discover marks this exact entry Installed.
4. Outside Discover, delete only the recorded plugin folder `<agent-plugins-dir>/github.com/microsoft/skills/.github/plugins/microsoft-foundry`. Leave `installed.json` unchanged.
5. Open Plugins: the installed marketplace plugin has disappeared. Return to Discover, re-search, and wait. Then run **Developer: Reload Window** and check Discover again.
6. Observe the entry still says **Installed**, with **Uninstall** but no Missing/Error state and no Repair.
7. Invoke Uninstall.

## Actual

Uninstall reports:

> Could not uninstall microsoft-foundry. This plugin cannot be uninstalled from the customization marketplace.

The action becomes **Retry Uninstall**. The durable installation record and `installed.json` entry both remain. Refreshing, waiting 30 seconds, and reloading did not repair this state.

A separate local plugin with the same name was present during testing. It remained independent and intact; the stale Installed claim persisted even though Plugins showed only that unrelated local plugin.

## Expected

Reconcile the record with the actual exact target: show Missing/Error when the folder no longer exists, offer Repair when supported, and allow Uninstall to clear the stale record without touching the unrelated plugin.

## Diagnostic comparison

Removing the marketplace plugin through **Plugins > ... > Uninstall** instead clears `installed.json`; Discover then correctly reports Missing files, Repair restores the same record/URI, and subsequent marketplace Uninstall succeeds.

Code inspection suggests reconciliation trusts the installed-plugin metadata without checking target existence/discovery, while uninstall requires the target in the discovered plugin list. This leaves a stale-metadata dead end.

Source: [customizationMarketplaceInstallService.ts at the tested commit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ae5e965fdd41026cd7bb60f232a339ea3c61761/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.ts).

issues.title: Plugin marketplace: failed ref clone leaves an empty cache that blocks unpinned installs

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
Found while testing #338175 / #337816. This is in the existing plugin repository/cache path, not established as a regression introduced by the installation-record PR.

## Environment

- Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev, commit `9ae5e965fdd41026cd7bb60f232a339ea3c61761`
- Windows x64, Git 2.55.0.windows.3, no sign-in
- Disposable profile, explicit isolated `--agent-plugins-dir <AP>`
- `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled: true`, `chat.plugins.enabled: true`
- Plugin `microsoft-foundry` 1.0.0, source `./.github/plugins/microsoft-foundry`

## End-to-end reproduction

1. Use a fresh isolated plugin cache where `<AP>/github.com/microsoft/skills` does not exist.
2. Configure `chat.plugins.marketplaces` with:

   ```json
   [
     "github/awesome-copilot#marketplace",
     "microsoft/skills",
     "microsoft/skills#23d0dac5f83f268166a17f0bc7dc6c73dc348a33"
   ]
   ```

3. Open Agent Customizations > Discover and search `microsoft-foundry`.
4. Install from the SHA-pinned `microsoft/skills#23d0dac...` source and accept trust. This currently fails because the SHA is passed to `git clone --branch` (a separate issue).
5. Inspect `<AP>/github.com/microsoft/skills`: the failed `ref_<SHA>` child is cleaned up, but its parent remains **empty**.
6. Install from the unpinned **microsoft/skills** source. Repeat with Retry Install.

## Actual

The unpinned source keeps failing with:

> Plugin source directory '.github/plugins/microsoft-foundry' not found in repository 'microsoft/skills'.

No marketplace record is written and `installed.json` is not created. Retry does not recover the empty cache.

Deleting **only the empty test cache directory** `<AP>/github.com/microsoft/skills` and retrying recovered the installation.

## Expected

A failed ref-specific clone must not poison an independent source's cache. An existing empty/non-repository folder should be validated/recovered, not treated as a successfully cloned repository.

## Diagnosis and confidence

The ref-specific cache is nested inside the unpinned clone path: `.../skills/ref_<ref>`. Code inspection suggests failed-clone cleanup removes only the child, while the unpinned repository lookup trusts folder existence instead of repository validity.

The failure, empty parent, retry failure, and recovery were reproduced. A first occurrence also followed two cancelled clones, but which ref was cancelled and what initiated cancellation were not proven; the SHA-failure sequence above is the concrete repro.

issues.body:
Testing #338175, related to #337816.

## Environment

- Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev, commit `9ae5e965fdd41026cd7bb60f232a339ea3c61761`
- Windows x64, disposable profile/workspace, no sign-in
- Marketplace and public GitHub Feed enabled
- `.github/skills` and `.agents/skills` enabled as skill locations
- Skill: GitHub Feed **Pdf**, declared name `pdf`, source `openai/skills/skills/.curated/pdf`
- Repair used immutable revision `49f948faa9258a0c61caceaf225e179651397431`.

## End-to-end reproduction

1. In a disposable workspace, create `.github/skills/pdf/SKILL.md` declaring `name: pdf` with clearly unrelated content.
2. Open Agent Customizations > Discover and search `pdf`.
3. Install the GitHub Feed **Pdf** skill from `openai/skills/skills/.curated/pdf`, choosing the different destination `.agents/skills/pdf`.
4. Edit the installed SKILL.md, add an extra file, and delete the recorded file `agents/openai.yaml` through Explorer.
5. Return to Discover and verify the installed entry says **Missing files**.
6. Invoke **Repair** and confirm, keeping the results list visible while repair runs.
7. Watch for an additional installed skill named `.customization-marketplace-<UUID>`.

## Actual

A screenshot captured a new installed row:

> .customization-marketplace-71a9174a-8d2c-491c-a8d6-dcf712e7b865

It displayed the PDF skill description and an **Uninstall** action. The Skills count briefly increased from 12 to 13. The real `pdf` installation was also visible.

The staging row disappeared after cleanup. Repair eventually restored the missing file and correctly preserved the edited file, extra file, and unrelated local skill.

## Expected

An internal repair staging directory must not be published as an installed user customization or expose a user Uninstall action. Only the recorded target should participate in this repair's visible lifecycle.

## Reproduction frequency

**Intermittent:** observed and screenshotted once. One subsequent instrumented warm repeat did not reproduce it. This report does not claim deterministic reproduction, data loss, or that clicking the temporary Uninstall action was tested.

## Suspected cause

Repair creates `.customization-marketplace-<UUID>` alongside the target beneath the scanned skill root. Discovery can publish that staging directory before it is removed.

Source: [customizationMarketplaceSkillInstaller.ts at the tested commit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ae5e965fdd41026cd7bb60f232a339ea3c61761/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceSkillInstaller.ts).

issues.title: Plugin marketplace: SHA-pinned source is discoverable but installation uses git clone --branch

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
Found while testing #338175 / #337816. This is in the existing plugin cloning path, not established as a regression introduced by the installation-record PR.

## Environment

- Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev, commit `9ae5e965fdd41026cd7bb60f232a339ea3c61761`
- Windows x64, Git 2.55.0.windows.3, disposable profile/cache, no sign-in
- `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled: true`, `chat.plugins.enabled: true`
- Explicit isolated `--agent-plugins-dir <AP>`
- Marketplace commit `23d0dac5f83f268166a17f0bc7dc6c73dc348a33` (microsoft/skills main/HEAD at test time)

## End-to-end reproduction

1. Configure `chat.plugins.marketplaces` to include:

   ```json
   [
     "microsoft/skills",
     "microsoft/skills#23d0dac5f83f268166a17f0bc7dc6c73dc348a33"
   ]
   ```

2. Open Agent Customizations > Discover.
3. Search `microsoft-foundry`. The SHA-pinned marketplace is successfully fetched and lists this plugin (version 1.0.0, relative source `./.github/plugins/microsoft-foundry`).
4. Click Install on the SHA-pinned source's row and accept trust.

## Actual

Installation invokes:

```text
git clone --branch 23d0dac5f83f268166a17f0bc7dc6c73dc348a33 -- https://github.com/microsoft/skills.git <AP>/github.com/microsoft/skills/ref_23d0dac5f83f268166a17f0bc7dc6c73dc348a33
```

Git fails with:

```text
fatal: Remote branch 23d0dac5f83f268166a17f0bc7dc6c73dc348a33 not found in upstream origin
```

The row offers Retry Install and no installation record is created. The failed clone can also leave an empty parent cache directory that breaks unpinned installs (reported separately).

## Expected

A commit-pinned marketplace that is successfully discovered should install the plugin from that commit. Commit SHAs must not be passed as branch/tag names to `git clone --branch`. If commit refs are intentionally unsupported, configuration/discovery should reject them explicitly instead of presenting an installable catalog entry.

The discovery/install mismatch and exact failing Git command were reproduced.

issues.title: Improve error handling and user feedback in GitHubGistProfileContentHandler
issues.body:
## Problem Statement
Currently, in `GitHubGistProfileContentHandler`, error handling during profile reading and saving is silent (`// ignore` block and silent `null` returns). If network requests fail or tokens expire, users get no feedback, leading to a confusing user experience.

## Proposed Solution
- Wrap the Gist API calls in robust `try-catch` blocks.
- Provide clear, localized error messages via `vscode.window.showErrorMessage()` when saving profiles fails.
- Log appropriate error details to the console during profile read failures instead of completely ignoring them.

## Additional Context
This minor enhancement improves the reliability and user experience of profile synchronization via GitHub Gists. I am happy to submit a Pull Request (PR) for this change if approved!

issues.title: SCM Repositories view repeatedly refreshes and re-expands on startup with many worktree repositories
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (only built-in extensions, `chat.disableAIFeatures: true`)

- VS Code Version: 1.140.0-insider
- OS Version: macOS 14.2 (arm64)

When a repository has many worktrees open as Source Control repositories, the **Source Control Repositories** view spends several seconds at startup refreshing the whole tree and collapsing/re-expanding the parent repository row again and again. Rows visibly flicker and get re-selected while the worktree repositories load.

This happens with the default `scm.repositories.explorer: false`, where worktree repositories are nested under their parent repository row.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Use a repository with 50+ worktrees (for example, `git worktree add ../wt-N -b wt-N` × 50).
2. Set `"git.detectWorktrees": true` (the default `git.detectWorktreesLimit` of 50 applies).
3. Open the main repository folder with the Source Control view's Repositories section visible.
4. Watch the Repositories view while the worktree repositories load.

**Expected:** Worktree rows appear under the parent row without the parent collapsing and re-expanding.

**Actual:** For ~9–16 s the parent row collapses and re-expands about twice per worktree repository, and the whole tree re-renders each time.

### Measurements

MutationObserver on `.scm-repositories-view`, clean profile, window focused, 50 worktree repositories opened, starting when the Repositories view appears:

| Configuration | DOM mutations | Parent collapse/re-expand cycles |
|---|---|---|
| Built-in extensions only | 116,653 | 99 |
| + GitLens + Copilot Chat, run 1 | 114,308 | 99 |
| + GitLens + Copilot Chat, run 2 | 114,991 | 99 |
| + GitLens + Copilot Chat, **with the fix below**, run 1 | 54,522 | 1 |
| + GitLens + Copilot Chat, **with the fix below**, run 2 | 53,691 | 1 |

### Root cause

In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmRepositoriesViewPane.ts`:

1. **`updateRepository()` falls through to a full refresh.** In non-explorer mode, for a child repository (`provider.parentId !== undefined`), it calls `updateParentRepository()` (refresh parent + `expand(parent)`) and then falls through to `await this.updateChildren()`, a full recursive refresh of the whole tree.
   - In non-explorer mode, the root's children are only repositories without a `parentId`, so a child repository change can't change them.
   - `updateChildren(parent)` already re-evaluates the parent's own `hasChildren` (`AsyncDataTree.doRefreshNode`).
   - So the full refresh is redundant, and it runs once per child repository event.
2. **The `historyItemRef` subscription isn't gated on explorer mode.** `onDidAddRepository()` subscribes to each repository's `historyProvider.historyItemRef` and calls `updateRepository()` on every change.
   - In non-explorer mode there are no artifact groups under a repository, so a ref change doesn't change the tree's structure.
   - The artifact-group subscription right above it is already gated on `explorerEnabledConfig`; this one isn't.
   - The result is another parent refresh plus expand per worktree as refs load.

With N worktree repositories, that's about 2N full-tree refreshes and parent re-expands during startup.

### Fix

PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338592

```diff
 		// HistoryItemRef changed
 		disposables.add(autorun(async reader => {
+			const explorerEnabled = this.scmViewService.explorerEnabledConfig.read(reader);
 			const historyProvider = repository.provider.historyProvider.read(reader);
-			if (!historyProvider) {
+			if (!explorerEnabled || !historyProvider) {
 				return;
 			}
@@
 			await this.updateParentRepository(repository);
+			return;
 		}

 		// Explorer mode
```

The "with the fix" rows above were measured by applying these two changes at runtime to Insiders 1.140.0 (patching `SCMRepositoriesViewPane.prototype` via CDP before the Repositories view initialized).

The remaining churn is one `updateChildren(parent)` per added worktree repository. A further improvement would be to coalesce child additions until `didFinishLoadingRepositories` and then refresh and expand the parent once, but that's a larger change and not part of this fix.

issues.body:
The new-session composer should keep the primary task focused while making advanced session choices easy to discover and review.

## Feature request

Group secondary new-session controls—such as repository, harness, mode, permissions, model, and other provider-specific options—behind a single progressive-disclosure control. When collapsed, summarize only meaningful non-default effective choices so users can understand consequential state without scanning a row of controls.

The experience should:

- preserve the existing composer layout unless the experimental layout is enabled
- remember expanded/collapsed state and applicable repository-scoped choices
- present the collapsed disclosure as one focus stop with one accessible name
- use standard toolbar and picker keyboard behavior
- support provider-neutral summaries so shared Sessions UI does not depend on individual Agent Host implementations
- remain usable in narrow layouts, high-contrast themes, and with screen readers
- avoid presenting immutable provider state as an interactive choice

issues.title: Agents Window: terminal sandbox shown Off becomes enabled after Dev Container startup

labels.name: bug

issues.body:
Testing #338248.

## Problem

In a new Agents Window session targeting a fresh Dev Container, **Sandboxing for terminal is shown Off before submission**, but after the container starts the session is shown as **terminal sandboxed**. A basic `hostname` tool call then fails because the unmodified sample image does not contain Bubblewrap.

The reported bug is the difference between the pre-start setting and the effective session setting, not merely the absence of Bubblewrap in an image.

## Environment

- VS Code Insiders: 1.140.0-insider
- Commit: `fee7930e951e766078247fc91b2513744f8b7ef5` (latest published Windows Insiders when checked on 2026-09-28)
- Windows 11 Enterprise x64, build 26200
- Local Docker Desktop 4.93.0 / Engine 29.8.1, WSL 2 backend, `desktop-linux` context
- Copilot in the Agents Window
- `chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled`: `true`
- Fresh clone of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-remote-try-node
- Repository commit: `42a8bcfd51e64ce623cb60260408c4b2d1f1a509`
- Unmodified image configuration: `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/javascript-node:1-18-bullseye`
- Container user: `node`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the sample repository into a new local folder; do not open it in a Dev Container beforehand.
2. Select the clone in the Agents Window and choose **Use Dev Container** from the workspace submenu.
3. Open the permissions menu. Observe **Sandboxing for terminal: Off**.
4. Select **Allow all** in the recorded run. Before submission, the picker shows `Interactive, Allow all`, with no `terminal sandboxed` suffix. Do not enable sandboxing.
5. Send: `Run hostname and report the output. Do not modify any files.`
6. Wait for container startup and the tool attempt.

## Actual result

After startup, the picker shows:

```text
Interactive, Allow all, terminal sandboxed
```

The terminal command fails before execution:

```text
GenericFailure, Sandboxing is enabled but not supported on this platform:
Bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed or not on PATH.
Install it via your package manager (e.g., apt install bubblewrap).
Version 0.5.0 or newer is required.
```

The UI also displays `Sandboxing is unavailable in this environment`.

## Expected result

The pre-start session setting and the effective container session setting should agree. If container/managed policy requires a different setting, communicate the override and requirements before the first tool call rather than presenting Off and then failing under enabled sandboxing.

This is not a request to bypass a policy requiring sandboxing.

## Additional observations

- Similar startup behavior was observed with Manual permissions in the earlier #338248 verification.
- In the earlier run, explicitly turning the optional sandbox off in the already-created container session allowed the read-only diagnostic commands to run.
- The recorded Allow all attempt did **not** reproduce the separately observed `Copilot SDK rejected permission mode 'allow-all'` error. This video must not be treated as evidence of that rejection.
- A separate unexpected worktree-creation warning also appears during startup. No shared root cause is asserted.

## Recording

An MP4 has been recorded and reviewed locally (120 seconds, 1200x992). It shows the pre-start permissions menu with sandboxing Off, selection of Allow all, startup, and the missing-Bubblewrap failure. Video uploaded: [watch the reproduction](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338534#issuecomment-5878639243).

issues.title: Agents Window: first Dev Container session creates a worktree with New Worktree off

labels.name: bug

issues.body:
Testing #338248.

## Problem

The first Copilot session in a fresh Dev Container attempts to create an isolated worktree even though **New Worktree is unchecked/disabled** in the Agents Window before submission.

The attempt fails because the non-root container user cannot create a sibling directory under `/workspaces`. The UI reports that it is continuing in the original folder.

## Environment

- VS Code Insiders: 1.140.0-insider
- Commit: `fee7930e951e766078247fc91b2513744f8b7ef5` (latest published Windows Insiders when checked on 2026-09-28)
- Windows 11 Enterprise x64, build 26200
- Local Docker Desktop 4.93.0 / Engine 29.8.1, WSL 2 backend, `desktop-linux` context
- Copilot session in the Agents Window; Manual permissions selected
- `chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled`: `true`
- Repository: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-remote-try-node
- Repository commit: `42a8bcfd51e64ce623cb60260408c4b2d1f1a509`
- Unmodified image configuration: `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/javascript-node:1-18-bullseye`
- Container user: `node`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Clone `microsoft/vscode-remote-try-node` into a **new local folder**. Do not open this clone in a Dev Container beforehand.
2. Open the Agents Window and select the clone.
3. In the workspace picker's folder submenu, choose **Use Dev Container**.
4. Observe that **New Worktree is off**. In the recorded run, Windows accessibility also reported `ToggleState.Off`.
5. Select Manual permissions and send: `Run hostname and report the output. Do not modify any files.`
6. Wait for the first container/session startup. Expand the completed steps if the startup warning has collapsed.

## Actual result

The session tries to create a worktree and displays:

```text
Couldn't create the isolated worktree. This session is continuing in the original folder.
A system error occurred (EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/workspaces/verify-338248-worktree-recorded.worktrees')
```

## Expected result

With New Worktree off, the session should use the original workspace without attempting to create an isolated worktree.

## Reproduction scope

- Observed in both fresh clones used for #338248, and reproduced again with additional fresh clones while preparing the recording.
- A subsequent new session in an already initialized reproduction container did **not** display the worktree error. This may be specific to first-container/session initialization; no root cause is asserted.
- A separate Bubblewrap-unavailable terminal error also appears in the recording because the sample image lacks the optional sandbox dependency. That error is **not** the worktree bug reported here.
- Shared server cache reuse was independently verified successfully for #338248.

## Recording

The recording shows the unchecked New Worktree control before submission, container startup, and the expanded worktree warning. Unrelated session history and other applications are excluded from the recorded region.

An MP4 reproduction has been recorded and reviewed locally (135 seconds, 1200x992). Video uploaded: [watch the reproduction](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338533#issuecomment-5878639204).

issues.title: Terminal-completion auto-turn loses custom agents and subagent invocation tool

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.67.0
- VS Code Version: 1.139.1
- OS Version: Windows
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode — custom agents / subagent handoff after a terminal tool call
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-6 Luna
- Logs: Not attached. Detailed tool-snapshot diagnostics were checked for the latest occurrence only.

Searched existing issues for `runSubagent`, terminal-completion notifications, and `chat-terminal-output-monitor` before filing. Did not find a report of a terminal-completion auto-turn dropping custom agents and the subagent invocation tool.

## Description

This has occurred at least twice. When a terminal command keeps running after the terminal tool returns, its eventual completion notification starts an automatic chat turn. In the diagnosed occurrence, that turn could not invoke a custom subagent that had been available earlier in the chat. A pending agent handoff stalled until another user message was sent.

## Observed behavior

The command was started through the terminal tool in sync mode, with no timeout specified. The tool returned while the command was still running and said it may be waiting for input.

When the command finished, Copilot received an automatic terminal-completion notification. That request had 27 tools, omitting `runSubagent`, `vscode_askQuestions`, and `testFailure`. Customization discovery for that turn listed 0 agents.

Later requests within the same automatic continuation retained the reduced tool set.

A normal user message ("try again") started a new turn. Customization discovery then listed 10 agents, the request had 30 tools including the three previously missing ones, and `runSubagent` succeeded. The model had not changed.

## Expected behavior

A terminal-completion continuation should retain the applicable agents and tools needed to finish an in-progress handoff, or provide a supported way to resume that handoff without requiring another user message.

## Impact

A workflow that delegates work to custom agents can stop after a terminal command completes, even though the command's completion notification reaches the main chat.

## Workaround

Send a normal follow-up message to start a fresh turn. That restored the agents and tools in the diagnosed occurrence.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In agent mode, with custom agents available, start a terminal command through the terminal tool in sync mode with no timeout specified, such that the tool returns while the command is still running (it reported it may be waiting for input).
2. Leave a custom-agent / `runSubagent` handoff pending.
3. Wait for the command to finish so Copilot receives the automatic terminal-completion notification.
4. Observe that the automatic turn's request has a reduced tool set (diagnosed occurrence: 27 tools, missing `runSubagent`, `vscode_askQuestions`, and `testFailure`) and customization discovery lists 0 agents. The handoff cannot proceed.
5. Send a normal user message (for example, "try again"). Customization discovery lists the agents again (diagnosed occurrence: 10), the request includes the previously missing tools (30 tools), and `runSubagent` succeeds. The model is unchanged.

Exact steps beyond this trace are not fully known. See limits below.

## Reproduction and limits

The symptom has been observed at least twice. Detailed tool-snapshot diagnostics were checked for the latest occurrence only.

The reason the terminal tool returned before the command completed is unknown.

This trace does not establish that the five-minute idle-silence threshold fired. The tool returned shortly after invocation, and the completion notice arrived roughly four minutes later.

The cause of the changed agent/tool set is also unknown.

issues.title: Copilot harness sends rejected allow-all mode when Manual permissions is selected
issues.body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Problem

When the Copilot harness is run with **Manual** permissions mode selected, submitting a request fails because the Copilot SDK receives and rejects the `allow-all` permission mode.

```text
Error: (sendFailed) Copilot SDK rejected permission mode 'allow-all'
```

The selected Manual mode and the permission mode sent to the SDK appear to be out of sync.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Copilot harness.
2. Select **Manual** permissions mode.
3. Submit a request that starts a turn.

## Actual behavior

The turn fails with `sendFailed` because the SDK rejects permission mode `allow-all`.

## Expected behavior

The harness should send the SDK permission mode corresponding to Manual permissions, and the turn should start normally. It should not request `allow-all` while Manual mode is selected.

issues.title: Chat unexpectedly resets to Ask across harnesses during mode availability changes
issues.body:
## Summary

Users report that Chat unexpectedly resets to **Ask** in both the Local and Copilot/Agent Host harnesses. Managed-settings or harness-availability changes are suspected, including reports involving `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode`, but the triggering event and regression commit are not yet confirmed.

## Code finding

There is a plausible persistence defect in the shared composer:

1. Mode-list changes run `validateCurrentChatMode()` and then `_restorePersistedCustomModeIfAvailable()`.
2. Validation applies automatic Agent/Ask fallbacks through `setChatMode()` with its default `storeSelection: true`.
3. `setChatMode2()` serializes that fallback into the session input state.
4. Custom-mode restoration then reads the potentially overwritten state.

This can erase a preferred mode during temporary mode unavailability. However, it does **not by itself explain an Ask transition**: with `chat.agent.enabled=true`, a missing custom mode normally falls back to Agent. `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` restricts auto-approval and does not directly disable Agent mode.

## Expected

Temporary provider, harness, or mode unavailability should not permanently replace the user's selected mode. Restoration must also respect current policy and any explicit user mode change made while the preferred mode is unavailable.

## History / attribution

- `fd9cf8e3dd1` (#278683) introduced the relevant session-input mode persistence mechanism.
- `61915ccbab01b` (#278650) added the Agent-disabled-to-Ask validation branch.
- `8fa554d6e0030` (#324843) added late custom-mode restoration after validation.
- `fa5d013e93f` (#331715) changes Claude/Codex availability under managed settings and may expose the persistence behavior for those sessions.
- There is not enough evidence to identify #331715 or #338172 as the regression for the reported cross-harness Ask reset.

## Investigation needed

Capture the event sequence when the reset occurs:

- session type / harness;
- current UI mode and persisted input-state mode;
- effective `chat.agent.enabled` value and policy source;
- mode list before and after the reset;
- managed-settings and provider/harness availability changes.

Add sequence-based coverage for:

- custom mode disappearance and reappearance;
- built-in Agent disable and re-enable;
- persisted custom mode while Agent mode becomes policy-disabled;
- explicit user selection while a preferred mode is unavailable;
- unrelated input-state synchronization during the availability gap.

A simple `storeSelection: false` change in validation is insufficient: custom-mode restoration can immediately undo Agent disablement, built-in Agent is not restored after re-enable, and later input-state synchronization can still serialize the fallback mode.

issues.title: Agents Window: User MCP config changes do not refresh until the next chat message

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
## Type of Issue

Bug

## Description

Changes to the Copilot CLI user MCP configuration are not reflected in the Agent Customizations UI while the current runtime session is idle. A newly added server appears only after sending another chat message.

This suggests that the Copilot runtime does not publish an updated MCP server inventory when `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` changes. The client therefore has no update to apply until unrelated chat activity causes the runtime to refresh.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start with no `slack-github` entry in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`.
2. Open **Agent Customizations** and select **MCP Servers**.
3. Add a user-level server, for example:

   ```sh
   copilot mcp add slack-github -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
   ```

4. Return to the MCP Servers list.
5. Observe that `slack-github` is not shown.
6. Send any new chat message.
7. Return to the MCP Servers list and observe that `slack-github` now appears.

## Expected

The Copilot runtime watches `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` (or otherwise observes user MCP configuration changes) and emits an updated server inventory. The Agent Customizations UI updates without requiring a new chat message or session restart.

## Actual

The MCP Servers list remains stale until another chat message causes the runtime to refresh.

## Related

Found while verifying #337998. That issue covers displaying the definition and source for an already-discovered user MCP server; this issue covers discovering configuration changes immediately.

Related to #338162

## UI nit

Rows that show a compatibility/status icon currently place the icon with the trailing actions. This shifts controls such as **Start**, the enablement toggle, and the overflow menu horizontally compared with rows that do not have a status indicator.

## Expected

Place the status icon in front of the corresponding status message (for example, before **Partially supported** or **Unsupported**) so the trailing action area has a stable alignment across rows.

- Rows without a status icon keep their actions aligned.
- Rows with a warning or error icon insert it into the action area and shift the other controls.

`[item name]`

issues.title: Agents setting does not enable experimental new-session composer layout

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
When `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` is enabled in the Agents settings target, the new-session composer layout does not change. The same value works from User settings.

The setting is registered with `ConfigurationScope.APPLICATION`, while the Agents settings target is backed by the sessions workspace configuration. Application-scoped values are intentionally excluded from workspace configuration, so the Agents value is ignored.

The setting is specific to the Agents window and should use window scope so either User or Agents settings can control it.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Enable `chat.experimental.sessions.unifiedWorkspacePicker`.
2. Add `"sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout": true` to Agents settings.
3. Open the new-session composer.

Expected: The experimental composer layout is enabled.
Actual: The Agents setting is ignored.

issues.title: Allow GitHub pull request links in Agents Window to open in external browser

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

issues.body:
When the GitHub Pull Requests extension is installed, clicking a GitHub pull request link in the Agents Window opens the pull request in the extension's PR editor view. There does not appear to be a way to open that link in the external browser instead.

Shift+click and the link context menu still route to the PR editor.

It would be useful to offer an explicit **Open in Browser** action (for example in the link context menu and/or via a modifier click) so users can bypass the extension's link handling when needed.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install/enable the GitHub Pull Requests extension.
2. Open an Agents Window conversation containing a link to a GitHub pull request.
3. Click the link, Shift+click it, or use the link context menu.

### Actual
The pull request opens in the GitHub Pull Requests extension PR editor view.

### Expected
There is an action to force the link to open in the external browser.

issues.title: Agents: Dev Container workspace submenu closes during refresh

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
## Type of Issue

Bug

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable:
   - `sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled`
   - `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout`
   - Dev Container Agent Host support
2. Open the Agents window and start a new Agent Host session.
3. Open the workspace picker.
4. Open the mode submenu for a folder with a Dev Container configuration.
5. Wait for a passive workspace-picker refresh.

## Actual Behavior

The folder mode submenu closes as its row is refreshed, making the submenu appear impossible to open or use.

## Expected Behavior

The open submenu remains attached to the same workspace row across passive refreshes.

## Additional Context

Workspace rows did not have stable identities, so submenu preservation could not match the refreshed row to the open submenu.

Fixed by #338447.

labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
## Type of Issue

Bug

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable `sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled`.
2. Open the Agents window and start a new session.
3. Open the workspace picker with enough recent folders for the list to scroll.
4. Scroll down and wait for passive workspace information, such as Dev Container availability, to refresh.

## Actual Behavior

The workspace picker repeatedly resets its scroll position to the top shortly after scrolling.

## Expected Behavior

Passive picker refreshes preserve the current viewport and do not interrupt browsing.

## Additional Context

The picker refresh rebuilds its rows while the filter retains focus, which reveals the checked or first row and moves the viewport back to the top.

Fixed by #338447.

issues.title: Agent Host: after a plugin preToolUse hook prints {}, later hooks (including deny hooks) don't run

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
## Summary

In a Copilot session on Agent Host, when a plugin's `preToolUse` hook prints `{}`, the `preToolUse` hooks after it never run, including a hook that would deny the tool call. If the first hook prints nothing, the second runs and the deny works. Copilot CLI runs both hooks in both cases.

This also works across plugins: one plugin's `{}` can stop another plugin's deny rule from running.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.139.1 (commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`), macOS 27.0 arm64
- Copilot Chat 0.67.0, bundled Copilot SDK runtime `1.0.15-unstable.35393089353.gfc44743`
- Session target: Copilot on Agent Host. The plugin is loaded through user-level `chat.pluginLocations`.
- For comparison: Copilot CLI 1.0.89

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a plugin folder with these two files.

   `plugin.json`

   ```json
   {"name": "hook-repro-a", "description": "Minimal preToolUse ordering repro", "version": "1.0.0", "hooks": "hooks.json"}
   ```

   `hooks.json`

   ```json
   {
     "version": 1,
     "hooks": {
       "preToolUse": [
         { "type": "command", "timeoutSec": 10, "bash": "echo hook1 >> /tmp/hooks-A.log; echo '{}'" },
         { "type": "command", "timeoutSec": 10, "bash": "echo hook2 >> /tmp/hooks-A.log; if grep -q BLOCK_ME; then echo '{\"permissionDecision\":\"deny\",\"permissionDecisionReason\":\"hook2 denied\"}'; fi" }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```

2. Add the folder to user-level `chat.pluginLocations`.
3. Start a new Copilot chat on Agent Host and send: `Create the file /tmp/out-A.txt containing BLOCK_ME using exactly one file creation. Do not retry.`
4. Check `/tmp/hooks-A.log` and whether `/tmp/out-A.txt` exists.
5. Control: repeat with a second plugin folder where hook 1 is `echo hook1 >> /tmp/hooks-B.log; true`, so it prints nothing.

## Results

| Case | Copilot CLI 1.0.89 | VS Code Agent Host |
|---|---|---|
| A: hook 1 prints `{}` | `hook1`, `hook2` ran; file blocked | **Only `hook1` ran; file written** |
| B: hook 1 prints nothing | `hook1`, `hook2` ran; file blocked | `hook1`, `hook2` ran; file blocked |

## Expected

Both hooks run, and the deny blocks the tool call:

- [VS Code agent plugins docs](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins): "When multiple hooks target the same event, all of them execute. For PreToolUse hooks, the most restrictive permission decision across all hooks wins."
- [GitHub Copilot hooks reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference): "If multiple hooks of the same type are configured, they execute in order. For `preToolUse`, if any hook returns `"deny"`, the tool is blocked."

## Other differences from Copilot CLI we observed

With the same plugin files on the same machine, Copilot CLI followed the GitHub hooks reference in each of these cases:

- `postToolUse` also stops after the first hook prints `{}`.
- A `preToolUse` hook that exits with code 2 is not treated as a deny.
- `matcher` is ignored, so a hook with `"matcher": "bash"` also runs for `apply_patch` and other tools.
- `agentStop` and `Stop` plugin hooks never run. `sessionStart`, `userPromptSubmitted` and `sessionEnd` do run.
- The `preToolUse` input has `workingDirectory` instead of the documented `cwd`.
- A repository hook in `.github/hooks/` that printed `{}` did **not** stop a plugin's deny. Only plugin hooks are affected.

issues.title: Terminal created with `location: { parentTerminal }` is not split when parent has a numeric ID
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A (the bug is in the extension API; reproducible with a minimal test extension)

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code 1.139.1 (Universal)
- OS Version:  macOS Tahoe 26.6.2

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In an extension, create a terminal and wait for it to open:
   ```ts
   const parent = vscode.window.createTerminal({ name: 'parent' });
   parent.show();
   await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000));
   ```
2. Create a second terminal with that terminal as its parent:
   ```ts
   vscode.window.createTerminal({ name: 'child', location: { parentTerminal: parent } });
   ```

**Expected:** `child` opens as a split next to `parent`.

**Actual:** `child` opens in its own terminal group, not split.

### Cause

`MainThreadTerminalService._deserializeParentTerminal` finds the parent with:

```ts
const parentTerminal = await this._extHostTerminals.get(location.parentTerminal.toString());
```

`_extHostTerminals` is keyed only by the temporary string ID (a UUID) that extension-created terminals get before they open. `ExtHostTerminalIdentifier` is `string | number`, though:

- When an extension-created terminal opens, `$acceptTerminalOpened` replaces its `_id` with the numeric instance ID, so later references to it send a number.
- Terminals the user created, or ones restored from a previous session, only ever have a numeric ID.

In both cases `location.parentTerminal.toString()` produces something like `"5"`. That never matches a UUID key, so the lookup returns `undefined` and the terminal is created without a parent. The split only works if the parent is an extension-created terminal that hasn't opened yet.

issues.title: Copilot Chat text overlaps tool/search activity in narrow panels

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
## Bug description

In a narrow Copilot Chat panel, tool/search activity rows can overlap the surrounding assistant response text. The activity labels and the following markdown are rendered on top of each other instead of being laid out vertically, making both difficult to read. The third screenshot also shows an inline result row clipped/overlapping the surrounding text.

This is separate from the magnifying-glass icon issue reported in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337773. The maintainer confirmed in that issue that this behavior is unrelated and appears to be poor wrapping.

## Screenshots

- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63c03d4d-6db1-4710-8588-925fbbba5eba
- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54eddbce-a380-48d6-9583-f4d1fefaf01b
- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/514a1ee4-56ff-4808-b850-af10d929d928

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Copilot Chat in a narrow panel.
2. Run an agent request that performs tool discovery/search and displays tool or search activity.
3. Observe the activity rows while the response is streaming and the subsequent markdown response is rendered.
4. Resize the panel wider and compare the layout.

## Actual behavior

At narrow widths, activity labels and response text overlap, with some rows appearing clipped or layered over adjacent content.

## Expected behavior

Each activity row and markdown block should occupy its own measured vertical space and wrap without overlapping or clipping, regardless of the chat panel width.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.140.0-insider (user setup)
- Commit: `fee7930e951e766078247fc91b2513744f8b7ef5`
- Date: 2026-09-28T09:45:12+02:00
- Electron: 43.7.3
- Chromium: 150.0.7871.250
- Node.js: 24.21.0
- GitHub Copilot: 1.0.89-3
- GitHub Copilot SDK: 1.0.15-preview.3
- OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19045
- Mode: Agent

## Related reports checked

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337727 reports bizarre rendering of search errors, but is a different rendering failure and is already closed.
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324559 concerns wrapped terminal output, not the Copilot Chat activity layout.
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330627 concerns intermediate responses being hidden in the completed-steps disclosure, not text overlap.

issues.title: agentHost: Avoid rescanning Codex sessions on existing rollout updates

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
## Context

#337300 added live discovery for external Codex sessions by recursively watching `<codexHome>/sessions` and refreshing the native catalog after file changes. The watcher currently uses `event.affects(sessions)`, so appends to an existing session rollout invalidate discovery just like creation of a new session.

`CodexChatDiscovery` coalesces invalidations to at most one scan every five seconds, which bounds the work but still permits repeated `thread/list` calls during a long streaming turn even though the set of sessions has not changed.

## Research notes

- Codex rollout paths currently look like `<codexHome>/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<thread-id>.jsonl`.
- `FileChangesEvent` preserves `ADDED`, `UPDATED`, and `DELETED` change types, so the listener can distinguish new rollout artifacts from appends to existing ones.
- Catalog and transcript refreshes currently share `CodexChatDiscovery.onDidInvalidate`: every discovery invalidation also invalidates subscribed `CodexChatHistory` instances. Simply ignoring all `UPDATED` events would risk breaking live transcript updates.
- The non-recursive home watcher also observes `session_index.jsonl` and `state_*.sqlite(-wal)`. SQLite WAL churn may be another source of catalog rescans even when only transcript content changed.
- The existing 60-second safety refresh should remain as recovery for missed watcher events and alternate native catalog locations.

## Suggested direction

Split storage changes into catalog and transcript invalidation paths, then scope catalog invalidation to changes that can add/remove or materially reclassify a session. A possible first pass:

- Treat an `ADDED` session rollout `.jsonl` as a catalog invalidation.
- Treat `UPDATED` rollout files as transcript-only invalidations.
- Keep `session_index.jsonl` changes as catalog invalidations for title/metadata updates.
- Determine whether `state_*.sqlite(-wal)` changes can be classified more narrowly; avoid catalog refreshes for ordinary turn persistence while preserving discovery for state-DB-only sessions.
- Retain debounce/retry/safety-refresh behavior as a correctness fallback.

The exact filter should account for cross-platform watcher behavior, including creation of dated directories, atomic replacement, and batched add/update events.

## Acceptance criteria

- Appending repeatedly to an existing external Codex session does not repeatedly call `thread/list`.
- Creating a new external Codex session appears promptly in the VS Code session list.
- Live history for an already observed external session continues to update.
- Metadata changes that affect the session list still propagate.
- Tests cover add versus update events, sustained writes, state DB/index changes, and the periodic safety refresh.

issues.title: Agents window: automation target silently reverts from "Use Dev Container" to "Use Remote Host"
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
