<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code: 1.139.1, commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`, stable, 2026-09-25
- OS: Windows host → WSL2 (Ubuntu-20.04) → Dev Container
- Remote - WSL: 0.104.3

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On a Windows host, open a folder in WSL2 that contains a `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`.
2. Open the **Agents** window and create an **Automation** (any prompt, any schedule).
3. In the automation's target picker, select **Use Dev Container**.
4. Save the automation.
5. Reopen the same automation's configuration.

### Expected

The picker still shows **Use Dev Container**, and scheduled runs execute inside the dev container — matching a manually created agent session, where choosing the same option correctly connects to the WSL host and starts the session inside the dev container.

### Actual

The picker shows **Use Remote Host**. The selection is silently discarded — no warning, no error, no indication that the choice is unsupported.

Inspecting the persisted automation confirms the target never captured the dev container:

- `providerId: agenthost-hex-<hex>` — hex-decodes to `wsl:Ubuntu-20.04`
- `folderUri` carries `?_ah=eyJzY2hlbWUiOiJmaWxlIn0` — base64-decodes to `{"scheme":"file"}`

Re-saving with **Use Dev Container** advances `updatedAt` but leaves the `target` block **byte-identical**.

Consequence: the scheduled session runs on the WSL host instead of in the container, so the prompt fails on container-only paths. In my case the workspace contains a git worktree whose `.git` file points at a path that exists only inside the container, so the very first git command failed with `fatal: not a git repository: /<container-only-path>`.

### Analysis

This looks structural rather than like a simple persistence bug. `ps` on the WSL host during a *manual* dev container session shows that the in-container agent host is an ephemeral **relay** spawned by the WSL agent host, not an independently registered provider:

```
WSL agent host
 └─ @devcontainers/cli/devcontainer.js exec --workspace-folder <workspace-folder>
     └─ docker exec -i -u <user> -w <container-workspace> <image-sha> … code … agent relay '<id>'
         └─ (in container) code … agent host --port 0 --new-instance --idle-timeout 300
                           bootstrap-fork --type=agentHost
                           copilot-runtime --headless
```

So "dev-container-ness" is resolved **live at session creation** and exists only in the running session — there is no persistable dev-container provider identity. An automation must serialize a *static* target; the schema can name a remote agent host (`providerId`) but appears to have no slot for "…then relay into the dev container," so the selection degrades to the plain `file:` folder under the WSL authority. The relay's `--new-instance --idle-timeout 300` also means it exits roughly five minutes after going idle, so it could not own a schedule even if it were nameable.

Supporting log evidence (WSL-side `agenthost.log`) shows the WSL agent host is the durable owner and executor of the schedule:

```
[AgentHostAutomationService] Claimed due Automation schedules: runs=2, automations=2
[AgentHostAutomationService] Created durable manual automation run …
[AgentHostAutomationService] Linked automation run to session …
```

### Ask

Either:

1. **Support it** — persist a dev-container target and have the owning agent host run `devcontainer up` / `devcontainer exec` at trigger time. This is exactly what I now do manually from inside the automation prompt, and it works reliably.
2. **Fail loudly** — if dev container targets are unsupported for automations, disable or hide the option in the automation target picker, or surface an explicit warning, rather than silently reverting the selection.

Option 2 alone would have saved considerable debugging: the failure mode is invisible until a scheduled run fails inside the prompt for an unrelated-looking reason.

### Workaround

Target the WSL host and have the prompt enter the container itself, resolving it by the stable dev container label rather than by the auto-generated container name (which changes on rebuild):

```bash
CID=$(docker ps -q --filter "label=devcontainer.local_folder=<workspace-folder>")
docker exec -u <user> -w <container-workspace> "$CID" bash -lc '<command>'
```

issues.title: MCP runtime enablement changes do not update the Customizations switch

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verification-found
labels.description: Issue verification failed

labels.name: chat-customizations
labels.description: Instruction, agent, skill, and prompt files related issues

issues.body:
## Type of Issue
Bug

## Reproduction
1. Open Chat in Code OSS.
2. Run `/mcp disable component-explorer` (or disable an MCP server from another Copilot CLI/runtime entry point).
3. Open **Agent Customizations** and select **MCP Servers**.

## Actual behavior
The Copilot runtime disables the MCP server and reports `session.mcp_server_status_changed`, but the MCP switch can remain enabled because only the runtime lifecycle state is updated. Changes made outside the VS Code MCP UI are not consistently reflected in the client-owned global enablement model.

A concurrent Agent Host reconciliation can also race an externally observed disable and immediately re-enable the server.

## Expected behavior
MCP enablement transitions reported by the Copilot SDK should update the corresponding scoped customization decision and the Agent Customizations switch, regardless of whether the change originated from a slash command, Copilot CLI, or another runtime entry point. Host-initiated reconciliation events must not be mistaken for external changes.

## Notes
The SDK exposes `session.mcp_server_status_changed`, including `disabled`, `pending`, `connected`, and other lifecycle states. The Agent Host should reconcile observed runtime enablement with its desired scoped enablement while preventing feedback loops.

issues.title: Agents window: allow a configurable or full-width conversation column
issues.body: ## The problem The dedicated Agents window constrains each conversation to a fixed, centered column. On a wide monitor this leaves substantial unused space on both sides, even when the content is inherently wide. A constrained default is reasonable for prose readability, but agent responses frequently contain content where width is more valuable than short line length, including: - Markdown tables - Mermaid architecture and dependency diagrams - Code blocks and diffs - Logs, stack traces, and command output - Side-by-side comparisons These currently require horizontal scrolling, excessive wrapping, or compressed/tall diagrams while usable monitor space remains empty. ## Illustrative examples These mockups use the same wide table and representative Mermaid architecture diagram. ### Current constrained conversation column The table is clipped behind horizontal scrolling and the diagram must be compressed into the narrow column: ### Proposed user-selected full-width conversation column The same table and diagram can use the available workspace width without hiding the Sessions, Changes, or Files areas: ## Proposed behavior Please provide a user-selectable way to widen the conversation column in the dedicated Agents window. For example: - Keep the current constrained width as the default. - Add a command or chat-layout control to toggle between the default and wide/full-width modes. - Optionally expose a setting for the preferred maximum conversation width. - Persist the choice globally or per workspace/session. An alternative would be to keep prose paragraphs constrained while allowing wide block content such as tables, diagrams, code blocks, and logs to expand into the available width. ## Why this should be configurable The ideal line length depends on the content. A narrow measure improves prose readability, but it works against the structured technical output that coding agents routinely produce. Making the layout user-selectable preserves the existing default while allowing people with wide monitors to optimize for their tasks. ## Related issues This request is specifically for the newer dedicated Agents window. Similar requests for earlier chat surfaces were closed before this window and its current workflows existed: - #251848 - #279870 - #311760 - #283355 - #282052 The dedicated Agents window and wide technical artifacts make the tradeoff different enough to warrant a configurable option rather than changing the default for everyone.

issues.title: GitHub Copilot Chat "Copilot CLI" model fails in VS Code after Business → Enterprise migration

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
Type: Bug Support Report: GitHub Copilot Chat "Copilot CLI" model fails in VS Code after Business → Enterprise migration ## Summary Since our GitHub account/organization was migrated from GitHub Copilot Business to GitHub Copilot Enterprise (on `dhl.ghe.com`, a GHE.com tenant with data residency) approximately 4 days ago, the built-in "Copilot CLI" agent/model inside VS Code's chat view fails on every message with: ``` Error: (sendFailed) Error: Request session.create failed with message: SDK session authentication failed: network fetch failed: request failed: error decoding response body ``` The GitHub Copilot Chat output channel additionally logs: ``` 2026-09-28 08:27:02.245 [error] [CopilotCLIModels] Failed to fetch available models: Error: Failed to fetch Copilot user info: 401 Unauthorized: {"message":"Bad credentials"} ``` All other Copilot Chat functionality (the classic chat models, e.g. Claude/GPT) authenticates and works normally in the same VS Code window. GitHub Copilot Enterprise on the web (`https://dhl.ghe.com`) also works normally. Other colleagues on the same Enterprise tenant do not report this issue. ## Environment - OS: Windows - VS Code version: 1.139.1 (commit 04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1), x64 - GitHub Copilot Chat is built into VS Code (no separate marketplace extension to update); "Help > Check for Updates" reports no updates available. - Auth provider: `github-enterprise`, `github-enterprise.uri` = `https://dhl.ghe.com` - `github.copilot.advanced.authProvider` = `github-enterprise` - Signed-in account: Victor-Hugo (single account; verified no conflicting `github.com` session is also signed in) - Copilot token SKU reported by extension: `copilot_enterprise_seat_quota` ## Timeline - ~4 days ago: GitHub account/org migrated from Copilot Business to Copilot Enterprise. - Since then: every attempt to chat using the "Copilot CLI" model/agent host in VS Code fails immediately with the error above. - Classic Copilot Chat (non-CLI models) in the same VS Code instance has continued to work without interruption throughout. ## Troubleshooting already performed 1. Signed out / signed back in to the GitHub account in VS Code — over 100 times. No change. 2. Restarted VS Code — over 200 times. No change. 3. Verified network connectivity is not the cause: - TCP connectivity to Copilot API endpoints succeeds. - No corporate proxy environment variables set (`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` empty). - Web-based GitHub Copilot Enterprise Chat (`https://dhl.ghe.com`) works normally from the same machine/network. - Other Copilot Chat models within the very same VS Code window/session authenticate and respond normally — only the "Copilot CLI" model/agent host fails. 4. Retrieved the local GH token used by the CLI integration (Windows Credential Manager entry `https://dhl.ghe.com:Victor-Hugo.copilot-cli`) and validated it directly: - `GET https://api.dhl.ghe.com/user` → `200 OK`, returns correct login (`Victor-Hugo`). - `GET https://dhl.ghe.com/api/v3/user` → `200 OK`. - `GET https://api.dhl.ghe.com/user/orgs` → `200 OK`, returns the correct org (`Copilot-Enterprise-Standard`), no `X-GitHub-SSO` authorization challenge header present (SSO is not the blocker). - The **same token**, when tested against the generic `https://api.github.com/user` endpoint, returns: ``` 401 Unauthorized {"message":"Bad credentials","documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/rest","status":"401"} ``` This is **the same "Bad credentials" message logged by the `CopilotCLIModels` component** in the GitHub Copilot Chat output channel. 5. Inspected VS Code's local session state (`open-sessions-state.json` under the Copilot CLI data folder): most `session.create` attempts from the last few days (including several from today) show `"working": false`, while sessions that do succeed show `"working": true`. This confirms the failure is reproducible and not a one-off transient event tied to a single stale chat thread. 6. Confirmed VS Code settings correctly point to the Enterprise tenant: ```json "github-enterprise.uri": "https://dhl.ghe.com", "github.copilot.advanced": { "authProvider": "github-enterprise" } ``` 7. Searched for a setting to override the API host specifically for the "Copilot CLI" agent host (`chat.modelConfiguration.panel.agent-host-copilotcli`) — no such override exists in the current build. ## Root cause (as far as we can determine client-side) The token is valid and correctly scoped to our GHE.com Enterprise tenant (`dhl.ghe.com` / `api.dhl.ghe.com`). However, the `CopilotCLIModels` component of the built-in "Copilot CLI" agent host in VS Code appears to send that Enterprise-scoped token to the **generic `api.github.com` host** instead of the tenant-specific host (`api.dhl.ghe.com`), which correctly rejects it as "Bad credentials." This happens specifically for the model-listing/session-creation call path used by the "Copilot CLI" model, while the rest of GitHub Copilot Chat (which correctly targets the Enterprise host) works fine. This appears to be a product defect in how the built-in "Copilot CLI" agent host resolves the API host for GHE.com tenants with a custom domain, surfacing right after our Business → Enterprise migration (possibly because this code path was not previously exercised, or previously defaulted correctly for Business but not for this Enterprise/GHE.com configuration). ## Requested action Please investigate why the `CopilotCLIModels` component (built-in "Copilot CLI" agent/model host in VS Code's Copilot Chat) does not honor the `github-enterprise.uri` setting / GHE.com tenant host when validating the user's Copilot token, and instead calls `api.github.com`, causing `401 Bad credentials` and the resulting `session.create` failure for every message sent to that model. ## Attachments available on request - Full `GitHub Copilot Chat` output log. - `open-sessions-state.json` excerpt showing repeated `"working": false` session-create attempts. - Screenshot of VS Code settings showing `github-enterprise.uri` configuration. issues.title: Repository-scoped Copilot content exclusions affect unrelated files in multi-repository workspaces

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

**AI disclosure**: This issue was drafted with AI assistance. A human reproduced the behavior and technically investigated it. This is a real problem observed in our company environment.

**Anonymization**: Repository names, paths, and remotes below are placeholders. The workspace structure and repository relationship reflect the reproduced setup.

**Summary**

A Copilot content exclusion configured for a nested repository appears to affect unrelated files in the outer repository when both repositories are present in the same VS Code workspace.

**Environment**
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.41
- VS Code Version: 1.139.1
- OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04.1
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): model independ
- Logs: see below

The content exclusion is configured only for the nested repository:
```
git@code.example.invalid:vendors/controller-kit.git:
  - "**/*"
```

**Workspace structure**
```
device-suite/                              [outer Git repository]
├── apps/
│   └── data-service/src/DatabaseControlService.hpp
├── services/
│   └── edge-gateway/src/api/firmware/mod.rs
└── vendors/
    └── controller-kit/                   [separate nested Git repository]
```

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open device-suite as a VS Code workspace.
2. Keep the nested vendors/controller-kit repository in the workspace.
3. Configure the `**/*` content exclusion for the nested repository only.
4. Ask Copilot to access a file elsewhere in the outer repository, such as one under apps/ or services/.

**Actual behavior**

Copilot reports files outside the nested repository as excluded:
```
[debug] File /workspaces/device-suite/apps/data-service/src/DatabaseControlService.hpp is ignored by content exclusion rule **/*
[debug] File /workspaces/device-suite/services/edge-gateway/src/api/firmware/mod.rs is ignored by content exclusion rule **/*
```
The behavior persists after reloading the VS Code window.

**Expected behavior**

The `**/*` rule should apply only to files within `vendors/controller-kit`. Files in the outer repository should remain available to Copilot unless they have their own applicable exclusion.

**Technical investigation**

Inspection of the installed extension bundle suggests that exclusion patterns from loaded repositories may be compiled into a shared matcher without preserving which repository supplied each pattern. This would allow the nested repository’s `**/*` rule to match files elsewhere in the workspace.

There is no `.copilotignore` file in the workspace, and Git does not report the affected files as ignored.

**Suggested fix**

Preserve the repository associated with each content exclusion and evaluate its path patterns only against files within that repository.

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Description

MCP Apps rendered in VS Code Insiders can successfully connect to the host and call MCP server tools via app.callServerTool(), but App-provided tools registered with App.registerTool() do not appear to be discovered or exposed to the Copilot agent.

Environment

Visual Studio Code - Insiders: 1.140.0-insider

MCP Apps protocol version reported by the host: 2026-01-26

SDK: @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps

Scenario

An MCP server tool (for example, show-datasources) opens an MCP App UI.

Before app.connect(), the App registers an ephemeral tool:

app.registerTool(
  "open-datasource-editor",
  {
    description: "Open the editor for the specified datasource",
    inputSchema: z.object({
      name: z.string(),
    }),
  },
  async ({ name }) => {
    // switch the current View from list mode to edit mode
  },
);

The App connects successfully.

The App can successfully call MCP server tools through app.callServerTool().

The Host initialization response includes capabilities such as:

{
  "hostCapabilities": {
    "serverTools": {
      "listChanged": true
    },
    "serverResources": {
      "listChanged": true
    }
  }
}

I instrumented the App iframe with window.addEventListener("message", ...) to inspect Host -> App messages.

No tools/list or tools/call request is ever sent from VS Code to the App.

On a follow-up request such as "open the editor for datasource test", Copilot calls the original MCP server tool (show-datasources) again, creating a second App instance, instead of invoking the App-provided open-datasource-editor tool in the existing View.

Expected behavior

If the App declares the tools capability and registers tools through App.registerTool(), VS Code should discover those App-provided tools, expose them to the active agent while the View is alive, and route tools/call back to the corresponding App instance when selected.

Actual behavior

App.registerTool() succeeds.

The MCP App itself renders correctly.

App -> Host -> MCP Server tool calls work.

No Host -> App tools/list request is observed.

No Host -> App tools/call request is observed.

The Copilot agent therefore appears unaware of the App-provided tool and invokes the MCP server tool again.

Question

Is support for App-provided / ephemeral tools registered through App.registerTool() currently implemented in VS Code's MCP Apps host integration?

If not, is this capability planned?

issues.title: Failed Automation session cannot be reopened after restart

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0-insider (`fee7930e951e766078247fc91b2513744f8b7ef5`)
- OS Version: macOS arm64
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents Window Automations
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol Fast (Internal only)
- Logs: Agent Host and AHP logs inspected locally; not attached because they contain session content.

### Description

An Automation session whose first turn fails can remain in the session list but become permanently unopenable after Agent Host restarts.

### Expected behavior

A failed session should reopen and show its recorded error, or be removed if no durable session was created.

### Actual behavior

Opening the session repeatedly fails with:

```text
Provider copilotcli is not ready to open copilotcli:/<session-id>; it may still be starting, so try again shortly
```

Waiting and retrying does not recover it.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Start an Automation run that creates a new Copilot session.
2. Make the first turn fail after session materialization but before the SDK writes restorable session metadata. The permission-mode race in #335928 is one current trigger.
3. Confirm that the Automation run fails and its session remains listed.
4. Restart VS Code or Agent Host.
5. Open the failed session.

### Root cause

**Confirmed:** Copilot emits `onDidMaterializeChat` before first-turn preflight completes. Agent Host then clears the provisional marker, publishes the session, and records it as ready.

If the first turn fails before the SDK persists session metadata, Agent Host retains the local failed turn but the provider cannot describe the session after restart. `CopilotAgent.getChatMetadata()` returns `undefined`, and restore classifies the registered-session metadata miss as a transient provider-startup error. Because the local session contains a turn, orphan reconciliation correctly does not discard it, leaving a permanently listed but unopenable session.

Relevant paths:

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts`
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts`
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentSideEffects.ts`

Possible directions are to keep the session provisional until provider backing is durable, or allow persisted Agent Host metadata to restore a registered failed session when SDK metadata is absent.

Related trigger: #335928.

**Type:** Bug / UX Improvement 

**Description:**
When dealing with a large number of merge conflicts, resolving a conflict causes the UI focus to jump unexpectedly. 

**Steps to Reproduce:** 

1. Open the Source Control view during a merge with many conflicted files.
2. Select and focus on the very first file under the "Merge Changes" section.

As soon as the conflict is resolved, the focus automatically jumps down to a file in the "Staged Changes" section. When there are dozens of files, this requires constant scrolling and manual searching to find where you left off.

The focus should move to the next available file in the "Merge Changes" list right below the one that was just resolved.

issues.title: BYOK Custom Endpoint: Mistral-hosted GLM 5.3 fails with `TypeError: e.replace is not a function` when response content is an array

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
# BYOK Custom Endpoint: Mistral-hosted GLM 5.3 fails with `TypeError: e.replace is not a function` when response content is an array

## Description

When using **GLM 5.3 hosted by Mistral AI** through the VS Code **Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) Custom Endpoint** provider, GitHub Copilot Chat fails even for a simple prompt such as `hello test`.

The same endpoint and API key work correctly with **Mistral Medium 3.5**.

Direct requests to the Mistral API using GLM 5.3 also succeed. However, the model returns a structured array containing `thinking` and `text` blocks instead of a plain string in `message.content`.

This appears to trigger a type error inside the Copilot extension, potentially because a string operation (`.replace()`) is being performed on an array.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the VS Code BYOK Custom Endpoint provider using a valid Mistral API key.
2. Add GLM 5.3 to `chatLanguageModels.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "Mistral AI",
  "vendor": "customendpoint",
  "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.179ce0dd}",
  "apiType": "chat-completions",
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "zai-glm-5-3",
      "name": "GLM 5.3 (Mistral Hosted)",
      "url": "https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions",
      "toolCalling": true,
      "vision": false,
      "thinking": true,
      "maxInputTokens": 872000,
      "maxOutputTokens": 128000
    }
  ]
}
```

3. Open GitHub Copilot Chat.
4. Select `GLM 5.3 (Mistral Hosted)` as the language model.
5. Start a new conversation.
6. Send the prompt `hello test`.
7. Observe the request failure.

## Actual Behavior

Copilot Chat displays repeated recovery messages:

```text
Autopilot recovered from a request error
Autopilot recovered from a request error
Autopilot recovered from a request error
```

Followed by:

```text
Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.

Reason: Please check your firewall rules and network connection then try again.

Error Code: e.replace is not a function.

TypeError: e.replace is not a function
    at xH._provideLanguageModelResponse
    at process.processTicksAndRejections
    at async xH.provideLanguageModelResponse
```

The stack trace points to:

```text
extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js
```

The displayed message suggests a firewall or network issue, but the underlying exception is a JavaScript type error.

## Expected Behavior

Copilot Chat should correctly process Chat Completions responses whose `message.content` contains structured content blocks rather than a plain string.

Ideally, it should:

- Extract and display the textual response from `text` blocks.
- Handle `thinking` blocks appropriately, respecting the model's reasoning capabilities.
- Preserve tool-calling functionality when supported by the model.
- Avoid attempting string operations on array objects.
- Provide an actionable error message if a response format is unsupported.

## Investigation

### 1. Model availability and capabilities

The model is correctly returned by the Mistral API:

```bash
curl -s https://api.mistral.ai/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MISTRAL_API_KEY" \
  | jq '.data[] | select(.id == "zai-glm-5-3")'
```

Relevant response fields:

```json
{
  "id": "zai-glm-5-3",
  "object": "model",
  "owned_by": "mistralai",
  "capabilities": {
    "completion_chat": true,
    "function_calling": true,
    "reasoning": true,
    "vision": false
  },
  "name": "zai-glm-5-3",
  "description": "Official Z.ai GLM 5.3 model",
  "max_context_length": 1048576,
  "aliases": [
    "zai-glm-5",
    "zai-glm-latest"
  ],
  "deprecation": null
}
```

This confirms that the model is available with the configured API key and supports chat completions, function calling, and reasoning.

### 2. Direct Chat Completions API test

The following request succeeds:

```bash
curl -sS https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MISTRAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "zai-glm-5-3",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}
    ],
    "stream": false,
    "max_tokens": 512
  }' | jq '{
    error,
    finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason,
    content_type: (.choices[0].message.content | type),
    chunk_types: (
      if (.choices[0].message.content | type) == "array"
      then [.choices[0].message.content[].type]
      else []
      end
    )
  }'
```

Actual output:

```json
{
  "error": null,
  "finish_reason": "stop",
  "content_type": "array",
  "chunk_types": [
    "thinking",
    "text"
  ]
}
```

The request succeeds without streaming and returns a completed response (`finish_reason: stop`).

However, **`message.content` is an array**, not a string.

### 3. Suspected root cause

Traditional OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions responses typically represent assistant content as a string:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": "Hello!"
  }
}
```

GLM 5.3 through Mistral instead returns structured content containing separate reasoning and text blocks.

If the Copilot Custom Endpoint implementation assumes `message.content` is always a string, an operation such as:

```javascript
content.replace(...)
```

would throw:

```text
TypeError: e.replace is not a function
```

This is consistent with the observed exception.

**This is a hypothesis based on the API response structure and the stack trace, not a confirmed root cause.** The specific value passed to `.replace()` has not been verified by inspecting the extension's internal implementation.

### 4. Comparison with another model

Mistral Medium 3.5 works successfully through the same BYOK Custom Endpoint configuration and API key.

This suggests that the issue is related to GLM 5.3's response format or the handling of its reasoning output, rather than general connectivity or API authentication.

## Environment

- **VS Code:** 1.139.1 (User Setup)
- **Commit:** `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`
- **Build date:** 2026-09-25
- **GitHub Copilot extension:** `1.0.85.r3537993703.g3514c9a`
- **GitHub Copilot Chat extension:** `1.0.15.3539089353.gcf44743`
- **OS:** Windows 11 x64 (`Windows_NT 10.0.26200`)
- **API tests:** Linux / WSL terminal
- **Electron:** 43.6.0
- **Node.js:** 24.20.0
- **Provider:** Custom Endpoint (`customendpoint`)
- **API type:** `chat-completions`
- **API endpoint:** `https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions`
- **Model:** `zai-glm-5-3`

## Additional Context

There is a potentially related issue concerning reasoning handling for GLM models through BYOK:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332870

However, this report specifically concerns a reproducible JavaScript type error when processing a response from GLM 5.3.

The model works through the Mistral API directly, and the returned content structure provides a concrete starting point for investigating the problem.

The failing request can be reproduced with a simple greeting, without requiring any workspace files, repository context, or complex tool calls.

issues.title: [chat-perf] TTFT and layoutDurationMs regressed >20% in multi-turn-user and many-small-chunks scenarios (first run)
issues.body:
**Summary**
First run of chat-perf pipeline: Detected two clear regressions exceeding the 20% threshold, with no prior baseline or open tracking issues covering these metrics/scenarios.

**Evidence**
- *multi-turn-user*: `timeToFirstToken` increased from 196ms ±10.5ms to 296.2ms ±35.12ms (+51.1%, p=0.001)
- *many-small-chunks*: `layoutDurationMs` increased from 139.48ms ±7.98ms to 169.55ms ±7.74ms (+21.6%, p=0)
- Both metrics are well outside typical noise and above regression threshold.
- No prior baseline window available, but absolute jumps and p-values indicate real regressions.
- No open tracking issues or Slack threads cover these scenarios/metrics.

**Suspect Commits**
- Unable to attribute to a specific commit due to lack of baseline history (first run).
- Recent changes affecting chat/session/agentHost code:
  - cb39ed9 (agent host: fix subagent rendering and tools)
  - bcb76ec (populate turn timings for agent-host providers)
  - 6cde2e9 (scope model and agent selection per chat)
  - d2f679c (fix bugs related to setting the right Chat model)

**Suggested Action**
- Open tracking issue for these regressions.
- Monitor next few runs to confirm persistence and begin commit attribution as baseline builds.
- Investigate recent changes in chat/agentHost/session handling for root cause.

issues.title: Add optional right-click drag to pan the editor viewport
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Currently, on tablets, the editor can be panned with a two-finger drag. On desktop devices without a touchpad, there doesn't seem to be an equivalent mouse-only gesture. Middle-button drag is already used for column selection in my setup, so I'd like to suggest an optional mouse-only gesture to pan/scroll the editor viewport like a canvas.

Right-click drag is one possible option, but I'm open to other similar approaches as well. If the maintainers prefer a different gesture, I'd be happy to use that instead.

For right-click drag specifically, a normal right-click should still open the context menu. Only a right-click drag beyond a small threshold would start panning, and it could suppress the context menu on release. This behavior could be disabled by default, for example behind a setting like `editor.rightClickDragToPan`, so it doesn't change the existing experience.

Thanks for considering this.

If there's anything I got wrong or missed above, feel free to point it out.

issues.title: Format Document silently no-ops on .py opened via an NTFS junction alias path (C:\Users → D:\Users); the real path works

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
Type: Bug ### Summary When a Python file is opened in VS Code through a **junction/alias drive letter** that differs from the path's `realpath`, the **Black Formatter** extension returns an *empty edit*: the document is unchanged, no notification is shown (even with `black-formatter.showNotifications: "always"`), and the `Black Formatter` Output channel stays completely empty. Opening the **same physical file** through its real path formats correctly. The bundled/CLI `black` itself is unaffected (it `realpath`s internally), and non-Python formatters (e.g. JS) work fine through the alias path — so the failure is localized to this extension's document-URI ↔ filesystem-path handling, before `black` is ever spawned. My setup aliases the whole user profile: `mklink /J C:\Users D:\Users`, so `C:\Users\Admin\...` and `D:\Users\Admin\...` are the same directory under two names. ### Environment - OS: Windows `` - VS Code: ` About>` - Black Formatter extension: `` - Python extension / Pylance: `` - Python interpreter: 3.10 (64-bit) `` - `black` (CLI): `` - VS Code launched as administrator: **yes** (but the real path succeeds under the same admin token, so privilege is *not* the variable) ### Steps to Reproduce (verified on author's machine) 1. Create a directory junction aliasing a folder, e.g. the user profile: ```cmd mklink /J C:\Users D:\Users ``` 2. Put a clearly unformatted Python file in it, e.g. `D:\Users\Admin\probe.py`: ```python x=1 def f( a,b ): return a+b if x==1: print( x ) ``` 3. In VS Code open the file **via the alias path**: `C:\Users\Admin\probe.py` (File ▸ Open File, type the `C:` path). Confirm `Copy Path` reports `c:/Users/Admin/probe.py`. 4. Run **Format Document** (or `Format Document With… ▸ Black Formatter`). - **Actual:** nothing happens. No text change, no toast, no entry in the `Black Formatter` Output channel — *even with* `"black-formatter.showNotifications": "always"`. 5. Close the tab, reopen the **same physical file via the real path**: `D:\Users\Admin\probe.py`. Confirm `Copy Path` reports `d:/...`. 6. Run **Format Document**. - **Expected & Actual:** file is formatted correctly. 7. Controls (same session): - A `.js` file inside `C:\Users\Admin\` formats fine via its alias path. - In a terminal, `python -m black C:\Users\Admin\probe.py` succeeds (CLI `black` is junction-transparent). ### Evidence matrix (what is author-verified) | Observation | Verified? | |---|---| | `C:\...\probe_root.py` Format Document = silent no-op | ✅ | | `C:\...\Documents\probe_docs.py` = silent no-op | ✅ | | `C:\...\probe_sub\probe_sub.py` = silent no-op | ✅ | | `C:\...\shuffle_down.py` = silent no-op | ✅ | | `D:\...\shuffle_down.py` = formatted | ✅ | | `D:\...\probe_root.py` = formatted | ⬜ *expected ✅ — author has not re-run this exact one; please confirm or I will* | | `python -m black C:\...\shuffle_down.py` = success | ✅ | | `.js` in `C:\Users\Admin\` formats fine | ✅ | | `showNotifications:"always"` → still silent on `C:` | ✅ | | Output channel “Black Formatter” empty on `C:` | ✅ | The `C:`-side failures hold across the profile root, `Documents`, and an arbitrary subdir, so it is **not** a per-directory or per-file quirk — the only variable that flips the result is the **drive letter / alias** used in the document URI. ### Why this points at the extension’s path handling, not `black` - `showNotifications: "always"` produces **no** notification on the alias path. If a `black` subprocess had been spawned and failed, this setting would surface it. Silence ⇒ the failure happens **before** spawn. - The `Black Formatter` Output channel is **empty** on the alias path ⇒ no subprocess argv/return was recorded ⇒ consistent with an empty-edit early return. - CLI `black` on the *same* alias path **succeeds** ⇒ `black` normalizes the junction fine; the discrepancy is in how the extension maps the `file:` URI / `fsPath` (and likely `${workspaceFolder}` / cwd / interpreter resolution) when the URI's drive letter ≠ `realpath`'s drive letter. - JS/other formatters work on the alias path ⇒ not a VS Code write-permission, workspace-trust, or file-system issue; specific to the Python formatter chain. ### Already ruled out (so please don't re-ask) - File is valid Python (Pylance reports no problems; CLI `black` parses & formats it). - Not a syntax-error / `force-exclude` / `pyproject.toml` skip (CLI on the same path returns “already well formatted / would be reformatted”, never a silent skip). - Not write permission / read-only / OneDrive / Defender controlled-folder-access (saving works; D-side same file formats; admin token identical both sides). - Not language mode (status bar shows `Python`; `Format Document With…` lists Black as the default provider). - Not workspace trust / restricted mode / stale `workspaceStorage` / a stray `.vscode\settings.json` (none exists at the profile root; clean-user-data-dir reproduces the same asymmetry once the formatter ext is loaded). - Not “single-file vs folder” open mode (alias-path single files fail; real-path single files succeed). - Line endings / encoding identical across both sides (same physical file). ### Hypothesis (clearly a hypothesis — please confirm or correct) The extension resolves the document to a `c:/…` URI but somewhere in its pre-spawn pipeline (cwd = `${workspaceFolder}` default, interpreter/env resolution, or the LSP/server document-sync path) it compares or re-derives the path against a `d:/…` `realpath`, the two strings disagree, and it returns an empty `TextEdit[]` instead of erroring. A junction/alias whose drive letter differs from `realpath` is the trigger. ### Settings not yet validated (would speed up triage) The following were **not** conclusively tested by the author on the alias path; if any one of them makes the `C:` side work, that localizes the bug further: - `black-formatter.cwd` set to `${fileDirname}` (default `${workspaceFolder}` is suspicious for alias/single-file cases) - `black-formatter.importStrategy` = `fromEnvironment` (vs default `useBundled`) - `black-formatter.serverTransport` = `pipe` (vs default `stdio`) - explicit `black-formatter.interpreter` / `black-formatter.path` pinned to the **real** `d:/…` python/black I can re-run these and update the issue if useful. ### Simpler repro to test generality (⚠️ NOT verified by author) To avoid touching the system profile dir, maintainers may try a plain junction: ```cmd mklink /J C:\jtest D:\jtest ``` then place `probe.py` in `D:\jtest` and compare opening it via `C:\jtest\probe.py` vs `D:\jtest\probe.py`. **If the generic-junction case does *not* reproduce**, the trigger may be specific to known-folder / profile path resolution rather than junctions in general — worth knowing either way. ### Current workaround Always open these files via the **real** path (`D:\Users\Admin\…`), never the alias (`C:\Users\Admin\…`). Pinning `D:\Users\Admin` in Explorer Quick Access and clearing alias-path entries from “Recently Opened” avoids accidentally re-triggering it. ### Notes Happy to provide wrapper-level logs proving `black` is never spawned on the alias path (a shim that records argv/cwd/exit before forwarding to real `black`), or to re-test any of the unvalidated settings above. If the root cause actually lives in core URI/`fsPath` junction handling or in `vscode-python` env resolution rather than this extension, let me know and I'll move/re-cross-reference accordingly. issues.title: Copilot Chat 0.67.0 (VS Code 1.139.1): GHES sign-in loop — models/user request hits api.github.com instead of the enterprise API host
issues.body:
### Summary

After signing in to GitHub Copilot with a GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) account, Copilot Chat immediately fails its models/user fetch and forces repetitive sign-in dialogs. Login itself succeeds (session is stored, a Copilot token is issued, its SKU is `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`), but the models request is sent to **api.github.com (dotcom)** instead of the enterprise host, and dotcom answers `401 {"message":"Bad credentials"}`. The client then marks the account as not signed in → infinite sign-in loop.

### Environment

- VS Code 1.139.1 on Linux x64, Ubuntu 22.04.5
- Copilot Chat 0.67.0 (bundled)
- GitHub Enterprise Server (host anonymized as `ghe.example.com` throughout)
- Settings: `github-enterprise.uri` = `https://ghe.example.com`, `github.copilot.advanced.authProvider` = `github-enterprise`
- Corporate HTTP(S) proxy in use

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the two enterprise settings above, then sign in with a GHES Copilot account.
2. Browser authorization completes normally.
3. Copilot Chat briefly shows the account as signed in, then repeatedly returns to the sign-in prompt.

Reproduced on a **brand-new `--user-data-dir` profile** containing only the two settings (no third-party extensions, no prior state), and after sign-out/sign-in, full app restarts, machine reboot, and remote OAuth revocation. Another machine on VS Code **1.133.0** with the same GHES works fine → regression introduced somewhere between 1.133.0 and 1.139.1.

### Expected vs. actual

Expected: models/user fetch against `https://api.ghe.example.com/...`
Actual: request sent to `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/user` carrying the enterprise token → 401.

### Log evidence

`GitHub Copilot Chat.log` (fresh profile):

    2026-09-28 13:08:21.780 [info] Logged in as <user>
    2026-09-28 13:08:22.689 [info] Got Copilot token for <user>
    2026-09-28 13:08:23.525 [info] copilot token sku: copilot_for_business_seat_quota
    2026-09-28 13:08:27.333 [error] [CopilotCLIModels] Failed to fetch available models: Error: network fetch failed: request failed: error sending request for url (https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/user)

In the regular profile the same URL is reached and returns `401 Unauthorized: {"message":"Bad credentials"}` — byte-identical to dotcom's standard response for an invalid token.

`agenthost.log` of the same run — the enterprise endpoints are known but not used by this request:

    2026-09-28 13:07:59.234 [info] [AgentHost] GitHub endpoints changed (api=https://api.ghe.example.com)
    2026-09-28 13:07:59.235 [info] [Copilot] Startup config changed (enterpriseHost=ghe.example.com), restarting CopilotClient
    2026-09-28 13:08:18.473 [info] [Copilot] Set CLI env: COPILOT_GH_HOST=ghe.example.com
    2026-09-28 13:08:20.485 [warning] [Copilot] Failed to refresh models (attempt 1), retrying in 521ms Request models.list failed with message: network fetch failed: request failed: error sending request for url (https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/user)

### Additional findings

- `api.ghe.example.com` (the enterprise API host) resolves and is reachable.
- In the bundled extension code (`resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js`), `copilotUserInfoURL` is built from `_dotcomAPIUrl`, which falls back to `https://api.github.com` when `_enterpriseUrlConfig` is unset for that service — even though the agent host already holds the enterprise endpoints (`_getDotComAPIUrl` → `https://api.<ghe-host>` would be correct).

### Impact

Copilot Chat is completely unusable with GHES on 1.139.1; the sign-in loop cannot be worked around from user settings.

issues.title: Test: Managed sandbox policies
issues.body:
Refs: #338172, #338274

- [x] macOS @roblourens 
- [x] Linux @rzhao271 
- [x] Windows @vijayupadya 

Complexity: 4

Authors: @dileepyavan


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338294%0A%0A&assignees=dileepyavan)

---

Test managed sandbox policies in Copilot Agent Host sessions. The main goal is that **sandbox enablement, bypass, and network access agree with managed policy, the UI remains understandable, and a managed sandbox-update conflict does not fail the session**.

## Set up

1. Use an Insiders build containing #338172 and #338274, or an author-provided build containing both. Record the build/commit. Use the **Copilot Agent Host / Copilot CLI provider**, not an unrelated chat provider.
2. Use a disposable workspace and a test machine/account where you are authorized to change managed policies. Record your original settings and back up any existing test policy file. Do not overwrite production enterprise policy or remove real organization restrictions.
3. Use one policy delivery source initially. The simplest is a file named `managed-settings.json` at the documented device location:

   | OS | File |
   |---|---|
   | macOS | `/Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json` |
   | Linux | `/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json` |
   | Windows | `%ProgramFiles%\GitHubCopilot\managed-settings.json` |

   Administrative permission may be required. Alternatively use [the mock policy server's File Deployment or server-managed setup](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/scripts/mock-policy-server/README.md). Use the nested JSON below, not flattened VS Code setting names, in the managed file. If other managed sources are present, ask the author to confirm the effective policy before testing.
4. **After changing a managed policy, fully quit/reopen VS Code and resume or create the specified session unless a scenario explicitly tests live refresh.**
5. Keep `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` set to **false** throughout this test (the default). This corresponds to `"enableCustomTerminalTool": false` in the Agent Host configuration and keeps sessions on the SDK's built-in shell tool.
6. In VS Code Settings, locate:

   | Purpose | User setting |
   |---|---|
   | Sandbox On/Off, macOS/Linux | `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` (`"on"` / `"off"`) |
   | Sandbox On/Off, Windows | `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows` (`"on"` / `"off"`) |
   | Permit bypass | `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` (boolean) |
   | Permit outbound network | `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` (boolean) |

   Below, **local enabled** means the OS-appropriate setting. **Session toggle** means **Sandboxing for terminal** in the session's permission picker; it is not the `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` (macOS/Linux) or `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows` (Windows) dropdown in Settings.
Each scenario below includes the managed JSON to use. Replace the test policy with that JSON rather than merging it with the previous scenario. Managed `true` for bypass/outbound permits access but does not override a more-restrictive local `false`.

## Understanding managed sandbox rules

The following table summarizes the policy-composition rules. These are runtime rules, not a promise that VS Code's Settings UI displays merged values for every field.

| Rule | Fields |
|---|---|
| Force-on (managed `true` wins) | `enabled` |
| Deny-wins (managed `false` wins) | `addCurrentWorkingDirectory`, `allowBypass`, `auth.git`, `auth.gh`, `allowDevToolAccess`, `network.allowOutbound`, `network.allowLocalNetwork`, `seatbelt.keychainAccess` |
| Floor-consistent (managed `true` wins) | `sandboxMcpServers`, `sandboxLspServers` |
| Intersection | `filesystem.readwritePaths`, `filesystem.readonlyPaths` |
| Union | `filesystem.deniedPaths` |
| Managed override, preserving user credentials | `network.proxy.url` |

Field names are relative to `sandbox`; `filesystem`, `network`, and `seatbelt` are under `sandbox.userPolicy` in the managed JSON.

For the four scenarios below:
- **enabled:** managed `true` requires sandboxing; managed `false` does not force a locally enabled sandbox Off. A supported, explicitly approved session bypass is separate from directly switching it Off.
- **allowBypass:** managed `false` blocks bypass. Managed `true` permits the approval flow but does not override local false or automatically approve a bypass. With managed enablement true and bypass omitted, bypass remains disabled.
- **allowOutbound:** managed `false` blocks outbound access. Managed `true` leaves the user free to choose local false through `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork`.

The other rows provide background only; they do not add filesystem or other test scenarios to this item.

## Test

### 1. enabled — managed sandbox enablement

1. Start with managed policy `{}`. Set `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` (macOS/Linux) or `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows` (Windows) to `"off"`. Create a session and ask the agent to run `pwd` in the terminal. Verify the setting and **Sandboxing for terminal** session toggle are editable.
2. Set managed policy to `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true } }`, restart VS Code, and resume the session. Verify the OS-appropriate setting above shows On and is disabled with an organization-managed indicator. The session toggle must also be On and locked, even though the saved local preference was Off.
3. Ask the agent to run `pwd`. Verify the session works and changing the session's approval level does not disable sandboxing.
4. Set managed policy to `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": false } }` and restart. Set the OS-appropriate local setting to On, then Off, using fresh sessions with no session override. Verify each follows the local value: managed false must not force sandboxing Off or lock the setting.

### 2. allowBypass — restrictions and approved session bypass

1. Set managed policy to `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "allowBypass": false } }`. Keep the saved local `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` preference true. Restart and verify its checkbox in Settings shows false and is disabled. Repeat with `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true } }`: omitted bypass permission must also leave bypass disabled.
2. Set managed policy to `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "allowBypass": true } }` and restart. Set `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` to false. Verify its checkbox remains false and editable; managed true must not force local bypass On.
3. Set `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` to true and `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` to false. Create two sessions. The **Sandboxing for terminal** toggle must still be On and locked in both; allowing bypass alone is not approval to disable the sandbox.
4. In the **first session**, ask the agent to run `curl http://example.com` in the terminal and request permission to retry outside the sandbox if blocked. On a supported sandbox-bypass prompt, reject/cancel once and verify sandboxing stays On. Retry and choose **Allow in this Session**. Verify the first session's toggle becomes Off only after approval succeeds; the second session and global sandbox setting remain unchanged. If no supported bypass prompt appears, report that rather than counting the step as passed.
5. Turn sandboxing back On in the first session. Verify the toggle becomes locked again and a new session-wide bypass requires another approval. A one-operation approval, if offered, must not disable sandboxing for the whole session.

### 3. allowOutbound — managed and local network restrictions

1. Set managed policy to `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "allowBypass": false, "userPolicy": { "network": { "allowOutbound": false } } } }`. Keep the saved local `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` preference true and restart. Verify its checkbox in Settings shows false and is disabled with an organization-managed indicator.
2. Ask the agent to run `curl http://example.com` in the terminal. Verify sandboxed outbound access is blocked; do not approve a bypass. Then ask it to run `pwd` and verify the session remains usable.
3. Change managed policy to `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "allowBypass": false, "userPolicy": { "network": { "allowOutbound": true } } } }` and restart. Set `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` to false. Verify its checkbox is false and editable, and `curl http://example.com` is still blocked. Managed true must not override local false.
4. Set `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` to true and repeat `curl http://example.com`. Verify it succeeds when the endpoint is reachable and no other restriction blocks it. Change the setting back to false while idle and verify the next terminal request is restricted again.
5. Repeat the local false/true check with managed policy `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "allowBypass": false } }`. With outbound policy omitted, `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` should remain editable and control network access.

### 4. Existing sessions and policy changes

1. With managed policy `{}`, create one session with an explicit **Sandboxing for terminal** On selection, one with Off, and one left at its default. Ask each to run `pwd` and keep their history. Include an older saved session if available.
2. Apply `{ "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "allowBypass": false, "userPolicy": { "network": { "allowOutbound": false } } } }`, restart, and resume the sessions. Verify sandboxing is On/locked, `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` and `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` show false/disabled, and an old saved Off does not bypass policy. `pwd` should work and `curl http://example.com` should be blocked.
3. Also resume a session that previously received **Allow in this Session** approval in scenario 2. Verify the current managed bypass denial revokes that escape: the old approval must not keep sandboxing disabled.
4. Remove the test restrictions by setting managed policy to `{}` and restart. Verify the OS-appropriate `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` / `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows` setting, `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands`, and `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` become editable and expose saved user preferences, unless another managed source still restricts them. An explicit session On stays On; a default session follows the current global setting. An old session Off invalidated by managed enforcement must not be silently restored.

issues.title: Agent Host: reconcile filesystem permissions with managed sandbox policies

milestone.title: On Deck
milestone.description: The Issues assigned to the **On Deck** milestone under consideration for the upcoming milestones.

issues.body:
## Summary
Investigate and define how Agent Host sandbox filesystem permissions should behave when local/client settings and runtime-managed policies differ, including read access required for VS Code-generated shell initialization scripts.

Related: #338172 and #338274. The shell-init dependency was identified in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338274#discussion_r4117181924.

## Current behavior
- VS Code builds the SDK sandbox configuration from current host settings and the session sandbox selection. The host resolves managed enablement/bypass/outbound restrictions, but does not compose the managed filesystem permission lists with local filesystem settings.
- A filesystem configuration that violates the runtime's managed restrictions can be rejected with `managed_sandbox_policy_conflict`.
- #338274 logs that conflict and continues using the runtime's last applied sandbox configuration, without publishing the rejected candidate as confirmed state. This avoids failing the session, but does not reconcile filesystem permissions or rewrite the local settings.
- Rejection applies to the configuration update as a whole; callers must not assume individual requested grants were applied.

## Shell initialization dependency
VS Code materializes shell-init scripts under:

```text
<userDataPath>/agentHost/shellInit/<sanitized-session-id>/<instance-id>/init.sh
```

PowerShell uses `init.ps1`. A typical macOS example is:

```text
/Users/alice/Library/Application Support/Code/agentHost/shellInit/abc-123/7f2a9c01/init.sh
```

Once a script is materialized, VS Code includes its session directory in the requested sandbox read grants and updates the sandbox before registering the script with the SDK.

Including the directory in the requested configuration is not proof that the runtime applied the grant. If the update is rejected and the retained configuration does not already allow the directory, new script registration must not be treated as ready. Existing tests document that unreadable init scripts can be silently skipped by the SDK.

## Illustrative scenario
1. Enable sandboxing and configure local filesystem grants.
2. Apply a managed filesystem policy that restricts those grants.
3. Create or resume a session and configure a shell initialization script.
4. If the combined candidate sandbox update is rejected, the runtime retains its previous configuration.
5. The session should remain usable, but a newly required script read grant may be absent. Local settings alone do not describe the effective runtime permissions.

This is a source-derived scenario, not a confirmed end-to-end reproduction against the currently bundled runtime. Verify the precise managed-filesystem conflict conditions and runtime behavior as part of this issue.

## Expected outcome / investigation
- Establish and document the runtime-owned rules for combining local filesystem preferences with managed restrictions. Preserve managed enforcement; do not bypass it or duplicate the runtime's policy parser in VS Code.
- Determine the appropriate runtime contract for required host-generated file access, including shell initialization scripts and session attachments.
- Distinguish requested filesystem permissions from those actually applied. Do not report rejected configuration as successful.
- Ensure operations that depend on new read grants are deferred or retried when those grants were not applied, while allowing normal session/turn startup to continue where safe.
- Cover first use, restored sessions, already-granted paths, rejected updates, and successful retries across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Relevant code
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionSandbox.ts`
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/sandboxConfigForSdk.ts`
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts` (`applySandboxConfig`)
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts` (`_sandboxExtraReadonlyPaths`, `_applyEffectiveSandboxConfig`, `_applyEffectiveShellInitScripts`)
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts` (shell init scripts suite)

issues.title: Copilot asks for node_modules read access if using pnpm global virtual store

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version:
  - @github/copilot: 1.0.85.r35379093703.g3514c9a
  - @github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.15.35393089353.gfc44743
- VS Code Version: 1.139.1
- OS Version: macOS (Darwin arm64 25.6.0)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-6 Sol, medium
- Logs: https://github.com/maxpatiiuk/vscode-pnpm-global-virtual-store/blob/main/docs/github-copilot-chat.log

## Summary

PNPM supports [virtualStoreType: global](https://pnpm.io/settings/node-modules#virtualstoretype), which stores `node_modules` dependencies as symlinks in a global directory, outside the project directory.

This causes VSCode Copilot to ask for `node_modules` read permission each time a new session is started.

## Reproduction

Barebones reproduction repository: https://github.com/maxpatiiuk/vscode-pnpm-global-virtual-store

Ensure pnpm 12 is installed.

1. Clone this repository

   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/maxpatiiuk/vscode-pnpm-global-virtual-store/
   cd vscode-pnpm-global-virtual-store
   ```

2. Install dependencies using pnpm

   ```sh
   pnpm install
   ```

3. Ask Copilot to read inside node_modules:

   > List contents of the node_modules/is-number/package.json file

   You get a permission prompt:

   ![Copilot prompt asking to read inside node_modules](https://github.com/maxpatiiuk/vscode-pnpm-global-virtual-store/raw/main/docs/image.png)

## Workarounds

The constant read access prompt is disruptive, and encourages blind "allow" clicking.

Ideally virtual global store is supported without additional config.

However, I wasn't able to get rid of permission prompt even after setting `github.copilot.chat.additionalReadAccessPaths` VSCode setting (see [.vscode/settings.json](https://github.com/maxpatiiuk/vscode-pnpm-global-virtual-store/blob/main/.vscode/settings.json)). Tried both in user and workspace config. Restarted VSCode.

issues.title: Agent Host default chat can remain archived after session unarchive

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
## Summary

An archived Agent Host session can be successfully unarchived while its default chat remains marked archived in host state. The next message is then rejected with:

> This chat is archived and read-only. Restore the chat to continue the conversation.

This is not an unarchive ordering race. In the captured incident, the host acknowledged the session unarchive and published the unarchived session status roughly 17 seconds before the rejected send; the archived worktree had also already been recreated.

## Observed sequence

1. Restore an archived session.
2. The restored session and default chat both have status `97` (`Idle | IsRead | IsArchived`).
3. Dispatch `session/isArchivedChanged { isArchived: false }`.
4. The host accepts it and publishes session status `33` (`Idle | IsRead`).
5. The default chat still has status `97`.
6. The next turn is rejected by `TurnAdmissionContribution` because it sees `chatArchived=true` while `sessionArchived=false`.

The affected resource was an `ahp-chat://default/...` chat. It was the only chat in the session and was never a peer chat or independently archived chat. No `chat/isArchivedChanged` action was sent for it.

## Model concern

Session archive and peer-chat archive are legitimately independent:

- `SessionState.status & IsArchived` is authoritative for session archival.
- `ChatState.status & IsArchived` is authoritative for independently archived, manageable peer chats.
- The default chat cannot be independently archived; its effective read-only state should derive from the session.

However, `createDefaultChatSummary` historically copied the complete `SessionSummary.status` bitset into the default chat. That copied session-owned `IsArchived` and `IsRead` flags into chat-owned state. Session unarchive correctly updates only the session reducer, because clearing every chat archive bit would incorrectly unarchive independently archived peers. The copied default-chat bit therefore becomes stale.

The underlying sharp edge is that `SessionStatus` is reused for session and chat states even though its orthogonal flags have different ownership at those scopes. `SessionChatSummary.archived` also provides a separate explicit representation of independent chat archival, so chat archive currently has multiple projections that must remain synchronized.

## Regression context

- The default-chat compatibility layer that copied the whole session status was introduced with #320931.
- The copied archive bit was initially mostly inert because admission checked only session archival.
- #337915 added independent nested-chat archival and began treating `ChatState.status & IsArchived` as authoritative during admission, exposing the stale bit on default chats.

## Expected invariant

When constructing the default chat from a session summary, only chat activity should be projected. Session-owned `IsRead` and `IsArchived` flags should not be copied into the default chat. Independent peer-chat archival should continue to flow through `ChatIsArchivedChanged` and persisted `chats[].archived` metadata.

It would also be worth considering a future Agent Host Protocol shape that separates activity from orthogonal read/archive fields, or uses distinct session/chat status types, so this ownership distinction is represented structurally.

## Telemetry gap

The incident currently appears only as an `agentHost.firstResponse` event with `outcome=error`. Admission rejection happens before turn tracking starts, so there is no `agentHost.turnCompleted` or `agentHost.turnFailed` event and no centrally queryable rejection reason. A dedicated bounded admission-rejection signal would make `reason=chatArchived && isDefaultChat=true` detectable as an invariant violation.

(Written by Copilot)

issues.title: [agent_stop] Prevent potential negative duration calculation due to clock skew

labels.name: unreleased
labels.description: Patch has not yet been released in VS Code Insiders

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
### Overview
In the `agent_stop` command handler, the duration of an active turn is calculated as:
`Timestamp::now().as_millisecond() - started_at.as_millisecond()`

If minor clock skew occurs between the agent host and client, this subtraction can potentially result in an invalid negative duration value.

### Proposed Solution
Add a defensive check during duration calculation to ensure that if `started_at` appears to be in the future relative to `Timestamp::now()`, the duration defaults safely to `0`.

Sign in using a GitHub account with an active Copilot subscription.
Open the Chat view from the Activity Bar.
Type any prompt and press Enter.
Observe the "Language model unavailable" error or the 403 Forbidden error.

issues.title: Enhance input validation and robustness in DefaultsOnlyConfigurationService.updateExperimentBasedConfiguration
issues.body:
### Description
While reviewing `DefaultsOnlyConfigurationService`, I noticed that `updateExperimentBasedConfiguration` accepts a `treatments` array without explicit validation or sanitization of its elements. Processing treatment keys or strings without checking for empty values, unexpected formatting, or malformed inputs could lead to redundant event firings or unexpected configuration state evaluations.

### Proposed Changes
1. **Input Sanitization:** Add strict validation to filter out empty, whitespace-only, or malformed treatment strings before triggering `_onDidChangeConfiguration`.
2. **Defensive Guard Clauses:** Ensure the method gracefully handles edge cases and invalid payloads securely.

### Benefit
This improves the overall robustness, predictability, and safety of the configuration service when handling dynamic or remote treatment arrays.

---
*I would love to submit a Pull Request addressing this improvement if this direction sounds good to the maintainers!*

issues.title: Test: Dev Container session lifecycle
issues.body:
Refs: #333955, #317380

- [x] macOS @federicobrancasi (local Docker)
- [x] linux @rzhao271 (local Docker)
- [x] windows @dileepyavan (local Docker)

Complexity: 3

Authors: @chrmarti

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338262%0A%0A&assignees=chrmarti)

---

Test automatic Dev Container shutdown, resume, and session cleanup in the Agents Window. **Mark as Done is the archive action.** Use local Docker on each assigned platform; remote hosts are out of scope.

## Set up

1. Use latest Insiders, sign in to Copilot, and verify `docker ps` works.
2. Clone [vscode-remote-try-node](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-remote-try-node) into a **fresh local folder**. Use disposable sessions and leave **New Worktree** disabled.
3. Enable `chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled` and set `chat.agentHost.devContainer.idleTimeout` to **15 seconds** (default: 300).
4. In the Agents Window, select the clone, choose **Use Dev Container** from its folder submenu, and send: **Run `hostname` and `pwd`, then stop.** Record the container ID using the hostname and `docker ps -a`.

Verify actual Docker state throughout: **stopped** containers remain in `docker ps -a`; **removed** containers do not. Never remove unrelated containers or the shared `vscode` volume.

## Test

### 1. Idle shutdown and resume

1. After the turn finishes with no unsent input, verify the container **stops**, rather than being removed, after the timeout. Allow extra time for Docker to finish stopping.
2. Reopen/reconnect the session and send **Run `pwd` again.** Verify the container restarts and the conversation continues without lost history or duplicate sessions.
3. Ask the agent to **Run `sleep 45`, wait for it to finish, then run `hostname`.** Verify it stays running during the turn and any approval prompt. After completion, shutdown should wait for a fresh inactivity period.

### 2. Shared container and Mark as Done

Set the idle timeout to **0** to disable automatic shutdown during these cleanup checks.

1. Create two sent sessions, **A** and **B**, in the same container. Ask both to run `hostname` to confirm they share it.
2. Mark A as done, then delete A from **Done**. The container must remain, and a follow-up in B must still work.
3. With no other session or real draft using the container, mark B as done. Verify the container is **removed**, even when the UI opens a blank composer.
4. Restore B from Done and send a follow-up. Verify a replacement container starts and the previous conversation remains usable.

### 3. Delete the last session

Delete the restored session (or a fresh disposable sent session if restoration failed). Verify both the session and its container are **removed**, not merely stopped, despite timeout 0 and any replacement blank composer.

## Finish and report

Reset the timeout to its default. For failures, include the OS, build, action times, Docker state, and whether other sessions or draft input were present. Attach the **Agent Host** and **Dev Container** output channels after checking them for private content.

---

Verify that ordinary peer chats can be archived and restored independently without affecting their owning session or sibling chats.

## Set up

3. Verify the main chat and sibling peer chat remain active and usable.
4. Verify the archived peer chat disappears from the active session hierarchy.

## Show and restore done chats

1. Open the Sessions filter menu and enable the **Done** filter.
2. Verify the done peer chat appears under the correct main chat with its title and done state.
3. Disable the **Done** filter and verify the peer chat is hidden again.
4. Open the main chat row's context menu and select **Show Done Chats**.
5. Verify the done peer chat becomes visible under that main chat.
6. Restore the peer chat using its primary restore action.
7. Verify it returns to the active hierarchy beneath the correct main chat.
8. Open it and verify its title and transcript are preserved.
9. Send another message and verify the restored chat can continue normally.
10. Reload and verify the restored state persists.

issues.title: Test: Dev Container server cache reuse
issues.body:
Refs: #336914

- [x] anyOS @bryanchen-d (local Docker)

Complexity: 3

Authors: @chrmarti


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338248%0A%0A&assignees=chrmarti)

---

Dev Container sessions in the Agents Window now share downloaded VS Code Servers through the Docker `vscode` volume. **Test with local Docker.**

## Set up

1. Use current Insiders and verify local Docker is running.
2. Enable `chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled`.
3. Clone [vscode-remote-try-node](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-remote-try-node) into **two different local folders**. Keep the same container configuration and user. Do not open either clone in a Dev Container beforehand. Leave **New Worktree** disabled.

Optional: You can also run the same test with Docker on an SSH, Dev Tunnel, or WSL host, but remote testing is not required. In that case, put both clones on the same remote host, update its Agent Host, and enable `chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled`. See #336716 for setup, including the Docker Sandbox option. Ordinary SSH/Tunnel host installations are not in scope.

## Test

1. In the Agents Window, select the first clone and choose **Use Dev Container** from the folder's submenu. Send this prompt:

   > Show the hostname. Run `readlink "$HOME/.vscode-server-insiders/cli/servers"` and `stat -c '%i %n' "$HOME"/.vscode-server-insiders/cli/servers/*/server/node`.

   Verify the session starts successfully and the link points under `/vscode/vscode-server-insiders/cli/servers/<platform>`.

2. Start a Dev Container session for the second clone and send the same prompt. Verify:
   - It runs in a different container (different hostname).
   - The cache target is the same, and the server's `node` file has the **same inode for the same commit**. This verifies reuse, rather than a separate copy in each container.
   - The second startup does not download that server version again. Docker image pulls or workspace setup are separate from the server download.

3. Send a follow-up prompt in each session and verify both still work.

For failures, attach the relevant **Agent Host** and **Dev Container** output channels and the prompt results. Review logs for private content before sharing. Do not delete your existing `vscode` volume for this test.
