issues.title: Test: Agent Host managed OTel export and restart

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: otel
labels.description: OTel (OpenTelemetry)

issues.body:
Refs: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9661, #337783, github/copilot-agent-runtime#22864

- [x] anyOS @jruales

Complexity: 5

Authors: @jruales

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338234%0A%0A&assignees=jruales)

---

Verify that enterprise-managed telemetry works in **Copilot Agent Host sessions without local OTel opt-in**. Local harness is covered separately by #337818; receiving Local harness telemetry does not pass this test.

## Setup

1. Use **1.140 Insiders containing both #337783 and an SDK roll that includes github/copilot-agent-runtime#22864**. Record the build/commit and bundled SDK/runtime versions. If the runtime fix is not bundled yet, mark the test blocked—not passed on the routing fix alone.
2. Use a disposable workspace and test profile signed into Copilot, with unrelated VS Code windows closed and no conflicting device policy. Leave `chat.agentHost.otel.enabled` and `chat.agentHost.otel.dbSpanExporter.enabled` off. Remove personal OTel overrides and launch without inherited `COPILOT_OTEL_*` or `OTEL_*` variables. Do not enable Local harness OTel as a workaround.
3. Start a local OTLP/HTTP JSON collector; the **Collector** section of #337818 provides a Docker setup. Capture incoming HTTP request paths using a local request inspector/proxy, or a collector that exposes them. Keep all output private.
4. Run `npm run mock-policy-server` from a current VS Code checkout and follow its [proxy setup](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/101c86fe138844c24b14ccb1a6636986f68e9bd2/scripts/mock-policy-server/README.md). Leave other endpoints on passthrough. Serve Managed Settings as HTTP 200:

  {
     "telemetry": {
       "enabled": true,
       "endpoint": "http://localhost:4318",
       "protocol": "http/json",
       "captureContent": false,
       "capture": { "identity": false }
     }
   }

   If using a forwarding request inspector, point `endpoint` at its listening port instead. **Keep the endpoint a bare base URL, without `/v1/traces`**, to exercise the routing regression.

5. Run **Developer: Sync Account Policy**, then **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host**. Confirm the mock served the intended policy. The native SDK has a separate policy cache: if it does not fetch the updated policy, follow the README's **Clear SDK policy cache** guidance. A successful editor policy sync alone is not proof the runtime received it.

## Test

- [ ] **Managed export:** Start a fresh same-machine **Copilot Agent Host** conversation, not Local harness, and send a harmless prompt. The response succeeds and the collector receives native Copilot session/model spans. Allow for export batching; check actual received spans, not just policy diagnostics or an “exporter configured” log.
- [ ] **Routing:** Verify trace requests use `POST /v1/traces`, not `/`, and receive a successful response.
- [ ] **Host restart and resume:** Run **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host** again without changing settings. Continue the existing conversation, then start a new one. Both respond and produce new spans at the same destination, without local opt-in.
- [ ] **Full application restart:** Fully quit and reopen the test instance, resume a conversation, and send another prompt. Managed export and routing still work. Note any recurring OTel restart/reload prompt and which surface shows it; the runtime fix does not itself claim to fix that warning.
- [ ] **Policy removal:** Change Managed Settings to HTTP 200 `{}`, sync, refresh the SDK cache if necessary, and restart the host. With local OTel still off, a new conversation works but produces no new native Copilot exports to the test collector. Ignore already-buffered records from the previous host.

## Known limitation

Managed `telemetry.headers` are currently supported by the Local Copilot Chat extension's OTel exporter, but are not delivered to Agent Host native/provider exporters. Header propagation is therefore **not a requirement for this TPI**. Do not add a local setting, environment variable, or proxy-injected header as a workaround; this test should validate only the managed endpoint, protocol, export behavior, and `/v1/traces` routing that Agent Host currently supports.

## Cleanup and results

Restore the original proxy/mock configuration, sync, and restart. Stop the collector and remove private test output. Report the build/SDK/runtime versions, OS, and failed or blocked checks. Do not attach tokens, raw traces, or private account data.

## Feature request

Support product-protocol links that open the Agents Window **New Session** composer with a workspace selected and an unsent prompt populated.

Proposed URL shape:

```text
vscode-insiders://agents/new?workspace=<encoded-workspace-uri>&prompt=<encoded-prompt>
```

For example:

```sh
open "vscode-insiders://agents/new?workspace=file%3A%2F%2F%2FUsers%2Fsandy081%2Fwork%2Fvscode&prompt=Explain%20how%20this%20project%20runs%20its%20tests.%20Do%20not%20run%20anything%20yet."
```

2. Open the **New Session** composer.

4. Populate this prompt without submitting it:

   > Explain how this project runs its tests. Do not run anything yet.

The prompt must remain an editable draft so the user can review or change it before sending.

An initial implementation was attempted in #337360.

issues.title: Test: Multi-chat sessions across folders and repositories
issues.body:
Refs: #337035, #337166, #337263, #337499, #337544, #337594, #337608, #337694, #337797, #337913, #337920, #337977

- [ ] anyOS (Copilot): @vritant24 
- [x] anyOS (Claude): @benibenj
- [x] anyOS (Codex): @Giuspepe

Complexity: 5

Authors: @sandy081


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338222%0A%0A&assignees=sandy081)

---

Verify that chats in one Agent Host session can implement one feature across different repositories while all chat-scoped and session-wide surfaces preserve the correct ownership.

Each tester should use the harness named beside their assignment. Feel free to use repositories that fit your normal development setup. The example below uses the `microsoft/agent-host-protocol` and `microsoft/vscode` repositories to add a concrete feature: an optional `description` on `ChatSummary`/`ChatState`, displayed in VS Code as descriptive text in the nested-chat hover.

## Enable multi-root support

Open **Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)** and enable the setting for your assigned harness:

- Copilot: `"chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled": true`
- Claude: `"chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.multiRootEnabled": true`
- Codex: `"chat.agentHost.codexAgent.multiRootEnabled": true`

Create a new session after changing the setting. Newly created sessions pick up the setting without restarting the Agent Host.

## Create the multi-repository session through the agent

> **Important:** There is currently no UI for adding a second repository to an existing session. Repository 2 must be added when the agent creates a peer chat in the current session with `create_session`. Start from repository 1 and ask the main chat to create the repository 2 chat.

1. Clone or prepare repository 1. For the example below, use `microsoft/agent-host-protocol`.
2. Clone or prepare repository 2 and note its absolute local path. For the example below, use `microsoft/vscode`.
3. Open repository 1 in the Agents Window and start a new session with your assigned harness.
4. In the main chat, first ask the agent to implement the repository 1 portion. For example:

   > Add an optional `description?: string` field to both `ChatSummary` and the denormalized summary fields in `ChatState`. Update the protocol documentation, generated schemas/clients, and focused protocol tests so the two representations stay consistent. Keep the change small and disposable. Do not make any VS Code changes yet.

5. Review the repository 1 implementation and wait for it to finish.
6. In that same main chat, ask the agent to create a separate peer chat in the **current session** for repository 2 and implement the corresponding consumer work. For example:

   > Now create another chat in this same session using the VS Code repository at `/absolute/path/to/vscode`. In that new chat, adopt the new AHP `ChatSummary.description` field, map it into the Sessions chat model, and show it as descriptive text in the nested-chat hover. Add a focused test proving the description is displayed and survives catalog restore. Keep the VS Code change small and disposable.

7. Verify the main chat continues working in repository 1 and the agent-created peer chat works in repository 2.

Feel free to use any two repositories and an equally concrete cross-repository feature that fits your development setup. If you use a different feature, state the exact protocol/API change and the exact consumer behavior before starting. Keep the changes safe to discard after testing.

## Initial session and chat listing

1. Verify the second chat appears nested under the main chat row in the session hierarchy.
2. Verify every chat row shows the folder/project it belongs to.
3. Hover the main chat row and verify the top of the hover shows the main chat's own folder.
4. In the same main-chat hover, verify the **Session summary** at the bottom includes both repositories/folders.
5. Hover the peer-chat row and verify its primary information shows that peer chat's folder rather than the main chat's folder.

## Implement and verify folder ownership

For each chat:

1. Continue the feature implementation in that chat repository.
2. Verify Files shows the correct folder.
3. Open a terminal and verify its cwd belongs to that chat folder.
4. Run or configure a task and verify it runs in that folder.
5. Open Chat Customizations and verify workspace-scoped customizations resolve from that folder.
6. Open files and verify they resolve against the intended repository.

## Changes and pull requests

1. Make and review the feature changes in both repositories.
2. In each chat, verify **Branch Changes** shows only the changes from that chat repository and branch.
3. In each chat, verify **Uncommitted Changes** shows only the current working-tree changes from that chat repository.
4. In each chat, verify **Last Turn Changes** shows only the changes from the most recent turn in that chat and repository.
5. Commit in one chat and verify the other repository state is unaffected.
6. Create a branch and pull request from each repository chat.
7. Verify each PR appears only on its owning chat/folder with the correct repository and branch.
8. Create or discover one PR through `gh pr create` and verify it is still attached to the correct peer chat.

## Session and chat listing after pull-request creation

1. Hover the main chat row and verify the top of the hover shows the main chat's own pull request.
2. In the same main-chat hover, verify the **Session summary** at the bottom includes the repositories/folders and pull requests from both the main chat and the peer chat.
3. Verify each pull request is listed only once in the main-chat hover.
4. Hover the peer-chat row and verify its primary information shows that peer chat's pull request.
5. Verify the peer-chat row and primary hover information do not incorrectly use the main chat's pull request.

## Multiple chats in the same folder

> **Important:** There is no UI for choosing a folder when creating this additional peer chat. Ask the main chat to create it in the current session for the specific repository path.

1. In the main chat, ask the agent to create another peer chat in the **current session** that uses the same repository as one of the existing chats. For example:

   > Create another chat in this same session using the repository at `/absolute/path/to/vscode`. Ask that chat to inspect the current branch changes and pull request, but do not modify anything yet.
2. Verify chats that share the same folder/repository show the same **Branch Changes** information.
3. Verify those chats show the same pull-request information for that repository and branch.
4. Enable or update Agent Merge for that folder and verify all chats using the folder show the same Agent Merge state and pull request.
5. Verify **Uncommitted Changes** and **Branch Changes** are shared by chats using that folder, while **Last Turn Changes** remains specific to the individual chat and its latest turn, even when the chats share a folder.

## Agent Merge

1. Enable Agent Merge independently on chats in repositories 1 and 2.
2. Configure different options where practical.
3. Verify each folder tracks its own PR, CI, reviews, notices, and repair turns.
4. Verify disabling one folder does not disable the other.

## Persistence and capability regression

1. Switch sessions and return, then reload the Agents Window.
2. Verify folders, Files views, branches, changes, PRs, and Agent Merge state restore correctly.
3. Disable your assigned harness multi-root setting.
4. Start a fresh session and verify unsupported current-session folder/worktree creation is no longer offered.
5. Verify ordinary shared-workspace chats still work.

issues.title: Test: Single-folder multi-chat regression coverage
issues.body:
Refs: #337035, #337263, #337499, #337594, #337608, #337920

- [x] anyOS @Giuspepe
- [x] anyOS @benvillalobos

Complexity: 4

Authors: @sandy081


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338220%0A%0A&assignees=sandy081)

---

Verify that the multi-folder implementation does not regress the existing multi-chat workflow where every chat shares one folder and checkout.

Use one suitable bug and split the work by responsibility: the main chat implements the fix, one peer chat adds tests, and another peer chat reviews the combined change. Feel free to use a bug from your own development area.

## Set up

1. Open the `microsoft/vscode` repository in the Agents Window and start a normal Agent Host session.
2. Use the existing checkout directly. Peer chats created through **New Chat in This Session** should inherit this shared folder and checkout.

## Implement one bug across three chats in the shared folder

1. In the main chat, ask the agent to find one suitable, recently updated open bug in your development area and implement a focused fix. For example:

   > Find one suitable recently updated open `editor-core` bug in `microsoft/vscode`. Explain the root cause, implement a focused fix in this main chat, and do not add tests yet.

2. Review the selected issue and verify it is an appropriate open bug for a small disposable fix.
3. Wait for the main chat to finish the implementation.
4. Use **New Chat in This Session** to create a peer chat for tests. In that chat, ask:

   > Add focused regression tests for the bug fix in the shared checkout. Run the smallest relevant test suite.

5. After the tests are complete, use **New Chat in This Session** again to create a second peer chat for review. In that chat, ask:

   > Review the implementation and tests in the shared checkout. Report meaningful correctness or coverage issues, but do not modify files.

6. Verify the two peer chats appear nested under the main chat.
7. Verify the main chat owns the implementation, the first peer chat owns the test work, and the second peer chat contains the review.
8. Verify all three chats use the same repository folder, checkout, and branch.
9. Verify the session is not presented as multi-project and chat rows do not show misleading different-folder labels.

## Shared folder behavior

1. Switch among the main chat and peer chats.
2. Verify Files remains on the shared repository.
3. Open terminals from different chats and verify each uses the same checkout cwd.
4. Run or configure tasks and verify they use the shared folder.
5. Open Chat Customizations and verify every chat resolves workspace customizations from the shared folder.

## Changes

1. Verify **Branch Changes** shows the same shared branch changes in the main chat and both peer chats.
2. Verify **Uncommitted Changes** shows the same current working-tree changes in all three chats.
3. Verify **Session Changes** shows the changes made during the session from the shared checkout in all three chats.
4. Verify the implementation and test changes appear in Branch Changes, Uncommitted Changes, and Session Changes as appropriate.
5. In the main chat, verify **Last Turn Changes** reflects the implementation work from its latest coding turn.
6. In the test peer chat, verify **Last Turn Changes** reflects the focused test changes from its latest coding turn.
7. In the review peer chat, verify **Last Turn Changes** is empty when the review did not modify files.
8. If the review identifies an issue, address it from the appropriate implementation or test chat and verify the shared Branch Changes, Uncommitted Changes, and Session Changes update for all chats.
9. Commit from one chat and verify the updated shared branch and working-tree state is visible from the other chats.

## Pull request and Agent Merge

1. Create one pull request for the shared branch.
2. Verify the main chat and all peer chats show the same pull-request information.
3. Hover the main and peer-chat rows and verify the pull request is not duplicated or attributed to a different folder.
4. Enable Agent Merge for the shared folder.
5. Verify the main chat and all peer chats show the same Agent Merge state and pull request.
6. Verify Agent Merge repair work and notices go to the chat that enabled it, while the folder-level state remains shared.

## Persistence and compatibility

1. Reload, switch sessions, and return.
2. Verify hierarchy, active chat, titles, shared Branch Changes, Uncommitted Changes, and Session Changes, plus chat-specific Last Turn Changes, pull request, and Agent Merge state restore.
3. Disable the provider multi-root setting and create more peer chats without workspace/worktree arguments.
4. Verify those chats still share the session folder and the existing single-folder workflow remains available.
5. Verify Quick Chats and workspaceless independent sessions are not accidentally treated as multi-folder sessions.

issues.title: Test: Multi-chat sessions in separate worktrees
issues.body:
Refs: #337166, #337263, #337499, #337544, #337594, #337608, #337913, #337965, #337977

- [x] anyOS @deepak1556 (Copilot)
- [x] anyOS @dileepyavan (Claude)
- [x] anyOS @aeschli (Codex)

Complexity: 5

Authors: @sandy081


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338219%0A%0A&assignees=sandy081)

---

Verify that chats in one session can use independent worktrees of the same repository without leaking folder, branch, changes, pull-request, or Agent Merge state.

Each tester should use the harness named beside their assignment.

## Enable multi-root support

Open **Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)** and enable the setting for your assigned harness:

- Copilot: `"chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled": true`
- Claude: `"chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.multiRootEnabled": true`
- Codex: `"chat.agentHost.codexAgent.multiRootEnabled": true`

Create a new session after changing the setting. Newly created sessions pick up the setting without restarting the Agent Host.

## Set up

1. Open the `microsoft/vscode` repository in the Agents Window and start a session with your assigned harness.
2. Use disposable worktrees and branches. Do not push the investigation-only changes unless you intentionally continue to the pull-request checks below.

## Create three investigation chats in fresh worktrees

> **Important:** There is no UI for creating a peer chat in a selected worktree. The main chat must create each peer chat in the current session and request a fresh worktree.

1. Choose a scenario from your own development setup that benefits from three independent investigations or implementation approaches in separate worktrees. Keep the changes small, disposable, and easy to distinguish.
2. Ask the main chat to create three peer chats in the current session, each using a fresh worktree for one investigation or approach.
3. For example, in `microsoft/vscode`, ask:

   > Search the `microsoft/vscode` repository for the three most recently updated open issues with the `editor-core` label. Choose three suitable bugs for a quick code investigation. For each issue, create a separate chat in this current session using a fresh worktree of this repository. In each chat, investigate where the fix likely belongs, but do not implement the fix. Add one temporary code comment in the most relevant source file describing why that location is likely involved.

4. If you use the example, review the three selected issues and verify they are open bugs carrying the `editor-core` label. If you use your own scenario, verify each peer chat has a distinct, clearly stated task.
5. Verify the agent creates three peer chats in the current session and one fresh worktree for each investigation.
6. Verify each peer chat is associated with its own worktree and branch.
7. Verify each peer chat investigates or implements a different task and adds only a small, clearly distinguishable change in its worktree. For the example scenario, this is one temporary comment at the likely fix location.
8. Verify all three peer chats appear nested under the main chat in the session hierarchy.
9. Verify each chat row shows the worktree/folder it belongs to.
10. Verify worktree-creation progress and announcements appear on the owning peer chat, not the main chat.

## Initial session and chat listing

1. Hover the main chat row and verify the top of the hover shows the main chat worktree/folder.
2. In the same main-chat hover, verify the **Session summary** at the bottom includes the repository/worktree folders used by the main chat and all peer chats.
3. Hover each peer-chat row and verify its primary information shows that peer chat worktree/folder rather than the main chat worktree.
4. Verify peer chats in different worktrees of the same repository remain distinguishable by their folder/worktree labels.
## Verify worktree isolation

For each worktree chat:

1. Verify Files shows that worktree.
2. Open a terminal and verify its cwd.
3. Check the branch name.
4. Make visibly different changes.
5. Verify Changes shows only that worktree changes.
6. Verify terminals and tasks are not reused across worktrees.
7. Commit in one worktree and verify the other remains unchanged.

## Changes and pull requests

1. Produce different edits in each worktree.
2. In each chat, verify **Branch Changes** shows only the changes from that chat's worktree and branch.
3. In each chat, verify **Uncommitted Changes** shows only the current working-tree changes from that chat's worktree.
4. In each chat, verify **Last Turn Changes** shows only the changes from that chat's most recent turn and worktree.
5. Commit in one worktree and verify the other worktrees remain unchanged.
6. If you continue beyond investigation-only comments, push each worktree branch and create a distinct pull request from each peer chat.
7. Verify each chat displays its own PR and the main chat does not claim peer-chat PRs.
8. Verify branch and PR status update independently for each worktree.

## Session and chat listing after pull-request creation

1. Hover the main chat row and verify the top of the hover shows only the main chat's own pull request, if it has one.
2. In the same main-chat hover, verify the **Session summary** at the bottom includes the worktree folders and pull requests from all chats.
3. Verify each pull request is listed only once in the main-chat hover.
4. Hover each peer-chat row and verify its primary information shows that peer chat's pull request.
5. Verify peer chats in different worktrees do not show a sibling worktree's Branch Changes, Uncommitted Changes, pull request, or Agent Merge state.

## Agent Merge

1. Enable Agent Merge for both worktree chats.
2. Trigger a review or CI repair in one worktree.
3. Verify only the owning chat executes and reports the repair.
4. Verify the sibling worktree remains unaffected.

## Lifecycle and cleanup

1. Archive one peer chat and verify siblings stay active.
2. Restore it and verify its worktree association.
3. Reload and verify all worktree ownership, branches, changes, PRs, and Agent Merge state restore.
4. Remove one chat and verify remaining worktrees continue working.
5. Permanently delete the session and verify owned detached worktrees are cleaned up or retained according to normal lifecycle rules.
6. If cleanup fails, verify ownership remains retryable rather than silently disappearing.

issues.title: Source Control Sync spins after amending an already-pushed commit
issues.body: Type: Bug Summary After using VS Code Source Control's Commit Amend on a commit that had already been pushed, the amended local commit was created correctly, but Sync Changes remained in progress without an actionable explanation. Environment - OS: Windows - VS Code: current stable build - GitHub Pull Requests and Issues extension: installed - Repository: local Git repository with origin/main - Date observed: 2026-09-27 Steps to Reproduce 1. Commit changes locally and push the commit to origin. 2. Stage additional files. 3. Use Source Control > Commit Amend to add the staged files to the already-pushed commit. 4. Select Sync Changes. 5. Observe the Source Control progress indicator. Actual Result - The local branch became ahead 1, behind 1 because the amended commit rewrote the previously-pushed commit. - The local and remote commits shared the same parent. - No Git process, index lock, merge, or rebase was active. - Sync remained cycling without explaining the non-fast-forward condition or the required resolution. - A blue Source Control progress line remained until reloading the VS Code window. - The operation was resolved outside the UI with: git push --force-with-lease origin main. Expected Result VS Code should stop waiting and clearly report that the local branch rewrote a previously-pushed commit. It should provide an actionable, appropriately guarded force-with-lease option, or a clear cancel action, instead of leaving the user with an indefinite progress state. Notes The Commit Amend operation itself appeared to work correctly. This report concerns the Sync feedback and persistent progress state after history rewriting.

issues.title: Add native Codex 5-hour and weekly usage limits to the VS Code status bar

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body: ### Feature request Please add a native Codex usage indicator to the VS Code status bar when Codex is authenticated through a ChatGPT plan. A compact status item could display: `Codex 5h: 65% | W: 94%` Hovering over it could show: - remaining 5-hour allowance and reset time - remaining weekly allowance and reset time - authenticated ChatGPT plan Clicking the status item could refresh the values or open more detailed Codex usage information. ### Motivation During longer autonomous Codex sessions, developers currently have no continuously visible indication of how much of their available Codex allowance remains. Having this information directly in the IDE is particularly useful when deciding whether to continue a long agentic task, use a lighter model or reasoning level, or reserve capacity for more demanding work. A small status-bar indicator provides this information without interrupting the development workflow. ### Working proof of concept We built a small VS Code Insiders extension to test the idea. It reads the authenticated Codex rate-limit information exposed locally by Codex and displays the actual remaining allowance directly in the VS Code status bar. For example: `Codex 5h: 65% | W: 94%` The tooltip additionally displays the exact reset timestamps and authenticated ChatGPT plan. The proof of concept requires: - no OpenAI API key - no usage estimation - no external/cloud service - no GitHub Copilot credit data The values are obtained from the authenticated local Codex session rather than estimated from token consumption. This demonstrates that the feature can fit naturally into the existing VS Code status bar with very little UI overhead. ### Environment tested - VS Code Insiders - Windows 11 - OpenAI Codex extension / Codex Agent Host - ChatGPT Plus authentication - Codex CLI 0.157.1 ### Screenshot Attached is a screenshot of the working proof of concept showing: - the Codex session inside VS Code Insiders - `Codex 5h: 65% | W: 94%` in the status bar - exact 5-hour and weekly reset times in the tooltip - the authenticated ChatGPT plan If useful, I can also provide the proof-of-concept source code and implementation details.

issues.title: Add a workspace context-menu option to keep multi-root folders alphabetically sorted

labels.name: *duplicate
labels.description: Issue identified as a duplicate of another issue(s)

issues.body:
## Feature request

Add a configurable option in the workspace context menu to keep the top-level folders of a multi-root workspace sorted alphabetically in Explorer.

## Current behavior

Workspace root folders appear in the order in which they were added or arranged. When I add another folder, I have to move it into place or edit the `folders` array in the `.code-workspace` file. The Explorer sort setting applies to items *inside* each root folder, but does not sort the roots themselves.

## Proposed behavior

Provide a workspace context-menu option such as **Sort Workspace Folders Alphabetically**. When enabled, Explorer should display the root folders in alphabetical order by their displayed names, including any custom `name` values in the workspace file. The order should stay alphabetical when folders are added, removed, or renamed and when the workspace is reopened.

This should be optional so users who deliberately arrange their roots can retain that order.

## Example

If a workspace contains `beta`, `alpha`, `gamma`, and `epsilon`, Explorer would show `alpha`, `beta`, `epsilon`, `gamma` regardless of the order in which those folders were added.

## Related issues and prior work

* #91843 requests **manual** ordering of Explorer items. This request concerns **automatic alphabetical** ordering of multi-root workspace folders.
* #27286 tracks several Explorer and Open Editors sorting requests, but its listed requests do not describe persistent alphabetical sorting of workspace roots.
* The [[WorkspaceSort extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=iciclesoft.workspacesort)](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=iciclesoft.workspacesort) demonstrates demand for this behavior and supports automatic sorting when folders are added. This request is for a built-in option accessible through the workspace context menu.

I searched for an existing request specifically covering this option and did not find one.

- VS Code Version: 1.139.1 (commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`, Electron 43.6.0). Also seen on 1.133.0 (Electron 42.8.0) and 1.138.0 (Electron 42.10.0).
- OS Version: macOS 27.0 (26A428), Mac16,5 (Apple Silicon), 128 GB RAM

This is the problem from #326913, which was closed after reports that 1.134 fixed it. It still happens. In that thread another user reported it on 1.137.0, and I added the data below [as a comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326913#issuecomment-5856195476). I am filing a new issue because #326913 is closed.

The macOS kernel kills a **window renderer** (`Code Helper (Renderer)`, the workbench renderer, not a webview) when its Mach port table is full at about 267,900 ports. VS Code then shows "The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'killed', code: '9')".

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On macOS, open a window and use the Claude Code extension for a long agent session that runs multi-agent workflows. Some of the agents work in git worktrees inside the workspace.
2. Keep working. After 25 minutes to a few hours, the window is killed with "The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'killed', code: '9')".

I don't have a short reproduction. The operations I tested in isolation are listed below; none of them triggers it.

## The kills

Each kill left a Crashpad dump in `~/Library/Application Support/Code/Crashpad/completed/`. I decoded the minidump exception stream. Its parameters are `[exception type, code0, code1]`.

| Time (local) | VS Code / Electron | Exception | Low bits of `code0` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-05 16:42 | 1.133.0 / 42.8.0 | EXC_CRASH, SIGKILL, original EXC_RESOURCE | 267,913 |
| 2026-09-08 19:47 | 1.133.0 / 42.8.0 | same | 267,903 |
| 2026-09-09 01:51 | 1.133.0 / 42.8.0 | same | 267,903 |
| 2026-09-26 17:19 | 1.138.0 / 42.10.0 | same | 267,932 |
| 2026-09-26 20:01 | 1.139.1 / 43.6.0 | same | 267,911 |
| 2026-09-27 08:33 | 1.139.1 / 43.6.0 | same | 267,966 |
| 2026-09-27 10:03 | 1.139.1 / 43.6.0 | EXC_RESOURCE, type 6 (PORTS), flavor 1 (PORT_SPACE_FULL), `0xc4000000000416a7` | 267,943 |
| 2026-09-27 14:11 | 1.139.1 / 43.6.0 | EXC_RESOURCE, type 6 (PORTS), flavor 1 (PORT_SPACE_FULL), `0xc4000000000416bf` | 267,967 |

- **How to read the EXC_CRASH codes:** in those dumps `code0` is `0x9b416xx`. That is signal 9 in bits 24–31 and the original exception `0xb` (EXC_RESOURCE) in bits 20–23. The low 20 bits are in the same range as in the two EXC_RESOURCE dumps.
- **Which process:** `main.log` has `CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: killed, code: 9)` for each kill, and the dumps are `--type=renderer`.

## Measurements

- **Windows affected:** only windows where the Claude Code extension ran long agent sessions were killed. Nine other windows open for the same 3.7 hours, with other extensions active, stayed at 325–351 ports.
- **A burst, not a slow climb:** I sampled every VS Code process with `top -stats ports` every 10 s for about 30 minutes, across 13 windows. Renderers stayed between 150 and 470 ports, and no process grew by more than 28.
- **Fastest kill:** a renderer that started at 09:37:54 was killed at 10:03:03.
- **Correlation with idle-process terminations:** I could not check the `memorystatus: killing_idle_process` correlation reported in #326913. `log show` returned no kernel lines on this machine.
- **Spotlight:** Spotlight worker churn (`mds` killing `mdworker`) was high before two of the kills. It was equally high at other times with no kill (515 worker kills in one 10-minute window) and absent before the 08:33 kill. I don't think it is related.

## Tested and ruled out

None of these raised the window renderer's port count significantly.

- **In my normal instance:**
  - creating 60,000 files in a workspace folder, then deleting them;
  - adding a git worktree inside the workspace, editing it for 40 s, then removing it.
- **In an isolated instance**, started with `--user-data-dir`, `--disable-extensions` and a test extension via `--extensionTestsPath`, with each operation sustained for 20–30 s:
  - `webview.postMessage` of a 3.6 MB object at 20/s (407 messages) and of a 4 MB string at 20/s;
  - 1 KB messages at 50/s;
  - setting `WebviewPanel.title` at 20/s;
  - `window.showInformationMessage` at 5/s;
  - `workspace.openTextDocument` plus `languages.getDiagnostics` at 20/s;
  - `vscode.diff` at 2/s;
  - `workspace.createFileSystemWatcher` and `dispose` at 20/s;
  - status bar text plus `setContext` at 20/s;
  - creating a terminal, writing output and disposing it at 1/s.
- Creating and disposing 40 webview panels added about 280 ports, and disposing the terminals released about 200 again. Neither comes close to the limit.

## Possibly related

- #326913: same signature; closed.
- #329210: according to the maintainer comment in #326913, this fixed a Mach port exhaustion case with attachments in the integrated browser. The integrated browser was not in use in my sessions.
- #336730, open: a window killed with code 9 while an agent edits files. It has no port data. The extension-host logs of my killed windows show no `changeLanguage` errors.

I can run an Insiders build, a specific trace or a sampling setup, or share the minidumps privately, if that helps.

issues.title: Agents: multiline approval row grows to thousands of pixels during sticky scrolling

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
## Bug

An expanded session with a multiline pending approval can grow from **98px to 3,218px** when its row becomes sticky while scrolling through child chats. The title is displaced into a mostly empty row, and the approval preview moves below the viewport.

## Reproduce automatically

[Standalone PowerShell script](https://gist.github.com/hediet/a3c33b5506f287e75dd4e567b6179e2f) — tested end to end with a fresh local Chrome profile.

**Requirements:** Windows, PowerShell 7, global `dbgjs` on PATH, Chrome or Edge, and internet access. No checkout, sign-in, agent host, or actual tool execution is required.

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest 'https://gist.githubusercontent.com/hediet/a3c33b5506f287e75dd4e567b6179e2f/raw/304a130800925d71bb00be9a20ec6cf52778276c/repro-vscode-338189.ps1' -OutFile .\repro-vscode-338189.ps1
pwsh -File .\repro-vscode-338189.ps1
```

The script:
- Launches a **visible Chrome/Edge window through dbgjs**, using an isolated profile.
- Opens `https://vscode.dev/agents?vscode-quality=insider` and injects fake sessions into the real list/model: one three-line pending approval and 30 expanded child chats.
- Scrolls the list and compares original CSS, a temporary fix, and original CSS again. It asserts the results and saves `bug.png` and `results.json` in the printed output directory.
- Leaves the browser open with the bug visible. Close it when finished; reloading removes the in-memory fixture. The sign-in overlay is hidden only for this synthetic demo.

The capture is pinned to Insiders commit `4a6a3612a562c50f54c2bd5211f0ea42915b974e`; the script explicitly stops if the deployed build changes rather than using incorrect debugger offsets.

## Reproduce manually

1. Use the compact Agents sessions list with sticky scroll enabled.
2. Expand a session with enough child chats to scroll through them.
3. Have that session's **main chat** awaiting approval of a command spanning at least three preview lines. Leave it pending.
4. Scroll down through its children so the parent becomes sticky, then back up. Repeat if necessary.

**Expected:** The row remains bounded at the normal title-plus-preview height.

**Actual:** The row height grows dramatically. A flat list without expanded child chats did not reproduce this; sticky parent rendering is the important prerequisite.

## Diagnosis and verified fix

`StickyScrollWidget.probeDynamicHeights` clears the sticky row's height and measures the approval preview before asynchronous code-block rendering completes. Its three placeholder blocks inherit the list row's `line-height` (the **whole row height**). The widget writes the inflated measurement back as height/line-height and propagates it to the main list, creating a feedback loop.

Measured progression: **98 -> 338 -> 1,058 -> 3,218px**. The tokenized preview later shrinks to about 57px, but the inflated row height remains.

Resetting line-height on the shared approval container prevents the feedback:

```css
.session-approval-row {
    line-height: 18px;
}
```

| Configuration | Final row heights across three scroll cycles |
| --- | --- |
| Original CSS | 3,218 / 3,218 / 3,218px |
| Explicit approval line-height | 98 / 98 / 98px |
| Override removed | 3,218 / 3,218 / 3,218px |

No artificial tokenization delay or renderer modification was needed. Regression coverage should exercise an **expanded sticky session with a multiline approval**, not just flat-list recycling.

Relevant code: [`sessionsList.css`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4a6a3612a562c50f54c2bd5211f0ea42915b974e/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/sessionsList.css), [`renderApprovalRowContent`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4a6a3612a562c50f54c2bd5211f0ea42915b974e/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts), and [`StickyScrollWidget`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4a6a3612a562c50f54c2bd5211f0ea42915b974e/src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/abstractTree.ts).

## Environment

- Windows; web Insiders 1.140.0-insider, commit `4a6a3612a562c50f54c2bd5211f0ea42915b974e`
- Fresh Chrome 153.0.8010.53; dbgjs 0.1.0 (`285cd647d9e8c7e0cca2f52cc30278fb7a3a4412`)
- Also reproduced in desktop Insiders commit `a3b0c130bdeeb42c8de4817bd4f5b00b051e8393`

## Screenshot

Synthetic web repro, scrolled to show the title displaced within the oversized selected row:

![Synthetic session row expanded to 3218 pixels during sticky scrolling](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52eeb283-e927-4922-a90c-33b827b5634a)

<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.139.1 (initially observed on 1.123.0)
- OS Version: Linux x64 7.0.0-28-generic

<details>
<summary>System Information Details (captured on 1.123.0)</summary>

- Date: 2026-06-03T11:29:03+02:00
- Electron: 42.2.0
- ElectronBuildId: 14159160
- Chromium: 148.0.7778.97
- Node.js: 24.15.0
- V8: 14.8.178.14-electron.0
</details>

Steps to Reproduce:

*(Note: This issue is intermittent and non-deterministic. The exact trigger is unknown; it occurs randomly during standard notebook editing sessions.)*

1. Open any Jupyter Notebook (`.ipynb`) file.
2. Edit code inside a cell in Edit Mode (blinking text cursor is active).
3. At random points during editing, attempt to press `Ctrl + A` to select all cell contents.
4. Attempt to highlight text or perform multi-cursor/column selection (hold click/drag).

Expected Behavior:

- `Ctrl + A` should highlight/select all content inside the active cell editor.
- Text selection and multi-cursor actions should respond smoothly without locking up.

Actual Behavior:

- Intermittently, even though the cell is explicitly in Edit Mode with a visible cursor, pressing `Ctrl + A` is completely ignored (no text is selected).
- Dragging to select text or creating multi-cursors intermittently freezes/locks up, as if keyboard/mouse selection focus is lost by the inner text editor.

Additional Context:

- **Reproducibility:** Intermittent. It does not happen on every cell or every keystroke, and there is no obvious specific sequence of keys that triggers it.
- **Mode verification:** Confirmed that the cell is in Edit Mode (not Command Mode).
- **Extensions:** The issue still occurs when all extensions are disabled.
- **Temporary workaround:** Clicking out to another cell or running `Developer: Reload Window` temporarily restores normal behavior until it randomly recurs.
- **Persistence:** The issue still occurs after updating to VS Code 1.139.1.
- **Related issue:** This may be related to #236300, which reports random `Ctrl + A` failures in Python Jupyter notebook cells on Windows. That issue describes needing to close and reopen the notebook to recover. This report adds the same class of intermittent selection failure on Linux and includes drag/multi-cursor selection lockups, so it may share an underlying notebook editor focus/selection desync rather than a keybinding-only problem.

issues.title: Test: Plugin custom-agent hook root expansion
issues.body:
PR: #337388

- [x] macOS @sandy081 or Linux
- [x] Windows @rzhao271

Complexity: 3

Authors: @pwang347

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338177%0A%0A&assignees=pwang347)

---

## Context

Custom agents contributed by Plugins can declare hooks that refer to their Plugin root. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` must resolve in hook commands and environment variables, including when the Plugin path contains spaces. The hook must still remain scoped to the contributing custom agent.

## Common setup

1. Enable `chat.useCustomAgentHooks`.
2. Create a local Plugin in an absolute path containing a space, for example `root hook tpi`.
3. Add that absolute folder to `chat.pluginLocations` and reload the window.
4. Under the Plugin, create `scripts/pre-tool.js`:

   ```js
   const fs = require('fs');
   const path = require('path');
   const root = process.env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT || process.env.PLUGIN_ROOT;
   fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'hook-ran.txt'), root || 'missing root');
   process.stdin.resume();
   ```

5. Create `agents/root-hook-tpi.md` with the variant below. Give the agent a short body instructing it to use a read-only tool when asked.

### Claude plugin variant (macOS or Linux)

Create `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:

```json
{ "name": "root-hook-tpi" }
```

Use this agent frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: root-hook-tpi
description: Verifies a Plugin-root hook.
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pre-tool.js"
---
```

### Open Plugin variant (Windows)

Create `.plugin/plugin.json`:

```json
{ "name": "root-hook-tpi" }
```

Use this agent frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: root-hook-tpi
description: Verifies a Plugin-root hook.
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - type: command
      bash: "node ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pre-tool.js"
      powershell: "node ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pre-tool.js"
---
```

## Test steps

1. Run **Chat: Open Customizations** and verify the local Plugin and `root-hook-tpi` agent are discovered and enabled.
2. Select `root-hook-tpi` in Chat and ask it to read a harmless workspace file.
3. Approve the tool if prompted. Verify `hook-ran.txt` is created in the Plugin root even though the path contains a space.
4. Open `hook-ran.txt`. Verify it contains the exact absolute Plugin path, with no literal `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` or `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` token.
5. Delete `hook-ran.txt`, switch to a different built-in/custom agent, and invoke the same tool. Verify the marker is not recreated.
6. Switch back to `root-hook-tpi` or invoke it through `runSubagent`. Verify the marker is recreated only for that agent.
7. Move or copy the Plugin to a second path containing spaces, update `chat.pluginLocations`, reload, and repeat once. Verify the command and environment resolve to the new path rather than retaining the old root.
8. Remove the test Plugin and restore the settings.

**Expected:** Plugin-provided custom-agent hooks expand the format-specific root token, quote paths safely for the active shell, expose the matching root environment variable, follow Plugin relocation, and run only when their contributing agent is active.

issues.body:
PR: #337649

- [x] anyOS @DonJayamanne 
- [x] anyOS @benibenj 

Complexity: 5

Authors: @pwang347

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338176%0A%0A&assignees=pwang347)

---

## Context

Copilot Connectors are an independently gated, authenticated source in the customization Marketplace and MCP management UI. VS Code owns catalog, consent, and status UI; the Copilot runtime owns session-time MCP projection and credentials.

Use a disposable profile with a GitHub account eligible for Copilot Connectors. Enable:

```json
"chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled": true,
"chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled": true
```

Leave `chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled` on initially so source independence can be checked. If the service is unavailable for the account or rollout, record the HTTP/status shown and mark the test blocked rather than changing account security settings.

## Authentication and connector lifecycle

1. Start signed out of GitHub and run **Chat: Open Customizations**.
2. Verify Discover still shows healthy non-connector sources. The Copilot Connectors source should present an explicit sign-in/recovery action rather than hiding other results or starting OAuth automatically.
3. Sign in with ordinary GitHub scopes. Browse the generic connector catalog and verify passive browsing does not unexpectedly request connector-management consent when the backend permits read-only access.
4. Open a connector such as Microsoft Learn Docs and use **Check Connection** or **Connect**. Verify any missing connector permission is requested explicitly for the same account. Cancel once and confirm no connection is created.
5. Repeat and authorize. Verify status updates without reopening Customizations, connector details remain accessible, and connected MCP servers appear under MCP Servers **Installed** while the product appears under **Connectors**.
6. Disable the GitHub Feed and verify Connectors remain available. Re-enable it, then disable only `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled`; verify fresh connector discovery stops without breaking the other Marketplace sources.
7. Re-enable Connectors, disconnect the connector, and verify its status and MCP entries update. Recoverable HTTP 403 or rollout failures should remain actionable and must not trigger passive re-consent loops.

## Fresh Copilot Agent session tool projection

1. Connect a connector that exposes an easily verifiable read-only tool, such as Microsoft Learn Docs.
2. Immediately create a completely fresh **Copilot Agent** session; do not reuse a session that existed before connecting.
3. Ask the agent to use the connector's tool (for Microsoft Learn Docs, request an official documentation lookup) and verify the tool is available in that first fresh session and returns a relevant result.
4. Verify a user/workspace MCP server with the same name keeps its normal precedence and is not overwritten by the managed connector projection.
5. Disconnect the connector, then create another fresh Copilot Agent session. Verify the disconnected connector tool is no longer exposed.
6. Disable `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled` and create one more fresh session. Verify connector tools remain absent while ordinary Copilot chat still starts successfully.

## Accessibility and cleanup

1. Navigate source recovery, connector cards, details, status actions, Installed, and Connectors using only the keyboard.
2. Verify sign-in, consent-required, connecting, connected, disconnecting, error, and disconnected states have understandable labels and do not rely on color alone.
3. Disconnect any test connector and restore the experimental settings.

**Expected:** Connector catalog access and consent are explicit and isolated from other sources; lifecycle status stays synchronized in Customizations; and a newly connected connector is reconciled before the first fresh Copilot Agent session becomes usable, without VS Code forwarding credentials directly to connector endpoints.

issues.title: Test: Customization Marketplace installation identity, repair, and uninstall
issues.body:
PR: #337816

- [x] anyOS @federicobrancasi
- [x] anyOS @dmitrivMS

Complexity: 4

Authors: @pwang347

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338175%0A%0A&assignees=pwang347)

---

## Context

Marketplace installation state now comes from durable installation records reconciled with the exact local target. A local customization with the same name or repository must not masquerade as the marketplace installation. Missing recorded files can be repaired without overwriting edits or extra files, and skill uninstall uses the normal confirmed deletion/Trash flow.

Use a disposable profile and workspace. Enable:

```json
"chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled": true,
"chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled": true
```

Claim one row above and run its section, then run the shared accessibility checks.

## Skill identity, repair, and uninstall

1. In Discover, find an installable multi-file skill from the GitHub Feed and note its declared name, source, and version.
2. Before installing it, create a workspace skill with the same declared name under `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, but give it clearly different content.
3. Refresh Discover. Verify the local skill remains separate and the marketplace entry is still available to install; the same name alone must not mark it installed.
4. Install the marketplace skill to a different destination. Verify only that exact marketplace entry becomes installed and its detail identifies the recorded target.
5. Edit one installed file, add an extra file, and delete a different recorded file through VS Code's Explorer.
6. Return to Discover and verify the marketplace entry becomes **Missing** and offers **Repair**. Keyboard and accessible descriptions should distinguish it from the unrelated same-name skill.
7. Run Repair and confirm it. Verify the missing recorded file returns, while the edited file and extra file are unchanged.
8. Start uninstall and cancel the confirmation. Verify both the installed target and its marketplace association remain.
9. Uninstall again and confirm. Verify the target follows the normal deletion/Trash flow, the record is removed, the unrelated same-name skill remains, and the marketplace entry becomes available to install again.

## Plugin or MCP exact association and uninstall

1. In Discover, choose an installable Plugin from **Configured Plugin Marketplaces** or an MCP server from **MCP Gallery**. Record the source, identifier, and displayed version.
2. If practical, configure or create a local item with the same display name before installing. Verify it does not mark the catalog entry installed.
3. Install the catalog item and verify only the exact source identity becomes installed. A same-name item from another source must remain independent.
4. Reload the window and verify the installed association survives and resolves to the same local Plugin URI or MCP server ID.
5. Remove or invalidate the recorded local target outside Discover, refresh, and verify the entry reports a missing/error state rather than silently binding to a same-name target.
6. Repair when offered, then uninstall. Verify the operation affects only the exact recorded target and clears only its record.

## Shared accessibility and cleanup checks

1. Use keyboard navigation to inspect installed, missing, repairing, and available states.
2. Open Accessibility Help and Accessible View. Verify exact-association and repair state are understandable and all available actions can be invoked without a pointer.
3. Remove the disposable same-name customization and restore the Marketplace settings.

**Expected:** Marketplace state follows durable source identity plus the exact installed target, survives reload, never relies on name matching, repairs only missing recorded content, and uninstalls through the established safe flow.

## Context

Agent Customizations now has a unified **Discover** surface. Marketplace visibility is gated independently from its sources, and Discover composes the GitHub Feed, MCP Gallery, and configured Plugin marketplaces without duplicating the default public catalogs.

Use a disposable profile. No custom registry is required for the core test.

## Baseline and visibility gate

1. Remove any explicit values for these settings, then set only `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled` to `false`:
   - `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled`
   - `chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled`
2. Run **Chat: Open Customizations**.
3. Verify the original **Overview** is shown. The MCP Servers and Plugins pages still contain their legacy **Available** sections, and no Discover content appears even though the GitHub Feed defaults on.
4. Set `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled` to `true`.
5. Verify **Discover** replaces Overview and the home action is named Discover.
6. Start a search, then turn Marketplace off before it completes. Verify Overview returns, stale results do not appear, and the legacy MCP/Plugin catalogs remain usable.
7. Turn Marketplace back on and verify a fresh Discover query starts.

## Source composition and de-duplication

1. Set `chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled` to `false`.
2. In Discover, verify the source picker offers **MCP Gallery** and **Configured Plugin Marketplaces**. Browse each source and verify its default catalog loads.
3. Verify discovery has moved out of the MCP Servers and Plugins management pages while Marketplace is visible; installed-item management remains there.
4. Re-enable `chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled`.
5. Verify **GitHub Feed** appears without reloading the window. Search for a public item that is also present in a default MCP or Plugin catalog and verify it is not duplicated across sources. Custom/workspace Plugin marketplaces, if configured, should remain available.
6. Scope the source picker to each source and then return to all sources. Verify the visible results and source label update each time.

## Search, paging, failure isolation, and accessibility

1. Search across multiple customization types. Exercise the type and installed filters, clear the search, and verify Featured content returns.
2. Scroll through enough results to load another page. Results already loaded should remain stable and equal-priority sources should stay interleaved rather than one source monopolizing the page.
3. Disable one source while a query is running. Verify healthy sources remain visible and retrying/re-enabling restarts that source from its first page.
4. Navigate Discover, its filters, source picker, cards, and list using only the keyboard. Open Accessibility Help and Accessible View and verify source, type, installation state, and available actions are announced.
5. Restore the settings when done.

**Expected:** Marketplace visibility never leaks feed work into the original Overview; enabling it exposes one coherent Discover experience; the three source families compose without duplicate default content; and toggling, filtering, paging, partial failure, and accessible navigation remain predictable.

issues.title: fix: await connector record persistence before asserting in WebKit test (build fix for vscode-engineering#3992)

labels.name: vscode-build
labels.description: VS Code build process issues

issues.body:
## Build failure

The macOS WebKit browser unit test suite failed on a single assertion in `CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService`:

```text
CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService > Copilot connectors > records a connector that was already connected outside this workbench
actual: recorded=[]; expected: recorded=["mail"]; both state.kind="installed"
```

The browser exited cleanly (code 0); the runner returned 1 solely for this assertion.

## Root cause

The test (`records a connector that was already connected outside this workbench`) marks a connector as connected, fires the change event, then waits only `await timeout(0)` before asserting that a record was persisted.

The listener registered in `updateEnablement()` responds by calling `void this.synchronizeConnectedConnectorRecords()`. That method computes the record id via `createConnectorRecord()`, which awaits `createInstallationRecordId(...)` — an async `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', ...)` — before calling `recordStore.upsert()`. A single macrotask (`timeout(0)`) does not guarantee that the digest promise has resolved and the upsert has run, so on slower/async digest completion the recorded-resource list is still empty when the assertion runs. `getInstallState()` can return `installed` directly from the connector's connection status without a stored record, which is why the state assertion passed while `recorded` was empty. This is a test synchronization defect, not a product regression.

## How the fix works

Instead of a fixed timer, the test now waits deterministically for the persistence to complete using the same pattern already established throughout this file (`Event.toPromise(Event.filter(service.onDidChange, ...))`):

```ts
const recorded = Event.toPromise(Event.filter(fixture.service.onDidChange, () => fixture.service.getRecordedResources().some(resource => resource.identifier === 'mail')));
fixture.connectedConnectors.add('mail');
fixture.connectorChanges.fire();
await recorded;
```

`recordStore.upsert()` triggers `recordStore.onDidChange`, which fires the service's `onDidChange`. The test therefore proceeds only once the connector record is actually persisted, regardless of how long the SHA-256 digest takes. Both original assertions (recorded resources and installed state) are preserved unchanged.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back.** Public culprit: not confirmed (strong suspect: the commit that introduced the timer-based assertion and async persistence path, microsoft/vscode#337649, but not verified by reproduction or bisect). Rationale: only one CI assertion is affected and no product data loss is established; a bounded, forward test-synchronization fix is far lower risk than reverting a broad feature with runtime integration. Owners to consult: `@pwang347`.

## Validation

Change is a focused edit to a single test. Repository dependencies were not installed in this environment, so `npm`-based typecheck/test runs could not be executed here. The edit uses `Event`/`Event.toPromise`/`Event.filter`, all already imported and used repeatedly in this file, and preserves the existing assertions. Recommended local validation: run this suite under WebKit, e.g. `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --build --browser webkit` filtered to `CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService`.

## Risk

Low. Test-only change; no production code touched. The deterministic wait matches the file's existing idiom and cannot mask a real failure because it still requires the record to be persisted before asserting.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@pwang347`

issues.body:
Refs: #335808, #335372, #336784
PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337179, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337093

Complexity: 3

Authors: @vritant24

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338162%0A%0A&assignees=vritant24)

---

## Setup

1. Enable `chat.customizations.mcpServerMigration.enabled`.
2. Open a disposable folder and create `.vscode/mcp.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "servers": {
       "migratable": {
         "type": "stdio",
         "command": "npx",
         "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"]
       },
       "not-migratable": {
         "type": "stdio",
         "command": "npx",
         "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"],
         "cwd": "."
       },
       "broken": {
         "type": "stdio",
         "command": "command-that-does-not-exist"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

3. Start a Copilot Agent Host session for the folder. (make sure to send a chat)
4. Run **Chat: Open Customizations** and open **MCP Servers**.

## Compatibility and error details

1. Verify the server list remains compact and identifies servers with compatibility or runtime problems.
2. Open `not-migratable`.
3. Verify its detail view:
   - Shows that the server is only partially supported.
   - Explains the unsupported `cwd` configuration and provides migration guidance.
   - Provides actions to open the source and edit the configuration.
4. Open `broken`.
5. Verify its detail view shows a persistent, actionable startup error with access to the full runtime details.
6. Fix the command or recreate the runtime server and verify the details update without reopening Customizations.

## Migratable and not-migratable servers

1. Open the MCP server migration page.
2. Verify:
   - The page shows explicit migratable and not-migratable counts.
   - `migratable` is available to migrate.
   - `not-migratable` remains visible with the reason it cannot be migrated.
3. Open `not-migratable` from the migration page and use **Edit Configuration**.
4. Verify `.vscode/mcp.json` opens with the `not-migratable` server selected.
5. Return to the migration page and migrate only `migratable`.
6. Verify:
   - `migratable` is moved to the workspace-root `.mcp.json`.
   - `not-migratable` and `broken` remain unchanged in `.vscode/mcp.json`.
   - Returning from server details restores keyboard focus to the migration list.

**Expected:** Customizations identifies partially supported, unsupported, and failing MCP servers without overwhelming the list; details provide actionable diagnostics and source navigation; and the migration page shows both eligible and ineligible servers while moving only selected compatible entries.

issues.title: Terminal throughput is limited by the flow control window and 5 ms output batching

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.139.1, commit 04c0d99f. The relevant files are unchanged on `main` at 157fc59.
- OS Version: macOS 27.0 on an Apple M5

Local terminal output seems to be held back by two things in the pty host:

1. `TerminalDataBufferer` [delays each chunk by 5 ms](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/terminalDataBuffering.ts#L38), which adds up to 5 ms to every echo.
2. The pty pauses once [`HighWatermarkChars`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/terminal.ts#L881), or 100,000 characters, are unacknowledged. Throughput is then roughly that much per round trip, and the 5 ms timer makes up most of each round trip.

During bulk output, both processes are mostly idle. In profiles of vtebench's `dense_cells`, the renderer's main thread was 81% idle and the pty host's was 91% idle.

## Measurements

I used [vtebench](https://github.com/alacritty/vtebench) payloads on a 158×41 grid in fresh profiles and checked that each build received identical bytes. Figures are medians over 3 launches of 8 samples, with 95% bootstrap intervals. Latency is the round trip of a cursor position report, `CSI 6 n`, which is answered only once everything before it has been parsed.

Builds of 1.139.1 with each change, relative to an unmodified build:

| | Idle round trip | `dense_cells` | `medium_cells` | `scrolling` | Messages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unmodified | 7.9 ms | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1102 |
| Leading-edge flush | 1.5 ms | 0.99 [0.98, 1.01] | 1.01 [0.98, 1.02] | 1.03 [1.01, 1.06] | |
| 1,000,000 watermark | 8.0 ms | 0.29 [0.29, 0.30] | 0.34 [0.32, 0.35] | 0.53 [0.51, 0.56] | |
| Both | 1.6 ms | 0.29 [0.29, 0.30] | 0.35 [0.32, 0.36] | 0.53 [0.52, 0.55] | 1050 |

The unmodified build took about 700 ms for 8 MiB of `dense_cells` and 2.1 s for `scrolling`. The watermark row comes from a separate batch with its own unmodified control. Messages is the number of IPC sends from the pty host for 110M characters of output. The leading-edge flush sends the first chunk right away and batches anything else that arrives within 5 ms, so bursts still coalesce. Setting `throttleBy` to 0 instead took 3217 messages and only brought the round trip down to 3.0 ms.

## Ctrl+C

Since flow control is there to keep Ctrl+C responsive, I also timed the gap between killing a flooding process and the next `CSI 6 n` reply. I didn't see a regression with both changes, including for unicode, which is slow to rasterize:

| Drain after kill | Unmodified | Both |
|---|---|---|
| `dense_cells` median | 7.5 ms | 4.7 ms |
| Unicode median | 4.7 ms | 5.9 ms |
| Unicode p90 | 207 ms | 128 ms |
| Unicode max | 536 ms | 449 ms |

Medians are over 20 and 30 drains respectively. The unicode median difference isn't significant, with a ratio of 1.20 [0.68, 1.92].

All of this was local. The [comment on `LowWatermarkChars`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/terminal.ts#L882-L891) mentions that the remote connection is shared, so a larger window may not suit remote. The leading-edge flush doesn't add messages, so it may be fine there, but I haven't tested it.

## Possible changes

A leading-edge flush in `TerminalDataBufferer`, with `flushBuffer` skipping empty batches:

```ts
this._callback(id, data);
const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => this.flushBuffer(id), throttleBy);
buffer = { data: [], timeoutId, dispose: ... };
```

Separately, `HighWatermarkChars` could be raised, perhaps only for local terminals.

issues.title: Pty host parses all terminal output a second time, even with persistent sessions disabled

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.139.1, commit 04c0d99f. The relevant files are unchanged on `main` at 157fc59.
- OS Version: macOS 27.0 on an Apple M5

Each terminal in the pty host [creates an `XtermSerializer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L784-L793), a full `@xterm/headless` instance with the Unicode 11 and shell integration addons, and every output chunk is written into it:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L822-L823

`terminal.integrated.enablePersistentSessions` doesn't change this. `shouldPersist` only affects [detach and revive](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L837), and `persistentSessionScrollback` only [sets the headless scrollback](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/code/electron-main/app.ts#L1263). So all output is parsed twice, and there's no way to opt out.

## Measurements

These use [vtebench](https://github.com/alacritty/vtebench) payloads on a 158×41 grid with a fixed amount of output per run.

- Across all 12 benchmarks, the pty host used 171 CPU seconds, against 277 for the renderer and 87 for the GPU process, averaged over 3 launches.
- In a profile of the pty host during four of those benchmarks, its main thread was busy 44% of the time, and 33 of those points went to `@xterm/headless` parsing through `XtermSerializer.handleData`. Sending data to the renderer took about 6%.
- Neither setting reduced pty host CPU, averaged over 2 launches of a 4-benchmark workload:

| Setting | Pty host CPU |
|---|---|
| Defaults | 16.7 s |
| `terminal.integrated.enablePersistentSessions: false` | 17.1 s |
| `terminal.integrated.persistentSessionScrollback: 0` | 16.8 s |

## Possible directions

- Skip the serializer when persistent sessions are off. It also hosts a `ShellIntegrationAddon`, and I haven't checked what else relies on it. A reload would then need to restore from the renderer or start blank.
- Buffer raw output and parse it only when a serialization is requested.

## Related

On desktop, the main process also [subscribes to `onProcessData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyHostService.ts#L176), though the renderer [receives data over its own MessagePort](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/electron-browser/localTerminalBackend.ts#L151). In the same profile, the main process's only notable work was IPC deserialization at 4.3% of samples, which suggests it decodes every data event and discards it.

issues.title: Copilot BYOK: MiMo via PrimaLabs splits the final answer mid-sentence into collapsed steps

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body: - Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.67.0 (bundled `copilot-chat` extension on the WSL server) - VS Code Version: 1.139.1, commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1` (Windows client and WSL server) - OS Version: Windows host with WSL Remote; remote Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS - Feature: Agent mode - Selected model: MiMo-V2.6-Pro via PrimaLabs Custom Endpoint, model ID `primalabs-ai/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL` - Logs: Raw SSE from an affected response has not been captured. A separate non-streaming curl request to the same endpoint/model succeeds. ### Description The assistant's ordinary answer is split mid-sentence between the collapsed "Completed N steps" section and the normal response area. With the steps collapsed, the visible answer starts halfway through a sentence. Expanding the steps reveals the missing beginning. This is not just reasoning being collapsed: normal answer prose, including the beginning of a sentence continued outside the section, is hidden there. ### Steps to reproduce / observed setup 1. Configure PrimaLabs as a Custom Endpoint using the Chat Completions API (configuration below; API key omitted). 2. Select MiMo-V2.6-Pro in Copilot Chat, in Agent mode. 3. Send a greeting or ask a question such as "Can you access the GDAI MCP?" (the latter example used a configured Godot MCP server). 4. After the response completes, compare the normal answer with the content revealed by expanding "Completed N steps". These examples were observed with this setup; the exact trigger and reproduction frequency are not yet isolated. ### Actual behavior Example 1 (workspace name redacted): - Hidden under "Completed 3 steps": `Hello! What would you like to work on in` - Visible as the normal answer: `the workspace today?` Example 2, in response to "Can you access the GDAI MCP?": - Under "Completed 8 steps in 35s": `I have`, followed by `GDAI MCP tools available — let me verify by querying the Godot project info:`, a tool invocation, and then `Yes, the GDAI MCP is connected`. - Outside the collapsed section: `and working.`, followed by the status summary. The second example could legitimately include intermediate commentary among the steps, but the final confirmation itself is divided between the two sections. ### Expected behavior The full final answer should remain visible and continuous. A completed-steps disclosure should not hide the first portion of a final-answer sentence while showing only its continuation. ### Configuration Relevant provider entry from `chatLanguageModels.json`, with credentials omitted: ```json { "name": "PrimaLabs", "vendor": "customendpoint", "apiType": "chat-completions", "models": [ { "id": "primalabs-ai/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL", "name": "MiMo-V2.6-Pro", "url": "https://api.primalabs.ai/v1/chat/completions", "toolCalling": true, "vision": true, "thinking": true, "streaming": true, "contextWindow": 1048576, "maxOutputTokens": 131072 } ] } ``` ### Additional context A separate non-streaming API request with the message "Hello" returned an assistant message containing both `content` and `reasoning_content`, with `finish_reason: "stop"`. Its `system_fingerprint` was `vllm-0.29.1rc1.dev449+geb8798058-tp8-ea63e23f`. This establishes that the endpoint responds, but does not establish the shape of the affected stream or identify the cause. No workaround has been verified yet. It is currently unclear whether the sentence is split during BYOK stream handling, response-part grouping, or completed-response rendering. ### Related issues checked - #330627: Intermediate replies being collapsed into "Completed N steps"; a maintainer described that behavior as intentional. This report concerns a single final-answer sentence being split across the disclosure boundary. - #329963: Content silently dropped when a Chat Completions delta contains empty `tool_calls: []`. Related stream handling, but a different observed symptom. I did not find an existing issue specifically reporting this MiMo/PrimaLabs mid-sentence split.

issues.title: Refactor macOS Universal Bundling script to dynamically discover platform-specific binaries and node_modules
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:**
Currently, in the macOS universal bundling script (`build/darwin/universal.ts`), platform-specific native modules, tools (such as `ripgrep`, `tgrep`), and packages (like Copilot and `mxc-sdk`) for `darwin-x64` and `darwin-arm64` are hardcoded in multiple arrays and iteration loops (e.g., `nodeModulesBases`, `filesToSkip`, `singleArchFiles`, and `x64ArchFiles`). 

Whenever a new package or platform-specific binary is added to the application, developers have to manually update this script. This introduces maintenance overhead and risks missing new dependencies during universal build packaging.

**Describe the solution you'd like:**
I propose refactoring the script to dynamically discover and handle platform-specific directories and binaries under `node_modules` and `node_modules.asar.unpacked` based on matching patterns (e.g., matching `darwin-x64` / `darwin-arm64` suffixes or specific directory structures) rather than maintaining explicit hardcoded paths.

**Additional context:**
This improvement would enhance maintainability, reduce boilerplate code, and automatically future-proof the universal build script against newly added native dependencies. I'd be happy to work on a Pull Request for this if the maintainers agree with this approach!

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

In the Source Control changes list, clicking a changed file opens its diff. Ctrl+click on Windows and Linux, or ⌘+click on macOS, should open the full working-tree file in a normal editor instead.

This would let me review a change with a regular click and jump straight to editing the file with a modifier-click. The existing **Open File** row action and context-menu item work, but they require a separate target or menu.

**Requested behavior**

1. Open Source Control with a modified file.
2. Click the file to open its diff.
3. Ctrl+click the file on Windows or Linux, or ⌘+click it on macOS, to open the full, editable file.

Related: #158138 asked for the same shortcut, but its author closed it after being shown the existing **Open File** button. This request is specifically for the modifier-click shortcut on all desktop platforms.
