issues.title: Copilot Chat gets stuck on "Considering..."/"Working..." - "no session host is registered"

labels.name: info-needed
labels.description: Issue requires more information from poster

issues.body:
## Description

GitHub Copilot Chat (VS Code, extension version **0.67.0**, the latest available version) repeatedly gets stuck showing "Considering..." / "Working..." even though no actual processing is happening. This occurs across essentially every new chat session, not tied to a specific project, workspace, or specific tool call.

Once stuck, the chat never recovers no matter how long I wait -- the only way to unblock it is to reload the VS Code window or fully restart VS Code.

## Evidence found in logs

Looking at `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\logs\process-*.log`, nearly every recent runtime log file (14 out of 14 checked, spanning roughly the last week) contains this warning, correlated in time with the chat getting stuck:

```
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::pending_request_flow] pending-request event was not delivered to the session host {"error":"GenericFailure, no session host is registered for session <session-id>"}
```

This suggests the runtime process (`copilot-runtime.exe`) finishes (or attempts to deliver) a response for a given session, but by that point no session host is registered to receive it -- so the response is silently dropped and the chat UI is left showing an in-progress state forever.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open VS Code and start a new Copilot Chat session.
2. Send any message / ask any question.
3. Randomly (not always reproducible on demand), the chat gets stuck on "Considering..." / "Working..." indefinitely.
4. Check `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\logs\process-<pid>.log` around that timestamp -- a `pending-request event was not delivered to the session host` warning appears with `no session host is registered for session <id>`.

## Workaround found

- Deleting old/stale chat sessions from the session list temporarily resolved the issue, but it recurred later.
- Reloading/restarting VS Code always unblocks the current stuck chat (a new runtime process + session host registration presumably resolves the mismatch).

## Environment

- GitHub Copilot Chat extension version: 0.67.0 (build 1, buildType prod) -- confirmed via `resources\app\extensions\copilot\package.json` in the VS Code install, and confirmed to be the latest available version at the time of reporting.
- OS: Windows
- Runtime binary: `@github/copilot-sdk-win32-x64` (`copilot-runtime.exe`)

## Suspected area

Possibly related to recently added multi-window Agent Host support and/or session cleanup features, where a session host can become deregistered (e.g., after a window reload, sleep, or abrupt close) while the runtime still has a pending session id it tries to deliver results to.

## Request

Please investigate why `pending-request event was not delivered to the session host` occurs and whether the runtime can detect this failure and surface an error/timeout to the chat UI instead of leaving it stuck indefinitely, and/or re-register/recover the session host automatically instead of requiring a full VS Code restart.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
Switching input sources through GNOME Shell's switcher closes the file rename input in Explorer when VS Code uses its native Wayland backend.

### Environment

- Ubuntu Linux, GNOME Shell 46.0, Wayland session
- VS Code 1.139.1 (`04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`)
- Electron 43.6.0, Chromium 150.0.7871.250
- Linux x64 7.0.0-34-generic
- English and Russian input sources

Also reproduced in a development build with extensions disabled and a separate user-data directory.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a GNOME Wayland session, configure at least two input sources.
2. Launch VS Code with `--ozone-platform=wayland`.
3. Open a folder, select a file in Explorer, and press F2.
4. Edit its name without pressing Enter or Escape.
5. Switch input sources using the configured GNOME shortcut, for example Super+Space.

**Actual:** The rename input closes. A valid pending filename can be accepted even though the user only switched input sources.

**Expected:** The rename input stays open, preserving the pending name and selection so typing can continue.

Launching the same application with `--ozone-platform=x11` avoids the problem. This is a comparison to isolate the Wayland path.

### Investigation

The blur handler in `FilesRenderer.renderInputBox` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/views/explorerViewer.ts`) checks `ownerDocument.hasFocus()` before checking whether the rename input remains the document's active element. Losing page focus can therefore finish editing even when DOM focus has not moved to another element.

A local change that checks `ownerDocument.activeElement` first fixes the input-source switching scenario in manual testing. An Electron regression test using the real renderer reproduces the page-blur case and fails without that change. A second test checks that moving focus to another input still finishes editing.

The automated tests cover page-focus handling; the GNOME input-source switching scenario was verified manually. No Wayland protocol trace was captured.

issues.title: Agent host: an automatic rename_chat overwrites a title the user set
issues.body:
An automatic `rename_chat` replaces a title the user gave an agent-host chat, both in the UI and in the persisted metadata, so the user's title is gone after a reload too.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start an agent-host session with an agent that fulfils the host's automatic title reminder (seen with Codex).
2. Rename the session or chat yourself.
3. Send another message. The agent calls `rename_chat` with `automatic: true`.
4. The title changes to the agent's. After a reload, the agent's title is still shown, with `customTitleSource: agent` in the session metadata.

**Expected**

An automatic rename leaves a title the user chose alone. A rename the user explicitly asks the agent for (`automatic` omitted) should still apply.

**Cause**

- `applyRenameChatTool` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/sessionServerTools.ts`) reads `automatic` only to decide whether to run the rename in the background. It does not pass the flag to `ISessionServerToolAccessor.renameChat`.
- `AgentService._renameChatFromTool` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts`) then persists the agent's title with source `agent` unconditionally.
- `SessionTitleContribution` records a user rename with source `user`, but nothing on the tool path checks that source before writing over it.

A fix with tests follows in a PR.

VS Code: `main` at c94d3d7ed24 (agent host)
OS: macOS

## Environment

- VS Code: **1.139.0-insider**

1. In the Agents window, open an SVG artifact in the built-in Image Preview editor, with breadcrumbs visible.
2. Click inside the image preview so its webview has focus.
3. Click the final filename breadcrumb to open the sibling-file picker.
4. Repeat if necessary: the failure is timing-dependent.

**Expected:** The breadcrumb picker remains open and focused until the user chooses an item, presses Escape, or deliberately moves focus elsewhere.

**Actual:** The picker appears and immediately disappears. In a captured trace, it was removed approximately **8 ms after its tree gained focus**. This was reproduced on the first automated click, then repeatedly.

Confirmed scope is this Agents/image-preview scenario; other webview editors and the normal workbench have not yet been tested.

## Investigation: stale asynchronous webview focus steals focus from the picker

Investigated against the live renderer with the global `dbgjs` CLI, using native CDP clicks, focus event tracing, DOM mutation observation, and a non-pausing conditional breakpoint. No restart was required.

The captured runtime call chain was:

```text
BreadcrumbsControl._onSelectEvent
  -> editorGroup.focus
  -> webviewEditor.focus
  -> overlayWebview.focus
  -> WebviewElement.focus
  -> WebviewElement._doFocus
```

Relevant sources in the affected build:

- [breadcrumbsControl.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a3b0c130bdeeb42c8de4817bd4f5b00b051e8393/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/breadcrumbsControl.ts): `_onSelectEvent` unconditionally calls `this._editorGroup.focus()` before opening the picker. The picker hides on `focusTracker.onDidBlur`.
- [webviewElement.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a3b0c130bdeeb42c8de4817bd4f5b00b051e8393/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/webviewElement.ts): `_doFocus` immediately focuses the outer webview and schedules another focus operation through a 50 ms `ThrottledDelayer`. The delayed callback checks the current active element and calls `_send('focus', undefined)`.
- [webview preload](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a3b0c130bdeeb42c8de4817bd4f5b00b051e8393/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/pre/index.html): the `focus` message handler focuses the inner frame.

The picker loads and focuses its tree asynchronously. The delayed callback can send the webview focus message while the outer iframe is still active, so the existing active-element guard permits it. If the message takes effect after the picker tree gains focus, it takes focus back and the picker closes on blur. If it takes effect before tree focus, the picker survives. A send-time guard does not eliminate this delivery-time race.

Representative failure (relative to the focus-message send):

```text
 0.0 ms  _send('focus'), active element = webview iframe
 9.2 ms  breadcrumb tree receives focus
17.6 ms  breadcrumb picker removed
```

## Controlled runtime experiment

Same live editor and same breadcrumb click, changing only whether the outgoing webview `focus` message was forwarded. Each check occurred 700 ms after clicking. The normal path was tested before and after suppression:

| Condition | Picker dismissed | Picker stayed open |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal behavior, before suppression | 2/3 | 1/3 |
| Suppress the queued webview focus message | 0/3 | 3/3 |
| Normal behavior, restored | 1/3 | 2/3 |

This is a small causal diagnostic, not a randomized statistical study.

A subsequent temporary, reversible hotfix suppressed only outgoing webview `focus` messages while a visible `.monaco-breadcrumbs-picker` existed in the same window. With that guard, **10/10 consecutive clicks kept the picker open and focused**. Separately confirmed that a normal webview focus request without a picker was forwarded and focused the image preview.

The hotfix remains in that renderer until reload, but is **not a proposed production DOM-selector dependency**. All tracing hooks and breakpoints were removed. No source fix has been implemented yet.

## Proposed fix steps

1. **Avoid focusing the editor pane solely to open the breadcrumb picker.** In `BreadcrumbsControl._onSelectEvent`, separate activating the owning group from transferring DOM focus to its active editor. For the picker-opening path, use the existing group activation API (for example, `this._editorGroup.groupsView.activateGroup(this._editorGroup)`) rather than `this._editorGroup.focus()`, then let the picker take focus. Review the exact placement against both file and outline branches.
2. **Preserve existing reveal/navigation behavior.** Retain editor focusing where the action actually reveals an item, including modifier-click/open-to-side paths. Verify inactive groups become active correctly and picker selection/Escape restore the intended focus. Also test `breadcrumbs.useQuickPick` rather than assuming the same change is safe there.
3. **Consider a general webview hardening follow-up:** invalidate/cancel stale asynchronous focus requests when focus intent changes, rather than relying only on a check before sending the message. Do not disable the picker's blur-to-close behavior or replace the race with a larger arbitrary timeout.
4. **Add a deterministic regression test** that controls the ordering: breadcrumb selection requests editor focus; the delayed webview focus is queued/sent; the picker finishes loading and focuses its tree; the stale request must not steal that focus. Also exercise the opposite ordering, where the picker is ready first.
5. **Validate the full interaction matrix:** repeated SVG/image-preview clicks in Agents; ordinary text-editor breadcrumbs; file and outline pickers; keyboard opening and navigation; selection, Escape and outside-click dismissal; modifier/open-to-side actions; inactive/multiple groups; quick-pick mode; ordinary webview focus with no picker.

The activation-only source change above is a proposed production fix, not yet implemented or validated. The verified live mitigation is the narrowly scoped focus-message guard described above.

issues.title: `run_in_terminal` returns `Command produced no output` for `git branch --show-current` while chat displays the branch name
issues.body:
This is a significant bug that affects all the models several times a day: a specific Git tool command is telling the model effectively that Git is in detached `HEAD` mode when it's actually on a branch. This bug has been present for many months. It wastes lots of time and tokens as the model tries to compensate by issuing other Git commands to try to determine whether Git is in detached `HEAD` mode or on a branch.

The bug report below was drafted by Claude Opus 5.5 after discussion.

## Summary

When Copilot Chat's `run_in_terminal` tool runs `git branch --show-current`, the model receives `Command produced no output`. The chat shows the current branch name as the output of that same tool call. It happens on every attempt in the environment below, and the reporter has seen it repeatedly across sessions and models. `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints the same branch name, and the model receives that output normally.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.139.1, commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`, x64, with GitHub Copilot Chat bundled
- OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200
- Integrated terminal: Git Bash (Bash 5.3.15, MINGW64, MSYS runtime 3.6.9)
- Git: 2.55.0.windows.4
- Model: Claude Opus 5.5. The reporter has seen the same behavior with other models, both more and less capable.

```
Version: 1.139.1 (user setup)
Commit: 04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1
Date: 2026-09-25T03:40:57Z
Electron: 43.6.0
ElectronBuildId: 15274685
Chromium: 150.0.7871.250
Node.js: 24.20.0
V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0
@github/copilot: 1.0.85.r35379093703.g3514c9a
@github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.15.35393089353.gfc44743
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, set Git Bash as the VS Code integrated terminal shell. Open a Git repository with a named branch checked out, such as `feature/widget`.
2. Ask Copilot Chat to run `git branch --show-current` and to quote the tool result it receives word for word. The model calls `run_in_terminal` with:

   ```json
   {
     "command": "git branch --show-current",
     "explanation": "Run the command under investigation and capture the exact result returned to the assistant.",
     "goal": "Reproduce missing branch output",
     "mode": "sync"
   }
   ```

   `timeout` and `isBackground` are omitted. The other calls listed below also used sync mode; only their `command`, `explanation`, and `goal` values differed.
3. Compare the output the chat shows under the tool call with the result the model quotes.

## Expected Result

The model receives `feature/widget`, the same output the chat shows. The tool's description says that in sync mode "the full output is returned when the command completes." If the output cannot be captured, the result should say that capture failed, not that the command produced no output.

## Actual Result

- The chat shows `feature/widget` as the output of the tool call.
- The model's tool result contains only this line, after some empty lines:

  ```text
  Command produced no output
  ```

- No exit status is reported. In these calls, a status line appeared only for non-zero exits; see the `git show-ref` row below.
- After this command ran as the most recent command in the tool's terminal, the terminal context attached to the next chat request showed that terminal with an empty `Last Command` and `Exit Code: (unknown)`. After `git status --short --branch`, the same context showed that command with `Exit Code: 0`.
- When the reporter typed the same command into another integrated Git Bash terminal, it printed `feature/widget` and exited with code 0, according to `terminal_last_command`.

Comparison of `run_in_terminal` results:

| Command | Calls | Result received by the model |
|---|---|---|
| `git branch --show-current` | 4 | `Command produced no output` |
| `git --no-pager branch --show-current` | 1 | `Command produced no output` |
| `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` | 1 | `feature/widget` |
| `git status --short --branch` | 1 | Complete output, starting with `## feature/widget...origin/feature/widget` |
| `git show-ref --quiet --verify <nonexistent ref>` | 2 | `Command produced no output`, then `Command exited with code 1` (correct; this command prints nothing) |

## Impact

`git branch --show-current` prints nothing when `HEAD` is detached. The false tool result therefore looks like a valid Git result meaning there is no current branch. In the session where this was reproduced, the model said it was checking for a detached `HEAD` and ran another command to find the branch. It then told the user the command had produced no output, which contradicted the output shown in chat. The user cannot see the result the model received, so the problem shows up only when the model says something incorrect. Any agent task that depends on the current branch, such as creating a new branch from it (the task in progress here), starts from a wrong picture of the repository.

issues.title: Custom Azure model configuration sends unsupported `temperature` value
issues.body:
## Description
Custom Azure model configuration sends unsupported temperature value. The issue appears to be caused by a default or internally overridden temperature value being sent instead of the value defined in `modelOptions`.

When using the following custom Azure model configuration in VS Code Copilot:

```json
{
  "name": "Azure",
  "vendor": "azure",
  "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.xyz}",
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "gpt-5.6-luna",
      "name": "GPT 5.6 Luna",
      "url": "https://example.com/api/dev/chat/completions",
      "toolCalling": true,
      "vision": true,
      "maxInputTokens": 128000,
      "maxOutputTokens": 16000,
      "modelOptions": {
        "temperature": 1
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

the request fails with HTTP `400`.

The configured temperature is `1`, which is the only value supported by this model. However, the error indicates that VS Code Copilot sends `temperature: 0.1` in the request.

## Error message

```text
Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.

Client Request Id: 74171b3c-cee2-44bd-b121-b258a1058507

Reason: Request Failed: 400 {"detail":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"message\": \"Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0.1 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.\",\n    \"type\": \"invalid_request_error\",\n    \"param\": \"temperature\",\n    \"code\": \"unsupported_value\"\n  }\n}"}
```

## Expected behavior

VS Code Copilot should either:

1. Respect the configured value:

   ```json
   "modelOptions": {
     "temperature": 1
   }
   ```

2. Omit the `temperature` parameter when the model only supports its default value.

## Actual behavior

The request contains:

```json
"temperature": 0.1
```

despite the configuration specifying:

```json
"temperature": 1
```

As a result, the Azure endpoint rejects the request with HTTP `400`.

## Environment

- VS Code: `1.137.`
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension: `0.41 (2026-03-25)`
- Provider: Azure-compatible endpoint
- Model: `gpt-5.6-luna`
- Endpoint: `https://example.com/api/dev/chat/completions`

## Additional information

I created proxy server which capture API request, update temperature value, and sends modified request with proper temperature value directly to a model to make copilot work properly.

issues.title: CLI agent host supervisor evicts the running Remote-SSH server from the shared server cache; on an NFS home this leaves a broken install (ServerNotExecutable)

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Issues that have not been triaged in an appropriate amount of time

issues.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. Only Remote - SSH is involved, and the code in question is the `code` CLI on the remote. - VS Code Version: 1.136.0 (commit `520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1`), `remote.SSH.useExecServer` at its default `true` - OS Version: client Windows 11 x64; remote Rocky Linux 8.10, kernel 4.18, `$HOME` on NFS 4.0 ## Symptom Two colleagues of mine could no longer connect with Remote - SSH to our Linux build hosts, on the same day. Every attempt ended with this error (their Remote - SSH was 0.128.0): ``` CodeError(ServerNotExecutable("/home//.vscode-server/cli/servers/Stable-520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/server/bin/code-server is not executable and permissions could not be restored: No such file or directory (os error 2)")) at Object.resolve (c:\Users\\.vscode\extensions\ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh-0.128.0\out\extension.js:2:291663) ``` For one of them, moving the `Stable-520fb30b…` folder aside and reconnecting made the connection work again. ## Cause All code links are at `520fb30b` (1.136.0). The code linked below is unchanged on `main` at `101c86fe`. `download_cache.rs`, `commands/agent_host.rs` and `tunnels/code_server.rs` have other changes there (in `download_cache.rs` a download lock around `create`, added on 2026-08-31), so line numbers on `main` differ. 1. **Every `serve` in exec server mode starts or reuses the user's agent host supervisor.** `command_shell` always passes the supervisor future ([commands/tunnels.rs#L162-L186](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/commands/tunnels.rs#L162-L186)), and `handle_serve` awaits it before it looks for a running server ([tunnels/control_server.rs#L851-L860](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/control_server.rs#L851-L860)). There is no setting or flag around it (#328397). 2. **The supervisor downloads the latest stable server into the same cache as the editor's server.** At startup it resolves the latest release and calls `ensure_downloaded` ([commands/agent_host.rs#L307-L325](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/commands/agent_host.rs#L307-L325)). Its update loop checks every 6 hours ([tunnels/agent_host.rs#L55](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L55)) and downloads a new release once its own agent host server is not running ([tunnels/agent_host.rs#L550-L574](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L550-L574)). It uses `ctx.paths.server_cache` ([commands/agent_host.rs#L288](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/commands/agent_host.rs#L288)), which is `/servers` ([state.rs#L195](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/state.rs#L195)), the `DownloadCache` the editor's server is installed into ([tunnels/code_server.rs#L470-L473](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L470-L473)). A client that stays on one release therefore gets one more cache entry per stable release. 3. **The editor's cache entry is recorded only when the server is first installed.** `DownloadCache::create` returns early, without `touch`, when the folder exists ([download_cache.rs#L89-L91](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/download_cache.rs#L89-L91)), and `get_running` does not use the cache ([tunnels/code_server.rs#L401](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L401)). The supervisor records its entry again on every `exists()` ([download_cache.rs#L50-L60](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/download_cache.rs#L50-L60)), which it calls in `get_cached_or_download` whenever it starts its agent host server ([tunnels/agent_host.rs#L397-L403](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L397-L403)) and in its update loop ([tunnels/agent_host.rs#L552](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L552)). 4. **`lru.json` is read once per process and written without a lock between processes.** `PersistedStateContainer::load_or_get` reads the file on first use and returns the in-memory copy from then on ([state.rs#L46-L59](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/state.rs#L46-L59)); `update` applies the change to that copy and overwrites the file with it ([state.rs#L128-L133](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/state.rs#L128-L133)). Each CLI process has one `DownloadCache` for the servers ([state.rs#L195](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/state.rs#L195)). The supervisor and each `command-shell` are separate processes, so the file holds whatever the last writer had in memory. A supervisor that was started before the editor's server was installed removes that server's entry on its next write (run B below). A supervisor started afterwards keeps the entry, and every later download moves it towards the end of the list (run A below). 5. **`touch` keeps 5 entries and deletes the folder of the last one without checking whether that server is running** ([download_cache.rs#L119-L139](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/download_cache.rs#L119-L139)). The entry is dropped from the list only if `remove_dir_all` succeeds or the folder does not exist. `prune_stopped_servers`, in contrast, skips running servers ([tunnels/paths.rs#L118-L127](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/paths.rs#L118-L127)). 6. **On NFS, deleting a running server stops halfway.** A file that a running process still has open is turned into a `.nfs*` file instead of being removed, so its directory cannot be removed and `remove_dir_all` fails. In run A this left the folder with `log.txt`, `pid.txt` and `server/`, without `server/bin/code-server`, with a `.nfs*` file in `server/bin/`, and with its entry still in `lru.json`. 7. **The CLI then reports `ServerNotExecutable` on every connection.** Once no process of the old server runs, `get_running` finds none, `create` returns early because the folder exists, and `ensure_executable` fails in `std::fs::metadata` with ENOENT ([tunnels/code_server.rs#L365-L375](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L365-L375)), which is returned as `ServerNotExecutable` ([tunnels/code_server.rs#L663-L674](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L663-L674)). `handle_serve` evicts only on `ServerUnexpectedExit` ([tunnels/control_server.rs#L914-L931](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/control_server.rs#L914-L931)), so the folder stays. In 1.121.0, before #316950 (first released in 1.122.0), a missing binary failed at `.spawn()`, which is mapped to `ServerUnexpectedExit` ([1.121.0 code_server.rs#L630-L634](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1.121.0/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L630-L634)), and the server was evicted ([1.121.0 control_server.rs#L812-L823](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1.121.0/cli/src/tunnels/control_server.rs#L812-L823)), so the next connection installed it again. 8. **The folder is removed only by a later `touch` of a process whose copy of the list still contains it**, once nothing runs from the folder any more (run A, step 5). On our build hosts, `ps` on 2026-09-27 shows agent host supervisors that were started on 2026-08-17 and are still running. ## Runs All runs used the real VS Code 1.136.0 CLI (`https://update.code.visualstudio.com/commit:520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli-linux-x64/stable`) and real server builds, with a scratch `--cli-data-dir` on an NFS 4.0 mount of the same host. The client side is the Node script below, run with VS Code's own Electron (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`): over `ssh` it starts `code command-shell`, answers `challenge_issue`/`challenge_verify` with VS Code's bundled `vsda` signer and sends a `serve` request as defined by `ServeParams` in `protocol.rs`. Supervisors were started with `code --cli-data-dir agent host`; where stated, `VSCODE_CLI_INITIAL_AH_VERSION` ([tunnels/agent_host.rs#L66-L71](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L66-L71)) pinned the first version they download. Output below is copied from the runs; `…` shortens commit hashes and paths. ### Run A: the editor's server is deleted while it runs In this run a new supervisor was started for each release after 1.136.0, so each one read the current `lru.json` at startup; this differs from a single supervisor that runs for weeks (see run B). **1. A window connects** (`serve` for `520fb30b`). The CLI installs and starts 1.136.0; the same `command-shell` starts a supervisor, which downloads the latest stable, 1.139.1: ``` serverlog: {"line":"Server integrity verified, version: 1.136.0 / 520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1 / x64 / ","level":0} serverlog: {"line":"Server started","level":2} SERVE RESPONSE: success lru.json = ["Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-04c0d99f…"] Stable-04c0d99f…: server Stable-520fb30b…: log.txt pid.txt server ``` **2. One supervisor start per release since 1.136.0**, pinned with `VSCODE_CLI_INITIAL_AH_VERSION`, while the window stays connected and the editor's server runs (version numbers added for reading): ``` supervisor start pinned to a44adf7f… (1.136.1) lru.json = ["Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-04c0d99f…"] supervisor start pinned to 88e44fa0… (1.136.2) lru.json = ["Stable-88e44fa0…","Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-04c0d99f…"] supervisor start pinned to 645f29cc… (1.137.0) lru.json = ["Stable-645f29cc…","Stable-88e44fa0…","Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-04c0d99f…"] supervisor start pinned to 7debcd0e… (1.138.0) lru.json = ["Stable-7debcd0e…","Stable-645f29cc…","Stable-88e44fa0…","Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…"] supervisor start pinned to 2242ebbb… (1.139.0) lru.json = ["Stable-2242ebbb…","Stable-7debcd0e…","Stable-645f29cc…","Stable-88e44fa0…","Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…"] Stable-520fb30b…: log.txt pid.txt server editor server processes: 2 bin/code-server: ls: cannot access '…/Stable-520fb30b…/server/bin/code-server': No such file or directory .nfs files: …/Stable-520fb30b…/server/bin/.nfs000000000217f4e90000b6c0 ``` At the 1.138.0 step, `Stable-04c0d99f…`, which no process ran from, was removed completely. At the 1.139.0 step the removal of the running `Stable-520fb30b…` stopped halfway, and `lru.json` has six entries. **3. Reconnect while the old server still runs:** the running server is reused. ``` serverlog: {"line":"Found running server (pid=1121056)","level":2} SERVE RESPONSE: success ``` **4. Reconnect after stopping the old server's processes (`kill`)**, twice, with the same result both times; the folder and its `lru.json` entry stay: ``` serverlog: {"line":"Checking …/Stable-520fb30b…/log.txt and …/Stable-520fb30b…/pid.txt for a running server...","level":2} serverlog: {"line":"Installing and setting up Visual Studio Code Server...","level":1} serverlog: {"line":"Server setup complete","level":1} serverlog: {"line":"Starting server...","level":2} serverlog: {"line":"Starting server process: \"…/Stable-520fb30b…/server/bin/code-server\"","level":1} SERVE RESPONSE: error {"code":-1,"message":"CodeError(ServerNotExecutable(\"…/Stable-520fb30b…/server/bin/code-server is not executable and permissions could not be restored: No such file or directory (os error 2)\"))"} ``` **5. A supervisor starts again** and downloads 1.139.1. The next `serve` downloads 1.136.0 again, which `create` does only when the folder does not exist, and succeeds: ``` info Downloading Visual Studio Code server -> /tmp/.tmp…/vscode-server-linux-x64.tar.gz info Starting server... info Server started ``` ### Run B: a long-running supervisor removes the editor's entry from `lru.json` **1.** A supervisor is started, pinned to 1.139.0, and keeps running: ``` lru.json after supervisor start: ["Stable-2242ebbb…"] ``` **2.** A separate `command-shell` installs and starts 1.136.0 (`serve` for `520fb30b`): ``` serverlog: {"line":"Server started","level":2} SERVE RESPONSE: success lru.json after serve: ["Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-2242ebbb…"] ``` **3.** A request with WebSocket upgrade headers is sent to the supervisor's port. Its log shows it starting its agent host server right after (`Server ready`), which goes through `get_cached_or_download` and with it `exists()` and `touch`; the log shows no other action of the supervisor between step 2 and the check. `lru.json` afterwards holds the list the supervisor read in step 1: ``` lru.json after supervisor started its server: ["Stable-2242ebbb…"] ls cli/servers: Stable-2242ebbb… Stable-520fb30b… lru.json ``` The editor's server kept running and its folder stayed, without an entry in `lru.json`. ### Run C: the same deletion on a local filesystem On `/tmp` (xfs) of the same host, with a copy of the 1.136.0 server as `Stable-520fb30b…`, four placeholder entries `Stable-fake1` to `Stable-fake4`, and `lru.json` listing `Stable-520fb30b…` last, the 1.136.0 server was started directly and a supervisor pinned to 1.139.0 was started. The supervisor's download removed the running server's folder completely and dropped its entry: ``` lru.json = ["Stable-2242ebbb…","Stable-fake4","Stable-fake3","Stable-fake2","Stable-fake1"] Stable-520fb30b… exists: no; contents: editor server still alive: yes ``` ## Workaround `"remote.SSH.useExecServer": false` in the client's user settings. Remote - SSH then installs the server to `~/.vscode-server/bin/` without the CLI, and no supervisor is started; the server starts its agent host as a child process (`--type=agentHost`). Windows that are already open stay in exec server mode until they are reloaded. To repair a broken install: stop the user's `~/.vscode-server/code-*` processes on the host, move `~/.vscode-server/cli/servers/Stable-` aside and reconnect. ## Related - #316950 introduced `ensure_executable`, `ServerNotExecutable` and the skipped eviction for it (first released in 1.122.0). - #328397: no way to keep the supervisor from starting over SSH.
serve-client.js (the Remote - SSH side of command-shell) ```js // Plays the Remote-SSH side of `code command-shell` (exec server mode) for a // reproduction: runs the remote CLI over ssh, passes its vsda challenge with // VS Code's own vsda signer, then sends the `serve` request Remote-SSH sends for // a commit and prints the CLI's answer. // // Run with VS Code's Electron as Node, so vsda loads: // ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 Code.exe serve-client.js // The remote command is ` --cli-data-dir command-shell 2>&1 1>>log`: // in stdio mode command-shell reads stdin and writes its RPC to stderr. // With "hold" the connection stays open, like an open VS Code window. 'use strict'; const { spawn } = require('child_process'); const path = require('path'); const [host, remoteCommand, commit, mode] = process.argv.slice(2); const vsda = require(path.join(path.dirname(process.execPath), '520fb30b2d', 'resources', 'app', 'node_modules', 'vsda')); // Minimal MessagePack, enough for this protocol's maps, strings, numbers and binaries. function encode(value) { if (value === null || value === undefined) return Buffer.from([0xc0]); if (value === true) return Buffer.from([0xc3]); if (value === false) return Buffer.from([0xc2]); if (typeof value === 'number') { if (Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 && value < 0x80) return Buffer.from([value]); if (Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 && value <= 0xffffffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xce; b.writeUInt32BE(value, 1); return b; } throw new Error('unsupported number ' + value); } if (typeof value === 'string') { const s = Buffer.from(value, 'utf8'); if (s.length < 32) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0xa0 | s.length]), s]); const h = Buffer.alloc(5); h[0] = 0xdb; h.writeUInt32BE(s.length, 1); return Buffer.concat([h, s]); } if (Array.isArray(value)) { if (value.length >= 16) throw new Error('array too long'); return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x90 | value.length]), ...value.map(encode)]); } const keys = Object.keys(value); if (keys.length >= 16) throw new Error('map too long'); return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x80 | keys.length]), ...keys.flatMap(k => [encode(k), encode(value[k])])]); } class Incomplete extends Error { } function decode(buf, pos) { const need = n => { if (pos + n > buf.length) throw new Incomplete(); }; need(1); const t = buf[pos++]; const str = n => { need(n); const s = buf.toString('utf8', pos, pos + n); pos += n; return s; }; const bin = n => { need(n); const b = buf.subarray(pos, pos + n); pos += n; return b; }; const arr = n => { const a = []; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const r = decode(buf, pos); a.push(r.value); pos = r.pos; } return a; }; const map = n => { const o = {}; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const k = decode(buf, pos); const v = decode(buf, k.pos); o[k.value] = v.value; pos = v.pos; } return o; }; const u = n => { need(n); const v = n === 1 ? buf[pos] : n === 2 ? buf.readUInt16BE(pos) : n === 4 ? buf.readUInt32BE(pos) : Number(buf.readBigUInt64BE(pos)); pos += n; return v; }; const i = n => { need(n); const v = n === 1 ? buf.readInt8(pos) : n === 2 ? buf.readInt16BE(pos) : n === 4 ? buf.readInt32BE(pos) : Number(buf.readBigInt64BE(pos)); pos += n; return v; }; let value; if (t < 0x80) value = t; else if (t >= 0xe0) value = t - 0x100; else if ((t & 0xe0) === 0xa0) value = str(t & 0x1f); else if ((t & 0xf0) === 0x90) value = arr(t & 0x0f); else if ((t & 0xf0) === 0x80) value = map(t & 0x0f); else switch (t) { case 0xc0: value = null; break; case 0xc2: value = false; break; case 0xc3: value = true; break; case 0xc4: value = bin(u(1)); break; case 0xc5: value = bin(u(2)); break; case 0xc6: value = bin(u(4)); break; case 0xca: need(4); value = buf.readFloatBE(pos); pos += 4; break; case 0xcb: need(8); value = buf.readDoubleBE(pos); pos += 8; break; case 0xcc: value = u(1); break; case 0xcd: value = u(2); break; case 0xce: value = u(4); break; case 0xcf: value = u(8); break; case 0xd0: value = i(1); break; case 0xd1: value = i(2); break; case 0xd2: value = i(4); break; case 0xd3: value = i(8); break; case 0xd9: value = str(u(1)); break; case 0xda: value = str(u(2)); break; case 0xdb: value = str(u(4)); break; case 0xdc: value = arr(u(2)); break; case 0xdd: value = arr(u(4)); break; case 0xde: value = map(u(2)); break; case 0xdf: value = map(u(4)); break; default: throw new Error('unsupported msgpack type 0x' + t.toString(16)); } return { value, pos }; } const log = (...a) => console.log(`[${new Date().toISOString().slice(11, 19)}]`, ...a); const child = spawn('C:\\Windows\\System32\\OpenSSH\\ssh.exe', ['-T', host, remoteCommand], { stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'inherit'] }); let pending = Buffer.alloc(0); const waiters = new Map(); let nextId = 1; function call(method, params) { const id = nextId++; child.stdin.write(encode({ id, method, params })); return new Promise(resolve => waiters.set(id, resolve)); } child.stdout.on('data', chunk => { pending = Buffer.concat([pending, chunk]); for (; ;) { let r; try { r = decode(pending, 0); } catch (e) { if (e instanceof Incomplete) break; throw e; } pending = pending.subarray(r.pos); const m = r.value; if (m && typeof m === 'object' && waiters.has(m.id)) { waiters.get(m.id)(m); waiters.delete(m.id); } else if (m && m.method === 'serverlog') log('serverlog:', JSON.stringify(m.params).slice(0, 240)); } }); child.on('exit', code => { log('ssh exited', code); process.exit(0); }); (async () => { const issued = await call('challenge_issue', { token: null }); if (issued.error) { log('challenge_issue error:', JSON.stringify(issued.error)); process.exit(1); } const response = new vsda.signer().sign(issued.result.challenge); const verified = await call('challenge_verify', { response }); log('challenge_verify:', verified.error ? JSON.stringify(verified.error) : 'ok'); log(`serve request for commit ${commit}`); const served = await call('serve', { socket_id: 1, commit_id: commit, quality: 'stable', extensions: [] }); log('SERVE RESPONSE:', served.error ? 'error ' + JSON.stringify(served.error) : 'success'); if (mode !== 'hold') { child.kill(); process.exit(0); } log('holding the connection open like an open window'); })(); ```
phase2.sh (run A, step 2) ```bash #!/bin/bash # Phase 2: supervisor starts, one per release since the client's 1.136.0. set -u T=$HOME/ah-repro; CLI=$T/code; DATA=$T/cli; SERVERS=$DATA/servers EDITOR=520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1 say() { echo "[$(date +%T)] $*"; } state() { say "lru.json = $(cat $SERVERS/lru.json 2>/dev/null)" for d in $SERVERS/Stable-*; do echo " $(basename $d): $(ls -A $d 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"; done; } say "state after the window connected (its command-shell also started a supervisor):"; state say "supervisor processes: $(pgrep -af '[c]ode --cli-data-dir .*agent host' | wc -l); editor server processes: $(pgrep -f "[s]ervers/Stable-$EDITOR/server/" | wc -l)" for c in "$@"; do $CLI --cli-data-dir $DATA agent kill >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 2 say "supervisor start pinned to $c" VSCODE_CLI_INITIAL_AH_VERSION=$c $CLI --cli-data-dir $DATA agent host >> $T/ah-run.log 2>&1 & for i in $(seq 1 120); do sleep 2; [ -d $SERVERS/Stable-$c ] && ! ls -d $SERVERS/*.staging* >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; done sleep 3; state done say "last supervisor left running; editor server processes: $(pgrep -f "[s]ervers/Stable-$EDITOR/server/" | wc -l)" say "bin/code-server: $(ls -la $SERVERS/Stable-$EDITOR/server/bin/code-server 2>&1)" say ".nfs files: $(find $SERVERS/Stable-$EDITOR -name '.nfs*' | tr '\n' ' ')" ``` Run as `phase2.sh a44adf7f53e00964ab890f9f8758a334f1fc15bc 88e44fa0e00b08f7758b4f6d05632e4fd5e4df6f 645f29cc3176500b4b5762ba887cf2a7f0ffdf2c 7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda`, then again with `2242ebbb54efeeb0129e08e919e7e8d43033cd83`.

issues.title: Agent Host (Copilot SDK) Windows sandbox: every sandboxed command fails at startup with 0xC0000022 (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED)
issues.body:
# Agent Host (Copilot SDK) Windows sandbox: every sandboxed command fails at startup with 0xC0000022 (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED)

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| VS Code | 1.139.1 (commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`, x64) |
| Copilot runtime | `copilot-runtime.exe` 1.0.85-unstable.r35379093703.g3514c9a |
| Copilot SDK package | `@github/copilot-sdk-win32-x64` 1.0.15-unstable.35393089353.gfc44743 |
| OS | Windows 11 Enterprise 25H2, build 26200.9448 |
| Required update | KB5124008 installed (2026-09-14) |
| Session type | Agent Host, Copilot SDK built-in shell (editor window) |
| Managed environment | Corporate device (WDAC policies, AppLocker, Microsoft Defender with ASR rules) |

Relevant user settings at the time of the failures:

```jsonc
"chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness": true,
"chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows": "on",   // "off" as a workaround
"chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows": true,			// "false" as a workaround
"chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands": true,
"chat.agent.sandbox.allowAutoApprove": true,
"chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork": true,
"chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.windows": {
    "allowRead": [],
    "allowWrite": ["C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\Temp"],
    "denyRead": []
}
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. On the environment above, enable the SDK sandbox: `"chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows": "on"` and `"chat.agentsandbox.sandbox.enabledWindows": "true"`
2. Start a new Copilot (Agent Host) session in any local folder.
3. Ask the agent to run any command, for example `node --version`, `Get-ChildItem` or `Get-Command node`.

## Expected

The command runs inside the sandbox and returns its output.

## Actual

Every sandboxed process fails immediately, in about 1 s, with exit code `-1073741790` (`0xC0000022`, STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED) and **no output at all**:

```
<shellId: 2 completed with exit code -1073741790>
```

- It affects every executable tried: `powershell.exe` (even a bare `Get-ChildItem`), `node.exe`, and the agent's built-in `grep` tool (`ripgrep exited with code -1073741790`).
- The behavior is the same with and without non-ASCII characters in the workspace path (`C:\<dev-with-accent>\...` and `C:\<ascii-path>\...`).
- Adding `C:\Program Files\nodejs` to `chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.windows` does not help.
- `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` is `true`, but running the command outside the sandbox is never offered (possibly related: #337310).
- With `"chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows": "off"`, the same commands succeed immediately (`node --version` → `v26.8.2`, exit 0).

The session log marks every failing call as sandboxed:

```
node --version  | exit=-1073741790 | sandboxApplied=true | sandboxed=true | 1302ms
Get-Command ... | exit=-1073741790 | sandboxApplied=true | sandboxed=true | 1023ms
Get-ChildItem   | exit=-1073741790 | sandboxApplied=true | sandboxed=true | 1046ms
```

The Agent Host log contains this error at every session creation, just before the sandbox configuration is applied. It also appears for other sessions:

```
[error] [Copilot:<session>] Copilot runtime did not report its resolved managed settings; continuing with available sandbox configuration
[info]  [Copilot:<session>] Applied SDK sandboxConfig via session.options.update
...
[info]  [Copilot:<session>] Managed settings resolved: source=client, managedKeys=permissions, bypassPermissionsDisabled=false, failClosed=false
[info]  [Copilot:<session>] Auto-approving sandboxed shell command for tool call <id>
```

## Diagnostics already performed

- **AppContainer creation works.** For each failing command, `Microsoft-Windows-AppModel-Runtime/Admin` logs `AppContainer Sandbox.{GUID} created successfully` (event 39), then `deleted successfully` (event 41), at the exact timestamp of the command. The failure therefore happens after the container is created, when the process starts or initializes inside it.
- **System DLL ACLs are correct.** `icacls C:\Windows\System32\kernel32.dll` grants `(RX)` to `BUILTIN\Users`, `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES` and `ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES`.
- **WDAC / Code Integrity:** no events at the times of the failures. Active corporate policies only block specific apps (Discord, Telegram, Firefox < 149, Python < 3.11).
- **AppLocker (EXE and DLL):** no events on the day of the failures.
- **Microsoft Defender:** no detection or block related to these processes. The only 1121 events are an unrelated ASR rule (LSASS credential-theft protection, `svchost.exe` → `lsass.exe`), at times that do not match the failures.
- **Application / System event logs:** no application errors related to `copilot-runtime`, `powershell`, `node` or `rg` during the failures.
- **Windows prerequisite:** KB5124008 is installed, and the build (26200.9448) is newer than the one it ships (26200.9445).

## Workaround

```jsonc
"chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows": "off"
```

Then start a new session. Commands then run unsandboxed.

## Attachments

All files are anonymized: `<user>`, `<machine>`, `<company>`, `<dev>` and `<project>` replace identifying values.

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `01-environment.txt` | VS Code, Copilot runtime and SDK versions, OS build, KB5124008, ACL of `kernel32.dll` |
| `02-settings-sandbox.jsonc` | Sandbox-related user settings |
| `03-session-commands.txt` | Every shell/grep call of the affected session, with exit code, `sandboxApplied` and duration (sandbox on, then off) |
| `04-agenthost-excerpt.log` | Filtered `agenthost.log` lines (sandbox, runtime, terminal, tool execution, errors), before and after the workaround |
| `05-windows-events.txt` | AppModel-Runtime AppContainer events, CodeIntegrity, AppLocker, Defender and Application/System errors during the failures |

- Surface the actual failing step when a sandboxed process exits with `0xC0000022` (process creation, DLL load, token or ACL setup), instead of only the exit code.

issues.title: Extension host did not start (debugBrk: true) on macOS — js-debug polls ::1 while the extension host listens on 127.0.0.1

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.139.1 (04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1, arm64)
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On a macOS machine, confirm that `localhost` resolves IPv6-first. This is the macOS default
   behavior — the system resolver handles `localhost` itself, so /etc/hosts changes do not affect it:

   $ node -e "require('dns').lookup('localhost',{all:true},(e,a)=>console.log(a))"
   [ { address: '::1', family: 6 }, { address: '127.0.0.1', family: 4 } ]

2. Open any extension project (reproduced with a plain TypeScript extension project) and press F5
   ("Run Extension").

3. The Extension Development Host window opens. After ~10 s VS Code reports:
   "Extension host did not start in 10 seconds, it might be stopped on the first line and needs a
   debugger to continue. (debugBrk: true)"
   and after 60 s: "The local extension host took longer than 60s to send its ready message."

Actual behavior:

The extension host (the debuggee) starts paused at --inspect-brk and listens on IPv4 only:

$ lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN
Code Helper (Plugin) <pid> ... TCP 127.0.0.1:53733 (LISTEN)

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:53733/json/version
{"Browser":"node.js/v24.20.0","Protocol-Version":"1.1"}     # host inspector reachable on IPv4

But the built-in JavaScript debugger (ms-vscode.js-debug 1.117.0) polls ::1:<port> and never
falls back to 127.0.0.1. The Debug Console repeats the following ~91 times within the 10 s window:

RequestError: connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:53733
    at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js:23:14613)

Since the debugger can never attach, the extension host stays paused forever.

Local verification that this is an address-family mismatch, not a missing listener (same machine):

$ node -e "require('http').get({host:'localhost',port:53733,path:'/json/version',autoSelectFamily:false},r=>{...}).on('error',e=>console.log('ERR:',e.message))"
ERR: connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:53733        # identical to the js-debug error
$ node --dns-result-order=ipv4first -e "<same request>"
OK 200
$ curl -s http://localhost:53733/json/version
OK

Expected behavior:

js-debug's attach/polling of the extension-host inspector should fall back across address families
(as curl and Node's default behavior do), or both sides should agree on the loopback address.

Attempted workarounds — none changed the behavior:

- Launching VS Code as: code --dns-result-order=ipv4first
- Commenting out "::1 localhost" in /etc/hosts and fully restarting VS Code. Note that on macOS this
  has no effect on resolving `localhost` (the system resolver keeps returning ::1 first, as shown above).

Notes:

- The same symptom was reported in the closed #140536 (2022). Based on the Debug Console output, the
  extension-host attach path still only attempts ::1 — no fallback to 127.0.0.1 is attempted (the
  listener is verifiably reachable on 127.0.0.1 during the whole failure window).
- Reading the shipped (minified) sources: VS Code starts the debuggee host with
  --inspect-brk=127.0.0.1:<port> (workbench.desktop.main.js, localProcessExtensionHost), while
  js-debug's extension-host launch polls http://localhost:<port>
  (ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js), with no address-family fallback on that path.
- Happy to provide full Debug Console logs or run further diagnostics. If this belongs in
  vscode-js-debug, please feel free to transfer.

[0926-after-F5.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32681019/0926-after-F5.log)

issues.title: [chat-perf] TTFT/layoutDurationMs regressed 29–45% in large-codeblock, long-prose, file-links, thinking-response scenarios
issues.body:
### Summary
*New regression detected*: Significant increases in `timeToFirstToken` (+29–45%) and `layoutDurationMs` (+21%) in the following chat scenarios: **large-codeblock, long-prose, file-links, thinking-response**. These are well outside the baseline window's normal noise and represent a clear step up from previous runs.

### Evidence
- **large-codeblock**: TTFT 507ms (was 373ms ±18), layoutDurationMs 207ms (was 171ms ±2.8)
- **long-prose**: TTFT 494ms (was 384ms ±13)
- **file-links**: TTFT 552ms (was 382ms ±5.6)
- **thinking-response**: TTFT 535ms (was 397ms ±17)

All are >100ms above the baseline mean and well outside baseline spread.

**Trend:**
- All four metrics show a sharp increase in the current run, after a long period of stability (see baseline window: no similar spikes, no prior regressions).
- The regression is not present in the last 6 baseline runs, all of which were stable.

**Suspect Commits:**
- The regression likely landed between the last baseline and this run. The most suspicious are recent changes touching chat/session/layout logic:
  - 4ccdb71 (sandy081): "sessions: Synchronize live last turn changes" — touches chat/session logic, landed just before this regression.
  - 1e3ed44 (sandy081): "agentHost: Scope server tools to exact chats" — also landed in this window, touches chat/agent logic.

### Suggested Action
- Bisect between the last good baseline and this run, focusing on 4ccdb71 and 1e3ed44 as likely culprits.
- Review changes in chat/session/layout code for performance impact on TTFT/layout.
- Roll back or optimize as needed.

---
**Please triage promptly: these are major regressions in core chat responsiveness.**

issues.title: Copilot Agent Window: BYOK custom models register in Chat but fail in agent sessions (session.model.switchTo 'not registered')
issues.body:
### Summary

BYOK custom models (`customendpoint/<vendor>/<model>` — e.g. Ollama Cloud endpoints configured through the supported BYOK path: `chatLanguageModels.json` + `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`) work fine in **Chat**, but cannot be selected in **Agent Window / agent host sessions**:

```
Error: (modelSelectionFailed) Error: Request session.model.switchTo failed with message:
Provider model 'customendpoint/Ollama Cloud/glm-5.3-flash:cloud' is not registered
```

The agent host's session registry contains only built-in models. The BYOK models are wired to the loopback proxy at boot, but never reach the session SDK registry that `session.model.switchTo` consults.

### What works / what doesn't

In Chat: BYOK models are listed and selectable. ✓

In the Agent Window (agent host session):

```
[Copilot:boot] Wired 52 BYOK model(s) across 3 provider(s) via loopback proxy http://127.0.0.1:56113
...
[Copilot:c7f7565c] Changing model to: customendpoint/Ollama Cloud/glm-5.3-flash:cloud
[Copilot] Found 31 models: Auto, Claude Sonnet 5, ...   <-- registry unchanged, zero customendpoint entries
[AgentSideEffects] modelSelection failed ... Provider model 'customendpoint/...' is not registered
```

The host resolves a BYOK session config for boot (`_resolveByokSessionConfig(boot)` in the session launcher code, `copilotSessionLauncher`) containing all the models — but nothing plumbs them into the session registry at boot, and the `BYOK bridge changed` handler (`_refreshByokModels`) only refreshes the wire-side catalog.

### Two runtime semantics we discovered empirically

While investigating we instrumented the runtime and found two behaviors that (if confirmed) would be worth documenting upstream, since they fundamentally constrain how a host can register BYOK models into an agent session:

**1. `session.rpc.provider.add` accepts exactly one referencing per provider name.**

Any call after the first — even with `providers: []` — is rejected wholesale with:

```
Error: Request session.provider.add failed with message: Duplicate BYOK provider name customendpoint.
```

...without registering the payload models. A successful registration is necessarily a **single batch call**:

```ts
session.rpc.provider.add({ sessionId, providers: <all BYOK providers>, models: <all BYOK models> });
```

Verified empirically: per-model registration attempts produced 520 rejected calls in a single boot session; one single batch call returned success and all models became switch-selectable.

**2. Permission mode `allow-all` is rejected by the SDK policy in headless agent sessions.**

`_getSdkPermissionMode()` maps an auto-approve session (`autoApprove` level) to `allow-all`, then the first send fails with:

```
[Copilot] Syncing permission mode: source=turn-start, agentMode=interactive, configuredLevel=autoApprove, sdkMode=allow-all, ...
error: Copilot SDK rejected permission mode 'allow-all'  ->  sendFailed
```

A graceful fallback (e.g. `assisted`) — or a documented way to enable the mode for agent hosts — would remove the trap.

### Repro

- Document the `provider.add` single-reference semantics (e.g. in `@github/copilot-sdk` types) and the permission-mode policy expectations for agent hosts.

### Environment

- VS Code 1.139.0 (user setup), commit `04c0d99f4f`, Windows 11 x64
- Agent host: `resources/app/out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js`
- Copilot runtime: `@github/copilot-win32-x64` (SDK surface: `@github/copilot-sdk` public types)

Thanks! Happy to provide full boot logs if useful.

issues.title: Remote agent sessions do not discover host MCP servers until messaged locally
issues.body:
## Type of Issue

Bug

## Reproduction

Both the local laptop and remote dev box have the Notion MCP server configured.

1. From the laptop, start an agent session on the dev box.
2. From the laptop, ask the remote session whether it has the Notion MCP server.
3. Observe that the session reports that it does not.
4. On the dev box, message the same session directly and ask the same question.
5. Observe that the session now reports that the Notion MCP server is available.
6. From the laptop, ask the same session again.
7. Observe that it now reports the server as available there as well.

## Expected Behavior

A remote session should discover MCP servers configured on the host machine when it starts, regardless of whether the session has first been messaged locally on that host.

## Actual Behavior

Host MCP servers are unavailable to a remotely initiated session until the same session is messaged locally on the host machine. After that local interaction, the MCP server becomes available remotely too.

## Additional Context

Agent Host logs were captured as `ah-logs-Notion-access-inquiry.zip` in the original report.

issues.title: Let primary AI agents delegate routine work to local models
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
VS Code already supports agent workflows, subagents, and local/BYOK models. I’d like those pieces connected more intelligently.
The idea is simple: let a high-capability reasoning model handle the larger task—architecture, difficult debugging, integration and review—while automatically delegating bounded, routine work to a local coding model such as Qwen Coder.
For example:
Primary reasoning model → local Qwen Coder → tests/results → primary model review
The local model could handle repository searches, repetitive edits, simple refactors, documentation, test generation and other low-risk work. The primary model would remain responsible for the overall task and review everything returned by the local agent.
This would reduce premium-model usage and latency, improve privacy, make useful use of local hardware, and reserve the strongest model for the work that actually needs it.
In short: don’t make one expensive model do everything. Let the coordinator intelligently distribute the work among available models.
There are already related issues around BYOK models being used as subagents (#333802 and #331904), so much of the underlying infrastructure appears to exist. What I’m asking for is the orchestration layer that makes heterogeneous models work together as one coding system.

issues.title: Managed enabledPlugins refresh does not reconcile active Agent Host sessions

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
## Problem

VS Code does not have an explicit host-side convergence path for managed `enabledPlugins` changes that arrive after an Agent Host session has started.

The runtime refreshes managed settings for long-running sessions, but a refreshed policy can be present while the active session retains its previous plugin inventory and plugin-provided skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and extensions. Users may need a new session or application restart before a managed plugin appears or disappears.

A September 24 enterprise customer meeting provided a concrete example: a managed marketplace appeared after refresh/restart, while the plugin did not become enabled for roughly 24 hours. The customer expected every new session or surface restart to fetch current settings, and already-running clients to apply hourly updates without requiring a restart.

## Expected behavior

- VS Code responds to each applied managed-settings generation.
- Managed plugin installation, enablement, disablement, and contributed resources converge in the active session when safe.
- If a new session or subsystem reload is required, the product states that explicitly and offers a recovery path instead of silently retaining stale behavior.
- Policy withdrawal removes contributions on the same documented lifecycle.
- Tests cover adding and withdrawing `enabledPlugins` while an Agent Host session remains open.

## Related work

- github/copilot-agent-runtime#22922 tracks the host-independent runtime contract.
- github/github-app#16986 tracks the Copilot App integration.
- microsoft/vscode#338071 fixed force-enablement for an already-installed plugin, but not live refresh convergence.

issues.title: Webview can stay on its old content when its HTML is replaced while that content is still loading

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Issues that have not been triaged in an appropriate amount of time

issues.body:
- VS Code version: 1.139.1 (latest stable) and `main` (949b097). The webview host page is byte-identical in both.
- OS: any. The logic is platform-independent; I reproduced it in Chromium on Windows 11.

## What happens

If a webview's HTML is replaced while the previous content is still loading, the new content can get stuck in `pending-frame` forever:

- The old content stays on screen.
- Every `postMessage` to the webview is queued for the new frame and never delivered.
- Messages from the new content to the host still arrive, so to the embedder the webview looks alive but deaf.

## Why

The host page shows new content in a pending frame, which becomes the active frame when it loads, or after a 200ms fallback timer when its load is slow. While a pending frame exists, every message to the webview is queued for it (L1246-L1254).

The fallback timer lives in one variable, `loadTimeout` (L420), shared by every frame. Each frame's `load` listener clears whatever timer that variable holds at the time:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/949b097abf4e9b62d9153e885657b32e01115920/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/pre/index.html#L1153-L1172

The failing sequence:

1. Content A is set. Its load is slow, so its fallback makes it the active frame while its own `load` event is still pending.
2. Content B is set. `hookupOnLoadHandlers` puts B's fallback timer into `loadTimeout`.
3. A's `load` event fires within B's 200ms window. A's listener clears B's timer, then calls `onLoad` for A, which does nothing because A is no longer the pending frame.
4. B's own `load` event later finds `loadTimeout` empty and does nothing.

B is never activated, and nothing retries.

It needs A's load to finish after B has been written. So it shows up when content with slow-loading parts, such as large inline scripts or nested frames, is replaced in quick succession, and much more often on slow or software-rendered machines.

## Steps to reproduce

This drives the real `index.html` from an embedding page, the way a webview element does:

1. Load the host page from its `<parentOriginHash>` host, for example `<hash>.localhost`, with `disableServiceWorker`.
2. Send `content` A, whose body holds its own load until told otherwise:
   ```html
   <iframe id="hold"></iframe>
   <script>const held = document.getElementById('hold').contentDocument; held.open(); held.write('held');</script>
   ```
3. Wait until A is `active-frame`. The fallback does this after about 200ms.
4. Send `content` B, which holds its load the same way.
5. As soon as B appears in `pending-frame`, close A's held document (`held.close()`), which fires A's `load`.
6. Release B's hold, then post a message to the webview.

**Expected:** B becomes the active frame and receives the message.

**Actual:** B stays pending, A stays on screen, and the message never arrives.

In 5 runs of each, with `main`'s `index.html` served from its hash host in Chromium:

| Scenario | Stock `index.html` | With a per-frame timer |
|---|---|---|
| Race above | 0 of 5 recover | 5 of 5 recover |
| Control: A finishes loading before B is sent | 5 of 5 fine | 5 of 5 fine |

A fix that gives each frame its own timer follows as a PR.

issues.title: Managed enabledPlugins true does not force-enable an installed plugin

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

issues.body:
## Problem

When the enterprise `ChatEnabledPlugins` policy maps an installed `plugin@marketplace` identity to `true`, the plugin is still governed by the stored user or workspace enablement choice. A user can disable it, removing its contributed hooks, skills, tools, or other customizations even though organization policy requires it.

The inverse policy value already behaves differently: a plugin mapped to `false` is disabled and cannot be re-enabled.

## Expected behavior

For plugins that are already installed and discovered:

- Managed `true` force-enables the exact `plugin@marketplace` identity.
- Managed `false` force-disables it.
- Local profile and workspace enablement writes cannot override either managed value.
- The underlying user choice is preserved and becomes effective again if the managed entry is removed.
- Plugins omitted from policy remain user-controlled; the setting stays additive rather than becoming an allowlist.
- A force-enabled plugin cannot be disabled or uninstalled through the plugin management UI.

## Verification

Configure three installed fixture plugins:

```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "required-demo@example-marketplace": true,
    "blocked-demo@example-marketplace": false
  }
}
```

Leave a third plugin omitted from policy, and pre-seed `required-demo` as locally disabled.

Verify that:

1. `required-demo` is enabled and its switch is locked.
2. `blocked-demo` is disabled and its switch is locked.
3. The omitted plugin remains user-toggleable.
4. The required plugin has no uninstall action.
5. Removing the policy entries restores the stored local choices.
6. A same-named plugin from another marketplace does not inherit the managed decision.

Fixed by #337209.

## Scope

This issue covers enablement and management controls for plugins that are already installed and discovered. Installation or restoration of a missing required plugin is tracked separately in #337221. Failure behavior when a required plugin cannot be acquired is also outside this issue.

issues.body:
Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337199
PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337586

- [x] macOS @lramos15
- [x] Linux @hawkticehurst

Complexity: 4

Authors: @anthonykim1

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338068%0A%0A&assignees=anthonykim1)

---

## Context
Private GitHub plugin marketplaces now load using your VS Code GitHub sign-in when normal Git can't authenticate.

## Setup
1. Make a **private** copy of `microsoft/vscode-team-kit` at https://github.com/new/import, named `team-kit-private-tpi`.
2. Create `managed-settings.json` in `/Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/` (macOS) or `/etc/github-copilot/` (Linux) using `sudo`, or in `%ProgramFiles%\GitHubCopilot\` (Windows) from an Administrator terminal ([learn more](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/administer-copilot/manage-for-enterprise/use-managed-settings/deploy-managed-settings#deploying-file-based-settings)):
   ```json
   { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "team-kit-private-tpi": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "<you>/team-kit-private-tpi" } } } }
   ```
3. From a regular terminal (not VS Code's), launch Insiders without your Git credentials:
   - macOS/Linux: `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 code-insiders --transient`
   - Windows (PowerShell): `$env:GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL='NUL'; $env:GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM='1'; $env:GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT='0'; code-insiders --transient`

## Test Steps
1. Without signing in, run **Chat: Open Customizations** and go to **Plugins** > **Available**
   - No `team-kit-private-tpi` plugins appear and no sign-in prompt is shown (a clone-failure notification is expected)
2. Sign in to GitHub with the account that owns the repository, then run **Chat: Refresh Plugin Marketplaces**
   - The private plugins, such as `handy-commands`, appear under **Available** and install normally

When done, delete `managed-settings.json`; it applies to your whole machine.

issues.title: agentHost: Windows E2E intermittently loses archive/read flags after host restart

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
## Observed behavior

The shared Agent Host E2E test **`archiving a never-restored session survives a host restart`** failed in two Windows / Electron attempts on the same commit of #337626, with different providers. The test changes archive/read flags without restoring the session, waits for the root summary notifications, restarts the host, and verifies that both flags persisted.

| Attempt | Provider | Expected after restart | Actual after restart |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [1](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36184550054/job/108234659436) | Claude | `{ restored: true, isArchived: true, isRead: true }` | `{ restored: true, isArchived: false, isRead: false }` |
| [2](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36184550054/job/108256666585) | Copilot | `{ restored: true, isArchived: true, isRead: true }` | `{ restored: true, isArchived: true, isRead: false }` |

Claude passed on attempt 2. Conformance and Codex passed in both attempts. These failures did not involve a replay cache miss or model-response mismatch.

## Reproduction and investigation

- Tested commit: `875390b33d99bf12da168afbd999b23987c49a02`.
- Shared scenario: [sessionPersistenceSuite.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/875390b33d99bf12da168afbd999b23987c49a02/src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/suites/sessionPersistenceSuite.ts#L258).
- The exact Claude scenario passed six local runs on macOS. Fourteen related passive-metadata/shutdown unit tests also passed.
- The SDK PR does not change the shared persistence implementation or this test. The cross-provider failure suggests a shared persistence, shutdown, or listing issue rather than a Claude-only regression, but the root cause is **not established**. No upstream-only reproduction has been obtained.
- Local metadata persistence precedes the root notification; central catalog synchronization follows asynchronously. Existing unit coverage verifies that shutdown drains published passive metadata writes. Any fix should preserve the existing responsiveness and durability contracts.
- The failed Windows job logs did not include an Agent Host failure log tail, and no Windows Electron log artifact was available. Better Windows diagnostics may be needed to distinguish lost writes from stale listing state or interrupted shutdown.

Keeping this investigation separate from the Claude SDK upgrade. No assertions have been weakened, timeouts raised, or tests skipped to unblock that PR.

issues.title: Test: Agent Host Copilot full output for large shell results
issues.body:
Refs: #328596, #335016, #337510

- [x] macOS @meganrogge 
- [x] linux @chrmarti
- [x] windows @amunger

Complexity: 3

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338053%0A%0A&assignees=anthonykim1)

---

Verify that when an Agent Host Copilot shell command produces more output than the chat terminal card can show, the card keeps a truncated preview and lets you open the complete output in a read-only editor, both live and after the Agent Host restarts or the window reloads.

## Setup

1. Use the latest VS Code Insiders.
2. Sign in to GitHub Copilot.
3. Keep `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` set to `false` (the default) so the session uses the Copilot SDK built-in shell tool.
4. Start a local Agent Host Copilot session.

Whenever a step needs large output, ask Copilot to run this as a normal (not background) shell command:

```text
node -e "process.stdout.write('FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN\n' + 'x'.repeat(131072) + '\nFULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE\n' + 'y'.repeat(131072) + '\nFULL_OUTPUT_END\n')"
```

**This command is only an easy way to trigger truncation. Please don't limit testing to it.** Also try other commands that produce large output in your usual shell, such as builds, test runs, `npm install`, `git log`, printing a large file, or a recursive directory listing, and repeat the checks below with them. We want feedback on the overall experience of working with large terminal output in chat, not only this command.

## Open the full output

1. Ask Copilot to run the large-output command.
2. When it completes, confirm the terminal card shows a truncated preview and the message "Output truncated. Click the output preview to view the full output."
3. Click inside the inline terminal preview box.
   - A read-only editor opens with the complete output, including `FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN`, `FULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE`, and `FULL_OUTPUT_END`.
4. Close the editor, then use the **Open Full Output (Read-Only)** button in the command header.
   - The same output opens.

## Restart and reload

1. Run **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host**, then open the card's full output again.
   - The complete output still opens.
2. Run **Developer: Reload Window**, return to the same session, and open the full output again.
   - The complete output still opens, and no terminal appears in the Terminal panel.

## Output that should not change

1. Ask Copilot to run a command with short output, such as `seq 1 20`.
   - The card shows the complete output with no truncation message and no **Open Full Output (Read-Only)** button.
2. Ask Copilot to run the large-output command followed by a failing exit.
   - The card reports the failure. If the preview is truncated, the full output still opens.
3. Ask Copilot to run a background or long-running command.
   - It keeps its existing running and completed behavior.

## Exploratory

Use Copilot naturally with commands that produce large output, such as builds, test runs, `npm install`, or recursive file listings, and watch for:

- a truncated card with no way to open the full output;
- full output missing its beginning, middle, or end, or containing another command's output;
- full output that disappears after restarting the Agent Host, reloading, or resuming the session;
- a completed command creating a terminal in the Terminal panel.

Claude and Codex sessions are out of scope until #337389 and #337390 are available in Insiders.

issues.body:
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328596
Follow-up from: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329724

Copilot shell tools now retain complete spilled output in the owning chat's session database and open it from the terminal card with **Open Full Output (Read-Only)**, both live and after the Agent Host restarts or the window reloads (#335016).

Codex command executions are not covered yet. Large Codex command output has no retained copy that the terminal card can open, live or after restore.

Acceptance criteria:

- Keep command output up to the existing 80,000-character inline limit unchanged.
- Store larger output in the owning chat's session database, within the existing 10 MiB limit, and show a preview with **Open Full Output (Read-Only)** live and after restore, without keeping a terminal alive.
- Use a stable tool-call id across live events and history replay so retained output reattaches to the correct card.
- Remove retained output when `thread/revert` or `thread/rollback` removes its turn, and when the session is deleted.
- Leave output over 10 MiB, subagent commands, and output that was not retained unchanged.

## Set Welcome Name action

2. Navigate to the heading with the keyboard and verify the edit action appears on focus, is focusable, and has an accessible label.

   - The Command Palette

1. Test with `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` both enabled and disabled. Verify welcome phrases work in both layouts.
2. Disable `sessions.chat.experimental.welcomePhrases` and verify the heading and heading-specific edit action are removed while the selected composer layout remains unchanged.
