issues.title: Copilot telemetry messages are truncated or lack structured content classification
issues.body:
## Summary

VS Code Copilot telemetry has two message-integrity issues that make downstream analysis unreliable:

1. Some message payloads are truncated or incomplete.
2. Some assistant messages do not include structured classification identifying whether their content is a summary, answer, context, thinking, or another content type. Some summary-like payloads are also malformed JSON.

## Affected events and fields

| Event | Field |
|---|---|
| `copilot-chat/engine.messages` | `messages_json` |
| `agent/engine.messages` | `messages_json` |
| `copilot-chat/conversation.messageText` | `message_text` |
| `copilot-chat/inlineConversation.messageText` | `message_text` |

## Issue 1: Truncated message content

Some values in the affected fields contain only part of the original message.

**Expected behavior:** Preserve the complete message content in telemetry. Add chunking support where a payload cannot be represented safely in one event.

## Issue 2: Missing or malformed content classification

Some messages provide no structured metadata indicating the purpose or visibility of their content. For example:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "Reasoning summary:"
}
```

Other message formats provide explicit classifications such as:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "thinking",
      "thinking": "[omitted]",
      "signature": "[omitted]"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "redacted_thinking",
      "data": "[omitted]"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "[omitted]",
  "reasoning_text": "[omitted]",
  "reasoning_opaque": "[omitted]"
}
```

Some summary-key content is malformed and cannot be parsed. For example, the JSON represented inside `content` is missing its closing brace:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "{summary: Example summary text"
}
```

**Expected behavior:** Emit structured metadata that consistently identifies content purpose and visibility, and ensure any structured content is valid and parseable JSON.

## Impact

Truncation prevents complete reconstruction of conversations. Missing classifications make it difficult to distinguish user-visible answers from summaries, context, reasoning, or redacted content. Malformed structured content causes downstream parsing failures.

## Environment

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Multiple/unknown
- VS Code Version: Multiple/unknown
- OS Version: Multiple/unknown
- Feature: Copilot Chat and agent telemetry
- Selected model: Multiple/unknown

issues.title: Test: Try This experiences in release notes and documentation
issues.body:
Refs: #337794, #337713, #337803

- [x] windows @dbaeumer
- [x] macOS @aiday-mar
- [x] linux @rzhao271

Complexity: 3

Authors: @ntrogh


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23338021%0A%0A&assignees=ntrogh)

---

## Context

Feature tryouts connect release-note links to trusted interactions registered by the installed product. The fetched Markdown supplies only a stable tryout ID; VS Code owns the title, description, behavior, sample data, availability checks, and setup actions.

This test uses two built-in examples:

- **Smart Diff Layout** opens an isolated, read-only comparison.
- **Model and Provider Selection** opens a new unsent composer in the Agents window and guides the model picker.

The feature must fail closed for unknown or malformed IDs and must preserve normal confirmation, Chat setup, accessibility, and product safety behavior.

## Setup

1. Use the latest VS Code Insiders.
2. Create a temporary Markdown file with the following contents:

	```markdown
	# Try This test

	## Smart diff layout

	This example opens an isolated comparison.

	[Try Smart Diff Layout](command:workbench.action.onboarding.tryFeature?%5B%22editor.smart-diff%22%5D)

	## Models and providers

	This example opens a new, unsent composer in the Agents window.

	[Explore Models and Providers](command:workbench.action.onboarding.tryFeature?%5B%22chat.model-provider-selection%22%5D)

	## Invalid examples

	[Unknown example](command:workbench.action.onboarding.tryFeature?%5B%22test.unknown%22%5D)

	[Malformed example](command:workbench.action.onboarding.tryFeature?%5B%22editor.smart-diff%22%2C%22unexpected%22%5D)

	## Existing release-note command

	[Open the Word Wrap setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22%40id%3Aeditor.wordWrap%22%5D)
	```

3. With the Markdown editor active, run **Developer: Open Current File as Release Notes**.
4. For the Agents-window test, make sure Chat is enabled and a model/provider is available. Do not change your current model or provider while testing.

## Release-note rendering and trust boundary

1. Inspect the rendered release notes.
2. Verify that:
	- The two registered examples are rendered as **Try This** links using titles and descriptions supplied by the installed product.
	- Merely rendering, hovering, or focusing a link does not run the example.
	- **Unknown example** is replaced with explanatory text saying that the example is unavailable in this version of VS Code; it is not an active link.
	- **Malformed example** is replaced with explanatory text saying that the link is invalid; it is not an active link.
	- The surrounding headings and ordinary release-note content still render normally.
3. Activate **Open the Word Wrap setting**.
4. Verify that the existing command link still opens the expected setting.

## Isolated Smart Diff example

1. Return to the test release notes and activate **Try This: Try Smart Diff Layout**.
2. Verify that an editor named **Smart Diff Layout Example** opens with bundled TypeScript sample text.
3. Verify that:
	- The example does not read or modify workspace files.
	- The sample cannot be edited and does not become dirty.
	- **Diff View** can switch between Inline, Side by Side, and Automatic.
	- Resizing the editor while using Automatic updates the layout as expected.
4. Close the sample editor.
5. Verify that no file is saved or left dirty.

## Guided model-picker example

1. Before running the example, put recognizable unsent text in an existing Chat or Agents draft.
2. Return to the test release notes and activate **Try This: Try Model and Provider Selection**.
3. Verify that:
	- The Agents window opens.
	- A new unsent composer is prepared.
	- The model picker for that composer is highlighted and opened.
	- The guidance describes differences in model capability, speed, provider, and billing or premium-request usage.
	- No prompt is submitted.
	- No model or provider is automatically selected.
	- The pre-existing draft is not overwritten or sent.
4. If another model picker is visible, verify that the spotlight remains attached to the newly prepared composer rather than an unrelated picker.
5. Press `Escape` to dismiss the guidance and close the picker without selecting a model.
6. Verify that dismissal does not cause any delayed selection, submission, or reopening.

## Chat availability and AI gating

1. If Chat or a model provider is not set up in the current profile, verify that the release notes explain the missing prerequisite and offer an explicit setup action instead of silently changing configuration.
2. If a setup action is offered, activate it and verify that it only opens the normal setup experience; it does not automatically rerun the example.
3. Set `chat.disableAIFeatures` to `true` and return to or reopen the test release notes.
4. Verify that the model/provider example and its label are hidden, while the Smart Diff example and ordinary release-note content remain available.
5. Restore `chat.disableAIFeatures` to its original value.

## External link confirmation

1. From a browser or terminal, open:

	```text
	vscode-insiders://tryout/editor.smart-diff
	```

2. Accept the browser or operating-system handoff, if prompted.
3. Verify that VS Code shows its own confirmation containing the installed example title and description.
4. Cancel the VS Code confirmation and verify that no sample editor opens.
5. Open the same URL again and choose **Open Example**.
6. Verify that the Smart Diff sample opens.
7. Open:

	```text
	vscode-insiders://tryout/test.unknown
	```

8. Verify that VS Code reports that the feature example is unavailable and does not execute anything.
9. Open a malformed URL containing additional data:

	```text
	vscode-insiders://tryout/editor.smart-diff?command=workbench.action.files.delete
	```

10. Verify that no feature example or supplied command runs.

## Optional: Create and invoke a tryout

1. Open the VS Code repository in a development instance.
2. Start an agent session and prompt it to add a temporary tryout experience one of your features and add the tryout link to your markdown test file.

3. Review the agent's proposed and completed changes. Verify that:
	- The agent follows `.github/skills/feature-tryouts/SKILL.md` and the onboarding contributor guide.
	- The tryout is registered by installed product code from its owning contribution.
	- The Markdown contains only the stable `tpi.custom-sample` ID and no command arguments, paths, sample contents, or other executable payload.
	- The sample is deterministic and read-only.
4. Build and launch the development instance as directed by the agent.
5. Open the temporary Markdown test file and run **Developer: Open Current File as Release Notes**.
6. Activate the rendered **Try This** link.
7. Verify that the locally registered sample opens and that no workspace or user file is changed.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Enable GitHub Copilot Autopilot.

The behavior has been observed in both Plan mode and Agent mode when Autopilot is enabled.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
## Verification

Verify the security hardening in #338011 for the `create_and_run_task` agent tool.

### Scenarios

1. Invoke the tool with a label matching an existing or active task.
   - No confirmation bypass occurs.
   - `.vscode/tasks.json` is not modified.
   - No task is executed.
2. Invoke the tool with a workspace folder outside the session working directory or open workspace.
   - The invocation is rejected before file access or task execution.
3. Invoke the tool in Auto-Approve or Autopilot, including with caller pre-approval.
   - Explicit user confirmation is still required before creating and running the task.
4. Verify a valid local and remote workspace invocation.
   - The confirmation identifies the target workspace and exact command.
   - Remote scheme and authority are preserved.
   - Only the newly created task in the approved workspace is executed.
5. Use task labels and commands containing Markdown syntax.
   - Confirmation content is rendered as inert text/code and cannot create command links.

### Expected

All scenarios behave as described, with no write or execution occurring on rejected invocations.

issues.title: Feature request: Expose per-response Copilot credit/token usage programmatically (no login/screenshot)
issues.body:
## Summary
VS Code Copilot Chat already shows a per-response "Response details" tooltip with the model, input/cached-input/output token counts, and a computed "credits" cost for that single turn (e.g. "Claude Sonnet 5 • 103.3 credits"). This is the same "credits" unit used on the GitHub Copilot /AI usage dashboard (Included Credits / Additional Usage).

## Problem
There is currently no supported way to read this per-response credit/token data programmatically (via an extension API, a local log/state file, or a CLI); it is only visible as a transient UI tooltip. Anyone who wants to track cumulative spend per project/session locally (without repeatedly logging into the web dashboard and taking screenshots) currently has no way to do so.

## Request
Please expose per-response token/credit usage data in a machine-readable, locally accessible way, for example:
- A Chat extension API event/callback that fires after each response with {model, inputTokens, cachedInputTokens, outputTokens, credits}, and/or
- A local append-only log file (similar to existing chat session logs) recording the same fields per turn, and/or
- A lightweight local command/API to query cumulative usage for the current window/session without requiring a browser login to the GitHub usage dashboard.

This would let users and tooling correlate per-task cost with the cumulative GitHub AI usage totals without manual screenshot tracking.

## Context
Observed in VS Code, Copilot Chat, response details tooltip showing "Claude Sonnet 5 • 103.3 credits" with Input/Cached input/Output token breakdown.

issues.title: Agents window: Changes editor loads every diff while the editor area is hidden

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
In the single-pane layout, the Changes tab is opened as a docked tab whenever the editor area is hidden (`ensureAllInputs` in `singlePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.ts`). With an empty group it becomes the active editor, so `SessionChangesEditor.setInput` runs and calls `input.getViewModel()`.

That resolves a text model for every file in the changeset (original and modified), even though nothing is shown. On every session switch the outgoing input is disposed and the incoming one fully resolved again.

With a large changeset (for example a stale base branch, #337420) this means thousands of text models created and disposed for a view the user never opened. A renderer trace of a session switch shows `_reconcileForeignChangesEditors` → `replaceEditors`, then `SessionChangesEditor.setInput` → `getViewModel` → `createModelReference` for every file, all while the editor part is hidden.

The Changes editor should not resolve its multi-diff until the editor area is actually visible. The tab, its active state and the detail-panel mapping only need the input to exist.

Related: #337420, #332670, #337989.

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

The Agents window new-session composer can feel impersonal and static. Add an optional welcome heading that rotates across a small set of concise prompts when a new composer is constructed.

Proposed behavior:

- Gate the feature behind the independent, default-off experimental setting `sessions.chat.experimental.welcomePhrases`.

- Show a Set Welcome Name edit action only when the heading is hovered or receives keyboard focus, and expose the same action in its context menu and the Command Palette.
- Keep the welcome-phrases experiment independent from `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout`.

issues.title: Renderer freezes during bulk text model cleanup

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

issues.body:
Switching sessions can freeze the renderer while many text models are being disposed.

Each removal repeatedly scans all remaining models in edit tracking, extension document state, and the editor worker.

- A renderer trace shows a 6.89-second stall.
- A local reproduction with 6,000 models takes 6.84 seconds and performs 18,000 full-model scans.

Bulk cleanup should not rescan every model for each removal or freeze the UI for several seconds.

Related to #337420. This issue covers model cleanup, not base-branch selection or binary-file loading.

issues.title: Agents window: Stop and Mark as Done don't work while a new session is still being created
issues.body:
When you send the first message of a new session in the Agents window, the session isn't ready right away. The agent host first has to set it up, which takes a few seconds with worktree isolation because it creates a git worktree. If you click **Stop** or **Mark as Done** during those seconds, it doesn't work.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In the Agents window, start a new Agent Host session with worktree isolation.
2. Send the first message.
3. Right away, while the session still shows "Working…", either:
   - click **Stop**, or
   - mark the session as **Done**.

### What happens

- **Stop:** the session stays at "Working…" forever, until you reload the window.
- **Mark as Done:** nothing happens. The session isn't moved to Done.

### What should happen

- **Stop:** the message is stopped and the session shows up as a normal, idle session.
- **Mark as Done:** the session moves to Done and stays there.

### Why it happens

Until the agent receives the first message, the window only has a draft of the session. The agent host tells the window about the real session only after the agent has received that message.

- **Stop:** the host drops the message before the agent receives it, so the host never tells the window about the session. The window keeps waiting for a session that never arrives.
- **Mark as Done:** the window tries to mark the real session as done, but it doesn't exist yet, so the request is quietly ignored.

issues.title: Agents window: picker changes made right after sending the first message are lost
issues.body:
In the Agents window, if you change a picker right after sending the first message of a new session, the change is lost once the session has finished starting.

This affects the permission level, mode and sandbox pickers, and the model and agent pickers.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In the Agents window, start a new session that uses a worktree, so start-up takes a few seconds.
2. Send the first message.
3. While the session is still starting, change a picker. For example, change the permission level, or pick a different model or agent.
4. Wait until the session has started, then switch to another session and back.

## Expected

The session keeps what you picked, and the agent uses it.

## Actual

The picker goes back to the value from before you sent the message, and the agent really uses that old value:

- **Permission level, mode, sandbox:** the new value is never sent to the agent host. The picker shows it for a moment, then jumps back to the old value.
- **Model and agent:** the session and your follow-up messages use the model or agent from before the first message.

## Why it happens

When you send the first message, your current picks are sent along with it. While the session is still starting, new picks only update a local draft. When the session is ready, the app restores the picks from before the message instead of your latest ones, and never tells the agent host about the changed settings.

issues.title: [Agents Window] MCP/tool management, authentication, and language-model response are inconsistent with Chat
issues.body:
<!--
This report is intentionally focused on behavior in the VS Code Agents experience.
The same MCP/model configuration works correctly in another agent/client and/or normal Chat.
-->Environment

- VS Code Version: Latest Stable release, fully updated
- OS Version: Windows 11
- Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes
- Third-party extension causing this issue: No
- Feature: Agents Window / Agent Host
- Model: The same model/configuration works correctly in another agent/client
- MCP: Multiple MCP servers, including authenticated MCP servers

Summary

I am experiencing several serious inconsistencies between the normal Chat experience and the Agents / Agent Host experience in VS Code.

The same general model/provider configuration and MCP setup work correctly in another agent/client and the normal Chat experience, but the VS Code Agents experience behaves differently.

This appears to involve three closely related areas:

1. Tool/MCP management in Agents is missing or not equivalent to Chat.
2. MCP authentication in Agents is unreliable/non-functional.
3. The Agents language-model request path can fail with "Response contained no choices" even when another agent using the same model/configuration works correctly.

These issues are especially problematic because MCP servers cannot always be disabled or excluded from an Agent request when one of them is unavailable, broken, rate-limited, or requires authentication.

---

Issue 1 — Agent tool/MCP management is not equivalent to Chat

The normal Chat experience provides a very useful tool-management UI where I can inspect available tools and selectively enable or disable them.

This is extremely important when an MCP server is broken, unavailable, slow, requires authentication, or exposes many tools.

According to the current VS Code documentation, Copilot Agent also supports tool management through the Tools tab, including enabling/disabling individual tools and entire tool groups.

However, in my Agents environment, I do not have the same reliably usable tool-management experience that I have in Chat.

Actual behavior

For example:

1. I have multiple MCP servers configured.
2. One MCP server may be unavailable, broken, or otherwise unusable.
3. In Chat, I can open the tools picker and disable the affected MCP server/tools.
4. The Chat request can then continue without those tools.
5. In Agents, I cannot reliably perform the equivalent operation.
6. The Agent may continue attempting to work with the configured MCP/tool environment even when I need to temporarily exclude a problematic MCP server.

This becomes especially problematic with large MCP configurations.

Expected behavior

The Agent experience should provide a reliable and fully functional equivalent of the Chat tool picker / Configure Tools functionality.

I should be able to:

- See all tools available to the Agent.
- See which MCP server each tool belongs to.
- Enable/disable individual tools.
- Enable/disable an entire MCP server or tool group.
- Temporarily exclude a broken MCP server without deleting or modifying its configuration.
- Have that selection actually affect the current Agent request/session.

For example:

MCP Server A
  ✓ tool_a
  ✓ tool_b
  ✗ tool_c

MCP Server B
  ✗ all tools disabled

MCP Server C
  ✓ all tools enabled

Disabling a server or tool should actually prevent it from being included in the Agent request.

This is particularly important because the current VS Code documentation explicitly describes tool management for agents.

---

Issue 2 — MCP authentication is inconsistent or non-functional in Agents

The MCP experience also appears to behave differently between Chat and Agents.

For some authenticated MCP servers:

1. The MCP server is detected by VS Code.
2. The Agent reports that authentication is required.
3. An Authenticate action/button is displayed.
4. Clicking Authenticate does nothing or does not start the expected authentication flow.
5. There is no useful error indicating why authentication failed.
6. The MCP server therefore cannot become usable from the Agent.

In other cases, MCP authentication/state appears inconsistent between Agent sessions and Chat.

Expected behavior

When VS Code displays:

The MCP server <server> requires authentication.
Authenticate?

clicking Authenticate should invoke the supported MCP authentication flow and allow the server to transition to a usable/ready state.

Authentication state should also be handled consistently between the relevant Chat and Agent/MCP components.

Why this is especially important

MCP authentication problems are already an active area of bugs in the Agents Window.

For example, VS Code has existing reports involving repeated MCP authentication prompts and Agent Host authentication state persistence, including issues #327137 and #329223.

These reports show that MCP authentication/state handling in the Agents environment has already had real regressions/bugs.

---

Issue 3 — Agent language-model response can fail with "Response contained no choices"

I also experience the following error inside the Agents experience:

Sorry, your request failed.

Client Request Id: 0ced01c0-9068-4358-b563-bfea01033bd1

Reason: Response contained no choices.: Error: Response contained no choices.
    at xH._provideLanguageModelResponse
    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
    at xH.provideLanguageModelResponse

The relevant stack trace points into the built-in Copilot extension:

resources\app\extensions\copilot\dist\extension.js

This is particularly suspicious because:

- The same model/configuration works in another agent/client.
- The model is not inherently unusable.
- No third-party extension is responsible for the issue.
- The VS Code installation is fully updated.
- The failure occurs specifically through the VS Code Agent language-model path.

I am not assuming that this has the same root cause as the MCP problems, but it may indicate another inconsistency in the Agent execution path.

Expected behavior

A successful model response should be handled correctly by the Agent runtime without producing:

Response contained no choices

when the same model/provider configuration is otherwise functioning correctly in another client.

If the upstream provider response is invalid, VS Code should expose the actual provider/protocol error rather than only returning the generic "Response contained no choices" message.

---

Why I believe this is not a third-party extension problem

I have reproduced the problem with extensions disabled as requested by the official issue template.

The behavior also persists despite using the latest Stable VS Code release.

The same model/provider configuration works correctly in another agent/client, which makes a VS Code Agent/Agent Host integration issue a strong possibility.

I am therefore not reporting this as an issue caused by an external extension.

---

Steps to reproduce

A. Tool/MCP management

1. Configure multiple MCP servers in VS Code.
2. Open normal Chat.
3. Open the tool picker / Configure Tools UI.
4. Observe that tools/MCP tools can be inspected and selectively enabled/disabled.
5. Open the Agents / Agent Host experience.
6. Attempt to perform the equivalent tool-management operation.
7. Observe that the same level of control is unavailable, inconsistent, or not correctly applied to Agent requests.

B. MCP authentication

1. Configure an MCP server that requires authentication.
2. Open an Agent session.
3. Trigger the MCP server.
4. Wait until VS Code reports that authentication is required.
5. Click Authenticate.
6. Observe that the expected authentication flow does not start or does not complete.
7. Compare the same MCP server's behavior in Chat.

C. Language-model response

1. Configure the same model/provider configuration that works correctly in another agent/client.
2. Open a VS Code Agent session.
3. Send a normal request.
4. Observe:

Response contained no choices

5. Retry using the other agent/client with the same model configuration.
6. Observe that the other agent successfully receives and processes the model response.

---

Expected overall behavior

Chat and Agents should provide a consistent underlying MCP/tool experience for the same VS Code installation.

At minimum:

MCP configuration
        ↓
MCP server state
        ↓
Available tools
        ↓
Tool enable/disable
        ↓
Authentication state
        ↓
Agent / Chat request

A disabled tool or MCP server should actually be excluded from the Agent request.

An MCP server requiring authentication should have a functional Authenticate action.

Authentication state should be handled consistently across Agent sessions and relevant Chat/MCP components.

The Agent language-model path should correctly process valid provider responses and expose meaningful protocol errors when a provider returns an invalid response.

---

Related documentation

VS Code documentation on tools with agents:

https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/tools

VS Code documentation on tools in AI agents:

https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/concepts/tools

---

Related existing issues

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327137
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329223
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327824

These appear related to MCP authentication/state handling in the Agents/Agent Host experience.

---

Additional information

This report is intentionally focused on behavior that is reproducible in the current fully updated Stable VS Code installation and is not caused by a third-party extension.

The main concern is the significant difference between what is available and functional in Chat versus Agents, especially for MCP/tool management and authentication.

issues.title: Build/Package fails at prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim due to .moduleignore stripping @github/copilot/sdk

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?:
 N/A (This is a local build/packaging failure from source, occurring before the application or extensions are loaded)

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version:  1.139.0 / 1.139.1 (Building from source, `main` branch)
- OS Version: Linux x64

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Clone the `microsoft/vscode` repository and checkout release `1.139.0` (or `1.139.1` / `main`).
2. Run `npm install` strictly following the "How to Contribute" guide.
3. Run a packaging gulp task, for example: `npm run gulp vscode-linux-x64`.
4. The build fails during the `prepareCopilotRipgrepShimTask` phase.

Expected Behavior:
The build should successfully package the VS Code binaries without missing dependencies.

Actual Behavior:
The build fails with the following error:
```text
Error: [prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim] Copilot SDK directory not found at <path>/resources/app/extensions/copilot/node_modules/@github/copilot/sdk
    at prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim (file:///<path>/build/lib/copilot.ts:273:9)
```

Root Cause Analysis:
There is a conflict between the `.moduleignore` configuration and the Copilot packaging script introduced in the 1.139.x releases.

1. `build/.moduleignore` contains the rule `@github/copilot/**` which strips the `@github/copilot` directory from the local `extensions/copilot` build.
2. However, `build/lib/copilot.ts` (specifically `prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim`) explicitly expects this directory to exist in order to copy target-platform `ripgrep` binaries into it:
```typescript
const copilotSdkBase = path.join(copilotBase, 'sdk');
if (!fs.existsSync(copilotSdkBase)) {
    throw new Error(`[prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim] Copilot SDK directory not found at ${copilotSdkBase}`);
}
```

Workaround:
Adding exceptions for the `package.json` and the `sdk` directory in `build/.moduleignore` allows the local packaging step to succeed. 

```text
@github/copilot/**
!@github/copilot/package.json
!@github/copilot/sdk/**
```

issues.title: compareIgnoreCase sorts ASCII punctuation [\]^_` after letters, contradicting its own ordering contract
issues.body:
`compareSubstringIgnoreCase` (which backs `compareIgnoreCase`) normalizes case by mapping lowercase ASCII letters *up* to uppercase (`code -= 32`, `src/vs/base/common/strings.ts:404-409`). That moves `a-z` (97-122) down to `A-Z` (65-90), i.e. below the punctuation block 91-96 (`[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `_`, backtick).

But the function's own test oracle (`src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.ts:95`) defines the intended order as `compare(a.toLowerCase(), b.toLowerCase())`, which keeps letters at 97-122, above 91-96. So for any letter-vs-punctuation pair in that range, the sign of the result is inverted relative to the documented contract:

```
compareIgnoreCase("[", "a")  // +26, oracle says negative
compareIgnoreCase("_", "b")  // +29, oracle says negative
```

This is user-visible: `compareIgnoreCase` is used as a real sort comparator, e.g. language-name sorting in `src/vs/editor/common/services/languagesRegistry.ts:295` and repository-group label sorting in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentSessionsViewer.ts:1442`. Any label starting with `[`, `^`, `_`, or backtick sorts after plain alphabetic labels instead of before them:

```
sorted by compareIgnoreCase: ["apple", "banana", "Cherry", "[brackets]", "^caret", "_config", "`tick`"]
expected (lowercase order):  ["[brackets]", "^caret", "_config", "`tick`", "apple", "banana", "Cherry"]
```

The existing tests (48 passing) miss this because none of the `compareIgnoreCase` cases pair a letter with a character in the 91-96 range. Mapping uppercase to lowercase (`code += 32`) instead would match the oracle; equality results are unaffected either way.

Seen on main at `51c141f0` (2026-09-25).

issues.title: Agent sessions: built-in GitHub MCP server is locked to a read-only 19-tool subset and its toolset cannot be configured
issues.body:
### Summary

Agent sessions in VS Code get a built-in GitHub MCP server that exposes only 19 tools, all marked `readOnlyHint: true`. There is no supported way to request additional toolsets (e.g. `projects`, `labels`), so the project-board write tools (`projects_write`, `label_write`, `issue_write`, `create_pull_request`) are unreachable from an agent session even when the user has the required OAuth scopes.

The remote endpoint supports these toolsets. The problem is that the agent host never sends `X-MCP-Toolsets` and offers no setting to add it.

Even when installing the github mcp and editing it's settings to all tools, the agents view still overwrites this and only claims 19 tools available to the agent.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| VS Code version | 1.139.1 |
| Copilot Chat extension | 0.67.0 |
| OS | macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83), arm64 |
| MCP server | `github-mcp-server` (built-in, agent host) |
| GitHub account scopes | `repo`, `read:org`, `read:user`, `user:email`, `read:packages`, `write:packages`, `read:project`, `project`, `gist`, `notifications` |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure `chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.enabled` is `true` (the default, even setting this to false didn't work for me, it still clinged to only 19 tools by default completely ignoring the github MCP i had downloaded and set up myself.).
2. Start an agent session and inspect the available GitHub MCP tools.
3. Note the tool list is 19 entries, every one annotated `readOnlyHint: true`.
4. Attempt to find a setting that configures the built-in server's toolsets.

### Actual behaviour

The agent session receives exactly these 19 tools:

```
actions_get, actions_list, get_commit, get_copilot_space, get_file_contents,
get_job_logs, issue_read, list_branches, list_commits, list_copilot_spaces,
list_issues, list_pull_requests, pull_request_read, search_code, search_issues,
search_pull_requests, search_repositories, search_users, web_search
```

All have `readOnlyHint: true`. `projects_write`, `projects_get`, `projects_list`, `issue_write`, `label_write`, and `create_pull_request` are all absent.

The only related setting, `chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.enabled`, is a boolean that can only disable the server entirely. It cannot configure the toolset.

### Expected behaviour

The user should be able to select which toolsets the built-in GitHub MCP server exposes — for example via a setting, or by supplying a server definition that the agent host honours — so that accounts with the `project` scope can use project-board tools from agent sessions.

### Evidence

**1. The remote endpoint supports the extra toolsets.**

Calling `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` directly with a token that has the scopes above:

| Request | Tools returned | `projects_write` | `label_write` |
|---|---|---|---|
| No `X-MCP-Toolsets` header | 48 | ❌ | ❌ |
| `X-MCP-Toolsets: all` | 99 | ✅ | ✅ |

So the capability exists server-side; it is purely a client-side header issue.

**2. The built-in server's headers are hardcoded.**

In `out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js`:

```js
var sr = "github-mcp-server",
    Hle = "X-MCP-Features",
    Ule = "remote_mcp_ui_apps,mcp_apps_disable_form_deferral",
    Nle = "X-MCP-Tools",
    dz = ["get_file_contents", "search_code", "get_copilot_space", "list_copilot_spaces", "web_search", "search_users"],
    Fle = ["search_repositories", "list_branches", "list_commits", "get_commit", "issue_read", "list_issues", ...];

function Ble(r, n = false) {
  let e = dS(r);
  if (!e) throw new Error("Unable to resolve the GitHub MCP server URL");
  let t = { [Hle]: Ule, [Nle]: Wle(n).join(",") };
  return { type: "http", url: e, headers: t };
}
```

Only `X-MCP-Features` and `X-MCP-Tools` are sent. `X-MCP-Toolsets` does not appear anywhere in the VS Code application bundle. The tool allowlists are hardcoded arrays in the source, not read from configuration.

**3. Agent sessions do not consume the user-level `mcp.json`.**

MCP discovery for agent sessions reads only:

```js
function Ipe(r, n) {                 // r = workingDirectory, n = userHome
  let e = [];
  r && (e.push(v.joinPath(r, ".claude", "settings.json")),
        e.push(v.joinPath(r, ".mcp.json")));
  e.push(v.joinPath(n, ".claude", "settings.json"));
  return e;
}
```

`~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/mcp.json` is not in this list. A server defined there is visible to the workbench/chat surface (its tool cache shows the server with 99 tools) but never reaches an agent session. This produces a confusing split where the same server appears configured in one place and absent in another.

**4. Supplying a server with a matching URL does not restore the toolsets.**

Because dedupe compares normalized URLs:

```js
_isGitHubMcpServer(e, t) {
  let i = this._gitHubMcpServerConfiguration?.type === "http"
    ? da(this._gitHubMcpServerConfiguration.url) : void 0;
  return e === sr || (i !== undefined && t.url !== undefined && da(t.url) === i);
}
```

a user-supplied `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` (with `X-MCP-Toolsets: all`) collides with the built-in identity. The result in practice was not the 99-tool set but the 48-tool default, i.e. the header was not applied to the session's server.

### Impact

Any workflow that needs project-board mutations, labels, or issue/PR creation from an agent session cannot be completed. In this case an issue-to-PR automation had to fall back to the `gh` CLI, because `projects_write` and friends were unreachable — despite the token holding the `project` scope and the remote server supporting them.

### Suggested fix

Either:

- add a setting (e.g. `chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.toolsets`, mirroring the existing `github.copilot.chat.githubMcpServer.toolsets`) that is translated into an `X-MCP-Toolsets` header on the built-in server, or
- honour a user-supplied GitHub MCP server definition for agent sessions, including its `headers`, instead of collapsing it into the built-in identity.

It would also help to document that `User/mcp.json` is not read by agent sessions, since the current behaviour is hard to diagnose.

issues.title: Agents Window uses incorrect base branch for Branch Changes with existing Git worktree
issues.body:
Type: Bug When starting an agent session in the VS Code Agents window using an existing Git worktree, the **Branch Changes** view uses `main` as the base branch instead of the branch that the feature branch was created from / tracks. In my repository: - The repository's default branch on GitHub is `dev`. - I create Git worktrees outside of VS Code. - The feature branch is created from `dev`. - The feature branch's upstream is `origin/dev`. - I open the existing worktree/folder in VS Code and use it for an Agents window session. - The Agents window nevertheless displays the comparison as: ```text feat/agency-office-types → main ``` I expect it to display: ```text feat/agency-office-types → dev ``` This results in **Branch Changes showing an incorrect and much larger diff**, because it includes differences between `dev` and `main` that have nothing to do with the feature branch. ## Steps to Reproduce Given a repository whose default branch is `dev`: ```bash git fetch origin git worktree add \ -b feat/test \ ../test-worktree \ origin/dev cd ../test-worktree git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/dev feat/test ``` Then: 1. Open the existing `test-worktree` folder in VS Code. 2. Open the **Agents** window. 3. Start an agent session using the existing folder/worktree. Do not ask VS Code to create a new worktree. 4. Make the session active. 5. Open **Changes**. 6. Select **Branch Changes**. ## Actual Behavior The Agents window compares the feature branch against `main`: ```text feat/test → main ``` As a result, Branch Changes includes unrelated changes between `main` and `dev`. ## Expected Behavior The Agents window should compare against `dev`: ```text feat/test → dev ``` For an existing worktree/folder, VS Code should determine the appropriate base branch from the existing Git repository rather than silently falling back to `main`, or allow user to change the base for comparison in the Changes pane. issues.title: TPI: Continue a ChatGPT Codex chat in VS Code
issues.body:
Refs: #337659

- [x] windows @haileyvictory
- [x] macos @aiday-mar
- [x] linux @connor4312

Complexity: 3

Authors: @Giuspepe 

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23337969%0A%0A&assignees=Giuspepe)

---


# TPI: Continue a ChatGPT Codex chat in VS Code

## Context

Codex chats created or updated in ChatGPT should appear in the VS Code Agents window within a few seconds. You should not need to reload the window or restart anything.

If ChatGPT still has control of a chat, VS Code should keep it readable and explain why you cannot continue it yet. You should be able to retry after quitting ChatGPT.

**You need a ChatGPT account and the ChatGPT app to test this TPI.**

## Test steps

1. Open the Agents window in VS Code. Make sure Codex and external sessions are enabled.
2. Create a Codex chat in ChatGPT and exchange a few messages. Watch for the chat in the Agents window. It should appear within a few seconds without a reload or restart.
3. Open the chat in VS Code while ChatGPT still has it open. Check that the transcript is current and that VS Code shows a lock banner above the input before you try to send.
5. Try sending a message from VS Code and use Retry while ChatGPT is still running. VS Code should not start a turn or add duplicate messages.
6. Fully quit ChatGPT, then use Retry again. The banner should disappear, your draft should remain, and VS Code should not send it automatically.
7. Send the draft yourself and check that the chat continues normally in VS Code.
8. Try continuing the chat in ChatGPT again

Here's an example video

issues.title: macOS 27: "Path does not exist" when opening folders with Portuguese (pt-BR) accented names on SMB share via File > Open Folder
issues.body:
Type: Bug After updating to macOS 27.0, I can no longer open folders or files located in folders with accented names (Portuguese, pt-BR — e.g. "Usuários", "Diário") on an SMB network share using File > Open Folder. This worked fine before the macOS update. Environment: - macOS 27.0, Apple Silicon (M1 Pro) - VS Code 1.137.0 (arm64) - Folder is on an SMB share mounted under /Volumes Steps to reproduce: 1. Connect to an SMB share containing folders with accented names (e.g. /Volumes//Usuários///Diário). 2. In VS Code, use File > Open Folder and select the folder through the dialog. Expected: the folder opens. Actual: error dialog "Path does not exist — The path '/Volumes//Usuários///Diário' does not exist on this computer." Diagnosis: The server stores the folder names in Unicode decomposed form (NFD). Checking the bytes: $ ls /Volumes/ | grep -i usu | xxd 00000000: 5573 7561 cc81 7269 6f73 0a Usua..rios. "á" is stored as "a" + U+0301 combining accent (61 cc81) instead of the precomposed form (c3a1). The path returned by the Open Folder dialog seems to use the precomposed (NFC) form, which does not match the name on the server, so the path is not found. Evidence that VS Code itself can handle the folder: - Passing the exact on-disk (NFD) path via the CLI works: `code -n ""` opens the folder normally. - Opening via File > Open Recent (after the folder was opened once via CLI) also works. - Other apps (e.g. Microsoft Excel) open files from the same folder through their own open dialogs without problems. So the issue appears to be in how the path returned by the native Open Folder dialog is handled (possibly NFC normalization) before it is used to access the file system. Workaround: open folders via the CLI or a Finder Quick Action that passes the exact path. Renaming the folders is not an option, since they are on a shared server used by other people. issues.title: [Feature Request] Display token and cost consumption of external Gateways (e.g., Vercel AI Gateway)

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

milestone.title: Backlog Candidates
milestone.description: Work that is not yet accepted for the Backlog. We wait for the community to weigh in.

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
### Feature Description

Following the implementation of milestone **1.126.0** (Issue #317977), VS Code introduced excellent per-message token usage and cost metrics badges. However, this telemetry metric framework is currently tightly coupled to internal GitHub Copilot billing schemas. 

As the **VS Code Agents** environment scales to allow developers to bring their own model endpoints and provider-agnostic infrastructure, there is currently no way to bubble up per-session cost tracking from third-party AI gateways like **Vercel AI Gateway**. Alternative tools like OpenCode already process this by default by remaining completely provider-agnostic while still tracking session spend.

When routing model traffic through a custom gateway, providers inject metadata headers directly into the stream payload (for instance, Vercel’s `x-vercel-ai-gateway-spend` or standard token counters). VS Code currently strips or discards these custom header footprints from the UI layer.

### Proposed Solution

1. **Expose an Extensible Metadata Parser Hook:** Allow the core chat and agent UI components to intercept response headers from the active language model provider stream.
2. **Support Dynamic Cost Badge Mapping:** Introduce a configuration setting or API hook where users or extensions can map arbitrary header keys (like `x-vercel-ai-gateway-spend` or custom token parameters) directly into the native UI session badge footer.
3. **Preserve Session Mapping:** Ensure that `chatSessionResource` contexts pass downstream response parameters accurately so extensions can reliably track session budgets without requiring brittle, backward-scanning hacks.

### Alternative Solutions Considered

- Using third-party extensions, but these cannot cleanly hook into the newly implemented native agent/chat session footer badges because the core framework discards custom provider telemetry headers.
- Constantly running `vercel ai-gateway api-keys inspect` in a side terminal, which breaks the flow of development inside the agent workspace.

### Additional Context

Giving developers real-time feedback on their chosen agnostic gateway's spending directly inside the active editor pane ensures proper budget boundaries and model optimization during long multi-agent loops.

Ref: #317977

issues.body:
## Description

When a chat is created with a worktree, the `Worktree created` message is not shown at the top of the new chat. This made it look as though no worktree had been created and was confusing.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new chat with a worktree.
2. Open the newly created chat.
3. Observe the top of the chat.

## Expected

The `Worktree created` message is shown at the top, confirming that the worktree was created.

## Actual

No creation message is shown.

Related: #316157 covers general worktree visibility, while this issue specifically tracks the missing creation confirmation in the newly created chat.

issues.title: Copilot Chat agent mode: rename tool reports success but does not modify the file
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In agent/chat mode, when Copilot Chat invokes its built-in `rename` tool to perform a semantic symbol rename, the tool call returns a success message with a specific edit count (e.g. `Renamed <symbol> to <newName> - N edits across M files`), but the workspace files are **not actually modified**. There is no error, warning, or partial-failure indicator anywhere in the response.

This creates a silent divergence between what the agent believes happened and the actual state of the workspace, which is risky in an autonomous/agentic workflow: any commit, build, or further edit that follows may fail unexpectedly or produce misleading assumptions, since the model has no built-in signal that the rename did not apply.

### Exact tool call and response observed

Tool call (as exposed to the model in agent mode):
```
rename(filePath: "<file>", symbol: "<OldName>", lineContent: "<line containing the symbol>", newName: "<NewName>")
```

Response returned by the tool:
```
Renamed `<OldName>` to `<NewName>` - N edits across M files.
```

No `applied`/`ok`/error fields are present in the response — just this human-readable success string, with no indication of whether it reflects a verified or merely attempted change.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In an agent-mode Copilot Chat session, ask the agent to rename a symbol (class/method/etc.) that is referenced in several files.
2. The agent calls the built-in `rename` tool; the tool returns the success message above with a non-zero edit/file count.
3. Immediately after, inspect the workspace independently of the tool (open the files, run `git diff`, or `grep` for the new name across the repo).
4. Result: the old name is still present everywhere; the new name does not appear anywhere in the workspace. `git diff` shows no changes from this call.
5. Repeating the exact same `rename` call with identical parameters reproduces the same false-positive "success" result — no changes are applied on the second attempt either.

### Expected behavior

- If no edits were actually applied, the tool result should reflect that (e.g. an `applied: false` field, an error, or a clear "no changes made" status) rather than reporting a specific non-zero edit/file count.
- The reported edit/file counts should correspond to changes that are verifiably present in the workspace after the call returns.

### Actual behavior

The tool call returns a confident success message with specific counts ("N edits across M files"), but a subsequent inspection of the workspace shows zero actual changes. The failure is silent — no exception, warning, or degraded-result marker is surfaced to the model or the user.

### Environment

- VS Code: latest
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension: latest
- Mode: Agent/Chat mode, using the built-in semantic `rename` tool
- Model: various (reproduced at least with a Claude-based model, e.g. claude-sonnet-5)
- OS: Windows

### Additional context

This was reproduced across multiple sessions/models in the same workspace, including retrying the identical call, which still resulted in the same false-positive success message with no actual file changes. It would be valuable if the built-in rename tool's result schema always reflected verified, not merely attempted/intended, changes.

issues.title: `code tunnel prune` broken because of case mismatch
issues.body:
Not be confused with git prune.

I use vscode to connect to a remote Linux server using SSH. Over time, my remote folder `${HOME}/.vscode-server/cli/servers` slowly fills up. `code tunnel prune` claims to clean this, but a case mismatch means not.

Actual command I ran is:
```
~/.vscode-servers/code-<ID> --cli-data-dir "${HOME}/.vscode-server/cli" tunnel prune
```

In my `vscode-server` folder, the servers are named `Stable-<ID>`:
```
$ ls ~/.vscode-server/cli/servers
lru.json
Stable-2242ebbb54efeeb0129e08e919e7e8d43033cd83
...
```

But when `tunnel prune` enumerates this folder, it is looking for lower case `stable-<ID>`. Here is Codex assessment:

```
For:

Stable-2242ebbb...

the split produces:

quality = "Stable"
commit  = "2242ebbb..."

But Quality::try_from() accepts only:

stable
insiders
insider
exploration
```

- VS Code Version: 1.139.0
- OS Version:
  - Remote: Ubuntu Jammy LTS

issues.body: ### Problem When working on Flutter projects with multiple flavors (dev / staging / production), I constantly switch between three controls that live in three different places: 1. **Run button** – in the Run and Debug view 2. **Launch configuration picker** – in the Run and Debug view header (only visible when that view is open) 3. **Target device selector** – in the status bar (contributed by the Dart/Flutter extension) To start the app with the right flavor on the right device, I have to open the Run and Debug view, pick a configuration, then look at the bottom-right corner to check or change the device. In JetBrains IDEs (Android Studio), all of these sit together in the top toolbar next to the search box, so the whole "what am I running, and where" state is visible and controllable in one place. `debug.toolBarLocation: "commandCenter"` moves the debug toolbar to the top, but only **during** an active session. It doesn't help with choosing the configuration or device **before** launching. ### Proposal 1. Add an option to show the **Run button + launch configuration picker** in the title bar next to the Command Center, visible at all times (not only during a debug session). For example: `debug.configurationPickerLocation: "commandCenter" | "debugView"`. 2. Provide an **extension contribution point** for the title bar / Command Center area, so extensions can place compact status items there (e.g. the Dart extension's device selector, or similar target pickers in other ecosystems like React Native, .NET MAUI, or embedded tooling). Both should be opt-in so the default layout stays unchanged. ### Screenshots - Current Run and Debug picker: - Current device selector in status bar: - Command Center area where these could live: ### Why this matters This isn't Flutter-specific. Any workflow with "configuration × target" (flavors, build variants, emulators, remote hosts) benefits from having that state visible at the top of the window instead of split between a sidebar view and the status bar.

issues.title: Terminal: Environment variable corruption and display overwrite when PATH contains carriage return

labels.name: terminal
labels.description: General terminal issues that don't fall under another label

issues.body:
### VS Code Version
1.139.0

### Operating System
Windows 10 / 11 (x64)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. In Windows PowerShell, append a carriage return (`\r`) to the user or process `PATH`:
   ```powershell
   $env:Path += "`r"
   ```
2. Open VS Code and open an integrated PowerShell terminal.
3. When an extension (such as Python's `ms-python.debugpy` or Copilot) mutates `PATH` via `EnvironmentVariableMutatorType.Append`, it directly appends its directory path using `(env[actualVariable] || '') + value`.
4. Run `$env:Path` in the integrated terminal.

### Expected Behavior
Environment variables should concatenate cleanly without display glitches or broken path resolution.

### Actual Behavior
- Because `\r` is embedded right before the extension's appended path, printing `$env:Path` hits the carriage return and moves the terminal cursor back to the line start, overwriting earlier characters with the appended path. Visually, the PATH looks like it got truncated right before the end.
- The path entry containing the trailing `\r` becomes invalid on Windows, causing commands in that directory to fail to resolve.
- *Note*: Splitting by semicolon (`$env:Path -split ';'`) outputs each entry on a separate line, which prevents the carriage return overwrite and makes all paths visible, making this issue particularly confusing to diagnose.

### Proposed Solution / PR
In `MergedEnvironmentVariableCollection.applyToProcessEnvironment` ([`environmentVariableCollection.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/environmentVariableCollection.ts#L88-L98)), defensively trim trailing/leading newlines (`[\r\n]+`) from the existing environment variable before applying `Append` or `Prepend`.
A PR with unit tests covering this fix and multi-byte / full-width paths is ready to submit.

issues.body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes, because copilot chat is a "built-in" extension Hi, One of my colleagues accidentally clicked on the "Disable AI Features" when trying to get setup with copilot in VS Code. It then said "This extension is disabled globally by the user". You can see here that he does not have VS Code open in a workspace, as there is no little arrow dropdown to the right to ask if he wants to do it in workspace or globally, so clicking the button does it globally. However, we could not figure out how to get it to be re-enabled - try clicking the disable button again doesn't change anything. I asked him if this setting is checked or unchecked: and he showed that it was unchecked. So I tried to replicate the problem myself: 1. I had VS Code open in a workspace folder and clicked "Disable AI Features in this workspace" 2. I visited the same setting and saw that it was still unchecked (even though surely it should then be checked?) for both user and workspace settings I fixed the issue by going to the user version of the setting and checking it, waiting a sec, then unchecking it, and this finally allowed me to bring copilot back. I asked my colleague to do the same and it also worked for him (he's on 1.138.0 and I'm on 1.139.1). - VS Code Version: 1.139.1 - OS Version: Windows 11 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Navigate to Github Copilot Chat extension view 2. Click "Disable AI features" (doesn't matter if its workspace or globally) and see that copilot chat and agent buttons are gone 3. Open VS Code settings and find "Chat > Disable AI features" 4. See that it is unchecked, even though it should be checked after the button being clicked 5. To fix, check it, then uncheck it again 6. See that copilot chat and agents buttons are back Also, some extra feedback for free: After clicking the "disable AI features" then in the github copilot chat extension view and clicking on the cog and selecting settings, it puts the filter in settings window as copilot chat, which doesn't have any settings under that name - its settings are gone because the extension is "disabled". Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (web UI, no extensions involved)

- VS Code Version: insiders.vscode.dev/agents (Agents window, web)
- OS Version: Android (Chrome for Android, current stable)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On an Android phone, open https://insiders.vscode.dev/agents in Chrome and open a session with an agent.
2. Have the agent produce a chat reply that contains Markdown links (e.g. a list of GitHub pull request URLs, either `[#1234](https://github.com/...)` links or bare URLs).
3. Tap any of the links in the chat reply.

**Expected:** the link opens (new tab or same tab), as it does on desktop browsers.

**Actual:** tapping does nothing. No navigation, no visual feedback. The same links work fine with a mouse on desktop Chrome — this is specific to touch input on mobile.

Additional detail:

- It is not only Markdown links in the chat responses. Small interactive elements rendered inside the conversation are also unresponsive to touch — for example a tiny "Skip" option shown alongside an agent question could not be activated by tapping it.
- Long-press on a link does not offer the usual "open in new tab" context menu either, which suggests the anchor is not receiving the touch events at all (possibly an overlay capturing pointer/touch events, or hover-only activation logic).
- Practical impact: any agent workflow that ends with "here are the PRs/issues to open" is unusable from a phone; the links have to be retyped by hand or published elsewhere (e.g. a gist or branch README on github.com) just to get tappable links.

Happy to provide a screen recording or try instrumented builds if that helps.

issues.title: Support persistent extension tabs beside Chat in the Secondary Side Bar (Gemini/Antigravity use case)
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

## Feature request

Provide a supported, persistent way for users to place an extension's view container as a tab in the Secondary Side Bar alongside Chat, with placement preserved across VS Code and extension updates.

## Use case

In my setup, installing Codex and Claude Code makes their tabs available alongside Chat. I want the same experience for my Gemini workflow, using the `google.google-antigravity` extension: a Gemini tab in the same strip, so I can switch assistants while keeping the editor and primary sidebar available.

Ideally, installing a compatible extension would make its tab available there automatically. Users should also be able to choose and retain that placement through supported VS Code UI or configuration.

## Current workaround and problem

I created a working customization:

https://github.com/arviphd/codex-customizations/tree/main/vscode/antigravity-gemini-sidebar

The script currently:

- Changes the extension manifest's view container from `activitybar` to `secondarySidebar`, assigns a new container ID, and labels it Gemini.
- Changes the extension's internal `viewLocation` from `sidebar` to `auxiliarybar` so its focus/close commands target the intended region.
- Updates VS Code's saved layout entries and clears stale extension scan caches, followed by a full restart.

I have observed losing this customization after updates. The repository documents one concrete cause: updating or reinstalling the extension replaces its installation directory and overwrites the patched files. I have not isolated a separate VS Code-update-only persistence bug.

Editing installed extension code and VS Code's layout database is a fragile way to maintain a preferred UI layout.

## Requested behavior

1. Make extension view containers discoverable as selectable tabs beside Chat in the Secondary Side Bar, through a supported extension contribution and/or a user placement action.
2. Preserve user-selected location, pinning, and order across restarts and normal VS Code/extension updates when extension and view identifiers remain stable.
3. Ensure supported view reveal/focus commands respect the selected location; document how extension authors should handle location-dependent behavior.
4. Allow this workflow without editing installed extension files, manipulating `state.vscdb`, or clearing extension scan caches.

## Scope and routing

The requested outcome is consistent placement of an extension's own UI as a sibling tab beside Chat. The example uses Google Antigravity, locally relabeled Gemini by my script.

The workaround already uses `contributes.viewsContainers.secondarySidebar`, so this is not a claim that VS Code has no Secondary Side Bar contribution mechanism. The gap I want addressed is achieving and retaining this experience through supported configuration and extension behavior.

If existing VS Code APIs and layout controls already cover the full scenario, please point to the supported approach and clarify which remaining changes belong with Google's extension. I recognize that VS Code cannot fix arbitrary location assumptions inside third-party extension code.

issues.body:
Title:
Copilot Chat replied in Russian during a Ukrainian-language conversation and gave inconsistent explanations

Description:

On September 25, 2026, I communicated with GitHub Copilot Chat entirely in Ukrainian. None of my messages were written in Russian. Despite this, Copilot initially replied in Russian.

Examples of the Russian responses:

"SSH-соединение установлено и ожидает пароль пользователя admin. Введите пароль непосредственно в терминале VS Code."

"Да, в большинстве случаев VPN будет работать за другим роутером даже при изменении WAN-адреса."

When I asked why Copilot switched to Russian, it gave several inconsistent explanations. It first referred to an "internal language instruction", then described it as a mechanically assigned locale parameter, and later stated that the session context contained:

"Respond in the following locale: ru"

Copilot later acknowledged that:

- none of my messages were in Russian;
- the locale did not come from my messages;
- the locale was not based on my country, location, IP address, project files, or VS Code settings;
- it did not know which component generated or supplied the instruction;
- its previous explanation about a mechanically assigned locale was an assumption and not a verified fact.

This behavior is confusing and reduces confidence in the reliability of Copilot Chat.

issues.title: Agents: cached tunnels trigger repeated GitHub sign-in loop

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
## Summary

Opening/reloading the Agents window can queue one interactive GitHub sign-in per cached remote Agent Host tunnel. Completing a sign-in immediately opens the next queued flow, creating an apparently endless sign-in cycle that only stops when VS Code exits.

## Observed behavior

On VS Code Insiders 1.140.0-insider on Windows:

- The Agents window restored 9 cached Dev Tunnels.
- No cached GitHub session initially satisfied the configured tunnel scopes (`read:org user:email`).
- 10 identical scope requests were made within one millisecond (9 tunnels plus the Agents setup flow).
- The GitHub authentication provider serialized the interactive requests.
- Successful sign-ins replaced the same account session (`added=1, removed=1`) and then the next queued request opened another browser flow.
- Exiting VS Code canceled the queue. After restart, the newly created scoped session was reused and the loop stopped.

The repeated browser callbacks also created several empty timestamped log-run directories. Those were callback processes, not crashes.

## Root cause

Automatic entry reconciliation starts connections with `userInitiated: false`:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/remoteAgentHostServiceImpl.ts

For gateway-capable tunnels with no saved location preference, the tunnel factory then changes the connection to user-initiated:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/electron-browser/tunnelAgentHostServiceImpl.ts

```ts
const connectOptions = this.getAutoConnectMode(tunnel) === 'prompt'
    ? { ...options, userInitiated: true }
    : options;
```

`!connectOptions.userInitiated` is subsequently passed as the `silent` argument to `_getToken*`. Each cached prompt-mode tunnel therefore performs interactive authentication during automatic startup reconciliation and calls `createSession` when no matching token exists.

The browser tunnel implementation has the same pattern:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/browserTunnelAgentHostService.ts

## Expected behavior

Automatic reconciliation of cached tunnels must never trigger interactive authentication. Only an explicit user connect action or the Agents setup flow should open sign-in.

Gateway endpoint selection may require interaction, but that should not convert background authentication into interactive authentication. Equivalent authentication requests should ideally also be coalesced or canceled after the first succeeds.

## Suggested fix

Separate the authentication interaction policy from the gateway-selection interaction policy:

- Preserve `userInitiated: false` for authentication during automatic reconciliation.
- Independently allow or defer gateway endpoint selection when a location preference is missing.
- Consider coalescing equivalent in-flight authentication requests as defense in depth.

## Additional notes

The GitHub `429` for optional EDU details and failures connecting to stale/local remote hosts occurred during the incident but were not causal.

issues.title: Claude agent host: steering messages sent mid-turn are never shown in the conversation

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
- VS Code Version: 1.139.0
- OS Version: macOS 27.0 (arm64)
- Harness: Claude agent host (Agents window), `chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction: "steer"` (default)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Claude session and send a prompt that takes a while.
2. While the turn is running, type a follow-up and send it (steer).

## Expected

The steering message appears in the conversation, as it does in the Claude Code CLI and in Copilot sessions, so the user can see what was sent and when.

## Actual

The message disappears from the input and never renders. The agent host log shows it was delivered (`injectSteering: enqueued id=request_… sdkUuid=request_…`), and the model's next output responds to it, but the transcript shows no user message for it, neither while the turn runs nor after it completes. It feels like the message was swallowed, and there's no record of what steered the turn when reading the session later.

## Related

- #333174 lists "Promote a steering message into its own turn" as unsupported for external harnesses. This request is narrower: just show the steered text inline in the running turn.
- #336692 (multiple steering messages replace each other) implies steering messages are visible for other harnesses.

releases.name: June 2025
releases.body:
Welcome to the June 2025 release of Visual Studio Code. There are many updates in this version that we hope you'll like, some of the key highlights include:

## Chat

- Explore and contribute to the open sourced GitHub Copilot Chat extension ([Read our blog post](https://code.visualstudio.com/blogs/2025/06/30/openSourceAIEditorFirstMilestone)).
- Generate custom instructions that reflect your project's conventions ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_generate-custom-instructions)).
- Use custom modes to tailor chat for tasks like planning or research ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_chat-mode-improvements)).
- Automatically approve selected terminal commands ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_terminal-auto-approval-experimental)).
- Edit and resubmit previous chat requests ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_edit-previous-requests-experimental)).


## MCP

- MCP support is now generally available in VS Code ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_mcp-support-in-vs-code-is-generally-available)).
- Easily install and manage MCP servers with the MCP view and gallery ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_mcp-server-discovery-and-installation)).
- MCP servers as first-class resources in profiles and Settings Sync ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_mcp-servers-as-first-class-resources)).

## Editor experience

- Delegate tasks to Copilot coding agent and let it handle them in the background ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_start-a-coding-agent-session-preview)).
- Scroll the editor on middle click ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_scroll-on-middle-click)).
If you'd like to read these release notes online, go to [Updates](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates) on [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/). Insiders: Want to try new features as soon as possible? You can download the nightly [Insiders](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders) build and try the latest updates as soon as they are available.

releases.name: March 2025
releases.body:
Welcome to the March 2025 release of Visual Studio Code. There are many updates in this version that we hope you'll like, some of the key highlights include:

* **Agent mode**
  * Agent mode is available in VS Code Stable. Enable it by setting `chat.agent.enabled:true` ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_agent-mode-is-available-in-vs-code-stable)).
  * Extend agent mode with Model Context Protocol (MCP) server tools ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_model-context-protocol-server-support)).
  * Try the new built-in tools in agent mode for fetching web content, finding symbol references, and deep thinking ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_agent-mode-tools)).

* **Code editing**
  * Next Edit Suggestions is now generally available ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_next-edit-suggestions-general-availability)).
  * Benefit from fewer distractions such as diagnostics events while AI edits are applied in the editor ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_ai-edits-improvements)).

* **Chat**
  * Use your own API keys to access more language models in chat (preview) ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_bring-your-own-key-byok-preview)).
  * Easily switch between ask, edit, and agent mode from the unified chat experience ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_unified-chat-experience)).
  * Experience improved workspace search speed and accuracy with instant remote workspace indexing ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_faster-workspace-searches-with-instant-indexing)).

* **Notebook editing**
  * Create and edit notebooks as easily as code files with support for edit and agent mode ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_ai-notebook-editing-improvements)).

For the complete release notes go to [Updates](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99) on [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com).

**Insiders:** Want to try new features as soon as possible? You can download the nightly [Insiders](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders) build and try the latest updates as soon as they are available.

Welcome to the October 2024 release of Visual Studio Code. There are many updates in this version that we hope you'll like, some of the key highlights include:

- [Copilot Chat in Secondary Side Bar](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_95#_chat-in-the-secondary-side-bar) - Keep Copilot Chat open and ready to-go while you work.
- [Multiple GitHub accounts](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_95#_multiple-github-accounts) - Log in to multiple GitHub accounts in VS Code simultaneously.
- [Copilot code reviews](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_95#_copilot-code-reviews) - Get a quick review pass or a deeper review of uncommitted changes.

releases.name: November 2022
releases.body:
Welcome to the November 2022 release of Visual Studio Code. There are many updates in this version that we hope you'll like, some of the key highlights include:

* **[Customize Explorer auto reveal](#custom-explorer-autoreveal-logic)** - Decide which files scroll into view in the Explorer.
* **[Hide Activity bar and Panel badges](#hide-badges-per-view-container)** - Simplify the editor UI by toggling state badges.
* **[Audio cues for notebooks and diff view](#audio-cues-for-notebook-execution)** - Sounds for cell run results, added or removed lines.
* **[Merge editor Undo/Redo](#merge-editor)** - Quickly revert or reapply merge conflict actions.
* **[Manage unsafe repositories](#manage-unsafe-git-repositories)** - Prevent Git operations on folders not owned by you.
* **[JavaScript console.profile collection](#javascript-debugging)** - Easily create CPU profiles for viewing in VS Code.
* **[Go to Definition from return](#go-to-definition-on-return)** - Jump to the top of JavaScript/TypeScript functions.
* **[Remote Tunnels](#remote-development)** - Create a connection to any machine, without needing SSH.
* **[Jupyter notebook "Just My Code" debugging](#jupyter)** - Avoid stepping into Python library code.
* **[Dev Container GPU support](#remote-development-extensions)** - Request a GPU when creating a Dev Container.

>If you'd like to read these release notes online, go to [Updates](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates) on [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com).

Welcome to the August 2022 release of Visual Studio Code. August is when many of the engineers on VS Code take their vacations, but there are still many updates in this version that we hope you'll like:

* **[TypeScript livestreams](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_71#typescript-livestreams)** - Watch TS "Crash Course" or "Tips and Tricks" on YouTube.
* **[Live Preview extension](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_71#live-preview)** - Live Preview now supports multi-root web projects.
* **[Markdown Language Server blog post](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_71#markdown-language-server)** - Learn how Markdown support moved to a Language Server.

**Insiders:** Want to try new features as soon as possible? You can download the nightly [Insiders](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders) build and try the latest updates as soon as they are available.
